`README.md`:

```md
# saga3

Agents write this project entirely; it is optimized for agent vibe coding,
debugging, and RSI.

Reverse-engineering workspace for 「ぼくのかいぞうしたさいこうの3.12」
(bokuno, Proto1.123), a well-known hack of Romancing SaGa 3 (SFC).

## Goal

1. Disassemble the bokuno ROM (event VM, maps, graphics, battle data).
2. Reimplement the game in **Go / Ebitengine** — the ROM's original
   65816 code is reference material, not the shipping artifact.
3. All text lives in **swappable translation tables**; adding a language is
   a data file, not a code change. First table: zh-TW (the owner's target
   language).

Nothing copyrighted is committed here. The ROM chain is rebuilt from the
user's own cartridge dump plus publicly distributed fan patches; this repo
tracks tools, notes, and verification data only.

## Play

```sh
go run ./cmd/saga3 --lang zh-TW
```

It reads `exports/data` (built by the chain below) and
`exports/translations/zh-TW.json`. The shell opens a window; headless
runs wrap the same flags in `xvfb-run` (`scripts/shell-smoke.sh` is the
worked example).

## Verified ROM chain

Reproduce with (outputs land in `patches/` and `data/`, the paths the
tools and `scripts/parity_gate.sh` read; the base dump and the two patch
files are user-provided, see Inputs):

```sh
# 1. the two patched ROMs
go run ./cmd/ipsapply <Romancing Sa-Ga 3 (Japan) (Rev 1).sfc> <ぼくのProto1.123.ips> patches/bokuno_jp.sfc
xdelta3 -d -f -s patches/bokuno_jp.sfc bokuno_ko_v0.118.xdelta patches/bokuno_ko.sfc

# 2. the glyph assignment, then the event dumps that decode through it
#    (glyphtable first: dumpevents reads the JSON glyphtable writes)
go run ./cmd/glyphtable tools/tables data/glyphs_jp.json
go run ./cmd/dumpevents data

# 3. the runtime exports the shell reads (exports/data). The tools that
#    take the ROM as their first positional default it to
#    patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, and the glyph-JSON positional to
#    data/glyphs_jp.json — drop leading arguments, the leftmost dropped
#    one is the ROM
cp data/events/index.json exports/data/events_index.json   # the VM's frame-end table
go run ./cmd/exportdialogue exports/data/events.json       # + events_names.json
go run ./cmd/dumpitems exports/data
go run ./cmd/exportmap all exports/data                    # maps/, field tables, figures/
go run ./cmd/exportbattle exports/data
go run ./cmd/exportbosslist exports/data

# 4. BGM — the one MesenCE-dependent step (docs/music.md); without it the
#    shell fails the boot at the catalog load
go run ./cmd/bgmrip rip
go run ./cmd/bgmrip convert
```

Verified 2026-11-24: steps 1-3 ran with outputs redirected into a fresh
directory; the rebuilt `events.json` and `events_index.json` compared
byte-identical to the committed exports (`cmp` clean), and the rebuilt
data dir booted the title screen (`SHELL-STATE final frame=2 screen=0 …`,
exit 0) and the 0249 field (`SHELL-SHOT … mean=40 size=512x448`) once the
ripped `bgm/` was in place. Step 4 is the MesenCE-dependent piece (the
rip itself is docs/music.md's pipeline, last run 2026-11-17,
`CONVERTED ok=90 silent=2 failed=0`); without it the boot fails loudly:
`saga3: shell: load bgm catalog: open …/data/bgm/catalog.json: no such
file or directory`. `exports/fonts/` and `exports/translations/`
are tracked and need no build step; the walk-sprite captures
(`exports/data/walk_sprites/`) and the SFX rip (`exports/data/sfx/`) are
separate captures this chain does not rebuild (docs/sprites.md,
docs/sfx.md).

| Stage | Size | CRC32 | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base: RS3 JP v1.1 (No-Intro Rev 1) | 4,194,304 | `6C50C2CF` | `3EFA91F1…16897` |
| bokuno JP (patched) | 8,388,608 | `7E165025` | `4793e142…f2da0` |
| bokuno KR (v0.118 xdelta applied) | 8,388,608 | `709120DF` | `703B5B3E…BF1B8` |

Sources: base dump verified against superfamicom.org; the two patched hashes
are the values published in beck4679-alt/bokuno-rs3-ko (upstream
docs/INSTALL.md, docs/FILES.md).

## Inputs (not in repo)

- Base ROM: user's own dump of the Japanese v1.1 cartridge.
- `ぼくのProto1.123.ips` — from `ぼくの（略更新.rar` at
  https://ux.getuploader.com/romancingsaga312/download/560 (author-run
  uploader; note it bans some datacenter ASNs via Cloudflare error 1005).
- `bokuno_ko_v0.118.xdelta` — https://github.com/beck4679-alt/bokuno-rs3-ko/releases
- Reference modules unpacked from that repo's
  `docs/localization-reference/*/` zips (opcode lengths, runtime text,
  event identity, ROM guard) — the working basis for the bokuno event VM.

## Tooling

All tools are Go (`module saga3`). The gate is `bash scripts/gate.sh`:
static checks over internal, cmd and tools, then the golden,
translation, shell-smoke and parity steps.

Chain tools:

- `cmd/ipsapply` — IPS applier.
- `cmd/glyphtable` — builds the glyph assignment from the RS3 community
  code tables (`tools/tables/`, Shift-JIS INIs).
- `cmd/dumpevents` — disassembles all 4,351 native events to
  `data/events/` with decoded Japanese text.
- `cmd/dumpnames` — extracts actor/item/indexed name tables.
- `cmd/exportdialogue` — converts events to the JSON the game consumes
  (`exports/data/events.json`: flattened dialogue pages + raw op stream).
- `cmd/checktranslations` — validates the translation tables against the
  exports; with no arguments it reads `exports/data/events.json` and
  `exports/translations`.
- `internal/bokuno` — the event VM's decode reference: opcode tables,
  operand decoding, event pointer lookup, linear walker, text decoder.

Map and battle probes:

- `cmd/mapheader` — decodes one submap header.
- `cmd/pathfind` — BFS over a submap's walkable grid; prints a direction
  program for the emulator walk harness.
- `cmd/proppoints` — walks a submap's property layer and prints every
  rectangle, flagging the 0x08/0x09 event-point entries.
- `cmd/reversegraph` — which maps' exits, destinations and edge events
  lead into a target map.
- `cmd/dumptriggers <rom> -map <id>` — one map's decode as text (exits,
  triggers, NPCs, chests); batch mode writes `map<ID>.json` per map plus
  `jump_table.json`.
- `cmd/eventrange` — prints the native event range for given ids
  (block-table lookup).
- `cmd/genenemynames` — regenerates `internal/battledata/names.go` (the
  enemy name arrays) from the ROM.

`ref/` holds the upstream bokuno-rs3-ko JS modules we ported from; they
are reference material, not part of the toolchain.

## Game data (the retired Godot prototype)

The GDScript/Godot prototype retired 2026-11-23 when every gate step
gained its Go equivalent (docs/migration.md's audit table holds the
mapping; the shell lives in `internal/game/shell` + `cmd/saga3`).
`exports/` (renamed from `godot/` 2026-11-24 when the engine retired) keeps only the engine-neutral data, read in place:

- `exports/data/` — the exports (events.json, per-map PPU forms, battle
  tables, bgm): `cmd/saga3` reads it at runtime (`--data` overrides).
- `exports/translations/<lang>.json` — translation tables:
  `{event id: {original page: translated page}}`; untranslated pages
  fall back to the extracted Japanese. zh-TW is the working table.
  `cmd/checktranslations` validates them against the exports; the shell
  applies them at display (flow.LoadTranslation + the Page lookup,
  fc66dc3; docs/migration.md, remaining items).
- `exports/fonts/` — the UI font the shell renders with.
- `exports/tests/` — the engine-derived goldens the Go tests read in
  place (fixture JSONs, `trails/*.trail.gz`); `cutscene_capture.lua`
  re-captures the cutscene golden from the ROM.

## IPS note

The IPS RLE record is count-then-value (`offset(3) 00 00 count(2 BE)
value(1)`), the Floating IPS / libips convention. The value-first reading
silently corrupts this project's patches; verified byte-identical against
Flips on Proto1.123 (2026-11-15).

`cmd/bgmrip/convert.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// trackEntry is one row of catalog.json, the contract the Godot scenes
// read (docs/music.md): pick BGM by id, get the ogg file to stream.
type trackEntry struct {
	ID          int      `json:"id"`
	Hex         string   `json:"hex"`
	NameJP      string   `json:"name_jp"`
	NameEN      string   `json:"name_en"`
	Slug        string   `json:"slug"`
	NameSource  string   `json:"name_source"`
	OGG         string   `json:"ogg"`
	Status      string   `json:"status"` // ok | silent | failed
	Reason      string   `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	DurationSec float64  `json:"duration_sec,omitempty"`
	MeanVolDB   *float64 `json:"mean_volume_db,omitempty"`
}

func convertCmd(args []string) error {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("convert", flag.ExitOnError)
	spcDir := fs.String("spc", "/tmp/bgm-agent/spc", "dir of .spc dumps")
	oggDir := fs.String("ogg", filepath.Join(repoRoot, "exports", "data", "bgm"), "output dir for .ogg")
	catalog := fs.String("catalog", filepath.Join(repoRoot, "exports", "data", "bgm", "catalog.json"), "catalog.json path")
	fs.Parse(args)

	var statuses []ripStatus
	statusDir := filepath.Join(*spcDir, "rip_status")
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(statusDir, "*.json"))
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no rip statuses in %s (run `bgmrip rip` first)", statusDir)
	}
	for _, p := range files {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", p, err)
		}
		var st ripStatus
		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &st); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", p, err)
		}
		statuses = append(statuses, st)
	}
	sort.Slice(statuses, func(i, j int) bool { return statuses[i].ID < statuses[j].ID })

	var entries []trackEntry
	okCount, silentCount := 0, 0
	for _, st := range statuses {
		name := nameFor(st.ID)
		e := trackEntry{
			ID:         st.ID,
			Hex:        fmt.Sprintf("%02X", st.ID),
			NameJP:     name.JP,
			NameEN:     name.EN,
			Slug:       name.Slug,
			NameSource: name.Source,
			Status:     "failed",
			Reason:     st.Reason,
		}
		if !st.OK {
			entries = append(entries, e)
			fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X skip (rip failed: %s)\n", st.ID, st.Reason)
			continue
		}
		spcPath := filepath.Join(*spcDir, e.Hex+".spc")
		ogg := fmt.Sprintf("%02X_%s.ogg", st.ID, name.Slug)
		oggPath := filepath.Join(*oggDir, ogg)
		if err := renderOGG(spcPath, oggPath); err != nil {
			e.Reason = "render: " + err.Error()
			entries = append(entries, e)
			fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X skip (%s)\n", st.ID, e.Reason)
			continue
		}
		dur, meanDB, maxDB, silent, err := probeOGG(oggPath)
		if err != nil {
			e.Reason = "probe: " + err.Error()
			entries = append(entries, e)
			fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X skip (%s)\n", st.ID, e.Reason)
			continue
		}
		firstSilent := silent
		if silent {
			// Retry once with the echo delay zeroed (see renderOGGNoEcho):
			// six ambient ids key voices in the dump but libgme's render of
			// the dumped echo setup is digital silence. Their ambience is
			// quiet by nature, so the retry counts as silent on PEAK level
			// (below -80 dB peak is the digital-silence floor; the mean rule
			// would reject a -35 dB-peak wind rumble whose mean is -81).
			if err := renderOGGNoEcho(spcPath, oggPath); err != nil {
				e.Reason = "render no-echo: " + err.Error()
				entries = append(entries, e)
				fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X skip (%s)\n", st.ID, e.Reason)
				continue
			}
			var maxRetry float64
			dur, meanDB, maxRetry, _, err = probeOGG(oggPath)
			if err != nil {
				e.Reason = "probe: " + err.Error()
				entries = append(entries, e)
				fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X skip (%s)\n", st.ID, e.Reason)
				continue
			}
			silent = maxRetry < -80 || math.IsInf(maxRetry, -1)
		}
		if silent {
			e.Status, e.Reason = "silent", "mean volume below -60 dB"
			silentCount++
			os.Remove(oggPath) // renderOGG already wrote it; a silent track ships no file
			fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X skip (silent, mean %.1f dB peak %.1f dB)\n", st.ID, meanDB, maxDB)
		} else {
			e.Status = "ok"
			e.OGG = ogg
			e.DurationSec = dur
			e.MeanVolDB = &meanDB
			okCount++
			note := ""
			if firstSilent {
				note = " (no-echo render: EDL zeroed, docs/music.md)"
			}
			fmt.Printf("CONV id=%02X ok %-40s %.1f s mean %.1f dB%s\n", st.ID, ogg, dur, meanDB, note)
		}
		entries = append(entries, e)
	}

	cat := trackCatalog{
		ROM:    "patches/bokuno_jp.sfc",
		Tracks: entries,
	}
	out, err := json.MarshalIndent(cat, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(*catalog, out, 0o644); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("write catalog: %w", err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("CONVERTED ok=%d silent=%d failed=%d -> %s\n", okCount,
		silentCount, len(entries)-okCount-silentCount, *catalog)
	return nil
}

type trackCatalog struct {
	ROM    string       `json:"rom"`
	Tracks []trackEntry `json:"tracks"`
}

// renderOGG reproduces rip_track.sh's verified conversion: libgme render
// capped at 40 s (some tracks never signal end; -stream_loop hangs on the
// non-seekable gme stream), the WAV doubled so the seam sits on the loop
// point, libvorbis -q:a 5.
func renderOGG(spcPath, oggPath string) error {
	wavPath := strings.TrimSuffix(oggPath, ".ogg") + ".wav"
	defer os.Remove(wavPath)
	if err := runCLI("ffmpeg", "-y", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error",
		"-t", "40", "-i", spcPath, wavPath); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return runCLI("ffmpeg", "-y", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error",
		"-i", wavPath, "-i", wavPath,
		"-filter_complex", "[0:a][1:a]concat=n=2:v=0:a=1",
		"-c:a", "libvorbis", "-q:a", "5", oggPath)
}

// renderOGGNoEcho is the fallback for the ambient-overlay dumps whose
// libgme render comes out as digital silence while the dump itself has
// keyed voices (DSP envelope maxed, OUTX non-zero — Mesen was audibly
// playing them). Zeroing the DSP echo-delay register EDL ($7D) in the
// dumped register image makes libgme render the dry path. Mechanism
// recorded in docs/music.md § "The six silent overlays".
func renderOGGNoEcho(spcPath, oggPath string) error {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(spcPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	const dspEDL = 0x10100 + 0x7D // DSP register image, register $7D = EDL
	if len(raw) < dspEDL+1 {
		return fmt.Errorf("spc too small for DSP image: %s", spcPath)
	}
	raw[dspEDL] = 0
	patched := spcPath + ".edl0"
	if err := os.WriteFile(patched, raw, 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer os.Remove(patched)
	return renderOGG(patched, oggPath)
}

// probeOGG returns duration, mean volume, peak volume, and whether the
// track is silent (mean volume below -60 dB, i.e. the rip captured no
// audible audio).
func probeOGG(path string) (dur float64, meanDB float64, maxDB float64, silent bool, err error) {
	out, err := runOutput("ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries",
		"format=duration", "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", path)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, err
	}
	dur, err = strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(out), 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, fmt.Errorf("ffprobe duration %q: %w", out, err)
	}
	out, err = runOutput("ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", path,
		"-af", "volumedetect", "-f", "null", "-")
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, err
	}
	m := regexp.MustCompile(`mean_volume: (-?[0-9.]+) dB`).FindStringSubmatch(out)
	if m == nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, fmt.Errorf("volumedetect: no mean_volume in output")
	}
	meanDB, err = strconv.ParseFloat(m[1], 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, err
	}
	mx := regexp.MustCompile(`max_volume: (-?[0-9.]+) dB`).FindStringSubmatch(out)
	if mx == nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, fmt.Errorf("volumedetect: no max_volume in output")
	}
	maxDB, err = strconv.ParseFloat(mx[1], 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, false, err
	}
	return dur, meanDB, maxDB, meanDB < -60 || math.IsInf(meanDB, -1), nil
}

func runCLI(name string, args ...string) error {
	if out, err := runOutput(name, args...); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w: %s", name, strings.Join(args, " "), err,
			strings.TrimSpace(lastLines(out, 5)))
	}
	return nil
}

func runOutput(name string, args ...string) (string, error) {
	cmd := exec.Command(name, args...)
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	return string(out), err
}

func lastLines(s string, n int) string {
	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(s, "\n"), "\n")
	if len(lines) > n {
		lines = lines[len(lines)-n:]
	}
	return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
}

`cmd/bgmrip/main.go`:

```go
// bgmrip batch-rips the vanilla RS3 song table (IDs 0x00-0x5B) of
// patches/bokuno_jp.sfc to .spc via the MesenCE song-dispatch hijack
// (tools/emulator/rip.lua), names each track, converts each to OGG in
// exports/data/bgm/ and writes catalog.json — the shell's BGM catalog
// (internal/game/shell/bgm.go reads it).
//
// Subcommands:
//
//	bgmrip rip    [-jobs N] [-ids LO-HI] [-work DIR] [-spc DIR]
//	bgmrip match  -spc DIR -ref ZIP
//	bgmrip convert [-spc DIR] [-ogg DIR] [-catalog FILE]
//
// The .spc dumps and the OGG files contain Square's copyrighted music and
// stay user-local (docs/music.md); only catalog.json's shape is documented
// in the repo. paths default to the repo at /home/newlix/projects/saga3.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		usage()
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	var err error
	switch os.Args[1] {
	case "rip":
		err = ripCmd(os.Args[2:])
	case "match":
		err = matchCmd(os.Args[2:])
	case "convert":
		err = convertCmd(os.Args[2:])
	default:
		usage()
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "bgmrip:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func usage() {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, `usage:
  bgmrip rip    [-jobs N] [-ids LO-HI] [-work DIR] [-spc DIR] [-repo DIR]
  bgmrip match  -spc DIR -ref ZIP
  bgmrip convert [-spc DIR] [-ogg DIR] [-catalog FILE] [-repo DIR]`)
}

`cmd/bgmrip/match.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"archive/zip"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// spcARAM returns the 64 KiB ARAM block of a .spc file (offset 0x100).
func spcARAM(data []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if len(data) < 0x10100 || string(data[:33]) != "SNES-SPC700 Sound File Data v0.30" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("not an SPC file (%d bytes)", len(data))
	}
	return data[0x100:0x10000], nil
}

// spcID666Title returns the ID666 song title (offset 0x2E, 32 bytes) when the
// tag is present (byte 0x23 != 0x1B) and non-empty.
func spcID666Title(data []byte) string {
	if len(data) < 0x2E || data[0x23] == 0x1B {
		return ""
	}
	t := string(data[0x2E : 0x2E+32])
	if i := strings.IndexByte(t, 0); i >= 0 {
		t = t[:i]
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(t)
}

// matchCmd names our dumps by byte-matching their ARAM against a community
// SPC set (zophar RS3 set; naming reference only, never a project asset).
// Score = count of matching 64-byte ARAM windows on any alignment; the same
// song's sequence data dominates ARAM, so a real match scores in the
// hundreds and different tracks in single digits.
func matchCmd(args []string) error {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("match", flag.ExitOnError)
	spcDir := fs.String("spc", "/tmp/bgm-agent/spc", "dir of our .spc dumps")
	ref := fs.String("ref", "", "community SPC set (zip)")
	fs.Parse(args)
	if *ref == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("match: -ref ZIP is required")
	}

	zr, err := zip.OpenReader(*ref)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("open ref zip: %w", err)
	}
	defer zr.Close()

	type refTrack struct {
		Title string
		ARAM  []byte
	}
	var refs []refTrack
	for _, f := range zr.File {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(f.Name), ".spc") {
			continue
		}
		rc, err := f.Open()
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", f.Name, err)
		}
		data, err := io.ReadAll(rc)
		rc.Close()
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", f.Name, err)
		}
		aram, err := spcARAM(data)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", f.Name, err)
		}
		title := spcID666Title(data)
		if title == "" {
			title = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(f.Name), ".spc")
		}
		refs = append(refs, refTrack{Title: title, ARAM: aram})
	}
	if len(refs) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no .spc files in %s", *ref)
	}

	matches := map[int]string{}
	for id := 0; id < numTracks; id++ {
		ours, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(*spcDir, fmt.Sprintf("%02X.spc", id)))
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		aram, err := spcARAM(ours)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("our dump %02X.spc: %w", id, err)
		}
		best, bestScore := "", 0
		second := 0
		for _, r := range refs {
			s := seqMatchLen(aram, r.ARAM)
			if s > bestScore {
				second = bestScore
				best, bestScore = r.Title, s
			} else if s > second {
				second = s
			}
		}
		if bestScore >= 64 && bestScore > 4*second {
			matches[id] = best
			fmt.Printf("MATCH id=%02X %-40s score=%d second=%d\n", id, best, bestScore, second)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("NOMATCH id=%02X best=%q score=%d second=%d\n", id, best, bestScore, second)
		}
	}
	out, err := json.MarshalIndent(matches, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(*spcDir, "matches.json"), out, 0o644)
}

// seqMatchLen is the exact contiguous match length at ARAM $2224, where
// the RS3 driver uploads every sequence (ARAMBase, docs/music.md). The
// same song aligns byte-exactly from $2224 (927-2061 bytes observed on
// five known tracks); different songs diverge within a couple of bytes,
// so there is no gap tolerance — one wrong byte ends the run.
func seqMatchLen(a, b []byte) int {
	const start = 0x2224
	if len(a) < start || len(b) < start {
		return 0
	}
	n := 0
	for i := start; i < len(a) && i < len(b) && a[i] == b[i]; i++ {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// nameFor returns the tabled name, or the unknown fallback (empty names,
// slug "unknown_XX" — file names stay unique via the hex id prefix).
func nameFor(id int) trackName {
	if n, ok := trackNames[id]; ok && n.Slug != "" {
		return n
	}
	return trackName{Slug: "unknown", Source: "unknown"}
}

`cmd/bgmrip/rip.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

const (
	numTracks   = 92                // vanilla RS3 song table entries, docs/music.md
	mesenUserTO = 320 * time.Second // kill a hung Mesen; Mesen's own -timeout is 300 s
	mesenDir    = "/tmp/mesence"
	repoRoot    = "/home/newlix/projects/saga3"
)

// ripStatus is what rip learns per track; convert reads it back.
type ripStatus struct {
	ID          int    `json:"id"`
	OK          bool   `json:"ok"`
	Reason      string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	HijackFrame int    `json:"hijack_frame,omitempty"`
	SPCPC       string `json:"spc_pc,omitempty"`
	SPCSHA256   string `json:"spc_sha256,omitempty"`

	spcBytes []byte // not serialized; written to the spc dir by ripOne
}

func ripCmd(args []string) error {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("rip", flag.ExitOnError)
	jobs := fs.Int("jobs", 4, "parallel Mesen instances")
	dumpFrame := fs.Int("dump-frame", 2400, "frame to dump SPC state (40 s in-song; lower it when a track fades out before then)")
	ids := fs.String("ids", fmt.Sprintf("0-%d", numTracks-1), "track ids: LO-HI range or comma list")
	work := fs.String("work", "/tmp/bgm-agent/work", "scratch dir per track")
	spcDir := fs.String("spc", "/tmp/bgm-agent/spc", "output dir for .spc dumps")
	repo := fs.String("repo", repoRoot, "repo root (holds tools/ and patches/)")
	fs.Parse(args)

	idList, err := parseIDs(*ids)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(*spcDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create spc dir: %w", err)
	}
	template, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(*repo, "tools", "emulator", "rip.lua"))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read rip.lua template: %w", err)
	}

	idCh := make(chan int)
	statusCh := make(chan ripStatus, numTracks)
	for i := 0; i < *jobs; i++ {
		go func() {
			for id := range idCh {
				statusCh <- ripOne(*repo, string(template), id, *work, *spcDir, *dumpFrame)
			}
		}()
	}
	go func() {
		for _, id := range idList {
			idCh <- id
		}
		close(idCh)
	}()

	for range len(idList) {
		st := <-statusCh
		state := "ok"
		if !st.OK {
			state = "FAIL " + st.Reason
		}
		fmt.Printf("RIP id=%d (0x%02X) %s\n", st.ID, st.ID, state)
		// One status file per id: a re-run of a subrange merges instead of
		// clobbering the full run's statuses (convert reads all of them).
		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(st, "", "  ")
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		statusDir := filepath.Join(*spcDir, "rip_status")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(statusDir, 0o755); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("create status dir: %w", err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(statusDir, fmt.Sprintf("%02X.json", st.ID)), b, 0o644); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("write status: %w", err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// parseIDs accepts "LO-HI" or a comma-separated list of ids.
func parseIDs(s string) ([]int, error) {
	var out []int
	if lo, hi, ok := strings.Cut(s, "-"); ok && !strings.Contains(s, ",") {
		var l, h int
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(lo, "%d", &l); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse -ids %q: %w", s, err)
		}
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(hi, "%d", &h); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse -ids %q: %w", s, err)
		}
		if l < 0 || h >= numTracks || l > h {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("range %d-%d outside 0-%d", l, h, numTracks-1)
		}
		for i := l; i <= h; i++ {
			out = append(out, i)
		}
		return out, nil
	}
	for _, f := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
		var v int
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(strings.TrimSpace(f), "%d", &v); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse -ids %q: %w", s, err)
		}
		if v < 0 || v >= numTracks {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("id %d outside 0-%d", v, numTracks-1)
		}
		out = append(out, v)
	}
	if len(out) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse -ids %q: no ids", s)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// ripOne hijacks one dispatch to TARGET and rebuilds the .spc from stdout.
// The log format is tools/emulator/rip.lua's; spc_build.py is the Python
// reference for the rebuild (verified byte-identical, see docs/music.md).
func ripOne(repo, template string, id int, workDir, spcDir string, dumpFrame int) ripStatus {
	dir := filepath.Join(workDir, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", id))
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return ripStatus{ID: id, Reason: "mkdir: " + err.Error()}
	}
	lua := strings.Replace(string(template),
		"local TARGET = 0x00", fmt.Sprintf("local TARGET = %d", id), 1)
	lua = strings.Replace(lua,
		"local DUMP_FRAME = 2400", fmt.Sprintf("local DUMP_FRAME = %d", dumpFrame), 1)
	luaPath := filepath.Join(dir, "rip.lua")
	if err := os.WriteFile(luaPath, []byte(lua), 0o644); err != nil {
		return ripStatus{ID: id, Reason: "write lua: " + err.Error()}
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), mesenUserTO)
	defer cancel()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, filepath.Join(mesenDir, "Mesen"),
		"-testRunner", luaPath, filepath.Join(repo, "patches", "bokuno_jp.sfc"),
		"-enableStdout", "-timeout=300")
	cmd.Env = withoutDisplay(os.Environ())
	logPath := filepath.Join(dir, "stdout.log")
	logFile, err := os.Create(logPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ripStatus{ID: id, Reason: "create log: " + err.Error()}
	}
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = logFile, logFile
	runErr := cmd.Run()
	logFile.Close()

	st := parseRipLog(logPath)
	if st.ID == -1 { // log unreadable or no RIPINFO at all
		st.ID = id
		st.Reason = "log parse failed: " + runErr.Error()
		return st
	}
	if !st.OK {
		return st
	}
	spcPath := filepath.Join(spcDir, fmt.Sprintf("%02X.spc", id))
	if err := os.WriteFile(spcPath, st.spcBytes, 0o644); err != nil {
		return ripStatus{ID: id, Reason: "write spc: " + err.Error()}
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(st.spcBytes)
	st.SPCSHA256 = hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
	return st
}

func parseRipLog(logPath string) ripStatus {
	st := ripStatus{ID: -1}
	var ram, dsp []byte
	var regs [6]string // pc a ps x y sp
	f, err := os.Open(logPath)
	if err != nil {
		return st
	}
	defer f.Close()
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 8192), 16384)
	for sc.Scan() {
		line := sc.Text()
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "RIPINFO "):
			st.ID = 0
			for _, fv := range strings.Fields(line)[1:] {
				k, v, _ := strings.Cut(fv, "=")
				switch k {
				case "target":
					fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &st.ID)
				case "hijack_frame":
					if v == "nil" {
						st.HijackFrame = -1
					} else {
						fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &st.HijackFrame)
					}
				case "spcpc":
					regs[0] = v
				case "a":
					regs[1] = v
				case "ps":
					regs[2] = v
				case "x":
					regs[3] = v
				case "y":
					regs[4] = v
				case "sp":
					regs[5] = v
				}
			}
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "SPCDATA "):
			b, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(line[len("SPCDATA "):])
			if err != nil {
				return ripStatus{ID: -1, Reason: "bad SPCDATA base64"}
			}
			ram = append(ram, b...)
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "DSPDATA "):
			b, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(line[len("DSPDATA "):])
			if err != nil {
				return ripStatus{ID: -1, Reason: "bad DSPDATA base64"}
			}
			dsp = append(dsp, b...)
		}
	}
	if st.ID < 0 {
		return ripStatus{ID: -1, Reason: "no RIPINFO in log"}
	}
	st.SPCPC = regs[0]
	if st.HijackFrame <= 0 {
		st.Reason = "song dispatcher never ran (hijack_frame nil)"
		return st
	}
	if len(ram) != 65536 {
		st.Reason = fmt.Sprintf("RAM dump %d bytes, want 65536", len(ram))
		return st
	}
	if len(dsp) != 128 {
		st.Reason = fmt.Sprintf("DSP dump %d bytes, want 128", len(dsp))
		return st
	}
	st.spcBytes = buildSPC(regs, ram, dsp)
	st.OK = true
	return st
}

// buildSPC assembles the format-v0.30 file: header + SPC700 registers +
// 64 KiB ARAM + DSP registers (same layout as tools/emulator/spc_build.py).
func buildSPC(regs [6]string, ram, dsp []byte) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 66048)
	copy(out, "SNES-SPC700 Sound File Data v0.30")
	out[0x21], out[0x22] = 0x1A, 0x1A
	out[0x23] = 0x1B // no ID666 tag
	out[0x24] = 0x30
	var pc uint16
	fmt.Sscanf(regs[0], "%04X", &pc)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[0x25:], pc)
	for i, off := range []int{0x27, 0x28, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B} { // a ps x y sp
		var v int
		fmt.Sscanf(regs[i+1], "%02X", &v)
		out[off] = byte(v)
	}
	copy(out[0x100:0x10000], ram)
	copy(out[0x10100:0x10180], dsp)
	return out
}

func withoutDisplay(env []string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, e := range env {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(e, "DISPLAY=") {
			out = append(out, e)
		}
	}
	return out
}

`cmd/checktranslations/main.go`:

```go
// Command checktranslations validates translation tables against the
// current dialogue export: stale keys (original page no longer produced by
// the VM), line-count mismatches, overlong lines.
//
// Usage: checktranslations [events.json] [translations-dir]
//
// Both arguments are optional; the defaults are exports/data/events.json
// and exports/translations. Exits 0 when every table validates, 1 on a
// validation or runtime failure, 2 on a usage error.
//
// Stale keys and line-count mismatches fail the run. Overlong lines
// (>22 chars) are reported as informational only — they are tolerated
// (original text can force them) — and never count toward the failure.
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

const (
	defaultEvents   = "exports/data/events.json"
	defaultTransDir = "exports/translations"

	// sampleCap caps each problem class's sample lines; the tail says
	// how many lines were held back. A decode change can mark every key
	// stale, and printing 57k lines would bury the verdict.
	sampleCap = 20
)

type opJSON struct {
	T string `json:"t"`
	S string `json:"s,omitempty"`
}

type eventJSON struct {
	ID  string   `json:"id"`
	Ops []opJSON `json:"ops,omitempty"`
}

func main() {
	eventsPath, dir, ok := parseArgs(os.Args[1:])
	if !ok {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr,
			"usage: checktranslations [events.json] [translations-dir]\n"+
				"  events.json defaults to %s\n"+
				"  translations-dir defaults to %s\n",
			defaultEvents, defaultTransDir)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	evRaw, err := os.ReadFile(eventsPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	var events []eventJSON
	if err := json.Unmarshal(evRaw, &events); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	pagesByEvent := map[string][]string{}
	for _, ev := range events {
		pagesByEvent[ev.ID] = buildPages(ev.Ops)
	}

	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	bad := 0
	for _, e := range entries {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".json") {
			continue
		}
		path := filepath.Join(dir, e.Name())
		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		var table map[string]map[string]string
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &table); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("%s: INVALID JSON: %v\n", e.Name(), err)
			bad++
			continue
		}

		var res result
		ids := make([]string, 0, len(table))
		for id := range table {
			ids = append(ids, id)
		}
		sort.Strings(ids)
		for _, id := range ids {
			pages := map[string]bool{}
			for _, p := range pagesByEvent[id] {
				pages[p] = true
			}
			for orig, zh := range table[id] {
				if len(pages) > 0 && !pages[orig] {
					res.stale++
					res.staleLines = append(res.staleLines, fmt.Sprintf(
						"%s %s: STALE key %q: delete keys the VM no longer produces (or re-export events.json)",
						e.Name(), id, head(orig)))
					continue
				}
				on, zn := countLines(orig), countLines(zh)
				if on != zn {
					res.mismatch++
					res.mismatchLines = append(res.mismatchLines, fmt.Sprintf(
						"%s %s: LINE COUNT %d -> %d: %q: the page must be %d lines",
						e.Name(), id, on, zn, head(zh), on))
				}
				for line := range strings.SplitSeq(zh, "\n") {
					if runeLen(line) > 22 {
						res.long++
						break
					}
				}
			}
		}

		// Verdict first; the fix rides on each sample line.
		fmt.Printf("%s: %s, %s, %d keys with overlong lines (tolerated)\n",
			e.Name(),
			plural(res.stale, "stale key", "stale keys"),
			plural(res.mismatch, "line-count mismatch", "line-count mismatches"),
			res.long)
		printSample(res.staleLines)
		printSample(res.mismatchLines)
		if res.stale > 0 || res.mismatch > 0 {
			bad++
		}
	}
	if bad > 0 {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

// result accumulates one table's counts and sample lines.
type result struct {
	stale, mismatch, long int
	staleLines            []string
	mismatchLines         []string
}

// parseArgs maps the positional arity: 0 args -> both defaults, 1 arg ->
// explicit events.json + default dir, 2 args -> both explicit.
func parseArgs(args []string) (eventsPath, dir string, ok bool) {
	switch len(args) {
	case 0:
		return defaultEvents, defaultTransDir, true
	case 1:
		return args[0], defaultTransDir, true
	case 2:
		return args[0], args[1], true
	default:
		return "", "", false
	}
}

// printSample prints the first sampleCap lines, then one tail line with
// the count held back.
func printSample(lines []string) {
	n := min(sampleCap, len(lines))
	for _, l := range lines[:n] {
		fmt.Println(l)
	}
	if extra := len(lines) - n; extra > 0 {
		fmt.Printf("… and %d more\n", extra)
	}
}

func buildPages(ops []opJSON) []string {
	var pages []string
	page := ""
	for _, o := range ops {
		switch o.T {
		case "text":
			page += o.S
		case "nl":
			page += "\n"
		case "win", "endmes", "end":
			if page != "" {
				pages = append(pages, page)
				page = ""
			}
		}
	}
	if page != "" {
		pages = append(pages, page)
	}
	return pages
}

func countLines(s string) int { return strings.Count(s, "\n") + 1 }

func runeLen(s string) int { return len([]rune(s)) }

func plural(n int, one, many string) string {
	if n == 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", n, one)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", n, many)
}

func head(s string) string {
	r := []rune(s)
	if len(r) > 20 {
		return string(r[:20]) + "…"
	}
	return s
}

// fail reports a runtime error (unreadable file, bad JSON): the tool ran,
// so 1 — 2 is reserved for usage errors.
func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}

`cmd/codedump/main.go`:

```go
// Command codedump converts selected ROM banks from raw .byte data into
// labeled ca65 code (docs/decomp.md Phase 1). It is the bridge between the
// Phase-0 split (cmd/romsplit) and the fully annotated disassembly.
//
// Discovery: recursive descent from seed addresses, following
// JSR/JMP/JSL/JML/branches and carrying M/X flag state through SEP/REP so
// immediate operand sizes come out right. Unreached bytes stay .byte data.
// Targets get ca65 labels: S_ = subroutine (JSR/JSL), L_ = branch/jump
// target, E_ = config seed.
//
// The reassembly gate (decomp/Makefile `make gate`) is the correctness
// proof: any wrong operand size, mode qualifier or opcode-table entry
// changes assembled bytes and fails the sha256 match. A bank that arrives
// at an address with a different M/X state than the first path keeps the
// first decoding — wrong guesses surface as gate failures, and the fix is
// a corrected seed state in the config, not assembler guessing.
//
// Operand sizes are forced with ca65 address-space qualifiers
// (z: a: f:) everywhere, never left to assembler defaults: ca65 without
// smart mode assembles `lda $12` as absolute, which would not match.
//
// Bank model: "bank" is a FILE bank (ROM_XX segment). CPU banks C0-FF map
// to file banks C0-FF; CPU banks 00-3F map to file banks 40-7D
// (cpuToFile). All vectors live in the CPU $00:FFxx page, physically in
// file bank 40.
//
// Usage:
//
//	codedump <rom> <config> <outdir>
//	codedump <config> <outdir>      (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)
//
// Config (decomp/codesrc.txt), one bank per line, '#' comments:
//
//	BANK FF m8 x8 seeds AUTO,0E44
//	BANK C0 m16 x16 seeds 58CC
//
// m/x state at seeds: m8 = A is 8-bit (power-on), m16 = 16-bit. AUTO seeds
// every nonzero vector in the CPU $00:FFE8-FFFF vector area (file bank 40,
// offsets 0xFFE8-0xFFFF), which covers reset and all handlers.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

const bankSize = 0x10000

// cpuToFile maps CPU bank:offset to the 8MB file offset. ExHiROM maps
// CPU banks 00-3D and 80-BD alike onto file banks 40-7D.
func cpuToFile(bank, off int) int {
	switch {
	case bank >= 0xC0:
		return (bank-0xC0)*bankSize + off
	case bank >= 0x80:
		return (bank-0x40)*bankSize + off
	case bank >= 0x40:
		return bank*bankSize + off
	default:
		return (0x40+bank)*bankSize + off
	}
}

// cpuBank is the inverse: file bank -> the CPU banks that see it.
func cpuBankName(fileBank int) string {
	if fileBank < 0x40 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%02X", 0xC0+fileBank)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%02X/%02X", fileBank, fileBank-0x40)
}

// seedSpec is one recursive-descent start: an offset (or -1 for AUTO,
// the CPU $00:FFE8-FFFF vector area) and the M/X state assumed there.
// The same bank may appear on several config lines — seeds merge, and
// each line's m/x applies to that line's seeds only.
type seedSpec struct {
	off  int
	m, x bool
}

type bankCfg struct {
	bank  int
	seeds []seedSpec
}

type config struct {
	banks map[int]*bankCfg
	order []int
}

func parseConfig(path string) (*config, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	cfg := &config{banks: map[int]*bankCfg{}}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
			continue
		}
		f := strings.Fields(line)
		if len(f) < 5 || f[0] != "BANK" || f[4] != "seeds" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: want \"BANK <xx> m8|16 x8|16 seeds <list>\", got %q", path, line)
		}
		bank, err := strconv.ParseInt(f[1], 16, 32)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: bank %q: %v", path, f[1], err)
		}
		// f[2]/f[3] are the m/x tokens (m8|m16, x8|x16); they apply to
		// this line's seeds only. Read them here — reading them from
		// f[5:] instead silently ignored every token (observed: all
		// seeds ran m8 x8 regardless of what the config said).
		m, x := false, false
		for _, fld := range f[2:4] {
			switch fld {
			case "m8":
				m = false
			case "m16":
				m = true
			case "x8":
				x = false
			case "x16":
				x = true
			default:
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: bad flag token %q", path, fld)
			}
		}
		var offs []int
		for _, fld := range f[5:] {
			switch {
			case fld == "m16":
				m = true
			case fld == "x16":
				x = true
			case strings.Contains(fld, ","):
				for _, part := range strings.Split(fld, ",") {
					if part == "" {
						continue
					}
					v, err := strconv.ParseInt(part, 16, 32)
					if err != nil || v < 0 || v >= bankSize {
						return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: bad seed %q", path, part)
					}
					offs = append(offs, int(v))
				}
			case fld == "AUTO":
				offs = append(offs, -1)
			default:
				s, err := strconv.ParseInt(fld, 16, 32)
				if err != nil || s < 0 || s >= bankSize {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: bad seed %q", path, fld)
				}
				offs = append(offs, int(s))
			}
		}
		if len(offs) == 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: bank %02X has no seeds", path, f[1])
		}
		bc, ok := cfg.banks[int(bank)]
		if !ok {
			bc = &bankCfg{bank: int(bank)}
			cfg.banks[bc.bank] = bc
			cfg.order = append(cfg.order, bc.bank)
		}
		for _, o := range offs {
			bc.seeds = append(bc.seeds, seedSpec{off: o, m: m, x: x})
		}
	}
	return cfg, nil
}

// addressing modes (operand length in bytes where fixed)
const (
	amIMP = iota // 0 operand bytes
	amIMM        // 1 or 2 per flag state / fixed class
	amDP         // 2 total
	amDPX
	amDPY
	amDPI  // (dp)
	amDPIX // (dp,X)
	amDPIY // (dp),Y
	amDPS  // sr,S
	amDPSY // (sr,S),Y
	amDPIL // [dp]
	amDPILY
	amABS // 3 total
	amABSX
	amABSY
	amABSL // 4 total
	amABSLX
	amREL   // 2 total
	amBLOCK // MVP/MVN, 3 total
	amRELL  // BRL/PER, 3 total
	amIND   // JMP (abs), 3 total
	amINDX  // JMP (abs,X), 3 total
	amINDL  // JML [dp], 2 total
	amJMPIX // JSR (abs,X), 2 total
)

const (
	immM   = iota // immediate size follows M (A ops)
	immX          // follows X (index ops)
	immFix        // fixed 2-byte total (REP/SEP/PEA/COP/BRK)
)

func opInfo(op byte) (mn string, am int, imm int) {
	type e struct {
		mn  string
		am  int
		imm int
	}
	t := [256]e{
		0x00: {"BRK", amIMM, immFix}, 0x01: {"ORA", amDPIX, immM}, 0x02: {"COP", amIMM, immFix}, 0x03: {"ORA", amDPS, immM},
		0x04: {"TSB", amDP, immM}, 0x05: {"ORA", amDP, immM}, 0x06: {"ASL", amDP, immM}, 0x07: {"ORA", amDPIL, immM},
		0x08: {"PHP", amIMP, immM}, 0x09: {"ORA", amIMM, immM}, 0x0A: {"ASL", amIMP, immM}, 0x0B: {"PHD", amIMP, immM},
		0x0C: {"TSB", amABS, immM}, 0x0D: {"ORA", amABS, immM}, 0x0E: {"ASL", amABS, immM}, 0x0F: {"ORA", amABSL, immM},
		0x10: {"BPL", amREL, immM}, 0x11: {"ORA", amDPIY, immM}, 0x12: {"ORA", amDPI, immM}, 0x13: {"ORA", amDPSY, immM},
		0x14: {"TRB", amDP, immM}, 0x15: {"ORA", amDPX, immM}, 0x16: {"ASL", amDPX, immM}, 0x17: {"ORA", amDPILY, immM},
		0x18: {"CLC", amIMP, immM}, 0x19: {"ORA", amABSY, immM}, 0x1A: {"INC", amIMP, immM}, 0x1B: {"TCS", amIMP, immM},
		0x1C: {"TRB", amABS, immM}, 0x1D: {"ORA", amABSX, immM}, 0x1E: {"ASL", amABSX, immM}, 0x1F: {"ORA", amABSLX, immM},
		0x20: {"JSR", amABS, immM}, 0x21: {"AND", amDPIX, immM}, 0x22: {"JSL", amABSL, immM}, 0x23: {"AND", amDPS, immM},
		0x24: {"BIT", amDP, immM}, 0x25: {"AND", amDP, immM}, 0x26: {"ROL", amDP, immM}, 0x27: {"AND", amDPIL, immM},
		0x28: {"PLP", amIMP, immM}, 0x29: {"AND", amIMM, immM}, 0x2A: {"ROL", amIMP, immM}, 0x2B: {"PLD", amIMP, immM},
		0x2C: {"BIT", amABS, immM}, 0x2D: {"AND", amABS, immM}, 0x2E: {"ROL", amABS, immM}, 0x2F: {"AND", amABSL, immM},
		0x30: {"BMI", amREL, immM}, 0x31: {"AND", amDPIY, immM}, 0x32: {"AND", amDPI, immM}, 0x33: {"AND", amDPSY, immM},
		0x34: {"BIT", amDPX, immM}, 0x35: {"AND", amDPX, immM}, 0x36: {"ROL", amDPX, immM}, 0x37: {"AND", amDPILY, immM},
		0x38: {"SEC", amIMP, immM}, 0x39: {"AND", amABSY, immM}, 0x3A: {"DEC", amIMP, immM}, 0x3B: {"TSC", amIMP, immM},
		0x3C: {"BIT", amABSX, immM}, 0x3D: {"AND", amABSX, immM}, 0x3E: {"ROL", amABSX, immM}, 0x3F: {"AND", amABSLX, immM},
		0x40: {"RTI", amIMP, immM}, 0x41: {"EOR", amDPIX, immM}, 0x42: {"WDM", amIMP, immM}, 0x43: {"EOR", amDPS, immM},
		0x44: {"MVP", amBLOCK, immM}, 0x45: {"EOR", amDP, immM}, 0x46: {"LSR", amDP, immM}, 0x47: {"EOR", amDPIL, immM},
		0x48: {"PHA", amIMP, immM}, 0x49: {"EOR", amIMM, immM}, 0x4A: {"LSR", amIMP, immM}, 0x4B: {"PHK", amIMP, immM},
		0x4C: {"JMP", amABS, immM}, 0x4D: {"EOR", amABS, immM}, 0x4E: {"LSR", amABS, immM}, 0x4F: {"EOR", amABSL, immM},
		0x50: {"BVC", amREL, immM}, 0x51: {"EOR", amDPIY, immM}, 0x52: {"EOR", amDPI, immM}, 0x53: {"EOR", amDPSY, immM},
		0x54: {"MVN", amBLOCK, immM}, 0x55: {"EOR", amDPX, immM}, 0x56: {"LSR", amDPX, immM}, 0x57: {"EOR", amDPILY, immM},
		0x58: {"CLI", amIMP, immM}, 0x59: {"EOR", amABSY, immM}, 0x5A: {"PHY", amIMP, immM}, 0x5B: {"TCD", amIMP, immM},
		0x5C: {"JML", amABSL, immM}, 0x5D: {"EOR", amABSX, immM}, 0x5E: {"LSR", amABSX, immM}, 0x5F: {"EOR", amABSLX, immM},
		0x60: {"RTS", amIMP, immM}, 0x61: {"ADC", amDPIX, immM}, 0x62: {"PER", amRELL, immM}, 0x63: {"ADC", amDPS, immM},
		0x64: {"STZ", amDP, immM}, 0x65: {"ADC", amDP, immM}, 0x66: {"ROR", amDP, immM}, 0x67: {"ADC", amDPIL, immM},
		0x68: {"PLA", amIMP, immM}, 0x69: {"ADC", amIMM, immM}, 0x6A: {"ROR", amIMP, immM}, 0x6B: {"RTL", amIMP, immM},
		0x6C: {"JMP", amIND, immM}, 0x6D: {"ADC", amABS, immM}, 0x6E: {"ROR", amABS, immM}, 0x6F: {"ADC", amABSL, immM},
		0x70: {"BVS", amREL, immM}, 0x71: {"ADC", amDPIY, immM}, 0x72: {"ADC", amDPI, immM}, 0x73: {"ADC", amDPSY, immM},
		0x74: {"STZ", amDPX, immM}, 0x75: {"ADC", amDPX, immM}, 0x76: {"ROR", amDPX, immM}, 0x77: {"ADC", amDPILY, immM},
		0x78: {"SEI", amIMP, immM}, 0x79: {"ADC", amABSY, immM}, 0x7A: {"PLY", amIMP, immM}, 0x7B: {"TDC", amIMP, immM},
		0x7C: {"JMP", amINDX, immM}, 0x7D: {"ADC", amABSX, immM}, 0x7E: {"ROR", amABSX, immM}, 0x7F: {"ADC", amABSLX, immM},
		0x80: {"BRA", amREL, immM}, 0x81: {"STA", amDPIX, immM}, 0x82: {"BRL", amRELL, immM}, 0x83: {"STA", amDPS, immM},
		0x84: {"STY", amDP, immM}, 0x85: {"STA", amDP, immM}, 0x86: {"STX", amDP, immM}, 0x87: {"STA", amDPIL, immM},
		0x88: {"DEY", amIMP, immM}, 0x89: {"BIT", amIMM, immM}, 0x8A: {"TXA", amIMP, immM}, 0x8B: {"PHB", amIMP, immM},
		0x8C: {"STY", amABS, immM}, 0x8D: {"STA", amABS, immM}, 0x8E: {"STX", amABS, immM}, 0x8F: {"STA", amABSL, immM},
		0x90: {"BCC", amREL, immM}, 0x91: {"STA", amDPIY, immM}, 0x92: {"STA", amDPI, immM}, 0x93: {"STA", amDPSY, immM},
		0x94: {"STY", amDPX, immM}, 0x95: {"STA", amDPX, immM}, 0x96: {"STX", amDPY, immM}, 0x97: {"STA", amDPILY, immM},
		0x98: {"TYA", amIMP, immM}, 0x99: {"STA", amABSY, immM}, 0x9A: {"TXS", amIMP, immM}, 0x9B: {"TXY", amIMP, immM},
		0x9C: {"STZ", amABS, immM}, 0x9D: {"STA", amABSX, immM}, 0x9E: {"STZ", amABSX, immM}, 0x9F: {"STA", amABSLX, immM},
		0xA0: {"LDY", amIMM, immX}, 0xA1: {"LDA", amDPIX, immM}, 0xA2: {"LDX", amIMM, immX}, 0xA3: {"LDA", amDPS, immM},
		0xA4: {"LDY", amDP, immM}, 0xA5: {"LDA", amDP, immM}, 0xA6: {"LDX", amDP, immM}, 0xA7: {"LDA", amDPIL, immM},
		0xA8: {"TAY", amIMP, immM}, 0xA9: {"LDA", amIMM, immM}, 0xAA: {"TAX", amIMP, immM}, 0xAB: {"PLB", amIMP, immM},
		0xAC: {"LDY", amABS, immM}, 0xAD: {"LDA", amABS, immM}, 0xAE: {"LDX", amABS, immM}, 0xAF: {"LDA", amABSL, immM},
		0xB0: {"BCS", amREL, immM}, 0xB1: {"LDA", amDPIY, immM}, 0xB2: {"LDA", amDPI, immM}, 0xB3: {"LDA", amDPSY, immM},
		0xB4: {"LDY", amDPX, immM}, 0xB5: {"LDA", amDPX, immM}, 0xB6: {"LDX", amDPY, immM}, 0xB7: {"LDA", amDPILY, immM},
		0xB8: {"CLV", amIMP, immM}, 0xB9: {"LDA", amABSY, immM}, 0xBA: {"TSX", amIMP, immM}, 0xBB: {"TYX", amIMP, immM},
		0xBC: {"LDY", amABSX, immM}, 0xBD: {"LDA", amABSX, immM}, 0xBE: {"LDX", amABSY, immM}, 0xBF: {"LDA", amABSLX, immM},
		0xC0: {"CPY", amIMM, immX}, 0xC1: {"CMP", amDPIX, immM}, 0xC2: {"REP", amIMM, immFix}, 0xC3: {"CMP", amDPS, immM},
		0xC4: {"CPY", amDP, immM}, 0xC5: {"CMP", amDP, immM}, 0xC6: {"DEC", amDP, immM}, 0xC7: {"CMP", amDPIL, immM},
		0xC8: {"INY", amIMP, immM}, 0xC9: {"CMP", amIMM, immM}, 0xCA: {"DEX", amIMP, immM}, 0xCB: {"WAI", amIMP, immM},
		0xCC: {"CPY", amABS, immM}, 0xCD: {"CMP", amABS, immM}, 0xCE: {"DEC", amABS, immM}, 0xCF: {"CMP", amABSL, immM},
		0xD0: {"BNE", amREL, immM}, 0xD1: {"CMP", amDPIY, immM}, 0xD2: {"CMP", amDPI, immM}, 0xD3: {"CMP", amDPSY, immM},
		0xD4: {"PEI", amDP, immM}, 0xD5: {"CMP", amDPX, immM}, 0xD6: {"DEC", amDPX, immM}, 0xD7: {"CMP", amDPILY, immM},
		0xD8: {"CLD", amIMP, immM}, 0xD9: {"CMP", amABSY, immM}, 0xDA: {"PHX", amIMP, immM}, 0xDB: {"STP", amIMP, immM},
		// 0xDC is JML (abs) — 16-bit pointer, 3 bytes (the ROM's BRK
		// handler at 00/FF07 is DC 00 13 and the NMI handler follows at
		// FF0A, proving the 3-byte form); ca65 has no 2-byte bracket JML.
		0xDC: {"JML", amIND, immM}, 0xDD: {"CMP", amABSX, immM}, 0xDE: {"DEC", amABSX, immM}, 0xDF: {"CMP", amABSLX, immM},
		0xE0: {"CPX", amIMM, immX}, 0xE1: {"SBC", amDPIX, immM}, 0xE2: {"SEP", amIMM, immFix}, 0xE3: {"SBC", amDPS, immM},
		0xE4: {"CPX", amDP, immM}, 0xE5: {"SBC", amDP, immM}, 0xE6: {"INC", amDP, immM}, 0xE7: {"SBC", amDPIL, immM},
		0xE8: {"INX", amIMP, immM}, 0xE9: {"SBC", amIMM, immM}, 0xEA: {"NOP", amIMP, immM}, 0xEB: {"XBA", amIMP, immM},
		0xEC: {"CPX", amABS, immM}, 0xED: {"SBC", amABS, immM}, 0xEE: {"INC", amABS, immM}, 0xEF: {"SBC", amABSL, immM},
		0xF0: {"BEQ", amREL, immM}, 0xF1: {"SBC", amDPIY, immM}, 0xF2: {"SBC", amDPI, immM}, 0xF3: {"SBC", amDPSY, immM},
		0xF4: {"PEA", amIMM, immFix}, 0xF5: {"SBC", amDPX, immM}, 0xF6: {"INC", amDPX, immM}, 0xF7: {"SBC", amDPILY, immM},
		0xF8: {"SED", amIMP, immM}, 0xF9: {"SBC", amABSY, immM}, 0xFA: {"PLX", amIMP, immM}, 0xFB: {"XCE", amIMP, immM},
		0xFC: {"JSR", amJMPIX, immM}, 0xFD: {"SBC", amABSX, immM}, 0xFE: {"INC", amABSX, immM}, 0xFF: {"SBC", amABSLX, immM},
	}
	// corrected entries vs a plain sweep table: WDM is 1 byte, 0xDB is
	// STP, 0xFB is XCE, 0xBB is TYX — all byte-matching critical.
	return t[op].mn, t[op].am, t[op].imm
}

func opLen(am, imm int, m, x bool) int {
	switch am {
	case amIMP:
		return 1
	case amIMM:
		switch imm {
		case immFix:
			return 2
		case immM:
			if m {
				return 3
			}
			return 2
		default: // immX
			if x {
				return 3
			}
			return 2
		}
	case amABS, amABSX, amABSY, amIND, amINDX, amJMPIX:
		return 3
	case amABSL, amABSLX:
		return 4
	case amREL:
		return 2
	case amBLOCK, amRELL:
		return 3
	default: // all dp-shaped modes: 2 total
		return 2
	}
}

// labelRef records one label reference baked into instr.ops.
type labelRef struct {
	off  int
	name string
}

type instr struct {
	off  int
	len  int
	mn   string
	ops  string     // operand text, ca65 syntax with qualifiers; "" = none
	refs []labelRef // in-bank label offsets referenced by ops, with the
	// name baked into ops; the name can be stale (a later JSL upgrades
	// the same offset L_ -> S_), so emission re-reads the label kind.
	m, x bool
}

type item struct {
	bank, off int
	m, x      bool
}

type disasm struct {
	rom    []byte
	cfg    *config
	state  map[int][2]bool // file byte offset -> first-arrival M/X state
	code   map[int]map[int]*instr
	cover  map[int]int // file byte offset -> owning instruction offset
	labels map[int]map[int]byte
	custom map[int]string // file byte offset -> caller-provided label name
	logs   []string
	conf   int
}

func (d *disasm) warn(format string, args ...any) {
	d.logs = append(d.logs, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
}

// mBit renders a flag as the config token digit (m8/m16, x8/x16).
func mBit(b bool) int {
	if b {
		return 16
	}
	return 8
}

func (d *disasm) addLabel(bank, off int, kind byte) {
	m := d.labels[bank]
	if m == nil {
		m = map[int]byte{}
		d.labels[bank] = m
	}
	if cur, ok := m[off]; ok && cur != kind {
		// a JSR target that is also a branch target: subroutine wins
		if cur != 'S' && kind == 'S' {
			m[off] = 'S'
		}
		return
	}
	m[off] = kind
}

func labelName(kind byte, bank, off int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%c_%02X_%04X", kind, bank, off)
}

// parseLabels reads a labels file: lines "BANK <xx> <off> <name>" with
// '#' comments. Named offsets become emission labels verbatim (they must
// be valid ca65 identifiers) and win over generated S_/L_/E_ names —
// this is where the hand-disassembled routine inventory (docs/*) enters
// the source.
func parseLabels(path string, d *disasm) error {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
			continue
		}
		f := strings.Fields(line)
		if len(f) != 4 || f[0] != "BANK" {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: want \"BANK <xx> <off> <name>\", got %q", path, line)
		}
		bank, err := strconv.ParseInt(f[1], 16, 32)
		if err != nil || bank < 0 || bank >= 0x100 {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: bad bank %q", path, f[1])
		}
		off, err := strconv.ParseInt(f[2], 16, 32)
		if err != nil || off < 0 || off >= bankSize {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: bad offset %q", path, f[2])
		}
		d.custom[int(bank)*bankSize+int(off)] = f[3]
	}
	return nil
}

// labelFor returns the emitted name for a label offset: the custom name
// if one is defined, else the generated kind name.
func (d *disasm) labelFor(bank, off int, kind byte) string {
	if name, ok := d.custom[bank*bankSize+off]; ok {
		return name
	}
	return labelName(kind, bank, off)
}

func (d *disasm) run() error {
	var queue []item
	queued := map[string]bool{}
	push := func(it item) {
		key := fmt.Sprintf("%02X.%04X.%v.%v", it.bank, it.off, it.m, it.x)
		if queued[key] {
			return
		}
		queued[key] = true
		queue = append(queue, it)
	}
	type seed struct {
		bank, off int
		m, x      bool
	}
	var seeds []seed
	for _, bank := range d.cfg.order {
		bc := d.cfg.banks[bank]
		for _, s := range bc.seeds {
			if s.off == -1 {
				// AUTO: every real vector in the CPU $00:FFE8-FFFF area
				// (file bank 40) seeds file bank 40 — CPU bank 00 is that
				// bank's mirror, whatever config line asked for AUTO.
				for v := 0xFFE8; v <= 0xFFFE; v += 2 {
					f := cpuToFile(0x40, v)
					off := int(d.rom[f]) | int(d.rom[f+1])<<8
					if off == 0 || off == 0xFFFF {
						continue // empty slot
					}
					d.addLabel(0x40, off, 'E')
					seeds = append(seeds, seed{0x40, off, s.m, s.x})
					d.warn("AUTO: vector %04X -> 00/%04X", v, off)
				}
				continue
			}
			d.addLabel(bank, s.off, 'E')
			seeds = append(seeds, seed{bank, s.off, s.m, s.x})
		}
	}
	for _, s := range seeds {
		push(item(s))
	}
	for len(queue) > 0 {
		it := queue[0]
		queue = queue[1:]
		d.discover(it, push)
	}
	// custom labels must exist in the labels map to enter the emission
	// walk, even at data offsets no code path references
	for key := range d.custom {
		d.addLabel(key/bankSize, key%bankSize, 'N')
	}
	sort.Strings(d.logs)
	for _, w := range d.logs {
		fmt.Println(w)
	}
	fmt.Printf("M/X conflicts: %d\n", d.conf)
	return nil
}

func (d *disasm) discover(it item, push func(item)) {
	if _, listed := d.cfg.banks[it.bank]; !listed {
		d.warn("flow into unlisted bank %02X/%04X m%v x%v (stays data)",
			it.bank, it.off, mBit(it.m), mBit(it.x))
		return
	}
	key := it.bank*bankSize + it.off
	if st, seen := d.state[key]; seen {
		if st != [2]bool{it.m, it.x} {
			d.conf++
			d.warn("M/X conflict at %02X/%04X: first %v wins over %v",
				it.bank, it.off, st, [2]bool{it.m, it.x})
		}
		return
	}
	d.state[key] = [2]bool{it.m, it.x}

	ins, follows, err := d.decode1(it)
	if err != nil {
		d.warn("decode fail %02X/%04X: %v", it.bank, it.off, err)
		return
	}
	k0 := it.bank*bankSize + ins.off
	for i := range ins.len {
		if owner, ok := d.cover[k0+i]; ok && owner != ins.off {
			d.warn("overlap at %02X/%04X: byte %04X owned by %04X",
				it.bank, it.off, ins.off+i, owner)
			return
		}
	}
	for i := range ins.len {
		d.cover[k0+i] = ins.off
	}
	m := d.code[it.bank]
	if m == nil {
		m = map[int]*instr{}
		d.code[it.bank] = m
	}
	m[ins.off] = ins
	for _, f := range follows {
		push(f)
	}
}

func (d *disasm) decode1(it item) (*instr, []item, error) {
	foff := cpuToFile(it.bank, it.off)
	data := d.rom[foff:]
	op := data[0]
	mn, am, immClass := opInfo(op)
	n := opLen(am, immClass, it.m, it.x)
	// PEA is 3 bytes, not the immFix 2 (see the emit note below); correct
	// before the bank-end guard so the length check sees the real size.
	if op == 0xF4 {
		n = 3
	}
	if it.off+n > bankSize {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("runs past bank end")
	}
	ins := &instr{off: it.off, len: n, mn: mn, m: it.m, x: it.x}
	var follows []item
	var flow item

	w8 := func(i int) byte { return data[i] }
	w16 := func(i int) int { return int(data[i]) | int(data[i+1])<<8 }
	label := func(bank, off int, kind byte) string {
		d.addLabel(bank, off, kind)
		name := labelName(kind, bank, off)
		ins.refs = append(ins.refs, labelRef{off, name})
		return labelName(kind, bank, off)
	}

	switch am {
	case amIMP:
		ins.ops = ""
	case amIMM:
		switch immClass {
		case immFix:
			ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("#$%02x", w8(1))
		case immM:
			if it.m {
				ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("#$%04x", w16(1))
			} else {
				ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("#$%02x", w8(1))
			}
		default:
			if it.x {
				ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("#$%04x", w16(1))
			} else {
				ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("#$%02x", w8(1))
			}
		}
	case amDP:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("z:$%02x", w8(1))
	case amDPX:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("z:$%02x,x", w8(1))
	case amDPY:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("z:$%02x,y", w8(1))
	case amDPI:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%02x)", w8(1))
	case amDPIX:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%02x,x)", w8(1))
	case amDPIY:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%02x),y", w8(1))
	case amDPS:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x,s", w8(1))
	case amDPSY:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%02x,s),y", w8(1))
	case amDPIL:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("[$%02x]", w8(1))
	case amDPILY:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("[$%02x],y", w8(1))
	case amABS:
		t := w16(1)
		switch mn {
		case "JSR":
			ins.ops = label(it.bank, t, 'S')
			flow = item{it.bank, t, it.m, it.x}
		case "JMP":
			ins.ops = label(it.bank, t, 'L')
			flow = item{it.bank, t, it.m, it.x}
		default:
			ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("a:$%04x", t)
		}
	case amABSX:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("a:$%04x,x", w16(1))
	case amABSY:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("a:$%04x,y", w16(1))
	case amABSL:
		tBank, tOff := int(data[3]), w16(1)
		// normalized file bank for flow + labels (see cpuToFile)
		fbank := tBank
		switch {
		case fbank < 0x40:
			fbank += 0x40
		case fbank >= 0x80 && fbank < 0xC0:
			fbank -= 0x40
		}
		switch mn {
		case "JSL":
			// The operand must be a raw 24-bit address: ca65 labels are
			// 16-bit (segment-relative), so `jsl S_xx` would encode bank
			// byte 00. The target still gets an S_ label where it lands.
			ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("f:$%02x%04x", tBank, tOff)
			if _, ok := d.cfg.banks[fbank]; !ok {
				d.warn("JSL to unlisted bank %02X%04X (stays data)", tBank, tOff)
			}
			label(fbank, tOff, 'S')
			flow = item{fbank, tOff, it.m, it.x}
		case "JML":
			ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("f:$%02x%04x", tBank, tOff)
			// Follow the jump like a JSL: the operand is absolute, flags
			// carry over. (Observed cost of not following: a manual census
			// of emitted `jml` operands kept surfacing dozens of undecoded
			// targets round after round.)
			flow = item{fbank, tOff, it.m, it.x}
		default:
			ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("f:$%02x%04x", tBank, tOff)
		}
	case amABSLX:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("f:$%02x%04x,x", int(data[3]), w16(1))
	case amREL:
		t := it.off + 2 + int(int8(data[1]))
		if t < 0 || t >= bankSize {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("branch target out of bank: %04X", t)
		}
		ins.ops = label(it.bank, t, 'L')
		flow = item{it.bank, t, it.m, it.x}
	case amRELL:
		t := it.off + 3 + int(int16(w16(1)))
		if t < 0 || t >= bankSize {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("long branch target out of bank: %04X", t)
		}
		switch mn {
		case "BRL":
			ins.ops = label(it.bank, t, 'L')
			flow = item{it.bank, t, it.m, it.x}
		default: // PER pushes a value; label the target but do not run it
			ins.ops = label(it.bank, t, 'L')
		}
	case amBLOCK:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x,$%02x", w8(1), w8(2))
	case amIND:
		t := w16(1)
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%04x)", t)
	case amINDX:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%04x,x)", w16(1))
	case amINDL:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("[$%02x]", w8(1))
	case amJMPIX:
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("($%04x,x)", w16(1))
	}

	// PEA always carries a 16-bit immediate, 3 bytes total regardless of
	// flags; the immFix class (REP/SEP/BRK/COP) is otherwise 2 bytes.
	// ca65 wants `pea $xxxx` with no hash (same trap family as PEI).
	if op == 0xF4 {
		n = 3
		ins.len = 3
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("$%04x", int(data[1])|int(data[2])<<8)
	}

	// BRK/COP carry a signature byte; MVP/MVN's bank operands are
	// mis-encoded by ca65 (observed: `mvn $7e,$7e` -> 54 00 00); PEI is
	// rejected outright by ca65 (illegal addressing mode in every
	// spelling, cc65 2.19). All four emit raw so the encoding is exact.
	if op == 0xD4 {
		ins.mn = ".byte"
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x,$%02x", op, w8(1))
	}
	if op == 0x00 || op == 0x02 {
		ins.mn = ".byte"
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x,$%02x", op, w8(1))
	}
	if op == 0x44 || op == 0x54 {
		ins.mn = ".byte"
		ins.ops = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x,$%02x,$%02x", op, w8(1), w8(2))
	}

	// flag state after this instruction (REP/SEP) and control flow
	nextM, nextX := it.m, it.x
	if op == 0xC2 || op == 0xE2 {
		f := int(data[1])
		if op == 0xC2 { // REP: set bits -> 16-bit
			nextM = nextM || f&0x20 != 0
			nextX = nextX || f&0x10 != 0
		} else { // SEP: clear bits -> 8-bit
			if f&0x20 != 0 {
				nextM = false
			}
			if f&0x10 != 0 {
				nextX = false
			}
		}
	}
	switch mn {
	case "JMP", "JML", "BRL", "RTS", "RTL", "RTI", "STP", "BRA", "BRK", "COP":
		// control leaves this point; no fallthrough
	default:
		follows = append(follows, item{it.bank, it.off + n, nextM, nextX})
	}
	if flow.bank != 0 || flow.off != 0 {
		// file banks are >= 0x40, so a zero item means "no flow target"
		follows = append(follows, item{flow.bank, flow.off, nextM, nextX})
	}
	return ins, follows, nil
}

func (d *disasm) emitBank(bank int, path string) error {
	f := cpuToFile(bank, 0)
	data := d.rom[f : f+bankSize]
	code := d.code[bank]
	labels := d.labels[bank]

	// merge code offsets and label offsets into one walk order
	offs := map[int]bool{}
	for o := range code {
		offs[o] = true
	}
	for o := range labels {
		offs[o] = true
	}
	var keys []int
	for o := range offs {
		keys = append(keys, o)
	}
	sort.Ints(keys)

	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; bank %s (file bank %02X) — generated by cmd/codedump\n",
		cpuBankName(bank), bank)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; from decomp/codesrc.txt seeds. Gate: decomp/Makefile.\n")
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, ".segment \"ROM_%02X\"\n", bank)
	// ca65 defaults to 6502; without .p816 the 65816 opcodes parse as labels
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, ".p816\n")

	next := 0 // next file byte not yet emitted
	emitData := func(end int) {
		for next < end {
			n := min(32, end-next)
			parts := make([]string, n)
			for i := range n {
				parts[i] = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x", data[next+i])
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, ".byte %s\n", strings.Join(parts, ","))
			next += n
		}
	}
	// ca65 sizes immediates from the .a/.i directives, not from the
	// operand: emit the flag state before every instruction so the
	// assembled size is explicit. A path arriving with a different M/X
	// state than the first decode therefore shows up as a gate failure,
	// which is the point.
	emitFlags := func(m, x bool) {
		if m {
			b.WriteString("        .a16\n")
		} else {
			b.WriteString("        .a8\n")
		}
		if x {
			b.WriteString("        .i16\n")
		} else {
			b.WriteString("        .i8\n")
		}
	}
	// Labels inside a claimed instruction span are never emitted (the
	// walk skips them); any instruction referencing such a label falls
	// back to raw bytes so the reference cannot dangle.
	emitted := map[int]bool{}
	next = 0
	for _, k := range keys {
		if k < next {
			continue
		}
		if _, ok := labels[k]; ok {
			emitted[k] = true
		}
		if ins, ok := code[k]; ok {
			next = k + ins.len
		}
	}
	next = 0
	for _, k := range keys {
		if k < next {
			continue
		}
		if kind, ok := labels[k]; ok {
			emitData(k)
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s:\n", d.labelFor(bank, k, kind))
		}
		if ins, ok := code[k]; ok {
			emitData(k)
			ops := ins.ops
			resolved := true
			for _, r := range ins.refs {
				if !emitted[r.off] {
					resolved = false
					break
				}
				if cur := labels[r.off]; cur != 0 {
					// the label kind may have been upgraded (L_ -> S_);
					// the operand must name the label as emitted
					ops = strings.Replace(ops, r.name,
						d.labelFor(bank, r.off, cur), 1)
				}
			}
			if !resolved {
				// overlap artifact: emit the raw instruction bytes
				emitData(k + ins.len)
				next = k + ins.len
				continue
			}
			emitFlags(ins.m, ins.x)
			if ops == "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "        %s\n", strings.ToLower(ins.mn))
			} else {
				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "        %s %s\n", strings.ToLower(ins.mn), ops)
			}
			next = k + ins.len
		}
	}
	emitData(bankSize)
	return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 3, 4, "usage: codedump <rom> <config> <outdir> [labels]\n"+
		"   or: codedump <config> <outdir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	romPath, outDir := args[0], args[2]
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "read ROM: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	cfg, err := parseConfig(args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "config: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	d := &disasm{
		rom: rom, cfg: cfg,
		state:  map[int][2]bool{},
		code:   map[int]map[int]*instr{},
		cover:  map[int]int{},
		labels: map[int]map[int]byte{},
		custom: map[int]string{},
	}
	if len(args) == 4 {
		if err := parseLabels(args[3], d); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "labels: %v\n", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
	}
	if err := d.run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	// codedump owns ALL of decomp/src: listed banks get labeled code,
	// every other bank (plus the tail pad) is emitted as plain .byte —
	// identical to the romsplit bootstrap output. A stale file from an
	// older config can then never linger and corrupt the link.
	const bankSizeF = 0x10000
	emitted := map[int]bool{}
	for _, bank := range cfg.order {
		emitted[bank] = true
	}
	for b := 0xC0; b <= 0xFF; b++ {
		if emitted[b] {
			continue
		}
		path := fmt.Sprintf("%s/rom_%02x.asm", outDir, b)
		if err := emitDataOnly(path, b, rom[(b-0xC0)*bankSizeF:(b-0xC0+1)*bankSizeF]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "emit %s: %v\n", path, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
	}
	for b := 0x40; b <= 0x7D; b++ {
		if emitted[b] {
			continue
		}
		path := fmt.Sprintf("%s/rom_%02x.asm", outDir, b)
		if err := emitDataOnly(path, b, rom[b*bankSizeF:(b+1)*bankSizeF]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "emit %s: %v\n", path, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
	}
	for _, bank := range cfg.order {
		path := fmt.Sprintf("%s/rom_%02x.asm", outDir, bank)
		if err := d.emitBank(bank, path); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "emit %s: %v\n", path, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
	}
	// tail pad beyond any mapped bank (0x7E0000 to EOF)
	if err := emitPad(outDir+"/rom_pad.asm", rom[0x7E0000:]); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "emit pad: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func emitDataOnly(path string, bank int, data []byte) error {
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; bank %s (file bank %02X) — raw data (cmd/codedump)\n",
		cpuBankName(bank), bank)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, ".segment \"ROM_%02X\"\n", bank)
	writeBytes(&b, data)
	return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
}

func emitPad(path string, data []byte) error {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("; tail padding beyond any mapped bank (cmd/codedump)\n")
	b.WriteString(".segment \"ROM_PAD\"\n")
	writeBytes(&b, data)
	return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
}

func writeBytes(b *strings.Builder, data []byte) {
	for i := 0; i < len(data); i += 32 {
		n := min(32, len(data)-i)
		parts := make([]string, n)
		for j := range n {
			parts[j] = fmt.Sprintf("$%02x", data[i+j])
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(b, ".byte %s\n", strings.Join(parts, ","))
	}
}

```

`cmd/disasm65816/main.go`:

```go
// Command disasm65816 is a linear-sweep 65816 disassembler for ROM probes.
//
// It decodes a byte range of a HiROM/ExHiROM SNES ROM into CPU addresses,
// mnemonic and operands, tracking M/X flag changes linearly (SEP/REP) so
// immediate-operand sizes stay right; branch targets resolve to absolute
// CPU addresses.
//
// Address mapping (repo docs): CPU bank C0-FF -> file offset
// (bank-0xC0)*0x10000 + addr; banks 40-7D -> bank*0x10000 + addr.
//
// Usage:
//
//	disasm65816 <rom> <Bank:Offset|0xfileoff> <count> [m=8|16] [x=8|16]
//	disasm65816 <Bank:Offset|0xfileoff> <count>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc; the m=/x=
// flags need the full form.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

const (
	amIMP = iota
	amIMM
	amDP
	amDPX
	amDPY
	amDPI
	amDPIX
	amDPIY
	amDPS
	amDPSY
	amDPIL
	amDPILY
	amABS
	amABSX
	amABSY
	amABSL
	amABSLX
	amREL
	amRELL
	amBLOCK
	amABSI  // JMP (abs)
	amABSIX // JMP/JSR (abs,X)
	amABSIL // JML [abs]
)

// opcode returns mnemonic and addressing mode for a 65816 opcode byte.
func opcode(op byte) (string, int) {
	type e struct {
		mn string
		m  int
	}
	t := [256]e{
		0x00: {"BRK", amIMM}, 0x01: {"ORA", amDPIX}, 0x02: {"COP", amIMM}, 0x03: {"ORA", amDPS},
		0x04: {"TSB", amDP}, 0x05: {"ORA", amDP}, 0x06: {"ASL", amDP}, 0x07: {"ORA", amDPIL},
		0x08: {"PHP", amIMP}, 0x09: {"ORA", amIMM}, 0x0A: {"ASL", amIMP}, 0x0B: {"PHD", amIMP},
		0x0C: {"TSB", amABS}, 0x0D: {"ORA", amABS}, 0x0E: {"ASL", amABS}, 0x0F: {"ORA", amABSL},
		0x10: {"BPL", amREL}, 0x11: {"ORA", amDPIY}, 0x12: {"ORA", amDPI}, 0x13: {"ORA", amDPSY},
		0x14: {"TRB", amDP}, 0x15: {"ORA", amDPX}, 0x16: {"ASL", amDPX}, 0x17: {"ORA", amDPILY},
		0x18: {"CLC", amIMP}, 0x19: {"ORA", amABSY}, 0x1A: {"INC", amIMP}, 0x1B: {"TCS", amIMP},
		0x1C: {"TRB", amABS}, 0x1D: {"ORA", amABSX}, 0x1E: {"ASL", amABSX}, 0x1F: {"ORA", amABSLX},
		0x20: {"JSR", amABS}, 0x21: {"AND", amDPIX}, 0x22: {"JSL", amABSL}, 0x23: {"AND", amDPS},
		0x24: {"BIT", amDP}, 0x25: {"AND", amDP}, 0x26: {"ROL", amDP}, 0x27: {"AND", amDPIL},
		0x28: {"PLP", amIMP}, 0x29: {"AND", amIMM}, 0x2A: {"ROL", amIMP}, 0x2B: {"PLD", amIMP},
		0x2C: {"BIT", amABS}, 0x2D: {"AND", amABS}, 0x2E: {"ROL", amABS}, 0x2F: {"AND", amABSL},
		0x30: {"BMI", amREL}, 0x31: {"AND", amDPIY}, 0x32: {"AND", amDPI}, 0x33: {"AND", amDPSY},

		0x48: {"PHA", amIMP}, 0x49: {"EOR", amIMM}, 0x4A: {"LSR", amIMP}, 0x4B: {"PHK", amIMP},
		0x4C: {"JMP", amABS}, 0x4D: {"EOR", amABS}, 0x4E: {"LSR", amABS}, 0x4F: {"EOR", amABSL},

		0x54: {"MVN", amBLOCK}, 0x55: {"EOR", amDPX}, 0x56: {"LSR", amDPX}, 0x57: {"EOR", amDPILY},
		0x58: {"CLI", amIMP}, 0x59: {"EOR", amABSY}, 0x5A: {"PHY", amIMP}, 0x5B: {"TCD", amIMP},
		0x5C: {"JML", amABSL}, 0x5D: {"EOR", amABSX}, 0x5E: {"LSR", amABSX}, 0x5F: {"EOR", amABSLX},
		0x60: {"RTS", amIMP}, 0x61: {"ADC", amDPIX}, 0x62: {"PER", amRELL}, 0x63: {"ADC", amDPS},
		0x64: {"STZ", amDP}, 0x65: {"ADC", amDP}, 0x66: {"ROR", amDP}, 0x67: {"ADC", amDPIL},
		0x68: {"PLA", amIMP}, 0x69: {"ADC", amIMM}, 0x6A: {"ROR", amIMP}, 0x6B: {"RTL", amIMP},
		0x6C: {"JMP", amABSI}, 0x6D: {"ADC", amABS}, 0x6E: {"ROR", amABS}, 0x6F: {"ADC", amABSL},

		0x78: {"SEI", amIMP}, 0x79: {"ADC", amABSY}, 0x7A: {"PLY", amIMP}, 0x7B: {"TDC", amIMP},
		0x7C: {"JMP", amABSIX}, 0x7D: {"ADC", amABSX}, 0x7E: {"ROR", amABSX}, 0x7F: {"ADC", amABSLX},
		0x80: {"BRA", amREL}, 0x81: {"STA", amDPIX}, 0x82: {"BRL", amRELL}, 0x83: {"STA", amDPS},
		0x84: {"STY", amDP}, 0x85: {"STA", amDP}, 0x86: {"STX", amDP}, 0x87: {"STA", amDPIL},
		0x88: {"DEY", amIMP}, 0x89: {"BIT", amIMM}, 0x8A: {"TXA", amIMP}, 0x8B: {"PHB", amIMP},

		0x98: {"TYA", amIMP}, 0x99: {"STA", amABSY}, 0x9A: {"TXS", amIMP}, 0x9B: {"TXY", amIMP},
		0x9C: {"STZ", amABS}, 0x9D: {"STA", amABSX}, 0x9E: {"STZ", amABSX}, 0x9F: {"STA", amABSLX},
		0xA0: {"LDY", amIMM}, 0xA1: {"LDA", amDPIX}, 0xA2: {"LDX", amIMM}, 0xA3: {"LDA", amDPS},
		0xA4: {"LDY", amDP}, 0xA5: {"LDA", amDP}, 0xA6: {"LDX", amDP}, 0xA7: {"LDA", amDPIL},
		0xA8: {"TAY", amIMP}, 0xA9: {"LDA", amIMM}, 0xAA: {"TAX", amIMP}, 0xAB: {"PLB", amIMP},
		0xAC: {"LDY", amABS}, 0xAD: {"LDA", amABS}, 0xAE: {"LDX", amABS}, 0xAF: {"LDA", amABSL},
		0xB0: {"BCS", amREL}, 0xB1: {"LDA", amDPIY}, 0xB2: {"LDA", amDPI}, 0xB3: {"LDA", amDPSY},
		0xB4: {"LDY", amDPX}, 0xB5: {"LDA", amDPX}, 0xB6: {"LDX", amDPY}, 0xB7: {"LDA", amDPILY},
		0xB8: {"CLV", amIMP}, 0xB9: {"LDA", amABSY}, 0xBA: {"TSX", amIMP}, 0xBB: {"TYX", amIMP},
		0xBC: {"LDY", amABSX}, 0xBD: {"LDA", amABSX}, 0xBE: {"LDX", amABSY}, 0xBF: {"LDA", amABSL},
		0xC0: {"CPY", amIMM}, 0xC1: {"CMP", amDPIX}, 0xC2: {"REP", amIMM}, 0xC3: {"CMP", amDPS},
		0xC4: {"CPY", amDP}, 0xC5: {"CMP", amDP}, 0xC6: {"DEC", amDP}, 0xC7: {"CMP", amDPIL},
		0xC8: {"INY", amIMP}, 0xC9: {"CMP", amIMM}, 0xCA: {"DEX", amIMP}, 0xCB: {"WAI", amIMP},
		0xCC: {"CPY", amABS}, 0xCD: {"CMP", amABS}, 0xCE: {"DEC", amABS}, 0xCF: {"CMP", amABSL},
		0xD0: {"BNE", amREL}, 0xD1: {"CMP", amDPIY}, 0xD2: {"CMP", amDPI}, 0xD3: {"CMP", amDPSY},
		0xD4: {"PEI", amDP}, 0xD5: {"CMP", amDPX}, 0xD6: {"DEC", amDPX}, 0xD7: {"CMP", amDPILY},
		0xD8: {"CLD", amIMP}, 0xD9: {"CMP", amABSY}, 0xDA: {"PHX", amIMP}, 0xDB: {"TDC", amIMP},
		0xDC: {"JML", amABSIL}, 0xDD: {"CMP", amABSX}, 0xDE: {"DEC", amABSX}, 0xDF: {"CMP", amABSLX},
		0xE0: {"CPX", amIMM}, 0xE1: {"SBC", amDPIX}, 0xE2: {"SEP", amIMM}, 0xE3: {"SBC", amDPS},
		0xE4: {"CPX", amDP}, 0xE5: {"SBC", amDP}, 0xE6: {"INC", amDP}, 0xE7: {"SBC", amDPIL},
		0xE8: {"INX", amIMP}, 0xE9: {"SBC", amIMM}, 0xEA: {"NOP", amIMP}, 0xEB: {"XBA", amIMP},
		0xEC: {"CPX", amABS}, 0xED: {"SBC", amABS}, 0xEE: {"INC", amABS}, 0xEF: {"SBC", amABSL},
		0xF0: {"BEQ", amREL}, 0xF1: {"SBC", amDPIY}, 0xF2: {"SBC", amDPI}, 0xF3: {"SBC", amDPSY},
		0xF4: {"PEA", amIMM}, 0xF5: {"SBC", amDPX}, 0xF6: {"INC", amDPX}, 0xF7: {"SBC", amDPILY},
		0xF8: {"SED", amIMP}, 0xF9: {"SBC", amABSY}, 0xFA: {"PLX", amIMP}, 0xFB: {"TYX", amIMP},
		0xFC: {"JSR", amABSIX}, 0xFD: {"SBC", amABSX}, 0xFE: {"INC", amABSX}, 0xFF: {"SBC", amABSLX},
	}
	return t[op].mn, t[op].m
}

// decode renders one instruction. mFlag/xFlag true = 8-bit A / index.
// pc is the file offset, used for branch targets.
func decode(b []byte, pc int, mFlag, xFlag bool) (string, int) {
	op := b[0]
	mn, am := opcode(op)

	cpuTarget := func(fileOff int) string {
		bank := fileOff >> 16
		cb := bank
		if cb < 0x40 {
			cb = 0xC0 + cb
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("$%02X/%04X", cb, fileOff&0xFFFF)
	}

	// immediate size: A-ops follow M, index-ops follow X
	imm16 := false
	if am == amIMM {
		imm16 = !mFlag
		switch mn {
		case "CPX", "CPY", "LDX", "LDY":
			imm16 = !xFlag
		case "SEP", "REP", "WDM":
			imm16 = false
		case "PEA", "PER":
			imm16 = true
		}
	}
	n := 1
	args := ""
	switch am {
	case amIMP:
	case amIMM:
		if imm16 {
			args = fmt.Sprintf("#$%04X", uint16(b[1])|uint16(b[2])<<8)
			n = 3
		} else {
			args = fmt.Sprintf("#$%02X", b[1])
			n = 2
		}
	case amDP:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X", b[1]), 2
	case amDPX:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X,X", b[1]), 2
	case amDPY:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X,Y", b[1]), 2
	case amDPI:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("($%02X)", b[1]), 2
	case amDPIX:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("($%02X,X)", b[1]), 2
	case amDPIY:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("($%02X),Y", b[1]), 2
	case amDPS:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X,S", b[1]), 2
	case amDPSY:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("($%02X,S),Y", b[1]), 2
	case amDPIL:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("[$%02X]", b[1]), 2
	case amDPILY:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("[$%02X],Y", b[1]), 2
	case amABS:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X%02X", b[2], b[1]), 3
	case amABSX:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X%02X,X", b[2], b[1]), 3
	case amABSY:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X%02X,Y", b[2], b[1]), 3
	case amABSL:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X%02X%02X", b[3], b[2], b[1]), 4
	case amABSLX:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("$%02X%02X%02X,X", b[3], b[2], b[1]), 4
	case amREL:
		off := int(int8(b[1]))
		args, n = cpuTarget(pc+2+off), 2
	case amRELL:
		off := int(int16(uint16(b[1]) | uint16(b[2])<<8))
		args, n = cpuTarget(pc+3+off), 3
	case amBLOCK:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("%02X->%02X", b[2], b[1]), 3
	case amABSI:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("($%02X%02X)", b[2], b[1]), 3
	case amABSIX:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("($%02X%02X,X)", b[2], b[1]), 3
	case amABSIL:
		args, n = fmt.Sprintf("[$%02X%02X]", b[2], b[1]), 3
	}
	raw := ""
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		raw += fmt.Sprintf("%02X ", b[i])
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%-9s %s %s", strings.TrimRight(raw, " "), mn, args), n
}

func mapOffset(cpuBank, addr int, romLen int) int {
	switch {
	case cpuBank >= 0xC0:
		return (cpuBank-0xC0)*0x10000 + addr
	case cpuBank >= 0x40:
		return cpuBank*0x10000 + addr
	case cpuBank < 0x20: // low banks mirror the C0 bank +0xC0
		return (cpuBank+0xC0)*0x10000 + addr
	default:
		return cpuBank*0x10000 + addr
	}
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 3, 0, "usage: disasm65816 <rom> <Bank:Offset|0xfileoff> <count> [m=8|16] [x=8|16]\n"+
		"   or: disasm65816 <Bank:Offset|0xfileoff> <count>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc; m=/x= need the full form)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	var fileOff int
	if strings.Contains(args[1], ":") {
		parts := strings.Split(args[1], ":")
		bank, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[0], 16, 32)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "disasm65816: bank %q: want hex\n", parts[0])
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		addr, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[1], 16, 32)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "disasm65816: offset %q: want hex\n", parts[1])
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		fileOff = mapOffset(int(bank), int(addr), len(rom))
	} else {
		v, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimPrefix(args[1], "0x"), 16, 64)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "disasm65816: address %q: want hex\n", args[1])
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		fileOff = int(v)
	}
	count, err := strconv.Atoi(args[2])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "disasm65816: count %q: want number\n", args[2])
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	mFlag, xFlag := true, true
	for _, a := range args[3:] {
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "m=") {
			mFlag = a[2:] == "8"
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "x=") {
			xFlag = a[2:] == "8"
		}
	}
	if fileOff < 0 || fileOff >= len(rom) {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "offset %x out of range\n", fileOff)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	pc := fileOff
	for i := 0; i < count && pc < len(rom); i++ {
		cpuBank := pc >> 16
		if cpuBank < 0x40 {
			cpuBank = 0xC0 + cpuBank
		}
		text, insLen := decode(rom[pc:], pc, mFlag, xFlag)
		fmt.Printf("%02X/%04X: %s\n", cpuBank, pc&0xFFFF, text)
		switch rom[pc] {
		case 0xC2, 0xE2: // REP/SEP
			v := rom[pc+1]
			set := rom[pc] == 0xE2
			if v&0x20 != 0 {
				mFlag = set
			}
			if v&0x10 != 0 {
				xFlag = set
			}
		}
		pc += insLen
	}
}
