```go
// Command dumpchars extracts the ROM's playable-character (仲間) stat
// tables into a readable dump, one character per line.
//
// Usage: dumpchars <rom> <outdir>
//
//	dumpchars <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc.
//
// It writes <outdir>/chars.txt covering both tables (ally IDs 0x00-0x2F at
// FE:0600 and 0xB0-0xCF at 5A:79C0) with their 成長率 rows, plus the
// protagonist selection (主人公選択) age table. Names come from the actor
// name table at FD:1480, decoded through data/glyphs_jp.json (same
// semantics as cmd/dumpnames); the glyph file is located next to the repo
// root of the ROM path or the working directory.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/charstats"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

// selectTableOffset (0x3E961B, FE:961B): 8 entries x 4 B
// {graphic, ally ID, age 歳, title 肩書き} for the eight protagonists.
const selectTableOffset = 0x3E961B
const selectCount = 8

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 2, "usage: dumpchars <rom> <outdir>\n"+
		"   or: dumpchars <outdir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	romPath, outDir := args[0], args[1]
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	glyphPath, err := findGlyphs(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(glyphPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	dec := bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot)

	allies, err := charstats.AllAllies(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	f, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(outDir, "chars.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	defer f.Close()

	fmt.Fprintln(f, "# id name HP(+g) LP str dex agi vit mag wil cha | 剣斧槍弓体 spell1 spell2 amplify grow flash sei forte cmd | g:剣斧槍弓体 蒼朱白玄太月 unk amp WP JP HP | techs | spells | gear")
	for _, a := range allies {
		g, err := charstats.GrowthAt(rom, a.ID)
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(f, "%02X %s %d%s %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d | %s %s %s %s %s %s %s %s | %d %s %d %s %d | %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d | %02X %02X %02X %02X | %02X %02X %02X %02X | %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n",
			a.ID, allyName(dec, rom, a.ID),
			a.HP, growsMark(a.HPGrows), a.LP,
			a.Strength, a.Dexterity, a.Agility, a.Vitality, a.Magic, a.Will, a.Charm,
			lvMark(a.Weapon[0]), lvMark(a.Weapon[1]), lvMark(a.Weapon[2]), lvMark(a.Weapon[3]), lvMark(a.Weapon[4]),
			spellMark(a.Spell1, spell1Schools[:]), spellMark(a.Spell2, spell2Schools[:]), lvMark(a.Amplify),
			a.GrowthType, charstats.FlashName(a.FlashType), a.Destiny, charstats.ForteName(a.ForteWeapon), a.Commander,
			g.Sword, g.Axe, g.Spear, g.Bow, g.Martial,
			g.Goryu, g.Suzaku, g.Byakko, g.Genbu, g.Solar, g.Lunar,
			g.Unknown11, g.Amplify, g.WP, g.JP, g.HP,
			a.InitialTechs[0], a.InitialTechs[1], a.InitialTechs[2], a.InitialTechs[3],
			a.InitialSpells[0], a.InitialSpells[1], a.InitialSpells[2], a.InitialSpells[3],
			a.Equipment[0], a.Equipment[1], a.Equipment[2], a.Equipment[3],
			a.Equipment[4], a.Equipment[5], a.Equipment[6], a.Equipment[7])
	}

	fmt.Fprintln(f, "")
	fmt.Fprintln(f, "# protagonist selection (FE:961B): graphic ally-ID age title")
	selRec := make([]byte, 4)
	for i := 0; i < selectCount; i++ {
		start := selectTableOffset + i*4
		copy(selRec, rom[start:start+4])
		fmt.Fprintf(f, "%d graphic=%02X ally=%02X age=%d title=%02X\n",
			i, selRec[0], selRec[1], selRec[2], selRec[3])
	}
	fmt.Printf("%d characters written to %s\n", len(allies), filepath.Join(outDir, "chars.txt"))
}

var spell1Schools = [4]string{"蒼龍", "朱鳥", "白虎", "玄武"}
var spell2Schools = [2]string{"太陽", "月"}

func growsMark(g bool) string {
	if g {
		return "+"
	}
	return ""
}

func lvMark(l charstats.GrowableLevel) string {
	s := fmt.Sprint(l.Level())
	if l.Grows() {
		s += "+"
	}
	return s
}

func spellMark(l charstats.GrowableLevel, schools []string) string {
	s := schools[l.SchoolBits()>>5]
	if l.Grows() {
		s += "+"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", s, l.Level())
}

// textDecoder is satisfied by the decoder from bokuno.NewTextDecoder.
type textDecoder interface {
	DecodeBuffer([]byte) bokuno.DecodeResult
}

// allyName reads the 8-byte name slot for the ally ID from the FD:1480
// actor table and decodes it; a read past the ROM yields "?".
func allyName(dec textDecoder, rom []byte, id int) string {
	start := charstats.NameTableOffset + id*charstats.NameEntrySize
	if start+charstats.NameEntrySize > len(rom) {
		return "?"
	}
	rec := rom[start : start+charstats.NameEntrySize]
	var buf []byte
	for i := 0; i < len(rec); i++ {
		b := rec[i]
		if b == 0x00 || b == 0x50 {
			break
		}
		buf = append(buf, b)
		if b < 0x50 && i+1 < len(rec) {
			buf = append(buf, rec[i+1])
			i++
		}
	}
	return dec.DecodeBuffer(buf).Text
}

// findGlyphs locates data/glyphs_jp.json: next to the repo root that holds
// the ROM (patches/..), else relative to the working directory.
func findGlyphs(romPath string) (string, error) {
	candidates := []string{
		filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(romPath)), "data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
		filepath.Join("data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
	}
	for _, p := range candidates {
		if st, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil && !st.IsDir() {
			return p, nil
		}
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("glyph assignment not found (tried %v); run from the repo root", candidates)
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumpenemies/main.go`:

```go
// Command dumpenemies extracts the ROM's enemy stat tables into a
// readable dump, one enemy per line.
//
// Usage: dumpenemies <rom> <outdir>
//
//	dumpenemies <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc.
//
// It writes <outdir>/enemies.txt covering both tables (IDs 0x000-0x13F at
// FE:3F8B — the array's gap region past 0x0FF feeds ids up to 0x13F — and
// 0x140-0x1FF at 5A:0000; the documented 5A:07D0 is that array's id-0x190
// tail. The router 5A:3600 picks by id*25 < $1F40,
// docs/enemy-records-bank7e.md). Names come from the name tables
// embedded in internal/battledata.
//
// It also writes <outdir>/patterns.txt, one row per enemy action slot:
// the two action patterns (stat bytes +17/+18) resolved into enemy-tech
// IDs (0x000-0x1FF) with decoded tech names.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/battledata"
	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

// Enemy-tech name tables (docs/battle-data.md "Action patterns"):
// 10-byte records, decoded through data/glyphs_jp.json. The extended
// table covers the hack's 拡張敵技 IDs 0x100-0x1FF.
const (
	techNameMainOffset = 0x3D31C0
	techNameExtOffset  = 0x5B40C0
	techNameStride     = 10
	techNameCount      = 256
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 2, "usage: dumpenemies <rom> <outdir>\n"+
		"   or: dumpenemies <outdir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	outDir := args[1]
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	enemies, err := battledata.AllEnemies(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	techNames := techNameTable(rom)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeEnemies(filepath.Join(outDir, "enemies.txt"), enemies); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writePatterns(filepath.Join(outDir, "patterns.txt"), rom, enemies, techNames); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("%d enemies written to %s\n", len(enemies), outDir)
}

func writeEnemies(path string, enemies []battledata.Enemy) error {
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	fmt.Fprintln(f, "# id  name  HP  str dex agi vit mag wil cha  tech spell growth flash  sp flags school u2 u3  act1 act2 wpn1 wpn2 shield armor1 armor2 held")
	for _, e := range enemies {
		name, _ := battledata.Name(e.ID)
		fmt.Fprintf(f,
			"%03X %s %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n",
			e.ID, name, e.HP,
			e.Strength, e.Dexterity, e.Agility, e.Vitality, e.Magic, e.Will, e.Charm,
			e.TechLV, e.SpellLV, e.GrowthLV, e.FlashLV,
			e.Species, e.SpeciesFlags, e.SchoolResist, e.TargetBits, e.AIMode,
			e.ActionPattern1, e.ActionPattern2, e.Weapon1, e.Weapon2, e.Shield, e.Armor1, e.Armor2, e.HeldItem)
	}
	return nil
}

// writePatterns dumps every enemy's two action patterns as one row per
// slot: id, name, pattern (1/2), weapon item ID, pattern ID, slot,
// resolved enemy-tech ID, extended flag, tech name.
func writePatterns(path string, rom []byte, enemies []battledata.Enemy, techNames []string) error {
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	fmt.Fprintln(f, "# id  name  pat  weapon  pattern  slot  tech  ext  tech-name")
	for _, e := range enemies {
		pats, err := battledata.PatternsFor(rom, e.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("enemy %#03x: %w", e.ID, err)
		}
		name, _ := battledata.Name(e.ID)
		for pi, p := range pats {
			for _, a := range p.Actions {
				fmt.Fprintf(f, "%03X %s %d %02X %02X %d %03X %d %s\n",
					e.ID, name, pi+1, p.Weapon, p.ID, a.Slot, a.TechID,
					boolInt(a.Extended), techName(techNames, a.TechID))
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// techNameTable decodes the two enemy-tech name tables.
func techNameTable(rom []byte) []string {
	names := make([]string, 2*techNameCount)
	dec := newTextDecoder(rom)
	if dec == nil {
		return names
	}
	copy(names, dec.NameTable(techNameMainOffset, techNameStride, techNameCount))
	copy(names[techNameCount:], dec.NameTable(techNameExtOffset, techNameStride, techNameCount))
	return names
}

func techName(names []string, id uint16) string {
	if int(id) < len(names) && names[id] != "" {
		return names[id]
	}
	return "?"
}

func boolInt(b bool) int {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// newTextDecoder builds the glyph decoder for the ROM's text tables;
// without data/glyphs_jp.json names stay empty and the dump falls back
// to "?".
func newTextDecoder(rom []byte) *bokuno.Ops {
	glyphPath, err := findGlyphs()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "tech names skipped: %v\n", err)
		return nil
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(glyphPath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "tech names skipped: %v\n", err)
		return nil
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "tech names skipped: %v\n", err)
		return nil
	}
	ops := bokuno.NewOps(rom)
	ops.SetText(bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot))
	return ops
}

// findGlyphs locates data/glyphs_jp.json relative to the working
// directory or the repo root two levels above patches/.
func findGlyphs() (string, error) {
	candidates := []string{
		filepath.Join("data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
		filepath.Join("..", "data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
	}
	for _, p := range candidates {
		if st, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil && !st.IsDir() {
			return p, nil
		}
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("glyph assignment not found (tried %v); run from the repo root", candidates)
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumpevents/main.go`:

```go
// Command dumpevents disassembles every native bokuno event to text.
//
// Usage: dumpevents <rom> <outdir> [glyph-assignment.json]
//
//	dumpevents <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and the glyph
// assignment to data/glyphs_jp.json; the glyph file defaults there
// whenever it is omitted.
//
// ROM identity is checked against the canonical bokuno_jp build
// (CRC32 7E165025). Output: <outdir>/events/<ID>.txt, index.json, plus a
// stop-reason tally on stdout — same formats as the retired Node dumper.
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
)

const bokunoJPSHA = "4793e1422295b8c13ba81b070b941288d36be339ff20f914652ce63cc06f2da0"

const (
	defaultROMPath    = "patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"
	defaultGlyphsPath = "data/glyphs_jp.json"
)

func main() {
	args := os.Args[1:]
	switch len(args) {
	case 1: // short form: ROM and glyph assignment take the defaults
		args = []string{defaultROMPath, args[0], defaultGlyphsPath}
	case 2: // today's form; the omitted glyph assignment takes the default
		args = []string{args[0], args[1], defaultGlyphsPath}
	case 3:
		// full form, maps as always
	default:
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpevents <rom> <outdir> [glyph-assignment.json]\n"+
			"   or: dumpevents <outdir>\n"+
			"   (defaults: rom patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, glyphs data/glyphs_jp.json)")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	romPath, outDir := args[0], args[1]
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(rom)
	got := fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum[:])
	if got != bokunoJPSHA {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "ROM mismatch: %s\nexpected %s (canonical bokuno_jp, CRC32 7E165025)\n", got, bokunoJPSHA)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	ops := bokuno.NewOps(rom)
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(args[2])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := parseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	ops.SetText(bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot))

	ids := nativeIDs()
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(outDir, "events"), 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	type indexEntry struct {
		ID     string `json:"id"`
		Entry  string `json:"entry,omitempty"`
		End16  string `json:"end16,omitempty"`
		Status string `json:"status"`
		Ops    *int   `json:"ops,omitempty"`
	}
	var index []indexEntry
	for _, id := range ids {
		hex := fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id)
		r, resLines, status, ok := ops.WalkEvent(id)
		if !ok {
			// node used id.toString(16) here: lowercase, unpadded
			index = append(index, indexEntry{ID: strconv.FormatInt(int64(id), 16), Status: "no-range"})
			continue
		}
		ops0 := len(resLines) // always present for walked events, even 0
		_ = ops0
		// File layout matches the Node dumper: header line ends with \n,
		// then the joined lines and one final \n (so empty events get the
		// trailing blank line the JS produced).
		head := fmt.Sprintf("event %s  entry %x  status %s  ops %d\n", hex, r.EntryCPU, status, len(resLines))
		content := head + strings.Join(resLines, "\n") + "\n"
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(outDir, "events", hex+".txt"), []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		index = append(index, indexEntry{
			ID:     hex,
			Entry:  strconv.FormatInt(int64(r.EntryCPU), 16),
			End16:  strconv.FormatInt(int64(r.End16), 16),
			Status: status,
			Ops:    &ops0,
		})
	}
	idxJSON, err := marshalIndent(index)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	idxJSON = append(idxJSON, '\n') // node wrote stringify(...) + '\n'
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(outDir, "events", "index.json"), idxJSON, 0o644); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	tally := map[string]int{}
	var order []string
	for _, e := range index {
		if _, seen := tally[e.Status]; !seen {
			order = append(order, e.Status)
		}
		tally[e.Status]++
	}
	sort.SliceStable(order, func(i, j int) bool { return tally[order[i]] > tally[order[j]] })
	fmt.Printf("events: %d\n", len(index))
	for _, k := range order {
		fmt.Printf("  %s: %d\n", k, tally[k])
	}
}

func nativeIDs() []int {
	var ids []int
	for id := 1; id <= 0xeff; id++ {
		if id>>8 != 0xd {
			ids = append(ids, id)
		}
	}
	for id := 0xc00; id <= 0xcff; id++ {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	for id := 0xe00; id <= 0xeff; id++ {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	for id := 0x4c00; id <= 0x4cff; id++ {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	return ids
}

func parseAssignment(raw []byte) (glyphs.Assignment, error) {
	// the JSON is {"char": slot, ...}; decode generically to keep order
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
	tok, err := dec.Token()
	if err != nil {
		return glyphs.Assignment{}, err
	}
	if d, ok := tok.(json.Delim); !ok || d != '{' {
		return glyphs.Assignment{}, fmt.Errorf("assignment JSON: want object")
	}
	a := glyphs.Assignment{Slot: map[string]int{}}
	for dec.More() {
		key, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return glyphs.Assignment{}, err
		}
		val, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return glyphs.Assignment{}, err
		}
		num, ok := val.(float64)
		if !ok {
			return glyphs.Assignment{}, fmt.Errorf("assignment slot for %q is not a number", key)
		}
		ch := key.(string)
		a.Order = append(a.Order, ch)
		a.Slot[ch] = int(num)
	}
	return a, nil
}

func marshalIndent(v any) ([]byte, error) {
	var out []byte
	buf := make([]byte, 0, 1<<20)
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// node's JSON.stringify(v, null, 1): one-space indent
	buf = append(buf, b...)
	_ = out
	return indentOne(buf), nil
}

// indentOne reformats compact JSON with one-space indentation the way
// JSON.stringify(v, null, 1) does.
func indentOne(compact []byte) []byte {
	var out []byte
	depth := 0
	inStr := false
	esc := false
	for _, c := range compact {
		if inStr {
			out = append(out, c)
			if esc {
				esc = false
			} else if c == '\\' {
				esc = true
			} else if c == '"' {
				inStr = false
			}
			continue
		}
		switch c {
		case '"':
			inStr = true
			out = append(out, c)
		case '{', '[':
			out = append(out, c)
			// look ahead: empty object/array stays inline
			depth++
			out = append(out, '\n')
			out = append(out, pad(depth)...)
		case '}', ']':
			depth--
			out = append(out, '\n')
			out = append(out, pad(depth)...)
			out = append(out, c)
		case ',':
			out = append(out, c, '\n')
			out = append(out, pad(depth)...)
		case ':':
			out = append(out, ':', ' ')
		default:
			out = append(out, c)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func pad(depth int) []byte {
	b := make([]byte, depth)
	for i := range b {
		b[i] = ' '
	}
	return b
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumpfont/main.go`:

```go
// dumpfont renders the RS3/bokuno message font to verification sheets.
//
// Usage: dumpfont <rom> <glyph-json> <outdir>
//
//	dumpfont <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and the glyph
// JSON to data/glyphs_jp.json.
//
// It decodes every slot assigned in the glyph JSON (char -> slot), draws one
// PNG sheet per font page (slots 16 per row, 2x scale, slot label under each
// glyph), and writes index.txt mapping each slot to its character and sheet
// cell.
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"

	"saga3/internal/fontfmt"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

// digit3x5 holds 0-9 A-F as 3x5 bitmaps, one byte per row, low 3 bits used.
var digit3x5 = map[byte][5]byte{
	'0': {0x07, 0x05, 0x05, 0x05, 0x07},
	'1': {0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02, 0x02},
	'2': {0x07, 0x04, 0x07, 0x01, 0x07},
	'3': {0x07, 0x01, 0x07, 0x01, 0x07},
	'4': {0x05, 0x05, 0x07, 0x01, 0x01},
	'5': {0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x01, 0x07},
	'6': {0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x05, 0x07},
	'7': {0x07, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01},
	'8': {0x07, 0x05, 0x07, 0x05, 0x07},
	'9': {0x07, 0x05, 0x07, 0x01, 0x07},
	'A': {0x07, 0x05, 0x07, 0x05, 0x05},
	'B': {0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x07},
	'C': {0x07, 0x07, 0x01, 0x07, 0x07},
	'D': {0x07, 0x05, 0x05, 0x05, 0x07},
	'E': {0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x07},
	'F': {0x07, 0x07, 0x07, 0x05, 0x05},
}

const (
	scale  = 2
	cellW  = 16 * scale
	cellH  = 16*scale + 6 // glyph plus label strip
	perRow = 16
)

var (
	inked   = color.RGBA{R: 0x20, G: 0x20, B: 0x20, A: 0xff}
	paper   = color.RGBA{R: 0xf8, G: 0xf8, B: 0xf8, A: 0xff}
	line    = color.RGBA{R: 0xf0, G: 0xb0, B: 0xb0, A: 0xff}
	labelPx = color.RGBA{R: 0x30, G: 0x30, B: 0x30, A: 0xff}
)

func drawLabel(img *image.RGBA, x, y int, text string) {
	for i := len(text) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		glyph, ok := digit3x5[text[i]]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		for ry := 0; ry < 5; ry++ {
			for rx := 0; rx < 3; rx++ {
				if glyph[ry]>>(2-rx)&1 != 0 {
					img.Set(x+rx, y+ry, labelPx)
				}
			}
		}
		x -= 4
	}
}

func hexSlot(slot int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%03X", slot)
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROMGlyphs(flag.Args(), "usage: dumpfont <rom> <glyph-json> <outdir>\n"+
		"   or: dumpfont <outdir>\n"+
		"   (defaults: rom patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, glyphs data/glyphs_jp.json)")
	romPath, jsonPath, outDir := args[0], args[1], args[2]

	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "read ROM: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(jsonPath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "read glyph json: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "parse glyph json: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "create outdir: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Group assigned slots by page so each sheet covers one page.
	byPage := map[int][]int{}
	seen := map[int]bool{}
	for _, slot := range func() []int {
		out := make([]int, 0, len(assign.Order))
		for _, ch := range assign.Order {
			out = append(out, assign.Slot[ch])
		}
		sort.Ints(out)
		return out
	}() {
		if seen[slot] {
			continue
		}
		seen[slot] = true
		page := slot >> 8
		byPage[page] = append(byPage[page], slot)
	}
	_ = byPage
	// Rebuild ordered per-page slot lists with chars attached.
	type cell struct {
		slot int
		ch   string
	}
	perPage := map[int][]cell{}
	for _, ch := range assign.Order {
		slot := assign.Slot[ch]
		perPage[slot>>8] = append(perPage[slot>>8], cell{slot, ch})
	}
	pages := make([]int, 0, len(perPage))
	for page := range perPage {
		pages = append(pages, page)
	}
	sort.Ints(pages)

	index, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(outDir, "index.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "create index: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer index.Close()

	total := 0
	for _, page := range pages {
		cells := perPage[page]
		sort.Slice(cells, func(i, j int) bool { return cells[i].slot < cells[j].slot })
		rows := (len(cells) + perRow - 1) / perRow
		img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, perRow*(cellW+1)+1, rows*(cellH+1)+1))
		for y := range img.Bounds().Dy() {
			for x := range img.Bounds().Dx() {
				img.Set(x, y, line)
			}
		}
		for i, c := range cells {
			g, err := fontfmt.Decode(rom, c.slot)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "decode slot %#x: %v\n", c.slot, err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			cx := (i % perRow) * (cellW + 1)
			cy := (i / perRow) * (cellH + 1)
			for y := 0; y < 16; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < 16; x++ {
					px := paper
					if g[y][x] != 0 {
						px = inked
					}
					for sy := 0; sy < scale; sy++ {
						for sx := 0; sx < scale; sx++ {
							img.Set(cx+x*scale+sx, cy+y*scale+sy, px)
						}
					}
				}
			}
			drawLabel(img, cx+cellW-4*len(hexSlot(c.slot)), cy+cellH-6, hexSlot(c.slot))
			fmt.Fprintf(index, "page %X idx %02X slot %03X  %s\n", page, c.slot&0xff, c.slot, c.ch)
		}
		name := filepath.Join(outDir, fmt.Sprintf("font_page%X.png", page))
		f, err := os.Create(name)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "create %s: %v\n", name, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if err := png.Encode(f, img); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "encode %s: %v\n", name, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		f.Close()
		fmt.Printf("wrote %s (%d glyphs, page %X)\n", name, len(cells), page)
		total += len(cells)
	}
	fmt.Printf("total glyphs: %d; index: %s\n", total, filepath.Join(outDir, "index.txt"))
}
```

`cmd/dumpitems/main.go`:

```go
// Command dumpitems extracts the item tables (道具) of the bokuno RS3
// hack with decoded names and per-kind fields.
//
// Usage: dumpitems <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <outdir>
//
//	dumpitems <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and the glyph
// assignment to data/glyphs_jp.json.
//
// Writes <outdir>/items.txt, one item per line, and <outdir>/items.json
// (the field-menu detail data): main table IDs 0x000-0x0FF then the
// extension table 0x100-0x1FF. Table addresses and field layouts are
// documented in docs/items.md; decoding lives in internal/items.
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/items"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROMGlyphs(os.Args[1:], "usage: dumpitems <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <outdir>\n"+
		"   or: dumpitems <outdir>\n"+
		"   (defaults: rom patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, glyphs data/glyphs_jp.json)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	dec := bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot)
	outDir := args[2]

	all, err := items.AllItems(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	f, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(outDir, "items.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	defer f.Close()

	var unmapped int
	jj := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(all))
	for _, it := range all {
		name, issues := decodeName(rom, dec, it.ID)
		unmapped += issues
		tag := ""
		if issues > 0 {
			tag = fmt.Sprintf("  [%d unmapped]", issues)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(f, "%03X %-10s %-10s %5d %s%s\n",
			it.ID, name, it.Kind, it.Price, fields(it), tag)
		jj = append(jj, jsonFields(it, name))
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(outDir, "items.json"), jj); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("items: %d entries, %d unmapped glyphs\n", len(all), unmapped)
}

// jsonFields renders one item as a JSON record. Shared keys id/name/kind/
// price always emit; the kind-specific keys only emit when the kind has
// them, so Godot can branch on the kind and read the rest directly.
func jsonFields(it items.Item, name string) map[string]any {
	if name == "" {
		name = items.Name(it.ID)
	}
	m := map[string]any{
		"id":    fmt.Sprintf("%02X", it.ID),
		"name":  name,
		"kind":  it.Kind.String(),
		"price": it.Price,
	}
	switch it.Kind {
	case items.Weapon:
		m["category"] = it.Category
		m["power"] = it.Power
		m["weight"] = it.Weight
		if it.Cursed {
			m["cursed"] = true
		}
		// 固有技 bytes: raw tech IDs, unresolved as names (docs/items.md
		// open questions).
		techs := []string{}
		for _, t := range []int{it.Tech1, it.Tech2} {
			if t >= 0 {
				techs = append(techs, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", t))
			}
		}
		if len(techs) > 0 {
			m["techs"] = techs
		}
	case items.Shield:
		m["category"] = it.Category
		m["defense"] = it.Defense
		m["evade"] = it.Evade
		m["block"] = it.ShieldBlock
		m["resist"] = it.ShieldResist
		m["weight"] = it.Weight
		if it.Cursed {
			m["cursed"] = true
		}
	case items.Armor:
		m["phys_def"] = it.PhysDef
		m["phys_resist"] = byte(it.PhysResist)
		m["mag_def"] = it.MagDef
		m["mag_resist"] = byte(it.MagResist)
		m["status_block"] = it.StatusBlock
		m["type_bits"] = it.TypeBits
		m["school_resist"] = it.SchoolResist
		m["stat_bonus"] = it.StatBonus
		m["misc"] = it.Misc
		m["weight"] = it.Misc & 0x07
	case items.Consumable:
		m["category"] = it.Category
		m["weight"] = it.Weight
		m["recover_power"] = it.RecoverPower
		m["cures_status"] = it.CuresStatus
	case items.Usable:
		m["effect"] = it.Effect
		m["amount"] = it.Amount
		if it.Amount == 0x80 {
			m["full"] = true
		}
	}
	return m
}

func writeJSON(path string, v any) error {
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o644)
}

// decodeName decodes one item's name record through the glyph assignment.
func decodeName(rom []byte, dec *bokuno.TextDecoder, id int) (string, int) {
	rec, err := items.RawNameRecord(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return "?", 0
	}
	d := dec.DecodeBuffer(rec)
	return d.Text, d.Issues
}

// fields renders the kind-specific columns.
func fields(it items.Item) string {
	switch it.Kind {
	case items.Weapon:
		// The 固有技 bytes do not index the 技名称 table (see
		// docs/items.md open questions), so print raw IDs.
		return fmt.Sprintf("cat=%s power=%d weight=%d techs=%s/%s",
			it.Category, it.Power, it.Weight,
			techRef(it.Tech1), techRef(it.Tech2))
	case items.Shield:
		judge := "garden"
		if it.ShieldBlock {
			judge = "shield"
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("cat=%s def=%d evade=%d(%s) resist=0x%02X",
			it.Category, it.Defense, it.Evade, judge, it.ShieldResist)
	case items.Armor:
		return fmt.Sprintf("phys=%d physres=0x%02X mag=%d magres=0x%02X status=0x%02X type=0x%02X resist=0x%02X bonus=0x%02X misc=0x%02X",
			it.PhysDef, byte(it.PhysResist), it.MagDef, byte(it.MagResist),
			it.StatusBlock, it.TypeBits, it.SchoolResist, it.StatBonus, it.Misc)
	case items.Consumable:
		return fmt.Sprintf("cat=%s power=%d cures=0x%02X unk=0x%02X",
			it.Category, it.RecoverPower, it.CuresStatus, it.ConsumableUnknown)
	default: // items.Usable
		return fmt.Sprintf("effect=0x%02X amount=%d", it.Effect, it.Amount)
	}
}

// techRef renders a weapon 固有技 reference (-1 = none).
func techRef(id int) string {
	if id < 0 {
		return "-"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%02X", id)
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumpmaps/main.go`:

```go
// dumpmaps renders Romancing SaGa 3 submaps from a patched ExHiROM SFC
// image and writes an index of the submap table.
//
// Usage: dumpmaps <rom> <outdir> [all|debug <id>|verify <cfg> <wram>|compare <id> <shot.png> [diff.png]]
//
//	dumpmaps <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and runs the
// default render; the mode keywords need the full form.
//
// The outdir receives one PNG per rendered map plus index.tsv describing
// every submap table entry. Map IDs 0x02 (Pidona old town) and 0x04
// (Pidona wharf) are rendered; both were verified visually against the
// in-game maps.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

// renderedIDs are the maps dumpmaps renders. Extend freely; any ID whose
// header is present renders, zeroed entries error and are skipped.
var renderedIDs = []int{0x02, 0x04, 0x249, 0x246, 0x24A, 0x24B, 0x250}

// parseMapID parses a submap id the way map ids are written everywhere in
// this project: hex, with the 0x prefix optional. Go's base-0 parsing read
// bare "249" as DECIMAL 249 = 0xF9 — a different map — which produced the
// misleading compare scores behind the 2026-11-17 "missing ground" hunt.
func parseMapID(s string) (int, error) {
	v, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimPrefix(s, "0x"), 16, 32)
	return int(v), err
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 0, "usage: dumpmaps <rom> <outdir> [all|debug <id>|verify <cfg> <wram>|compare <id> <shot.png> [diff.png]]\n"+
		"   or: dumpmaps <outdir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	if err := run(args[0], args[1]); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpmaps:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func run(romPath, outdir string) error {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read ROM: %w", err)
	}
	if len(os.Args) > 3 && os.Args[3] == "all" {
		return renderAll(mapfmt.ROM(rom), outdir)
	}
	if len(os.Args) > 3 && os.Args[3] == "debug" {
		if len(os.Args) != 5 {
			return fmt.Errorf("usage: dumpmaps <rom> <outdir> debug <mapid-hex>")
		}
		id, err := parseMapID(os.Args[4])
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return debugMap(mapfmt.ROM(rom), int(id))
	}
	if len(os.Args) > 3 && os.Args[3] == "verify" {
		if len(os.Args) != 6 {
			return fmt.Errorf("usage: dumpmaps <rom> <outdir> verify <config-hex> <wram-dump>")
		}
		cfg, err := parseMapID(os.Args[4])
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return verifyObjects(mapfmt.ROM(rom), byte(cfg), os.Args[5])
	}
	if len(os.Args) > 3 && os.Args[3] == "compare" {
		if len(os.Args) < 6 || len(os.Args) > 7 {
			return fmt.Errorf("usage: dumpmaps <rom> <outdir> compare <mapid-hex> <screenshot.png> [diff.png]")
		}
		id, err := parseMapID(os.Args[4])
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		var diffPath string
		if len(os.Args) == 7 {
			diffPath = os.Args[6]
		}
		return compareScreenshot(mapfmt.ROM(rom), int(id), os.Args[5], diffPath)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outdir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create outdir: %w", err)
	}
	for _, id := range renderedIDs {
		if err := renderOne(mapfmt.ROM(rom), outdir, id); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return writeIndex(mapfmt.ROM(rom), outdir)
}

// renderAll renders every submap whose header decodes; zeroed or corrupt
// entries are skipped and counted.
func renderAll(rom mapfmt.ROM, outdir string) error {
	ok, skipped := 0, 0
	reasons := map[string]int{}
	for id := 0; id < 1024; id++ {
		if err := renderOne(rom, outdir, id); err != nil {
			skipped++
			msg := err.Error()
			// Group per-map errors by their shared suffix (message
			// after the "render submap 0xNNNN: " prefix).
			if i := strings.Index(msg, ": "); i >= 0 {
				msg = msg[i+2:]
			}
			reasons[msg]++
			continue
		}
		ok++
	}
	fmt.Printf("rendered %d maps, skipped %d\n", ok, skipped)
	for msg, n := range reasons {
		fmt.Printf("skip %4d x %s\n", n, msg)
	}
	return writeIndex(rom, outdir)
}

func renderOne(rom mapfmt.ROM, outdir string, id int) error {
	rendered, err := mapfmt.RenderSubmap(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("render submap %#04x: %w", id, err)
	}
	path := filepath.Join(outdir, fmt.Sprintf("map%04x.png", id))
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	err = png.Encode(f, rendered.Image)
	closeErr := f.Close()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if closeErr != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("close %s: %w", path, closeErr)
	}
	fmt.Printf("wrote %s (%dx%d tiles)\n", path, rendered.Width, rendered.Height)
	return nil
}

// debugMap prints the raw layer/object composition of one submap for
// renderer debugging.
func debugMap(rom mapfmt.ROM, id int) error {
	off, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	h, err := mapfmt.ReadHeader(rom, off)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Printf("map %#04x record %06X flags1 %#04x L1 %#08x L2 %#08x L3 %#08x prop %#08x chipset %#04x pal %#04x objcfg %#04x size %dx%d\n",
		id, off, h.Flags1, h.Layer1, h.Layer2, h.Layer3, h.Prop,
		h.Chipset, h.PaletteSet, h.ObjectConfig, h.SizeX+1, h.SizeY+1)
	objs, err := mapfmt.LoadObjectSet(rom, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("objects: %v\n", err)
	} else {
		chips := 0
		for _, o := range objs.Objects {
			chips += len(o.Chips)
		}
		fmt.Printf("objects: %d objects, %d chips\n", len(objs.Objects), chips)
	}
	for _, lp := range []struct {
		name string
		off  int
	}{{"L1", h.Layer1}, {"L2", h.Layer2}, {"L3", h.Layer3}} {
		if lp.off < 0 {
			fmt.Printf("%s: absent\n", lp.name)
			continue
		}
		if err := debugLayer(rom, lp.off, objs); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("%s: %v\n", lp.name, err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// debugLayer walks a display layer's raw record stream and prints stats.
func debugLayer(rom mapfmt.ROM, off int, objs *mapfmt.ObjectSet) error {
	size, _ := rom.U8(off)
	base, _ := rom.U16LE(off + 1)
	dsize, _ := rom.U16LE(off + 3)
	fmt.Printf("layer at %06X: size %#02x (%dx%d tiles) base %#04x dsize %#04x\n",
		off, size, int(size>>4)*32, int(size&0xF)*32, base, dsize)
	var counts [4]int
	badOID, badCoord, oobStop := 0, 0, 0
	q := off + 5
	end := off + dsize
	for q < end {
		x, _ := rom.U8(q)
		y, _ := rom.U8(q + 1)
		flag, _ := rom.U8(q + 2)
		q += 3
		switch flag & 3 {
		case 0:
			oid, _ := rom.U8(q)
			q++
			counts[0]++
			if int(oid) >= len(objs.Objects) {
				badOID++
			}
			if int(x) > int(size>>4)*32 || int(y) > int(size&0xF)*32 {
				badCoord++
			}
		case 1, 2:
			q++
			counts[flag&3]++
		default:
			q += 4
			counts[3]++
			if q > end {
				oobStop++
			}
		}
	}
	l, err := mapfmt.DecodeLayer(rom, off, objs)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("decode: %w (records obj=%d chip=%d rep=%d badOID=%d badCoord=%d oobStop=%d, consumed %d/%d)",
			err, counts[0], counts[1]+counts[2], counts[3], badOID, badCoord, oobStop, q-off, dsize)
	}
	nonzero := 0
	for _, t := range l.Tiles {
		if t.Word != 0 {
			nonzero++
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("  decode ok: records obj=%d chip=%d rep=%d badOID=%d badCoord=%d oobStop=%d consumed %d/%d; tiles %d/%d nonzero\n",
		counts[0], counts[1]+counts[2], counts[3], badOID, badCoord, oobStop, q-off, dsize, nonzero, len(l.Tiles))
	return nil
}

// verifyObjects compares the decoded object config stream against a
// MesenCE WRAM dump of the engine's decoded object tables
// (tools/emulator/shot_wramdump.lua): object start offsets at $7E:2000,
// entry-end offsets at $7E:2200, 3-byte chip entries (chip lo / palette
// byte / pos x<<4|y) at $7E:2400.
func verifyObjects(rom mapfmt.ROM, config byte, wramPath string) error {
	wram, err := os.ReadFile(wramPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	rd := func(wramAddr int) int {
		i := wramAddr - 0x2000
		return int(wram[i]) | int(wram[i+1])<<8
	}
	objs, err := mapfmt.LoadObjects(rom, config)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	total, matched, badObjects := 0, 0, 0
	for k := 0; ; k++ {
		st, en := rd(0x2000+2*k), rd(0x2200+2*k)
		if st == 0xFFFF || en == 0xFFFF || en < st {
			fmt.Printf("GT objects: %d\n", k)
			break
		}
		total++
		if k >= len(objs) {
			fmt.Printf("obj%d: missing from decode\n", k)
			badObjects++
			continue
		}
		o := objs[k]
		gtCount := wram[0x2400-0x2000+st]
		want := int(gtCount) + 1
		if len(o.Chips) != want {
			fmt.Printf("obj%d: chip count dec=%d gt=%d\n", k, len(o.Chips), want)
			badObjects++
			continue
		}
		bad := 0
		p := 0x2400 - 0x2000 + st + 1
		for i, c := range o.Chips {
			lo := wram[p]
			pal := wram[p+1]
			pos := wram[p+2]
			gx, gy := int(pos>>4), int(pos&0xF)
			decLo := c.Word & 0xFF
			decPal := c.Word >> 8
			if int(lo) != decLo || int(pal) != decPal || gx != c.X || gy != c.Y {
				if bad == 0 {
					fmt.Printf("obj%d chip%d: dec=(lo %#02x pal %#02x, %d,%d) gt=(lo %#02x pal %#02x, %d,%d)\n",
						k, i, decLo, decPal, c.X, c.Y, lo, pal, gx, gy)
				}
				bad++
			}
			p += 3
		}
		if bad == 0 {
			matched++
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("obj%d: %d/%d chips differ\n", k, bad, len(o.Chips))
			badObjects++
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("objects %d decoded; gt %d; fully matched %d; bad %d\n",
		len(objs), total, matched, badObjects)
	if len(objs) == total && badObjects == 0 {
		fmt.Println("VERIFY PASS")
	} else {
		fmt.Println("VERIFY FAIL")
	}
	return nil
}

func writeIndex(rom mapfmt.ROM, outdir string) error {
	path := filepath.Join(outdir, "index.tsv")
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	if _, err := fmt.Fprintln(f, "id\tdataOffset\tflags1\tlayer1\tlayer2\tprop\tchipset\tpaletteSet\tobjectConfig\tposX\tposY\tsizeX\tsizeY\tnameID"); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for id := 0; id < 1024; id++ {
		off, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(rom, id)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		h, err := mapfmt.ReadHeader(rom, off)
		if err != nil {
			// Zeroed entries (maps removed by the patch) are expected.
			continue
		}
		line := fmt.Sprintf("%#04x\t%#08x\t%#04x\t%#08x\t%#08x\t%#08x\t%#04x\t%#04x\t%#04x\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%#04x",
			id, off, h.Flags1, h.Layer1, h.Layer2, h.Prop,
			h.Chipset, h.PaletteSet, h.ObjectConfig,
			h.PosX, h.PosY, h.SizeX, h.SizeY, h.NameID)
		if _, err := fmt.Fprintln(f, line); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("wrote %s\n", path)
	return nil
}

// compareScreenshot renders submap id and searches the rendered map for
// the 32x28-tile window that best matches an emulator screenshot
// (256x224 px, tile-by-tile mean-RGB distance, robust trimmed score that
// ignores sprite-covered tiles). Prints alignment and match statistics.
// With diffPath set, writes a side-by-side PNG (screenshot left, the
// matched render window right) for eyeballing which tiles differ.
func compareScreenshot(rom mapfmt.ROM, id int, shotPath, diffPath string) error {
	rendered, err := mapfmt.RenderSubmap(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	f, err := os.Open(shotPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	shot, err := png.Decode(f)
	f.Close()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("decode %s: %w", shotPath, err)
	}
	const tw, th = 32, 28 // visible tiles on a 256x224 SNES screen
	if shot.Bounds().Dx() != tw*8 || shot.Bounds().Dy() != th*8 {
		return fmt.Errorf("screenshot %s is %dx%d, want 256x224", shotPath, shot.Bounds().Dx(), shot.Bounds().Dy())
	}
	// per-tile mean RGB of the screenshot
	means := make([][3]float64, tw*th)
	for ty := 0; ty < th; ty++ {
		for tx := 0; tx < tw; tx++ {
			var r, g, b float64
			for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
					rr, gg, bb, _ := shot.At(tx*8+x, ty*8+y).RGBA()
					r += float64(rr >> 8)
					g += float64(gg >> 8)
					b += float64(bb >> 8)
				}
			}
			means[ty*tw+tx] = [3]float64{r / 64, g / 64, b / 64}
		}
	}
	// per-tile mean RGB of the render
	rm := rendered.Image
	rmean := func(tx, ty int) [3]float64 {
		var r, g, b float64
		for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
				rr, gg, bb, _ := rm.At(tx*8+x, ty*8+y).RGBA()
				r += float64(rr >> 8)
				g += float64(gg >> 8)
				b += float64(bb >> 8)
			}
		}
		return [3]float64{r / 64, g / 64, b / 64}
	}
	best := struct {
		tx, ty int
		score  float64
		match  int
	}{score: 1e18}
	for oy := 0; oy+th <= rendered.Height; oy++ {
		for ox := 0; ox+tw <= rendered.Width; ox++ {
			var total float64
			match := 0
			dists := make([]float64, 0, tw*th)
			for ty := 0; ty < th; ty++ {
				for tx := 0; tx < tw; tx++ {
					m := rmean(ox+tx, oy+ty)
					s := means[ty*tw+tx]
					d := abs(m[0]-s[0]) + abs(m[1]-s[1]) + abs(m[2]-s[2])
					dists = append(dists, d)
					total += d
				}
			}
			// trimmed: drop worst 25% of tiles (sprites, windows, HUD)
			sort.Float64s(dists)
			trimmed := 0.0
			kept := int(float64(len(dists)) * 0.75)
			for i := 0; i < kept; i++ {
				trimmed += dists[i]
			}
			trimmed /= float64(kept)
			for _, d := range dists {
				if d < 90 {
					match++
				}
			}
			if trimmed < best.score {
				best = struct {
					tx, ty int
					score  float64
					match  int
				}{ox, oy, trimmed, match}
			}
			_ = total
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("best window at tile (%d,%d): trimmed mean tile distance %.1f, tiles under threshold %d/%d (%.0f%%)\n",
		best.tx, best.ty, best.score, best.match, tw*th, 100*float64(best.match)/(tw*th))
	if diffPath != "" {
		side := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, tw*8*2+8, th*8))
		for y := 0; y < th*8; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < tw*8; x++ {
				side.Set(x, y, shot.At(x, y))
				side.Set(x+tw*8+8, y, rm.At((best.tx)*8+x, (best.ty)*8+y))
			}
		}
		df, err := os.Create(diffPath)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", diffPath, err)
		}
		err = png.Encode(df, side)
		closeErr := df.Close()
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", diffPath, err)
		}
		if closeErr != nil {
			return closeErr
		}
		fmt.Printf("wrote %s (screenshot | matched window)\n", diffPath)
	}
	return nil
}

func abs(x float64) float64 {
	if x < 0 {
		return -x
	}
	return x
}
```

`cmd/dumpnames/main.go`:

```go
// Command dumpnames extracts the ROM's name tables (actors, items, and the
// other indexed string tables) with decoded Japanese.
//
// Usage: dumpnames <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <outdir>
//
//	dumpnames <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and the glyph
// assignment to data/glyphs_jp.json.
//
// Table addresses come from rs3_runtime_text_v30 (FD:1480 actor names,
// FD:0280 items, ...). Records are NUL/fullwidth-space terminated with
// two-byte glyphs for lead bytes below 0x50 (C0:3126/3222/3309 semantics).
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

type table struct {
	file   string // output base name
	offset int
	stride int
	count  int
	note   string
}

var tables = []table{
	{"actors", 0x3d1480, 8, 256, "actor names (4A 39 4F_2F)"},
	{"items", 0x3d0280, 8, 256, "item names (3A)"},
	{"table_11", 0x3d1dc0, 10, 256, "4F_11 table"},
	{"table_12", 0x3d0a80, 8, 256, "4F_12 table"},
	{"table_14", 0x3d0000, 10, 256, "4F_14 table"},
	{"table_15", 0x3d1c80, 10, 256, "4F_15 table"},
	{"tech_names", 0x3d27c0, 10, 256, "TECH NAME table (256x10; formerly mislabeled 12-bit item names — the tech agent verified adjacency to 敵技名称 at 0x3D2EC0). The 4F_13 4096-entry item table location is an open question."},
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROMGlyphs(os.Args[1:], "usage: dumpnames <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <outdir>\n"+
		"   or: dumpnames <outdir>\n"+
		"   (defaults: rom patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, glyphs data/glyphs_jp.json)")
	romPath, glyphPath, outDir := args[0], args[1], args[2]
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(glyphPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	dec := bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot)

	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	for _, t := range tables {
		f, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(outDir, t.file+".txt"))
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(f, "# %s  file 0x%06x  %d x %d B  (%s)\n", t.file, t.offset, t.count, t.stride, t.note)
		var unmapped int
		for i := 0; i < t.count; i++ {
			start := t.offset + i*t.stride
			rec := recordBytes(rom, start, t.stride)
			d := dec.DecodeBuffer(rec)
			unmapped += d.Issues
			label := fmt.Sprintf("%3d %s", i, d.Text)
			if d.Issues > 0 {
				label += fmt.Sprintf("  [%d unmapped]", d.Issues)
			}
			fmt.Fprintln(f, label)
		}
		f.Close()
		fmt.Printf("%s: %d entries, %d unmapped glyphs\n", t.file, t.count, unmapped)
	}
}

// recordBytes returns the bytes of one record, stopping at the terminator
// (0x00 or 0x50) or the stride limit; a lead byte below 0x50 always copies
// one more byte, even at the nominal record edge.
func recordBytes(rom []byte, start, limit int) []byte {
	var out []byte
	for i := 0; i < limit && start+i < len(rom); i++ {
		b := rom[start+i]
		if b == 0x00 || b == 0x50 {
			break
		}
		out = append(out, b)
		if b < 0x50 && start+i+1 < len(rom) {
			out = append(out, rom[start+i+1])
			i++
		}
	}
	return out
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumpsprites/capture.go`:

```go
package main

// Capture-mode figure extraction: reassembled MesenCE dump directories
// (tools/emulator/oam_reassemble.py layout: cap_<frame>_oam.bin,
// cap_<frame>_vram.bin, cap_<frame>_cgram.bin, cap_<frame>_shot.bin)
// carry the frame-end OAM, VRAM and CGRAM of standing-walk instants.
// This file composites the OAM sprite layer (the composed walking
// figures, palette indices + per-pixel subpalette) and exports each
// figure as a 16x24 PNG for the Godot map view (exports/data/walk_sprites,
// gitignored). The composed figure exists only in VRAM/OAM at runtime —
// never in ROM (docs/sprites.md) — so the capture is the only truthful
// source for the party figure.

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

const (
	screenW = 256
	screenH = 224
)

type spr struct {
	y, x, tile, attr int
	size             bool
}

func parseOAM(oam []byte) []spr {
	out := make([]spr, 128)
	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		y, x, t, a := int(oam[i*4]), int(oam[i*4+1]), int(oam[i*4+2]), int(oam[i*4+3])
		up := oam[512+i/4]
		xmsb := int(up>>(i%4*2+1)) & 1
		size := up>>(i%4*2)&1 == 1
		tile := (a&1)<<8 | t
		out[i] = spr{y: y, x: x | xmsb<<8, tile: tile, attr: a, size: size}
	}
	return out
}

func visibleS(s spr) bool { return s.y < 0xE0 && s.x < 0x100 }

func w8b(v byte, bit int) int {
	if v&(1<<bit) != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// tilePixels decodes one 4bpp tile (32 bytes) to 64 palette indices.
func tilePixels(b []byte) []byte {
	px := make([]byte, 64)
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		b0, b1, b2, b3 := b[y], b[y+8], b[y+16], b[y+24]
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			bit := 7 - x
			px[y*8+x] = byte(w8b(b0, bit) | w8b(b1, bit)<<1 | w8b(b2, bit)<<2 | w8b(b3, bit)<<3)
		}
	}
	return px
}

// spritePixels returns the sprite's palette indices at (dx, dy) inside its
// box, PPU flips applied. 8x8 or 16x16 per the size bit; tiles grid order
// left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
func spritePixels(s spr, vram []byte) ([]byte, int, int) {
	w := 8
	if s.size {
		w = 16
	}
	px := make([]byte, w*w)
	for r := 0; r < w/8; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < w/8; c++ {
			idx := s.tile + r*2 + c
			off := idx * 32
			if off+32 > len(vram) {
				continue
			}
			t := tilePixels(vram[off : off+32])
			for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
					dx, dy := c*8+x, r*8+y
					if s.attr&0x40 != 0 {
						dx = w - 1 - dx
					}
					if s.attr&0x80 != 0 {
						dy = w - 1 - dy
					}
					px[dy*w+dx] = t[y*8+x]
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return px, w, w
}

// layer is the composited sprite canvas: palette index and OAM subpalette
// per pixel, lower OAM index on top (as the PPU prioritizes).
type layer struct {
	idx     []byte // 4bpp palette index, 0 = transparent
	pal     []byte // OAM subpalette 0-7 per pixel
	touched []bool
}

func composite(sps []spr, vram []byte) *layer {
	l := &layer{
		idx:     make([]byte, screenW*screenH),
		pal:     make([]byte, screenW*screenH),
		touched: make([]bool, screenW*screenH),
	}
	for i := 127; i >= 0; i-- {
		s := sps[i]
		if !visibleS(s) {
			continue
		}
		px, w, _ := spritePixels(s, vram)
		pal := s.attr >> 1 & 7
		for y := 0; y < w; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				v := px[y*w+x]
				if v == 0 {
					continue
				}
				sx, sy := s.x+x, s.y+y
				if sx < screenW && sy < screenH {
					o := sy*screenW + sx
					l.idx[o] = v
					l.pal[o] = byte(pal)
					l.touched[o] = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return l
}

// cgramColors converts the full 512-byte CGRAM dump into 256 RGBA colors.
func cgramColors(cg []byte) ([256]color.RGBA, error) {
	var out [256]color.RGBA
	if len(cg) != 512 {
		return out, fmt.Errorf("cgram: %d bytes, want 512", len(cg))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		w := int(cg[i*2]) | int(cg[i*2+1])<<8
		out[i] = color.RGBA{
			R: byte((w & 31) << 3),
			G: byte((w >> 5 & 31) << 3),
			B: byte((w >> 10 & 31) << 3),
			A: 255,
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// renderPNG colorizes the sprite layer over transparency.
func renderPNG(l *layer, colors [256]color.RGBA) *image.RGBA {
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, screenW, screenH))
	for y := 0; y < screenH; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < screenW; x++ {
			o := y*screenW + x
			if !l.touched[o] || l.idx[o] == 0 {
				continue
			}
			img.SetRGBA(x, y, colors[int(l.pal[o])*16+int(l.idx[o])])
		}
	}
	return img
}

// figures splits the sprite layer into connected components (8-neighbours,
// gaps of one transparent pixel bridged) and returns the bounding boxes of
// figure-sized ones (12..20 x 18..30 px — the composed 16x24 walk figure
// and its ±1 px draw rounding).
func figures(l *layer) []image.Rectangle {
	seen := make([]bool, screenW*screenH)
	var boxes []image.Rectangle
	for sy := 0; sy < screenH; sy++ {
		for sx := 0; sx < screenW; sx++ {
			o := sy*screenW + sx
			if seen[o] || !l.touched[o] || l.idx[o] == 0 {
				continue
			}
			// BFS with a one-pixel bridge tolerance
			minX, minY, maxX, maxY := sx, sy, sx, sy
			type pt struct{ x, y int }
			stack := []pt{{sx, sy}}
			seen[o] = true
			for len(stack) > 0 {
				p := stack[len(stack)-1]
				stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
				for dy := -1; dy <= 1; dy++ {
					for dx := -1; dx <= 1; dx++ {
						nx, ny := p.x+dx, p.y+dy
						if nx < 0 || ny < 0 || nx >= screenW || ny >= screenH {
							continue
						}
						no := ny*screenW + nx
						if seen[no] || !l.touched[no] || l.idx[no] == 0 {
							continue
						}
						seen[no] = true
						stack = append(stack, pt{nx, ny})
						if nx < minX {
							minX = nx
						}
						if nx > maxX {
							maxX = nx
						}
						if ny < minY {
							minY = ny
						}
						if ny > maxY {
							maxY = ny
						}
					}
				}
			}
			w, h := maxX-minX+1, maxY-minY+1
			if w >= 12 && w <= 20 && h >= 18 && h <= 30 {
				boxes = append(boxes, image.Rect(minX, minY, maxX+1, maxY+1))
			}
		}
	}
	return boxes
}

// runFigures extracts walk figures from reassembled dumps: one output PNG
// per figure-sized component per frame, plus the full sprite layer for
// visual validation against the capture's screenshot.
// ids: list of "frame[:name]" tokens; name names the figure (output
// walk_sprites/<name>/<facing-from-name>.png when it looks like a name).
func runFigures(dumpDir, outDir string, tokens []string) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, tok := range tokens {
		parts := strings.SplitN(tok, ":", 2)
		frame := parts[0]
		name := ""
		if len(parts) == 2 {
			name = parts[1]
		}
		oam, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frame+"_oam.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", frame, err)
		}
		vram, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frame+"_vram.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", frame, err)
		}
		cg, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frame+"_cgram.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", frame, err)
		}
		colors, err := cgramColors(cg)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", frame, err)
		}
		l := composite(parseOAM(oam), vram)
		full := renderPNG(l, colors)
		// full layer, scaled 4x, for visual validation
		dbg := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, screenW*4, screenH*4))
		for y := 0; y < screenH; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < screenW; x++ {
				c := full.RGBAAt(x, y)
				for dy := 0; dy < 4; dy++ {
					for dx := 0; dx < 4; dx++ {
						dbg.SetRGBA(x*4+dx, y*4+dy, c)
					}
				}
			}
		}
		dbgPath := filepath.Join(outDir, "layer_"+frame+".png")
		if err := writePNG(dbgPath, dbg); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		for i, box := range figures(l) {
			out := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, box.Dx(), box.Dy()))
			for y := 0; y < box.Dy(); y++ {
				for x := 0; x < box.Dx(); x++ {
					out.SetRGBA(x, y, full.RGBAAt(box.Min.X+x, box.Min.Y+y))
				}
			}
			suffix := strconv.Itoa(i)
			if name != "" {
				suffix = name
			}
			path := filepath.Join(outDir, fmt.Sprintf("fig_%s_%s.png", frame, suffix))
			if err := writePNG(path, out); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Printf("figure %s: box %s -> %s\n", frame, box.String(), path)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func writePNG(path string, img image.Image) error {
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	return png.Encode(f, img)
}
```

`cmd/dumpsprites/main.go`:

```go
// dumpsprites renders Romancing SaGa 3 submap walking-character sprites
// from a patched ExHiROM SFC image.
//
// Usage: dumpsprites <rom> <outdir> [id ...]
//
//	dumpsprites <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc.
//
// The outdir receives one PNG per character graphic: its seven 24x24
// blocks in a grid (one row per block) over a magenta transparent
// background, with hairline grid lines separating the 24x8 bands.
// Without extra arguments a fixed set of townsfolk graphic IDs is
// rendered; further IDs select entries from the character graphic table
// at file offset 0x5A8370 (docs/sprites.md).
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"

	"saga3/internal/sprites"
)

// defaultIDs are graphic table entries whose blobs decode as raw
// townsfolk sprites; all were verified visually.
var defaultIDs = []int{0x96, 0x97, 0x2F, 0x80, 0x62, 0x6A, 0x54, 0x32}

const defaultROMPath = "patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"

// background marks transparent pixels.
var background = color.RGBA{R: 255, A: 255, B: 255}

// grid marks block and band boundaries.
var grid = color.RGBA{R: 200, G: 200, B: 200, A: 255}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "orig" {
		// orig <rom> <outdir> <id>... renders original-table ($F9A000)
		// entries, the source the resolver reads for ids < 0x70.
		if len(os.Args) < 4 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpsprites orig <rom> <outdir> <id>...")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if err := runOrig(os.Args[2], os.Args[3], os.Args[4:]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites orig:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "shotfig" {
		// shotfig <maprender.png> <dumpdir> <outdir> <frame:name>...
		if len(os.Args) < 6 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpsprites shotfig <maprender.png> <dumpdir> <outdir> <frame[:name]>...")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if err := shotFig(os.Args[3], os.Args[4], os.Args[2], os.Args[5:]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites shotfig:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "pair" {
		// pair <dumpdir> <outdir> <maprender.png> <A:B[:name]>...
		if len(os.Args) < 6 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpsprites pair <dumpdir> <outdir> <A:B[:name]>...")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if err := pairFig(os.Args[2], os.Args[3], os.Args[4], os.Args[5:]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites pair:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "cropfig" {
		// cropfig <dumpdir> <frame> <out.png> <x> <y> <w> <h>
		if len(os.Args) != 9 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpsprites cropfig <dumpdir> <frame> <out.png> <x> <y> <w> <h>")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		nums := make([]int, 4)
		for i, a := range os.Args[5:9] {
			v, err := strconv.Atoi(a)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites cropfig:", err)
				os.Exit(2)
			}
			nums[i] = v
		}
		if err := cropFig(os.Args[2], os.Args[4], os.Args[3], nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], nums[3]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites cropfig:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 2 && os.Args[1] == "figures" {
		// figures <dumpdir> <outdir> <frame[:name]>...
		if len(os.Args) < 5 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpsprites figures <dumpdir> <outdir> <frame[:name]>...")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if err := runFigures(os.Args[2], os.Args[3], os.Args[4:]); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites figures:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumpsprites <rom> <outdir> [id ...]\n"+
			"   or: dumpsprites <outdir>   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)\n"+
			"   or: dumpsprites figures <dumpdir> <outdir> <frame[:name]>...")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	args := os.Args[1:]
	romPath, outdir := args[0], ""
	if len(args) == 1 { // short form: ROM takes the default
		romPath = defaultROMPath
		outdir = args[0]
	} else {
		outdir = args[1]
	}
	ids := defaultIDs
	if len(args) > 2 {
		ids = nil
		for _, arg := range args[2:] {
			id, err := strconv.ParseInt(arg, 0, 32)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites: bad id %q\n", arg)
				os.Exit(2)
			}
			ids = append(ids, int(id))
		}
	}
	if err := run(romPath, outdir, ids); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func run(romPath, outdir string, ids []int) error {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read ROM: %w", err)
	}
	rom := sprites.ROM(data)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outdir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create outdir: %w", err)
	}
	decoded, skipped := 0, 0
	for _, id := range ids {
		if err := writeSheet(rom, outdir, id); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dumpsprites: skip id %#04x: %v\n", id, err)
			skipped++
			continue
		}
		decoded++
	}
	fmt.Printf("rendered %d characters, skipped %d -> %s\n", decoded, skipped, outdir)
	return nil
}

// writeSheet renders graphic id's seven 24x24 blocks into one PNG, one
// block per row, with grid lines on the 24x8 band boundaries.
func writeSheet(rom sprites.ROM, outdir string, id int) error {
	e, err := sprites.TableEntry(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if e.Offset < 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("entry absent (table row zeroed)")
	}
	pal, err := sprites.LoadPalette(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return writeSheetOff(rom, outdir, fmt.Sprintf("char%02x", id), e.Offset, pal)
}

// writeSheetOff renders the seven 24x24 walk-figure blocks at file
// offset off into outdir/<name>.png with the given palette.
func writeSheetOff(rom sprites.ROM, outdir, name string, off int, pal sprites.Palette) error {
	frames, err := sprites.Frames(rom, off)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	const scale = 4
	const cell = 2 // gap between blocks
	w := (24*scale + cell) + cell
	h := (24*scale+cell)*len(frames) + cell
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, w, h))
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			img.Set(x, y, background)
		}
	}
	for i, fr := range frames {
		fx := cell
		fy := cell + i*(24*scale+cell)
		for py := 0; py < 24; py++ {
			for px := 0; px < 24; px++ {
				v := fr.Pixels[py*24+px]
				if v == 0 {
					continue
				}
				c := pal.Colors[v]
				rgba := color.RGBA{R: c[0], G: c[1], B: c[2], A: 255}
				for sy := 0; sy < scale; sy++ {
					for sx := 0; sx < scale; sx++ {
						img.Set(fx+px*scale+sx, fy+py*scale+sy, rgba)
					}
				}
			}
		}
		// band grid lines
		for _, b := range []int{8, 16} {
			for x := 0; x < 24*scale; x++ {
				img.Set(fx+x, fy+b*scale, grid)
			}
		}
	}
	path := filepath.Join(outdir, name+".png")
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	defer f.Close()
	if err := png.Encode(f, img); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

`cmd/dumpsprites/orig.go`:

```go
package main

// Original-table sheet rendering: the walking-character resolver
// (C4:FF60, docs/sprites.md) reads the original RS3 table at SNES
// $F9A000 (file 0x39A000) for engine graphic ids < 0x70, with the same
// 4-byte entry layout as the patch table. Its pointers are packed:
// SNES address = ((byte1 & 0x1F) + 0xDA) << 16 | (word & 0xFFE0).
// The palette source for these ids is unsettled (docs/sprites.md): the
// pool directly before $F9A000 rendered implausible colors, so
// origPalette falls back to the patch-table pool by the same id.

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"

	"saga3/internal/sprites"
)

// runOrig renders one sheet per original-table id into outdir.
func runOrig(romPath, outdir string, args []string) error {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read ROM: %w", err)
	}
	rom := sprites.ROM(data)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outdir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create outdir: %w", err)
	}
	for _, arg := range args {
		id, err := strconv.ParseInt(arg, 0, 32)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("bad id %q: %w", arg, err)
		}
		kind, off, err := origEntry(rom, int(id))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if off < 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("original table entry %d is absent", id)
		}
		pal, err := origPalette(rom, int(id))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "orig id %#x: kind %02x file %06X\n", id, kind, off)
		// writeSheet renders the seven 24x24 blocks at a file offset.
		if err := writeSheetOff(rom, outdir, fmt.Sprintf("orig%02x", id), off, pal); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

const origTableFile = 0x39A000

// origEntry decodes one original-table row into kind and file offset.
func origEntry(rom sprites.ROM, id int) (kind byte, off int, err error) {
	base := origTableFile + id*4
	if base+4 > len(rom) {
		return 0, -1, fmt.Errorf("original table entry %d: outside ROM", id)
	}
	kind = rom[base]
	lo := int(rom[base+1]) | int(rom[base+2])<<8
	bank := (int(kind)&0x1F + 0xDA) << 16
	addr := bank | lo&0xFFE0
	off, err = rom.ToFile(addr)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, -1, fmt.Errorf("original table entry %d: %w", id, err)
	}
	return kind, off, nil
}

// origPalette reads the original-table pool palette for id.
func origPalette(rom sprites.ROM, id int) (sprites.Palette, error) {
	// The pool directly before $F9A000 rendered implausible colors; the
	// patch-table pool by the same id is the better candidate so far.
	return sprites.LoadPalette(rom, id)
}
```
