`cmd/dumpsprites/shotfig.go`:

```go
package main

// Shot-mode figure extraction: the field party's figure never appears in
// ROM or in render-truthful VRAM dumps (docs/sprites.md), but the PNG
// screenshots are ground truth, and the map render (exports/data/maps/
// <id>/map.png, verified against emulator frames) gives the exact
// background under the party. This file aligns a screenshot to the map
// render, diffs out the background, and exports each figure-sized
// component as a transparent RGBA PNG for the Godot map view.

import (
	"image/png"

	"fmt"
	"image"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"image/color"
)

// shotFig extracts figures from one screenshot against one map render.
// token: <frame>:<name>, with files cap_<frame>_shot.bin in dumpDir and
// the map render given as an absolute path.
func shotFig(dumpDir, outDir, mapPath string, tokens []string) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	mr, err := loadMapRender(mapPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("map render: %w", err)
	}
	for _, tok := range tokens {
		parts := strings.SplitN(tok, ":", 2)
		frame, name := parts[0], ""
		if len(parts) == 2 {
			name = parts[1]
		}
		shotPath := filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frame+"_shot.bin")
		shot, err := loadImage(shotPath)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", frame, err)
		}
		ox, oy, err := align(shot, mr)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", frame, err)
		}
		fmt.Printf("frame %s: scroll (%d,%d)\n", frame, ox, oy)
		boxes, crops := figureTiles(shot, mr, ox, oy)
		for i, b := range boxes {
			suffix := name
			if suffix == "" {
				suffix = strconv.Itoa(b.Min.X) + "_" + strconv.Itoa(b.Min.Y)
			}
			path := filepath.Join(outDir, fmt.Sprintf("fig_%s_%s.png", frame, suffix))
			if err := writePNG(path, crops[i]); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Printf("figure %s: box %s -> %s\n", frame, b.String(), path)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// figureTiles finds figure components at tile granularity and returns
// their bounding boxes plus transparent RGBA crops from the screenshot.
// A 16x16 tile is "strong" when more than a third of its pixels differ
// strongly from the background (animated ground and dither noise stay
// under that); figures are 1-2 x 2 tile clusters of strong tiles.
func figureTiles(shot, mr *image.RGBA, ox, oy int) ([]image.Rectangle, []*image.RGBA) {
	const strongAt = 48
	const weakAt = 30
	w, h := shot.Bounds().Dx(), shot.Bounds().Dy()
	strong := make([]int, w*h)
	tw, th := w/16, h/16
	var tstamp []bool = make([]bool, tw*th)
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			s := shot.RGBAAt(x, y)
			m := mr.RGBAAt(ox+x, oy+y)
			d := func(a, b uint8) int {
				v := int(a) - int(b)
				if v < 0 {
					return -v
				}
				return v
			}
			t := d(s.R, m.R) + d(s.G, m.G) + d(s.B, m.B)
			if t >= strongAt {
				strong[y*w+x] = 1
			}
		}
	}
	for ty := 0; ty < th; ty++ {
		for tx := 0; tx < tw; tx++ {
			n := 0
			for y := ty * 16; y < ty*16+16; y++ {
				for x := tx * 16; x < tx*16+16; x++ {
					n += strong[y*w+x]
				}
			}
			tstamp[ty*tw+tx] = n > 85
		}
	}
	// tile components (4-neighbours)
	seen := make([]bool, tw*th)
	type pt struct{ x, y int }
	var boxes []image.Rectangle
	var crops []*image.RGBA
	for sy := 0; sy < th; sy++ {
		for sx := 0; sx < tw; sx++ {
			o := sy*tw + sx
			if seen[o] || !tstamp[o] {
				continue
			}
			var tiles []pt
			stack := []pt{{sx, sy}}
			seen[o] = true
			for len(stack) > 0 {
				p := stack[len(stack)-1]
				stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
				tiles = append(tiles, p)
				for _, d := range []pt{{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}} {
					nx, ny := p.x+d.x, p.y+d.y
					if nx < 0 || ny < 0 || nx >= tw || ny >= th {
						continue
					}
					no := ny*tw + nx
					if seen[no] || !tstamp[no] {
						continue
					}
					seen[no] = true
					stack = append(stack, pt{nx, ny})
				}
			}
			minX, minY, maxX, maxY := tw, th, -1, -1
			covered := map[pt]bool{}
			for _, t := range tiles {
				covered[t] = true
				if t.x < minX {
					minX = t.x
				}
				if t.x > maxX {
					maxX = t.x
				}
				if t.y < minY {
					minY = t.y
				}
				if t.y > maxY {
					maxY = t.y
				}
			}
			if maxX-minX+1 > 4 || maxY-minY+1 > 4 {
				continue // figures never span more than ~3x3 tiles
			}
			// crop pixels: weak diff inside the covered tiles, plus
			// hole-filling: any pixel within the bbox whose 4-neighbours
			// are all sprite joins the sprite (a figure pixel equal to the
			// background colour would otherwise punch holes).
			bx0, by0, bx1, by1 := minX*16, minY*16, (maxX+1)*16, (maxY+1)*16
			crop := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, bx1-bx0, by1-by0))
			cw := bx1 - bx0
			sel := make([]bool, cw*(by1-by0))
			for y := by0; y < by1; y++ {
				for x := bx0; x < bx1; x++ {
					tile := covered[pt{x / 16, y / 16}]
					if !tile {
						continue
					}
					s := shot.RGBAAt(x, y)
					m := mr.RGBAAt(ox+x, oy+y)
					d := func(a, b uint8) int {
						v := int(a) - int(b)
						if v < 0 {
							return -v
						}
						return v
					}
					if d(s.R, m.R)+d(s.G, m.G)+d(s.B, m.B) >= weakAt {
						sel[(y-by0)*cw+(x-bx0)] = true
					}
				}
			}
			// hole fill: 3 passes of "surrounded on 3 of 4 sides"
			for pass := 0; pass < 3; pass++ {
				for y := 1; y < by1-by0-1; y++ {
					for x := 1; x < cw-1; x++ {
						if sel[y*cw+x] {
							continue
						}
						n := 0
						if sel[y*cw+x-1] {
							n++
						}
						if sel[y*cw+x+1] {
							n++
						}
						if sel[(y-1)*cw+x] {
							n++
						}
						if sel[(y+1)*cw+x] {
							n++
						}
						if n >= 3 {
							sel[y*cw+x] = true
						}
					}
				}
			}
			for y := 0; y < by1-by0; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < cw; x++ {
					if sel[y*cw+x] {
						crop.SetRGBA(x, y, shot.RGBAAt(bx0+x, by0+y))
					}
				}
			}
			boxes = append(boxes, image.Rect(bx0, by0, bx1, by1))
			crops = append(crops, crop)
		}
	}
	return boxes, crops
}

// loadMapRender loads a map render (8 px per tile) scaled 2x with
// nearest-neighbour resampling. Screenshots are 16 px per tile; every
// comparison below runs in screenshot pixels, so the render must be in
// the same scale. The unscaled render silently misaligned everything
// (walkfig's leader export never noticed: pair mode only uses the scroll
// delta between two shots, which cancels the error).
func loadMapRender(path string) (*image.RGBA, error) {
	img, err := loadImage(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return upscale2x(img), nil
}

// upscale2x doubles img with nearest-neighbour resampling.
func upscale2x(img *image.RGBA) *image.RGBA {
	b := img.Bounds()
	out := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, b.Dx()*2, b.Dy()*2))
	for y := 0; y < out.Bounds().Dy(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < out.Bounds().Dx(); x++ {
			out.SetRGBA(x, y, img.RGBAAt(b.Min.X+x/2, b.Min.Y+y/2))
		}
	}
	return out
}

func loadImage(path string) (*image.RGBA, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	img, err := png.Decode(f)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	out := image.NewRGBA(img.Bounds())
	for y := img.Bounds().Min.Y; y < img.Bounds().Max.Y; y++ {
		for x := img.Bounds().Min.X; x < img.Bounds().Max.X; x++ {
			out.SetRGBA(x-img.Bounds().Min.X, y-img.Bounds().Min.Y, img.At(x, y).(color.RGBA))
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// align finds the map-render offset where the screenshot's background
// matches best. The map render is 8 px per screen tile while the shot is
// 16, so the coarse pass scores a 2x-downsampled pair and a fine pass
// refines +-2 px at full resolution.
func align(shot, mr *image.RGBA) (int, int, error) {
	b := shot.Bounds()
	w, h := b.Dx(), b.Dy()
	small := downsample2x(shot)
	msmall := downsample2x(mr)
	sb := small.Bounds()
	sw, sh := sb.Dx(), sb.Dy()
	bestX, bestY, bestScore := -1, -1, int64(1)<<62
	for oy := 0; oy+sh <= msmall.Bounds().Dy(); oy++ {
		for ox := 0; ox+sw <= msmall.Bounds().Dx(); ox++ {
			var score int64
			for y := 0; y < sh; y += 2 {
				for x := 0; x < sw; x += 2 {
					score += diffScore(small.RGBAAt(sb.Min.X+x, sb.Min.Y+y),
						msmall.RGBAAt(ox+x, oy+y))
				}
			}
			if score < bestScore {
				bestScore, bestX, bestY = score, ox*2, oy*2
			}
		}
	}
	if bestX < 0 {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("no alignment found")
	}
	for fy := bestY - 2; fy <= bestY+2; fy++ {
		for fx := bestX - 2; fx <= bestX+2; fx++ {
			if fx < 0 || fy < 0 || fx+w > mr.Bounds().Dx() || fy+h > mr.Bounds().Dy() {
				continue
			}
			var score int64
			for y := 0; y < h; y += 2 {
				for x := 0; x < w; x += 2 {
					score += diffScore(shot.RGBAAt(b.Min.X+x, b.Min.Y+y),
						mr.RGBAAt(fx+x, fy+y))
				}
			}
			if score < bestScore {
				bestScore, bestX, bestY = score, fx, fy
			}
		}
	}
	return bestX, bestY, nil
}

func diffScore(s, m color.RGBA) int64 {
	dr := int(s.R) - int(m.R)
	dg := int(s.G) - int(m.G)
	db := int(s.B) - int(m.B)
	if dr < 0 {
		dr = -dr
	}
	if dg < 0 {
		dg = -dg
	}
	if db < 0 {
		db = -db
	}
	v := int64(dr + dg + db)
	if v > 60 {
		v = 60 // sprites are a bounded outlier, not a gradient
	}
	return v
}

// downsample2x halves the image, averaging each 2x2 block.
func downsample2x(img *image.RGBA) *image.RGBA {
	b := img.Bounds()
	out := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, (b.Dx()+1)/2, (b.Dy()+1)/2))
	for y := 0; y < out.Bounds().Dy(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < out.Bounds().Dx(); x++ {
			var r, g, bl, n int
			for dy := 0; dy < 2; dy++ {
				for dx := 0; dx < 2; dx++ {
					px := img.RGBAAt(b.Min.X+x*2+dx, b.Min.Y+y*2+dy)
					r += int(px.R)
					g += int(px.G)
					bl += int(px.B)
					n++
				}
			}
			out.SetRGBA(x, y, color.RGBA{byte(r / n), byte(g / n), byte(bl / n), 255})
		}
	}
	return out
}

// pairFig extracts figures from frame A using frame B as the background
// reference: both are standing shots on the same map, the camera scroll
// differs, and everything that is identical in map coordinates (ground,
// tree shadows, overlays the map render does not model) cancels out.
// Each frame is aligned to the map render first; the pixel comparison
// runs in map coordinates. Token format: A:B[:name]. mapPath is the map
// render PNG.
func pairFig(dumpDir, outDir, mapPath string, tokens []string) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	mr, err := loadMapRender(mapPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("map render: %w", err)
	}
	scrolls := map[string][2]int{}
	for _, tok := range tokens {
		for _, f := range strings.SplitN(tok, ":", 3)[:2] {
			if _, ok := scrolls[f]; ok {
				continue
			}
			shot, err := loadImage(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+f+"_shot.bin"))
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			ox, oy, err := align(shot, mr)
			if err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("frame %s: %w", f, err)
			}
			scrolls[f] = [2]int{ox, oy}
		}
	}
	for _, tok := range tokens {
		parts := strings.SplitN(tok, ":", 3)
		if len(parts) < 2 {
			return fmt.Errorf("bad token %q, want A:B[:name]", tok)
		}
		frameA, frameB := parts[0], parts[1]
		name := ""
		if len(parts) == 3 {
			name = parts[2]
		}
		a, err := loadImage(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frameA+"_shot.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		b, err := loadImage(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frameB+"_shot.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		sa, sb := scrolls[frameA], scrolls[frameB]
		dx, dy := sb[0]-sa[0], sb[1]-sa[1]
		fmt.Printf("pair %s vs %s: scroll A %v B %v delta (%d,%d)\n", frameA, frameB, sa, sb, dx, dy)
		// name "facing:x:y:w:h" cuts one explicit rect with background
		// transparency from frame B; figure extraction needs no rect then.
		if nums := strings.Split(name, ","); len(nums) == 5 {
			rect := make([]int, 4)
			for i := range rect {
				v, err := strconv.Atoi(nums[i+1])
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				rect[i] = v
			}
			crop := alphaRect(a, b, dx, dy, rect[0], rect[1], rect[2], rect[3])
			path := filepath.Join(outDir, fmt.Sprintf("fig_%s_%s.png", frameA, nums[0]))
			if err := writePNG(path, crop); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Printf("figure %s: rect %v -> %s\n", frameA, rect, path)
			continue
		}
		boxes, crops := figureTilesPair(a, b, dx, dy)
		for i, bx := range boxes {
			suffix := name
			if suffix == "" {
				suffix = strconv.Itoa(bx.Min.X) + "_" + strconv.Itoa(bx.Min.Y)
			}
			path := filepath.Join(outDir, fmt.Sprintf("fig_%s_%s.png", frameA, suffix))
			if err := writePNG(path, crops[i]); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Printf("figure %s: box %s -> %s\n", frameA, bx.String(), path)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// figureTilesPair is figureTiles with the background coming from the
// other screenshot, offset by the scroll delta (ox, oy).
func figureTilesPair(a, b *image.RGBA, ox, oy int) ([]image.Rectangle, []*image.RGBA) {
	const strongAt = 40
	const weakAt = 24
	w, h := a.Bounds().Dx(), a.Bounds().Dy()
	strong := make([]int, w*h)
	tw, th := w/16, h/16
	tstamp := make([]bool, tw*th)
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			s := a.RGBAAt(x, y)
			m := b.RGBAAt(clamp(ox+x, 0, b.Bounds().Dx()-1), clamp(oy+y, 0, b.Bounds().Dy()-1))
			d := func(p, q uint8) int {
				v := int(p) - int(q)
				if v < 0 {
					return -v
				}
				return v
			}
			if d(s.R, m.R)+d(s.G, m.G)+d(s.B, m.B) >= strongAt {
				strong[y*w+x] = 1
			}
		}
	}
	for ty := 0; ty < th; ty++ {
		for tx := 0; tx < tw; tx++ {
			n := 0
			for y := ty * 16; y < ty*16+16; y++ {
				for x := tx * 16; x < tx*16+16; x++ {
					n += strong[y*w+x]
				}
			}
			tstamp[ty*tw+tx] = n > 85
		}
	}
	seen := make([]bool, tw*th)
	type pt struct{ x, y int }
	var boxes []image.Rectangle
	var crops []*image.RGBA
	for sy := 0; sy < th; sy++ {
		for sx := 0; sx < tw; sx++ {
			o := sy*tw + sx
			if seen[o] || !tstamp[o] {
				continue
			}
			var tiles []pt
			stack := []pt{{sx, sy}}
			seen[o] = true
			for len(stack) > 0 {
				p := stack[len(stack)-1]
				stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
				tiles = append(tiles, p)
				for _, d := range []pt{{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}} {
					nx, ny := p.x+d.x, p.y+d.y
					if nx < 0 || ny < 0 || nx >= tw || ny >= th {
						continue
					}
					no := ny*tw + nx
					if seen[no] || !tstamp[no] {
						continue
					}
					seen[no] = true
					stack = append(stack, pt{nx, ny})
				}
			}
			minX, minY, maxX, maxY := tw, th, -1, -1
			covered := map[pt]bool{}
			for _, t := range tiles {
				covered[t] = true
				if t.x < minX {
					minX = t.x
				}
				if t.x > maxX {
					maxX = t.x
				}
				if t.y < minY {
					minY = t.y
				}
				if t.y > maxY {
					maxY = t.y
				}
			}
			if maxX-minX+1 > 4 || maxY-minY+1 > 4 {
				continue
			}
			bx0, by0, bx1, by1 := minX*16, minY*16, (maxX+1)*16, (maxY+1)*16
			crop := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, bx1-bx0, by1-by0))
			cw := bx1 - bx0
			sel := make([]bool, cw*(by1-by0))
			for y := by0; y < by1; y++ {
				for x := bx0; x < bx1; x++ {
					if !covered[pt{x / 16, y / 16}] {
						continue
					}
					s := a.RGBAAt(x, y)
					m := b.RGBAAt(clamp(ox+x, 0, b.Bounds().Dx()-1), clamp(oy+y, 0, b.Bounds().Dy()-1))
					d := func(p, q uint8) int {
						v := int(p) - int(q)
						if v < 0 {
							return -v
						}
						return v
					}
					if d(s.R, m.R)+d(s.G, m.G)+d(s.B, m.B) >= weakAt {
						sel[(y-by0)*cw+(x-bx0)] = true
					}
				}
			}
			for pass := 0; pass < 3; pass++ {
				for y := 1; y < by1-by0-1; y++ {
					for x := 1; x < cw-1; x++ {
						if sel[y*cw+x] {
							continue
						}
						n := 0
						if sel[y*cw+x-1] {
							n++
						}
						if sel[y*cw+x+1] {
							n++
						}
						if sel[(y-1)*cw+x] {
							n++
						}
						if sel[(y+1)*cw+x] {
							n++
						}
						if n >= 3 {
							sel[y*cw+x] = true
						}
					}
				}
			}
			for y := 0; y < by1-by0; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < cw; x++ {
					if sel[y*cw+x] {
						crop.SetRGBA(x, y, a.RGBAAt(bx0+x, by0+y))
					}
				}
			}
			boxes = append(boxes, image.Rect(bx0, by0, bx1, by1))
			crops = append(crops, crop)
		}
	}
	return boxes, crops
}

// alphaRect cuts one rect from frame A with background transparency: each
// pixel keeps its colour where it differs from frame B at the scroll delta
// (the moving figure), with the same 3-pass hole fill as figureTilesPair.
func alphaRect(a, b *image.RGBA, dx, dy, x, y, wd, ht int) *image.RGBA {
	crop := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, wd, ht))
	sel := make([]bool, wd*ht)
	bx := b.Bounds()
	for yy := 0; yy < ht; yy++ {
		for xx := 0; xx < wd; xx++ {
			s := a.RGBAAt(x+xx, y+yy)
			m := b.RGBAAt(clamp(x+xx+dx, bx.Min.X, bx.Max.X-1), clamp(y+yy+dy, bx.Min.Y, bx.Max.Y-1))
			d := func(p, q uint8) int {
				v := int(p) - int(q)
				if v < 0 {
					return -v
				}
				return v
			}
			if d(s.R, m.R)+d(s.G, m.G)+d(s.B, m.B) >= 24 {
				sel[yy*wd+xx] = true
			}
		}
	}
	for pass := 0; pass < 3; pass++ {
		for yy := 1; yy < ht-1; yy++ {
			for xx := 1; xx < wd-1; xx++ {
				if sel[yy*wd+xx] {
					continue
				}
				n := 0
				if sel[yy*wd+xx-1] {
					n++
				}
				if sel[yy*wd+xx+1] {
					n++
				}
				if sel[(yy-1)*wd+xx] {
					n++
				}
				if sel[(yy+1)*wd+xx] {
					n++
				}
				if n >= 3 {
					sel[yy*wd+xx] = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	for yy := 0; yy < ht; yy++ {
		for xx := 0; xx < wd; xx++ {
			if sel[yy*wd+xx] {
				crop.SetRGBA(xx, yy, a.RGBAAt(x+xx, y+yy))
			}
		}
	}
	return crop
}

func clamp(v, lo, hi int) int {
	if v < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if v > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return v
}

// cropFig cuts a rectangle from one capture screenshot: the final step
// that places an isolated figure (found via pair mode) into the Godot
// walk_sprites layout.
func cropFig(dumpDir, out string, frame string, x, y, wd, ht int) error {
	a, err := loadImage(filepath.Join(dumpDir, "cap_"+frame+"_shot.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	b := a.Bounds()
	if x < 0 || y < 0 || x+wd > b.Dx() || y+ht > b.Dy() {
		return fmt.Errorf("crop %d,%d %dx%d outside %dx%d shot", x, y, wd, ht, b.Dx(), b.Dy())
	}
	crop := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, wd, ht))
	for y2 := 0; y2 < ht; y2++ {
		for x2 := 0; x2 < wd; x2++ {
			crop.SetRGBA(x2, y2, a.RGBAAt(x+x2, y+y2))
		}
	}
	if err := writePNG(out, crop); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Printf("crop %s (%d,%d %dx%d) -> %s\n", frame, x, y, wd, ht, out)
	return nil
}

```

`cmd/dumpstatus/main.go`:

```go
// Command dumpstatus prints the 追加効果 (added-effect) evidence:
// the effect-setting table at 0x3FF200 and per-technique status-effect
// bytes for the tech, spell, and enemy-tech tables.
//
// Usage:
//
//	dumpstatus <rom> table              decode the 0x3FF200 effect table
//	dumpstatus <rom> techs|spells|enemies  list records with effect ids
//	dumpstatus table|techs|spells|enemies  the ROM defaults to
//	                                    patches/bokuno_jp.sfc
//
// Glyph decoding needs data/glyphs_jp.json, located next to the repo root
// that holds the ROM (the same lookup as cmd/dumpchars).
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/techs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 2, "usage: dumpstatus <rom> table|techs|spells|enemies\n"+
		"   or: dumpstatus table|techs|spells|enemies\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	ops, err := newTextOps(rom, args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	switch args[1] {
	case "table":
		dumpTable(rom)
	case "techs", "spells", "enemies":
		dumpRecords(rom, ops, args[1])
	default:
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "unknown mode:", args[1])
		os.Exit(2)
	}
}

func dumpTable(rom []byte) {
	for id := 0; id < techs.AddedEffectCount; id++ {
		eff, err := techs.AddedEffectAt(rom, byte(id))
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		if empty(eff) {
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("%02X spec=%02X[%s] st1=%02X[%s] st2=%02X[%s] down=%02X[%s] amt=%d up=%02X[%s]\n",
			id, eff.Species, speciesLabel(eff.Species),
			eff.Status1, bitsLabel(eff.Status1, techs.Status1Names),
			eff.Status2, bitsLabel(eff.Status2, techs.Status2Names),
			eff.StatDown, bitsLabel(eff.StatDown, techs.StatDownNames),
			eff.DownAmount, eff.StatUp, statUpLabel(eff.StatUp))
	}
}

func dumpRecords(rom []byte, ops *bokuno.Ops, which string) {
	label := map[string]string{"techs": "TECH", "spells": "SPELL", "enemies": "ETECH"}[which]
	for id := 0; id < techs.Count; id++ {
		var t techs.Technique
		var err error
		var nameBase int
		nameRec := func() ([]byte, error) { return nil, nil }
		switch which {
		case "techs":
			t, err = techs.TechAt(rom, uint16(id))
			nameBase = techs.TechNameOffset
			nameRec = func() ([]byte, error) { return techs.TechNameRecord(rom, uint16(id)) }
		case "spells":
			t, err = techs.SpellAt(rom, uint16(id))
			nameBase = techs.SpellNameOffset
			nameRec = func() ([]byte, error) { return techs.SpellNameRecord(rom, uint16(id)) }
		case "enemies":
			if id >= techs.ExtEnemyTechIDBase+techs.Count {
				continue
			}
			t, err = techs.EnemyTechAt(rom, uint16(id))
			nameBase = 0x3D31C0
			if id >= techs.ExtEnemyTechIDBase {
				nameBase = 0x5B40C0
			}
			nameRec = func() ([]byte, error) { return techs.NameRecord(rom, nameBase, uint16(id%techs.Count)) }
		}
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		name := "-"
		if rec, err := nameRec(); err == nil && len(rec) > 0 {
			name = ops.DecodeText(rec)
		}
		fmt.Printf("%s%03X eff=%02X set=%02X statuses=[%s] hit=%3d pow=%02X hits=%d grow=%d | %s\n",
			label, id, t.StatusEffect, t.SpecialSettings,
			statusesLabel(rom, t), t.HitRate, t.BasePower, t.HitCount, t.Growth, name)
	}
}

// statusesLabel decodes the applied statuses: the 技の性能 byte +3 indexes
// the 0x3FF200 table only when the 特殊設定 byte has bit 0x80.
func statusesLabel(rom []byte, t techs.Technique) string {
	if t.SpecialSettings&0x80 == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	eff, err := techs.AddedEffectAt(rom, t.StatusEffect)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Sprintf("?%02X", t.StatusEffect)
	}
	return bitsLabel(eff.Status1, techs.Status1Names)
}

func bitsLabel(v byte, names map[byte]string) string {
	if v == 0 {
		return "-"
	}
	s := ""
	for bit := byte(1); bit != 0; bit <<= 1 {
		if v&bit != 0 {
			if s != "" {
				s += "/"
			}
			if name, ok := names[bit]; ok {
				s += name
			} else {
				s += fmt.Sprintf("%02X", bit)
			}
		}
	}
	return s
}

func statUpLabel(v byte) string {
	s := bitsLabel(v&0xF8, techs.StatUpNames)
	if amt := int(v & 0x07); amt > 0 {
		if s != "" && s != "-" {
			s += "/"
		}
		s += fmt.Sprintf("x%d", amt*2)
	}
	if s == "" {
		return "-"
	}
	return s
}

func speciesLabel(v byte) string {
	s := bitsLabel(v&0xE0, techs.SpeciesFlags)
	if lo := v & 0x1F; lo != 0 {
		if s != "" && s != "-" {
			s = techs.SpeciesNames[lo] + "/" + s
		} else {
			s = techs.SpeciesNames[lo]
		}
	}
	if s == "" {
		return "-"
	}
	return s
}

func empty(e techs.AddedEffect) bool {
	return e.Species == 0 && e.Status1 == 0 && e.Status2 == 0 &&
		e.StatDown == 0 && e.DownAmount == 0 && e.StatUp == 0
}

// newTextOps locates data/glyphs_jp.json next to the repo root that holds
// the ROM (same lookup as cmd/dumpchars) and builds the text decoder.
func newTextOps(rom []byte, romPath string) (*bokuno.Ops, error) {
	paths := []string{
		filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(romPath)), "data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
		filepath.Join("data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
	}
	var raw []byte
	var err error
	for _, p := range paths {
		raw, err = os.ReadFile(p)
		if err == nil {
			break
		}
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ops := bokuno.NewOps(rom)
	ops.SetText(bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot))
	return ops, nil
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumptechs/main.go`:

```go
// Command dumptechs extracts the ROM's technique (技) and spell (術)
// tables into a readable dump, one entry per line.
//
// Usage: dumptechs <rom> <outdir>
//
//	dumptechs <outdir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc.
//
// It writes <outdir>/techs.txt and <outdir>/spells.txt, each covering the
// 256 records of its table (tech table FE:0F00, spell table 5B:AA00; see
// internal/techs and docs/techniques.md). Names come from the ROM's name
// tables at 0x3D27C0 (tech) and 0x5BA000 (spell), decoded through
// data/glyphs_jp.json.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/techs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 2, "usage: dumptechs <rom> <outdir>\n"+
		"   or: dumptechs <outdir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	romPath, outDir := args[0], args[1]
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	glyphPath, err := findGlyphs(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(glyphPath)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	dec := bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	techs_, err := techs.AllTechniques(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	spells, err := techs.AllSpells(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	if err := writeTechs(filepath.Join(outDir, "techs.txt"), "TECH", techs.TechNameOffset, rom, techs_, dec); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeTechs(filepath.Join(outDir, "spells.txt"), "SPELL", techs.SpellNameOffset, rom, spells, dec); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("%d techs and %d spells written to %s\n", len(techs_), len(spells), outDir)
}

// textDecoder is the DecodeBuffer surface of bokuno.NewTextDecoder (the
// concrete type is unexported).
type textDecoder interface {
	DecodeBuffer(rec []byte) bokuno.DecodeResult
}

// writeTechs dumps one table: id, name, hit rate, base power (byte and
// in-game x4 value), hit count, growth, cost, class, schools.
func writeTechs(path, kind string, nameBase int, rom []byte, entries []techs.Technique, dec textDecoder) error {
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	fmt.Fprintln(f, "# id  name  hit  power(=byte x4)  hits  growth  cost  class  spellSchool  techType  raw(+3..+8)")
	for _, e := range entries {
		var name string
		rec, err := techs.NameRecord(rom, nameBase, e.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		name = dec.DecodeBuffer(rec).Text
		resource := "WP"
		if e.Cost&techs.CostJP != 0 {
			resource = "JP"
		}
		if e.Cost&techs.CostAll != 0 {
			resource += "*"
		}
		raw := []byte{e.StatusEffect, e.Attributes, e.Range, e.SpecialEffects,
			e.Attributes2, e.SpecialSettings}
		fmt.Fprintf(f, "%s%03X %s hit=%d pow=%d(%d) n=%d g=%d cost=%s%d class=%02X school=%02X type=%02X % X\n",
			kind, e.ID, name,
			e.HitRate, e.BasePower, int(e.BasePower)*4,
			e.HitCount, e.Growth,
			resource, e.CostAmount(),
			e.Class, e.SpellType, e.TechType,
			raw)
	}
	return nil
}

// findGlyphs locates data/glyphs_jp.json: next to the repo root that holds
// the ROM (patches/..), else relative to the working directory.
func findGlyphs(romPath string) (string, error) {
	candidates := []string{
		filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(romPath)), "data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
		filepath.Join("data", "glyphs_jp.json"),
	}
	for _, p := range candidates {
		if st, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil && !st.IsDir() {
			return p, nil
		}
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("glyph assignment not found (tried %v); run from the repo root", candidates)
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/dumptriggers/main.go`:

```go
// dumptriggers decodes the per-map exits and event triggers of the maps
// dumpmaps renders.
//
// Usage: dumptriggers <rom> <outdir>
//
//	dumptriggers <rom> -map <id-hex>
//
// Batch mode: the outdir receives map<ID>.json for each rendered map
// (exits, event triggers, placed NPCs, chests, edge/X-button events, the
// raw movement destinations of block 4 and any structural warnings) and
// index.tsv summarizing every decoded map. It also writes jump_table.json,
// the global destination table event code 11xx (VM op 0x11 mapJump) uses.
//
// Map mode: prints one map's decode as text (exits, triggers, NPCs, edge
// events, destinations) — the spot-check view of the same decode.
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
	"saga3/internal/triggers"
)

var renderedIDs = []int{0x02, 0x04,
	// Pidona area and the intro chain (blob-NPC reachability, 2026-11-16)
	0x00, 0x01, 0x03, 0x05, 0x1DE, 0x246, 0x249, 0x24A, 0x24B, 0x4B, 0x4F, 0x312, 0x239, 0x252, 0x24E, 0x24D, 0x255, 0x258, 0x2FB,
	// blob-NPC maps from probeblobs
	0x3E, 0x2F, 0x3B, 0x1AA, 0x1F1, 0x288, 0x185, 0x5F, 0x15B, 0x92,
	0x1D0, 0x1DA, 0x1CF, 0x1C2, 0x68, 0xA5, 0xAE, 0x200,
	// prologue chain (Sinon forest -> Podorui road/town -> Rohan)
	0x250, 0x251, 0x253, 0x254, 0x25B, 0x25D, 0x25E, 0x25F, 0x24C, 0x24F,
	0x70, 0x72, 0x74, 0x75, 0x50, 0x5A, 0x5B, 0x59, 0x5D, 0x4C,
}

func main() {
	args := os.Args[1:]
	if len(args) == 3 && args[1] == "-map" {
		var id int
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(args[2], "%x", &id); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dumptriggers: map id %q: want hex\n", args[2])
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if err := printMap(args[0], id); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumptriggers:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if len(args) != 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: dumptriggers <rom> <outdir> | dumptriggers <rom> -map <id-hex>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	if err := run(args[0], args[1]); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dumptriggers:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func printMap(romPath string, id int) error {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read ROM: %w", err)
	}
	m, err := triggers.Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("decode map %#04x: %w", id, err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("map %#06x %dx%d npcs=%d\n", id, m.Width, m.Height, len(m.NPCs))
	for _, e := range m.Exits {
		fmt.Printf("  exit (%d,%d) %dx%d -> %#06x (%d,%d)\n", e.X, e.Y, e.W, e.H, e.TargetMap, e.TargetX, e.TargetY)
	}
	for _, t := range m.Triggers {
		fmt.Printf("  trig (%d,%d) %dx%d ev=%#06x\n", t.X, t.Y, t.W, t.H, t.EventID)
	}
	for _, n := range m.NPCs {
		fmt.Printf("  npc g=%#04x (%d,%d) ev=%#06x\n", n.Graphic, n.X, n.Y, n.EventID)
	}
	fmt.Println("  edge:", m.EdgeEvents)
	for _, e := range m.Destinations {
		fmt.Printf("  dest -> %#06x (%d,%d)\n", e.TargetMap, e.TargetX, e.TargetY)
	}
	return nil
}

func run(romPath, outdir string) error {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read ROM: %w", err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outdir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create outdir: %w", err)
	}
	for _, id := range renderedIDs {
		m, err := triggers.Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
		if errors.Is(err, triggers.ErrZeroed) {
			fmt.Printf("map %#04x: skipped (%v)\n", id, err)
			continue
		}
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("decode map %#04x: %w", id, err)
		}
		if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(outdir, fmt.Sprintf("map%04x.json", id)), m); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		fmt.Printf("map %#04x: %d exits, %d triggers, %d npcs, %d chests, %d destinations, %d warnings\n",
			id, len(m.Exits), len(m.Triggers), len(m.NPCs), len(m.Chests), len(m.Destinations), len(m.Warnings))
		for _, w := range m.Warnings {
			fmt.Printf("  warning: %s\n", w)
		}
	}
	jumps, err := triggers.JumpTable(mapfmt.ROM(rom))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("decode jump table: %w", err)
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(outdir, "jump_table.json"), jumps); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Printf("jump table: %d entries\n", len(jumps))
	return nil
}

func writeJSON(path string, v any) error {
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	enc := json.NewEncoder(f)
	enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
	err = enc.Encode(v)
	closeErr := f.Close()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if closeErr != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("close %s: %w", path, closeErr)
	}
	return nil
}
```

`cmd/encounterscan/main.go`:

```go
// encounterscan surveys the trigger classes of every decodable submap:
// event point ids by high byte, NPC event ids, edge/X-button ids, and the
// flag2-0x20 battle sub-block bytes. Survey tool for the 0x2000
// battle-encounter class decode (docs/triggers.md open question 2).
//
// Usage: encounterscan [<rom>]   (default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
	"saga3/internal/triggers"
)

func main() {
	romPath := "patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"
	if len(os.Args) == 2 {
		romPath = os.Args[1]
	} else if len(os.Args) != 1 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: encounterscan [<rom>]   (default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "read ROM:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	hi := map[int]int{} // trigger id high byte -> count
	hiIDs := map[int][]int{}
	npcHi := map[int]int{}
	edgeHi := map[int]int{}
	ids := map[int]bool{}
	maps := 0
	for id := 0; id < 0x400; id++ {
		m, err := triggers.Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		maps++
		ids[id] = true
		for _, t := range m.Triggers {
			hi[t.EventID>>8]++
			hiIDs[t.EventID>>8] = append(hiIDs[t.EventID>>8], t.EventID)
		}
		for _, n := range m.NPCs {
			npcHi[n.EventID>>8]++
		}
		for _, e := range m.EdgeEvents {
			edgeHi[e>>8]++
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("maps decoded: %d\n", maps)
	fmt.Println("-- event point trigger id high bytes --")
	keys := make([]int, 0, len(hi))
	for k := range hi {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Ints(keys)
	for _, k := range keys {
		uniq := map[int]bool{}
		for _, v := range hiIDs[k] {
			uniq[v] = true
		}
		fmt.Printf("  %02Xxx: %d triggers, %d distinct ids\n", k, hi[k], len(uniq))
	}
	fmt.Println("-- NPC event id high bytes --")
	keys = keys[:0]
	for k := range npcHi {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Ints(keys)
	for _, k := range keys {
		fmt.Printf("  %02Xxx: %d npcs\n", k, npcHi[k])
	}
	fmt.Println("-- event point 20xx-22xx ids and maps --")
	for id := 0; id < 0x400; id++ {
		m, err := triggers.Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		for _, t := range m.Triggers {
			if t.EventID>>8 >= 0x20 && t.EventID>>8 <= 0x22 {
				fmt.Printf("  map %#04X (%d,%d) %dx%d id %04X\n", id, t.X, t.Y, t.W, t.H, t.EventID)
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Println("-- NPC 16xx-22xx ids and maps (first 200) --")
	shown := 0
	for id := 0; id < 0x400 && shown < 200; id++ {
		m, err := triggers.Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		for _, n := range m.NPCs {
			if n.EventID>>8 >= 0x16 && n.EventID>>8 <= 0x22 {
				fmt.Printf("  map %#04X (%d,%d) g=%d kind=%#04X id %04X\n", id, n.X, n.Y, n.Graphic, n.Quality, n.EventID)
				shown++
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Println("-- monster-class NPC distinct ids (16xx-1Fxx, 2000, 22xx) --")
	counts := map[int]int{}
	kinds := map[int]map[int]bool{}
	for id := 0; id < 0x400; id++ {
		m, err := triggers.Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		for _, n := range m.NPCs {
			hi := n.EventID >> 8
			if (hi >= 0x16 && hi <= 0x1F) || n.EventID == 0x2000 || hi == 0x22 {
				counts[n.EventID]++
				if kinds[n.EventID] == nil {
					kinds[n.EventID] = map[int]bool{}
				}
				kinds[n.EventID][n.Quality>>8] = true
			}
		}
	}
	dk := make([]int, 0, len(counts))
	for k := range counts {
		dk = append(dk, k)
	}
	sort.Ints(dk)
	for _, k := range dk {
		ks := []string{}
		for q := range kinds[k] {
			ks = append(ks, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", q))
		}
		sort.Strings(ks)
		fmt.Printf("  id %04X: %d npcs, kind bytes %v\n", k, counts[k], ks)
	}
	fmt.Println("-- edge event id high bytes --")
	keys = keys[:0]
	for k := range edgeHi {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Ints(keys)
	for _, k := range keys {
		fmt.Printf("  %02Xxx: %d edges\n", k, edgeHi[k])
	}
}
```

```go
// eventrange prints the native event range for given ids (block-table lookup).
//
// Usage: eventrange [<rom>] <id-hex>...   (default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 0, "usage: eventrange [<rom>] <id-hex>...   (default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, fmt.Errorf("read ROM: %w", err))
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	o := bokuno.NewOps(rom)
	for _, a := range args[1:] {
		var id int
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(a, "%x", &id); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "eventrange: id %q: want hex\n", a)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		r, ok := o.NativeRange(id)
		if !ok {
			fmt.Printf("%04X: unresolved\n", id)
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("%04X: entry %02X:%04X end16 %04X start file %X source %s\n", id, r.EntryCPU>>16, r.EntryCPU&0xffff, r.End16, r.Start, r.Source)
	}
}
```

`cmd/exportbattle/main.go`:

```go
// Command exportbattle converts the extracted enemy/ally tables into the
// JSON the Go battle engine (internal/game/battle) reads.
//
// Usage: exportbattle <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <data-dir>
//
//	exportbattle <data-dir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and the glyph
// assignment to data/glyphs_jp.json.
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/battle"
	"saga3/internal/battledata"
	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/charstats"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/items"
	"saga3/internal/techs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROMGlyphs(os.Args[1:], "usage: exportbattle <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <data-dir>\n"+
		"   or: exportbattle <data-dir>\n"+
		"   (defaults: rom patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, glyphs data/glyphs_jp.json)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	glyphRaw, err := os.ReadFile(args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(glyphRaw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	ops := bokuno.NewOps(rom)
	ops.SetText(bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot))
	dir := args[2]
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	// The battle RNG table D7:E63C (C2:032E rolls lo + T[$14] mod n).
	const battleRNGOffset = 0x17E63C
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "battle_rng.bin"), rom[battleRNGOffset:battleRNGOffset+0x400], 0o644); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	// Ally names live in the ACTOR table (FD:1480, 8B stride), not the
	// enemy name table.
	allyNames := ops.NameTable(0x3d1480, 8, 256)

	enemies, err := battledata.AllEnemies(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	ej := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(enemies))
	for i, e := range enemies {
		// AllEnemies returns ids in order: 0x000-0x13F (main table) then
		// 0x140-0x1FF (bank 5A), so the slice index is the id.
		id := uint16(i)
		name, _ := battledata.Name(id)
		enemy := map[string]any{
			"id":   fmt.Sprintf("%03X", id),
			"name": name,
			"hp":   e.HP,
			// struct bytes +6..+12 (docs/battle-data.md)
			"str": e.Strength,
			"dex": e.Dexterity,
			"agi": e.Agility,
			"vit": e.Vitality,
			"mag": e.Magic,
			"wil": e.Will,
			"cha": e.Charm,
			// struct byte +1: spell-school resistance bits + 投げ/音波/凝視/浮遊
			"school_resist": e.SchoolResist,
		}
		// action patterns: slots in unlock order, each an enemy-tech id
		// with the pattern weapon's item-table attack power (§2.1 攻).
		pat, perr := battledata.PatternsFor(rom, id)
		if perr == nil && len(pat) > 0 {
			var pats []map[string]any
			for _, p := range pat {
				acts := []string{}
				for _, act := range p.Actions {
					acts = append(acts, fmt.Sprintf("%03X", act.TechID))
				}
				watk := 0
				if it, ierr := items.ItemAt(rom, int(p.Weapon)); ierr == nil && it.Kind == items.Weapon {
					watk = it.Power
				}
				pats = append(pats, map[string]any{
					"weapon":     p.Weapon,
					"weapon_atk": watk,
					"actions":    acts,
				})
			}
			enemy["patterns"] = pats
		}
		// struct byte +13: the enemy's tech class level — the §2.1 LV for
		// the C table and the spark-chance diff.
		enemy["tech_lv"] = e.TechLV
		// struct bytes +2/+3: the record's +7 (& 3F) and +0x0B (AI mode)
		// the enemy decision chain reads (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md)
		enemy["target_bits"] = int(e.TargetBits & 0x3F)
		enemy["ai_mode"] = int(e.AIMode)
		// struct byte +0: the record's +3 (sex bits 0x80/0x40 for the
		// sex target pick C2:57C4)
		enemy["species"] = int(e.Species | e.SpeciesFlags)
		// struct byte +16 閃きLV: the record's +33h, the level an ally's
		// spark against this enemy is measured with (C2:A7BF)
		enemy["flash_lv"] = int(e.FlashLV)
		// struct bytes +21..+23: shield and two armor items — the target's
		// 斬/打/突/射 phys_def lives in these records (docs/battle-data.md),
		// so the battle scene joins their item-table defense values. 0xFF =
		// empty slot.
		defense := 0
		armorIDs := []string{}
		for _, b := range []byte{e.Shield, e.Armor1, e.Armor2} {
			if b == 0xFF {
				continue
			}
			it, ierr := items.ItemAt(rom, int(b))
			if ierr != nil {
				continue
			}
			armorIDs = append(armorIDs, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", b))
			switch it.Kind {
			case items.Shield:
				defense += it.Defense
			case items.Armor:
				defense += it.PhysDef
			}
		}
		enemy["armor_ids"] = armorIDs
		enemy["phys_def"] = defense
		// struct byte +15 (wiki column 上): the §8.2 battle-end growth
		// 敵上昇Lv for the winning side's rolls.
		enemy["rise_lv"] = e.GrowthLV
		// spoils candidates per slot (§16.3): item id in items.json form,
		// "" = empty or the unmodeled own-equipment codes FD/FE.
		drops, derr := battledata.DropsFor(rom, id)
		if derr != nil {
			fail(derr)
		}
		dj := make([]string, len(drops))
		for s, d := range drops {
			if d.Raw == battledata.DropNone || d.Raw >= battledata.DropOwnEquipFirst {
				continue
			}
			dj[s] = fmt.Sprintf("%02X", d.ItemID())
		}
		enemy["drops"] = dj
		// the raw slot bytes: the drop walk C2:E0D8 rolls every slot that
		// is not FF, own-equipment codes FD/FE included
		rawDrops := make([]int, len(drops))
		for s, d := range drops {
			rawDrops[s] = int(d.Raw)
		}
		enemy["drop_codes"] = rawDrops
		// drop row byte 8: the gold base (C2:E1D5 via 55:CA60)
		enemy["gold"] = int(rom[battledata.DropTableOffset+int(id&0x1FF)*battledata.DropRowSize+8])
		// FE:D107 fit sizes against the hensei width/height limits.
		fw, fh, ferr := battledata.FitSize(rom, id)
		if ferr != nil {
			fail(ferr)
		}
		enemy["fit_width"] = fw
		enemy["fit_height"] = fh
		ej = append(ej, enemy)
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "enemies.json"), ej); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	allies, err := charstats.AllAllies(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	aj := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(allies))
	for _, a := range allies {
		techIDs := []string{}
		for _, tid := range a.InitialTechs {
			if tid != 0xFF {
				techIDs = append(techIDs, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", tid))
			}
		}
		spellIDs := []string{}
		for _, sid := range a.InitialSpells {
			if sid != 0xFF {
				spellIDs = append(spellIDs, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", sid))
			}
		}
		// 初期装備 +31..+38: eight slots in 腕1-4 then 体1-4 order, 0xFF
		// = empty slot. Slot positions are kept (null) so the UI can show
		// gaps the way the ROM does.
		equipment := make([]any, 0, len(a.Equipment))
		for _, item := range a.Equipment {
			if item == 0xFF {
				equipment = append(equipment, nil)
			} else {
				equipment = append(equipment, fmt.Sprintf("%02X", item))
			}
		}
		// Class levels feed the WP/JP pool formula (godot/battle_math.gd
		// max_pool): weapons +13..+17, schools +18/+19; 増幅 does not
		// count (docs/battle-formulas.md §12.1). max_wp/max_jp mirror the
		// Go computation for parity checks.
		wlevels := []int{}
		for _, w := range a.Weapon {
			wlevels = append(wlevels, w.Level())
		}
		slevels := []int{a.Spell1.Level(), a.Spell2.Level()}
		// 成長率 row (§8.2 battle-end growth probabilities; docs §8.5
		// opens the bokuno column mapping — the struct layout in
		// charstats.Growth is the community dump's).
		g, gerr := charstats.GrowthAt(rom, int(a.ID))
		growth := map[string]any{}
		if gerr == nil {
			growth = map[string]any{
				"sword": g.Sword, "axe": g.Axe, "spear": g.Spear,
				"bow": g.Bow, "martial": g.Martial,
				"goryu": g.Goryu, "suzaku": g.Suzaku, "byakko": g.Byakko,
				"genbu": g.Genbu, "solar": g.Solar, "lunar": g.Lunar,
				"amplify": g.Amplify, "wp": g.WP, "jp": g.JP, "hp": g.HP,
			}
		}
		// the stats the game sets on joining: entry + 宿星 row + 得意武器
		// row (charstats.LiveStats); the hero slot's rows come from the
		// new-game $F308/$F309, which the opening capture showed equal to
		// the entry's own +40/+42
		live, lerr := charstats.LiveStats(rom, a, a.Destiny, a.ForteWeapon)
		if lerr != nil {
			fail(lerr)
		}
		aj = append(aj, map[string]any{
			"id":        fmt.Sprintf("%02X", a.ID),
			"name":      allyNames[a.ID%256],
			"techs":     techIDs,
			"spells":    spellIDs,
			"equipment": equipment,
			"hp":        a.HP,
			"lp":        a.LP,
			"str":       live[0],
			"dex":       live[1],
			"agi":       live[2],
			"vit":       live[3],
			"mag":       live[4],
			"wil":       live[5],
			"cha":       live[6],
			// struct byte +2: the battle record's +3 (0x80 男, 0x40 女),
			// read by the enemy's sex target pick (C2:57C4)
			"species": a.Gender,
			"wlevels": wlevels,
			"growth":  growth,
			"slevels": slevels,
			// struct byte +20 増幅LV: the battle record's +30h, halved and
			// square-rooted by the battle-start check C2:1C26
			"amp_lv": a.Amplify.Level(),
			// struct byte +22 閃きタイプ: the battle record's +36h, the bit
			// the spark walk tests in the tech's FE:353F word (C2:A85B)
			"flash_type": a.FlashType,
			// struct byte +42 得意武器: the hero's new-game bonus row
			// (hero_forte.json, read through $F309)
			"forte": a.ForteWeapon,
			// victory growth (C2:DB7C): the raw 16-byte rate row (cols
			// 0-11 classes, 12 増幅 for the reserve, 13 WP gate, 14 JP
			// gate, 15 HP), 成長タイプ (+21, the order row) and 初期術
			// (+41, the school slot of the first spell level)
			"growth_row":  growthRow(rom, int(a.ID)),
			"growth_type": a.GrowthType,
			// entry +18 / +19 raw: bits 5-6 pick the school slot, bit 7
			// grows the level with $F532 (FF:6B25 / FF:6B5D, FF:6DAC)
			"spell_raw":    []int{int(a.Spell1), int(a.Spell2)},
			"start_school": a.StartSchool,
			"max_wp":       battle.MaxPool(wlevels),
			"max_jp":       battle.MaxPool(slevels),
		})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "allies.json"), aj); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	techniques, err := techs.AllTechniques(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	tj := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(techniques))
	for i, t := range techniques {
		nameRec, err := techs.TechNameRecord(rom, uint16(i))
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		name := ops.DecodeText(nameRec)
		tj = append(tj, map[string]any{
			"id":         fmt.Sprintf("%02X", i),
			"name":       name,
			"hit":        t.HitRate,
			"power":      t.BasePower,
			"hits":       t.HitCount,
			"growth":     t.Growth,
			"cost":       t.CostAmount(),
			"jpcost":     t.Cost&0x20 != 0,
			"class":      t.Class,
			"type":       t.TechType,
			"effect":     t.StatusEffect,
			"special":    t.SpecialEffects,
			"attributes": t.Attributes,
			"settings":   t.SpecialSettings,
			"statuses":   effectStatuses(rom, t),
			// byte +0x0B 術タイプ: the field-shift step after each action
			// (C2:69B3) reads it
			"school": t.SpellType,
		})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "techniques.json"), tj); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	spells, err := techs.AllSpells(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	sj := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(spells))
	for i, sp := range spells {
		nameRec, err := techs.SpellNameRecord(rom, uint16(i))
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		name := ops.DecodeText(nameRec)
		sj = append(sj, map[string]any{
			"id":       fmt.Sprintf("%02X", i),
			"name":     name,
			"hit":      sp.HitRate,
			"power":    sp.BasePower,
			"hits":     sp.HitCount,
			"growth":   sp.Growth,
			"cost":     sp.CostAmount(),
			"jpcost":   sp.Cost&0x20 != 0,
			"class":    sp.Class,
			"school":   sp.SpellType,
			"type":     sp.TechType,
			"effect":   sp.StatusEffect,
			"statuses": effectStatuses(rom, sp),
		})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "spells.json"), sj); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	// enemy technique names (main 0x3D31C0, hack ext 0x5B40C0) + stats
	// (main 0x3E1D00, ext 0x5B4AC0) — battle log, enemy damage and
	// enemy added effects.
	etn := map[string]any{}
	for i := 0; i < 512; i++ {
		nameBase := 0x3D31C0
		if i >= techs.ExtEnemyTechIDBase {
			nameBase = 0x5B40C0
		}
		rec, err := techs.NameRecord(rom, nameBase, uint16(i%256))
		if err == nil {
			if name := ops.DecodeText(rec); name != "" {
				etn[fmt.Sprintf("%03X", i)] = name
			}
		}
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "enemy_tech_names.json"), etn); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	var etj []map[string]any
	for i := 0; i < 512; i++ {
		et, err := techs.EnemyTechAt(rom, uint16(i))
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		etj = append(etj, map[string]any{
			"id":         fmt.Sprintf("%03X", i),
			"hit":        et.HitRate,
			"power":      et.BasePower,
			"hits":       et.HitCount,
			"growth":     et.Growth,
			"effect":     et.StatusEffect,
			"tech_type":  et.TechType,
			"school":     et.SpellType,
			"class":      et.Class,
			"attributes": et.Attributes,
			"statuses":   effectStatuses(rom, et),
			// bytes +5/+8/+9: target range, 行動最初/最後 and special
			// settings, special target pick (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md)
			"range":    et.Range,
			"settings": et.SpecialSettings,
			// byte +6 特殊効果: the counter spark's gate and kind filter
			// read it on the incoming tech (C2:AC44, ADD4)
			"special":     et.SpecialEffects,
			"target_pick": et.TargetPick,
		})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "enemy_techs.json"), etj); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	// Spark (閃き) tables (docs/techniques.md "Spark"): ext/main/counter
	// groups keyed by source (class code or tech id), the two live bokuno
	// chance rows (68:E900 見切り, 68:E920 閃き; docs/battle-formulas.md
	// §4.6), and the FE tail block (semantics open). Group entries are
	// [tech-id-hex, difficulty]; entries with difficulty >= 0x80 are gated
	// (never spark normally). The vanilla FE:3180/3195 chance copies are
	// stale in bokuno (no code reads them) and are not exported.
	spark := map[string]any{}
	hackChance, err := battle.HackChanceRows(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	spark["chance"] = map[string]any{
		"mikiri": hackChanceTables(hackChance[0]),
		"spark":  hackChanceTables(hackChance[1]),
	}
	// The spark walk's threshold rows, indexed by 10 + (difficulty - the
	// target's 閃きLV) clamped to 0..26 (FE:E8A7): 68:E920 for a tech whose
	// FE:353F word has the actor's 閃きタイプ bit and passes the WP/JP test
	// C2:C03D, 68:E900 when that test fails, 5B:FEC0 without the bit.
	rowAt := func(off int) []int {
		out := make([]int, 27)
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = int(rom[off+i])
		}
		return out
	}
	spark["rows"] = map[string]any{
		"type_wp":  rowAt(0x68E920),
		"type":     rowAt(0x68E900),
		"off_type": rowAt(0x5BFEC0),
	}
	typeBits := map[string]any{}
	for t := 0; t < 256; t++ {
		typeBits[fmt.Sprintf("%02X", t)] = int(rom[0x3E353F+2*t]) | int(rom[0x3E353F+2*t+1])<<8
	}
	spark["type_bits"] = typeBits
	ext, err := battle.ExtSparkGroups(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	main, err := battle.MainSparkGroups(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	counter, err := battle.CounterGroups(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	tail, err := battle.FETailGroups(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	spark["ext"] = sparkGroups(ext)
	spark["main"] = sparkGroups(main)
	spark["counter"] = sparkGroups(counter)
	spark["fe_tail"] = sparkGroups(tail)
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "spark.json"), spark); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	formations, err := AllFormations(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "formations.json"), formations); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	enemyFormations, err := AllEnemyFormations(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "enemy_formations.json"), enemyFormations); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// The victory level bumps (C2:DA7C, C2:DAD8 -> 5B:FF40): the rank rise
	// table FE:9B7D, the per-race group rows 5E:6500 (17 rows of 16 curve
	// ids, FF = no bump; row 16 for non-random battles), the curves
	// 5E:6610 (8 bytes each) and the caps FE:9C05 / FE:9C06.
	bytesAt := func(off, n int) []int {
		out := make([]int, n)
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = int(rom[off+i])
		}
		return out
	}
	var groupRows, curves [][]int
	for r := 0; r < 17; r++ {
		groupRows = append(groupRows, bytesAt(0x5E6500+r*16, 16))
	}
	for c := 0; c < 8; c++ {
		curves = append(curves, bytesAt(0x5E6610+c*8, 8))
	}
	levels := map[string]any{
		"rank_rise":  bytesAt(0x3E9B7D, 8),
		"group_rows": groupRows,
		"curves":     curves,
		"global_cap": int(rom[0x3E9C05]),
		"group_cap":  int(rom[0x3E9C06]),
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "levels.json"), levels); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// The hero's new-game forte bonus (C5:9645 -> 5B:7B8F): per 得意武器
	// ($F309) three bytes: the level column (record +0x25 + n) raised by
	// 1, the item placed in the second weapon slot (+0x48, 0 = none) and
	// the extended-item flag (+0x7E bit 6).
	var heroForte [][]int
	for f := 0; f < 10; f++ {
		heroForte = append(heroForte, bytesAt(0x5B7B70+f*3, 3))
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "hero_forte.json"), heroForte); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// Victory growth tables: the 成長タイプ order rows FE:34BF (8 x 16
	// codes: 00-0B class, 0D WP, 0E JP, 0F HP, 0C / FF skip), the chance
	// table FE:31AA (21 bytes, index 10 - clamp(raise - lower, -10, 10)),
	// and the HP lower term max HP * FE:3170 / FE:3171 and the counter
	// multiplier FE:317E.
	var orderRows [][]int
	for t := 0; t < 8; t++ {
		orderRows = append(orderRows, bytesAt(0x3E34BF+t*16, 16))
	}
	growthTables := map[string]any{
		"order_rows":  orderRows,
		"chance":      bytesAt(0x3E31AA, 21),
		"hp_mul":      int(rom[0x3E3170]),
		"hp_div":      int(rom[0x3E3171]),
		"counter_mul": int(rom[0x3E317E]),
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "growth.json"), growthTables); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// Fixed-formation battles (battle word 19xx): every FE:7F5B record,
	// decoded by battledata.FixedBattleAt (docs/battle-data.md "Fixed
	// formations"); enemy ids keep bit 0x4000 = key enemy in "key".
	var fixed []map[string]any
	for id := 0; id < battledata.FixedCount; id++ {
		f, ferr := battledata.FixedBattleAt(rom, id)
		if ferr != nil {
			fail(ferr)
		}
		var ids []int
		var key []bool
		for _, w := range f.Enemies {
			ids = append(ids, int(w&0x1FFF))
			key = append(key, w&0x4000 != 0)
		}
		var reinf []int
		for _, w := range f.Reinf {
			reinf = append(reinf, int(w))
		}
		var pairs [][]int
		for _, p := range f.ScriptPairs {
			pairs = append(pairs, []int{int(p[0]), int(p[1])})
		}
		var pos [][]int
		for _, p := range f.Pos {
			pos = append(pos, []int{int(p[0]), int(p[1])})
		}
		var chain []int
		for _, cb := range f.Chain {
			chain = append(chain, int(cb))
		}
		var startSlots []int
		for _, w := range f.StartWords {
			startSlots = append(startSlots, int(w))
		}
		fixed = append(fixed, map[string]any{
			"id": id, "type": int(f.Type), "talk": int(f.Talk),
			"hp_leader": f.HPLeader, "hp_others": f.HPOthers, "flags": int(f.Flags),
			"field": int(f.Field), "enc": int(f.Enc), "level": int(f.Level),
			"extra": int(f.Extra), "leader": int(f.Leader & 0x1FFF), "hensei": f.Hensei,
			"enemies": ids, "key": key, "pos": pos, "reinforcements": reinf,
			"round": int(f.Round), "tech": int(f.Tech), "script": int(f.Script),
			"script_gate": int(f.ScriptGate), "script_pairs": pairs,
			"spawn_cap": f.SpawnCap, "spawn_chance": f.SpawnChance, "chain": chain,
			"start_slots": startSlots,
			"initiate":    int(f.Initiate),
			"key_mask":    int(f.KeyMask), "key_slot": int(f.KeySlot),
		})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "fixed_battles.json"), fixed); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// the per-round script table FE:926B (8 x 9 bytes, C2:5DDD): entry 0
	// = gate byte, then four (mask, tech) pairs; the type-11 records and
	// the type-0x0E chain links address it by entry
	scripts := make([][]int, 0, 8)
	for m := 0; m < 8; m++ {
		e, serr := battledata.ScriptEntry(rom, m)
		if serr != nil {
			fail(serr)
		}
		row := []int{int(e[0])}
		for p := 0; p < 4; p++ {
			row = append(row, int(e[1+2*p]), int(e[2+2*p]))
		}
		scripts = append(scripts, row)
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "battle_scripts.json"), scripts); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// C2:C18B (the common tail's last step): 16 entries of 10 bytes at
	// FE:9E8E — [0] the marker (0x00 = usable, anything else skips the
	// entry), [1] the roll(1,100) threshold, [2..9] an FF-terminated
	// enemy-id list. The first entry whose bit in the persistent $F4DA
	// bitmask is unset and whose list contains one of this battle's
	// enemies with id < 0x100 consumes one roll and marks the bit (every
	// shipped threshold is 100, so the roll always succeeds). The written
	// $16D8 cell has no reader (write-only).
	unlocks := make([]map[string]any, 0, 16)
	for m := 0; m < 16; m++ {
		e := 0x3E9E8E + 10*m
		var ids []int
		if rom[e] == 0x00 {
			for k := 2; k < 10; k++ {
				if rom[e+k] == 0xFF {
					break
				}
				ids = append(ids, int(rom[e+k]))
			}
		}
		unlocks = append(unlocks, map[string]any{"index": m, "marker": int(rom[e]),
			"threshold": int(rom[e+1]), "ids": ids})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "battle_unlocks.json"), unlocks); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// The fixed-battle opening messages (docs/battle-data.md): the talk
	// row's +0 byte names a FD:9800 content id ((b & 0x3F) + 0x32; 0x15
	// keeps the previous), whose word points at the FD block decoded with
	// the battle text encoding. Verified live: battle 0x2's window draws
	// the same two lines (probe b18). The later row bytes (+3/+4/+5) have
	// unresolved triggers - exported, not shown.
	talks := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(fixed))
	prevID := 0
	for _, fr := range fixed {
		f, ferr := battledata.FixedBattleAt(rom, fr["id"].(int))
		if ferr != nil {
			fail(ferr)
		}
		if f.Talk == 0xFF {
			continue
		}
		row := make([]int, 0, len(f.TalkRow))
		var text string
		if len(f.TalkRow) > 0 {
			for _, b := range f.TalkRow {
				row = append(row, int(b))
			}
			low := int(f.TalkRow[0]) & 0x3F
			id := prevID
			if low != 0x15 {
				id = low + 0x32
			}
			prevID = id
			w := int(rom[0x3D9800+2*id]) | int(rom[0x3D9800+2*id+1])<<8
			blk := 0x3D0000 + w + 0x9A00
			end := blk + 0x200
			if end > len(rom) {
				end = len(rom)
			}
			text = ops.DecodeBattleText(rom[blk:end])
		}
		talks = append(talks, map[string]any{"id": fr["id"], "talk": int(f.Talk),
			"row": row, "text": text})
	}
	if err := writeJSON(filepath.Join(dir, "battle_talks.json"), talks); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("enemies: %d, allies: %d, techs: %d, spells: %d, enemy techs: %d, spark groups: %d+%d+%d+%d, formations: %d, enemy formations: %d+%d -> %s\n",
		len(ej), len(aj), len(tj), len(sj), len(etj), len(ext), len(main), len(counter), len(tail), len(formations),
		len(enemyFormations["hensei"].([]map[string]any)), len(enemyFormations["appearance"].([]any)), dir)
}

// FormationCount is the party-side 陣形テーブル length: ids 0x00-0x1F
// (docs/battle-data.md). Enemy-side rows (id >= 0x80, bitmap page $7E143B
// per C2:E550) live outside this table.
const FormationCount = 32

// formationFileBase is the hack's 陣形データ table at 5E:A000, rows of
// the vanilla 11-byte layout at a 0x80 stride: the battle reads it through
// 5E:F000 ($38 * 0x80 + A000) for the target rates (C2:BC37) and the
// position bytes (C2:6586). The vanilla table at FE:68CB (11-byte stride)
// is not read by the hack's battle and differs in 15 of 32 rows (formation
// 0A position 0: vanilla level +1, the hack 0x40 = level 0, which the
// opening battle's agility 20 confirms).
const formationFileBase = 0x5EA000
const formationRowStride = 0x80

// AllFormations decodes the 陣形テーブル. Per formation id (docs/battle-data.md):
// +0..+4 cumulative target-selection rates (被弾率 thresholds over 255),
// +5..+9 per-position bonus bitfields, +10 heal byte. Bonus bits (community
// struct def RS3_陣形データ): 0x01-0x03 = speed-amp level, 0x04 = invert
// (amp becomes a slow), 0x08 spell-attack up, 0x10 ranged-attack up,
// 0x20 melee-attack up, 0x40 back-defense, 0x80 front-defense.
// speed_level carries the signed level (negative when bit 0x04 is set); the
// 攻速 factor is 1000 + 250*speed_level (docs/battle-formulas.md §5).
func AllFormations(rom []byte) ([]map[string]any, error) {
	if len(rom) < formationFileBase+(FormationCount-1)*formationRowStride+11 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("rom too small for formation table at %#x", formationFileBase)
	}
	out := make([]map[string]any, 0, FormationCount)
	for id := 0; id < FormationCount; id++ {
		row := rom[formationFileBase+id*formationRowStride : formationFileBase+id*formationRowStride+11]
		positions := make([]map[string]any, 0, 5)
		for p := 0; p < 5; p++ {
			b := row[5+p]
			level := int(b & 0x03)
			if b&0x04 != 0 {
				level = -level
			}
			positions = append(positions, map[string]any{
				"speed_level":   level,
				"spell_attack":  b&0x08 != 0,
				"ranged":        b&0x10 != 0,
				"melee":         b&0x20 != 0,
				"back_defense":  b&0x40 != 0,
				"front_defense": b&0x80 != 0,
			})
		}
		out = append(out, map[string]any{
			"id":        fmt.Sprintf("%02X", id),
			"rates":     []int{int(row[0]), int(row[1]), int(row[2]), int(row[3]), int(row[4])},
			"positions": positions,
			"heal":      fmt.Sprintf("%02X", row[10]),
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// AllEnemyFormations exports the field-encounter composition tables
// (internal/battledata encounter.go; docs/field-monsters.md "Encounter
// composition"): hensei limits and slots, the 9-bit appearance pairs,
// the companion patterns and the companion budget constant.
func AllEnemyFormations(rom []byte) (map[string]any, error) {
	hensei := make([]map[string]any, 0, battledata.HenseiCount)
	for id := 0; id < battledata.HenseiCount; id++ {
		off := battledata.HenseiOffset + id*battledata.HenseiEntrySize
		if off+battledata.HenseiEntrySize > len(rom) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("hensei %X at %#x past ROM end", id, off)
		}
		row := rom[off : off+battledata.HenseiEntrySize]
		slots := make([]map[string]any, 0, 5)
		for s := 0; s < 5; s++ {
			slots = append(slots, map[string]any{
				"x": int(row[3+2*s]),
				"y": int(row[4+2*s]),
			})
		}
		hensei = append(hensei, map[string]any{
			"id":    fmt.Sprintf("%X", id),
			"count": int(row[0]),
			// FE:D107: an added enemy's height must be <= +1 ($5C) and
			// its width <= +2 ($5B).
			"height_max": int(row[1]),
			"width_max":  int(row[2]),
			"slots":      slots,
		})
	}
	appearance := make([]any, 0, battledata.AppearanceRaces)
	for race := 0; race < battledata.AppearanceRaces; race++ {
		bands := make([]map[string]any, 0, battledata.AppearanceBands)
		for band := 0; band < battledata.AppearanceBands; band++ {
			p, err := battledata.AppearanceAt(rom, race, band)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			bands = append(bands, map[string]any{
				"leader": int(p.Leader),
				"hensei": int(p.Hensei),
			})
		}
		appearance = append(appearance, bands)
	}
	companions := make([]any, 0, battledata.CompanionPatterns)
	for p := 0; p < battledata.CompanionPatterns; p++ {
		c, err := battledata.CompanionsFor(rom, p)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		rows := make([][]int, 0, len(c))
		for _, e := range c {
			rows = append(rows, []int{int(e.Level), int(e.ID)})
		}
		companions = append(companions, rows)
	}
	return map[string]any{
		"hensei":          hensei,
		"appearance":      appearance,
		"companions":      companions,
		"companion_bonus": int(rom[battledata.CompanionBonusOffset]),
	}, nil
}

// hackChanceTables renders a live chance row as plain ints, ascending by
// over (index 0 = over −16 … 26 = over +10), with the ≥0xE0 never-spark
// values already folded to 0 the way the 68:E940 wrapper does.
func hackChanceTables(t battle.HackChanceRow) []int {
	out := make([]int, 0, battle.HackChanceEntries)
	for over := -16; over <= 10; over++ {
		out = append(out, t.Base(over))
	}
	return out
}

// sparkGroups renders decoded spark groups for the battle scene.
func sparkGroups(groups []battle.SparkGroup) []map[string]any {
	out := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(groups))
	for _, g := range groups {
		entries := make([]any, 0, len(g.Entries))
		for _, e := range g.Entries {
			entries = append(entries, []any{
				fmt.Sprintf("%02X", e.TechID),
				int(e.Difficulty),
			})
		}
		out = append(out, map[string]any{
			"source":  fmt.Sprintf("%02X", g.Source),
			"entries": entries,
		})
	}
	return out
}

// effectStatuses decodes the applied statuses of a 技の性能 record: the
// byte +3 effect id indexes the 0x3FF200 table only when the 特殊設定
// byte (byte +8) carries bit 0x80 追加効果有効 — records without the bit
// (e.g. ウィークネス, 撹乱) carry stale ids that the engine ignores, so
// the field is nil there. Only the 状態異常1 bits are exported; the
// self/secondary bits (透明化, かすみ2段, 術スタン…) have no battle-scene
// machinery yet and stay in the raw effect id.
func effectStatuses(rom []byte, t techs.Technique) []string {
	if t.SpecialSettings&0x80 == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	eff, err := techs.AddedEffectAt(rom, t.StatusEffect)
	if err != nil || eff.Status1 == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	statuses := []string{}
	for bit := byte(1); bit != 0; bit <<= 1 {
		if eff.Status1&bit != 0 {
			statuses = append(statuses, techs.Status1Names[bit])
		}
	}
	if len(statuses) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return statuses
}

func writeJSON(path string, v any) error {
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o644)
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}

// growthRow is the raw 16-byte growth-rate row: FE:31BF + 16 * id, the
// hack's 5A:7FC0 + 16 * (id - 0xB0) for its extra characters (C2:DE63
// and siblings read it through the same id). The 6F:0000 override for
// record +1 in 0x70..0xAF (5A:BEA0) is not modelled.
func growthRow(rom []byte, id int) []int {
	base := charstats.GrowthMainTableOffset + id*charstats.GrowthEntrySize
	if id >= charstats.ExtTableIDBase {
		base = charstats.GrowthExtTableOffset + (id-charstats.ExtTableIDBase)*charstats.GrowthEntrySize
	}
	out := make([]int, charstats.GrowthEntrySize)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = int(rom[base+i])
	}
	return out
}
```

`cmd/exportbosslist/main.go`:

```go
// Command exportbosslist exports the immovable-boss id list that arms
// C2:5665 (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md "The immovable revert C2:5665").
//
// The setup gate FE:D1BF sets $22 bit 3 iff the battle has exactly one
// enemy ($34 == 1) and enemy 0's id word (and #$1FFF) appears in the
// FF-terminated word list at 59:FF00 (read long lda $59FF00,x). The list
// holds 124 real ids, three FFFE filler words (FFF8-FFFD, never matching
// a masked real id) and the FFFF terminator at FFFE; ids run continuously
// 59:FF00-59:FFF7 with no interior FFFF. Those bosses take TWO actions
// per round (their real AI once + pattern 2 once).
//
// Usage: exportbosslist <rom> <data-dir>
//
//	exportbosslist <data-dir>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc.
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

// cpuToFile maps CPU bank:offset to the 8MB file offset (same ExHiROM
// layout as cmd/codedump: banks 00-3D and 80-BD alike onto file banks
// 40-7D).
func cpuToFile(bank, off int) int {
	switch {
	case bank >= 0xC0:
		return (bank-0xC0)*0x10000 + off&0xFFFF
	case bank >= 0x80:
		return (bank-0x40)*0x10000 + off&0xFFFF
	default:
		return bank*0x10000 + off&0xFFFF
	}
}

// bossListOffset is 59:FF00.
func bossListOffset() int {
	return cpuToFile(0x59, 0xFF00)
}

// extract reads the 59:FF00 list: real ids up to the FFFF terminator,
// skipping the FFFE fillers.
func extract(rom []byte) (ids []int, filler int, err error) {
	base := bossListOffset()
	for i := 0; i+1 < 0x100; i += 2 {
		w := int(rom[base+i]) | int(rom[base+i+1])<<8
		addr := 0xFF00 + i
		if w == 0xFFFF {
			if addr != 0xFFFE {
				return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("interior FFFF at 59:%04X", addr)
			}
			return ids, filler, nil
		}
		if w == 0xFFFE {
			filler++
			continue
		}
		ids = append(ids, w)
	}
	return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("no FFFF terminator at 59:FFFE")
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 2, 2, "usage: exportbosslist <rom> <data-dir>\n"+
		"   or: exportbosslist <data-dir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	ids, filler, err := extract(rom)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if filler != 3 {
		fail(fmt.Errorf("59:FF00 filler word count %d, want 3 (FFF8-FFFD)", filler))
	}
	dir := args[1]
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(ids)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "boss_double_actions.json"), b, 0o644); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("exportbosslist: %d ids, %d filler words -> %s\n",
		len(ids), filler, filepath.Join(dir, "boss_double_actions.json"))
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}

```

`cmd/exportbosslist/main_test.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// ---- fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------------

// listROM returns a minimal ROM image whose 59:FF00 window holds words;
// extract never indexes outside that window.
func listROM(t *testing.T, words ...uint16) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	if len(words) > 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("%d words overflow the 128-word 59:FF00 window", len(words))
	}
	rom := make([]byte, bossListOffset()+0x100)
	for i, w := range words {
		rom[bossListOffset()+2*i] = byte(w)
		rom[bossListOffset()+2*i+1] = byte(w >> 8)
	}
	return rom
}

// terminatedWords pads head with padID to the full 128-word window and
// closes it with the FFFF terminator at window offset 0xFFFE, the shape
// the shipped ROM list has.
func terminatedWords(head []uint16, padID uint16) []uint16 {
	words := append([]uint16(nil), head...)
	for len(words) < 0x7F {
		words = append(words, padID)
	}
	return append(words, 0xFFFF)
}

// romBytes reads the canonical patched ROM for byte-level parity checks.
func romBytes(t *testing.T) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("ROM not available: %v", err)
	}
	return rom
}

// ---- cpuToFile ----------------------------------------------------------------

// cpuToFile maps the three ExHiROM bank ranges onto the 8MB file: banks
// below 0x80 map flat, banks 0x80-0xBF fold back 0x40 (file banks 40-7D),
// and banks 0xC0-0xFF restart the file (same layout as cmd/codedump).
func TestCPUToFileMapsCPUBanksToROMFileOffsets(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		bank, off, want int
	}{
		{0x59, 0xFF00, 0x59FF00}, // the boss list: 59:FF00
		{0x00, 0x0000, 0x000000},
		{0x7F, 0xFFFF, 0x7FFFFF},
		{0x80, 0x0000, 0x400000},
		{0xBD, 0xFFFF, 0x7DFFFF},
		{0xBF, 0x0001, 0x7F0001},
		{0xC0, 0x0000, 0x000000},
		{0xC6, 0x0200, 0x060200},
		{0xFF, 0x1234, 0x3F1234},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := cpuToFile(c.bank, c.off); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("cpuToFile(%02X:%04X) = %06X, want %06X", c.bank, c.off, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

// bossListOffset pins the list window at CPU 59:FF00, the address the
// setup gate FE:D1BF reads (lda $59FF00,x).
func TestBossListOffsetIsCPU59FF00(t *testing.T) {
	if got := bossListOffset(); got != 0x59FF00 {
		t.Errorf("bossListOffset() = %#X, want 0x59FF00 (CPU 59:FF00)", got)
	}
}

// ---- extract ------------------------------------------------------------------

// extract reads the window as little-endian words in order: FFFE fillers
// are counted and kept out of the ids, a real id of 0x0000 is kept, and
// the FFFF at 0xFFFE ends the list.
func TestExtractReturnsListWordsSkippingFillersUpToTerminator(t *testing.T) {
	head := []uint16{0x143, 0x00C, 0xFFFE, 0x19A, 0x0000, 0xFFFE}
	ids, filler, err := extract(listROM(t, terminatedWords(head, 0x143)...))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("extract: %v", err)
	}
	want := []int{0x143, 0x00C, 0x19A, 0x0000}
	for range 0x7F - len(head) {
		want = append(want, 0x143)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(ids, want) {
		t.Errorf("ids = %v, want %v", ids, want)
	}
	if filler != 2 {
		t.Errorf("filler count %d, want 2", filler)
	}
}

// An FFFF before 0xFFFE is a corrupt list, not an early terminator:
// extract rejects it and reports the offending window address.
func TestExtractRejectsInteriorTerminator(t *testing.T) {
	head := []uint16{0x143, 0xFFFF, 0x19A}
	_, _, err := extract(listROM(t, terminatedWords(head, 0x143)...))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("extract accepted a list with FFFF at 59:FF02")
	}
	if err.Error() != "interior FFFF at 59:FF02" {
		t.Errorf("error = %q, want \"interior FFFF at 59:FF02\"", err)
	}
}

// The scan window ends at 0xFFFE: a list without the FFFF terminator
// there is rejected, not silently truncated.
func TestExtractRejectsListWithoutTerminator(t *testing.T) {
	words := make([]uint16, 0x80) // 128 words, no FFFF anywhere
	for i := range words {
		words[i] = 0x143
	}
	ids, filler, err := extract(listROM(t, words...))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("extract accepted a window with no FFFF terminator (ids %d, filler %d)", len(ids), filler)
	}
	if err.Error() != "no FFFF terminator at 59:FFFE" {
		t.Errorf("error = %q, want \"no FFFF terminator at 59:FFFE\"", err)
	}
}

// ---- ROM parity ---------------------------------------------------------------

// Byte parity against the shipped ROM (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md "The
// immovable revert C2:5665"): the 59:FF00 list decodes to the documented
// shape — 124 real ids plus three FFFE fillers (FFF8-FFFD), ids
// continuous FF00-FFF7 with no interior FFFF.
func TestROMBossListYields124IdsAnd3Fillers(t *testing.T) {
	ids, filler, err := extract(romBytes(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(ids) != 124 {
		t.Fatalf("id count %d, want 124", len(ids))
	}
	if filler != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("filler count %d, want 3 (FFF8-FFFD)", filler)
	}
}

// Membership pins the list as exactly the immovable set: it opens
// 0143 0144 0145 0146 and ships the known top-band leaders, while ids
// outside the set — the other ダンターグ statline 0x14E and a common
// random encounter slot 0x020 — stay out.
func TestROMBossListContainsKnownLeadersNotCommonSlots(t *testing.T) {
	ids, _, err := extract(romBytes(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	leaders := []int{0x143, 0x144, 0x145, 0x146, // the opening four
		0x00C, // ヤマ 12
		0x00F, // アスラ 28
		0x01C, // ザッハーク 169
		0xA9,  // ディープテンタクラー 410
		0x19A, // ドラゴンルーラー 159
		0x9F,  // クジンシー (fixed battle 149's enemy)
		0x14A, // ボクオーン
		0x14C, // サルーイン
		0x15F}
	for _, w := range leaders {
		if !slices.Contains(ids, w) {
			t.Errorf("id %#04X missing from the exported list", w)
		}
	}
	for _, w := range []int{0x14E, 0x020} {
		if slices.Contains(ids, w) {
			t.Errorf("id %#04X must not be in the exported list", w)
		}
	}
}

// ---- main ---------------------------------------------------------------------

// main() ends in os.Exit on every failure, so each case runs the test
// binary again as a subprocess whose helper calls main() with the given
// arguments (joined on newlines).
const runMainEnv = "EXPORTBOSSLIST_RUN_MAIN_ARGS"

// TestMainHelper is the subprocess entry: the parent sets runMainEnv,
// this test swaps os.Args and calls main(). Without the env var it is a
// no-op in the normal test run.
func TestMainHelper(t *testing.T) {
	if args := os.Getenv(runMainEnv); args != "" {
		os.Args = append([]string{"exportbosslist"}, strings.Split(args, "\n")...)
		main()
	}
}

// runMain runs main() in a subprocess with the given arguments and
// returns its combined output and exit code.
func runMain(t *testing.T, args ...string) (string, int) {
	t.Helper()
	return runMainDir(t, "", args...)
}

// runMainDir is runMain with the subprocess working directory set (the
// short form resolves the DefaultROM path against it).
func runMainDir(t *testing.T, cwd string, args ...string) (string, int) {
	t.Helper()
	exe, err := os.Executable()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("locate test binary: %v", err)
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(exe, "-test.run=^TestMainHelper$")
	cmd.Dir = cwd
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), runMainEnv+"="+strings.Join(args, "\n"))
	var out bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout = &out
	cmd.Stderr = &out
	err = cmd.Run()
	code := 0
	if exit, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
		code = exit.ExitCode()
	} else if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("run main subprocess: %v", err)
	}
	return out.String(), code
}

// main() takes the short-fixture list (124 ids, three FFFE fillers,
// terminator at 0xFFFE), writes the ids as a JSON array to
// boss_double_actions.json in a directory it creates, and reports the
// counts and the written path on stdout.
func TestMainWritesBossListJSONIntoCreatedDir(t *testing.T) {
	romPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "rom.sfc")
	rom := listROM(t, terminatedWords([]uint16{0x143, 0xFFFE, 0xFFFE, 0xFFFE}, 0x143)...)
	if err := os.WriteFile(romPath, rom, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	dir := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "out") // does not exist yet: main creates it

	out, code := runMain(t, romPath, dir)
	if code != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("exit code %d, want 0 (output %q)", code, out)
	}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "boss_double_actions.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read exported list: %v", err)
	}
	wantIDs := make([]int, 124) // the head id plus the pad
	for i := range wantIDs {
		wantIDs[i] = 0x143
	}
	want, err := json.Marshal(wantIDs)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(b, want) {
		t.Errorf("boss_double_actions.json = %s, want %s", b, want)
	}
	// the test binary prints its own passing summary after main() returns
	out = strings.TrimSuffix(out, "PASS\n")
	if summary := fmt.Sprintf("exportbosslist: 124 ids, 3 filler words -> %s\n",
		filepath.Join(dir, "boss_double_actions.json")); out != summary {
		t.Errorf("stdout = %q, want %q", out, summary)
	}
}

// main() rejects a list whose filler count differs from the documented
```
