`cmd/exportdialogue/main.go`:

```go
// Command exportdialogue converts events into the JSON the game shell/flow
// loads: one entry per event, ops flattened to what a dialogue box needs
// (text runs, newlines, window/page breaks, terminators).
//
// Usage: exportdialogue <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <out.json>
//
//	exportdialogue <out.json>
//
// The short form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and the glyph
// assignment to data/glyphs_jp.json.
package main

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/glyphs"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
)

const bokunoJPSHA = "4793e1422295b8c13ba81b070b941288d36be339ff20f914652ce63cc06f2da0"

// opJSON is one dialogue-box op. t: text|nl|win|endmes|end|other.
type opJSON struct {
	T string `json:"t"`
	S string `json:"s,omitempty"` // decoded text
	N string `json:"n,omitempty"` // op note, for 'other'
}

type rawOpJSON struct {
	K         string `json:"k"`    // cmd|text|jumpL|jump16
	Addr      string `json:"addr"` // bank:addr of this op
	Hex       string `json:"hex,omitempty"`
	Note      string `json:"note,omitempty"`
	Operand   string `json:"operand,omitempty"` // JSON object string for flag ops
	Text      string `json:"text,omitempty"`
	Target    string `json:"target,omitempty"`     // jumpL/jump16 destination addr
	GateTrue  string `json:"gate_true,omitempty"`  // gates: "addr XX:XXXX" | "event NNNN"
	GateFalse string `json:"gate_false,omitempty"` // gates: same forms
}

type eventJSON struct {
	ID     string      `json:"id"`
	Status string      `json:"status"`
	Ops    []opJSON    `json:"ops,omitempty"`
	Raw    []rawOpJSON `json:"raw,omitempty"`
}

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROMGlyphs(os.Args[1:], "usage: exportdialogue <rom> <glyph-assignment.json> <out.json>\n"+
		"   or: exportdialogue <out.json>\n"+
		"   (defaults: rom patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, glyphs data/glyphs_jp.json)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(rom)
	if got := fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum[:]); got != bokunoJPSHA {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "ROM mismatch: %s\nexpected %s (canonical bokuno_jp, CRC32 7E165025)\n", got, bokunoJPSHA)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	assign, err := glyphs.ParseAssignment(raw)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}

	ops := bokuno.NewOps(rom)
	ops.SetText(bokuno.NewTextDecoder(assign.Order, assign.Slot))
	ops.SetNameTables()

	var out []eventJSON
	for _, id := range nativeIDs() {
		dops, status, ok := ops.DialogueOps(id)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		ev := eventJSON{ID: fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id), Status: status}
		for _, d := range dops {
			switch d.Kind {
			case "text":
				if d.Text != "" {
					ev.Ops = append(ev.Ops, opJSON{T: "text", S: d.Text})
				}
			case "nl":
				ev.Ops = append(ev.Ops, opJSON{T: "nl"})
			case "win":
				ev.Ops = append(ev.Ops, opJSON{T: "win"})
			case "endmes":
				ev.Ops = append(ev.Ops, opJSON{T: "endmes"})
			case "end":
				ev.Ops = append(ev.Ops, opJSON{T: "end"})
			}
		}
		// raw is what the Godot VM executes: every skip/gate target decoded
		_, recs, _, _ := ops.WalkReachable(id)
		for _, rec := range recs {
			if rec.Kind == "jumpL" || rec.Kind == "jump16" || rec.Kind == "join" {
				ev.Raw = append(ev.Raw, rawOpJSON{K: rec.Kind, Addr: rec.Addr, Target: rec.Note})
				continue
			}
			raw := rawOpJSON{K: rec.Kind, Addr: rec.Addr, Note: rec.Note, GateTrue: rec.GateTrue, GateFalse: rec.GateFalse}
			if rec.Kind == "text" {
				raw.Text = rec.Text
				raw.Hex = rec.TextHex
			} else {
				raw.Hex = rec.Hex
				raw.Operand = rec.Operand
			}
			ev.Raw = append(ev.Raw, raw)
		}
		out = append(out, ev)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(args[2], b, 0o644); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	namesPath := strings.TrimSuffix(args[2], ".json") + "_names.json"
	if err := writeNames(ops, namesPath); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("events: %d -> %s (names -> %s)\n", len(out), args[2], namesPath)
}

func writeNames(ops *bokuno.Ops, path string) error {
	type namesJSON struct {
		Actors map[string]string `json:"actors"`
		Places map[string]string `json:"places"`
	}
	n := namesJSON{Actors: map[string]string{}, Places: map[string]string{}}
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		if a := ops.ActorName(i); a != "" {
			n.Actors[strconv.Itoa(i)] = a
		}
		if p := ops.PlaceName(i); p != "" {
			n.Places[strconv.Itoa(i)] = p
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(n)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o644)
}

func nativeIDs() []int {
	var ids []int
	for id := 1; id <= 0xeff; id++ {
		if id>>8 != 0xd {
			ids = append(ids, id)
		}
	}
	for id := 0xc00; id <= 0xcff; id++ {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	for id := 0xe00; id <= 0xeff; id++ {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	for id := 0x4c00; id <= 0x4cff; id++ {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	return ids
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

`cmd/exportmap/bgm.go`:

```go
package main

// Per-map BGM derivation for the Godot map view.
//
// There is no BGM field anywhere in the submap record (the 2-658 record
// walk in docs/triggers.md accounts for every byte; the engine never reads
// one). The track a map plays on arrival travels in the 5-byte movement
// records instead — both the per-map block-4 records and the global
// op-0x11 table at 0x3CFB00 (docs/triggers.md block 4): the little-endian
// word's bits 10-15 carry a 6-bit music request id, applied only when the
// flag byte's bit2 (music change valid) is set and the id differs from the
// current track (WRAM $7EF546; handler at SNES $C0:2C2D-2CFC, plays via
// $C0:BCF2).
//
// The request id reaches the song table through two vanilla hooks, both
// byte-verified and vanilla-identical in bokuno:
//
//  1. request 0x13 means "the current protagonist's town theme": the play
//     wrapper at $FF:064A replaces it with (party-leader char id + 0x13)
//     before playing (vanilla `LDA $7EF000; CLC ADC #$13`; bokuno swaps
//     the inline add for JSL $59EA00 over a per-char request table at file
//     0x606D00). This port has no protagonist selection yet and resolves
//     it as Julian, whose request stays 0x13.
//  2. every request below 0x7C then passes through the in-ROM remap table
//     at file 0x62A2A (SNES $C6:2A2A, byte-identical vanilla vs bokuno):
//     entry 0x13-0x1A = the eight protagonist themes, 0x1B-0x1F = the
//     fixed dungeon themes (魔王殿地下, ジャングル, 海底宮, 水晶の廃墟,
//     氷湖), 0x20 and up identity. Cross-checked against kaerulabo's
//     observed 主人公変更バグ table
//     (http://kaerulabo.web.fc2.com/rs3/data/chara_data_BGM.html) row for
//     row (Lance town = request 0x05 -> track 0x05 聖王の町ランス;
//     protagonist slot 8 -> 0x1B -> 0x46; slot 12 -> 0x1F -> 0x17; slot
//     0x0E -> 0x21 -> 0x21 field theme; slot 0x0F -> 0x22 -> 0x55; slot
//     0xF2 -> (0x13+0xF2)&0xFF = 0x05 -> Lance's theme, kaerulabo row F2).
//
// All higher ids (and the hack's extended tracks 0x5C+) play directly.
// Event-op BGM changes (dispatch word `1D xx` -> handler $C0:C570, same
// play path) are runtime-only and out of scope here: their operands are
// track ids, not per-map data.

import (
	"fmt"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
	"saga3/internal/triggers"
)

const (
	bgmRemapAddr = 0x62A2A // request -> song-table id, SNES $C6:2A2A
	bgmRemapLen  = 0x7C    // ids at or above play as-is

	submapCount = 1024

	// maxTrustedDestinations bounds one map's block-4 contribution. Every
	// map whose decode is trustworthy has at most 59 destinations; every
	// overrunning garbage decode (bokuno-repointed records whose block
	// flags this decoder does not fully know) yields 85+ (measured across
	// all 1024: clean max 59, garbage minimum 85). Beyond the cap the map
	// contributes nothing — its block-4 walk is already nonsense.
	maxTrustedDestinations = 64
)

// bgmIndex maps a target map id to the music request ids of every arrival
// record that requests a music change for it: rows of the global op-0x11
// table plus every map's block-4 destinations.
type bgmIndex map[int][]int

// buildBGMIndex walks the global jump table and every decodable map's
// destinations. Undecodable maps contribute nothing; their count comes
// back so the caller can report skips.
func buildBGMIndex(r mapfmt.ROM) (bgmIndex, int, error) {
	jt, err := triggers.JumpTable(r)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("global jump table: %w", err)
	}
	ix := bgmIndex{}
	for _, d := range jt {
		if d.MusicChange {
			ix[d.TargetMap] = append(ix[d.TargetMap], d.Music)
		}
	}
	skipped := 0
	for id := 0; id < submapCount; id++ {
		t, err := triggers.Decode(r, id)
		if err != nil || len(t.Destinations) > maxTrustedDestinations {
			skipped++
			continue
		}
		for _, d := range t.Destinations {
			if d.MusicChange {
				ix[d.TargetMap] = append(ix[d.TargetMap], d.Music)
			}
		}
	}
	return ix, skipped, nil
}

// resolveTrack returns the song-table id a request id plays, and whether
// the request is in range. Tracks with no ogg (catalog status silent) are
// the Godot side's fallback problem, not the resolver's.
func resolveTrack(r mapfmt.ROM, request int) (int, bool) {
	if request < 0 || request > 0x3F {
		return 0, false
	}
	if request < bgmRemapLen {
		if bgmRemapAddr+request >= bgmRemapAddr+len(r) {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(r[bgmRemapAddr+request]), true
	}
	return request, true
}

// track returns map id's arrival track: the most frequent resolved request
// among its arrival records, ties broken toward the lowest track id. ok is
// false when no arrival record for this map requests a music change (the
// engine keeps the previous track in that case; the Godot side falls back
// to the field theme).
func (ix bgmIndex) track(r mapfmt.ROM, id int) (int, bool) {
	requests, ok := ix[id]
	if !ok || len(requests) == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	counts := map[int]int{}
	for _, req := range requests {
		track, ok := resolveTrack(r, req)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		counts[track]++
	}
	if len(counts) == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	best, bestN := -1, 0
	for track, n := range counts {
		if n > bestN || (n == bestN && track < best) {
			best, bestN = track, n
		}
	}
	return best, true
}
```

`cmd/exportmap/bgm_test.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// bgmROM builds a 8 MiB ExHiROM image with just the regions the resolver
// reads: the remap table at 0x62A2A and the global jump table at 0x3CFB00.
func bgmROM(remap []byte, jump [][5]byte) mapfmt.ROM {
	r := make(mapfmt.ROM, 0x400000)
	copy(r[0x62A2A:], remap)
	for i, rec := range jump {
		p := 0x3CFB00 + i*5
		copy(r[p:p+5], rec[:])
	}
	return r
}

// remapFixture is the real remap table's meaningful prefix: identity below
// 0x13 is broken by {01:0x16, 04:0x13, 0x0D:0x19, 0x11:0x10, 0x12:0x42},
// entries 0x13-0x1A are the protagonist themes, 0x1B-0x1F the dungeon
// themes, then identity.
func remapFixture() []byte {
	t := make([]byte, 0x7C)
	for i := range t {
		t[i] = byte(i)
	}
	for _, e := range [][2]byte{{0x01, 0x16}, {0x04, 0x13}, {0x0D, 0x19}, {0x11, 0x10}, {0x12, 0x42},
		{0x13, 0x04}, {0x14, 0x2C}, {0x15, 0x0F}, {0x16, 0x39}, {0x17, 0x1F}, {0x18, 0x26},
		{0x19, 0x0D}, {0x1A, 0x38}, {0x1B, 0x46}, {0x1C, 0x47}, {0x1D, 0x49}, {0x1E, 0x53}, {0x1F, 0x17}} {
		t[e[0]] = e[1]
	}
	return t
}

func jumpRec(flag byte, target int, music int) [5]byte {
	return [5]byte{flag, byte(target & 0xFF), byte(target>>8)&0x03 | byte(music)<<2, 0, 0}
}

func TestResolveTrack(t *testing.T) {
	r := bgmROM(remapFixture(), nil)
	cases := []struct {
		request int
		want    int
	}{
		{0x00, 0x00}, // mute
		{0x05, 0x05}, // Lance town theme plays as-is
		{0x13, 0x04}, // protagonist tag -> Julian's theme (port default)
		{0x1B, 0x46}, // dungeon theme class -> 魔王殿地下
		{0x21, 0x21}, // field theme identity
		{0x2A, 0x2A}, // ordinary track identity
		{0x3F, 0x3F}, // highest vanilla request
		{0x3E, 0x3E}, // near the top of the 6-bit record field
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, ok := resolveTrack(r, c.request)
		if !ok || got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("resolveTrack(0x%02X) = %d,%v; want %d,true", c.request, got, ok, c.want)
		}
	}
	if _, ok := resolveTrack(r, 0x40); ok {
		t.Fatal("request 0x40 is outside the 6-bit record field and must not resolve")
	}
}

// TestBGMIndexJumpTableArrivals pins the index's global-table half: only
// rows with the music-change bit (flag byte bit2) land in the index, a
// protagonist-theme request (0x13) resolves through the remap table, and
// a map no arrival record names resolves no track.
func TestBGMIndexJumpTableArrivals(t *testing.T) {
	r := bgmROM(remapFixture(), [][5]byte{
		jumpRec(0x05, 0x08A, 0x05), // Lance entry: music change valid
		jumpRec(0x01, 0x08A, 0x13), // facing only, bit2 clear: must be ignored
		jumpRec(0x04, 0x08B, 0x13), // protagonist theme request
	})
	// The fixture has no submap table at 0x380500, so every map's block-4
	// walk skips; the jump-table rows still land in the index.
	ix, _, err := buildBGMIndex(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, ok := ix.track(r, 0x08A); !ok || got != 0x05 {
		t.Fatalf("track(08A) = %d,%v; want 0x05,true", got, ok)
	}
	if got, ok := ix.track(r, 0x08B); !ok || got != 0x04 {
		t.Fatalf("track(08B) = %d,%v; want 0x04 (protagonist resolved),true", got, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := ix.track(r, 0x300); ok {
		t.Fatal("map with no arrivals must not resolve a track")
	}
}

func TestBGMTieBreaksLowest(t *testing.T) {
	r := bgmROM(remapFixture(), [][5]byte{
		jumpRec(0x04, 0x08C, 0x21),
		jumpRec(0x04, 0x08C, 0x05),
	})
	ix, _, err := buildBGMIndex(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, ok := ix.track(r, 0x08C)
	if !ok || got != 0x05 {
		t.Fatalf("track tie = %d,%v; want lowest 0x05,true", got, ok)
	}
}

// TestBGMIndexCountsMajority pins the vote: a request named by two
// arrival records wins over a single lowest-id request (0x05 < 0x21).
func TestBGMIndexCountsMajority(t *testing.T) {
	r := bgmROM(remapFixture(), [][5]byte{
		jumpRec(0x04, 0x08D, 0x21),
		jumpRec(0x04, 0x08D, 0x21),
		jumpRec(0x04, 0x08D, 0x05), // minority, lowest id: must lose
	})
	ix, _, err := buildBGMIndex(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, ok := ix.track(r, 0x08D)
	if !ok || got != 0x21 {
		t.Fatalf("track(08D) = %d,%v; want the majority track 0x21,true", got, ok)
	}
}

// bgmBlock4ROM builds an 8 MiB ExHiROM with one decodable submap record
// (hack table id 5) whose block 4 names map 2 with a music change and
// map 7 without the bit, plus the non-zeroed bound records (ids 6-10)
// that stop the block-4 walk. Record shape per docs/triggers.md: the
// event point list has no flag gate and ends at the first 0xFF.
func bgmBlock4ROM() mapfmt.ROM {
	r := make(mapfmt.ROM, 0x800000)
	setEntry := func(id, file int) {
		v := file + 0xC00000
		r[0x5A6A50+id*3] = byte(v)
		r[0x5A6A50+id*3+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		r[0x5A6A50+id*3+2] = byte(v >> 16)
	}
	rec := 0x383000
	setEntry(5, rec)
	copy(r[rec:], []byte{
		0x00,             // flag1: no layer 2/3
		0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // layer 1 (unused)
		0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, // property pointer: none
		0x00, 0x00, // chipset set, palette set
		0x00,       // object config
		0x00, 0x00, // display position
		0x1F, 0x1F, // size
		0x01,                         // name id
		0x00,                         // 禁止操作
		0x00,                         // flag2
		0x00,                         // flag3
		0xFF,                         // event point list terminator
		0x04, 0x02, 0x00, 0x11, 0x12, // dest: music change, word 0002 -> map 2, request 0, at (11,12)
		0x00, 0x07, 0x00, 0x21, 0x22, // dest: no music bit, map 7 at (21,22)
	})
	for i := 29; i < 34; i++ {
		r[rec+i] = 0x01
	}
	for id := 6; id <= 10; id++ {
		setEntry(id, rec+29+(id-6))
	}
	return r
}

// TestBGMIndexBlock4Arrivals pins the index's per-map half: map 5's
// block-4 destination with the music-change bit lands in the index
// (request 0 -> remap 0x55) and the one without the bit does not.
func TestBGMIndexBlock4Arrivals(t *testing.T) {
	r := bgmBlock4ROM()
	r[bgmRemapAddr] = 0x55 // request 0 resolves to track 0x55
	ix, skipped, err := buildBGMIndex(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if skipped == submapCount {
		t.Fatal("map 5's record decodes; the skip count must not cover every submap")
	}
	if got, ok := ix.track(r, 2); !ok || got != 0x55 {
		t.Fatalf("track(0002) = %d,%v; want 0x55 from map 5's block-4 destination,true", got, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := ix.track(r, 7); ok {
		t.Fatal("block-4 destination without the music-change bit must not index map 7")
	}
}

func TestBuildBGMIndexSkipsUndecodable(t *testing.T) {
	r := bgmROM(remapFixture(), nil) // no submap table at 0x380500: every map skips
	_, skipped, err := buildBGMIndex(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if skipped != submapCount {
		t.Fatalf("skipped = %d, want %d", skipped, submapCount)
	}
}
```

`cmd/exportmap/catalog_test.go`:

```go
package main

// Wiring check over the exported catalog (exports/data/map_catalog.json is
// gitignored generated data, so the test skips without it): every exported
// exit's target map must be a valid submap in the ROM. A target missing
// from the catalog but present in the ROM is an export-skip (render or
// walkable decode failure), reported with the ids, not a wiring bug.

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

func TestExportedExitTargetsExistInROM(t *testing.T) {
	romBytes, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no ROM: %v", err)
	}
	cb, err := os.ReadFile("../../exports/data/map_catalog.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no catalog (run: exportmap <rom> all exports/data): %v", err)
	}
	var cat struct {
		Maps map[string]struct {
			Exits []struct {
				X     int    `json:"x"`
				Y     int    `json:"y"`
				ToMap string `json:"to_map"`
			} `json:"exits"`
		} `json:"maps"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(cb, &cat); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("catalog: %v", err)
	}
	if len(cat.Maps) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("catalog has no maps")
	}
	r := mapfmt.ROM(romBytes)
	total, malformed, dead := 0, 0, 0
	for id, m := range cat.Maps {
		for _, e := range m.Exits {
			total++
			var target int
			if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(e.ToMap, "%x", &target); err != nil || target < 0 || target >= 1024 {
				t.Errorf("exit %s (%d,%d): target id %q does not decode to an in-range submap id", id, e.X, e.Y, e.ToMap)
				malformed++
				continue
			}
			if !mapfmt.HasSubmap(r, target) {
				// bokuno repacked the submap table: records the vanilla ROM
				// keeps valid (checked: 0000, 0001, 002B, 00C2, 0239, 02B8,
				// 02CB) are zeroed or overwritten here, so exits pointing
				// there are dead data of the hack, not a decode bug.
				dead++
			}
		}
	}
	if malformed > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d exits have malformed target ids", malformed)
	}
	t.Logf("checked %d exits over %d catalog maps: %d live (target exports or has a valid header), %d dead targets (bokuno-repacked records)", total, len(cat.Maps), total-dead, dead)
}
```

`cmd/exportmap/figures.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
)

// Field figures from the ROM (docs/sprites.md "VRAM and OAM are
// truthful"): a graphic id resolves to a kind, a tile blob and an OBJ
// palette through one of two tables (C0:7B3F with 5A:A770/A786/A797):
// $EFF7 = FF (5A:BFA8: the leader slot with gid >= 0x70, any other slot
// whose event's high byte, $D9D2, is 0C or 4C) selects 5A:8370 with
// palettes at 5A:8770 + gid*32 (C4:FFDB); otherwise F9:A000, whose 4th
// byte indexes the palettes at EC:8000. The kind picks a sprite set (E1:kind*4, the actor's $D99B);
// the set gives, per facing ($D9A9) and frame ($D9A4), a cell list
// (FF:2AEC): a header byte (rows << 4 | width), then per cell a blob
// tile (+0x80 when the frame pointer has bit 15), FE blank, FF none.
// FF:2B40 uploads the cells to VRAM; a width-5 list is one 32x32 sprite
// (columns 0-3) and three 8x8 sprites in a row below it (column 4,
// rows 0-2), drawn at object (x - 8, y - 33) on 0233's capture.
const (
	figHighTable = 0x5A8370
	figOrigTable = 0x39A000
	figPalTable  = 0x2C8000 // EC:8000, 32 bytes per palette
	figHighPals  = 0x5A8770
	figSetBank   = 0x210000 // bank E1
)

type figSource struct {
	kind    int
	blob    int // file offset
	palette []byte
	palID   int // EC:8000 palette index; -1 for the 5A:8370 table
	gid     int
}

// figPalCycle is the palette FF:A5A1 animates: each step of that gfx
// script loads EC:8000 palette AD + ($14 & 2) / 2 into the OBJ slot that
// holds AD (01E6's graphic 121), so AD figures also get an _AE variant.
const figPalCycle = 0xAD

// figFrames is the length of facing d's frame list (4 for townsfolk,
// 5 for kind 38h, 6 for kind 0Bh); FF:2AEC clamps $D9A4 to it.
func figFrames(rom []byte, src figSource, d int) int {
	b := func(a int) int { return int(rom[figSetBank+a]) }
	set := b(src.kind*4) | b(src.kind*4+1)<<8
	y := 2
	for i := 0; i < d; i++ {
		y += b(set+y) + 1
	}
	return b(set + y)
}

// figFacings counts the facing groups ($D9A9) a set holds: 0-3 are up,
// down, left, right; more follow for some kinds (0321's graphic 224 shows
// facing 4; op 2B poses facing + 5). The groups run on until a list is
// empty, longer than 16, or names a cell list that is not one (a header
// outside 1-8 x 1-8), at most 9.
func figFacings(rom []byte, src figSource) int {
	b := func(a int) int { return int(rom[figSetBank+a]) }
	w := func(a int) int { return b(a) | b(a+1)<<8 }
	set := w(src.kind * 4)
	p96 := w(set)
	y := 2
	d := 0
	for ; d < 9; d++ {
		n := b(set + y)
		if n == 0 || n > 16 {
			break
		}
		ok := true
		for f := 0; f < n; f++ {
			dp := w(p96+b(set+y+1+f)*4) & 0x7FFF
			h := b(dp)
			if h&15 < 1 || h&15 > 8 || h>>4 < 1 || h>>4 > 8 {
				ok = false
			}
		}
		if !ok {
			break
		}
		y += n + 1
	}
	return d
}

// figFacingName is facing d's file stem.
func figFacingName(d int) string {
	if d < 4 {
		return []string{"up", "down", "left", "right"}[d]
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("f%d", d)
}

// figKey is a graphic id and its table (high: 5A:8370).
type figKey struct {
	gid  int
	high bool
}

// dir is the figure folder name: "<gid>", or "h<gid>" for 5A:8370.
func (k figKey) dir() string {
	if k.high {
		return fmt.Sprintf("h%d", k.gid)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d", k.gid)
}

// npcFigKey is 5A:BFA8 for a non-leader slot.
func npcFigKey(gid, event int) figKey {
	hb := event >> 8
	return figKey{gid, hb == 0x0C || hb == 0x4C}
}

func figResolve(rom []byte, k figKey) (figSource, bool) {
	gid := k.gid
	if k.high {
		e := figHighTable + gid*4
		a := int(rom[e+1]) | int(rom[e+2])<<8 | int(rom[e+3])<<16
		if a == 0 {
			return figSource{}, false
		}
		return figSource{kind: int(rom[e]), blob: snesFile(a), palette: rom[figHighPals+gid*32 : figHighPals+gid*32+32], palID: -1, gid: gid}, true
	}
	e := figOrigTable + gid*4
	b1, b2 := int(rom[e+1]), int(rom[e+2])
	if b1 == 0 && b2 == 0 {
		return figSource{}, false
	}
	bank := (b1 & 0x1F) + 0xDA
	addr := bank<<16 | (b1|b2<<8)&0xFFE0
	p := figPalTable + int(rom[e+3])*32
	return figSource{kind: int(rom[e]), blob: snesFile(addr), palette: rom[p : p+32], palID: int(rom[e+3]), gid: gid}, true
}

func snesFile(a int) int {
	b := a >> 16
	if b >= 0xC0 {
		return (b-0xC0)<<16 | a&0xFFFF
	}
	return a
}

// figCells is FF:2AEC for facing d, frame f (clamped to the last): the
// cell list and the frame's OAM layout pointer (the entry's 2nd word).
func figCells(rom []byte, set, d, f int) (width, rows, base int, cells []int, layout int, ok bool) {
	b := func(a int) int { return int(rom[figSetBank+a]) }
	w := func(a int) int { return b(a) | b(a+1)<<8 }
	p96 := w(set)
	y := 2
	for i := 0; i < d; i++ {
		y += b(set+y) + 1
	}
	n := b(set + y)
	if n == 0 {
		return 0, 0, 0, nil, 0, false
	}
	if f >= n {
		f = n - 1
	}
	idx := b(set + y + 1 + f)
	dp := w(p96 + idx*4)
	layout = w(p96 + idx*4 + 2)
	if dp&0x8000 != 0 {
		dp &= 0x7FFF
		base = 0x80
	}
	h := b(dp)
	width, rows = h&15, h>>4
	for i := 0; i < width*rows; i++ {
		cells = append(cells, b(dp+1+i))
	}
	return width, rows, base, cells, layout, width > 0 && rows > 0
}

// figReach bounds a piece's offset from the object; kind 3A's layouts
// hold values like (-7167, -2817), which are not a figure.
const figReach = 128

// figImage composes facing d, frame f as the OAM does: the cell list is
// uploaded one cell per VRAM tile (row r, column c -> tile r*16 + c,
// FF:2B40), and the layout (E1:layout: a count, then per piece x, y
// (signed 16-bit), tile, attribute: bit 0 32x32 else 8x8, 40h H-flip,
// 80h V-flip) places the pieces around the object. The image is cropped
// to the pieces; off is its top-left relative to the object.
func figImage(rom []byte, src figSource, d, f int) (img *image.RGBA, off image.Point, err error) {
	set := int(rom[figSetBank+src.kind*4]) | int(rom[figSetBank+src.kind*4+1])<<8
	width, _, base, cells, layout, ok := figCells(rom, set, d, f)
	if !ok {
		return nil, off, nil
	}
	var pal [16]color.RGBA
	for i := range pal {
		c := int(src.palette[2*i]) | int(src.palette[2*i+1])<<8
		pal[i] = color.RGBA{uint8((c & 31) << 3), uint8((c >> 5 & 31) << 3), uint8((c >> 10 & 31) << 3), 255}
	}
	vram := map[int]int{} // VRAM tile -> blob tile
	for i, t := range cells {
		if t < 0xFE {
			vram[(i/width)*16+i%width] = t + base
		}
	}
	b := func(a int) int { return int(rom[figSetBank+a]) }
	s16 := func(a int) int { return int(int16(uint16(b(a) | b(a+1)<<8))) }
	n := b(layout)
	var box image.Rectangle
	for p := 0; p < n; p++ {
		e := layout + 1 + p*6
		px, py, attr := s16(e), s16(e+2), b(e+5)
		size := 8
		if attr&1 != 0 {
			size = 32
		}
		if px < -figReach || py < -figReach || px > figReach || py > figReach {
			return nil, off, fmt.Errorf("kind %#x facing %d frame %d: piece at (%d,%d)", src.kind, d, f, px, py)
		}
		box = box.Union(image.Rect(px, py, px+size, py+size))
	}
	if box.Empty() {
		return nil, off, nil
	}
	img = image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, box.Dx(), box.Dy()))
	for p := 0; p < n; p++ {
		e := layout + 1 + p*6
		px, py, tile, attr := s16(e)-box.Min.X, s16(e+2)-box.Min.Y, b(e+4), b(e+5)
		size := 8
		if attr&1 != 0 {
			size = 32
		}
		for y := 0; y < size; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < size; x++ {
				sx, sy := x, y
				if attr&0x40 != 0 {
					sx = size - 1 - x
				}
				if attr&0x80 != 0 {
					sy = size - 1 - y
				}
				t, ok := vram[(tile+(sy/8)*16+sx/8)&0xFF]
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				o := src.blob + t*32
				if o+32 > len(rom) {
					continue
				}
				r, bit := sy%8, uint(7-sx%8)
				v := (rom[o+r*2]>>bit)&1 | ((rom[o+r*2+1]>>bit)&1)<<1 | ((rom[o+16+r*2]>>bit)&1)<<2 | ((rom[o+16+r*2+1]>>bit)&1)<<3
				if v != 0 {
					img.SetRGBA(px+x, py+y, pal[v])
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return img, box.Min, nil
}

// writeFigures writes figures/<key>/<facing>[_<frame>].png (facings up,
// down, left, right = $D9A9 0-3; frames 1.. of the walk cycle $D9A4, as
// many as the facing's list holds)
// for every graphic placed on a map, and offsets.json {stem: [x, y]},
// each image's top-left relative to the object. Frames whose layout is
// not a figure (figReach) are skipped and counted in bad.
func writeFigures(rom []byte, dir string, keys map[figKey]bool) (n, bad int, err error) {
	ids := make([]figKey, 0, len(keys))
	for k := range keys {
		ids = append(ids, k)
	}
	sort.Slice(ids, func(i, j int) bool { return ids[i].dir() < ids[j].dir() })
	for _, k := range ids {
		src, ok := figResolve(rom, k)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		sub := filepath.Join(dir, "figures", k.dir())
		wrote, b, err := writeFigureDir(rom, sub, src)
		bad += b
		if err != nil {
			return n, bad, fmt.Errorf("figure %s: %w", k.dir(), err)
		}
		if !wrote {
			continue
		}
		n++
		if src.palID == figPalCycle {
			alt := src
			p := figPalTable + (figPalCycle+1)*32
			alt.palette = rom[p : p+32]
			if _, _, err := writeFigureDir(rom, sub+"_AE", alt); err != nil {
				return n, bad, fmt.Errorf("figure %s_AE: %w", k.dir(), err)
			}
		}
	}
	return n, bad, nil
}

// writeFigureDir writes one graphic's frames and offsets.json into sub;
// frames whose layout is out of reach are reported and counted in bad.
func writeFigureDir(rom []byte, sub string, src figSource) (wrote bool, bad int, err error) {
	offs := map[string][2]int{}
	for d := 0; d < figFacings(rom, src); d++ {
		name := figFacingName(d)
		for f := 0; f < figFrames(rom, src, d); f++ {
			img, off, ferr := figImage(rom, src, d, f)
			if ferr != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s: %v\n", sub, ferr)
				bad++
				continue
			}
			if img == nil {
				continue
			}
			if err := os.MkdirAll(sub, 0o755); err != nil {
				return false, bad, err
			}
			stem := name
			if f > 0 {
				stem = fmt.Sprintf("%s_%d", name, f)
			}
			if err := writePNG(filepath.Join(sub, stem+".png"), img); err != nil {
				return false, bad, err
			}
			offs[stem] = [2]int{off.X, off.Y}
		}
	}
	if len(offs) == 0 {
		return false, bad, nil
	}
	js, err := json.Marshal(offs)
	if err != nil {
		return false, bad, err
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sub, "offsets.json"), js, 0o644); err != nil {
		return false, bad, err
	}
	// meta.json: the palette the figure loads, as the OBJ palette slot list
	// ($D6E2) tells palettes apart: the EC:8000 index, or 1000h + gid for a
	// 5A:8370 graphic's own palette
	pal := src.palID
	if pal < 0 {
		pal = 0x1000 + src.gid
	}
	mj, err := json.Marshal(map[string]int{"palette": pal})
	if err != nil {
		return false, bad, err
	}
	return true, bad, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sub, "meta.json"), mj, 0o644)
}
```

`cmd/exportmap/figures_test.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"os"
	"reflect"
	"testing"
)

// TestFigCellsSailor pins FF:2AEC on the sailors of 0233: set E1:0180,
// facing 2, frame 0 is the cell list whose VRAM upload the emulator
// logged (6040 = 47, 6100-6120 = 38-40, 6140 = 48, 6200-6220 = 41-43,
// 6240 = 49, 6300-6320 = 44-46).
func TestFigCellsSailor(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no rom")
	}
	w, rows, base, cells, _, ok := figCells(rom, 0x0180, 2, 0)
	want := []int{255, 255, 255, 255, 47, 38, 39, 40, 255, 48, 41, 42, 43, 255, 49, 44, 45, 46, 255, 255}
	if !ok || w != 5 || rows != 4 || base != 0 || !reflect.DeepEqual(cells, want) {
		t.Fatalf("cells %d x %d +%#x %v, want 5 x 4 %v", w, rows, base, cells, want)
	}
	src, ok := figResolve(rom, figKey{0x43, false})
	if !ok || src.kind != 1 || src.blob != 0x1EA180 {
		t.Fatalf("graphic 43: %+v", src)
	}
	// 00E3: graphic 222 with event 4CA9 loads blob 62:0000 and OBJ
	// palette 5A:A330; graphic 115 with event 062A loads E0:1680
	k := npcFigKey(222, 0x4CA9)
	src, ok = figResolve(rom, k)
	if !k.high || !ok || src.blob != 0x620000 || &src.palette[0] != &rom[0x5AA330] {
		t.Fatalf("graphic 222 event 4CA9: %v %+v", k, src.blob)
	}
	k = npcFigKey(115, 0x062A)
	src, ok = figResolve(rom, k)
	if k.high || !ok || src.blob != 0x201680 {
		t.Fatalf("graphic 115 event 062A: %v %#x", k, src.blob)
	}
}
```

`cmd/exportmap/main.go`:

```go
// Command exportmap converts rendered submaps into the map-view format
// the shell's field renderer reads: one PNG + map.json per map (image,
// grid size, walkable rows, triggers, NPCs, exits, arrival BGM track)
// plus a map_catalog.json index. Catalog entries carry the map's nameID,
// bgm and its triggers/NPCs/exits, not the walkable grid (that stays in
// per-map map.json). bgm comes from the map's arrival records (bgm.go);
// maps whose arrivals request no music change export without the field
// and the shell falls back to the field theme.
//
// Usage: exportmap <rom> <map-id-hex>[,<map-id-hex>...] <data-dir>
//
//	exportmap <rom> all <data-dir>
//	exportmap <map-id-hex>[,...]|all <data-dir>
//
// The last form defaults the ROM to patches/bokuno_jp.sfc. all exports
// every submap whose header decodes (same skip logic as
// dumpmaps renderAll). Maps that fail to render, whose walkable grid or
// whose trigger data does not decode are counted and reported, not
// fatal; file IO errors abort the run.
package main

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
	"saga3/internal/toolargs"
	"saga3/internal/triggers"
)

func main() {
	args := toolargs.WithROM(os.Args[1:], 3, 3, "usage: exportmap <rom> <map-id-hex>[,...] <data-dir>\n"+
		"   or: exportmap <rom> all <data-dir>\n"+
		"   or: exportmap <map-id-hex>[,...]|all <data-dir>\n"+
		"   (rom default: patches/bokuno_jp.sfc)")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	dir := args[2]
	if err := writeJumps(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeAttrClasses(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeEffectWaves(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeGfxTables(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeFieldTables(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeGraphicHitboxes(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := writeActionBank(rom, dir); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	// The arrival index needs every map's block-4 records regardless of how
	// many maps are exported, so it is built once up front.
	arrivals, skipped, err := buildBGMIndex(mapfmt.ROM(rom))
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if skipped > 0 {
		fmt.Printf("bgm index: %d maps undecodable, no arrivals collected from them\n", skipped)
	}
	if args[1] == "all" {
		exportAll(rom, dir, arrivals)
		return
	}
	catalog := map[string]mapEntry{}
	for _, idStr := range strings.Split(args[1], ",") {
		id, err := strconv.ParseInt(idStr, 16, 32)
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		if !mapfmt.HasSubmap(mapfmt.ROM(rom), int(id)) {
			fmt.Printf("map %04X: skipped (no valid header)\n", id)
			continue
		}
		entry, err := exportOne(rom, dir, int(id), arrivals)
		if err != nil {
			fail(err)
		}
		catalog[fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id)] = entry
	}
	writeCatalog(dir, catalog)
}

// stepError tags which export step failed so all mode can count render
// failures and trigger-decode failures separately; an error without a
// step is a fatal file IO error.
type stepError struct {
	step string
	err  error
}

func (e *stepError) Error() string { return e.step + ": " + e.err.Error() }
func (e *stepError) Unwrap() error { return e.err }

// exportAll exports ids 0..1023, skipping entries with no valid header
// and maps whose render, walkable-grid or trigger decode fails; each
// skip is counted and reported per map, then in the summary line.
func exportAll(rom []byte, dir string, arrivals bgmIndex) {
	catalog := map[string]mapEntry{}
	noHeader, renderFail, walkFail, trigFail := 0, 0, 0, 0
	for id := 0; id < 1024; id++ {
		if !mapfmt.HasSubmap(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id) {
			noHeader++
			continue
		}
		entry, err := exportOne(rom, dir, id, arrivals)
		if err != nil {
			var se *stepError
			if !errors.As(err, &se) {
				fail(err)
			}
			switch se.step {
			case "render":
				renderFail++
			case "walkable":
				walkFail++
			case "triggers":
				trigFail++
			}
			fmt.Printf("map %04X: skipped (%s: %v)\n", id, se.step, se.err)
			continue
		}
		catalog[fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id)] = entry
	}
	fmt.Printf("exported %d maps, skipped %d (no header: %d, render failed: %d, walkable failed: %d, triggers failed: %d)\n",
		len(catalog), noHeader+renderFail+walkFail+trigFail, noHeader, renderFail, walkFail, trigFail)
	writeCatalog(dir, catalog)
	gids := map[figKey]bool{}
	for _, e := range catalog {
		for _, n := range e.NPCs {
			ev, err := strconv.ParseInt(n.Event, 16, 32)
			if err != nil {
				fail(fmt.Errorf("npc event %q: %w", n.Event, err))
			}
			gids[npcFigKey(n.Graphic, int(ev))] = true
		}
	}
	// the eight protagonists' field graphics: FE:961B {graphic, ally,
	// age, title} (cmd/dumpchars)
	prot := map[string]int{}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		g, ally := int(rom[0x3E961B+i*4]), int(rom[0x3E961B+i*4+1])
		prot[fmt.Sprintf("%02X", ally)] = g
		gids[figKey{g, g >= 0x70}] = true // 5A:BFA8, leader slot
	}
	if b, err := json.Marshal(prot); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	} else if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "figures"), 0o755); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	} else if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "figures", "protagonists.json"), b, 0o644); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	nf, bad, err := writeFigures(rom, dir, gids)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("figures: %d of %d placed graphics (%d frames skipped: layout out of reach)\n", nf, len(gids), bad)
}

// exportOne renders, decodes and writes map id, returning its catalog
// entry. Render, walkable-grid and trigger-decode failures come back as
// stepError so the caller can skip them; file IO errors are fatal.
func exportOne(rom []byte, dir string, id int, arrivals bgmIndex) (mapEntry, error) {
	r := mapfmt.ROM(rom)
	trig, err := triggers.Decode(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, &stepError{"triggers", err}
	}
	// The image shows the fresh-game load: unconditional variant layers
	// stamped on (FF:070B); conditional ones export separately below.
	var alwaysLayers []mapfmt.VariantLayer
	for _, v := range trig.Variants {
		if v.Always && v.Kind != 0x80 {
			alwaysLayers = append(alwaysLayers, mapfmt.VariantLayer{Kind: v.Kind, Ptr: v.Ptr})
		}
	}
	chests, layers, props, _ := trig.FreshLoad()
	rendered, err := mapfmt.RenderSubmapVariants(r, id, alwaysLayers, props)
	if err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, &stepError{"render", err}
	}
	// Walkable re-decodes the property layer, which HasSubmap does not
	// validate, so it can fail on maps whose header and render are fine.
	// The grid is the fresh-game load: closed chests and the
	// unconditional variants; conditional variants depend on runtime
	// flags.
	walk, err := mapfmt.WalkableVariants(r, id, chests, layers, props)
	if err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, &stepError{"walkable", err}
	}
	off, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, err
	}
	h, err := mapfmt.ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, err
	}
	var bgm *int
	if track, ok := arrivals.track(r, id); ok {
		bgm = &track
	}
	entry := buildEntry(r, id, rendered, h, trig, bgm)
	for i := range entry.NPCs {
		entry.NPCs[i].Hitbox = hitboxFor(r, entry.NPCs[i].Graphic)
	}
	// Chip value table (record flag3 bit 0x04) is additive metadata;
	// maps whose record walk fails for it export without the field.
	chipVals, err := mapfmt.ChipValues(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		chipVals = nil
	}
	if rendered.Indexed != nil {
		entry.LayerDims = rendered.Indexed.Dims
	}
	words := func(ws []mapfmt.Word) []int {
		out := make([]int, len(ws))
		for i, w := range ws {
			out[i] = int(uint16(w))
		}
		return out
	}
	for i, c := range chests {
		cp, err := mapfmt.ChestWords(r, id, alwaysLayers, props, c)
		if err != nil {
			return mapEntry{}, &stepError{"chest words", err}
		}
		e := &entry.Chests[i]
		e.Layer = cp.Layer
		e.Rect = [4]int{cp.Rect.Min.X, cp.Rect.Min.Y, cp.Rect.Dx(), cp.Rect.Dy()}
		e.Closed, e.OpenLoad, e.Open = words(cp.Closed), words(cp.OpenLoad), words(cp.Open)
	}
	if err := writeOne(r, dir, id, rendered, walk, chipVals, entry); err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, err
	}
	if err := writeConditionalVariants(r, dir, id, trig, alwaysLayers); err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, err
	}
	if err := writeTileAnims(r, dir, id, trig, alwaysLayers, props); err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, err
	}
	if err := writeFootprints(r, dir, id, alwaysLayers, layers, props, chests); err != nil {
		return mapEntry{}, err
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"chest_closed.png", "chest_open.png"} {
		if rmErr := os.Remove(filepath.Join(dir, "maps", fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id), name)); rmErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rmErr) {
			return mapEntry{}, rmErr
		}
	}
	return entry, nil
}

// buildEntry assembles the catalog entry for one exported map: image
// path, grid size, nameID, arrival track and triggers/NPCs/exits. It is
// pure so the catalog shape is testable without a ROM.
func buildEntry(r mapfmt.ROM, id int, rendered *mapfmt.Rendered, h mapfmt.Header, trig *triggers.MapTriggers, bgm *int) mapEntry {
	entry := mapEntry{
		Image:  fmt.Sprintf("maps/%04X/map.png", id),
		Width:  rendered.Width,
		Height: rendered.Height,
		NameID: int(h.NameID),
		BGM:    bgm,

		EncounterPartyBase: trig.EncounterPartyBase,
		Bounds:             mapBounds(h, rendered.Width, rendered.Height),
		EdgeEvents:         trig.EdgeEvents,
		Slope:              trig.Slope,
		Screen:             trig.Screen,
		Effect:             trig.Effect,
		GfxAnims:           gfxAnims(r, h, trig),
		PalBank:            int(h.Flags1 & 3),
		MapType:            trig.Type,
		Camera:             cameraBounds(h, rendered.Width, rendered.Height),
		Open:               h.Controls&0x80 != 0,
		CamShift:           camShift(h),
		BG3Top:             h.Controls&0x20 != 0,
		Drift:              drift(r, trig),
		Parallax:           trig.HasScroll && trig.Scroll[0]&0x40 != 0,
		ScrollMode:         scrollMode(trig),
	}
	for _, c := range trig.Chests {
		entry.Chests = append(entry.Chests, chestEntry{X: c.X, Y: c.Y, Flags: c.Flags, Content: c.ContentID, OpenFlag: c.OpenFlagID, Event: c.EventID})
	}
	for _, t := range trig.Triggers {
		entry.Triggers = append(entry.Triggers, e{X: t.X, Y: t.Y, Event: fmt.Sprintf("%04X", t.EventID)})
	}
	for i, n := range trig.NPCs {
		entry.NPCs = append(entry.NPCs, npcEntry{X: n.X, Y: n.Y, Event: fmt.Sprintf("%04X", n.EventID), Graphic: int(n.Graphic),
			Index: i, Facing: n.Facing >> 6, Speed: (n.Facing & 0x30) >> 4,
			Script:    ((n.Facing&0x0C)<<6 | n.Quality>>8) & 0x0FFF,
			GateFlags: gateFlags(n.Quality&0xFF, n.Graphic),
			Judged:    n.Judged, PlaceID: n.PlaceID, PlaceLo: n.PlaceLo})
	}
	for _, x := range trig.Exits {
		entry.Exits = append(entry.Exits, e{X: x.X, Y: x.Y,
			ToMap: fmt.Sprintf("%04X", x.TargetMap), ToX: x.TargetX, ToY: x.TargetY})
	}
	for _, d := range trig.Destinations {
		entry.Destinations = append(entry.Destinations, newJumpEntry(r, d))
	}
	return entry
}

type e struct {
	X       int    `json:"x"`
	Y       int    `json:"y"`
	Event   string `json:"event,omitempty"`
	ToMap   string `json:"to_map,omitempty"`
	ToX     int    `json:"to_x,omitempty"`
	ToY     int    `json:"to_y,omitempty"`
	Graphic int    `json:"graphic,omitempty"` // NPC sprite graphic id (0x5A8370 table)
}

// npcEntry is one map NPC with the fields the loader turns into its
// object slot (C0:4A79-4C96, docs/action-scripts.md "NPC spawn"): the
// record entry index (the slot tag, also the start stagger), facing,
// speed row and action script from the facing byte and Quality, and
// the placement gate for judged entries.
type npcEntry struct {
	X       int    `json:"x"`
	Y       int    `json:"y"`
	Event   string `json:"event,omitempty"`
	Graphic int    `json:"graphic,omitempty"` // NPC sprite graphic id (0x5A8370 table)
	Index   int    `json:"index"`
	Facing  int    `json:"facing"`
	Speed   int    `json:"speed"`
	Script  int    `json:"script"`
	Judged  bool   `json:"judged"`
	PlaceID int    `json:"place_id"`
	PlaceLo int    `json:"place_lo"`
	// GateFlags is the object's initial $D9B2 low bits (C0:4B30, from
	// the Quality word's low byte): bits 4-5 = 0x10 pick the gate rule
	// that blocks on class bit 4 only, bits 4-7 otherwise AND the class.
	GateFlags int `json:"gate_flags"`
	// Hitbox is the collision shape per facing (C0:7892): x/y offset
	// from the object's position, then rows of mask bytes, 1 bit = 4 px.
	Hitbox [4]hitbox `json:"hitbox"`
}

type hitbox struct {
	XOff int     `json:"xoff"`
	YOff int     `json:"yoff"`
	Rows [][]int `json:"rows"`
}

func gateFlags(q, graphic int) int {
	f := q&0x0C | q>>6
	if q&0x30 != 0x30 {
		f |= q & 0x30
	}
	if graphic >= 0xFD { // C0:7B0A
		f |= 0x0C
	}
	return f
}

// hitboxFor follows the loader's shape chain (C0:7B3F-7B71): graphics
// FD-FF take fixed tables (C0:7B01), the others sprite id =
// F9A000[graphic*4] (5A:A786 reads it while $EFF7 != FF, the live case:
// 0149's slots get $D9D0 0F96/0FB2 from it; 5A8370 is the $EFF7 = FF
// table), shape table $D9D0 = E1:0002[sprite*4] (less 0x200 past 0x200,
// 5A:D830), record = E1:[$D9D0 + facing*2] = x offset, y offset, width
// bytes, height rows, then the mask rows.
func hitboxFor(r mapfmt.ROM, graphic int) [4]hitbox {
	const e1 = 0x210000
	var d0 int
	switch {
	case graphic == 0xFF: // C0:7B34: no sprite, the party's shape
		d0 = 0x0F82
	case graphic >= 0xFD: // C0:7B29
		d0 = 0x0F8C
	default:
		sprite := int(r[0x39A000+graphic*4])
		x := sprite * 4
		if x >= 0x200 {
			x -= 0x200
		}
		d0 = int(r[e1+x+2]) | int(r[e1+x+3])<<8
	}
	var out [4]hitbox
	for f := 0; f < 4; f++ {
		rec := e1 + (int(r[e1+d0+f*2]) | int(r[e1+d0+f*2+1])<<8)
		h := hitbox{XOff: int(int16(uint16(r[rec]) | uint16(r[rec+1])<<8)), YOff: int(int16(uint16(r[rec+2]) | uint16(r[rec+3])<<8))}
		w, ht := int(r[rec+4]), int(r[rec+5])
		for row := 0; row < ht; row++ {
			var bytes []int
			for c := 0; c < w; c++ {
				bytes = append(bytes, int(r[rec+6+row*w+c]))
			}
			h.Rows = append(h.Rows, bytes)
		}
		out[f] = h
	}
	return out
}

type chestEntry struct {
	X        int `json:"x"`
	Y        int `json:"y"`
	Flags    int `json:"flags"`
	Content  int `json:"content"`
	OpenFlag int `json:"open_flag"`
	Event    int `json:"event"`
	// The chest as tile words (mapfmt.ChestWords): layer 0 BG1, 1 BG2,
	// 2 BG3; rect [x, y, w, h]; closed / open_load / open words of rect.
	Layer    int    `json:"layer"`
	Rect     [4]int `json:"rect,omitempty"`
	Closed   []int  `json:"closed,omitempty"`
	OpenLoad []int  `json:"open_load,omitempty"`
	Open     []int  `json:"open,omitempty"`
}

// mapEntry is one map_catalog.json value.
type mapEntry struct {
	Image  string `json:"image"`
	Width  int    `json:"width"`
	Height int    `json:"height"`
	NameID int    `json:"name_id"`
	BGM    *int   `json:"bgm,omitempty"` // arrival track id (bgm.go), absent when none
	// $D2FE -> $1308: the encounter party term's base (triggers.MapTriggers)
	EncounterPartyBase int        `json:"encounter_party_base"`
	Triggers           []e        `json:"triggers"`
	NPCs               []npcEntry `json:"npcs"`
	Exits              []e        `json:"exits"`
	// block-4 destination records: event op `10 xx` moves to record xx
	Destinations []jumpEntry `json:"destinations"`
	// Bounds is the gate's tile window [x0, y0, x1, y1) (C0:4F6E-4FE8:
	// the header's position/size bytes, then x0 += 2, y0 += 4, x1 -= 2,
	// y1 -= 1); C0:5841-5857 blocks steps outside it on maps that do
	// not wrap.
	Bounds [4]int `json:"bounds"`
	// Chests are the record's treasure chests (C0:3E88, opened at
	// C0:A920): the open flag is a bit index into the flag array at
	// $F4EA; flags&0x0C picks the content type (0 item EF01 -> event
	// 0108, 4 money content*{1,10,100,1000}[flags&3] -> event 0208,
	// 8 the chest's own event word).
	Chests []chestEntry `json:"chests"`
	// EdgeEvents are the flag2-bit6 words [north, south, west, east]
	// ($D0DF/$D0E1/$D0E3/$D0E5): the party's step onto the bounds edge
	// in that direction enqueues the word (C0:5970-5A3E); all zero when
	// the map has none ($D0DE = 0).
	EdgeEvents [4]int `json:"edge_events"`
	// Slope: the party's map-wide slope byte ($D2FB), -1 for none.
	Slope int `json:"slope"`
	// Screen: the flag3-bit-4 screen setup (triggers.Screen), nil when
	// the map has none (17/17, no colour math).
	Screen *triggers.Screen `json:"screen"`
	// Effect: the screen effect the graphics animation list selects
	// (triggers.ScreenEffect), 0 for none.
	Effect int `json:"effect"`
	// GfxAnims: the graphics animation list (FF:9935) with each palette
	// entry's ROM palette id resolved; PalBank is header flags1 & 3
	// ($D2D8), the bank of those ids (EC:A400 + bank*0x2000).
	GfxAnims []gfxAnim `json:"gfx_anims"`
	PalBank  int       `json:"pal_bank"`
	// MapType: $D2D7 (triggers.MapTriggers.Type).
	MapType int `json:"map_type"`
	// Camera: the leader-position window the camera follows in, map px
	// [x min, y min, x max, y max] ($D2E8, $D2E6, $D2EC, $D2EA; C0:4F6E).
	Camera [4]int `json:"camera"`
	// Open: Controls bit 7, an open map ($D0DD): the camera wraps.
	Open bool `json:"open"`
	// CamShift: 12 with Controls bit 4, which starts BG scroll at -12 and
	// $D6DD 12 px left (C0:A33F): the leader sits 12 px further right.
	CamShift int `json:"cam_shift"`
	// BG3Top: Controls bit 5 sets $2105 bit 3 (C0:C562), BG3's priority
	// bit: BG3 draws above BG1/BG2; without it below them.
	BG3Top bool `json:"bg3_top"`
	// LayerDims: each layer's size in tiles (mapfmt.Indexed.Dims).
	LayerDims [3][2]int `json:"layer_dims"`
	// Drift: BG2's own scroll (triggers.MapTriggers.Scroll): per axis a
	// 16-bit rotating mask and the px added at each carry, applied every
	// field frame (C0:8801); zero masks for none.
	Drift [4]int `json:"drift"`
	// Parallax: $D976 bit 6, BG2 steps by C0:82F5 while the camera
	// follows the leader (C0:8478, C0:833E).
	Parallax bool `json:"parallax"`
	// ScrollMode: $D977 & 3 (C0:40ED), -1 without the scroll pair. Mode 3
	// ($35 = 9) scrolls BG3 horizontally at twice the camera's rate.
	ScrollMode int `json:"scroll_mode"`
}

// gfxAnim is one graphics animation entry. Chip is the chip id, or for
// palette scripts (first byte 0x40-0xFF) the CGRAM palette number;
// PalID is FC:F400[set*7 + palette - 1] for those (FF:9BFB, FF:9CAD).
type gfxAnim struct {
	Script int `json:"script"`
	Chip   int `json:"chip"`
	PalID  int `json:"pal_id"`
}

// gfxAnims resolves the list's palette ids for the field's VM.
func gfxAnims(r mapfmt.ROM, h mapfmt.Header, trig *triggers.MapTriggers) []gfxAnim {
	out := make([]gfxAnim, 0, len(trig.GfxAnims))
	for _, g := range trig.GfxAnims {
		a := gfxAnim{Script: g.Script, Chip: g.Chip}
		if g.Chip >= 1 && g.Chip <= 7 {
			a.PalID = int(r[paletteSetTable+int(h.PaletteSet)*7+g.Chip-1])
		}
		out = append(out, a)
	}
	return out
}

func writeOne(r mapfmt.ROM, dir string, id int, rendered *mapfmt.Rendered, walk *mapfmt.WalkGrid, chipVals map[int]int, entry mapEntry) error {
	sub := filepath.Join(dir, "maps", fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id))
	if err := os.MkdirAll(sub, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := writeOver(filepath.Join(sub, "map_over.png"), rendered.Over); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := writeBG3(filepath.Join(sub, "map_bg3.png"), rendered.BG3); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := writeTiles(filepath.Join(sub, "tiles.bin"), rendered.Indexed); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := writePNG(filepath.Join(sub, "chr.png"), rendered.Indexed.CHR); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := writePNG(filepath.Join(sub, "cgram.png"), cgramImage(rendered.Indexed)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	pngPath := filepath.Join(sub, "map.png")
	f, err := os.Create(pngPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	encErr := png.Encode(f, rendered.Under)
	closeErr := f.Close()
	if encErr != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", pngPath, encErr)
	}
	if closeErr != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("close %s: %w", pngPath, closeErr)
	}

	rows := make([][]int, walk.H)
	walkCount := 0
	for y, row := range walk.Walk {
		rows[y] = make([]int, walk.W)
		for x, w := range row {
			if w {
				rows[y][x] = 1
				walkCount++
			}
		}
	}
	meta := map[string]any{
		"image":     entry.Image,
		"tile_size": 16,
		"width":     entry.Width,
		"height":    entry.Height,
		"walkable":  rows,
		"attr":      byteRows(walk.Attr),
		"low":       byteRows(walk.Low),
		"triggers":  entry.Triggers,
		// $D2FE -> $1308: the encounter party term's base and the battle's
		// $1308 & 0F (map_view.encounter_party_base)
		"encounter_party_base": entry.EncounterPartyBase,
		"npcs":                 entry.NPCs,
		"exits":                entry.Exits,
		"destinations":         entry.Destinations,
		"bounds":               entry.Bounds,
		"edge_events":          entry.EdgeEvents,
		"slope":                entry.Slope,
		"screen":               entry.Screen,
		"effect":               entry.Effect,
		"gfx_anims":            entry.GfxAnims,
		"pal_bank":             entry.PalBank,
		"map_type":             entry.MapType,
		"camera":               entry.Camera,
		"open":                 entry.Open,
		"cam_shift":            entry.CamShift,
		"bg3_top":              entry.BG3Top,
		"layer_dims":           entry.LayerDims,
		"drift":                entry.Drift,
		"parallax":             entry.Parallax,
		"scroll_mode":          entry.ScrollMode,
		"chests":               entry.Chests,
	}
	if entry.BGM != nil {
		meta["bgm"] = *entry.BGM
	}
	if len(chipVals) > 0 {
		// Per-chip value table (docs/map-format.md, chip value table):
		// key = decimal chip id, value = the 6-bit table value. On the
		// maps checked, water chips share value 8 (map 0x02's canal
		// chips 106/122; map 0x04's sea chips 0x180/0x187); the value's
		// game meaning (2-658's animation-pattern guess) is unverified.
		cvs := map[string]int{}
		for c, v := range chipVals {
			cvs[fmt.Sprintf("%d", c)] = v
		}
		meta["chip_values"] = cvs
	}
	mb, err := json.Marshal(meta)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sub, "map.json"), append(mb, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Printf("map %04X: %dx%d tiles, %d/%d walkable, %d triggers, %d npcs, %d exits -> %s\n",
		id, entry.Width, entry.Height, walkCount, walk.W*walk.H,
		len(entry.Triggers), len(entry.NPCs), len(entry.Exits), sub)
	return nil
}

// jumpEntry is one jump_table.json record: where event op `11 xx` sends
// the party (global table 0x3CFB00, index xx).
type jumpEntry struct {
	ToMap string `json:"to_map"`
	ToX   int    `json:"to_x"`
	ToY   int    `json:"to_y"`
	// Stay is flag bit 6: the move only places the leader at (to_x,
	// to_y) on the current map; to_map is never loaded (C0:C270 ->
	// C2B6). Jump record E4 (to 0331) is the only one in the global
	// table.
	Stay bool `json:"stay,omitempty"`
	// Arrival is flag bits 4-5 ($D0A6 & 30h, C0:C371): 10h and 20h pick
	// special arrivals; any other value on a type-1 map runs C0:C3D9
	// (leader x - 4, then the FF:B1E4 sequence through objOp 51).
	Arrival int `json:"arrival,omitempty"`
	// NoFade is flag bit 7 ($D013 = $D0A6 & 80h, C0:C237): the fade-in
	// C0:0A22 is skipped, so a type-1 arrival's objOp 51 runs 2 field
	// ticks after the install instead of 16 (027F via 02B6#5: 2; 027A,
	// 027C: 16).
	NoFade bool `json:"no_fade,omitempty"`
	// Music is the resolved track the record plays on arrival (word bits
	// 10-15 when flag bit 2 is set, C0:2C2D -> C0:BCF2, through the
	// remap in resolveTrack); absent = the record changes no music, the
	// current track keeps playing (0250 via 084C's record: song 33).
	Music *int `json:"music,omitempty"`
	// Facing is flag bits 0-1: the leader's facing after the load
	// (C0:C333 LDA $D0A6 / AND #3 / STA $D9A9; 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3
	// right). The opening's 024A move 01 (flags 86) lands facing left.
	Facing int `json:"facing"`
}

func newJumpEntry(r mapfmt.ROM, d triggers.Destination) jumpEntry {
	j := jumpEntry{ToMap: fmt.Sprintf("%04X", d.TargetMap), ToX: d.TargetX, ToY: d.TargetY, Stay: d.DestFlags&0x40 != 0, Arrival: int(d.DestFlags & 0x30), NoFade: d.DestFlags&0x80 != 0, Facing: int(d.DestFlags & 3)}
	if d.MusicChange {
		if t, ok := resolveTrack(r, d.Music); ok {
			j.Music = &t
		}
	}
	return j
}

// actionBankOffset is bank F8 (file 0x380000): the object action-script
// pointer table F8:0000 and the scripts (docs/action-scripts.md), copied
// whole for the port's action-script runner.
const actionBankOffset = 0x380000

// writeTiles writes the map's tile words for the field's tile shader:
// u16 W, u16 H (tiles), then BG1, BG2, BG3 as W*H little-endian words
// each, zeros for an absent layer.
func writeTiles(path string, ix *mapfmt.Indexed) error {
	b := make([]byte, 4, 4+3*2*ix.W*ix.H)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b, uint16(ix.W))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[2:], uint16(ix.H))
	for _, grid := range ix.Words {
		for i := 0; i < ix.W*ix.H; i++ {
			var w uint16
			if grid != nil {
				w = grid[i]
			}
			b = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(b, w)
		}
	}
	return os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o644)
}

// cgramImage lays CGRAM's BG palettes out as a 128x1 strip, colour p*16+i.
func cgramImage(ix *mapfmt.Indexed) *image.RGBA {
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 128, 1))
	for p, pal := range ix.CGRAM {
		for i, c := range pal.Colors {
			img.SetRGBA(p*16+i, 0, color.RGBA{c[0], c[1], c[2], 255})
		}
	}
	return img
}

// writeBG3 writes layer 3 alone (drawn above everything, or added onto
// the screen on maps whose screen setup puts BG3 on the sub screen), or
// removes a stale file when the map has no layer 3.
func writeBG3(path string, img *image.RGBA) error {
	if img == nil {
		if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return err
		}
		return nil
	}
	return writePNG(path, img)
}

// writeOver writes the tiles drawn above field sprites (word bit 13),
// or removes a stale file when the map has none.
func writeOver(path string, img *image.RGBA) error {
	for i := 3; i < len(img.Pix); i += 4 {
		if img.Pix[i] != 0 {
			return writePNG(path, img)
		}
	}
	if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

// writeTileAnims writes the map's tile animations (mapfmt.TileAnimations)
// as tile_anims.json plus two atlases of frame patches stacked top to
// bottom: anims.png (below the field sprites) and anims_over.png (above).
// Each entry: rect [x, y, w, h] in tiles, timer, start, script (FF:1F04
// bytes through the 0x80 loop) and frames {value: atlas y in pixels}.
// Maps without animations get none (stale files are removed).
func writeTileAnims(r mapfmt.ROM, dir string, id int, trig *triggers.MapTriggers, always []mapfmt.VariantLayer, props []int) error {
	sub := filepath.Join(dir, "maps", fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id))
	var specs []mapfmt.AnimSpec
	for _, a := range trig.Animations {
		specs = append(specs, mapfmt.AnimSpec{Object: a.Object, Kind: a.Kind})
	}
	anims, err := mapfmt.TileAnimations(r, id, always, props, specs)
	if err != nil || len(anims) == 0 {
		for _, f := range []string{"tile_anims.json", "anims.png", "anims_over.png"} {
			if rmErr := os.Remove(filepath.Join(sub, f)); rmErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rmErr) {
				return rmErr
			}
		}
		return nil // a map whose animations do not decode keeps its still image
	}
	// stale patch images from the baked-sprite field
	for _, f := range []string{"anims.png", "anims_over.png"} {
		if rmErr := os.Remove(filepath.Join(sub, f)); rmErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rmErr) {
			return rmErr
		}
	}
	// Frames: script value -> the restamped layer's words in Rect,
	// row-major; Layer 0 BG1, 1 BG2, 2 BG3.
	type entry struct {
		Rect   [4]int           `json:"rect"`
		Layer  int              `json:"layer"`
		Timer  int              `json:"timer"`
		Start  int              `json:"start"`
		Script []int            `json:"script"`
		Frames map[string][]int `json:"frames"`
	}
	var out []entry
	for _, a := range anims {
		layer, ok := map[int]int{0x40: 0, 0x20: 1, 0x10: 2}[a.LayerKind]
		if !ok {
			return fmt.Errorf("map %04X: animation on layer kind %#x", id, a.LayerKind)
		}
		e := entry{Rect: [4]int{a.Rect.Min.X, a.Rect.Min.Y, a.Rect.Dx(), a.Rect.Dy()}, Layer: layer, Timer: a.Timer, Start: a.Start, Script: a.Script, Frames: map[string][]int{}}
		for v, words := range a.FrameWords {
			ws := make([]int, 0, a.Rect.Dx()*a.Rect.Dy())
			for y := a.Rect.Min.Y; y < a.Rect.Max.Y; y++ {
				for x := a.Rect.Min.X; x < a.Rect.Max.X; x++ {
					ws = append(ws, int(uint16(words[image.Pt(x, y)])))
				}
			}
			e.Frames[fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)] = ws
		}
		out = append(out, e)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sub, "tile_anims.json"), append(b, '\n'), 0o644)
}

// writeFootprints writes footprints.json {grid: rows, >= 0 on footprint
// tiles (mapfmt.FootprintPatches), layer}: a step there adds facing+1
// to that layer's word (C0:7C75). Maps without footprint tiles get none.
func writeFootprints(r mapfmt.ROM, dir string, id int, always []mapfmt.VariantLayer, ptrs, props []int, chests []mapfmt.ChestStamp) error {
	sub := filepath.Join(dir, "maps", fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id))
	fs, err := mapfmt.FootprintPatches(r, id, always, ptrs, props, chests)
	if err != nil || fs == nil {
		for _, f := range []string{"footprints.json", "footprints.png", "footprints_over.png"} {
			if rmErr := os.Remove(filepath.Join(sub, f)); rmErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rmErr) {
				return rmErr
			}
		}
		return nil
	}
	for _, f := range []string{"footprints.png", "footprints_over.png"} {
		if rmErr := os.Remove(filepath.Join(sub, f)); rmErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rmErr) {
			return rmErr
		}
	}
	off, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	h, err := mapfmt.ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// grid: >= 0 on footprint tiles; layer: 0 BG1, 1 BG2 (Controls bit 3)
	layer := 0
	if h.Controls&0x08 != 0 {
		layer = 1
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"grid": fs.Grid, "layer": layer})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sub, "footprints.json"), append(b, '\n'), 0o644)
}

func scrollMode(trig *triggers.MapTriggers) int {
	if !trig.HasScroll {
		return -1
	}
	return trig.Scroll[1] & 3
}

func camShift(h mapfmt.Header) int {
	if h.Controls&0x10 != 0 {
		return 12
	}
	return 0
}

// driftTable is FF:2A98: 4-byte entries (mask, speed).
const driftTable = 0x3F2A98

// drift returns [x mask, x speed, y mask, y speed] (C0:4131-41A9).
func drift(r mapfmt.ROM, trig *triggers.MapTriggers) [4]int {
	var d [4]int
	if r == nil || !trig.HasScroll {
		return d
	}
	a, b := trig.Scroll[0], trig.Scroll[1]
	if mode := b & 3; mode == 1 || mode == 3 || b&0x40 == 0 {
		return d
	}
	entry := func(o int) (int, int) {
		m := int(r[driftTable+o]) | int(r[driftTable+o+1])<<8
		s := int(int16(uint16(r[driftTable+o+2]) | uint16(r[driftTable+o+3])<<8))
		return m, s
	}
	if a&0x0C != 0 {
		d[0], d[1] = entry(b & 0x0C)
		if a&0x08 != 0 {
			d[1] = -d[1]
		}
	}
	if a&0x30 != 0 {
		d[2], d[3] = entry((a & 3) * 4)
		if a&0x20 != 0 {
			d[3] = -d[3]
		}
	}
	return d
}

// cameraBounds is C0:4F6E's follow window from the header: x from
// (PosX + 0x11)*8 to (SizeX - 0x11)*8, y from (PosY + 0x10)*8 to
// (SizeY - 0x0D)*8, a SizeY below 0x20 counting as 0x1C.
func cameraBounds(h mapfmt.Header, w, ht int) [4]int {
	sy := int(h.SizeY)
	if sy < 0x20 {
		sy = 0x1C
	}
	c := [4]int{(int(h.PosX) + 0x11) * 8, (int(h.PosY) + 0x10) * 8, (int(h.SizeX) - 0x11) * 8, (sy - 0x0D) * 8}
	if w*ht*2 == 0x800 {
		c[2]++ // C0:488E: a 32x32 map's x max one pixel on
	}
	return c
}

// mapBounds is the gate window C0:4F6E builds from the header, widened
// by 2 tiles left and right when Controls bit 4 is set (C0:3D59-3D62).
//
// C0:4884-48BC then fixes x1 by the map's size ($D0C5, bytes) and width
// ($D0C4 tiles): a 32x32 map's x1 one tile on; otherwise, without
// Controls bit 4, a window narrower than 1Eh tiles opens to x0 + 1Fh,
// clamped to width - 1 (0267: header x1 29, the engine's $D2F1 33).
func mapBounds(h mapfmt.Header, w, ht int) [4]int {
	b := [4]int{int(h.PosX) + 2, int(h.PosY) + 4, int(h.SizeX) - 2, int(h.SizeY) - 1}
	if h.Controls&0x10 != 0 {
		b[0] -= 2
		b[2] += 2
	}
	if w*ht*2 == 0x800 {
		b[2]++
	} else if h.Controls&0x10 == 0 && b[2]-b[0] < 0x1E {
		b[2] = min(b[0]+0x1F, w-1)
	}
	return b
}

// byteRows converts a byte grid to ints: encoding/json writes []byte
// as base64.
func byteRows(g [][]byte) [][]int {
	out := make([][]int, len(g))
	for y, row := range g {
		out[y] = make([]int, len(row))
		for x, b := range row {
			out[y][x] = int(b)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// attrClassOffset is F9:A400: 4 bytes per attr byte, which C0:5BC6
// loads into $D8FC-$D8FF for the object gate (C0:57FF).
const attrClassOffset = 0x39A400

func writeAttrClasses(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "attr_class.bin"), rom[attrClassOffset:attrClassOffset+256*4], 0o644)
}

// fieldTablesOffset is FF:6500-69FF: the object speed rows (FF:65C3
// move pattern, 65CC steps per tile), axis patterns (65E8), per-row
// velocities (65F0 + row*64 + dir*4, C0:6323) and walk offsets (6700),
// which the action runner reads as the engine does, past row 3 into the
// data that follows too.
const fieldTablesOffset = 0x3F6500

// writeGraphicHitboxes writes every graphic's collision shape per facing
// (hitboxFor), for objects the field creates at runtime (objOp 2E).
func writeGraphicHitboxes(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	out := make([][4]hitbox, 256)
	for g := range out {
		out[g] = hitboxFor(mapfmt.ROM(rom), g)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "graphic_hitboxes.json"), append(b, '\n'), 0o644)
}

func writeFieldTables(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "field_tables.bin"), rom[fieldTablesOffset:fieldTablesOffset+0x500], 0o644)
}

// paletteSetTable is FC:F400, seven ROM palette ids per palette set.
const paletteSetTable = 0x3CF400

// gfxScriptsStart..End is the graphics VM's handler table (FF:A5FF),
// script pointer table (FF:A6CF) and script data (FF:A79F-B1C7+), bank
// FF; romPalettes is EC:A400, the ROM palettes, four banks of 0x100.
const (
	gfxScriptsStart = 0x3FA5FF
	gfxScriptsEnd   = 0x3FB300
	romPalettes     = 0x2CA400
)

// writeGfxTables writes the graphics VM's script bytes (offset 0 =
// FF:A5FF) and the ROM palettes it swaps in.
func writeGfxTables(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "gfx_scripts.bin"), rom[gfxScriptsStart:gfxScriptsEnd], 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "rom_palettes.bin"), rom[romPalettes:romPalettes+4*0x2000], 0o644)
}

// bg3WaveOffset is FF:7218, the BG3 wave's per-line horizontal offsets
// (screen effect 3, C0:E1BB): 16 signed words, then a second copy.
const bg3WaveOffset = 0x3F7218

// bg12WaveOffset is FF:7158, screen effect 2's per-line (x, y) offsets
// for BG1 and BG2 (C0:E0E9): 16 word pairs, then a second copy.
const bg12WaveOffset = 0x3F7158

// bg2WaveOffset is FF:6FD8, screen effect 8's per-line (x, y) offsets
// for BG2 (C0:DFDA).
const bg2WaveOffset = 0x3F6FD8

// bg2WaveD/bg2WaveF are FF:70D8 and FF:7058, screen effects 0D's and
// 0F's per-line (x, y) offsets for BG2 (C0:E8E7, C0:E814).
const (
	bg2WaveD = 0x3F70D8
	bg2WaveF = 0x3F7058
)

// writeEffectWaves writes the screen effects' line offset tables.
func writeEffectWaves(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	s16 := func(o int) int { return int(int16(uint16(rom[o]) | uint16(rom[o+1])<<8)) }
	// effect 0A's band tables (C0:E283, C0:E2B3): boundaries FF:6E58,
	// heights FF:6E3E, rate masks FF:6E72, speeds FF:6E88
	words := func(o, n int) []int {
		out := make([]int, n)
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = int(rom[o+2*i]) | int(rom[o+2*i+1])<<8
		}
		return out
	}
	variants := func(o int) []int {
		var out []int
		for v := 0; v < 3; v++ {
			out = append(out, words(o+v*0x3E, 5)...)
		}
		return out
	}
	s16s := func(o, n int) []int {
		out := make([]int, n)
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = s16(o + 2*i)
		}
		return out
	}
	wave := make([]int, 16)
	x12 := make([]int, 16)
	y12 := make([]int, 16)
	x2 := make([]int, 16)
	y2 := make([]int, 16)
	xd, yd, xf, yf := make([]int, 16), make([]int, 16), make([]int, 16), make([]int, 16)
	for i := range wave {
		wave[i] = s16(bg3WaveOffset + 2*i)
		x12[i] = s16(bg12WaveOffset + 4*i)
		y12[i] = s16(bg12WaveOffset + 4*i + 2)
		x2[i] = s16(bg2WaveOffset + 4*i)
		y2[i] = s16(bg2WaveOffset + 4*i + 2)
		xd[i], yd[i] = s16(bg2WaveD+4*i), s16(bg2WaveD+4*i+2)
		xf[i], yf[i] = s16(bg2WaveF+4*i), s16(bg2WaveF+4*i+2)
	}
	// camera step tables by speed row: C0:82DD (BG1, the leader's step)
	// and C0:82F5 (BG2 with $D976 bit 6), 4-byte entries (mask, speed)
	var stepBG1, stepBG2 []int
	for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
		for _, t := range []struct {
			base int
			out  *[]int
		}{{0x82DD, &stepBG1}, {0x82F5, &stepBG2}} {
			o := t.base + 4*i
			*t.out = append(*t.out, int(rom[o])|int(rom[o+1])<<8, s16(o+2))
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(map[string][]int{"bg3": wave, "bg12_x": x12, "bg12_y": y12, "bg2_x": x2, "bg2_y": y2,
		"bg2d_x": xd, "bg2d_y": yd, "bg2f_x": xf, "bg2f_y": yf, "step_bg1": stepBG1, "step_bg2": stepBG2,
		"e0a_bound": words(0x3F6E58, 12), "e0a_height": words(0x3F6E3E, 12), "e0a_mask": words(0x3F6E72, 12), "e0a_speed": words(0x3F6E88, 12),
		// effect 09 (C0:E66C): BG1's offset-per-tile columns, x FF:7258
		// (whole tiles) and y FF:7218, 16 signed words each
		"e09_x": s16s(0x3F7258, 16), "e09_y": s16s(0x3F7218, 16),
		// effect 0B (C0:E46E, C0:E4E8): band boundaries FF:6F08, heights
		// FF:6EFE, timers FF:6F1C and start offsets FF:6F12 (low bytes),
		// 5 per variant ($D09E 0-2: each table + 3Eh * variant), then the
		// shared offset cycle FF:6F26 (ends at 8000)
		"e0b_bound": variants(0x3F6F08), "e0b_height": variants(0x3F6EFE), "e0b_timer": variants(0x3F6F1C), "e0b_start": variants(0x3F6F12), "e0b_cycle": words(0x3F6F26, 11)})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "effect_waves.json"), b, 0o644)
}

func writeActionBank(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	if actionBankOffset+0x10000 > len(rom) {
		return fmt.Errorf("action bank F8 past ROM end")
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "bank_f8.bin"), rom[actionBankOffset:actionBankOffset+0x10000], 0o644)
}

func writeJumps(rom []byte, dir string) error {
	ds, err := triggers.JumpTable(mapfmt.ROM(rom))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jump table: %w", err)
	}
	out := make([]jumpEntry, len(ds))
	for i, d := range ds {
		out[i] = newJumpEntry(mapfmt.ROM(rom), d)
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "jump_table.json"), append(b, '\n'), 0o644)
}

func writeCatalog(dir string, catalog map[string]mapEntry) {
	cb, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"maps": catalog})
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "map_catalog.json"), append(cb, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("catalog: %d maps -> %s\n", len(catalog), filepath.Join(dir, "map_catalog.json"))
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	os.Exit(1)
}

func writePNG(path string, img image.Image) error {
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	encErr := png.Encode(f, img)
	closeErr := f.Close()
	if encErr != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", path, encErr)
	}
	return closeErr
}

// writeConditionalVariants exports each flag-conditional variant layer
// (C0:42E0: applies while lo <= flag nibble < hi) as variant_<n>.png and
// variant_<n>.json {kind, flag, lo, hi, walkable}: the map as the loader
// leaves it with that variant on top of the unconditional ones. The
// field swaps image and walk grid at load when the condition holds.
// Records whose variants do not decode export none (map 03CE's lists
// are garbage).
func writeConditionalVariants(r mapfmt.ROM, dir string, id int, trig *triggers.MapTriggers, always []mapfmt.VariantLayer) error {
	chests, layers, props, _ := trig.FreshLoad()
	type spec struct {
		Kind     int     `json:"kind"`
		Flag     int     `json:"flag"`
		Lo       int     `json:"lo"`
		Hi       int     `json:"hi"`
		Walkable [][]int `json:"walkable"`
		Attr     [][]int `json:"attr"`
		Low      [][]int `json:"low"`
	}
	var out []spec
	var imgs []*mapfmt.Rendered
	for _, v := range trig.Variants {
		if v.Always || v.Kind == 0x80 {
			continue
		}
		rend, err := mapfmt.RenderSubmapVariants(r, id, append(append([]mapfmt.VariantLayer{}, always...), mapfmt.VariantLayer{Kind: v.Kind, Ptr: v.Ptr}), props)
		if err != nil {
			return nil
		}
		walk, err := mapfmt.WalkableVariants(r, id, chests, append(append([]int{}, layers...), v.Ptr), props)
		if err != nil {
			return nil
		}
		rows := make([][]int, walk.H)
		for y, row := range walk.Walk {
			rows[y] = make([]int, walk.W)
			for x, w := range row {
				if w {
					rows[y][x] = 1
				}
			}
		}
		out = append(out, spec{Kind: v.Kind, Flag: v.Flag, Lo: v.Lo, Hi: v.Hi, Walkable: rows, Attr: byteRows(walk.Attr), Low: byteRows(walk.Low)})
		imgs = append(imgs, rend)
	}
	sub := filepath.Join(dir, "maps", fmt.Sprintf("%04X", id))
	for i, s := range out {
		if err := writePNG(filepath.Join(sub, fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d.png", i)), imgs[i].Under); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := writeOver(filepath.Join(sub, fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d_over.png", i)), imgs[i].Over); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := writeBG3(filepath.Join(sub, fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d_bg3.png", i)), imgs[i].BG3); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := writeTiles(filepath.Join(sub, fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d_tiles.bin", i)), imgs[i].Indexed); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		b, err := json.Marshal(s)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sub, fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d.json", i)), b, 0o644); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```
