## Fixed formations (battle word 19xx, decoded 2026-11-21)

FE:7F5B: 256 word offsets into bank FE (the hack moved only entry 0x60,
to FE:8DF2). Each record (C2:0A03 -> 5A:B717 -> C2:072C; op 0D reads the
RAM record 7E:EF00 instead) is a 6-byte header — +0 battle type
(`$141A`), +1 in-battle message row (FE:915B + 8n, FF none), +2 HP
multipliers (low nibble enemy `$2000`, high nibble the rest; earlier
notes that called this byte the background are wrong), +3/+4 flags word
(`$03`), +5 field id (`$1307`, FF = the map's) — and a body by type
(loaders C2:13C0, extra fields C2:0A6C):

| Type | Body |
|---|---|
| 00/01/02 | `[enc][lvl]` (02: `+[$141D]`); 01/02 run the random composition with the level from `$F532` +- lvl when lvl != 0 |
| 03 | `[enc][lvl][leader word][hensei]`: fixed leader, rolled copies and companions |
| 04/05/09/0B/10/12 | `[word]`, hensei 0B |
| 07/08/0A/0C | `[n][n words][n (X, Y)]` |
| 0D | `[n][n words]`: a chain, one enemy at a time |
| 0E | `[hensei][5 words, FFFF empty][5 reinforcement words]...` |
| 0F/13 | `[n][n words][hensei][R][T]`: the leader casts tech T in round R |
| 11 | `[n][n words][hensei][M]`: per-round script FE:926B + 9M (FF none) |
| 14 | `[n][n words][hensei][S]`: `$37` = 1 if the party's mean agility >= S, else 2 |

Enemy words: id = w & 0x1FFF, bit 0x4000 = key enemy. Op 19 always sets
contact `$37` = 4 (FE:C60B) except type 14; the battle-start check
C2:1C26 runs as for op 18. 64 ids appear on map NPCs (cmd/encounterscan).
battledata.FixedBattleAt decodes every record; exportbattle writes
fixed_battles.json. The port (main.gd `_start_field_battle`, battle.gd
`encounter_fixed`) runs 19xx battles from it: list types with their
enemies, HP multipliers, contact 4, type 14's initiative test, the race
bumps on row 16; type 01 through the random composition with the level
override, type 03 around its fixed leader and hensei; types 0F/13 end
after round R's actions with enemy 0 casting T (C2:62AA -> 63B3 ->
64DB; `$50` = 4; the tech fire sets `$25` bit 1 (C2:642E), which makes
the battle-over handler C2:DA2E return before the growth/reward block
- the port granting none matches this early return). The end fires
inside phase 2's per-action loop - 62AA is the post-action death/end
processor (it early-outs on the battle-end flag `$1B` bit 1, processes
the `$55` death bitmap, then 63B3 casts) - and the cast sets the end
flag, so the main loop exits before phases 4/5: the ending round of a
0F/13 battle consumes NO phase-5 rolls, matching the port's skip
(resolved 2026-11-22, closes the dead06f open item). DP $0E (WRAM
$090E) is NOT an outcome bitfield - it is the player-1 SNES pad word
($004218), refreshed every battle frame by the NMI's pad reader
FE:A3C5/A3C9 under the forced DP $0900 (FE:B867): 0x0080/0x8000/0x0800/
0x0400/0x0200 = A/B/Up/Down/Left held. The `LDX $0E` ladders in the
phase handlers (C2:29B0 command window, 2BCB A-confirm, ...) read the
buttons; phase 5's D22F skips its end trigger while any button is held
(decoded 2026-11-23, docs/battle-result-cell.md - a live write-watch
showed the only writers are the NMI store and two harmless bank-5F
icon-loader temps). The real battle-end markers ($1B bits set by the
kill path C2:9DC2, the 0F/13 cast, and the outcome windows' A-confirms
such as C2:2BE6) are independent of this cell; the per-round
scripts (11) run as ported since (below), and so
do the 0D chains and the 0E reinforcements (below). Positions are
not ported (the battle has no graphics); the opening messages are,
decoded below. The setup common tail is decoded below (the type-09
buff, the level scaling and the C18B unlock rolls ported). Open: the
key-enemy death swap behind the talk rows' +4 lines (5A:4200
word->word/item, C2:9D47 -> F1F9/F247; decoded in the talk-rows
section below, not ported), the no-leave flag
FE:D1BF's blow-away consumer C2:5665 (the enemy leave mechanic is not
ported at all).

### The setup common tail (C2:1371's post-loader block, decoded 2026-11-22)

Every battle - fixed or random - ends its setup with the same block
(C2:139C-13BF, after the per-type loader): the per-enemy record build
(C2:1976 -> 19BD/1BAF, stride-$80 records at $2000), FE:D1BF, FE:D250
(screen positions, not ported), C2:1C82, FE:D2B4 (the unit-record copies
$0F02+6i, one per enemy, $0F01 = the count), C2:1CB0, FE:D32D, FE:CD7A,
the battle-start check C2:1C26 and C2:C18B. Only three of these touch
the RNG:

- C2:1C82: type 09's extra fields. The loader helper C2:0ADB (the
  extra-field dispatch table C2:0A6C indexed by $141A, entered by
  `JMP ($0A6C,X)` at C2:0A68) stores body[2] -> $1420 and body[3] ->
  $1421; the tail ORs the mask into enemy record byte $1421 and buffs
  record byte 0x0C (when $1421 = 5) or 0x0D (otherwise) by
  `max(0, $40 - record+0x14 >> 4) + roll(1,64)`, clamped FF (record
  +0x14/+0x16 hold the final HP). The target bytes start at 0 (zeroed at
  C2:1B2C/1B31). Shipped data: battles 0x0D and 0xB3, both mask 10 slot
  5, so the stat is the roll alone (both enemies' HP >> 4 exceeds $40).
  $1421 ships as FF (init FE:C556) and the record read (C2:09D4 JSR 09F4
  -> 0A03) runs after the init (C2:097C JSL FE:C4DE), so the stores
  reach the tail. Ported; LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-11-23 via the skip-intro
  recipe (docs/mesence-skip-intro.md): battle 0x0D injected at frame 700
  shows the buff's roll(1,64) at C2:1C82 (RNG core entry with A=0040),
  index 20 -> 21, result 33 in record byte 0x0C = 1 + table[0x20] % 64
  exactly, HP $7E2014 = 0x0F76 = 3958 (the port's selftest pin), mask 10
  in $1420 and record byte 5, slot 5 in $1421, $1422/$1423 at their init
  1; the check roll follows (21 -> 22) and C18B consumes nothing (enemy
  0x116 >= 0x100). The five pre-recipe probe generations (tail-tail7)
  lost to the intro's scripted battle chain; savestates made it moot.
- C2:1C26: the battle-start check roll (ported; its `($BA),Y` stats are
  the party record's, the port's `_party_last`).
- C2:C18B: the AI-unlock entries. 16 entries of 10 bytes at FE:9E8E
  (battle_unlocks.json): byte 0 a marker (nonzero skips the entry; 7-15
  ship nonzero), byte 1 the roll(1,100) threshold, bytes 2-9 an
  FF-terminated enemy-id list. The first entry whose persistent $F4DA
  bitmask bit is unset and whose list contains one of this battle's
  enemies with id < 0x100 rolls once per matching enemy until a success,
  then marks the bit and stops (all shipped thresholds are 100). Entry 1
  ships only ids E2/E8, which the id < 0x100 gate never matches, like
  entries 5/6 (empty lists). The written $16D8 cell has no reader -
  write-only, the hack's unfinished feature; the roll consumption is
  what parity needs. $F4DA persists across battles (SRAM save at
  C6:346C; the port keeps game_state.ai_unlock_bits, not yet saved -
  same status as $F532).

The record build (C2:1BAF) also decodes: record+0x16/+0x14 = the row HP,
scaled by the flags word's bit 8 before the multiplier - hp += hp>>5 *
($F532 global level >> 3; 160 of the records ship bit 8) - then HP = the
scaled HP x the header nibble ($1422 for record 0 / $1423 for the rest,
both init to 1 at FE:C575, so random encounters keep the row HP). The
flags word's other in-battle bits: 0x01 (C2:0906/0C37), 0x02 (D988),
0x04 (F284) - decoded below. FE:D1BF sets $22 bit 3 for one-enemy battles
whose id is on the 41-entry list at 59:FF00 ($16D2 is the spawn registry
FED139 fills, a different table) - the immovable flag behind the
blow-away revert C2:5665; the leave states and the revert are decoded in
docs/battle-enemy-ai.md. Roll helpers: C2:0379 roll(1,100), C2:0387
roll(0,1), C2:0393 the isqrt walk (no RNG); the RNG index is battle DP
$14 = WRAM $0914 (direct page $0900), advanced at C2:0360 with the wrap
at $400.

The battle main loop (C2:0009) dispatches phases by $27 through the
table at C2:0058 (`JSR ($0058,X)`, X = 2*$27; byte-verified 2026-11-23,
docs/battle-menu.md): 0 = 1DF4 (INC $26, the round counter), 1 = 1E08
(the ally command phase; ends `LDA #3; STA $27` at 1E44), 2 = 52BC (the
round driver), 3 = 44EF (post-command; ends $27 = 2 at 4528), 4 = 60CA,
5 = D1FF, 6 = 20C2, 7 = 8F3B. The earlier list ("3 = EFBC, 4 = CA44,
6 = FF60") was a misdecode - EFBC has no caller anywhere in the ROM.
Phase 5 runs after every round's actions, the final round included (its
$0E == 0 exit is the battle-end trigger), and its first call C2:D260
rolls roll(0,3) unconditionally - the animated-background gate (on roll
== 0 and the FE:9C16[$1307] entry's bit 7); battle type 0x0A adds one
roll(0,7) at C2:D979 -> 0C8B ($143A | 0x80, the screen-actor slot
rebuild); the reinforcements C2:F57F run after both. The port consumes
both rolls at the round end in battle.gd's `_next_actor` (before
`_reinforce`), pinned in the selftest. The other phase handlers consume
no RNG (static scan of their C2 subtrees; phase 1's JML into bank 67
unverified).

#### The flags word and the field id (decoded 2026-11-22)

The word lives at battle DP $03 = WRAM $0903-$0904. The battle main
loop (C2:0025-004B) runs one per-round stage per pass ($27 selects via
the table C2:0058: 0 = 1DF4 round-counter ++ / state mask reset, 2 =
52BC the decisions, 5 = D1FF the enemy round and reinforcements) and
the phase machine C2:0837 on $50 (table C2:0849, real entries 0-4,
5-15 point at the idle 0920). The roll helpers are reachable only from
bank C2: the whole ROM holds zero JSL to C2:032E/0379/0387 (scan; every
caller is a bank-C2 JSR), so an FE/C1/55 subtree consumes RNG only
through a C2 frame it calls. Shipped-data counts below are from
fixed_battles.json (all 256 records).

- `0x0001` - battles 0x7A/0x7B. Consumers C2:0C37 (battle-start chain
  C2:09D4-09EC, after the loader, before F346) and C2:0906 (phase 3,
  the party-entrance phase). Set: battle start runs screen command 0x1A
  (C1:0316) instead of command 1 (C1:0145, the walk-in placement; it
  divides $0F41-1 by 0x13 at C1:015C) or command 0, DEC $0F41 (the
  party-slot count in the command block) once when $1B bit 6 is clear,
  and phase 3 skips the command-09 entrance queue (FEE34E + FEEB70: per
  qualifying unit - record +5 & 0xC0 == 0 and +7 & 0x84 == 0 - one
  entry with param $52 = 8). Clear: command 1 (0 when $F329 != 0, or
  type 0x12 with $24 bit 1), and phase 3 queues the walk-in.
  Screen-side; no RNG in either subtree.
- `0x0002` - battle 0x09 only (type 0x0A; battle 0x08 ships 0x4000
  without it). Consumer C2:D988 in stage 5: JSR 0C8B = roll(0,7) into
  $143A | 0x80 (one RNG tick per round), a rebuild of the eight
  screen-actor entries at $0F1D (stride 14; the entry whose index
  matches $143A & 0x7F gets +0xC = 0, the rest 0x63), then screen
  command 0x10 + FEBD28. Second consumer C1:3BF0 (screen script: when
  the bit is set, clear actor attribute $ADA0,Y bit 7). Battle data
  unaffected; RNG = 1 tick per round.
- `0x0004` - 20 battles (types 4/5/11). Consumer C2:F284 in the
  marked-enemy respawn (death handler C2:9D47: slot word bit 0x4000 and
  type not 0x0D -> table 5A:4200, 5-byte entries word/byte/word; the
  new word goes into the slot and F247 rebuilds the record): copies the
  word to $1433 and & 0x1FFF into the record's +1 ($1682), and when the
  table byte ($1431) != FF raises $21 bit 1. The bit-1 consumer F2BD
  (round-end chain C2:66A8) INCs $1435, sets $0F1B = $1431 and runs
  screen command 0x11 ($5A69E0); F247 itself raises $21 bit 2 (F27C),
  and round-end F3B0/F3E1 turn bit 2 into the opening-message line
  $1438 + 4 + $1435 while $1435 < 5 - the trigger framework behind the
  +4/+5 lines (the +3 line's trigger stays open). No RNG (F29D makes no
  calls).
- `0x0040` - battle 0x19 only (with 0x0100). Read at FED3C5 from the
  decision build (C2:2005): when set and $26 == 1, every enemy's action
  record is forced to 0x0D and its unit record +5 |= 1 - the enemies
  idle through round 1. C2:F9A5 clears the bit when $23 bit 0 fires.
  No RNG.
- `0x0080` - 68 battles ship it; no consumer. The whole-ROM scan over
  `LDA $03`/`LDA $04` (word, DP, absolute, indexed, long) and `BIT $03`
  finds no test of this bit - write-only in the shipped data, like the
  AI-unlock writes.
- The rest, site level only: `0x0008` (battle 0x20) gates an extra
  screen step in the C1 command-0 handler (C1:0190); `0x0800` is tested
  beside it (C1:012F; battles 0xA9/0xBA/0xFB-0xFE); `0x0010`/`0x0020`
  (battles 0x14/0xF1, 0x1B) read at C2:0435 (target check against
  $143D), C2:CB0C and FE:CDF9/FE:E7C8 (BIT #$0030); `0x0400` (battle
  0x16) at C2:6328 - the type-0F/13 end block: with $1B bit 0 clear and
  $30 == 1, scans the slots for enemy id 0x001F and arms $20 bit 0 /
  $23 bit 5; `0x8000` at C2:1036 (widens a stat-row copy into record
  +0x0B..+0x11; also taken when $27 == 7; no shipped battle sets it);
  `0x4000` read at FE:DEB5 / C1:3BA4. The high byte beyond 0x0100 stays
  undecoded past these sites.

The field id $1307 (header +5; FF keeps the map's $D2FC): stored at
C2:0A17 (the header parse) and C2:FE2A (the second header parser),
forced to 0x45 at FE:C811/FE:C93D when $F4A2 bit 2 is set. Readers:
FE:C5C1 (battle-screen init) loads FE:9C16[$1307] into 5B:7260 - the
byte selects the battle background from the 256-entry table FE:9C16
(entries mostly 00/01/03/20, several with bit 7: 81/83/88/90/...). And
C2:D260, the first call of stage 5, rolls roll(0,3) unconditionally -
every battle pays one RNG tick per round here (JSR 032E at D266) - and
on roll == 0, when the table entry has bit 7, runs the field-effect
dispatch FEE979 with $82 = entry & 0x7F (handler tables FE:E9A1/E9A7)
plus FB47: the animated-background event. The tick is the
parity-relevant part; the effects are screen-side. Field-side readers
6A:0B50 (bit 6 picks the 5A:0000 vs E6:9920 tile-table copy) and banks
01/2B - not decoded.

The two common-tail FE calls, call-tree verified: FE:D32D makes no
calls at all - $5E = enemy 0's word & 0x1FFF when the id is < 0x100 and
its low nibble <= 0x0A, else $F532 >> 4 (party level). No reader of
WRAM $095E turned up in the battle banks (the `LDA $5E` hits in banks
03/08/1A/60/66/6E are other banks' own DP frames - UNVERIFIED whether
any of them runs with DP $0900). No RNG. FE:CD7A walks the $2280 unit
records (count $34), collecting the indices whose record +7 bit 7 and
+5 & 0xC0 are clear into $152F+X, count in A/$35; no calls, no RNG -
the earlier no-RNG classification holds (both subtrees contain no calls
to recurse into).

### The opening messages (FE:915B talk rows, decoded 2026-11-22)

Header +1 = FF: none. Otherwise C2:0A1D stores `$1438` = FE:915B +
8*talk and the dispatch tail C2:F346/D16B opens the field-side prep
window BEFORE the battle screen and any battle roll - the window
consumes no RNG ticks and no FE:C14E waits (probe: $0914 static
across the message; battle 0x2's window drew「そうかんたんに　私が
倒せるかな？」). Every row byte is a message line in one format: FF =
nothing; bits 7-6 = the window style (`$7D` = b >> 6 via C2:0411; 0
draws the text with no frame, 1-3 draw the frame window, C2:D19C/
D1A2); low 6 bits = content id `(b & 0x3F) + 0x32`, except 0x15,
which keeps `$65` - the previous line's id (C2:D1CA-D1D1 stores `$65`
back unchanged), so a 0x15 byte re-renders the previous message in
the new window style; the text block lives at FD:(FD:9800 + 2*id) +
0x9A00, encoded with the battle text bytes (0x24 space, 0x25 0x14
newline, 0x25 0x28 end, wide leads 0x28/0x29).

The later lines' triggers (static decode 2026-11-22; the later lines
were never observed live, only the +0 window was probed). Each
consumer loads `$B0` = the row-byte address and `$B2` = FE and falls
into D16B. Shipped rows arm only +0/+3/+4/+5 - +1/+2/+6/+7 are FF in
every shipped row (talk bytes ship 0x01-0x1F, so 29 distinct rows;
battle_talks.json's 46 entries are battle-row pairs):

- row+0 - the opening, C2:F346 (setup C2:09EC).
- row+1/+2 - the round-2/3 lines, C2:F35B, called per action (C2:6234
  in the `$1611` action-queue loop): fires when `$26` (the round
  counter, INC C2:1DFA) is 2 or 3 AND the acting entry is a party
  member (the queue entry's byte 0 == $80, the marker written into
  every party command buffer each round at C2:52DD; enemy buffers
  carry the enemy word's low byte, so enemy id 0x80/0x180 would
  false-positive). `$26` - 1 selects +1 or +2. Inert in shipped data.
- row+3 - the slot-0 death line, C2:F38C: enemy record 0's byte 7
  (`$2007`, the stride-$80 records at $2000) bit 7 SET. Spawn stores
  the enemy row byte 2 & 0x3F (< $80, C2:1AED <- 5A:4190); an attack
  kill stores $80 into the victim's byte 7 (C2:A022, from the damage
  death path C2:9F8F -> 9FD9, taken when the acting buffer's byte 5
  bit 7 is set); empty type-0E slots ship $80 (C2:1DD8). So bit 7 set
  = the slot is dead or empty - the same test that admits the type-0E
  refill (C2:F601), which the live probe b16b verified. Called at
  every screen refresh (C2:66A2 inside the common refresh C2:6652;
  callers: per action C2:6283, the round-end driver D380/D539/D678,
  the results window F4D7), so the line re-draws after each later
  action while slot 0 stays vacant - there is no once-guard;
  single-enemy battles end on the kill, which is why each battle
  ships one death line.
- row+4+`$1435` - C2:F3B0 (fires on `$21` bit 4, the pulse raised when
  a key enemy dies into a swap-table entry - 5A:4200 five-byte rows
  word -> word/item, matched on the raw slot word including its 0xC000
  bits; C2:9D47 -> F1F9 -> F247 raises bit 4 at C2:F27E - and F3B0
  clears it) and C2:F3E1 (the refresh's other branch, C2:668F, gated
  by the F38C slot-0 test instead of the pulse). `$1435` (init 0,
  FE:C520) is the cursor: 0D-chain completion sets it to 1 (C2:F341,
  after playing the hardcoded completion message whose byte at
  C2:F345 is $90 -> id $42), and C2:F2BD increments it when a swap
  carried an item (`$1431` != FF; raised only when the header flags
  word has bit 0x0004, C2:F284 -> F29D -> F2B6; the item window
  $0F00 = $11 then plays). So +4 fires first and each item swap moves
  the next firing one byte later (+5, +6, ...); at `$1435` = 4 the
  read would land on the NEXT row's +0 (the CMP #$05 skips at
  C2:F3C5/F3F3 cap it only from 5). Shipped +5: talk 05 only (the
  three 0D-chain battles 0xCB/0xDB/0xEB, id $43, the short line after
  the hardcoded id-$42 completion message).
- row+6-indexed - C2:F40F, battle over (C2:DA38, the `$27` = 6 handler
  reached from C2:003C), only when `$25` bit 1 is set (set only at
  C2:642E, the type-0F/13 scripted-tech round): row+6 is an index b
  and the line byte is read at row + 4 + 2*b, FF = nothing. Shipped
  0F/13 battles (0x70-0x72 talk 02, 0x8D talk 07) have +6 = FF and
  the byte at row+$202 is FF for both rows, so nothing draws. The
  branch RETURNS right after (C2:DA3B -> DA6A), skipping the growth/
  reward block - the "0F/13 grants no rewards" behavior is this
  early return.

The shipped texts match the gates: the +3/+4 bytes are the enemy's
death lines ("はかったな大佐ー！", "うっ‥強い‥", "バカな‥",
"がはっ‥", the Muse/シェラハ death speeches).

RNG: none. Every talk consumer ends in D16B (the window the $0914
probe already cleared), F2BD's item window is $0F00 = $11 + 5A:69E0,
and the swap/rebuild path F1F9/F247 calls no roll helper (055F/1182/
C215/FB0B/FE:CBCC/FE:CC0B contain none, and the whole ROM holds no
JSL to C2:0360/0379/0387 from outside bank C2). The later lines
consume zero RNG ticks.

Ported: exportbattle writes the 46 decoded messages to
battle_talks.json and battle.gd logs the +0 message at battle start;
the +3/+4/+5 bytes are exported only, and their consumers (F35B/F38C/
F3B0/F3E1/F40F) are not ported.

### The 0D chain and the 0E reinforcements (decoded 2026-11-22, live-verified)

Type 0x0D (chain): the loader C2:18B9 spawns ONE member — word[0] of
the body list, `ORA #$C000` (key + fixed) into slot 0; the extra-field
handler C2:0AF5 stores the length n into `$1451`. At the member's
death C2:F55D increments `$1450` (cursor) and `$1452` (kill count) and,
while the cursor is below n, raises `$21` bit 3; the frame driver
C2:F2DA sees the bit, clears it, zeroes the round counter `$26` and
re-runs the type loader C2:1371 — the next word spawns into slot 0
with full HP and no RNG. The death→next-member order was watched live
(probe b15b: words 0x24/47/4A/EC/4C of record 0xC0 spawned in
sequence). The battle-end handler C2:E344 (type 0x0D only) grants the
real victory only when `$1450 == n && $1452 == n`.

Type 0x0E (reinforcements): the loader C2:18EA spawns every non-FFFF
start word at its own slot position (`ORA #$8000`; C2:1DD1 marks empty
slots `$2000`), stores the five reinforcement words `$145D..`, the
per-round cap `$1467` = body[0x15] and the chance `%` `$1468` =
body[0x16]. After the round's actions, while the battle continues,
C2:F57F -> C2:F636 walks slots 0..4, skips slots holding a living
enemy, and per pending slot rolls roll(1,100); on <= chance,
roll(0,4) picks the reinforcement word (full record build, no key
bit); the pass stops at the cap. A spawned reinforcement that later
dies is refilled the same way (watched live, probe b16b: record 17,
cap 2 chance 50, spawns in slots 1/3/2/4 across rounds with roll
pairs (1,100)+(0,4)). The chain link `$1469` = body[0x17] raw
[T][T*10 bytes][M]: at each round start C2:5338 (type 0x0E only)
scans T blocks of five words; a block is consumed when all five match
a slot's word & 0x1FFF with the `$2000` marker set — dead enemies
keep their id word without the marker, so with the shipped data no
block ever matches and M arms FE:926B entry M every round (records
0x2C/0xB1/0xEF: T=2 M=0; record 0x4F's T=3 reads past the record end,
faithfully exported).

Ported in battle.gd (`_chain_advance`, `_reinforce`,
`_chain_script_entry`; fixed_battles.json `spawn_cap`/`spawn_chance`/
`chain`/`start_slots`; the table itself in battle_scripts.json).

### The type-11 per-round script (FE:926B, decoded 2026-11-22)

The type-11 setup handler C2:0B65 reads M = body[2n+2] and, when M is
not FF, stores `$1539 = M` and `$153A = FE:926B + 9*M` (C2:5DDD); the
loader C2:1846 proper never touches M. The round driver C2:52BC calls
the consumer C2:53DC before the decision loop every round. Entry byte
0 packs the gates: bits 7/6/5 force rounds 1-3 (round table C2:5465 =
`80 40 20`, no RNG), bits 2-0 are the fallback count C (fires when
roll(1,8) <= C). Fired: up to 3 attempts, pair = roll(0,3) into the
four (mask, tech) pairs; mask bits 0-4 mark enemy slots (bit 7 set
fires with at least one marked enemy idle, clear requires all marked
idle; C2:3209's idle test). Success: the marked group executes the
pair's tech as one action with ONE shared target (tech row into the
group record `$15E2`, `$15E2[7]` = 3/4 by tech < 0x50, target via
FED885 + C2:BB9F) and acts at order priority 1 (C2:472D); the members
skip the normal AI (C2:572E). No fire or all attempts failed: the
round runs normally; the script never ends the battle (that is the
0F/13 mechanism, C2:62AA). All eight entries (M 2-7; 0 and 1
unreferenced) belong to the type-11 battles 0x12/0x20-0x23/0x31/0x3F/
0x46/0x55/0x89; every tech is < 0x50 (the standard enemy tech table)
and none is in the owning enemies' pattern lists. Ported in battle.gd
`_script_round` (fixed_battles.json `script_gate`/`script_pairs`).
Type 0x07 has an M handler too (C2:0AB4) but no battle uses it; a
0x0E reinforcement chain can re-point $153A at a script (C2:53BA) and
no record does.

## Own-equipment drops (55:C9B0, decoded 2026-11-21)

A drop slot byte FD / FE drops the enemy's own pattern-1 / pattern-2
weapon (battle record +47h / +48h = stat row +13h / +14h, the extended
item flag from record +7Eh bit 7 / 6); when that weapon slot is FF the
slot makes no roll at all. Other bytes below FD drop that item, the row's
flag byte bit 0 picking the extended table ($09FF). 30 enemies use FD/FE
(e.g. 000 スケルトン: FD -> weapon 08). Ported in battle.gd
`_victory_spoils` (the extended-table flags are not modelled).

```

`docs/battle-defeat.md`:

```md
# The party-wipe (defeat) routing, decoded statically (bokuno_jp.sfc)

Decoded from patches/bokuno_jp.sfc bytes (cmd/disasm65816 + raw hex reads)
on 2026-11-23; every claim below is byte-anchored unless marked [I]
(inferred) or UNVERIFIED. Battle DP is $0900, so a `STA $3F` and a
`STA $093F` are the same cell (seen at C2:08B9 `85 3F` vs C2:08E6
`8D 3F 09`). This doc builds on docs/battle-enemy-ai.md (action loop),
docs/battle-result-cell.md (the pad word and the $1B/$50 readers),
docs/battle-menu.md (phase table), docs/battle-data.md (0F/13 end) and
docs/music.md (BGM id 0x0A).

**Live confirmation (2026-11-23, same day):** the wipe was forced
end-to-end in MesenCE and the whole route traced; §4's UNVERIFIED tail is
replaced by the measured result. Probe scripts:
tools/emulator/wipe1.lua (wipe) and wipe2.lua (victory control), logs
and decoded screenshots under /tmp/wipe/run1..run5.

## 0. Corrections this forces in the other docs

- The battle-end flag is **$1B bit 0**, not bit 1: the main loop tests
  `BIT #$01` at C2:0036-38 and the post-action processor C2:62AA does the
  same at C2:62AC-62AE. docs/battle-data.md's "`$1B` bit 1" is a misread.
  battle-result-cell.md's "a window-confirm flag, not a battle state"
  needs the refinement below: bit 0 is set both by the evaluator
  C2:9DC2-9DC6 and directly by the battle-ending window confirms
  (C2:2BE6, 35D6, 3C1A, E7C3, EAAD - its own list), because those
  confirms END the battle with outcome class 3.
- The `$50`/`$51` pair is the **battle outcome pair**, settled here; the
  "$50/$51 = 3 reward pair on victory" reading of battle-result-cell.md
  is retracted (3 is the window-confirm/escape class, see §4). The pair
  feeds three consumers: C2:DA3D (victory gate), C2:0846 (exit-arm jump
  table), FE:C38B (packs it into $F4A3).
- FE:E4A5's "every ally is out" slot[5] = 0x0C write sits downstream of
  this chain and is untouched here.

## 1. The per-death chain

The damage-executor region ends every lethal action the same way
(~30 sites, C2:6F21/6F2C, 6F69/6F74, ... 847D/8488, plus C2:C51E for the
scripted-fire path):

```
JSR $8F22   (spread/hit tail, docs/battle-enemy-ai.md)
JSR $99D5
JSR $9DC9   <- per-death presentation (below)
JSR $9EDA   ; BNE skips JSR $9A53
JSR $9A53   (conditional)
JSR $9D8A   <- the battle-end evaluator (§2)
JSR $C568
JSR $AB94
```

**C2:9DC9 (death presentation)**: `JSR $C550`, `JSR $0450`, `JSR $9DF5`,
`JSR $9EF2`, `NOP`, `JSR $9E25`, `JSR $9E91`, then
`JSL $FEDBC3 / $FEDC02 / $FEDC3F / $FEDC50 / $FEDC65 / $FEDBA7`. The FE
side ones gate on record bytes (`($9E)` bit 0x80, `($9E)+7` == 1, `($B8)+9`
bit 0x40, ...) - sound/visual death effects. No RNG call appears in this
chain as decoded (the roll helpers C2:0387/5A19/5AC7 are absent); the
undecoded interiors of FEDBC3-DC65 are the only gap (UNVERIFIED: probe
scope - no roll is expected there, presentation only).

The $55 death bitmap processing runs later, per action, in the
post-action processor C2:62AA (`ASL $55` walk at C2:62BD-62E9, per dead
ally `JSR $BA11 / $64DB / $6328`), and 63B3 is the 0F/13 cast
(docs/battle-data.md) - unchanged by this decode.

## 2. The battle-end evaluator C2:9D8A

```
C2/9D8A  JSL $FEDD52   ; special end A -> FF, sets $50=1,$51=0 inside
C2/9D8E  BNE $9DC2     ; end
C2/9D90  JSL $FEDD96   ; special end B -> FF, sets $50=1,$51=0 inside
C2/9D94  BNE $9DC2
C2/9D96  JSL $FECD1E   ; ally live list rebuild, A = live count
C2/9D9A  BNE $9DA6     ; allies remain
C2/9D9C  LDA #$02 STA $50 ; LDA #$00 STA $51   <- WIPE
C2/9DA4  BRA $9DC2
C2/9DA6  JSL $FECD7A   ; enemy live count
C2/9DAA  BNE $9DB6     ; enemies remain
C2/9DAC  LDA #$00 STA $50 ; LDA #$02 STA $51   <- VICTORY
C2/9DB2  BRA $9DC2
C2/9DB6  JSL $FEDDC0   ; special battle types (table FE:DDEB: 0A 0B 0C 0E 0F 10 13 FF,
                        ; handler table FE:DDF3 -> FE:DE01/DE22/DE3B/DEA1x4)
C2/9DBA  BNE $9DC2
C2/9DBC  JSL $FEE558   ; continue: sets acted bits in the 9-byte records $164B/$1681
C2/9DC0  BRA $9DC8     ; RTS, $1B untouched
C2/9DC2  LDA $1B / ORA #$01 / STA $1B   <- THE battle-end flag
C2/9DC8  RTS
```

(The two JSL targets are `22 52 DD FE` and `22 96 DD FE` - the first
draft of this doc said FEDD50/FEDD94, labels two bytes low; the routines
were always entered at DD52/DD96, as the realigned bytes below show.)

- **FE:CD1E** builds the ally live list $152A-$152E (FF-filled first):
  per ally i < `$2D` over the 0x80-records at $2280, skip when
  `rec[7] & 0x84 != 0` (bit 0x80 dead / bit 0x40 left), list the rest,
  count `$2E` (listed) and `$30` (listed AND `rec[5] & 0xC0 == 0`);
  returns `$30` if any listed else 0. So the wipe condition is **no ally
  with rec[7] & 0x84 == 0 and rec[5] & 0xC0 == 0** - death (0x80) and the
  C0-state byte both disqualify.
- **FE:CD7A** is the enemy twin over $2000 records ($152F list, count
  `$35`, skip `rec[7] & 0x80`), always returning `$35`.
- **FE:DD52** (special end A): `LDX $B6` (the acting/dying unit's record
  pointer); `CPX #$2280 / BCC fail` (`90 3A`) + `CPX #$2501 / BCS fail`
  (`B0 35`) = must be an ally record; `LDY #0; LDA ($B6),Y; CMP $F000`
  (8-bit rec[0] vs the field party record 0 at WRAM $F000), `BNE fail`;
  `LDY #7; LDA ($B6),Y; BIT #$80`, `BNE set` - the dead bit alone sends
  it to `$50=1, $51=0, A=FF`; otherwise (unit alive) `$141A != 0x0D` AND
  `$2D == 1` AND `rec[5] & 0xC0 != 0` also sets it. This is the
  **protagonist-down special end** [I on the reading of rec[0] == the
  $F000 record byte; the instructions are byte-verified].
- **FE:DD96** (special end B): ally-record range test (same CPX pair)
  AND `$23 bit 7` set AND the ally's `rec[7] & 0x80` -> `$50=1, $51=0`,
  FF. **Measured:** `$23` holds 0x80 for the whole battle (live STATE
  line `23=80`), so the bit is armed in a normal battle; the special end
  never fired because `rec[7]` bit 0x80 never got set (below).
- **FE:DDC0** ends special battle types early; **FEE558** continues.

The evaluator therefore ends the battle on every lethal action with the
outcome pair set: 2/0 wipe, 0/2 victory, 1/0 protagonist-down (or the
$23-bit-7 case).

**Live record facts (wipe run):** dying by HP damage (HP word -> 0)
leaves `rec[7]` bit 0x80 CLEAR for every ally - run 4's STATE lines show
`ahp=0000,0000,0000,0000,0001,0001 dead=00` mid-battle, `dead` staying 00
through the wipe settle - so the wipe condition of FE:CD1E was satisfied
through its other mask bits (`rec[7] & 0x84` bit 0x04 or `rec[5] &
0xC0`; not captured which). Consequence: the special ends, which both
test `rec[7] & 0x80`, never fire on an HP-damage wipe - the measured
outcome of a five-member wipe was `5051=0200`, not 1/0.

## 3. What runs at battle end (C2:0028-0054, the main loop)

```
C2/0028 loop: JSR ($0058,X)           ; phase table (docs/battle-menu.md)
C2/0036  LDA $1B / BIT #$01 / BEQ loop
C2/003C  JSR $DA2E                    ; battle-over handler
C2/003F  JSR $E280                    ; teardown
C2/0042  LDA $1B / BIT #$01 / BEQ loop ; neither DA2E nor E280 clears bit 0
C2/0048  JSR $0837                    ; the $50-indexed exit arm
C2/004B  JSL $FEC38B                  ; pack the outcome
C2/004F  LDA #$00 / STA $1318         ; clear the in-battle reset request
C2/0054  JML $FEEE58                  ; leave the battle (below)
```

**C2:DA2E**: `$27 = 6` (phase 6 = C2:20C2, never dispatched after this -
the loop exits at 0042 while `$1B` bit 0 is still set). If `$25` bit 1
(the 0F/13 scripted-end marker, docs/battle-data.md): `JSR $F40F`, done.
If `$50 == 0 && $51 == 2` (victory): the reward chain DA6B -> DA7C
(battle rank, `$F532` bumps, docs/roadmap.md 2b-field) -> `JSL $FEEB47`
-> growth DB7C/DFEB/E088/E230 unless `$141A == 0x0D`. **On wipe
($50 == 2) DA2E does nothing but set `$27`** - no reward, growth, rank or
drop rolls run, and victory's FEEB47 wait string does not run either.

**C2:E280**: `$27 = 7`; `JSL $FEECFE / $FEED0C` (screen teardown);
per-type exits (0x0B -> E2D6 which restores `$F319`/`$38`/`$F322` from
`$1900`, 0x0C -> E303, 0x0D -> E309, 0x10 -> E3E5; else FEEC2F/EC6E);
then `JSL $FEC5DB`, `JSR $1022`, `JSL $FEC46C/$FEC482/$FEED6B`. Runs for
both outcomes.

**C2:0837** (both outcomes): `$27 = 8`; `JMP ($0849,X)` with
`X = ($50 & 0xF) * 2` - table bytes at C2:0849: `$0869 $08AA $08D7 $0904
$0925 $0920 $0920`:

- `$50=0` victory -> C2:0869: type 0x0B/0x0C/0x12 variants, default
  `$0F1B = 4; $0F00 = $13` (the FE result-window screen command) +
  `JSL $FEB839` (one FE/C1 screen pass), `JSL $FEC194`.
- `$50=1` special -> C2:08AA: `$3F = $0A` then `JSL $FEEEFC` (plays BGM
  0x0A, same cell the wipe arm uses), `JSL $FEEDE6`, possibly
  `$0F00 = $0F`, `JSL $FEC194`.
- `$50=2` **wipe -> C2:08D7**:
  1. `$3F = $0A` (`STA $093F`), `JSL $FEEEFC` -> sets `$25 |= 0x40`, SPC
     command `$10` with track `$3F` = **BGM 0x0A 全滅のテーマ**
     (docs/music.md id 0x0A; byte-verified FE:EEFC-FEF1: `$1C00 = $10`,
     `$1C01 = $3F`, `JSL $C60004`).
  2. `JSL $FEEDE6`: walks table FE:EE32 (4-byte entries: flags word
     tested `BIT $03`, match byte vs `$50`, param byte); a match
     (e.g. entries 0x0010/2 and 0x0020/2) overrides with
     `$0F1B = param; $0F00 = $13` and returns 0. Otherwise returns
     nonzero.
  3. If not overridden: **`$0F00 = $0E`** (FE screen command 0x0E) +
     `JSL $FEB839`. FE:B839 runs `JSR $B88B` then `JSL $C10000` = one
     C1 screen pass; C1:0000 jumps to **C1:0031**, the command
     dispatcher (`LDA $0F00`, then a DEC ladder at C1:007C-C130, one
     entry per command value). Command 0x0E -> **C1:0296**: window
     layout reset (`TRB $1038`, `JSR $04A6/$36E3/$3A04`), loading the
     pointer-table word at $E6CAA1 into `$11B4`.
  4. `JSR $CE54` (the defeat window, §3a).
  5. `JSL $FEC1E5` (screen restore, common tail of all arms).
- `$50=3` -> C2:0904 (`$03` bit 0 test, `JSL $FEE34E`, `$52 = 8`,
  `$0F00 = 9`, `JSL $FEEB70`).
- `$50=4` -> C2:0925 (type 0x0F: rewrites `$50=0, $51=2` - byte-verified).

### 3a. The defeat window C2:CE54

`$B0 = $CE71` (a 20-byte window descriptor, byte 0 = `$D5`), `$22 |= 0x80`,
`JSR $D16B` (the battle message-window renderer): text id =
descriptor byte `& 0x3F` = **0x15**, window style = `& 0xC0` = `$C0`;
`JSR $0707` resolves id 0x15 through the battle text table
(`FD:9800 + 2*id` word `+ $9A00`, bank FD - docs/battle-menu.md's text
block) to glyph-decoded string
**「(名)のパーティーは全滅した・・・」** (the `28`/`24` bytes are the
name-substitution controls). Back in CE85: the `$0289` flag picks text
pushes `$13/$29/$05` vs `$14/$2A/$09`, then `JSL $FEA414/$FEAADA/
$FEB585`, `JSL $FEB8A3` (wait), `JSL $FEC194` (wait), `JSL $FEC19D`
(**wait until the pad word is zero** - the release gate,
docs/battle-result-cell.md). The window therefore shows the 全滅 text and
waits for a button press and release before the battle exits.

## 4. What carries out of the battle

**FE:C38B** (called at C2:004B): `LDA $50 / ASL x4 / ORA $51 / STA $F4A3`
- the outcome cell the field reads:

| `$50`,`$51` | `$F4A3` | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0, 2 | `$02` | victory |
| 1, 0 | `$10` | protagonist-down / `$23`-bit-7 special end |
| 2, 0 | `$20` | wipe |
| 3, 0 | `$30` | battle-ending window confirm (escape class) [I] |

Then `$1318 = 0` (cancels the in-battle soft-reset request
FE:C1A6's `$1318 = 1`, docs/battle-result-cell.md) and `JML $FEEE58`:
`JSL $FEEE93` (kill the frame hook), `$130B = 0`, restore `$1300` NMI
pointer and the saved DP/DB/stack -> back into the field dispatcher at
**C0:C0B5** (the `JSL $C20000` battle entry returns).

**The field side (C0:C0B5-C0:C108), byte-verified:**

1. Restore `DB = $7E`, `DP = 0`; `STZ $D09F`; `JSR $0B98`.
2. `LDA $D014 / BEQ` + `LDA $1318 / BEQ`: if a soft reset was requested
   (L+R in battle, FE:C1A6) -> `JSR $019A; JML $C000C4` -> the reset
   chain into C0:0000 (the boot/title path - C0:0000 is the reset boot:
   SEI, stack init, WRAM clear, NMI pointer `$1300 = $FF00B1`). This is
   the ONLY jump to the title reachable from a battle return, and it is
   the L+R reset, not the wipe.
3. `JSR $BE47` (field housekeeping); `$D0A6 & 0x30 == 0x20` ->
   `$D77B = 0x0E`, `$D943 = $FFFC` (unrelated to the outcome).
4. If `$F4A2` bit 0x10 clear -> `JML $67F630`: `$7EEFFF = 3` only when
   `$F4A3` high nibble == **3** (the escape class), else 0; then
   `LDA #$0408; JML $C0C100` -> `LDY #$FFFF; JSR $AF91` - enqueue the
   queue word `$0408` (MEASURED: the helper stores A, and A=$0408
   there - the live run saw the word land and be consumed as an op by
   C0:B03D the same frame, not flushed; an earlier draft of this doc
   called it the `$FFFF` terminator). The `$FFFF` terminator itself is
   the field-idle enqueue (C0:B01B: a word with high byte FF -> `$D6BB
   = 0`, queue flushed). The escape grace: while `$7EEFFF != 0`, the
   next op-18 contact is aborted (67:F610 -> C0:BFBB -> `PLY / JSR
   $B030 / RTS`), and 67:F650 (reached from the play-clock tick
   FF:00CC-DB at 60 frames) decrements `$7EEFFF` once per clock second.
   MEASURED on the wipe: `$7EEFFF` is written 0 - the grace is not
   armed.
5. RTS - the field VM resumes normally.

**No CPU code branches on the wipe nibble** - the whole-ROM scan for
readers of `$F4A3`/`$7EF4A3` (abs/long/indexed) finds only 67:F630/67:F650,
the battle bank itself, C3:60AC and the C5 intro-battle sites - but the
consumer is not CPU code: it is the field's **post-battle event script**,
one dispatch layer below (VM bytecode, C0:1B93's interpreter). MEASURED
(2026-11-23, tools/emulator/wipe1.lua): battle 0x0D injected on the
settled field (map 0x0249), every party record's HP word (+0x14) poked
to 1 (five members, `$2D`=05, plus the spare slot-5 record), the
enemy's to 9999, A-mash until the enemy actions kill everyone. The
complete route, frames from cold boot (log /tmp/wipe/run4.log):

```
W f39720 50 FF>02 pc=C2:9DA0        <- evaluator: WIPE, $50=2 $51=0
W f39720 51 FF>00 pc=C2:9DA4
X f39888 ARM-WIPE pc=C2:08D7        <- the $50=2 exit arm
X f39888 BGM-SW  pc=FE:EEFC         <- BGM switch call
W f39888 1C00 00>10 pc=FE:EF12      <- SPC command $10 (play)
W f39888 1C01 00>0A pc=FE:EF17      <- track 0x0A 全滅のテーマ
X f39965 DEFEAT-WIN pc=C2:CE54      <- the defeat window routine
W f40140 F4A3 00>20 pc=FE:C396      <- window confirmed; $F4A3 = $20
```

The window screenshot (decoded run2 shot_f40038.png) shows
「ユリアンのパーティーは全滅した・・・」 - battle text 0x15 with the name
substitution, on the command-0x0E screen layout, party gone. The confirm
was a probe A tap (the window waits press + release, FEC194/FEC19D);
a second SPC command ($70, FE:EF4F) lands on the pack frame.

The field return then runs §4's static chain instruction by instruction
(RTN trace, run4): C0:C0B5 entry -> DB/DP restore -> `LDA $D014` = 0 ->
**BEQ taken, the soft-reset branch is NOT taken** -> JSR $BE47 ->
`$D0A6 & 0x30 != 0x20` -> `LDA $F4A2 / AND #$10`: bit clear ->
`JML $67F630` runs (escape-grace call) and 67:F645 writes `$7EEFFF = 0`
- the 3-second contact grace is escape-class-only, never armed on a
wipe -> C0:C100 `LDY #$FFFF; JSR $AF91` (the stub enqueues word $0408
- the helper stores A, and A=$0408 there, Y unused for the store;
consumed by C0:B03D the same frame) -> RTS at C0:C108.

Then the post-battle event script resumes in the VM interpreter
(C0:1B93 -> JSL $5AAFA0 -> `JMP ($3AD6,X)`): the run's enqueue callers
are C0:C105 (the stub's own terminator) and twice **C0:1C0D**
(`LDA $8D; JSR $AF91; INC $78; INC $78` - the interpreter enqueues ops
41 set2B / 45 chkMem, the pointer/compare pair of vm-semantics.md op
2.1), and finally the script dispatches token 0x3B through the
`$3AD6` table (word at C0:3B4C = `0E 25`) to:

```
C0/250E: STZ $01                    <- reset-request cell cleared
C0/2510: SEP #$20
C0/2512: LDA #$F0 / STA $1C00       <- SPC command $F0 (mute)
C0/2517: LDA #$00 / STA $004200     <- NMI/DMA off
C0/251D: JMP $0000                  <- absolute jump in DB=C0: soft boot
```

Live: `W f40197 1C00 00>F0 pc=C0:2517` then `X f40197 RESET pc=C0:0000`
(the JMP lands two instructions after the logged store; the stack top at
C0:0000 still holds the stale VM-interpreter return C0:06B5 from the
JSR at C0:06B3 - the entry is the JMP, no push). The boot's WRAM clear
then erases the battle state: `W f40204 F4A3 00>00 pc=C0:001C` ($F4A3 =
$20 lives ~64 frames after the pack). Unattended, the boot runs the
story montage; with a press it shows the title (boot policy, run.sh).

**The routing answer: a wipe does not stay in the field.** The engine
plays the defeat window over BGM 0x0A, returns to the field cleanly for
~43 frames, and the post-battle event script then reboots the console
(op 0x3B token -> C0:250E -> C0:0000). The player lands on the boot ->
title screen. "Defeat -> title" is right as a player-visible outcome,
but the mechanism is the script's soft reset after a clean field return
- not a field-side branch on `$F4A3`, not the C0:C0D2 reset branch
($D014/$1318 were both 0), and not a dedicated game-over screen.

**Victory control (wipe2.lua, /tmp/wipe/run5.log):** the same injection
won instead (enemy HP poked to 1): `5051=0002`, `F4A3 00>02 pc=FE:C396`,
the same field return and the same C0:1C0D enqueues - and `reset=nil`:
no C0:250E, no SPC $F0, no boot; map 0249 is back by f36400 and the
field song ($1C00=$11/$1C01=$21) resumes at f36500. The reboot is
outcome-specific: the post-battle script's branch (op 41/45 pointer
check, then token 0x3B) discriminates wipe from victory. The battle
type cell $141A (09) rides untouched through both returns and is only
erased by the boot; nothing in the traced path branches on it. `$7E:FFFF`
never moved on the wipe path either (only the boot's WRAM clear wrote
it) - the `$FFFF` of the return stub lives in Y, not in that cell.

## 5. RNG and state writes on the defeat path

- Rolls: none in the chain as decoded. The wipe skips everything that
  rolls on victory (DA2E's DA84 rank roll, DB23 per-group rolls, DB7C
  growth rolls, E149 drops, E1DE gold - docs/battle-enemy-ai.md), and
  also skips victory's 32 FEEB47 waits. Gap: the interiors of
  FEDBC3/FEDC02/FEDC3F/FEDC50/FEDC65/FEDBA7 (presentation) are undecoded.
- Waits: the wipe arm adds `FEEEFC`'s SPC handshake, the `FEB839` screen
  pass, `FEB8A3`, `FEC194`, `FEC19D` (release gate) inside CE54.
- State: `$F4A3 = $20`; `$1318 = 0`; `$25 |= 0x40` (FEEEFC, cleared
  in the same call). MEASURED: the standard exit carries the battle
  records back as-is (no defeat-specific reset on the CPU path - the
  party HP/dead state was never restored to the field records before
  the boot), and then the script's op 0x3B reboots the machine, so none
  of it survives: the boot's WRAM clear zeroes `$F4A3`, the queue cells
  and the battle records region. No HP carry-back is observable.
- `$27` exits as 8, `$F319`/`$38`/`$F322` restored from `$1900` only for
  battle type 0x0B (C2:E2D6).
- SPC timeline (live): $10/$0A at the wipe arm -> $70 at the pack ->
  $F0 at the op-0x3B reset -> the boot clears $1C00/$1C01.

## 6. The port's current behavior and deviations

Port: `godot/battle.gd` `_check_end` (allies_alive == 0 -> log
「敗北…」, `finished.emit(false)`), `godot/main.gd`
`_on_battle_finished(false)` -> 1.8 s timer -> copy battle HP into
`GameState.hp` -> `_show_title()`, map input locked
(docs/roadmap.md 2b "defeat returns to the title (UNVERIFIED)").

Measured answer first (§4): the engine's wipe route is BGM 0x0A ->
defeat window (text 0x15, press + release) -> `$F4A3 = $20` -> clean
field return -> post-battle script reboots the console -> boot/title.
The port's terminal behavior (defeat ends at the title) matches the
engine's player-visible outcome; what is missing is the presentation
and what is wrong is the HP carry-back:

1. **No 全滅 window - add it.** The engine opens the defeat message
   window (battle text 0x15 「…のパーティーは全滅した・・・」, C2:CE54/
   CE71/D16B/0707, live screenshot with ユリアン) and waits for a button
   press + release (FEC194/FEC19D); the port prints 「敗北…」 into the
   battle log and moves on after a wall-clock timer. Port fix: show the
   name-substituted 全滅 window and advance on the first confirmed
   press, not on a timer.
2. **No 全滅のテーマ - add it.** The engine plays BGM 0x0A via SPC
   command `$10` at the wipe arm, before the window (C2:08D7 ->
   FE:EEFC; live `$1C00=$10, $1C01=$0A`); a second SPC command ($70)
   lands at the pack. The port has no defeat BGM. (The `$50=1` arm
   C2:08AA plays the same track - any port of the special end shares
   it.)
3. **No screen command 0x0E.** The engine switches the FE screen to the
   command-0x0E layout (C1:0296) before the window; the port has no
   equivalent. Presentation-level; model as part of the defeat window
   state.
4. **Defeat vs special end - the single defeat branch matches, for
   HP-damage wipes.** The engine distinguishes the wipe (`$50=2`) from
   the special ends (`$50=1`, FE:DD52/DD96), but both special ends key
   on `rec[7] & 0x80`, and the measured HP-damage death path never sets
   that bit (§2) - a five-member wipe settles 2/0. The port's single
   defeat branch therefore reproduces everything a normal wipe does;
   the special ends stay unported until a death path that sets the bit
   is found.
5. **No victory rolls on defeat - port matches** (`_check_end`'s defeat
   branch runs no growth/spoils/level bumps, matching DA2E's early
   return; also roll-free, matching §5).
6. **HP carry-back - remove it.** The port copies battle HP into
   `GameState.hp` before deciding the outcome, so the wiped party's
   0 HP lands in the title reload path. The engine never carries it:
   the field return keeps the records as they were and the reboot
   erases the battle state entirely (§5) - the player continues from
   the pre-battle save. Port fix: on defeat, do not write the battle
   HP into `GameState.hp`; go to the title with the pre-battle state.
7. **Outcome cell.** The engine parks the outcome in `$F4A3`
   (FE:C38B) and lets the field's post-battle script read it; the port
   hardcodes the route in `main.gd`. Port-side this is fine, but the
   escape class `$30` and the `$7EEFFF` 3-second contact grace
   (67:F610/F630/F650) have no port equivalent at all (the port's
   escape is the party-window non-victory exit, docs/battle-menu.md §C
   - separate open item). Measured for the wipe: `$7EEFFF` is written
   0, the grace is escape-only.
8. **Defeat BGM stop + reboot.** The engine stops the defeat BGM at the
   pack (SPC $70) and the reboot mutes the SPC ($F0) before the boot;
   the port going to the title (which plays its own BGM) covers both
   transitions - no extra work beyond switching tracks at the right
   points.

## Byte-verification notes

- FE:DD52/DD96 were aligned from a raw hex dump (the linear sweep
  misreads the `CPX #$2280 / CPX #$2501` pair as a `JSL`); all four
  BNE/BEQ offsets (`90 3A / B0 35 / D0 16 / F0 1B / D0 15 / F0 0C`,
  `90 20 / B0 1B / F0 15 / F0 0C`) land on the shared tails DD91/DD93/
  DDBB/DDBD, which is the alignment check. The evaluator's JSL targets
  are `22 52 DD FE` / `22 96 DD FE` (disasm65816 C2:9D8A).
- The C1 command ladder (C1:007C-C130) was extracted byte-by-byte:
  entries `3A / D0 03 / 4C lo hi`; command 0x0E -> C1:0296, 0x13 -> C1:02F4.
- The C2:0849 jump table was dumped raw: `69 08 AA 08 D7 08 04 09 25 09
  20 09 20 09`.
- The jump-table scan for C2:9DC9 found 26 executor sites + C2:C51E; the
  9D8A sites pair 1:1 with them except C2:7468/74AF/751F/75C0/7B22/7C70/
  7F46/8008/8540/9F5F/9F8F/A044/C581/C5AF/D44C/D460/D59F (9D8A without
  9DC9 - non-lethal ends) and C2:1C91 (9D14, setup).
- Battle text 0x15 decoded with data/glyphs_jp.json (slot semantics per
  internal/glyphs).
- The reset handler (2026-11-23 live round): raw bytes `C0:250E 64 01
  E2 20 A9 F0 8D 00 1C A9 00 8F 00 42 00 4C 00 00` = `STZ $01 / SEP
  #$20 / LDA #$F0 / STA $1C00 / LDA #$00 / STA $004200 / JMP $0000`
  (the JMP is bank-absolute, no far operand - a whole-ROM scan for
  `4C 00 00 C0` misses it). Its dispatch entry: the interpreter table
  at C0:3AD6 (`JMP ($3AD6,X)` at C0:1BDA), word at C0:3B4C (byte
  offset 0x76 = entry 0x3B) = `0E 25`. The interpreter enqueue site:
  `C0:1C09 A5 8D 20 91 AF` = `LDA $8D; JSR $AF91`. The stub's enqueue:
  `C0:C100 A0 FF FF 20 91 AF` = `LDY #$FFFF; JSR $AF91` (16-bit Y).
- FE:A40F (`5C 00 FF 00` JML $00FF00) and C4:4183 (`5C 00 FF C0` JML
  $C0FF00) also reset the machine (FE:A3F8 mutes the SPC first: `A9 FF
  8D 00 1C ...`), but none of them ran on the wipe (run 3's exec
  watches over all six JML sites + both routine entries stayed
  silent); the wipe's reset is the op-0x3B handler only.
- Live log lines quoted in §4 come from /tmp/wipe/run4.log (wipe) and
  /tmp/wipe/run5.log (victory control); scripts
  tools/emulator/wipe1.lua and wipe2.lua; screenshots decoded with the
  FRMB64 dump (512x478 or 256x239 per SCR lines) into run1../run5/.

```

`docs/battle-enemy-ai.md`:

```md
# Enemy turn decision and initiative (bank C2)

Decoded statically from patches/bokuno_jp.sfc (cmd/disasm65816) on
2026-11-21 and checked against the opening battle's captured roll order
(docs/parity.md). Battle DP is $0900. `slot` = the enemy's 15-byte action
slot ($9E = $1597 + 15*i), `rec` = its 0x80-byte record ($B8 = $2000 +
0x80*i), `A0rec` = its 9-byte record ($A0 = $1681 + 9*i; allies $164B +
9*i), `tech` = [$B0] after C2:0450 (FE:1D00 + 16*slot[8], or 5B:4AC0 +
16*slot[8] when slot[0x0E] = FE). `roll(lo, hi)` = C2:032E; a logged
caller is the JSR address + 2. Marked "inferred" where the code alone
does not say.

## Round order

1. Allies' commands.
2. Allies' SP rolls (C2:2588; the opening battle: five, 1..20/13/14/16/14).
3. Driver C2:52BC, per enemy i < $34: slot[0] = 0x80|i; if FE:D3B6 (rec[7]
   & 0x84, else rec[5]) or ($26 == 1 and $37 == 1): slot[5] = 0x0D, rec[5]
   |= 1 (no action); else the dispatcher C2:56D9.
4. After the loop: C2:5D77, the initiative loop C2:5C3E, 5CB4, 5D19.
5. Actions.

## Dispatcher C2:56D9

```
if C2:5B17 != 0: goto 56E9        ; (rec[0x0B]&1F) >= 4: scripted mode chose slot[8]
if C2:572E != 0: return           ; $1F bit 2 and slot[0] in $163C..$1640: slot[5]=0D
C2:59FF                           ; pattern: $82 = 0 (pattern 1) or 8 (pattern 2)
C2:5A43                           ; unlocked range $83
C2:5AE6                           ; slot[8] = tech
56E9: C2:5B2C                     ; usability check, fallback attack
f = JSL 5B:7840                   ; 1 if slot[0x0E] == FE
slot[7] = 5B:3EC0[f*256 + slot[8]]; if slot[7]: C2:38B9
if slot[5] == 0x0D: return
if C2:5BD4 == 0: return           ; target fixed by the tech
C2:575D                           ; special targeting
if slot[5] == 0xFF: JSL FE:D885 ; C2:BB9F
```

## Steps

- **C2:59FF pattern**: if A0rec[0] bit 7 == 0 and roll(0, 1) (C2:0387, logs
  038F) == 0: $82 = 8. Else r = roll(1, 8) (5A19); T = C2:5A38[rec[0x0B]
  & 1F] (07 06 04 02); $82 = (T >= r) ? 0 : 8.
- **C2:5A43 unlocked range**: id = rec[0..1] & 0x1FFF; X = id < 0x100 ?
  ((id & F0) >> 4) + 1 : 0; lvl = $F532[X] ($F532 global, $F533+race);
  $8A = ($F532 >= lvl) ? ($F532 - lvl) >> 5 : 0, then + (rec[0x0B] & E0)
  >> 5; hi = ((3 * ($1308 & 0F) + 3 * $26) >> 4) & FF (FE:3178/3179 = 3,
  hardware multiply); r = roll(1, hi) (5AC7; hi 0 gives 0, no advance);
  $83 = min(7, r + $8A).
- **C2:5AE6 tech**: r = roll(0, $83) (5AEC); slot[8] = rec[0x37 + $82 + r];
  then JSL 5B:7730 with rec[0x47] (pattern 1) / rec[0x48]: slot[0x0A] =
  weapon byte | (rec[0x7E] bit 7/6 at 0x80), slot[9] = its FE:2D40 pair or
  FF, slot[7] = the weapon byte (stale until 5700); slot[0x0E] = FE if
  (rec[0x25 or 0x26] >> $BF) & 1, else FF ($BF = the last roll's value).
- **C2:5B2C usability**: if C2:204F (cost: tech[0x0D] & 1F against rec[0x1A],
  or rec[0x1C] with tech[0x0D] bit 0x20; 0x40 全消費) or C2:5B7F (0 when
  tech[5] bit 0x40 or A0rec[0] bit 7, else FF) fails, or the tech is not in
  the enemy's usable set (5E:6690 for FE ids, FE:9B5D bit table otherwise;
  0xAA..0xD3 and slot[0x0A] != FF skip this): fallback C2:5B9B (slot[8] from
  FE:379F via the weapon's class, slot[0x0E] = FF); if 5B7F still fails:
  slot[5] = 0x0D, rec[5] |= 1. Cost modifiers C2:C027, FE:E6BE, FE:E0A6,
  FF:E180 are not decoded.
- **C2:5BD4 fixed target** (slot[5] == FF only), t5 = tech[5]: with bit 0x20,
  (t5 & 6) = 2: slot[5] = 0x80 (all enemies), 4: 0x00 (all allies), 6: 0x0A,
  0: return FF; without 0x20, (t5 & 6) = 0: self (slot[0]|0x80); tech[8]
  bit 0x02: rec[7] |= 0x40, slot[5] = 0x0B; else return FF.
- **C2:575D special targeting**: C2:59DC: v = rec[7] & 3; v == 3 or roll(0,
  3) (59EF) < v: continue, else return. b = tech[9]; for bits 7, 6, 5, 4, 3
  set in b (in that order, $1534..$1538 = FF first) run the handler until
  slot[5] != FF: bit 7/6 C2:57C4 (units with (rec[3] & E0) == 0x80/0x40),
  bit 5 C2:5821 (weighted, roll(0, 255) at 5861), bit 4 C2:BC7A (uniform),
  bit 3 C2:588C (lowest HP rec[0x14..15]); lists end in C2:5988: one entry
  or roll(0, n - 1) (5996). Units with rec[7] & 0x84 or rec[9] & 0x20 are
  skipped. The side: own with tech[5] bit 0x02, else the other (C2:59A8).
- **FE:D885**: slot[5] = 0x80 if tech[5] bit 0x02 matches "actor is an
  enemy", else 0x00.
- **C2:BB9F individual target** (retries $0A39 up to 0x14): ally side: if
  every ally is out (FE:E4A5): slot[5] = 0x0C; else, when !($38 & 0x80),
  ($38 & 7F) not 0C/0D and $32 == 0: C2:BC37 (weighted: r = roll(0, 255)
  at BC5A; slot[5] = count of k in 0..4 with 5E:A000[($38 & 7F) * 0x80 +
  k] < r; row 0 = 37 69 9B CD FF; the opening battle used row 0Ah), else C2:BC7A (uniform over $152A,
  roll(0, $2E - 1) at BC94); re-pick on an out target. Enemy side: C2:BCA6,
  roll(0, $35 - 1) (BCB6) over $152F. C2:BCCD re-picks targets whose 9-byte
  record +0 is FF or has bit 7 clear.

## Initiative loop C2:5C3E

Per slot i < $34 (no liveness check): if C2:472D (slot listed in $15E2[0..4])
then 1; elif C2:25B5 ((slot[5] & 7F) < 0C and tech[8] bit 4 行動最後: 2,
bit 8 行動最初: FE); else C2:B679 sets $147E = min(99, rec[0x20] + rec[0x11])
(agility), S2 = (2 * $147E) & FF, r = roll(1, S2 >> 1) (5C7B), A = S2 + r
+ $4F + carry, at least 3; C2:5CFB doubles it when $26 == 1 and $37 == 2.
$162B[$31 + i] = A. $4F is the battle-start check C2:1C26 (docs/parity.md).

## Ally initiative C2:2556

Per ally i < `$2D` (slot $153D + 15*i, record $2280 + 0x80*i): JSL
5E:F200 (`$4C` != 0: FF; slot[0] != 0 and !(`$38` & 0x80) and record
+0x7F bit 7: 2), else C2:25B5 (行動最後 2 / 行動最初 FE), else C2:25DB
(FE:E0CA zero: roll(0, 9), 0 gives FE; else 5E:F1D0: FD / 3 / 0 from
the 5E:F430 bits), else 2 * `$147E` + roll(1, `$147E`) (C2:2586, no
`$4F`, CLC), at least 3, doubled by FE:D716 when `$26` == 1 and `$37`
== 0. `$162B`[i] = A.

Byte-verified 2026-11-23: the SP-roll call is `a9 01 85 bf 20 2e 03` at
C2:2582-2588 — lo `$BF` = 1, hi `$C0` = (2 * `$147E`) >> 1 = agility
(`lda $147E / asl / pha / lsr / sta $C0` at 257A-2581), the roll site
the capture logs as C2:2588 (the JSR at 2586 + 2). After the roll:
`pla / clc / adc $BF / cmp #$03` (2589-258E, floor 3) and JSL FED716
(`22 16 d7 fe` at 2593). The opening battle's five rolls (1..20/13/14/
16/14) replay from the live RNG at index 02B6; the stream_waits probe
reproduced them and the whole 81-roll battle (see the wait-chunk
section).

## Contact type `$37` (FE:C5F9-C657, set at battle start)

| `$37` | Condition | Round 1 |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | `$1314` != 18h, or facings head-on (FE:C667 opposite table) | none |
| 0 | perpendicular facings, `$130C` = 1 | allies' initiative x2 (FE:D716) |
| 1 | same facing, `$130C` = 1 | enemies take no action (C2:5D0E) |
| 2 | perpendicular with `$130C` = 0, same facing with `$130C` = 0, or `$130B` != 0 | enemies' initiative x2 (C2:5CFB) |

The routine is FE:C60B-C657 (FE:C5F9 is a separate `$23` routine); the
two marked 2 branches also run JSL 5E:F180 and set `$1B` bit 7. Field
inputs (C0:BFC7-C06D, decoded statically 2026-11-21):

- `$130C` = the last C0:AB2E argument, copied into the queue entry
  (`$D6CE`): 1 = the party started the contact (blocked step C0:8049, or
  the examine probe C0:AB26), 0 = the monster's step landed on the party
  (C0:5656); 0 for an entry queued without a slot; a script-queued 18/19
  word carries the stale last value.
- `$1309` = leader facing & 3; `$130A` = the touched object's facing
  (`$D9A9`) when below 4, else leader ^ 1 (head-on). Facings: 0 up, 1 down,
  2 left, 3 right (FF:6700 step offsets).
- `$130B` = 1 when the leader's speed row differs from its base row
  (`$D9BC` != `$D9BB`), except the slow-ground step-down (`$D9D7` & 90 ==
  10 and base - 1 == row): the leader was dashing.
- `$1314` = the queued op: 18 random encounter, 19 fixed formation, 0D the
  hack's `$0049` path. A monster-started contact can give only 4 or 2.

A write watch shows `$37` = 2 written at FE:C657 in the opening battle,
with `$38` left at 0Ah (no 5E:F180): the perpendicular, monster-stepped-in
branch.

## Record fields from the stat row (C2:19D1-1AAF)

rec[3] = row+0 (species), rec[4] = row+1 (resist), rec[0x1E..0x24] =
str, dex, agility, vit, mag, will, charm (row+6..+12), rec[0x25..0x29] and
rec[0x30] = row+13 (技LV), rec[0x2A..0x2F] = row+14, rec[0x47/0x48/0x49] =
row+0x13/0x14/0x15 (weapons), rec[0x4B/0x4C] = row+0x16/0x17, rec[0x4F] =
row+0x18. So the battle-start check C2:1C58 rolls 1..(will + 2 * charm)
and adds 技LV / 2 (rec[0x30] >> 1). rec[0x0B] (AI mode, low 5 bits, and
the unlock bonus, top 3) is row+3 (C2:1AF2; forced to 1F when `$F4A2`
bit 1), and rec[7] is row+2 & 3F (JSL 5A:4190); row+2 bits 7/6 select
the extended pattern table for pattern 1/2 (5A:4198). A write watch on
`$7E:200B` showed both stores at battle start (FE:BEB4 clears, C2:1AFC
loads). exportbattle writes them as enemies.json ai_mode / target_bits
(地狼: 0 / 0).

## Action order C2:614E

Built before any action: repeatedly take the highest `$162B` entry
(strict >, so a tie goes to the lowest slot; 0 = taken), zero it, append
it to the list `$1611`, then +5 to the remaining entries of the OTHER
side. Re-measured against the raw bytes 2026-11-23 (this paragraph's
earlier "own side" note had the dispatch polarity inverted; see the port
implication below): the pick site tests the picked slot pointer —
`cpx #$1597` (C2:618B), `bcs` (618E) to JSL FED8AE at 6196 when the pick
is an enemy slot ($A0 >= $1597), fall-through JSL FED8DE at 6190 when it
is an ally slot. FED8AE bumps `$162B[0..$31-1]` (the ally block:
`a2 00 00 a5 31 48`, X from 0, count $31), FED8DE bumps
`$162B[$31..$31+$36-1]` (the enemy block: `a5 31 aa a5 36 48`, X = $31,
count $36; $36 is the enemy-slot count C2:5D19 tallies). Each bump skips
0 (taken), values under 3 (the 行動最後 2 markers) and FD..FF (行動最初
FE and the cap), and stores min(entry + 5, FD) — a 16-bit `adc #$0005`
on the zero-extended byte, so no wrap. The whole order, bumps included,
is complete before any action executes. Fallen and sleeping combatants
keep their place and bump; they skip at execution. ($31 is the live ally
count and $36 the live enemy-slot count: the scan's pointer walk C2:61C5
steps $9E by 15 from $153D and reloads it to $1597 when its countdown
hits $36, so the enemy order entries start at index $31.)

Port implication: godot/battle.gd `_bump_opponents` bumps the OTHER
side - and that is what the engine does; the port already matches and
stays unchanged. The "own side" reading above was a misalignment: the
raw bytes put `cpx #$1597` at 618B and the `bcs` at 618E, whose target
6190+06 = 6196 is `22 AE D8 FE` (JSL FED8AE, the ALLY-block bumper -
`a2 00 00 a5 31 48`: X from 0, count $31), while the fall-through 6190
is `22 DE D8 FE` (JSL FED8DE, the enemy-block bumper - `a5 31 aa a5 36
48`: X = $31, count $36). So an enemy pick (X >= $1597) bumps the ally
block and an ally pick bumps the enemy block. Live-confirmed 2026-11-23
(MesenCE probe battle 3, 5 enemies, 3 rounds, 30+ picks: every enemy
pick took 6196 and +5'd exactly the ally entries, every ally pick 6190
and +5'd exactly the enemy entries, e.g. the first pick's
[3A 26 29 26 1D 30 34 32 29 2C] -> [3A 26 29 26 1D 35 39 37 2E 31]).
The opening battle's sequence is insensitive to the difference (its one
enemy entry leaves the board before any ally bump lands), which is why
its selftest never caught the question. Pinned: battle.gd
`_sim_order_side` (a 2+2 battle whose order is [1, 2, 0, 3] only under
the engine's side; the flipped reading builds [1, 0, 2, 3] and the pin
fails on it - shown by running the selftest against a flipped
`_bump_opponents`), plus the existing action-order bump pin. The port's
`_pick_actor` strict > tie rule already matches.

## Per-action wait chunks (decoded + live-captured 2026-11-23)

The action half of the parity.md roll-order capture, mapped engine-site
by engine-site. Every FE:C14E wait advances the battle RNG index by 1
(24 callers, docs/parity.md §4.4); the chunks below are the only places
the index moves during an action. Logged caller names = the call-site
return address - 1, matching the older capture's convention.

Wait helpers (all FE bank): C14E one VBlank (index +1, wraps 400h);
C17A repeats it `$16` times — its 18 call sites load fixed counts
(`a9 nn 85 16 22 7a c1 fe`: 2, 4, 8, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60, 120, 180 —
site FE:B7B2 loads its count from script memory and has no callers), so
the capture's x4/x30 chunks are single counts and its x34/x38 chunks
are consecutive blocks merging in the log; B839 one wait + ABus pad;
B8B4 one wait; B8C9 button-or-10-frame-timeout wait (per frame); C194
flag wait until `$0E` (the pad word) is set — input timing, index
advances per frame waited; B8A3 the count-4 block; C016 the
enemy-attack animation routine (below); BD28 cursor settle + one wait
(logged BD49).

Round flow, measured on the opening battle (tools/emulator/
stream_waits.lua, A every 16 frames; 81 rolls, 293 waits, victory tail
ends at index 037E — the same value the port selftest pins):

1. Menus (already modelled): per ally C181 x4, B8CC xN, C181 x8, B8CC
   x6, C181 x4, B83F x2. Each x4 is the `jsl $FEB8F4` at C2:1E07
   (phase-1 start); FEB8F4's tail calls B8A3 = 4 waits.
2. Ally SP rolls C2:2588 x5, then exactly one C181 x4 chunk before the
   driver C2:52BC: the `jsl $FEB8F4` at C2:1E3F (round setup, after
   `jsr $2556 / jsr $2600 / jsl $FED729` at 1E30-1E39). Between the two
   B8F4 calls sits C2:2600 (no waits).
3. Enemy decisions (5A1B/5AC9/5AEE/59F1/BC5C...), enemy initiative
   5C7D, order build 614E — no waits.
4. Action loop C2:6206: one B839 at 620B (round start, logged B83F).
5. Per action: BODY C2:6A47 → spark A70F (ally actors only; the 13
   C142 rolls) → for an ENEMY actor C2:C860 → FE:C016 = 40 waits:
   C01E x1 (the jsl C14E at C01B) + C181 x4 (B8A3 at C028) + C181 x30
   (count 1E at C02C) + C181 x4 (B8A3 inside B8F4, called at C034) +
   C057 x1 (the jsl at C054). Ally actors run none. The executor's hit
   roll (1..100), the 90B4 roll and the POSTACT 69C7 roll all land
   AFTER that animation block.
6. Per action tail C2:6652: B839 at 667F, B839 at 6697, BD28 at 669B —
   the capture's "B83F x2 and BD49 after each" action. Between the two
   B839s the damage/HP-drain animation runs ~90 frames WITHOUT advancing
   the index (measured: idx frozen at 02F0 across the span and none of
   the wait-site callbacks fired there; the drain handoff FE:DABA JMLs
   into 5E:0B50, whose per-frame sync site is undecoded — but it is
   measurably not FEC14E, and FE has no other direct C14E caller).
   So an action advances the index by exactly: enemy actor 40 + 3, ally
   actor 0 + 3.
7. Victory C2:DA2E, index walk from 0305 (the port selftest's values):
   DA84 rank roll, DB23 x16 group rolls (0306-0315), EB47's 30 (the
   `jsl $FEC17A` at FE:EB5A, count 1E — logged idx 0317-0334), B839
   (0335), BD28 (0336); growth DB7C's 15 rolls (0336-0344); the
   nobody-grew message: B839 + BD28 + a C181 x4 (the `jsl $FEB8A3` in
   the victory message prologue C2:EB70-85) + C194 x7 until the button
   (input timing); the reserve rolls DC7B/DCC6/E033 (0352-0354); a
   C181 x4 (spoils preamble, 0355-0358); drop rolls E149 (0359/035A),
   gold E1DE (035B); the closing 34 = E230's 4 + FE:EB47's 30 again —
   the index walks 035C-037D and lands at 037E.

Which roll sites are effects-only: NONE. All three groups the capture
flags at 0..255 bear visible effects, and all three are already ported:

- C142 x13 (spark, C2:A70F): a success replaces the executed tech —
  damage changes. Ported (`_spark_threshold`).
- DB23 x16 + DA84 (victory level bumps): the roll feeds 5B:FF40, which
  scans the 8-byte curve at 5E:6610 + (row byte & 0F) * 8 against the
  roll (leading-below count 0..8), adds max(0, `$142F` - `$1430`) (the
  global/race level >> 4 delta) and stores `$F533[group] =
  min(old + that, FE:9C06[group])`; DA84 does the same for the global
  `$F532` (curve FE:9B7D, cap FE:9C05, delta direction `$1430` -
  `$142F`). `$F532/$F533` are the unlock levels C2:5A43 reads for the
  AI's unlocked-range bonus in every later battle. The 16 table bytes
  at 5E:6500 + race*16 select the curve (FF = empty group skips the
  roll's consumer — the roll itself still advances the index). Ported
  (`EnemyAIClass.level_bumps`; the port's curve indexing by row byte
  matches the engine byte-for-byte — at 5B:FF40's entry A holds the row
  byte loaded at C2:DB28, not the roll).
- DD81/DC7B/DD24 x15 (growth): stats persist and messages display.
  Ported (battle_growth.gd).

Port implication: the port ticks the index only in its menus today. The
chunk map above is the replacement plan — tick 4 after the ally
initiative and before the enemy decisions, 40 per enemy action before
the executor, 3 per action tail, and the victory-chain chunks at the
steps the selftest already walks; the damage-drain frames contribute
nothing and must NOT tick. The C194 button waits stay input-timing (the
port's `message_button_wait`).

## Action and victory rolls (decoded statically 2026-11-21)

Checked against the opening battle's roll and wait capture (docs/parity.md
"Roll order"); [I] = inferred.

Action loop C2:6206: one wait at round start (C2:620B FEB839), then per

enemy target; the group keyed by the tech used (5E:5F20, or 5B:9100 when

< threshold * (8 - `$143C`) >> 3, no roll once `$143C` >= 8; the first
success replaces the tech. Rows: 68:E920 (閃き) or 5B:FEC0 by A85B.
Opening: ハリード's 剣 group 01, 13 eligible entries, all failed.
