`docs/map-format.md`:

```md
# RS3 submap format (bokuno_jp.sfc)

Decoded from the hacking community's documentation (2-658氏 `サブマップ解析.txt`,
AL982 memos, RS3MapEditor2 manual) and verified byte-for-byte against
`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` (SHA-256 `4793e142...`, 8 MB ExHiROM). Decoder:
`internal/mapfmt`. Renderer: `cmd/dumpmaps`.

## Addressing

8 MB ExHiROM. SNES banks C0-FF map to file offset `(bank-0xC0)*0x10000`;
banks 40-7D map to `bank*0x10000`. All pointers stored in the data regions
below are 3-byte little-endian SNES addresses in the C0-FF range (e.g.
`F70180` -> file `370180`). `FFFFFF` means "absent".

The community docs quote plain file offsets (`380500` etc.); for the
second half of the ROM those equal the file offsets here, because
`(bank-0xC0)*0x10000` reproduces them.

## Fixed data regions

| Address (file) | Contents |
|---|---|
| `5A6A50` | **Submap table the hack's loader reads**: 3-byte SNES pointer per map ID (1024 entries). The loader passes the map id to 5A:7650, which loads `[$B7]` from it (C0:3C6F). 471 entries point at relocated records in banks 44-50 (00C3 at `$44:6370`, 0379 at `$45:55A0`) |
| `380500` | Vanilla submap table (2-byte entry + `380000`): dead in this hack; decoding it read stale records for those 471 maps |
| `380C00`.. | Vanilla submap data records (still the target of the other 553 entries) |
| `370000` | Object config table: 128 3-byte SNES pointers, one per config stream; streams follow contiguously from `370180` (last entries `FFFFFF`) |
| `39A800` | Chipset set list: 5 bytes per set = five chipset graphic IDs |
| `39AD00` | Chipset graphic pointer table: 3-byte SNES pointers, indexed by graphic ID |
| `3CF400` | Palette set list: 7 bytes per set = seven palette IDs |
| `2CA400` | Palette data: 32 bytes per palette = 16 BGR555 words (word bit0-4 R, 5-9 G, 10-14 B) |

Evidence: the table at `380500` reads `00 0C 6D 0C 1C 0D ...` = data
offsets `380C00`, `380C6D`, `380D1C`, matching the community CSV exactly;
map 8's record at `3813AE` matches its documented fields (see below); the
object table's entry 0 points at `370180`, the first byte after the table.

## Submap header (block 1)

At the record start:

```
flag1            1  bit0-1 palette bank; bit6 layer 2 present; bit5 layer 3 present
layer1 offset    3  SNES pointer, front layer
layer2 offset    3  present if flag1 bit6 (else 3 bytes skipped only when bit set)
layer3 offset    3  present if flag1 bit5
prop offset      3  SNES pointer
chipset set      1  indexes 39A800 (5 graphic IDs)
palette set      1  indexes 3CF400 (7 palette IDs); bank = flag1 bit0-1
object config    1  indexes the 370000 table
pos X, pos Y     2
size X, size Y   2  tile dimensions minus one (0x3F = 64 tiles)
name ID          1
...              remaining bytes: restriction flags, flags2, flags3, event data (not needed for rendering)
```

Verified: map 2 record at `380D1C` = `C2 B5 DF F1 00 00 F0 FA 21 F4 3A 4F
28 00 00 3F 3F 35 ...` -> flag1 C2, L1 `F1DFB5`, L2 `F00000`, prop
`F421FA`, chipset `3A`, palette set `4F`, object config `28`, pos (0,0),
size (3F,3F) = 64x64 tiles; the layer pointer `F1DFB5` -> file `31DFB5`
matches the community map list value for this map exactly. Several map
headers (0, 1, 7) are zeroed in the bokuno ROM (maps replaced by the
patch); `dumpmaps` skips zeroed records.

## Display layer

At the layer offset:

```
size byte        1  hi nibble*32 = width tiles, lo nibble*32 = height tiles
base chip word   2
data size        2  includes this 5-byte header
placement records...
```

Base word: `base&0x3FF >= 0x100` = fill word `base-0x100` MVN-copied
over the whole layer; `base&0x3FF < 0x100` = the low byte names an
OBJECT that tiles the whole layer (see the walker paragraph below).
`0x0100` fills the transparent word 0 — map 0x250's layer 1.

Placement records, until data size runs out:

```
X                1  tile column
Y                1  tile row
flag             1
args...          depends on flag bit0-1
```

- flag bit0-1 == 0: place object; arg = object ID (1 byte, passed
  through the config stream's id-remap bands, see "Object composition
  streams") into the config's object list. flag bit6/7 = horizontal/
  vertical flip: the render EORs the flip bits into every chip word
  (FF/0E08) AND mirrors each chip's position within the object's
  16-chip grid (pos byte EOR $F0 / $0F, FF/0D6B-0D7B).
- flag bit0-1 == 1-2: place one chip directly: word =
  ((flag-1)<<8 | next byte) — chip = word&0x3FF, palette field =
  flag bits 2-4, flips = flag bits 6-7 (FF/0749-079A).
- flag bit0-1 == 3: tile-repeat command. 13 handlers at
  $FF:07AB..08D9, dispatched through the 64-slot table at $FF:0B7E on
  `(flag>>1)&0x7E`/2 (FF/073D-0746); flags 0x37+ index past the table
  into data and never occur in clean streams. Every op reads a chip
  word stored HIGH BYTE FIRST (the stream reader XBA-swaps,
  FF/0B1A/0B44/0B78) and then branches on `chip&0x3FF`: below 0x100 it
  is an OBJECT id, stamped per step with its property bytes; at or
  above 0x100 it is a chip word minus 0x100, tiled as words only.
  Decoded grammar (2026-11-17, byte-level; verified by write-sequence
  equality against the engine's FF/0DDA watch — see "Render
  verification"):

  | flag | args | semantics |
  |---|---|---|
  | 03 | w1 w2 chip | rect: end offsets w1.lo+1/w1.hi+1, steps w2.lo+1/w2.hi+1 |
  | 07 | size step chip | rect: end = (size>>4)+1/(size&F)+1, steps from `step` nibbles |
  | 0B | w1 size chip | rect: end = w1 bytes +1 each, steps from `size` nibbles |
  | 0F | w1 w2 chip | 03 + brick offset: odd rows shift x by xstep/2, ystep halves |
  | 13 | size step chip | 07 + brick offset |
  | 17 | w1 size chip | 0B + brick offset |
  | 1B | n w chip | linear run of n+1 chips/stamps, step word +1 each nibble |
  | 1F | n size chip | linear run of n+1, steps from `size` nibbles |
  | 23 | n size chip | 1F walking LEFT (x step negated, FF/0860) |
  | 27 | w1 chip | rect, end offsets w1 bytes +1, steps 1,1 |
  | 2B | size chip | rect, end offsets from `size` nibbles, steps 1,1 |
  | 2F | size w | stretch copy: end offsets from `size`, steps from `w` (below) |
  | 33 | w1 w | stretch copy, end offsets from w1 bytes |

  All coordinates are 8-bit: a rect's end is `(base+offset)&0xFF` and
  the loops stamp the row FIRST, advance, then compare — a base near
  255 wraps around the map edge (0x250's tree at (89,254) fills the
  map's top-right corner this way). Object rects reset x to the
  record's column at each row end (brick wrap added on odd rows) and
  cap both coordinates at $F0 (FF/0949/097D). The stretch copy
  (FF/0A5A loop, FF/0A9C copier) copies each cell's word to
  (x+xstep, y+ystep), growing the x step by one per cell and the y
  step by one per row, reading the live grid so copies chain. Chips
  ≥ 0x100 are written as tile words only (FF/0A2C — no walk-attr
  write); objects stamp their property bytes too (below).

  The optional palette-override byte the handlers read when DP $A6
  bit 5 is set is NOT decoded: at map load $A6 bit 5 is clear (the
  record streams consume exactly their dsize with the shapes above),
  and the record flag's bit 5 (values 23/2B/2F/33) is NOT the gate.

The engine's own layer walker lives at SNES `$FF:0724` (same
`[$8D],Y`-stream pattern as the object decompressor): the caller
(`FF:06EF`/`FF:070B`, stubs `FF:066C`/`FF:0670`) reads the size byte
into `$D0C3/D0C4/D0C5` (= layer height, width and word count),
the base word into `$D0C7`, the data size into `$90`, runs the base
fill (`$FF:0B98`) and then walks records until Y reaches the data
size. The base word branches on `base&0x3FF` (FF/0B9E): at or above
0x100 the FILL WORD `base-0x100` is MVN-copied over the whole layer
tile grid; below 0x100 the low byte names an OBJECT (remapped) that
tiles the whole layer by its chip bounding box from `(-minX,-minY)`
stepping (objW,objH), columns `ceil(W/objW)` rows `ceil(H/objH)`
(FF/0BC8-0CC6) — with its property bytes (JSR $0CC2 per tile), which
is how map 0x04's sea is painted and blocked. Map 0x250's layer-2
base `0x0000` tiles object 0 this way; the earlier reading of base
`0x003B` as "the water chip fill" was wrong — it is object 0x3B
tiled.

## Chip graphics

A map uses five chipset graphics (128 chips each; chip word bits 0-9 give
`set = chip>>7`, `tile = chip&0x7F`). Each chipset graphic stream at its
`39AD00` pointer holds four same-size run-coded blocks, one per bitplane:

- flag `01-7F`: repeat next byte flag+1 times
- flag `80-FE`: copy `(flag&0x7F)+1` literal bytes
- flag `00`: end of block

Each block is 1024 bytes = 128 tiles x 8 rows (one byte per row). The
interleave "100 200 101 201 ... 107 207 / 300 400 ... 307 407" rebuilds
the standard SNES 4bpp tile (32 bytes: 16 bytes bitplanes 0/1, then
bitplanes 2/3). Verified: chipset `4A`'s blocks are exactly 1024 bytes;
pixel column c of a row takes bit 7-c of each plane byte (SNES order).

## Palettes

Palette set -> 7 palette IDs (`3CF400`); actual palette = ID + (flag1
bits 0-1)<<8; data at `2CA400 + id*32`. Word 15 = BGR555. Index 0 is the
SNES transparent color (skipped when compositing layers). Chip word
palette field 1-7 selects set[0-6]; field 0 renders with set[0].

## Object composition streams

Per map config (header byte), a compressed stream. Grammar reverse-
engineered from the engine's decompressor at SNES `$FF:0E44` (bokuno
ROM, disassembled 2026-11-16) and verified entry-for-entry against the
engine's own decode: a MesenCE run standing on the opening-area map
dumped the engine's object tables from WRAM (`tools/emulator/
shot_wramdump.lua`; per-object start offsets at `$7E:2000+2i`, entry
ends at `$7E:2200+2i`, 3-byte chip entries `[chip lo][palette byte]
[pos x<<4|y]` at `$7E:2400+start`), and the decoder in
`internal/mapfmt/objects.go` reproduces all 131 objects of config 0x02
byte-exactly (`dumpmaps ... verify 0x02 <wram-dump>` -> VERIFY PASS on
two independent captures).

```
leading bytes   b0; if b0 != 0 read b1; then b2; if b2 != 0 read b3
objects         until a `00 FF FF` terminator (checked at each header)
```

The leading bytes are the OBJECT-ID REMAP bands (FF/0E68-0E8A:
b0 -> `$D0BD`, b1 -> `$D0BE`, b2 -> `$D0BF`, b3 -> `$D0C0`): every
object id the layer records reference passes through FF/0CC2 before
lookup — ids at or above the larger non-zero threshold shift by
(offset - threshold), the smaller band below it (config 0x26 = identity
via T=O=0x30; config 0x07 shifts ids >= 0xED by -0x27; config 0x02
ids >= 0xD0 by -0x4F). `LoadObjectSet` exposes the bands as
`ObjectSet.Remap`. They are identity for every object id below the
thresholds on the verified maps.

Object header: read count byte and next byte. If both are `00 FF`, the
third byte terminates the stream; otherwise a next byte of `FF` makes
the third byte the object width (count byte `00` -> a 1-chip object,
the chip taken from the following bytes). Without the `FF` marker the
width defaults to 0x10 and the next byte is the first chip byte. The
count byte is chips-1: the engine's down-counter yields count+1 chips
per object.

Chip phase (exactly count+1 chips; every byte is one op, op =
`(b>>2)&3`; an `FF` byte is an escape prefix only while the common
palette byte is set, re-dispatching the next byte as an op):

- op 0: skip `(b>>4)+1` grid cells. Skips move the linear cell index
  `cx += s+1` and then `cy = cx/width` — cx may exceed the width, and
  rendered cell = `(cx&0xF, cy&0xF)` from the 8-bit pos byte
  `(cx<<4|cy)&0xFF` the engine stores per entry.
- op 1: emit `(b>>4)+1` copies of one chip. With the common set the
  palette byte is the common and one chip byte follows; without it a
  palette byte precedes the chip byte.
- op 2: set the common palette byte from the next byte (bits 0-1 chip
  index high, bits 2-4 palette field, bits 5-7 priority/h/v flip).
- op 3: emit one transparent tile (chip `0xFF`, palette = common) when
  `b&0xF0 != 0`, else clear the common palette (`0x0C` included).
- `FF` with no common set: palette byte `FF` (chip high 3, palette
  field 7) for the following chip byte.
- with the common set, every non-`FF` byte is a plain chip (palette =
  common); without it, bytes with `b&3 != 3` are a palette byte plus
  chip byte.

Property phase: the loop reads until the property counter (the raw
count byte) hits zero, checked after each write — i.e. it consumes
count+1 stream values; `FF n` writes n+1 literal `FF` values from 2
bytes. Consumed and discarded (2-658's チッププロパティ).

The entry's palette byte maps 1:1 onto the high byte of the layer chip
word: bits 0-1 chip index high, 2-4 palette field, 5 priority (draw in
front of characters), 6 horizontal flip, 7 vertical flip.

Verified: config 0x02 decode vs engine WRAM tables — all 131 objects,
every chip's lo/pal byte/position identical, on two captures 6000
frames apart; config 0x02's obj0 is the same 2x2 block of chips
`01/02/11/12` with palette byte `04` (stream bytes `03 FF 02 0B 04 01
02 11 12 FF 03`) that the classic community fragment documents; streams
0x26 (50 objects, map 0x249) and 0x0A (170 objects, map 0x04) decode
without overrun.

## Property layer

At the header `prop` pointer (decoder: `internal/mapfmt/walkable.go`):

```
data size      2  LE; the following entries consume exactly this many
                  bytes (the engine counts entry bytes down from it,
                  FF:1468-14AF; there is no terminator list)
entries...     until the size runs out
default byte   1  the map's default walk attribute; also the overlay
                  stream's transparent marker (see "Chip default
                  passability" below)
overlay RLE    the walk-attr run stream FF:14D7-1562 decodes into the
                  attr grid
```

Entry: `flag [1] X [1] Y [1] size`. Flag bit 0 selects the size
encoding: even flag = `W [1] H [1]`, odd flag = one byte, high nibble W,
low nibble H. Two consecutive size-0 rectangles are a normal filler.
The engine parses the counted region mechanically — it never checks the
flag against a known set, so neither does the decoder. Some maps (0x04)
continue with further `[size:2][entries...]` chunks after the overlay
stream; the engine's chunk iterator consumes them separately and they
never re-fill or re-overlay the attr grid.

Flag meanings:

- Verified against the ROM and 2-658's notes: `08/09` = event point
  (ordered, links to block 3's event list), `20-23` = display mask,
  `40-43` = layer-2 front/back toggle, `80-83` = layer-1 front/back
  toggle (map 0x04 really uses `22` and `42`; the extra low bits are a
  size/variant encoding, not a different property).
- Walkability attributes (SUPERSEDED for the runtime effect, see writer
  4 in "Chip default passability": rect entries never write the attr
  grid — every entry EOR-stamps `flag&0xFE` into the `$7F:0000` low
  buffer over `(x,y,w+1,h+1)`, and only bit 3 of that buffer blocks the
  party's step, i.e. the event points. The old per-flag walkability
  layer is engine-disproved by the cs_grid5/6/7 write-watches; the
  editor-palette naming below survives only as the flags' NAMES, useful
  for guessing what a stamp value does to NPCs/terrain). Flag bit 0
  selects the size encoding; the attribute table follows the
  RS3MapEditor2 property palette, whose NUL-separated string list inside
  `RS3MapEditor2.exe` (extracted from `RS3主人公追加パッチ.zip`) reads,
  in order: イベントポイント, レイヤーマスク, レイヤー2前後切替,
  レイヤー1前後切替, 進入許可00, 進入許可01, 進入許可02, 水中00, 水中01,
  プレイヤー以外進入禁止, 進入禁止0, 進入禁止1, キャラクターを前面表示,
  歩行速度低下, 強制下移動, 強制上移動, 乾いた大河, 設定無し. Anchored
  on the byte-verified assignments (attribute 4 = event point at flags
  08/09, 16 = mask at 20/21+, 32 = layer-2 toggle at 40/41+, 64 =
  layer-1 toggle at 80/81+):

  | attr | flags | name | low-buffer stamp (flag&0xFE) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | 00/01 | 進入許可00 | 00 |
  | 1 | 02/03 | 進入許可01 | 00 |
  | 2 | 04/05 | 進入許可02 | 04 (blocks nobody) |
  | 3 | 06/07 | 水中00 | 06 |
  | 4 | 08/09 | event point (verified) | 08 = the step-blocking bit |
  | 5 | 0A/0B | 水中01 | 0A |
  | 6 | 0C/0D | プレイヤー以外進入禁止 | 0C |
  | 7 | 0E/0F | 進入禁止0 | 0E |
  | 8 | 10/11 | 進入禁止1 | 10 |
  | 9 | 12/13 | キャラクターを前面表示 | 12 |
  | 10 | 14/15 | 歩行速度低下 | 14 |
  | 11 | 16/17 | 強制下移動 | 16 |
  | 12 | 18/19 | 強制上移動 | 18 |
  | 13 | 1A/1B | 乾いた大河 | 1A |
  | 14 | 1C/1D | 設定無し | 1C |

  2-658 leaves flags 02/03, 04/05 and 10/11 blank in his flag table —
  exactly the entries this alignment fills. The pixel coincidence that
  started the old reading still stands as geometry: map 0x04's flag-04
  rectangles (all anchored at (0,9)) cover exactly the rendered sea,
  and 188 of the maps with a property region carry flag-04 rectangles
  (top: 0x058, 0x1E5, 0x09A at 77 each). Usage weights over those maps:
  flag 00 x7032, 04 x3251, 09 x690, 01 x959, 81 x110. But their RUNTIME
  effect is the low-buffer EOR stamp of writer 4 ("Chip default
  passability"): flag 04 stamps 0x04, which blocks nobody — the sea's
  walk block must come from its composer chip bytes (open item (f)),
  and the 進入禁止 family 0E-11's 29 entries were never the general
  wall source: that is the composer's `1E`/`1F` tree bytes plus the
  table's `E0` rows.
- `30` appears between block-2 entries (tiny 1x0 rectangles) with
  unidentified meaning; parsing accepts it, walkability ignores it.

Walkability model (RS3MapEditor2 manual, `説明書/RS3MapEditor2.txt`;
the zone bit model survives in the ENGINE bytes, not in the rect
entries): a tile's movement zone rides bits 4-5 of its attr byte
(`24`/`25` = zone 2 water, `1E`/`1F` = zone 1 land), the gate's
land-actor path blocks table row 0x04 (byte 0 bit 4) for water-zone
tiles, and the manual's chip-property section pins the 水中扱い
semantics: 「水中扱いのエリアは、主人公の周りに波紋が出来るように
なり、魚型のモンスターが移動可能になります」. The party wades
水中-stamped tiles with a ripple effect; only 進入禁止 blocks
(「水中扱いや歩行速度低下などの属性も、進入禁止属性を上書きすると
進入可能になるので注意してください」).

Former ANSWER paragraph (blocks vs swim), corrected 2026-11-17: the
claim that the party never enters flag-04/attr-2 tiles on foot was an
inference from the zone-check code, and the cs_grid7 write-watch plus
the decoded gate disprove it — those rect entries never touch the attr
grid and their low-buffer stamp (0x04) blocks nobody. Whether the party
wades composer-written pond bytes (0x24) is open item (g): the gate
table row `00 08 00 00` passes the zone-0 party; `AttrWalkable` keeps
them blocked until a probe walks into a pond.

Map 0x04's walkability is unsettled while its sea-block source is open
(open item (f) in "Chip default passability"): the old 54.0% figure
came from treating flag-04 rectangles as the sea's zone-2 walls, and
cs_grid7 disproved that writer — the rectangles only stamp 0x04 into
the low buffer, which blocks nobody. Map 0x02 (Pidona old town) and
map 0x03, which share the property pointer `F421FA`, carry no zone
rectangles at all — two event points and one layer-1 toggle, then
unknown data (below) — so their canals decode as walkable. That is a
property of the original data: the region is byte-identical in the RS3
v1.1 base ROM. The canals are therefore gated by the remaining wall
source, the composer's per-chip property bytes — decoded 2026-11-17,
next section.

After the counted entries, every prop region carries the walk-attr
overlay stream (default byte + RLE runs; decoded 2026-11-17, see "Chip
default passability" below — 2-658's キャラ移動後に足跡を残したりする
ためのデータ reading was wrong on both counts: the data is not
footprints and the engine writes it into the attr grid, not the
`$7F:0000` buffer). Map 0x02/0x03's `FF C7 01 3F 01 00 61 ...` is that
stream: leading `FF` = the default byte position's stream bytes. The
real per-character footprint marks are runtime `$7F:0000`-buffer writes
(stamper C0:7830), unrelated to this region.

## Layer toggle and mask zones (engine runtime; disassembled 2026-11-16)

The property flags `20-23` (レイヤーマスク), `40-43` (layer-2 front/back
toggle) and `80-83` (layer-1 front/back toggle) are applied by the
engine's scrolling ROW BUILDER, not to the stored map. The layers' ROM
data is never modified; the effect reaches only the 64x64-tile VRAM
tilemap window around the camera (BG tilemap at VRAM `$3000`, written by
the row-builder descriptor setup at `$FF:2948`: `LDA $A2; ASL ASL ASL;
ADC #$3000` = quadrant base `$3000 + $A2*8`, source row buffer `($9F)`,
row length `$0020` words). Everything below is static disassembly of
`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`; no runtime trace has yet confirmed the cell
mapping, so the renderer does not model any of it (justification at the
end of this section).

### Zone registration (per visible rect row)

The property-rect handlers `$FF:282D` and `$FF:2846`, and three
same-family merge blocks — `$FF:2094` (same four table pairs, same
buffer pointers; an `EOR #$FF / AND (dp),Y` clear phase then a 16-bit
`ORA (dp),Y` phase (a lone `DEY` at `$FF:20B9` restores Y between the
phases; the loop's overall Y-stride over its `$4E` bytes is not
decoded),
`$FF:2116` (the OR/clear/re-OR form decoded below) and `$FF:21E7`
(`JSR $21B1`, six chunks, shift-left form) — plus the fill call at
`$FF:1FD3` all hang off one row-builder dispatcher: at `$FF:1FD6-1FE6`
it reads the zone record's type `LDY $D5A5 / LDA $D5B1,Y / AND #$000E /
TAX / SEP / JMP ($67E7,X)` — a WRAM-built pointer table whose matching
ROM words sit at `$FF:1F03`. The handlers stamp the zone into the per-cell table
`$7E:B100` and the record arrays `$D5B0-$D5CE`, indexed by `$D5A5`:

```
$FF:2863  B9 BA D5    LDA $D5BA,Y        ; row word offset (below)
$FF:2866  38 E9 00 28 SEC SBC #$2800
$FF:286A  0A          ASL
$FF:286B  18 69 00 B1 CLC ADC #$B100     ; $B1 = $7E:B100 + (D5BA-0x2800)*2
$FF:2872  99 C6 D5    STA $D5C6,Y        ; [B1]   = A   (word (x,   y))
$FF:2875  92 B1       STA ($B1)
$FF:2878  B1 E6       LDA ($E6),Y        ; source word, $E6 set outside this region
$FF:2879  E6 B1 E6 B1 INC $B1 / INC $B1
$FF:287B  1A          INC A
$FF:287C  99 C8 D5    STA $D5C8,Y        ; [B1+2] = A+1 (word (x+1, y))
$FF:287F  92 B1       STA ($B1)
$FF:2882..            ; $B1 += 0x3E -> +0x40: the same two words one tilemap
                      ; row down ((x,y+1), (x+1,y+1)), row stride 0x40 words
```

`$D5BA[Y]` itself is built at `$FF:2805-2816`:
`((($D5C3[Y]&0xFF)<<8 >>1) + $D5C4[Y])>>1 + 0x2800` = the WORD offset of
(row `$D5C3[Y]`, column `$D5C4[Y]`) in a 64-tile-wide, 128-bytes-per-row
layer tilemap based at `$7E:2800`. The four stored words are therefore
the 2x2-cell block at (x,y) — each cell carries a 16-bit value in
`$7E:B100`, and a second copy lands in the `$D5C6`-family arrays (which
the descriptor at `$FF:289F-28CF` hands to the DMA-shaped job table at
`$00..$1F`: copy 4 bytes from `$7E:$D5BA[Y]` to `$7E:$D5C6+Y` and 4 more
from `+0x20`).

### Row merge (the `$FF:2116` / `$FF:21E7` loops)

Before each merge, `$FF:2921` copies the previous row's words
`[+0x20..+0x3F] -> [+0x00..+0x1F]` and `[+0x60..+0x7F] -> [+0x40..+0x5F]`
of the `($9F)` row buffer (16-bit `LDA $0020,X / STA $0000,X`, 16
iterations), and `$FF:2A2B`/`$FF:2A5F` seed the `+0x00/+0x40` and
`+0x20/+0x60` blocks — 16 words each, 64 words = one full 64-tile row —
from the 64-byte table `$7E:D37F..D3BE`. The merge loop then folds the
zone values from the scratch tables `$7E:D33F..D37E` into four 16-byte
chunks of that row buffer (variant 1): `($A8)=($9F)+0`, `($93)=($9F)+16`,
`($AB)=($9F)+64`, `($96)=($9F)+80` — with `+0/+16` being the low bytes of
row words 0-15 after the `$FF:2921` copy. Variant 2 (`$FF:21E7`) adds
`($99)=($9F)+32` and `($9C)=($9F)+96` (six chunks). Variant 1, raw bytes
with the arithmetic:

```
$FF:2110  A2 00 00    LDX #$0000         ; X = 0,2,..,30 over the loop
$FF:2113  A0 00 00    LDY #$0000         ; Y = chunk byte index 0..15
$FF:2116  BD 3F D3    LDA $D33F,X        ; a
$FF:2119  EB          XBA
$FF:211A  BD 5F D3    LDA $D35F,X        ; A16 = a<<8 | b   (b = D35F[X])
$FF:211D  C2 20       REP #$20
$FF:211F  4A 4A       LSR LSR            ; A = (a<<8|b) >> 2
$FF:2121  E2 20       SEP #$20
$FF:2123  48          PHA                ; T = low byte, T2 = a>>2 (high byte)
$FF:2124  11 93       ORA ($93),Y        ; chunk93[Y] |= T
$FF:2126  91 93       STA ($93),Y
$FF:2128  68 49 FF    PLA / EOR #$FF     ; ~T
$FF:212B  C8          INY
$FF:212C  31 93       AND ($93),Y        ; chunk93[Y+1] &= ~T
$FF:212E  91 93       STA ($93),Y
$FF:2130  88          DEY
$FF:2131  EB          XBA                ; A8 = T2 = a>>2
$FF:2132..213D        ; the same OR / ~AND pair on chunkA8 = ($A8),Y
$FF:213F  BD 40 D3    LDA $D340,X        ; second subtable pair (a', b')
$FF:2143  BD 60 D3    LDA $D360,X
$FF:214C  11 93 91 93 ORA ($93),Y / STA   ; chunk93[Y+1] |= T'   (pure OR,
$FF:2150  EB 11 A8 91 A8 XBA / ORA ($A8),Y / STA ; no clear — pair 1 already
                                           ; cleared these bits)
$FF:2155  88          DEY
$FF:2156..2193        ; the same four chunks of the second buffer group
                      ; ($96=$9F+$50, $AB=$9F+$40) with the tables shifted
                      ; +0x10 ($D34F+X/$D36F+X and $D350+X/$D370+X)
$FF:2195  C8          INY
$FF:2196  E8 E8       INX INX
$FF:2198  C0 10 00    CPY #$0010         ; 16 iterations: Y=0..15, X=0,2..,30
$FF:219B  F0 03       BEQ $FF/21A0
$FF:219D  4C 16 21    JMP $FF/2116
```

The OR / clear / re-OR pattern leaves each chunk byte j with
`(~T(j-1) & old) | T'(j-1) | T(j)` — idempotent under re-application,
with the second subtable supplying the bits that land one byte further.
Net: one 2-bit value per byte position, two bytes per (a,b) pair. The
`>>2` shift discards the low two bits of every table byte, so each
byte-pair contributes exactly eight 2-bit values to two chunk bytes.
Variant 2 (`$FF:21E7`) is the same shape with four `ASL A / ROL $8D`
pairs (shift LEFT 4, overflow caught in `$8D`) in place of `LSR LSR`,
and six chunks (`$93=$9F+$10`, `$99=$9F+$20`, `$9C=$9F+$60` added).

### Table fill (`$FF:1FF7`, called at `$FF:1FD3`)

```
$FF:1FF9  9C 3F D3    STZ $D33F          ; clear D33F-D340 (word)
$FF:1FFC  9C 5F D3    STZ $D35F
$FF:2001  A6 90       LDX $90            ; start index, from $FF:29CA:
                                         ;   $90 = ($A5>>1 & 0xF8) | ($A5>>1 & 7)
                                         ;   = $7E:B000 + (rect row>>1 & 0xFF)
$FF:2006  22 E6 E0 59 JSL $59E0E6         ; PATCHED CALL (three NOP padding
                                         ;   bytes EA EA EA follow): returns
                                         ;   a source word A0 (X is the index)
$FF:2011  85 8D 4A    STA $8D / LSR      ; t1 = A0 >> 1
$FF:2016  99 62 D3    STA $D362,Y        ; D362[Y] = t1 & 0xFF
$FF:2019  EB          XBA
$FF:201A  99 42 D3    STA $D342,Y        ; D342[Y] = A0 >> 9
$FF:2020  05 8D 4A 05 8D                 ; t3 = ((t1 | A0) >> 1) | A0
$FF:2027  99 61 D3    STA $D361,Y        ; D361[Y] = t3 & 0xFF
$FF:202B  99 41 D3    STA $D341,Y        ; D341[Y] = t3 >> 8
$FF:202E  C8 C8 E8   INY INY / INX      ; Y += 2, X += 1
$FF:2031  C0 10 00    CPY #$0010         ; once Y hits 0x10: X += 0x78
$FF:2036  ... 69 78 00 ADC #$0078 / TAX
$FF:2040  C0 1E 00    CPY #$001E         ; until Y = 0x1E (15 iterations)
$FF:2045..2064       ; post loop: for X=Y=0,2,..,0x3A:
                     ;   D33F[Y] |= D342[X]   ($FF:204E-2051)
                     ;   D343[Y] |= D342[X]   ($FF:2054-205A)
```

The bit-spread (`x | (x|x>>1)>>1`) doubles each set bit downward —
consistent with building 2-bit-per-cell fields out of single source bits.
The callee `$59:E0E6` is
`CPX #$7FFF / BCC / LDA $EC0000,X / XBA / LDA $EC0008,X / RTL` (and the
same on `$600000,X` for X ≥ 0x7FFF): it merges the LOW BYTES of two
16-bit ROM words eight bytes apart — a bank-`EC` bit table (file
`0x2C0000`) for small X.

### What this decodes, and what it does not

Verified statically: the merge loop byte semantics above; the
registration 2x2-cell stamping into `$7E:B100` with the word-offset
arithmetic; the fill's bit-spread formulas; the row-buffer seed/copy
flow (`$FF:2921`, `$FF:2A2B`, `$FF:2A5F`); the descriptor/DMA hand-off
(`$FF:289F-28CF`, `$FF:2948`).

NOT determined, with the exact blockers:

1. Rect geometry -> table/cell mapping. The fill's start index is `$90`,
   set at `$FF:29CA` from `$A5` (`B000 + rect_row>>1`) in one path but at
   `$FF:1FA0-1FCF` from `$8D` (a `0x2000`-range tilemap row offset) in the
   dispatcher path — the two never meet in the decoded region, and the
   code that consumes the `JSL $59E0E6` result into per-cell fields of a
   NAMED map cell is not traced. The merge's Y covers only chunk bytes
   0..15 (row words 0..15 of each 32-word half), so which half-row
   iteration processes which map columns — and why the other 16 words per
   half are never merged — is unresolved.
2. The meaning of the merged bits inside the final VRAM word (chip
   replace vs priority vs palette) — the consumer of the merged chunks
   `($9F)+0/+16/+64/+80` after `$FF:21A0` (`JSR $2948`) is not decoded.
3. The `($E6),Y` read at `$FF:2878`: the `$E6` pointer is set outside
   every decoded region.

Do NOT use WRAM captures of `$D340-$D3BE` as per-map toggle data: on two
different maps (opening scene and the previous session's map-0x250
capture) the bytes are identical (`$D353..$D35D` =
`0c 00 1e 0c 3f 12 3f 12 1e 0c 0c`, and an `aa 00 55 00` checker at
`$D380+`) — map-independent UI scratch. The `$D37F..D3BE` row-seed table
is written by the opening-screen uploader `$C0:1A2A`
(`LDA $FDE020,X; STA $D37F,X`, X = 0..0x1E; the same routine uploads
`FD:E000` to VRAM `$3000` and `FD:E802` to CGRAM), i.e. it mirrors ROM
screen data, not map state.

### Renderer decision

`render.go`/`layer.go` model none of this. Reasons: (a) the effect is a
runtime, camera-window row-build effect; the ROM layer data the renderer
decodes is never modified; (b) on map 0x250 — the only map with
screenshot ground truth — every cell of all seven flag-81 rectangles
holds the blank L1 fill word `0x0100` over the blank L2 fill word
`0x0000` (probe decoding both layers' record streams per the grammar
this file documents), so a correct model
of the swap could not change a single pixel there and the verified
835/896-tile match cannot drop; (c) the 273 maps carrying block-1 toggle
rectangles (survey over all 1024 records) cannot be modeled without
resolving blocker 1-2 above, and guessing would risk the 803-map
render-all. Re-opening this: run
`tools/emulator/mask_layertables.lua` while standing inside a toggle
rect, and correlate `$7E:B100` word offsets with the rect geometry.

## Chip value table (record flag3 bit 0x04; decoder: `ChipValues`)

The submap record's flag3-0x04 section (2-658's アニメーション設定) is a
per-chip table: a count byte, then count 16-bit little-endian words,
each chip ID (bits 0-9) with a 6-bit value (bits 10-15). A word at or
above 0xFC00 instead carries one extended byte and sets no chip.
Verified by exact record walks on maps 0x02/0x03
(`04 6A 20 7A 20 04 04 05 04` = chips 0x06A and 0x07A value 8, chips 4
and 5 value 1) and 0x04 (`03 90 81 80 21 87 21` = chips 0x180 and 0x187
value 8, chip 0x190 value 32); all byte-identical in the RS3 v1.1 base
ROM. Across records that walk cleanly to their end, values span 0-55 —
a 6-bit field, not the 0x00-0x1D walk-attribute palette, which supports
2-658's reading of the 6 bits as an animation pattern (his パターン？).
Water chips share value 8 (map 0x04's chips 0x180/0x187 sit inside the
pixel-verified flag-04 sea rectangles; map 0x02/0x03's canal chips
0x06A/0x07A carry the same value), but across 58 maps only 34.8% of
value-8 chip placements fall inside flag-04 rectangles, so value 8 is
not by itself a water signal and the section has no verified effect on
walkability. `cmd/exportmap` exports the table per map as
`chip_values` in map.json (decimal chip id -> value); godot may use it
for water animation or canal gating after in-game verification.

## Object chip property byte

The object stream's per-chip property byte (2-658's チッププロパティ)
is the composer's walk-attribute stamp: the engine keeps it in its
WRAM chip-entry table and STA's it over every tile the chip covers at
map load (FF:0DDA; write-verified, see "Chip default passability"
below). `decodeObject` now keeps it (objects.go) and `AttrGrid` applies
it. On map 0x02 it varies per chip instance (the same chip
carries several values through different objects). On map 0x04 the
composer's water coverage is unverified (the sea-block source is open
item (f) in "Chip default passability").

## Chip default passability (engine load-time; fully decoded 2026-11-17)

The engine keeps TWO per-tile walk byte grids in WRAM bank `$7F`,
both indexed `y*stride + x` with stride DP `$D0D1` = map width:

- the ATTR GRID at base `$7F:$1C`, where DP `$1C` = `$D0D5>>1` (the
  allocator at C0:48B8 does `pla; lsr; sta $1C`, and `$D0D5` mirrors
  the load size: 0x3000 for a 96x64 map -> base 0x1800; 0x2000 for
  64x64 -> 0x1000; 0x1000 for 32x64 -> 0x0800; watch-confirmed by the
  fill STA offsets of tools/emulator/cs_grid7.lua);
- the LOW BUFFER at base `$7F:$19` with `$19` = 0x0000, sitting right
  below the attr grid (its size is the same `$D0C5>>1` tile count).

The load-time fill writes BOTH buffers back to back: `STA [$96]` at
`$7F:0000` and at `$7F:$1C` (writer PC FF/15AE, two writes) followed by
MVN runs (FF/15CF). The low buffer fills with `00` on every map watched
(0x249, 0x24A, 0x250); the attr grid fills with the prop region's
default walk byte. The movement gate then consults both:

- C0:5BE1 `LDA [$1C],Y` — the attr byte, mapped through a 256-row ROM
  table at `$F9:A400` (file `39A400`, 4 bytes per attr byte -> WRAM
  `$D8FC`/`$D8FE`). Decoded gate order (S_C0_57FF, party on foot,
  party zone `$D9B2&0x30` = 0 measured on the roads):
  1. row byte 2: `(b2 & 0x88) == 8` -> block; else if bit 7 clear and
     bit 1 set -> block (rows 0x06/0x0A via bit 3, 0x0D/0x32 via bit 1).
  2. low buffer `LDA [$19],Y` at E_C0_58CC: bit 3 set -> block
     (C0:58CF `BIT #$08`, `BNE` -> return 1). THIS is the only
     low-buffer bit that stops the on-foot party: the bits-4-5 zone
     check behind it (C0:58DA-58EA vs `$D990`) never blocks — it only
     runs while `$D991` is set (not measured on foot) and otherwise
     merely clears `$D8FD` bit 3, a terrain flag no C0 code reads.
  3. table byte 0 by actor zone: a land-zoned actor (`$D9B2&0x30`
     == 0x10) is blocked by byte 0 bit 4 (row 0x04, 進入許可02, the
     boat zone); every other actor is blocked by `(byte0 & 0xC0) ==
     0xC0` — rows 0x0E-0x25's `E0`, the 進入禁止 family — and finally
     by the per-quadrant test `byte0 & (8 >> ($D9BA&3))`.
  Consequences: attr bytes `1E/1F` (trees) block via the C0 test; the
  pond byte `24` (row `00 08 00 00`) does NOT block the zone-0 party —
  its row only sets `$D8FD` bit 3, a terrain trigger (bit 7 of `$D8FD`
  is the ripple consumer at C0:778A/C0:7857); behavioral confirmation
  still pending, so `AttrWalkable` keeps zone-2 bytes conservatively
  blocked (see below).
- C0:58CC `LDA [$19],Y` — the low buffer, bit 3 blocking the step.

Attr-grid byte sources, stamped at map load (write-watch
tools/emulator/cs_grid5.lua frames 28443-28516 on the 0x250 load;
cs_grid6.lua held the watch to frame 43100 with ZERO further writes —
no runtime pass exists; cs_grid7.lua re-watched the WHOLE $7F bank
across the 0x249 -> 0x24A -> 0x250 loads). The attr grid's only
load-time writers, in engine order:

1. **The prop region's default walk byte** — the first byte after the
   counted entry list, replicated over the whole grid (FF:14B3-14C3,
   JSR $15A6 MVN). Map 0x250's byte is `01`, 0x24A's is `01`, 0x249's
   is `00`. A single per-map byte, not a per-chip table.
2. **Object chip property bytes** — 2-658's チッププロパティ. The engine
   keeps them in its WRAM chip-entry table and the composer STA's one
   byte per composed tile over the grid (FF:0DDA/0DDB, `CMP #$FF` /
   `BEQ` skip; 0x250: 3895 writes over 3347 distinct tiles, all inside
   `$7F:$1C..+$1C`). On 0x24A the composer DID write `00` fourteen
   times (vals `1F x666 1E x303 24 x83 00 x14 25 x3 06 x3`). A `00`
   property stamps `00` like any other byte (only `FF` is skipped): the
   batch sweep (below) found 1431 wrong tiles on 004B and 1389 on 0322
   while the decoder skipped `00`. On 0x249 the composer
   wrote NOTHING: every object chip property byte is `FF` there, so
   both 0x249 byte grids settle all-zero.
3. **The prop region's overlay RLE** — decoded INTO THIS GRID by
   FF:14D7-1562 (STA at FF:153E, reported as writer PC `FF/1540`;
   0x250: 232 writes `24 x134 1E x87 01 x7 1F x4`; 0x24A: 35 writes).
   This is the pass the earlier session mistook for a runtime rewrite
   and 2-658 mistook for 圧縮された足跡データ — both halves wrong: the
   buffer target is the attr grid, and the data is attr runs, not
   footprints. Grammar (byte-exact, see `applyAttrOverlay` and
   `TestAttrOverlay250`):

   - header `[v1][v2][v3?]`: v1 = the transparent marker (equals the
     default walk byte); v2 is the first write value; when v2 == v1 a
     third byte takes its place (FF:14F6-150A).
   - run loop: a count byte (`FF` = 16-bit LE word) runs the current
     value; writing is skipped while the current value equals v1, and a
     current value of `FF` writes v1 instead (FF:1532-153E). After each
     run the current value toggles between v1 and the alternate
     (FF:154E-155E).
   - a `00` count is context-dependent: reached after a toggle (FF/150F)
     it is a VALUE CHANGE — the next byte replaces both the current and
     the alternate value (FF:1527-152E); reached after a value change
     (FF/150B) it ENDS the stream (FF:1562 RTS). The loop also stops
     once width*height tiles are consumed.

   The engine reaches the routine per prop chunk: C0:4451 calls
   FF:144A (entries + fill) and C0:4463 calls FF:14D7 (overlay) back to
   back; maps such as 0x04 carry several counted chunks in a row, and
   only the first fill runs, so later chunks contribute entries but
   never re-fill or re-overlay the grid.

4. **The prop region's rect entries stamp the LOW BUFFER, not the attr
   grid** — writer PC FF/158F (the FF:1563 rect loop, right after the
   overlay routine), one EOR per tile: value = `flag & 0xFE` (bit 0 is
   the size encoding, dropped), rect = `(x, y, W+1, H+1)` (both size
   encodings, the nibble form inclusive of the +1). Write-verified
   byte-exact on three maps (cs_grid7.lua; `gridprint ... capture`
   reconstructs and diffs: 0/4096, 0/2048, 0/6144 tiles differ):
   event points (flags 08/09) stamp `08` — the gate's bit-3 block, so
   EVENT TILES STOP THE STEP (bump-triggered events); mask rects
   (20/21) stamp `20`, layer-2 toggles (40/41) `40`, layer-1 toggles
   (80/81) `80`; overlaps EOR (0x40 over 0x80 -> `C0`, `0x40` over
   `0x20` -> `60`, a duplicate rect cancels to `00`). Flags 04/05 stamp
   `04` and block nobody — the former "attr-2 water rectangles" model
   of the property layer is engine-disproved, and map 0x04's sea block
   must ride whatever its composer writes (still open, needs a 0x04
   load watch). Decoder: `internal/mapfmt.LowGrid`; `Walkable` ANDs its
   bit-3 tiles into the walk grid.

   The former "footprint marks live in the low buffer" reading is also
   corrected by cs_grid7: the stamper C0:7830-family (writer PCs
   C0/787B, C0/79C5) writes the THIRD per-tile buffer at `$7F:$1F`
   (DP `$1F` = `$D0D5`, the actor movement/terrain scratch), never the
   `[$19]` low buffer — its writes sat at `$7F:2103+` (0x249),
   `$7F:10FB+` (0x24A) and `$7F:3098+` (0x250), each `stride*leaderRow`
   indexed.

Decoder: `internal/mapfmt.AttrGrid` — fill byte, then object props,
then `applyAttrOverlay` (that order is the watch's write order), and
`internal/mapfmt.LowGrid` for the low buffer. `AttrWalkable`'s rule is
the gate's own ROM table row (below): the former conservative zone-2
extra rule is RETRACTED — behavioral evidence 2026-11-17 shows the
party standing on and wading `24` tiles (see the full-map section).

## THE WALK GRID IS THE FULL MAP (2026-11-17, winorigin2.lua; supersedes
## the retracted camera-window reading)

tools/emulator/winorigin2.lua watched, with PCs, the move gate's attr
fetch (read at PC C0/5BE1), the bounds cells `$D2EE-$D2F1` and the
whole `$7F:1800-2FFF` attr-grid region while the party walked north on
0x250 (frames 28443-42000, up/right legs, stored py 488 -> 304 = tiles
58 -> 38). Facts, each watch-backed:

- **One grid byte = one map TILE, and the grid is the whole map.** The
  fetch offset is `(py>>3)*D0D1 + (px>>3)` with `$D9AA/$D9AC` read
  directly: at frame 20001 the leader (296,280) fetched offset 0x0D45
  = row 35, col 37 = (280>>3, 296>>3) exactly; at the walk's stop
  (104,304) it fetched (13,38) = byte `01` = the model's AttrGrid
  value at that tile (probe TestProbeWinOriginCorridor). The stored
  positions are 8px units; `>>3` IS the map tile. `D0C5>>1` grid bytes
  = W*H tiles — 6144 on 0x250 = the full 96x64 map. There is no window
  and no origin.
- **The grid is never rewritten after load.** Zero writes into
  `$7F:1800-2FFF` across frames 28900-42000 while the party walked
  twenty tiles north. (The retracted "streamer rewrites the grid"
  inference came from pocket_probe2's fetch log, whose cycling rows —
  59/25/38... — were WANDERING-NPC fetches: the gate serves every
  actor, and the pocket_probe2 watch attributed all fetches to the
  leader's coordinates.)
- **The bounds are map TILE margins, set once per map load.** The
  C0:4F6E stream handler ran at frames 21293 (0x249), 24409 (0x24A)
  and 28443 (0x250) and never again (WCELL write PCs C0/4F73-4FEB). It
  reads five stream bytes `[$B7],Y`: `$D2EF`=b1, `$D2EE`=b2,
  `$D2F1`=b3, `$D2EC`=b4 (16-bit STA with a high byte), `$D2F0`=b5;
  derives `$D2E6`=(b2+16)<<3, `$D2E8`=(b1+17)<<3, `$D2EA`=(b5-13)<<3
  (b5 < 0x20 -> (0x1C-13)<<3 = 0x78); then applies the fixed deltas
  C0:4FD0-4FE8 (`EF+=2, EE+=4, F1-=2, F0-=1`) and sets `$D591` = 
  (`$D2E8` >= `$D2EC`). S_C0_57FF then confines every step to map
  tiles X [`$D2EF`, `$D2F1`) and Y [`$D2EE`, `$D2F0`) by comparing
  `$99`=(px+anim)>>3 and `$9C`. Measured settled boxes: 0x249
  [2,61)x[4,55); 0x24A [2,29)x[4,49) (a second writer, PCs C0/48B3 and
  C0/48BF, touches `$D2F1` on that load); 0x250 [2,93)x[4,62).
- **Edge events fire from the bounds edge.** Map 0x250 carries no
  event-point tiles at all (its prop region's only entries are the
  seven flag-81 layer-1 toggles; the LowGrid has zero bit-3 stamps),
  and the bounds' Y minimum is 4 — so the N-edge event 084E can only
  be triggered by PUSHING the y=4 bounds edge. The walker holds north
  at row 4 (tools/emulator/walk3loane.lua). The 0x24A->0x250 crossing
  at frame 28435 fits the same shape: a push into 0x24A's south bound
  y=49.
- **The pond byte `24` is engine-open on foot, now behaviorally
  proven** (was open item (g)): the party STOOD on `24` in the arrival
  clearing (fetch (13,58) = `24`, frame 28908) and waded the `24` band
  at rows 43-44 walking north. `AttrWalkable` models the gate's ROM
  table row directly now (F9:A400: block on row byte 2 `(b2&0x88)==8`
  — rows 06/0A water, 31; on b2 bit 7 clear + bit 1 set — 0D/32/33/36;
  on row byte 0 `&0xC0==0xC0` — the E0 進入禁止 rows; or any quadrant
  bit `b0 & (8>>quadrant)` — modeled all-quadrant-clear). The gate's
  bits-4-5 zone check never blocks a zone-0 party (still only clears
  `$D8FD` bit 3).
- **Party tile = ($D9AA>>3, $D9AC>>3)**; the stored position wobbles
  ±1 column with the walk animation (px 96..104 across cols 12/13) and
  the fetch adds the per-frame animation offset (table `$FF:6700`,
  indexed by `$D9BA` walk-state) before `>>3`, so a step check can read
  the neighbour cell mid-stride. Actor 0 = leader, stride 0x40.

The composer/fill/overlay stamps and the low-buffer rect stamps ARE the
full map's content: `gridprint ... capture` diffs of the cs_grid7
snapshots (0/6144 on 0x250, 13/2048 on 0x24A, 0/4096 on 0x249) compare
like with like — model tile grid vs engine tile grid at the same
coordinates. The model is engine-exact for planning; the walk planner
BFSes on it from the live tile (walk3loane.lua embeds gridprint's
engine-true print of 0x250).

Party position cells (kept from the earlier section): actor record
stride `0x40` from `$D9AA` — position X `$D9AA/$D9AB`, position Y
`$D9AC/$D9AD` per actor (C0:5469 `$D9AA,Y LSR LSR LSR` = tile X fed to
the tile fetch, C0:5D24 reads). Actor 0 = leader. The intro scripted
walk always deposits the party in the 0x250 arrival clearing, tiles
(12..13, 58..59), regardless of input program (grid5, dir round 1,
walk5, probe2, winorigin2 all land there).

Chain-map identification: the object-config byte `$D2E3` alone is NOT
a map fingerprint — road map 0x253 (64x128, the camp-journey road) shares
cfg `02` with 0x250. The runtime state is the triple
(cfg `$D2E3`, `$D0C5`, `$D0D1`); settled values seen: 0x24B =
05/3000/60, 0x249 = 26/0800/40, 0x24A = 07/1000/20, 0x250 = 02/3000/60,
0x24E camp = 2E/2000/40, 0x253 = 02/4000/40, and the post-ambush story
montage revisits 35/0800/40, 01/1000/20, 24/3000/40, 39/.../80 and
22/.../40 (walk7 SRAM-continue run). (D0C5 flaps through transient
values during a load — poll until it settles.) The engine bank dump of
the 0x253 load diffs 0/8192 against the model's AttrGrid/LowGrid
(gridprint capture on the walk3loane run log) — the full-map model
holds on the chain's own road map.

The camp-journey chain so far (walk3-walk7 evidence): 0x250 N-edge
push (y=4) -> edge event 084E -> camp 0x24E arrival (31,21), cutscene
advances on busy-A taps, then a mapJump to road 0x253 with the party

## Batch map sweep (2026-11-20; attr grid and low buffer, 178 of 179 targets exact)

Method: `tools/emulator/mapsweep.lua` boots the row-0 opening, then for
each global jump-table index writes the queue word `11 xx` into the empty
queue (`$D6BD`) and lets the engine's own drain load the map; after it
settles it dumps bank `$7F` and logs `GEO` (`$D2E3` = the loaded header's
ObjectConfig, D0C5/D0D1/D0D5, and `map=` from `$D0A7`). `gridprint
<rom> sweep <log> [map]` diffs the attr grid at `$7F:(D0D5>>1)` with
stride D0D1 against `mapfmt.AttrGridVariants` (fresh-game extras from
`triggers.MapTriggers.FreshLoad`) and prints a diff grid for one map.
`probe_sweepseq_test` diffs composer/overlay write sequences against a
write-watch log (the sweep script plus a `$7F` write callback).

Result over the 179 distinct jump targets: **178 maps byte-exact on
both the attr grid and the low buffer, none differing**. 0331 never
loads through `11 E4`, by design: record E4 (`C0 31 03 1F 26`) has flag
bit 6, and C0:C270 -> C2B6 then only places the leader at (31, 38) on
the current map (probe: C109/C10E/C153/C22B run, `$D0A7` stays 0250).
E4 is the only global jump record with bit 6; exportmap marks such
records `stay` and the field repositions instead of loading. Low-buffer bits 0-1 change after the load (footprints:
C0:7C9E-7CCC ORs them in as actors walk and swaps the layer-1 tile);
the sweep counts them apart. Targets the first logs could not check
(jumps that stalled behind an arrival event, or ended on another map)
were rerun three per fresh boot.

Model fixes the sweep forced, each confirmed by the engine code and the
sweep counts (commit messages carry the per-map numbers):

1. `00` object properties stamp (only `FF` is skipped).
2. Repeat-op chip words are read high byte first by every reader
   (`LDA [$8D],Y` / `XBA`); ops 6-10 read them low first, op 10 two bytes
   late (FF/08A7 takes the chip right after the size byte).
3. The grid (and render) size is the layers' size, not the header's.
4. Object rect loops: after each step an end in the `$F0+` zone stops
   once the coordinate wraps below `$80`; otherwise a coordinate in the
   `$F0+` zone continues, and the loop runs while coordinate < end
   (FF/0943-0959, FF/0975-098B).
5. Object rect/run read a palette-override byte after the chip word
   when chip bit 13 is set (FF/08FF, FF/09A1) — `$A6` is the high byte
   of the word in `$A5`, the record flag only for direct placements.
6. Object chip skip: cx = (cx+S) mod width, cy += (cx+S) div width
   (FF/0F49-0F62); the old "mod width + width" reading kept later
   chips on one row.
7. The record table is the hack's `5A6A50` (above).
8. Record field order after flag3 bit1 (C0:40DB-4626): flag2 bits 7, 6,
   5, 4 (variants), 3, then the `$D2F7` blocks (flag2 bit0's second
   byte) bits 6, 7, flag2 bit2's two bytes, bits 5, 4, 3. The chest
   block is a 3-byte header (count, chest object `$D0ED`, `$D0EE`) plus
   per chest flag, content (unless flag&0C == 08), open flag, x, y,
   event word (when flag&0C == 08).
9. Layer 3 (flag1 bit5) is composed after layers 2 and 1 and stamps
   its chip properties too (00FD's pond).
10. Variant property regions also EOR their rect entries into the low
   buffer.
11. Post-overlay passes, in loader order: chest objects (FF:1CEE, object
   `$D0ED` (+1 opened) at (x-1, y-2)); variant layers kinds 10/20/40
   (`$D2DD`/`$D2DB`/`$D2D9`, the base composer); variant property
   regions kind 80 (no fill, `$D8F3`; overlay RLE over the grid).

Palette override (FF/0DF7-0E23): `$B4 = (byte>>2)&0x1C`, zero disables;
a chip whose palette field equals byte bits 4-6 gets `word & E3FF |
(byte&0xF)<<10`. Tile words against the dumps' layer buffers: 62150
differing words over 168 layers with this rule, 66837 with the old one.

Priority pass FF:19B7 (ported, `mapfmt.applyPriority`): word bit 13 is
toggled (`EOR #$20` on the high byte, FF:19D5; the disassembly listing
misaligns it as ORA) on layer-1 tiles whose low-buffer byte has bit 7,
in one linear loop over `$D0D5` bytes, and, with flag1 bit 6, on layer-2
tiles whose low byte has bit 6 (2-D loop over the layer's own size). A
toggle, not a set: 0250's (5,16) chip word carries the bit (composer
writes 6D at FF:0E36) and the pass writes 4D (FF:19D9). `gridprint
<rom> tiles <sweep log>` compares tile words with the dumps: over 96
layers the words differing only in bit 13 drop from 2750 (no pass) to 14,
and 78 layers are exact (70 before the stretch-copy fix below); the
rest are tile-word gaps (3-188 words on
small layers) or layers whose buffer the 0x200-aligned base search does
not find in the 32 KB dump (128-wide layers, 0176, 0000).

The field draws in mode 1 with the BG3 priority bit (`$2105` = 09 on
0250 and 007A) and field sprites at OBJ priority 2 (OAM probe on 0250).
Layers 1/2/3 sit at the buffers `$D2D9/$D2DB/$D2DD` (2800/4800/6800 on
64-wide maps, 5000/9000/D000 on 128-wide ones): with those exact bases
every layer 1 and 2 of 0000, 0004, 009D, 0176, 0232, 0379 and 00FD
matches the model word for word (the earlier "large mismatches" were
the 32 KB best-base search). Layer 3 is BG3: its buffer holds chip -
0x280 with bit 13 forced on (00FD: 3996 blank words 2000 and 100 such
words), drawn from its own 2bpp tiles (header bytes after the palette
set: `$D2E1` -> F9:AD00 stream to VRAM 0x3000, FF:1065; `$D2E2` -> 16
colours from EC:A000, FF:1179). Bottom to top: BG2, BG1 without bit 13,
sprites, BG2, BG1 with it, then BG3. exportmap writes `map.png` (below
sprites), `map_over.png` (above) and `map_bg3.png` (layer 3 alone),
likewise per variant.

The record's flag3-bit-4 block is the screen setup (C0:3F55): main
screen (bit 5 makes it conditional on a vanilla flag range, 2 bytes),
sub screen, `$2130`, `$2131`, `$2132` (fixed colour); without it, or
outside the range, 17/17 and no colour math (C0:3F3B). The field adds
or subtracts layer 3 when it sits on the sub screen only (007A: 13/04,
math 13), and tints the map with the fixed colour when math reads it
(the common 17/00 with math 93/83). Halving and per-layer enables are
approximated (see `map_view._apply_screen`). The same holds for BG1
and BG2: 024C (main 16, sub 15, math 03) keeps BG1 (darkness and torch
halos) on the sub screen only and adds it onto BG2. Composed that way
(main BG3, else BG2 + sub BG3/BG1, else backdrop) it matched 56144/57344
screenshot pixels; BG1 drawn over BG2 matched 210. The field composes
the screen per pixel (tile_layers.gd SCREEN, two priority classes
around the sprites: BG3.1, BG1.1, BG2.1 above; BG1.0, BG2.0, BG3.0,
backdrop below; main from $212C layers, sub from $212D layers or the
fixed colour, math by the main pixel's layer bit, halving skipped on a
sub backdrop). tests/screencheck.gd on emulator screenshots: 024C
56144, 007A 57224 (effect 3 phase 12), 02B8 56985 (effect 2 phase 1)
of 57344, the rest sprites; at the best offset (screencheck saves the
composed map with offset -1) 00FD 54538, 0233 45831 (its sea is A2C6's
animation at another phase, plus sprites). 0010, 0178, 0249 and 01E6
were black at the capture (screen off, an entry event); their "matches"
were black against black and prove nothing.

The camera (C0:8668-86E8, map_view._update_camera): after the party
step the screen's left edge `$D6DD` (= `$D93F` + 12, BG HOFS) and top
`$D6DF` (VOFS, first row shown VOFS + 1) are the leader at x - 124,
y - 116, the leader clamped into the follow window C0:4F6E builds from
the header: x (PosX + 0x11)*8 .. (SizeX - 0x11)*8, y (PosY + 0x10)*8 ..
(SizeY - 0x0D)*8 (SizeY below 0x20 counts as 0x1C; a 32x32 map's x
max one pixel more, C0:488E). The object gate window ($D2EE-$D2F1,
map.json bounds) is PosX + 2, PosY + 4, SizeX - 2, SizeY - 1 (Controls
bit 4: x widened 2 each side); then C0:4884-48BC fixes x1: a 32x32 map
one tile more, otherwise, without Controls bit 4, a window narrower
than 1Eh tiles opens to x0 + 1Fh, clamped to the width - 1 (0267: the
header's 29 becomes the engine's 33; 250 maps change). An open map
(Controls bit 7, `$D0DD`) does not clamp. With Controls bit 4 (C0:A33F:
BG scroll starts at -12, `$D6DD` 12 px left) the left edge is the leader
x - 136; 0011's walk matched on all 309 frames (tests/camera_0011.json). A 0249 walk (right, then down)
matched on 309 of 309 frames (tests/camera_0249.json, selftest), and the
formula reproduces the screenshot offsets of 024C (124, 61), 02B8 (236,
285) and 00FD (124, 21). The camera only moves with the leader's steps
and with op 1B on the leader (a camera pan, docs/action-scripts.md
"Op 1B"), so a teleported leader (the 007A probe) leaves it behind. Field figures
draw at the map's scale with their top-left at object (x - 5, y - 22)
(00FD's leader: 279/302 px); they used to draw at half scale with a
4x-zoomed view. Sprites take no colour math yet (the 0x93
darkening maps darken sprites in the ROM). Effect 7 (024C, C0:E1D9) shifts BG1
alone by FF:7218 on screen lines [96 - phase, 176 - phase): FF:9B5B
points HDMA bands 0-5 and 11 at plain rows (D853) and 6-10 at the wave
rows (D813), band 0 holding 16 - phase lines, phase every 4th frame;
the emulator's table matched at passes 170-180. The field takes screen
line 0 as 112 px above its camera centre.

The field draws tile layers with a shader (godot/tile_layers.gd) from
exportmap's `tiles.bin` (u16 W, H, then BG1/BG2/BG3 words), `chr.png`
(chip pixels as palette indices, 128 px wide, 2bpp BG3 tiles from chip
0x280) and `cgram.png` (BG palettes 0-7 as 128 colours), so graphics
animations can rewrite chips and colours. Baked `map.png`/`_over`/`_bg3`
stay as the oracle: tests/tilecheck.gd renders every map and variant 1:1
and compares (1007 maps and 12 variants pixel-exact on 2026-11-21).
A word's palette field indexes CGRAM directly: field 0 is CGRAM 0-15,
the layer-3 palette, or on maps without layer 3 the text palette FD:E802
(only FF:1179 writes CGRAM 0 at map load; 004E showed it). 20252 layer
1/2 words on 518 maps use field 0; the renderer used palette 1 for them.

The flag3-bit-2 list (C0:4054, FF:9935) is the graphics animation
list: a count (bit 7: install once, per-frame count cleared, only 01B6)
and per entry a word, chip = low 10 bits, script = (word >> 10) + 1, 0x40
meaning one more byte + 1; scripts are FF:A6CF pointers in bank FF. A
script whose first byte is F6-FF selects a screen effect `$D77B` instead
(FF -> 1, FE -> 2, FD -> 3, FC -> 7, FB -> 8, FA -> 0A, F9 -> 0B, F8 ->
0D, F7 -> 0F, F6 -> 10), run each field frame from C0:DEEC through
C0:DB67 (normal and window frames). Effect 3 (21 maps) is the BG3 wave:
HDMA channel 4 writes `$2111/$2112` per line from 7E:D7E2 (16 bands of
16 lines, all pointing at the rows at D893), row k's offset = BG3 scroll
+ 0x0C + FF:7218[(scroll_y & 15) + k], first band from row `$D77C`,
which steps every 4th frame. On 007A that matched 2156/2156 BG3 pixels
of an emulator screenshot. Effect 2 (23 maps, C0:E084) shifts BG1
and BG2 per line by FF:7158's (x, y) pairs (x all 0, y 0 1 1 1 0 0 and
ten -1): channel 4 feeds BG1 from D7B1 -> rows D853, channel 3 BG2 from
D780 -> rows D813 (C0:E842/E86C), row k = scroll + 0x0C + table[r0 + k]
with r0 = BG1 V scroll & 15, so again index (map_y - 13 + phase) & 15.
Its phase is 1 from the first call and steps when `$D77D`, reloaded
with 10, counts down to 0 (every 11 frames). 02B8: rows 16/16 at passes
170-180, and 56985/57344 screenshot pixels with the y offsets at phase 1
(45029 at the best offset without them). Effect 8 (11 maps, C0:E72D)
is BG2 alone by FF:6FD8's (x, y) pairs (C0:DF90 rows at D813, index from
BG2 V scroll), phase every 4th call; no reachable map to capture.
Effects 0D (0308, C0:E896) and 0F (01E6, C0:E734) are BG2 alone by
FF:70D8 / FF:7058 (x, y) pairs, phase every 4th call, 0F counting down;
rows matched the formula on 9 of 11 passes, the others caught BG2's
own scroll mid-update. 0F also toggles `$D6F3` bit 0 each frame (not
traced). Effect 10 (01B7/01B8, C0:E791) runs two: BG1 by FF:7158 with
effect 2's phase (C0:E027 after its own 11-frame counter `$D77E/$D77F`)
and BG2 by FF:6FD8 with a phase every 4th call (C0:DF90); the shader
takes a separate BG2 phase. No reachable map to capture. Effect 0A
(0013, C0:E283/E2B3) is ported: twelve BG2 x scrolls `$C858` start at 0,
each stepped by its speed (FF:6E88) whenever its rotating mask (`$C878`
from FF:6E72) carries; HDMA channel 3 (mode 2, `$210F`) sets BG2's x
scroll per band from BG2 row y0 = `$D93E`*8 + `$D949` + 4 (`$D93E`*8 =
load camera top - 12, so y0 = camera top - 8 + BG2's parallax y): the
first band k ends at FF:6E58[k], bands k+1..10 last FF:6E3E[j] lines,
then 8 for the rest (no table when y0 >= 0x130). On a 0013 capture the
accumulators matched after 180 and 230 frames and the table (06 001D,
18 000F, 01 0008 at y0 = 258) matched the model (selftest). That
capture's screen was dark (brightness 1, `$212C` = 0 after the injected
jump); with `$2100` = 0F and `$212C/$212D` = 17 written just before the
screenshot (the map's default setup) it matched 57336/57344 px at the
camera's offset (128, 221) with BG2's parallax y 46 and the bands
(57241 without the bands, 54712 without the parallax). Effect 0B
(026B, C0:E46E/E4E8) is ported: BG3 takes effect
3's wave with its phase every 8th frame (C0:E4C5 -> E181), and BG2
five bands built like 0A's (boundaries FF:6F08, heights FF:6EFE),
each band's x scroll = BG1's + FF:6F26[index], the index stepping when
its byte timer (FF:6F1C, reloaded) runs out (start FF:6F12; the cycle
1 2 2 1 0 -1 -2 -2 -1 0 loops at 8000); after the table the last value
holds. After 180 frames indices, timers and scrolls equalled the
engine's and the table (0B 000C, 48 000C, 10 000A) the model's
(selftest). On 026B's forced-screen capture: 49516/57344 px (46684
without the base offset below, 40339 without the bands; the rest is
BG3's twinkling stars). The variant `$D09E` is the effect entry's
parameter (the list word's low 10 bits, `$E463`, which FF:9B30 passes to
C0:E46A): 0 on 0261/026A/026B, 1 on 026C, 2 on 026D; bounds, heights,
timers and starts each move by 3Eh per variant, the cycle FF:6F26 is
shared. On 026D (reached by map moves 026B -> 026C -> 026D) variant 2's
tables explain all 317 logged frames of the engine's band state
(variants 0 and 1: none); the selftest checks the state 163 ticks in.
Variants 0 and 1 share timers and starts, so 026C is told apart by its
bands: the engine's table (`$D780`) at y0 148 ran 43, 80, 88, 16 lines,
variant 1's bounds (variant 0 would start with 75); the port's bands at
that y0 end at 191, 271, 359, 375 (selftest).

Two screen rules this map showed. `$2105` = 01 | (Controls bit 5) >> 2
(C0:C562): BG3 is above BG1/BG2 only with Controls bit 5 (996 maps),
else below them (11 maps; map.json bg3_top). And each layer wraps at
its own size (map.json layer_dims): a layer that fits its 64x32 tilemap
is uploaded whole, shown at screen + its own scroll, which counts from
the load camera, so against the camera's map px it sits (12 - load
left, 12 - load top) away (026B's 32x32 BG3: 0, -272).

BG2 drifts on its own on these maps: `$D943`/`$D949` (BG2 x/y offsets
added to the camera scroll) step every 4 frames (0308 x +1, 01E6 x +1
y -1). Effect 0D increments `$D943` when its rotating mask `$D980`
carries (C0:DB72); load (C0:A24A-A39C) zeroes the offsets and velocity
bytes `$D951-$D961`, applies type 3's `$D943 = -4`, Controls bit 4's -12
shift, and sets up per-layer scroll state from the record's flag2-bit-7
bytes `$D976/$D977`. The drift is ported (map.json "drift", the
compositor's bg2_off): with `$D977` bit 6 and scroll mode (`$D977 & 3`)
0 or 2, x takes FF:2A98[`$D977 & 0C`] when `$D976 & 0C` (bit 3 negates)
and y FF:2A98[(`$D976 & 3`)*4] when `$D976 & 30` (bit 5 negates); each
field frame both masks rotate right and a carry adds the speed (C0:8801).
17 maps drift; 0308 and 01E6 get 8888/+1 (and 01E6 8888/-1 on y), the
rates the engine's offsets showed. BG2's walking parallax is ported
too (map.json "parallax"): each camera step (C0:8441 x, C0:830D/835D y)
gives BG1 C0:82DD's one-shot mask for the leader's speed row (normal
walk 00FF x1: 8 px in 8 frames) and, with `$D976` bit 6, BG2 C0:82F5's
(0077 x1: 6 px, frames 1-3 and 5-7); a new step starts when the camera
moves after BG1's mask ran out. 0084's emulator walk (tests/
parallax_0084.json) matched on 310 of 310 frames, including a row-3 hop
(0003 x3). Scroll mode (`$D977 & 3`) 3 (9 maps, 0148-0159; `$35` = 9):
BG3's x scroll `$D94D` (its HOFS = `$D94D` + 12, PPU state checked) is
twice the camera's `$D93F`, its y `$D94F` equals `$D941`; 0149's walk
held that on 279 of 279 frames (tests/bg3scroll_0149.json). The
scroll counts from the map origin, not from the load position: the load
fills each layer from column S = camera column - 17 (C0:9DA3; BG1's
`$D900` = 62 on 0149), and with `$36` set (mode 3) BG3's `$D902` becomes
(2 * S) mod its width (C0:9E45; 28 on 0149). So in map space BG3 sits
8 * (S3 - S1) plus the camera's movement since load away from BG1: -300
on a forced-screen 0149 capture, 56306/57344 px (51370 and 51064 at 3
px either side; hiding BG3 gave 42824). Mode 3 (and 0 with `$35` set) also splits BG2 by HDMA
(FF:0439): rows below `$35`*8 (row = camera top - 8 + BG2's parallax y
+ line, as effect 0A's) scroll at `$D945` + 12, half the camera's x
truncated toward 0, the rest normally (0149: 44 lines at -3, then -18,
as its table showed); with it BG1/BG2 matched 42824 vs 40599 without. Mode 2
(0249, 0315; `$D019` = 1, `$35` = 0x26): FF:687C sets 64x64 tilemaps and
uploads the whole BG1/BG2 buffers, not BG3 (its tilemap stayed zero;
C0:4112 clears `$D8F5`), so BG3 is hidden. HDMA channel 3 (mode 3,
D780: one line, then end) writes BG2's scroll once per frame from
`$D945` + 12 / `$D94B` + 12: x = (camera x + 2) div 4, y = 88 + camera y
div 2, camera = `$D93F/$D941` (0249 walk: 310 of 310 frames,
tests/scroll_0249.json). The PPU state read after the frame showed the
CPU's later write (`$D943`, double rate), which HDMA overrides. A
forced-screen 0249 capture matched 54689/57344 px with BG2's row at line
0 = y + 12 (BG1's is its scroll + 1); 38463 with + 1.

The other entries are the graphics VM (godot/gfx_anim.gd). FF:9935
buffers, per entry, by the script's first byte b: b < 0x40, b chips
(chip + the next b offsets) from VRAM; 0x80-0xBF, b & 0x7F colours of
CGRAM palette `chip` (slots p*16 + offset); C0-F5, those colours as
5-bit components; 0x40-0x7F nothing but the palette's ROM id
(FC:F400[set*7 + p - 1]). The first timer is the list count minus the
entry's index. FF:9CDB (field frames without a window, C0:06C4) counts
each timer down; at 0 it reads the step (frames, parameter) at
steps + step*2, runs the script's handler (FF:A5FF), and an FF after the
step restarts the list. Handlers: 9F27/9F6E/A20D copy n/2, n/3, n/4
buffered chips from frame `parameter` onto chip.., 9D56 one chip, 9D43
one chip after replacing the hold with a field RNG roll 3-10 (C0:0726;
gfxcheck loads the engine's $0A/$0B per tick, since NPC scripts share
the stream), A1B5
one chip and then mirrors that buffered chip (E1:5526 is a bit
reversal); 9DE3 writes each colour to its slot and rotates the slots
(it reads no parameter, so its list is one step); A0C5 steps every
component by -1 (parameter != 0) or +1, wrapping as a byte and shown
clamped (E0-FF -> 0, above 1F -> 1F), parameter 80 loads ROM palette
id + the next byte and reloads 11 components from its colours 5-15, FE
plays sound effect (next byte) through C0:E9F7; 9FC7 loads ROM palette
id + parameter into palette p. 0000, 004C, 00FD, 0091, 0233, 0235 and 0272 matched an
emulator log of chips and CGRAM before each of 421 ticks exactly
(digests every 20 ticks in tests/gfx_digests.json, in the gate). A5A1
(01E6) finds palette AD in the OBJ slot list `$D6E2` (`$D6E1` long) and
queues EC:8000 palette AD + (`$14` & 2) / 2 into that slot; its step is
two bytes (the second unused) and runs every frame: the emulator's slot
read AD, AD, AE, AE before ticks at `$14` 8609-8612 and on (selftest).
The field shows figures drawn in AD as their exported _AE variant while
AE is loaded. A548 copies
n/6 chips; A25E/A4EC copy n/3, n/2 BG3 tiles while `$D8F5` (BG3 shown:
layer 3 present, cleared when the screen block's flag range fails,
C0:3D0D/3FBC; events toggle it at C0:20E3/21A9) is set. A2C6 rotates its
six 16 px chip pairs right by a pixel each call and copies like 9F6E,
advancing only when `$14 & 7 == 0`. A32C/A492 run every frame: on even
`$14` they rotate the colour slots (A32C from entry 7), and the step's
first byte is a frame mask, rewriting the colours while mask & `$14` !=
0, else fading a step (clamp 80-FF -> 0). gfxcheck injects the engine's
`$14`; the field counts its own. Map type `$D2D7` (bits 1-4 of `$D2F6`)
1 (12 maps, 0272 on) runs FF:6806 at load: a fixed single screen (scroll
0, buffers copied straight to the tilemaps) and FF:B1CF, which lowers
the first six entries' components by 0x20. 0272's later fade-in comes
from an event routine (FF:B1E4: 32 rounds of FF:B3FD), not the VM, so
its fixture stops at tick 340. Types 2, 3, 8 set a 32x32 BG2 tilemap
($2108 = 58). The type-1 screen needs no camera of its own: on 0272
(Controls bit 4, SizeY 31) the follow window clamps the screen to left
0, top 12, which the emulator showed, and the compositor with the
capture's CGRAM (screencheck's SCREENCHECK_CGRAM) matched 55116/57344

The type-1 arrival (ported 2026-11-21, godot/arrival_fade.gd): C0:C371
reads the arrival record's byte 0 (`$D0A6`, exported as `arrival` = bits
4-5); 10h and 20h pick special arrivals, anything else on a type-1 map
goes to C0:C3D9, which moves the leader (and `$D9EA`) 4 px left and

ticks after the VM install (0272: install 19607, objOp 51 at 19632). The
12 type-1 maps (0272, 027A-0281, 028F-0291) are entered only through
jump and move records (no walk-on exits) and all hold the same six
colour entries (A492, A32C x5), so the sequence's entry index is the
list index; a load without a record runs no sequence. 027A (jump D5)
runs it the same way: 16 ticks from install to objOp 51, and the replay
matches all 1777 ticks (tests/arrival_027A.json, the same lag cut-over
at 847), palette 7's B2D6 colours included. After the masks step OBJ is
subscreen-only and is added to BG2: the field moves the figures into a
viewport the compositor reads as its subscreen OBJ layer (an opaque
pixel replaces BG1 there unless BG1's tile is high priority), and
figures overlap by object y, the engine's OAM order. With the figures
as that layer (screencheck SCREENCHECK_OBJ) the frame-20778 capture is
57344/57344 exact (55116 without them). 027C, entered through real
records (jump 78, moves 08 -> 01AE, 01 -> 0120, 10 -> 0123), matches all

destinations; each now has a fixture anyway (2026-11-23,

3CFB00h + 5*D5 + 1; TRAILMAP confirms the retargeted map loaded) and

0272's emulator run (per FF:9CDB tick: `$14`, RNG, CGRAM) has 1744 ticks

Effect 09 (C0:E66C) writes BG1 offset-per-tile columns each frame: start
index ((`$D93F` >> 2) & 1E) + `$14`, x FF:7258 (whole tiles), y FF:7218;
the captured table at frame 20782 (VRAM 2800h) matches the formula
(k0 = 12). The probe's screenshot shows the screen 4 frames before its
```
