Tile animations (FF:1695) and footprints now rewrite the shader's tile
words instead of drawing pre-rendered patches.

The flag2-bit-1 list (`$D148`/`$D149`) is the tile-animation table
(ported: `mapfmt.TileAnimations`, exportmap `tile_anims.json` +
`anims[_over].png`, `map_view._tick_anims`). Entries are 4 bytes:
object id, kind (`$D14A`: low 7 bits index the timers FF:1EF5 and the
scripts FF:1F04, bit 7 staggers the start by `$D146`), sound step and
sound. FF:1BF7 registers each composer stamp of a listed id when the
object set has a second remap band (`$D0BF` != 0, id >= `$D0BF`, below
`$D0BD` when that band is higher), up to 22 entries; FF:1695 (FF:067C,
called by the field frame C0:06BC after the objects) counts each timer
down and steps its script: `81 n` waits n frames, `80` loops, any other
byte v restamps object id+v (C0:0CC2, raw chip words, so the load-time
priority toggles are lost on those tiles). 92 maps carry the list, 41
register entries; on 00B0's sweep dump all 48 words that differed from
the load-time model are animation frames (`gridprint tiles`). Sounds
(`$D14B/$D14C`) and the attr bytes the restamp writes are not modeled.

## Map BGM (not a record field)

**Port (2026-11-21):** exportmap writes each jump / move record's
resolved track as `music` (absent when flag bit 2 is clear); main passes
it on entry and map_view plays it, keeps the current track when the
record changes none, and uses the map-level `bgm` below only for an
entry without a record. The opening's 0250 then plays song 33 as the
emulator does (cutscenecheck). Event music words (queue `1D xx`) play
through map_view.play_track.

A submap record carries no BGM field — the 2-658 walk above accounts for
every byte, and the engine never reads one. The track a map plays on
arrival travels in the movement records (docs/triggers.md block 4 and the
global op-0x11 table at `3CFB00`): the 5-byte record's word bits 10-15
hold a 6-bit music request id, applied only when the flag byte's bit2
(music change valid) is set and the id differs from the current track
(engine: WRAM `$7EF546`; handler `$C0:2C2D` stores it, `$C0:BCF2` plays).
Event-op changes (dispatch word `1D xx`, handler `$C0:C570`) are
runtime-only.

The request id reaches the song table through two hooks, both
vanilla-identical in bokuno and located by static disassembly plus a
MesenCE runtime trace (2026-11-16):

1. Request `0x13` = "current protagonist's town theme": the play wrapper
   at SNES `$FF:064A` replaces it with (party-leader char id + `0x13`)
   before playing (`LDA $7EF000; CLC ADC #$13`; bokuno swaps the inline
   add for `JSL $59EA00`, a per-char request table at file `0x606D00` —
   the hack reordered the protagonist slots, its first eight values are
   still exactly `13 18..1A`'s set).
2. Every request below `0x7C` passes through the in-ROM remap table at
   file `0x62A2A` (SNES `$C6:2A2A`): entries `0x13`-`0x1A` = the eight
   protagonist themes, `0x1B`-`0x1F` = the fixed dungeon themes
   (魔王殿地下, ジャングル, 海底宮, 水晶の廃墟, 氷湖), `0x20`+ identity.
   Byte-identical vanilla vs bokuno. This table is kaerulabo's observed
   主人公変更バグ table shifted by `0x13`
   (http://kaerulabo.web.fc2.com/rs3/data/chara_data_BGM.html); spot
   checks agree row for row (request `0x05` = 聖王の町ランス plays in
   Lance; `0x13`+slot `0x0C` → `0x1F` → 氷湖; slot `0x0E` → `0x21`
   field theme; slot `0xF2` → `(0x13+0xF2)&0xFF` = `0x05` — kaerulabo
   row F2 リューシアナッサ = Lance's theme).

`cmd/exportmap` derives each map's `bgm` from this: it collects the
music-change records that target the map (global table plus every
map's block 4, skipping decodes with more than 64 destinations — the
measured garbage-decode floor is 85), resolves each request through the
hooks (request `0x13` resolved as protagonist ユリアン until the port
has protagonist selection), and exports the most frequent track (ties
to the lowest id) as `bgm` in map.json and map_catalog.json. Maps whose
arrivals request no music change export without the field; the Godot
map view then keeps the field theme (`godot/map_view.gd`). Verified
exports: `008A` (Lance) = track `05` 聖王の町ランス, `0010` (魔王殿) =
`07` 魔王殿, `0004` (Pidona wharf, a town map) = `04` protagonist
theme — all three match kaerulabo's observed placement.

## Render verification (2026-11-16, MesenCE screenshots; 2026-11-17 status)

The renderer (`internal/mapfmt/render.go`) draws layer 2 first, layer 1
over it, layer 3 last (overlay: map 0x249's layer 3 is 9 placements of
a tree-crown object).

PRIMARY EVIDENCE, upgraded 2026-11-17: the decode is verified against
the ENGINE'S OWN WRITE STREAM, which is stronger than the pixel proxy —
the composer write sequence (tile order, position, value) matches the
engine IDENTICALLY on 0x250 (3895/3895) and 0x24A (1072/1072), and the
settled attr grid is byte-exact (0/4096 on 0x249, 0/6144 on 0x250, 13
tiles write-0x00-vs-noop on 0x24A, walk-equivalent). The renderer's
INPUT is therefore exactly what the engine feeds PPU; pixel diffs vs
screenshots then measure only sprite overlays, HUD and party position.

Historical pixel comparison (2026-11-16): walk13
(`tools/emulator/shot_maprender.lua`) captures full-frame PNGs while
standing still, compared per-tile by `dumpmaps ... compare <id>
<shot.png>` (sliding 32x28 window, per-tile mean-RGB distance, worst
25% trimmed). The 2026-11-16 session recorded best window (52,16),
distance 27.7, 835/896 (93%) on map 0x250.

RESOLUTION 2026-11-17 of the "garbled map 0x249" hunt (the two traps
behind every sub-70% score recorded that day — the renderer was never
wrong):

1. **The `/tmp/shotcap-r2/shot_*_0249.png` captures are MAP 0x250.** The
   shot filename came from the scratch `$7E:2011` MAP cell read after the
   down-walk had already crossed 0x249 -> 0x24A -> 0x250; the load
   fingerprint at capture time is `cfg=02 d0c5=3000 d0d1=0060` = 0x250
   (the same fingerprint `ground_vram2.lua` logs). Compared against their
   real map, all six shots score 99% (888/896 tiles, trimmed distance
   9.5-9.7, best window (2,36)); the same shots against 0x249 score 61%.
   The historical "best windows around (2,15)" and the 65-67% sweep
   scores were this cross-map comparison, not renderer semantics.
2. **`dumpmaps compare 249` compared DECIMAL id 249 = 0xF9**, not map
   0x249: Go's `ParseInt(s, 0, ...)` reads a bare number as decimal.
   `parseMapID` now strips the optional `0x` and parses hex, the way map
   ids are written everywhere else in the project.

Ground truth for 0x249 itself (`tools/emulator/ground_shots249.lua`,
shot_22000, fingerprint `cfg=26 d0c5=0800 d0d1=0040`): 93% (836/896,
distance 9.8, window (32,29)). Map 0x249 is GENUINELY a dark dusk
forest — its layer-2 grass words carry palette field 6 = palette id
0x3a, the dark teal, and the engine's CGRAM at capture confirms it.

Palette evidence (`ground_vram2.lua`/`ground_shots249.lua` CGRAM
readback through `emu.read(emu.memType.snesCgRam)`): on 0x249 the
engine's CGRAM fields 1-7 are exactly palette ids `[0x36, 0x37, 0x00,
0x38, 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3c]` = set 0x30 bank 0; on the 0x250 state they are
`[0x22a, 0x22b, 0x25e, 0x226, 0x22e, 0x23d, 0x25f]` = set 0x14 bank 2
(`0x250` flag1 = 0xC2 -> bank 2). The renderer's field -> set[field-1]
mapping and the flag1 palette bank are engine-exact on both maps.

VRAM readback stays a dead end, re-confirmed: `emu.read(emu.memType.
snesVideoRam)` returns stale garbage (1132 "words", 0 tilemap matches),
and a CPU write watch on PPU `$2118`/`$2119` sees nothing (vramw=0 while
the CGRAM register counts 67k writes) — the tilemap rows reach VRAM
through DMA (channel 2, control 0x18, source $7E:E2xx row buffer;
`ground_vram2.lua` logs the DMA registers and its header records both
dead ends).

The remaining mismatched
clusters are tree canopies drawn as sprites in-game (the party walks
under them; out of scope for the map renderer).

Layer toggle/mask zones: decode status moved to their own section below
("Layer toggle and mask zones — engine runtime, decoded 2026-11-16"); the
renderer still does not model them, for the reasons given there.

The engine's object-config byte is the record header field this file
documents: a write watch on the engine's config cell `$D2E3`
(`tools/emulator/shot_d2e3_probe.lua`) shows each map load reading it
from the submap record via the sequential reader at `$C0/3D30` —
record+17 for bit5-set headers (map 0x249 -> 0x26), record+12 for the
rest (map 0x24A -> 0x07, map 0x250 -> 0x02).

## Party position and walk control (2026-11-16, MesenCE headless)

Facts established by scripted walks of the prologue area (walk13 timing;
tools/emulator/pos_hunt.lua, pos_y.lua, water_sweep.lua; raw logs in the
session's /tmp/journey2-agent):

- **Direction input needs ~900-frame holds to start a walk.** Holds of
  20 and 120 frames produced no party movement at all (WRAM unchanged
  beyond the ambient drift set); walk13's 900-frame legs do move the
  party. Harnesses that hold a direction for shorter bursts never walk,
  which masquerades as a hang.
- **Member-x candidate cells: `$7E:DBA8` and `$7E:DBE8`** (little-endian
  16-bit). On a 900-frame west leg both move (767→511 and 511→767 —
  −256 px and a partner swap, the formation reordering), and the east
  leg restores them exactly. `$7E:DBF4`/`$7E:DBB4` behave the same with
  a 512-px step. The Y cells are still unpinned: every northward probe
  was blocked within 200 px (trees/water-zone pocket), so no cell showed
  a monotone vertical walk. The live leader cell is therefore not
  settled; navigation so far is driven by 900-frame legs plus the
  `dumpmaps compare` window of screenshots.
- **The map-id cell `$7E:2011/2012` is scratch during walks** (reads
  0249 before and 0000 after the party crosses submaps, per sprites.md's
  second session and this session's leg dumps). The stable map-load
  fingerprint is `$D2E3` (the record's object config byte, e.g. 02 for
  map 0x250) — but some map loads bypass the write watch on it, so poll
  the cell instead of watching writes.
- **The intro's story gate hangs a no-A harness.** Walking up/left out
  of the opening park fires a VM position check (a cutscene) whose
  dialogs wait for A; a leg program without the A-while-busy policy
  froze the game (WRAM static for thousands of frames). With the
  policy the legs run clean.

### Correction (2026-11-17, chain-walk session): the "member-x cells"
### are animation/phase counters, not positions

`tools/emulator/chain_walk.lua` runs (walk2-walk7, plain
`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`) overturned the member-x reading above. Evidence
(raw lines in the session's /tmp/chain-agent):

- The cell values quantize to `k*256-1` (255, 511, 767, 1023, and the
  low-value forms 0/1/2/3, 258, 514, 770): `$7E:DBA8` walked 771→3→771→0
  across three consecutive legs — no walk covers 3 tiles west then 3
  tiles east then 3 west in alternating 900-frame legs.
- Up legs moved the same cells by ±256/+512 (walk4 LEG 9/12: "up" legs
  with dA8=+512/+256), and battle-result windows reset them (walk3
  LEG 3 evaluated mid-battle-end: 266→517 with the battle screens on).
- The decisive check is on-screen: with the cells oscillating ±256/512
  per leg (walk7, legs 4-31), 16 screenshots taken across 29000 frames
  all match the SAME `dumpmaps compare` render window of map 0x250 —
  tile (52,15), trimmed mean distance 27.4, 94% — i.e. the party and
  camera never moved while the cells kept cycling.

The party-position hunt therefore restarts from zero: the differential
scans that found DBA8/DBE8 were locking onto walk-animation phase, and
the real cells remain unfound. Navigation evidence that DOES hold:
per-leg screenshots + `go run ./cmd/dumpmaps patches/bokuno_jp.sfc
<outdir> compare 0x250 <shot.png>` (sliding 32x28-tile window) — the
walk7 end state sits in the (52,15) window of 0x250, i.e. around tile
(60±8, 22±7), for every post-battle frame checked.

Battle cadence on the intro road (walk2/3/4/7, deterministic across
runs on the same input script): scripted battles fire at frames
37660/40284/43102/46787 with victory at +2100..+3200 each, won by
mashing A every 30 frames after the first 420 battle frames
(battle_sfx.lua policy). The battle-result windows hold `$76 != 0` for
30+ frame stretches (D51B=0E64 PC=FC:C830, then 0B44) — an event
detector must ignore busy stretches within ~3000 frames of a battle
end, or every result screen masquerades as a story event.

### Release condition of the 0x250 "frozen arena" (2026-11-17,
### release session: the intro is over; walk to the north edge)

`tools/emulator/release_probe.lua` ($76 write-watch, OAM sampling,
scroll-register watch, screenshots; logs in /tmp/release-agent/run1..3)
settles what holds at the arena:

- **No VM state and no engine hold survives at the freeze.** The intro
  chain ended normally — machine evidence in docs/vm-semantics.md
  §6.6 (close-out C0:3783 completed, frame record PC=FC:23C6/end=23C8,
  all close-out flags zero). The battles the west-leg scripts won are
  wandering-monster NPC touch events (0804 wrappers), not story gates.
- **The story exit is the map's north edge.** Map 0x250 carries no map
  data exit at all (0 exits, 0 triggers, its single Destinations entry
  unreferenced); the only way out is `EdgeEvents[0] = 084E`, the N-edge
  fragment that opens the camp-journey chain (`11 0c` → 0x24E (31,21),
  later `11 0e` → 0x4B (31,77) — in the consecutive fragments it
  tail-dispatches through, see docs/vm-semantics.md §6.6). Walking off
  y=0 fires it engine-side. The prescription for the walk harness: hold
  a north-biased leg program (900-frame legs) until y=0, with the
  battle A-mash policy — there is no input that releases a cutscene,
  because none is running.
- **Party movement is real and bounded by terrain, not by an engine
  lock.** The position cells ARE known now (2026-11-17): actor record
  stride 0x40 from `$D9AA`, pixel X `$D9AA/$D9AB`, pixel Y `$D9AC/$D9AD`
  (leader = actor 0); walk legs move them (walk1: dY=-24..-80 per clean
  450-frame leg) and they are the navigation instrument for scripted
  walks (tools/emulator/walk2loane_walk.lua). OAM evidence: walk7's up legs walked the party's sprites
  net +8 tiles north (screen y 210→82) while blocked after; run1's
  straight-up hold from a different intro path stood at a fixed screen
  position against a tree line for 36000 frames. What stops further
  progress is chip-collision terrain (the wall source still undecoded,
  see the walkability section above) plus the wandering monsters. A
  blind right-hand wall-follower (run6, 600-frame legs, OAM-0 blocked
  detection) swept the spawn clearing for 80000 frames without finding
  the way north: it cycles between the window's west edge and the tree
  band at screen y≈82 — the corridor north is NOT reachable by blind
  leg programs from the walk13 end spot and needs either the per-chip
  walkability table decoded (then BFS on the tile grid) or a
  position-cell instrument to plan around the trunks. (2026-11-17
  addendum: pocket_probe2.lua's straight up-holds DID walk the party
  out of the arrival clearing twelve tiles north before stopping at
  the tree band — the run6 follower's 600-frame legs with its
  right-hand bias were the problem, not a seal; and the "walkability
  table" is the camera-windowed grid, see "The walk grid is a camera
  window".)
- **The field camera does not scroll in this state.** walk7's net 8-tile
  north walk (OAM y 210→82) and the release run's wall-follower walk
  (run6: the leader reached screen y=12, the window's top edge) both kept
  the render window at (52,15/16) — a follow camera would have panned
  long before. The run's battle-time screenshots matched windows
  (43,3)/(46,3), but battles render on the field with their own battle
  camera, so they are NOT field-camera evidence. Mechanism: the only
  writes to $210D-$2110 are an FF-bank 0C/00 reset pair every frame plus
  C0:A3E0-family code pinning scroll 0 during cutscene transitions, and
  the C1-bank NMI shadow cells ($7E:1011-1018) read 0000 — the field
  camera is implemented elsewhere (tilemap streaming, not BG-scroll
  registers). Locating that path is still the cheapest probe into the
  chip-collision question, since the streaming code must read the party
  position cell the sessions have been hunting.



Verified against ROM bytes (multiple independent sources agree):

- submap table, header layout and layer/object/palette pointer semantics
- layer record grammar (exact dsize consumption, coordinate bounds)
- chipset run codec, block structure and SNES 4bpp interleave
- palette addressing and BGR555 layout
- object stream head/tail structure, common-palette mechanism, terminator
- property-layer entry grammar and block layout, flag semantics for
  event points, masks, layer toggles, and flag 04 = the water zone
  (pixel-verified on map 0x04; the party-side block/swim split is the
  tool-manual model above)
- the record's flag3-0x04 chip value table: section layout and word
  format, walked byte-exactly on maps 0x02/0x03/0x04 (see the chip
  value table section)
- the layer toggle/mask engine mechanics: zone registration into
  `$7E:B100`, row-buffer merge loops `$FF:2116`/`$FF:21E7`, table fill
  `$FF:1FF7` (offsets, raw bytes and arithmetic in the toggle section
  above; the cell mapping is explicitly open)

Not fully verified (rendered plausibly; exact game semantics unknown):

- the repeat-op grammar is now byte-verified against the engine's
  FF/0DDA write watch (see "Display layer"); the palette-override byte
  gated on DP $A6 bit 5 is the one piece left undecoded (absent from
  the verified streams)
- layer 3 is parsed as a pointer only
- the walkability attribute alignment beyond the two anchors (event
  point at attribute 4, sea at attribute 2): the attribute ids come from
  the RS3MapEditor2 palette order, not from byte-verified engine reads;
  the per-tile in-game check has not been traced
- whether the party's on-foot stop on attr-2 water-zone tiles is the
  zone-mismatch path described above (behavioral emulator probe pending;
  see the walkability model)
- the layer toggle/mask cell mapping and word effect (blockers 1-3 in
  the toggle section above); the renderer therefore ignores the zones,
  which is exact for every rect whose two layers hold equivalent blank
  fills (all seven on map 0x250) and unmodeled elsewhere
- the overlay stream's terrain bits beyond walk/zone (attribute bits
  0-2 and 6-7; open item (d) in "Chip default passability")
- the chip value table's meaning: 6-bit values 0-63, water chips share
  value 8, game effect (animation?) unverified
- tile bit order is the SNES standard (bit 7 = leftmost); the alternative
  mirrors each tile
- the arrival-BGM majority rule: the track a map really plays is
  path-dependent (arrival record + event ops); the exported `bgm` is the
  most frequent arrival request, a static approximation (see Map BGM)

## Map IDs (from the community CSV, original map numbering)

0x00-0x07 Pidona (city, wharf, pub, inn, shop), 0x08-0x0D Pidona royal
palace (dream), 0x0E-0x28 Makai (Demon lord's palace) complex,
0x29-0x2E Stanley, 0x2F-0x3E Brigand's lair, 0x3F+ Cave temple ruins, and
so on for ~900 entries (`解析結果/サブマップ一覧.csv` in
`新バイナリ神ロダ補完/ツール・テキスト.zip`, also
`メモ集（AL982氏）/サブマップデータ一覧.txt` for the 3.12plus variant).
The bokuno ROM re-points some entries and zeroes others, so a given ID can
differ from the original game; the rendered examples that follow the
original numbering still match: 0x02 = Pidona old town, 0x04 = Pidona
wharf.

Stretch copy (layer ops 11/12, FF/08C0-08ED -> FF/0A5A): the step word
is stored raw in `$AE/$AF` and is the destination's absolute top-left
(FF/0A9C writes row `$AF`, column `$AE`); the source rect starts at the
record's (x, y). It moves tile words only (no property bytes), so the
attr sweep could not see it: the model had added 1 and treated the word
as an offset, leaving 000B's layer 2 with 188 wrong words (write watch:
the composer writes 0852 at frame 19549, FF/0AE5 then 0804 within the
same layer decode).

Footprints (C0:5413 -> C0:7C75, ported): a passed step leaves one on the
tile the object stands on when that tile's class has byte 3 bit 1 and
not byte 2 bit 5, and `$D9B2 & 0x30 != 0x10`: the first time
(low-buffer bit 1) the footprint layer's word gains facing+1 (1-4). The
layer is 2 when the record's 禁止操作 byte (`Header.Controls`,
`$D2F3`) has bit 3, else 1 (C0:3D66). exportmap writes footprints.json
(per-tile combo index) and footprints[_over].png (combo rows, deltas
1-4); the runner reports footprints and map_view draws them. On the
sweep dumps every differing word of 00A0 (79), 0206 (12) and 0342 (3)
is a footprint. The same byte's bit 4 widens the horizontal bounds by 2
tiles each side (C0:3D59; 28 maps, now in map.json `bounds`) and bit 7
is the open-map flag `$D0DD`.

## The OBJ palette slot list ($D6E2) and subscreen OBJ math (decoded 2026-11-23, static; refined + corrected 2026-11-23 by docs/subscreen-obj.md)

Closes the "subscreen OBJ math (only 0372 and event actors can reach
slot 4)" open item: the reach condition is data, not code. docs/subscreen-obj.md
holds the full lifecycle (11 funnel callers, rescan semantics, the slot
frees, objOp 69); the corrections it forces are applied in place below.

**The list.** Eight bytes at `$D6E2`, length `$D6E1`. The map load
resets them to `FF` at three sites (C0:3DEB in the record-flag parse;
C0:EAE1 from the load finalize C0:BE0F; C0:085B). Every figure graphic assignment
funnels through C0:7B3F — eleven call sites, all in bank C0 (4C25 and
4D5D/4D6B/4D79 load finalize, 4EFF generic spawn, 634A interpreter op 19
graphic-set, B4AD leader re-adopt, B5D7 leader init from `$F001`, B6BB
objOp 21 graphic-set, D78B objOp 2E, D9C0 objOp 2C) — whose tail is the
allocation scan C0:7B8A:

    LDY #$0000
    loop: LDA $D6E2,Y
          JSL $5AA7B1     ; compare is helper-mediated, not CMP $F9A003,X
          BEQ found       ; match: its palette already holds a slot
          CMP #$FF        ; empty slot
          BEQ taken
          INY; CPY #$0008; BEQ full; BRA loop
    full: LDY #$0000      ; all 8 taken: overwrite slot 0
    taken: TYA; INC A; CMP $D6E1; BCC +3; STA $D6E1
          JSL $5AA7C3     ; palette byte to register (helper)
          STA $D6E2,Y; JSR $7BE0   ; queue the CGRAM upload
    found: TYA; ASL; AND #$0E                      ; slot*2
          ORA $D9B1,Y; STA $D9B1,Y                 ; OAM attr palette bits 1-3

The helpers (5AA7B1/5AA7C3) branch on `$EFF7` (set by 5A:BFA8 at every
funnel entry): the normal path compares/registers the figure's F9:A000
byte 3; the patch-figure path (figure 0 with graphic id >= 0x70, or
class 0C/4C) compares against `FE` and stores `FD` — FE matches nothing
and no normal palette is FD, so a patch figure always takes a fresh
empty slot and only another patch figure reuses it after a free.

The slot is the sprite palette: C0:7BE0 queues an upload of
EC:8000 + 32 * palette (WRAM `$7E:E2B6` when palette = `$BC`) to CGRAM word
`$80 + slot*16` (colours 128 + slot*8), and the load finalize
re-uploads the whole list in slot order (C0:BE85-BE9D). The free
routine C0:7BC5 (`$D9D4,Y >= FD` skips; `$D9B1,Y >> 1 & 7` names the
slot; writes `FF` back) DOES run mid-map: three call sites, all
despawn/hide paths — C0:6753 (interpreter op 3A "remove this figure"),
C0:6619 (the runtime-dispatched 65C9-region body, when `$D9B8,Y != 0`),
C0:6DA0 (the 7022-level per-frame step op 03, `$D9B8,Y != 0` and
`$D9B9,Y == 30`). A freed slot returns to `FF` and the next scan can
take it — the port's grow-only list is NOT engine-faithful. The
order is funnel-caller order, not y and not a rule: the opening screen
loads the leader FIRST (live: palette 01 into slot 0 before montage
figures 03/04/05), while 0301's leader landed in slot 5 and 0372's in 7
(capture order). objOp 2C party members (C0:D976: graphic
`$F001 + 128 * member`, the FE:961B table) and objOp 2E event actors
(C0:D72D: `$EF00` graphic, `$EF01/$EF02` tile*8 x/y, slot-0 block
copied) allocate at spawn.

**The slot-4 reach condition.** None in code. The scan has no map-type
test, no arrival-record bit (`$D0A6`), no `$D93F` use; the complete
write-set of `$D6E2` in the ROM is the three `FF` resets, the register
at C0:7BB3, the free at C0:7BDB (three callers, above), and one entry
rewrite (81h -> 80h, C0:CA26, requeueing that slot's upload). A figure takes
slot 4 exactly when slots 0-3 hold four distinct palettes none of which
is its own: on-screen palette diversity. 0372 qualifies ($D6E2 = AD 34
33 32 39 3A 36 + leader 01) and so does 0301 (10 0F C9 20 23 + leader
01, slot 5) — "only 0372" was true of the captures, not the engine.

**The read-back.** The per-map screen block (flag3 bit 4, C0:3F55 and
C0:3FCB) fills `$D009-$D00D`, applied by the load finalize at C0:BEC0
(`$D009` -> `$212C` main, `$D00A` -> `$212D` sub, `$D00C` -> `$2130`
select, `$D00D` -> `$2131` math, `$D00B` -> `$2132` fixed). Two
distinct roles for OBJ:

- Subscreen layer (type-1 arrival): the masks step writes `$212C` = 02
  and `$212D` = 11 directly (FF:B20A, FF:B212) — `$212D` bit 4 puts the
  whole OBJ layer in the subscreen, and with `$2130` = 02, `$2131` = 02
  the compositor adds it to BG2 whatever the palette slot. There is no
  separate subscreen OAM: the same figure OAM entries (x/y `$D9AA`/
  `$D9AC`, layout FF:2AEC, palette attr `$D9B1` bits 1-3) and their
  blob tiles in VRAM are all there is.
- Colour math (0372 and 45 other maps: the `screen` export's `select`
  bit 1 + `math` bit 4, e.g. 010D, 0112, 0116, 02A0/02A1, the math-33h
  group from 02B9 on, 0233): sprites in palette slots 4-7 take the math (capture
  rule, sprites.md), the subscreen pixel being the other operand. The
  slot-4 figure therefore shows (obj + subscreen)/2 over opaque BG3 on
  0372 and its raw palette over the backdrop; slots 0-3 stay raw. The
  figure's palette itself is whichever F9:A000 byte 3 landed in
  `$D6E2[4]` (0372: 39h, graphic 59 — the earlier "graphic 89" was a
  nibble slip: id 89's F9 byte 3 is 91).

**Port.** map_view.gd `_figure_palette_slot` matches the C0:7B8A scan's
one-shot shape (first match, first empty, else overwrite slot 0), reset
at map start, fed placed NPCs, the leader, then objOp 2C/2E spawns
through `_show_spawned`. Four divergences, all decoded in
docs/subscreen-obj.md §Port implication: (1) the engine re-runs the
scan at every graphic assignment — objOp 21, interpreter op 19, the
B410 adopt, a spawn with a changed `$D9D4` — so a mid-map graphic
change with a fresh palette takes a new slot where the port keeps its
spawn slot; (2) slot frees are reachable in normal play (op 3A and the
two gated despawn paths) and the port has no free-on-despawn hook, so
its slot numbering drifts after the first despawn; (3) patch figures
must key the constant `FD` with compare key `FE`, never matched;
(4) objOp 69 (`17 69` -> C0:CA26) is unported: slot entry 81 -> 80, the
live-figure sweep D9 -> 80, `$D6B8` counting, and the slot's CGRAM
fading one step from palette 81's data toward palette 80's per firing.
The arrival's subscreen OBJ layer (`obj_sub`/`obj_tex`) and
the slots 4-7 math (`sub_out`/OBJ_MATH) are modeled and pinned.

**Next probe (live only):** whether any shipped script runs `17 69`
while a slot actually holds `81` (the fade path is decoded, never
observed live); how the load finalize's second upload list at WRAM
`$0100` (the `$D2F3` bit-6 mirror, C0:7C33-7C6D) is consumed; the
runtime tables that dispatch B410 and the 65C9-region body (likely the
WRAM `JMP ($9AB9,X)` tables at C0:544D/553F, fill site unresolved).

```

`docs/mesence-skip-intro.md`:

```md
# MesenCE: reaching a late-game battle without playing the intro

How to make a `-testRunner` probe land in a specific battle (e.g. the
type-09 fixed battle 0x0D or battle-254) on a fresh headless boot, with
no intro playthrough. This unblocks live probes of battle types that
the intro chain preempts.

## Verdict

**The savestate round trip works.** Approach 3 (savestate file API) in
the probe plan, adapted to what this MesenCE build actually ships:

- `emu.saveSavestateFile` / `emu.loadSavestateFile` do not exist in
  this build (`attempt to call a nil value`).
- `emu.createSavestate()` and `emu.loadSavestate(string)` both exist
  and both work headless — but each **throws unless called inside an
  exec memory operation callback for the main CPU**:

  ```
  LOAD ok=false err=This function must be called inside an exec memory
  operation callback for the main CPU
  API createSavestate ok=false err=This function must be called inside
  an exec memory operation callback for the main CPU
  ```

- The exec context is easy to get: the native NMI vector (read from
  `$FFEA`, observed `FF07`) fires every frame, so an exec memory
  callback on that one address is a reliable "run this in CPU context"
  hook. Both save and load ride it.
- So the recipe is: capture the target state once with a boot+walk
  probe (35k frames), print the state as base64, embed that string in
  later probes, and load it at frame ~600 of a fresh boot. The battle
  word injection then lands ~100 frames later.

No SRM crafting and no story-flag poking were needed. Both pending
targets ran live with this: battle 0x0D (type 09) and battle 0xFE
(phantom), verified by WRAM identity cells and screenshots.

## VERIFIED facts (log evidence)

All runs: `/tmp/mesence_t007A/Mesen -testRunner <script>.lua
patches/bokuno_jp.sfc -enableStdout --timeout=600` from the repo root,
fresh boot (the SRM's presence or absence does not matter — runs
succeeded both ways).

1. **API table**: `createSavestate` and `loadSavestate` exist;
   `saveSavestateFile`/`loadSavestateFile` do not (probe
   `/tmp/saga3-srm-probe/api.lua`, lines `EMUKEYS`, `API ...` above).
2. **Exec-callback requirement**: quoted errors above (probes
   `api.lua`, `loadsv.lua`).
3. **Capture at the settled field state** (probe `capfield.lua`,
   proven boot+walk schedule from `tools/emulator/journey_teleport.lua`):

   ```
   SIG at-capture f34600 76=00 rng=30 map=0249 d6bb=00 d6bd=FF d6be=00 seed=0E50
   SVLEN 135736
   ```

   Frame 34600: story chain done (`$76`=0, field idle), map 0x0249,
   queue empty (`$D6BD`=FF terminator, write index `$D6BB`=0).
4. **Battle 0x0D is type 09, live** (probe `recipe_verify.lua`):

   ```
   INJECT f700 map=0249
   STATE f1000 busy=0 map=0000 q=00 FF 0D id1306=0D t141A=09 e1424=20 e1428=00 rng=35 seed=1F50
   ```

   `id1306=0D` is the injected id; `t141A=09` is the battle type —
   held from f1000 to f12000 (run end). Screenshot at f1800 shows the
   battle with the command window open (`shot_3.png` in the probe dir).
5. **Battle 0xFE (phantom) is live** (probe `recipe_254.lua`):

   ```
   INJECT f700 map=0249
   STATE f1000 busy=0 map=0000 q=00 FF FE id1306=FE t141A=12 e1424=00 e1428=01 rng=21 seed=2F50
   ```

   Type 0x12, `$1428`=1. Screenshot shows the phantom void enemy
   (`p254_5.png`).
6. **The injection dispatches through the engine's own path**: a write
   watch on `$2011/$2012` caught the dispatch chain ~29 frames after
   the injection (probe `recipe_diag.lua`):

   ```
   WMAP f729 pc=FE:BEB4 a=7E2011 val=00
   WMAP f734 pc=C2:1B1D a=7E2011 val=00
   WMAP f734 pc=C2:1B22 a=7E2012 val=00
   ```

   The queue processor reads `$D6BD` every frame (read watch: PCs
   `C0:B01E` and `C0:7DF2`), consumes the word and restores the `$FF`
   terminator — so the probe injects **once**, it never holds.

## Cell addresses

| cell | meaning | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$D6BD`/`$D6BE` | deferred dispatch word (little-endian: `$D6BD`=op `0x19` = fixed battle, `$D6BE`=battle id); `$FF` at `$D6BD` = queue empty | read watch every frame at `C0:B01E`; injection consumed ~f700-729 |
| `$D6BB` | queue write index (0 when empty) | STATE dumps |
| `$1306` | battle id once the battle is up — this is the verification cell for "the injected id took" | `id1306=0D` / `id1306=FE` |
| `$141A` | battle type once the battle is up (09 for 0x0D, 12 for 0xFE) | STATE dumps |
| `$1424`/`$1428` | phantom escalation stage cells (0xFE run: `e1424=00 e1428=01`) | STATE dumps |
| `$0914` | battle RNG index | STATE dumps (ticks slowly while the battle waits on input) |
| `$F30D`/`$F30E` | battle RNG seed; varies per run, not stabilized by this recipe | STATE dumps |
| `$76` | story-script busy flag. 0 on the settled field AND during these battles — not a battle-active flag | STATE dumps |
| `$2011`/`$2012` | current map id (0x0249 at the capture point; zeroed once a battle loads) | WMAP watch |
| `$FFEA` | native NMI vector; the exec hook address for save/load context | `NMIVEC FF07` |

## Recipe

### Step 1 — one-time capture (`capfield.lua`)

Boot+walk press schedule verbatim from
`tools/emulator/journey_teleport.lua` (start mash 300..6800 step 60,
title presses at 7000/7800/8600/9000/9800/10600, then A-while-busy /
down-right walk 20800..34000). At frame 34600 arm the NMI exec hook and
`createSavestate()` once, then print the state base64:

```lua
local nmi = emu.read(0xFFEB, emu.memType.snesMemory) * 256
  + emu.read(0xFFEA, emu.memType.snesMemory)
emu.addMemoryCallback(function()
  if not captured then
    local ok, st = pcall(emu.createSavestate)
    if ok then state = st; captured = true end
  end
end, emu.callbackType.exec, nmi, nmi, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesMemory)
```

Print `b64(state)` on one `SVB64 ` line (base64 encoder in the full
script at `/tmp/saga3-srm-probe/capfield.lua`; a captured
`field.b64` is beside it — /tmp is ephemeral, regenerate when gone).

### Step 2 — embed and inject (`recipe.lua` skeleton)

```lua
local BATTLE_ID = 0x0D            -- sed this per target
local B64 = table.concat({ "<30000-char chunk>", "<chunk>", ... })
-- unb64(s): strip "=+$", decode 4-char groups; see /tmp/saga3-srm-probe/recipe.lua
emu.addEventCallback(function()
  frames = frames + 1
  if frames == 600 and not unb64ed then
    unb64ed = true
    local ok, st = pcall(unb64, B64)
    local nmi = emu.read(0xFFEB, emu.memType.snesMemory) * 256
      + emu.read(0xFFEA, emu.memType.snesMemory)
    local function hook()
      if loaded then return end          -- REQUIRED, see gotcha 2
      loaded = true
      pcall(emu.loadSavestate, st)
    end
    emu.addMemoryCallback(hook, emu.callbackType.exec, nmi, nmi,
      emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesMemory)
  end
  if frames == 700 and loaded then       -- inject ONCE, never hold
    emu.write(0xD6BD, 0x19, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)
    emu.write(0xD6BE, BATTLE_ID, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)
  end
  -- verify: from ~f1000, wr(0x1306)==BATTLE_ID and wr(0x141A) is the type
end, emu.eventType.inputPolled)
```

Embedding (the b64 is ~181k; keep Lua line lengths sane):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
b64 = open('field.b64').read().strip()
chunks = [b64[i:i+30000] for i in range(0, len(b64), 30000)]
PY
```

Battle is up by frame ~1000; probe until `emu.stop()` as usual.

### Gotchas found on the way (all observed, not documented elsewhere)

1. `emu.write` from `inputPolled` works for the injection (the word
   dispatched); it is the savestate pair, not write, that needs the
   exec context.
2. **The load hook must be one-shot by a Lua flag.** A loaded state
   rewinds the emulator to the capture point — which is inside the NMI
   hook — so an unguarded hook reloads every frame forever (time never
   advances). `emu.removeMemoryCallback` did **not** remove the exec
   hook (observed: hook kept firing after a remove call with the
   `addMemoryCallback` argument list); the Lua flag guard is the
   reliable mechanism.
3. **Never hold the queue word.** Holding `$D6BD=0x19` every frame
   (the tail10 tactic from the old probe generations) leaves the battle
   stalled after dispatch: map cells zeroed at f729/f734, then no
   further progress for 11k frames. Inject once; the processor consumes
   the word and restores `$FF` itself.
4. A throwing Lua callback dies silently — the base64 decoder must be
   correct (padding) or the whole branch vanishes with no log line.
   pcall everything; print UNB64/LOAD results.
5. `$76`=0 does NOT mean "not in battle" — it is the story-script busy
   flag and stays 0 through these battles. Verify a battle through
   `$1306`/`$141A`, not `$76`.

## Unverified / open observations

- The two every-frame queue readers (`C0:B01E`, `C0:7DF2`) and the
  dispatch chain `FE:BEB4` → `C2:1B1D/1B22` were observed by PC watch
  only; their exact roles are not decoded here.
- `$0914` decrements by 0x0C every ~500 frames while these battles sit
  at the input-wait; not correlated with roll activity.
- The capture is tied to frame 34600 of that exact press schedule; if
  the schedule changes, re-check the SIG line (map 0x0249, `$76`=0,
  `$D6BD`=FF) before trusting the state.
- Battle seed `$F30D` still varies per run. If a probe needs a pinned
  seed, write it after the load (untested).

```

# Migration: Godot/GDScript → Ebitengine (Go)

## Constraints that shape the architecture (all measured)

- Ebiten has no UI toolkit and no true headless mode: it always needs a

  settled this in 2026-10). Therefore ALL game logic lives in pure Go

- The gate's nine godot-dependent steps (scripts/gate.sh) were the
  re-verification surface: selftest, battleselftest, tilecheck,

## Order

1. Infra: the `internal/game/...` tree reading exports/data in place; a
   test harness package that re-hosts the fixtures (read them from
   exports/tests/ in place — they are engine-neutral data; do not copy).
2. Logic domains in golden order: battle math (already green) → RNGs →
   event VM → game_state → battle engine → action scripts → field
   logic. Each domain re-greens its own goldens before the next starts.
3. Flow + shell last; the godot/ tree retired once every gate step had
   a green Go equivalent (done 2026-11-23, the audit table below).

## Working rules for migration agents

- Translate from the GDScript reference; the docs/*.md decodes are the
  ground truth when reference and doc disagree (check the bytes first).
- A domain's goldens move to Go BEFORE or WITH the domain port, never
  after; a pin that cannot fail is not a pin (expectations come from
  the engine traces/decodes, not from the port's own output).
- No behavior changes during translation: port fixes go through the
  decode → GDScript reference (or doc) → Go path, never straight into
  Go by feel.
- Keep the full gate green throughout: until a domain's Go equivalent
  lands, its GDScript checks stay in the gate.
- Committing while siblings are mid-flight (measured necessity with
  five agents sharing one tree, 2026-11-23): the gate compiles the
  WORKING tree, so sibling untracked WIP can keep it red for hours. An
  agent may commit its own files without a green shared gate when (1)
  its own packages pass gofmt/vet/staticcheck/go test, (2) the
  commit's dependency closure is entirely committed code (`git
  commit --only` keeps sibling files out), and (3) the commit trailer
  quotes its green evidence verbatim and the exact sibling-file
  failure that blocked the full gate. The full tree-wide GATE OK
  still gates the round's final commit.

# Music: the bokuno soundtrack in the Go shell

## Full 92-track rip (2026-11-16, silent-id fix 2026-11-17): pipeline, names, catalog

This section is the current state; everything below is the decision
record. The consumer is the Go shell's BGM catalog
(`internal/game/shell/bgm.go`) — the Godot scenes this rip was originally
built for retired with the engine 2026-11-23.

### Pipeline (batch, `cmd/bgmrip`)

    bgmrip rip       # hijack dispatch per id, dump .spc (MesenCE headless)
    bgmrip match     # optional: name ids by byte-match vs a community SPC set
    bgmrip convert   # .spc -> OGG in exports/data/bgm/ + catalog.json

1. `rip`: for each id 0x00-0x5B, rewrites `local TARGET` in
   tools/emulator/rip.lua, runs the same MesenCE `-testRunner` hijack as
   rip_track.sh (4 instances in parallel), parses RIPINFO/SPCDATA/DSPDATA
   from stdout, and assembles the format-v0.30 `.spc` — the Go rebuild is
   byte-identical to tools/emulator/spc_build.py (`cmp` clean; spc_build.py
   had a 256-byte buffer-resize defect — `out[0x100:0x10000] = ram` — fixed
   to `out[0x100:0x10100]`). Per-id status lands in
   `/tmp/bgm-agent/spc/rip_status/XX.json`; a subrange re-run merges
   (`-ids` takes `LO-HI` or a comma list).
2. Dump timing matters. The default `-dump-frame 2400` (≈37 s in-song)
   catches looping tracks mid-play, but short tracks have already ended
   (17 renders came out silent or as 0.05 s blips). Frame sweeps per
   class: long/looping tracks fine at 2400; short pieces audible at 300;
   one-shot jingles (0x4C/0x4D/0x50, ~10 s) only at ~220 (they stop
   within ~1 s of the forced dispatch). Silent under every dump frame
   tried (200-2400): 0x00 by design plus 0x33, 0x3B, 0x40, 0x44,
   0x4F, 0x57 — the ambient/overlay pieces (kaerulabo's 風の音/
   乾いた大河?/地鳴り/車の爆走音 class). The 2026-11-16 run skipped them
   as "never key voices"; that was a libgme render artifact, see
   § "The six silent overlays" below — five of the six now ship.
3. `convert`: same verified chain as rip_track.sh — libgme render capped
   with `-t 40` (these dumps never signal an end; the render loops
   forever), WAV doubled so the seam sits on the loop point, libvorbis
   `-q:a 5` — into `exports/data/bgm/XX_slug.ogg`. Silence check with
   ffmpeg volumedetect (mean < -60 dB = silent → one retry with the
   dumped echo delay EDL zeroed, then silent on peak < -80 dB; see
   § "The six silent overlays"). Writes exports/data/bgm/catalog.json.
4. Environment note: a parallel agent's Mesen runs and system load
   (load average 100-220 at times) starved some rip runs below 20 fps so
   they missed the kill cap; the per-id status files make re-running
   only the failed ids cheap.

### Naming: how each id got its name

The pointer-table order is id order (verified in § "What is in the ROM"),
but the superfamicom wiki's description column is wrong from row 4 on
(row 4 "Silence?" is actually Julian's Theme; row 0x1A "The Last Battle"
is actually Four Noble Devils 2). Three independent sources were
cross-checked instead, and they agree with each other:

1. **Community SPC byte-match** (`bgmrip match -ref <zophar zip>`): the
   zophar.net RS3 set (naming reference only — license rules above) is
   ripped from the same driver, so the uploaded sequence at SPC ARAM
   `$2224` (ARAMBase) is byte-identical for the same song and diverges
   within ~2 bytes for different songs (strict contiguous match; self-test
   56796 bytes on identical vs 1 on a different track). 74 of the 92 ids
   matched a titled community track (scores 117-2061 bytes, second-best
   <= 4x smaller); the other 18 have no file in that set.
2. **Town-BGM table at file 0x62A3D** (bokuno_jp.sfc): slots 0-7 hold the
   eight protagonist theme ids; slots 8+ agree slot-for-slot with
   kaerulabo's observed 主人公変更バグ table
   (http://kaerulabo.web.fc2.com/rs3/data/chara_data_BGM.html). Slots
   0x0C=0x17 (氷湖), 0x13=0x18 (ペット捕獲大作戦), 0x04=0x1F
   (ハリードのテーマ), 0x01=0x2C (エレンのテーマ), 0x02=0x0F
   (サラのテーマ) are each confirmed by community byte-match too.
3. **superfamicom-wiki rows** for ids neither source covers (all flagged
   in the table below).

Japanese titles come from the OST correspondence of each matched English
title (https://saga.fandom.com/wiki/Romancing_SaGa_3_Music_List). Ids with
no name in any source stay `unknown` in catalog.json.

Notable corrections for existing assets: the pre-existing `field.ogg` was
ripped from id 0x05, which is **聖王の町ランス (Lance town theme)** — the
actual field theme is id 0x21. `battle.ogg` (0x01 The Battle) and
`dungeon1.ogg` (0x02 Dungeon 1) are correctly named.

### catalog.json contract (the shell's BGM catalog)

`exports/data/bgm/catalog.json`, written by `bgmrip convert`, regenerated
whenever the ROM or pipeline changes; the ogg files and the catalog are
user-local (gitignored `/exports/data/`), never committed.

    {
      "rom": "patches/bokuno_jp.sfc",
      "tracks": [
        {
          "id": 1,                       // song-table id, 0-91
          "hex": "01",
          "name_jp": "バトル1",           // null-equivalent "" when unknown
          "name_en": "The Battle",
          "slug": "the_battle",
          "name_source": "zophar-match | zophar-match+kaerulabo | town-table | superfamicom-wiki | unknown",
          "ogg": "01_the_battle.ogg",    // "" when silent/failed
          "status": "ok | silent | failed",
          "reason": "",                  // non-empty when not ok
          "duration_sec": 66.4,
          "mean_volume_db": -31.6
        }
      ]
    }

Shell side: `internal/game/shell/bgm.go` loads the JSON at boot
(`loadMusic` — a missing or unparseable catalog fails the boot, loud by
design), keeps the `status == "ok"` entries' ogg files, looks up by `id`
and streams the file on loop. The id comes
from the map's arrival track: `cmd/exportmap` exports each map's `bgm`
(request id from its movement records, resolved through the two engine
hooks — the full mechanism and offsets live in docs/map-format.md
§ "Map BGM"). Event op changes (dispatch word `1D xx` = direct track id,
handler `$C0:C5C4`: no-op when `xx` equals the cached current track
`$F546`, else SPC handshake with `xx` into `$1C01`) are runtime-only and
not exported yet. (`C0:C570` is the `1F xx` variant, `JSL $FF0063`
instead of `$FF0024` — docs/vm-semantics.md §2.8.) Tracks with
`status != "ok"` have no file; maps without a `bgm` and tracks without an
ogg fall back to the field theme `21_field.ogg`.

### The six silent overlays: they play; the render was the problem (2026-11-17)

The 2026-11-16 run marked 0x33, 0x3B, 0x40, 0x44, 0x4F, 0x57 as
"silent — never key voices under a forced dispatch". That conclusion
was wrong, and the tracks now ship. What the dumps actually contain:

- The dispatch DID upload and play them. Each of the six `.spc` dumps
  differs from the mute dump `00.spc` by ~10 KB of ARAM (the uploaded
  sequence), and the DSP register image shows keyed voices with a full
  envelope at the dump frame (0x57 alone keys none at frame 2400):

  ```
  33: EDL=$05 ESA=$C9 keyed: v0:SRCN=$20 P=$00DE ENVX=$7F OUTX=$1C;
      v1:SRCN=$20 P=$00DE ENVX=$7F OUTX=$1C
  44: EDL=$05 ESA=$C9 keyed: v0:SRCN=$23 P=$00B7 ENVX=$7F OUTX=$ED;
      v2/v4/v5 same sample at pitches $00B7/$0096
  ```

- libgme still rendered them as digital silence (max −84.3 dB for all
  six, an identical floor). The trigger is the dumped echo setup: all
  six carry EDL=`$05` / ESA=`$C9` (echo ring buffer `$C900`, delay 5).
  Zeroing EDL in the dumped DSP image makes libgme render the dry path:
  peaks −34.9 dB (0x33), −22.4 (0x40), −20.6 (0x44), −51.0 (0x3B),
  −55.2 (0x4F). Mesen, the emulator that made the dumps, had these
  voices keyed with a full envelope at capture time; the difference is
  an emulator-behavior divergence on this echo configuration, the same
  class of problem bokuno's own INSTALL notes for Snes9x echo
  handling. UNVERIFIED: which emulator's echo behavior matches real
  hardware — no audio capture exists in the headless `-testRunner`
  path (docs/sfx.md approach table).

- `bgmrip convert` now retries a silent render once with EDL zeroed
  (`renderOGGNoEcho`) and classifies the retry on PEAK volume (below
  −80 dB peak is the digital-silence floor; the mean rule would reject
  a −35 dB-peak wind rumble whose mean sits at −81 because the pitch
  is ultra-low, P=`$00DE`). The five audible ids ship as OGG with their
  natural (quiet) level, each 4.0 s — libgme detects the sequence end
  at ~2 s, so these are one-shot ambience stingers, not loops; the
  echo tail is lost on exactly those five renders. 0x57 stays silent:
  no voices keyed at dump frames 600/1200/2400/3600/4800, and the
  EDL-zeroed renders are digital silence every time. 0x00 stays silent
  by design (the mute entry).

`convert` run (2026-11-17): `CONVERTED ok=90 silent=2 failed=0` — the
five EDL-patched rows print a "(no-echo render: EDL zeroed)" note.
