Goal: RS3 soundtrack (as it exists in `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`) playing in the
Godot 4.7 project with reasonable effort. SFX is a later, separate problem
(the driver treats it differently, see below). This doc is the decision
record; the first milestone to implement is Milestone 1 at the bottom.

## License and legal notes

- SPC rips of a commercial ROM contain Square's copyrighted music data and
  its copyrighted SPC700 driver code. Rips are for the user's local use
  only. Like the ROM chain (README), **nothing derived from them is
  committed here**: no `.spc`, no rendered audio, no extracted BRR samples
  in the repo. The build pipeline regenerates them from the user's own
  ROM/dumps.
- Do not use existing community SPC sets (zophar.net has an RS3 set of 83
  tracks by CzarDragon/Mana Sword/Osaka) as project assets — same copyright
  status, and provenance is unverifiable. They are useful only as a
  reference for track naming/numbering.
- If the project ever ships, engine-side playback must respect the license
  chain: libgme is LGPL-2.1-or-later (dynamic linking), gd_libvgm is
  MIT-only by design. Offline OGG conversion carries no engine license at
  all.

## What is in the ROM (verified)

Facts below verified byte-for-byte against
`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` (SHA-256 `4793e142…f2da0`, 8 MB ExHiROM) and the
base `Romancing Sa-Ga 3 (Japan) (Rev 1).sfc` (v1.1, 4 MB), same addressing
as docs/map-format.md: file offset `(bank-0xC0)*0x10000`.

- The driver is Square's own SPC700 driver of the "AKAO" family
  (FF4 → RS1 → FF5 → RS2/FF6 → RS3 lineage). RS3 is its own variant
  (`ARAMBase=$2224`, `VCmdStart=$C4`, RS3-specific v-commands F4 and FD).
  Structured comparison: loveemu
  https://loveemu.hatenablog.com/entry/20130611/SNES_Square_AKAO_SPC_Version_Difference
- Song pointer table at SNES `$C6:0FC6` (file `0x60FC6`): 92 entries of
  3-byte little-endian pointers, then zero padding. Entry n = track ID n
  (IDs `0x00`–`0x5B`). Entry 0 = `$CBA876` (the wiki names it
  "Silence"), 1 = `$CBA89C` ("The Battle"), 2 = `$CBB0CC` ("Dungeon 1").
- **The table is byte-identical between base v1.1 and bokuno_jp.** All
  92 original tracks are unchanged in bokuno. The hack's extra tracks
  (IDs `0x5C` and above: the SaGa Frontier/RS1/RS2 imports and the new
  town themes) live in extended regions added by the hack and are
  dispatched by patched driver code. This matches the community BGM docs
  (below), whose extended-ID list starts at `5C`.
- BRR sample pointer table at `$C6:0CE4,x` (banks `$C6`–`$CB`), per the
  JCE3000GT trace log on https://wiki.superfamicom.org/romancing-saga-3 .
  That page's per-track address annotations contain internal
  inconsistencies; the table location itself is confirmed by the trace
  above and by our ROM probe.
- How music IDs travel in-game (for the Godot side, already extracted):
  map jumps carry the music request id in bits 10-15 of the destination
  word, ids ≤ `0x3F` (docs/triggers.md block 4 and the global table at
  `0x3CFB00`); events change BGM with dispatch word `1D xx` — engine
  handler `$C0:C5C4` (queue-word table `C0:B06B` entry 0x1D), `xx` =
  track id directly, so bokuno uses extended ids here too. The request id resolves through the protagonist hook and
  the remap table before it reaches the song table (docs/map-format.md
  § "Map BGM" for the offsets and evidence).

### The hack-side composition pipeline (community docs in the mirror)

`新バイナリ神ロダ補完/` (read-only reference) documents how bokuno
authors compose and insert tracks:

- RS3ExTool2/3 (Windows, Delphi): dumps a track's sequence from the ROM
  into an 8-channel MML text file and compiles MML back into ROM data.
  `MML仕様.txt` defines the format (`#WAVE`, `#DRUM`, `%v`/`%b` echo,
  `$` = infinite loop point, `;` ends a channel); `音楽データ解説.txt`
  lists the RS3-type sequence control codes and notes RS3 shares them
  with FF6/LIVE A LIVE.
- `BGM改変パッチ(β用).ZIP` documents the extended track map for the
  sister hack ああβ: extended data regions (e.g. `460000+`, `63DC7C…`),
  which ID a track uses, and per-map theme assignments (ツヴァイク 【F4】,
  ピドナ 【CA】, …). Event op `1D` = BGM change appears in its annotated
  event dumps. bokuno uses the same RS3ExTool pipeline.

Consequence for us: the hack's added tracks are ordinary driver sequences
in ordinary ROM regions — an SPC dump captures them exactly like the
original ones. No special handling.

## Playback options for Godot 4

Godot 4 has no native chiptune support (import options are WAV/OGG/MP3
only, docs.godotengine.org "Importing audio samples"). The choices:

| Option | License | Godot 4 status | Effort | Risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Offline rip → `ffmpeg` (libgme) → OGG → `AudioStreamOggVorbis` | none engine-side (vorbis) | n/a | low (~1 day incl. ripping) | minimal; pipeline already proven on this machine | **recommended, Milestone 1** |
| 2a. gd_libvgm GDExtension, https://github.com/PurpBatBoi/gd_libvgm | MIT (deliberately permissive-only chip cores; SPC core is Snaggletooth) | 4.5+, v0.3 (2026-10-21) with prebuilt release | low (drop in `addons/`) | brand-new single-maintainer project (2026-10, <10 stars); SPC DSP accuracy unproven — must A/B listen | candidate for later |
| 2b. GameMusicEmu-GDExtension, https://github.com/not-magic/GameMusicEmu-GDExtension | MIT wrapper + LGPL-2.1 libgme inside | 4.5+, v0.9.1 (2026-10-02), drop-in importer (`AudioStreamGME`, `track_index`, `looping`) | low | same newness risk; its libgme contains blargg's snes_spc, the accuracy reference | candidate for later, prefer over 2a if in-engine needed |
| 3. Reimplement the RS3 driver in GDScript/GDExtension | — | — | weeks | very high | rejected: goal is playback, not composition |

Ruled out: godot-FLMusicLib (Godot 3 GDNative only), p-meijer33
Godot-AudioStreamGME (self-declared "as is", broken unpause, no Windows
build), libopenspc (no bindings, unmaintained since 2020), audacious GME
plugin (Debian builds audacious-plugins without GME — checked
debian/control), `spc2wav`/`audio-overload` (no Debian packages).

Why offline OGG wins for Milestone 1: the pipeline is one command with
zero new dependencies, the license is clean, and playback fidelity is
identical to what libgme would render in-engine. The cost is asset size
(~1.5–2.5 MB per track at `-q:a 5`; ~90+ tracks ≈ 150–250 MB, local-only,
regenerable) and a re-render step whenever a track must change — which
does not happen: the soundtrack is fixed by the ROM.

## SPC ripping procedure

The practical bulk-rip path uses the game's own debug Music Test
(TCRF, https://tcrf.net/Romancing_SaGa_3): enable debug with the
Pro Action Replay codes listed there ("All Towns + Debug Mode", 23
writes to `$7EF46A`–`$7EF47F`), enter Neft's Den on the world map, menu
`07 = Music Test`, and dump each track while it plays. ~92 + extended
tracks, one manual dump each — roughly a day of manual work.

Emulator for dumping: snes9x ≤ 1.52 or ZSNES (`File → Save SPC`); newer
snes9x trimmed the feature. bsnes/higan/ares have no SPC dump. The
bokuno author's recommended emulator is uosnes; bokuno's own INSTALL
notes that echo-buffer behavior differs across emulators (Snes9x 1.60+:
"Separate echo buffer from RAM" fixes BGM breakage) — for dumping, verify
each rip's tail against in-emulator playback.

UNVERIFIED (reason: not tested): whether the TCRF debug codes and Music
Test still work in bokuno_jp (v1.1 base + Proto1.123). First rip session
should confirm this on one track before budgeting the full batch. Fallback:
a minimal 65816 harness that loads each track ID into the driver the way
`Music Test` does — small, since the dispatch trace is already documented.

Loop points: the SPC format has no header loop field; looping lives in
the sequence data itself (the `$` infinite loop of the MML), so a dumped
`.spc` loops by nature when played. Length/loop metadata for players is
optional `xid6` chunks (intro/loop/end/fade lengths in 1/64000 s ticks,
SPC format spec v0.30, ocremix.org/info/SPC_Format_Specification).

## Milestones

**Milestone 1 — one track audible in Godot (first thing to build).**

1. Dump one looping track (e.g. the field theme) from bokuno_jp.sfc to
   `.spc` via the Music Test route above.
2. Convert: `ffmpeg -i track.spc -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 track.ogg`.
   Verified on this machine: `ffmpeg version 7.1.5-0+deb13u1`,
   `ffmpeg -demuxers` lists `D libgme`; it decoded a real `.spc` to OGG
   in 23.7× realtime, carrying ID666 title/composer into OGG metadata,
   and the default render is one full loop plus echo/fade tail — exactly
   what whole-file looping needs.
3. Godot: load as `AudioStreamOggVorbis`, set `loop = true`
   (whole-file loop reproduces the sequence's own loop; `loop_offset` is
   the fallback if a track has a non-looping intro — render intro and
   loop separately, or render two iterations with
   `ffmpeg -stream_loop 1` and set `loop_offset` to the first end).
4. Add a `MusicPlayer` autoload (play/stop/crossfade, one
   AudioStreamPlayer on the Music bus).

Gate: the track loops in-game with no audible seam.

**Milestone 2 — full soundtrack + ID table.**

- Batch-rip all tracks (Music Test, one `.spc` each), convert with a
  scripted loop, keep `.spc` and `.ogg` outside the repo (same treatment
  as the ROM).
- Build the ID → track table the game drives: IDs arrive from map jumps
  (bits 10-15, docs/triggers.md) and event op `1D`. Name tracks from the
  community docs (BGM改変 readme map themes, zophar numbering for
  originals, bokuno additions per its own readme). The bokuno table is
  identical to base for IDs `0x00`–`0x5B` (verified), so base-game
  naming carries over; extended IDs come from the hack docs.

**Milestone 3 — optional: in-engine playback via GDExtension.**

Trigger only if OGG proves painful (disk size, instant track switching
under 1 frame, or wanting SFX through the same synth later). Trial
GameMusicEmu-GDExtension first (blargg core), gd_libvgm second (cleaner
license, unproven SPC DSP). Half a day to A/B both against the OGG
reference on three tracks (a percussion-heavy one, an echo-heavy one,
a quiet one).

**SFX (later).** RS3 driver SFX goes through v-command FD ("Play SFX")
with its own sample bank, separate from music. The Godot side will
likely reuse game-extracted samples with plain AudioStreamPlayers; do
not couple it to the music decision.

## Risks

- Debug Music Test may not work in bokuno_jp (UNVERIFIED) — cheap to
  test first; fallback harness is small.
- ~200 MB of local OGG assets: acceptable because they regenerate from
  the ROM; never committed.
- Both GDExtensions are October-2026 single-maintainer projects with
  <10 stars; pin the release zip (they ship prebuilt artifacts) and keep
  the OGG fallback intact.
- bokuno may ship further track additions in future hack versions
  (KR v0.118+); the rip table is regenerated from whatever ROM is
  current, not hand-maintained.
- Emulator SPC dumps can differ in echo handling (see INSTALL.md note);
  verify each rip by ear before conversion.

## Milestone 1 status (2026-11-16): three tracks ripped and converted

This supersedes the "SPC ripping procedure" section above: instead of the
TCRF debug route (whose codes stay UNTESTED on bokuno — the codes from
tcrf.net are 22 PAR writes of `FF` to `$7EF46A-$7EF47F`, Music Test is menu
`07` in Neft's Den), the rip goes through MesenCE's `-testRunner` headless
mode with a song-dispatch hijack (harness per docs/parity.md §9 M0 log;
emulator binary stays in `/tmp/mesence/`, scripts in `tools/emulator/`):

1. `rip.lua` boots the ROM and, on every execution of the SNES-side song
   dispatcher's table read — `LDA $C60FC6,X` at SNES `$5E:191B`, the
   original-id path of the function entered with A = X = track_id × 3
   (`CMP #$0114` = 92 tracks × 3; `CMP #$0174` = 124 × 3) — forces A/X to
   the wanted track. The dispatcher then resolves the sequence pointer from
   the `$C6:0FC6` table and the game uploads and plays that track itself.
   (For ids ≥ 92 the same function reads extended pointer tables at
   `$5A65DC` and `$5E184C` — from static disassembly only, UNVERIFIED at
   runtime.) Entry point found at runtime with an exec memory callback;
   reads of the table itself are not observable (MesenCE read callbacks do
   not fire on ROM, see parity.md §9).
2. At frame 2400 (≈31 s into the song) it dumps SPC700 RAM (64 KiB), DSP
   registers `$00-$7F`, and the SPC700 registers (PC/A/X/Y/PS/SP) over
   stdout as base64; `spc_build.py` assembles a format-v0.30 `.spc`.
3. `rip_track.sh` converts: ffmpeg's libgme render capped with `-t 40`
   (some tracks never signal an end and the WAV would grow unbounded;
   `-stream_loop` hangs on the non-seekable gme stream), two copies
   concatenated, `libvorbis -q:a 5`, into `exports/data/bgm/` (gitignored
   via `/exports/data/`, same license chain as the ROM — nothing committed).

Tracks ripped from `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` (SHA-256 `4793e142…`, under
`RamPowerOnState=AllZeros`):

| id | name (§ "What is in the ROM") | ogg | duration | mean RMS | peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x01` | The Battle | `exports/data/bgm/battle.ogg` | 66.4 s | -31.6 dB | -10.2 dB |
| `0x02` | Dungeon 1 | `exports/data/bgm/dungeon1.ogg` | 80.0 s | -25.2 dB | -7.1 dB |
| `0x05` | (field theme, community numbering) | `exports/data/bgm/field.ogg` | 80.0 s | -24.5 dB | -9.4 dB |

Validation (all verified): `ffmpeg volumedetect`/`astats` on the decoded
OGG show non-silent audio with substantial 200 Hz-4 kHz band energy; the
three `.spc` dumps are distinct (sha256 `5e19bedf…` / `09b2d4e7…` /
`7ea4b443…`); a no-hijack control dump differs from the hijacked battle
dump, so the forced id is what selects the track; a rerun reproduces the
`.spc` byte-identically. Listen-through before Milestone 1's "loops with no
audible seam" gate is still open (headless machine).

```

`docs/naming.md`:

```md
# Name entry (kana grid) — engine decode

Sources: decomp bank C5 (read on-machine, not copied), a live MesenCE
capture of the real machine playing the intro (/tmp/naming, harness kept as
`tools/emulator/naming_probe.lua`), and the decoded actor-name table
(`data/names/actors.txt`, cmd/dumpnames). The port side is
`godot/naming_screen.gd`.

## Where the name lives

- WRAM `$7E:F300`, 8 bytes, `$50`-terminated (docs/parity.md §2.7;
  docs/vm-semantics.md op 2F resolves the leader's member record to this
  buffer, C0:31A6). Length cursor: `$3D89` (insert appends at `$3D89`,
  delete writes `$50` and decrements — C5:8E7F/C5:8ECE).
- Screen state: `$3D84` picked actor, `$3D85` mode (0 hiragana / 1
  katakana), `$3D87`/`$3D88` cursor.

## Opening the screen: default name prefill

The naming UI's init (C5:8B39) copies the actor-name table entry
`FD:1480 + <$3D84>*8` (8 bytes) into `$7E:F300` and counts the pre-`$50`
length into `$3D89`. `$3D84` is the picked protagonist's actor id, so the
default name per character = the decoded actor names:

| actor id | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| name | ユリアン | エレン | サラ | トーマス | ハリード | ミカエル | モニカ | カタリナ |

(トーマス/ハリード carry the chōonpu glyph; the dump tool renders it 一.)
Live capture run5: right after the male-page pick, the buffer held
`A6 A9 82 AE 50 50 50 50` (`$3D89=04`) = ユリアン — the prefill fires at
the pick, before the grid shows.

## The grid (live capture, rel450 shot)

The window (hiragana mode) shows a ひらがな/カタカナ header, then per row a
5-char gojūon block plus a dakuten/small block, then 終了:

```
あ い う え お   わ   ん
か き く け こ   ゃ ゅ ょ っ
さ し す せ そ   が ぎ ぐ げ ご
た ち つ て と   ざ じ ず ぜ ぞ
な に ぬ ね の   だ ぢ づ で ど
は ひ ふ へ ほ   ば び ぶ べ ぱ
ま み む め も   ー
や ゆ よ
ら り る れ ろ
              終了
```

The on-screen layout comes from the cell tables at `C5:85C9` (hiragana) /
`C5:862C` (katakana): `index = (row-1)*7 + col`, `$FF` = empty cell, row 0
(the cursor's `$3D88==0`) is the header/control row that reads the 7 bytes
in front of the table. The stored bytes are the hack's own glyph codes, not
the vanilla ids (e.g. cursor insert at the な cell wrote `0x65`, at the や
row `0x75`; the actor-table name bytes are `A6 A9 82 AE`). The port does
not need those codes — it stores the picked characters as a string.
Katakana mode's exact cell set was not separately captured; the port ships
the counterpart reading of the same layout.

## Keys (on the engine's own panel)

- A: enter the highlighted kana (auto-repeat held; max 8 chars,
  `$3D89==8` guard).
- B: `Bボタン: 1文字消す` — delete the last kana.
- START: `スタートボタン: 終了` — finish with the buffer as it stands
  (the buffer holds the default name until edited).
- Up/Down on the header row toggle ひらがな/カタカナ (`$3D85 ^= 1`).
- 終了 cell = confirm.

Port mapping: arrows move, Enter/Space insert (終了 finishes), Backspace
deletes, Tab toggles mode, Esc finishes.

## Engine quirk not ported

The engine's cursor can walk off the 7-wide table rows (`$3D87` range
0..0x0A with stride 7), aliasing into the next row's cells; the port keeps
the cursor inside the real 5+4-column layout.

## Port wiring

- `godot/naming_screen.gd` — grid UI, buffer starts at the default name.
- `main.gd` — title -> select -> naming -> opening 0B31.
- `GameState.protagonist_name` (`""` = engine default) +
  `GameState.DEFAULT_NAMES` (per select row, via SELECT_ROWS).
- `save_manager.gd` — additive `protagonist_name` field.
- `field_menus.gd` — the status tab's leader row shows the entered name.

## Where the entered name appears in dialogue

Both actor-name ops compare the actor id with the leader member record
`$7EF000` (the select pick, `SELECT_ROWS[row]`) and copy the `$F300`
buffer on a match, the table name otherwise:

- op `4A id` (19323 uses): handler C0:3188 (`INC $78; LDA [$78]; CMP
  $7EF000; BEQ $31CB`). Live-proven 2026-11-20
  (`tools/emulator/name_handler.lua`): the operand byte of event 0800's
  `4a 01` at FC:1A72 is read at C0:318E, and the engine printed
  「なあエレン、」 inline. The vanilla table entry C0:226F (a window-style
  setter) never executes in bokuno — `name_window.lua` watched it and
  `$D599` writes across the opening (0 hits, `$D599` only 00/01).
- op `4F 2F x` (10 uses): C0:31A6, id = `$EF00[x]`, same compare.

The port: `GameState.custom_name_for` + `event_vm.gd _actor_name`; pinned
in `--selftest` ("actor names ok"). Operands FC/FD are plain table
entries (お兄様 / 男爵), not specials.

```

`docs/parity.md`:

```md
# Emulator-parity harness: verifying the Go event VM against the real ROM

Design for a harness that proves the port's event VM behaves identically
to the event VM of `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` (SHA-256 `4793e142…f2da0`) as
executed by a real SNES emulator. The compared side is today
`internal/game/vm`'s lockstep against the MesenCE capture, run by
`bash scripts/parity_gate.sh` (§12; the GDScript `godot/event_vm.gd` this
design originally targeted retired with the engine 2026-11-23, and the
dated M0/M1/M3 logs below are history). Semantics reference:
`docs/vm-semantics.md`. Trigger data: `docs/triggers.md` (`cmd/dumptriggers`).

## 1. What parity means here

The comparison unit is one event run, recorded as a trace. Two traces are
equal when, for the same visible game state and the same menu selections:

- **event id** — the native id currently executing (`$D51B`, vm-semantics
  §1.4) and the interpreter position (`$78/$79/$7A`) evolve through the
  same sequence of ops;
- **branch** — every gate (33/34/45/49-check/0D-check) lands on the same
  TRUE(+3)/FALSE(+5) position, every selGoto picks the same record,
  every tail dispatch resolves to the same event id;
- **text** — every dialogue page contains the same glyph sequence, read
  from the WRAM text buffer `$D56D` (§1.2) on the ROM side and from the
  VM's page output on the port side.

Not compared: frame timing, window animation, sound, PPU output. The
ROM-side capture is per interpreter step, not per frame, so those do not
interfere.

## 2. Capture is RAM watching, not CPU hooks

The engine keeps its whole interpreter state in WRAM at documented
addresses (§1.1, §1.2, §2.3, §2.5). The harness therefore needs only:

| WRAM (CPU addr) | role | source |
|---|---|---|
| `$00:76` | frame active flag | §1.1 |
| `$00:77` | call depth | §1.1 |
| `$00:78/79/7A` | script PC (lo/hi/bank) | §1.1 |
| `$00:7B/7C` | current frame end16 | §1.1 |
| `$7E:D51B` | current dispatch id (set at C0:1B50) | §1.4 |
| `$7E:D3BF/D3C0/D3C1` | selection / menu-open / option count | §2.3 |
| `$7E:D56D…` | text buffer, executed as `$7E`-bank script | §1.2 |
| `$7E:D502, $7E:D3C2+32*idx` | per-option window state | §2.3 |
| `$7E:D51D + 5*depth` | call-frame records (PC, bank, end) | §1.4 |
| `$7E:D6BD…` | deferred dispatch queue | §1.4 |
| `$7E:D519, $7E:D599, $7E:D6B9/BB/CD/CE` | op-30 slot, 4D window flag, queue state | §2.3, §2.8 |
| `$7E:F46A…` | vanilla nibble flags | §2.5 |
| `$7E:EF00…` | `$EF00` variable space (op 45, 3A, 43, 4F_2F) | §2.1, §2.7 |
| `$7E:F300…8` | custom protagonist name | §2.7 |

So no emulator debugger is needed for the parity check itself: watch
WRAM, run, diff. Emulator scripting exists in the harness only for
inputs, savestates, and the watch loop.

## 3. Reference emulator choice

Requirements: headless scripted runs on Debian 13 x86_64 (no display,
xvfb available), frame-level RAM access, savestates, input injection,
license compatible with a private RE workspace (ROM never committed).

Evidence for each row is from the project source at the current state of
each repo (checked 2026-11-16), not release notes.

| option | scripting | headless on Linux | savestates from Lua/script | input injection | license | risk / effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MesenCE** (community fork of Mesen 2, nesdev-org/MesenCE, v2.2.1) | Lua built in: `emu.read/write` per `emu.memType.SnesWorkRam`, `emu.addEventCallback` (startFrame/endFrame), `emu.addMemoryCallback` (read/write watch on an address range), `emu.setInput(port, subport, {…})`, `emu.createSavestate()`/`emu.loadSavestate()` as strings, `emu.stop`, `emu.log` | **yes, by design**: `Mesen -testRunner script.lua rom.sfc -timeout=N -enableStdout` runs `InitializeEmu(…, IntPtr.Zero, IntPtr.Zero, useSoftwareRenderer=true, noAudio=true, noVideo=true, noInput=true)` + `EmulationFlags.ConsoleMode` + `MaximumSpeed`, before any Avalonia UI init (`UI/Utilities/TestRunner.cs`) | yes (strings; can be written to files by the script if Lua file IO is enabled, or exported via `emu.log`) | yes (`emu.setInput`) | GPL-3 | low |
| libretro core + custom driver (Debian: `libretro-snes9x` 1.63 non-free, `libretro-bsnes-mercury-accuracy` main) | none — hand-written C driver (~300 lines) calling `retro_run`, `retro_serialize`, `retro_set_input_state`, `retro_get_memory_data(RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM)` | yes — no GUI at all | yes (`retro_serialize`) — but only states made inside the same driver, or by the same core in RetroArch | yes | snes9x non-commercial (non-free), mercury GPL-3 | medium: hand-rolled driver, core-config knobs (overclocks, input polling) affect determinism; everything (traces, state extraction) must be built from scratch |
| BizHawk (TASEmulators) | Lua (richest API ecosystem) | nominal `--headless` exists; Linux/headless history is rough and version-dependent | yes | yes | mostly GPL-2+ | high install effort on a headless Debian box; .NET + display shims; UNVERIFIED (Linux headless SNES runs) |
| bsnes-plus (devinacker) | **none** — the repo tree contains no Lua/scripting (verified via the git tree) | GUI only, under xvfb | manual, via GUI | manual | GPL-2 | unusable for an automated harness; only useful for one-off manual confirmation |
| snes9x-rr | Lua (snes9x-rr API) | Windows-centric, last real release 2014 | yes | yes | non-commercial | high: stale codebase, Linux build risk |
| ares (Debian main, 134) | none | — | — | — | GPL-3 | no scripting: unusable |

Rust "lightweight" SNES cores (the `rustic`-style suggestion) were ruled
out without further research: none of the known Rust SNES projects ship a
scripting API or savestate tooling; they would add a correctness risk to
a harness whose entire value is being a trusted reference.

### Recommendation

**MesenCE, driven by its `-testRunner` headless mode with Lua capture
scripts.** It is the only option that meets every requirement with
shipped code: true headless (audio/video/input explicitly disabled in
the test runner path), per-step RAM watches, savestates and input
injection from the same script, GPL-3, Linux x64 release artifacts
(~40 MB zip, requires SDL2; UNVERIFIED (release contents): whether the
zip bundles the .NET 8 runtime or needs it installed — settle this in
milestone 0).

Mesen 1 (archived) also had `/testrunner`, and Mesen-S (Mono) is
obsolete — MesenCE supersedes both. Mono itself is not needed anywhere
in this design.

## 4. Harness architecture

```
                  ROM side (reference)                      Godot side (system under test)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ MesenCE -testRunner capture.lua bokuno_jp│    │ godot --headless --path godot \        │
 │   -enableStdout                          │    │   -- --parity <event> --state st.json  │
 │                                          │    │   --rng <seed>                         │
 │ watch: writes to $78/79/7A, $D51B,       │    │ EventVM.next_page() / choose()         │
 │        $D3BF/$D3C1, reads of $D56D       │    │ trace: op addresses, gate decisions,   │
 │ trace: step log → stdout (emu.log)       │    │   pages (already computed in the VM)   │
 └──────────────┬───────────────────────────┘    └──────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                │ parity_rom.json                               │ parity_godot.json
                └────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                 ▼
                     checker (Go, future cmd/paritycheck)
                     normalizes both traces to one schema:
                     [event id, op addr, branch, page text]
                     → diff → pass/fail
```

The checker is a separate small tool (not designed in detail here); the
two trace files are its contract. `emu.log` lines go to stdout when the
emulator runs with `-enableStdout` (`EmulationFlags.OutputToStdout`,
verified in `CommandLineHelper.cs`), so the Lua script never needs file
access — this sidesteps the Mesen 2 "scripts may not touch the file
system by default" behavior entirely.

### 4.1 ROM-side capture script (Lua)

- On `emu.eventType.startFrame`: read `$76`, `$77`, `$D51B`; read
  `$D3BF`, `$D3C0`, `$D3C1`; read the text buffer `$D56D` up to its
  terminator and the menu option table.
- For a per-step trace (needed for exact branch capture):
  `emu.addMemoryCallback(fn, emu.callbackType.write, 0x78, 0x7A,
  emu.memType.SnesWorkRam)` — one callback event per interpreter PC
  advance — plus a write watch on `$D51B` for tail dispatches and one on
  `$D3BF` for selections. Gate each callback on
  `$76 == 1 && $D51B == <target event>` so the log stays small.
- Emit one JSON object per line via `print` (M0 finding: `emu.log` feeds only
  the UI script window; `print` is what reaches stdout, see M0 log):
  `{"pc":"73:03a9","id":"0x0001","ev":"gate33@03a6->TRUE"}` — the exact
  schema is fixed later, together with the Godot driver.
- `emu.stop(exitCode)` ends the run; `-timeout=…` is the watchdog.

UNVERIFIED (source reading only): whether `emu.read` on
`emu.memType.SnesWorkRam` takes full CPU addresses (`0x7ED51B`) or raw
WRAM offsets (`0xD51B`), and whether direct-page `$00:xx` mirrors need
the `$7E:0000+xx` form. The first probe script asserts both.

### 4.2 Text decode

Text buffer bytes are glyph codes: bytes ≥ 0x50 are single glyphs,
ranges with lead bytes 0x20–0x23/0x18/0x46 are 2-byte glyphs, `00`/`50`
terminates (§1.2). Map codes to codepoints with the existing
`data/glyphs_jp.json` (same table `cmd/dumpevents` uses), then compare
against the Godot page string. The 4F text subs (name/number/table
insertion, §2.7) resolve on the ROM side through the same engine
routines, so parity on the final buffer covers them end to end —
including the open `$68:36F0` transform behind op 45 and the actor-name
path (ROM name table vs. `$F300` custom name).

### 4.3 Seeding the ROM into a known state

Priority order:

1. **User savestate (primary).** The owner plays the game in MesenCE
   GUI (same build as the harness), reaches the spot before event E,
   saves a savestate. The Lua harness reads that file (enable the
   script-IO config toggle for the capture script, or pass its bytes via
   a one-line boot script) with `emu.loadSavestate(...)`, then injects
   the few inputs that trigger the event. Valid because the harness
   dumps the WRAM flag/variable regions (§2 table) into `state.json`
   and feeds them to the Godot side — the comparison is between VMs on
   the *same* inputs, whatever those inputs are.
2. **WRAM poke + walk (deterministic, no playthrough needed).** From a
   clean boot: write the vanilla flag space and `$EF00` variables to the
   target values, warp the party by writing the current-map state and
   position to the values `cmd/dumptriggers` reports for the map, then
   walk to the event-point rectangle with scripted inputs
   (`emu.setInput` per frame from a startFrame callback). Best for CI:
   fully reproducible. Cost: finding which WRAM cells hold map id and
   party position (one-time, ~a day with the memory-write watch on the
   GUI build; the values themselves are already known from
   docs/triggers.md).
3. **Full scripted input from power-on (rejected as the default.**
   Brittle against menu timing and animation waits; keep only as the
   fallback if both above fail for an event.

Selection menus: run each target event twice — once letting the menu
time out / closing it (`$D3BF == 0xFF` → engine fallback `$D3C1-1`,
§2.3), once injecting the selection by pressing the confirm input when
`$D3C0 == 1` — and feed Godot `state.menu_selection` accordingly.

### 4.4 Random branch `4f 16 nn` (§2.6) and the two RNGs

**Field RNG (C0:0733), ported exactly** (now `internal/game/rng`; the
field selftest pins 40 live calls; the formula reproduces 400
consecutive live calls):
state `$0A` (a) and `$0B` (b, 0..14); a roll advances `a = a*3 + b`,
`b = (b+1) mod 15` and returns `lo + a mod (hi-lo+1)` on 8 bits
(width 256 returns a). Consumers share one stream: the random branch
(C0:2EFA), the action-script interpreter (C0:5D43-6FE1 — NPC wander
directions and waits, 330+70 of the 400 captured calls), the map
loader (C0:4605) and bank FF through the long wrapper C0:0726. The
seed: C0:019A-01B1 sets `$0A = ~$213C` (the PPU horizontal-counter
latch; `$0B` untouched) at boot, on queue dispatches (C0:B892-B9ED)
and map jumps (C0:C0D2). That value depends on cycle timing, so the
port cannot derive it: exact comparisons inject the engine's `$0A`
at each reseed, and exact random-branch outcomes also need the
action scripts to consume the stream frame-exactly. Until then the
checker verifies membership (`random: expected {E+1..E+nn}`).

**Battle RNG (C2:032E)**, generator ported (`internal/game/rng`):
rand in `[$BF..$C0]` = `lo + T[$14] mod (hi-lo+1)` (hardware divide at
C2:02A3), T = the 1024-byte table at `D7:E63C` (`battle_rng.bin`);
`lo == hi`, `hi == 0` or `hi < lo` return 0 without advancing
(C2:033E). Battle code runs with D = 0x0900, so `$14` is `$0914`, not
the NMI frame counter at DP-0 `$14` (FF:0300). Battle start seeds it
with the play clock's frame (`$F30D`, 0-59) times 16 (FE:C5A8-C5B4);
each roll (C2:036B) and each battle frame wait (FE:C14E, 24 callers)
advances it, wrapping at 0x400. Live (opening battle, frame 45076):
`$F30D` = 21 -> index 0210, then 11 rolls (1..8, 1..15, 1..65) match
the model; the selftest pins them. The play clock (`$F30A-$F30D`)
ticks in game_state every frame. The port's battle code rolls this
generator (internal/game/battle); exact sequences also need the engine's
roll order and battle frame count.

Play-clock rules, measured on a full new-game run to the first battle
(per-frame traces of `$F30A-$F30D` and the tick sites C5:0ECD/C5:F327):
the tick is a call in the hack's main-loop mode dispatch (the FF:00D1
NMI only carries seconds -> minutes -> hours, so the tick is skipped on
whole frames, not inside one); the clock RESETS to zero when the
opening event 0800 starts (the title and the stat screens never count:
10394 frames walked there, dropped live at frame 10622); and it holds
during a map load's black span - the load frame through the frame the
brightness ramp starts (024B 178, 0249 158, 024A 99, 0250 188 frames;
the ramp itself ticks) - and from the battle handoff's fade-out
(fade-out start to the battle screen, 125 frames, so the battle seed
reads a clock frozen 25 frames earlier). Ported: only the reset. The
hold lengths are the load's CPU cost (they vary per map with the
install work and stretch with lag), which the port does not model -
the same class as arrivalcheck's lag cut-over - so the port's clock at
the first battle stays ~655 frames behind the engine's and the battle
seed differs (340 vs 330 in the opening extension).

Roll order, measured (2026-11-21, the opening ensemble battle with A
every 16 frames: ROLL lines at C2:032E with the JSR caller, BWAIT lines
at FE:C14E): 81 rolls and 289 frame waits to the battle's end, as
`caller lo..hi count` and `W<waits>`:

C2:1650 1..0, C2:166C 1..0, C2:1694 1..8, C2:16D5 1..8, C2:14E4 1..15 x4,
C2:1520 1..15 x4, C2:1C58 1..65 | W155 | C2:2588 1..20 x5 (turn order) |
W4 | C2:5A1B 1..8, 5AC9 1..0, 5AEE 0..0, 59F1 0..3, BC5C 0..255, 5C7D
1..22 | W41 | C2:0383 1..100, 90B4 1..9, 69C7 0..3 | W3 | C2:C142
0..255 x13, 0383 1..100, 90B4 1..21, 69C7 0..3 | W3 | C2:DA84 0..255,
DB23 0..255 x16 | W32 | DD81/DC7B/DD24 0..255 x15 | W13 | DC7B 0..255,
DCC6 1..3, E033 0..255 | W4 | E149 0..30 x2, 0383 1..100 | W34

The final W34 are the spoils' closing 4 (C2:E230) plus FE:EB47's 30
(one loop caller FE:C181, index 035C-037D), skipped when the battle
type $141A is 0x0C; the port runs both (battle.gd `_victory_spoils`,
the battleselftest pins the tail's index at 037E and the 0x0C skip).

The waits come in a few blocks (the intro's 155, then 3-41 between
steps), not one per screen frame, so the index stays countable. The port
still ticks the index every physics frame (battle.gd `_physics_process`),
so its sequence leaves the engine's at the first frame; that tick stands
until the waits are modelled. Wait callers (second capture, return
addresses): FE:C181 198, FE:B8CC 59, FE:B83F 18, FE:C197 7, FE:BD49 5,
FE:C01E 1, FE:C057 1. The intro repeats a group (C181 x4, B8CC xN,
C181 x8, B8CC x6, C181 x4, B83F x2) with N = 8, 5, 4, 7, 5; every B8CC
block ends one frame before a multiple of 16, the probe's A press, so
B8CC waits for a button and N is the phase against the press cadence,
not content. FE:C14E is one wait (NMI, then the index + 1 mod 400h).
FE:C17A repeats it `$16` times; its 18 callers load fixed counts (C2:E870
2, EAE1 8, EC74 8, FDFA 15, FED6 180, FEF9 60, FF65 2; EB:EB58 20, EC14
120; FE:B767 8, B8AF 4, C030 30, C13B 2, C18F 60, C1D3 12, C1ED 2, EB5A
30; FE:B7B2 from elsewhere). FE:C194 repeats it until `$0E` is set (a
flag wait). The intro's five groups are the five allies' command menus
(C181 x4 open, B8CC per frame until the button, C181 x8, B8CC until the
target button, C181 x4, B83F x2), so the port's per-frame tick is right
while a menu waits for input. During an action the index barely moves:
frames 45732-45883 (150 frames of animation) hold two waits (B83F x2),
and the animation frames between them advance the index by zero
(measured 2026-11-23, stream_waits.lua).
Per action the capture shows short chunks: C181 x4 before the AI rolls
(5A1B-5C7D), B83F, C01E, C181 x38, C057 before the hit rolls (0383 1..100,
90B4, 69C7), B83F x2 and BD49 after each, C181 x30 / x34 at the next
steps. Resolved 2026-11-23 (one full opening battle captured live;
docs/battle-enemy-ai.md "Per-action wait chunks" carries the site map):
the x4 before the AI rolls is the `jsl $FEB8F4` at C2:1E3F (its inner
B8A3 waits 4) between the SP rolls and the driver; the B83F + C01E +
C181 x38 + C057 run is the enemy actor's C2:C860 → FE:C016 animation
(1 + 4 + 30 + 4 + 1 = 40 waits; ally actors run none); the B83F x2 +
BD49 are the action tail C2:6652 (B839 at 667F, B839 at 6697, BD28 at
669B), with the ~90-frame damage drain between the two B839s advancing
nothing; the C181 x30 / x34 at the next steps are the victory chain
(FE:EB5A's 30, then E230's 4 + EB47's 30 again = 34, index 035C-037D,
ending at 037E). An action moves the index by exactly 40 + 3 for an
enemy actor and 0 + 3 for an ally actor. The roll-site question is
closed too: none of the flagged 0..255 groups is effects-only. The
spark rolls (C142) replace the executed tech; the victory level bumps
(DA84 + DB23 x16) raise `$F532`/`$F533` — the unlock levels C2:5A43
reads for the AI's unlocked range in every later battle (consumer
5B:FF40, decoded in docs/battle-enemy-ai.md); the growth rolls persist
into stats and messages. All three are already ported. The port's
remaining chunk work is mechanical: tick 4 between the ally initiative
and the enemy decisions, 40 per enemy action before its executor, 3 per
action tail, and the victory-chain chunks the battle selftest already
walks (it pins the whole tail through index 037E, not just the first 11
rolls).

## 5. Setup on this machine (Debian 13, x86_64, headless)

```sh
# runtime deps
sudo apt install -y libsdl2-2.0-0 unzip

# emulator
mkdir -p ~/tools/mesence && cd ~/tools/mesence
curl -LO https://github.com/nesdev-org/MesenCE/releases/download/2.2.1/Mesen_2.2.1_Linux_x64.zip
unzip Mesen_2.2.1_Linux_x64.zip

# if the zip turns out not to be self-contained (settle in milestone 0):
# install .NET 8 runtime via https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh (not in Debian apt)

# smoke test, no display needed:
unset DISPLAY
./Mesen -testRunner boot_probe.lua /home/newlix/projects/saga3/patches/bokuno_jp.sfc \
    -timeout=30 -enableStdout
```

No xvfb needed for the test-runner path (video/audio/input disabled by
the runner itself). xvfb stays useful only if we ever drive the GUI
build (e.g. the one-time WRAM hunt in §4.3-2).

Harness scripts live under `scripts/parity/` (`boot_probe.lua`,
`capture.lua`, plus the trace files), checker under `cmd/paritycheck`
— all future files, none exist yet.

## 6. First milestone

**M0 — boot the ROM headless and prove the capture path** (est. 1–2 h):

1. Install MesenCE per §5; run `boot_probe.lua` with `-enableStdout`
   against `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`. UNVERIFIED (not yet run): the zip's
   runtime bundling, and that the process exits without `DISPLAY` set.
   The probe asserts exactly this: it calls `emu.log`, then
   `emu.stop(0)`, and the shell checks exit code 0 and non-empty stdout.
2. In the same probe: read one byte each at `$7E:0076` (frame flag),
   `$7E:7ED51B`, and a known WRAM cell via direct-page form; print all
   values. Assert the three address forms behave as expected (resolves
   the §4.1 UNVERIFIED item).
3. **Determinism**: run twice, `emu.log` a stable probe line each
   startFrame (frame number + `$78/79/7A` + `$D51B`), hash stdout;
   hashes must be equal.

**M1 — event-id assertion against the pointer tables** (est. 0.5 day):

1. `capture.lua` traces, from a clean boot through the title screen and
   into an attract/opening event: every write to `$D51B` and every PC
   write while `$76 == 1`, as JSON lines on stdout.
2. A small Go step resolves each `$D51B` through the same resolver rules
   the project already implements (`internal/bokuno` event pointer
   lookup; §1.4 `5A:AC70` paths) and asserts:
   - the resolved start equals `$78/$79/$7A` observed at the first step
     of that event;
   - the first byte at PC is a plausible op (`< 0x50` or a glyph lead),
     and the op stream walks at least 5 ops in `data/events/`-style
     decoding;
   - `$00:76 == 1` exactly while `$77`/PC change and the frame closes
     with `43` or PC == end16.
3. Output: `parity_rom.json` + a pass/fail line; wire into
   `scripts/gate.sh` only after M3.

**M2 — text parity on one real event** (est. 1–2 days): user savestate
before a known NPC event (from `dumptriggers` output), harness triggers
it, decodes `$D56D` pages via `data/glyphs_jp.json`; Godot side replays
the same event with the dumped `state.json`; checker diffs page text.
Repeat with a selection-menu event, both menu paths (choice, timeout
fallback).

**M3 — gate/branch parity across a set** (est. 2–3 days): pick ~20
events covering every gate family (33/34/45/49/0D, selGoto, jump16,
jumpL, callL), run both sides, wire the checker into `scripts/gate.sh`.
This is the steady-state regression gate; `--selftest-full` coverage of
all 4,351 events is a later scale-up (the ROM side costs ~seconds per
event at MaximumSpeed).

## 7. Risks

- **MesenCE release runtime**: UNVERIFIED whether the Linux zip is
  self-contained. Fallback is the dotnet-install script, or building
  from source (`COMPILING.md`). Milestone 0 settles it.
- **Address domains** (§4.1): cheap to assert, easy to fix in the Lua
  script.
- **Lua script IO gating**: avoided by design — all output through
  `emu.log`/stdout; savestate bytes can also pass through `emu.log` in
  a pinch, but loading a *file* savestate inside Lua needs the config
  toggle enabled for that script.
- **Memory-callback overhead**: watches are single-cell, gated on
  `$76 == 1`; Mesen halts execution per callback at MaximumSpeed, which
  is the main performance unknown (UNVERIFIED). If too slow, drop to
  startFrame polling (loses intra-frame steps; branch capture moves to
  "next observed PC" semantics, which the checker normalizes).
- **Emulator accuracy**: Mesen's SNES core is cycle-accurate; parity
  conclusions about VM logic do not depend on PPU/APU subtleties since
  capture is WRAM-only.
- **Godot-side gaps** (`event_vm.gd` transparent ops, placeholder
  names for 39/3A, op 45's undecoded transform, ext-flag space with
  unknown RAM base): the harness will *find* these as mismatches — that
  is its job. Expected first findings, not noise; each maps to a §4
  OPEN item in vm-semantics.md.
- **Seeding dependence on the user's play** (§4.3-1) for M2: the
  poke-and-walk path (§4.3-2) removes it for CI.

## 8. What the harness resolves beyond parity

Running real events with WRAM watches directly answers several OPEN
items in vm-semantics.md §4:

- **ext-flag (0D) RAM base** — watch WRAM writes while an event with a
  `0d 00`-style gate executes; the written cells are the space.
- **op 45 `$68:36F0` transform** — dump `$EF00[a]` before and the
  compared value after; the transform's output is observable per input.
- **op 49 sub-semantics** — per-sub-op RAM deltas over the packed-4
  space (`$FE00` table contents notwithstanding, the *effects* are
  observable).
- **callL return address** — the PC write watch shows the exact restored
  PC at frame pop (§1.4), pinning the one PLAUSIBLE detail in §2.4-3.
- **`0d 19` callIndirect** — only reachable by emulation (0 dump
  occurrences); reachable here by crafting a test event stream in WRAM
  (the text-buffer mechanism shows WRAM scripts are executable).

## 9. M0 log (executed 2026-11-16, MesenCE 2.2.1)

Setup results and deviations from §5, all verified by running:

- Release tag is `2.2.1`, not `v2.2.1` (§5 fixed). The zip unpacks to a single
  self-contained ELF (`Mesen`, 83 MB, bundled .NET runtime, `ldd` clean) —
  the dotnet-install fallback (§5, §7) is not needed. Only runtime dep is
  SDL2 (`libsdl2-2.0-0` 2.32.4, Debian). Extracted to `/tmp/mesence/`
  (untracked); `tools/emulator/run.sh` wraps the `-testRunner` invocation.
  Harness scripts live in `tools/emulator/`, not `scripts/parity/` (§5).
- **`settings.json` is required for headless mode**: `Program.Main` runs the
  Avalonia first-run wizard *before* the testRunner branch when no config
  exists, and the wizard dies with `System.Exception: XOpenDisplay failed`
  under no DISPLAY. Fix: portable mode — a `settings.json` next to the
  binary. Ours sets `Snes.Port1.Type = 1` (SnesController: when a config
  file exists, `InitializeDefaults` never runs, the port type stays `None`,
  and Lua `setInput`/`getInput` find no control device) and
  `Snes.RamPowerOnState = 1` (AllZeros, for determinism below).
- **Output channel**: `print()` reaches stdout (`MessageManager::Log` +
  `OutputToStdout`); `emu.log` does NOT (buffers for the UI script window,
  `ScriptingContext::Log`), and `emu.displayMessage` does not either. All
  harness output uses `print` (§4.1 corrected in place).
- **Address forms** (§4.1 UNVERIFIED resolved): memory APIs take full CPU
  addresses, `bank<<16 | offset`. `$00:0076` equals `$7E:0076` through the
  SNES WRAM mirror at `$0000-$1FFF`, but `$00:D51B` is not the WRAM cell
  (bank `$00` `$8000+` maps to ROM on this ExHiROM) — boot probe at frame
  1200: `76dp=00 76bank=00 00D51B=06 7ED51B=A8`. Every §2 address must use
  the `0x7Exxxx` form.
  **CORRECTED in the M1 log (§10), the M0 conclusion above is backwards**:
  `emu.read`/`emu.write` on `snesWorkRam` take **raw WRAM offsets**
  (`0x76`, `0xD51B`), not full CPU addresses. The `$00:D51B` read in the
  boot probe hit the real WRAM cell; `0x7ED51B` is past the 128 KiB WRAM
  array and wraps (`0x7ED51B mod 0x20000` = `0x1D51B` = bank `7F:D51B`,
  an unrelated cell) — that is where the probe's `A8` came from. §2's
  watch addresses must all use the raw-offset form — the §10 M1 trace only
  went live after this fix.
- **Memory callbacks**: write watch on WRAM verified; exec watch on ROM
  verified; read watch on ROM does NOT fire even when the hooked instruction
  executes (exec watch on the same address does). §2's capture relies on
  write watches — usable; ROM read watches are unusable.
- **Lua API call shapes**: parameter lists are consumed last-to-first, so
  tables come first — `emu.setCpuState({a=…, x=…}, emu.cpuType.snes)`,
  `emu.setInput({start=1}, 0, 0)`. Button names are lowercase
  (`a b x y l r start select up down left right`). SNES/SPC state tables use
  lowercase keys (`a x y sp d pc k dbr ps`; spc: `a x y pc ps sp`).
  `emu.stop` does not synchronously halt callbacks — guard final output
  with a done flag or the log differs by one extra line.
- **Determinism** (M0 step 3): three consecutive boot_probe runs produce
  byte-identical stdout (sha256 `0a7f9dc2…`), and two full rip runs
  (1200+ frames of gameplay with music) produce byte-identical stdout under
  `RamPowerOnState=1` (`68791e47…`). A rip rerun reproduces the `.spc`
  byte-identically (`5e19bedf…`, see the M1 note in docs/music.md).
- Files: `tools/emulator/boot_probe.lua`, `run.sh`, `find_song_dispatch.lua`
  (song-dispatch discovery, also used for the BGM rip in docs/music.md),
  `rip.lua`, `rip_track.sh`, `spc_build.py`.
- Known load-failure trap: TestRunner wraps `LoadScript` in a silent
  `try/catch` — a Lua syntax error means the script never runs and the
  emulator just runs to `-timeout`. Scripts print a load marker
  (`RIP-LOADED`) that the shell driver checks.

## 10. M1 log (executed 2026-11-16, MesenCE 2.2.1)

Recon for M1 ("boot through the title screen into an opening event") plus
the harness scripts. Findings, all verified by running:

- **Boot timeline** (RamPowerOnState=AllZeros): unattended, the opening
  prologue auto-plays for ~6900 frames (narration pages advance on their
  own), ~7200 the Squaresoft logo, ~7500 the title screen; the attract
  loop restarts the prologue at ~frame 16290. **The prologue is
  skippable**: START presses every 60 frames from frame 300 reach the
  title screen by ~frame 333 (title song 43, vs 6906 unattended). Songs
  seen at the dispatcher: 72 = opening/prologue, 43 = title, 41 = the
  new-game cutscene at 10779.
- **`setInput` reaches the game only from the `inputPolled` callback.**
  Driven from `startFrame`, the joypad latch registers `$4218/$4219` stay
  `00` forever (probe: START held frames 400-700, `$4219=00` every frame);
  driven from `inputPolled`, the same hold reads `$4219=10` (START bit).
  Every earlier probe that pressed buttons from `startFrame` therefore
  never actually pressed anything — the "title ignores START" phase of
  the recon was this, not game behavior.
- **`emu.write` WORKS in `-testRunner` mode** (corrected 2026-11-22): the
  old no-op claim came from a probe that passed the arguments reversed —
  the signature is `emu.write(address, value, memType)` (the sweep
  scripts' order), and `write(0x1306, 0xAB, snesWorkRam)` from
  `inputPolled` reads back `AB` (wtest3). With reversed arguments the
  call throws `value out of range`, which killed the whole Lua callback
  silently (no LUAERR line) — when a probe's callbacks stop firing,
  look for an unguarded throwing call first. `loadSavestate` still works
  (GUI savestate
  `bokuno_jp_11.mss` embedded as base64, loaded inside an exec callback —
  that savestate turns out to be on the title screen, all 128 OAM slots
  hidden).
- **`takeScreenshot` works headless** and returns the PNG bytes (base64
  them over stdout to inspect a run). Each call costs seconds under
  load; never screenshot per frame.
- M1 capture scripts: `tools/emulator/trace_events.lua` (per-frame VM
  state-change trace over the scripted boot → new game → cutscene) with
  checker `tools/emulator/trace_check`; OAM/VRAM capture for
  docs/sprites.md in `tools/emulator/oam_capture.lua` +
  `oam_decode.py`. All presses use the `inputPolled` callback per above,
  and every press value must be a button table (`{ a = 1 }`) — passing a
  bare `true` made `setInput` a silent no-op and the trace stalled on
  the protagonist select (trace3..trace6).
- **0Cxx pseudo-events resolve to garbage (pre-existing, untouched)**:
  the engine's 0Cxx resolver branch (5A:AC70 `CMP #$0C`) reads its
  pointer table at `5A:A870+3*i` (`ADC #$A870` in the disassembly —
  §1.4 says `A970`), and both candidate bases yield unmapped banks, which
  is why all 237 `0Cxx` dumps decode 0 ops. Harmless at runtime: the
  `0c 42`-style pairs in dumps are op `0C` (first byte ≥ 0x0C means "not
  an event id", §1.5), so no dispatch flows through that table.

### M1 result (trace8, 2026-11-16): PASS

The harness plays a full new game headless (input schedule in
`trace_events.lua`: START mash 300-6800 skips the prologue — title music
by frame 333 — and lands on protagonist select; A at 7000/7800 confirms
gender 男 and character ユリアン; START at 8600 takes the default name;
A at 9000/9800/10600 confirms weapon/stats; the opening cutscene scene
event fires at ~10620). Everything the checker needs is the per-frame
VM state change log — the exec-hook and write-watch routes are gone (see
below). Raw stdout lines that the checker asserts on:

```
VM frame=10621 76=01 depth=00 PC=FC:0802 END=08EF D51B=0800
VM frame=10625 76=01 depth=02 PC=FC:DF8D END=DFA0 D51B=0BF1
VM frame=10694 76=01 depth=01 PC=FC:1394 END=155F D51B=0846
```

```
$ go build -o /tmp/parity-agent/trace_check ./tools/emulator/trace_check
$ /tmp/parity-agent/trace_check patches/bokuno_jp.sfc /tmp/parity-agent/trace8.log
PASS id=0800 frame=10621 entry=FC:0800 end16=08EF src=native-u16-block-table (PC advanced 2 bytes into the event before first sample) ops>=5
PASS id=0BF1 frame=10625 entry=FC:DF8D end16=DFA0 src=native-u16-block-table (PC == entry) ops>=5
PASS id=0846 frame=10694 entry=FC:1394 end16=155F src=native-u16-block-table (PC == entry) ops>=5
SUMMARY dispatches=3 fails=0 -> PASS
```

All three opening-scene dispatches resolve through the same
`internal/bokuno.NativeRange` rules the Godot side uses, the observed PC
equals the resolved entry exactly (or one op in, for 0800, whose sample
followed the frame boundary), 5+ ops decode at every entry, and the trace
walks every op boundary of the cutscene event (FC:1394 → … → FC:1417 → …
through end16 155F) — M1's "event-id assertion against the pointer
tables" holds end to end.

Engine facts the trace pinned beyond the checker:

- **`$D51B` is not restored when a call returns.** After the nested
  0BF1 frame returned (frame ~10635), `$D51B` stayed `0BF1` while the
  outer 0800 stream continued to walk (PC `FC:08xx…`, END `08EF`) until
  0846 dispatched at 10694. §1.4's "current dispatch id" is therefore
  the most recent tail-dispatch, not the owning frame's id.
- **Dispatch capture stays at per-frame polling of `$D51B`** (raw
  offset). An exec hook on `C0:1B50` (the dispatch store) was tried
  first; the runs that used it showed the store executing three times
  (ids 0800/0BF1/0846) but were inconclusive on whether the hook
  perturbs the dispatch, because they still read WRAM through the
  broken `0x7Exxxx` form — every zero-state observation in trace3..6 is
  explained by the address bug alone. Re-test an exec hook only after
  this if write-exact dispatch capture is ever needed.
- Write watches on WRAM (`$78-$7A` PC bytes) attached only while
  `$76==1` stay silent in trace8 (0 PCW lines while 198 VM lines show
  the interpreter stepping) — the per-write halt either does not fire
  for these raw-offset watches or the resolver writes PC through a path
  the watch does not see; unresolved (RESOLVED in §11: the watches
  fired all along; trace_events.lua discarded the captures by resetting
  `pcw` before the print). The PCW capture stays in the
  script for the gate-level milestone (M3); the checker consumes VM
  lines only.
- Determinism across runs and scripts is intact once the address forms
  are fixed: probe_vm ran twice with byte-identical DELTA lines
  (including `DELTA frame=11000 0076:00->01 … D51B:00->46 D51C:00->08`),
  and trace8's dispatch frames (10621/10625/10694) match those deltas.
- The opening prologue, title and menus are all scriptable headless;
  the full boot→new-game→cutscene timeline is stable across runs (same
  frame numbers for songs: 72@179, 43@333, 41@10779).

## 11. Watch-form resolution (2026-11-16): the watch works; trace8 had a capture-order bug

The §10 negative ("write watches on `$78-$7A` gated on `$76==1` stay
silent in trace8") does NOT reproduce at the API level. All three
suspected forms were probed in one run
(`tools/emulator/watch_probe.lua`, 10800 frames, watches attached once
at the first `$76==1`, never detached):

```
$ tools/emulator/run.sh /tmp/.../watch_probe.lua ...   (raw stdout)
X1 frame=10621 D51B=0000 at C0:1B50
WATCH-ATTACHED frame=10621
W1HIT frame=10623 addr=79 val=08 at C0:1C93
W1HIT frame=10623 addr=78 val=03 at C0:1C93
X1 frame=10625 D51B=0800 at C0:1B50
...
SUMMARY W1=347,347,5 W2=0 W3=699
PROBE-DONE frames=10800
```

- **W1 — raw WRAM offsets + `snesWorkRam`**
  (`emu.addMemoryCallback(fn, emu.callbackType.write, 0x78, 0x78,
  emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)`): FIRES. 347/347/5 hits on
  `$78/$79/$7A`. This is the trace_events.lua form — **PASS**, this is
  the working form.
- **W3 — `snesMemory` with CPU addresses `$0078-$7A`**: FIRES, 699
  (= 347+347+5, the same writes — the interpreter addresses PC through
  direct page, whose effective address lands in bank `$00`). Equally
  usable.
- **W2 — `snesMemory` with `$7E0078-$7E007A`**: 0 hits. The game never
  writes PC via bank-`$7E` absolute addressing, so this form watches the
  wrong access path; it is not broken, just unused for these cells.
- **Exec hook at `C0:1B50` retested with raw-offset reads inside the
  callback**: fires exactly 3× (frames 10621/10625/10694 — the three
  dispatch stores of the M1 trace) and reads WRAM fine, but the read
  returns the PREVIOUS dispatch id (`D51B=0000/0800/0BF1`): the exec
  callback runs at instruction start, before that store commits.
  Usable for write-exact dispatch capture with the one-store lag.

Root cause of trace8's silence: a capture-order bug in
trace_events.lua, not the watch API. The script reset `pcw = {}` in the
same startFrame callback *before* the `if #pcw > 0` print, so every
frame's captured writes were discarded before being logged — the
watches fired silently all along. Proof: the byte-identical script with
only the reset moved after the print produced 196 PCW lines over the
same run, starting

```
PCW frame=10624 n=21 79=08 78=03 79=08 78=04 79=08 78=05 ...
PCW frame=10625 n=7 79=91 78=C1 79=91 78=C2 7A=FC 78=8D 79=DF
```

(the same writes the probe's W1 saw; the fixed copy lives in the M1
retest log only — trace_events.lua itself is unchanged, since its VM
lines are what the checker consumes).

Overhead (same run batch, machine at load 40-66 of 16 cores):

- poll-per-frame (the M1/trace8 form: 6 raw reads per startFrame):
  12500 frames in 113 s wall (~110 fps) — cheap; remains the simpler
  default for M3.
- per-write watch (W1 form, attached during the cutscene only): 699 Lua
  callbacks over ~70 frames, no measurable slowdown vs the poll-only
  run. Attach once and detach deliberately; do not attach an always-on
  `$78-$7A` watch from frame 0 — boot's WRAM-clear DMA writes these
  cells constantly and stalls the run (M1 recon, §10).


## 12. M3 log (executed 2026-11-17): gate/branch parity checker wired into the gate

Scope per §6 M3: replay the headless-reachable events on both sides and
diff every gate TRUE/FALSE decision and dispatch target. All numbers below
are from `scripts/parity_gate.sh` runs (numbered dirs under
`/tmp/saga3-parity-runs/`); the ROM-side capture is deterministic across
runs — all runs recorded identical SEG frames
(10621/10625/10694/15022/16388/18263) and gate lines.

### 12.1 Architecture (as built)

- `tools/emulator/parity_gate.lua` — ROM-side capture, via `-testRunner`:
  - **SEG/SNAP**: a write watch on `$D51B/$D51C` (raw offsets; the
    range-watch callback delivers full CPU addresses — mask with
    `% 0x10000`, measured). Each tail-dispatch store prints the new id and
    a base64 snapshot of the gate-readable WRAM (vanilla flags `$F46A`,
    EF00, ext flags raw `$1FF90`, scratch raw `$1F900`, menu `$D3BF`,
    gold/bank `$F31A`, party `$F319-$F328`, inventory `$F32A`).
  - **GATE**: exec watches fire at the one handler address each gate's
    TRUE / FALSE continuation enters, giving the decision directly. The
    gate op's own address is `$78 - 2` at every watched point (the
    handlers consume opcode+operands with two INCs before branching).
  - **TGT**: exec watches where each dispatch handler has its target
    assembled (selGoto record, jump16/jumpL/callL).
  - **PCW**: the ordered `$78/$79/$7A` write trail (diagnostics only).
  - Watches attach at frame 9000: after boot's WRAM-clear DMA (§10 stall)
    and before the first dispatch (10621), so the opening event's own
    SEG/SNAP are captured.
- `cmd/paritygate` — Go checker: `prepare` (segments + snapshots →
  `jobs.json`), `compare` (lockstep diff, exit 1 on any conflict), and
  `-selftest` / `TestComparatorSelftest` (the comparator passes on
  identical inputs and flags a flipped decision or a flipped jump target).
- `godot -- --paritygate jobs.json` (in `main.gd`): replays each job's
  event from the snapshot state through the real `EventVM` and prints
  GATE/DISP/CALL/RET/SELGOTO/JUMP lines.

### 12.2 Gate decisions are exec-watched, not trail-inferred

The first design inferred TRUE/FALSE from the `$78` write trail. That is
unsound: the FALSE skip walks its two bytes with INCs (op33 handler
`C0:2FA5` = `INC $78` × 3 — machine-decoded), and the dominant dump idiom
(`33 id win / 4e nn / …` with both arms converging) produces *identical*
PC-write sequences for both decisions. Example measured in the run: event
0BF1's `33 2a 0e` at `FC:df97` — TRUE and FALSE paths emit the same trail
`df9a df9b df9c …` because the TRUE arm is a `4e 03` skip whose
consumption INCs exactly where the FALSE arm's consumption does. The
checker therefore never decides from the trail; the handler watches do:

| gate | handler | TRUE watch | FALSE watch |
|------|---------|------------|-------------|
| 33 chkFlag | C0:2F5F | C0:2F8C | C0:2FA5 |
| 34 chkBit | C0:2FC1 | C0:2FE4 / C0:2FE8 | C0:2FEA |
| 45 chkMem | C0:2F22 | C0:2F3C (the BRA; 2F46 is the FALSE fall-through merge) | C0:2F3E |
| 0d 00 chk4 | 5A:B05E | 5A:B08B | 5A:B08F |
| 0d 01 chk01 | 5A:B09B | 5A:B0BE / 5A:B0C2 | 5A:B0C4 |
| 2F selGoto | C0:2E73 | dispatch C0:2E9C (`$8D`), inline C0:2E96 (`$78`) | — |
| 0d 16 jump16 | 5A:B980 | 5A:B989 (`$78` = target-1) | — |
| 0d 17 jumpL | 5A:B990 | 5A:B9A5 (A = target, bank in `$7A`) | — |
| 0d 18 callL | 5A:B9B0 | 5A:B9E9 (A = target-1, bank in `$7A`) | — |

49-family gates stay unwatched: the six sub-op handlers sit behind the
`$FE00` table (§4-5) and no headless-reachable event contains a 49 check.

### 12.3 Engine facts the harness pinned beyond parity

- **The end16 frame pop is exact.** 0BF1's frame (`end16 DFA0`, from
  `data/events/index.json`) pops at `FC:dfa0` — the dump's op stream
  continues into a `jumpL` + chkBit fragment the frame *never executes*
  (no GATE line at `45:1600` in any run; the jumpL TGT never fires in
  0BF1's segment). The event dumps include shared code past end16, so a
  VM that executes to the end of the dump over-runs the real frame.
- **0BF1 is dispatched from inside the callL subroutine.** The TGT CALLL
  at frame 10624 (target `72:91c0`, from `FC:0806`) precedes the 0BF1
  dispatch store at 10625: the bank-72 subroutine tail-dispatches 0BF1,
  and after 0BF1's fragment pops, execution resumes in the subroutine
  (gates `72:91c2`, `72:91ce`). `$D51B` then still reads `0BF1` while
  0800's own gate bodies run (`FC:0812`–`FC:08dc`, frames 10637–10692) —
  extending §10's "not restored on return" observation.
- **The linear event dump is not the runtime instruction stream.** The
  runtime skip `4e 05` at `FC:080b` lands on `FC:0812`, which the ROM
  executes as a gate (`33 31 aa`, GATE line at frame 10637) — while the
  dump decodes `00 33` (one call op) at `FC:0811` and never produces an
  op boundary at `0812`. The walker decodes linearly per block; runtime
  paths that cross a mid-op boundary are unrepresentable in the current
  event data (structural, §12.5).

### 12.4 Godot-side fixes (the first two found by the harness, the last two by wiring it)

All in `godot/event_vm.gd` / `godot/event_catalog.gd`; `--selftest`
output stays identical (verified against a scratch copy of the pre-change
tree: same 38-page smoke line; two assertions that encoded over-executed
shared code were corrected — see below).

1. **end16 frame pop** (the §12.3 finding): `EventVM` now pops the frame
   when the op at the frame's end16 address is reached
   (`catalog.end16()`, loaded from `exports/data/events_index.json` = the
   `data/events/index.json` copy). Before this, tail-dispatch chains
   over-ran into neighbouring fragments — the source of "godot-only"
   gates at `45:1600` / `FC:190d` in the first runs.
   - Selftest corrections: the +1500 gold grant lives in fragment 002F
     (`FA:12dc`/`FA:12e2`), not 0029 (whose frame pops at `FA:11e8` =
     002A's entry) — the assert now replays the 0029..002F fragment
     chain. 0B31 alone pays nothing: its +2000 reward (`FC:ca80`) lies
     past its end16 `c6d0`.
2. **Call-with-return for dispatch words** (`00-0C/0E`, `syscall`,
   `pad`; engine C0:B847, §2.8), behind `calls_enabled` (on in the
   parity harness only, so the interactive modes are unchanged): pushes
   a frame, loads the callee, resumes at the byte after the word.
3. **jump16 bank-relative targets**: the dump omits the bank when it
   equals the op's own bank (`016A`'s target `8ef0`); the VM now
   prefixes it instead of finishing the event.
4. **selGoto fallback wrap**: engine C0:2E7A computes `$D3C1 - 1` then
   `AND #$00FF` — a 0 option count wraps to 255; the VM used `-1`.

### 12.5 Result and coverage

Compare verdict (6 dispatch segments, 26 ROM gate decisions — 5 TRUE,
21 FALSE: 18 chkFlag, 8 chkMem):

```
segment 0800#1 id=0800 rom_gates=0  matched=0 rom_only=0 godot_only=0 rom_tgts=1 tgt_matched=1 OK
segment 0BF1#1 id=0BF1 rom_gates=18 matched=1 rom_only=17 godot_only=0 rom_tgts=0 tgt_matched=0 OK
segment 0846#1 id=0846 rom_gates=4  matched=4 rom_only=0 godot_only=0 rom_tgts=0 tgt_matched=0 OK
segment 0848#1 id=0848 rom_gates=0  matched=0 rom_only=0 godot_only=0 rom_tgts=0 tgt_matched=0 OK
segment 0849#1 id=0849 rom_gates=1  matched=1 rom_only=0 godot_only=0 rom_tgts=0 tgt_matched=0 OK
segment 084A#1 id=084A rom_gates=3  matched=3 rom_only=0 godot_only=0 rom_tgts=0 tgt_matched=0 OK
ALIGNMENT: 3/26 ROM gate addresses are not decoded gate ops in events.json
coverage: compared=9 matched=9 conflicts=0
PARITY PASS: 9 gate decisions and 9 dispatch targets agree
```

Every comparable decision agrees (0 conflicts); the checker exits 1 on
any conflict, and gate.sh runs it when the emulator and ROM are present
(SKIP otherwise). Family coverage over the reachable events:

| family | watched | exercised by the run |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| 33 chkFlag | yes | yes (25 of 33 decisions) |
| 34 chkBit | yes | yes |
| 45 chkMem | yes | yes |
| 0d 00 chk4 | yes | yes (0BF1) |
| 0d 01 chk01 | yes (watch installed) | no instance in the reachable set |
| 2F selGoto | yes | watch installed, but no selGoto executed in the opening run (the static selGoto occurrences in the chain dumps sit in code the runtime path did not reach — 0 TGT/SELGOTO lines in the whole capture) |
| 49 family | no (sub-ops behind `$FE00`, §4-5) | no: 0 occurrences in the whole opening chain (0800-085F, 0BF1, 0B31-0B5F); the 158 events with 49 checks are NPC-dialogue families not reachable headless without hand-navigation |
| 0d 16 jump16 | yes | no: 5 events ROM-wide (016A, 0153, 07CC, 07D7, 07D8), none reachable |
| 0d 17 jumpL | yes | yes (0BF1 → `45:1600`) |
| 0d 18 callL | yes | yes (0800 → `72:91c0`, target value compared) |

Known coverage gaps, all structural, all reported per segment by the
checker rather than failing:

- **Bank-72 subroutine bodies**: `72:91c0` and friends are not in the
  event catalog (only FA-FC entry events are dumped), so the 17 gates
  inside segment 0BF1 that are not 0BF1's own fragment (the subroutine's
  `72:91c2`/`72:91ce` gates and 0800's `FC:0812`-`FC:08dc` gate bodies)
  have no Godot counterpart; the 3 non-decoded ROM gate addresses in the
  ALIGNMENT line are `FC:0812` (§12.3) and the two bank-72 gates.
- **The undecoded runtime boundary `FC:0812`** (§12.3): stops Godot's
  0800 job right after the first skip, which is why no chain dispatches
  are reproduced inside the jobs (CHAIN-GAP lines) — each segment is
  compared against its own replay instead, which the checker reports.
- **callL/jumpL targets outside the catalog** (`72:91c0`, `45:1600`):
  compared by target value, execution not followed.

To widen coverage: fix the walker to decode runtime-accurate boundaries
(§12.3), export bank-72 subroutines into the catalog, and extend the
input schedule past frame 24000 (the run ends inside 084A; 084B-085F
continue the same chain). The checker, the harness, and the wiring need
no changes for any of these.

Roll-order diff (2026-11-21; battle_rng.gd `trace` records [lo, hi,
index]): the port's field path (game state's opening party, seed 21h,
`_compose_encounter` race 2 base 0, then the battle with plain attacks)
matches the engine's first 12 rolls exactly, ranges and indices
0210-0219 (the level terms' two no-advance roll(1, 0), roll(1, 8) twice,
the copies/companions roll(1, 15) x8). First divergence: the engine's
C2:1C58 roll at 021A, 1..(rec[23h] + 2 * rec[24h]) on the record at
($BA), through C2:0412, plus rec[30h] >> 1 (C2:0393), giving
`$4F` = max(0, `$83` - sum): a battle-start check not ported. The
routine (C2:1C26) takes `$83` = `$1308` & 0F and skips the roll when
`$1B` bit 6 or record byte 7 bit 7 is set. The bound 65 = 11h + 2 * 18h
fits only the last ally's record (slot 10, char 06; the others give 59,
50, 59, 53, 51, the enemy 37), so ($BA) is that ally's record here; why
that ally is open. Its consumer (a read watch on `$00:094F`: written 0
at C2:1C81, frame 45081; read at C2:5C84, frame 45639) is the enemy rank
loop C2:5C60: per enemy 2 * `$147E` + roll(1..`$147E`) + `$4F`, at least
3, through C2:5CFB into `$162B`,X (the opening battle: `$147E` = 22, the
1..22 roll). That loop closes the enemy decision chain C2:59F1-5CFB
(rolls 1..8, 1..0, 0..0, 0..3, 0..255, 1..22 at the enemy's turn), which
the port replaces with one pick among the unlocked techs: the next unit
to port. Correction (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md, decoded 2026-11-21): the
5C7B roll is the enemies' initiative (2 * agility + roll(1..agility) +
`$4F`), rolled after every enemy's decision chain, so the engine's round
is commands, allies' SP (C2:2588), enemy decisions, enemy initiative,
actions; the port rolls all SP before any enemy decides. After it the engine's
turn order rolls 5 times (1..20/13/14/16/14 at 02B6) where the port
rolls 7 (0..N at 0222), the next item. The capture (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md) shows why: five allies fight,
not six. Open: the allies' battle stats differ from allies.json (records
5-10 vs charstats FE:0600: e.g. ハリード 21 12 20 17 15 19 20 in the
record vs 19 14 21 15 16 18 19 exported, every member differs), because the
game adds two modifier rows when a character joins (C5:E8B3): the 宿星
row (FE:9649 + 8 * entry +40) and the 得意武器 row (5B:7B20 + 8 * entry
+42), signed-magnitude bytes; the hero slot reads `$F308`/`$F309`
instead. allies.json now carries these live stats
(charstats.LiveStats, tested against all six opening records). The
battle record is a block copy (FE:C8BC) of the WRAM record `$F000` +
0x80 * member, then battle agility drops by armour weight and moves by
the formation's speed level (C2:1182, C2:6586). The enemy decision chain and
both initiative loops are ported (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md "Port"); the
battle selftest matches the opening round's 11 rolls and outputs.
Since 2026-11-21 (later) the selftest replays every roll of the opening
battle after the battle-start check: the round (02B6-02C2), the enemy's
action (02EC-02EE), ハリード's spark walk and attack (02F2-0301), the
level bumps (0305-0315), growth (0336-0344, 0352-0354) and the spoils
and gold (0359-035B), with the waits between them; the field side pins
the composition rolls (0210-0219) and the check (021A). Open: the menu
waits depend on input timing (the selftest sets the index at each step),
and the battle's last 30 waits after the gold.


## 13. Opening-cutscene comparison (2026-11-21)

`exports/tests/cutscene_capture.lua` (ROM side) and
`exports/tests/cutscenecheck.gd` (port runner + comparer) compare the new
game's opening scene by scene. Schedule: §10's new-game presses, then A
every 16 frames from 11400 (the port: dialogue advance every 16 physics
ticks at `--fixed-fps 60`), to the first field control on 0250 (VM idle
from frame 18826; the capture stops at 19100). Fixture
`exports/tests/cutscene_opening.json` (positions, track ids, brightness,
screen and text-unit digests; no ROM bytes). Not in the gate: the port
diverges today, so the check exits 1.

```
rm -f /tmp/mesence_t007A/Saves/bokuno_jp.srm
/tmp/mesence_t007A/Mesen -testRunner exports/tests/cutscene_capture.lua patches/bokuno_jp.sfc -enableStdout --timeout=900 > rom.log
godot --headless --path godot -s tests/cutscenecheck.gd -- --record rom.log    # refresh the fixture
godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 --path godot -s tests/cutscenecheck.gd [-- --rom-log rom.log]
```

Facts the capture pinned:

- Dialogue text is not in `$D56D` (that buffer only holds inserted
  names); each glyph goes through FF:1F7C with the slot in `$8D/$8E`
  (`$8E` = 0 or the lead byte). A text unit = the slots between a 2C
  pause (C0:26C9) or a 2A window close (C0:217B) and the next; the
  port's unit = one PAUSE_MARK segment of a page. 0849's first page
  (FC:1852) closes after a timed `2b 40` with no 2C, which is why 2A
  counts. Known limit: a window that ends any other way, or two equal
  pages in a row on the port side (the runner sees label changes),
  would show as a text mismatch.

  172/164; screencheck 024B at (172, 165) = 50309/57344 exact, at (12,
  12) 4203.
- The ROM draws byte 50h as a blank cell (0846's `24 50 50 6A`,
  FC:152A); the exported event text drops it, so the comparer leaves
  slot 0 out of the digests.
- 0849 starts through the queue drain: the `$D51B` store at C0:1B53
  (frame 13134) returns to C0:B859, after the VM sat idle for 730
  frames (12405-13135) while the camera panned over 0249. The port

### Extension: 0250 from its load to the first battle (2026-11-21)

Same schedule (A every 16 frames, no direction). The first battle
comes at frame 19503 (song 1), not 45076: 45076 belongs to brolls4.lua's
schedule (no press from 10600 to 35000, then walking legs). The capture's
R/U rows still stop at 19100, so the gated scenes and their fixture rows
do not change. X lines go on to the first battle wait. The fixture's
`ext` holds 828 passes, the touch and the battle. cutscenecheck prints
the extension before the gated summary line (the gate's `grep -q` cuts
off output after it), under its own last line
(`cutscenecheck extension: ...`), and it does not change the exit status.
`-- --inject-rng` sets the port's `$0A/$0B` to the ROM's at the anchor.

Alignment is by logic pass from an anchor. On the ROM side the anchor is
the first pass with `$76` = 0 (p206, f18827). On the port side it is the
first tick on 0250 with no event and no arrival (t5664).

ROM facts the capture pinned:

- From frame 18000, through the 0250 load (18424) and events 0B4B/0B49,
  to the anchor, `$0A/$0B` stay 43/08. No C0:0733 roll and no write to
  `$0A` outside the roll happens in that span. The monsters (slots 1-10)
  hold until the VM is idle, while the event actors (slots 13-15) walk;
  the first roll runs one pass after the anchor.
- On 0250 the monsters spawn at speed row 0 with move pattern
  `$D9C5/$D9C6` = AA on slot 1 and 55 on slot 2 (dumped), so they move
  1 px every other pass. `$D9C6` is the working pattern: the walk
  continuations rotate it (C0:6B2B `LDA $D9C6,Y; LSR; ... STA $D9C6,Y`);
  `$D9C5` only keeps a copy. The spawn (C0:4A79, called per record from
  C0:3E7D) sets it at C0:4AD3-4B0C: C0:6876 loads FF:65C3[speed row],
  then it is rotated right `$D8 & 7` times, `$D8` counting the objects
  spawned before this one (STZ at C0:3E0A, INC at C0:4BF4); `$D9B7` =
  (`$D9` & 1F) + 1, `$D9` the record index (INC at C0:3E80, skipped
  records included). One rotation per slot against one pass of wait per
  record puts every slot on the same step passes. Ported in map_view.gd
  `_spawn_npcs`; main.gd's selftest pins the dumped AA/55.
- The touch: at C0:7797 slot 1's blocked step sets the latch `$D6B6`
  = 1 (C0:780D, p820, f19441, with slot 1 at (97,472) walking left).
  C0:5635 dispatches it 8 passes later (C0:AB2E arg 0, f19449), and the
  monster keeps walking to (89,472) meanwhile. The battle then seeds 15
  play-clock frames after the latch (clock 00:02:16.52 -> index 340,
  f19483). The contact inputs: leader facing 2, `$130A` = 3, `$130B/$130C`
  0, op 18, so `$37` = 4. Slot 1's `$D9A9` was 2 at the dispatch pass;
  3 equals the leader facing ^ 1, the fallback for a facing byte of 4 or
  more (docs/battle-enemy-ai.md). Which one applied is not traced. Encounter 62 gives one 地狼 (record +0 = 20h,
  74 HP), and the composition takes 11 rolls (340 -> 34B).
- The play clock is not a frame counter: it ticks once per field pass
  (622 ticks over passes 206-828) but only 7 times over the 34 frames
  from the dispatch to the seed. The port ticks it every physics frame.
- The screen digest `scr` differs between two captures on 77 of 360
  rows; every other field repeats exactly. It is not compared.

First divergences (`--inject-rng`, in pass order):

| check | ROM | port |
|---|---|---|
| play clock at the anchor | 00:02:06.23 | 00:01:55.28 (655 frames behind; UNVERIFIED cause: the cutscene's length, or the clock's pauses above) |
| seed after the latch | 15 play-clock frames (340) | 9 (330), UNVERIFIED cause: the clock's pauses above |

Page passes, ported 2026-11-21 (docs/vm-semantics.md §2.7.4): field
pages type a glyph a step and wait at each 2C for the press, and the
runner presses on 0250 on the pass the capture's press frame (a multiple
of 16) falls into, since a port tick is a pass and the ROM has pass-less
frames (the load, window closes, 3C). Every VM step on 0250 then lands
on the ROM's pass: the 4A page on p108-p148, the press at p152, 2A at
p153, 0B49 on p155-p170, `2b 10` on p172, the close-out in p205's step
(scratch trace against the probe's step lines). The anchor line prints
"204 ticks after" against 205 passes: the port's first 0250 pass runs in
the tick that switches the map, before the runner sees 0250, so its
count starts one pass later; the passes after it pair one to one.

Battle start (docs/field-monsters.md "Chase/bump trigger"): the port
latches the bump and dispatches it at the leader's next C0:5585. With
`--inject-rng` the RNG and every slot agree on all 623 passes from the
anchor to the latch, the latch agrees (slot 1 at anchor+614), the
dispatch comes 8 passes after it on both sides, the contact is 4 on both
(port object facing 3), and the composition agrees (enemy ids [32], 11
rolls). Only the seed differs, through the play clock (330 against 340).

Without injection the RNG differs from the anchor on (2D/01 against
43/08). The port then bumps slot 5 at anchor+677, against slot 1 at
anchor+614 on the ROM.

`docs/roadmap.md`:

```md
# Roadmap: bokuno RS3 → Godot with swappable translations

Goal: play the game in Godot in Traditional Chinese. Verification standard:
per-domain extraction byte-identical to the ROM; per-system behavioral
parity against the emulator. 2026-11-17 the user raised the bar: build a
full BYTE-MATCHING disassembly first (docs/decomp.md), then port against
that source — behavioral parity remains for the Godot port itself.

2026-11-23 the user evaluated Ebitengine (Go 2D engine) as a Godot
replacement and decided: after parity completes, migrate the port to
Ebitengine in ONE pass — until then Godot/GDScript stays the target and
parity work continues there. Measured facts behind the decision: the
game is 14,836 lines of GDScript (19 files) plus 5 check drivers with
21 fixtures, the Go side already carries 28,115 lines with reference
twins of the battle math (internal/battle) and the event VM
(internal/bokuno), and all 615 MB of game data are engine-neutral
exports. Ebiten constraints that shape the later migration: no UI
toolkit (hand-rolled) and no true headless — it always needs a window
system (Xvfb hidden-window rendering; PR #3908 closed). Migration
order when it starts: re-host the goldens as go tests first, then the
golden-pinned logic core, then the shell last.

## Font decision (settled by docs/font.md)

The ROM font is fully decoded (5 pages, 1261 glyphs verified). For
zh-TW dialogue the prototype uses the system Noto CJK font; the ROM
bitmap font covers Japanese only and has no TC glyphs. Options when
authenticity matters (menus, name entry): render zh-TW text with Noto
into bitmap tiles, or keep Noto TTF. Not blocking dialogue work.

  a dispatch target (vs 101 of 0400–04FF); the pointer entries lead into
  data regions. Translation permanently skips them.

# SFX: how bokuno triggers sound effects, and the exports/data/sfx rip

Status: mechanism verified by runtime trace (MesenCE 2.2.1 headless,
2026-11-16) and pinned by the SPC-side decode (same day, `cmd/spcdisasm`
on the rip-pipeline ARAM captures, section below). Battle catalog
