```md
## The request channel (verified at runtime)

Every sound request — BGM and effect sounds alike — travels as a 4-byte
message packet written to the S-CPU→SPC communication ports
`$2140-$2143`:

- Sender: zero-page packet routine ending at `C6:061B-0630`
  (writes `$2143`←`$03`, `$2142`←`$02`, `$2141`←`$01`, then `$2140`←`$00`
  as the go/ack byte, then polls `$2142`/`$2140` for the SPC echo with
  `LDX #$0400` timeout). A second copy of the same writer exists at
  `C6:0A66-0A75` (used for BGM play), plus bulk-transfer loops at
  `C6:0702/0708/070E` (sequence/sample upload, ~7917 writes each during a
  song change) and `C6:09AD` (the upload handshake, ~8010 `$2140` writes).
- Packet fields (SPC-side decode below settles all four; this list is
  the decoded reading, replacing the earlier "state-dependent" caveat):
  - `$2140` — the command byte, not a go/tag byte. The SPC dispatches on
    it (ranges below); the sound-carrying commands are `$18`-`$1F`.
  - `$2141` — sound id, confirmed by the SPC-side decode: the play
    handlers store it into the driver's current-sound cell (`MOV $BD,$8F`
    at ARAM `$0C0D`) and the sequence lookup keys on it.
  - `$2142` — argument to the sound (volume class: `FF` loud, `7F`/`40`
    softer; stored to `$4D` at `$0C10`).
  - `$2143` — sound class / task gate (`04` effect class, `07` song
    class, `05` battle variants; the tail at `$0C16` compares its low
    nibble against the running class in `$81` and resets the task on a
    switch).

Evidence lines (`tools/emulator/sfx_trace.lua`, input timeline of
trace_events.lua; raw stdout, `CMD` = write to `$2140-$2143` with PC):

```
CMD frame=10750 port=2143 val=07 at C6:0A66   <- BGM play packet begins
CMD frame=10750 port=2142 val=FF at C6:0A6B
CMD frame=10750 port=2141 val=29 at C6:0A70   <- song id 0x29 = 41
CMD frame=10750 port=2140 val=10 at C6:0A75   <- go byte
<7917 x 3 upload writes, frames 10750-10779>  <- sequence+samples to ARAM
CMD frame=10787 port=2141 val=00 ... val=07 at C6:0630   <- track 0 = stop

CMD frame=7000 port=2143 val=04 at C6:061B    <- menu sound packet begins
CMD frame=7000 port=2142 val=FF at C6:0620
CMD frame=7000 port=2141 val=01 at C6:0625    <- id 0x01, tag F2 = task control, not a sound
CMD frame=7000 port=2140 val=F2 at C6:0630
```

The `$2141`-field-as-id claim rests on the song-id correlation above and
the stop packet; the class split (`04` vs `07`) on the observed catalog
below. SPC-side decode would pin both (later slice).

## Catalog observed (new game flow, frames 300-10787)

Distinct message packets (`$2141`/`$2142`/`$2143`), sent from the
`C6:0630` sender (BGM play from its `C6:0A75` copy); frames from the
scripted boot → new game → opening cutscene run
(`tools/emulator/sfx_trace.lua`):

| `$2141` | `$2142` | `$2143` | tag | count | observed at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01` | `FF` | `04` | `F2` | 1 | first A press (7000, gender select) |
| `01` | `7F` | `04` | `F2` | 9 | every later A press / START confirm |
| `10` | `7F` | `04` | `18` | 5 | confirm blip following `01` |
| `06` | `7F` | `04` | `18` | 5 | second confirm variant |
| `10` | `00` | `04` | `80` | 1 | cutscene start (10716) |
| `29` | `FF` | `07` | `10` | 1 | BGM play: song 41 (10750) |
| `00` | `FF` | `07` | `80` | 2 | BGM stop / silence (10787) |

So the UI sound packets carry `$2141` = `01` (on every confirm),
`10`, `06` (the secondary blip, varying with the dialog answered);
BGM play carries the 92-entry track id. The SPC-side decode below
settles the field question: the id is `$2141` for effects exactly as
for BGM; the `F2`/`18` tag pair is two different commands, not an
alternative id carrier.

Pacing caveat discovered while capturing: both the BGM-muted runs and
the from-scratch watcher scripts ran on a shifted timeline (~3900
frames early), so fixed-frame input schedules miss the menus. Reruns of
the same script are exact (sfx2 ≡ sfx3, dump3 ≡ dump4 on every packet
line), so the effect is deterministic per script — the safe pattern is
the one the final PoC uses: build on the verified sfx_trace.lua
skeleton and keep its exact callback set.

Not yet cataloged: field and scene sounds outside the opening chain;
the battle slice below covers the opening scenario's battles.

## SPC-side decode (2026-11-16): the request grammar

The SPC700 program is resident in ARAM in every rip-pipeline capture
(`tools/emulator/spc_build.py` dumps carry the full 64 KiB; the driver
occupies roughly `$0200-$2000` with sound data above). Disassembled with
`cmd/spcdisasm` (this repo; opcode table generated from the Mesen 2
`Spc.Instructions.cpp` case dispatch the harness emulator runs, byte
counts cross-checked against fullsnes.txt on 184 opcodes). All offsets
below are ARAM addresses read from a run10 battle capture
(`beep_PRE.spc`); the driver code is identical across every capture
checked.

### Receive path

```
$089C  poll $F4; tag $00 -> drop; two equal reads = stable
       tag $01-$0F            -> enqueue (4 bytes at $F16C+X, index $D8, wraps $40)
       tag $10-$17            -> drop here; the transfer task claims it ($1103)
       tag $18+               -> enqueue
$08DD  dequeue into dp cells  $8E=tag $8F=id $90=a2 $91=a3, CALL $0BB6 per packet
```

### Command dispatch ($0BB6)

`X = tag`. `BPL` on the tag's bit 7 splits the table below; `AND A,#$0F`,
`ASL` builds the index `Y = (tag & $0F) * 2`.

| tag range | behavior | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `$80-$8F`, `$E0-$FF` | driver control: dispatch `($17C1 + (tag & $1F) * 2)` | `$0BB9 BPL`, `$0BC3 JMP $0EDB`, `$0EDB CMP X,#$F0 / CMP X,#$90` |
| `$90-$EF` | ignored (these tags are the bulk-transfer byte stream) | `$0EE1 BCS -> RET` |
| `$01-$0F` | queued + echoed, no action (CPU-side ping) | `$0BCA CMP X,#$10 / BCC $0BEF` (echo path `$0BEF` writes all four ports back) |
| `$10-$17` | transfer channel; echo first (`$0D06`), then the `$1781` handler | `$0BD2`-`$0BE2` four pushes; `RET` lands in `$17A1[Y]` = `$0D06` |
| `$18-$1F` | immediate sound command: handler = word at `$1781[Y]` | `$0BE3 CMP X,#$20 / BCS $0BEF`, `$0BE7`-`$0BEE` |
| `$20+` | consumed + echoed, no action | `$0BE5 BCS $0BEF` |

The echo at `$0D06` writes id to `$F5` and tag to `$F4` — the echo the
S-CPU sender polls for at `C6:0624`.

### The `$1781` sound-command table (16 words, indexed by tag low nibble)

The dispatch is `word[$1781 + (tag & $0F) * 2]`, and the two tag halves
are different commands — the first decode of this table mapped tags
`10`/`18`, `11`/`19` onto the same handlers, which is wrong. The
byte-level dispatch turns on `$0BD0`'s `CMP X,#$18`: tags `$10`-`$17`
push TWO return addresses
(`$0BD2`-`$0BE2`) — the `$17A1[Y]` handler (all eight words are `$0D06`,
the port echo) runs first, then the `$1781[Y]` play handler — while tags
`$18`-`$1F` push only the `$1781[Y]` handler (`$0BE7`-`$0BEE`) and echo
inline through `$F5`/`$F4` (`$0BEF`).

| tag | handler | behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `10` | `$0BFB` after echo | BGM play: bank `$BA=$10`, shared tail |
| `11` | `$0C03` after echo | BGM play: bank `$BA=$20`, tail |
| `12`/`13` | `$0BFB`/`$0C03` after echo | same plays, second voice class |
| `14`/`15` | `$0BF8`/`$0C00` after echo | reload sample region (`$14E6` copies `$F200-$F2FF` to `$F800`) + play |
| `16`/`17` | `$0BF8`/`$0C00` after echo | same reloads, second voice class |
| `18`/`19` | `$0DA3`/`$0DAB` | effect: per-voice sequence pointers from ARAM `$3100 + id*4` (voice pair 4/3) |
| `1A`/`1B` | `$0DB3`/`$0DBB` | same effect machinery (voice pair 2/1) |
| `1C`/`1D` | `$0E67`/`$0E6B` | sample-reload variants (undecoded) |
| `1E`/`1F` | `$1421` | undecoded |

So the effects (tag `18`/`19`, a3=4/5 class) never touch the tail or the
slot cells: `$0DA3` builds `$94/$95 = $3100 + id*4` (`$0DC9 MOV $94,$8F`,
two ASL/ROL, `+$3100`) and reads two 16-bit per-voice sequence pointers
(`$0DE4`-`$0DED`, into `$02+X`/`$03+X`) — the shared per-id sequence
table the uploads maintain.

The `10`-`17` tail at `$0C06`: DSP `$5C` (KOF) ← `$FF` (all voices
off), `$BD ← $8F` (**the sound id**, `$0C0D`), `$4D ← $90` (**the a2
argument**), class check, then voice setup through the `$0797` DSP-write
helper — and the slot check at `$0C24`: `Y = $F164`; `BEQ $0C4D` skips
it while the slot is cleared (`$F164` = 0, the battle-time state in
every capture — the game sends `tag 80, id 00` at battle start). The
lookup computes `word[$F160] + Y * word[$F168]` (`$0C2A`-`$0C42`, two
`MUL YA` 8x8) with **the slot value, not the play id**, and uses it only
as a validity probe: a zero high byte clears `$F164`/`$F161`
(`$0C45`-`$0C4A` = disarm). The player tick at `$15B8`-`$15D5` keeps
that product invariant (decrement `$F164`, add `$F168/$F169` to
`$F160/$F161`), so the probed address is the END of the armed region:
`$F160/$F161` = region base (the packet's a2 is its high byte),
`$F164` = block count (the packet id), `$F168/$F169` = per-block stride
(`$0F38` derives it from consecutive base highs: `(new - old) << 8 /
id`). The play id never enters this computation.

### Driver-control table `$17C1` (32 words, indexed `(tag & $1F) * 2`)

Key entries: index 0 (tags `$80`/`A0`/`C0`/`E0`) → `$0EF1`: bank/sound-set
select — one packet updates BOTH slot pairs (`$0EF7` path = slot 0, then
`JMP $0F05` = slot 2), writing the packet id into `$F164+X` (id `00`
clears the slot = silence); the game follows it with the ~7917-byte
sequence/sample upload. Index 18 (tags `92`/`D2`/`F2`) → `$0FFB`: task
control — `$0FFB` bit-tests the packet id and enables/disables driver
tasks (`$86`/`$87` flag cells); **no sound**. Index 14 (tags `8E`) →
`$1F8E`: BGM fade control — id `00` clears the fade flag, any other id
arms fade counters (`$E2`/`$E4`, ×$40 step at `$1FAD`): the battle-start
packet is a music fade, not a discrete effect. Slot cells (writer
`$0EF1`-`$0F35`): `$F160+X/$F161+X` = region base (packet a2 = high
byte), `$F164+X` = block count (packet id), `$F168+X/$F169+X` =
per-block stride — `X = 0` → song slot `$F160/$F164/$F168`, `X = 2` →
effect slot `$F162/$F166/$F16A` (twin tick at `$15EE`).

### Runtime slot state (2026-11-16, `tools/emulator/sfx3_bankcell.lua`)

The one UNVERIFIED piece — the play lookup `word[$F160] + track *
word[$F168]` guarded by `$F164 != 0` — is settled by the static decode
above plus a fresh capture that logs the slot cells and the `$3100`
entries two frames after each play packet:

```
BGM frame=147  id=48(72)  bd=48 f160=FF00 f164=00 stride=0000 t=366C/367D
BGM frame=6879 id=2B(43)  bd=2B f160=0000 f164=00 stride=F010 t=0000/0000
BGM frame=9559 id=2B(43)  bd=2B f160=FF00 f164=00 stride=0000 t=A137/AD37
```

(ids hex; `t` = the two words at ARAM `$3100 + id*4`.) The title song
plays repeatedly with the slot UNARMED (`$F164 = 00`) — the play does
not depend on the armed region at all — and its `$3100` entry goes from
zeros to real sequence pointers (`$37A1/$37AD`) exactly across the
sound-set upload, confirming `$3100 + id*4` as the per-id sequence
pointer table the player starts from. The slot cells are the region
bookkeeping of the `$10`-`$17` tail only. The first decode's reading —
"when a bank is armed the tail computes the sequence entry address
word[$F160] + id * word[$F168]" — was wrong on both halves: the
multiplier is the slot value (not the id) and the result is a validity
probe (region end), not the played address.

(The captures are attract-flow only: this script is built from scratch,
not on the sfx_trace skeleton, and its timeline shifted — title song at
6879, the unattended timing — so the fixed-frame PRESSES missed the
menus and the new game never started. Per the dead-ends section that is
the known from-scratch hazard; the slot question does not need the game
flow, so the captures stand.)

### Answers this pins

- **The id field is `$2141`** (SPC `$F5`) for effects and songs alike —
  stored to `$BD` at `$0C0D` (`$10`-`$17` tail) / `$94` (`$0DA3` effects)
  and consumed by the sequence/voice setup, never by the slot lookup. The
  `F2`/`18` tag pair is two commands: `F2` = task control (no sound),
  `18` = the real play command.
- **Tags are commands, not go bytes.** The opening-catalog reading
  ("UI-sound sender always tags `F2`/`18`") was wrong: each packet
  carries exactly one command tag.
- **`$2142` is the volume-class argument** (`FF` loud blips, `7F`
  confirms, `40`/`64` hit variants), `$2143` the sound class gating the
  play task.
- **Victory jingle** travels as BGM play (`tag 10`, id `03`) through the
  same `$1781` table — one dispatch path for songs and jingles; effects
  use `tag 18/19`.

## Battle slice (2026-11-16): reach a battle, catalog, rip

Harness: `tools/emulator/battle_sfx.lua` (catalog + screenshots) and
`tools/emulator/battle_sfx_rip.lua` (adds per-effect SPC dumps and the
tech navigation). Both keep the byte-verified sfx_trace.lua callback
skeleton; input is oam_walk.lua's walk13 policy (opening PRESSES through
10600; from frame 20800 A every 30 frames while busy, walk program when
idle). Runs are deterministic — every landmark reproduces exactly.

### Opening landmarks (frames, run8/run10)

```
BGM 10750 id=41  opening movie (dispatches through the same BGM channel)

```
### Rip procedure (what produced exports/data/sfx/)

1. Run `tools/emulator/battle_sfx_rip.lua` (MesenCE headless via
   `tools/emulator/run.sh <script> --timeout=3000` — the test runner
   kills the emu after `--timeout` seconds, default 100, and exits 255 =
   stop code -1; the first "crashes" investigated here were exactly
   this). The script watches the packet sender; on each distinct id
   (a3=4 class) it dumps PRE (at the `$2141` write), POST (+1 frame)
   and LATE (+30); the victory jingle is keyed on the song dispatch
   (`detect_bgm` id 3) with POST at +55, after the play packet's
   sequence/sample upload; then it stops at victory+200.
2. Split + build + render: `tools/emulator/rip_build.py <log>
   <dir>` (per DUMP block → `tools/emulator/spc_build.py` →
   `ffmpeg -t 3` libgme → libvorbis q5). 26 dumps from run10 all built
   and rendered.
3. Variant pick per effect: the PoC's discriminator — 4-8 kHz band mean
   of the first 0.6 s (highpass 2k+4k, volumedetect). Evidence:
   beep POST +5.9 dB over PRE, victory POST +3.7 dB over PRE, hit_a
   POST +4.7 dB full-band (max −0.9 dB vs −8.6).
4. Assemble: `tools/emulator/assemble_catalog.py <log> <dumpdir>
   <mapping.json> exports/data/sfx` re-renders the
   winning variant with a 0.4 s tail fade into
   `exports/data/sfx/<tag>_<name>.ogg` and writes catalog.json.

All captures carry the battle BGM under the effect (battle music plays
through every capture; only the victory jingle's own request stops it).
The game plays these effects over its own BGM anyway, so the residue is
masked in use; an ear-check per effect is still the standing gate
(music.md Milestone 1 rule).
```

```
## Enemy-act ids 6C/38: sequence decode and attribution (2026-11-17)

Closes the "ear attribution of two enemy-act ids" roadmap item. The
captures are the field slice's `e38_*` / `e6C_*` dumps
(`/tmp/sfx2-agent/field_dumps/`, POST = one frame after the packet).
The SPC700 cannot be listened to, so the attribution rests on the
decoded sequence structure plus the render contrast; anything a decoder
cannot settle is marked UNVERIFIED.

Method. The per-id effect sequences live at ARAM `$3100 + id*4` (two
16-bit pointers, the voice pair of the tag-18 handler `$0DA3`). They
decode under the RS3/AKAO vcmd grammar: the driver's vcmd length table
at ARAM `$16CD` is byte-identical to loveemu's `RS3_VCMD_LEN_TABLE`
(github.com/loveemu/spc_converters_legacy, akaospc), and the vcmd
handler table sits at `$1655` (vcmd `$C4` first byte) — both read
directly from the capture. The akaospc Rev4 parser then converts each
sequence cleanly: rebuild the song header at ARAM `$2200` as
`[base=$2224][end][8 track pointers]` with the wanted sequence pointer
as track 0 and an `EB` byte (Rev4 end-of-track) as the filler
tracks, and run `akaospc fake.spc out.mid out.html`. Decoded streams:

id `38` (voice pair `$38FE` / `$3914`) — the file
`exports/data/sfx/18_enemy_act_b.ogg`:

- voice A: volume 0 fading to max (`C4 00` + `C5 2B 7F` volume fade),
  instrument patch `$16`, echo on (`D4`), then a loop of 6 pitch slides
  (`E2 05` … `E3`): each iteration plays `C8 17 F4` (slide, speed 23,
  key −12 semitones) on one 16-len note and transposes down a 4th
  (`DA FB`, −5 semitones) — C6 → G5 → D5 → A4 → E4 → B3.
- voice B: same swell, pitch-mod on (`D2`), a very deep tremolo
  (delay 0, rate 5, depth 207 — `CB 00 05 CF`), 6 slides descending by
  a minor 3rd each (`DA FD`) — C6 → A5 → F#5 → D#5 → C5 → A4.

So the effect swells in while the pitch sweeps down over and over,
each sweep lower than the last, with heavy amplitude and pitch
modulation. That is a descending, pulsing roar — structurally a
monster's attack cry (the dive/bite kind), not a UI or hit blip.
Context: battle 3, frame 35384 (+964 after the battle BGM started),
the loudest new render of the slice (PRE → POST +8.4 dB mean, max
−0.1 dB). Attribution: enemy roar / falling sweep cascade.
UNVERIFIED (no literal listening; structural decode + render
contrast only).

id `6C` (voice pair `$3F49` / `$3F56`) — the file
`exports/data/sfx/18_enemy_act_a.ogg`:

- voice A: instrument patch `$03`, one 48-len note with a −5-semitone
  slide (speed 48), then a long 96-len tie sliding down 29 semitones
  (speed 72) — a falling sweep.
- voice B: pitch-mod on, octave 3, one 96-len note from C2 sliding UP
  41 semitones (speed 96) — a fast rising sweep.

Two opposed glissandi crossing each other: a swoosh with a rising edge
against a falling edge. Context: battle 3, frame 35193 (+773), quiet
render (PRE → POST +1.7 dB mean, max −7.2 dB). Attribution: enemy
swipe/swoosh (crossed rise/fall sweep). UNVERIFIED (same caveat).

Whether each id belongs to a specific enemy species of battle 3 or to
the shared enemy-act sound set is still open — the run log carries no
enemy id. The catalog keeps the file names `18_enemy_act_a.ogg` (6C) /
`18_enemy_act_b.ogg` (38): the attribution is structural, not aural,
so the files are not renamed after sound descriptions.
```

```
## Rip approach decision

Options:

| approach | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| A. SPC capture per effect mid-play → libgme render (the BGM pipeline) | **recommended** | pipeline already proven end to end (bgmrip: dump → spc_build → ffmpeg libgme → OGG); captures exactly what the driver plays, including SFX-specific sample banks |
| B. record the APU output segment per effect | rejected | unavailable in the harness: `-testRunner` initializes with `noAudio=true` (TestRunner.cs `InitializeEmu(..., true, true, true, true)`), and the Lua API has no audio-sample accessor (function table checked in MesenCE 2.2.1 source). It would need GUI + xvfb + audio device runs outside the headless design |

Evidence that SFX cannot be ripped by the BGM batch route (forced
dispatch per id): music.md's rip found 7 track-table entries that render
silently under forced dispatch (0x33, 0x3B, 0x40, 0x44, 0x4F, 0x57 —
kaerulabo labels them wind/moans/rumble class). Effect sounds are keyed
by their request packet, not by track dispatch, so the rip must trigger
them in real gameplay: run the game (scripted inputs or a user
savestate), watch the packet sender, and on each UI-sound packet dump
the SPC700 state a frame later, while the effect is still sounding.

The SPC decode (above) explains the silent overlays without an
in-game trigger hunt: a song plays as a two-step flow — first a
driver-control packet (`tag 80`, sound-set id in `$2141`) selects the
bank by writing it into the slot config `$F164` (`$0EF1`/`$0F05`), the
game uploads that bank's sequence+sample block (~7917 writes), then a
`tag 10` packet with the track id plays the sequence at
`word[$F160] + track * word[$F168]` in the **loaded bank** (the lookup
runs only while `$F164` ≠ 0). The batch rip sent only the `tag 10` play
packet against whatever bank was resident at the title screen; ids
`33`/`3B`/`40`/`44`/`4F`/`57` have no sequence in that bank, so libgme
renders silence. Their triggers are the scene-entry `tag 80` packets —
every song change in the battle logs is preceded by one (`MSG
frame=21206 tag=80 id=10 a2=0 a3=7` → song 36 at 21239; same pattern at
24343/28343). Ripping them needs a scripted walk that enters their
scenes so the `tag 80` bank load fires first.

(2026-11-17 correction of the last paragraph's conclusion: the two-step
arm is real for scene BGM changes, but the batch rip's silence for the
six overlay ids was NOT a missing bank — their dumps carry the uploaded
sequence and keyed voices, and the silence was libgme's render of the
dumped echo setup. The full evidence and the rip fix live in
docs/music.md § "The six silent overlays"; those tracks ship as OGG
now.)

PoC (2026-11-16): the three-dump capture — PRE inside the beep packet,
POST one frame after the tag write, LATE 45 frames later — verifies the
mechanics end to end (result lines below). Two dead ends are on record:

- Muting BGM by hijacking every dispatch to track `0x00` changes game
  pacing: the flow auto-plays to the cutscene ~3900 frames early and no
  menu beep ever fires (two runs, both `SFXDUMP-NO-BEEP`).
- Watcher scripts built from scratch (rather than on the verified
  sfx_trace.lua) also ran on a shifted timeline — packets at frames
  6846/6912 instead of 10716/10787, no beep at the scripted A press —
  although every callback in them is passive (reads and cpu-state
  queries only), and reruns of the same script are byte-identical
  (two sfx_trace runs and two from-scratch runs each matched every
  packet line). Mechanism
  unresolved. The working PoC therefore adds the dump machinery to the
  byte-identical sfx_trace.lua skeleton (`tools/emulator/sfx_dump.lua`)
  and stops immediately after the last dump, where pacing no longer
  matters.

Harness scripts this section rests on: `tools/emulator/sfx_trace.lua`
(catalog watcher), `tools/emulator/sfx_dump.lua` (PoC dump),
`tools/emulator/battle_sfx.lua` / `battle_sfx_rip.lua` (battle slice),
`tools/emulator/sfx2_field2.lua` (field/scene slice: the run6 input
policy verbatim, catch-all rip of every unripped sound id, map-id
logging — a first take built on the repo `battle_sfx_rip.lua` policy
diverged after battle 1 and missed battles 2-3, so the field slice
clones the run6 producer's policy instead),
`tools/emulator/watch_probe.lua` (watch-form probe, see
docs/parity.md §11), and `cmd/spcdisasm` (SPC700 disassembler for the
ARAM decode above).

Result (`tools/emulator/sfx_dump.lua`, run 2026-11-16; title BGM still
playing, so all three dumps carry it):

```
PRE-TRIGGER frame=7000
MSG frame=7000 tag=F2 id=01 a2=255 a3=4
MSG frame=7000 tag=18 id=10 a2=127 a3=4
RIPINFO target=PRE  hijack_frame=7000 dump_frame=7000 spcpc=02D5
RIPINFO target=POST hijack_frame=7001 dump_frame=7001 spcpc=0330
RIPINFO target=LATE hijack_frame=7045 dump_frame=7045 spcpc=0BA1
SFX5-DONE frames=7045
```

All three dumps build through `spc_build.py` and render non-silently
through libgme (`ffmpeg -i X.spc -t 2`). First-0.6 s octave-band energy
of the renders: POST carries +5.2 dB at 2-4 kHz and +9.2 dB at 4-8 kHz
over PRE, with low bands quieter; LATE is back at PRE levels. The
effect's spectrum appears exactly between the packet and packet+45 —
the beep is in the captured SPC state and survives the libgme render.
(Instant-voice evidence such as DSP `$4C` (KON) is useless here: the
driver writes KON/KOF transiently and it reads `00` at any dump
instant.)

Pipeline of the later slice:

1. run with the packet watcher (same as this PoC), dump `.spc` at
   packet+1 frame per effect id;
2. assemble with `spc_build.py` / `bgmrip`'s Go builder (unchanged);
3. render via `ffmpeg -t 2` (effects are short; the render has no loop
   point to cap around), silence-trim, `libvorbis -q:a 5` into
   `exports/data/sfx/`;
4. catalog.json keyed by the observed packet payload (effect id once
   the SPC-side decode settles which field carries it).

Open risks: BGM contamination (a dump while BGM plays mixes the two;
the PoC quantifies the effect spectrally but the shipped OGG should come
from captures at quiet moments, or the residual BGM is masked by the
game's own playback anyway — decide per effect by ear), resume
transients (the first ~0.3 s of a libgme render from a mid-play
snapshot differs from continuous playback — trim or crossfade the head
per effect), and effects whose SFX sample bank is only uploaded with a
BGM change (re-verify per id). Ear-check of each captured effect is a
standing gate, same as music.md Milestone 1.
```

```md
## Graphic ID table (file `5A8370`)

One 4-byte entry per character graphic ID: `kind[1]` + `offset[3]`
(3-byte little-endian SNES address; `000000` = absent). The community
BNE2 config (`sfc_RS3改造関連/ぼくの(略用)/BNE2/RS3拡張_キャラグラオフセット.ini`)
declares exactly this: base `5A8370`, stride 4, 1020 entries — the pool
of character graphics the RS3主人公追加パッチ ecosystem edits, and the
same `拡張キャラオフセット` struct documented in the RS3主人公追加パッチ
`Struct.def追記用.txt` (`BYTE 種類(0x00仲間、0x01一般住人); BYTE
オフセット[3]`; "カラーパレットはキャラグラフィックに1対1で対応する").

Kind bytes observed, named by `オフセット種類.idn`:

| kind | meaning |
|---|---|
| `00` | 仲間: party-member sprite set (map sprite + battle graphics) |
| `01` | 一般住人: townsfolk walking sprite |
| `1C` | ユニークキャラ: unique character walking sprite |
| `2D` | 一枚絵(3x4): single 3x4-tile picture |

The `.idn` also names every ID (00 ユリアン, 01 エレン, … 97 ボクトツ,
…). Verified pointers: ID 0x96 -> file `1E8800`, ID 0x97 -> file
`1E9080` (both white-bearded old men — the decoded sprites show exactly
that), ID 0xA0 (ユリアン) -> `1A1C60`, ID 0xB5 (アルベルト) -> `528AC0`.
IDs 0x00-0x0F are zeroed in the bokuno table: the party members' map
sprites are resolved by the original game code elsewhere (open question,
below).

## Palette pool (file `5A03F0` = table − 1020×32)

One 32-byte palette (16 BGR555 words, layout as in docs/map-format.md)
per table entry, palette for graphic ID i at `5A03F0 + i*32`. Evidence:
the region directly before the table is full of 32-byte BGR555 blocks
whose word 1 is white/near-white, matching the documented RS3 character
palette convention (簡易マニュアル: `00:背景, 01:白, 02:黒, 06～08:肌`).
Rendered with this mapping, IDs 0x96/0x97/0x2F produce plausible colors
(white beard + dark robe for ボクトツ). Probable but not byte-verified
against the game; see open questions.

## Tile format

Raw, uncompressed SNES 4bpp tiles (32 bytes each): rows 0-7 interleave
(plane0, plane1) per row in bytes 0-15, then (plane2, plane3) in bytes
16-31; bit 7 = leftmost pixel. Same interleave the verified chipset
decoder uses (docs/map-format.md). Verified by content: the blobs
contain exact-duplicate tiles and exact mirror-image tile pairs at
row-slot positions, and decode to coherent chibi figures.

## Frame layout (filmstrip, verified; per-band offsets open)

A townsfolk blob is 0x880 bytes = 68 tiles = a **24-px-wide vertical
filmstrip**: 22 bands of 24x8 pixels (three tiles each, left to right)
plus two trailing tiles. `sprites.Frames` slices it into seven 24x24
blocks of three bands each (stride nine tiles, tiles 9k..9k+8); tiles
63..67 are the trailing 16x16 object graphic (金塊グラフィック layout),
not a frame (`sprites.ObjectTile`).

Verified by content, independent of any layout guess:

- The blob is not 16-px frames. Every candidate that slices it into
  16-px-wide frames (the implemented 16x24 interleave, contiguous
  16x32 blocks, column-major variants) produces fragmented figures;
  scoring torso similarity over all 8-frame layouts confirms none of
  them (best identical-row fraction 0.006 over all frame pairs).
- 24-px bands are real. Assembling tiles 0,1,2 as one 24x8 band and
  tiles 3,4,5 as the next renders a complete head + face for every
  townsfolk blob checked (0x96, 0x80, 0x97): hair centered, brim tips
  flanking it, face with eyes below, all centered in the 24-px width.
- The community GIF format agrees. The artist sheets shipped with
  RS3主人公追加パッチ (`RS3キャラドット`) and the `マップ配置用ドット`
  WSCSaGa/敵キャラドット sheets are 176x133 with separator marks every
  25 px: cells of 24x32 content. RS3 map sprites are drawn on a 24-px
  wide canvas, wider than one SNES sprite pair, which only works if
  the game composites more than two 16x16 sprites per figure.
- Tile identity classes repeat at fixed offsets across every townsfolk
  blob, confirming one shared layout: +7 (tile t == t+7), +8, +9
  (sometimes chains t, t+9, t+18), +19, +21. E.g. blob 0x80: tiles
  4==11, 6==14, 24==31, 41==50==59, 42==51==60, 43==61, 44==53; blob
  0x6A has a 13-tile identical run (all-empty head-top positions).

What stays open: the game composites the visible sprite from these
bands with per-band X offsets (the figures lean diagonally; identical
content reappears one or two bands lower, shifted a tile right, e.g.
0x80 face-bottom at band 1 px 6..17 and band 3 px 13..23). Those
offsets live in the upload/compositing code path, not in the blob, so
`Frames` output shows each 24x24 block unshifted: the top bands of a
block line up, lower bands of one figure continue in the next block.
See the OAM/VRAM capture section below for what an in-game capture
established about the mechanism.

## OAM/VRAM capture (2026-11-16, MesenCE headless, opening scene)

`tools/emulator/oam_capture.lua` boots the ROM headless, plays through
to new game (input schedule in docs/parity.md M1 log), and dumps OAM
(544 bytes), CGRAM and full VRAM as base64 on stdout at a chosen frame;
`tools/emulator/oam_decode.py` reassembles them. Capture at frame 20000
(village after the opening dialogue starts, party + NPCs on screen):

- **The composed figure is OAM strips.** Visible characters are drawn
  as vertical strips of SNES sprites stepping 8 px per entry
  (y = 100, 108, 116, …), each strip 16 px wide, with the strip's
  tiles in VRAM at a stride of 16 tiles (0x10, i.e. 512 B) per step.
  Left and right halves of one figure are separate strips whose X
  offsets differ by 16 px (x=106 and x=122 in the dump); left halves
  carry the H-flip bit (attr 0x40). Palette bits in the attribute byte
  distinguish characters on screen at the same time.
- **None of the on-screen sprite tiles come from the 5A8370 blob
  table.** Every OAM-referenced VRAM tile was compared against all
  1020 table graphics three ways — byte-exact 32-byte tiles,
  pixel-exact tiles under both SNES 4bpp decodings (row-interleaved
  and grouped-plane), and sliding 8-px windows over every 24-px band
  with H-flips — zero matches; a whole-ROM byte search for the VRAM
  tile bytes also found nothing. Two conclusions: the graphics on the
  opening scene are the original RS3 map sprites (the 5A8370 table is
  the RS3拡張キャラグラ table for the patch's ADDED characters, as the
  community docs say — original NPCs and party members do not use
  it), and **the per-band X offsets are applied when the game uploads
  the bands into VRAM**: the composed tiles exist in VRAM only, not in
  ROM, so the band shift is baked into the sprite VRAM at load time
  and OAM then places strips of it. For the Godot port the same
  compositing must be reproduced at texture-upload time, not via OAM
  positions alone.
- Consequence for the Godot port: the filmstrip layout above stays the
  verified decode for blob-backed (added) characters, but resolving
  band→OAM offsets for them needs a capture on a map where a placed
  character uses a blob-backed graphic ID (block-2 IDs from
  docs/triggers.md). The opening village reached headless has none.

## Runtime graphic-table resolution (2026-11-16, disassembly, byte-verified)

The capture above left the important question open — who consults
5A8370, and for which characters. The answer is in the resolver the
harness runs past every frame (hand-disassembled from
`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`; raw bytes quoted in the capture notes):

- **C4:FF60 (offset right, bank CORRECTED 2026-11-17: the old "4F" never parses under the file mapping — the hand-disassembled machine code lives in bank C4; the signature `BF 70 83 5A` is at C4:FF88) is the walking-character graphic resolver.** With X =
  engine graphic id × 4 (`AND #$00FF; ASL; ASL; TAX`), it branches on
  `CPX #$01C0`: ids ≥ **0x70** read the patch table
  (`BF 70 83 5A` = `LDA $5A8370,X`, stride 4, engine id = community
  table id directly); ids < 0x70 jump to C4:3EB0, which reads the
  **original RS3 table at SNES $F9A000** (file `0x39A000`, same 4-byte
  entry layout). Both paths load {kind, pointer word, pointer bank}
  the same way and converge on the shared upload code (JMP C4:3F07) —
  **the strip composition is engine-level and identical for vanilla
  and blob graphics**; the resolver only swaps the source pointer.
- The original table encodes its pointers split: SNES address =
  `((byte1 & 0x1F) + 0xDA) << 16 | (word(byte1,byte2) & 0xFFE0)`
  (`AND #$FFE0` on the 16-bit load, `AND #$001F; ADC #$DA` on the
  8-bit reload, C4:3EE0-3F06). Verified by content: $F9A000 id 01
  decodes to a coherent 68-tile townsfolk filmstrip at file
  `0x1A1C60` — the same address the 5A8370 table's kind-00 entry A0
  points at — and the ids of map 0x246's placed townsfolk (1E-25)
  decode with the filmstrip tile-identity signature (duplicate tile
  pairs: 1E→4, 1F→4, 20→11, 24→5, 25→10).
- The kind byte gates a source adjustment that is part of the same
  computation (`+0x2A0` for kind 01 一般住人, `+0x3C0` for other
  kinds, applied to the `$02:$00 = $C4C977 + id*32` pointer); that
  region's role is still open (it is populated, but reads as all
  `0xFFFF` words at the offsets this computation produces).
- **Which placed characters render from 5A8370 blobs:** exactly those
  whose block-2 graphic-id byte is ≥ 0x70 with a non-zero entry
  (797 of 3616 NPC placements over all decoded maps,
  `go run ./cmd/probeblobs patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`). Examples: the
  Pidona old-town map 0x02/0x03 has one at (17,50), g=FE; the Pidona
  pub 0x05 has five (g=C1/CC/CD/D6/FF). The opening village (map
  0x249, jump-table entry 5 of event 0846 → spawn (16,16)) has one
  placed character, g=61 at (36,52) — **below the 0x70 threshold**, so
  it renders from $F9A000 (kind 05), and the opening-scene characters
  (party members, ids 00-07) have empty 5A8370 entries resolved by
  other code. That is the precise reason the frame-20000 capture has
  zero blob matches — not evidence that the engine ignores the table.
- **OBSEL is 00 at runtime** (dumped in the walk captures:
  `CAPSTATE … OBSEL=00`), so sprite tiles address VRAM from
  0x0000 — the name-base ambiguity is closed; OAM tile numbers index
  VRAM directly.
- The 5A8370 entries below 0x70 (runs 1E-71, non-zero) are not read
  by this resolver; a second consumer exists (the `LDA $5A8370; RTL`
  stub at 5A:A793) but its caller is untraced — open question.

### Capture tooling (this task)

- `tools/emulator/oam_walk.lua` — timeline harness: boots to new game,
  drives the opening event chain and walks the player (policy history
  and the lessons per run are in the file header); dumps OAM every
  2000 frames, OAM+CGRAM (full 512 B, sprite half included)+VRAM and a
  PNG screenshot every 4000 frames from 34000. Run with
  `tools/emulator/run.sh tools/emulator/oam_walk.lua -timeout=1500`
  (the `-timeout` is mandatory: the testRunner default is ~100 s and
  kills longer runs — walk1-walk4 all died at exactly ~100 s).
- `tools/emulator/oam_reassemble.py` — reassembles the dump log
  (handles both `STATE` and `CAPSTATE` frame lines; `oam_decode.py`
  misattributes dumps made after the last `CAPSTATE`).
- `tools/emulator/shot_ascii.py` — renders a reassembled screenshot
  dump as ASCII (stdlib-only PNG decode).
- `cmd/oamanalyze` — the decoder: parses OAM, composites the visible
  sprites onto a 256×224 canvas with flips applied, and slides every
  blob band's 16-px windows over every screen position (exact match;
  `matchorig` mode matches the $F9A000 blobs, `relax` tolerates
  foreign-sprite overlap on band index 0). Usage:
  `oamanalyze patches/bokuno_jp.sfc <dumpdir> <frame> match [vram_base]`.
- `cmd/probeblobs` — cross-references every placed NPC's graphic id
  with the resolver semantics (who renders from 5A8370 blobs, on which
  maps).

### Still open after this task

- The per-band X offsets are still unpinned. The composed figure is
  16 px wide (two 8-px strips), so the engine uploads a 16-px window
  of each 24-px band row at a per-band offset; the exact offsets need
  a capture where a blob-backed townsfolk (kind 01, engine id ≥ 0x70)
  stands on screen — the nearest candidates are story-gated (Pidona
  0x02/0x03/0x05; map 0x1DE's exit (5,9) → 0x03 is the only entrance
  to the old town). walk13 (the current oam_walk.lua policy) does clear
  the chain and walks the opening village — the frame-34000 screenshot
  shows two figures side by side in a village street (the player and,
  by position, the g=61 NPC) — but that NPC is kind 05
  ($F9A000, not a townsfolk blob) and the party leader renders from the
  unresolved third path, so the capture still has no band source. What
  remains is walking one of the story-gated maps' g≥0x70 townsfolk into
  view (or injecting a savestate there once one exists). Snapshot also
  catches OAM mid-update (single frames show figure strips fragmented;
  the same character reconstructs differently across frames), so
  captures should be validated against a screenshot before use.
- The 0x70-threshold's second consumer (5A:A793 stub) and the
  $C4C977 region's role (see above).

### Field walk-figure pipeline (2026-11-17, six headless runs)

`tools/emulator/sp_walk.lua`, `sp_probe.lua`, `sp_dma.lua`,
`sp_shadow.lua`, `sp_stage.lua`, `sp_pose.lua` replay the verified
intro timeline (byte-exact across runs 1/2/5/6/7: same battle frames
29444/31520, same final wedge position (136,496)) and capture the free
walk on map 0x250 (camera window tile (2,36), `dumpmaps compare` 100%,
trimmed distance 9.3). Established, every claim executed against
MesenCE headless:

- **The field walking figure has NO pose cycle.** Per-frame
  screenshots across the two verified walk legs (down 35933-35965,
  right 36780-36819, leader 1 px/frame) show the figure graphic
  constant modulo the ±1 px draw rounding: the position-tracked crop
  residual between consecutive walk frames is 249-403 quantized
  pixels (a 1 px shift of the 16-px-wide figure) and identical-hash
  standing frames are exactly 0. The figure graphic changes only with
  FACING: the post-down-walk stand and the post-right-walk stand
  produce different constant figures, and the right-walk frame shows
  the right-facing one. The "walk cycle" of the field path is
  therefore one composed figure per direction moved at 1 px/frame
  (8 frames per tile); the Kani memo's 上下左の歩行グラフィック is
  one walking figure per direction, not cycle frames.
- **Frame-end OAM never contains the party on the road maps.** The
  OAM shadow at WRAM `$7E:AD00` (544 bytes) is byte-identical to the
  frame-end OAM (`emu.read(snesSpriteRam)` from the startFrame
  callback; verified byte-for-byte at two instants), and it carries
  only the small wandering actors (e.g. one 8-px-wide, 3-strip actor
  with VRAM tiles 12/28/44 stepping 1 px/frame) plus parked
  entries. The DMA register state (startFrame reads of `$430x`) lists
  two channels targeting `$2104` (ch0 source `$7E:2220`, ch6 source
  `$7E:AF20`; possibly stale config) — either way the party's strips
  do not survive to frame end. In the intro's pocket scene the
  persistent OAM (figures at `$7E:AD00`) is what the montage
  captures saw.
- **`emu.read(snesVideoRam)` does not return the rendered VRAM.**
  Neither the leader figure's tiles, nor the on-screen BG tree tiles,
  nor any filmstrip band window (1-px sliding, both flips, both tile
  byte orders) match any of the 1024 dumped VRAM tiles, while the
  same tiles obviously render (screenshots). VRAM dumps are
  scene-dependent but not render-truthful; sprite/figure VRAM
  analysis through this API is void. The only VRAM-side facts that
  survive: OBSEL (`$2101`) reads 00, and one 2-tile region
  (`$4540`, tiles 558/559) cycles three change signatures every
  12 frames — decoded through all 16 BG palettes it is a mottled
  grass chip (terrain animation), not the figure.
- **The staged figure at WRAM `$7E6E00` (DMA ch7 source) is static**
  across the whole walk (identical tile bytes at 35920 and 36634+)
  and does not reproduce the on-screen figure under either candidate
  tile layout — not the pose carrier either. A composed 16x24 figure
  assembles coherently from it under a 16-tile (512 B) row stride,
  matching the OAM strip stride of the cutscene path, but it cannot
  be matched to any 5A8370/`$F9A000` blob band window (the party
  renders from the unresolved third source).
- **Actor-array cells (WRAM, byte-verified).** The leader's live
  pixel position is `$D9AA/$D9AC` (updates every frame while
  walking, 1 px/frame). Per-actor counter blocks sit at
  `$DA60 + i*0x40`: field +0x02 is a mod-16 down-counter ticking
  every frame, field +0x24 a mod-8 down-counter ticking every 2
  frames (16-frame period), field +0x08 (word) the `k*256-1`
  quantized cells already retracted as positions in
  docs/map-format.md. None of them gates the field figure (no pose
  cycle exists to drive); their consumer is the cutscene/OAM path.
- Consequence for the Godot port: the field walk needs ONE composed
  figure per facing (down/up/left, right = mirrored or separate) plus
  1 px/frame stepping — no cycle table. The band compositing question
  (per-band X offsets) stays open only for blob-backed graphics and
  still needs a blob-backed capture (story-gated maps above).

### Journey toward the blob capture (2026-11-16, second session)

Scripted-input sessions past walk13's opening-village park. Verified
facts (every claim executed against MesenCE headless; raw log lines in
the session's /tmp/pidoam-agent):

- **Current-map cell: WRAM `$7E:2011/2012`, high byte first.** A WRAM
  scan at the forest free-walk found exactly two cells holding `0249` /
  `0246` (`MAPHIT 2011 word=0249`, `MAPHIT 3586 word=0246`); `$7E:2011`
  stayed `0249` for all 38 STATE lines of a 70000-frame forest walk. In
  cutscene contexts the same cell reads scratch values (`8101`, `061D`,
  `007D`), and after some intro handoffs it reads `0000` — so it is a
  field indicator only, not reliable inside events.
- **Protagonist select rows** (down-presses between the gender confirm
  at frame 7000 and the character confirm at 7800): row 0 = ユリアン
  (event chain 0846→0848→0849→084A→084B→084C→0B49), row 2 = ミカエル
  (chain 0844→0849→0845→0852→0858→085A→0B3B→085B, then the common 0846
  chain; event 0845's text is the camp-gate scene
  「様がいらっしゃいました！よし、通せ。」). Rows 1 and 3 replay the
  0846 common chain. Row 1's first run matched row 0's event ids frame
  for frame, so the row-1 down-press may not have registered.
- **Mikael's route is unusable headless.** His start field reads map id
  `0000`, whose submap record the patch zeroed (dumptriggers:
  `map 0x0000: skipped (submap record is zeroed at 380C00)`) — the
  render shows a field with no placed characters and walking never
  leaves it. The bokuno FAQ independently warns that Mikael gets stuck
  around ロアーヌ (「ミカエルが分身する、時期によってはロアーヌから
  二度と出られなくなる」), so this is a known hack bug, not a harness
  one.
- **Input-policy rules (each verified by a broken run).** (1) The
  intro's dialog syscalls wait for A with `$76 == 0` — an A-only-while-
  busy policy stalls inside Mikael's 0852 (`PC parked at FC:2DD0 =
  syscall 0b37`), and unconditional periodic A breaks through
  (`0B3B → 085B → 0846`). (2) But pressing B to close a "ring menu"
  (D3C0-guard) skips cutscene text and derails the handoff: with the
  guard, every protagonist landed in a hidden state — the field scene
  renders with no player sprite in OAM and walking does nothing. (3)
  Starting the A-mash at frame 12000 instead of 20800 compresses the
  dialog pacing and breaks the field handoff the same way. The only
  policy that reaches the visible free-walk field is walk13's exact
  one: presses only at 20800+, A while busy, held direction while
  idle.
- **The player figure renders only after the down leg.** walk13's
  down/right program shows two figures from frame 34000; every up/right
  variant keeps the village-spawn scene playerless. The spawn (16,16)
  is indoors; the street door is below.
- **Map 0x249 (シノンの森) has no record-level exit** — identical bytes
  in the patched and the original ROM (dumptriggers -map on
  `Romancing Sa-Ga 3 (Japan) (Rev 1).sfc`): no exits, no event points,
  `edge: [0 0 0 0]`, NPC g=61 (kind 05 馬) at (36,52). The forest exit
  and the ガルダウィング battle are VM position checks inside the intro
  event chain, not map-record data. The per-tile walkable grid (after
  the header fix below) says row y=16 is walkable the full 64 tiles
  east from spawn; blind walking never triggered the battle in three
  programs × 100000+ frames each: up/right one-shot, up/right then
  hold-east, and walk13's down/right cycled for 100000 frames (all
  stayed `MAP=0249`, `D51B=0B49`, `$76=00` to the last frame). The exit
  tile/trigger coordinates are hardcoded in the intro event chain and
  are still unknown — a position-cell read or a savestate from a real
  playthrough are the remaining ways in (position-cell hunts with
  byte-pair and 16-bit word differential scans over all 128 KiB WRAM
  both came up empty; see the tooling list).
- **`mapfmt.ReadHeader` parsed bit-5/6 headers wrong (fixed).** Layer 2
  was read unconditionally (present only when flag1 bit6 is set) and
  the two undocumented bytes after the palette-set byte (flag1 bit5)
  were skipped nowhere, desyncing every bit5-set header: map 0x249 read
  object config 225 (out of range) instead of 0x26 and size 32x32
  instead of 64x57. ReadHeader now follows the byte-verified walk in
  `internal/triggers`; map 0x249 decodes to the 2-658 CSV values
  (chip 0x26, palette 0x30, object 0x26, 64x57, NameID 80), renders,
  and `mapfmt.Walkable` returns a corrected grid.
- **Blob-NPC inventory near the intro** (probeblobs + dumptriggers):
  宿営地 outdoor 0x24F has g=E1 (kind 00) at (70,29) plus the eight
  protagonist sprites g=00..06 at (72..82,24..30), all ev=2000; ロアーヌ
  city 0x4B has g=C2 at (23,66), (37,51), (23,39) with real events, and
  g=CC/FC/BD/C4/C9; palace rooms 0x25B (g=FE at (12,14) and (12,16)),
  0x25D/0x25E/0x25F (g=C2 ×3 at (13,39), ev=2000). All are kind 00 —
  the engine-level strip composition is identical, but the kind-01
  townsfolk blobs (g=84 ×3 on 0x1DE, g=84 on 0x1DF/0x1E4) sit deep in
  the world and need the post-prologue freedom.
- **Per-protagonist branch consequences**: only Harid's forest-exit
  branch enters the 宿営地 (bokuno wiki オープニング page:
  「ハリードは宿営地へ。他の主人公は…ポドールイへの道へ」), and every
  forest starter must first survive the exit battle. Which select row is
  ハリード (1 or 3) is still undetermined — both replay the common 0846
  chain up to the park.

Journey tooling added this session (all in tools/emulator/):
pidoam_journey.lua (WRAM map-id scan + walk13 policy), pidoam_select.lua
(character-select screen probe), pidoam_journey2.lua and
pidoam_journey3.lua (protagonist-branch harnesses; journey3 is the
walk13-timing one), pidoam_posfind.lua / pidoam_posfind2.lua (failed
position-cell hunts: byte-pair and 16-bit word-pair differential scans
found no party-position WRAM cell — the survivor `$7E:0074` = (128,1)
turned out to be the `$76` frame-flag/call-depth pair, not a position).
cmd/ holds reversegraph (reverse map-graph), pathfind (BFS on the
walkable grid), proppoints, mapheader, and dumptriggers -map (record
dumps against either ROM).

### Journey toward the blob capture (2026-11-16, third session)

Post-prologue sweeping on the north road (map 0x250, the first map the
walk13 program reaches with `$D2E3=02`, its object config) with full
OAM/CGRAM/VRAM/screenshot captures every 2000 frames
(`tools/emulator/water_sweep.lua`; captures in the session's
/tmp/journey2-agent/sweep_out). Findings:

- **No blob sighting.** `oamanalyze match` and `matchorig` (3822
  5A8370 bands, 2352 $F9A000 bands) find zero band hits on all 15 sweep
  captures. The figures on screen render from other sources, consistent
  with the opening-scene capture analysis above.
- **RESOLVED (main session, 2026-11-17): the "NPC parse disagreement"
  was a hex/decimal misread, not a bug.** The exported catalog stores
  graphic ids as DECIMAL integers (the map_view contract: "decimal
  graphic-table id"); map 0x250's entries are graphic 76 = 0x4C and
  84 = 0x54 — both below 0x70, i.e. NOT blob graphics. probeblobs was
  correct all along: 0x250 has no blob townsfolk. (Verified by
  replicating probeblobs' exact slot/override logic against
  triggers.Decode(0x250): 10 NPCs, graphics 0x4C x5 / 0x54 x5, slot
  offsets -1.) The blob maps from probeblobs' hex output (e.g. 0x24F
  g=E1, 0x4B g=C2, 0x25B g=FE, 0x2D5 g=84) remain the true list.
  Duplicate catalog coordinates on 0x249 (several identical entries)
  are a separate, real open question — duplicates cannot all be
  standing on screen; likely inherit-flag artifacts in the block-2
  walk, unverified.
- **Movement input needs ~900-frame holds.** Direction holds of 20 and
  120 frames produced no WRAM movement at all (pos_hunt3/4); walk13's
  900-frame legs do (pos_hunt5: member-x cells move −256 px on a west
  leg and return on the east leg, and formation partners swap values —
  `$7E:DBA8`/`$7E:DBE8`, `$7E:DBF4`/`$7E:DBB4`, candidates for member
  position/scroll, with the live leader cell and the Y cells still
  unpinned). This hold threshold is why several earlier harnesses
  "froze": their short holds never started a walk.
- **The intro's story gate fires on walking up/left out of the park**
  and hangs a harness without the A-while-busy policy (pos_hunt4);
  with the policy the legs run clean (pos_hunt5). The gate is the VM
  position check sprites.md's second session describes, not map data.
- **Emulator-API blockers for state injection** (2026-11-16,
  state probes): `emu.createSavestate()` is refused in -testRunner
  ("must be called inside an exec memory operation callback" for
  `emu.loadSavestate`), `emu.write` is a no-op (parity.md section 11),
  and `emu.loadSavestate(...)` — tried with the base64 of a crafted
  .mss and with its file path, in an exec callback on the main loop at
  C0:6E1A — completes without error but loads nothing (the WRAM is
  unchanged after the call). `emu.getState()` returns the serializer
  key space minus the big memories (WRAM/VRAM/OAM/CGRAM). A crafted
  .mss (template key layout + captured memories + VM-hijack bytes,
  assembled by a Python script in the session's /tmp/journey2-agent) is
  therefore verified byte-correct but not loadable by any API this
  build exposes headless. Remaining in-game route to the Pidona old
  town: the story chain (map 0x250's north edge event 084E jumps to
  the 宿営地 0x24E, then ロアーヌ 0x4B per jump table), a multi-map
  scripted journey with story battles, still unopened.
- Session tooling (tools/emulator/): pos_hunt.lua (position-cell hunt,
  four designs documented in-file), pos_y.lua (north-west zigzag with
  cell tracking), journey_teleport.lua (full-state dumper: WRAM/VRAM/
  OAM/CGRAM plus the emu.getState() table), water_sweep.lua (north-road
  sweep with captures). Session-only artifacts (research ROM with the
  2-byte submap-table patch, crafted .mss, capture logs and analysis
  scripts) live in /tmp/journey2-agent.

### Chain-walk session (2026-11-17): toward the 084E north-edge event

`tools/emulator/chain_probe.lua` / `chain_walk.lua` / `chain_capture.lua`
(the chain harnesses; raw logs in the session's /tmp/chain-agent,
walk1-walk8) pushed the scripted walk toward 0x250's north edge, where
`EdgeEvents[0] = 084E` lives (dumptriggers -map; 084E chains its battle, then
mapJump 11 0C -> camp 0x24E (31,21), later 11 0E -> Loane 0x4B (31,77)
— Loane holds the g=C2 blob townsfolk at (23,66)/(37,51)/(23,39), the
blob-capture target). Established, all on the plain patched ROM:

- **walk13's end state is deterministic and mid-map.** Every run boots
  to the same state at frame 35200 (DBA8=767 DBE8=511, MAP cell 0249,
  $D2E3=02). `dumpmaps compare` pins every post-battle screenshot to
  map 0x250's render window (52,15/16), 94-95% tiles under threshold —
  the party stands around tile (60±8, 22±7) of 0x250, not in the west
  pocket the earlier sessions assumed.
- **The scripted battle sequence on the road is deterministic** (frames
  37660/40284/43102/46787 on the west-leg input script; six battles won
  headless in one round each by the battle_sfx A-mash policy). Battle
  results hold busy stretches that mimic story events — see the
  correction in docs/map-format.md.
- **The DBA8/DBE8 "member-x cells" are walk-animation phase counters,
  not positions** — the docs correction in map-format.md has the cell
  evidence; the party-position hunt restarts from zero with per-leg
  screenshots + `dumpmaps compare` as the only working position
  instrument.
- **The left/up walk program is a dead pocket, and so is everything
  else**: walk7's 12+ west and 10+ up 900-frame legs produced 16
  byte-identical render windows; walk8/9's down/right and walk11's
  84-leg serpentine (450-frame holds, 6 across + 1 down, 7 rows, settle
  A-taps with B menu recovery) swept the same screen-sized arena with
  all 42 screenshots pinned to the identical (52,16) window. The scene
  at 0x250 (60±8, 22±7) is a LOCKED-CAMERA cutscene arena: the camera
  never pans, the party moves only inside the screen (the diff-mask of
  two shots shows moving sprite blobs over a static background), no
  dialog window is waiting for A ($76==0 throughout, A taps in the
  settle windows found nothing), no battle fires on this path
  (walk8-11 are battle-free where the west-leg script hit four), and
  the ring menu never opens (D3C0=0). The intro story at this point
  waits on something that scripted input cannot provide — the same
  wall the earlier sessions hit at the park exit, now one map further
  on and measured properly.
- **Harness API facts** (each paid for with a dead run): Lua locals
  must be defined before the functions that read them
  (`shotdump` before `wr` errored every frame as "call a nil value");
  `print`-based dump bodies must feed b64encode a numeric table, not
  `string.char` results (arithmetic on strings aborts the callback
  silently — probe1 lost all WRAM bodies to this); Mesen headless is
  run-to-run deterministic on the same input script (walk2/3 replayed
  battle frames 37660/40284/43102 exactly); the mesen `--timeout` is
  the real run budget — an outer `timeout 590` wrapper kills runs
  mid-story (walk3 died at its fourth battle).
- **Input-policy state machine that reached the arena** (chain_walk.lua
  final form): A every 30 while busy or within 600 frames of the last
  busy frame or in battle (battle via the SPC BGM dispatch, port1
  captured on the raw $2141 write, pc C6:0A75); B every 60 while the
  ring menu is open ($D3C0) outside cutscenes; held direction legs
  otherwise; A taps every 100 frames in the settle window between
  holds so a native A-window cannot freeze the scene silently. The
  walk8 lesson generalizes: unconditional A on an idle field opens the
  ring menu and the menu swallows all direction input (walk7 froze
  29000 frames this way — its OAM snapshots show the menu border
  pattern).
- **The chain harnesses are ready for the event**: `eventSeen` (long
  busy away from battles, or a busy map load) switches to unconditional
  A every 30 frames — the chain's native windows wait for A with
  $76==0 (walk7/walk12 lesson) — and the battle policy (BGM dispatch
  via the C6:0A75 writer, port1 captured on the raw $2141 write) wins
  the 084E battles. `chain_capture.lua` adds the Loane approach legs
  (spawn (31,77): up ~660 frames, left ~480) and dense
  OAM/CGRAM/VRAM/screenshot captures for the band->OAM pin, plus
  per-leg WRAM dumps for the Loane position-cell diff.

### Walk-figure export for the Godot map view (2026-11-17)

The Godot map view draws real walk figures from
`exports/data/walk_sprites/` (gitignored, like all ROM-derived data):
`leader/<facing>.png` for the party leader and `<decimal graphic id>/<facing>.png`
for NPCs, each a 16x24 RGBA PNG, transparent background, facing one of
down/up/left/right. The party leader resolves by role, not by graphic
id: the engine's party-figure source is a third path (docs above), so
its ROM-side id is unknown. NPC facing data is not decoded; the view
loads `down` for NPCs. The right-facing figure is the horizontal mirror
of the left-facing one (Kani memo's 上下左: townsfolk store down, up,
left; right is mirrored), and the exported left.png is that mirror.

The figures cannot come from the decoders in this repo: the figure is
composed only at render time — never present in ROM, and VRAM dumps
through MesenCE's `emu.read(snesVideoRam)` are not render-truthful on
the field path (established above). The export therefore cuts the
figures from PNG screenshots, diffed against a second screenshot at a
different party position so every static background pixel (including
the color-math tree shadows the map render does not model) cancels:

1. `tools/emulator/run.sh tools/emulator/walkfig.lua -timeout=1200`
   boots to new game with walk13's verified policy, walks the 0x250
   street with retry-queue legs (battle-resilient; the road battles
   freely) and dumps a PNG screenshot every 100 frames inside each
   standing window.
2. `python3 -I tools/emulator/oam_reassemble.py <log> <dumpdir>` splits
   the log into `cap_<frame>_shot.bin` PNGs.
3. `go run ./cmd/dumpsprites pair <dumpdir> <outdir>
   exports/data/maps/0250/map.png <frameA>:<frameB>:<name>` aligns both
   frames to the map render, diffs A against B in map coordinates, and
   exports figure-sized components. `<name>` of the form
   `facing,x,y,w,h` instead cuts one explicit 16x24 rect with
   background transparency — the final step, once the leader's screen
   rect is known.
4. The PNGs are installed as `exports/data/walk_sprites/leader/<facing>.png`.

Captured so far: all four leader facings (the 0x250 street scene at
scroll (12,284); down from walkfig's 36100 window against 54200, right
from 34100 against 49400, up from 44000 against 54200, left = mirrored
right). Two known blemishes, both occlusions on screen: the right
figure's left edge lost its leftmost columns to a wandering actor drawn
over the party, and a few wolf-edge pixels ride the down figure's left
edge. A re-run with different wander positions can replace them.

Not exported: NPC figures. Map 0x249's only NPC (g=61, the horse) sits
behind the intro's story gate in map space (the party cannot walk back
north to its screen area), and no blob- or original-table character was
on screen during the captures. The Godot side falls back to a white
tile per NPC and picks up `<gid>/down.png` exports automatically once a
capture exists.

### NPC figure export, first two gids (2026-11-18)

`exports/data/walk_sprites/99/down.png` (16x24, the blonde party girl —
the intro actor standing at map 0x249 (16,63)) and
`exports/data/walk_sprites/97/down.png` (24x32, the horse) are cut from
walknpc/walknpc2 screenshots with `/tmp/alphacut` (uncommitted scratch
probe; alpha rule mirrors `alphaRect`). Verified 2026-11-18 in the
Godot map_view (xlab.sh, retired with the engine 2026-11-23): the girl
rendered at (16,63) and the horse at (36,52), no white tiles. The same
boots today are the shell's xvfb one-shots (`scripts/shell-smoke.sh` is
the pattern):

    go build -o /tmp/saga3 ./cmd/saga3
    xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 800x600x24" /tmp/saga3 \
        --map 0249 16 57 --frames 30 --press right:10:25 \
        --screenshot /tmp/saga3-0249a.png
    xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 800x600x24" /tmp/saga3 \
        --map 0249 36 46 --frames 30 --screenshot /tmp/saga3-0249b.png

Each prints `SHELL-SHOT path=… mean=…` (verified 2026-11-24: mean=40,
512x448, both runs). In today's shell the girl's tile sits outside
0249's 64x57 bounds (`cmd/dumptriggers <rom> -map 0249`), off the
clamped camera, and (36,52) shows the grey marker fallback rather than
the horse — a live divergence from the 2026-11-18 view, not yet chased.
`97` is the party's dismounted MOUNT from frame 23800, not the placed
(36,52) NPC itself (that one never comes on screen; the mount is the
same horse graphic).

Capture runs: `tools/emulator/walknpc.lua` and `walknpc2.lua`
(`run.sh ... -timeout=1500`), the walkfig timeline with screenshots
every 100 frames from 20800; walknpc2's STATE lines add the party tile
(reads `$B910/$B911`, proven by dupnpc_249) and the map-id cell
`$2011/$2012`. Runtime map-id truth from walknpc2: the intro montage
maps are 0x249 (fp 26/00/40) → **pub 0x007D** (fp 07/00/20, party
parked at (26,49) through the cutscene) → street 0x250 (fp 02/00/60).
Map 0x249's 13 stacked NPC entries at (16,63) are the intro story
actors on the party's own spawn tile — graphic 99 is what the story
scene shows there. The pub's placed townsfolk are g=83 (x4) and g=85
(x2), and the street's are g=76/g=84 (x5 each) — still unexported: the
pub cutscene actors are static, so the pair-diff has nothing moving,
and the render-diff fails because the in-game pub carries a lighting
overlay the map render does not model (screen-vs-render diff keeps
40%+ of the background). Both go white in the port until a capture
exists; the wiring now picks exports up automatically.

Two tooling facts worth keeping:

- `dumpsprites align`/`shotfig` scrolled-alignment was silently broken:
  it compared the 16 px/tile screenshot against the 8 px/tile map render
  1:1 (both sides even downsampled to mismatched scales). The leader
  export never noticed because pair mode only uses the scroll delta
  between two same-scale screenshots, which cancels the error.
  `loadMapRender` now upscales the render 2x nearest-neighbour, but the
  SAD itself still cannot find the true offset on tinted scenes (night
  forest, lit pub) — visual blend calibration against the render, or
  the party-tile anchor from walknpc2's STATE lines, are the working
  methods. `/tmp/alphacut` also cuts against another screenshot at a
  scroll delta (`-b`) and against bare luma (`-luma`) for bright
  figures on dark scenes.
- The NPC white-tile fallback in `godot/map_view.gd` never loaded any
  export: the caller passed `"res://...<gid>/down"` (full path) into
  `_figure_image`, which joins `FIGURE_DIR` again — the path never
  existed, so every NPC drew the marker regardless of exports. Fixed
  2026-11-18 by passing the bare gid subdirectory.

## Where the sheet comes from

`cmd/dumpsprites` renders IDs 0x96 (ジーン・ムーア), 0x97 (ボクトツ),
0x2F (クラックス), 0x80 (ルートヴィッヒ), 0x62 (ヤン), 0x6A (ウィリアム),
0x54 (ハンニバル), 0x32 (ゾンビのトミー) — all kind `01` entries. Each
`char<id>.png` shows the seven 24x24 blocks, one per row, with grid
lines on the band boundaries, over a magenta background. Verification:
programmatic pixel checks (every sheet has 24k-37k sprite pixels;
0x96 block 0 band 0 has 944 head pixels in its 5..19 x 2..7 window)
plus the ASCII renders quoted in the analysis. A previous decoder
(`DecodeWalkFrames`, 16x24 interleaved) was removed: it produced
fragmented figures (see Frame layout).

## VRAM and OAM are truthful after all (2026-11-21, map 0233)

The "VRAM dumps are not render-truthful" conclusion above was wrong: it
came from comparing tiles in the wrong planar layout (MesenCE's
`snesVideoRam` returns SNES bytes: planes 0/1 interleaved for 8 rows,
then planes 2/3). Read correctly, BG chip graphics equal the chipset
decode byte for byte (docs/map-format.md), and sprites rebuild from OAM:

- OBSEL is not 00: `emu.getState()` gives `ppu.oamBaseAddress` = 24576
  (word 6000h, byte C000h), `ppu.oamAddressOffset` = 4096 (second name
  table +1000h words), `ppu.oamMode` = 1 (8x8 small, 32x32 large).
  The `$2101` register capture saw no write in the probe window.
- With those, the frame-end OAM (`snesSpriteRam`, 544 bytes) rendered
  from the dumped VRAM and CGRAM 128-255 reproduces every character on
  a 0233 screenshot (leader and four sailors; 382/1256 px equal, the
  rest a 1 px placement or BG occlusion not yet checked).
- Each field figure is one 32x32 sprite plus three 8x8 sprites below
  (24x32 drawn, the top 8 rows blank), tiles laid out 16 per VRAM row.
- All 39 non-blank sprite tiles are raw in the ROM (banks DA/DE): the
  sailors' (map graphic 67) are blob 50 tiles 38-49 of the 5A8370 table
  as three-wide rows; the leader's are blob 160 tiles 64-66 and more.
  Blob 50 tiles 38-49 form a clean frame; the 12-tile runs starting at
  2, 14, 26 and 50 do not, so each frame is a tile list chosen by the
  upload path, not a contiguous run.

The tile lists are in the ROM (done 2026-11-21).

- Cells: the NMI DMA list at 1400h (6-byte entries, FF:01B0) is filled
  by FF:2B40 from a cell list FF:2AEC picks: the actor's sprite set
  ($D99B = E1:kind*4) lists, per facing ($D9A9), the frame entries
  for the walk cycle ($D9A4); an entry is a cell-list pointer (bit 15
  adds 0x80 to the tiles) and an OAM layout pointer. The list is
  (rows << 4 | width), then one blob tile per cell (FE blank, FF
  none); cell (row r, column c) goes to VRAM tile r*16 + c.
- Layout (E1:layout): a count, then per piece x, y (signed 16-bit,
  from the object), tile, attribute (bit 0 32x32 else 8x8, 40h
  H-flip, 80h V-flip). Standing frames put the 32x32 piece at
  (-8, -33), walking frames one line lower; right-facing entries reuse
  the left cell lists with a flipped layout at x - 16; frame 3 is often
  frame 1 flipped; wide kinds use two 32x32 pieces.
- Blob and palette (C0:7B3F, 5A:A770/A786/A797): $EFF7 picks the
  table. 5A:BFA8 sets it FF for the leader slot with a graphic >= 70h,
  and for any other slot whose event's high byte ($D9D2) is 0C or 4C;
  FF selects 5A:8370 (kind, 24-bit blob address) with palettes at
  5A:8770 + 32 * gid (C4:FFDB). Otherwise F9:A000 (kind, blob = bank
  (b1 & 1F) + DA, word & FFE0), palette EC:8000 + 32 * byte 3. The
  ">= 70h uses 5A8370" rule above (C4:FF60) is the menu screens' path.
- Leader: the protagonist's field graphic from the select table
  FE:961B {graphic, ally, age, title} (exported as
  figures/protagonists.json). Graphic 00 (ally 06) has no F9:A000
  entry and keeps the captured images.

exportmap writes figures/<gid or h<gid>>/<facing>[_<frame>].png, each
cropped to its pieces, and offsets.json with each image's top-left
relative to the object; the field draws it at object + offset in map
pixels and steps the frame when a step starts from a tile-aligned
position (0249 walk: `$D9A4` +1 & 3 per step, across turns, held at a
stop). Kind 3A's layouts hold values like (-7167, -2817) and are
skipped (graphic 94, 8 frames).

Checks against emulator captures (OAM rendered from VRAM and CGRAM, and
screenshots):

| capture | figures | pixels equal |
|---|---|---|
| 0233 screenshot vs BG | graphic 67 left at object + offset, 3 sailors | 299/299 each (one line off: 98/299) |
| 0233 screenshot | leader graphic 1 up | 359/359 |
| 0233 walking right | leader graphic 1 right_2 | 336/336 |
| 00E3 OAM | 107 left, 8 right, 62 up, 115 up_3, 129 down/up x4, h222 down | 267/267, 305/305, 345/345, 319/319, 357-373/373 and 350-364/364 (overlaps), 344/344 |

| 0239 OAM | 160 up, 63 left_1, 62 right_3, 95 down_1 | 366/366, 316/316, 401/401, 76/76 |
| 0241 OAM | 129 right x4 | 307/307 each |
| 007A OAM | 79 down_4 (kind 0B: 6 frames a facing) | 189/189 |
| 0272 OAM | 226 (kind 18h, 21 pieces, 2228 px) | shape 2228/2228; colour 1869 (the leader stands in front; OBJ palette 0 = F2 exact) |
| 01E6 OAM | 121 (palette AD, cycled to AE by FF:A5A1) | _AE: 42/42, 9/9 |

Sprite colour math (2026-11-21). Only OBJ palettes 4-7 take part
(`$2131` bit 4 on 110 maps). Placed figures take OBJ palette slots in
object-slot order, one per distinct palette, the leader the next slot
after them (0301: NPC palettes 10 0F C9 20 23 in slots 0-4, the leader's
01 in 5; 0233: sailors 0, the two graphic-120 NPCs (BA) 1, leader 2). On 0301's forced-screen capture
(math 93h: subtract, fixed colour E2h) all 655 pixels of slots 4-7 were
2 darker than CGRAM and slots 0-3 unchanged (1047; the other 85 overlap).
exportmap writes figures/<key>/meta.json {palette}; the field gives slot
4-7 figures tile_layers OBJ_MATH (+/-, halved with bit 6; the sum is
halved before clamping, as 0372's capture shows; it used to clamp first,
and no fixed-colour add+half capture exists). The other colour is the fixed colour (64 maps; 292/292 px =
source - 2 in a render check), or with `$2130` bit 1 the subscreen under
the pixel, read from a third compositor pass (SCREEN `sub_out`, one texel
per map px, alpha 0 on the backdrop, where halving is skipped).
The slot list is `$D6E2` (C0:7B8A): a figure takes the slot already
holding its palette, else the first empty one; with all 8 taken it
overwrites slot 0. Event actors (objOp 2E) run the same routine after
the placed figures and the leader. The engine takes the first FF entry;
whether a slot is ever freed during a map is unknown, and the field's
list only grows.

0372 (`$212C` 13, `$212D` 04, `$2130` 02, `$2131` 73, `$2132` E0: add BG3,
halve) is the one map whose placed figures reach slot 4: palettes 173
52 51 50 50 57 58 54 in slots 0-6 and the leader's 01 in 7 (`$D6E2` = AD
34 33 32 39 3A 36 01). Reached by jump 25 -> move 05 (0010) -> move 00
(035F); its record at file 0x47FF94 was patched in the emulator to land
the leader at (25, 42) so graphics 89 (slot 4) and 75 (slot 5) are on
screen. Emulator data alone (OAM, OBJ CHR, CGRAM, BG3 from VRAM): slot
4-7 pixels over opaque BG3 were (obj + BG3) / 2 (153; 3 raw, 3 other),
over clear BG3 unchanged (1123; 2 other). tests/screencheck.gd
(SCREENCHECK_FIGS, frame 20122; BG3 offset, wave phase and animation
frames fitted to the screenshot; "without" = every figure in slot 0):
the patched landing, figure pixels 1329/1329 exact with the math, 1147
without; the unpatched landing (leader slot 7 under the fog) 332/332
leader pixels, 244 without; the patched landing with two actors injected
by queue word `17 2E` 2270/2270, 2082 without. The actor of graphic 89
took OAM palette 4 (its own pixels 364/364, 359 without), graphic 164
palette 0 (its C7 replaced AD in slot 0), graphic 87 palette 3. On 0301
(slots 0-5 taken) an injected graphic 164 took the empty slot 6
(`$D6E2` 10 0F C9 20 23 01 C7, OAM palette 6), so it gets the fixed-colour
math there. The render check
(tilecheck `_obj_math_check`) pins the shader; `_obj_math_0372_check`
pins which figures and actors take it.

On these probes every OBJ palette was left mid-fade (all colours from
white with only red stepped back, frames 19929-19964, so the figures
show cyan). It is a probe artefact: the second move was injected 60
frames after the first; held 600 frames on 035F first, 0372's OBJ
palettes load their own colours. The comparisons above recolour the
figures with the
capture's OBJ CGRAM (SCREENCHECK_FIGPAL). A slot-0 overwrite recolours
the figures already in slot 0; the field keeps their own palette. Outside
the figures the frame differs in one pillar column at the right edge
that the compositor draws and the emulator does not (BG, open). The
type-1 arrival sequence, where OBJ is subscreen-only, is added to BG2
whatever its palette (map-format.md).

Figures overlap in OAM order, which is by object y: the lowest on screen
first and in front (0233: sailors at y 408, 376, 360, then the leader at
344); the field sets z from the object y.

Some sets hold more facing groups than up/down/left/right: 0321's
graphic 224 stands in facing 4, and op 2B poses facing + 5. exportmap
writes groups 4+ as f4, f5, ... while a set's lists stay valid (a list
of 1-16 frames whose cell lists have 1-8 x 1-8 headers, at most 9
groups); the field takes the object's full facing.

Frame lists differ per kind (4 townsfolk, 5 kind 38h, 6 kind 0Bh, 7 on
0Bh's facing 4); exportmap writes every frame of each facing's list and
the field wraps the walk count at that length; a larger `$D9A4` (0272's
hidden slot: frame 3 of a 3-frame list) is clamped by FF:2AEC. A slot
with `$D99A` bit 20h (C0:7B05) has no figure. Kind 23h's two-piece layout is checked (0233's lower deck, the
leader walked down a planned route: 8 down, 5 left, 2 down).

## Open questions

- Per-band X offsets of the diagonal sprite compositing and the
  direction order (see Frame layout and Still open after this task
  above).
- Party-member IDs 0x00-0x0F are zeroed in the bokuno table; the
  original game must map party characters to map sprites via other
  data (see Runtime graphic-table resolution: party ids 00-07 fall
  below the 0x70 threshold, so $F9A000 is the table in play — its id
  00 entry is empty too, so a third resolution path exists for the
  party leader).
- Palette source: settled (2026-11-21, see "The tile lists are in the
  ROM"): 5A:8770 + 32 * gid for the 5A:8370 table, EC:8000 + 32 *
  byte 3 for F9:A000. `5A03F0 + id*32` was wrong.
- The trailing 0x80 bytes are the 16x16 object graphic
  (`sprites.ObjectTile`); their relationship to the map objects is not
  traced.
- Kind `2D` (一枚絵 3x4) and the enemy/symbol kinds from the Kani memo
  (`05` 馬 … `3B` カムシーン) are not implemented (map 0x249's g=61 is
  kind `05`).
```
