```md
### Protagonist walk figures + the row -> walk-id mapping (2026-11-18)

The character-select screen renders each candidate's own walking figure;
the exports live in `exports/data/walk_sprites/protagonist/<ally hex>/down.png`
(gitignored like all ROM-derived data) and the field and the port's select
screen load them by ally id (`MapView.protagonist_ally`,
`GameState.PROTAGONIST_WALK_IDS`).

**The engine structure, machine-verified (one MesenCE run per select row,
`tools/emulator/selwatch*.lua`-style watchers, raw logs in the session's
/tmp/walkfig-decode):** the engine's select flow is GENDER first (male /
female page of 4 candidates each — down presses past row 3 on one page
are simply ignored), then the character page. After the character confirm
the leader member record holds WRAM `$F000` = FE:961B+1 (the ally id,
`CURSOR frame=8200 F000=04 F001=06` for row 3) and `$F001` = FE:961B+0.
The intro montage itself walks EVERY protagonist with the shared ensemble
lead figure: `$F322` is written 0x0A by the common 0846-chain `4f 45`
(`cpu=C0:36AA`, frame 10711) identically for rows 0, 1, 3 and stays 0x0A
through the village walk (watched to frame 24000) — the per-protagonist
figure is the record byte, not $F322, in everything the scripted intro
reaches. Row -> ally and row -> figure therefore both pin to the FE:961B
table:

```
row:      0  1  2  3  4  5  6  7
ally:     00 03 05 04 02 01 06 07   (FE:961B+1, machine: $F000)
figure:   01 03 02 06 05 04 00 6C   (FE:961B+0, machine: $F001)
```

Two independent corroborations: the community struct doc
(`patches/ぼくの（略更新/テキスト/05_構造体.def.txt`, `struct 主人公選択
{ BYTE キャラグラフィックID; BYTE キャラID; byte 歳; BYTE 肩書き; }`)
defines exactly this 4-byte layout — and the 歳 column is the age shown on
the engine's select screen (20/22/27/33 male, 16/20/19/24 female, read off
the screenshots); original-table id 01 decodes to file `1A1C60`, the blob
the patch ecosystem names ユリアン (patch-table entry A0), matching row 0
-> 01. The per-row graphic ids resolve through the engine's party-figure
path (docs above), not the 5A8370 blob table — id 00 (モニカ) is zeroed
there yet renders fine as a protagonist.

**Export pipeline** (both steps in tools/emulator/):

1. `tools/emulator/run.sh tools/emulator/selsnap.lua --timeout=300`
   boots to the select screen and dumps a PNG every 20 frames while the
   candidates idle-animate (`MALE=0` runs the female page: down + A at
   the gender confirm). Reassemble with
   `python3 -I tools/emulator/oam_reassemble.py <log> <dir>`'s
   DUMPBEGIN/DUMPDATA framing, or split on the `SHOT frame=` lines.
2. `python3 -I tools/emulator/cutselect.py <outdir>` keys figure pixels
   against the parchment shades (sampled from the clean right panel) and
   cuts one tight native-res crop per candidate — the engine draws the
   select figures at ~14-17 x 25-30 px, larger than the field figure
   canvas, which the renderer scales as needed.

The captures are the select screen's left-facing profiles stored as
`down.png`: only one pose exists per candidate there, and the field
renderer shows it for every facing rather than swapping identities
mid-walk (godot/map_view.gd `_player_figure_image`).

## Monster figure capture (2026-11-18, map 0x250 wandering monsters)

Field-monster walk figures for the two kinds on map 0x250, extracted from
the monfig.lua screenshot run (593 shots, frames 20800-80000, camera
locked while the party sits parked on tile (17,26); predecessor run
preserved at /tmp/monfig/run1):

- `exports/data/walk_sprites/76/down.png` — 地狼 (kind byte A2, event
  1862 slots): gray wolf with orange markings, front (down-facing) pose.
- `exports/data/walk_sprites/84/down.png` — 牙蛇 family (kind byte AA,
  event 186A slots): purple snake with green coil, front pose.

Both are 24x24 RGBA, feet at the canvas bottom edge, content centered —
the placement godot/map_view.gd `_place_monster_node` expects
(centered on tile, feet on the tile's bottom edge; the formula is
texture-size aware since this change).

Method: median over the 515 parked-state shots builds the static
background (party included); per-frame diff components matched to trace
slots via a constant scene offset — rendered sprite bbox =
`($D9AA-21 … $D9AA)` × `($D9AC-301 … $D9AC-279)` in engine px
(8 px/tile), verified by displacement matching (e.g. slot 1 moved
(-164,0) between frames 60000→61000 while its diff component moved
(-165,0)); stalled frames (same slot px at f-100 and f) isolate standing
poses; pose clusters (left profile / front / back / walk frames)
separated by pairwise pixel agreement; per-pose majority vote fills the
diff holes (sprite pixels that happen to equal the background in single
frames).

Verification (numeric, against shots NOT in the merge sets): the A2
front sprite matches 7 stalled frames at 100% pixel agreement and the AA
front sprite 18 frames at 100% (threshold: per-pixel RGB distance ≤ 60
on all sprite-alpha pixels); in-engine on map 0250 — both figures
rendered at their tiles, zero red fallback markers (2026-11-18, the
Godot map_view via xlab.sh, retired with the engine). The shell's
one-shot today:

    go build -o /tmp/saga3 ./cmd/saga3
    xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 800x600x24" /tmp/saga3 \
        --map 0250 12 58 --frames 120 --press right:30:60 \
        --screenshot /tmp/saga3-0250.png

prints `SHELL-SHOT path=… mean=…` (verified 2026-11-24: mean=56,
512x448); `scripts/shell-smoke.sh` runs this shape as a gate step.

Side/profile poses exist too (left profile verified pixel-perfect at
12 frames): extract with the same pipeline from /tmp/monfig2 if the
port ever needs per-facing monster sprites — the trace's velocity labels
do NOT predict the rendered pose (the scene's staged movement drives
facing), so cluster poses by pixel agreement instead.

`tools/emulator/mon_oam.lua` (this task) dumps OAM+CGRAM every 400
frames and full VRAM twice on the same timeline — kept for future
VRAM-level figure work; note its OAM shows the scene's figure strips
placed at screen positions unrelated to the slot cells (staging), while
the screenshot diff pipeline above is what actually produced the
exports.

```

`docs/subscreen-obj.md`:

```md
# Subscreen OBJ palette slots: the allocation lifecycle, the rescans, and the objOp 69 rewrite (decoded 2026-11-23)

Closes the two open gaps left in docs/map-format.md ("The OBJ palette slot
list ($D6E2) and subscreen OBJ math"): what re-runs the allocation scan
C0:7B8A mid-screen and what a re-run does, and the `81h -> 80h` entry
rewrite at C0:CA26. Everything below is byte-verified in
patches/bokuno_jp.sfc (hand-disassembled; decomp/src only covers bank C0
to ~4A94, so this region is raw bytes) plus one live probe
(tools/emulator/subobj_watch.lua, logs quoted in the last section).

## The assignment funnel C0:7B3F (refined)

`A` = graphic id (8-bit), `Y` = figure index. `A >= FD` takes the hide
path (C0:7B01: `$D99A |= 20`, `$D9B2 |= 0C`, `$D9D0 = 0F8C/0F82` by
`A == FF`) and returns BEFORE the scan - invisible figures never touch
`$D6E2`. Otherwise `X = A*4` and the funnel resolves the graphic record
through the 5A helpers, then runs the scan:

    C0/7B4D: JSL $5AA770   ; A770: JSR $5ABFA8 (sets $EFF7), then source
    C0/7B56: STA $D99F,Y   ;  byte ($5A8373,X patch path / $5AD9E0 decode)
    C0/7B59: JSL $5AA786   ; $EFF7==FF -> LDA $5A8370,X ; else $F9A000,X
    C0/7B6A: STA $D99B,Y   ; -> *4 -> JSL $5AD830 -> word
    C0/7B6D: LDA $E10002   ; -> $D9D0,Y
    C0/7B75: JSL $5AA797   ; tile word ($F9A001,X & FFE0 / $5A8371)
    C0/7B7C: STA $D99D,Y
    C0/7B81: LDA $D9B1,Y; AND #$F1; STA $D9B1,Y   ; clear palette bits 1-3
    C0/7B8A: <the allocation scan, below>
    C0/7BB9: TYA; ASL; AND #$0E; PLY; ORA $D9B1,Y; STA $D9B1,Y

**$EFF7** is the patch-table/normal-table selector for this one
assignment, set fresh by 5A:BFA8 at every funnel entry (all its `LDA
$EFF7`/`STA $EFF7` sites are in bank 5A; no other bank writes it except
one `LDX $EFF7` at E4:9AC0):

    5A/BFA8: CPY #$0000; BNE $BFB4
             CPX #$01C0; BCS $BFC5          ; Y=0 (figure 0) and X >= $1C0
             BRA $BFBF
      $BFB4: LDA $D9D2,Y; CMP #$0C; BEQ $BFC5
             CMP #$4C; BEQ $BFC5            ; class 0C or 4C
      $BFBF: LDA #$00 -> STA $EFF7          ; normal
      $BFC5: LDA #$FF -> STA $EFF7          ; patch-table figure

So `$EFF7 = FF` iff the assigned figure is figure 0 with graphic id
`>= 0x70` (the 5A8370 patch table, sprites.md's resolver threshold
`CPX #$01C0`), or its `$D9D2,Y` class is `0C`/`4C`. The helpers then read
the record from `5A:8370,X` (patch, stride 4) instead of `F9:A000,X`
(normal; SNES `$F9A000` = file `0x39A000`, verified: the doc's capture
palette lists resolve - e.g. 0372's `AD 34 33 32 39 3A 36` are the byte-3
values of ids 79/4F-51/4E-52/50-5B/59/4B-58/4D-53).

**The scan C0:7B8A** (the map-format pseudocode is exact except that the
compare and the store are helper-mediated):

    C0/7B8A: LDY #$0000
    loop:    LDA $D6E2,Y
             JSL $5AA7B1            ; compare (below); Z set = match
             BEQ found
             CMP #$FF; BEQ taken    ; empty slot
             INY; CPY #$0008; BEQ full; BRA loop
    full:    LDY #$0000
    taken:   TYA; INC; CMP $D6E1; BCC +3; STA $D6E1
             JSL $5AA7C3            ; palette byte to register (below)
             STA $D6E2,Y; JSR $7BE0 ; queue the CGRAM upload
    found:   TYA; ASL; AND #$0E; PLY; ORA $D9B1,Y; STA $D9B1,Y

    5A/A7B1: PHA; LDA $EFF7; CMP #$FF; BEQ $A7BF
             PLA; CMP $F9A003,X; RTL     ; normal: figure's F9 byte 3
      $A7BF: PLA; CMP #$FE; RTL          ; patch: compare against FE

    5A/A7C3: LDA $EFF7; CMP #$FF; BEQ $A7CF
             LDA $F9A003,X; RTL          ; normal: register F9 byte 3
      $A7CF: REP #$20; TXA; LSR; LSR; SEP #$20
             STA $02F8,Y; LDA #$FD; RTL  ; patch: store FD (+ graphic id
                                         ; aside in $02F8,Y)

The patch-figure asymmetry is real and load-bearing: a patch figure's
scan compares each slot byte against `FE` but a taken slot is written
with `FD`. `FE` never matches anything - a byte-scan of the F9:A000
table finds no graphic with byte 3 = FD or FE, and the only `$D6E2`
writers are the three FF resets (C0:3DEB, C0:EAE1, C0:085B), the scan
store at 7BB3, the free at 7BDB, and objOp 69's `80` at C0:CA41 - so no
slot ever holds `FE`. Consequences, all byte-forced:

- Every patch-figure assignment (leader graphic `>= 0x70`, class `0C`/
  `4C`) takes the first EMPTY slot and writes `FD`; two patch figures
  burn two slots. The slot's CGRAM upload (7BE0, source
  `EC:8000 + 32*FD`) is the same palette data both times.
- No normal figure can ever match an `FD` slot either (no F9 byte 3 =
  FD), so `FD` slots are only ever reused by another patch figure after
  a free re-empties them.
- The `$EFF7 == FF` branch of the upload queue (C0:7BF7 -> JSL
  $5AA8F4: `CMP #$FD` on the palette byte, `$EFF7 = FF` if equal) exists
  but nothing in the funnel reads `$EFF7` afterwards; it is a leftover
  write on this path.

The upload queue C0:7BE0: palette `$BC` uploads from WRAM `$7E:E2B6`
instead of the EC table; otherwise `A = palette; AND #$00FF; XBA; LSR
LSR LSR; ADC #$8000` = `EC:$8000 + 32*palette`, and the record's CGRAM
word is `TYA; ASL ASL ASL ASL; ORA #$80` = `$80 + slot*16`
(colours 128 + slot*8). `$D2F3` bit 6 mirrors each upload into the
second list at WRAM `$0100` (C0:7C33-7C6D, consumption untraced -
carried over from map-format.md as an open item).

## Callers of the funnel and their triggers

Byte-scan of bank C0 for `JSR $7B3F` (JSL into C0:7B3F from other banks:
none; jump-table entry: none) - eleven call sites, grouped by dispatch:

| site | dispatch | event |
|---|---|---|
| C0:4C25 | load finalize (BE1B `JSR $4D0D` family) | placed figure of the map record, in record order; passes `$D9D4,Y`, hiding first if `>= FD` |
| C0:4D5D | same family | leader graphic from `$D8FA` |
| C0:4D6B | same family | leader graphic from `$D8FB` (the `PLA; CMP #$01` branch) |
| C0:4D79 | same family | leader graphic from JSL `$5AD4F1` |
| C0:4EFF | routine entry C0:4E62 (`JSR` from 4D8B and B55B only) | generic object spawn: finds a free slot (stride `$40`, 32 objects), builds from the `$D8F6-$D8F9` record, re-runs the funnel with the figure's current `$D9D4,Y` |
| C0:634A | action-script interpreter op 19 (`JMP ($70AA,X)` at C0:53CB/53FF; table C0:70AA entry 0x19 -> 6334) | graphic-set op: `JSR $574C` returns the new graphic -> `$D9D4,Y` -> funnel |
| C0:B4AD | no static caller (runtime-dispatched; body starts C0:B410) | figure 0 adopts figure Y: copies `$D9A9/$D9B3/$D9A3/$D9CB/$D9CD/$D9D4` from Y into 0, deactivates Y (`$D9A9,Y &= ...`, `$D99A,Y = 0`), re-runs the funnel with Y=0 |
| C0:B5D7 | no static caller | leader init: `Y=0`, `$D9D4 = $F001` (the party record's graphic byte), funnel, then default fields |
| C0:B6BB | objOp 21 (`17 21`, `JMP ($B0AB,X)`; table C0:B0AB entry 0x21 -> B69B) | set this object's graphic to the op parameter `$EF01` |
| C0:D78B | objOp 2E (table entry 0x2E -> D72D) | event-actor spawn: copies the slot-0 object block, then `$EF00` -> JSL `$5AA947` -> funnel |
| C0:D9C0 | objOp 2C (table entry 0x2C -> D976) | party-member spawn: member `$EF00` -> `$F000+128*member` record -> JSL `$5AA90D` -> funnel |

The two class-0C setters that feed BFA8's test: 5A:A947 (objOp 2E path;
entered with `$EFF7 = FF` preset by 5A:BFD2's `LDA #$FF; STA $EFF7;
JML $C0D72D`) writes `$D9D2,X = 0C` before the funnel and 5A:A95D then
overwrites the class with `20` after it; 5A:A90D (objOp 2C path) writes
`$D9D2,X = 0x350C` (class `0C`, `$D9D3 = 35`) only when the member's
`$F0xx` record byte 0 is `>= B0`, else leaves the caller's `0x0020`.

Allocation order is per-load-path, not a rule: the opening screen's live
run allocates the leader (palette `01`, slot 0) BEFORE the montage
figures `03/04/05` (slots 1-3) - on maps 0301/0372 the captures had the
leader after the placed figures. Both orders come out of this table.

## Rescan semantics (gap 1)

The scan never rebuilds the list and never moves an existing entry:

- Re-running for a palette that already holds a slot hits the `BEQ
  found` leg: the slot index is recomputed and written back into
  `$D9B1,Y` unchanged; `$D6E2` and `$D6E1` are untouched. Every funnel
  call with an unchanged graphic is a no-op on the list.
- A NEW palette takes the first `FF` slot (or matches an existing one
  first). A graphic change mid-map (objOp 21, interpreter op 19, the
  B410 adopt, a spawn) therefore ADDS a slot; the figure's old slot is
  not released by the funnel itself.
- The only entry mutation besides adds is objOp 69's `81 -> 80` and the
  full case: with all 8 slots distinct, `full` falls to `LDY #$0000`,
  overwrites `$D6E2[0]` with the new palette and re-uploads slot 0's
  CGRAM - whoever still points at slot 0 silently recolours. No shuffling
  exists anywhere else.

## Slot frees (correction: they do happen)

C0:7BC5 (the free) reads the figure's own slot from `$D9B1,Y` (`LSR;
AND #$0007`), skips figures whose `$D9D4,Y >= FD`, writes `FF` into
`$D6E2[slot]`. map-format.md says it has no JSR caller - refuted; three
call sites, all on despawn/hide paths:

- C0:6753 - interpreter op 3A (table C0:70AA entry 0x3A -> 6750):
  `$5740` select, `JSR $7BC5`, `$7956`, `$D99A,Y = 0` (deactivate),
  RTS. The action-script "remove this figure" op.
- C0:6619 - body 65C9-6627 (no static entry; runtime-dispatched like
  B410): stashes object 0's tile coords into `$E1DA/$E1DB[$D8*2]`,
  `JSR $5DC8`, then if `$D9B8,Y != 0` (figure live): free, `$7956`,
  deactivate; else just the next fetch (`JMP $60E8`).
- C0:6DA0 - inside the 7022-level interpreter's op 03 handler (table
  C0:7022 entry 0x03 -> 6D2B, the per-frame step op): after restoring
  x/y from `$E1DA/$E1DB` and `JSR $5DC8`, frees when `$D9B8,Y != 0` AND
  `$D9B9,Y == 30` (the action state stored per action-scripts.md).

So a freed slot returns to `FF` and the next allocation - any palette
scan - can take it. The port's grow-only list diverges as soon as one
despawn fires.

## objOp 69: the 81h -> 80h rewrite (gap 2)

Dispatch: VM `17 69` -> `JMP ($B0AB,X)` -> table C0:B0AB entry 0x69
(bytes `26 ca` at C0:B17D, odd parity matches the table base) ->
C0:CA26. The whole handler:

    C0/CA26: PLY; JSR $B030
             LDA $D6E1; STA $8D
             LDY #$0000
    loop:    LDA $D6E2,Y; CMP #$81; BEQ found
             INY; DEC $8D; BNE loop; RTS     ; no 81 entry: done
    found:   LDA #$80; STA $D6E2,Y           ; the rewrite
             TYA; CLC; ADC #$08; STA $BAB7   ; CGRAM word index (slot+8)*16
             LDX #$0040; LDA #$1F; STA $8D
    sweep:   LDA $D99A,X; BEQ next           ; object inactive: skip
             LDA $D9D4,X; CMP #$D9; BNE next
             LDA #$80; STA $D9D4,X           ; graphic D9 -> 80
    next:    REP; TXA; CLC; ADC #$0040; TAX; SEP
             DEC $8D; BNE sweep
             INC $D6B8                       ; screen-busy flag on (census below)
             STZ $D8ED                       ; sequence-finished flag off
             LDA #$81; STA $BAB5; LDA #$80; STA $BAB6
             JSL $FFBDD2                     ; stage EC palettes 81 and 80
             LDA #$20                        ; 32 iterations, two frames each
    fade:    PHA; JSL $FFBE61                ; one 3-channel step + upload
             JSR $06EB; JSR $06EB            ; run two full frames
             PLA; DEC; BNE fade              ; bytes CA92-CA94: 68 3A D0 F1
             STZ $D6B8                       ; flag off, in-handler (CA96)
             LDA #$01; STA $D8ED             ; sequence finished (CA99-CA9B)
             RTS                             ; CA9E: A9 01 8D ED D8 60

What it means, byte by byte:

- It re-keys the slot that holds palette `81` to palette `80`. In the
  F9:A000 table, graphic `D9` is the ONLY id with byte 3 = `81`
  (`F9:A364 = 2c 26 82 81`); graphic `80` has byte 3 = `80`
  (`F9:A200 = 2c 26 82 80`; id `A3` shares it). The sweep rewrites every
  live figure currently showing graphic `D9` to graphic `80`, so their
  palette byte becomes `80` and the list entry must follow or future
  scans would never match them.
- The CGRAM refresh does not show palette `80` directly, and one firing
  runs the whole fade - it is not spread over repeated `17 69`s.
  FF:BDD2 stages both palettes from the EC table into WRAM as FIVE
  BYTES PER COLOUR (`$8000+32*p` -> `$BB25` for `81`, -> `$BB75` for
  `80`, driver FF:B878: byte `+0` = word & `$1F` (R), word `+1..2` =
  word & `$03E0` (G, left in place), word `+3..4` = `(word>>8) & $007C`
  (B, pre-shifted DOWN 8 bits - the store is `LDA $94; AND #$007C`,
  and m16 `LDA $94` reads dp `$94-$95`, i.e. the source word's high
  byte)). FF:BE61 = JSR FF:BE7A + JSR FF:BF76, and the handler calls
  it 32 times (the `LDA #$20`/`fade` loop above, two `JSR $06EB`
  frames per iteration, ~64 frames per firing). Each FF:BE7A call
  steps every channel one unit toward the `$BB75` target: the R byte
  `+1`/`-1`, the G word `+$20`/`-$20`, the B word `+$04`/`-$04` (high
  bit set always steps up, equal stays). After each step FF:BF2B
  recompresses the 5-byte channels into the 2-byte upload buffer
  `$7E:C125` and stores ONLY the `R|G` word (`$90`, clamped at
  `$1F`/`$03E0`): the B word is computed into `$91` (clamped at
  `$007C`) and BF2B returns without storing it (`BF6C: LDA $90; STA
  $C125,Y`). FF:BF76 then queues the 32-byte upload of `$C125` to CGRAM
  word `$BAB7*16 = $80 + slot*16` (count `$0020`, record `{$40,
  idx<<4, $C125, $7E, $0020}`). The uploaded words are therefore
  BLUE-LESS: R and G fade, B is dropped on every firing - in this
  handler and in every sibling fade op that shares BF2B (6C, 82, the
  second-dispatch family, FF's 2C engine). `$D6B8` is not a firing
  counter: it holds 1 for the duration of the blocking fade (INC at
  CA71, STZ at CA96 before the RTS) and is read only as a busy test
  (census below).
- `STZ $D8ED` clears the sequence-finished flag (vm-semantics.md's name
  for `$D8ED`), so the script chain keeps running.

There is no path to CA26 other than this objOp: byte-scans find no
`JSR`/`JMP`/`JML`/`JSL`/immediate or word-table reference to it (the
only in-bank `26 ca` word is the table entry itself). The connection to
the subscreen math is data, not code: the slot index is unchanged, so
the figure's membership in the slots 4-7 colour math does not move -
only that slot's colours fade from palette 81's to palette 80's. The
"fixed colour flag" guess in the brief does not hold; `$D00B`/`$2132`
are untouched by this handler.

31 `17 69` byte pairs exist in the script banks (45, 4B, 4D, 50 x2, 51,
5B x3, 5C x2, 5E, 67, 6C x2, 71 x3, 73 x2, 74 x6, 7B x5).

## The $D6B8 census (2026-11-23 byte re-verification)

The probe's `$D6B8` ticks are not objOp 69 - the INC at CA71 is
reachable only through `found` (the no-81 scan path RTSes at CA3E),
and the flag is written all over the scene system. Every write is one
of the two absolute forms: `INC $D6B8` (EE B8 D6), 20 sites, and
`STZ $D6B8` (9C B8 D6), 23 sites; no `STA`/`DEC`/`TSB`/`TRB`
absolute form to `$D6B8` exists in the ROM, and no dp form can be one
either - the scene runner sets the direct page to `$0000` (`LDA #$7E;
PHA; PLB; LDX #$0000; PHX; PLD`, C0:B8DB-B8E3), so `85 B8`-class
operands target `$00:B8`, and no `LDA #$D600; TAD` (nor its XBA
variant) exists anywhere. Byte-coincidences in the indexed forms
(`INC $D6B6,X` at 4B:BF15, read bases `$D6B0-$D6B8` at 0C/0E/10/14)
sit only in script/data banks. Equal offsets under file 0x400000 are
the same bytes duplicated, not more writers. Block moves (MVN/MVP)
run `$7E` <-> FD/34/37 only; whether any dynamic range covers `$D6B8`
is runtime-shaped and unverified.

    INC                              clears via
    C0:B90B, BDC8, C234, BFD3        scene-reset / teleport /
                                     queue-flush ops; the B90B/BDC8/
                                     C224 bodies run the JSL $C0E283
                                     map load and RTS with the flag
                                     still set
    (cleared by:)                    C0:BE3E - the map-load-finalize
                                     op (its body is the JSR $4D0D
                                     chain, then `STZ $D6B8; STA
                                     $D8ED=1`), C3D0 - the field-entry
                                     tail (`STZ $D6B9; STZ $D6B8`),
                                     C0:0801 - the boot clear block
    C0:2442, 247D, 24A5              $2100 brightness ramp ops (fade
                                     in 15 / out 10 / out 30 frames,
                                     one JSR $06EB per step)
    ->                               2477 / 249F (24A5 shares 249F)
    C0:24C7, 24D6                    one-call sync ops ($0999/$094D)
    ->                               24D0 / 24DF
    C0:BF8B                          $D013/$D006=FF blackout op
    ->                               BF9F
    C0:CA71                          objOp 69 (found path only)
    ->                               CA96 (in-handler, before RTS)
    C0:CAEF                          objOp 82 (the BC rewrite; scan
                                     gate CMP #$BC) -> CB0F
    C0:CB67                          objOp 6C (staged palette to
                                     black + the 8x[6x CCD2] swirl)
                                     -> CBB9
    C0:CBD3, CC2A, CC57, CCEF, CD2F  fade ops with NO B0AB table entry
                                     (a second dispatch, untraced):
                                     the EF-parameter fades, the
                                     32x[FFB614+3x C00714] body, the
                                     $BB75 gradient build, FFBD54's
                                     4-buffer fade
    ->                               CC1D, CC4A, CCBC, CD22, CD39
    FF:BC1E, BC8E                    bank FF's palette-2C fade engine,
                                     JSL'd from one-line ops (17 79 ->
                                     JSL $FFBC89 at C0:C9BA)
    ->                               FF:BC64, BCE6

Readers, both a plain busy test (`LDA $D6B8; BNE <skip>`): C0:AB31 -
the VM's background-activity block; C0:EA6B - the field object-update
step. No other read form lands in a decoded code bank. (The second
dispatch could in principle also reach CA26; its no-81 RTS bounds that
- no dispatch path can increment the flag without an `81` slot.)

## Live probe

tools/emulator/subobj_watch.lua (schedule cribbed from
journey_teleport.lua; logs `$D6E1/$D6E2`, `$D6B8`, `$BAB5-BAB7`, map
cell each frame, print-on-change). Run:
`/tmp/subobj-mesence/Mesen -testRunner tools/emulator/subobj_watch.lua
patches/bokuno_jp.sfc -enableStdout --timeout=555` (24000 frames).

The original run quoted:

    SUBOBJ f=10715 m=1403 00:FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=01 ...
    SUBOBJ f=10892 m=0181 01:01 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=01 ...
    SUBOBJ f=10901 m=0181 02:01 03 FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 ...
    SUBOBJ f=10903 m=0181 03:01 03 04 FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 ...
    SUBOBJ f=10905 m=0181 04:01 03 04 05 FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 ...
    SUBOBJ f=10906 m=0181 04:01 03 04 05 FF FF FF FF d6b8=01 ...
    SUBOBJ f=10923 m=0181 04:01 03 04 05 FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 ...

A 2026-11-23 rerun of the same script (this time logging the full
signature, not the `...` truncated form) reproduces both ticks and adds
the `$BAB5-BAB7` fields:

    SUBOBJ f=10715 m=1403 00:FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=01 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10808 MAP=0181
    SUBOBJ f=10892 m=0181 01:01 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=01 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10899 m=0181 01:01 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10901 m=0181 02:01 03 FF FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10903 m=0181 03:01 03 04 FF FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10905 m=0181 04:01 03 04 05 FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10906 m=0181 04:01 03 04 05 FF FF FF FF d6b8=01 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00
    SUBOBJ f=10923 m=0181 04:01 03 04 05 FF FF FF FF d6b8=00 b5=00 b6=00 b7=00

Corrects the earlier reading: objOp 69 does NOT fire in this segment.
At both ticks no slot holds `81` (`FF` x8, then `01 03 04 05`), so the
handler's scan falls to the RTS at CA3E and its INC at CA71 is
unreachable; and `b5/b6/b7` stay `00`, while every fade-family writer
sets at least one of them (69 sets `81/80/slot+8`, 82 and 6C set the
slot or `07`, FF's 2C engine sets `$2C`). The ticks are the plain
screen-effect/load ops of the census above. Tick 1 (f=10715, held
~184 frames across the 1403->0181 map load, cleared by f=10899) is one
of the scene-reset/map-load ops (INC sites B90B/BDC8/C234 - the flag
stays set past their RTS until a finalize tail like BE3E clears it).
Tick 2 (f=10906, cleared by f=10923, <= 17 frames, right after the
montage slots fill) is a short fade/sync op - the 15-frame `$2100`
ramp-in at C0:2442 fits the window (the 10-frame ramp-out at 247D and
the 1-3-frame sync ops at 24C7/24D6/BF8B also fit; this log cannot
separate them). Still confirmed by the probe: the handler is a no-op
while no slot holds `81`; the leader allocates palette `01` into slot 0
first, the montage figures `03/04/05` fill slots 1-3; no free fires in
this segment and the list stays `01 03 04 05` through frame 24000.

## Corrections this doc forces on docs/map-format.md

- "The free routine C0:7BC5 has no JSR caller in the ROM - slots are
  never freed mid-map" is wrong: three callers (above). The port's
  grow-only list is NOT engine-faithful.
- The scan pseudocode's `CMP $F9A003,X` and `LDA $F9A003,X` are
  helper-mediated (5AA7B1/5AA7C3) and conditional on `$EFF7`; the patch
  path compares `FE` and stores `FD`, which never match anything.
- "Placed figures in record order, the leader after them" is
  capture-specific: the opening screen loads the leader first. Order is
  whatever funnel-caller order the map's load path uses.
- 0372's slot-4 note "(0372: 39h, graphic 89)": id `89`'s F9 byte 3 is
  `91`; `39` belongs to id `59`. The palette value is right, the graphic
  id reads like a nibble slip.

## Port implication

map_view.gd's `_figure_palette_slot` is the one-shot scan (first match,
first empty, else overwrite slot 0), reset at map start, fed spawns
once. Against this decode:

- The rescan is per-assignment, not per-event; for an unchanged graphic
  it is a no-op, so the port's "keep the spawn slot" is correct as long
  as the figure's palette byte never changes. It diverges exactly when a
  funnel caller with a NEW palette runs mid-map: objOp 21, interpreter
  op 19, the B410 adopt, or a spawn with a changed `$D9D4` - the engine
  adds/reuses a slot, the port keeps the old one.
- Slot frees are reachable in normal play (interpreter op 3A and the two
  gated despawn paths). The port needs a free-on-despawn hook keyed by
  the figure's own `$D9B1` slot bits, or its slot numbering drifts from
  the engine's after the first despawn - which silently moves figures in
  or out of the slots 4-7 colour math.
- Patch figures (leader id `>= 0x70`, class `0C`/`4C`) must be keyed by
  the constant `FD` with a compare key of `FE` - i.e. never matched,
  always a fresh empty slot, CGRAM from EC palette FD. Keying them by
  their F9 byte 3 (garbage for ids `>= 0x70`) reproduces neither the
  slots nor the uploads.
- The full-8 case overwrites slot 0 and re-uploads its CGRAM; the port
  must copy the re-upload, not just the list write.
- objOp 69 (`17 69`) needs porting as a unit: slot entry `81 -> 80`, the
  live-figure sweep `D9 -> 80`, then ONE blocking firing that runs the
  whole fade in-handler: 32 iterations, two frames each (~64 frames),
  each iteration stepping the slot's staged palette one unit toward
  palette 80's data in all three channels (R `+1`, G `+$20`, B `+$04`)
  and re-uploading the recompressed words. The recompression stores
  only `R|G` - the engine's uploaded words are blue-less (B = 0), so a
  port that uploads the true BGR555 value diverges in blue from the
  first firing on. `$D6B8` is the screen-busy flag (set at firing
  start, cleared before the RTS), not a counter.
- The reset-to-FF sites and the leader/2C/2E allocation contents are
  already modeled (map-format.md); only the order caveat above applies.

Open items carried forward: how the `$0100` mirror list is consumed;
the runtime tables that dispatch B410 and the 65C9-region free path (no
static caller; likely the WRAM `JMP ($9AB9,X)` tables at C0:544D/553F,
fill site unresolved); whether any shipped script runs `17 69` when a
slot actually holds `81` (the fade path is decoded but never observed
live); the second dispatcher behind the CBD3/CC2A/CC57/CCEF/CD2F fade
ops (no B0AB entry); which scene-reset op's INC site (B90B/BDC8/C234/
BFD3) produced the probe's two ticks and which clear tail pairs with
it.

```

`docs/techniques.md`:

```md
# Techniques (技) and spells (術)

Tables of per-technique combat parameters in `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`
(CRC32 7E165025), decoded by `internal/techs` and `cmd/dumptechs`.

## Sources

- Struct layout: community struct dump shipped in the bokuno patch
  archive, `patches/ぼくの（略更新/テキスト/05_構造体.def.txt` (Shift-JIS):
  `struct 技の性能` (14 bytes), used unchanged by both `struct RS3_技データ`
  and `struct RS3拡張_術データ`. The spell table carries the same 14-byte
  record; there is no separate spell struct.
- Per-technique values: the bokuno wiki, 技 page
  (`https://www.wikihouse.com/bokuno/index.php?%B5%BB`, EUC-JP) and 術 page
  (`...%BD%D1`).

## Offsets

| table | file offset | CPU bank | extent |
|---|---|---|---|
| tech data (技データ) | 0x3E0F00 | FE:0F00 | 256 × 14 B, ends at 0x3E1D00 |
| tech names (技名称) | 0x3D27C0 | — | 256 × 10 B, ends at 0x3D2EC0 |
| enemy tech data (敵技データ) | 0x3E1D00 | FE:1D00 | 256 × 16 B 敵技性能, ends at 0x3E2D00 |
| enemy tech data, hack extension (RS3拡張_敵技性能) | 0x5B4AC0 | — | 256 × 16 B, ids 0x100-0x1FF |
| enemy tech names (敵技名称) | 0x3D31C0 | — | 256 × 10 B (exact position per docs/battle-data.md; this file's earlier 0x3D2EC0 neighbor inference was wrong) |
| enemy tech names, hack extension | 0x5B40C0 | — | 256 × 10 B, ids 0x100-0x1FF |
| spell names (術名称) | 0x5BA000 | 5B:A000 | 256 × 10 B, ends at 0x5BAA00 |
| spell data (術データ) | 0x5BAA00 | 5B:AA00 | 256 × 14 B, ends at 0x5BB800 |
| added-effect settings (拡張用RS3_技の追加効果) | 0x3FF200 | — | 128 × 6 B, indexed by byte +3 |

The tables are contiguous with their neighbors, which is itself evidence:
tech data 0x3E0F00 + 256×14 = the enemy tech table's verified start, tech
names 0x3D27C0 + 256×10 = the enemy tech name table's start, spell names
0x5BA000 + 256×10 = the spell data table's start.

The def file gives each table as `BYTE space[<offset>]` followed by one
`技の性能` entry per ID: 4067072 (0x3E0F00) tech data, 4007872 (0x3D27C0)
tech names, 6004736 (0x5BA000) spell names, 6007296 (0x5BAA00) spell
data. The stream is anchored to this ROM because the same file's
`RS3_敵データ` skip lands at 0x3E3F8B, exactly the enemy stat table
address already verified in docs/battle-data.md.

## Record layout (14 bytes, `技の性能`)

| byte | field | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| +0 | 命中・発動率 | hit (techs) / activation (spells) rate in percent; 255 = no roll |
| +1 | 基本ダメージ | base power byte; in-game 威力 = byte × 4 (docs/battle-formulas.md §2 uses 威力×4×回数) |
| +2 | 回数・威力 | high nibble hit count (回数), low nibble growth term (成長) |
| +3 | 追加効果 | index into the added-effect table at 0x3FF200 (see below); 0xFF/0xFE = none |
| +4 | 属性 | 0x01 状態, 0x02 雷, 0x04 冷, 0x08 熱, 0x10 射, 0x20 貫, 0x40 叩, 0x80 斬 |
| +5 | 攻撃範囲 | 0x02 味方, 0x04 敵, 0x08 横一列, 0x10 縦一列, 0x20 全体, 0x40 遠単, 0x80 両手 |
| +6 | 特殊効果 | 0x02 盾有効, 0x08 見切り可, 0x10 カウンター有効, 0x80 閃き派生有効 |
| +7 | 属性2 | 0x01 水, 0x08 投げ, 0x10 音波, 0x20 凝視, 0x40 飛行特攻, 0x80 地面 |
| +8 | 特殊設定 | 0x02 カウンター技, 0x04 行動最後, 0x08 行動最初, 0x20 固有技扱い, 0x80 追加効果有効 |
| +9 | ？？？？ | unknown |
| +10 | 技タイプ | damage-formula family selector (docs/battle-formulas.md §2.x) |
| +11 | 術タイプ | 0x00 物理, 0x01 太陽, 0x02 月, 0x03 アビス, 0x08 蒼竜, 0x10 朱鳥, 0x18 白虎, 0x20 玄武 |
| +12 | 種類 | 0x00 剣, 0x10 大剣, 0x21 斧, 0x31 棍棒, 0x42 小剣, 0x52 槍, 0x63 弓, 0x74 体術, 0x85 蒼竜, 0x96 朱鳥, 0xA7 白虎, 0xB8 玄武, 0xC9 太陽, 0xDA 月, 0x0E 陣形技, 0x0F アイテム |
| +13 | 消費 | low 5 bits WP/JP amount; 0x20 JP, 0x40 全消費, 0x80 武器破壊 |

Name records are 10 bytes, NUL (0x00) or fullwidth-space (0x50)
terminated, in the ROM's glyph encoding (decode via data/glyphs_jp.json
through internal/bokuno, as cmd/dumpnames does). The hack's name table
renders the long vowel as 一 (U+4E00), e.g. マタド一ル.

## Added effects (byte +3 → table at 0x3FF200)

Byte +3 indexes the `拡張用RS3_技の追加効果` table (def file:
`BYTE space[4190720]` = file 0x3FF200; one 6-byte `技の追加効果` per id,
128 entries in the bokuno ROM). The effect applies only when the 特殊設定
byte (+8) carries bit 0x80 追加効果有効 — records with the bit clear hold
stale ids the engine ignores (verified: ウィークネス/撹乱/ゴーストライト
carry ids that contradict their wiki-documented effects while every
set-bit record matches). 0xFF/0xFE also mean none.

Record layout (one `技の追加効果`):

| byte | field | bits |
|---|---|---|
| +0 | 特効 species-critical | 0x01 獣人 0x02 獣 0x03 蛇 0x04 ドラゴン 0x05 カエル 0x06 鳥 0x07 昆虫 0x08 植物 0x09 スライム 0x0A 魚 0x0B 水棲 0x0C 玄竜 0x0D 悪魔 0x0E 骸骨 0x0F 巨人 0x10-0x1F 地精系/拡張, +0x20 アンデッド +0x40 女 +0x80 男 |
| +1 | 状態異常1 | 0x01 スタン 0x02 毒 0x04 混乱 0x08 暗闇 0x10 眠り 0x20 マヒ 0x40 石化 0x80 即死 |
| +2 | 状態異常2 | 0x01 自分透明化 0x02 かすみ2段 0x04 自分強制スタン 0x80 術スタン; 0x08/0x10/0x20/0x40 = hack-era extension bits, semantics open (users: 黄龍剣 0x72, 無明剣 0x71, 不動剣 0x70) |
| +3 | 能力低下 | 0x01 物理熱防 0x02 魅 0x04 意 0x08 魔 0x10 体 0x20 早 0x40 器 0x80 腕 |
| +4 | 低下量 | per §6.2-added stat down |
| +5 | 能力上昇 | low 3 bits = amount (doubled on use), 0x08 魔防 0x10 早 0x20 体 0x40 魔 0x80 腕 |

Ids 0x00-0x2F are the vanilla table and match the kaeru 追加効果一覧
(`kaerulabo.web.fc2.com/rs3/material/additional_effect_table.html`) row
for row: 00 スタン (なぎ払い), 01 毒 (ミヅチ), 02 混乱, 03 暗闇 (サミング),
04 眠り (ブラックジャック), 05 マヒ, 06 石化 (クリスタライザー), 07 即死
(バックスタッブ), 08 術スタン, 09 自分透明化, 0A 全能力低下2 (エルフショット),
0B-1F species/effect composites, 20-25 ジャイアントスイング(1)-(5), 2A-2F
self-stat-ups (2D スマッシュ/グライダースパイク 早+腕+8 …). The hack adds
ids 0x30-0x67 and beyond; the highest id referenced by any tech/spell is
0x72. Cross-checks that anchor the hack-added ids against the bokuno wiki
(術/技 page effect notes):

- カース (spell 0x5D, eff 0x5D): record = スタン + 魔/体/早/器/腕 down 5 —
  wiki: 「[スタン　腕・器・早・体・魔5低下]」
- イーブルスピリット (0x65, eff 0x5D): same record, same wiki note
- ブラスター (0x26, eff 0x59): 即死 + all stats down 8 — wiki: 「[気絶
  腕・器・早・体・魔・意・魅・物防・魔防8低下]」
- 幻夢の一撃 series 0x17-0x1C: 混乱/眠り/毒/石化/即死 in the exact wiki
  order
- Enemy techs (16 B records, same byte +3/+8 semantics): 毒針 0x01, マヒ爪
  0x05, 石化クチバシ 0x06, クチバシ 0x03 暗闇, エルフショット 0x0A,
  マイティサイクロン/体落とし 0x00 スタン, グライダースパイク 0x2D,
  石化ガス (0x0A1) 0x06, 猛毒ガス (0x0A2/0x0A3) 0x01 — each matching its
  name/wiki effect

Dump with:

```
go run ./cmd/dumpstatus patches/bokuno_jp.sfc table     # 0x3FF200 records
go run ./cmd/dumpstatus patches/bokuno_jp.sfc techs     # + spells|enemies
```

cmd/exportbattle carries the decoded statuses into `techniques.json`
(field `statuses`, only when the 0x80 gate passes; the raw 特殊効果 byte
goes to `special`), `spells.json`, and `enemy_techs.json` (ids
0x000-0x1FF); the spark tables go to `spark.json` (see the Spark section).

## Enemy tech record (敵技性能, 16 bytes)

`技の性能` (14 B) + 見切り対応技 (+14) + 未使用 (+15), per the def file.
Stride evidence: at 16 B stride the basic swings line up with the wiki
敵技 table (ブレード hit 120 / power byte 0x0A = wiki 威力 40; 打撃 130/0;
…爪 120/0/1/2), while 14 or 15 B strides shift every field into garbage.
The engine table holds ids 0x000-0x0FF at 0x3E1D00 and hack ids 0x100-0x1FF
at 0x5B4AC0 (docs/battle-data.md 行動パターン section).

## Spark (閃き) — which techs can be learned mid-battle

Three tables hold the spark pools (group = marker byte + count byte +
count × (tech ID, difficulty), FF FF terminated; verified by walking the
patched ROM — `internal/battle/spark.go`, `TestExtSparkSwordGroup` and
friends):

| table | file offset | CPU | extent | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ext spark table (RS3拡張_技閃き派生) | 0x5E5F20 | 5E:5F20 | ends 0x5E6470 | canonical, wiki-verified; see "Engine pointer" below |
| main spark table (RS3_技閃き設定) | 0x3E3A4B | FE:3A4B | ends 0x3E3C67 | vanilla engine table, byte-identical to v1.1 |
| counter table (RS3_技閃き設定（カウンター）) | 0x3E3F1B | FE:3F1B | ends 0x3E3F3B | 7 groups, bokuno-edited difficulties |
| FE tail block | 0x3E3F0B | FE:3F0B | ends 0x3E3F19 | 3 groups, vanilla, semantics open |
| chance rows (see §4.6 of battle-formulas) | 0x68E900 / 0x68E920 | 68:E900 / 68:E920 | 2 × 32 B (27 live) | 見切り row / 閃き row; vanilla FE:3180/3195 copies are stale in bokuno |

Group markers are spark SOURCES: 0x00 素手, 0x01 剣, 0x02 大剣, 0x03 斧,
0x04 棍棒, 0x05 小剣, 0x06 槍, 0x07 弓, 0x09 氷の剣 normal attack, 0x6D 銃,
0xD4 幻魔 (the nine class groups at the table heads), and tech IDs whose
use sparks derivations (0x10 なぎ払い → 十文字斬り…, 0x11 かすみ二段 →
失礼剣…, …). Entry difficulty >= 0x80 marks entries that never spark
normally: enemy tech mirrors (0xD8-0xFF), 見切り techs, and weapon-gated
techs (e.g. 催眠 0xF3 in the 剣 derivations).

### Which table the engine reads — VERIFIED by disassembly (2026-11-16)

The spark group walk is at C2:A76A (`LDA [$AD],Y; CMP $82` = marker
compare against the spark source, then count → `2 + 2×count` stride to the
next group, C2:A778 vanilla). The table pointer differs:

- vanilla C2:A75A: `A2 4B 3A` LDX #$3A4B; `A9 FE` LDA #$FE; `85 AF` STA $AF
  → indirect long [$AD] = FE:3A4B (the main table).
- bokuno C2:A75A: `A2 20 5F` LDX #$5F20; `22 DC 04 5E` JSL $5E04DC — the
  stub picks the bank per actor struct ($9E): byte +0 == 0 and +7 == 0 →
  5B:9100 (`A2 00 91` LDX #$9100; `A9 5B` LDA #$5B; fixed-stride variant,
  groups of marker + 16 pairs, stride 0x21 = 33 B, advance via JML $5E04F0
  `A9 21`), else byte +0x0E != 0 → 5E:5F20 (67:FC00 `A9 5E` LDA #$5E),
  else 6E:5F20 (`A9 6E` LDA #$6E). So the hack ships THREE pool tables:
  5B:9100 (fixed 16-pair groups, sources include new-class codes such as
  0xAA/0xB1/0xB8), 5E:5F20 (the wiki-exact table above, classic classes),
  and 6E:5F20 (pair-style, semantics open).

The chance roll (docs/battle-formulas.md §4.6, verified): reader FE:E8A7
computes X = clamp(10 − (class level − difficulty), 0, 26) and loads the
base from row 68:E900 ($85=0, 見切り) or 68:E920 ($85≠0, 閃き) — bokuno
rewired vanilla's `BF 80 31 FE` / `BF 95 31 FE` to `BF 00 E9 68` /
`BF 20 E9 68` and widened the negative clamp #0A→#10. Wrapper 68:E940
folds any base ≥ 0xE0 to 0 (never). The comparison (C2:C0F2, vanilla
identical): `JSR $032E` → $BF = rand(0..255) (RNG table value mod 256,
C2:02A3 divides by $C6 = 256); `REP #$20; AND #$00FF; INC; CMP base; BCC`
→ success when **base > rand(0..255)+1**, P = (base−1)/256 — [gcgx]'s
見切り max 19.2% is base 50 → 49/256. The per-actor 閃きタイプ byte (+22)
has no bitmask in this path; type selection happens through the three
table switch above (actor bytes +0/+7/+0x0E) and the hack stubs JSL
$5FBF90 / $5E0530 / $5E0560 in the entry loop (per-actor byte tables
68:0B00-0F00, all FF = disabled in this ROM). "Crown" (王冠) is display
state: the earlier reading of FE:3180/3195 as 王冠あり/なし rows was
wrong — those are the vanilla 見切り row (kaeru's 見切り list verbatim)
and vanilla 閃き row; FE:31AA is the growth 境界値 row (§8.2).

The def file's space anchor for the main table (RS3_技閃き設定
space[4078155] = FE:3D4B) matches neither ROM — it is stale; the actual
main table sits at FE:3A4B in vanilla v1.1 AND bokuno, byte-identical
between the two (540 B, verified against
`Romancing Sa-Ga 3 (Japan) (Rev 1).sfc`). The counter region is likewise
original: vanilla carries the same 3-group head block (棍棒 → 切り落とし
(0x2A) d15, 術 → 乱れ雪月花 d13 + 地ずり残月 d24, 逆風の太刀 → 地ずり残月
d24) and the seven カウンター groups — vanilla 素手 → [集気法 d6,
カウンタ一 d9], 剣 → パリイ d12, 大剣 → [切り落とし d13, 無形の位 d18],
棍棒 → ジャストミート d12, 小剣 → マタドール d13, 槍 → かざぐるま d13,
無形の位 → 無刀取り d22 — of which bokuno edits the difficulties (剣
パリイ d13 …) and reduces 素手 to カウンタ一 d14. The decoder anchors by
the group walk, not the def anchors.

### Difficulties match the wiki exactly

The ext table's difficulties equal the bokuno wiki 技派生表 parenthesized
numbers entry for entry (URL:
`https://www.wikihouse.com/bokuno/index.php?%B5%BB%C7%C9%C0%B8%C9%BD`):

- 剣 normal attack → なぎ払い (07), かすみ二段 (10), 失礼剣 (11),
  十文字斬り (16), 飛水断ち (19), みじん斬り (20), バックスタッブ (22),
  龍尾返し (23), 疾風剣 (27), 残像剣 (29), 亜空間斬り (25), 五月雨斬り (33),
  分身剣 (31), 黄龍剣 (42) — ROM group 0x01 entries `10:07 11:0A 12:0B
  13:10 14:13 1E:14 15:16 16:17 17:1B 18:1D 19:19 1A:21 1B:1F 1D:2A`
- なぎ払い → 十文字斬り (13), 飛水断ち (16), 龍尾返し (22), 剣閃 (39),
  烈風剣 (29), 音速剣 (20) — ROM group 0x10
- counter table 剣 → パリイ (13), matching the wiki tree's パリイ (13)
  (the counter table is where counter-only techs live)

The FE main table holds the same techs with LOWER difficulties (剣 →
なぎ払い (3), 黄龍剣 (38)) and is byte-identical to vanilla v1.1 — it is
the original RS3_技閃き設定, left in place by the hack. The ext table
(matching the wiki, which documents the hack's behavior) is the patch's
replacement; which table the engine reads is **open** (no disassembly
evidence either way — the wiki's exact match suggests the ext table is
live). The Godot prototype uses the ext table.

### Chance roll

`diff = class level − entry difficulty`, clamped to −10..+10; the base is
the chance-table value at that diff (tables stored descending by diff in
the ROM; `battle.ChanceTable` reverses them):

- 王冠あり (crown): diff −10..+10 → 1 3 4 5 7 10 13 16 19 22 26 29 32 35
  38 40 43 45 47 48 50
- 王冠なし (no crown): 1 3 3 3 4 6 9 11 14 17 21 24 27 30 32 35 37 38 40
  40 41
- third row (semantics open): 0 0 1 1 1 1 2 3 5 8 16 32 36 40 50 60 60 70
  80 90 100

Roll shape (adopted from the 見切り system, whose chance table and roll
are engine-verified — docs/battle-formulas.md §4.4, [gcgx]
`https://gcgx.games/rs3/mikiri.html`): **spark when base > rand(1..255)**.
At diff +10 the crown base 50 gives max ≈ 19.6% per attempt.
**UNVERIFIED for the tech-spark roll itself** — no disassembly evidence;
the assumption is that the sibling table at FE:3180 uses the same
SFC-style roll as the 見切り table documented by [gcgx]. The 王冠
(crown) vs 王冠なし row split likely corresponds to aptitude
(閃きタイプ適性): the def file labels the tables 王冠ありorJP0 / 王冠なし,
and the extension defines a separate RS3拡張_適正なし技閃き確率 (21 B).

### Per-type aptitude — open

The bokuno wiki 閃きタイプ別索引 (URL:
`https://www.wikihouse.com/bokuno/index.php?%C1%AE%A4%AD%A5%BF%A5%A4%A5%D7%CA%CC%BA%F7%B0%FA`)
documents 16 spark types (00 太陽 01 剣 02 大剣 03 斧 04 棍棒 05 小剣
06 槍 07 弓 08 体術 09 銃 0A 万能 0B 月 0C 蒼龍 0D 朱鳥 0E 白虎 0F 玄武)
and which techs each type can spark; the ally struct carries a 閃きタイ
プ byte (struct 味方のステータス, byte +22 — `docs/char-stats.md` FE:0600
48 B/char), the enemy struct a 閃きLV byte (+16). The per-tech aptitude
bitmask table (one WORD per tech, one bit per type — the shape of the def
file's RS3_技習得フラグ WORD list) has **not been located** in the bokuno
ROM: scans of bank FE and the 5B/5E extension region under the wiki's
aptitude constraints (失礼剣/バックスタッブ no for 剣-type, 流星蹴り no for
any type, all 小剣 techs yes for 小剣-type) produce no candidate. The
prototype therefore keys pools by weapon class only and uses the crown
row for every roll.

Exported to `exports/data/spark.json` by `cmd/exportbattle` (chance rows
ascending by diff; groups keyed by source hex; entries `[tech-hex,
difficulty]`), consumed by `godot/battle.gd` (`_try_spark` after an ally
attack — at most one learn per action — and `_try_counter_spark` after an
enemy hit, counter group keyed on the weapon class).

## Cross-verification against the wiki

Decoder values were compared against every wiki row whose five numeric
columns are plain digits, anchored by the ROM's own name table (a wiki
row counts only if its name equals the ROM name). 威力 compared as
byte × 4, cost amount as the low 5 bits of +13.

- 技: 182 name-anchored rows; **152 match exactly** on hit, power,
  count, growth, and cost. 13 more match after name-variant normalization
  (wiki calls ids 0x01-0x07 and 0x6D 通常攻撃 where the ROM name table
  says 剣/大剣/.../銃; 神速三段突き for 0x37; 全角/半角 and 汗/一 glyph
  variants). 15 rows could not be attributed: 8 sit in the 0xE8-0xFD
  tail outside the player list, 7 are wiki rows whose ID column collides
  with a different tech (固有技 rows mis-parse on the flattened page,
  e.g. id 0x63 carries 天叢雲剣 instead of マタドール). 2 rows disagree
  (below).
- 術: 193 name-anchored rows; **187 match** on every present numeric
  column. 6 disagree, all with special wiki cells (威力 given as a
  formula like 10+35×意志 or ？, or runtime-computed hits — 妖魔の小手,
  アースライザー, 光の壁, ファイアウォール, 風と樹のうた, マッドサンダー).

Sample matches (wiki row → dump line):

- 技 0x13 十文字斬り: WP 4, 命中 120, 威力 80, 回数 2, 成長 4
  → `TECH013 十文字斬り hit=120 pow=20(80) n=2 g=4 cost=WP4`
- 技 0x17 疾風剣: WP 7, 命中 110, 威力 200, 回数 4, 成長 9
  → `TECH017 疾風剣 hit=110 pow=50(200) n=4 g=9 cost=WP7`
- 技 0x0F パリイ: wiki 基礎発動率 45 → `TECH00F パリイ hit=45 ...`
- 術 0x5A デスハンド: JP 15, 命中 255, 威力 720, 回数 2, 成長 14
  → `SPELL05A デスハンド hit=255 pow=180(720) n=2 g=14 cost=JP15`
- 術 0x14 ウィークネス: JP 4, 命中 60 → `SPELL014 ウィ一クネス hit=60 ... cost=JP4`

Reproduce with:

```
go run ./cmd/dumptechs patches/bokuno_jp.sfc /tmp/techs_out
```

## Open questions

- 技 0x18 残像剣 (ROM hit 255, power 80, 0 hits) and 技 0xC5 疾風打 (ROM
  hit 90, power 80) differ from their wiki rows (110/220/1/7 and
  255/80/2/11). Either the wiki page lags the 3.12 ROM for these two, or
  the runtime reads different records for them (both are special-cased
  techs: 分身技 and a counter).
- Ids 0xDD-0xFF of the tech table decode as plausible records with
  type=FF and enemy-flavored names (斬り払い, ふみつけ, 触手, ...). They
  are not in the wiki's player list; they may be enemy-tech mirrors or
  staging data. The def file's own 技データ listing stops at 221 entries.
- Byte +9 is unassigned in the struct dump; no hypothesis tested yet.
- Added-effect table ids 0x68-0x7F are all-zero except 状態異常2
  (+2) bits on 0x6F-0x73. RESOLVED 2026-11-16 (wiring VERIFIED by
  disassembly; damage semantics PLAUSIBLE from the bokuno wiki text):
  these are hack-era caster-side damage modifiers, not target statuses.
  The apply path is the added-effect dispatcher C2:C5BC — `LDA $FFF201,X`
  (Status1) / `$FFF202,X` (Status2) / `$FFF203,X` (StatDown). CORRECTED
  2026-11-17 (battle agent, diffed against vanilla): the Status2 bit-scan
  C2:C637 (vector table C2:C677) NO-OPS bits 0x04-0x80 — all six vector
  entries are a bare `RTS` at C2:C687, byte-identical to vanilla; only
  0x01→$C6CD and 0x02→$C6D5 apply anything. The C2:9F63/A061 handlers
  belong to the Status1 scan C2:C5E3 (table C2:C627). The damage
  modifiers are read on the DAMAGE side in two hack-added paths instead
  (docs/battle-formulas.md §13 has the full math, engine-anchored):
  bits 0x08/0x40 add attack-scaled bonuses to the raw 攻 byte before
  AND #$7F (0x08 黄龍剣/共震剣: `攻 += 5AC200[攻&7F]`, signed, up to +47
  at attack 79; 0x40 サクション: `攻 += 5AC1F0[種類と重さ&7]`),
  bits 0x10/0x20 run via the 5A:37C0 stub after the envelope ÷128
  (0x10 無明剣: `(HP snapshot − current) × 4` floored at 0; 0x20 不動剣:
  word table 602D00 indexed by the LP current/max delta). Bit → users
  (ROM rows 0x3FF200, 6 B stride; corrected 2026-11-17 per
  battle-formulas.md §13.1): 0x08 = eff 0x72 → 黄龍剣 (0x1D) +
  共震剣 (0xC1); 0x10 = eff 0x71 → 無明剣 (0xD1); 0x20 = eff 0x70 →
  不動剣 (0x26); 0x40 and 0x74 UNUSED in this ROM — the earlier
  "0x40 = eff 0x73 → サクション" attribution was wrong: サクション's own
  敵技性能 record has the added-effect byte disabled (+8 = 0x00) and no
  row carries +3 = 0x73. The per-bit
  damage math is IMPLEMENTED (internal/battle/status2.go +
  godot/battle_math.gd, ROM-anchored goldens); a live battle trace with
  one of the techs cast was not captured (none castable headless) — the
  wiring/tables/gate bytes are ROM-verified. Tech effect text:
  `https://www.wikihouse.com/bokuno/index.php?%B5%BB` (技 page, EUC-JP;
  黄龍剣/不動剣/無明剣/共震剣 rows, fetched 2026-11-16).
- 特効 low-nibble codes 0x10-0x1F are labeled 地精? in the def file;
  デスハンド (eff 0x4F) carries 0x14 where the wiki documents 人間特効 —
  0x14 may be the hack's 人間 code [single observation].
- Spell ids 0x00-0x03 are unused (0xFF-filled, no name).
- Enemy tech byte +12 (def: 種類) reads 0x04/0x14/0x24… on the basic
  weapon swings (剣/大剣/斧) where the def labels say 0x00/0x10/0x21 — it
  looks like an effect/animation id for those entries while spells carry
  the class codes (螢惑の砂 0x96 朱鳥術); semantics open.

```

`docs/translation_followup/README.txt`:

```txt
Translation follow-up after the text decoder fix (2026-11-21).

The dialogue export used to stop a text run at the single-byte glyphs
FD/FE/FF (者 聖 言), so 3493 zh-TW keys were written from truncated
originals. After the fix:

- zh-TW.review.json: event id -> {new original: old original} for the
  2594 translations moved to their new keys (difflib ratio >= 0.8, same
  line count). Their translated text was written from the truncated
  original and can miss the restored words (e.g. 冒険者に, 言って):
  re-translate them against the new original.
- zh-TW.parked.json: event id -> {old original: translation} for the
  899 keys with no confident match. They are not loaded; those pages
  show untranslated until re-translated.

```

`docs/translation_followup/transcov-anomalies.md`:

```md
# The two open --transcov anomalies (roadmap item 2c tail)

Both anomalies were recorded against the Godot harness, not a Go tool:
`--transcov` is `_transcov()` in `godot/main.gd`, walking each translated
event through the Event VM (`godot/event_vm.gd`) with `calls_enabled`
false and true on a fresh `GameState.setup_new_game` state, and printing
any walk that reaches 100 pages. Everything below was reproduced
headlessly (`godot --headless --path godot -- --transcov --lang zh-TW`)
and with scratch `--script` probes reusing the same VM; no emulator run.

Reproduction (2026-11-23):

    transcov calls=false: 2268 events, 3375 pages, 989 translated
    transcov big calls=true 0695: 110 pages, depth 0, last 達オレオレ
    transcov big calls=true 0802: 110 pages, depth 0, last 達オレオレ
    transcov big calls=true 0B4F: 110 pages, depth 0, last 達オレオレ
    (also 0696, 0697, 0B51, 0B52, 0B53 at 110, and 0565 at 169)
    transcov calls=true: 2268 events, 4535 pages, 948 translated

No tax-family event (0900-095F) reached the 100-page print.

## 1. Tax-menu re-entry at depth ~475 (090F-0953) — stale; loop no longer exists, but a real off-by-one remains underneath

The re-entry cycle is in the bytes: the family's shared body calls
itself and tail-dispatches back into the menu.

- 090F entry FC:586b: `04 19` (call 0419, the intro check), FC:586f
  `09 11` (call 0911), FC:5871 `09 12` (call 0912, the tax fragment).
- 0912's shared body: FC:5a76 `09 0f` (call 090F — re-entry), FC:5a78
  and FC:5a86 `32 09 10` (tail dispatch to 0910), FC:61f7 `32 09 16`,
  FC:6207 `32 09 0f`.

The recorded depth ~475 belongs to the interpreter before the two
2026-11-20 frame commits:

- before `op 2E returns` (70c5b01): op 2E closed a window instead of
  popping, so every `09 xx` call frame stayed on the stack for good;
- before `op 32 tail-dispatches` (952dd5e): `32 09 10` was transparent,
  so 0915's callee (`09 15` -> event 0915, entry FC:5a7b, ending
  `32 09 10`) ran on linearly through the following fragments instead of
  replacing the script.

In that interpreter the cycle 0912 -> `09 0f` -> 090F -> `09 12` -> 0912
pushed call frames every pass and never popped one ("the harness repeats
中止" = the selGoto fallback re-picking the cancel branch each pass);
`all_pages`' 1000-page guard stopped the walk at depth ~475.

Today both commits landed and the loop does not reproduce. Headless
transcov prints no 09xx walk; probes walking 090F/0910/0911/0912/0914/
0915 with calls on end after 1-3 pages, every `09 xx` call balanced by
op 2E and every `32 xx xx` replacing the script. The item can be closed
as stale.

### The real defect found underneath: op 27 optC is counted as an option

`event_vm.gd` increments the option count for both markers:

    if note == "optB" or note == "optC":
        menu_options.append(_option_text)
        state.menu_count += 1

The engine does not count op 27. From patches/bokuno_jp.sfc
(file offset = CPU address, bank C0 at $400000):

- op 25 optA C0:1F49: `9c c0 d3` STZ $D3C0; `9c c1 d3` STZ $D3C1;
  `9c bf d3` STZ $D3BF; JMP $1C7A.
- op 26 optB C0:1F55: copies the window state at index $D3C1 and ends
  `ee c1 d3` INC $D3C1; `a9 01 8d c0 d3` LDA #1 STA $D3C0; JMP $1C7A.
- op 27 optC C0:1F9E..C0:2043 (ends JMP $1C7A): STZ $D015, STZ $D3C0,
  display calls over $D3BF (`jsr $3835/$38ae/$06f4/$3860`, `ee bf d3`
  INC / `ce bf d3` DEC / `8d bf d3` STA / `9c bf d3` STZ on $D3BF),
  one read `ad c1 d3` LDA $D3C1 — **no write to $D3C1 anywhere in the
  body**. docs/vm-semantics.md §2.3's "builds the same way as 26" is
  wrong about the count.
- selGoto fallback C0:2E7A: `ad bf d3; c9 ff; d0 04; ad c1 d3; 3a` —
  r = $D3BF, or $D3C1 - 1 when nothing was picked.

So wherever a menu ends with op 27, the VM's fallback r = menu_count - 1
is one past the engine's, and the branch lands one 2-byte record beyond
the table:

- 0910 main menu (6 options: optA FC:58be, optB x6, optC FC:58e6,
  selGoto FC:58ea, records FC:58eb-FC:58f5): VM menu_count 7 (probe:
  `final menu_count=7`), fallback r=6 -> record at FC:58f7, which is
  the middle of the `48 00 03 80 4d 00` fill op at FC:58f6, so it is
  not in the address index and the VM silently sets `_finished` — the
  walk dies mid-menu. Probe evidence: 0912 entered directly stops at
  `T65 STEP addr=FC:58ea` (the selGoto) with `finished=true` and one
  stranded `09 15` call frame (final depth 1) — a frame leaked past the
  end of the walk.
- 0912/0914 tax-rate menu (4 options: optA FC:5a01, optB x4, optC
  FC:5a1e, selGoto FC:5a22, records FC:5a23/25/27/29): fallback r=4 ->
  record FC:5a2b, which is the 軽い税 handler (`40 10 0a` sets the 10%
  rate) — cancel would silently apply light tax instead of running the
  reopen-menu word `09 10` at FC:5a29.
- two-choice prompts (optB + optC): fallback r=1 instead of the
  engine's r=0. Probe evidence in the 0802 chain:
  `SELGOTO addr=FC:d099 sel=1 target=FC:d09c` — the second choice where
  the engine's fallback picks the first.

With engine semantics (op 27 not counted) every fallback lands on the
real last option: main menu 終わり -> `2a` closeWin at FC:58f5, tax-rate
menu 中止 -> `09 10` at FC:5a29 (reopen the main menu). The walks then
terminate: rate-menu cancel reopens 0910, whose 終わり path redraws the
status lines and returns through op 2E.

### Harness fix (described, not implemented)

1. `godot/event_vm.gd`: count options only for `optB` —
   `if note == "optB": menu_options.append(_option_text);
   state.menu_count += 1`, and let `optC` fall through to the
   transparent path. This makes the selGoto fallback match C0:2E7A
   arithmetic everywhere (main menu, rate menu, 2-choice prompts).
   Interactive `pending_choices` inherits the same correction (op 27
   rows were never engine options).
2. Optional hardening in `_transcov` (godot/main.gd): a menu with no
   player is a walk boundary — stop after the first selGoto pause
   (e.g. install a choice handler that ends the walk) so menu-driven
   events contribute only their pre-menu pages, instead of simulating
   an engine fallback pick.

## 2. 110 pages at depth 0 (0695/0802/0B4F-0B53) — real callee text on a fresh-state path, no misinterpreted op

Per-page attribution probe (same VM, calls on, fresh state):

    === event 0695: 110 pages, final depth 0, finished true
        from 0695: 1 pages
        from 0B52: 84 pages
        from 0B62/0B64/0B66/0B67/0B69/0B6B/0B6D: 3 pages each
        from 0B70/0B73: 2 pages each
    === event 0802: 110 pages (0B52 85 + the same callee pages)
    === event 0B4F: 110 pages (identical distribution)

The chain, op by op:

1. 0695 -> 0802: `08 02` at FB:ce4f (also FB:ce6c, FB:ce83) — queue
   word 0x0802, call-with-return through C0:B847 (vm-semantics §2.8,
   VERIFIED). Later passes of the same word produce no pages because
   the first pass mutates state (e.g. `36 81 04` setFlag at FC:cff2),
   so the re-entry takes different gate arms — the engine mutates the
   same way.
2. 0802 -> 0B4F -> 0B51 -> 0B52: three op 45 chkMem gates whose TRUE
   arm is an event dispatch (tail dispatch, frame replaced, no push —
   hence depth 0 at the end, exactly as recorded):
   - 0802 FC:090e `41 10 03 ef` (EF00[10..11] = $EF03), FC:0912
     `45 10 00` chkMem WRAM[$EF03] == 0 -> event 0B4F;
   - 0B4F FC:c9e3 `41 10 02 ef`, FC:c9e7 `45 10 00` -> event 0B51;
   - 0B51 FC:ca14 `45 10 00` -> event 0B52.
   All three compare a WRAM context byte against 0 and pass on the
   fresh state (0 == 0). Tail dispatch cannot grow depth; op 43's
   `STZ $77` exists precisely because depth persists across dispatches
   (vm-semantics §2.3 op 32).
3. 0B52 (battle-aftermath cutscene): three waves of unconditional
   member-fragment calls — `0b 62`..`0b 73` queue words at
   FC:cfab-cfdb, FC:d370-d3bf, FC:d4e3-d548 — each callee returns
   through op 2E (frames balanced, final depth 0), interleaved with
   chkFlag/chkMem gates that on the fresh state take the FALSE arms
   (flags zero) and TRUE arms (0 == 0). Only some callees show text on
   this state (0B62/0B64/0B66/0B67/0B69/0B6B/0B6D 3 pages each,
   0B70/0B73 2 pages each; 0B63/0B65/0B6C/0B6E/0B71/0B72/0B68/0B6A
   return without pages because their internal gates fail).

Verdict: every one of the 110 pages sits on a real dispatch or call
edge, and the text is the real dialogue of the callee fragments — the
walk misinterprets nothing. What the count is not: a gameplay-true
number. It is the fresh-GameState reading — $EF02/$EF03 == 0 passes the
scenario gates, zero flags pick the FALSE arms, and the 0 == 0 chkMem
gates let every member fragment speak (pages thank ハリード/トーマス/
ユリアン/エレン/モニカ in one run). In play the same edges exist but
state values select a subset. Consequence for the coverage metric:
`--transcov` page counts are fresh-state coverage, not per-event
playback truth; pinning the gameplay-true set needs per-event state
setup (an emulator-side check of $EF02/$EF03 at the opening battle can
validate the three gates).

Same signature, not investigated further: 0565 walks to 169 pages, all
from 0565 itself (party-name pages; the party-list menu at FB:7a89
`41 00 32 ef` + `45 00 a9` chkMem over $EF32 and a selGoto loop at
FB:7aa6) — the same fresh-state gate readings driving a loop.

```
