`docs/triggers.md`:

```md
# RS3 submap triggers: exits, event points, placed characters (bokuno_jp.sfc)

How the game wires maps to movement: which tiles trigger which native
event, and which tiles move the party to another map. Decoded from the
community analysis (2-658氏 `サブマップ解析.txt` in
`新バイナリ神ロダ補完/ツール・テキスト.zip`, plus the AL982 supplement and
the RS3MapEditor2 manual) and byte-verified against
`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` (SHA-256 `4793e142…`). Decoder:
`internal/triggers`. CLI: `cmd/dumptriggers`. Map records and addressing
as in docs/map-format.md (banks C0-FF → file `(bank-0xC0)*0x10000`).

## Where triggers live

```
submap record (per map, via the hack's 5A6A50 table; docs/map-format.md "Fixed data regions")
├── block 1  display header; flag2/flag3 gate optional fields
├── block 2  placed characters, each with an event id        (flag3 0x80)
├── block 3  chests, screen effects, animation,
│            X-button + map-edge events,
│            event point list (ids, terminated by 0xFF)
├── block 4  movement destinations, 5 bytes per 10xx id
└── property layer (separate pointer)
             └── 0x08/0x09 records = event point rectangles
```

The event point list in block 3 supplies only the ids, in order. The
positions come from the map's property layer: every record with flag
`0x08`/`0x09` is one event point rectangle, associated with the list in
left-top-first order (2-658氏; the sorted pairing is confirmed for maps
0x02/0x04, where the stored order is also raster order — see OPEN
questions).

## Block 1 (header) — fields beyond docs/map-format.md

After the fields map-format.md documents:

```
禁止操作        1
flag2           1
flag3           1
[2]             if flag2 bit0 (0x01)
count + 4*count if flag2 bit1 (0x02)   (AL982: animation objects)
```

Two deviations from 2-658氏 that the byte checks forced:

- when flag1 bit5 (0x20) is set, the header carries **two extra
  undocumented bytes after the palette set id** (the doc places two
  `不明[1byte]` there). Verified by map 0x19 (flag1 0xE2): without the
  skip the character block misparses.
- flag1 bit6 (0x40) gates the layer-2 pointer's presence: with the bit
  clear the 3 bytes are absent entirely (docs/map-format.md's
  `ReadHeader` always reads it — only correct for bit6-set maps).

VERIFIED: map 0x02 and map 0x04 walk every block to exactly the last
byte of their records with zero leftovers (130 and 125 bytes; the
records are identical in the 3.12plus variant per the AL982 list).

## Block 2 — placed characters (flag3 0x80)

Repeated until a flag byte with bit7 set. Each byte of flag4 gates a
field (fields are in this order; see the inheritance rule below):

```
flag4           bit7 end, bit6 設置判定, bit0 SAVE marker
[2]             bit5 (0x20): placement check (flag id, window byte)
[3]             bit4 (0x10): X, Y, facing (facing in bits 6-7: 0=up? 1..3)
[1]             bit3 (0x08): graphic id
[2]             bit2 (0x04): event id, LITTLE-endian
[2]             bit1 (0x02): 性質 (quality), little-endian
```

**Engine semantics (disassembled 2026-11-16, `C0:3E07`-`3E82` + the spawn
routine `C0:4A79`; this replaces the "inherit from the previous
character" reading).** The walker keeps a 10-byte save set ($B904-$B90D)
beside the staged fields ($B90E-$B917):

- every entry starts by restoring the staged fields FROM the save set
  (`JSR $4A3D` at the loop top, `C0:3E0E` — a NEAR JSR, so the routine
  is C0:4A3D, verified `AD 04 B9` LDA $B904; an earlier note misread it
  as bank 4A, whose file bytes are zero), then overwrites the fields
  its flag4 carries;
- flag bit0 set → the staged fields are stored INTO the save set
  (`JSR $4A02` = C0:4A02, verified `AD 0E B9 8D 04 B9` LDA $B90E /
  STA $B904, at `C0:3E7A`) before the spawn. bit0 is a **save marker**,
  not an inherit marker: a field an entry carries does NOT reach later
  entries unless that entry also has bit0;
- fields present in neither entry nor save set read as zero. The engine's
  save set begins each block from WRAM leftovers of earlier loads (not
  reinitialized) — `triggers.Decode` approximates it with zeros. Blocks
  whose early entries inherit from that initial set (no bit0 save before
  them) are exposed to the difference: map 0x4F's townsfolk event ids
  read 0 under the approximation, the engine's leftover value at runtime.
- flag bit6 (設置判定) gates the spawn: bit6 clear → the entry spawns
  unconditionally (`INC $8E` at `C0:3E25`, `LDA $8E / BNE $4A9C` in the
  spawn routine bypasses the check); bit6 set → the engine fetches the
  2-bit value of WRAM flag `$B90E` (from `$7EF46A + id/2`, low/high
  nibble by id bit0 — `C0:370D`; event ids 0x0Cxx/0x4Cxx use the variants
  `$5AB044`/`$5AE004`, dispatched at `$5AAD50`) and spawns only while
  `$B90F>>4 <= value < ($B90F&0x0F)+1`. The outcome is runtime flag
  state, so `Decode` exports `Judged`, `PlaceID` and `PlaceLo` per NPC
  and does not apply the gate.

Evidence for the field layout unchanged: across 503 characters on the
first 256 maps, the little-endian reading of the event id yields 472 ids
in the valid native ranges (≤0x1FFF block tables, 0x0Cxx, 0x0Exx,
0x31xx, 0x4Cxx) against 31 suspect; big-endian fails on 184. The ids
resolve into banks FA/FB: map 0x02's NPCs carry 0x0574–0x0578 and all
five walk to `end` in `data/events/` (`fb7f0b`–`fb7fa8`). The value
0x2000 recurs on battle-placed characters (wharf and dungeon maps) and
is accepted verbatim.

Map 0x02 (Pidona old town) decodes to six townsfolk, all positions
within the 64x64 map: (54,22), (37,45), (26,26), (40,13), (10,16),
(17,50) — the last one stands exactly on the map's second event point.

**Duplicate coordinates are engine-true.** Map 0x249's 14 entries are
one 0x2000 battle monster at (36,52), a kind-05 馬 (g=0x61) at (36,52),
and TWELVE flag-0x00 continuations stacked at (16,63) (raw bytes
`38B88A`: `1F 24 34 F0 00 00 20 00 01 | 09 61 | 1B 10 3F 40 63 00 01 |
00 ×12 | FF`). Every one of them reaches the spawn routine, and no entry
carries flag bit6 — the walker's `INC $8E` (`C0:3E25`) then bypasses the
placement gate for every entry (`LDA $8E / BNE $4A9C` in the spawn
routine) — so all 14 slots spawn unconditionally: the engine stacks the
slots (`X += $0040` per spawn, `C0:4BEC`), the parse does not
over-count, and the duplicates can only be hidden by runtime
despawn logic outside the loader. Golden tests:
`TestDecodeNPCSaveSet`, `TestDecodeMap0249NPCs`.

On the parse fix: the previous per-entry inheritance misread 181 entries
on 36 maps (e.g. map 0x4F's nine flag-0x58 townsfolk took event id
0x0C00 from a non-saving earlier entry; the engine gives them the save
set's event id 0).

A runtime probe for the spawn/skip outcome was attempted
(`tools/emulator/dupnpc_249.lua`) and never produced a line: exec
callbacks on bank C0 addresses never fire in this harness (a control
watch on rip.lua's proven bank-5E address fires, so the mechanism works
for bank 5E), and write watches on WRAM `$D9`/`$B90E` stayed silent
although the analogous `$D2E3` write watch (shot_d2e3_probe.lua) is
byte-proven working — mechanism unresolved, see the script header for
the variants tried. The static reading above does not depend on it.

## Block 3 — event data

Sub-blocks appear in this order, each gated by one flag bit:

| flag | block | layout |
|---|---|---|
| flag3 0x40 | treasure chests | count, then per chest: open obj, closed obj, content flag, [content id], open flag id, X, Y, [event id] — the content id is present when content flag bits 2-3 != 0x08, otherwise a 2-byte LITTLE-endian event id is (7 vs 8 bytes) |
| flag3 0x20 | display-range masks | 5 bytes |
| flag3 0x10 | transparency | 1 + (2 if flag byte bit5) + 4 |
| flag3 0x08 | unknown | count + 2*count |
| flag3 0x04 | animation | count, then count × 2-byte words (little-endian), +1 extra byte per word >= 0xFC00 |
| flag3 0x02 | X-button event | 2 bytes, BIG-endian |
| flag2 0x04 | undocumented | 2 bytes (see below) |
| flag2 0x80 | unknown | 2 bytes |
| flag2 0x40 | map-edge events | N, S, W, E — 4 × 2-byte BIG-endian ids |
| flag2 0x20 | battle | default background 1 byte, + 2 bytes if flag3 0x01 clear |
| flag2 0x10 | unknown | flag byte, then 4-byte groups {0x80-marker, 3-byte SNES pointer} while the marker's high bit is set |
| flag2 0x08 | transition | effect + two sound ids, 3 bytes |
| — | event point list | 2-byte BIG-endian ids until a 0xFF byte |

Two additions beyond 2-658氏, both forced by the byte walks:

- **flag2 bit2 (0x04) skips 2 bytes** between the X-button block and the
  event point list. Without it, maps with that bit (e.g. the Pidona pub
  0x05) read a garbage first list entry; with it, map 0x05's list reads
  clean (`10 00`, `05 48`) and the record ends exactly at its last byte.
  Placement relative to the other sub-blocks is unverified (no test map
  combines 0x04 with the later flag2 blocks).
- **flag2 bit1 (0x02) also adds the count + 4-byte-entries block to
  block 1** (AL982's supplement), consumed before block 2.

Endianness of the ids is **big-endian in block 3** (movement ids are
0x10xx: byte `0x10` then the sequential xx — little-endian reading would
make them 0x0110, contradicting both the doc's "10xx" and the
destination pairing below). Note the contrast with block 2, where event
ids are little-endian.

Map 0x02's list: `10 02`, `05 4E`, end. Map 0x04's: `10 01` × 4, end.

## Block 4 — movement destinations

Immediately after the list's 0xFF terminator, one 5-byte record per
destination, identical to the 移動イベント struct in the bokuno patch's
`05_構造体.def.txt`:

```
0   flag: bit4-7 transition effect (0 normal, 1 fall, 2 shake, 3 whiteout),
        bit3 hide character, bit2 music change valid, bit0-1 new facing
1-2 little-endian word: bits 10-15 music id (<=0x3F), bits 0-9 map id
3   target X
4   target Y
```

The little-endian word is confirmed by semantics: map 0x04's records
read map `0x000` at (56,22), map `0x001` at (88,56) and map `0x2A9` at
(105,39) — all Pidona maps, all landing tiles inside the targets
(128x64); the big-endian reading gives Godwin's Cave, which the wharf
cannot reach. Map 0x02's records read map 0x000 at (4,18), map 0x010
(魔王殿) at (15,58) with music change, and 0x303/0x301 (both ピドナ旧市街
in the 2-658 CSV) at (17,30) and (21,32).

The id `10xx` in the list/edge/X-button positions references record `xx`
of this block **from zero** (map 0x02's east edge event `1000` lands on
record 0 = the new-streets door). Records unreferenced by any list entry
exist (map 0x04's record 0, the 0x2A9 wharf variant) and are exported
verbatim as `Destinations`.

## Property layer — event point rectangles

The block-1 prop pointer targets a sequence of chunks:

```
u16 size (little-endian)
records filling exactly `size` bytes:
    flag     1
    X        1
    Y        1
    size     flag odd (0x09): 1 byte, hi nibble = X span, lo nibble = Y span
             flag even (0x08): 2 bytes, X then Y
4-byte tail    skipped after each chunk (contents unknown: observed
               00000000, 01010100, 01011fff, 1e1e1e00)
```

Records with flag `0x08`/`0x09` are the event points ("イベント発生ポイント
(扉で移動など)", 2-658氏). Other documented flags: 02/03, 04/05 (meaning
unknown), 10/11, 20/21 (display-range mask), 40/41 (draw in front of
characters), 80/81 (draw behind characters). W/H are stored as span-1
(analogous to the header's sizeX/sizeY convention) — the +1 is a
convention choice, not verified.

The layer has **no stored end** and neighboring maps' prop pointers
alias into each other's layers (map 0x6B's pointer lands on map 0x04's
third chunk), so `internal/triggers` bounds the walk by the next larger
property pointer in the table and widens it while fewer rectangles than
list entries come out. Map 0x02 yields exactly its two points,
(16,34) 1x1 and (17,50) 1x1; map 0x04 yields five, of which four are
in bounds: (31,5) 4x1, (22,39), (20,28), (34,29) — the fifth, (16,89),
is outside the 128x64 map and ignored.

Pairing: rectangles are sorted by (Y, X) — the doc's "左上から順に…関連
付けられる" — and matched against the list ids by index. Map 0x02:
(16,34) → `1002` (exit to 旧市街 map 0x303), (17,50) → `054E` (native
event; id exists but its slot duplicates a neighboring event in the FA/FB
block table, so no standalone dump). Map 0x04's four list entries are
all `1001` → every exit tile leads to map 0x000 at (56,22).

## The 0x2xxx field ids are NOT an encounter class — decoded 2026-11-18

triggers.md's open question 2 ("the recurring char event id 0x2000 — how the
engine maps it to an encounter") is CLOSED with a negative result: **0x2xxx
placed characters and event-point rectangles dispatch nothing.** The real
field battle-encounter class is the placed-character ids **0x18xx/0x19xx**
(1467 NPCs in the decode set; map 0x250's road monsters 0x1862/0x186A).
Evidence, all byte-anchored in `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` unless noted:

**Both field dispatchers enqueue the id as a VM queue word, byteswapped.**

- Touch dispatcher **C0:AB2E** (party bumps an NPC — called from C0:5656
  with Y = NPC slot; the chase variant C0:8049 calls it with arg 1 when a
  monster with behavior bits 1/3 reaches the party, via the aggro check
  C0:7A38): `REP #$20; LDA $D9D2,Y; PHA; JSR $AF91` — the id word read
  a16 at $D9D2,Y is the byte-swap of the big-endian id (spawn stores
  `id>>8` at $D9D2 and `id&0xFF` at $D9D3, C0:4AAA-4AAE), so NPC id
  `1862` enqueues the word `6218` = op `18`, operand `62`.
  Immediately after the enqueue: `CMP #$18 / BEQ done; CMP #$19 / BEQ
  done` (C0:AB49-AB4F) — ops 18/19 (the battle dispatch words,
  docs/vm-semantics.md §4.7.1) return WITHOUT the facing flip that every
  other id applies to the touched character. Every other id gets the
  standard queue treatment: op 17 = objOp, ops 00-0E = event calls, low
  byte >= 0x20 = skipped by the queue processor 5A:E654.
- Event-point rectangle dispatcher **C0:EA6B** (walked onto a prop-layer
  rectangle; rect X coords at WRAM `$D2FF,X`, id words at DP `$0037,X`,
  both per-map copies): same enqueue of the byteswapped id word, then
  `PLA; AND #$00FF; CMP #$0010` (C0:EAA6-EAAD) — movement ids `10xx`
  byteswap to words with low byte `10` (op 10 = the map-move dispatch,
  C0:C1DF, the "undecoded single" of vm-semantics §2.8).

**Consequence for 0x2xxx:** byteswapped, id `2000` is the word `0020`, id
`2005` is `0520`, id `221A` is `1A22` — every one has queue-word low byte
`0x20`-`0x22`, and the queue processor skips every word with low byte
>= `$20` (5A:E654, vm-semantics §2.8, machine-verified there). A 0x2xxx
bump therefore falls through to the facing-flip path (the monster turns
toward the party) and dispatches nothing. The id's own low nibble never
reaches the battle chain.

**The 0x18xx/0x19xx battle chain, end to end** (live MesenCE trace,
tools/emulator/enc_dispatch.lua, run /tmp/encdisp/run1, unattended boot →
intro → road map 0x250 walk; the party bumped a placed 0x1862 monster):

```
WQUEUE frame=29391 addr=7ED6BD val=18 pc=C0:AF98 a=6218 x=0000 y=0040
WQUEUE frame=29391 addr=7ED6BE val=62 pc=C0:AF98 a=6218 x=0000 y=0040
W1314 frame=29392 val=18 pc=C0:BFB4 a=0018 x=0030 y=0000
W1306 frame=29392 val=62 pc=C0:C048 a=0062 x=0000 y=0000
FEREAD frame=29425 addr=FE77FC val=00 pc=5A:7674 a=0040 x=0040 y=0020
FEREAD frame=29425 addr=FE77FB val=20 pc=5A:7682 a=0000 x=0040 y=0020
BATTLE-START frame=29444
```

and, in the same run, 30 s after that battle ended, a bump of a slot
whose id word read `0x0020` (the 0x2000 class) enqueued and dispatched
nothing:

```
WQUEUE frame=30981 addr=7ED6BD val=20 pc=C0:AF98 a=0020 x=0000 y=FFFF
WQUEUE frame=30981 addr=7ED6BE val=00 pc=C0:AF98 a=0020 x=0000 y=FFFF
```

(no `WD51B` line follows it; the next event dispatch is minutes later).

Semantics, per docs/battle-data.md 敵編成 section: op 18 → C0:BFAF sets
`$1314=$18` and `$1306` = word high byte = id low byte; battle init
S_C2_09F4 copies `$141B = $1306`; S_C2_13EA reads race = `$141B & 0x0F`
(0x62 → race 2), the enemy-level band comes from S_C2_15E6 (per-race
enemy level `$F533[race]` at fresh game = 0, rolls bounded by the party
size stay under 32 → band 0; the trace's pair read at X = `race*32 +
band*2` = 0x40 = race 2, band 0 ✓), and the FE:77BB pair (leader 0x20
地狼, hensei 0) seeds the battle record. Id high nibble `F` selects the
preset-party variant S_C2_1461; `$141B & 0x0F` is still the race.

**Port consequence:** godot battles fire on NPC/rect ids 0x18xx/0x19xx
with race = id & 0x0F, band 0 at fresh game; 0x2xxx NPCs and rectangles
stay silent (engine-true), so map 0x249's monster sprites turn toward
the party but never battle — map 0x250 carries the battle-capable
monsters. Runtime state (`$F533` race levels) that would move the band
past 0 is battle-count-driven and not yet modeled.

Survey tool: `go run ./cmd/encounterscan patches/bokuno_jp.sfc` (id-class
census over all decodable maps: 0x18xx = 1204 NPCs / 19 rects, 0x19xx =
263 NPCs, 0x2xxx = 432 NPCs + 66 rects).

## op 0x11 mapJump

`11 xx` — 2 bytes: opcode + destination index. VM-wise it is a dispatch
word (docs/vm-semantics.md §2.8: enqueued to the effect machinery); its
effect is a map jump into the **global destination table at file
0x3CFB00**, one 5-byte record per entry in exactly the block-4 layout
above. `xx` indexes from zero; the table holds exactly 256 entries and
ends at 0x3D0000, where the FD bank pointer page starts — a one-byte
operand with no gaps, matching `ControlLen[0x11] = 2` in
`internal/bokuno/ops.go`.

Evidence: the table decodes plausibly at every entry (all map ids
≤0x3FF, all music ids ≤0x3F); the hottest operands in the dumps resolve
to named places, e.g. `11 00` → map 0x239 (16,16), `11 11` → map 0x04B
(23,39), `11 2B` → map 0x0C9 (16,37). 3690+ occurrences across the dump
set use only this 2-byte form. In-event `10xx` ids are a *different*
mechanism (the per-map block 4); `11 xx` is the global table.

## Verification status

Verified against ROM bytes (multiple independent signals agree):

- block 1 field walk incl. flag1-bit5 extra bytes and the flag2-bit1
  extension; maps 0x02/0x04 walk both to their exact record end
- block 2 field order, inheritance, little-endian event ids (472:31
  id-validity over 503 characters; 0574-0578 dump round-trip)
- block 3 sub-block order and sizes; the flag2-bit2 2-byte skip
- event list big-endian ids with 0xFF terminator; 10xx = movement
- block 4 5-byte records, little-endian map/music word, zero-based xx
  (map 0x02's east edge → map 0x000 (4,18))
- property chunk grammar [u16 size][records][4-byte tail] on maps
  0x02/0x04/0x05; 0x08/0x09 rectangles as event points
- global jump table: exactly 256 × 5 bytes at 0x3CFB00, ending at the
  FD bank boundary

Not fully verified (decoded plausibly; exact engine semantics unknown):

- the 4-byte property chunk tail and the size-field +1 convention
- raster-order pairing (the doc asserts it; maps 0x02/0x04 cannot
  distinguish stored from sorted order because they agree)
- the flag2-bit2 skip's placement among the other sub-blocks
- chest event-id endianness (read little-endian, like block 2; single
  sample: map 0x0D's chest → 0x056B)
- facing values (raw bits 6-7/0-1 exported; 0-3 = up/left/right/down?
  unconfirmed)
- op 0x11's engine-side effect (transition effect id mapping), and the
  block-2 性質 field beyond its coarse split (high byte = sprite kind,
  indexed into the `$F80000` table at `C0:4B90-4B9D` — the `05` 馬 … `3B`
  カムシーン kinds docs/sprites.md lists; low byte = behavior bits
  stored to `$D9B2,X` at `C0:4B31-4B59`; per-bit meanings unverified)

## Usage

```
go run ./cmd/dumptriggers patches/bokuno_jp.sfc /tmp/triggers_out
```

writes `map0002.json`, `map0004.json`, `jump_table.json`. Extend
`renderedIDs` in `cmd/dumptriggers/main.go` for more maps; maps whose
record is zeroed report `triggers.ErrZeroed`. API:
`triggers.Decode(rom, id) (*MapTriggers, error)` with `Exits`,
`Triggers`, `NPCs`, `Chests`, `EdgeEvents`, `XButtonEvent`,
`Destinations` and per-map `Warnings`; `triggers.JumpTable(rom)` for the
op-0x11 destinations.

```

`docs/vm-semantics.md`:

```md
# bokuno 3.12 event VM — control-flow and data op semantics

Semantics of the event-VM control-flow and data ops of
「ぼくのかいぞうしたさいこうの3.12」, for the Godot reimplementation.
Evidence classes:

- **VERIFIED** — read from engine machine code in the patched ROM
  (`patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`, SHA-256 `4793e142…f2da0`) **and** consistent
  with the 3,690 dumps in `data/events/`. Engine addresses are CPU
  addresses; file offset = `(bank-0xC0)*0x10000` for banks C0–FF,
  `bank*0x10000` for banks 0x40–0x7D.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — one independent source (community doc, ref tool
  comment, or dump statistics only).

## 1. Runtime architecture

Engine facts below are VERIFIED unless marked otherwise.

### 1.1 Interpreter state (direct page, lives in WRAM page 0)

| DP   | meaning |
|------|---------|
| `$76` | frame active flag (1 = script running) |
| `$77` | call depth (0 = root frame) |
| `$78/$79` | script PC, low/high byte of the 24-bit fetch pointer |
| `$7A` | fetch pointer bank byte |
| `$7B/$7C` | current frame's end address (event `end16`); PC == end ends the frame |

One op step = `JSL $C0:1B8F` → `JSR $C0:1B93` (C0:1B93, returns after one op):

```
1B93: if ($76 == 0) return            ; no active frame
1BB6: if (PC == end) JSR $C0:3756     ; pop frame / end event
1BC6: JSL $5A:AFA0                    ; classify next op (see 1.3)
1BCA: BCC -> $1BDD                    ; carry clear: dispatch-word op
1BCC: CMP #$50 ; BCS -> $1C29         ; >= 0x50: text/glyph run
1BD0: JMP $5A:AFE0                    ; else: control-op dispatch
```

There is no automatic PC increment: each handler advances PC itself with
`INC $78` as it consumes bytes, then jumps to `JMP $C0:1C7A` (INC once +
end-check + return) as its last byte, or returns directly when PC should
stay on a byte that the *next* step must execute as an op.

### 1.2 Text path

Ops ≥ 0x50 and the 2-byte glyph ranges (0x20–0x23, 0x18, 0x46 lead
bytes) are text: the run is copied into the text buffer at WRAM
`$D56D`, which is itself executed as a script with fetch bank `$7E`
(frame switch at C0:3245, return records same as §1.4). Text-copy
contract: byte `0x00`/`0x50` terminates; a lead byte `< 0x50` copies one
more byte (engine C0:3126/3222/3309, also `copyName` in
`ref/source/BOKUNO_COMPAT_VM_PROJECT/tools/rs3_runtime_text_v30.mjs`).

### 1.3 Op classification and the dispatch table

Vanilla code at C0:1BC6 was `LDA [$78]; CMP #$20; BCC enqueue-path;
CMP #$50; BCS text-path` (vanilla bytes `a7 78 c9 20 90 11 c9 50 b0 59`,
unchanged in the patched ROM). The patched game replaces the first two
instructions with `JSL $5A:AFA0` — bokuno's classifier, which for every
normal op returns A = opcode and, for ops `0x0D` and `0x49`, the
redirect value `0x37`. Control then reaches `5A:AFE0`:

```
AFE0: CMP #$37 / BNE $AFEE
AFE4:   LDA [$78]           ; re-read opcode byte
AFE6:   CMP #$0D / BEQ $AFF6 ; -> 0D-mode dispatch
AFEA:   CMP #$49 / BEQ $B009 ; -> 49-sub dispatch
AFEE: SEC / SBC #$20 / ASL A  ; index = (op-0x20)*2
AFF2: JMP $C0:1BD4           ; -> table dispatch
```

C0:1BD4: `STA $8D; STZ $8E; LDX $8D; JMP ($3AD6,X)`.

**The table at C0:3AD6 is therefore indexed by `(op-0x20)*2` in the
patched game.** (The same bytes also form a table indexed by raw opcode
`X = op` — that was the vanilla indexing, dead after the patch
redirected `C0:1BD0` from `JMP $C0:1BD4` to `JMP $5A:AFE0`.) Effective
handler map used by the patched game (VERIFIED — several entries
cross-checked against behavior, e.g. `3A→32EC` reads `$EF00[id]` for the
item-name text macro, `4E→2254` is skip, `2F→2E73` is selGoto):

| op | handler | op | handler | op | handler | op | handler |
|----|---------|----|---------|----|---------|----|---------|
| 25 | 1F49 | 2F | 2E73 | 39 | 31F2 | 43 | 277D |
| 26 | 1F55 | 31 | 1F97 | 3A | 32EC | 44 | 3445 |
| 27 | 1F9E | 32 | 2F14 | 3B | 30B4 | 45 | 2F22 |
| 28 | 212F | 33 | 2F5F | 3C | 332F | 46 | 1C8C |
| 29 | 2149 | 34 | 2FC1 | 3D | 337B | 48 | 21FD |
| 2A | 217B | 35 | 3009 | 3E | 340B | 49* | 2B5B |
| 2B | 24E5 | 36 | 3051 | 3F | 1E5D | 4A | 226F |
| 2C | 26C9 | 37 | 3069 | 40 | 2226 | 4B | 2277 |
| 2D | 2756 | 38 | 3087 | 41 | 30A3 | 4C | 2B4E |
| 2E | 2779 | — | — | 42 | 3149 | 4D | 2267 |
|    |      |    |      |    |      | 4E | 2254 |
|    |      |    |      |    |      | 4F | 1C8F |

(*the 49 row of this table is the money-gate handler at 2B5B in the
patched table; op 49's real sub-dispatch is `JMP ($FE00,X)` at 5A:B019 —
see OPEN questions.)

Note `op 0x37` doubles as the redirect class: `0x0D`/`0x49` are
classified as `0x37`, then `5A:AFE0` re-reads the true opcode.

### 1.4 Frames, calls, tail-dispatch

- **Tail dispatch** (replace current script, no return): load a native
  event id into `$8D` (16-bit) and `JMP $C0:1B4C`. 1B4C stores the word
  to WRAM `$D51B` (the "current dispatch id", read by op 46) and `JMP
  $5A:AC70`, the resolver:
  - `0Cxx` → 3-byte pointer table at 5A:A970 + 3*(id-0xC00): PC = entry
    word, bank = entry byte 2, end = PC-1;
  - `4Cxx` → catalog table 5E:F500 via `JMP $5A:FD60`;
  - `31xx` → 5A:E5C0; `0Exx` → 5A:B600;
  - everything else (incl. `0Fxx` → bank FD, `08xx`–`1Fxx` → banks
    FA–FC) → u16 block table in bank `0xFA+(id>>10)`: start =
    `table[slot-1]+0x800` (or `0x800` for slot 0), end =
    `table[slot]+0x800`. (Matches
    `rs3_event_identity_v30.mjs nativeRange`.)
- **Call with return**: `JSR $C0:1B22` pushes the caller's PC (16-bit),
  bank and end into the frame record at WRAM `$D51D + 5*depth`
  (5 bytes: PC lo/hi, bank, end lo/hi), then increments depth.
- **Return**: C0:3756 pops the record (depth-- first), restores PC,
  bank, end; if the restored PC equals the restored end it pops again
  (loop); with depth 0 it runs the end-of-event close-out (C0:3783:
  window close etc.).
- **Deferred dispatch queue**: WRAM `$D6BD` array of 16-bit dispatch
  words terminated by `0xFF`, write index `$D6BB`, slot byte per entry
  at `$D6CD,X` (from Y or `0xFF`), previous-queue link at `$D6CE,X`.
  `$AF91` (C0:AF91) enqueues; `$B013` (C0:B013) processes immediately
  unless already processing (`$D6B9`). Ops enqueue words and the queue
  processor later runs them through the same machinery.

### 1.5 Inline event-id pairs are big-endian

Wherever an op tail-dispatches an *inline* 2-byte pair, the engine does
`LDA [$78]` (little-endian load), then `XBA` before storing to `$8D` —
i.e. the pair bytes are `(b0<<8)|b1`, b0 = high byte of the native event
id. VERIFIED at the tails of ops 33/34/45 (C0:2F9C/2FFE/2F54), selGoto
2F (C0:2E9B), op 32 (C0:2F1A), op 49-family (C0:2B7D), op 46 (via
`$D51B+r`). The byte before the pair is always tested `< 0x0C`; pairs
whose first byte is ≥ 0x0C are not event ids.

**Exception:** op `0x30`'s pairs are consumed *without* the XBA
(C0:2ED8 `LDA [$78]` → `JSR $AF91` directly), i.e. little-endian — but
op 0x30 never appears in any of the 3,690 dumps, so this matters only
for completeness.

## 2. Per-op semantics

### 2.1 Conditional skips — the gate family

The VM has no compare-and-branch. A **gate op** tests a condition and
then jumps the interpreter to one of two positions immediately after
itself:

```
        S: gate-op operands...
        S+3  <- condition TRUE continues here
        S+5  <- condition FALSE continues here
```

Both positions are examined the same way (VERIFIED, engine):

- byte at the position `< 0x0C` → the position and the next byte are a
  big-endian native event id; the event is **tail-dispatched**
  (current script replaced);
- byte `>= 0x0C` → PC stays there; the interpreter executes that byte as
  the next op.

Idiom in dumps: TRUE position holds `4e nn` (skip over the FALSE
branch) and FALSE position holds the FALSE-branch content, or vice
versa. Example `data/events/0001.txt` (flag 134 nibble 6, names #6/#7):

```
73:03a6  33 86 66   chkFlag  range [6,6]
73:03a9  4e 05      skip        <- TRUE lands here; skips 5 bytes
73:03ab  4f 16 06   4F_16       <- FALSE lands here
73:03ae  4e 03      skip
73:03b0  4f 16 07   4F_16       <- TRUE branch continues here
```

**op 33 chkFlag** (`33 id window`, 3 bytes) — VERIFIED (C0:2F5F).
Reads nibble flag `id` (§2.5), passes if
`(window>>4) <= value <= (window&0x0F)`. TRUE → S+3, FALSE → S+5.

**op 34 chkBit** (`34 id arg`, 3 bytes) — VERIFIED (C0:2FC1).
`test = (flagByte(id) & (arg&0x0F)) != 0 XOR (arg&0x80 != 0)`
(`$370D` value AND low-nibble mask; `$80` inverts). pass → S+3, fail →
S+5. Note `$370D` returns a *nibble*; with a low-nibble mask the AND is
the identity, so the effective test is `value != 0` unless a high-nibble
variant exists elsewhere (OPEN: is there a byte-wide reader?).

**op 45 chkMem** (`45 a b`, 3 bytes) — VERIFIED (C0:2F22, live
2026-11-20). `X = $EF00[a]` as a **16-bit WRAM address**, `A = $7E:X`
(68:36F0), `AND #$7F` when X is a member-record byte +0x25..+0x2F
(68:3730 range list F025-F030, F0A5-F0B0, ...); equal to `b` → S+3,
else → S+5. Events set the pointer first: `41 00 00 f0` / `45 00 07`
compares the leader record's actor id ($F000 = the select pick),
`41 10 19 f3` / `45 10 06` the member count. Pointer targets in the
dump set: $F319 (156 gates, plus 157 through `48 20 06 19 f3 ...`
fills), $F4CC/$F4CD (45), $F2D3 (10), $F000 (8), $F017/$F30E (4 each),
$F4A5-7, $0113, $0502, $0AC0, and EF00 slots. Live
(tools/emulator/protag_route.lua, 2026-11-20): row 3 ハリード logs
`CHK vmpc=FC089E a=04 b=04 ptr=F000` then `id=0847`; row 0 ユリアン
falls through to `id=0846`; `ptr=F319 a=06` on the party-count chains.
The port's GameState.mem_read_byte models $F000/$F319/$F322/$F323-8,
EF00 and the vanilla flag bytes $F46A-$F4E9 ($F4CC/$F4CD/$F4A5-7 are
flag pairs, C0:370D); $F30E is the map-header byte $D2F2 (C0:3D44,
C0:EC89), not modeled yet; other targets are recorded as
`chkMem<-addr` transparent ops.

**op 49 family** (`49 m a b`) — tail is the same pair gate
(`49`-family gate at C0:2B5B–2B82: byte at PC tested `<0x0C` → tail
dispatch else RTS). Operand semantics (check/bit-test/bit-write/nibble
set/inc/dec over the packed-4 space) per `ops.go` / ref tool, which the
dump set decodes coherently (939+ events end through `49` gates) —
PLAUSIBLE (ref) / VERIFIED (encoding only).

**0D gates** (`0d 00 id window` chk-range, `0d 01 id arg` bit test) —
machine-VERIFIED (0D-mode table entries 5A:B05E / 5A:B09B). These are
4-byte gates: TRUE continues at the byte right after the op (S+4),
FALSE skips two more bytes (S+6). Reader 5A:B044 returns the nibble at
**WRAM `$7F:FF90`** (id>>1; even id = high nibble) — this resolves the
ext-flag RAM base. The gate contract matches the dumps (`0B31` at
FC:c6b0: `0d 00 4d 9f` then TRUE arm `4e 03` at c6b4, FALSE arm
`37 ad` at c6b6).

### 2.2 op 4E skip — VERIFIED (C0:2254)

`4e nn` — unconditional forward skip. Engine: consume opcode, read `nn`,
advance PC by `nn` more bytes, then the usual 1C7A step (1 byte). Total
footprint = `nn + 2` bytes: the next op executes at `S+2+nn`.

It is **not** itself conditional and its operand is a **byte count, not
an op count**. The conditionality comes from the preceding gate op
choosing whether the `4e` is executed at all (§2.1). Chains like
`4e 02; 4e 0c` are nested skips each controlled by a different gate.

### 2.3 Selection menus

State (all WRAM, VERIFIED via handlers):

| addr | role |
|------|------|
| `$D3BF` | selected option, 0-based; `0xFF` = none selected |
| `$D3C1` | option count built so far (0-based next index); also used as fallback selection |
| `$D3C0` | menu-open flag |

- **op 25 optA** (1 byte) — VERIFIED (C0:1F49): `STZ $D3C0; STZ $3C1;
  STZ $3BF` — reset menu state.
- **op 26 optB** (1 byte) — VERIFIED (C0:1F55): registers one option:
  increments `$D3C1`, copies current window/message state into the
  option table (`$D502,$D3C2+32*idx`).
- **op 27 optC** (1 byte) — VERIFIED (C0:1F9E): clears `$D015` then
  builds the same way as 26 plus display calls (`$3835/$38AE`) — second
  menu style. It does NOT increment `$D3C1`: its whole body
  C0:1F9E..C0:2043 ends `JMP $1C7A` touching only `$D3BF`/`$D3C0`
  (the earlier "same as 26" note over-counted; optC options display
  but the selGoto fallback `r = $D3C1-1` must not see them).
- **op 31** (1 byte) — VERIFIED (C0:1F97/1FA1): sets `$D015=1` and
  opens the menu (calls `$3835/$38AE/$06F4`...). This is "show the
  choices that 25/26/27 registered".
- **op 2F selGoto** (1 byte + pairs) — VERIFIED (C0:2E73). Layout after
  the opcode: N consecutive 2-byte records (option targets). Semantics:

  ```
  r = $D3BF
  if r == 0xFF: r = $D3C1 - 1      ; no choice made: engine fallback
  PC += 2*r + 1                    ; PC now at record r's first byte
  b = [PC]; id = ([PC]<<8)|[PC+1]  ; big-endian (XBA)
  if b < 0x0C: tail-dispatch event id   (frame replaced, no return)
  else:        RTS; interpreter executes at [PC] as the next op
  ```

  Dump idiom: every record is `4e nn`, each skip landing at that
  option's code (e.g. `016A.txt` FA-menu: records `4e 25 / 4e 42 /
  48 01 03 88 13 00` → weapon / armor / money branches).

- **op 30** (1 byte + pairs) — VERIFIED engine (C0:2EA3), **unused in
  all dumps**. Same selection arithmetic, but the selected pair is
  *enqueued* via `$AF91` (with slot `$D519>>2` if `$D519≠FF`, else FF)
  — a call-with-return through the queue: PC resumes after the pair
  list (`PC = word + 1 + 2*$D3C1`). Pairs are little-endian here (§1.5).

- **op 32** (3 bytes `32 b0 b1`) — VERIFIED (C0:2F14): tail-dispatch of
  the big-endian pair (`XBA` → `$1B4C`). For `32 0F xx` the resolver's
  block-table path lands in bank FD — the vanilla FD:0000 pointer page
  (matches ref tool comment "Native 32 0F xx instead uses the vanilla
  FD:0000 pointer page. Evidence: C0:2F14").

- **op 4C xx** — dispatch-word semantics: the bokuno classifier treats
  `4C` with first operand `08/2E/4E` as inline handled words (5A:B01E
  special-cases exactly `0x084C/0x2E4C/0x4E4C`); a bare word `$004C` is
  translated at queue time (5A:E654) to low byte `$0C` and runs through
  the call-with-return handler C0:B847 with the XBA'd word `$4C00` —
  i.e. catalog event `$4C00 ≡ 0F00`. Other `4C xx` words have low byte
  `$4C ≥ $20` and are skipped by the queue processor.
  Catalog identity: `0Fxx` ≡ native `4Cxx` (ref
  `rs3_event_identity_v30.mjs`, engine 5A:AC70 `BEQ -> $5A:FD60`).

### 2.4 Jumps and calls (0D modes 16–19)

Encodings are VERIFIED by dump coherence over the whole set
(3689/3690 events walk to `end`/`reached-end16`; only 33 `crossed-bank`,
6 `unknown:4f ee`, 2 `limit-exceeded` — and the 2 limit-exceeded are
9997 identical placeholder events, see §3):

- **`0d 16 lo hi` (jump16, 4 bytes)** — target = `lo | hi<<8`,
  **absolute 16-bit address in the current bank**, little-endian.
  Machine-VERIFIED (0D-mode table entry 5A:B980): `INC PC; A := [PC]
  word; PC := A-1; JML C0:1C7A` — the 1C7A step INCs once more, so PC
  ends on the word. The earlier candidate C0:32B2 (bank $7E) is a
  different, still-unrouted handler (§4.2).
- **`0d 17 lo mid bank` (jumpL, 5 bytes)** — absolute far jump, operand
  order **lo, mid, bank**. Machine-VERIFIED (5A:B990): PC word from the
  first two bytes, third byte → fetch bank `$7A`. No return record.
- **`0d 18 lo mid bank` (callL, 5 bytes)** — same encoding; call.
  Machine-VERIFIED (5A:B9B0): pushes a frame record
  (`$D51D,$77*5`: PC+5, end `$7B`, bank `$7A`), `$77++`, jumps to
  word in bank[byte 3], sets `end := target`. Return address = the byte
  after the 5-byte op, as the dump model assumed.
- **`0d 19 id` (callIndirect, 3 bytes)** — machine-VERIFIED (5A:BA00):
  pushes the same return record (PC+2), then jumps to the far pointer
  `EF00[id..id+2]` (lo/mid in `EF00`, bank in `EF00[id+2]`), `end :=
  target`. Still 0 occurrences in the dumps.

### 2.5 Flag spaces

- **Vanilla nibble flags** — VERIFIED. One byte per two flags at WRAM
  `$7E:F46A` + (id>>1); even id = high nibble, odd id = low nibble.
  Reader `$370D` (C0:370D: `LSR` id, load byte, `BCS`-on-id-bit0 picks
  low nibble else `LSR×4`), writer `$3727`. Used by ops 33/34/45 and
  the 0D-00-style gates. Writers: op 35 (C0:3009: `arg&0x80` selects
  OR/AND with `arg&0x0F`), op 36 (C0:3051: set to `arg&0x0F`), op 37
  (C0:3069: INC, saturating below 0x10), op 38 (dec; symmetric).
  Matches the ref operand model in `ops.go` exactly (`rawArg 0x81` = or,
  mask 1 — seen in dumps, e.g. `016A.txt`).
- **packed4 (op 49)** — PLAUSIBLE (ref model; see ops.go): byte-packed
  4-bit fields, sub-ops 00 check / 01 bit-any(±invert) / 02
  and-or-write / 03 set / 04 inc / 05 dec, saturating 0–15. Encoding
  VERIFIED by dump coherence.
- **ext flags (0D 00–03)** — VERIFIED (machine): nibble array at WRAM
  **`$7F:FF90`** (reader 5A:B044: `LDA $7FFF90,X` after `id>>1`; even
  id = high nibble, odd id = low nibble, same packing as vanilla).
  Writers not yet located.

### 2.6 Random branch `4f 16 nn` — VERIFIED (C0:2EED)

The random-selection handler C0:2EED is reached from the 4F-sub table
(C0:3B36, sub `0x16` → 2EED): **`4f 16 nn`** (3 bytes; 218 occurrences
in the dump set). Engine: load `nn`, roll `r` in `0..(nn||256)-1`
(`nn-1` into `$0D`, `JSR $0733`). `r == 0` → continue in place
(`JMP $1C7A`); `r >= 1` → tail-dispatch native event `$D51B + r`,
where `$D51B` is the id of the **currently executing event** (stored at
C0:1B50). So `4f 16 nn` inside event E runs one of `E+1 .. E+nn`
instead of E. Matches
`rs3_static_conditions_v32.mjs randomEventAlternatives` exactly
(event 0001: `4f 16 06/07` randomly tail-dispatch one of events
0002..0007/0008).

Bare **op 0x46** (1 byte) is *not* this: its dispatch entry (1C8C) is
just the advance-1 step, i.e. a visible no-op. It has 0 occurrences in
the dump set. (The ref comment "C0:2EED selects r…" names the address,
not the opcode.)

### 2.7 4F subcommands — dialogue text injection

Subcommand table at C0:3B36 indexed by `sub*2` (dispatcher C0:1C8F),
lengths per `Sub4F` in ops.go. Text subs write into the WRAM text
buffer `$D56D` which is then executed as a WRAM script (§1.2). VERIFIED
handlers for:

| sub | bytes | meaning (engine) |
|-----|-------|------------------|
| 2F | 3 | actor name (op `4A id` is the same rule with an inline id, handler C0:3188 — the C0:226F table entry is vanilla and dead in bokuno, docs/naming.md): `id = $EF00[operand]`; if `id == WRAM[$F000]` (party leader record) copy the custom protagonist name from WRAM `$F300` (8 bytes, `00/50`-terminated), else copy ROM name-table entry `0x3D1480 + 8*id` (C0:31A6) |
| 43 | 3 | 3-digit decimal of `$EF00[operand]` via the digit formatter `$3503`, digits copied into `$D56D` (C0:33AC) |
| 11 | 2 | table text, no operand, index from WRAM `$D2F2`, table 0x3D1DC0 (ref model; handler 30A3 loads bank FD pointer) |
| 12/13/14/15 | 3 | table text: read `$EF00[operand]` index into ROM tables `0x3D0A80` (8-byte), `0x3D27C0` (10-byte, 12-bit id), `0x3D0000`, `0x3D1C80` (10-byte) — PLAUSIBLE (ref model, consistent table stride/terminators in the engine text-copy); handlers 3149/30FD/30C5/30D2 |
| 16 | 3 | random branch, same handler as op 46 (§2.6) — VERIFIED |

The whole sub-2F/43/11..15 model matches
`rs3_runtime_text_v30.mjs` (`TEXT_4F` set, `copyName` contract, table
bases), which this analysis confirms at engine level for 2F and 43.

### 2.7.1 op 2C pause — C0:26C9

Blinks a cursor in the window (tile 207F at `$D5BC[$D5A5]`, 20 frames on
and off through C0:06EB) until a button is down (`$D002` & F0: A X L R;
`$D003` & D0: B Y Select Start), writes tile 2002 over the cursor and
returns; the window is not cleared, so the text after it goes on in the
same window. The port puts EventVM.PAUSE_MARK in the page; the dialogue
types to each mark and waits for the advance key (a mark right before
the window closes is the page's own wait). Translation keys are the page
without marks, so a translated page shows whole until its translation
carries marks of its own. 237 reachable pages of events 0001-03FF hold
a mark (selftest: 000B).

### 2.7.2 op 2B wait — C0:24E5

`2b nn` runs one frame without an object pass (C0:06F4), then nn times
two C0:06EB frames, then C0:06D6, then the end check C0:1C7E: 2nn + 1
object passes inside the op's step (nn = 0 loops 256 times). The port
counts them in the step costs below. 0848 needs the waits: without them
objOp 43's pan down and script 010A's pan right start in one tick, and
the install cuts the pan down off.

### 2.7.3 One VM step per field frame (2026-11-21)

The field frame C0:06AA runs the queue drain C0:B013, the object pass
C0:5188, the party step C0:7DA9, then one VM step C0:1B93, then the
frame wait. One step is one op, one glyph of a text run, or one frame
pop: C0:1BB6 pops at PC == end and returns, so the pop takes the step.
Control ops (20-4F, and 0D through 5A:AFE0) end at C0:1C7A/1C7E, which
pops in the same step when PC reaches the end; dispatch words (00-1F,
C0:1BDD) and text runs return without that check, so their frame's
pop is the next step. C0:3756 pops every frame whose restored PC is at
its end; at depth 0 it closes out (C0:3783, frames without passes).

Frame routines an op's handler calls: C0:06EB (queue, objects, party)
and C0:06D6 (queue, objects, no party step, no FF:1695) run an object
pass; C0:06F4/06F1 (the tail of 06EB) and C0:0714 do not. So an op's
step runs extra passes: `2b nn` 2nn + 1; 4F_0C (fade in, C0:2442:
06D6, 06F1, 15 x 06EB) 16; 3C one (probe below; handler C0:332F not
read through). 2A (C0:217B) closes the window in frames without passes.
2C (C0:26C9) runs 06F4, then 06EB frames until a button, then 06D6.

Probe (cutscene_capture.lua schedule, exec hooks at C0:1BC6 for the
step's op, C0:51F7 for the pass, C0:06AA/06D6/06EB/B013/5188/7DA9;
passes numbered from the 0250 load): 084C's `40 01 3e` at pass 2, `0b
4b` at 3, 0B4B's 31 ops on 3-33 (objOp 2C installs on 7, 13, 19, 25,
31), its pop on 34, `2b 18` on 35, 4F_0C on 85, `33 36 cc` on 102, 3C
on 104, the page's glyphs one a pass from 109, 2C on 148, the press
seen after pass 151, 06D6 pass 152, 2A on 153, `0b 49` on 154, 0B49's
16 ops on 155-170, its pop on 171, `2b 10` on 172, the last pass with
`$76` = 1 on 205, and the close-out inside that step: 206 is the first
pass with the VM idle.

Port (event_vm `timed_waits`, field events): each op costs one pass
plus its extra passes, a separate pop one more; main runs the VM step
after map_view's frame (`field_frame_done`), as C0:06AA orders it.
Inside a page the steps go on as §2.7.4 lists. Selftests: main
`_selftest_step_passes` (ops outside pages), `_selftest_page_passes`
(the two probed pages below).

### 2.7.4 Dialogue page steps (2026-11-21)

Two probes on the cutscene_capture.lua schedule, one line per VM step
(exec C0:1B93: PC, op byte) and per pass (C0:51F7), with the frame
calls 06EB/06D6/06F4/217B/26C9/3756 and FF:1F7C (a glyph drawn):
0250 (frames 18380-18900) and 024A (0800, frames 14900-16000). Costs
in passes, i.e. VM steps:

- A glyph is one step, a 2-byte glyph (`22 57`, `20 b3`) too. The
  exported text has one character per glyph on all 296108 runs (byte
  50h is its own op, `op50`, one step with nothing drawn).
- `24` newline: one step; when the line count reaches the window's
  capacity it scrolls inside the step (C0:1EA7 -> C0:0DA9, two 06EB):
  +2. 0800 FC:1A14 on a 3-line window: nl at p344, next glyph p347.
- 4A and the other name ops: the op's step copies the name to `$D56D`,
  which runs as a frame: one step per glyph, then the frame's pop is a
  step of its own (0250: 4A p108, glyphs p109-111, pop p112, 様 p113).
- 28/29/4D/4B/4F_1D/4F_30/4F_33/2A: one step each (29 and 2A spend
  frames with no pass, which do not count). 3C: two (06D6 inside).
- 2C (C0:26CF): 06F4, `STZ $D002` (a press in the frame right after
  the 2C step is lost), then a loop of 06EB + button test, so one pass
  per frame waited; the frame the press is seen runs 06D6 (one pass),
  and the next step comes one pass later (0250: 2C p148, 06EB p149-151,
  press frame 18768 = 06D6 p152, 2A p153).
- Presses during typing do nothing (0250: presses at frames 18736 and
  18752 fell mid-page and the glyphs went on one a pass).

Window capacity (`$D5C1`, line count `$D5C3`, C0:12B7 copies byte 10 of
the 16-byte shape FD:EB00 + 16*idx): 3C's idx is its size byte & 7F
(bit 7 = slot 1); 28/29 open slot 0/1 at idx slot*4 + the speaker's
facing; `$D599`*8 is added to idx < 8 (4D sets `$D599` = 1, 4F_1D 0,
4F_1B 3). Caps: idx 00-07 4, 08-0F 3, 10-17 2, 18-1F 1, 22 4, 23 3.
Logged (WO lines, C0:1346) over the opening: 3C 22 -> 4, 23/A3 -> 3;
29 after 4D -> idx 0C-0F, 3; after 4F_1D -> 05-07, 4; after 4F_1B ->
1E, 1. 28/29 on a slot already open with text on its line end that
line first (C0:2169 -> 1EA7, the scroll included).

Port: next_page returns the whole page (the translation lookup needs
it) and `page_steps`, one entry per step after the pull: [passes since
the previous step, SILENT/SHOW/PAUSE, characters shown]; `page_tail`
is the passes from the last entry to the op that closed the page. main
plays the entries on the field frames (`_run_page_steps`), waits at a
PAUSE entry for a press made at least two frames after it, resumes two
passes after the press (the 06D6 pass, then the next step), and runs
the closing op `page_tail` passes after the last entry when the page
does not end on a pause (0849's FC:1852 page closes after `2b 40` with
no 2C). Field pages now type a character per field frame (60 a second,
the tween was 33) and a press during typing no longer finishes the
page. Not modelled: the side effects of ops inside a page (installs,
flags) still run at the pull, not at their step; a window opened by
text with no window open (FC:1D9F) is UNVERIFIED beyond that case; the
facing part of a 28/29 idx is not tracked (it never changes the cap).

### 2.8 Ops 0x00–0x1F: dispatch words, not local ops

Ops with first byte `< 0x20` never reach the C0:3AD6 table. The main
loop (C0:1BDD) reads the **word** `[PC] = opcode | next<<8`, enqueues it
via `$AF91` and advances PC by 2 — that is their whole inline effect
(VERIFIED flow):

- opcodes `0x00–0x0F` and `0x17/0x18/0x19`: queue is also processed
  immediately (`JSR $B013`) — synchronous dispatch;
- opcodes `0x10–0x16`, `0x1A–0x1F`: enqueue only — deferred to when the
  engine drains the queue.

**Queue-word processing (VERIFIED, C0:B013 → 5A:E654 → C0:B054):** the
processor takes the queue word into A, then 5A:E654 translates three
special whole-word forms (`$004C`→`$000C`, `$0049`→`$000D`,
`$0031`→`$000E`), skips words with low byte ≥ `$20`, and dispatches
everything else through **`JMP ($C0:B06B,X)` with `X = (word&FF)*2` =
opcode*2** (K = `$C0`). Handler map (entries byte-verified by
`cmd/vmprobe`):

| op | handler | semantics |
|----|---------|-----------|
| 00–0C | C0:B847 | **call-with-return**: `XBA` the word → native id `opcode<<8 \| operand`, `JSR $C0:1B22`. So `0b 39` = call event `$0B39` (block FA), `0c 00`… = block calls; the slot byte `$D6CD,Y` → `$D519` first |
| 0D, 11 | C0:C109 | **map jump** (11 = `11 xx`; the 0D entry also serves the `$0049` translation): far path via `JML 5A:B640`, then a 5-byte record at `FC:FB00 + xx*5` (xx = operand); byte 0 → `$D0A6` |
| 0E | C0:B847 | call-with-return (also the `0031` translation target) |
| 0F | C0:BBF7 | engine command: `$7E0600 = 06`, `$7E0601 = xx`, into C5:3000 (§4.7) |
| 10 | C0:C1DF | **map move** (event-point rectangle dispatch, decoded 2026-11-18): the rect handler C0:EA6B enqueues the byteswapped rect id; `10xx` rects become words with low byte `10` = this op — the field map-move command (docs/triggers.md "The 0x2xxx field ids are NOT an encounter class") |
| 12 | C0:C168 | undecoded single |
| 13 | C0:BC29 | undecoded single |
| 14 | C0:B85D | engine command 0: `$7E0600 = 00`, `$7E0601 = xx`, `JSL C5:0000` (object command) |
| 15 | C0:B92C | undecoded single |
| 16 | C0:B9B5 | undecoded single |
| 17 | C0:B1B6 | **objOp**: `JMP ($B0AB,X)` (table C0:B0AB; the disassembler dropped the operand's high byte, so earlier text said C0:00AB), `X = operand*2` (`17 20` = install an object action script, 2788 of 3948 objOp sites; docs/action-scripts.md; `17 43` = C0:D11B, `$D0DD` = 1 and the leader instruction `1B 5B`, a camera pan 27 steps down, docs/action-scripts.md "Op 1B") |
| 18 | C0:BFAF | `$1314 = $18`, `JML 67:F610` |
| 19 | C0:BFA8 | `$1314 = $19`, `JML 67:F610` |
| 1A | C0:C626 | pending pointer: if `$7D == 0`, load `FC:ED80[xx]` (word) → `$7E`, `$7A`-style bank `$80 = $FC`, `$81 = 1`, `$7D = 1` (consumer = field SFX-sequence interpreter FF:1ACC, §4.7.1); if `$7D` already set, queue sound-request bit `$D6EA = 1` instead |
| 1B | C0:BBC5 | engine command: `$7E0600 = 08`, `$7E0601 = xx`, into C5:3000 |
| 1C | C0:BA6E | engine command: `$7E0600 = 0A`, `$7E0601 = xx`, into C5:3000 |
| 1D | C0:C5C4 | **BGM change**: no-op if `xx == $F546` (current track); otherwise SPC handshake (`$1C00 = $F0` → `JSL FF0024` → `$1C00 = $10`, track `xx` → `$1C01`, caches `$F546`/`$D8D3`) |
| 1E | C0:C618 | sound op: `JSR $EA47` with `$FF`, then `JSR $E9FB` with `xx` |
| 1F | C0:C570 | BGM variant: same as 1D but `JSL FF0063` |

Consequence for the old text: `11 9a` = map jump through record 9A
(§ above), `17 20` = objOp table entry $20, `0b c7` = call event $0BC7,
`00 00` = call event `$0000` (a no-op-looking block event). The
special-casing inside `$AF91` (word&FF == 0x17 or 0x10 and high byte <
0x10 → merge/replace queue head) shows these words act as single-slot
deferred actions (PLAUSIBLE: merging intent not fully decoded).

### 2.9 The 0D-mode and 49-sub tables (bank 5A)

The 0D redirect (5A:AFF6) reads the mode byte after `0d`, computes
`mode*2` and jumps through **`$5A:ADA0`** (`JMP ($ADA0,X)` at 5A:B006 —
near-indirect, so the table lives in the *executing* bank 5A, not bank
00; this is what the old bank-00 hunt missed). The 49 redirect (5A:B009)
uses **`$5A:FE00`** the same way; sub-operands ≥ `$F0` bypass the table
(5A:E63B: sub-0xF0)*5 → far call into the `5A:FB00` block. `cmd/vmprobe`
asserts the table entries and handler prologues.

Notable 0D-mode entries (all VERIFIED at machine level):

| mode | handler | semantics |
|------|---------|-----------|
| 00 | 5A:B05E | chk-range gate over ext flags (`$7F:FF90`), window byte = `[start<<4 \| end]`; TRUE → S+4, FALSE → S+6 (§2.1 note) |
| 01 | 5A:B09B | chk-bit gate over ext flags, `arg&0x0F` mask, `$80` inverts; TRUE → S+4, FALSE → S+6 |
| 16/17/18/19 | 5A:B980/B990/B9B0/BA00 | jump16 / jumpL / callL / callIndirect (§2.4) |
| 30 | 5A:C000 | `0d 30 a b`: `scratch[b] = EF00[0]` where scratch = WRAM `$7FF900`; the first operand is read and discarded |
| 31 | 5A:C020 | `0d 31 a b`: `EF00[b] = scratch[a]; scratch[a] = 0` |

**`0d 30/31` are a variable spill pair, not object or party swaps** (the
ref tool's swapOut/swapBack names mislead). In event 0B31 the pair
`0d 30 50 00 / 17 20 / 0d 31 00 50` snapshots `EF00[0]` into scratch
slot 0 around the `17 20` object command and copies the saved byte into
`EF00[$50]`. Across the dumps the pair always uses slots 0/0 — a
save/copy idiom. The port models it as `state.scratch` +
`EF00[0]` (implemented in `godot/event_vm.gd`).

**op 2E return** (1 byte, dump name `endMes`) — VERIFIED (C0:2779,
live 2026-11-20). `JSR $3756`: pop one call frame (restore `$78/$7A`
and the frame end `$7B` from `$D51D + 5*depth`, popping again while the
restored PC equals its frame end); at depth 0 it ends the script
through C0:3783 (window close-out). It is not a window close: the
port treated it as one and kept executing the next variant's code
(event 0B31: every path in `[c671, c6d0)` ends in `2e`). Live
(tools/emulator/protag_route.lua): `OP2E vmpc=FCDF9F depth=2` (0BF1
returning into the bank-72 callL script) and `vmpc=7291D1 depth=1`
(that script returning into 0800 at FC:080b).

**op 43 end** (1 byte) — VERIFIED (live capture below): handler 277D region and
the fact that 2709 dumps terminate exactly at `43` with clean endings;
community doc 【初心者向け】ロマサガ３イベント作成講座.txt: 「イベントコード43とは、すべてのイベントを終了するコードです」. The handler
C0:277D is `STZ $77; JMP $3783` — depth forced to 0, so a 43 inside a
called event ends the caller too. Dispatch traced statically
(2026-11-20): the pre-dispatch hook 59:E100 reads 59:E200[op] = 0 for
43 (not hooked; 2E/45/4A read 0 as well), 5A:B01E/5A:AFC6 pass it on,
5A:AFE0 computes (op-0x20)*2 and JMLs to C0:1BD4 `JMP ($3AD6,X)`,
entry C0:3B1C = 277D. (4A's dead table entry is explained by 4A living
inside text runs, which the text output path consumes.) LIVE
(2026-11-20, tools/emulator/eventinject.lua): event 049A (`0c be`,
`43`) injected into the empty queue dispatched 0CBE; C0:277D ran at
frame 19618 with `$77 = 01` and C0:3783 followed in the same frame
with `$77 = 00`. A `43` that ends a text run (event 0005 at 73:0448)
never reaches C0:277D — the text interpreter consumes it like 4A —
yet the script still ends at C0:3783 with `$77 = 00`. The opening
window to frame 60000 executes no 43.

**op 4D** (1 byte) — VERIFIED (C0:2267): `STA $D599 = 1` (flag consumed
by the end-of-event close-out — "show window 4D"). Ops 4A/4B set
`$D599 = 2 / 3` (C0:226F/2277), op 44 clears it (C0:227F).

**op 46** (1 byte) — visible no-op: dispatch entry 1C8C = `JMP $1C7A`
(consume one byte). 0 dump occurrences; see §2.6 for the actual random
branch, which is `4f 16 nn`.

## 3. Where this contradicts / confirms current dumper assumptions

1. **jump16 absolute-target assumption: CONFIRMED.** `0d 16 lo hi` →
   `lo|hi<<8` in the same bank, little-endian. No change needed in
   `internal/bokuno/walk.go`.
2. **jumpL operand order lo/mid/bank: CONFIRMED** by dumps and by the
   engine far-jump usage pattern.
3. **callL is a call (walker skips it): CONFIRMED** as the only model
   consistent with 3689/3690 clean walks; exact return address
   PLAUSIBLE.
4. **Effective dispatch indexing is `(op-0x20)*2` in the patched game**,
   not the raw-opcode indexing the same table also encodes (vanilla).
   Irrelevant to the dumper, but any future engine-level tooling must
   not read that table naively.
5. **~9997 events are identical placeholders** (`0d 17 00 00 4b` → bank
   4B offset 0, i.e. into the pointer page). The walker decodes pointer
   bytes as ops and reports `limit-exceeded` (2 dumps) or huge op counts;
   that is inherent to the data, not a dumper bug.
6. **op 30 pairs are little-endian** (all other inline pairs
   big-endian). op 30 is unused in the dump set, so no dumper impact.

## 4. OPEN questions (and what was tried)
1. ~~Bank-00 dispatch tables~~ **RESOLVED (2026-11-16):** the tables were
   never in bank 00. `JMP ($xxxx,X)` targets the *current program bank*,
   and each dispatcher runs in a known bank: the 0D-mode table is
   **5A:ADA0** (dispatch at 5A:B006, K=$5A), the 49-sub table
   **5A:FE00** (5A:B019, K=$5A), and the queue-word table **C0:B06B**
   (C0:B054→C0:B05D via 5A:E64C, K=$C0). All three are decoded in
   §2.9; `cmd/vmprobe` asserts the entries against the ROM bytes.
2. **Handler C0:32B2** reads a word, pushes a return record, sets
   `PC := word`, `end := 0xFFFF` and the fetch bank to `$7E` (WRAM).
   Which op/mode routes here is unresolved; mode 16 is now
   machine-verified (5A:B980) and does NOT route here, so C0:32B2 is a
   WRAM sub-script call (the text buffer mechanism §1.2 also uses bank
   7E).
3. ~~callIndirect (0d 19)~~ decoded (§2.9, 0D-mode entry 5A:BA00):
   `EF00[id..id+2]` holds a far pointer (lo/mid/bank); the call jumps
   there with a return record. Still 0 occurrences in the dumps.
4. ~~op 45's `JSL $68:36F0`~~ **RESOLVED (2026-11-20):** pointer read
   through the EF00 word, §2.1 op 45.
5. **op 49 sub-semantics at engine level**: the 2B5B handler region
   mixes a money-compare (`$7E:F31A` vs `#$2710`) with the pair gate;
   the six sub-op handlers are behind the now-located `$FE00` table
   (§2.9) — not yet walked per sub-op. Semantics stay per ref model.
6. ~~ext-flag (0D) RAM base~~ **RESOLVED:** the ext-flag nibble array
   lives at WRAM **`$7F:FF90`** (reader 5A:B044: `LDA $7FFF90,X`,
   same high/low nibble packing as vanilla).
7. ~~op 0x1A's pending pointer~~ **RESOLVED (2026-11-17):** the
   consumer is the per-frame **field SFX-sequence interpreter at
   FF:1ACC** (§4.7.1). `1a xx` arms it; the FC:ED80 entries point at
   small `ff`-framed command streams in bank FC (FC:EE00-FFxx) that the
   interpreter consumes one command per frame as field sound-effect
   sequences. See §4.7.1 for the command set and the pump path.
   (The op 1e reader `$D6EA`, which the busy path of 1a sets to 1, is
   the SPC request bitfield drained by the C0:DC28 processor.)
8. **C5:3000 commands 06/08/0A** (ops 0F/1B/1C): the switch at
   C5:3000 handles 02/03/04/0B/0C inline; other commands fall through
   to a coroutine hand-off (C5:304E saves `$7E1300`, resumes
   C5:F3C5). What 06/08/0A do downstream is not decoded.

### 4.7.1 Op 1a consumer: the field SFX-sequence interpreter FF:1ACC
### (RESOLVED 2026-11-17)

All addresses below are byte-verified against `patches/bokuno_jp.sfc`
(`cmd/vmprobe` pins the quoted bytes); the whole chain is vanilla RS3
engine code, unchanged by the hack.

**Pump path.** The VM-idle frame function (entered as gate stub
C0:06A6 → C0:06AA; also JSL'd as `$C006A6` from the attract-script loop
at FF:B21C) runs one VM op (`JSR $C0:1B93`), then the sound pump:

```
C0:06BC  JSL $FF067C      ; engine call, A = $D2E3 (mode byte)
C0:06C0  JSL $FF0680      ; -> JSR $FF:1ACC   <- the pump
C0:06C4  JSL $FF9CDB
```

FF:0660-06BB is a far-call gate table (one `JSR xxx; RTL` stub per
engine routine in bank FF); stub FF:0680 lands on the interpreter.

**Interpreter (FF:1ACC).** One call processes one command:

```
1ACC  LDA $7D; BEQ -> RTS           ; idle: nothing armed
1AD1  LDA $81; BEQ +; DEC $81; BNE RTS ; frame-delay countdown
1AD9  LDA [$7E]                     ; long read: bank byte $80 = $FC
      FF -> 1B26: STZ $7D; LDA #$01; STA $D8ED   (sequence done)
      FE +b -> INC $7E; b -> $81    (delay b pump frames)
      FD +b -> INC $7E; JSL $C0:E9F7 with b  (sound op, same routine op 1e uses)
      FC -> $7D = 1                 (select upload channel 1)
      FB -> $7D = 2                 (select upload channel 2)
      else -> b = request id; INC $7E; word = [$7E] (big-endian) -> $D2;
              JSR $1B3C  (build an SPC upload request: per-channel
              descriptor $D2D9/$D2DB, target buffer bank $98 = $7F,
              ring allocator $FF:0CC2 over $D0BD/$D0BF)
      then INC $7E; if [$7E] == FF the sequence ends now, else RTS
```

So `$7D` = armed/channel flag, `$81` = frame-delay counter, `$7E/$80` =
the fetch pointer into bank FC, `$D8ED` = sequence-finished flag
(readers: C0:7DB9 post-frame housekeeping). Op 1a's busy path writes
`$D6EA = 1` (SPC request bitfield) instead of disarming the running
sequence. The FC:ED80 blobs are note/event streams for the field SFX
channels, e.g. entry 00 (FC:EE00) decodes as `FC FB` (channel select),
cmd `00` word `1020`, `FE 10` (16-frame delay), `FD 10` (sound op $10),
`FF` (end); entries 05/06 (event 0B31's `1a 05`/`1a 06`) are single
`cmd EE/ED word 2518; FD 53; FF` — switch-click/stone-statue sounds.

**Arm path (op 18/19, same dispatcher).** Queue words with low byte
`18`/`19` dispatch to C0:BFAF/BFA8 (`$1314 = $18/$19`, then the hack's
engine-command router 67:F610, which JMLs back to C0:BFBB/C0:BFC7).
C0:BFC7 clears the queue, and C0:BFD6 reads the word back:
`$130C` = the last C0:AB2E argument (1 party-started contact, 0
monster-started; docs/battle-enemy-ai.md), `$D018` = slot byte, and C0:C042
`LDA $D6BE,Y; STA $1306` — the word's **high byte** becomes the
scenario id `$1306` (values `$F0-$F3` select a preset-party row in the
formation loader FE:C3C6, §6.5), while `$1307/$1308` come from
`$D2FC[X]`/`$D2FE` and `$1309/$130A` from the protagonist `$D9A9`.



## 5. GDScript implementation notes

Model the VM exactly as the engine does: **PC never auto-advances**;
every op consumes its own bytes. Gates select one of two continuation
positions; everything else is a plain linear op. Pseudocode:

```gdscript
class Frame:
    var bank: int          # script bank (CPU bank byte)
    var pc: int            # 16-bit offset in bank
    var end16: int         # event end offset

var stack: Array[Frame] = []   # call frames (engine: 5-byte records)
var tail_word: int = 0         # $D51B: id of event now running

func run_event(id: int) -> void:
    var f := _resolve(id)      # engine 5A:AC70: table lookups
    stack = [f]
    while not stack.is_empty():
        var f := stack.back()
        if f.pc == f.end16:
            stack.pop_back()   # engine C0:3756 (loops if parent also done)
            continue
        if not _step(f):
            return             # tail-dispatch replaced the stack
        # loop until the root frame ends

func _step(f: Frame) -> bool:
    var op := _fetch8(f)
    match op:
        0x43: stack.pop_back(); return stack.size() > 0   # end
        0x4E:                                             # skip
            var n := _fetch8(f)
            f.pc = (f.pc + n) & 0xFFFF                    # +n more bytes
            return true
        0x33, 0x34, 0x45:                                 # gates
            var pos := _eval_gate(op, f)      # f.pc now at S+3 or S+5
            return _continue_or_tail(f, pos)
        0x2F:                                             # selGoto
            var r := sel_result()             # $D3BF, FF -> $D3C1-1
            f.pc = (f.pc + 2 * r + 1) & 0xFFFF
            return _continue_or_tail(f, f.pc)
        0x25: menu_reset(); f.pc += 1; return true
        0x26: menu_add_option(); f.pc += 1; return true
        0x27: menu_add_option2(); f.pc += 1; return true
        0x4F:                                             # 4F subcommands
            var sub := _fetch8(f)
            if sub == 0x16:                               # random branch
                var n := _fetch8(f)
                var r := rng.randi_range(0, (n if n != 0 else 256) - 1)
                if r != 0: return _tail(tail_word + r)
                return true
            return _exec_4f_sub(sub, f)   # 11/12/13/14/15/2F/43 text etc.
        0x31: menu_show(); f.pc += 1; return true
        _:
            return _exec_op(op, f)   # table ops, text runs, 0D/49 modes

# gate/selGoto tail: byte at pc selects inline continuation or tail call
func _continue_or_tail(f: Frame, pos: int) -> bool:
    f.pc = pos
    var b0 := _fetch8(f, false)          # peek, do not consume... engine
    if b0 < 0x0C:                        # consumes: pair (b0,b1) big-endian
        var b1 := _fetch8(f)
        return _tail((b0 << 8) | b1)     # replaces stack via _resolve
    return true                          # execute at b0 as next op

func _tail(id: int) -> bool:
    var f := _resolve(id)
    if f == null: push_error("bad event id"); return false
    stack = [f]; tail_word = id
    return true
```

Implementation cautions:

- Keep `_fetch8` advancing `pc` exactly once per consumed byte; the
  skip/gate/selGoto arithmetic above depends on it.
- Encode gate TRUE/FALSE positions as fixed offsets (+3 / +5) from the
  gate opcode; do **not** parse "pairs" before knowing which side is
  taken — the FALSE side of `33/34/45` is at +5 even when the TRUE side
  is an op with operands.
- op `49` and `0D`-mode gates follow the same +3/+5 contract; implement
  their condition evaluation from `ops.go` operand decoding.
- `end16` semantics: a frame whose PC reaches `end16` pops (possibly
  repeatedly, if the parent also sits at its own end).
- Deferred dispatch (ops 0x00–0x1F) can be a plain `Array[int]` queue of
  words processed between frames; for dialogue-faithful playback only
  the immediate ops (0x0B syscall, 0x11 mapJump, 0x17–0x19) need
  effects wired up.
- Do not implement op 0x30/`0d 19`: unused in the whole event set.


## 6. Runtime-state ops: party, inventory, gold (GDScript port scope)

Evidence classes as in §2. WRAM addresses below were located by scanning the
patched engine banks C0–FF for references to `$7E:F3xx` and decoding the
surrounding handlers; each op row names the handler and a real dump
instance.

### 6.1 Spaces

- **EF00 variables** — 256 bytes at WRAM `$EF00`. Writers: op 40 set1B
  (C0:2226: `EF00[id] = byte`), op 41 set2B (C0:223C: 16-bit word
  `lo | hi<<8` at `EF00[id]` — little-endian, 4-byte op), op 48 fill
  (C0:21FD: `48 id n b1..bn`, n == 0 means 1). Readers: op 45 chkMem, op 3A
  / 4F_50 item-name macros, getItem, 4F_10/4F_19 money ops, 0D 07.
- **Inventory** — 32 slots of (id, count) at WRAM `$7EF32A`, 2 bytes per
  slot, id `$FF` = empty (the empty scan at C0:29E4 tests `id == $FF`).
  getItem (C0:2E1F) scans for an existing slot of the item: found →
  `count++` with the increment suppressed at `count >= 99` (`CMP #$63`,
  C0:2E54); empty slot → id stored, count 1. VERIFIED.
- **Gold** — 16-bit at WRAM `$7EF31A`; two bank deposits at `$7EF31C` /
  `$7EF31E` (the 金取引所 handlers C0:29B9/C0:39C5 read and subtract
  them). VERIFIED (handler decode; no dump-side op name for the bank).
- **Party** — member count byte at WRAM `$F319`; 128-byte member records
  at `$F000 + 128*i`; the record-shift routine at C0:391B (4F sub 06)
  copies offsets `$18/$1A/$1C` from record i+1 into record i over that
  stride, confirming the 128-byte layout. Leader identification: 4F sub 2F
  (C0:31A6) compares an actor id against WRAM `[$F000]` and copies the
  custom protagonist name from `$F300` on match. op 39 (C0:31F2) computes
  the record address as `$F000 + 128*operand` for the member-name macro.

Handler addresses are entries of the effective dispatch table (§1.3) or

Dump instances grounding the money/item ops (event 004E, the 神王教 donation

```

The 0D 07 operand is a variable index, and the checked ids are key items,
not actors: event 016A sets `EF00 = 0x13D` (レディホーク) before `0d 07 00`,

(タイニィフェザー, matching the 「ようせいから天使の翼をもらえる」 event note
in テキスト/02_イベント解説.txt). The ref tool's names for this family
("inparty?", "removePartyActor") are misleading; the engine handler is
behind the unresolved 0D-mode table, so "party carries item" rests on the
dump evidence above, not on machine code.

### 6.3 Party membership: op 4F_31 writes the party slot list

The engine party is a **6-slot list at WRAM `$F323-$F328`** (one ally id
per slot, `$FF` = empty), with the member count at `$F319` and the
128-byte member records at `$F000 + 128*i`. `4f 31 b0..b5` (C0:20EC)
stores three 16-bit reads as six bytes straight into that list — this
is the membership write the earlier round missed. The list consumers
scan for `$FF` empties (fill routine FE:C73B: unused slots become
`$FF`) and treat slot values as ally ids.

Real event evidence — event **0B31** (opening クジンシー battle, one
variant per protagonist) builds the party slot by slot, gated by
`chkMem` on `$EF10`:

```
FC:c733  40 00 1f            set1B   EF00 = 0x1F
FC:c736  41 20 22 f3         set2B   EF20 word = 0xF322 (pointer target)
FC:c73a  4f 45 00 20         4F_45   $F322 = EF00[EF00[0]]   (walk id)
FC:c73e  4f 31 00 ff ff ff ff ff   party = [00] + empties
...
FC:c7ac  4f 31 00 ff ff ff ff ff   party = [00] + empties (after a battle branch)
FC:c7bb  4f 31 00 01 ff ff ff ff   party = [00 01]
FC:c7ca  4f 31 00 01 02 ff ff ff   party = [00 01 02]
FC:c7d9  4f 31 00 01 02 03 ff ff   party = [00 01 02 03]
FC:c7e8  4f 31 00 01 02 03 04 ff   party = [00 01 02 03 04]
FC:c7f7  4f 31 00 01 02 03 04 05   party = [00 01 02 03 04 05]
```

Final opening party = allies `00 ユリアン, 01 エレン, 02 サラ, 03
トーマス, 04 ハリード, 05 ミカエル` (06 モニカ / 07 カタリナ join only
through their own routes). The opening chains 0800-0846 set the same
list three times (FC:117e `4f 31 05 01 02 03 04 00`, FC:13d0 `4f 31 01
02 03 04 00 05`, FC:158b `4f 31 00 01 02 03 04 05` — rotations of the
same six, the last call wins).

The remaining dispatch words are now decoded (§2.8) and none of them
touches `$F319`/`$F323-$F328`:

- `1d xx` (2,338) is a **BGM change** (C0:C5C4: no-op when `xx` equals
  the current track `$F546`, else SPC handshake). Event 0015 pairs
  `1d 0c` with boarding a ship — boarding music. The ref names
  (removePartyActor etc. for 0d 08/0a — 0 occurrences) stay rejected.
- `1c xx` = engine command `$7E0600=0A` (C0:BA6E), `1e xx` = sound op
  (C0:C618), `1f xx` = BGM variant (C0:C570). None of the C5:3000
  command paths (§4.8) writes the party area.
- `0d 30/31` are the EF00[0] scratch spill (§2.9).
- There is **no single join/leave op**: membership changes rewrite the
  whole 6-slot list with 4F_31. The port keeps `join()`/`remove_member()`
  for menu-side edits and maps 4F_31 to `set_party_list()`.

Party-count `$F319` writers in the whole ROM (byte-scan): FE:C3D0
(formation loader, §6.5), FE:C8FA/C915/C938/C953 (preset party
scenarios), FE:C904/C927/C942 region, 5E:F82D/F835 (party-menu add),
C5 shop paths — none reachable from a decoded event op, so the VM
derives the count from the list (empties dropped).

### 6.4 Equipment, techs, HP/LP

No event op writes equipment, learned techs/spells, or HP/LP: the 4F subs
that scan member records (`4f 44`, `4f 51`, 139/123 instances) only read
them for display, and the equip/unequip machinery (held-item pointer
`$7EF347`, handler family C0:2C36/C0:2C42/C0:2D37-area) is driven by the
field menus, not by events. In the port these live in GameState for the
menus and battle to mutate; events only read (item-name macros, the 0D 07
possession gate covers equipped items).


### 6.5 Initial party / gold / items (game start)

- **Gold starts at 0.** The only `$F31A` writes in the ROM are the event
  money paths (C0:3979/C0:39BD/C0:39C5 = 4F_19/金取引所, C0:29A1-family
  = 4F_10) and the shop spend loop (C5:AAE7). No engine new-game routine
  or event op seeds an opening amount. The bokuno wiki オープニング page
  (https://www.wikihouse.com/bokuno/, EUC-JP) puts the first income at
  the opening-end クジンシー reward: +2000 オーラム (+4000 for ハリード)
  — the `4f 19` grants in events 0B31-0B5F (`48 01 03 d0 07 00` =
  EF01 word 2000; ハリード variants 4000).
- **Items come from opening supply events.** The wiki lists the
  シノンの森 exit supply (non-ハリード protagonists): 傷薬5, 小盾3,
  兵士の鎧3, ブロードソード1, 精霊石4; the opening chain issues them as
  `getItem` bursts (e.g. 0846 at FC:2dd7: `41 00 00 01` then `42 00`
  ×4 / `42 01` ×2 — one getItem per unit). No ROM-side item template
  is copied at new-game time.
- **Correction (2026-11-21):** 4F_31 and the loader rows list RECORD
  slots ($F000 + 0x80 * k), not ally ids. Record +0 (the ally id) is
  written by C5:F002 (called from C5:FA77) during the intro; the opening
  capture (hero ユリアン) held 00 01 02 03 04 06 in records 0-5, so the
  opening party is ユリアン エレン サラ トーマス ハリード モニカ
  (GameState.RECORD_IDS). Other heroes are not captured.
- **Party** = the 4F_31-built opening list (§6.3, record slots 0-5), later
  reshaped by story events. An engine-side formation loader also exists
  (FE:C3C6 → FE:C3D0: scans a 21-byte-row table at `FE:9F2E` for the id
  in `$1306`, writes `$F322`, `$F319` = row+2 (count 6), `$F323-$F328` =
  row+3..+8, then per member record (base `$B8`, stride `$80`):
  record+1 = row+9+i, record+0x0B = row+15+i, record+0x2A-0x2F = 1;
  gated on `$F4A2` bit 1) — triggered by engine dispatch with `$1306`
  preset, not by a decoded event op.
- **The loader is NOT select-row driven — RESOLVED (2026-11-17,
  machine-verified).** `$1306` = the high byte of a `18 Fx` queue word
  (§4.7.1: dispatch at C0:C042, `LDA $D6BE,Y`). The intro chain
  dispatches `F0 → F1 → F2 → F3` in a fixed sequence (headless frames
  9535/10208/10991/11660) **identically for every protagonist select
  row** — byte-identical runtime observed for rows 0 ユリアン, 1
  トーマス, 2 ミカエル, 3 ハリード (`tools/emulator/form_watch.lua`,
  4 runs, write PC C0:C048). The four `FE:9F2E` rows are intro-stage
  presets, not per-protagonist parties; they all hold allies 00-05 and
  differ only in walk id and leading slot: F0 walk `$0A` party
  `[00 01 02 03 04 05]`, F1 walk `$04` same, F2 walk `$09` party
  `[05 00 01 02 03 04]`, F3 walk `$04` same. Port consequence: the
  Godot battle scene needs no per-row formation table from this loader;
  the opening party stays the event-built 4F_31 list.
- The per-protagonist formation data that DOES exist is battle-side:
  char-table byte +39 固有陣形 (docs/char-stats.md) = index into the
  battle formation table, allies 00-07 = `02 02 09 02 0A 08 00 02`
  (ユリアン/エレン/サラ/トーマス/ハリード/ミカエル/モニカ/カタリナ);
  the battle formation table itself is still undecoded in this repo.
  The select row → ally id mapping lives in FE:961B +1:
  `[0,3,5,4,2,1,6,7]` (0 ユリアン, 1 トーマス, 2 ミカエル, 3 ハリード,
  4 サラ, 5 エレン, 6 モニカ, 7 カタリナ) — note godot
  `GameState.SELECT_ROWS` asserts identity mapping, which is wrong.
- **Protagonist select rows** = 0 ユリアン, 1 トーマス, 2 ミカエル,
  3 ハリード, 4 サラ, 5 エレン, 6 モニカ, 7 カタリナ (community
  structure doc `patches/ぼくの（略更新/テキスト/05_構造体.def.txt`,
  `RS3_仲間主人公選択設定`; matches sprites.md's row-0 ユリアン /
  row-2 ミカエル probe). Ported as `GameState.SELECT_ROWS` with row 0
  the default.

### 6.6 The intro chain's field handoff, and what holds at the map-0x250
### "frozen arena" (2026-11-17 release session, machine-verified)

The opening chains 0800→0846→0848→…→084C are consecutive fragment
ranges of one linear block of bank-FC code (eventrange, u16 block table):
0800 = `[FC:0800, FC:08EF)`, 0846 = `[1394,155F)`, 0848 = `[1821,1852)`,
0849 = `[1852,1917)`, 084A = `[1917,1B50)`, 084B = `[1B50,1C54)`,
084C = `[1C54, 23C8)`, 084D = `[23C8, 23F2)`, 084E = `[23F2, 2494)`,
084F = `[2494, 24C9)`, … — the story flows through them via gate
tail-dispatches (the TRUE branch's `< $0C` byte pair is the next id,
e.g. `33 36 cc / 08 4d` at FC:2380). The same applies to the 0B31-0B5F
"road scene": 0B44 = `[FC:C872, FC:C890)`, 0B45 = `[C890, C8A2)`, 0B49
= `[C8CC, C905)` — tiny fragments (a few objOps, one dialog line, one
gate), NOT one giant cutscene; the dumps that walk from an entry past
its end16 decode shared code under many ids.

The frozen post-intro state on map 0x250 (`$76=00`, "locked-camera
arena" in docs/map-format.md) is **event 084C having ended normally**,
not a wait:

- MesenCE write-watch on `$76` (tools/emulator/release_probe.lua, runs
  in /tmp/release-agent/run1..3): the chain goes `V76=1 vm=FC:0800
  D51B=0800` (boot) → … → `V76=1 vm=FC:1852 D51B=0849` → `V76=0
  cpu=C0:37A6 vm=FC:23C8 D51B=0B49 D2E3=02` — the last transition is the
  close-out (`C0:37A6` inside C0:3783), with VM PC = 084C's end16.
- The frame record at `$D51D` = `c6 23 fc c8 23` — PC `$FC:23C6`, end
  `$FC:23C8`: the caller's resume point after the `0b 49` call at
  `FC:23C4` returned — 0B49's fragment `[FC:C8CC, FC:C905)` (party
  display setup: `set2B $F319` / `chkMem` / `set1B 82..85` + `objOp`
  runs; each `17 20` gives member n's figure, which 0B4B's objOp 2C
  spawned, script 013C back into the leader, docs/action-scripts.md)
  hit its end16 and popped back. `$78/$79 = $23C8` = the frame
  reached its end and was popped.
- Every close-out flag is zero in the frozen WRAM dumps (`$D516`, `$D590`,
  `$D592`, `$D599`, `$D8F5`), i.e. C0:3783 ran to completion. Nothing is
  parked; the field is free.

The road "battles" the chain harnesses win are **not story events**:
The road "battles" the chain harnesses win are **not story events**:
event **0804** (`FC:092F`: `0b 45 / 0b 42 / 4f 3a / 4f 0c`, end
`FC:0937`) — a 134-frame VM wrapper that launches the battle engine and
leaves `D51B=0B44` behind (the road-scene fragment family's id stays in
`$D51B`). `V76=1 vm=FC:092F D51B=0804` → `V76=0 vm=FC:0937 D51B=0B44`
per run log. What fires it is UNRESOLVED: random-encounter dispatch and
the wandering monster NPCs (0x1862/0x186A — ids that do not resolve
through any block table, eventrange) are both consistent with the logs;
battles fired both mid-walk and while standing against a wall.
Deterministic per input script through the step/RNG state, which is why
they masqueraded as scripted ambushes.

Exit from map 0x250 is `EdgeEvents[0] = 084E` (map north edge, y=0;
the other three edges are `$2000` = none). 084E is the first fragment of
the camp-journey chain: the mapJumps (`11 0c` → 宿営地 0x24E (31,21),
later `11 0e` → ロアーヌ 0x4B (31,77)) live in the consecutive fragments
it tail-dispatches through, not in 084E's own range. The intro story
does not gate the edge — the flag-54 gate below only picks the briefing
variant.

**Nibble-gate argument semantics, machine-VERIFIED (C0:2F5F)** — `33 id
win` reads flag `id`'s nibble via C0:370D, then: TRUE iff
`(win>>4) <= value < (win&0x0F)+1` (C0:2F81 `INC $8E`, then `BCS` on
`value >= $8E`), i.e. `value <= (win&0x0F)` as in §2.1; the TRUE continuation byte `< $0C`
is a big-endian event id and tail-dispatches (e.g. `33 36 cc / 08 4d` at
`FC:2380`: flag 54 == 12 → dispatch 084D, else fall through). Writers:
`36 id v` sets the nibble to `v&0x0F`; observed story values 0/1/3/6/12/15
(set 12 = "walking the road" phase at `FC:114E`, set 15 at `FC:1045` and
`FC:31D5`). The walk13-lineage runs sit at flag 54 = `$A` (10) at the
frozen state — the A-mash through selection windows diverges the
flavour path, harmlessly: both branches of the `FC:2380` gate end at
`FC:23C8`/`FC:23F2` and hand the field to the player.

-- the stats confirm), then A every 16 frames from 11400, through events
