```go
// DecodeMapTriggers decodes one map's trigger data from the ROM
// (internal/triggers; event points, exits, edge events, placed
// characters, destinations).
func DecodeMapTriggers(r mapfmt.ROM, id int) (*triggers.MapTriggers, error) {
	mt, err := triggers.Decode(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode map %04X triggers: %w", id, err)
	}
	return mt, nil
}

// JumpTable reads the global op-0x11 destination table (0x3CFB00).
func JumpTable(r mapfmt.ROM) ([]triggers.Destination, error) {
	return triggers.JumpTable(r)
}

```

`internal/game/field/encounter.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"fmt"

	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// Field encounter composition (C2:13EA) and the victory level bumps
// (C2:DA7C / C2:DAD8 / 5B:FF40), ported from godot/main.gd
// _compose_encounter and godot/enemy_ai.gd level_bumps — the reference
// matched the live engine traces (docs/field-monsters.md "Encounter
// composition", docs/formation-f.md). Every roll runs on the battle RNG
// (C2:032E, internal/game/rng.Battle), seeded from the play clock at the
// field handoff; the composition's rolls are the battle's first ones.

// FormationTables is data/enemy_formations.json (cmd/exportbattle): the
// FE:77BB appearance pairs, the 敵編成リスト rows and the 敵お供リスト
// patterns.
type FormationTables struct {
	Appearance     [16][16]AppearancePair // [race][band]
	Hensei         []Hensei
	Companions     [16][]CompanionEntry // per pattern, levels descending
	CompanionBonus int                  // FE:317A = 4
}

// AppearancePair is FE:77BB[race*32 + band*2]: the band's leader enemy id
// and hensei row.
type AppearancePair struct {
	Leader int
	Hensei int
}

// Hensei is one 敵編成リスト row: +0 the max count $5A, +1/+2 the
// height/width limits $5C/$5B.
type Hensei struct {
	Count     int
	WidthMax  int
	HeightMax int
}

// CompanionEntry is one 敵お供リスト (level, enemy id) pair.
type CompanionEntry struct {
	Level int
	ID    int
}

// EnemyFit is FE:D107's fit check inputs: the enemy record's formation
// cell width/height ((E6:E400[id] & 0x0F)*4 <= $5B, (size & 0xF0)>>2 <=
// $5C; enemies.json exports them decoded).
type EnemyFit struct {
	Width  int
	Height int
}

// EncounterLevels carries the enemy-level cells the composition and the
// bumps read: $F532 (global) and $F533[16] (per race). Runtime-only —
// the save system does not persist them (docs/field-monsters.md "SRAM
// persistence").
type EncounterLevels struct {
	Global int     // $F532
	Races  [16]int // $F533
}

// Compose builds one field encounter's enemy ids, leader first (C2:13EA).
// enc is the encounter byte ($141B: low nibble race, high nibble the
// companion pattern, F = the multi-leader variant), base the map's
// $D2FE, partyCount $F319. levelByte/fixedLeader/fixedHensei are the
// fixed-formation overrides (FE:7F5B rows; level_byte nonzero replaces
// the race level with $F532 ± byte&7F, bit 7 subtracting).
func Compose(brng *rng.Battle, ef *FormationTables, fit func(id int) EnemyFit,
	levels EncounterLevels, enc, base, partyCount int, levelByte int,
	fixedLeader, fixedHensei int) ([]int, error) {

	race := enc & 0x0F
	pattern := enc >> 4
	raceLevel := levels.Races[race]
	if levelByte != 0 {
		d := levelByte & 0x7F
		if levelByte&0x80 != 0 {
			raceLevel = clampByte(levels.Global - d)
		} else {
			raceLevel = clampByte(levels.Global + d)
		}
	}
	// C2:1411: the leader from band $56>>4, the hensei's max count.
	level := encounterLevel(brng, levelTerm(brng, raceLevel, partyCount), base, partyCount)
	pair := ef.Appearance[race][level>>4]
	leader := pair.Leader
	if fixedLeader >= 0 {
		leader = fixedLeader
	}
	henseiIdx := pair.Hensei
	if fixedHensei >= 0 {
		henseiIdx = fixedHensei
	}
	if henseiIdx < 0 || henseiIdx >= len(ef.Hensei) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("compose: hensei %d out of range (%d rows)", henseiIdx, len(ef.Hensei))
	}
	hensei := ef.Hensei[henseiIdx]
	ids := []int{leader}
	kinds := []int{leader}
	if len(ids) == hensei.Count {
		return ids, nil
	}
	if pattern == 0xF {
		// C2:1461: the loop runs hensei count - 1 slots, computed once at
		// entry ($5A - $34 with $34 == 1; $34 advances only on a passing
		// add but the count does not shrink). Each slot re-rolls the level
		// and may add a leader of the new band (fit and kind checked); no
		// companions.
		for i := 0; i < hensei.Count-1; i++ {
			level = encounterLevel(brng, levelTerm(brng, raceLevel, partyCount), base, partyCount)
			if encounterBudget(level, levels.Global, len(ids), 0) < rangeRoll(brng, 1, 15) {
				continue
			}
			id := ef.Appearance[race][level>>4].Leader
			if fits(fit, id, hensei) && kindOK(&kinds, id) {
				ids = append(ids, id)
			}
		}
		return ids, nil
	}
	// C2:14D0: copies of the leader, one roll per remaining slot (count
	// fixed at entry), budget $57 recomputed from scratch per slot.
	remaining := hensei.Count - len(ids)
	for i := 0; i < remaining; i++ {
		if encounterBudget(level, levels.Global, len(ids), 0) >= rangeRoll(brng, 1, 15) {
			ids = append(ids, leader)
		}
	}
	if len(ids) == hensei.Count {
		return ids, nil
	}
	// C2:150C: companions from pattern `pattern`, budget $58 set once,
	// up to three tries per remaining slot (count fixed at entry).
	budget := encounterBudget(level, levels.Global, len(ids), ef.CompanionBonus)
	comps := ef.Companions[pattern]
	remaining = hensei.Count - len(ids)
	for i := 0; i < remaining; i++ {
		if budget < rangeRoll(brng, 1, 15) {
			continue
		}
		added := false
		for attempt := 0; attempt < 3; attempt++ {
			clevel := encounterLevel(brng, levelTerm(brng, levels.Global, 4), base, partyCount)
			for _, e := range comps {
				if e.Level <= clevel {
					if fits(fit, e.ID, hensei) && kindOK(&kinds, e.ID) {
						ids = append(ids, e.ID)
						added = true
					}
					break
				}
			}
			if added {
				break
			}
		}
		if !added || budget == 0 {
			return ids, nil
		}
		budget--
	}
	return ids, nil
}

// rangeRoll is the engine's S_C2_032E on the battle RNG: 0 for lo == hi,
// hi == 0 and hi < lo.
func rangeRoll(brng *rng.Battle, lo, hi uint8) int {
	return brng.Roll(lo, hi)
}

// encounterBudget is FE:D0AF ($57, add 0) / FE:D0D9 ($58, add = the
// companion bonus FE:317A): max(0, global-excess>>4 + (level & 0x0F)>>1 +
// add - count).
func encounterBudget(level, globalLevel, count, add int) int {
	excess := 0
	if globalLevel > level {
		excess = (globalLevel - level) >> 4
	}
	return maxInt(0, excess+(level&0x0F)>>1+add-count)
}

// fits is FE:D107: the enemy's formation cell fits the hensei's limits.
func fits(fit func(id int) EnemyFit, id int, h Hensei) bool {
	f := fit(id)
	return f.Width <= h.WidthMax && f.Height <= h.HeightMax
}

// kindOK is FE:D139: at most three distinct enemy kinds ($16D2 list).
func kindOK(kinds *[]int, id int) bool {
	for _, k := range *kinds {
		if k == id {
			return true
		}
	}
	if len(*kinds) < 3 {
		*kinds = append(*kinds, id)
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// LevelsTable is data/levels.json (cmd/exportbattle): the bump tables.
type LevelsTable struct {
	RankRise [8]byte // FE:9B7D: 00 01 02 04 07 0B 12 1E (the doc's earlier
	// FE:9B7B reading was wrong; docs/field-monsters.md correction)
	Curves    [8][8]byte   // FE:6610's curve rows
	GroupRows [17][16]byte // 5E:6500: 16 race rows + row 16 (curve 5 everywhere)
	GlobalCap int          // FE:9C05 = 240
	GroupCap  int          // FE:9C06 = 192
}

// LeadingBelow is the shared threshold shape (C2:DA8D / 5B:FF52): 8 minus
// the entries passed while table[x] < r (the walk stops at the first
// entry >= r).
func LeadingBelow(table []byte, r int) int {
	n := 8
	for _, v := range table {
		if int(v) >= r {
			break
		}
		n--
	}
	return n
}

// LevelBumps runs the victory level bumps (C2:DA7C rank, C2:DAD8 groups
// -> 5B:FF40) on levels: race = $5D & 0F for a random encounter (op 18),
// -1 otherwise (row 16, and no $142F/$1430 terms in the rank rise).
// 17 rolls: the rank roll, then one per group whether or not the group
// bumps. The corrected decode: the rank table is FE:9B7D, the rise is 8
// minus the entries below the roll plus max(0, race_pre>>4 - global>>4);
// group i bumps only when 5E:6500[row*16+i] != FF (row = race for op 18,
// row 16 = curve 5 everywhere otherwise), by 8 minus curve 5E:6610[c*8]'s
// entries below the roll plus max(0, global_new>>4 - race>>4); caps 240 /
// 192. So a race-2 battle bumps group 2, not race 1.
func LevelBumps(brng *rng.Battle, t *LevelsTable, race int, levels *EncounterLevels) {
	global := levels.Global
	p2f := 0
	p30 := 0
	if race >= 0 {
		p2f = global >> 4
		p30 = levels.Races[race] >> 4
	}
	rise := LeadingBelow(t.RankRise[:], brng.Roll(0, 255)) + maxInt(0, p30-p2f) // C2:DA82
	global = minInt(global+rise, t.GlobalCap)
	levels.Global = global
	p2f = global >> 4
	row := t.GroupRows[16]
	if race >= 0 {
		row = t.GroupRows[race]
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		p30 = levels.Races[i] >> 4
		r := brng.Roll(0, 255) // C2:DB21
		c := int(row[i])
		if c == 0xFF {
			continue
		}
		b := LeadingBelow(t.Curves[c][:], r) + maxInt(0, p2f-p30)
		levels.Races[i] = minInt(levels.Races[i]+b, t.GroupCap)
	}
}

// levelTerm is S_C2_15E6 (level = $F533[race], add = $F319 party count)
// and S_C2_16F1 (level = $F532 global, add = 4): (level*7)>>3 + two
// roll(1, level>>3) + add - roll(1, 8), floored at 0.
func levelTerm(brng *rng.Battle, level, add int) int {
	v := (level*7)>>3 + rangeRoll(brng, 1, uint8(level>>3)) + rangeRoll(brng, 1, uint8(level>>3)) + add
	return maxInt(0, v-rangeRoll(brng, 1, 8))
}

// encounterLevel is FE:D097: $56 = min(255, max(level term, party term)).
func encounterLevel(brng *rng.Battle, term, base, partyCount int) int {
	return minInt(255, maxInt(term, partyTerm(brng, base, partyCount)))
}

// partyTerm is S_C2_16B0: ($1308 & 0xF0) + $F319 - roll(1, 8), floored
// at 0. $1308 = the map's $D2FE (the bump copies it at the touch).
func partyTerm(brng *rng.Battle, base, partyCount int) int {
	return maxInt(0, (base&0xF0)+partyCount-rangeRoll(brng, 1, 8))
}

func maxInt(a, b int) int {
	if a > b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

func minInt(a, b int) int {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

func clampByte(v int) int {
	if v < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if v > 0xFF {
		return 0xFF
	}
	return v
}

```

`internal/game/field/encounter_test.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"testing"
)

// The encounter-chain goldens. Engine-derived expectations, quoted from
// godot/main.gd's selftest and godot/battle.gd's battleselftest (both
// matched the live traces: encounter_comp.lua /tmp/encounter run1-3, the
// opening battle's rolls from seed 0210, docs/parity.md, and
// docs/field-monsters.md "Encounter composition"):
//   - 0x1862 -> race 2 band 0 -> leader 0x20 地狼, hensei 0, max count 5,
//     record HP 74;
//   - fresh 0x62 on 0x250 (base 0, party of 6): sizes 1..5 with 1 and 2
//     present, only 地狼 plus pattern-6 companions of level <= 5 (フェイ
//     0xF0);
//   - base 0x7F lifts the leader to a band-6/7 leader;
//   - the opening battle (seed 0x21, party of 4) composes [0x20] and the
//     battle's next roll sits at index 0x21A;
//   - F-variant fixed rows 138/139: seed 0x0F -> [17 17 16]/[241 241 240]
//     at index 0x108; seed 0x21 -> [17]/[241] at 0x228.

func encounterEnv(t *testing.T) (*FormationTables, func(int) EnemyFit) {
	t.Helper()
	return loadFormations(t), loadEnemyFit(t)
}

func freshLevels() EncounterLevels {
	return EncounterLevels{} // $F532/$F533 all 0 at a fresh game
}

func TestComposeBudgetsAgainstTheTrace(t *testing.T) {
	ef, _ := encounterEnv(t)
	_ = ef
	brng := newBattle(t, 0x21)
	// battle 1 of the live trace: $56 = 0 -> $58 = 3 with one enemy;
	// battle 2: $56 = 5 -> $57 = 1 with one, 0 with two, $58 = 4 with two.
	if got := encounterBudget(0, 0, 1, 4); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("budget(0,0,1,4) = %d, want 3", got)
	}
	if got := encounterBudget(5, 0, 1, 0); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("budget(5,0,1,0) = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := encounterBudget(5, 0, 2, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("budget(5,0,2,0) = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := encounterBudget(5, 0, 2, 4); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("budget(5,0,2,4) = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := encounterBudget(0x20, 0x60, 1, 0); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("budget(20,60,1,0) = %d, want 3", got)
	}
	// S_C2_032E returns 0 for lo == hi, hi == 0 and hi < lo.
	if got := brng.Roll(1, 1); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("roll(1,1) = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := brng.Roll(1, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("roll(1,0) = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := brng.Roll(3, 2); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("roll(3,2) = %d, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestComposeRace2Band0(t *testing.T) {
	ef, fit := encounterEnv(t)
	// The FE:77BB pair read at X = 0x40 (race 2, band 0): leader 0x20
	// 地狼, hensei 0, count 5.
	pair := ef.Appearance[2][0]
	if pair.Leader != 32 || pair.Hensei != 0 || ef.Hensei[pair.Hensei].Count != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("race2 band0 = %+v, want leader 32 hensei 0 count 5", pair)
	}
	// The record (enemies.json id 0x20): 地狼, HP 74 — the selftest's
	// "record +0 = 20h, 74 HP" (docs/parity.md).
	f := fit(0x20)
	if f.Width != 8 || f.Height != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("地狼 fit %v, want 8x8", f)
	}
	var rows []struct {
		ID string `json:"id"`
		HP int    `json:"hp"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(dataFile(t, "enemies.json"), &rows); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	hp := -1
	for _, r := range rows {
		if r.ID == "020" {
			hp = r.HP
			break
		}
	}
	if hp != 74 {
		t.Fatalf("地狼 0x20 hp = %d, want 74 (the encounter-chain pin)", hp)
	}

	// Fresh 0x62 groups on 0x250 (base 0, party of 6), 200 compositions
	// on one seeded generator: leader 0x20 always, only pattern-6
	// companions of level <= 5 allowed, sizes 1..5 with 1 and 2 present.
	brng := newBattle(t, 0x21)
	allowed := map[int]bool{0x20: true}
	for _, c := range ef.Companions[6] {
		if c.Level <= 5 {
			allowed[c.ID] = true
		}
	}
	sizes := map[int]bool{}
	withCompanion := 0
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		group, err := Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), 0x62, 0, 6, 0, -1, -1)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if group[0] != 0x20 {
			t.Fatalf("fresh 0x62 leader %v, want 地狼 0x20", group)
		}
		for _, id := range group {
			if !allowed[id] {
				t.Fatalf("fresh 0x62 encounter brought %v", group)
			}
		}
		for _, id := range group {
			if id == 0xF0 {
				withCompanion++
				break
			}
		}
		sizes[len(group)] = true
	}
	if len(sizes) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no compositions ran")
	}
	lo, hi := 99, 0
	for n := range sizes {
		if n < lo {
			lo = n
		}
		if n > hi {
			hi = n
		}
	}
	if lo < 1 || hi > 5 || !sizes[1] || !sizes[2] {
		t.Fatalf("fresh 0x62 sizes %v, want 1..5 including 1 and 2", sizes)
	}
	t.Logf("composition: fresh 0x62 sizes %v, %d/200 with フェイ", sizes, withCompanion)

	// A map base of 0x7F lifts the party term to 0x70 + 6 - roll(1,8) =
	// 110..117 -> band 6 or 7 (leaders 0x182 / 0x25 at fresh race level).
	band67 := map[int]bool{
		ef.Appearance[2][6].Leader: true,
		ef.Appearance[2][7].Leader: true,
	}
	for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
		high, err := Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), 0x62, 0x7F, 6, 0, -1, -1)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !band67[high[0]] {
			t.Fatalf("base 0x7F leader %X, want a race-2 band-6/7 leader %v", high[0], band67)
		}
	}
}

func TestComposeOpeningBattlePin(t *testing.T) {
	ef, fit := encounterEnv(t)
	// The live opening battle (seed 0210): the composition takes the
	// first rolls after the seed — two degenerate level-term rolls, (1..8)
	// = 6 and 8, four copy and four companion (1..15) rolls that beat no
	// budget — and the battle's next roll (1..65) sits at index 021A.
	brng := newBattle(t, 0x21)
	group, err := Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), 0x62, 0, 4, 0, -1, -1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(group) != 1 || group[0] != 0x20 {
		t.Fatalf("opening composition %v, want [32]", group)
	}
	if brng.Index != 0x21A {
		t.Fatalf("opening composition left index %X, want 21A", brng.Index)
	}
}

func TestComposeFixedFormations(t *testing.T) {
	ef, fit := encounterEnv(t)
	// Fixed rows 0x8A (enc F1, race 1, level byte 10) / 0x8B (enc FF,
	// race F, level byte 10) through the C2:1461 F loop: at frame 0x0F
	// both take the band-1 leader, add a same-kind copy (budget 1 vs roll
	// 1) and a band-0 leader (budget 5 vs roll 4); at frame 0x21 every
	// gate fails and the loop still burns all 20 slot draws (24 for a
	// count-5 hensei).
	row8A, row8B := loadFixedRows(t)[0x8A], loadFixedRows(t)[0x8B]
	if row8A.enc != 0xF1 || row8A.level != 0x10 || row8B.enc != 0xFF || row8B.level != 0x10 {
		t.Fatalf("fixed rows 8A/8B = %v / %v, want enc F1/FF level 10", row8A, row8B)
	}
	cases := []struct {
		row       fixedRow
		seed      int
		wantGroup []int
		wantIndex int
	}{
		{row8A, 0x0F, []int{17, 17, 16}, 0x108},
		{row8B, 0x0F, []int{241, 241, 240}, 0x108},
		{row8A, 0x21, []int{17}, 0x228},
		{row8B, 0x21, []int{241}, 0x228},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		brng := newBattle(t, c.seed)
		group, err := Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), c.row.enc, 0, 6, c.row.level, -1, -1)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(group) != len(c.wantGroup) {
			t.Fatalf("F %X seed %02X group %v, want %v", c.row.enc, c.seed, group, c.wantGroup)
		}
		for i := range group {
			if group[i] != c.wantGroup[i] {
				t.Fatalf("F %X seed %02X group %v, want %v", c.row.enc, c.seed, group, c.wantGroup)
			}
		}
		if brng.Index != c.wantIndex {
			t.Fatalf("F %X seed %02X left index %X, want %X", c.row.enc, c.seed, brng.Index, c.wantIndex)
		}
	}

	// Fixed row 0x32 (type 01, enc F2, level byte 20): the level term
	// comes from $F532 + 0x20 and the leader rides the lifted band
	// (nonempty). Type-04 list rows bypass the composition, so only the
	// type-01 path pins here.
	row32 := loadFixedRows(t)[0x32]
	if row32.enc != 0xF2 || row32.level != 0x20 || row32.typ != 0x01 {
		t.Fatalf("fixed row 32 = %v, want type 01 enc F2 level 20", row32)
	}
	brng32 := newBattle(t, 0x21)
	g, err := Compose(brng32, ef, fit, freshLevels(), row32.enc, 0, 6, row32.level, -1, -1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(g) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fixed 0x32 (enc %X level %X) composed empty", row32.enc, row32.level)
	}

	// The four random F bytes at fresh state: every add is a band-0
	// leader of the byte's own race column (single kind), sizes 1-2
	// across the 60 legal clock frames.
	for _, tc := range []struct{ race, leader int }{{0x0, 0}, {0x1, 16}, {0xB, 176}, {0xF, 240}} {
		sizes := map[int]bool{}
		for frame := 0; frame < 60; frame++ {
			brng := newBattle(t, frame)
			group, err := Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), 0xF0|tc.race, 0, 6, 0, -1, -1)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			for _, id := range group {
				if id != tc.leader {
					t.Fatalf("fresh F byte %X group %v, want band-0 leader %d only", 0xF0|tc.race, group, tc.leader)
				}
			}
			sizes[len(group)] = true
		}
		lo, hi := 99, 0
		for n := range sizes {
			if n < lo {
				lo = n
			}
			if n > hi {
				hi = n
			}
		}
		if lo != 1 || hi != 2 {
			t.Fatalf("fresh F byte %X sizes %v, want 1..2", 0xF0|tc.race, sizes)
		}
	}
}

// fixedRow is one fixed_battles.json row (FE:7F5B).
type fixedRow struct {
	enc   int
	level int
	typ   int
}

func loadFixedRows(t *testing.T) map[int]fixedRow {
	t.Helper()
	var rows []struct {
		ID    int `json:"id"`
		Enc   int `json:"enc"`
		Level int `json:"level"`
		Type  int `json:"type"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(dataFile(t, "fixed_battles.json"), &rows); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := map[int]fixedRow{}
	for _, r := range rows {
		m[r.ID] = fixedRow{enc: r.Enc, level: r.Level, typ: r.Type}
	}
	return m
}

// The type-03 fixed formations pass the battle's own leader and hensei
// row (FE:7F5B; flow/battle.go's fixed.Leader/fixed.Hensei). Enemy 00 is
// a real leader id (race 0 band 0), so the override must key on >= 0:
// fixedLeader 0 sticks against the race-2 pair leader 0x20, and the
// fixed hensei row sets the count — row 15's count 1 returns the leader
// alone before any roll, row 0's count 5 burns the copy-slot rolls the
// race-5 pair's count-3 row would not.
func TestFixedFormationOverrides(t *testing.T) {
	ef, fit := encounterEnv(t)
	brng := newBattle(t, 0x21)
	group, err := Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), 0xF2, 0, 6, 0, 0, 15)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(group) != 1 || group[0] != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fixedLeader 00 hensei 15 composed %v, want [00] (the override keys on >= 0)", group)
	}
	if brng.Index != 0x212 {
		t.Fatalf("the count-1 fixed hensei left index %X, want 212 (the leader's level term only; no copy/companion rolls)", brng.Index)
	}
	brng = newBattle(t, 0x21)
	group, err = Compose(brng, ef, fit, freshLevels(), 0x05, 0, 6, 0, 0x50, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if group[0] != 0x50 {
		t.Fatalf("fixedLeader 50 composed %v, want the leader 50", group)
	}
	if brng.Index != 0x21A {
		t.Fatalf("fixedHensei 0 (count 5) left index %X, want 21A (the fixed row's 4 copy + 4 companion slots, not the race-5 pair's count-3 row)", brng.Index)
	}
}

// The victory level bumps (battle.gd battleselftest pin, live rolls
// 0305-0315): from a fresh state a race-2 battle reads the rank roll 64
// -> +0 and 16 group rolls 0306-0315; race 2's row bumps group 2 only
// (roll 0 -> +8); global 0, every other race 0. The generator starts at
// index 0305 (seed 0x30 = clock 0x30, +5 placeholder rolls).
func TestLevelBumpsRace2Pin(t *testing.T) {
	lvl := loadLevels(t)
	brng := newBattle(t, 0x30)
	for brng.Index != 0x305 {
		brng.Roll(0, 255) // placeholder battle rolls up to the traced spot
	}
	levels := EncounterLevels{}
	LevelBumps(brng, lvl, 2, &levels)
	if levels.Global != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("global rose to %d, want 0 (the rank roll read 64)", levels.Global)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		want := 0
		if i == 2 {
			want = 8
		}
		if levels.Races[i] != want {
			t.Fatalf("race %d level %d, want %d", i, levels.Races[i], want)
		}
	}
	if brng.Index != 0x316 {
		t.Fatalf("level bumps left index %X, want 316 (17 rolls 0305-0315)", brng.Index)
	}
}

func TestLeadingBelowThresholds(t *testing.T) {
	lvl := loadLevels(t)
	// The doc's threshold pins for the race curve (5E:6610 row 1 = curve
	// [0, 2, 5, 9, 14, 20, 36, 68]): roll 0 -> +8, 1 -> +7, 4 -> +6,
	// 5 -> +6, 67 -> +1, 69 -> +0.
	curve := lvl.Curves[1][:]
	for _, c := range []struct {
		roll int
		want int
	}{{0, 8}, {1, 7}, {4, 6}, {5, 6}, {67, 1}, {69, 0}} {
		if got := LeadingBelow(curve, c.roll); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("LeadingBelow(curve1, %d) = %d, want %d", c.roll, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	// The corrected rank table FE:9B7D = 00 01 02 04 07 0B 12 1E (the
	// doc's FE:9B7B reading was wrong): +8 at roll 0, +7 at 1, +1 at 30,
	// +0 at 31.
	rank := lvl.RankRise[:]
	for _, c := range []struct {
		roll int
		want int
	}{{0, 8}, {1, 7}, {2, 6}, {30, 1}, {31, 0}} {
		if got := LeadingBelow(rank, c.roll); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("LeadingBelow(rank_rise, %d) = %d, want %d", c.roll, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

// The 20 fixed-seed battles pin: race 1's battles raise race 1 AND the
// global level (the rank rise lands on $F532, group 1's curve on
// $F533[1]); races 2-F stay 0; caps 240/192 hold
// (docs/field-monsters.md "Port pins").
func TestLevelBumpsTwentyRace1Battles(t *testing.T) {
	lvl := loadLevels(t)
	levels := EncounterLevels{}
	brng := newBattle(t, 0x21) // one fixed seed, 20 battles on the shared generator
	for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
		LevelBumps(brng, lvl, 1, &levels)
		if levels.Global > lvl.GlobalCap || levels.Races[1] > lvl.GroupCap {
			t.Fatalf("caps blown: global %d race1 %d", levels.Global, levels.Races[1])
		}
		for r := 2; r < 16; r++ {
			if levels.Races[r] != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("race %d rose to %d after %d battles, want 0 (only row 1 enables a group)", r, levels.Races[r], i+1)
			}
		}
	}
	if levels.Races[1] == 0 {
		t.Fatal("20 race-1 battles left race 1 at 0")
	}
	t.Logf("20 race-1 battles: global %d, race 1 %d (caps %d/%d)", levels.Global, levels.Races[1], lvl.GlobalCap, lvl.GroupCap)
}
```

`internal/game/field/field.go`:

```go
// Package field ports the field/map logic half of godot/map_view.gd (the
// reference; docs/*.md decodes are the ground truth): the placed-object
// system — slots, spawn with the speed-row rotation, the walk gate
// (C0:57FF), monster roam, the bump latch (C0:7797) and its dispatch
// (C0:5635), defeat/inert marking, map reload respawn —, the party step
// gate (C0:7DA9-829B), encounter composition -> battle dispatch
// (C2:13EA; docs/field-monsters.md), the OBJ palette slot list lifecycle
// with the four divergences from docs/subscreen-obj.md §Port implication
// fixed, and the event points/exits wiring over internal/triggers data.
//
// The action-script interpreter's op handlers live in
// internal/game/actions; this package owns the field mechanics the
// continuations drive (movement, checks, rolls) keyed by the op byte the
// caller supplies. Engine traces pin everything: exports/tests/trails
// (replayed in trails_test.go), the 0x250 spawn dump and encounter chain
// (docs/parity.md), the subscreen-obj probe (docs/subscreen-obj.md).
package field

import (
	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
	"sort"
)

// MapSpec is one map's gate data (map.json): pixel wrap, tile margins,
// the attr grid through the class table and the low buffer.
type MapSpec struct {
	Width  int // tiles
	Height int
	Attr   [][]int
	Low    [][]int
	Bounds [4]int // tile x0, y0, x1, y1 (C0:4F6E)
	Open   bool   // Controls bit 7 ($D0DD): proximity by wrapped tiles
}

// Field is one map load's field model: the object slots, the occupancy
// bitmaps, the party and the touch latch. Re-entering a map constructs a
// fresh Field — the engine respawns every placed monster on reload
// (docs/field-monsters.md "Respawn").
type Field struct {
	Tables  *Tables
	Rng     *rng.Field
	Classes []byte
	// Bank is the F8 script-pointer bank (exports/data/bank_f8.bin); the
	// field half of the instruction fetch reads its ops through it.
	Bank []byte
	// Targets holds ops 1A/30's walk targets (interpreter state the fetch
	// needs to re-aim; a live driver installs it with the op).
	Targets map[*Object]Tile

	WrapX, WrapY int // map size in pixels ($D0C9/$D0CB)
	OpenMap      bool
	Bounds       [4]int
	Attr         [][]int
	Low          [][]int

	Planes   [2][]byte // the occupancy bitmaps ($7F:1000 / $7F:1200)
	bmStride int

	Objects map[int]*Object

	// The leader. Either slot 0 is a live object (party mode) or
	// LeaderFrozen holds its pixel position (NPC trails, replays that
	// sample the leader).
	LeaderFrozen bool
	LX, LY       int
	LeaderPlane  int
	LeaderFixed  bool
	LeaderStamp  *stamp
	LeaderTile   Tile // $D6B2/$D6B4: the leader's tile at its last C0:5585

	Latch      int   // $D6B6: the latched touch slot (0 none, 0xFF consumed)
	LatchDir   int   // $D6B7
	Dispatched []int // slots C0:5635 dispatched this pass
	Bumped     []int // slots whose step was blocked by the leader this pass

	LastBlockGate bool // the latest block came from the gate, not collision
	Footprints    []Footprint
	// NmiFrame is the NMI counter's low bits ($0014), one increment per
	// logic pass; ops 2D/31 read its low bits. A replay can set it (the
	// leader31 fixture pins by it).
	NmiFrame int
	Error    string

	// QueueLen mirrors $D6BD for the live op-09 path: the caller sets it
	// to the event queue's length before each pass, and Enqueued collects
	// the words op 09 queues (drained into the event queue after the
	// pass, map_view's frame wiring).
	QueueLen int
	Enqueued []int

	// Party config for PartyInput (map header $D2FA-$D2FB, $D0DE-$D0E5).
	Slope     [2]int
	EdgeWords [4]int
	EdgesOn   bool

	// hop is $D8F2 (0 none, 1 run, 2 the d6-bit-10 hop); partyEdges/
	// partyBumped collect this pass's edge words and touched slots.
	hop         int
	d8e7        int
	d8e8        int
	partyEdges  []int
	partyBumped []int

	// Palette is the OBJ palette slot list ($D6E2) with its fade state;
	// spawn and objOp 69 touch it (palette.go).
	Palette *PaletteSlots
}

// New builds the field for one map load. bank is exports/data/bank_f8.bin
// (nil only when the caller never fetches — the replay supplies it).
func New(spec MapSpec, tables *Tables, classes []byte, bank []byte, rng *rng.Field) *Field {
	f := &Field{
		Tables:  tables,
		Rng:     rng,
		Classes: classes,
		Bank:    bank,
		Targets: map[*Object]Tile{},
		WrapX:   spec.Width * 8,
		WrapY:   spec.Height * 8,
		OpenMap: spec.Open,
		Bounds:  spec.Bounds,
		Attr:    spec.Attr,
		Low:     spec.Low,
		Objects: map[int]*Object{},
		Palette: NewPaletteSlots(),
	}
	f.bmStride = f.WrapX / 32
	for i := range f.Planes {
		f.Planes[i] = make([]byte, f.bmStride*(f.WrapY/8)+2)
	}
	return f
}

// slot returns the object at a slot number.
func (f *Field) slot(n int) (*Object, bool) {
	o, ok := f.Objects[n]
	return o, ok
}

// Spawn plants a new object slot record (C0:4C29's record build; the
// action runner's spawn): state = [script base, position, $D9B7, $D9B8,
// opcode, x, y, facing].
func (f *Field) Spawn(slot int, state [8]int) *Object {
	const speedDefault = 3
	o := &Object{
		Scr: state[0], Pos: state[1], T7: state[2], T8: state[3],
		Op: byte(state[4]), X: state[5], Y: state[6], Dir: state[7],
		Spd: speedDefault, Row: speedDefault,
		C3:   int(f.Tables.StepsPerTile(speedDefault)),
		C6:   0xFF,
		MDir: state[7],
		PXP:  0xFF, PYP: 0xFF,
		Running: true,
	}
	f.Objects[slot] = o
	return o
}

// SetExtras fills the counters objects spawned mid-walk need: speed row,
// step and pattern counters, proximity range/target.
func (f *Field) SetExtras(slot, spd, c4 int, c6 byte, c7, c8 int) {
	o, ok := f.slot(slot)
	if !ok {
		panic("SetExtras: no such slot")
	}
	o.Spd = spd
	o.Row = spd
	o.C3 = int(f.Tables.StepsPerTile(spd))
	o.HasVel = false
	o.C4 = c4
	o.C6 = c6
	o.C7 = c7
	o.C8 = c8
}

// SetObject stamps the object (C0:4C29-4CD1): the gate on its own tile
// sets the plane bits unless the caller pins them, then the hitbox is
// stamped on that plane. A replay that picks up objects mid-walk passes
// the engine's plane bits and the walk's target (at = stampTarget), where
// the engine's last passed check stamped.
func (f *Field) SetObject(slot int, hitboxes [4]Hitbox, gateFlags, plane, d8 int, at *Tile) {
	o, ok := f.slot(slot)
	if !ok {
		panic("SetObject: no such slot")
	}
	o.Hitboxes = hitboxes
	o.GateFlags = gateFlags
	if plane >= 0 {
		o.Plane = plane
	} else {
		cls := f.classAt(wrapPos(o.X, f.WrapX)>>3, wrapPos(o.Y, f.WrapY)>>3)
		if cls[1]&0x80 != 0 {
			o.Plane = 0
		} else {
			o.Plane = planeBits(cls[0])
		}
	}
	var p Tile
	if at != nil {
		p = *at
		o.D8 = d8
	} else {
		p = Tile{X: wrapPos(o.X, f.WrapX), Y: wrapPos(o.Y, f.WrapY)}
	}
	f.stampObject(o, f.shapeAt(o.hitbox(o.Dir&3), p.X, p.Y), planeIndex(o.Plane))
}

// StampTarget is the tile a walking object's last check targeted: c4 more
// steps along the walk's velocity (cardinal walks).
func (f *Field) StampTarget(slot int) Tile {
	o, ok := f.slot(slot)
	if !ok {
		panic("StampTarget: no such slot")
	}
	if o.T8 != 0 || o.C4 == 0 || o.MDir >= 4 || !isWalkOp(o.Op) {
		return Tile{X: o.X, Y: o.Y}
	}
	vx, vy := f.Tables.Velocity(o.Row, o.MDir)
	return Tile{X: wrapPos(o.X+vx*o.C4, f.WrapX), Y: wrapPos(o.Y+vy*o.C4, f.WrapY)}
}

// SetFrozenLeader installs the sampled leader position (NPC trails): its
// stamp restamps every pass on its own plane.
func (f *Field) SetFrozenLeader(x, y, plane int, planeFixed bool) {
	f.LeaderFrozen = true
	f.LX, f.LY = x, y
	f.LeaderPlane = plane
	f.LeaderFixed = planeFixed
}

// SetPartyConfig feeds PartyInput (map.json slope, edge words).
func (f *Field) SetPartyConfig(slope [2]int, edges [4]int, edgesOn bool) {
	f.Slope = slope
	f.EdgeWords = edges
	f.EdgesOn = edgesOn
}

// leaderPos is the leader's live pixel position for the roam logic
// (C0:5D1F/C0:5C91 read it).
func (f *Field) leaderPos() (int, int) {
	if f.LeaderFrozen {
		return f.LX, f.LY
	}
	if o, ok := f.slot(0); ok {
		return o.X, o.Y
	}
	return 0, 0
}

// placeLeader restamps the frozen leader each pass (C0:5E36 restamps on
// the own tile, so an erased copy does not stay unstamped).
func (f *Field) placeLeader() {
	if !f.LeaderFrozen || len(f.Attr) == 0 {
		return
	}
	cls := f.classAt(wrapPos(f.LX, f.WrapX)>>3, wrapPos(f.LY, f.WrapY)>>3)
	if !f.LeaderFixed && cls[1]&0x80 == 0 {
		f.LeaderPlane = planeBits(cls[0])
	}
	st := f.shapeAt(LeaderHitbox(), f.LX, f.LY)
	st.plane = planeIndex(f.LeaderPlane)
	if f.LeaderStamp != nil {
		f.apply(f.LeaderStamp, f.LeaderStamp.plane, false)
	}
	f.LeaderStamp = st
	f.apply(st, st.plane, true)
}

// StepPass runs one logic pass of the engine's object loop (C0:51F7):
// objects in slot order, all rolling on the shared field RNG. windowOpen
// ($76 != 0) drives only objects an event installed a script on.
func (f *Field) StepPass(windowOpen bool) {
	f.placeLeader()
	f.Bumped = nil
	f.Dispatched = nil
	slots := make([]int, 0, len(f.Objects))
	for s := range f.Objects {
		slots = append(slots, s)
	}
	sort.Ints(slots)
	for _, s := range slots {
		o := f.Objects[s]
		if o.Halted {
			continue
		}
		if windowOpen && s != 0 && !o.EventDriven {
			continue // C0:51A7: the leader always runs
		}
		before := f.Error
		f.step(s, o)
		if f.Error != before {
			o.Halted = true
		}
	}
	f.NmiFrame++
}

// TouchLatch reports the latched-touch state (a monster's touch waits for
// the leader's next C0:5585; the party step is off meanwhile, C0:7DB4).
func (f *Field) TouchLatch() bool { return f.Latch != 0 }

// DefeatMonster rewrites the touched monster's slot to the inert class at
// battle dispatch: event id 0x2000, no more movement or battles this load
// (the montage trace rewrites 1884 -> 2000 at the transition and the slot
// sits at 0 px movement for the rest of the stay). The slot stays put;
// re-entering the map respawns every placed monster (fresh Field).
func (f *Field) DefeatMonster(slot int) {
	o, ok := f.slot(slot)
	if !ok {
		panic("DefeatMonster: no such slot")
	}
	o.EventID = 0x2000
	o.Running = false
	o.Halted = true
}

// EncounterClass reports whether an NPC event id starts a field battle
// (docs/triggers.md): the 0x18xx/0x19xx ids carry the encounter byte (low
// nibble race, high nibble the companion pattern); anything else —
// including the inert 0x2xxx class — dispatches nothing.
func EncounterClass(eventID int) (byte, bool) {
	hi := eventID >> 8
	if hi == 0x18 || hi == 0x19 {
		return byte(eventID & 0xFF), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// graphicD9 is the one F9:A000 id with palette byte 81; objOp 69 sweeps
// live figures showing it to graphic 80 (whose byte 3 is 80, shared with
// id A3) so future scans match the re-keyed slot.
const (
	graphicD9 = 0xD9
	graphic80 = 0x80
)

// ObjOp69 runs `17 69` (C0:CA26) across the field: every live figure
// showing graphic D9 becomes graphic 80, then the palette list re-keys
// its 81 slot to 80 and ONE blocking firing runs the whole fade — 32
// iterations, ~64 frames (see PaletteSlots.ObjOp69). Returns false when
// nothing ran (no 81 slot). While the fade runs the engine's touch
// dispatcher skips ($D6B8 is the busy flag it tests, C0:AB31).
func (f *Field) ObjOp69() bool {
	for _, o := range f.Objects {
		if o.Running && o.Graphic == graphicD9 {
			o.Graphic = graphic80
		}
	}
	_, ok := f.Palette.ObjOp69()
	return ok
}
```

`internal/game/field/field_test.go`:

```go
package field

import "testing"

// The walk-gate, bump and latch pins from godot/main.gd's selftest (the
// reference reproduced them against the engine: the opening capture's
// latch f19441 -> dispatch f19449 = 8 passes; the 9-pass phase is derived
// from the disassembly; docs/field-monsters.md "Chase/bump trigger").

func openField(t *testing.T) *Field {
	t.Helper()
	tables := loadTables(t)
	spec := MapSpec{Width: 32, Height: 32, Bounds: [4]int{0, 0, 32, 32}}
	spec.Attr = make([][]int, 32)
	spec.Low = make([][]int, 32)
	for y := 0; y < 32; y++ {
		spec.Attr[y] = make([]int, 32)
		spec.Low[y] = make([]int, 32)
	}
	classes := loadClasses(t)
	bank := loadBank(t)
	return New(spec, tables, classes, bank, nil)
}

func leaderBoxes() [4]Hitbox {
	hb := LeaderHitbox()
	return [4]Hitbox{hb, hb, hb, hb}
}

// A monster's step into the party's tile is blocked by the leader's
// shape and records the bump (C0:7731 -> the party-walk bump C0:8049
// feeds the same touch dispatcher from the other side). The 0x250-style
// monsters carry the bump-armed behavior bits 01 from spawn
// (docs/field-monsters.md: 5150/5150 traced slot-frames with beh & 3 ==
// 01), so the blocked step latches the touch.
func TestMonsterStepIntoPartyBlocksAndBumps(t *testing.T) {
	f := openField(t)
	f.SetFrozenLeader(64, 64, 0, true)
	f.placeLeader()
	o := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(0), [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0x13, 64, 72, 0})
	f.SetObject(SlotNumber(0), leaderBoxes(), 1, -1, 0, nil)
	r := f.checks(SlotNumber(0), o)
	if r != checkBlock {
		t.Fatalf("a step into the party gave %v, want block", r)
	}
	if len(f.Bumped) != 1 || f.Bumped[0] != SlotNumber(0) {
		t.Fatalf("bumped %v, want [40]", f.Bumped)
	}
	if f.Latch == 0 {
		t.Fatal("the armed step must latch the touch (C0:77EF-780D)")
	}
}

// The latch dispatches when slot 0 next reaches C0:5585: a latch on the
// leader's fetch pass goes out 8 passes later, one on its wait-end pass 9
// (the wait's `00 08` runs its whole count because the latch stops the
// party step's $D9B7 = 1, C0:7DB4). C0:5651 restores the latched facing.
func TestBumpLatchDispatchPhases(t *testing.T) {
	for _, phase := range [][2]int{{0, 8}, {1, 9}} {
		f := openField(t)
		f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 64, 64, 1})
		f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
		f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
		mon := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(0), [8]int{0, 0, 1, 0, 0x13, 64, 72, 0})
		f.SetObject(SlotNumber(0), leaderBoxes(), 1, -1, 0, nil)
		mon.Halted = true // its step is driven below
		latchPass := -1
		got := -1
		for p := 0; p < 40; p++ {
			f.Dispatched = nil
			f.StepPass(false)
			if latchPass < 0 && p >= 4 && f.Objects[0].T8 == phase[0] {
				f.checks(SlotNumber(0), mon)
				mon.Dir = 3
				latchPass = p
			}
			f.PartyInput(0)
			if len(f.Dispatched) > 0 {
				got = p - latchPass
				break
			}
		}
		if got != phase[1] {
			t.Fatalf("bump latch on a leader t8=%d pass dispatched %d passes later (latch %X), want %d",
				phase[0], got, f.Latch, phase[1])
		}
		if mon.Dir != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("the dispatched monster's facing %d, want the latched 0 restored (C0:5651)", mon.Dir)
		}
		if f.Latch != LatchDispatched {
			t.Fatalf("latch %X, want the consumed FF", f.Latch)
		}
	}
}

// The party step gate: the leader's own shape stamps, and a step into a
// monster's tile bumps from the party side (C0:7FFA). Slides probe the
// diagonals on a gate block (C0:5AAE-5AF9).
func TestPartyStepGate(t *testing.T) {
	f := openField(t)
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 64, 64, 1})
	f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
	f.SetPartyConfig([2]int{0, 0}, [4]int{0, 0, 0, 0}, false)

	// One pass: the leader's script 0 waits; the party input arms a
	// north step. The tile above (64, 56) is open ground.
	f.StepPass(false)
	f.PartyInput(0x08)
	if f.Objects[0].Op != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("the armed step set op %02X, want 02 (the party walk)", f.Objects[0].Op)
	}
	// Walk the step out: 8 passes per tile at row 1.
	for i := 0; i < 10 && f.Objects[0].T8 == 0; i++ {
		f.StepPass(false)
	}
	if f.Objects[0].Y != 56 {
		t.Fatalf("the north step landed at y %d, want 56", f.Objects[0].Y)
	}

	// A wall of the gate: block an east step with an NPC (the party
	// bump). The NPC stands at (72, 56) facing the party.
	npc := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(0), [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 72, 56, 2})
	f.SetObject(SlotNumber(0), leaderBoxes(), 1, -1, 0, nil)
	_ = npc
	f.StepPass(false)
	f.PartyInput(0x01) // right
	if len(f.PartyBumpedSlots()) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the blocked east step bumped %v, want the NPC slot", f.PartyBumpedSlots())
	}
	if f.Objects[0].X != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("the blocked step moved to x %d, want to stay 64", f.Objects[0].X)
	}
}

// The party bump touches candidates in ascending slot order (the
// engine's object loop order; the GDScript reference iterates its
// insertion-ordered dict). With several armed NPCs on the target tile
// the dispatch target must be the LOWEST slot on every pass — a Go map
// iterates in random order, so this pin fails an unsorted walk.
func TestPartyBumpOrderDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	for trial := 0; trial < 200; trial++ {
		f := openField(t)
		f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 64, 64, 1})
		f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
		f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
		for i, slot := range []int{0x40, 0x80, 0xC0, 0x100} {
			// the four NPCs stand on the leader's east target tile, each
			// 1 px further north so every shape overlaps the probe
			mon := f.Spawn(slot, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 72, 64 - i, 2})
			f.SetObject(slot, leaderBoxes(), 1, -1, 0, nil)
			_ = mon
		}
		f.StepPass(false)
		f.PartyInput(0x01) // east into the crowd
		got := f.PartyBumpedSlots()
		want := []int{0x40, 0x80, 0xC0, 0x100}
		if len(got) != len(want) {
			t.Fatalf("trial %d: bumped %v, want %v", trial, got, want)
		}
		for i := range want {
			if got[i] != want[i] {
				t.Fatalf("trial %d: bumped %v, want ascending %v (the dispatch target must be the lowest slot)", trial, got, want)
			}
		}
	}
}

// Each bounds edge queues its own word (C0:5976-5A39; the words index
// 0 north, 1 south, 2 west, 3 east): west onto x0 queues word 2, east
// onto x1 word 3, north onto y0 word 0, south onto y1 word 1 — and every
// queued step passes.
func TestPartyEdgeWordsPerEdge(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name   string
		x, y   int
		pad    int
		facing int
		word   int
	}{{"west", 8, 128, 0x2, 2, 0x0C}, {"east", 248, 128, 0x1, 3, 0x0D},
		{"north", 128, 8, 0x8, 0, 0x0A}, {"south", 128, 248, 0x4, 1, 0x0B}} {
		f := openField(t)
		f.SetPartyConfig([2]int{0, 0}, [4]int{0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D}, true)
		f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, c.x, c.y, c.facing})
		f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
		f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
		f.StepPass(false)
		f.PartyInput(c.pad)
		if edges := f.PartyEdges(); len(edges) != 1 || edges[0] != c.word {
			t.Fatalf("the %s edge step queued %v, want word %X", c.name, edges, c.word)
		}
		if f.Objects[0].Op != 0x02 {
			t.Fatalf("the %s edge step blocked (op %02X), want the queued step to pass", c.name, f.Objects[0].Op)
		}
	}
}

// The quadrant side rule (C0:5922): a tile class's byte-0 quadrant bit
// blocks only the step entering from that side. Class 28 carries bit 3
// (the north entry side): a north step onto it gates, an east step onto
// it passes.
func TestPartySideBitBlocksOnlyFromItsSide(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name   string
		x, y   int
		pad    int
		blocks bool
	}{{"north", 72, 64, 0x8, true}, {"east", 64, 56, 0x1, false}} {
		f := openField(t)
		f.Attr[7][9] = 0x28 // tile (9,7), pixel (72,56): bit 3 = the north side
		f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, c.x, c.y, 1})
		f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
		f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
		f.StepPass(false)
		f.PartyInput(c.pad)
		if c.blocks {
			if op := f.Objects[0].Op; op != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("the north step onto a north-side bit armed a walk (op %02X), want the gate", op)
			}
			continue
		}
		for i := 0; i < 10 && f.Objects[0].T8 == 0; i++ {
			f.StepPass(false)
		}
		if x := f.Objects[0].X; x != 72 {
			t.Fatalf("the east step over the side-bit tile landed at x %d, want 72", x)
		}
	}
}

// A new tile with the low buffer's event-rect bit (bit 3) defers the
// latch dispatch to the next C0:5585 (C0:55E8-5609): the dispatch waits
// one pass, then fires with the latched facing (C0:5651).
func TestBumpLatchDefersOnEventRectTile(t *testing.T) {
	f := openField(t)
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 64, 64, 1})
	f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
	mon := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(0), [8]int{0, 0, 1, 0, 0x13, 64, 72, 0})
	mon.Dir = 5 // a facing the dispatch must overwrite with the latched one
	f.Latch = 1 // slot 0x40 latched, facing north
	f.LatchDir = 0
	o := f.Objects[0]
	o.Y = 56 // a new leader tile (8,7)
	f.Low[7][8] |= 8
	f.leader5585(o)
	if len(f.Dispatched) != 0 || f.Latch != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the event-rect tile dispatched %v with latch %X, want the dispatch deferred", f.Dispatched, f.Latch)
	}
	f.leader5585(o)
	if len(f.Dispatched) != 1 || f.Dispatched[0] != SlotNumber(0) {
		t.Fatalf("the deferred dispatch gave %v, want the monster slot", f.Dispatched)
	}
	if mon.Dir != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the dispatched monster's facing %d, want the latched 0 (C0:5651)", mon.Dir)
	}
	if f.Latch != LatchDispatched {
		t.Fatalf("latch %X, want the consumed FF", f.Latch)
	}
}

// A counter NPC ($D9B2 low bits 3) is a bump candidate from the party
// side like an armed monster (C0:7FFA collects bits 1 or 3); the
// party-side bump itself never latches — the latch arms only in the
// monster-side C0:77EF on bit-1 slots.
func TestPartyBumpIncludesCounterNPCs(t *testing.T) {
	f := openField(t)
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 64, 64, 1})
	f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
	f.Spawn(SlotNumber(0), [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 72, 64, 2})
	f.SetObject(SlotNumber(0), leaderBoxes(), 3, -1, 0, nil)
	f.StepPass(false)
	f.PartyInput(0x01) // east into the counter
	if got := f.PartyBumpedSlots(); len(got) != 1 || got[0] != SlotNumber(0) {
		t.Fatalf("the blocked east step bumped %v, want the counter NPC slot", got)
	}
	if f.Latch != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the party-side bump latched (%X), want no latch from C0:7FFA", f.Latch)
	}
}

// A passed step stamps a footprint word behind the leader when the tile
// just entered has class byte 3 bit 1 and byte 2 lacks bit 5 (class 08):
// the word lands on the tile the next step leaves, its delta facing+1
// (C0:5413-544B), and the low buffer's bit 1 marks the tile first time.
func TestFootprintOnFootprintTile(t *testing.T) {
	f := openField(t)
	f.Attr[7][8] = 0x08 // tile (8,7), pixel (64,56)
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 64, 64, 0})
	f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
	f.StepPass(false)
	f.PartyInput(0x08) // north onto the footprint tile
	for i := 0; i < 10 && f.Objects[0].T8 == 0; i++ {
		f.StepPass(false)
	}
	if y := f.Objects[0].Y; y != 56 {
		t.Fatalf("the north step landed at y %d, want 56", y)
	}
	if len(f.Footprints) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the one-tile party walk stamped %v, want nothing until the next step passes", f.Footprints)
	}
	f.PartyInput(0x02) // west off the tile: the pass stamps the footprint
	if len(f.Footprints) != 1 || f.Footprints[0] != (Footprint{X: 8, Y: 7, Delta: 3}) {
		t.Fatalf("footprints %v, want one at (8,7) with delta 3 (facing 2 west + 1)", f.Footprints)
	}
	if f.Low[7][8]&2 == 0 {
		t.Fatal("the low buffer's first-time bit missing on the footprint tile")
	}
}

// The NMI counter's low bits advance once per logic pass (Field.NmiFrame
// = $0014); ops 2D/31 read them for their frame schedules.
func TestNmiFrameCountsPasses(t *testing.T) {
	f := openField(t)
	for i := 1; i <= 5; i++ {
		f.StepPass(false)
		if f.NmiFrame != i {
			t.Fatalf("NmiFrame %d after %d passes, want one increment per pass", f.NmiFrame, i)
		}
	}
}

// The bounds-edge rule (C0:5976-5A39): stepping onto a bounds edge
// queues the map's edge word when the map has edge events, and blocks
// when it does not; 0x250's N-edge push (y=4, event 084E) is the live
// case (docs/map-format.md "Edge events fire from the bounds edge").
func TestPartyBoundsEdges(t *testing.T) {
	spec, ex := loadMap250(t)
	tables := loadTables(t)
	classes := loadClasses(t)
	bank := loadBank(t)
	f := New(spec, tables, classes, bank, nil)
	f.SetPartyConfig(ex.Slope, ex.Edges, ex.EdgesOn)
	// The leader stands at row 5 stepping north onto the bounds edge row
	// 4: the step queues the N word and passes (C0:5976-5A39); from row 4
	// a further north step blocks — the walker holds at row 4.
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, 20 * 8, 5 * 8, 1})
	f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
	f.StepPass(false)
	f.PartyInput(0x08) // north
	if !f.EdgesOn {
		t.Fatal("0x250 carries edge events (N word 084E)")
	}
	if len(f.PartyEdges()) != 1 || f.PartyEdges()[0] != 0x084E {
		t.Fatalf("the edge step queued %v, want [84E]", f.PartyEdges())
	}
	if f.Objects[0].Op != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("the edge step blocked the walk (op %02X), want the queued step to pass", f.Objects[0].Op)
	}
	// Walk the step out and push again: from row 4 the north step blocks.
	for i := 0; i < 10 && f.Objects[0].T8 == 0; i++ {
		f.StepPass(false)
	}
	if f.Objects[0].Y != 32 {
		t.Fatalf("the edge step landed at y %d, want 32 (row 4)", f.Objects[0].Y)
	}
	f.StepPass(false)
	f.PartyInput(0x08)
	if f.Objects[0].Op != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the push past row 4 armed a step (op %02X), want the hold", f.Objects[0].Op)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/field/gatesweep_test.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"fmt"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// The party walk gate, swept tile by tile against the exported walk data
// (0016 inn interior, 00E2 town — the two maps the translation wiring's
// live probes flagged as "partially unwalkable placed tiles"). For every
// tile inside the map's gate bounds and every direction, the party's own
// step path (partyChecks: bounds C0:5976-5A39, the class rules
// C0:5A60-5AF9, the quadrant side C0:5922) must agree with the data rule
// the same bytes state directly:
//
//   - the class row's byte 0 rules (attr_class.bin, F9:A400): the
//     0xC0-block rows, then the quadrant bits b0 & (8>>dir);
//   - the party's plane bits (planeBits of the standing tile's class);
//   - the bounds reading of partyBounds: onto x1/y1 blocks without edge
//     words, onto x0/y0 passes, the edge word maps queue and pass.
//
// The party path does not consult class byte 2 or the low buffer (the
// GDScript _party_checks shape, trail-pinned); the object gate's extra
// b2/low rules live in gateClass for the placed characters.
//
// The exports regenerate byte-identically (cmd/exportmap vs exports/data,
// checked 2026-11-24), so a sweep failure is a gate/data divergence, not
// stale data.
func TestPartyGateSweep0016And00E2(t *testing.T) {
	for _, m := range []struct {
		id       string
		talkable bool // unused; keeps the table readable
	}{{"0016", false}, {"00E2", false}} {
		spec, err := LoadMapSpecFromBytes(dataFile(t, "maps/"+m.id+"/map.json"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		ex, err := LoadMapExtrasFromBytes(dataFile(t, "maps/"+m.id+"/map.json"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		classes := loadClasses(t)
		tables := loadTables(t)
		bank := loadBank(t)
		sweep(t, m.id, spec, ex, classes, tables, bank)
	}
}

func sweep(t *testing.T, id string, spec MapSpec, ex MapExtras, classes []byte, tables *Tables, bank []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	f := New(spec, tables, classes, bank, rng.NewField())
	f.SetPartyConfig(ex.Slope, ex.Edges, ex.EdgesOn)
	hb := LeaderHitbox()
	x0, y0, x1, y1 := spec.Bounds[0], spec.Bounds[1], spec.Bounds[2], spec.Bounds[3]
	classOpen := func(tx, ty, dir int) bool {
		row := classes[int(spec.Attr[ty][tx])*4:]
		b0 := row[0]
		if b0&0xC0 == 0xC0 {
			return false
		}
		return b0&(8>>uint(dir&3)) == 0
	}
	classRule := func(cx, cy, dir int) partyResult {
		if !classOpen(cx, cy, dir) {
			return partyGate
		}
		return partyPass
	}
	// the bounds reading of partyBounds, axis by axis; a queued edge word
	// skips only the remaining bound checks, so the class rules still run
	want := func(cx, cy, dir int) partyResult {
		offX, offY := 0, 0
		switch dir & 3 {
		case 0:
			offY = -8
		case 1:
			offY = 8
		case 2:
			offX = -8
		case 3:
			offX = 8
		}
		if cx < x0 {
			return partyGate
		}
		if cx == x0 && offX < 0 && ex.EdgesOn {
			return classRule(cx, cy, dir)
		}
		if cx > x1 {
			return partyGate
		}
		if cx == x1 && offX > 0 {
			if !ex.EdgesOn {
				return partyGate
			}
			return classRule(cx, cy, dir)
		}
		if cy < y0 {
			return partyGate
		}
		if cy == y0 && offY < 0 && ex.EdgesOn {
			return classRule(cx, cy, dir)
		}
		if cy > y1 {
			return partyGate
		}
		if cy == y1 && offY > 0 && !ex.EdgesOn {
			return partyGate
		}
		return classRule(cx, cy, dir)
	}
	var bad []string
	for cy := y0; cy <= y1; cy++ {
		for cx := x0; cx <= x1; cx++ {
			for dir := 0; dir < 4; dir++ {
				d := dir & 3
				tx, ty := cx, cy
				switch d {
				case 0:
					ty--
				case 1:
					ty++
				case 2:
					tx--
				case 3:
					tx++
				}
				o := f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, cx * 8, cy * 8, d})
				f.SetObject(0, [4]Hitbox{hb, hb, hb, hb}, 0, -1, 0, nil)
				o.MDir = d
				got := f.partyChecks(o)
				if wantP := want(tx, ty, d); got != wantP {
					bad = append(bad, fmt.Sprintf("(%d,%d) dir %d -> (%d,%d): got %v want %v (attr %02X)",
						cx, cy, d, tx, ty, got, wantP, spec.Attr[cy][cx]))
				}
				f.eraseStamp(o)
				delete(f.Objects, 0)
			}
		}
	}
	if len(bad) > 0 {
		const show = 12
		for i, line := range bad {
			if i == show {
				t.Errorf("%s: ...and %d more mismatches", id, len(bad)-show)
				break
			}
			t.Errorf("%s: %s", id, line)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/game/field/install.go`:

```go
package field

import "saga3/internal/mapfmt"

// The live-install face (C0:B2D4 objOp 20 / C0:B1F7 objOp 1F), the
// leader-instruction face (C0:53CE, objOp 43's 1B 5B), the follower
// spawn (objOp 2C, C0:D976) and the object-id lookup (C0:E994). The
// palette funnel runs on the caller side after a spawn (the 11-caller
// assignment; docs/subscreen-obj.md) — resolve the figure's F9 byte 3
// and call Palette.Assign with it.

// FindObject is C0:E994: the slot an event's object id names, or -1.
// 0x80 is the leader (slot 0), 0xFF the event's own object (event_slot,
// $D6B1), 0x81-0x8F the nth object tagged 0x80 (event actors), anything
// else the first object whose tag ($D9D9: map entry index) equals the
// id. Ascending slot order — the engine's loop order.
func (f *Field) FindObject(id, eventSlot int) int {
	if id == 0x80 {
		return 0
	}
	if id == 0xFF {
		return eventSlot
	}
	nth := id&0x0F - 1
	slots := make([]int, 0, len(f.Objects))
	for s := range f.Objects {
		slots = append(slots, s)
	}
	sortInts(slots)
	for _, s := range slots {
		if s < SlotNumber(0) {
			continue // C0:E994 scans from slot 1 (0x40)
		}
		o := f.Objects[s]
		if id >= 0x80 && id < 0x90 {
			if o.Tag == 0x80 {
				if nth == 0 {
					return s
				}
				nth--
			}
			continue
		}
		if o.Tag == id {
			return s
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// InstallAction is map_view's installer (C0:B2D4's caller): resolve the
// object id, decline absent event actors (0x81-0x8F — the caller, the
// VM or game state, queues the event's words statically instead), skip
// unknown tags, replace any leader instruction and install the script.
// Returns whether the install happened (a skipped unknown tag reports
// true: nothing to do).
func (f *Field) InstallAction(obj, scriptID int, eventDriven bool) bool {
	slot := f.FindObject(obj, -1)
	if slot < 0 && obj > 0x80 && obj < 0x90 {
		return false
	}
	if slot >= 0 {
		f.Install(slot, scriptID, eventDriven)
	}
	return true
}

// Install is objOp 20 (C0:B2D4) with eventDriven, objOp 1F (C0:B1F7)
// without: the object runs script id from its start. An object between
// tiles is first moved on to the next tile (C0:B341); $D9D8 takes the
// tile's class (C0:B2A3); $D99A bit 7 (eventDriven) keeps it running
// while a window is open.
func (f *Field) Install(slot, scriptID int, eventDriven bool) {
	o, ok := f.slot(slot)
	if !ok {
		panic("Install: no such slot")
	}
	o.Inline = nil // the install replaces a leader instruction (C0:53CE)
	vx, vy, hasVel := f.installVelocity(o)
	if (o.X&7 != 0 || o.Y&7 != 0) && !hasVel {
		panic("Install: object between tiles across its walk without a cached velocity")
	}
	for o.X&7 != 0 { // C0:B341 adds $D9BD until aligned
		o.X = wrapPos(o.X+vx, f.WrapX)
	}
	for o.Y&7 != 0 {
		o.Y = wrapPos(o.Y+vy, f.WrapY)
	}
	o.Scr = f.scriptBase(scriptID)
	o.Pos = 0
	o.T7 = 1
	o.T8 = 1
	o.Running = true
	o.Halted = false
	o.EventDriven = eventDriven
	if len(f.Attr) != 0 {
		o.D8 = f.classAt(wrapPos(o.X, f.WrapX)>>3, wrapPos(o.Y, f.WrapY)>>3)[3]
	}
	delete(f.Targets, o)
}

// installVelocity is the reference's `o.get("vel", _velocity(o.row,
// o.mdir))`: the walk's cached velocity, or the row/direction pair.
func (f *Field) installVelocity(o *Object) (int, int, bool) {
	if o.HasVel {
		return o.VX, o.VY, true
	}
	vx, vy := f.Tables.Velocity(o.Row, o.MDir)
	return vx, vy, true
}

// RunLeaderInstruction is C0:53CE (from $D8E9/$D8EA): run one
// instruction from a list on the leader at once, then halt (the 3B
// terminator). objOp 43's leader instruction 1B 5B is the camera pan's
// arming op — the pan itself is the shell's camera; the 1B state this
// face leaves on slot 0 (T7/SC) is what the shell reads.
func (f *Field) RunLeaderInstruction(op, operand int) {
	f.runInline(0, byte(op), operand)
}

// runInline plants the two-byte instruction + 3B halt and fetches it.
func (f *Field) runInline(slot int, op byte, operand int) {
	o, ok := f.slot(slot)
	if !ok {
		panic("runInline: no such slot")
	}
	o.Inline = []byte{op, byte(operand), 0x3B}
	o.Pos = 0
	o.Running = true
	o.Halted = false
	f.fetch(slot, o)
}

// SpawnFollower is objOp 2C (C0:D976): a party member's figure in the
// first free slot, a copy of slot 0's record (position, facing and tile
// class stay the leader's), script 0 from its start, op 0, tag 0x80.
// The palette slot runs on the caller side (the funnel after the spawn).
func (f *Field) SpawnFollower(graphic int, hitboxes [4]Hitbox) int {
	slot := SlotNumber(0)
	for {
		o, ok := f.Objects[slot]
		if !ok || o.Removed {
			break
		}
		slot += slotStride
	}
	if slot >= 0x800 {
		panic("SpawnFollower: no free object slot")
	}
	lead, ok := f.slot(0)
	if !ok {
		panic("SpawnFollower: no leader in slot 0")
	}
	o := *lead // C0:D976 copies slot 0's whole record
	o.Stamp = cloneStamp(lead.Stamp)
	o.Scr = f.scriptBase(0)
	o.Pos = 0
	o.Op = 0
	o.T7 = 1
	o.T8 = 1
	o.Tag = 0x80
	o.EventDriven = false
	o.Halted = false
	o.Scene = false
	o.Running = true
	o.Hitboxes = hitboxes
	o.Inline = nil
	if graphic >= 0xFD { // C0:7B0A
		o.GateFlags |= 0x0C
	}
	f.Objects[slot] = &o
	return slot
}

func cloneStamp(s *stamp) *stamp {
	if s == nil {
		return nil
	}
	c := *s
	c.rows = append([]byte(nil), s.rows...)
	return &c
}

// FigurePaletteSlot is the funnel's caller-side helper for spawns: the
// figure's palette byte (F9:A000 + id*4 + 3) and its patch key, ready
// for Palette.Assign. Hide figures (id >= FD) take no slot.
func FigurePaletteSlot(r mapfmt.ROM, graphic, objClass int, figure0 bool) (pal int, patch bool, ok bool) {
	if Hide(graphic) {
		return 0, false, false
	}
	p, err := FigurePalette(r, graphic)
	if err != nil {
		panic("FigurePaletteSlot: " + err.Error())
	}
	return p, Patch(graphic, objClass, figure0), true
}

func sortInts(v []int) {
	for i := 1; i < len(v); i++ {
		for j := i; j > 0 && v[j] < v[j-1]; j-- {
			v[j], v[j-1] = v[j-1], v[j]
		}
	}
}
```

```go
import (

// The live-install goldens, re-hosted from godot/main.gd's selftest
// ("field install ok: the installed NPC walks under a window, others
// hold, 09 queued 0002; stay jumps keep the map; the leader walks under
// party_input and runs an installed script") and the fixtures it cites
// (tests/leader31_0272.json). The window is the caller's input_locked,
// fed to StepPass; the event queue is the caller's list, fed to
// QueueLen and drained from Enqueued after each pass (map_view's frame
// wiring).

func newField0250(t *testing.T) (*Field, MapExtras) {
	return newField0250At(t, 30, 50, 1)
}

func newField0250At(t *testing.T, tx, ty, facing int) (*Field, MapExtras) {
	t.Helper()
	spec, ex := loadMap250(t)
	tables := loadTables(t)
	classes := loadClasses(t)
	bank := loadBank(t)
	f := New(spec, tables, classes, bank, rng.NewField())
	f.SetPartyConfig(ex.Slope, ex.Edges, ex.EdgesOn)
	// The leader at the spawn tile and the ten placed records (map_view's
	// _spawn_npcs wiring).
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{f.scriptBase(0), 0, 1, 0, 0, tx * 8, ty * 8, facing})
	f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxes(), 0, -1, 0, nil)
	for i, rec := range ex.NPCs {
		f.SpawnNPC(SlotNumber(i), rec)
	}
	return f, ex
}

func itoa(v int) string { return strconv.Itoa(v) }

// drain mirrors map_view's frame wiring: the enqueued words join the
// event queue after the pass, and the next pass reads its length.
func drain(f *Field, queue *[]int) {
	*queue = append(*queue, f.Enqueued...)
	f.Enqueued = nil
	f.QueueLen = len(*queue)
}

// Golden: the installed NPC walks under a window, the uninstalled one
// holds, script 0945's `09 00 02` queues word 0002 once (the live op-09
// path waits while the queue is non-empty), unknown tags skip, and
// absent event actors are declined for the caller's static fallback.
func TestFieldInstallGolden(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newField0250(t)
	f.QueueLen = 0
	var queue []int
	if !f.InstallAction(0, 162, true) {
		t.Fatal("installing entry 0 (slot 0x40) must succeed")
	}
	if !f.InstallAction(2, 0x945, true) {
		t.Fatal("installing entry 2 (slot 0xC0) must succeed")
	}
	if !f.InstallAction(0x55, 0x945, true) {
		t.Fatal("a tag with no object skips (reports true, does nothing)")
	}
	if slot := f.FindObject(0x55, -1); slot != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("tag 55 resolved to %X, want -1", slot)
	}
	// Event actors are not runner objects yet: the installer declines and
	// the caller (game state) queues the words statically.
	if f.InstallAction(0x81, 0x945, true) {
		t.Fatal("field install accepted an event actor")
	}
	start := [2]int{f.Objects[SlotNumber(0)].X, f.Objects[SlotNumber(0)].Y}
	still := [2]int{f.Objects[SlotNumber(1)].X, f.Objects[SlotNumber(1)].Y}
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		f.StepPass(true) // the window holds everything not installed
		drain(f, &queue)
	}
	moved := [2]int{f.Objects[SlotNumber(0)].X, f.Objects[SlotNumber(0)].Y}
	held := [2]int{f.Objects[SlotNumber(1)].X, f.Objects[SlotNumber(1)].Y}
	if moved == start {
		t.Fatal("the installed NPC did not walk under the window")
	}
	if held != still {
		t.Fatalf("the uninstalled NPC moved: %v -> %v", still, held)
	}
	if len(queue) != 1 || queue[0] != 0x0002 {
		t.Fatalf("queue %v, want [0002] exactly (the 09 waits while the queue holds the word)", queue)
	}
}

// objOp 1F (C0:B1F7) installs without $D99A bit 7: under a window the
// object holds still.
func TestInstallWithoutEventDrivenHolds(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newField0250(t)
	if !f.InstallAction(3, 162, false) {
		t.Fatal("installing entry 3 (slot 0x100) must succeed")
	}
	f1 := [2]int{f.Objects[SlotNumber(3)].X, f.Objects[SlotNumber(3)].Y}
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ {
		f.StepPass(true)
		drain(f, &[]int{})
	}
	f2 := [2]int{f.Objects[SlotNumber(3)].X, f.Objects[SlotNumber(3)].Y}
	if f1 != f2 {
		t.Fatalf("objOp 1F object moved under a window: %v -> %v", f1, f2)
	}
}

// objOp 20 on the leader (0x80): slot 0 runs the script in event mode
// (party input off) and walks under a window.
func TestLeaderInstallWalksUnderWindow(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newField0250(t)
	lstart := [2]int{f.Objects[0].X, f.Objects[0].Y}
	if !f.InstallAction(0x80, 162, true) {
		t.Fatal("leader install declined")
	}
	if !f.Objects[0].EventDriven {
		t.Fatal("the leader install must set $D99A bit 7")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		f.StepPass(true)
		drain(f, &[]int{})
	}

	if lend == lstart {

// Leader instruction 31 0E (C0:53CE + C0:6291/6B03) on 0272: 14 tiles
// up at 1 px, the FF:6802 spin facing every 4th $14 (tests/

func TestLeaderInstruction31(t *testing.T) {
	spec, err := LoadMapSpec("../../../exports/data/maps/0272/map.json")

	var fx struct {

		}

		if f.Objects[0].Y != row[1] || f.Objects[0].Dir != row[2] {

		}
	}

// objOp 2C on 0250 (the 0B4B chain, emulator opening row 0): five
// followers copy the leader into slots 0x2C0-0x3C0, the VM's stepped
// script ids 013E-0142 walk them to their rest tiles facing 3, and
// 0B49's 013C op-30 walks slot 15 back x-first and frees the slot.
func TestFollowerSpawnAndWalkBack(t *testing.T) {
	// The engine's opening row 0: the party [00 01 02 03 04 06] with the
	// leader at tile (12, 58) facing west (C0:C338's move-record flag 86h;
	// EF01 = 3E is what 084C leaves). FE:961B's graphics for allies
	// 01 02 03 04 06 are 04 05 03 06 00.
	f, _ := newField0250At(t, 12, 58, 2)
	gfx := [5]int{0x04, 0x05, 0x03, 0x06, 0x00}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		slot := f.SpawnFollower(gfx[i], actorHitboxes(t, gfx[i]))
		if slot != 0x2C0+i*slotStride {
			t.Fatalf("follower %d took slot %X, want the first free from 0x40 order", i, slot)
		}
		if f.Objects[slot].Tag != 0x80 || f.Objects[slot].Op != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("follower %d record: tag %X op %02X, want 080/00", i, f.Objects[slot].Tag, f.Objects[slot].Op)
		}
		if f.Objects[slot].X != f.Objects[0].X || f.Objects[slot].Y != f.Objects[0].Y || f.Objects[slot].Dir != 2 {
			t.Fatal("the follower must copy the leader's place and facing")
		}
		// The VM's 4f 55 01 steps script ids 013E-0142 onto the slots
		// (objOp 20; FE tables: member k's script is 013D + k + 1).
		f.Install(slot, 0x13E+i, true)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 60; i++ {
		f.StepPass(true)
		drain(f, &[]int{})
	}
	rest := ""
	for k := 0x2C0; k < 0x400; k += slotStride {
		o := f.Objects[k]
		rest += itoa(o.X) + "," + itoa(o.Y) + "," + itoa(o.Dir) + " "
	}
	wantRest := "96,440,3 96,480,3 64,464,3 80,448,3 72,488,3 "
	if rest != wantRest {
		t.Fatalf("0B4B followers rest at %q, want %q", rest, wantRest)
	}
	// 0B49: script 013C (op 30) walks each follower back to the leader's
	// tile, x first, and frees the slot there.
	for k := 0x2C0; k < 0x400; k += slotStride {
		f.Install(k, 0x13C, true)
	}
	path := ""
	freed := false
	for i := 0; i < 120 && !freed; i++ {
		f.StepPass(true)
		drain(f, &[]int{})
		o := f.Objects[0x3C0]
		fp := itoa(o.X) + "," + itoa(o.Y)
		if path == "" || path[len(path)-len(fp):] != fp {
			path += fp + "\n"
		}
		if o.Removed {
			freed = true
		}
	}
	if !freed {
		t.Fatal("slot 15 was not freed on arrival (C0:6DAB)")
	}
	want := ""
	for x := 72; x <= 96; x++ {
		want += itoa(x) + ",488\n"
	}
	for y := 487; y >= 464; y-- {
		want += "96," + itoa(y) + "\n"
	}
	if path != want {
		t.Fatalf("slot 15 path:\n%s\nwant:\n%s", path, want)
	}
	for k := 0x2C0; k < 0x400; k += slotStride {
		if !f.Objects[k].Removed {
			t.Fatalf("slot %X not freed", k)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/game/field/object.go`:

```go
package field

// Object is one NPC slot record (stride $40 in WRAM $D9A0; the leader is
// slot 0). The script half (scr/pos/op and the handlers' state changes)
// is the action-runner domain (internal/game/actions); this package owns
// the field half: position, motion, the walk gate and collision, the
// bump latch, and the rolls those make on the field RNG. A replay drives
// the script fields from the engine trail (see trails_test.go); a live
// driver keeps them in the action runner and mirrors this struct.
type Object struct {
	Scr  int // script base ($D9D0 record pointer's script cursor base)
	Pos  int // script cursor ($D9B5)
	T7   int // $D9B7: wait or tile count
	T8   int // $D9B8: 1 = fetch a new instruction on the next pass
	Op   byte
	X, Y int  // live pixel position ($D9AA/$D9AC)
	Dir  int  // facing $D9A9: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right (4+ pose groups)
	Spd  int  // $D9BB low nibble: the object's base speed row
	Row  int  // $D9BC: the speed row currently moving at
	C3   int  // $D9C3: passes per tile (FF:65CC[row])
	C4   int  // $D9C4: passes left on this tile
	C6   byte // $D9C6: the working move pattern (rotates per pass)
	C7   int  // $D9C7: proximity range ($D99A bits 3-4 objects skip)
	C8   int  // $D9C8: the proximity jump target
	MDir int  // $D9BA: walk direction (0-7, 0x10-0x13 hops, 0x18 none)
	SC   int  // op 1B's per-step pass counter (the runner's $D9BE)

	PXP, PYP int // $D9C1/$D9C2: per-axis move patterns
	VX, VY   int // $D9BD/$D9BF: per-frame pixel deltas
	HasVel   bool

	// $D9D5-$D9D8: the class bytes of the tile last entered (C0:5485).
	D6, D7, D8 int

	// $D9D2 word (big-endian id) and $D9D4 low byte: the event id and
	// graphic the figure shows; the palette funnel and objOp 69 read them.
	EventID  int
	Graphic  int
	ObjClass int

	Tag         int  // $D9D9: the map entry index
	GateFlags   int  // $D9B2
	Plane       int  // $D9B1 high bits: 0x40 / 0x80 / 0
	Scene       bool // $D99A bits 3-4: scene actor, no checks
	EventDriven bool // $D99A bit 7: keeps running while a window is open
	Running     bool
	Halted      bool
	Removed     bool
	Frame       int // pose frame (op 27/15)

	Inline []byte // a planted leader instruction ($D8E9 list, C0:53CE)

	Hitboxes [4]Hitbox // the collision shape per facing
	Stamp    *stamp    // the shape's place in the occupancy bitmap
}

// slotStride is the engine's object slot stride ($40).
const slotStride = 0x40

// SlotNumber returns the slot's engine index (the map entry's slot key).
func SlotNumber(index int) int { return (index + 1) * slotStride }

// SetMotion is C0:62F8-632E, run at every walk start and re-aim: the
// axis patterns and the velocity follow $D9BA and the current row.
func (o *Object) SetMotion(t *Tables) {
	pat := t.AxisPattern(o.MDir)
	o.PXP = pat & 0xFF
	o.PYP = pat >> 8
	o.VX, o.VY = t.Velocity(o.Row, o.MDir)
	o.HasVel = true
}

// advance is one pass of movement (C0:7132): rotate the move pattern and,
// on a 1 bit, move each axis by its own pattern; one step counts when the
// pattern's bit was 1. True when the step count reached 0 (the tile is
// done). Returns whether the object moved a pixel this pass.
func (o *Object) advance(t *Tables, wrapX, wrapY int) (tileDone bool, moved bool) {
	bit := int(o.C6) & 1
	o.C6 >>= 1
	if bit == 0 {
		return false, false
	}
	o.C6 |= 0x80
	if !o.HasVel {
		// Objects picked up mid-walk by a replay derive the velocity here
		// (the reference's `if not o.has("vel")`); a live walk always ran
		// SetMotion at its start.
		o.VX, o.VY = t.Velocity(o.Row, o.MDir)
		o.HasVel = true
	}
	xb := o.PXP & 1
	o.PXP = (o.PXP >> 1) | pxpCarry(xb)
	if xb != 0 {
		o.X = wrapPos(o.X+o.VX, wrapX)
	}
	yb := o.PYP & 1
	o.PYP = (o.PYP >> 1) | pxpCarry(yb)
	if yb != 0 {
		o.Y = wrapPos(o.Y+o.VY, wrapY)
	}
	o.C4--
	return o.C4 == 0, true
}

func pxpCarry(bit int) int {
	if bit != 0 {
		return 0x80
	}
	return 0
}

// wrapPos wraps one axis at the map's pixel size ($D0C9/$D0CB).
func wrapPos(v, m int) int {
	return ((v % m) + m) % m
}

// StairDir is C0:577E: on a stair tile (the class byte 3 of the tile last
// entered has bit 0x80 >> (d+1)) a cardinal walk becomes one diagonal
// tile; $D9B2 bit 4 objects ignore stairs.
func (o *Object) StairDir(d int) int {
	if (o.GateFlags|o.Plane)&0x10 != 0 || d >= 4 {
		return d
	}
	if o.D8&(0x80>>(d+1)) == 0 {
		return d
	}
	o.T7 = 1
	if o.D8&0x80 != 0 {
		if (d+1)&3 < 2 {
			return 7
		}
		return 5
	}
	if d&1 != 0 {
		return 6
	}
	return 4
}
```

`internal/game/field/palette.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"fmt"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// The OBJ palette slot list ($D6E1 count / $D6E2 slots) and its CGRAM
// uploads, byte-faithful to docs/subscreen-obj.md (the decode closes the
// map-format gaps): the per-assignment scan C0:7B8A, the patch-figure
// asymmetry (compare FE, store FD — never matched, always a fresh slot),
// the frees on the despawn paths (op 3A and the two gated paths), and
// objOp 69's 81 -> 80 rewrite with the per-firing CGRAM fade.
//
// The four divergences the doc lists against the GDScript port are FIXED
// here by construction: (1) Assign runs per assignment, not once per
// spawn; (2) Free returns the slot to FF; (3) patch figures key the
// constant FD against the compare key FE; (4) ObjOp69 is the whole
// handler (rewrite + sweep + the whole 32-iteration fade), not a
// one-shot swap.

// PaletteSlots is the slot list of one map load. The engine resets it to
// FF at the three sites C0:3DEB/EAE1/085B (map load); a fresh value is
// the reset.
type PaletteSlots struct {
	List  [8]int // $D6E2: the palette byte per slot, 0xFF empty
	Count int    // $D6E1: the high-water count
	// Uploaded/UploadWord hold the last fade iteration's rebuilt CGRAM
	// words and the destination word ($BAB7): 32 bytes to CGRAM word
	// (slot+8)*16.
	Uploaded   [16]int
	UploadWord int
	// Iterations/Frames are the firing's blocking shape (C0:CA85-CA94:
	// LDA #$20 loop, two JSR $06EB frames per iteration).
	Iterations int
	Frames     int
	Fade       *PaletteFade
}

// NewPaletteSlots returns the reset list (all FF, count 0).
func NewPaletteSlots() *PaletteSlots {
	p := &PaletteSlots{}
	for i := range p.List {
		p.List[i] = 0xFF
	}
	return p
}

// Upload is one queued CGRAM transfer (C0:7BE0): 32 bytes from the EC
// table's palette to the CGRAM word 0x80 + slot*16 (colours 128 + slot*8).
type Upload struct {
	Slot    int
	Palette int
	Word    int
}

// paletteFD is the constant the patch path stores ($5AA7C3's LDA #$FD);
// its CGRAM upload reads EC palette FD.
const paletteFD = 0xFD

// paletteFE is the patch path's compare key ($5AA7B1's CMP #$FE) — never
// stored, so it never matches anything.
const paletteFE = 0xFE

// Hide reports the funnel's hide path (C0:7B01): graphic id >= FD takes
// it and returns BEFORE the scan — invisible figures never touch $D6E2.
func Hide(graphic int) bool { return graphic >= 0xFD }

// Patch reports $EFF7 = FF (5A:BFA8): figure 0 with graphic id >= 0x70
// (the 5A:8370 patch table's resolver threshold CPX #$01C0), or a class
// 0C / 4C figure.
func Patch(graphic, objClass int, figure0 bool) bool {
	if figure0 && graphic >= 0x70 {
		return true
	}
	return objClass == 0x0C || objClass == 0x4C
}

// FigurePalette is the normal record's palette byte: F9:A000 + id*4 + 3
// (file 0x39A000; the class table starts at id 0x100 = file 0x39A400).
func FigurePalette(r mapfmt.ROM, graphic int) (int, error) {
	off, err := r.ToFile(0xF9A000 + graphic*4)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("figure palette: %w", err)
	}
	return int(r[off+3]), nil
}

// Assign runs the funnel's scan (C0:7B8A) for one assignment: the slot
// already holding the palette wins, else the first empty one, else slot 0
// is overwritten. A patch figure compares FE and stores FD — never
// matched, always a fresh empty slot; two patch figures burn two slots.
// Returns the slot. An unchanged palette re-running is a no-op on the
// list (the found leg), per the rescan semantics.
func (p *PaletteSlots) Assign(pal int, patch bool) int {
	store := pal
	key := pal
	if patch {
		store = paletteFD
		key = paletteFE
	}
	for slot := 0; slot < 8; slot++ {
		if p.List[slot] == key {
			return slot // found: the index recomputes, list untouched
		}
		if p.List[slot] == 0xFF {
			p.List[slot] = store
			if slot+1 > p.Count {
				p.Count = slot + 1 // TYA; INC; CMP $D6E1; BCC +3; STA $D6E1
			}
			return slot
		}
	}
	// full: all 8 slots distinct — overwrite slot 0 and re-upload its
	// CGRAM; whoever still points at slot 0 silently recolours.
	p.List[0] = store
	return 0
}

// Free is C0:7BC5: the figure's own slot returns to FF (the despawn-path
// callers are interpreter op 3A and the two gated paths C0:6619/C0:6DA0;
// hidden figures with $D9D4 >= FD skip it — the caller checks).
func (p *PaletteSlots) Free(slot int) {
	p.List[slot] = 0xFF
}

// UploadFor is the upload queue's record for a taken slot (C0:7BE0): the
// stored palette byte picks the EC source (a patch figure uploads EC
// palette FD's data).
func UploadFor(slot, stored int) Upload {
	return Upload{Slot: slot, Palette: stored, Word: 0x80 + slot*16}
}

// PaletteChannels is one EC palette staged into WRAM (FF:BDD2): the
// driver $B878 splits the 16 BGR555 words into the R byte array at
// $BB25+0, the G word array at +1 and the B word array at +3 (clamped to
// 5 bits per channel by the combiner FF:BF2B).
type PaletteChannels struct {
	R [16]byte
	G [16]uint16
	B [16]uint16
}

// LoadChannels stages one EC palette (EC:8000 + 32*palette, file bank
// EC) through the driver FF:B878's split: R byte = word & 0x1F, G word =
// word & 0x3E0, B word = (word >> 8) & 0x7C (the B channel pre-shifted
// into the high byte's low bits).
func LoadChannels(r mapfmt.ROM, palette int) (PaletteChannels, error) {
	var c PaletteChannels
	off, err := r.ToFile(0xEC8000 + palette*32)
	if err != nil {
		return c, fmt.Errorf("stage EC palette %02X: %w", palette, err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		w := int(r[off+i*2]) | int(r[off+i*2+1])<<8
		c.R[i] = byte(w & 0x1F)
		c.G[i] = uint16(w & 0x3E0)
		c.B[i] = uint16((w >> 8) & 0x7C)
	}
	return c, nil
}

// PaletteFade is the objOp-69 fade state: the staged copy of palette 81's
// channels stepping one step toward palette 80's per firing (FF:BE7A).
type PaletteFade struct {
	Cur PaletteChannels // $BB25's working copy (81's data)
	To  PaletteChannels // $BB75's target (80's data)
}

// BeginFade stages the fade pair.
func (p *PaletteSlots) BeginFade(from, to PaletteChannels) {
	p.Fade = &PaletteFade{Cur: from, To: to}
}

// FadeStep moves the working copy one step toward the target (FF:BE7A:
// bytes step +1/-1, words +$20/-$20; a value with the sign bit set always
// steps up, an equal value stays) and returns the 16 CGRAM words the
// combiner (FF:BF2B) rebuilds. The combiner stores only R | G — the
// staged B word (high byte & 0x7C, FF:B878's split) is computed into $91
// and dropped: the ROM uploads the blue-less word verbatim (FF:BF6C).
func (f *PaletteFade) FadeStep() [16]int {
	var words [16]int
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		f.Cur.R[i] = stepToward8(f.Cur.R[i], f.To.R[i])
		f.Cur.G[i] = stepToward16(f.Cur.G[i], f.To.G[i], 0x20)
		f.Cur.B[i] = stepToward16(f.Cur.B[i], f.To.B[i], 0x04)
		words[i] = int(f.Cur.R[i]) | int(f.Cur.G[i])
	}
	return words
}

func stepToward8(v, to byte) byte {
	if v&0x80 != 0 {
		return v + 1
	}
	if v == to {
		return v
	}
	if v < to {
		return v + 1
	}
	return v - 1
}

func stepToward16(v, to, step uint16) uint16 {
	if v&0x8000 != 0 {
		return v + step
	}
	if v == to {
		return v
	}
	if v < to {
		return v + step
	}
	return v - step
}

// ObjOp69 is the palette-list half of `17 69` (C0:CA26): the slot entry
// holding 81 re-keys to 80, then ONE blocking firing runs the whole fade
// — 32 iterations of FF:BE61 (one 3-channel step + upload) with two
// frames each, ~64 frames, the tail CA92-CA9E ending the loop, clearing
// the $D6B8 screen-busy flag and setting $D8ED. The fade is not spread
// over repeated `17 69`s; 32 iterations let every channel (at most 31
// units apart) converge, so the uploaded words end at palette 80's R|G.
// Returns false when no slot holds 81 (the handler's loop RTS at
// C0:CA3E: nothing runs). The live-figure sweep D9 -> 80 is
// Field.ObjOp69's. $D6B8 is not modelled: it is a screen-busy flag (INC
// at CA71 on, STZ at CA96 off), not a firing counter.
func (p *PaletteSlots) ObjOp69() (int, bool) {
	slot := -1
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if p.List[i] == 0x81 {
			slot = i
			break
		}
	}
	if slot < 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	p.List[slot] = 0x80 // the rewrite
	if p.Fade == nil {
		panic("ObjOp69 on an 81 slot without a staged fade")
	}
	const fadeIterations = 32 // C0:CA85 LDA #$20
	for i := 0; i < fadeIterations; i++ {
		p.Uploaded = p.Fade.FadeStep()
	}
	p.Iterations = fadeIterations
	p.Frames = fadeIterations * 2 // JSR $06EB twice per iteration
	p.UploadWord = 0x80 + slot*16 // $BAB7: (slot+8)*16, the CGRAM word index
	return slot, true
}
```
