```go
package field

import "testing"

// The subscreen-obj lifecycle (docs/subscreen-obj.md, byte-verified with
// one live probe): the leader-first allocation, the per-assignment
// rescan, the despawn-path frees, the patch-figure FD asymmetry, the
// full-8 overwrite and the objOp-69 fade.

func TestPaletteLeaderFirstAllocation(t *testing.T) {
	// Live probe (tools/emulator/subobj_watch.lua, quoted in
	// docs/subscreen-obj.md): the opening screen allocates the leader
	// palette 01 into slot 0 FIRST, then the montage figures 03/04/05
	// fill slots 1-3 (SUBOBJ f=10892..10905: `01`, `01 03`, `01 03 04`,
	// `01 03 04 05`).
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	if got := p.Assign(0x01, false); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("leader palette 01 took slot %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x03, false); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("palette 03 took slot %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x04, false); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("palette 04 took slot %d, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x05, false); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("palette 05 took slot %d, want 3", got)
	}
	if p.Count != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("count %d, want 4", p.Count)
	}
	want := [8]int{0x01, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}
	if p.List != want {
		t.Fatalf("list %v, want %v", p.List, want)
	}
}

func TestPaletteRescanNoOp(t *testing.T) {
	// Rescan semantics (docs/subscreen-obj.md "Rescan semantics"): every
	// funnel call with an unchanged graphic is a no-op on the list; a NEW
	// palette adds a slot (a mid-map graphic change does not release the
	// old one).
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	p.Assign(0x01, false)
	p.Assign(0x03, false)
	if got := p.Assign(0x01, false); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("re-assign of 01 returned slot %d, want the found 0", got)
	}
	if p.Count != 2 || p.List[2] != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("re-scan mutated the list: count %d, slot 2 %02X", p.Count, p.List[2])
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x0F, false); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("new palette 0F took slot %d, want the first empty 2", got)
	}
	if p.List[0] != 0x01 {
		t.Fatal("the new palette released the old slot 0 entry")
	}
}

func TestPaletteFree(t *testing.T) {
	// Slot frees (docs/subscreen-obj.md "Slot frees"): op 3A and the two
	// gated despawn paths write FF back; the next allocation can take it.
	// The GDScript grow-only list diverged here — fixed in this port.
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	p.Assign(0x01, false)
	p.Assign(0x03, false)
	p.Free(0)
	if p.List[0] != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("freed slot holds %02X, want FF", p.List[0])
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x20, false); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the next allocation took slot %d, want the freed 0", got)
	}
}

func TestPalettePatchFD(t *testing.T) {
	// The patch-figure asymmetry (5AA7B1/5AA7C3): a patch figure's scan
	// compares each slot byte against FE but a taken slot is written with
	// FD — FE never matches anything, so every patch assignment takes the
	// first EMPTY slot; two patch figures burn two slots; a normal figure
	// can never match an FD slot either.
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	if got := p.Assign(0x10, true); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("first patch figure took slot %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if p.List[0] != paletteFD {
		t.Fatalf("patch slot holds %02X, want FD", p.List[0])
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x10, true); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("second patch assignment took slot %d, want the empty 1 (FD is never matched)", got)
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x10, true); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("third patch assignment took slot %d, want the empty 2 (each patch figure burns a slot)", got)
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0x10, false); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("normal figure took slot %d, want the empty 3 (no F9 byte 3 = FD or FE exists)", got)
	}
	// The GDScript's keying by the F9 byte 3 "reproduces neither the
	// slots nor the uploads": the upload reads EC palette FD for both.
	if got := UploadFor(1, p.List[1]); got.Palette != paletteFD || got.Word != 0x80+1*16 {
		t.Fatalf("patch upload = %+v, want EC palette FD at CGRAM word 90", got)
	}
}

func TestPaletteHideNoSlot(t *testing.T) {
	// The hide path (C0:7B01) returns before the scan: graphic id >= FD
	// never touches $D6E2.
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	if !Hide(0xFD) || !Hide(0xFF) {
		t.Fatal("the hide threshold is FD")
	}
	if Hide(0xFC) {
		t.Fatal("FC takes the scan")
	}
	p.Assign(0x01, false)
	if p.Count != 1 {
		t.Fatal("hidden figures must not burn slots")
	}
}

func TestPaletteFullOverwrite(t *testing.T) {
	// The full case: with all 8 slots distinct, `full` falls to
	// LDY #$0000, overwrites $D6E2[0] and re-uploads slot 0's CGRAM.
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		p.Assign(0x10+i, false)
	}
	if got := p.Assign(0xC7, false); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the ninth palette took slot %d, want the overwritten 0", got)
	}
	if p.List[0] != 0xC7 {
		t.Fatalf("slot 0 holds %02X, want C7 (0372: event actor graphic 164's palette C7 replaced AD)", p.List[0])
	}
	if got := UploadFor(0, 0xC7); got.Word != 0x80 {
		t.Fatal("the overwrite re-uploads slot 0's CGRAM")
	}
}

func TestPalettePatchAndClassSelection(t *testing.T) {
	// $EFF7 = FF iff figure 0 with graphic id >= 0x70 (the CPX #$01C0
	// threshold) or class 0C/4C (5A:BFA8).
	if !Patch(0x70, 0, true) || !Patch(0xA5, 0, true) {
		t.Fatal("leader graphic >= 0x70 is a patch figure")
	}
	if Patch(0x6F, 0, true) {
		t.Fatal("graphic 6F is below the patch threshold")
	}
	if !Patch(0x05, 0x0C, false) || !Patch(0x05, 0x4C, false) {
		t.Fatal("class 0C/4C is a patch figure")
	}
	if Patch(0x05, 0x20, false) || Patch(0x05, 0, false) {
		t.Fatal("plain placed figures are not patch figures")
	}
	// The class-0C setters: 5A:A947 (objOp 2E) writes $D9D2 = 0C before
	// the funnel and 20 after; 5A:A90D (objOp 2C) only when the member
	// record's byte 0 is >= B0. The funnel keys on the class DURING it.
	if Patch(0x05, 0x20, false) {
		t.Fatal("the post-funnel class 20 must not re-trigger the patch path")
	}
}

// The objOp-69 fade: palette bytes from the ROM (EC:8000 + 32*81 / 80),
// the per-step and per-firing upload words computed from those bytes.
func TestObjOp69Fade(t *testing.T) {
	r := rom(t)
	from, err := LoadChannels(r, 0x81)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	to, err := LoadChannels(r, 0x80)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	p := NewPaletteSlots()
	// The engine path into an 81 slot: graphic D9 is the ONLY F9:A000 id
	// with byte 3 = 81 (F9:A364 = 2c 26 82 81); graphic 80's byte 3 is 80
	// (F9:A200), shared with id A3.
	d9, err := FigurePalette(r, 0xD9)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g80, err := FigurePalette(r, 0x80)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if d9 != 0x81 || g80 != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("F9 byte 3: D9 = %02X (want 81), 80 = %02X (want 80)", d9, g80)
	}
	p.BeginFade(from, to)

	// No slot holds 81: the handler is a no-op (C0:CA3E RTS). The live
	// probe ran it with palettes 01/03/04/05 in the list and nothing
	// changed; $D6B8's ticks there belong to its other writers (it is a
	// screen-busy flag, not a firing counter).
	list := p.List
	if _, ok := p.ObjOp69(); ok {
		t.Fatal("ObjOp69 ran without an 81 slot")
	}
	if p.List != list || p.Iterations != 0 {
		t.Fatal("the no-81 path mutated the list or ran the fade")
	}

	// One FF:BE7A step, pinned directly: the R byte ±1, the G word ±$20,
	// the B word ±$04 toward palette 80's channels; the combiner uploads
	// ONLY the R|G word (FF:BF2B computes B into $91 and never stores it).
	first := p.Fade.FadeStep()
	wantFirst := [16]int{0x0000, 0x00A5, 0x03FF, 0x037B, 0x0294, 0x018C, 0x0108,
		0x02F9, 0x0233, 0x01AF, 0x016B, 0x02F9, 0x0294, 0x0339, 0x014C, 0x00A5}
	if first != wantFirst {
		t.Fatalf("first fade step upload = %04X, want %04X (EC 81 stepped one step toward EC 80; blue-less)", first, wantFirst)
	}

	// The firing: the slot entry 81 -> 80 (C0:CA41), then ONE blocking
	// firing of 32 iterations (C0:CA85-CA94, LDA #$20; two frames each,
	// 64 frames) — the whole fade inside the handler, not spread over
	// repeated `17 69`s. The upload goes to the CGRAM word (slot+8)*16
	// ($BAB7), and the last iteration's words are palette 80's R|G.
	p.List[5] = 0x81
	slot, ok := p.ObjOp69()
	if !ok || slot != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("ObjOp69 reported slot %d ok %v, want 5 true", slot, ok)
	}
	if p.List[5] != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("slot 5 holds %02X, want 80 after the rewrite", p.List[5])
	}
	if p.Iterations != 32 || p.Frames != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("firing shape %d iterations / %d frames, want 32 / 64 (LDA #$20, JSR $06EB x2)", p.Iterations, p.Frames)
	}
	if p.UploadWord != 0x80+5*16 {
		t.Fatalf("upload word %X, want %X ((slot+8)*16)", p.UploadWord, 0x80+5*16)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		want := int(to.R[i]) | int(to.G[i])
		if p.Uploaded[i] != want {
			t.Fatalf("channel %d at %04X, want palette 80's R|G %04X after the completed fade", i, p.Uploaded[i], want)
		}
	}

	// A second `17 69` with the slot now holding 80 finds no 81 entry and
	// RTSes (C0:CA3E) — the fade is not re-run until something re-arms
	// the 81 slot.
	if _, ok := p.ObjOp69(); ok {
		t.Fatal("the second firing must no-op once the slot holds 80")
	}
	if p.Iterations != 32 {
		t.Fatalf("iterations %d, want the untouched 32 from the first firing", p.Iterations)
	}
}

// Field.ObjOp69 sweeps the live figures showing graphic D9 to graphic 80
// (C0:CA52-CA6F) before the palette rewrite; inactive slots skip.
func TestObjOp69Sweep(t *testing.T) {
	spec := MapSpec{Width: 32, Height: 32, Attr: [][]int{}, Low: [][]int{}}
	tables := loadTables(t)
	f := New(spec, tables, nil, nil, nil)
	live := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(0), [8]int{0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1})
	live.Graphic = graphicD9
	live.Running = true
	dead := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(1), [8]int{0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1})
	dead.Graphic = graphicD9
	dead.Running = false
	other := f.Spawn(SlotNumber(2), [8]int{0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1})
	other.Graphic = 0x20
	f.Palette.List[2] = 0x81
	f.Palette.BeginFade(PaletteChannels{}, PaletteChannels{})
	if !f.ObjOp69() {
		t.Fatal("ObjOp69 with an 81 slot must run")
	}
	if live.Graphic != graphic80 {
		t.Fatalf("live figure graphic %02X, want 80 (the sweep)", live.Graphic)
	}
	if dead.Graphic != graphicD9 {
		t.Fatal("the inactive slot skipped the sweep (BEQ next)")
	}
	if other.Graphic != 0x20 {
		t.Fatal("a non-D9 figure must keep its graphic")
	}
	if f.Palette.List[2] != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("slot 2 holds %02X, want the 81 -> 80 rewrite", f.Palette.List[2])
	}
}
```

`internal/game/field/party.go`:

```go
package field

import "sort"

// The party leader (slot 0) under joypad control: C0:7DA9 runs each field
// frame after the object loop; a step it starts moves from the next
// frame's loop. pad = $02 (the high joypad byte: 01 right, 02 left, 04
// down, 08 up, 40 Y = run). Slope is the map header's $D2FA/$D2FB; edges
// collects the edge words a step onto the bounds' edge queues
// (C0:5976-5A39); PartyBumped the slots a blocked step touches
// (C0:7FFA -> AB2E).

// PartyBumped reports the slots the party's blocked step touched this
// pass (the caller clears it before PartyInput, as map_view does).
func (f *Field) PartyBumpedSlots() []int { return f.partyBumped }

// PartyEdges reports the edge words queued this pass.
func (f *Field) PartyEdges() []int { return f.partyEdges }

// PartyInput runs the party step (C0:7DA9). The leader is slot 0.
func (f *Field) PartyInput(pad int) {
	o, ok := f.slot(0)
	if !ok {
		panic("PartyInput: no leader object in slot 0")
	}
	f.partyEdges = nil
	f.partyBumped = nil
	if o.EventDriven || f.Latch != 0 { // C0:7DAC, 7DB4
		return
	}
	f.hop = 0
	if o.T8 == 0 { // C0:7DD0
		if o.Op != 0 && !(o.Op == 0x0B && pad&0x0F != 0) {
			return
		}
	} else if o.Op != 0 && o.Op != 0x02 {
		return
	}
	o.T7 = 1                            // C0:7E0B
	if pad&0x40 != 0 && pad&0x0F != 0 { // C0:7E14: Y runs one row faster
		if o.Spd&0x0F+1 != o.Row {
			f.setRow(o, o.Spd&0x0F+1)
		}
		if o.D6&0x20 != 0 {
			f.hop = 1
		}
	} else if o.Spd&0x0F != o.Row {
		f.setRow(o, o.Spd&0x0F)
	}
	if o.D7&0x90 == 0x10 && o.Row != 0 { // C0:7E7A: slow ground
		f.setRow(o, o.Row-1)
	}
	if o.D6&0x10 != 0 { // C0:7E95
		f.hop = 2
		f.setRow(o, 1)
	}
	f.d8e7 = pad | 0x10
	f.d8e8 = 0
	f.partyDispatch(o, pad)
}

// partyDispatch is C0:8052: right, left, down, up in that order.
func (f *Field) partyDispatch(o *Object, bits int) {
	switch {
	case bits&1 != 0:
		f.partyStep(o, 3)
	case bits&2 != 0:
		f.partyStep(o, 2)
	case bits&4 != 0:
		f.partyStep(o, 1)
	case bits&8 != 0:
		f.partyStep(o, 0)
	}
}

// partyStep is C0:8090/8129/81CB/8252: the walk direction (hop, stairs
// from $D9D8, then the map slope) and the facing passed to 62C3.
func (f *Field) partyStep(o *Object, d int) {
	mdir := d
	face := d
	stairBit := [4]int{0x40, 0x20, 0x10, 0x08}[d]
	slopeBit := 0
	if d < 2 {
		slopeBit = 0x40
	} else {
		slopeBit = 0x20
	}
	if f.hop != 0 {
		mdir = f.hop*4 + [4]int{0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x0F}[d]
	} else if o.D8&stairBit != 0 {
		hi := o.D8&0x80 != 0
		mdir = o.D8&4 + partyDiag(d, hi)
		face = partyDiagFace(d, hi)
	} else if f.Slope[0] != 0 && f.Slope[1]&slopeBit != 0 {
		hi := f.Slope[1]&0x80 != 0
		mdir = (f.Slope[1]&1)<<2 + partyDiag(d, hi)
		face = partyDiagFace(d, hi)
	}
	o.MDir = mdir
	f.face62c3(o, face)
	o.SetMotion(f.Tables)
	r := f.partyChecks(o)
	switch r {
	case partyGate:
		f.partySlide(o, d)
	case partyBlock:
		f.partyBump(o)
	default:
		f.partyGo(o)
	}
}

func partyDiag(d int, hi bool) int {
	table := [4][2]int{{4, 7}, {6, 5}, {4, 5}, {6, 7}}
	if hi {
		return table[d][1]
	}
	return table[d][0]
}

func partyDiagFace(d int, hi bool) int {
	table := [4][2]int{{2, 3}, {3, 2}, {2, 2}, {3, 3}}
	if hi {
		return table[d][1]
	}
	return table[d][0]
}

// face62c3 is C0:62C3's facing part: a tile class with $D9D7 bit 5 forces
// $D9D8 & 3; a changed facing on a diagonal or slope walk shows west or
// east.
func (f *Field) face62c3(o *Object, face int) {
	if o.D7&0x20 != 0 {
		face = o.D8 & 3
	}
	if face != o.Dir {
		o.Dir = face
		if o.MDir >= 4 && o.MDir < 0x10 {
			o.Dir = ((o.MDir & 2) >> 1) | 2
		}
	}
}

// partySlide is C0:80F8 (vertical) / 821F (horizontal): one retry toward
// the slide direction the gate left in $D8E7.
func (f *Field) partySlide(o *Object, d int) {
	if f.d8e8 != 0 {
		return
	}
	f.d8e8 = 1
	if d < 2 {
		f.d8e7 &= 3
		switch {
		case f.d8e7&1 != 0:
			f.partyStep(o, 3)
		case f.d8e7&2 != 0:
			f.partyStep(o, 2)
		}
	} else {
		f.d8e7 &= 0x0C
		switch {
		case f.d8e7&4 != 0:
			f.partyStep(o, 1)
		case f.d8e7&8 != 0:
			f.partyStep(o, 0)
		}
	}
}

// partyGo is C0:7F73: a passed step walks one tile (op 02), or hops (op 0F).
func (f *Field) partyGo(o *Object) {
	switch o.Op {
	case 0x0F, 0x11, 0x12, 0x1D, 0x1E:
		return
	}
	if f.hop != 0 { // C0:7F8A: hop 1 moves at row 2, hop 2 at row 1
		row := 2
		if f.hop == 2 {
			row = 1
		}
		o.VX, o.VY = f.Tables.Velocity(row, o.MDir&3)
		o.HasVel = true
		o.PXP = 0xFF
		o.PYP = 0xFF
		o.C4 = 0
		o.Op = 0x0F
	} else {
		o.C4 = o.C3
		o.Op = 0x02
	}
	o.T8 = 0
}

// partyBump is C0:7FFA: a step blocked by an object touches the objects
// whose $D9B2 low bits are 1 or 3 and whose shape meets the leader's
// target. The engine's loop walks the slots in ascending order (GDScript
// dicts iterate in insertion order; the spawn path inserts 0x40..), so
// the dispatch target of a multi-NPC bump is the LOWEST slot — sort
// before iterating, a Go map's order is random.
func (f *Field) partyBump(o *Object) {
	slots := make([]int, 0, len(f.Objects))
	for s := range f.Objects {
		slots = append(slots, s)
	}
	sort.Ints(slots)
	for _, s := range slots {
		if s == 0 {
			continue
		}
		n := f.Objects[s]
		if n.Scene || n.Stamp == nil {
			continue
		}
		g := n.GateFlags & 3
		if g == 1 || g == 3 {
			found := false
			for _, b := range f.partyBumped {
				if b == s {
					found = true
					break
				}
			}
			if !found {
				f.partyBumped = append(f.partyBumped, s)
			}
		}
	}
}

type partyResult int

const (
	partyPass partyResult = iota
	partyGate
	partyBlock
)

// partyChecks is C0:593E + 7731 for slot 0: gate (with the slide probes
// run), block (collision) or pass.
func (f *Field) partyChecks(o *Object) partyResult {
	offX, offY := f.Tables.WalkOffset(o.MDir)
	tx := o.X + offX
	ty := o.Y + offY
	if tx < 0 || ty < 0 {
		return partyGate
	}
	cx := tx >> 3
	cy := ty >> 3
	if !f.partyBounds(cx, cy, offX, offY) {
		return partyGate
	}
	cx = wrapPos(cx, f.WrapX>>3)
	cy = wrapPos(cy, f.WrapY>>3)
	cls := f.classAt(cx, cy)
	flags := o.GateFlags | o.Plane
	fc := cls[0]
	if flags&0x30 == 0x10 { // C0:5A60: bit-4 rule, no slide
		if fc&0x10 != 0 {
			return partyGate
		}
	} else if fc&0xC0 == 0xC0 || flags&0xF0&fc != 0 { // C0:5A8A
		if cls[2]&0x84 == 0x04 {
			f.d8e8 = 1
		}
		if f.d8e8 == 0 && o.MDir < 4 {
			f.partyProbe(o, cx, cy, o.MDir)
		}
		return partyGate
	}
	if fc&(8>>(o.MDir&3)) != 0 { // C0:5922, no slide
		return partyGate
	}
	// C0:7731 on slot 0
	keep := cls[1]&0x80 != 0
	var testPlane int
	if keep {
		testPlane = planeIndex(o.Plane)
	} else if cls[0]&0xC0 == 0x40 {
		testPlane = 1
	}
	f.apply(o.Stamp, planeIndex(o.Plane), false)
	st := f.shapeAt(o.hitbox(o.Dir&3), tx, ty)
	if f.hits(st, testPlane) {
		f.apply(o.Stamp, planeIndex(o.Plane), true)
		return partyBlock
	}
	f.stampObject(o, st, testPlane)
	if !keep {
		o.Plane = planeBits(cls[0])
	}
	f.footprint(o)
	o.D6, o.D7, o.D8 = cls[1], cls[2], cls[3]
	return partyPass
}

// partyBounds is C0:5976-5A39: bounds x0..x1, y0..y1 inclusive. Stepping
// onto x0/y0 queues that edge's word when the map has edge words
// (otherwise it is just open); stepping onto x1/y1 queues it or, without
// edge words, blocks. A queued word skips the remaining bound checks.
func (f *Field) partyBounds(cx, cy, offX, offY int) bool {
	x0, y0, x1, y1 := f.Bounds[0], f.Bounds[1], f.Bounds[2], f.Bounds[3]
	if cx < x0 {
		return false
	}
	if cx == x0 && offX < 0 && f.EdgesOn {
		f.partyEdges = append(f.partyEdges, f.EdgeWords[2])
		return true
	}
	if cx > x1 {
		return false
	}
	if cx == x1 && offX > 0 {
		if !f.EdgesOn {
			return false
		}
		f.partyEdges = append(f.partyEdges, f.EdgeWords[3])
		return true
	}
	if cy < y0 {
		return false
	}
	if cy == y0 && offY < 0 && f.EdgesOn {
		f.partyEdges = append(f.partyEdges, f.EdgeWords[0])
		return true
	}
	if cy > y1 {
		return false
	}
	if cy == y1 && offY > 0 {
		if !f.EdgesOn {
			return false
		}
		f.partyEdges = append(f.partyEdges, f.EdgeWords[1])
	}
	return true
}

// partyClassOK is C0:5AFA-5BC5: the slide probes' class rules (no $D8FE
// tests, no low buffer, no side bit).
func (f *Field) partyClassOK(o *Object, cls [4]int) bool {
	flags := o.GateFlags | o.Plane
	fc := cls[0]
	if flags&0x30 == 0x10 {
		return fc&0x10 == 0
	}
	return fc&0xC0 != 0xC0 && flags&0xF0&fc == 0
}

// partyProbe is C0:5AAE-5AF9: probe the two tiles diagonally ahead; the
// first open one sets the slide direction (2/1 west/east for north-south
// steps, 8/4 north/south for west-east steps).
func (f *Field) partyProbe(o *Object, cx, cy, d int) {
	w := f.WrapX >> 3
	h := f.WrapY >> 3
	tries := [2][3]int{}
	switch d {
	case 0, 1:
		tries = [2][3]int{{-1, 0, 2}, {1, 0, 1}}
	default:
		tries = [2][3]int{{0, -1, 8}, {0, 1, 4}}
	}
	for _, t := range tries {
		cls := f.classAt(wrapPos(cx+t[0], w), wrapPos(cy+t[1], h))
		if f.partyClassOK(o, cls) {
			f.d8e7 = t[2]
			return
		}
	}
}

```

`internal/game/field/roam.go`:

```go
package field

import "fmt"

// The field half of the action-script interpreter: what the per-pass
// continuations and the fetch do to POSITION, MOTION, the gate/collision
// checks and the field RNG. The op handlers' interpreter-side state
// (targets, poses, event words, enqueues, the camera) lives in
// internal/game/actions; a replay of exports/tests/trails drives those
// fields from the engine samples and asserts the outputs this package
// computes (trails_test.go). Ops and roll grammar per docs/action-scripts.md.
//
// Walk continuations (C0:6B2B for 02/13, C0:6975 for 01, C0:6DB3 for
// 06/07): rotate the move pattern, move on a 1 bit (C0:7132), count
// steps; a finished tile decrements $D9B7 (0 ends the walk), re-rolls
// the wander/chase direction, then runs the checks.

// isWalkOp: ops whose continuation is the walk (action_runner WALKS).
func isWalkOp(op byte) bool {
	switch op {
	case 0x01, 0x02, 0x13, 0x31, 0x06, 0x07, 0x2C, 0x3F, 0x3D, 0x14,
		0x10, 0x1A, 0x30, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x3C, 0x17, 0x18, 0x37, 0x38, 0x39:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// fetchChains: handlers that end JMP $536D and fetch again in the same
// pass (C0:70AA).
var fetchChains = map[byte]bool{
	0x04: true, 0x05: true, 0x08: true, 0x09: true, 0x0A: true, 0x16: true,
	0x19: true, 0x20: true, 0x21: true, 0x32: true, 0x33: true, 0x34: true,
	0x41: true,
}

var spin31 = [4]int{2, 1, 3, 0} // FF:6802: op 31's turn every 4th frame
var turn24 = [4]int{3, 2, 0, 1} // C0:6504
var turn25 = [4]int{2, 3, 1, 0} // C0:6500

// step runs one object's logic pass (C0:53CE's continuation side).
func (f *Field) step(slot int, o *Object) {
	if o.T8 != 0 {
		f.fetch(slot, o)
		return
	}
	switch o.Op {
	case 0x00, 0x0B, 0x03, 0x3E: // C0:68AF, 68C4, 6D34
		o.T7--
		if o.T7 == 0 {
			if slot == 0 {
				f.leader5585(o)
			}
			o.T8 = 1
		}
		// C0:68A6 (00) checks the proximity range every pass, C0:68BB
		// (0B, 3E) when the count's low nibble is 0; 03 never (0103: a
		// monster jumped out of its 00 wait).
		if o.Op == 0x00 || (o.Op != 0x03 && o.T7&0x0F == 0) {
			if f.inProximity(o) {
				f.proximityJump(o)
			}
		}
	case 0x35: // C0:6A8C
		f.walk35(slot, o)
	case 0x0F: // C0:6C6D: move every frame along the arc; a hop is 16 frames
		f.hopPass(slot, o)
	case 0x27: // C0:6F5D: every 8th pass the next pose frame; done after frame 4
		o.T7--
		if o.T7 == 0 {
			o.T7 = 8
			o.Frame++
			if o.Frame >= 5 {
				o.T8 = 1
			}
		}
	case 0x2B: // C0:7001: 02's walk, then each new tile at speed row + 2
		f.walk(slot, o)
		if o.C3 == o.C4 && o.T8 == 0 {
			f.setRow(o, o.Spd+2)
		}
	case 0x1C: // C0:6FB5: count down; at the end of a pose cycle re-roll
		if o.T7 >= 0x0E {
			o.T7--
			return
		}
		if 6-(o.T7>>1) == 6 {
			o.Dir = f.Rng.Roll(0, 4)
			o.T7 = f.Rng.Roll(0, 0x32) // C0:6FD9 loads 0x14 but stores $0C = 0
		}
		o.T7--
	case 0x2D: // C0:691A: done when that object runs op 06, or op 07 on this object's frame
		target := (o.T7 + 1) << 6
		if t, ok := f.slot(target); ok {
			if t.Op == 0x06 || (t.Op == 0x07 && f.NmiFrame&0x1F == slot>>6) {
				o.T8 = 1
			}
		}
	case 0x1B:
		// C0:5E1F: camera steps. The pan itself is the shell's camera
		// (map_view's _tick_pan); the pass counter here only drives when
		// the op ends.
		o.SC--
		if o.SC == 0 {
			o.T7--
			if o.T7 == 0 {
				o.T8 = 1
				return
			}
			o.SC = o.C3
		}
	default:
		if isWalkOp(o.Op) {
			if o.Op == 0x31 && f.NmiFrame&3 == 0 { // C0:6B03
				o.Dir = spin31[o.Dir&3]
			}
			f.walk(slot, o)
		} else {
			f.Error = fmt.Sprintf("slot %X: continuation of op %02X not modeled", slot, o.Op)
		}
	}
}

// setRow is C0:6876: a speed row sets the move pattern (FF:65C3), the
// steps per tile $D9C3 (FF:65CC) and $D9BC; 0A/32/33 copy it into $D9BB,
// 2B does not.
func (f *Field) setRow(o *Object, r int) {
	r &= 0x0F
	o.Row = r
	o.C6 = f.Tables.MovePattern(r)
	o.C3 = int(f.Tables.StepsPerTile(r))
}

// hopPass is op 0F's continuation (C0:6C6D).
func (f *Field) hopPass(slot int, o *Object) {
	o.X = wrapPos(o.X+o.VX, f.WrapX)
	o.Y = wrapPos(o.Y+o.VY, f.WrapY)
	arc := f.Tables.HopArc(o.C4)
	if arc >= 0x8000 {
		arc -= 0x10000
	}
	o.Y = wrapPos(o.Y-arc, f.WrapY)
	o.C4++
	if o.C4 != 16 {
		return
	}
	o.C4 = 0
	if slot == 0 {
		f.leader5585(o) // C0:6C9E
	}
	o.T7--
	if o.T7 == 0 {
		o.T8 = 1
		return
	}
	switch f.checks(slot, o) {
	case checkProx:
		f.proximityJump(o)
	case checkBlock:
		o.T8 = 1
	}
}

// walk35 is op 35's continuation (C0:6A8C): walk on; a blocked tile end
// leaves $D9C4 = 0 and the object retries the checks every frame.
func (f *Field) walk35(slot int, o *Object) {
	if o.C4 == 0 {
		o.T7--
	} else {
		done, _ := o.advance(f.Tables, f.WrapX, f.WrapY)
		if !done {
			return
		}
		if slot == 0 {
			f.leader5585(o) // C0:6AA8
		}
		o.T7--
		if o.T7 == 0 {
			o.T8 = 1
			return
		}
	}
	switch f.checks(slot, o) {
	case checkProx:
		f.proximityJump(o)
	case checkBlock:
		o.T7++
	default:
		o.C4 = o.C3
	}
}

// walk is the walk continuation (C0:6975/6A02/6BBE/6D6D/6DB3).
func (f *Field) walk(slot int, o *Object) {
	// 3C (C0:6A02) waiting at a blocked tile ($D9C4 = 0) re-runs the
	// tile-end logic each frame without moving or counting the tile.
	// 01/2C/3C store $0D (4 / 0x10 / 4) every frame before the pattern
	// test (C0:6975, 696F, 6A07); a later 3C wait roll reads what the
	// last object left there, rolled or not.
	switch o.Op {
	case 0x01:
		f.Rng.D = 4
	case 0x2C:
		f.Rng.D = 0x10
	case 0x3C:
		if o.C4 != 0 {
			f.Rng.D = 4
		}
	}
	waiting := o.Op == 0x3C && o.C4 == 0
	if !waiting {
		done, _ := o.advance(f.Tables, f.WrapX, f.WrapY)
		if !done {
			return
		}
		if slot == 0 {
			f.leader5585(o) // the tile end: C0:6B42, 6990, 6DCA, 6A22
		}
		o.T7--
		if o.T7 == 0 {
			o.T8 = 1
			return
		}
	}
	retry := false
	switch o.Op {
	case 0x01, 0x3C: // C0:69A3 / 6A35; 3C's wait path rolls 0..$0D as left
		d := byte(4)
		if waiting {
			d = f.Rng.D
		}
		if f.Rng.Roll(0, d) == 1 {
			o.Dir = f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
			o.MDir = o.Dir
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables) // C0:62C3
		}
	case 0x2C:
		if f.Rng.Roll(0, 16) == 1 { // C0:696F: $0D = 0x10, then 6975's roll
			o.Dir = f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
			o.MDir = o.Dir
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables) // C0:62C3
		}
	case 0x17, 0x18: // C0:6BBE: roll 0..3, a 1 re-aims along the axis
		if f.Rng.Roll(0, 3) == 1 {
			o.Dir = f.axisToward(o, o.Op == 0x18)
			o.MDir = o.Dir
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables) // C0:62C3
		}
	case 0x1A, 0x30: // C0:6D6D: re-aim at the target every tile
		td := f.towardPoint(o)
		if td < 0 {
			o.T8 = 1
			if o.Op == 0x30 { // C0:6D99: the object leaves (its slot is free)
				o.Running = false
				o.Halted = true
				o.Removed = true
			}
			return
		}
		o.Dir = td
		o.MDir = td
		o.SetMotion(f.Tables) // C0:62C3
		retry = true
	case 0x06, 0x07:
		if f.Rng.Roll(0, 3) == 1 { // C0:6DE5
			d := f.toward(o)
			if o.Op == 0x07 {
				d ^= 1
			}
			o.Dir = d
			o.MDir = o.Dir
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables) // C0:62C3
			retry = true
		}
	}
	if o.Scene {
		o.C4 = o.C3
		return
	}
	r := f.checks(slot, o)
	if r == checkBlock && retry { // C0:6E30: one random retry after a re-aim
		o.Dir = f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
		o.MDir = o.Dir
		o.SetMotion(f.Tables) // C0:62C3
		r = f.checks(slot, o)
	}
	switch r {
	case checkProx:
		f.proximityJump(o)
	case checkBlock:
		if o.Op == 0x3C {
			o.C4 = 0 // C0:6A86: wait at the tile, retry next frame
		} else {
			o.T8 = 1
		}
	default:
		// C0:6B2B -> C0:5585 at the tile end: a non-leader object's row
		// returns to its base row (C0:6876) before the step count
		// reloads, so op 2B's raise holds one tile at a time.
		if slot != 0 && o.Spd&0x0F != o.Row {
			f.setRow(o, o.Spd&0x0F)
		}
		o.C4 = o.C3
	}
}

// proximityJump is C0:5D1F's jump: the script cursor moves to $D9C8.
func (f *Field) proximityJump(o *Object) {
	o.Pos = o.C8
	o.C7 = 0
	o.T8 = 1
}

// toward is C0:5D1F: direction toward the leader.
func (f *Field) toward(o *Object) int {
	lx, ly := f.leaderPos()
	if o.X == lx && o.Y == ly {
		return f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
	}
	r := f.Rng.Roll(0, 16)
	if r == 8 {
		return f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
	}
	if r < 8 {
		if o.Y == ly {
			return f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
		}
		if o.Y > ly {
			return 0
		}
		return 1
	}
	if o.X == lx {
		return f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
	}
	if o.X > lx {
		return 2
	}
	return 3
}

// axisToward is C0:5ED0/5EA4: toward the leader along one axis.
func (f *Field) axisToward(o *Object, horizontal bool) int {
	lx, ly := f.leaderPos()
	if horizontal {
		if o.X == lx {
			return f.Rng.Roll(2, 3)
		}
		if o.X < lx {
			return 3
		}
		return 2
	}
	if o.Y == ly {
		return f.Rng.Roll(0, 1)
	}
	if o.Y < ly {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// face is C0:6561: the facing toward p; the longer axis wins, y on a tie.
func (o *Object) face(p Tile) int {
	dx := o.X - p.X
	dy := o.Y - p.Y
	if absInt(dy) < absInt(dx) {
		if dx >= 0 {
			return 2
		}
		return 3
	}
	if dy >= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return 1
}

// towardPoint is C0:5DC8: direction toward o's target, x axis first; -1
// once there. (Target lives with the interpreter; the walk ops 1A/30 use
// it on the pass the interpreter hands over.)
func (f *Field) towardPoint(o *Object) int {
	t, ok := f.Targets[o]
	if !ok {
		return -1
	}
	if o.X == t.X {
		if o.Y == t.Y {
			return -1
		}
		if o.Y > t.Y {
			return 0
		}
		return 1
	}
	if o.X > t.X {
		return 2
	}
	return 3
}

// startWalk is C0:60E8: start a walk; non-scene objects check the first
// tile (C0:614A-6157) and a blocked start ends the walk at once.
func (f *Field) startWalk(slot int, o *Object) {
	if o.Op != 0x14 && o.Op != 0x10 {
		o.MDir = o.Dir // C0:60E8 stores the walk direction in $D9BA
	}
	o.MDir = o.StairDir(o.MDir)
	if o.MDir >= 4 { // C0:60EE: diagonal and slope walks face west or east
		if o.MDir&3 < 2 {
			o.Dir = 2
		} else {
			o.Dir = 3
		}
	}
	o.SetMotion(f.Tables)
	f.walkFromHere(slot, o)
}

// walkFromHere is C0:6101-6157: the first tile's checks of a walk set up
// by the caller.
func (f *Field) walkFromHere(slot int, o *Object) {
	o.T8 = 0
	o.C4 = o.C3 // C0:6135: only the step count reloads; the pattern keeps its phase
	if o.Scene {
		return
	}
	switch f.checks(slot, o) {
	case checkProx:
		f.proximityJump(o)
	case checkBlock:
		o.T8 = 1
	}
}

// restampHere is C0:66F2: $D9BA = 0x18 (no offset), then the gate and
// C0:7731 on the object's own tile, results unused: the stamp moves to
// the plane the tile's class picks unless that spot is taken.
func (f *Field) restampHere(o *Object) {
	o.MDir = 0x18
	if o.Stamp == nil {
		return
	}
	cls := f.classAt(wrapPos(o.X, f.WrapX)>>3, wrapPos(o.Y, f.WrapY)>>3)
	var testPlane int
	if cls[1]&0x80 != 0 {
		testPlane = planeIndex(o.Plane)
	} else if cls[0]&0xC0 == 0x40 {
		testPlane = 1
	}
	f.apply(o.Stamp, planeIndex(o.Plane), false)
	st := f.shapeAt(o.hitbox(o.Dir&3), o.X, o.Y)
	if f.hits(st, testPlane) {
		f.apply(o.Stamp, planeIndex(o.Plane), true)
	} else {
		f.stampObject(o, st, testPlane)
	}
}

// eraseStamp is C0:6703: erase the object's stamp (C0:7956). The saved
// shape stays, so a later erase clears those bits again, as the engine's
// does.
func (f *Field) eraseStamp(o *Object) {
	if o.Stamp != nil {
		f.apply(o.Stamp, planeIndex(o.Plane), false)
	}
}

// bankByte reads one script byte ($D9B3 + $D9B5 + k, bank F8); a planted
// leader instruction reads its inline list instead (C0:53CE).
func (f *Field) bankByte(o *Object, k int) byte {
	if o.Inline != nil {
		i := o.Pos + k
		if i >= len(o.Inline) {
			i = len(o.Inline) - 1
		}
		return o.Inline[i]
	}
	if f.Bank == nil {
		panic("field: script fetch needs exports/data/bank_f8.bin in Field.Bank")
	}
	return f.Bank[(o.Scr+o.Pos+k)&0xFFFF]
}

// scriptBase is the F8 script-pointer table: (id & 0x0FFF) * 2.
func (f *Field) scriptBase(id int) int {
	if f.Bank == nil {
		panic("field: script fetch needs exports/data/bank_f8.bin in Field.Bank")
	}
	i := (id & 0x0FFF) * 2
	return int(f.Bank[i]) | int(f.Bank[i+1])<<8
}

// fetch is the field half of the instruction fetch (C0:536D's dispatch):
// the cursor and interpreter-side state changes the trail resyncs anyway,
// but the ROLLS (the wander/chase grammar), the speed-row changes, and
// the walk starts' first-tile checks are this package's — a replay
// without them desyncs the RNG and the stamps.
func (f *Field) fetch(slot int, o *Object) {
	for guard := 0; guard < 64; guard++ {
		b := f.bankByte(o, 0)
		a1 := int(f.bankByte(o, 1))
		a2 := int(f.bankByte(o, 2))
		o.Op = b
		switch b {
		case 0xFF:
			if slot == 0 { // C0:5395: object 0 reloads script 0, leaves event mode
				o.Scr = f.scriptBase(0)
				o.Running = false
				o.EventDriven = false
			}
			o.Pos = 0
			continue
		case 0x16:
			o.Scr = f.scriptBase(a1 | a2<<8)
			o.Pos = 0
		case 0x08:
			o.Pos = a1 // absolute (C0:679E)
		case 0x00, 0x0B: // C0:5E36: wait a1 frames, restamped on the own tile
			o.T7 = a1
			o.T8 = 0
			o.Pos += 2
			f.restampHere(o)
		case 0x03: // C0:647F: hold, facing = nn>>6
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.Dir = a1 >> 6
			o.T8 = 0
			o.Pos += 2
		case 0x02:
			o.Dir = a1 >> 6
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x13, 0x31: // C0:6291 (31 also turns while it walks)
			o.T7 = a1
			o.Dir &= 3
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x01: // C0:5E6B: wander
			o.T7 = a1
			f.fetchWanderTurn(o, 4)
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x04: // C0:65B7: proximity range
			o.C7 = a1
			o.Pos += 2
		case 0x05: // C0:65C0: proximity jump target
			o.C8 = a1
			o.Pos += 2
		case 0x06, 0x07: // C0:6666/6672: walk toward (away from) the leader
			o.T7 = a1
			d := f.toward(o)
			if b == 0x07 {
				d ^= 1
			}
			o.Dir = d
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x32: // C0:67FD: speed row +1 below row 4
			if o.Spd+1 < 4 {
				o.Spd++
				f.setRow(o, o.Spd)
			}
			o.Pos++
		case 0x33: // C0:6821: speed row -1
			if o.Spd >= 1 {
				o.Spd--
				f.setRow(o, o.Spd)
			}
			o.Pos++
		case 0x1F: // C0:66D8: scene actor, stamp erased; ends the frame
			o.Scene = true
			o.D8 = 0
			f.eraseStamp(o)
			o.T8 = 1
			o.Pos++
		case 0x2C: // C0:5E65: wander with a 1-in-17 turn
			o.T7 = a1
			f.fetchWanderTurn(o, 16)
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x1A: // C0:662A: walk to tile (a1, a2)
			f.Targets[o] = Tile{X: a1 * 8, Y: a2 * 8}
			o.T7 = 0xFF
			o.Pos += 3
			td := f.towardPoint(o)
			if td < 0 {
				return // already there: $D9B8 stays set (C0:5DDA)
			}
			o.Dir = td
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x30: // C0:65C9: a scene actor walks to the leader's tile, then leaves
			o.Scene = true
			o.D7 &= 0xC0
			o.D8 = 0
			f.eraseStamp(o)
			lx, ly := f.leaderPos()
			f.Targets[o] = Tile{X: (lx >> 3) * 8, Y: (ly >> 3) * 8}
			o.T7 = 0xFF
			o.Pos++
			td := f.towardPoint(o)
			if td < 0 { // already there: C0:6619 frees the slot
				o.Running = false
				o.Halted = true
				o.Removed = true
				return
			}
			o.Dir = td
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x22: // C0:6534: face the leader, end the frame
			lx, ly := f.leaderPos()
			o.Dir = o.face(Tile{X: lx, Y: ly})
			o.Pos++
		case 0x23: // C0:6545: face tile (a1, a2), end the frame
			o.Dir = o.face(Tile{X: a1 * 8, Y: a2 * 8})
			o.Pos += 3
		case 0x17, 0x18: // C0:5ECA/5E9E: walk along y (17) or x (18) toward the leader
			o.T7 = a1
			o.Dir = f.axisToward(o, b == 0x18)
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0E: // C0:61F8/620D/6222: diagonal and slope walks
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			extra := map[byte]int{0x0C: 4, 0x0D: 8, 0x0E: 12}[b]
			o.Dir = (a1 >> 6) | extra
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x37, 0x38, 0x39: // C0:6237/6255/6273: diagonal/slope walks keeping the facing
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			extra := map[byte]int{0x37: 4, 0x38: 8, 0x39: 12}[b]
			o.MDir = (a1 >> 6) | extra
			o.Pos += 2
			keep := o.StairDir(o.Dir) // C0:624F: 577E on the facing
			if keep != o.Dir {        // C0:62D5
				o.Dir = keep
				if o.MDir >= 4 && o.MDir < 0x10 {
					o.Dir = ((o.MDir & 2) >> 1) | 2
				}
			}
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables)
			f.walkFromHere(slot, o)
		case 0x3C: // C0:5E6B start (as 01); a blocked start turns and retries (C0:616F)
			o.T7 = a1
			f.fetchWanderTurn(o, 4)
			o.Pos += 2
			for turns := 0; turns < 4; turns++ { // C0:6168: only a gate block turns and retries
				f.startWalk(slot, o)
				if o.T8 == 0 || !f.LastBlockGate {
					break
				}
				o.Dir = (o.Dir + 1) & 3
			}
		case 0x14, 0x10: // C0:62A2: walk nn&63 tiles toward nn>>6 keeping the facing
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.MDir = a1 >> 6
			o.Dir &= 3
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x3F, 0x3D: // C0:60D8, same as 02
			o.Dir = a1 >> 6
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.Pos += 2
			f.startWalk(slot, o)
		case 0x35: // C0:6186: walk a1&3F tiles toward a1>>6; a block retries the op
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.Pos += 2
			o.MDir = o.StairDir(a1 >> 6)
			if o.MDir >= 4 {
				if o.MDir&3 < 2 {
					o.Dir = 2
				} else {
					o.Dir = 3
				}
			} else {
				o.Dir = o.MDir
			}
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables)
			o.T8 = 0
			switch f.checks(slot, o) {
			case checkProx:
				f.proximityJump(o)
			case checkBlock:
				o.Pos -= 2
				o.T8 = 1
			default:
				o.C4 = o.C3
			}
		case 0x0F: // C0:5F04: hop a1&3F times 32 px toward a1>>6
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.Pos += 2
			o.Dir = a1 >> 6
			o.MDir = o.Dir + 0x10
			o.PXP = 0xFF
			o.PYP = 0xFF
			o.VX, o.VY = f.Tables.Velocity(2, o.Dir) // C0:5F3F: row 2 whatever the speed
			o.HasVel = true
			o.C4 = 0
			o.T8 = 0
			switch f.checks(slot, o) {
			case checkProx:
				f.proximityJump(o)
			case checkBlock:
				o.T8 = 1
			}
		case 0x24, 0x25: // C0:64A8/64D4: turn by C0:6504 / C0:6500; ends the frame
			d := o.Dir
			if d >= 5 {
				d -= 5
			}
			if b == 0x24 {
				o.Dir = turn24[d&3]
			} else {
				o.Dir = turn25[d&3]
			}
			o.Pos++
		case 0x2A, 0x29: // C0:66CB/670C: no longer a scene actor, restamped; ends the frame
			o.Scene = false
			o.Pos++
			f.restampHere(o)
			o.T8 = 1
		case 0x28: // C0:6728: scene actor (bits 3-5), stamp erased; ends the frame
			o.Scene = true
			o.D8 = 0
			f.eraseStamp(o)
			o.T8 = 1
			o.Pos++
		case 0x1C: // C0:6390: idle; pose 0, facing 0, t7 = roll(20..50)
			o.Dir = 0
			o.T7 = f.Rng.Roll(0x14, 0x32)
			o.T8 = 0
			o.Pos++
		case 0x2D: // C0:5E36: wait on object a1+1, restamped first
			o.T7 = a1
			o.Pos += 2
			f.restampHere(o)
			o.T8 = 0
		case 0x27: // C0:63E7: pose: frame 0 in facing group + 5, 8 passes a frame
			o.Pos++
			o.Frame = 0
			o.Dir = (o.Dir & 3) + 5
			o.T7 = 8
			o.T8 = 0
		case 0x2B: // C0:63B4: 7 tiles along the facing, pose facing+5 (C0:60FE)
			d := o.Dir
			if d >= 5 {
				d -= 5
			}
			d &= 3
			o.Pos++
			o.MDir = d
			o.Dir = d + 5
			o.T7 = 7
			o.SetMotion(f.Tables)
			f.walkFromHere(slot, o)
		case 0x41: // C0:678F: the object's event word ($D9D2)
			o.EventID = a1 | a2<<8
			o.Pos += 3
		case 0x3B: // C0:6843: RTS without advancing: the object halts here
			return
		case 0x20: // C0:6742: toggle $D8D8 (the leader's check switch)
			o.Pos++
		case 0x3E: // C0:5E48: wait 5..60 frames, rolled, restamped on the own tile
			o.T7 = f.Rng.Roll(5, 0x3C)
			o.T8 = 0
			o.Pos++
			f.restampHere(o)
		case 0x0A: // C0:685C: speed row; C0:6876 reloads the move pattern
			o.Spd = a1 & 0x0F
			f.setRow(o, o.Spd)
			o.Pos += 2
		case 0x1B: // C0:5E1F: camera steps
			o.T7 = a1 & 0x3F
			o.T8 = 0
			o.SC = o.C3
			o.Pos += 2
		case 0x15: // C0:6377: pose frame a1, facing 4
			o.Dir = 4
			o.Pos += 2
		case 0x21:
			o.X = a1 * 8
			o.Y = a2 * 8
			o.Pos += 3
		case 0x09: // C0:67AE: a call word waits for an empty queue
			// Battle words 18/19 also wait on the leader: not modeled.
			if a1 < 0x0C && f.QueueLen > 0 {
				o.T8 = 1
				return
			}
			f.Enqueued = append(f.Enqueued, a1<<8|a2)
			f.QueueLen++
			o.Pos += 3
		default:
			f.Error = fmt.Sprintf("slot %X: op %02X not modeled", slot, b)
			return
		}
		if !fetchChains[b] {
			return
		}
	}
	f.Error = fmt.Sprintf("slot %X: fetch did not settle", slot)
}

// fetchWanderTurn is the 01/3C (1-in-5) and 2C (1-in-17) turn roll at
// fetch (C0:5E6B/5E65).
func (f *Field) fetchWanderTurn(o *Object, hi byte) {
	if o.Dir < 4 {
		if f.Rng.Roll(0, hi) == 1 {
			o.Dir = f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
		} else if o.Dir >= 5 {
			o.Dir -= 5
		}
	} else {
		o.Dir = f.Rng.Roll(0, 3)
	}
}

```

`internal/game/field/spawn.go`:

```go
package field

// Placed-NPC spawning (C0:3E07 block-2 walker -> C0:4A79 spawn ->
// C0:4AD3-4B0C pattern) and the defeat/inert marking. Docs:
// docs/parity.md "On 0250 the monsters spawn at speed row 0 with move
// pattern AA on slot 1 and 55 on slot 2 (dumped)" and docs/field-monsters.md.

// NpcRecord is one map.json NPC entry (exportmap's decode of the block-2
// placed character; internal/triggers.NPC is the ROM-level view).
type NpcRecord struct {
	Index     int // the record index ($D9): stagger and slot tag
	X, Y      int // tiles
	Facing    int
	Event     string // the big-endian event id as text, e.g. "1862"
	Graphic   int
	Speed     int // the speed row the record selects
	Script    int // the F8 script-pointer id
	Judged    bool
	PlaceID   int
	PlaceLo   int
	GateFlags int
	Hitboxes  [4]Hitbox
}

// SpawnPattern is C0:4AD3-4B0C: the move pattern $D9C6 is the speed
// row's FF:65C3 entry (C0:6876) rotated right once per object spawned
// before this one ($D8 & 7; the block-2 walker zeroes $D8 at C0:3E0A and
// increments it at C0:4BF4, so the count is the NPC record index — the
// leader spawns on a different path). With t7 = record index + 1 every
// slot lands on the same step passes. Map 0x250 dumps AA on slot 1 and
// 55 on slot 2 (docs/parity.md).
func SpawnPattern(t *Tables, row, spawnedBefore int) byte {
	p := t.MovePattern(row)
	for i := 0; i < spawnedBefore&7; i++ {
		p = p>>1 | (p&1)<<7
	}
	return p
}

// SpawnStagger is $D9B7 = ($D9 & 1F) + 1: the start wait that staggers
// the records onto the step passes ($D9 = the record index, skipped
// records included, C0:3E80).
func SpawnStagger(index int) int {
	return (index & 0x1F) + 1
}

// EncounterID parses the record's event text ("1862") to its integer.
func EncounterID(ev string) (int, error) {
	if len(ev) != 4 {
		return 0, nil
	}
	v := 0
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c := ev[i]
		var d int
		switch {
		case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
			d = int(c - '0')
		case c >= 'A' && c <= 'F':
			d = int(c-'A') + 10
		case c >= 'a' && c <= 'f':
			d = int(c-'a') + 10
		default:
			return 0, nil
		}
		v = v<<4 | d
	}
	return v, nil
}

// SpawnNPC plants one placed character on its slot ((index+1)*0x40,
// C0:4BEC's X += $0040) with the record's script, stagger, speed-row
// pattern and collision shape. The battle-encounter class is the
// 0x18xx/0x19xx event ids (docs/triggers.md).
func (f *Field) SpawnNPC(slot int, n NpcRecord) *Object {
	id, err := EncounterID(n.Event)
	if err != nil {
		panic("SpawnNPC: " + err.Error())
	}
	o := f.Spawn(slot, [8]int{f.scriptBase(n.Script), 0, SpawnStagger(n.Index), 0, 0, n.X * 8, n.Y * 8, n.Facing})
	pattern := SpawnPattern(f.Tables, n.Speed, n.Index)
	f.SetExtras(slot, n.Speed, 0, pattern, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(slot, n.Hitboxes, n.GateFlags, -1, 0, nil)
	o.EventID = id
	o.Graphic = n.Graphic
	o.Tag = n.Index
	return o
}

// PlacementPasses is C0:4A7D-4A9A: a judged entry spawns while the 4-bit
// flag place_id lies in [place_lo >> 4, (place_lo & 0x0F) + 1). The
// 0Cxx/4Cxx flag variants behind the hack hook 5A:AD50 are not modeled.
// flagValue reads the runtime flag state (0 without game state).
func PlacementPasses(n NpcRecord, flagValue func(idx int) int) bool {
	v := 0
	if flagValue != nil {
		v = flagValue(n.PlaceID)
	}
	return v >= n.PlaceLo>>4 && v < (n.PlaceLo&0x0F)+1
}

// InertEventID is the class the touched monster's slot is rewritten to at
// battle dispatch (C0:D74A/D993 store the id word big-endian 0x2000).
const InertEventID = 0x2000

// IsInert reports the inert battle-placed class (docs/triggers.md: the
// 0x2xxx ids dispatch nothing — their byteswapped queue words carry a low
// byte >= $20 and the queue processor 5A:E654 skips them).
func IsInert(eventID int) bool {
	return eventID&0xF000 == 0x2000
}

```

`internal/game/field/spawn_rotation_test.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// The spawn rotation pins: docs/parity.md "On 0250 the monsters spawn at
// speed row 0 with move pattern $D9C5/$D9C6 = AA on slot 1 and 55 on
// slot 2 (dumped)", set at C0:4AD3-4B0C = FF:65C3[speed row] rotated
// right $D8 & 7 times ($D8 = the NPC record index: STZ at C0:3E0A, INC
// at C0:4BF4), and $D9B7 = ($D9 & 1F) + 1. The dump is the live engine's.

func TestSpawnPattern0x250Dump(t *testing.T) {
	tables := loadTables(t)
	if got := tables.MovePattern(0); got != 0xAA {
		t.Fatalf("FF:65C3[0] = %02X, want AA (the dump's speed-row-0 base)", got)
	}
	cases := []struct {
		index int
		want  byte
	}{
		{0, 0xAA}, // slot 1 (record 0): dumped AA
		{1, 0x55}, // slot 2 (record 1): dumped 55
		{2, 0xAA}, // the rotation alternates; the 0250 trail's first
		{3, 0x55}, // samples (AA AA 55 AA 55 55 55 55 55 55) show the same
		{4, 0xAA}, // parity after each record's walk rotations
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := SpawnPattern(tables, 0, c.index); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("SpawnPattern(row 0, before %d) = %02X, want %02X", c.index, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	// A speed-row-1 record (the 0250 trail's slot 0x40 record carries row
	// 1 after its script's op 32): FF:65C3[1] = FF, rotation-invariant.
	if got := tables.MovePattern(1); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("FF:65C3[1] = %02X, want FF", got)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if got := SpawnPattern(tables, 1, i); got != 0xFF {
			t.Fatalf("SpawnPattern(row 1, before %d) = %02X, want FF", i, got)
		}
	}
	// The rotation itself runs RIGHT (C0:4AD3-4B0C's ROR): row 9's pattern
	// 08 steps 04 02 01 80 — a left rotation would read 10 after one turn.
	rights := []byte{0x08, 0x04, 0x02, 0x01, 0x80}
	for i, want := range rights {
		if got := SpawnPattern(tables, 9, i); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("SpawnPattern(row 9, before %d) = %02X, want %02X (the rotation is ROR)", i, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestSpawnStagger(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct{ index, want int }{
		{0, 1}, {1, 2}, {9, 10}, {31, 32}, {32, 1}, {33, 2},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := SpawnStagger(c.index); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("SpawnStagger(%d) = %d, want %d ($D9B7 = ($D9&1F)+1)", c.index, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestEncounterClass(t *testing.T) {
	// docs/triggers.md + main.gd selftest pin: 1862 -> byte 62, 1939 ->
	// 39; the 0x2xxx inert class, 221A and the 17C0 objOp id dispatch
	// nothing. Live: the 0x1862 bump enqueued a=6218; the 0x2000 bump
	// enqueued a=0020 and no WD51B followed.
	if b, ok := EncounterClass(0x1862); !ok || b != 0x62 {
		t.Fatalf("EncounterClass(1862) = %X %v, want 62 true", b, ok)
	}
	if b, ok := EncounterClass(0x1939); !ok || b != 0x39 {
		t.Fatalf("EncounterClass(1939) = %X %v, want 39 true", b, ok)
	}
	for _, id := range []int{0x2000, 0x221A, 0x17C0, 0x0574} {
		if _, ok := EncounterClass(id); ok {
			t.Fatalf("EncounterClass(%04X) dispatched, want nothing", id)
		}
	}
	// The inert class is the whole 0x2xxx top byte (C0:D74A stores the
	// byteswapped 2000 word; the 5A:E654 queue processor skips low bytes
	// >= $20), not the single id 2000.
	if !IsInert(0x2000) || !IsInert(0x21FF) {
		t.Fatal("0x2xxx ids are the inert battle-placed class")
	}
	if IsInert(0x1862) || IsInert(0x1002) {
		t.Fatal("a live event id reads inert")
	}
}

func TestDispatchWordByteswap(t *testing.T) {
	// The live trace (tools/emulator/enc_dispatch.lua run1): NPC 0x1862's
	// touch enqueued `a=6218` at C0:AF98; the 0x2000 slot enqueued `a=0020`.
	if got := DispatchWord(0x1862); got != 0x6218 {
		t.Fatalf("DispatchWord(1862) = %04X, want 6218", got)
	}
	if got := DispatchWord(0x2000); got != 0x0020 {
		t.Fatalf("DispatchWord(2000) = %04X, want 0020", got)
	}
	if got := DispatchWord(0x1002); got != 0x0210 {
		t.Fatalf("DispatchWord(1002) = %04X, want 0210 (op 10 = map move)", got)
	}
}

// Spawning map 0x250's records gives slots 0x40.. with the dumped
// pattern/stagger and the encounter-capable events; the judged gate and
// the inert class follow the decode.
func TestSpawnNPC0x250(t *testing.T) {
	tables := loadTables(t)
	classes := loadClasses(t)
	bank := loadBank(t)
	spec, ex := loadMap250(t)
	f := New(spec, tables, classes, bank, rng.NewField())
	for i, rec := range ex.NPCs {
		slot := SlotNumber(i)
		o := f.SpawnNPC(slot, rec)
		if o.T7 != SpawnStagger(rec.Index) {
			t.Fatalf("slot %X stagger %d, want %d", slot, o.T7, SpawnStagger(rec.Index))
		}
		if i < 2 && o.C6 != SpawnPattern(tables, rec.Speed, rec.Index) {
			t.Fatalf("slot %X pattern %02X, want the C0:4AD3 rotation %02X", slot, o.C6, SpawnPattern(tables, rec.Speed, rec.Index))
		}
		if o.EventID == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("slot %X: event %q parsed to 0", slot, rec.Event)
		}
		if _, battle := EncounterClass(o.EventID); !battle {
			t.Fatalf("slot %X: event %04X is not the 0x18xx/0x19xx class", slot, o.EventID)
		}
		if IsInert(o.EventID) {
			t.Fatalf("slot %X: a fresh monster reads inert", slot)
		}
	}
}

// The touched monster's slot rewrites to the inert 0x2000 at battle
// dispatch and stops moving for the rest of the load (montage trace:
// slots 1884 -> 2000 at the transition, 0 px movement after); re-entering
// the map respawns it (fresh Field).
func TestDefeatMonsterMarksInert(t *testing.T) {
	spec, ex := loadMap250(t)
	f := New(spec, loadTables(t), loadClasses(t), loadBank(t), rng.NewField())
	for i, rec := range ex.NPCs {
		f.SpawnNPC(SlotNumber(i), rec)
	}
	slot := SlotNumber(0)
	f.DefeatMonster(slot)
	o := f.Objects[slot]
	if o.EventID != InertEventID || !IsInert(o.EventID) {
		t.Fatalf("defeated slot carries %04X, want 2000", o.EventID)
	}
	if _, battle := EncounterClass(o.EventID); battle {
		t.Fatal("the inert slot still classifies as an encounter")
	}
	x, y := o.X, o.Y
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		f.StepPass(false)
		if o.X != x || o.Y != y {
			t.Fatalf("the inert slot moved on pass %d: %d,%d -> %d,%d", i, x, y, o.X, o.Y)
		}
	}
}

func TestPlacementGate(t *testing.T) {
	rec := NpcRecord{Judged: true, PlaceID: 5, PlaceLo: 0x24}
	// C0:4A7D-4A9A: the 4-bit flag lies in [lo>>4, (lo&0x0F)+1) = [2, 5).
	if !PlacementPasses(rec, func(int) int { return 2 }) {
		t.Fatal("flag 2 in [2, 5) should pass")
	}
	if !PlacementPasses(rec, func(int) int { return 4 }) {
		t.Fatal("flag 4 in [2, 5) should pass")
	}
	if PlacementPasses(rec, func(int) int { return 5 }) {
		t.Fatal("flag 5 is outside [2, 5)")
	}
	if PlacementPasses(rec, nil) {
		t.Fatal("without game state the flag reads 0, outside [2, 5)")
	}
}
```

`internal/game/field/tables.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

// Tables is the bank-FF field data at $FF:6500 (exports/data/field_tables.bin,
// 1280 bytes): speed rows, walk offsets and per-axis move patterns. The
// engine reads it with the FF data bank mapped; the export keeps the region
// from $6500.
type Tables struct {
	raw []byte
}

// tablesBase is the first byte's engine address ($FF:6500).
const tablesBase = 0x6500

// tablesSize is the exported region: $6500-$69FF.
const tablesSize = 0x500

// LoadTables reads exports/data/field_tables.bin in place.
func LoadTables(path string) (*Tables, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load field tables: %w", err)
	}
	return LoadTablesFromBytes(b)
}

// LoadTablesFromBytes parses the exported $FF:6500 region.
func LoadTablesFromBytes(b []byte) (*Tables, error) {
	if len(b) != tablesSize {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("field tables: got %d bytes, want %d ($FF:6500 region)", len(b), tablesSize)
	}
	return &Tables{raw: append([]byte(nil), b...)}, nil
}

func (t *Tables) byteAt(engineAddr int) byte {
	return t.raw[engineAddr-tablesBase]
}

func (t *Tables) wordAt(engineAddr int) int {
	i := engineAddr - tablesBase
	return int(t.raw[i]) | int(t.raw[i+1])<<8
}

// signedPair reads two little-endian words as one signed (x, y) pair.
func (t *Tables) signedPair(engineAddr int) (int, int) {
	i := engineAddr - tablesBase
	x := int(t.raw[i]) | int(t.raw[i+1])<<8
	y := int(t.raw[i+2]) | int(t.raw[i+3])<<8
	if x >= 0x8000 {
		x -= 0x10000
	}
	if y >= 0x8000 {
		y -= 0x10000
	}
	return x, y
}

// MovePattern is FF:65C3[row]: the per-pass walk pattern a speed row
// starts from (C0:6876). Row 0 = AA (one step every other pass).
func (t *Tables) MovePattern(row int) byte {
	return t.byteAt(0x65C3 + row&0x0F)
}

// StepsPerTile is FF:65CC[row]: passes one tile takes at that row
// (08 08 04 02 01 01 01 01 10; rows past 8 read what follows, as the
// engine does).
func (t *Tables) StepsPerTile(row int) byte {
	return t.byteAt(0x65CC + row&0xFF)
}

// WalkOffset is FF:6700 + dir*4: the check offset of walk direction dir
// (0-7 full-tile and diagonal, 8-15 half steps, 0x10-0x13 op 0F's 32 px
// hops, 0x18 none).
func (t *Tables) WalkOffset(mdir int) (int, int) {
	return t.signedPair(0x6700 + mdir*4)
}

// AxisPattern is FF:65E8[mdir>>2]: the per-axis move patterns by walk
// axis (FFFF, FFFF, AAFF, 88FF).
func (t *Tables) AxisPattern(mdir int) int {
	return t.wordAt(0x65E8 + (mdir>>2&3)*2)
}

// Velocity is FF:65F0 + row*64 + dir*4 (C0:6323): the per-frame pixel
// delta of a walk, signed. Rows past 3 read the data after the table, as
// the engine does.
func (t *Tables) Velocity(row, mdir int) (int, int) {
	return t.signedPair(0x65F0 + row*64 + mdir*4)
}

// HopArc is FF:6780 + step*2: op 0F's hop height per frame.
func (t *Tables) HopArc(step int) int {
	return t.wordAt(0x6780 + step*2)
}

// Hitbox is one facing's collision shape: the shape's top-left offset
// from the object position and one mask byte per 4 px row.
type Hitbox struct {
	XOff int
	YOff int
	Rows []byte
}

// LeaderHitbox is the party shape 0F82 (C0:7B34): mask 0F at x-4.
func LeaderHitbox() Hitbox {
	return Hitbox{XOff: -4, YOff: 0, Rows: []byte{0x0F}}
}

```

`internal/game/field/trails_test.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"compress/gzip"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// The movement-trail goldens: exports/tests/trails/*.trail.gz are engine
// recordings (tools/emulator/acttrail.lua sampled at the object-loop
// start C0:51F7; PASS/TR lines with the counters). This replay drives the
// FIELD half of the model — positions, the walk gate, collision, the bump
// latch and the field RNG — while the interpreter half of each object
// (script cursor, op transitions, targets) re-syncs from the engine's own
// samples every pass, the same division --actreplay uses: this replay
// asserts slot POSITIONS/gates; internal/game/actions (the sibling port)
// asserts script ops.
//
// Per-slot first-sample spawn; per-pass resync; the pass's roll grammar
// and checks run here. Any x/y mismatch or RNG divergence fails.

type trailLine struct {
	pass                 int
	slot                 int
	scr, pos, t7, t8, op int
	x, y, dir, spd       int
	c4                   int
	c6                   byte
	c7, c8, mdir         int
	tag                  int
	hasTag, b2           bool
	plane                int
}

type trailPass struct {
	num    int
	window bool
	rngA   int
	rngB   int
}

type trailPTY struct {
	pad                 int
	edgesOK, latch, veh bool // ed / b6 / eb
}

type trailInstall struct {
	pass int
	tag  int
	id   int
}

type trailActor struct {
	pass       int
	slot       int
	gfx        int
	x, y       int
	ef3        int
	off, shift int
}

type trailData struct {
	passes   map[int]trailPass
	lines    map[int]map[int]trailLine
	pty      map[int]trailPTY
	installs []trailInstall
	actors   []trailActor
}

var (
	rePASS = regexp.MustCompile(`^PASS (\d+) frame=\d+ w76=(\w+) rnga=(\w+) rngb=(\w+)$`)
	reTR   = regexp.MustCompile(`^TR f=(\d+) y=(\w+) scr=(\w+) pos=(\w+) t7=(\w+) t8=(\w+) op=(\w+) x=(\w+) yy=(\w+) dir=(\w+) bb=(\w+) c3=\w+ c4=(\w+) c6=(\w+) d99a=\w+ c7=(\w+) c8=(\w+) ba=(\w+)(?: tag=(\w+))?(?: b2=(\w+))?(?: \w+=\w+)*$`)
	rePTY  = regexp.MustCompile(`^PTY f=(\d+) j=(\w+).*? ed=(\w+) b6=(\w+) eb=(\w+)$`)
	reINS  = regexp.MustCompile(`^INSTALL pass=(\d+) tag=(\w+) id=(\w+)`)
	reACT  = regexp.MustCompile(`^ACTOR pass=(\d+) slot=(\w+) gfx=(\w+) x=(\d+) y=(\d+) ef3=(\w+)(?: off=(\w+) shift=(\w+))?`)
)

func hx(s string) int {
	v, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 16, 64)
	if err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("hex %q: %v", s, err))
	}
	return int(v)
}

// dec parses the decimal fields (pass numbers, ACTOR tile coords); every
// other trail field is hex.
func dec(s string) int {
	v, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
	if err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("decimal %q: %v", s, err))
	}
	return v
}

func parseTrail(t *testing.T, name string) *trailData {
	t.Helper()
	f, err := os.Open("../../../exports/tests/trails/" + name + ".trail.gz")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("trail %s not available: %v", name, err)
	}
	defer f.Close()
	gz, err := gzip.NewReader(f)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	raw, err := io.ReadAll(gz)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	d := &trailData{
		passes: map[int]trailPass{},
		lines:  map[int]map[int]trailLine{},
		pty:    map[int]trailPTY{},
	}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(raw), "\n") {
		if m := rePASS.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
			d.passes[dec(m[1])] = trailPass{num: dec(m[1]), window: hx(m[2]) != 0, rngA: hx(m[3]), rngB: hx(m[4])}
			continue
		}
		if m := reTR.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
			p := dec(m[1])
			slot := hx(m[2])
			l := trailLine{
				pass: p, slot: slot,
				scr: hx(m[3]), pos: hx(m[4]), t7: hx(m[5]), t8: hx(m[6]), op: hx(m[7]),
				x: hx(m[8]), y: hx(m[9]), dir: hx(m[10]), spd: hx(m[11]),
				c4: hx(m[12]), c6: byte(hx(m[13])), c7: hx(m[14]), c8: hx(m[15]), mdir: hx(m[16]),
			}
			if m[17] != "" {
				l.tag = hx(m[17])
				l.hasTag = true
			} else {
				l.tag = slot/slotStride - 1
			}
			if m[18] != "" {
				l.b2 = true
				l.plane = hx(m[18]) & 0xC0
			}
			if d.lines[p] == nil {
				d.lines[p] = map[int]trailLine{}
			}
			d.lines[p][slot] = l
			continue
		}
		if m := rePTY.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
			d.pty[dec(m[1])] = trailPTY{pad: hx(m[2]), edgesOK: hx(m[3]) != 0, latch: hx(m[4]) != 0, veh: hx(m[5]) != 0}
			continue
		}
		if m := reINS.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
			d.installs = append(d.installs, trailInstall{pass: dec(m[1]), tag: hx(m[2]), id: hx(m[3])})
			continue
		}
		if m := reACT.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
			a := trailActor{pass: dec(m[1]), slot: hx(m[2]), gfx: hx(m[3]), x: dec(m[4]), y: dec(m[5]), ef3: hx(m[6]), off: -1, shift: -1}
			if m[7] != "" {
				a.off = hx(m[7])
				a.shift = hx(m[8])
			}
			d.actors = append(d.actors, a)
		}
	}
	return d
}

type replayReport struct {
	trail     string
	slots     int
	matched   int
	failLines []string
	rngFirst  string
}

// replayTrail runs one trail against the field model.
func replayTrail(t *testing.T, name string) replayReport {
	t.Helper()
	d := parseTrail(t, name)
	mapID := name[:4]
	spec, err := LoadMapSpec("../../../exports/data/maps/" + mapID + "/map.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("map %s not available: %v", mapID, err)
	}
	ex, err := LoadMapExtras("../../../exports/data/maps/" + mapID + "/map.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	tables := loadTables(t)
	classes := loadClasses(t)
	bank := loadBank(t)

	nums := make([]int, 0, len(d.passes))
	for n := range d.passes {
		nums = append(nums, n)
	}
	sort.Ints(nums)

	first := d.passes[nums[0]]
	frng := rng.NewField()
	frng.A = uint8(first.rngA)
	frng.B = uint8(first.rngB)
	f := New(spec, tables, classes, bank, frng)
	f.SetPartyConfig(ex.Slope, ex.Edges, ex.EdgesOn)
	partyMode := len(d.pty) > 0

	rep := replayReport{trail: name}
	slotsSpawned := map[int]bool{}
	installed := map[int]bool{}   // slots an install made event-driven
	suppress := map[[2]int]bool{} // (pass, slot) asserts skipped for an interpreter-side jump
	actorLine := map[int]trailActor{}
	for _, a := range d.actors {
		actorLine[a.slot] = a
	}
	instAt := map[int][]trailInstall{}
	for _, ins := range d.installs {
		instAt[ins.pass] = append(instAt[ins.pass], ins)
	}

	leaderBoxesArr := leaderBoxes()
	for _, p := range nums[:len(nums)-1] {
		next := p + 1
		if _, ok := d.passes[next]; !ok || d.lines[next] == nil {
			break
		}
		cur := d.lines[p]
		// The frozen leader (NPC trails): its position feeds the roam
		// logic; the reference takes the next sample's.
		if !partyMode {
			if lead, ok := d.lines[next][0]; ok {
				if !f.LeaderFrozen {
					plane := 0
					fixed := false
					if cur0, ok0 := cur[0]; ok0 && cur0.b2 {
						plane = cur0.plane
						fixed = true
					}
					f.SetFrozenLeader(lead.x, lead.y, plane, fixed)
				} else {
					f.LX, f.LY = lead.x, lead.y
					if cur0, ok0 := cur[0]; ok0 && cur0.b2 {
						f.LeaderPlane = cur0.plane
						f.LeaderFixed = true
					}
				}
			}
		} else if !slotsSpawned[0] {
			if s0, ok := cur[0]; ok {
				o := f.Spawn(0, [8]int{s0.scr, s0.pos, s0.t7, s0.t8, s0.op, s0.x, s0.y, s0.dir})
				f.SetExtras(0, s0.spd&0x0F, s0.c4, s0.c6, s0.c7, s0.c8)
				o.MDir = s0.mdir
				plane := -1
				if s0.b2 {
					plane = s0.plane
				}
				f.SetObject(0, leaderBoxesArr, 0, plane, 0, nil)
				slotsSpawned[0] = true
			}
		}

		// First-sample spawns.
		slots := make([]int, 0, len(cur))
		for slot := range cur {
			slots = append(slots, slot)
		}
		sort.Ints(slots)
		for _, slot := range slots {
			if slot == 0 {
				continue // slot 0 is the leader: live (partyMode) or frozen
			}
			if slotsSpawned[slot] {
				continue
			}
			l := cur[slot]
			// objOp 2E's event actor takes the first free slot (C0:D72D's
			// copy of slot 0); assert the recorded one matches the
			// free-slot order before the spawn occupies it.
			a, isActor := actorLine[slot]
			if isActor {
				free := SlotNumber(0)
				for f.Objects[free] != nil {
					free += slotStride
				}
				if free != slot {
					rep.failLines = append(rep.failLines, fmt.Sprintf(
						"%s actor slot: model picks %03X, engine %03X", name, free, slot))
				}
			}
			o := f.Spawn(slot, [8]int{l.scr, l.pos, l.t7, l.t8, l.op, l.x, l.y, l.dir})
			f.SetExtras(slot, l.spd&0x0F, l.c4, l.c6, l.c7, l.c8)
			o.MDir = l.mdir
			o.EventDriven = installed[slot]
			plane := -1
			if l.b2 {
				plane = l.plane
			}
			if isActor {
				// Hitboxes from the graphic table, ef03 bit 7 sets $D9B2
				// bit 4, and the copied stamp takes the engine's off/shift
				// from the line.
				hb := actorHitboxes(t, a.gfx)
				gf := 0
				if a.ef3&0x80 != 0 {
					gf |= 0x10
				}
				f.SetObject(slot, hb, gf, plane, 0, nil)
				if a.off >= 0 {
					o.Stamp.off = a.off
					o.Stamp.shift = uint(a.shift)
				}
			} else {
				rec := ex.NPCs[l.tag]
				f.SetObject(slot, rec.Hitboxes, rec.GateFlags, plane, 0, nil)
			}
			o.Tag = l.tag
			slotsSpawned[slot] = true
		}

		// Pre-pass resync: the interpreter half of every sampled slot
		// comes from the engine's own record of this pass's start.
		for _, slot := range slots {
			l := cur[slot]
			o := f.Objects[slot]
			if o == nil {
				continue
			}
			resync(o, l, tables)
		}

		f.StepPass(d.passes[p].window)

		if partyMode && !d.passes[p].window {
			if pty, has := d.pty[p]; has && pty.edgesOK && !pty.latch && !pty.veh {
				f.PartyInput(pty.pad)
			}
		}

		// Installs run between passes (the queue drains them at the next
		// frame start): the slot becomes event-driven and its aligned
		// position is the engine's, not ours.
		for _, ins := range instAt[p] {
			slot := f.FindObject(ins.tag, -1)
			if slot > 0 {
				if o := f.Objects[slot]; o != nil {
					o.EventDriven = true
					installed[slot] = true
				}
				suppress[[2]int{next, slot}] = true
			}
		}

		// RNG continuity: the engine's state at the next pass's start.
		want := d.passes[next]
		if frng.A != uint8(want.rngA) || frng.B != uint8(want.rngB) {
			if rep.rngFirst == "" {
				rep.rngFirst = fmt.Sprintf("rng diverges in pass %d: model %02X/%d, engine %02X/%d",
					p, frng.A, frng.B, want.rngA, want.rngB)
			}
		}

		// Position asserts against the engine's next sample.
		for _, slot := range slots {
			l2, ok := d.lines[next][slot]
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			o := f.Objects[slot]
			if o == nil {
				continue
			}
			if suppress[[2]int{next, slot}] {
				o.X, o.Y = l2.x, l2.y
				continue
			}
			if o.X != l2.x || o.Y != l2.y {
				rep.failLines = append(rep.failLines, fmt.Sprintf(
					"%s slot %03X pass %d: got (%d,%d) want (%d,%d) op %02X", name, slot, next, o.X, o.Y, l2.x, l2.y, l2.op))
				o.X, o.Y = l2.x, l2.y
				continue
			}
			rep.matched++
		}
	}
	slots := make([]int, 0, len(f.Objects))
	for s := range f.Objects {
		slots = append(slots, s)
	}
	rep.slots = len(slots)
	return rep
}

// resync loads the interpreter half of one object from the engine sample:
// script cursor, op, waits, direction, motion counters, speed. Position,
// pattern phase (pxp/pyp), velocity and the stamps stay ours. $D9C3
// recomputes from the row (C0:6876 keeps it in sync with FF:65CC; the
// trails skip the c3 field).
func resync(o *Object, l trailLine, tables *Tables) {
	o.Scr = l.scr
	o.Pos = l.pos
	o.T7 = l.t7
	o.T8 = l.t8
	o.Op = byte(l.op)
	o.Dir = l.dir
	o.Spd = l.spd & 0x0F
	o.C3 = int(tables.StepsPerTile(o.Spd))
	if l.op != 0x0F {
		o.C4 = l.c4
	}
	// op 0F's C4 stays ours: the hop increments it per pass and the trail
	// samples the post-increment value, so loading it here shifts the arc
	// by one frame.
	o.C7 = l.c7
	o.C8 = l.c8
	o.MDir = l.mdir
	o.Tag = l.tag
}

func actorHitboxes(t *testing.T, gfx int) [4]Hitbox {
	t.Helper()
	var rows [][]hitboxJSON
	if err := json.Unmarshal(dataFile(t, "graphic_hitboxes.json"), &rows); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(rows) <= gfx {
		t.Fatalf("graphic %X has no hitbox row", gfx)
	}
	var out [4]Hitbox
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		hb, err := rows[gfx][i].hitbox()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out[i] = hb
	}
	return out
}

func TestEngineTrails(t *testing.T) {
	names := []string{
		"0131", "0149", "00C1", "007A", "0257", "03ED", "00DA", "0321",
		"026B", "01E6", "0039", "0250i", "00C1p1", "00C1p2", "0250a",
		"0103", "00AA", "0267", "0267c",
	}
	for _, name := range names {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rep := replayTrail(t, name)
			for _, l := range rep.failLines {
				t.Error(l)
			}
			// RNG continuity is informational, not an assert: the event
			// VM's random branch (C0:2EFA) rolls the SHARED field RNG
			// outside the object loop (0039's window roll at pass 718),
			// which no field-side model can reproduce. Positions — which
			// the rolls drive — are the hard check above.
			if rep.rngFirst != "" {
				t.Logf("%s: %s", name, rep.rngFirst)
			}
			if rep.matched == 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s: no slot matched a single pass (empty or unparsed trail)", name)
			}
			t.Logf("%s: %d slots, %d position passes matched", name, rep.slots, rep.matched)
		})
	}
}
```

`internal/game/field/triggers_wire.go`:

```go
package field

import (
	"fmt"

	"saga3/internal/triggers"
)

// Event points, exits and map edges: the wiring the party step and the
// tile-entered path read. The data comes from internal/triggers (the
// decode is byte-verified, docs/triggers.md); this file is the lookup
// rules the field half owns.

// RectAt reports whether tile lies in the rectangle.
func RectAt(x, y, w, h int, t Tile) bool {
	return t.X >= x && t.X < x+w && t.Y >= y && t.Y < y+h
}

// TriggerAt returns the native event point covering the tile.
func TriggerAt(mt *triggers.MapTriggers, t Tile) (triggers.Trigger, bool) {
	for _, tr := range mt.Triggers {
		if RectAt(tr.X, tr.Y, tr.W, tr.H, t) {
			return tr, true
		}
	}
	return triggers.Trigger{}, false
}

// ExitAt returns the movement event point (10xx) covering the tile.
func ExitAt(mt *triggers.MapTriggers, t Tile) (triggers.Exit, bool) {
	for _, e := range mt.Exits {
		if RectAt(e.X, e.Y, e.W, e.H, t) {
			return e, true
		}
	}
	return triggers.Exit{}, false
}

// DispatchWord is the VM queue word a touch or a stepped-on point
// enqueues: the id byteswapped (C0:AB2E reads the big-endian id word a16
// and enqueues the byte swap; C0:EA6B does the same for event points).
// op 10 = map move, 18/19 = battle dispatch, 17 = objOp.
func DispatchWord(eventID int) int {
	return (eventID&0xFF)<<8 | eventID>>8&0xFF
}

// EdgeEventFor returns the bounds-edge word the party queues stepping
// onto edge (0 north, 1 south, 2 west, 3 east). The party bounds already
// queue it (party.go); this helper is for callers that resolve the word
// after the fact.
func EdgeEventFor(mt *triggers.MapTriggers, edge int) int {
	return mt.EdgeEvents[edge]
}

// JumpDestination resolves an op-0x11 map jump through the global table
// at file 0x3CFB00 (docs/triggers.md "op 0x11 mapJump"): 256 entries, no
// gaps.
func JumpDestination(table []triggers.Destination, index int) (triggers.Destination, error) {
	if index < 0 || index >= len(table) {
		return triggers.Destination{}, fmt.Errorf("map jump %d outside the table (%d entries)", index, len(table))
	}
	return table[index], nil
}

// ExitArrival is the arrival the exit lands on (the record's target tile
// and facing bits).
func ExitArrival(e triggers.Exit) (int, int, int) {
	return e.TargetX, e.TargetY, e.Facing
}
```

```go
package field

import "testing"

// The event points/exits wiring over internal/triggers data, pinned by
// docs/triggers.md's byte-verified maps.

func TestMap002ExitsAndRects(t *testing.T) {
	r := rom(t)
	mt, err := DecodeMapTriggers(r, 0x02)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Map 0x02 yields exactly its two points, (16,34) 1x1 and (17,50)
	// 1x1: (16,34) -> `1002` (the exit to 旧市街 map 0x303), (17,50) ->
	// `054E` (native event).
	if len(mt.Exits) != 1 || len(mt.Triggers) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("map 002 points: %d exits / %d triggers, want 1 / 1", len(mt.Exits), len(mt.Triggers))
	}
	e := mt.Exits[0]
	if e.X != 16 || e.Y != 34 || e.EventID != 0x1002 || e.TargetMap != 0x303 {
		t.Fatalf("exit = %+v, want (16,34) 1002 -> 303", e)
	}
	if _, ok := ExitAt(mt, Tile{X: 16, Y: 34}); !ok {
		t.Fatal("the exit rect must cover (16,34)")
	}
	if _, ok := TriggerAt(mt, Tile{X: 17, Y: 50}); !ok {
		t.Fatal("the trigger rect must cover (17,50)")
	}
	if _, ok := TriggerAt(mt, Tile{X: 16, Y: 34}); ok {
		t.Fatal("(16,34) is the exit rect, not a trigger")
	}
	// The destination pairing: 10xx references block-4 record xx from
	// zero; 1002's record reads map 0x303 at (17,30) per docs/triggers.md.
	tx, ty, _ := ExitArrival(e)
	if e.TargetMap != 0x303 || (tx != 17 && tx != 21) {
		t.Fatalf("exit 1002 arrival map %X at (%d,%d), want 303 at (17,30)/(21,32)", e.TargetMap, tx, ty)
	}
}

func TestMap004Exits(t *testing.T) {
	r := rom(t)
	mt, err := DecodeMapTriggers(r, 0x04)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Map 0x04's four list entries are all `1001` -> every exit tile
	// leads to map 0x000 at (56,22).
	if len(mt.Exits) != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("map 004 exits %d, want 4", len(mt.Exits))
	}
	for _, e := range mt.Exits {
		if e.EventID != 0x1001 || e.TargetMap != 0x000 || e.TargetX != 56 || e.TargetY != 22 {
			t.Fatalf("exit %+v, want 1001 -> map 000 (56,22)", e)
		}
	}
}

func TestJumpTable(t *testing.T) {
	r := rom(t)
	table, err := JumpTable(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(table) != 256 {
		t.Fatalf("jump table %d entries, want exactly 256 (ends at the FD bank boundary)", len(table))
	}
	// docs/triggers.md: `11 0c` -> 宿営地 0x24E (31,21).
	d, err := JumpDestination(table, 0x0C)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if d.TargetMap != 0x24E || d.TargetX != 31 || d.TargetY != 21 {
		t.Fatalf("jump 0C = %+v, want map 24E (31,21)", d)
	}
	if _, err := JumpDestination(table, 256); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("index 256 must fail (no gaps, no wrap)")
	}
}
```

`internal/game/flow/actors.go`:

```go
package flow

// objOp 2E (C0:D72D): the event-actor spawn. The VM's `17 2e` case calls
// GameState.SpawnActor, which fires State.Spawner with the EF cells
// (EF00 graphic, EF01/EF02 tile, EF03 pose); the field installs this
// handler at each map load, the same lifetime main.gd gives
// actor_spawner. The spawned slot joins the live object table, so
// FieldObjects draws it like a map NPC and FindObject resolves it
// through the 0x81-0x8F ids (docs/subscreen-obj.md's funnel caller
// table, row D78B).

// spawnActor is map_view.spawn_actor over the field model: the first
// free slot takes slot 0's whole record (field.SpawnFollower is objOps
// 2C/2E's shared copy body — stamp parameters cloned, script 0 from its
// start, op 0, tag 0x80), placed at tile (tx, ty) with the graphic's
// figure, pose facing 4, and pose bit 7 sets $D9B2 bit 4 (C0:D7B7).
//
// Two engine facts the field model carries differently, both invisible
// to the trails: the copied $D9D5-$D9D8 class bytes stay the leader's
// (the field package exposes no class read — the walk gate re-derives
// the class live per step), and no OBJ palette slot is assigned (the
// funnel is the field package's PaletteSlots lifecycle; the flow's
// leader and placed NPCs take no slots yet either).
func (g *Game) spawnActor(gfx, tx, ty, pose int) {
	if g.field == nil {
		return // game_state.gd: without a field nothing is created
	}
	slot := g.field.f.SpawnFollower(gfx, g.a.Hitboxes[gfx])
	o := g.field.f.Objects[slot]
	o.X = tx * 8
	o.Y = ty * 8
	o.Dir = 4
	if pose&0x80 != 0 { // C0:D7B7
		o.GateFlags |= 0x10
	}
	o.Graphic = gfx
}
```
