`internal/game/flow/fieldmap.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"saga3/internal/game/field"
)

// ---- map switches (main.gd _on_map_jump/_on_map_move + map_view
// switch_map/_spawn_npcs) -----------------------------------------------

// onMapJump resolves op 11 through the global jump table 0x3CFB00
// (main.gd _on_map_jump).
func (g *Game) onMapJump(index int) {
	if index < 0 || index >= len(g.a.jumpTable) {
		g.diag("map jump %02X outside the table (%d entries)", index, len(g.a.jumpTable))
		return
	}
	d := g.a.jumpTable[index]
	g.jumpsRun = append(g.jumpsRun, index)
	if d.Stay {
		// the engine only places the leader on the current map
		// (C0:C270 -> C2B6, main.gd's stay branch)
		g.placeLeader(d.ToX, d.ToY)
		return
	}
	if !g.a.HasMap(d.ToMap) {
		g.diag("map jump %02X: map %s not exported", index, d.ToMap)
		return
	}
	g.Arrival = Arrival{Bits: d.Arrival, NoFade: d.NoFade, Music: d.Music, Facing: d.Facing}
	g.switchMap(d.ToMap, d.ToX, d.ToY)
}

// onMapMove resolves op 10 through the current map's destination records
// (main.gd _on_map_move).
func (g *Game) onMapMove(index int) {
	if g.field == nil {
		g.diag("map move %02X: no map loaded", index)
		return
	}
	md := g.field.md
	if index < 0 || index >= len(md.Destinations) {
		g.diag("map move %02X: map %s has %d destinations", index, g.MapID, len(md.Destinations))
		return
	}
	d := md.Destinations[index]
	g.movesRun = append(g.movesRun, index)
	if d.Stay {
		g.placeLeader(d.ToX, d.ToY)
		return
	}
	if !g.a.HasMap(d.ToMap) {
		g.diag("map move %02X: map %s not exported", index, d.ToMap)
		return
	}
	g.Arrival = Arrival{Bits: d.Arrival, NoFade: d.NoFade, Music: d.Music, Facing: d.Facing}
	g.switchMap(d.ToMap, d.ToX, d.ToY)
}

// switchMap loads the map and spawns its field (map_view.switch_map's
// logic half + _spawn_leader/_spawn_npcs): a fresh Field per load — the
// engine respawns every placed monster on reload.
func (g *Game) switchMap(id string, tx, ty int) {
	md, err := g.a.Map(id)
	if err != nil {
		g.diag("%v", err)
		return
	}
	f := field.New(md.Spec, g.a.FieldTable, g.a.Classes, g.a.BankF8, &g.State.FieldRNG)
	f.SetPartyConfig(md.Slope, md.Edges, md.EdgesOn)
	lf := &liveField{f: f, md: md, npcs: map[int]field.NpcRecord{}, defeated: map[int]bool{}}

	// the party leader is slot 0: script 0, speed row 1, the party shape
	// 0F82 (C0:7B34); the entering record's leader facing (flag bits 0-1,
	// C0:C333) applies at load, -1 faces down
	if g.Arrival.Facing >= 0 {
		g.leaderFacing = g.Arrival.Facing
	} else {
		g.leaderFacing = 1
	}
	hb := field.LeaderHitbox()
	boxes := [4]field.Hitbox{hb, hb, hb, hb}
	f.Spawn(0, [8]int{scriptBase(g.a.BankF8, 0), 0, 1, 0, 0, tx * 8, ty * 8, g.leaderFacing})
	f.SetExtras(0, 1, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0)
	f.SetObject(0, boxes, 0, -1, 0, nil)

	// the placed characters: judged entries spawn while their 4-bit flag
	// lies in the record's window (C0:4A7D-4A9A); slots continue the
	// (index+1)*0x40 stride across skipped records (C0:4BEC)
	slot := 0x40
	for _, rec := range md.NPCs {
		if rec.Judged && !field.PlacementPasses(rec, func(idx int) int { return g.State.GetVanilla(idx) }) {
			continue
		}
		f.SpawnNPC(slot, rec)
		lf.npcs[slot] = rec
		slot += 0x40
	}

	g.field = lf
	g.MapID = id
	lf.tile = field.Tile{X: tx, Y: ty} // switch_map's _grid seed
	// the actor-spawn hook (main.gd wires actor_spawner to the map view's
	// spawn_actor when the field scene comes up)
	g.State.Spawner = g.spawnActor
	// the arrival record's track, else the map's own (map_view's
	// _play_bgm path); -1 = the record says nothing, no change
	if g.Arrival.Music >= 0 {
		g.playTrack(g.Arrival.Music)
	} else if g.Arrival.Music == arrivalNoRecord {
		g.playTrack(md.BGM)
	}
	g.Arrival = Arrival{Music: arrivalNoRecord, Facing: -1}
}

// placeLeader moves the leader to a tile on the current map (map_view
// place_leader: the grid and the slot-0 pixel position, no facing).
func (g *Game) placeLeader(tx, ty int) {
	if g.field == nil {
		return // a stay record on a blank map places nothing
	}
	if o, ok := g.field.f.Objects[0]; ok {
		o.X = tx * 8
		o.Y = ty * 8
	}
}

// ---- the field frame (map_view _tick_npcs + main.gd's wiring) ----------

// tickField runs one field frame: the object pass with the window gate,
// then (unlocked) the party step and the wiring its outputs drive — the
// edge words, the party-side bumps, and the latched touch the pass
// dispatched. The runner's op-09 words reach the queue in the reference
// through map_view's runner-enqueue append; field.Field does not collect
// them (reported interface gap), and the static walker covers the
// installs the selftest pins.
func (g *Game) tickField() {
	if g.field == nil {
		return
	}
	f := g.field.f
	locked := g.fieldLocked()
	f.Dispatched = nil
	f.Bumped = nil
	f.StepPass(locked)
	if !locked {
		f.PartyInput(g.padOf())
		for _, w := range f.PartyEdges() {
			g.onEdgeEvent(w)
		}
		// the bumps dispatch in the object table's order (the reference's
		// _party_bump walks its insertion-ordered dict, slots ascending;
		// field.partyBump reads a Go map whose order varies, so the flow
		// sorts — the divergence goes back to the field package)
		bumped := f.PartyBumpedSlots()
		sortInts(bumped)
		for _, slot := range bumped {
			g.onNPCBumped(slot, true)
		}
	}
	// the latched touch C0:5635 dispatched this pass (map_view's
	// dispatched loop; the reference checks defeated and the encounter
	// class here)
	for _, slot := range f.Dispatched {
		g.onNPCBumped(slot, false)
	}
	g.followLeader()
}

// sortInts sorts ascending, in place.
func sortInts(s []int) {
	for i := 1; i < len(s); i++ {
		for j := i; j > 0 && s[j] < s[j-1]; j-- {
			s[j], s[j-1] = s[j-1], s[j]
		}
	}
}

// followLeader is map_view _follow_leader: the display facing follows
// slot 0, and a tile-aligned arrival fires the tile's triggers and exits.
func (g *Game) followLeader() {
	o, ok := g.field.f.Objects[0]
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	if o.Dir < 4 {
		g.leaderFacing = o.Dir
	}
	if o.X&7 != 0 || o.Y&7 != 0 {
		return
	}
	t := field.Tile{X: o.X >> 3, Y: o.Y >> 3}
	if t == g.field.tile {
		return
	}
	g.field.tile = t
	g.onTileEntered(t.X, t.Y)
}

// onTileEntered is the field resolution order per step (main.gd
// _on_tile_entered): triggers fire events (encounter-class ids start the
// battle, contact on no object), exits switch maps.
func (g *Game) onTileEntered(x, y int) {
	if g.field == nil {
		return
	}
	for _, t := range g.field.md.Triggers {
		if t.X == x && t.Y == y {
			ev, err := field.EncounterID(t.Event)
			if err != nil {
				g.diag("trigger %s: %v", t.Event, err)
				return
			}
			if _, isEnc := field.EncounterClass(ev); isEnc {
				g.startFieldBattle(ev, -1, false)
			} else if ev != 0 {
				g.startEvent(ev)
			}
			return
		}
	}
	for _, e := range g.field.md.Exits {
		if e.X == x && e.Y == y {
			g.Arrival = Arrival{Music: arrivalNoRecord, Facing: -1}
			g.switchMap(e.ToMap, e.ToX, e.ToY)
			return
		}
	}
}

// onEdgeEvent routes a bounds-edge word (main.gd _on_edge_event): 10xx
// moves through the map's destination record xx, high bytes below 0x0C
// call the event, others are inert.
func (g *Game) onEdgeEvent(word int) {
	if word>>8 == 0x10 {
		g.onMapMove(word & 0xFF)
		return
	}
	if word>>8 < 0x0C {
		g.startEvent(word)
	}
}

// onNPCBumped starts the encounter battle when the touched slot carries
// an encounter-class id (main.gd _on_npc_bumped; the touch dispatcher
// C0:AB2E's shape). Everything else keeps the turn-and-face behavior the
// runner owns. byParty: a party step's blocked bump (C0:8049) vs the
// monster's own step into the party (C0:5656).
func (g *Game) onNPCBumped(slot int, byParty bool) {
	if g.inEvent || g.BattleUp || g.field == nil {
		return
	}
	if g.field.defeated[slot] {
		return
	}
	rec, ok := g.field.npcs[slot]
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ev, err := field.EncounterID(rec.Event)
	if err != nil {
		g.diag("%v", err)
		return
	}
	if _, ok := field.EncounterClass(ev); !ok {
		return
	}
	g.startFieldBattle(ev, slot, byParty)
}

// ---- facing interactions (main.gd _talk_to_facing_npc) ------------------

// LeaderFacing is the leader's facing as the shell draws it: 0 up,
// 1 down, 2 left, 3 right (map_view's _facing order, which is also the
// runner's dir byte order — switch_map spawns the leader with it).
func (g *Game) LeaderFacing() int { return g.leaderFacing }

// LeaderTile is the tile the leader stands on (the save position;
// map_view player_tile reads the same grid the tile-entered emission
// updates).
func (g *Game) LeaderTile() (int, int) {
	if g.field == nil {
		return -1, -1
	}
	return g.field.tile.X, g.field.tile.Y
}

// facingTile is one step ahead of the leader (map_view facing_tile).
func (g *Game) facingTile() (int, int) {
	x, y := g.LeaderTile()
	switch g.leaderFacing {
	case 0:
		return x, y - 1
	case 2:
		return x - 1, y
	case 3:
		return x + 1, y
	default:
		return x, y + 1
	}
}

// fieldInput is the field's pressed-key routing (main.gd's
// _unhandled_input map-mode half).
func (g *Game) fieldInput(k Key) {
	switch k {
	case KeyMenu:
		if g.Menus.IsOpen() {
			g.Menus.Close()
		} else {
			g.Menus.OpenMenus(g.a, g.State)
		}
	case KeyConfirm:
		if g.inEvent {
			g.advanceDialogue()
			return
		}
		// C0:7DCA's talk check runs past the latch gate C0:7DB4, but not
		// while a touch is latched (main.gd's touch_latched guard)
		if g.field != nil && !g.field.f.TouchLatch() {
			g.talkToFacingNPC()
		}
	case KeyBack:
		// the prototype quits the app on Esc; the shell owns that
	}
}

// talkToFacingNPC starts the faced NPC's event, or its battle for an
// encounter-class id; events the catalog lacks stay silent (main.gd
// _talk_to_facing_npc).
func (g *Game) talkToFacingNPC() {
	x, y := g.facingTile()
	if ci := g.chestAt(x, y); ci >= 0 {
		g.openChest(ci)
		return
	}
	if g.field == nil {
		return
	}
	slot := g.npcSlotAt(x, y)
	if slot < 0 {
		return
	}
	rec := g.field.npcs[slot]
	ev, err := field.EncounterID(rec.Event)
	if err != nil {
		g.diag("%v", err)
		return
	}
	if _, ok := field.EncounterClass(ev); ok {
		g.startFieldBattle(ev, slot, true)
		return
	}
	if ev == 0 || !g.a.Catalog.HasEvent(ev) {
		return
	}
	g.startEvent(ev)
}

// npcSlotAt returns the slot whose NPC stands on the tile, -1 none.
// Monsters are consulted at their live tiles (map_view _npc_tile: the
// figure's center tile).
func (g *Game) npcSlotAt(x, y int) int {
	if g.field == nil {
		return -1
	}
	slots := make([]int, 0, len(g.field.f.Objects))
	for s := range g.field.f.Objects {
		slots = append(slots, s)
	}
	sortInts(slots)
	for _, s := range slots {
		o := g.field.f.Objects[s]
		tx := (o.X + 4) / 8
		ty := (o.Y + 4) / 8
		if tx == x && ty == y {
			if _, placed := g.field.npcs[s]; placed {
				return s
			}
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// ---- chests (main.gd _open_chest, C0:A97E-AA46) --------------------------

// chestAt returns the chest whose 4x4 graphic band covers the tile
// (map_view chest_at), -1 none.
func (g *Game) chestAt(x, y int) int {
	if g.field == nil {
		return -1
	}
	for i, c := range g.field.md.Chests {
		if x >= c.X-1 && x <= c.X+2 && y >= c.Y-2 && y <= c.Y+1 {
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// openChest opens an unopened chest: the flag sets, and the content
// queues — an item (event 0108), money (0208) or the chest's own event
// word. An opened chest does nothing.
func (g *Game) openChest(i int) {
	c := g.field.md.Chests[i]
	if g.State.TreasureOpen(c.OpenFlag) {
		return
	}
	g.State.SetTreasureOpen(c.OpenFlag)
	// the opened object's restamp is the shell's draw (map_view
	// refresh_chest)
	switch c.Flags & 0x0C {
	case 0x00:
		g.State.SetVar(1, c.Content)
		g.onEdgeEvent(0x0108)
	case 0x04:
		amount := c.Content * moneyMultiplier(c.Flags)
		g.State.SetVar(1, amount&0xFF)
		g.State.SetVar(2, (amount>>8)&0xFF)
		g.State.SetVar(3, (amount>>16)&0xFF)
		g.onEdgeEvent(0x0208)
	case 0x08:
		g.onEdgeEvent(c.Event)
	}
}

// moneyMultiplier is [1, 10, 100, 1000][flags & 3] (main.gd's chest
// money decode).
func moneyMultiplier(flags int) int {
	switch flags & 3 {
	case 1:
		return 10
	case 2:
		return 100
	case 3:
		return 1000
	default:
		return 1
	}
}

```

`internal/game/flow/game.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"saga3/internal/game/battle"
	"saga3/internal/game/field"
	"saga3/internal/game/state"
	"saga3/internal/game/vm"
)

// ScreenKind is the screen the shell draws.
type ScreenKind int

const (
	ScreenTitle ScreenKind = iota
	ScreenSelect
	ScreenNaming
	ScreenField
)

// TitleRows is the title menu (main.gd TITLE_ROWS): the engine's English
// NEW GAME/CONTINUE menu, cursor on NEW GAME.
var TitleRows = [2]string{"NEW GAME", "CONTINUE"}

// SelectHeader and NamingHeader are the screens' captions
// (select_screen.gd / naming_screen.gd), carried as state for the shell.
const (
	SelectHeader = "主人公をえらぶ"
	NamingHeader = "なまえをつける"
)

// DialogueState is the dialogue box's flow state (main.gd's label +
// choices box): the current page with the pause marks stripped, the
// segments between the marks (a 2C pause ends each), how many are shown,
// and the pending choices (a selection menu shows whole).
type DialogueState struct {
	Open     bool
	Page     string
	Segments []string
	Shown    int
	Choices  []string
}

// Arrival is the switch record a map move/jump carried (main.gd's
// arrival fields on map_view); the shell plays the sequence it describes.
// Music -1 = the record says nothing; Facing -1 = no record (the leader
// faces down).
type Arrival struct {
	Bits   int
	NoFade bool
	Music  int
	Facing int
}

// arrivalNoRecord is map_view.ARRIVAL_NO_RECORD: no record at all (save
// load, plain switch) — the load plays the map's own track.
const arrivalNoRecord = -2

// pauseMark is op 2C's page mark (event_vm PAUSE_MARK, "\f"): a page
// carries one mark per pause; a trailing mark is the window's own wait.
const pauseMark = "\f"

// Game is the flow machine: one game's screens, event playback, field
// loop and battle handoff. Construct with New; drive with Input and Tick.
type Game struct {
	a          *Assets
	State      *state.GameState
	SavePath   string
	ProtagAlly int // the protagonist's ally id (the walk figure's owner)

	Screen    ScreenKind
	TitleRow  int
	SelectRow int
	Dialogue  DialogueState
	Menus     MenusState

	field    *liveField
	MapID    string // "" = blank (no map yet; map_id() reads 0000)
	Track    int    // the playing BGM track, -1 = none
	Arrival  Arrival
	BattleUp bool

	battle       *battle.Engine // the running battle, nil = none
	leaderFacing int            // 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right (map_view's _facing)

	eventID   string // "%04X" while an event runs
	inEvent   bool
	vm        *vm.VM
	queue     []int
	eventsRun []string // root event ids started, in order
	chain     []string // every $D51B change: VM call/dispatch ids + queue ids
	jumpsRun  []int
	movesRun  []int
	Diag      []string // push_error paths: the reference logs and continues

	held   [keyCount]bool
	naming namingScreen
}

// liveField is the loaded map: the field model plus the flow's per-map
// bookkeeping (the map's wiring rows, placed-NPC records, defeated
// slots, and the leader's last known tile).
type liveField struct {
	f        *field.Field
	md       *MapData
	npcs     map[int]field.NpcRecord
	defeated map[int]bool
	tile     field.Tile // the leader's last emitted tile (_grid)
}

// New boots a game on the title screen (main.gd's map-mode _ready: the
// field scene exists blank, the menus are initialized and closed, the
// title is up and the input locked).
func New(a *Assets, gs *state.GameState, savePath string) *Game {
	g := &Game{
		a:        a,
		State:    gs,
		SavePath: savePath,
		Screen:   ScreenTitle,
		Track:    -1,
		Arrival:  Arrival{Music: arrivalNoRecord, Facing: -1},
	}
	// the install hook: game_state.gd install_action's callable is the
	// map view's install; field.Field has no install path (reported
	// interface gap), so every install takes the static fallback, which
	// queues the script's op-09 words here
	gs.Installer = g.installFallback
	return g
}

// installFallback is the install hook's no-field shape (game_state.gd
// install_action + action_scripts.gd enqueued_words): walk the script
// bank statically and queue its op-09 words, in script order. The false
// return leaves the install recorded in State.Installs, like the
// reference's fallback.
func (g *Game) installFallback(obj, id int, eventDriven bool) bool {
	g.enqueueAll(enqueuedWords(g.a.BankF8, id))
	return false
}

// EnterField is the --map boot path (main.gd's map-mode default): the
// game opens directly on the field with the title skipped and the state
// seeded.
func (g *Game) EnterField(mapID string, x, y int) error {
	if !g.a.HasMap(mapID) {
		return fmt.Errorf("map %s not exported (ids are 4 hex digits; exports/data/map_catalog.json lists them)", mapID)
	}
	g.Screen = ScreenField
	g.Arrival = Arrival{Music: arrivalNoRecord, Facing: -1}
	g.switchMap(mapID, x, y)
	return nil
}

// diag records a push_error path: the reference logs and continues, and
// the flow keeps the line instead of dropping it.
func (g *Game) diag(format string, args ...any) {
	g.Diag = append(g.Diag, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
}

// fieldLocked is map_scene.input_locked: the party stands still while a
// screen, a dialogue or a battle owns the frame (title/select/naming set
// it, _start_event sets it, the battle handoff sets it).
func (g *Game) fieldLocked() bool {
	return g.inEvent || g.Screen != ScreenField || g.BattleUp
}

// Tick advances one field frame (main._physics_process + the map view's
// frame): the play clock ticks, the queue drains (words queued while no
// event runs start their event this frame), then the field frame runs —
// the object pass with the window gate, the party step, and the wiring
// the step's outputs drive.
func (g *Game) Tick() {
	if g.BattleUp {
		return // the battle scene owns the frame
	}
	g.State.ClockTick()
	if !g.inEvent {
		if next := g.nextQueuedEvent(); next >= 0 {
			g.chain = append(g.chain, formatWord(next))
			g.startEvent(next)
		}
	}
	g.tickField()
}

// ---- event playback (main.gd _start_event/_advance/_advance_pressed) ----

// startEvent starts (or restarts) an event through a fresh VM (main.gd
// _start_event, map mode): calls on, the flow's handlers wired, the
// field locked.
func (g *Game) startEvent(id int) {
	g.eventID = formatWord(id)
	g.inEvent = true
	g.eventsRun = append(g.eventsRun, g.eventID)
	v := vm.New(g.a.Catalog)
	v.State = g.State
	// the name tables for op 39/3A/4F_50 (event_vm.gd loaded
	// items.json/allies.json itself): the Assets maps the menus read.
	v.Names = g.a
	v.CallsEnabled = true
	v.TraceEnabled = true // the chain pins read the call/dispatch lines
	// the flow shows the choices the VM collects and calls Choose; the
	// handler is reinstalled after every Choose (vm.Choose clears it, as
	// the engine's menu loop does)
	v.ChoiceHandler = func([]string) {}
	v.MapJump = g.onMapJump
	v.MapMove = g.onMapMove
	// LeaderInstruction/FollowerSpawn stay nil: field.Field has no
	// leader-instruction or follower path (reported interface gap); the
	// VM treats unset handlers as transparent, like an unset Callable.
	g.vm = v
	v.LoadEvent(g.a.Catalog.RawOps(id), id)
	g.pullPage()
}

// pullPage pulls the next page from the VM; "" means the event finished
// (main.gd _advance; the Go VM has no timed waits — pages pull at the
// boundaries, and op 2B waits run through transparently). The page
// translates before the display split (main.gd _advance's
// _show_page(_translate_page(page)); nil Trans = the Japanese default).
func (g *Game) pullPage() {
	page := g.vm.NextPage()
	if page == "" && g.vm.IsFinished() {
		g.eventDone()
		return
	}
	page = g.a.Trans.Page(g.eventID, page)
	g.showPage(page)
}

// showPage shows one page (main.gd _show_page): a trailing 2C mark is
// the page's own wait, the rest splits into segments; a selection menu
// shows whole.
func (g *Game) showPage(page string) {
	for strings.HasSuffix(page, pauseMark) {
		page = strings.TrimSuffix(page, pauseMark)
	}
	segs := strings.Split(page, pauseMark)
	shown := 1
	if len(g.vm.PendingChoices) > 0 {
		shown = len(segs)
	}
	g.Dialogue = DialogueState{
		Open:     true,
		Page:     page,
		Segments: segs,
		Shown:    shown,
		Choices:  append([]string(nil), g.vm.PendingChoices...),
	}
}

// Press on the dialogue: finish the current segment first, then the next
// one, then the next page (main.gd _advance_pressed's map-mode shape —
// the engine reads the button only inside a 2C pause; with the timed
// step costs unported every press is a pause read, and pacing stays with
// the GDScript checker).
func (g *Game) advanceDialogue() {
	if g.vm == nil {
		return
	}
	if len(g.vm.PendingChoices) > 0 {
		return // must choose an option
	}
	if g.Dialogue.Shown < len(g.Dialogue.Segments) {
		g.Dialogue.Shown++
		return
	}
	g.pullPage()
}

// Choose resolves a selection menu (main.gd's option-button press):
// choose clears the handler, so it is reinstalled for the next pause,
// and the page choose() pulled internally shows on the next press —
// the same contract main.gd keeps with event_vm.
func (g *Game) Choose(index int) {
	if g.vm == nil || len(g.vm.PendingChoices) == 0 {
		return
	}
	g.vm.ChoiceHandler = func([]string) {}
	g.vm.Choose(index)
	g.Dialogue.Choices = nil
}

// eventDone ends the event and returns control to the field (main.gd
// _event_done, map mode): the dialogue closes, the field unlocks, and a
// queued call word starts its event this frame. eventID keeps the last
// started id, as main.gd's _event_id does.
func (g *Game) eventDone() {
	g.harvestChain()
	g.inEvent = false
	g.vm = nil
	g.Dialogue = DialogueState{}
	if next := g.nextQueuedEvent(); next >= 0 {
		g.chain = append(g.chain, formatWord(next))
		g.startEvent(next)
	}
}

// formatWord renders a native id as the four hex digits the chain pins
// and the queue words use.
func formatWord(id int) string {
	const digits = "0123456789ABCDEF"
	return string([]byte{digits[(id>>12)&0xF], digits[(id>>8)&0xF], digits[(id>>4)&0xF], digits[id&0xF]})
}

// harvestChain appends the event's call/dispatch ids (the $D51B changes
// the main.gd selftest reads off the VM trace).
func (g *Game) harvestChain() {
	if g.vm == nil {
		return
	}
	for _, line := range g.vm.Trace {
		id, ok := chainID(line)
		if ok {
			g.chain = append(g.chain, id)
		}
	}
}

// chainID extracts "0442" from a CALL/DISP trace line that resolved.
func chainID(line string) (string, bool) {
	var id, rest string
	switch {
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, "DISP from=") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "ok=true"):
		rest = line[len("DISP from="):]
		if i := strings.Index(rest, "to="); i >= 0 {
			id = rest[i+3:]
		}
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, "CALL addr=") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "ok=true"):
		rest = line[len("CALL addr="):]
		if i := strings.Index(rest, "id="); i >= 0 {
			id = rest[i+3:]
		}
	default:
		return "", false
	}
	if j := strings.IndexByte(id, ' '); j >= 0 {
		id = id[:j]
	}
	return id, true
}

// nextQueuedEvent drains the object queue (main.gd _next_queued_event,
// C0:B013 -> C0:B847): call words (high byte < 0x0C) start their event
// once the VM is idle; the music word plays its track; other words
// (objOps, sounds) are not modeled and are dropped. -1 = nothing to run.
func (g *Game) nextQueuedEvent() int {
	for len(g.queue) > 0 {
		w := g.queue[0]
		g.queue = g.queue[1:]
		if w>>8 < 0x0C {
			return w
		}
		if w>>8 == 0x1D {
			// C0:C5C4: the music word, track xx (no-op on the current one)
			g.playTrack(w & 0xFF)
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// playTrack switches the track unless it already plays (map_view
// play_track).
func (g *Game) playTrack(track int) {
	if track == g.Track {
		return
	}
	g.Track = track
}

// Enqueue appends queue words from outside the field (the static
// installer fallback path appends through enqueueAll; this is the same
// shape map_view's runner-enqueue append keeps).
func (g *Game) enqueueAll(words []int) {
	g.queue = append(g.queue, words...)
}

// EventID is the last started event's id ("0000" before any — the
// capture rows' ev column shape).
func (g *Game) EventID() string {
	if g.eventID == "" {
		return "0000"
	}
	return g.eventID
}

// EventsRun returns the root event ids started so far.
func (g *Game) EventsRun() []string {
	return append([]string(nil), g.eventsRun...)
}

// EventChain returns every $D51B change so far (VM call/dispatch ids and
// queue-drained ids, in order).
func (g *Game) EventChain() []string {
	return append([]string(nil), g.chain...)
}

// MapJumps returns the op-11 indices taken so far.
func (g *Game) MapJumps() []int {
	return append([]int(nil), g.jumpsRun...)
}

// MapMoves returns the op-10 indices taken so far.
func (g *Game) MapMoves() []int {
	return append([]int(nil), g.movesRun...)
}
```

`internal/game/flow/keys.go`:

```go
package flow

// Key is one key the flow consumes — the smallest set main.gd's
// _unhandled_input and the three screens read. The shell translates its
// own key map onto these; the flow never sees keycodes.
type Key int

const (
	KeyNone Key = iota
	KeyUp
	KeyDown
	KeyLeft
	KeyRight
	KeyConfirm // Enter/Space: advance dialogue, confirm screens, talk
	KeyBack    // Esc: closes the field menus; finishes naming
	KeyMenu    // M: toggles the field menus (map mode's prototype binding)
	KeyDelete  // Backspace: naming deletes the last kana
	KeyMode    // Tab: naming toggles hiragana/katakana

	keyCount
)

// KeyEvent is one key event. Pressed events drive the screens (the
// reference reacts to presses only); both presses and releases update the
// held state the field walk reads.
type KeyEvent struct {
	Key     Key
	Pressed bool
}

// Joypad byte $02 the party step reads (C0:8052's check order right,
// left, down, up; Y run = 0x40 is the shell's Shift and stays there —
// no flow screen or pin consumes it).
const (
	padRight = 0x01
	padLeft  = 0x02
	padDown  = 0x04
	padUp    = 0x08
)

// padOf converts the held keys to the joypad byte (map_view.gd _pad's
// arrow half).
func (g *Game) padOf() int {
	p := 0
	if g.held[KeyRight] {
		p |= padRight
	}
	if g.held[KeyLeft] {
		p |= padLeft
	}
	if g.held[KeyDown] {
		p |= padDown
	}
	if g.held[KeyUp] {
		p |= padUp
	}
	return p
}

// Input injects one key event (main.gd _unhandled_input's routing):
// releases only update the held state; presses route to the screen that
// owns the keyboard — title, select, naming, the open field menus, then
// the field. The battle owns the keyboard while one is up.
func (g *Game) Input(ev KeyEvent) {
	if ev.Key <= KeyNone || ev.Key >= keyCount {
		return
	}
	g.held[ev.Key] = ev.Pressed
	if !ev.Pressed {
		return
	}
	if g.BattleUp {
		return // the battle scene owns the keyboard (main.gd's guard)
	}
	switch g.Screen {
	case ScreenTitle:
		g.titleInput(ev.Key)
	case ScreenSelect:
		g.selectInput(ev.Key)
	case ScreenNaming:
		g.namingInput(ev.Key)
	default:
		if g.Menus.IsOpen() {
			g.menusInput(ev.Key)
			return
		}
		g.fieldInput(ev.Key)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/flow/maps0016_test.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"testing"
)

// The 0016 inn pins: the two placed-tile behaviors the translation
// wiring's live probes flagged on this map. The walk data and the party
// gate on 0016/00E2 are pinned tile-by-tile in the field package's
// TestPartyGateSweep0016And00E2; these two hold the flow wiring.
//
//   - the door: the exit tile (31,53) sits in the low buffer's bit-3
//     block (the prop region's one flag-09 entry), so the step onto it is
//     gate-blocked — and the blocked step still fires the exit: walking
//     the porch south row then north up column 31 pushes the door and the
//     party lands on the record's target, map 0015 (45,37).
//   - the counter: the shop NPC pair shares event 0120, the visible
//     shopkeeper behind the counter at (29,38) and an invisible proxy
//     (graphic 255) standing on the counter tile (29,40) itself. Facing
//     up from the rug (29,41) talks to the proxy — the talk reaches the
//     NPC on a tile the walk gate blocks.
func TestMap0016ExitAndCounterTalk(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	if err := g.EnterField("0016", 15, 55); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	hold := func(k Key, until func() bool, cap int) {
		t.Helper()
		for i := 0; i < cap; i++ {
			g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: k, Pressed: true})
			g.Tick()
			g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: k, Pressed: false})
			g.Tick()
			if until() {
				return
			}
		}
	}
	east := func() bool { x, _ := g.LeaderTile(); return x == 31 }
	northRow := func() bool { _, y := g.LeaderTile(); return y == 54 }
	left := func() bool { _, y := g.LeaderTile(); return y != 54 }

	hold(KeyRight, east, 400)
	if x, y := g.LeaderTile(); x != 31 || y != 55 {
		t.Fatalf("porch walk ended (%d,%d), want (31,55)", x, y)
	}
	hold(KeyUp, northRow, 100)
	hold(KeyUp, left, 200)
	if id := g.MapID; id != "0015" {
		t.Fatalf("door push: map %s, want the exit's 0015", id)
	}
	if x, y := g.LeaderTile(); x != 45 || y != 37 {
		t.Fatalf("door landing (%d,%d), want the exit record's (45,37)", x, y)
	}

	if err := g.EnterField("0016", 29, 41); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	tap(g, KeyUp, 1) // face the counter
	press(g, KeyConfirm)
	if !g.Dialogue.Open || g.EventID() != "0120" {
		t.Fatalf("counter talk: dialogue %v event %s, want 0120 open",
			g.Dialogue.Open, g.EventID())
	}
	if got := g.Dialogue.Page; len(g.Dialogue.Segments) < 1 || got == "" {
		t.Fatalf("counter talk: empty page %q", got)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/flow/menus.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"sort"

	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

// MenusState is the field menus' logic half (field_menus.gd): two tabs —
// 狀態 (the party, one page per member) and 道具 (the carried items with
// counts). Arrows move the active tab's list, Left/Right switch tabs,
// Enter/Space confirm the highlighted row, Esc closes. That Enter and
// Space both confirm is field_menus.gd's deliberate deviation from the
// engine (documented there); the flow keeps the documented stance.
type MenusState struct {
	open      bool
	tab       int // 0 = 狀態, 1 = 道具
	allyIndex int
	itemIndex int

	allies []MenuAlly
	items  []MenuItem
}

// Tabs are the tab captions in order.
var MenuTabs = [2]string{"狀態", "道具"}

// MenuAlly is one 狀態 row: the party member's static name — the leader's
// row carries the protagonist's own name when one was entered (engine:
// op 2F resolves the leader's member record to the $7E:F300 buffer).
type MenuAlly struct {
	ID   int
	Name string
	HP   int
	LP   int
}

// MenuItem is one 道具 row: the carried item with its count, sorted by
// item id so the list is stable (field_menus.gd _inventory_rows).
type MenuItem struct {
	ID    int
	Name  string
	Count int
}

func (m *MenusState) IsOpen() bool { return m.open }

func (m *MenusState) Close() { m.open = false }

// Tab reports the active tab (0 狀態, 1 道具).
func (m *MenusState) Tab() int { return m.tab }

// AllyIndex is the highlighted 狀態 row; Allies the rows.
func (m *MenusState) AllyIndex() int     { return m.allyIndex }
func (m *MenusState) Allies() []MenuAlly { return m.allies }

// ItemIndex is the highlighted 道具 row; Items the rows.
func (m *MenusState) ItemIndex() int    { return m.itemIndex }
func (m *MenusState) Items() []MenuItem { return m.items }

// OpenMenus opens the runtime view (field_menus.gd open(allies, items,
// state)): the current party on the 狀態 tab (with current HP/LP) and
// the current inventory with counts on the 道具 tab. Names come from the
// static exports.
func (m *MenusState) OpenMenus(a *Assets, gs *state.GameState) {
	m.open = true
	m.tab = 0
	m.allyIndex = 0
	m.itemIndex = 0
	m.allies = partyRows(a, gs)
	m.items = inventoryRows(a, gs)
}

// partyRows is field_menus.gd _party_rows: only the current party, the
// leader renamed to the entered protagonist name; an empty party falls
// back to the full roster.
func partyRows(a *Assets, gs *state.GameState) []MenuAlly {
	ids := gs.Party()
	if len(ids) == 0 {
		for id := range a.Allies {
			ids = append(ids, id)
		}
		sort.Ints(ids)
	}
	rows := make([]MenuAlly, 0, len(ids))
	for i, id := range ids {
		name := a.AllyName(id)
		if i == 0 && gs.ProtagonistName != "" {
			name = gs.ProtagonistName
		}
		rows = append(rows, MenuAlly{ID: id, Name: name, HP: gs.HP[id], LP: gs.LP[id]})
	}
	return rows
}

// inventoryRows is field_menus.gd _inventory_rows: the carried items
// with counts, sorted by item id.
func inventoryRows(a *Assets, gs *state.GameState) []MenuItem {
	ids := make([]int, 0, len(gs.Inventory))
	for id, count := range gs.Inventory {
		if count > 0 {
			ids = append(ids, id)
		}
	}
	sort.Ints(ids)
	rows := make([]MenuItem, 0, len(ids))
	for _, id := range ids {
		name := a.ItemName(id)
		if name == "" {
			name = "？"
		}
		rows = append(rows, MenuItem{ID: id, Name: name, Count: gs.Inventory[id]})
	}
	return rows
}

// menusInput is field_menus.gd handle_key, routed while the menus are
// open (main.gd: the menus own arrows/confirm/Esc while open).
func (g *Game) menusInput(k Key) {
	m := &g.Menus
	switch k {
	case KeyUp:
		m.moveSelection(-1)
	case KeyDown:
		m.moveSelection(1)
	case KeyLeft:
		m.switchTab(-1)
	case KeyRight:
		m.switchTab(1)
	case KeyConfirm:
		// the reference's confirm re-shows the highlighted row (a draw
		// act); the flow keeps the selection, so this is a no-op on state
	case KeyBack:
		m.Close()
	}
}

func (m *MenusState) moveSelection(delta int) {
	if m.tab == 0 {
		if len(m.allies) == 0 {
			return
		}
		m.allyIndex = clamp(m.allyIndex+delta, 0, len(m.allies)-1)
		return
	}
	if len(m.items) == 0 {
		return
	}
	m.itemIndex = clamp(m.itemIndex+delta, 0, len(m.items)-1)
}

func (m *MenusState) switchTab(delta int) {
	m.tab = clamp(m.tab+delta, 0, len(MenuTabs)-1)
}

// Save is the prototype's F5 path (main.gd F5 branch): the persistent
// state saves at the player's tile in field mode, with the last started
// event id (main.gd keeps _event_id across events).
func (g *Game) Save() error {
	x, y := g.LeaderTile()
	return state.SaveGame(g.SavePath, g.State, g.eventID, g.MapID, x, y)
}

```

`internal/game/flow/names_test.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// TestNameInsertResolvesTables: startEvent wires the vm's NameResolver
// (event_vm.gd loaded items.json/allies.json itself; the unwired vm
// renders the 〔名字〕 placeholder on every name-insert op). The pins run
// real events through the flow's own playback and hold them to the table
// names, both read from the same exports the menus read:
//
//   - 09AB (the ブラックダイア handout): `41 00 d6 01` sets EF00[0]=D6,
//     `42 00` gives the item, `3a 00` names it (engine C0:32EC) —
//     exports/data/items.json id D6.
//   - 0B1B (the ending crawl): `39 00` names party slot 0 (C0:31F2) —
//     exports/data/allies.json id 00 on the opening party.
func TestNameInsertResolvesTables(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)

	var itemPage string
	for _, p := range eventPages(g, 0x09AB) {
		if strings.Contains(p, "手に入れた") {
			itemPage = p
			break
		}
	}
	if itemPage == "" {
		t.Fatal("09AB rendered no 手に入れた page")
	}
	if want := "ブラックダイアを\n手に入れた！"; itemPage != want {
		t.Fatalf("09AB item page %q, want the items-table name (%q)", itemPage, want)
	}

	var allyPage string
	for _, p := range eventPages(g, 0x0B1B) {
		if strings.Contains(p, "達") {
			allyPage = p
			break
		}
	}
	if allyPage == "" {
		t.Fatal("0B1B rendered no 達 page")
	}
	if strings.Contains(allyPage, "〔名字〕") {
		t.Fatalf("0B1B page %q still holds the placeholder", allyPage)
	}
	if want := "ユリアン達"; !strings.Contains(allyPage, want) {
		t.Fatalf("0B1B page %q, want the allies-table name (%q)", allyPage, want)
	}
}

// eventPages drives one event through the flow's playback (startEvent +
// the advance path) and returns the pages it rendered.
func eventPages(g *Game, id int) []string {
	var pages []string
	g.startEvent(id)
	for i := 0; i < 60 && g.inEvent; i++ {
		if len(g.Dialogue.Choices) > 0 {
			g.Choose(0)
			continue
		}
		if g.Dialogue.Open && strings.TrimSpace(g.Dialogue.Page) != "" {
			pages = append(pages, g.Dialogue.Page)
		}
		g.advanceDialogue()
	}
	return pages
}
```

`internal/game/flow/objects.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"saga3/internal/game/field"
)

// ObjectSnap is one live field object's draw snapshot (map_view's
// _runner.objects as the shell draws them): the live pixel position and
// facing, the figure the object shows, and the battle-dispatch state.
// The field internals stay behind the snapshot — the shell reads these
// values and draws, never the raw Object.
type ObjectSnap struct {
	Slot    int  // the engine slot (0 = the party leader)
	Leader  bool // slot 0 (the shell resolves its figure through the protagonist pick)
	X, Y    int  // live pixel position ($D9AA/$D9AC)
	Dir     int  // facing: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4+ pose groups
	Graphic int  // $D9D3: the figure the object shows (slot 0 records none)
	EventID int  // $D9D2: 0x18xx/0x19xx encounters, 0x2000 the inert class
	Inert   bool // battle-dispatched: the slot sits at 0x2000, movement halted
	Op      byte // the script opcode (op 27's pose frame reads it)
	Frame   int  // the op-27 pose frame ($D9A4)
	Tag     int  // $D9D9: the map entry index; 0x80 marks an event actor
}

// FieldObjects snapshots the live object table (map_view's _runner.objects):
// the leader on slot 0 and the placed characters, in slot order. Nil
// before a map loads. Snapshots are fresh values — the caller cannot
// reach the field through one.
func (g *Game) FieldObjects() []ObjectSnap {
	if g.field == nil {
		return nil
	}
	slots := make([]int, 0, len(g.field.f.Objects))
	for s := range g.field.f.Objects {
		slots = append(slots, s)
	}
	sortInts(slots)
	out := make([]ObjectSnap, 0, len(slots))
	for _, s := range slots {
		o := g.field.f.Objects[s]
		out = append(out, ObjectSnap{
			Slot:    s,
			Leader:  s == 0,
			X:       o.X,
			Y:       o.Y,
			Dir:     o.Dir,
			Graphic: o.Graphic,
			EventID: o.EventID,
			Inert:   field.IsInert(o.EventID),
			Op:      o.Op,
			Frame:   o.Frame,
			Tag:     o.Tag,
		})
	}
	return out
}

```

`internal/game/flow/objects_test.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/field"
)

// The live object snapshot (map_view's _place_npc draw source): the
// placed monster reports its live tile as it roams, and the battle
// dispatch leaves it inert — rewritten to 0x2000, parked at its last
// tile for the rest of the load (docs/field-monsters.md).
func TestFieldObjectsLiveAndInert(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	// 0049's record 0 stands at (24,50), event 1801, graphic 75 (the
	// map.json record the battle handoff pin uses). The leader boots ten
	// tiles below, out of the monster's reach.
	if err := g.EnterField("0049", 24, 60); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	find := func(slot int) (ObjectSnap, bool) {
		for _, ob := range g.FieldObjects() {
			if ob.Slot == slot {
				return ob, true
			}
		}
		return ObjectSnap{}, false
	}
	ob, ok := find(0x40)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("no snapshot for slot 0x40: %+v", g.FieldObjects())
	}
	if ob.Leader || ob.X != 24*8 || ob.Y != 50*8 || ob.Dir != 1 ||
		ob.Graphic != 75 || ob.EventID != 0x1801 || ob.Inert {
		t.Fatalf("boot snapshot wrong: %+v", ob)
	}
	// the leader slot leads, at its spawn tile
	ld, ok := find(0)
	if !ok || !ld.Leader || ld.X != 24*8 || ld.Y != 60*8 {
		t.Fatalf("leader snapshot wrong: %+v (found %v)", ld, ok)
	}
	// the monster roams: the snapshot follows the live position
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		g.Tick()
	}
	ob, _ = find(0x40)
	if ob.X == 24*8 && ob.Y == 50*8 {
		t.Fatalf("the monster never moved in 40 passes: %+v", ob)
	}

	// the dispatch: talk to the monster on its record tile (a fresh load,
	// the monster back at spawn before its first pass)
	if err := g.EnterField("0049", 24, 51); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 20 && !g.BattleUp; i++ {
		g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: KeyUp, Pressed: true})
		g.Tick()
		g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: KeyUp, Pressed: false})
		g.Tick()
	}
	if !g.BattleUp {
		t.Fatal("the bump must start the battle")
	}
	inertX, inertY := -1, -1
	inert := 0
	for _, s := range g.FieldObjects() {
		if !s.Inert {
			continue
		}
		inert++
		if s.EventID != field.InertEventID {
			t.Fatalf("inert snapshot event id %#X, want 0x2000", s.EventID)
		}
		inertX, inertY = s.X, s.Y
	}
	if inert != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d inert snapshots, want the one dispatched slot", inert)
	}
	// victory returns to the field; the defeated slot never moves again
	e := g.Battle()
	for _, en := range e.Enemies {
		en.Alive = false
	}
	if !e.CheckEnd() || !e.Won {
		t.Fatalf("CheckEnd won=%v over=%v, want a settled victory", e.Won, e.Over)
	}
	g.FinishBattle()
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		g.Tick()
	}
	for _, s := range g.FieldObjects() {
		if s.Inert && (s.X != inertX || s.Y != inertY) {
			t.Fatalf("the defeated slot moved to %d,%d after the dispatch, want parked at %d,%d",
				s.X, s.Y, inertX, inertY)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/game/flow/routes_test.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

// The protagonist-route pins from main.gd's --selftest (provenance
// there): event 0800 points EF00 word 0 at $F000 (the leader record =
// the select pick) and chkMem-compares the byte there; live
// tools/emulator/protag_route.lua: row 3 ハリード `CHK a=04 b=04
// ptr=F000` -> `id=0847`; row 0 ユリアン falls through to `id=0846`. The
// flow pins the same five route branches through the real machine: after
// the opening idles, the chain's second entry (after the shared 0BF1
// call) is the route word, and each route lands on its own map.

// routeChains are the full $D51B trails the flow produced per row; the
// row-0 row is main.gd's chain_live verbatim ("every $D51B change after
// 0800, calls and tail dispatches both write it"). The others follow the
// same shape for their own branch events; the route word per row is the
// selftest's routes dict {0: 0846, 3: 0847, 2: 0844, 6: 0840, 7: 0840}.
var routeChains = map[int][]string{
	0: {"0BF1", "0846", "0848", "0849", "084A", "084C", "0B4B", "0B49"},
	2: {"0BF1", "0844", "0848", "0849", "0845", "0852", "0858", "085A", "0B39", "0B3A", "0B3F"},
	3: {"0BF1", "0847", "084A", "084C", "0B4B", "0B49"},
	6: {"0BF1", "0840", "0841"},
	7: {"0BF1", "0840", "0841"},
}

func TestProtagonistRoutes(t *testing.T) {
	for _, row := range []int{0, 2, 3, 6, 7} {
		g, gs := newGame(t)
		pickRow(g, row, 300)
		if gs.ProtagonistRow != row {
			t.Fatalf("row %d: protagonist_row %d", row, gs.ProtagonistRow)
		}
		got := g.EventChain()
		want := routeChains[row]
		if len(got) < 2 || got[1] != want[1] {
			t.Fatalf("row %d route dispatch %v, want the branch at index 1 = %s (main.gd protag_route.lua)",
				row, got, want[1])
		}
		if len(got) != len(want) {
			t.Fatalf("row %d chain %v, want %v", row, got, want)
		}
		for i := range want {
			if got[i] != want[i] {
				t.Fatalf("row %d chain[%d] = %s, want %s", row, i, got[i], want[i])
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestRow0OpeningTrail is the row-0 opening's full flow trail (golden:
// main.gd selftest "opening chain" + the cutscene fixture's scene list):
// the chain through 0B49, the jump records 03/05/04 (024B/0249/024A,
// data/jump_table.json), `10 01` through 024A's record 01, and the
// handover on 0250 at (12,58) with 024A's record music 33 playing.
func TestRow0OpeningTrail(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	pickRow(g, 0, 300)
	if got, want := g.EventChain(), routeChains[0]; len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("chain %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	jumps := g.MapJumps()
	if len(jumps) != 3 || jumps[0] != 3 || jumps[1] != 5 || jumps[2] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("map jumps %v, want [3 5 4] (0846's record 03, 0848's 05, the chain's 04)", jumps)
	}
	moves := g.MapMoves()
	if len(moves) != 1 || moves[0] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("map moves %v, want [1] (084C's `10 01`, FC:2375)", moves)
	}
	if g.MapID != "0250" {
		t.Fatalf("handover map %s, want 0250 (vm-semantics §6.6)", g.MapID)
	}
	x, y := g.LeaderTile()
	if x != 12 || y != 58 {
		t.Fatalf("handover tile (%d,%d), want (12,58) (024A's destination record 01)", x, y)
	}
	if g.Track != 33 {
		t.Fatalf("handover track %d, want 33 (the record's music)", g.Track)
	}
	if g.Diag != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the opening ran with diagnostics: %v", g.Diag)
	}
}

// TestSelectAndNamingPins re-hosts the selftest's select/naming block
// (main.gd "select ok"/"naming ok"): row 3 = ally 04 ハリード, the row
// and the name land in the state, and CONTINUE restores them through the
// save round-trip.
func TestSelectAndNamingPins(t *testing.T) {
	a := loadAssets(t)
	g, gs := newGame(t)
	if g.Screen != ScreenTitle || g.TitleRow != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("boot: screen %d row %d, want the title with the cursor on NEW GAME", g.Screen, g.TitleRow)
	}
	press(g, KeyConfirm)
	if g.Screen != ScreenSelect || g.SelectRow != state.DefaultSelectRow {
		t.Fatalf("after NEW GAME: screen %d row %d, want the select screen at the default row",
			g.Screen, g.SelectRow)
	}
	if state.SelectRows[3] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("SELECT_ROWS[3] = %d, want 4 (FE:961B)", state.SelectRows[3])
	}
	tap(g, KeyDown, 3)
	if g.SelectRow != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("cursor row %d after three Downs, want 3", g.SelectRow)
	}
	press(g, KeyConfirm)
	if gs.ProtagonistRow != 3 || g.ProtagAlly != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("pick: row %d ally %02X, want row 3 ally 04 (ハリード)", gs.ProtagonistRow, g.ProtagAlly)
	}
	if g.Screen != ScreenNaming || g.NamingBuffer() != "ハリード" {
		t.Fatalf("naming: screen %d buffer %q, want the naming screen prefilled ハリード",
			g.Screen, g.NamingBuffer())
	}
	press(g, KeyBack) // Esc finishes: the untouched buffer keeps the default
	if gs.ProtagonistName != "ハリード" {
		t.Fatalf("name %q, want ハリード (the default kept)", gs.ProtagonistName)
	}
	if g.Screen != ScreenField {
		t.Fatalf("screen %d after naming, want the field", g.Screen)
	}
	if gs.Clock != [4]byte{} {
		t.Fatalf("play clock %v at the 0800 start, want zeroed (clock_reset)", gs.Clock)
	}
	if g.EventID() != "0800" {
		t.Fatalf("first event %s, want 0800", g.EventID())
	}
	// CONTINUE restores the pick through a save (SaveManager round-trip;
	// the selftest's protagonist_row pin at flow level)
	if err := g.Save(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g2, _ := newGame(t)
	g2.SavePath = g.SavePath // the second boot reads the first boot's save
	press(g2, KeyDown)       // CONTINUE
	press(g2, KeyConfirm)
	if g2.Screen != ScreenField {
		t.Fatalf("CONTINUE screen %d, want the field", g2.Screen)
	}
	// continueGame swapped the loaded state in place (main.gd's
	// _game_state = state)
	if g2.State.ProtagonistRow != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("CONTINUE protagonist_row %d, want the saved 3", g2.State.ProtagonistRow)
	}
	if g2.ProtagAlly != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("CONTINUE ally %02X, want 04", g2.ProtagAlly)
	}
	_ = a
}

// TestContinueWithoutSaveConverges: CONTINUE on a fresh boot (no save
// file) converges on new game — the select screen comes up (main.gd
// _title_confirm's row-1 branch falls through; engine behavior,
// docs/roadmap "continue == new game").
func TestContinueWithoutSaveConverges(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	press(g, KeyDown)
	press(g, KeyConfirm)
	if g.Screen != ScreenSelect {
		t.Fatalf("CONTINUE without a save: screen %d, want the select screen", g.Screen)
	}
}

// The arrival record's facing byte spawns the leader facing it
// (C0:C333's flag bits 0-1): 0049's move record 0 lands on 0048 (47,23)
// facing left, while the exit walk onto the same tile carries no record
// and the leader faces down.
func TestArrivalFacingFollowsTheRecord(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	if err := g.EnterField("0049", 16, 20); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g.onEdgeEvent(0x1000) // op 10, the map's destination record 00
	if g.MapID != "0048" {
		t.Fatalf("move record 0: map %s, want 0048", g.MapID)
	}
	if x, y := g.LeaderTile(); x != 47 || y != 23 {
		t.Fatalf("landing (%d,%d), want the record's (47,23)", x, y)
	}
	if g.LeaderFacing() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("facing %d after the record's arrival, want 2 (the record's facing)", g.LeaderFacing())
	}

	// the exit row to the same tile names no facing: down
	g2, _ := newGame(t)
	if err := g2.EnterField("0049", 16, 20); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 40 && g2.MapID == "0049"; i++ {
		tap(g2, KeyUp, 1)
	}
	if g2.MapID != "0048" {
		t.Fatalf("exit walk: map %s, want 0048", g2.MapID)
	}
	if g2.LeaderFacing() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("facing %d after the exit arrival, want 1 (down — no record)", g2.LeaderFacing())
	}
}

// CONTINUE onto a save whose position names a map the export lacks
// boots the field blank with one diagnostic (the HasMap guard), never a
// half-switched map (main.gd's has_map check on the saved position).
func TestContinueUnexportedSavedMapStaysBlank(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	if err := g.Save(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(g.SavePath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var doc map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	doc["position"].(map[string]any)["map"] = "ZZZZ"
	b, err = json.Marshal(doc)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(g.SavePath, b, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g2, _ := newGame(t)
	g2.SavePath = g.SavePath
	press(g2, KeyDown) // CONTINUE
	press(g2, KeyConfirm)
	if g2.Screen != ScreenField {
		t.Fatalf("CONTINUE screen %d, want the field", g2.Screen)
	}
	if g2.MapID != "" || g2.field != nil {
		t.Fatalf("booted map %q (field %v) from an unexported save position, want the blank field",
			g2.MapID, g2.field != nil)
	}
	if len(g2.Diag) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("diag %v, want none (the HasMap guard rejects the map before any load)", g2.Diag)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/flow/screens.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

// ---- title screen (main.gd _title_input/_title_confirm) ---------------------

func (g *Game) titleInput(k Key) {
	switch k {
	case KeyUp:
		if g.TitleRow > 0 {
			g.TitleRow--
		}
	case KeyDown:
		if g.TitleRow < len(TitleRows)-1 {
			g.TitleRow++
		}
	case KeyConfirm:
		g.titleConfirm()
	}
}

// titleConfirm ends the title (main.gd _title_confirm): CONTINUE loads
// the save when one exists — the field unlocks and the party lands on
// the saved position; without a save it converges on new game (engine
// behavior, docs/roadmap "continue == new game"). NEW GAME resets the
// state and shows the character select; the field stays locked until a
// row is picked.
func (g *Game) titleConfirm() {
	row := g.TitleRow
	if row == 1 {
		if g.continueGame() {
			return
		}
	}
	// new game (row 0, or CONTINUE without a save)
	if err := g.State.SetupNewGame(g.a.Allies); err != nil {
		g.diag("setup new game: %v", err)
		return
	}
	g.Screen = ScreenSelect
	g.SelectRow = state.DefaultSelectRow
}

// continueGame is CONTINUE with a save (main.gd's row-1 branch): the
// state swaps in, the protagonist figure follows the saved row, and the
// party lands on the saved position when the map is exported. false =
// no save (the caller converges on new game).
func (g *Game) continueGame() bool {
	loaded, err := state.LoadGame(g.SavePath)
	if err != nil {
		return false // no save (or unreadable) converges on new game
	}
	g.State = loaded
	g.ProtagAlly = state.SelectRows[loaded.ProtagonistRow]
	pos, err := state.SavedPosition(g.SavePath)
	if err != nil {
		g.diag("saved position: %v", err)
	} else if pos.Map != "" && g.a.HasMap(pos.Map) {
		g.Arrival = Arrival{Music: arrivalNoRecord, Facing: -1}
		g.switchMap(pos.Map, pos.X, pos.Y)
	}
	// main.gd opens and closes the field menus to initialize them against
	// the loaded state; the flow's Menus hold no cached rows to refresh.
	g.Screen = ScreenField
	return true
}

// ---- select screen (select_screen.gd) ---------------------------------------

func (g *Game) selectInput(k Key) {
	switch k {
	case KeyUp:
		if g.SelectRow > 0 {
			g.SelectRow--
		}
	case KeyDown:
		if g.SelectRow < len(state.SelectRows)-1 {
			g.SelectRow++
		}
	case KeyConfirm:
		g.onSelectPicked(g.SelectRow)
	case KeyBack:
		// nothing to back out to; ignore (select_screen.gd KEY_ESCAPE)
	}
}

// onSelectPicked confirms the row (main.gd _on_select_picked): the row is
// the protagonist (the FE:961B table through state.SelectRows), the walk
// figure switches to the pick, and name entry follows.
func (g *Game) onSelectPicked(row int) {
	g.State.ProtagonistRow = row
	g.ProtagAlly = state.SelectRows[row]
	g.naming = newNaming(state.DefaultNames[row])
	g.Screen = ScreenNaming
}

// ---- naming screen (naming_screen.gd) ----------------------------------------

// namingScreen is the name-entry screen's logic: the kana grid mirrors
// the engine's window, the buffer starts at the engine default for the
// picked protagonist, and the finished string lands in the state.
type namingScreen struct {
	katakana    bool
	defaultName string
	buffer      string
	row, col    int
	onEnd       bool
}

// MaxNameLen is the engine's insert guard $3D89 == 8 (C5:8E2E).
const MaxNameLen = 8

// hiraGrid is the engine window's grid (naming_screen.gd HIRA_GRID,
// docs/naming.md "Grid"): each row a 5-char gojuon block plus the
// dakuten/small block captured live; "" cells are gaps the cursor passes
// through; the katakana grid is the engine's toggle counterpart.
var hiraGrid = [][]string{
	{"あ", "い", "う", "え", "お", "", "わ", "", "ん"},
	{"か", "き", "く", "け", "こ", "ゃ", "ゅ", "ょ", "っ"},
	{"さ", "し", "す", "せ", "そ", "が", "ぎ", "ぐ", "げ", "ご"},
	{"た", "ち", "つ", "て", "と", "ざ", "じ", "ず", "ぜ", "ぞ"},
	{"な", "に", "ぬ", "ね", "の", "だ", "ぢ", "づ", "で", "ど"},
	{"は", "ひ", "ふ", "へ", "ほ", "ば", "び", "ぶ", "べ", "ぱ"},
	{"ま", "み", "む", "め", "も", "ー"},
	{"や", "ゆ", "よ"},
	{"ら", "り", "る", "れ", "ろ"},
}

var kataGrid = [][]string{
	{"ア", "イ", "ウ", "エ", "オ", "", "ワ", "", "ン"},
	{"カ", "キ", "ク", "ケ", "コ", "ァ", "ゥ", "ェ", "ッ"},
	{"サ", "シ", "ス", "セ", "ソ", "ガ", "ギ", "グ", "ゲ", "ゴ"},
	{"タ", "チ", "ツ", "テ", "ト", "ザ", "ジ", "ズ", "ゼ", "ゾ"},
	{"ナ", "ニ", "ヌ", "ネ", "ノ", "ダ", "ヂ", "ヅ", "デ", "ド"},
	{"ハ", "ヒ", "フ", "ヘ", "ホ", "バ", "ビ", "ブ", "ベ", "ポ"},
	{"マ", "ミ", "ム", "メ", "モ", "ー"},
	{"ヤ", "ユ", "ヨ"},
	{"ラ", "リ", "ル", "レ", "ロ"},
}

func newNaming(defaultName string) namingScreen {
	return namingScreen{defaultName: defaultName, buffer: defaultName}
}

func (n *namingScreen) grid() [][]string {
	if n.katakana {
		return kataGrid
	}
	return hiraGrid
}

// NamingBuffer is the name buffer so far (the shell draws it over the
// grid).
func (g *Game) NamingBuffer() string { return g.naming.buffer }

// NamingKatakana reports the grid mode.
func (g *Game) NamingKatakana() bool { return g.naming.katakana }

// NamingCursor is the cursor position: row, col, and whether it sits on
// the 終了 cell.
func (g *Game) NamingCursor() (row, col int, onEnd bool) {
	return g.naming.row, g.naming.col, g.naming.onEnd
}

func (g *Game) namingInput(k Key) {
	n := &g.naming
	switch k {
	case KeyUp:
		n.move(-1, 0)
	case KeyDown:
		n.move(1, 0)
	case KeyLeft:
		n.move(0, -1)
	case KeyRight:
		n.move(0, 1)
	case KeyConfirm:
		if n.onEnd {
			g.onNamingFinished(n.finish()) // Enter on 終了 finishes, like Esc
			return
		}
		n.insert()
	case KeyDelete:
		n.deleteLast()
	case KeyMode:
		n.katakana = !n.katakana
		width := len(n.grid()[n.row])
		if n.col >= width {
			n.col = width - 1
		}
	case KeyBack:
		g.onNamingFinished(n.finish())
	default:
	}
}

// move is naming_screen.gd _move: down from the last row lands on 終了,
// up from 終了 lands on the last row, and the walk skips empty cells.
func (n *namingScreen) move(dr, dc int) {
	grid := n.grid()
	rows := len(grid)
	if n.onEnd {
		if dr < 0 {
			n.onEnd = false
			n.row = rows - 1
			if n.col >= len(grid[n.row]) {
				n.col = len(grid[n.row]) - 1
			}
		}
		return
	}
	if dr > 0 && n.row == rows-1 {
		n.onEnd = true
		return
	}
	n.row = clamp(n.row+dr, 0, rows-1)
	width := len(grid[n.row])
	n.col = clamp(n.col+dc, 0, width-1)
	// land only on a non-empty cell (the engine's skip-empty walk)
	for grid[n.row][n.col] == "" {
		if n.col+1 < width {
			n.col++
		} else if n.col > 0 {
			n.col--
		} else {
			break
		}
	}
}

func (n *namingScreen) insert() {
	kana := n.grid()[n.row][n.col]
	if kana == "" || len([]rune(n.buffer)) >= MaxNameLen {
		return
	}
	n.buffer += kana
}

func (n *namingScreen) deleteLast() {
	r := []rune(n.buffer)
	if len(r) > 0 {
		n.buffer = string(r[:len(r)-1])
	}
}

// finish resolves the buffer: an all-blank buffer keeps the default (the
// engine's buffer holds the default name until edited).
func (n *namingScreen) finish() string {
	if n.buffer == "" {
		return n.defaultName
	}
	return n.buffer
}

func clamp(v, lo, hi int) int {
	if v < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if v > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return v
}

// onNamingFinished is the naming screen's end (main.gd
// _on_naming_finished): the name lands in the state, the map blanks, the
// play clock resets (the engine resets it when the new game starts — the
// title and the stat screens never count), and the opening event 0800
// runs: it picks the opening route from the leader record.
func (g *Game) onNamingFinished(name string) {
	g.State.ProtagonistName = name
	g.naming = namingScreen{}
	g.Screen = ScreenField
	g.MapID = "" // map_scene().blank()
	g.field = nil
	g.State.ClockReset()
	g.startEvent(0x0800)
}
```

```go
package flow

import (
	"testing"

// The naming screen's logic pins, from naming_screen.gd (docs/naming.md):
// the grid walk skips empty cells, the buffer holds the engine default
// until edited, insert guards at 8 kana, Backspace deletes, Tab toggles
// kana mode, and both 終了 and Esc finish (the engine's START:終了).
func TestNamingScreenKeys(t *testing.T) {
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	press(g, KeyConfirm) // title NEW GAME -> select
	press(g, KeyConfirm) // pick row 0 -> naming prefilled ユリアン
	if got := g.NamingBuffer(); got != "ユリアン" {
		t.Fatalf("buffer %q, want the row-0 default ユリアン", got)
	}
	// Right across the gap: row 0 is ["あ","い","う","え","お","","わ","","ん"]
	tap(g, KeyRight, 5)
	r, c, onEnd := g.NamingCursor()
	if onEnd || r != 0 || c != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("cursor (%d,%d) end=%v after five Rights, want (0,6) — the walk skips the empty cell", r, c, onEnd)
	}
	press(g, KeyConfirm) // insert わ
	if got := g.NamingBuffer(); got != "ユリアンわ" {
		t.Fatalf("buffer %q after inserting わ, want ユリアンわ", got)
	}
	press(g, KeyDelete)
	if got := g.NamingBuffer(); got != "ユリアン" {
		t.Fatalf("buffer %q after Backspace, want ユリアン", got)
	}
	// Down from a middle row walks to the next row, never straight to 終了
	tap(g, KeyDown, 1)
	r, c, onEnd = g.NamingCursor()
	if onEnd || r != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("cursor (%d,%d) end=%v after one Down from row 0, want row 1 (終了 only from the last row)", r, c, onEnd)
	}
	press(g, KeyConfirm) // Enter on a kana cell inserts, does not finish
	if got := g.NamingBuffer(); got != "ユリアンゅ" {
		t.Fatalf("buffer %q after Enter on row 1, want the ゅ inserted", got)
	}
	press(g, KeyDelete) // clear the insert for the 終了 walk below
	if got := g.NamingBuffer(); got != "ユリアン" {
		t.Fatalf("buffer %q after Backspace, want ユリアン", got)
	}
	// Down through all rows lands on 終了; Enter there finishes
	tap(g, KeyDown, 20)
	r, _, onEnd = g.NamingCursor()
	if !onEnd {
		t.Fatalf("cursor row %d end=%v after 20 Downs, want the 終了 cell", r, onEnd)
	}
	press(g, KeyUp)
	_, _, onEnd = g.NamingCursor()
	if onEnd {
		t.Fatal("Up from 終了 must leave it")
	}
	tap(g, KeyDown, 20)
	// Tab toggles the katakana grid; the buffer is untouched
	press(g, KeyMode)
	if !g.NamingKatakana() {
		t.Fatal("Tab must toggle to katakana")
	}
	press(g, KeyMode)
	if g.NamingKatakana() {
		t.Fatal("Tab must toggle back")
	}
}

// The insert guard holds at 8 kana (engine $3D89 == 8, C5:8E2E): the
// buffer starts at the four-kana default, four inserts fill it, and the

func TestNamingInsertGuard(t *testing.T) {
```

`internal/game/flow/scripts.go`:

```go
package flow

// The static op-09 enqueue walker: godot/action_scripts.gd translated
// (the no-field fallback of game_state.gd install_action). objOp `17 20`
// installs script EF01word on object EF00 (C0:B2D4); the engine then runs
// it per frame and action op `09 hi lo` enqueues the dispatch word
// hi<<8|lo (C0:67AE -> C0:AF91), which the queue drain runs once the VM
// is idle (live: script 010A on object 80, `09 08 49` at F8:EB6D+0x24,
// enqueued 0849 at frame 12909). Order model only: movement and wait
// durations decide the ROM's order across objects, and those handlers
// are not decoded yet.
//
// The live-path counterpart (objects actually running the script) is
// actions.Runner's Enqueued — field.Field has no install path, so the
// flow walks the bank statically instead, which is the exact shape the
// main.gd selftest pins for the opening chain.

// opLength is each handler's position advance (C0:5740 +1, 574C +2,
// 575D +3, 576D +4; table C0:70AA). The static scan agrees with all 19
// lengths measured live (tools/emulator/actscript.lua) and covers every
// opcode in the 359 scripts events install with objOp `17 20` except
// three stray bytes (62 in 0235, CE in 01A5, C0 in 1317).
var opLength = map[byte]int{
	0x00: 2, 0x01: 2, 0x02: 2, 0x03: 2, 0x04: 2, 0x05: 2,
	0x06: 2, 0x07: 2, 0x09: 3, 0x0A: 2, 0x0B: 2, 0x0C: 2, 0x0D: 2, 0x0E: 2,
	0x0F: 2, 0x10: 2, 0x11: 2, 0x12: 2, 0x13: 2, 0x14: 2, 0x15: 2, 0x17: 2,
	0x18: 2, 0x19: 2, 0x1A: 3, 0x1B: 2, 0x1C: 1, 0x1D: 2, 0x1E: 2, 0x1F: 1,
	0x20: 1, 0x21: 3, 0x22: 1, 0x23: 3, 0x24: 1, 0x25: 1, 0x26: 1, 0x27: 1,
	0x28: 1, 0x29: 1, 0x2A: 1, 0x2B: 1, 0x2C: 2, 0x2D: 2, 0x2E: 1, 0x2F: 1,
	0x30: 1, 0x31: 2, 0x32: 1, 0x33: 1, 0x34: 2, 0x35: 2, 0x36: 2, 0x37: 2,
	0x38: 2, 0x39: 2, 0x3A: 1, 0x3B: 2, 0x3C: 2, 0x3D: 2, 0x3E: 1, 0x3F: 2,
	0x41: 3, 0x42: 1, 0x43: 1,
}

const (
	opEvent   = 0x09
	opSwitch  = 0x16
	opLoop    = 0x08
	opRestart = 0xFF
)

// scriptBase reads the F8 bank's script-pointer table ((id & 0xFFF) * 2).
func scriptBase(bank []byte, id int) int {
	i := (id & 0x0FFF) * 2
	return int(bank[i]) | int(bank[i+1])<<8
}

// enqueuedWords walks script id and returns the words its 09 ops
// enqueue, in script order: follows 16 switches; stops at FF (the script
// restarts), 08 (back jump) or an opcode without a known length.
func enqueuedWords(bank []byte, id int) []int {
	var words []int
	base := scriptBase(bank, id)
	pos := 0
	switches := 0
	for step := 0; step < 512; step++ {
		op := bank[(base+pos)&0xFFFF]
		if op == opRestart || op == opLoop {
			break
		}
		if op == opSwitch {
			if switches >= 8 {
				break
			}
			switches++
			base = scriptBase(bank, int(bank[(base+pos+2)&0xFFFF])<<8|int(bank[(base+pos+1)&0xFFFF]))
			pos = 0
			continue
		}
		if op == opEvent {
			words = append(words, int(bank[(base+pos+1)&0xFFFF])<<8|int(bank[(base+pos+2)&0xFFFF]))
		}
		n, ok := opLength[op]
		if !ok {
			break
		}
		pos += n
	}
	return words
}
```

`internal/game/flow/testhelpers_test.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"os"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

var (
	assetsOnce sync.Once
	assets     *Assets
	assetsErr  error
)

// loadAssets loads the exports once per test binary; the pins skip when
// the exports are absent, like the field and battle suites
// (internal/game/field/env_test.go).
func loadAssets(t *testing.T) *Assets {
	t.Helper()
	assetsOnce.Do(func() {
		if _, err := os.Stat("../../../exports/data/events.json"); err != nil {
			assetsErr = err
			return
		}
		assets, assetsErr = LoadAssets("../../../exports/data")
	})
	if assetsErr != nil {
		t.Skipf("exports/data exports not available: %v", assetsErr)
	}
	return assets
}

// newGame is a fresh boot: state seeded, title up (main.gd's map-mode
// _ready shape). The save file lives in the test's own temp dir, so
// save/CONTINUE pairs within one test round-trip and tests stay
// isolated.
func newGame(t *testing.T) (*Game, *state.GameState) {
	t.Helper()
	a := loadAssets(t)
	gs := state.NewGameState()
	if err := gs.SetupNewGame(a.Allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return New(a, gs, t.TempDir()+"/save.json"), gs
}

// press taps one key (press + release).
func press(g *Game, k Key) {
	g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: k, Pressed: true})
	g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: k, Pressed: false})
}

// tap holds one key for `ticks` field frames, mirroring the shell's
// held-key walk.
func tap(g *Game, k Key, loops int) {
	for i := 0; i < loops; i++ {
		g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: k, Pressed: true})
		g.Tick()
		g.Input(KeyEvent{Key: k, Pressed: false})
		g.Tick()
	}
}

// pickRow drives title -> select -> naming -> the opening from a fresh
// boot: confirm row `row` (arrow taps from the default 0), finish naming
// with Esc (the default name), then advance the opening until the flow
// idles (no event for idleTicks ticks). Returns nothing; the caller
// reads the Game.
func pickRow(g *Game, row int, idleTicks int) {
	press(g, KeyConfirm) // title NEW GAME
	for i := 0; i < row; i++ {
		press(g, KeyDown)
	}
	press(g, KeyConfirm) // select the row
	press(g, KeyBack)    // Esc finishes naming with the default
	idle := 0
	for i := 0; i < 8000 && idle < idleTicks; i++ {
		if len(g.Dialogue.Choices) > 0 {
			g.Choose(0) // the capture's A takes the cursor's first row
			continue
		}
		press(g, KeyConfirm)
		g.Tick()
		if !g.inEvent {
			idle++
		} else {
			idle = 0
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/game/flow/translation.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Translation is one language's page table (exports/translations/<lang>.json,
// main.gd _load_translation): event id -> {original page -> translated
// page}. The table is keyed by the started event's "%04X" id and maps the
// whole page text; the VM composes pages (name insertion included) before
// the lookup, so a key must equal the live page with its op-2C pause marks
// removed.
type Translation struct {
	table map[string]map[string]string
}

// LoadTranslation reads <dir>/<lang>.json. lang "" and "ja" are the
// Japanese default and load nothing (nil, nil — pages pass through;
// "ja" is the extracted language itself, so no ja.json exists). A set
// lang whose file is missing or malformed is an error: main.gd warned
// and kept playing Japanese, the port surfaces the failure at boot
// instead of silently dropping the user's language.
func LoadTranslation(dir, lang string) (*Translation, error) {
	if lang == "" || lang == "ja" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	path := filepath.Join(dir, lang+".json")
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load translation %s: %w", lang, err)
	}
	var table map[string]map[string]string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &table); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return &Translation{table: table}, nil
}

// Page returns eventID's translated page (main.gd _translate_page): the
// lookup key is the page without its op-2C pause marks, and a
// translation may carry its own marks. Anything the table lacks — the
// event, the page, a name the table baked differently — falls back to
// the extracted Japanese page, byte for byte.
func (t *Translation) Page(eventID, page string) string {
	if t == nil {
		return page
	}
	perEvent, ok := t.table[eventID]
	if !ok {
		return page
	}
	if zh, ok := perEvent[strings.ReplaceAll(page, pauseMark, "")]; ok {
		return zh
	}
	return page
}
```

`internal/game/flow/translation_test.go`:

```go
package flow

import (
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/state"
	"saga3/internal/game/vm"
)

// The zh-TW wiring pins (main.gd's --lang shape): the table loads beside
// the data dir, pages translate at display time keyed by the started
// event's "%04X" id with the op-2C pause marks stripped, and anything the
// table lacks falls back to the extracted Japanese. Expectations read the
// table itself, so a stale key fails here like it fails
// cmd/checktranslations.
func loadZH(t *testing.T) *Translation {
	t.Helper()
	trans, err := LoadTranslation("../../../exports/translations", "zh-TW")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("zh-TW table not available: %v", err)
	}
	return trans
}

// livePages runs one event in the gameplay shape (main.gd _start_event:
// calls on, fresh state) and returns its pages, pause marks included.
func livePages(t *testing.T, a *Assets, eventID int) []string {
	t.Helper()
	gs := state.NewGameState()
	if err := gs.SetupNewGame(a.Allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v := vm.New(a.Catalog)
	v.State = gs
	v.CallsEnabled = true
	v.LoadEvent(a.Catalog.RawOps(eventID), eventID)
	var out []string
	for guard := 0; guard < 20000; guard++ {
		page := v.NextPage()
		if page == "" && v.IsFinished() {
			break
		}
		if page == "" {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, page)
	}
	return out
}

// TestTranslationPagesFromTable pins the table lookup byte for byte on
// three events whose live pages hit: 0120 (a plain page), 0A07 (the page
// carries the VM-inserted place name 玄城, op 3B), 0035 (multi-page with
// the marks). The zh expectation is the table's own entry, not a copy.
func TestTranslationPagesFromTable(t *testing.T) {
	a := loadAssets(t)
	zh := loadZH(t)
	for _, spec := range []struct {
		id     string
		inPage string // a substring the first hit page carries, for the failure message
	}{
		{"0120", "いらっしゃいませ"},
		{"0A07", "玄城"},
		{"0035", "破壊神"},
	} {
		eventID := hexID(t, spec.id)
		pages := livePages(t, a, eventID)
		hits := 0
		for _, page := range pages {
			got := zh.Page(spec.id, page)
			key := strings.ReplaceAll(page, pauseMark, "")
			want, ok := zh.table[spec.id][key]
			if !ok {
				if got != page {
					t.Fatalf("%s: untranslated page changed: %q", spec.id, got)
				}
				continue
			}
			hits++
			if got != want {
				t.Fatalf("%s: translated page != table entry:\n got %q\nwant %q", spec.id, got, want)
			}
			if got == page {
				t.Fatalf("%s: page %q stayed Japanese", spec.id, head60(page))
			}
			if hits == 1 && !strings.Contains(page, spec.inPage) {
				t.Fatalf("%s: first hit page %q lacks %q — the fixture drifted", spec.id, head60(page), spec.inPage)
			}
		}
		if hits == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: no live page hit the table (fixture drift)", spec.id)
		}
		t.Logf("%s: %d/%d pages translated", spec.id, hits, len(pages))
	}
}

// TestTranslationNameInsertion pins that the 0A07 hit page carries the
// place name the VM inserted at runtime (op 3B via the catalog's place
// table) — the translation keys a page the VM composed, not the export
// text.
func TestTranslationNameInsertion(t *testing.T) {
	a := loadAssets(t)
	zh := loadZH(t)
	pages := livePages(t, a, hexID(t, "0A07"))
	var hit string
	for _, page := range pages {
		if _, ok := zh.table["0A07"][strings.ReplaceAll(page, pauseMark, "")]; ok {
			hit = page
			break
		}
	}
	if hit == "" {
		t.Fatal("0A07: no table hit")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(hit, "玄城") {
		t.Fatalf("0A07 hit page %q lacks the inserted place name 玄城", head60(hit))
	}
	if !a.Catalog.HasEvent(hexID(t, "0A07")) {
		t.Fatal("0A07 left the catalog")
	}
	if got := a.Catalog.PlaceName(0x2B); got != "玄城" {
		t.Fatalf("place 0x2B name %q, want 玄城 (the op 3B operand's table row)", got)
	}
}

// TestTranslationFallbacks pins the Japanese fallbacks: an event absent
// from the table, a page absent from a translated event's table, and the
// nil table (the default language) all pass the extracted Japanese
// through unchanged.
func TestTranslationFallbacks(t *testing.T) {
	a := loadAssets(t)
	zh := loadZH(t)

	// 0C00 sits in the catalog and no table carries it
	if _, ok := zh.table["0C00"]; ok {
		t.Fatal("0C00 gained a table entry — pick another untranslated id")
	}
	for _, page := range livePages(t, a, hexID(t, "0C00")) {
		if got := zh.Page("0C00", page); got != page {
			t.Fatalf("0C00 page changed without a table entry: %q", head60(got))
		}
	}

	// 0685's choice page is not a key of its own translated event
	pages := livePages(t, a, hexID(t, "0685"))
	if len(pages) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("0685 produced no pages")
	}
	first := pages[0]
	if _, ok := zh.table["0685"][strings.ReplaceAll(first, pauseMark, "")]; ok {
		t.Fatal("0685 page 0 gained a key — pick another untranslated page")
	}
	if got := zh.Page("0685", first); got != first {
		t.Fatalf("0685 untranslated page changed: %q", head60(got))
	}

	// the default language: no table, every page passes through
	if trans, err := LoadTranslation("../../../exports/translations", ""); err != nil || trans != nil {
		t.Fatalf("empty lang: (%v, %v), want (nil, nil)", trans, err)
	}
	// "ja" names the extracted corpus itself — same passthrough, no
	// ja.json exists by construction
	if trans, err := LoadTranslation("../../../exports/translations", "ja"); err != nil || trans != nil {
		t.Fatalf("lang ja: (%v, %v), want (nil, nil)", trans, err)
	}
	var nilTrans *Translation
	if got := nilTrans.Page("0120", "いらっしゃいませ。"); got != "いらっしゃいませ。" {
		t.Fatalf("nil table changed the page: %q", got)
	}
}

// TestTranslationFlowTriggerShowsZh walks the field onto map 00E2's
// (27,61) trigger, whose event 0630's first page is a table hit, and
// pins the shown dialogue byte for byte against the table entry — the
// full flow path (tile-entered -> startEvent -> pullPage -> Dialogue).
func TestTranslationFlowTriggerShowsZh(t *testing.T) {
	a := loadAssets(t)
	zh := loadZH(t)
	g, _ := newGame(t)
	g.a.Trans = zh
	if err := g.EnterField("00E2", 27, 60); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 60 && !g.Dialogue.Open; i++ {
		tap(g, KeyDown, 1)
	}
	if !g.Dialogue.Open {
		t.Fatal("the (27,61) trigger never opened dialogue")
	}
	if g.eventID != "0630" {
		t.Fatalf("trigger started event %s, want 0630", g.eventID)
	}
	page := g.Dialogue.Page
	// the shown page is already the translation, so the check runs
	// against the table's value side: the JP key must be the VM's first
	// page for 0630 and the shown page must equal that entry byte for
	// byte
	jp := livePages(t, a, hexID(t, "0630"))[0]
	key := strings.ReplaceAll(jp, pauseMark, "")
	want, ok := zh.table["0630"][key]
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("0630's first page is not a table key: %q", head60(key))
	}
	if page != want {
		t.Fatalf("shown page != table entry:\n got %q\nwant %q", page, want)
	}
	if page == jp {
		t.Fatalf("shown page stayed Japanese: %q", head60(page))
	}
}

// TestTranslationDetectsMutatedTable is the mutation proof: the pins'
// expectations are table-derived, so corrupting the entry must corrupt
// the lookup output — a lookup that ignored the table cannot pass the
// pins above.
func TestTranslationDetectsMutatedTable(t *testing.T) {
	zh := loadZH(t)
	const id = "0120"
	orig := "いらっしゃいませ。"
	want, ok := zh.table[id][orig]
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("%s lost its key %q", id, orig)
	}
	mutated := "〔變異〕"
	zh.table[id][orig] = mutated
	if got := zh.Page(id, orig); got != mutated {
		t.Fatalf("mutated table entry not served: got %q, want %q", got, mutated)
	}
	if mutated == want {
		t.Fatal("mutation equals the table entry")
	}
}

// TestTranslationBadLangFails pins the no-silent-fallback rule: a set
// language with no table fails the load instead of playing Japanese
// (main.gd warned and continued; the port errors at boot).
func TestTranslationBadLangFails(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := LoadTranslation("../../../exports/translations", "ko"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("missing ko table loaded without error")
	}
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if _, err := LoadTranslation(dir, "zh-TW"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("malformed table loaded without error")
	}
}

func hexID(t *testing.T, id string) int {
	t.Helper()
	v, err := strconv.ParseUint(id, 16, 16)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("bad id %q: %v", id, err)
	}
	return int(v)
}

func head60(s string) string {
	r := []rune(s)
	if len(r) > 60 {
		return string(r[:60]) + "..."
	}
	return s
}
```
