`internal/game/gfx/anim_test.go`:

```go
package gfx

import (
	"crypto/md5"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// The gfxcheck digest rule (exports/tests/gfxcheck.gd _vm_state): MD5 over
// the chips lo..hi inclusive — each chip's 8x8 palette-index pixels,
// rows then columns, from the Chr atlas — then CGRAM slots 16..127
// skipping each palette's colour 0 (i % 16 == 0), each slot three bytes
// of 5-bit components (the stored bytes >> 3). gfxcheck digests the
// state BEFORE every tick; the fixtures sample every 20th tick.

func digestState(m *TileMap, lo, hi int) string {
	h := md5.New()
	for c := lo; c <= hi; c++ {
		for row := 0; row < 8; row++ {
			for col := 0; col < 8; col++ {
				h.Write([]byte{m.Chr.GrayAt(c%16*8+col, c/16*8+row).Y})
			}
		}
	}
	for i := 16; i < 128; i++ {
		if i%16 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		c := m.Cgram[i]
		h.Write([]byte{c[0] >> 3, c[1] >> 3, c[2] >> 3})
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
}

// TestDigestSelfTest pins the digest rule itself before any fixture is
// trusted: identical state digests equally, one flipped chip pixel or
// one flipped CGRAM 5-bit digit diverges, colour-0 slots are skipped,
// and Go's MD5 matches the GDScript HashingContext's known vectors.
func TestDigestSelfTest(t *testing.T) {
	if got := fmt.Sprintf("%x", md5.Sum([]byte("abc"))); got != "900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72" {
		t.Fatalf(`md5("abc") = %s, want 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72 (Go MD5 must match HashingContext.HASH_MD5)`, got)
	}
	if got := fmt.Sprintf("%x", md5.Sum(nil)); got != "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e" {
		t.Fatalf(`md5("") = %s, want d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`, got)
	}
	m := miniTileMap()
	other := miniTileMap()
	if digestState(m, 0, 3) != digestState(other, 0, 3) {
		t.Fatal("identical states digest differently")
	}
	other.Chr.SetGray(1, 1, color.Gray{Y: other.Chr.GrayAt(1, 1).Y ^ 1})
	if digestState(m, 0, 3) == digestState(other, 0, 3) {
		t.Fatal("a flipped chip pixel went undetected")
	}
	third := miniTileMap()
	third.Cgram[17][0] ^= 0x08 // one 5-bit digit of slot 17 (not colour 0)
	if digestState(m, 0, 3) == digestState(third, 0, 3) {
		t.Fatal("a flipped CGRAM digit went undetected")
	}
	// colour-0 slots are skipped: flipping one must not move the digest
	fourth := miniTileMap()
	fourth.Cgram[16][0] ^= 0x08
	if digestState(m, 0, 3) != digestState(fourth, 0, 3) {
		t.Fatal("colour-0 slot flipped the digest; slots i%16==0 must be skipped")
	}
}

// TestColourClampBoundaries pins the two component clamps' boundaries:
// A42B's signed clamp reads 80h-FFh as 0 (80h itself included) and caps
// at 1Fh; A14E's byte clamp starts the wrap at E0h.
func TestColourClampBoundaries(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		v, want int
	}{
		{0x1F, 0x1F},
		{0x7F, 0x1F}, // above 1F caps
		{0x80, 0x00}, // 80h itself reads as 0
		{0xFF, 0x00},
	} {
		if got := clampSigned(tc.v); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("clampSigned(%02Xh) = %02Xh, want %02Xh", tc.v, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		v, want int
	}{
		{0x1F, 0x1F},
		{0xDF, 0x1F}, // 20h-DFh reads as 1Fh
		{0xE0, 0x00}, // the wrap starts at E0h
		{0xFF, 0x00},
	} {
		if got := clamp5(tc.v); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("clamp5(%02Xh) = %02Xh, want %02Xh", tc.v, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// miniTileMap builds a small TileMap covering the fixtures' smallest
// digest range (00FD/0272: chips 0..3) and a CGRAM strip.
func miniTileMap() *TileMap {
	m := &TileMap{Width: 1, Height: 1}
	m.Chr = image.NewGray(image.Rect(0, 0, 128, 384))
	for i := 0; i < len(m.Chr.Pix); i++ {
		m.Chr.Pix[i] = uint8(i * 7)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		m.Cgram[i] = [3]uint8{uint8(8 + i), uint8(16), uint8(24)}
	}
	return m
}

// gfxFixtures is one gfx_digests.json row.
type gfxFixtures struct {
	Lo    float64           `json:"lo"`
	Hi    float64           `json:"hi"`
	Ticks map[string]string `json:"ticks"`
	Rng   []string          `json:"rng"`
	Frame []float64         `json:"frame"`
}

// loadGfxFixtures reads the digests (read in place, never copied, per
// docs/migration.md).
func loadGfxFixtures(t *testing.T) map[string]gfxFixtures {
	t.Helper()
	fb, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "tests", "gfx_digests.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read gfx_digests.json: %v", err)
	}
	var fx map[string]gfxFixtures
	if err := json.Unmarshal(fb, &fx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse gfx_digests.json: %v", err)
	}
	return fx
}

// TestGoldenGfxDigests re-hosts exports/tests/gfx_digests.json: the
// animation engine steps each fixture's map from its install state and
// the digests taken before every 20th tick must match the emulator's.
func TestGoldenGfxDigests(t *testing.T) {
	data := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data")
	scripts, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(data, "gfx_scripts.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read gfx_scripts.bin: %v", err)
	}
	palettes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(data, "rom_palettes.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read rom_palettes.bin: %v", err)
	}
	fx := loadGfxFixtures(t)
	for id, spec := range fx {
		t.Run(id, func(t *testing.T) {
			dir := filepath.Join(data, "maps", id)
			m, err := LoadMap(dir, "tiles.bin")
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("LoadMap: %v", err)
			}
			mj, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "map.json"))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read map.json: %v", err)
			}
			var mdata struct {
				GfxAnims []AnimSpec `json:"gfx_anims"`
				PalBank  int        `json:"pal_bank"`
				MapType  int        `json:"map_type"`
			}
			if err := json.Unmarshal(mj, &mdata); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("parse map.json: %v", err)
			}
			g := NewGfxAnim(scripts, palettes, rng.NewField())
			g.BG3On = m.Present[BG3]
			g.Install(mdata.GfxAnims, m, mdata.PalBank)
			if mdata.MapType == 1 {
				g.Darken(6)
			}
			last := -1
			for k := range spec.Ticks {
				if v, err := strconv.Atoi(k); err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("tick key %q: %v", k, err)
				} else if v > last {
					last = v
				}
			}
			lo, hi := int(spec.Lo), int(spec.Hi)
			bad := 0
			first := ""
			for tk := 0; tk <= last; tk++ {
				if want, ok := spec.Ticks[strconv.Itoa(tk)]; ok {
					if got := digestState(m, lo, hi); got != want {
						bad++
						if bad == 1 {
							first = fmt.Sprintf("tick %d: got %s want %s", tk, got, want)
						}
					}
				}
				if spec.Rng != nil {
					if tk >= len(spec.Rng) {
						t.Fatalf("rng array has %d entries, tick %d reached", len(spec.Rng), tk)
					}
					st := spec.Rng[tk]
					if len(st) != 4 {
						t.Fatalf("rng entry %d %q: want 4 hex digits", tk, st)
					}
					a, err := strconv.ParseUint(st[0:2], 16, 8)
					if err != nil {
						t.Fatalf("rng entry %d: %v", tk, err)
					}
					b2, err := strconv.ParseUint(st[2:4], 16, 8)
					if err != nil {
						t.Fatalf("rng entry %d: %v", tk, err)
					}
					g.RNG.A = uint8(a)
					g.RNG.B = uint8(b2)
				}
				if spec.Frame != nil {
					if tk >= len(spec.Frame) {
						t.Fatalf("frame array has %d entries, tick %d reached", len(spec.Frame), tk)
					}
					g.Frame = int(spec.Frame[tk])
				}
				if err := g.Tick(); err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("tick %d: %v", tk, err)
				}
			}
			if bad > 0 {
				t.Errorf("%d of %d sampled ticks differ, first %s", bad, len(spec.Ticks), first)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestGoldenDigestDetectsMutation proves the digest pins can fail: the
// engine reruns 00FD's fixture with one CGRAM 5-bit digit of a hashed
// slot flipped and must diverge from the golden at tick 0.
func TestGoldenDigestDetectsMutation(t *testing.T) {
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data", "maps", "00FD")
	m, err := LoadMap(dir, "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadMap: %v", err)
	}
	spec := loadGfxFixtures(t)["00FD"]
	want := spec.Ticks["0"]
	if digestState(m, int(spec.Lo), int(spec.Hi)) != want {
		t.Fatal("unmutated 00FD does not match its golden; the pin is broken before the mutation")
	}
	m.Cgram[20][0] ^= 0x08 // palette 1 colour 4, red digit 0
	if got := digestState(m, int(spec.Lo), int(spec.Hi)); got == want {
		t.Fatal("flipping CGRAM[20][0] went undetected; the digest pin cannot fail")
	}
	t.Log("mutation detected: CGRAM[20][0] one 5-bit digit flipped the tick-0 digest")
}
```

`internal/game/gfx/arrival.go`:

```go
package gfx

import "fmt"

// FF:B1E4, the type-1 map arrival sequence (godot/arrival_fade.gd;
// objOp 51, enqueued by C0:C3D9 when $D0A6 & 30h is neither 10h nor
// 20h). Each Step is one main-loop iteration (one C0:06A6 wait); it
// applies the colour steps to the gfx VM and returns the events the
// field applies itself. Call order and waits follow the routine; 0272's
// emulator run measured every gap (lag frames aside, which come from
// CPU load).
//
// The list7 snapshot lives here, not on GfxAnim: arrival_fade.gd keeps
// it on the gfx object, but only this sequence reads it (FF:B2D6 is
// called from FF:B1E4 alone), and the op program always runs list7
// before the first fade7.

// The events Step returns; the field driver (flow) applies them.
const (
	EVMasks  = "masks"        // $212C = 02, $212D = 11 (FF:B20A)
	EVMode2  = "mode2"        // C0:FCB9: redraw, $2105 = 0A, effect 09
	EVShift  = "bg1_shift"    // $D93F += 100h (FF:B234)
	EVLeader = "leader_31_0e" // $D8E9 = 31, $D8EA = 0E, C0:53CE
	EVMove   = "map_move_0"   // queue word 0010 (FF:B2B7)
	EVFreeze = "freeze"       // a frame C0:065E waits out (NMI only): the field does not run, so no VM tick (0272: 6 frames but 4 ticks from the last B353 to the next B3FD)
)

type arrivalOpKind int

const (
	opWait arrivalOpKind = iota
	opFreeze
	opFade
	opList7
	opFade7
	opEvent
)

type arrivalOp struct {
	kind  arrivalOpKind
	entry int    // opFade's entry k
	event string // opEvent's name
}

// ArrivalFade is one arrival sequence. Build a fresh one when the map's
// objOp 51 frame arrives (arrivalcheck replays set it at start_f).
type ArrivalFade struct {
	ops   []arrivalOp
	pc    int
	list7 [16][3]int // FF:B2D6's snapshot, taken by the list7 op
}

// NewArrivalFade builds the routine's op list (arrival_fade.gd _init).
func NewArrivalFade() *ArrivalFade {
	a := &ArrivalFade{}
	a.wait(240) // B2BE: 60 x 4 waits
	for range 32 {
		a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opFade})
		a.wait(4)
	}
	a.wait(240)
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opList7})
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opEvent, event: EVMasks})
	for range 32 {
		a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opFade7})
		a.wait(4)
	}
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opEvent, event: EVMode2})
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opFreeze}) // C0:FCBD and FD1C each wait a frame (C0:065E)
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opFreeze})
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opEvent, event: EVShift})
	for range 32 {
		for k := 1; k <= 5; k++ {
			a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opFade, entry: k})
			a.wait(1)
		}
	}
	a.wait(720) // three B2BE
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opEvent, event: EVLeader})
	for range 32 {
		a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opFade})
		a.wait(4)
	}
	a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opEvent, event: EVMove})
	return a
}

func (a *ArrivalFade) wait(n int) {
	for range n {
		a.ops = append(a.ops, arrivalOp{kind: opWait})
	}
}

// Finished says every op ran.
func (a *ArrivalFade) Finished() bool {
	return a.pc >= len(a.ops)
}

// Step runs ops up to and including the next wait and returns the
// events so far. A freeze frame returns immediately: the field skips
// that iteration's VM tick. The caller loops on EVFreeze (a frozen
// frame's ops continue within the same main-loop iteration's place in
// the sequence).
func (a *ArrivalFade) Step(g *GfxAnim) ([]string, error) {
	var events []string
	for a.pc < len(a.ops) {
		op := a.ops[a.pc]
		a.pc++
		switch op.kind {
		case opWait:
			return events, nil
		case opFreeze:
			events = append(events, EVFreeze)
			return events, nil
		case opFade:
			if err := g.FadeEntry(op.entry, 1); err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("arrival fade: %w", err)
			}
		case opList7:
			a.list7 = g.LoadList7()
		case opFade7:
			g.FadeList7(&a.list7, -1)
		case opEvent:
			events = append(events, op.event)
		}
	}
	return events, nil
}
```

`internal/game/gfx/arrival_test.go`:

```go
package gfx

import (
	"crypto/md5"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// The arrivalcheck fixture rule (exports/tests/arrivalcheck.gd --fixture):
// the type-1 arrival sequence (FF:B1E4) replays against an emulator log
// of TK lines (one per FF:9CDB call: frame, $14, RNG, CGRAM 0-255) and
// counts the ticks whose BG colours differ. The committed fixtures hold
// per-tick $14, RNG and colour digests, no ROM bytes.

// arrivalFixtures is arrivalcheck.gd's FIXTURES, in its order.
var arrivalFixtures = []string{
	"0272", "027A", "027C", "027F", "027B", "027D", "027E",
	"0280", "0281", "028F", "0290", "0291",
}

// arrivalLagTick is arrivalcheck.gd's LAG_TICK: from this tick on only
// the sorted digests are compared (in the emulator the main loop
// overran a frame and the NMI raised $14 to odd in the middle of the VM
// pass, so entry 5 skipped the A32C rotation entries 1-4 made; CPU load
// is not modelled).
const arrivalLagTick = 847

// arrivalTick is one fixture row: [frame, $14, rng "AABB", exact
// digest, sorted digest].
type arrivalTick struct {
	Frame  int
	F14    int
	Rng    string
	Exact  string
	Sorted string
}

func (t *arrivalTick) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {
	var row []json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &row); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(row) != 5 {
		return fmt.Errorf("arrival tick row: %d entries, want 5", len(row))
	}
	var num float64
	if err := json.Unmarshal(row[0], &num); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("arrival tick frame: %w", err)
	}
	t.Frame = int(num)
	if err := json.Unmarshal(row[1], &num); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("arrival tick $14: %w", err)
	}
	t.F14 = int(num)
	for i, dst := range []*string{&t.Rng, &t.Exact, &t.Sorted} {
		if err := json.Unmarshal(row[2+i], dst); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("arrival tick field %d: %w", 2+i, err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

type arrivalFixture struct {
	Map          string        `json:"map"`
	LagTick      int           `json:"lag_tick"`
	StartF       int           `json:"start_f"`
	VMFirst      bool          `json:"vm_first"`
	Ticks        []arrivalTick `json:"ticks"`
	ExpectDiffer []int         `json:"expect_differ"`
}

// loadArrivalFixture reads one exports/tests/arrival_*.json in place.
func loadArrivalFixture(t *testing.T, mapID string) arrivalFixture {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "tests", "arrival_"+mapID+".json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read arrival fixture %s: %v", mapID, err)
	}
	var fx arrivalFixture
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &fx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse arrival fixture %s: %v", mapID, err)
	}
	if fx.Map == "" {
		fx.Map = "0272" // arrivalcheck.gd's default
	}
	if fx.LagTick == 0 {
		fx.LagTick = arrivalLagTick
	}
	return fx
}

// arrivalDigestCols is arrivalcheck.gd's _digest_cols: MD5 over the 128
// colours as 8 rows of 16, big-endian 2 bytes each; sorted per-row when
// sorted (so a rotation within a row does not count).
func arrivalDigestCols(cols []uint16, sorted bool) string {
	h := md5.New()
	for row := range 8 {
		r := slices.Clone(cols[row*16 : (row+1)*16])
		if sorted {
			sort.Slice(r, func(i, j int) bool { return r[i] < r[j] })
		}
		for _, v := range r {
			h.Write([]byte{byte(v >> 8), byte(v)})
		}
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
}

// arrivalDigestTL is arrivalcheck.gd's _digest_tl: the TileMap's CGRAM
// 0-127 packed ((r>>3)<<10 | (g>>3)<<5 | (b>>3)) — R high, the same
// permutation _digest_cg applies to the PPU's BGR words.
func arrivalDigestTL(m *TileMap, sorted bool) string {
	cols := make([]uint16, 128)
	for i, c := range m.Cgram {
		cols[i] = uint16(c[0]>>3)<<10 | uint16(c[1]>>3)<<5 | uint16(c[2]>>3)
	}
	return arrivalDigestCols(cols, sorted)
}

// replayArrival is arrivalcheck.gd's _replay: step the gfx VM and the
// arrival sequence over the fixture's ticks, comparing the CGRAM digest
// before each tick (exact below lag_tick, sorted after; a tick whose
// frame follows a gap is an overrun frame's part-upload and skips). It
// returns the number of differing ticks and, in diffOut, their indexes.
func replayArrival(fx arrivalFixture, scripts, palettes []byte, diffOut *[]int) (int, error) {
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data", "maps", fx.Map)
	m, err := LoadMap(dir, "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("load map %s: %w", fx.Map, err)
	}
	mj, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "map.json"))
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("read map.json %s: %w", fx.Map, err)
	}
	var mdata struct {
		GfxAnims []AnimSpec `json:"gfx_anims"`
		PalBank  int        `json:"pal_bank"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(mj, &mdata); err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("parse map.json %s: %w", fx.Map, err)
	}
	g := NewGfxAnim(scripts, palettes, rng.NewField())
	g.BG3On = m.Present[BG3]
	g.Install(mdata.GfxAnims, m, mdata.PalBank)
	g.Darken(6)
	var seq *ArrivalFade
	bad := 0
	for ti := range fx.Ticks {
		row := &fx.Ticks[ti]
		exact := ti < fx.LagTick
		lagged := ti > 0 && row.Frame-fx.Ticks[ti-1].Frame > 1
		if !lagged && arrivalDigestTL(m, !exact) != row.digestFor(exact) {
			bad++
			*diffOut = append(*diffOut, ti)
		}
		g.Frame = row.F14
		a, errA := strconv.ParseUint(row.Rng[0:2], 16, 8)
		b, errB := strconv.ParseUint(row.Rng[2:4], 16, 8)
		if errA != nil || errB != nil {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("arrival %s tick %d rng %q: %v %v", fx.Map, ti, row.Rng, errA, errB)
		}
		g.RNG.A = uint8(a)
		g.RNG.B = uint8(b)
		if seq == nil && row.Frame >= fx.StartF {
			seq = NewArrivalFade()
		}
		if fx.VMFirst {
			if err := g.Tick(); err != nil {
				return 0, fmt.Errorf("arrival %s tick %d: %w", fx.Map, ti, err)
			}
		}
		if seq != nil && !seq.Finished() {
			for {
				evs, err := seq.Step(g)
				if err != nil {
					return 0, fmt.Errorf("arrival %s tick %d: %w", fx.Map, ti, err)
				}
				if !slices.Contains(evs, EVFreeze) {
					break
				}
			}
		}
		if !fx.VMFirst {
			if err := g.Tick(); err != nil {
				return 0, fmt.Errorf("arrival %s tick %d: %w", fx.Map, ti, err)
			}
		}
	}
	return bad, nil
}

func (t *arrivalTick) digestFor(exact bool) string {
	if exact {
		return t.Exact
	}
	return t.Sorted
}

// TestArrivalDigestSelfTest pins the digest rule: identical colours
// digest equally, a flipped digit diverges, a rotation within a row
// moves the exact digest but not the sorted one, and Go's MD5 matches
// the GDScript HashingContext's known vectors.
func TestArrivalDigestSelfTest(t *testing.T) {
	if got := fmt.Sprintf("%x", md5.Sum(nil)); got != "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e" {
		t.Fatalf(`md5("") = %s, want d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e (Go MD5 must match HashingContext.HASH_MD5)`, got)
	}
	cols := make([]uint16, 128)
	for i := range cols {
		cols[i] = uint16(i * 13)
	}
	if arrivalDigestCols(cols, false) != arrivalDigestCols(slices.Clone(cols), false) {
		t.Fatal("identical colours digested differently")
	}
	// a rotation within row 0: exact moves, sorted does not
	rot := slices.Clone(cols)
	rot[0], rot[1] = rot[1], rot[0]
	if arrivalDigestCols(cols, false) == arrivalDigestCols(rot, false) {
		t.Fatal("a within-row rotation left the exact digest unchanged")
	}
	if arrivalDigestCols(cols, true) != arrivalDigestCols(rot, true) {
		t.Fatal("a within-row rotation moved the sorted digest")
	}
	// a value change moves both
	ch := slices.Clone(cols)
	ch[5] ^= 1
	if arrivalDigestCols(cols, false) == arrivalDigestCols(ch, false) {
		t.Fatal("a flipped colour left the exact digest unchanged")
	}
	if arrivalDigestCols(cols, true) == arrivalDigestCols(ch, true) {
		t.Fatal("a flipped colour left the sorted digest unchanged")
	}
}

// TestGoldenArrivals re-hosts the 12 arrivalcheck fixtures: the gfx VM
// and the arrival sequence (arrival.go) replay each map's logged ticks
// and every compared digest must match. 027F is the no_fade record with
// a recorded overrun-run; its diff set must equal expect_differ exactly
// (a port regression that changes the set fails either way).
func TestGoldenArrivals(t *testing.T) {
	data := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data")
	scripts, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(data, "gfx_scripts.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read gfx_scripts.bin: %v", err)
	}
	palettes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(data, "rom_palettes.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read rom_palettes.bin: %v", err)
	}
	for _, id := range arrivalFixtures {
		t.Run(id, func(t *testing.T) {
			fx := loadArrivalFixture(t, id)
			var diff []int
			bad, err := replayArrival(fx, scripts, palettes, &diff)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s: %v", id, err)
			}
			if len(fx.ExpectDiffer) == 0 {
				if bad != 0 {
					t.Errorf("%s: %d of %d ticks differ, first at %d", id, bad, len(fx.Ticks), diff[0])
				}
				return
			}
			if !slices.Equal(diff, fx.ExpectDiffer) {
				t.Errorf("%s: differs at %v, want %v", id, diff, fx.ExpectDiffer)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestGoldenArrivalDetectsMutation proves the arrival pins can fail:
// fixture 0272 rerun with one CGRAM 5-bit digit flipped at tick 0 must
// diverge from the golden (the digest is taken before any tick, so the
// flip is visible immediately).
func TestGoldenArrivalDetectsMutation(t *testing.T) {
	data := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data")
	scripts, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(data, "gfx_scripts.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read gfx_scripts.bin: %v", err)
	}
	palettes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(data, "rom_palettes.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read rom_palettes.bin: %v", err)
	}
	fx := loadArrivalFixture(t, "0272")
	var diff []int
	bad, err := replayArrival(fx, scripts, palettes, &diff)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if bad != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unmutated 0272 differs on %d ticks; the pin is broken before the mutation", bad)
	}
	// flip one 5-bit digit of a hashed slot (palette 1 colour 4's red)
	// and rebuild the tick-0 digest the replay compares at tick 0: the
	// comparator must see the divergence.
	dir := filepath.Join(data, "maps", fx.Map)
	m, err := LoadMap(dir, "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.Cgram[20][0] ^= 0x08
	if arrivalDigestTL(m, false) == fx.Ticks[0].Exact {
		t.Fatal("flipping CGRAM[20][0] went undetected; the arrival digest pin cannot fail")
	}
	t.Log("mutation detected: CGRAM[20][0] one 5-bit digit flipped 0272's tick-0 digest")
}
```

`internal/game/gfx/compare.go`:

```go
package gfx

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
)

// Compare applies tests/tilecheck.gd's rule to two images of equal
// size: a pixel matches when both alphas are 0, else all four straight
// RGBA bytes must be equal. It returns the number of differing pixels
// and a description of the first one; a size mismatch is an error.
func Compare(got, want image.Image) (int, string, error) {
	gb, wb := got.Bounds(), want.Bounds()
	if gb.Dx() != wb.Dx() || gb.Dy() != wb.Dy() {
		return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("compare: sizes %dx%d and %dx%d differ", gb.Dx(), gb.Dy(), wb.Dx(), wb.Dy())
	}
	bad := 0
	first := ""
	for y := wb.Min.Y; y < wb.Max.Y; y++ {
		for x := wb.Min.X; x < wb.Max.X; x++ {
			g := nrgbaAt(got, x, y)
			w := nrgbaAt(want, x, y)
			if g.A == 0 && w.A == 0 {
				continue
			}
			if g != w {
				bad++
				if first == "" {
					first = fmt.Sprintf("(%d,%d) got %v want %v", x, y, g, w)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return bad, first, nil
}

// nrgbaAt reads a pixel's straight RGBA bytes (the PNGs and this
// package's renders hold alpha 0 or 255 only).
func nrgbaAt(img image.Image, x, y int) color.NRGBA {
	c := color.NRGBAModel.Convert(img.At(x, y)).(color.NRGBA)
	return c
}

// BlendRect alpha-blends src over dst in place: Godot's
// Image.blend_rect on straight-alpha images, as tilecheck composites
// the screen-hi reference from the over and bg3 renders.
func BlendRect(dst, src *image.RGBA) {
	for y := 0; y < dst.Bounds().Dy(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < dst.Bounds().Dx(); x++ {
			s := nrgbaAt(src, x, y)
			if s.A == 255 {
				dst.SetRGBA(x, y, color.RGBA{s.R, s.G, s.B, 255})
				continue
			}
			if s.A == 0 {
				continue
			}
			d := nrgbaAt(dst, x, y)
			sa := int(s.A)
			dst.SetRGBA(x, y, color.RGBA{
				uint8((int(s.R)*sa + int(d.R)*(255-sa)) / 255),
				uint8((int(s.G)*sa + int(d.G)*(255-sa)) / 255),
				uint8((int(s.B)*sa + int(d.B)*(255-sa)) / 255),
				uint8(sa + int(d.A)*(255-sa)/255),
			})
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/game/gfx/fx.go`:

```go
package gfx

import (
	"image"
)

// ScreenOpts carries the SCREEN shader's extras (godot/tile_layers.gd's
// SCREEN fragment path beyond the plain priority/colour-math walk the
// tilecheck goldens pin): the per-layer wave tables, the scroll offsets,
// the effect bands, the mode-2 offset-per-tile and the subscreen OBJ
// layer. A nil *ScreenOpts is the plain path.
type ScreenOpts struct {
	// Dims is each layer's size in px; its tilemap wraps there (map.json
	// layer_dims, 0 = the map's own size).
	Dims [3][2]int
	// BaseOff is per layer the added offset for a layer that fits its
	// 64x32 tilemap (uploaded whole, shown at screen + its own scroll
	// counting from the load camera): (12 - loadLeft, 12 - loadTop);
	// BG1 adds the arrival's $D93F + 100h on top.
	BaseOff [3][2]int
	// Bg2Off is BG2's own scroll (drift, walking parallax and scroll
	// mode 2's HDMA row), Bg3Off BG3's (scroll mode 3).
	Bg2Off, Bg3Off [2]int
	// Present overrides the layer presence bitmask (1|2|4); 0 = the
	// map's own. Effect 09 and scroll mode 2 clear BG3 here.
	Present int
	// WaveMask bit per layer with wave tables; Wx/Wy hold the per-line
	// offsets indexed (map_y - 13 + phase) & 15.
	WaveMask int
	Wx, Wy   [3][16]int
	Phase    int  // $D77C, stepped by the effect dispatcher
	Phase2   int  // BG2's phase when it differs (effect 10), -1 = Phase
	Band1    bool // effect 7: BG1's wave only inside the screen band
	BandTop  int  // the map row of screen line 0 (cam_top + 1)
	// E0A is effect 0A/0B's (and scroll mode 3's) per-band BG2 x scroll:
	// band j covers BG2 rows below E0AEnd[j] from row E0AY0 (row =
	// BandTop + line), lines past the last band take E0ARest instead of
	// the normal E0AShift.
	E0A      bool
	E0AY0    int
	E0AN     int
	E0AEnd   [12]int
	E0AX     [12]int
	E0AShift int
	E0ARest  int
	// Opt is effect 09's mode-2 offset-per-tile on BG1: screen column
	// c >= 1 (8 px from OptCamX) takes entry (OptK0 + c - 1) & 15 of
	// (OptDX, OptDY) on top of BG1's scroll; column 0 keeps the plain
	// scroll. The x entries are whole tiles.
	Opt     bool
	OptK0   int
	OptCamX int
	OptDX   [16]int
	OptDY   [16]int
	// ObjTex is the subscreen OBJ layer in map coordinates (the type-1
	// arrival after its mask step: $212D bit 4). An opaque pixel is the
	// subscreen colour unless BG1 has a high-priority tile there (OBJ
	// priority 2 sits between BG high and low).
	ObjTex *image.RGBA
	ObjSub bool
	// SubOut makes the pass output the subscreen instead: the pixel is
	// the subscreen colour, alpha 0 where it is the backdrop (the fixed
	// colour). OBJ_MATH reads it for figures in OBJ palettes 4-7 when
	// the colour math takes the subscreen ($2130 bit 1).
	SubOut bool
}

// ScreenOptsFull renders one priority class with the extras (tile_layers
// SCREEN's full fragment path). o nil is the plain path Screen renders.
func (m *TileMap) ScreenOptsFull(hi bool, regs Regs, o *ScreenOpts) (*image.RGBA, error) {
	if err := m.validateChips(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, m.Width*8, m.Height*8))
	s := screen{
		m: m, mainMask: regs.Main, subMask: regs.Sub,
		mathMask: regs.Math & 0x3F,
		useSub:   regs.Sel&0x02 != 0,
		subtract: regs.Math&0x80 != 0,
		half:     regs.Math&0x40 != 0,
		fixed5:   fixedColor(regs.Fixed),
		o:        o,
	}
	for py := 0; py < m.Height*8; py++ {
		for px := 0; px < m.Width*8; px++ {
			col, alpha, opaque := s.pixel(px, py, hi)
			if !opaque {
				continue // the hi class with no tile discards
			}
			col.A = alpha
			img.SetRGBA(px, py, col)
		}
	}
	return img, nil
}

// modFloor is the shader's mod() (the result takes the divisor's sign).
func modFloor(v, m int) int {
	r := v % m
	if r < 0 {
		r += m
	}
	return r
}

// floorDiv is the shader's floor(x / m).
func floorDiv(v, m int) int {
	if v >= 0 {
		return v / m
	}
	return -((-v + m - 1) / m)
}

// ObjMathOn says the map's OBJ colour math is active: OBJ on the main
// screen ($212C bit 4) and in the math bands ($2131 bit 4).
func ObjMathOn(regs Regs) bool {
	return regs.Main&0x10 != 0 && regs.Math&0x10 != 0
}

// ObjMath applies the OBJ colour math to one figure pixel in an OBJ
// palette slot 4-7 (tile_layers OBJ_MATH; only those palettes take
// part, $2131 bit 4). c and sub are 5-bit components; subOpaque is the
// sub_out pass's alpha (0 where the subscreen pixel is the backdrop,
// which skips the halving).
func ObjMath(c [3]int, regs Regs, sub [3]int, subOpaque bool) [3]uint8 {
	subtract := regs.Math&0x80 != 0
	half := regs.Math&0x40 != 0
	useSub := regs.Sel&0x02 != 0
	other := fixedColor(regs.Fixed)
	if useSub {
		if subOpaque {
			other = sub
		} else {
			half = false
		}
	}
	var r [3]int
	for d := 0; d < 3; d++ {
		if subtract {
			r[d] = max(c[d]-other[d], 0)
		} else {
			r[d] = c[d] + other[d]
		}
		if half {
			r[d] /= 2
		}
		r[d] = min(r[d], 31)
	}
	return [3]uint8{uint8(r[0] * 8), uint8(r[1] * 8), uint8(r[2] * 8)}
}
```

```go
package gfx

import (
	"encoding/json"

// The SCREEN fixture replays the selftest drove on the live GDScript
// field (godot/main.gd's camera/effects block), re-hosted at the
// machine level: each fixture row feeds the machine the camera the
// emulator logged and the machine's state must equal the engine's.
// The full-field replays (the follow camera itself, the pan's leader
// instruction chain) stay with the field/shell owners; what is pinned
// here is the pure integer math this package owns.

// fxMapsDir is the exports/data export root.
var fxMapsDir = filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data")

// fxTestRows reads one exports/tests/*.json's rows column.
func fxTestRows(t *testing.T, name string) [][]int {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "tests", name))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", name, err)
	}
	var fx struct {
		Rows [][]int `json:"rows"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &fx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse %s: %v", name, err)
	}
	if len(fx.Rows) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s has no rows", name)
	}
	return fx.Rows
}

// fxMapConfig parses a map.json's SCREEN fields and installs its
// gfx_anims (the effect entry's chip is the effect argument, FF:9B30).
func fxMapConfig(t *testing.T, mapID string) (effect, scrollMode, camShift int, parallax bool, arg int) {
	t.Helper()
	dir := filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "maps", mapID)
	mj, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "map.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s map.json: %v", mapID, err)
	}
	var mdata struct {
		Effect     int        `json:"effect"`
		ScrollMode int        `json:"scroll_mode"`
		CamShift   int        `json:"cam_shift"`
		Parallax   bool       `json:"parallax"`
		GfxAnims   []AnimSpec `json:"gfx_anims"`
		PalBank    int        `json:"pal_bank"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(mj, &mdata); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse %s map.json: %v", mapID, err)
	}
	if len(mdata.GfxAnims) == 0 {
		return mdata.Effect, mdata.ScrollMode, mdata.CamShift, mdata.Parallax, 0
	}
	m, err := LoadMap(dir, "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadMap %s: %v", mapID, err)
	}
	scripts, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "gfx_scripts.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read gfx_scripts.bin: %v", err)
	}
	palettes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "rom_palettes.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read rom_palettes.bin: %v", err)
	}
	g := NewGfxAnim(scripts, palettes, rng.NewField())
	g.Install(mdata.GfxAnims, m, mdata.PalBank)
	return mdata.Effect, mdata.ScrollMode, mdata.CamShift, mdata.Parallax, g.EffectArg
}

// TestParallaxFromFixture replays tests/parallax_0084.json: rows
// [x, y, $D93F, $D941, $D943, $D949, speed row]; BG2's offset is
// BG2 - BG1 (main.gd: BG2's offset is $D943 - $D93F, $D949 - $D941).
func TestParallaxFromFixture(t *testing.T) {
	_, _, _, parallax, _ := fxMapConfig(t, "0084")
	if !parallax {
		t.Fatal("0084 map.json parallax is false; the fixture map must carry the flag")
	}
	w, err := LoadWaveSet(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "effect_waves.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rows := fxTestRows(t, "parallax_0084.json")
	fx := &ScreenFX{Waves: w, Parallax: true}
	fx.camPrev = [2]int{rows[0][2] + 12, rows[0][3] + 12}
	bad := 0
	for i, r := range rows {
		if len(r) != 7 {
			t.Fatalf("row %d has %d columns, want 7", i, len(r))
		}
		fx.LeaderRow = r[6]
		fx.tickParallax(r[2]+12, r[3]+12)
		want := [2]int{r[4] - r[2], r[5] - r[3]}
		if fx.bg2Drift != want {
			bad++
			if bad == 1 {
				t.Logf("row %d: bg2 offset %v, want %v", i, fx.bg2Drift, want)
			}
		}
	}
	if bad > 0 {
		t.Errorf("0084 parallax differs on %d of %d rows", bad, len(rows))
	}
}

// TestBG3ScrollFromFixture replays tests/bg3scroll_0149.json (scroll
// mode 3, load camera left 508): BG3 sits 8*(S3 - S1) = -272 from BG1
// (S1 = 62, S3 = 28, the engine's $D900/$D902), plus the camera's
// movement since load; the fixture's BG3 column is the engine's
// absolute scroll, so the expectation strips the camera's own 2x move.
func TestBG3ScrollFromFixture(t *testing.T) {
	_, scrollMode, camShift, _, _ := fxMapConfig(t, "0149")
	if scrollMode != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("0149 scroll_mode %d, want 3", scrollMode)
	}
	if camShift != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("0149 cam_shift %d, want 0 (the -272 pin assumes it)", camShift)
	}
	m, err := LoadMap(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "maps", "0149"), "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rows := fxTestRows(t, "bg3scroll_0149.json")
	fx := &ScreenFX{ScrollMode: 3, MapW: m.Width, MapH: m.Height}
	fx.haveCam = true
	fx.camLoad = [2]int{508, rows[0][3] + 12}
	bad := 0
	for i, r := range rows {
		if len(r) != 6 {
			t.Fatalf("row %d has %d columns, want 6", i, len(r))
		}
		fx.tickScroll(508+r[2], r[3]+12)
		want := [2]int{-272 + r[4] - r[2], 0}
		if fx.bg3Scroll != want {
			bad++
			if bad == 1 {
				t.Logf("row %d: bg3 scroll %v, want %v", i, fx.bg3Scroll, want)
			}
		}
	}
	if bad > 0 {
		t.Errorf("0149 BG3 scroll differs on %d of %d rows", bad, len(rows))
	}
	// the -272 is 8*(S3-S1) with S1 = 62 from the load camera: the pin
	// dies if the map width or the S1 arithmetic drifts
	s1 := max(0, floorDiv(508+124, 8)-17)
	if s1 != 62 {
		t.Fatalf("S1 = %d, want 62", s1)
	}
	if 8*(modFloor(2*s1, m.Width)-s1) != -272 {
		t.Fatalf("8*(S3-S1) = %d, want -272 (map width %d)", 8*(modFloor(2*s1, m.Width)-s1), m.Width)
	}
}

// TestE0BVariants replays the selftest's three effect-0B maps: 026B
// (variant 0) after 180 ticks — band indices [4 4 12 12 0E] in the
// engine's hex ($C858), timers [2 2 0C 0C 0C] ($C878), and at y0 = 276
// the bands end 287/359/375 with x 12/12/10; 026D (variant 2) after
// 163 ticks holds indices 2 2 2 14 12 and timers 5 5 5 5 13; 026C
// (variant 1) at y0 = 148 ends its four bands at 191/271/359/375.
func TestE0BVariants(t *testing.T) {
	w, err := LoadWaveSet(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "effect_waves.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Run("026B", func(t *testing.T) {
		effect, _, _, _, arg := fxMapConfig(t, "026B")
		if effect != 0x0B {
			t.Fatalf("026B effect %d, want 11", effect)
		}
		if arg != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("026B effect arg %d, want 0", arg)
		}
		fx := &ScreenFX{Waves: w, Effect: 0x0B, EffectArg: arg}
		fx.haveCam = true
		fx.camLoad = [2]int{12, 284}
		for f := 0; f < 180; f++ {
			fx.tickE0B(12, 284)
		}
		wantIdx := [5]int{4, 4, 0x12, 0x12, 0x0E}
		wantTimer := [5]int{2, 2, 0x0C, 0x0C, 0x0C}
		if fx.e0bIdx != wantIdx || fx.e0bTimer != wantTimer {
			t.Fatalf("idx %v timer %v, want %v / %v", fx.e0bIdx, fx.e0bTimer, wantIdx, wantTimer)
		}
		b := fx.e0aBands
		if b.n != 3 || b.end[0] != 287 || b.end[1] != 359 || b.end[2] != 375 ||
			b.x[0] != 12 || b.x[1] != 12 || b.x[2] != 10 {
			t.Fatalf("bands n %d ends %v xs %v, want 3 / [287 359 375] / [12 12 10]", b.n, b.end, b.x)
		}
	})
	t.Run("026D", func(t *testing.T) {
		effect, _, _, _, arg := fxMapConfig(t, "026D")
		if effect != 0x0B {
			t.Fatalf("026D effect %d, want 11", effect)
		}
		if arg != 2 {
			t.Fatalf("026D effect arg %d, want 2", arg)
		}
		fx := &ScreenFX{Waves: w, Effect: 0x0B, EffectArg: arg}
		fx.haveCam = true
		fx.camLoad = [2]int{12, 284}
		for f := 0; f < 163; f++ {
			fx.tickE0B(12, 284)
		}
		wantIdx := [5]int{2, 2, 2, 14, 12}
		wantTimer := [5]int{5, 5, 5, 5, 13}
		if fx.e0bIdx != wantIdx || fx.e0bTimer != wantTimer {
			t.Fatalf("idx %v timer %v, want %v / %v", fx.e0bIdx, fx.e0bTimer, wantIdx, wantTimer)
		}
	})
	t.Run("026C", func(t *testing.T) {
		effect, _, _, _, arg := fxMapConfig(t, "026C")
		if effect != 0x0B {
			t.Fatalf("026C effect %d, want 11", effect)
		}
		if arg != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("026C effect arg %d, want 1", arg)
		}
		fx := &ScreenFX{Waves: w, Effect: 0x0B, EffectArg: arg}
		fx.haveCam = true
		fx.camLoad = [2]int{12, 156}
		fx.tickE0B(12, 156)
		b := fx.e0aBands
		if b.n != 4 || b.end[0] != 191 || b.end[1] != 271 || b.end[2] != 359 || b.end[3] != 375 {
			t.Fatalf("bands n %d ends %v, want 4 / [191 271 359 375]", b.n, b.end)
		}
	})
}

// TestE0BDetectsMutatedWaveTable proves the effect pins can fail: a
// shifted variant-0 band bound must move 026B's pinned band ends.
func TestE0BDetectsMutatedWaveTable(t *testing.T) {
	w, err := LoadWaveSet(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "effect_waves.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, _, _, _, arg := fxMapConfig(t, "026B")
	tick := func(waves *WaveSet) e0aBands {
		fx := &ScreenFX{Waves: waves, Effect: 0x0B, EffectArg: arg}
		fx.haveCam = true
		fx.camLoad = [2]int{12, 284}
		for f := 0; f < 180; f++ {
			fx.tickE0B(12, 284)
		}
		return fx.e0aBands
	}
	good := tick(w)
	if good.n != 3 || good.end[0] != 287 {
		t.Fatalf("unmutated bands n %d end0 %d; the pin is broken before the mutation", good.n, good.end[0])
	}
	mutated := *w
	mutated.E0BBound[2]++ // variant 0's first band above y0 = 276 (the 287 end)
	if bad := tick(&mutated); bad.end[0] == good.end[0] {
		t.Fatal("shifting E0BBound[2] left the band ends unchanged; the pin cannot fail")
	}
}

// TestEffectPhases pins the two screen-effect phase counters the
// selftest drove: 007A's effect 3 (BG3 wave) steps its phase every 4th
// field frame — phase 2 after 9 frames; 02B8's effect 2 (C0:E084)
// shows BG1/BG2 phase 1 from the first frame and 2 from the 12th.
func TestEffectPhases(t *testing.T) {
	effect7A, _, _, _, _ := fxMapConfig(t, "007A")
	if effect7A != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("007A effect %d, want 3", effect7A)
	}
	fx := &ScreenFX{Effect: effect7A}
	for f := 0; f < 9; f++ {
		fx.tickEffect()
	}
	if fx.phase != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("007A wave phase %d after 9 frames, want 2", fx.phase)
	}
	effect2B8, _, _, _, _ := fxMapConfig(t, "02B8")
	if effect2B8 != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("02B8 effect %d, want 2", effect2B8)
	}
	fx2 := &ScreenFX{Effect: effect2B8}
	phases := make([]int, 12)
	for f := 0; f < 12; f++ {
		fx2.tickEffect()
		phases[f] = fx2.phase
	}
	if phases[0] != 1 || phases[10] != 1 || phases[11] != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("02B8 effect 2 phases %v, want 1 at frames 1 and 11 and 2 at 12", phases)
	}
}

// TestObjPalADCycle replays the selftest's 01E6 OBJ palette cycle
// (handler FF:A5A1): stepping 01E6's installed anims at $14 = 8590...
// reads AD, AD, AE, AE ... from $14 = 8608 on (each tick loads
// AD + ($14 & 2) / 2), so graphic 121 shows its _AE figure while AE
// holds. The figure swap itself is the shell's (figures.go); the pin
// here is the palette slot the swap reads.
func TestObjPalADCycle(t *testing.T) {
	dir := filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "maps", "01E6")
	mj, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "map.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var mdata struct {
		GfxAnims []AnimSpec `json:"gfx_anims"`
		PalBank  int        `json:"pal_bank"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(mj, &mdata); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m, err := LoadMap(dir, "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	scripts, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "gfx_scripts.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	palettes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(fxMapsDir, "rom_palettes.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g := NewGfxAnim(scripts, palettes, rng.NewField())
	g.BG3On = m.Present[BG3]
	g.Install(mdata.GfxAnims, m, mdata.PalBank)
	bad := 0
	for f := 8590; f < 8690; f++ {
		g.Frame = f
		if err := g.Tick(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("tick at $14 %d: %v", f, err)
		}
		if f >= 8608 {
			want := 0xAD
			if f&2 != 0 {
				want = 0xAE
			}
			if g.ObjPalAD != want {
				bad++
				if bad == 1 {
					t.Logf("$14 %d: obj palette %X, want %X", f, g.ObjPalAD, want)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if bad != 0 {
		t.Errorf("01E6 OBJ palette cycle: %d of 82 ticks differ", bad)
	}
	if g.ObjPalAD == 0xAE {
		t.Fatal("cycle ended on AE; the A5A1 entry never held AD")
	}
}
```
