`internal/game/shell/audio.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"

	"github.com/ebitengine/oto/v3"
	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2/audio"
	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2/audio/vorbis"
)

// audioSys plays the BGM catalog: one player for the map track (the
// same slot map_view._bgm holds — it keeps playing under the battle,
// whose theme rides on a second player) and one for the battle/wipe
// swap. The oggs decode whole (44100 stereo, the rip pipeline's fixed
// render — anything else is an error, the catalog is data).

// audioSampleRate is the context rate; every catalog ogg renders at it
// (docs/music.md: the libgme render chain). A different rate errors at
// play — the rip pipeline's own contract.
const audioSampleRate = 44100

type audioSys struct {
	ctx     *audio.Context
	music   *Music
	dataDir string

	mapPath    string        // the ogg the map player holds, "" none
	mapPlayer  *audio.Player // map_view._bgm's slot
	battlePath string
	battle     *audio.Player // the battle theme / defeat swap player

	disabled bool // no audio device (headless runs); one note printed
}

func newAudioSys(dataDir string, music *Music) *audioSys {
	return &audioSys{music: music, dataDir: dataDir}
}

// probeAudioDevice reports whether an audio device opens in THIS
// environment: it runs the binary again with the __audioprobe sentinel
// and reads the exit code (0 = the context opened). The probe runs
// before the first audio.NewContext — once a context exists, a failed
// device init is a fatal RunGame error ("RunGame returns an error when
// ... an audio error happens"), so an unavailable device (every
// headless box) must skip audio entirely.
func probeAudioDevice() bool {
	self, err := os.Executable()
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	return exec.Command(self, "__audioprobe").Run() == nil
}

// ProbeAudio is the probe child's body: open the audio device the same
// way the playback path will (oto, the backend ebiten's audio wraps)
// and report. Exit 0 = device available. It runs before any
// audio.NewContext so a failing device never reaches RunGame's fatal
// audio-error path.
func ProbeAudio() error {
	op := &oto.NewContextOptions{
		SampleRate:   audioSampleRate,
		ChannelCount: 2,
		Format:       oto.FormatFloat32LE,
	}
	ctx, ready, err := oto.NewContext(op)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	<-ready
	return ctx.Err()
}

// ensureCtx creates the audio context on first use. A context cannot
// fail to construct; the device failure surfaces at player creation,
// which disables the system with one printed note (headless boxes run
// silent, the environment's own shape).
func (a *audioSys) ensureCtx() bool {
	if a.disabled {
		return false
	}
	if a.ctx != nil {
		return true
	}
	a.ctx = audio.NewContext(audioSampleRate)
	return true
}

// errNoAudioDevice is the probe's failure note.
var errNoAudioDevice = errors.New("no audio device")

// disable flips the system off with one printed note, on stderr like
// the other boot failures.
func (a *audioSys) disable(err error) {
	if a.disabled {
		return
	}
	a.disabled = true
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "shell: audio unavailable, running silent: %v\n", err)
}

// decode loads one ogg into a looping f32 stream (the whole-file loop
// reproduces the sequence's own loop, the AudioStreamOggVorbis loop =
// true shape).
func (a *audioSys) decode(path string) (*audio.Player, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load ogg: %w", err)
	}
	stream, err := vorbis.DecodeF32(bytes.NewReader(b))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if stream.SampleRate() != audioSampleRate {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode %s: sample rate %d, want %d", path, stream.SampleRate(), audioSampleRate)
	}
	loop := audio.NewInfiniteLoopF32(stream, stream.Length())
	return a.ctx.NewPlayerF32(loop)
}

// playMapTrack switches the map player to the track (map_view
// play_track: the same track keeps playing; the caller watches
// flow.Track and calls only on change).
func (a *audioSys) playMapTrack(track int) error {
	path := a.music.oggPath(a.dataDir, track)
	if path == a.mapPath && path != "" {
		return nil
	}
	if path == "" {
		a.stopMap()
		return nil
	}
	if !a.ensureCtx() {
		a.mapPath = path
		return nil
	}
	p, err := a.decode(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if a.mapPlayer != nil {
		a.mapPlayer.PauseAndStopReading()
	}
	a.mapPlayer = p
	a.mapPath = path
	p.Play()
	return nil
}

// stopMap stops the map player (the next track restarts from the
// file's head).
func (a *audioSys) stopMap() {
	if a.mapPlayer != nil {
		a.mapPlayer.PauseAndStopReading()
		a.mapPlayer = nil
	}
	a.mapPath = ""
}

// playBattle starts the battle theme on the battle player (battle.gd
// _ready: battle.ogg loops under the fight).
func (a *audioSys) playBattle() error {
	return a.playAux(trackBattle)
}

// playDefeat swaps the battle player to 全滅のテーマ (battle.gd
// _show_wipe_window: stop, swap the stream, play).
func (a *audioSys) playDefeat() error {
	return a.playAux(trackDefeat)
}

func (a *audioSys) playAux(track int) error {
	path := a.music.oggPath(a.dataDir, track)
	if path == a.battlePath {
		return nil
	}
	if path == "" {
		a.stopAux()
		return nil
	}
	if !a.ensureCtx() {
		a.battlePath = path
		return nil
	}
	p, err := a.decode(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if a.battle != nil {
		a.battle.PauseAndStopReading()
	}
	a.battle = p
	a.battlePath = path
	p.Play()
	return nil
}

// stopAux stops the battle player (the scene's end; the map player's
// track resumes underneath, as the GDScript's two players leave it).
func (a *audioSys) stopAux() {
	if a.battle != nil {
		a.battle.PauseAndStopReading()
		a.battle = nil
	}
	a.battlePath = ""
}
```

`internal/game/shell/battlecmd_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/battle"
)

// The battle command windows over the headless engine (battle.gd's UI
// half): the per-ally menu with the category pager and the affordance
// gates, the target cursor, and battle 254's commander party window.
// The engines are hand-built battle.Data through the real NewEngine, so
// the pins run the engine's own round machinery.

// cmdRNG is a deterministic stand-in: every roll returns its lo.
type cmdRNG struct{}

func (cmdRNG) Roll(lo, hi uint8) int { return int(lo) }
func (cmdRNG) Tick()                 {}

func cmdData() *battle.Data {
	return &battle.Data{
		Items: map[string]battle.ItemRow{
			"0A": {ID: "0A", Name: "長剣", Kind: "weapon", Category: "剣", Power: 10},
			"30": {ID: "30", Name: "傷薬", Kind: "consumable", RecoverPower: 10, CuresStatus: 0x81},
		},
		Techniques: map[string]battle.TechRow{
			"00": {ID: "00", Name: "素手", Class: 116},
			"01": {ID: "01", Name: "剣", Class: 0, Power: 10},
			"10": {ID: "10", Name: "かすみ二段", Class: 0, Cost: 3},
			"20": {ID: "20", Name: "足ばらい", Class: 82, Cost: 4},
			"2A": {ID: "2A", Name: "術一閃", Class: 15, Cost: 2, JPCost: true},
		},
		Formations: map[string]battle.Formation{"01": {ID: "01", Rates: make([]int, 16)}},
		// the enemy tech carries the leave bit (docs/battle-menu.md $C,
		// C2:5BD4): the pick-time flee skips the whole action body, so
		// the rounds stay shallow
		EnemyTechs: map[string]battle.EnemyTechRow{"01": {ID: "01", Settings: 0x02}},
		// the victory level bumps read the rank row and the 16 group
		// rows; a quiet table (every cell FF = no bump) keeps the pins
		// off the growth machinery
		Levels: battle.LevelsData{RankRise: []int{0}, GlobalCap: 99, GroupCap: 99, GroupRows: ffRows()},
		// a quiet growth table: every chance cell 0 (nothing passes the
		// roll), the HP divisor 1 (HPThreshold's math stays defined),
		// the type-0 order row all FF (no code runs)
		Growth: battle.GrowthData{Chance: make([]int, 21), HPMul: 0, HPDiv: 1,
			OrderRows: [][]int{ff16()}},
		HeroForte: [][]int{{0, 0, 0}},
	}
}

// pad5 pads the weapon levels to the record's five bytes.
func pad5(v []int) []int {
	out := []int{0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	copy(out, v)
	return out
}

// ff16 is 16 FF cells (the growth thresholds' no-op cells), ffRows the
// 17x16 table of them (the victory level bumps' no-op cells).
func ff16() []int {
	return []int{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF,
		0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}
}

func ffRows() [][]int {
	out := make([][]int, 17)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = ff16()
	}
	return out
}

// cmdEngine builds one ally vs one enemy through the real NewEngine.
// id: the ally id (00 matches the World's protagonist row and takes the
// HeroForte raise), wlevels/slevels set the WP/JP pools.
func cmdEngine(t *testing.T, id string, wlevels, slevels []int) *battle.Engine {
	// the record joins want the five weapon-level bytes (12 raw level
	// bytes +0x25..+0x30)
	t.Helper()
	d := cmdData()
	row := &battle.AllyRow{ID: id, Name: "ユリアン", HP: 120,
		Techs:   []string{"10", "20", "2A"},
		WLevels: pad5(wlevels), SLevels: slevels, SpellRaw: []int{0, 0},
		GrowthRow: ff16(),
		Equipment: []string{"", "0A", "", "30"}}
	d.Allies = []battle.AllyRow{*row}
	idNum := 0
	for _, c := range id {
		var v int
		switch {
		case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
			v = int(c - '0')
		default:
			v = int(c-'A') + 10
		}
		idNum = idNum*16 + v
	}
	d.AllyByID = map[int]*battle.AllyRow{idNum: row}
	// the 8-slot pattern feeds the battle-254 phantom decisions (their
	// forced modes 9/10 pick pattern 0's slots)
	enemy := &battle.EnemyRow{ID: "10", Name: "地狼", HP: 500, AIMode: 20,
		DropCodes: []int{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF},
		Patterns: []battle.Pattern{{Actions: []string{"01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01"}},
			{Actions: []string{"01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01"}}}}
	d.Enemies = []battle.EnemyRow{*enemy}
	d.EnemyByID = map[int]*battle.EnemyRow{0x10: enemy}
	e, err := battle.NewEngine(d, stubWorld{}, cmdRNG{}, battle.Config{
		Party: []int{idNum}, Enemies: []int{0x10}, Formation: "01"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NewEngine: %v", err)
	}
	return e
}

// boundary drives the view to the round's command phase.
func boundary(t *testing.T, b *BattleView, e *battle.Engine) {
	t.Helper()
	b.roundClock = roundFrames - 1
	b.Step(e)
	if b.Phase != battleCmds {
		t.Fatalf("phase %d after the round boundary, want the command phase", b.Phase)
	}
}

func TestCmdRowsAndPages(t *testing.T) {
	e := cmdEngine(t, "02", []int{3}, []int{2})
	rows := CmdRows(e, 0)
	want := []string{"攻撃", "かすみ二段 (WP3)", "足ばらい (WP4)", "術一閃 (JP2)", "傷薬", "防御"}
	if len(rows) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("rows = %v, want %v", rows, want)
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if rows[i].Label != w {
			t.Fatalf("row %d = %q, want %q", i, rows[i].Label, w)
		}
	}
	if rows[0].Pick.Kind != battle.CmdPlain || rows[0].Pick.ID != "01" {
		t.Fatalf("plain row pick %+v, want CmdPlain 01 (the equipped 剣)", rows[0].Pick)
	}
	if rows[4].Pick.Kind != battle.CmdItem || rows[4].Pick.ID != "30" {
		t.Fatalf("item row pick %+v, want CmdItem 30 (the equipped 道具)", rows[4].Pick)
	}
	if rows[5].Pick.Kind != battle.CmdDefend {
		t.Fatalf("defend row pick %+v, want CmdDefend", rows[5].Pick)
	}
	// the category pager (docs/battle-formulas.md §16.1): the 剣 page
	// holds 攻撃 + the 剣-class tech + 防御, then the spell-class and 槍
	// pages, the 道具 page last
	pages := CmdPages(e, 0, rows)
	if len(pages) != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("%d pages, want 4: %v", len(pages), pages)
	}
	if got := pages[0]; got[0] != 0 || got[1] != 1 || got[2] != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("page 0 = %v, want rows [攻撃, かすみ二段, 防御]", got)
	}
	if got := pages[1]; len(got) != 1 || got[0] != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("page 1 = %v, want 術一閃 (class 15) alone", got)
	}
	if got := pages[2]; len(got) != 1 || got[0] != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("page 2 = %v, want 足ばらい (class 82) alone", got)
	}
	if got := pages[3]; len(got) != 1 || got[0] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("page 3 = %v, want the 道具 page last", got)
	}
	// the pools: WP 3*2+3 = 9, JP 2*2+2 = 6 — both techs affordable
	for _, ri := range []int{1, 3} {
		if rows[ri].Disabled {
			t.Fatalf("row %d disabled, want affordable (%s)", ri, rows[ri].Label)
		}
	}
}

func TestCmdRowsAffordanceGate(t *testing.T) {
	// WP = 1*2+1 = 3: かすみ二段's cost 3 stays payable, 足ばらい's 4
	// disables; JP = 0 disables 術一閃's cost 2.
	e := cmdEngine(t, "02", []int{1}, []int{0})
	rows := CmdRows(e, 0)
	if rows[1].Label != "かすみ二段 (WP3)" || rows[1].Disabled {
		t.Fatalf("WP-affordable row wrong: %+v", rows[1])

		t.Fatalf("足ばらい (WP4) must disable at WP 3")
	}
	if !rows[3].Disabled {
		t.Fatalf("術一閃 (JP2) must disable at JP 0")
	}
	// the cursor skips disabled rows (Godot's focus arrows)
	b := &BattleView{Phase: battleCmds, Mode: modeCmd, current: 0, rows: rows,
		pages: CmdPages(e, 0, rows)}
	b.cursor = b.firstEnabledOn(0)
	if b.cursor != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("first enabled row = %d, want 0 (攻撃)", b.cursor)
	}
	b.Vertical(1) // row 1 affordable
	if b.cursor != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("cursor = %d, want 1", b.cursor)
	}
	b.Vertical(1) // page 0's rows are [攻撃, かすみ二段, 防御]: land on 防御
	if b.cursor != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("cursor over the page = %d, want 5 (防御)", b.cursor)
	}
	// a Confirm on a disabled row is inert
	b.cursor = 2 // 足ばらい, disabled
	before := len(e.Chosen)
	b.Confirm(e)
	if len(e.Chosen) != before {
		t.Fatalf("confirm on a disabled row chose %+v", e.Chosen)
	}
}

func TestCmdTargetFlow(t *testing.T) {
	e := cmdEngine(t, "02", []int{3}, []int{2})
	b := &BattleView{}
	boundary(t, b, e)
	if b.Mode != modeCmd || b.current != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d current %d, want the ally 0 command menu", b.Mode, b.current)
	}
	// 攻撃 opens the enemy-side cursor
	b.Confirm(e)
	if b.Mode != modeTarget || len(b.rows) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d rows %d, want the enemy target cursor", b.Mode, len(b.rows))
	}
	if b.rows[0].Label != "地狼 (500)" {
		t.Fatalf("target row %q, want 地狼 (500)", b.rows[0].Label)
	}
	// Esc returns to the command menu (battle.gd _unhandled_input)
	if !b.Back(e) {
		t.Fatal("Esc on the target cursor must be consumed")
	}
	if b.Mode != modeCmd || len(b.rows) != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("after Esc: mode %d rows %d, want the command menu rebuilt", b.Mode, len(b.rows))
	}
	// ...and the confirm again, this time through: the plain attack with
	// the target cursor's row (the queue drains -> the round begins)
	b.Confirm(e)
	b.Confirm(e)
	if b.Phase != battleRun {
		t.Fatalf("phase %d after the last command, want the round running", b.Phase)
	}
	ch, ok := e.Chosen[0]
	if !ok || ch.Kind != battle.CmdPlain || ch.Target != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("chosen %+v, want the plain attack on enemy 0", ch)
	}
	if e.Round != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("round %d, want BeginRound run", e.Round)
	}
	if e.Enemies[0].HP >= 500 {
		t.Fatalf("enemy HP %d after the round, want the attack to land", e.Enemies[0].HP)
	}
}

func TestCmdDefendAndItemFlow(t *testing.T) {
	e := cmdEngine(t, "02", []int{3}, []int{2})
	e.Allies[0].HP = 60 // room for the item's heal

	}

	// the item: pages 剣 -> 術 -> 槍 -> 道具, so Cycle x3 — the cursor
	// opens on the ALLY side (docs/battle-formulas.md §16.2: every
	// battle item is tech 08 術, range 味方)
	b.roundClock = roundFrames - 1

	}

	b.Cycle(1)
	b.Cycle(1)
	if b.page != 3 || b.cursor != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("page %d cursor %d, want the 道具 page's 傷薬", b.page, b.cursor)
	}
	b.Confirm(e)
	if b.Mode != modeTarget {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d, want the ally target cursor", b.Mode)
	}
	if b.rows[0].Label != "ユリアン (60/120)" {
		t.Fatalf("ally target row %q, want ユリアン (60/120)", b.rows[0].Label)
	}
	b.Confirm(e)
	if b.Phase != battleRun {
		t.Fatalf("phase %d, want the round running", b.Phase)
	}
	ch = e.Chosen[0]
	if ch.Kind != battle.CmdItem || ch.ID != "30" || ch.Target != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("chosen %+v, want CmdItem 傷薬 on ally 0", ch)
	}
	if e.Allies[0].HP != 70 {
		t.Fatalf("HP %d after the item, want 60+10 回復", e.Allies[0].HP)
	}
}

func TestCmdQueueSkipsStatused(t *testing.T) {
	d := cmdData()

func TestPartyWindowEscapeAndFiring(t *testing.T) {
	// two fighters: a solo party's escape would wipe it (the end check
	// counts a fled record as gone), the window pins need the battle to
	// carry on past the escape like t255e's rounds 12 -> 0x14
	d := cmdData()
	a0 := &battle.AllyRow{ID: "00", Name: "ユリアン", HP: 120,
		Techs: []string{"10", "20", "2A"}, WLevels: pad5([]int{3}),
		SpellRaw: []int{0, 0}, GrowthRow: ff16(),
		Equipment: []string{"", "0A", "", "30"}}
	a1 := &battle.AllyRow{ID: "02", Name: "ポーラ", HP: 90,
		WLevels: pad5([]int{3}), SpellRaw: []int{0, 0}, GrowthRow: ff16()}
	d.Allies = []battle.AllyRow{*a0, *a1}
	d.AllyByID = map[int]*battle.AllyRow{0: a0, 2: a1}
	enemy := &battle.EnemyRow{ID: "10", Name: "地狼", HP: 500, AIMode: 20,
		DropCodes: []int{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF},
		Patterns: []battle.Pattern{{Actions: []string{"01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01"}},
			{Actions: []string{"01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01", "01"}}}}
	d.Enemies = []battle.EnemyRow{*enemy}
	d.EnemyByID = map[int]*battle.EnemyRow{0x10: enemy}
	e, err := battle.NewEngine(d, stubWorld{}, cmdRNG{}, battle.Config{
		Party: []int{0, 2}, Enemies: []int{0x10}, Formation: "01"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NewEngine: %v", err)
	}
	e.Fixed = &battle.FixedBattle{Type: 0x12}
	// round 1 disarmed: the fighter windows run normally
	b := &BattleView{}
	boundary(t, b, e)
	if b.Mode != modeCmd {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d, want the fighter windows while the gate sits disarmed", b.Mode)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		b.Confirm(e) // both fighters take the plain attack on enemy 0
	}
	if e.Round != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("round %d, want round 1 run", e.Round)
	}
	// round 2 armed: ($1429&F) 2 > ($1428&F) 0, $53 covers the cost 5
	e.EscapeTarget = 2
	e.PhantomTimer = 0
	e.Res53 = 2
	b.roundClock = roundFrames - 1
	b.Step(e)
	if b.Mode != modeParty {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d, want the commander party window before any fighter window", b.Mode)
	}
	rows := PartyRows(e)
	if rows[0].Label != "逃げる" || !rows[0].Disabled {
		t.Fatalf("escape row %+v, want 逃げる disabled at $53=2", rows[0])
	}
	if rows[1].Label != "行動" {
		t.Fatalf("go row %q, want 行動", rows[1].Label)
	}
	// a Confirm on the disabled escape is inert
	b.Confirm(e)
	if b.Mode != modeParty || b.Phase != battleCmds {
		t.Fatal("the disabled escape must not leave the window")
	}
	// $53 reaches the cost: the escape confirms (docs/battle-menu.md §C:
	// $53 pays 5, $1427 logs it, the command phase ends and the round
	// runs — commander mode has no fighter windows)
	e.Res53 = 5
	b.rows = PartyRows(e) // the gate re-reads on the press (C2:31EC)
	b.Confirm(e)
	// SelectEscape pays the 5 and logs $1427=5; the surviving fighter's
	// default attack then runs ($1427 relogs its cost 0 at C2:B70C) —
	// the paid $53 is the round's observable
	if e.Res53 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after the escape: $53=%d, want the cost 5 paid", e.Res53)
	}
	if b.Phase != battleRun || e.Round != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("phase %d round %d, want the escape to end the command phase", b.Phase, e.Round)
	}
	if len(e.Chosen) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("chosen %+v, want none: the queue cleared", e.Chosen)
	}

	// one firing per round: the same round never shows it twice, and 行動
	// hands over to the fighter windows; a re-armed gate shows it again
	// next round
	e.EscapeTarget = 3
	e.PhantomTimer = 0
	e.Res53 = 5
	b.roundClock = roundFrames - 1
	b.Step(e)
	if b.Mode != modeParty {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d, want the re-armed gate to show the party window", b.Mode)
	}
	b.cursor = 1 // 行動
	b.Confirm(e)
	if b.Mode != modeCmd || b.current != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mode %d current %d, want 行動 to open the fighter windows", b.Mode, b.current)
	}
	if !b.partyShown {
		t.Fatal("the window must not fire twice in one round")
	}
}

```

`internal/game/shell/battleview.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"

	"saga3/internal/game/battle"
)

// The battle screen's shell-side state over the headless engine
// (battle.gd's UI half in its ported scope): the fight collects every
// living ally's command through the interactive windows first (the
// per-ally command menu with the category pager and the affordance
// gates, the target cursor, battle 254's commander party window with the
// escape), then the round's turns and actions resolve headlessly one
// round at a cadence, victory settles for main.gd's 1.8 s, defeat opens
// the wipe window (docs/battle-defeat.md §6 items 1-2: the name-
// substituted 全滅 window advancing on one confirm press, 全滅のテーマ
// under it) and one press ends the battle.

// battlePhase is the screen's state.
type battlePhase int

const (
	battleRun    battlePhase = iota // rounds advance
	battleCmds                      // the command windows collect the round's orders
	battleSettle                    // victory's field-return settle
	battleWipe                      // the defeat window waits for a press
)

// cmdMode is the window battleCmds shows: the commander party window
// (battle 254), an ally's command menu, or the target cursor.
type cmdMode int

const (
	modeParty cmdMode = iota
	modeCmd
	modeTarget
)

// roundFrames spaces the headless rounds (0.75 s each, enough to read
// the engine's message lines); settleFrames is main.gd's 1.8 s timer at
// 60 fps.
const (
	roundFrames  = 45
	settleFrames = 108
)

// CmdRow is one window row: the label with its cost suffix, the command
// it confirms into, and the affordance gate — a disabled row shows dim,
// skips the cursor and ignores Confirm (a Godot disabled button).
type CmdRow struct {
	Label    string
	Pick     battle.Command
	Disabled bool
}

// itemPageKey and the missing-tech key sort the category pages; neither
// is a real tech class byte.
const (
	itemPageKey    = -1 // the 道具 page
	plainPageKey   = -2 // the plain attack's page when the catalog lacks it
	noTargetTarget = -1
)

// BattleView drives and stages one battle.
type BattleView struct {
	Phase battlePhase
	Mode  cmdMode // the active window while Phase == battleCmds

	roundClock  int
	settleClock int
	done        bool // the phase ran out: the shell calls FinishBattle

	// the command collection (battle.gd _start_round's _cmd_queue)
	queue      []int
	current    int      // the ally the open window asks
	rows       []CmdRow // the open window's rows
	pages      [][]int  // the command menu's category pages (row indexes)
	page       int      // the shown page
	cursor     int      // the cursor's row index
	partyShown bool     // the commander window fired this round
}

// Step advances one frame. The engine settles when Over is set — both
// end paths set it (CheckEnd and ScriptedRoundEnd; Finished is
// CheckEnd's own flag, a scripted end never sets it), so Over is the
// only complete condition.
func (b *BattleView) Step(e *battle.Engine) {
	switch b.Phase {
	case battleRun:
		if e.Over {
			if e.Won {
				b.Phase = battleSettle
				b.settleClock = 0
			} else {
				b.Phase = battleWipe
			}
			return
		}
		b.roundClock++
		if b.roundClock < roundFrames {
			return
		}
		b.roundClock = 0
		// the round's command windows first (battle.gd _start_round):
		// the round's orders collect fresh (_chosen = {}), and every
		// living, waking, sane ally is asked; sleep and confusion
		// decay/skip in the engine with the default plain attack
		e.Chosen = map[int]battle.Command{}
		b.partyShown = false
		b.queue = b.queue[:0]
		for i, a := range e.Allies {
			if a.Alive && a.Sleep == 0 && !a.Confusion {
				b.queue = append(b.queue, i)
			}
		}
		b.Phase = battleCmds
		b.askNext(e)
	case battleCmds:
		// the windows wait for input
	case battleSettle:
		b.settleClock++
		if b.settleClock >= settleFrames {
			b.done = true
		}
	case battleWipe:
		// the window waits for Confirm
	}
}

// askNext opens the next window (battle.gd _ask_next_command): the
// commander party window once per round while its append gate arms
// (docs/battle-menu.md §C), then one command menu per queued ally; a
// drained queue begins the round.
func (b *BattleView) askNext(e *battle.Engine) {
	if !b.partyShown && e.Fixed != nil && e.Fixed.Type == 0x12 && e.EscapeArmed() {
		b.partyShown = true
		b.Mode = modeParty
		b.rows = PartyRows(e)
		b.pages = nil
		b.cursor = 0
		return
	}
	if len(b.queue) == 0 {
		// the orders are in: the initiative rolls and the actions run
		e.BeginRound()
		e.RunRound()
		b.Phase = battleRun
		return
	}
	b.current = b.queue[0]
	b.queue = b.queue[1:]
	b.Mode = modeCmd
	b.rows = CmdRows(e, b.current)
	b.pages = CmdPages(e, b.current, b.rows)
	b.page = 0
	b.cursor = b.firstEnabledOn(0)
}

// Confirm presses the cursor's row: the wipe window's confirm, the
// commander window's escape/proceed, a command row, a target row. A nil
// engine answers only the wipe (the shell's smoke injects before the
// engine variable is read).
func (b *BattleView) Confirm(e *battle.Engine) {
	switch {
	case b.Phase == battleWipe:
		b.done = true // battle.gd _wipe_confirmed
	case b.Phase != battleCmds || e == nil:
	case b.Mode == modeParty:
		b.confirmParty(e)
	case b.Mode == modeCmd:
		b.confirmCmd(e)
	case b.Mode == modeTarget:
		b.confirmTarget(e)
	}
}

// confirmParty is the commander window's press (battle.gd
// _show_party_window's buttons): row 0 the escape (gated $53 >= 5,
// C2:31EC), row 1 proceeds to the fighter windows.
func (b *BattleView) confirmParty(e *battle.Engine) {
	if b.cursor < 0 || b.cursor >= len(b.rows) || b.rows[b.cursor].Disabled {
		return
	}
	if b.cursor == 0 {
		// the confirmed 0x56 (docs/battle-menu.md §C): $53 pays, the
		// protagonist's record flees, and the command phase ends — the
		// remaining allies run default attacks (battle.gd _escape_chosen's
		// documented commander-mode stand-in)
		e.SelectEscape()
		b.queue = b.queue[:0]
		b.askNext(e)
		return
	}
	b.askNext(e) // 行動
}

// confirmCmd is a command row's press (battle.gd _on_command): techs and
// the plain attack open the target cursor on the enemy side, the item on
// the party side (every battle item is tech 08 術, range 味方, docs/
// battle-formulas.md §16.2); 防御 confirms without a target.
func (b *BattleView) confirmCmd(e *battle.Engine) {
	if b.cursor < 0 || b.cursor >= len(b.rows) || b.rows[b.cursor].Disabled {
		return
	}
	pick := b.rows[b.cursor].Pick
	switch pick.Kind {
	case battle.CmdItem:
		b.showTargets(e, "ally", pick)
	case battle.CmdDefend:
		e.Chosen[b.current] = pick
		b.askNext(e)
	default:
		b.showTargets(e, "enemy", pick)
	}
}

// showTargets opens the target cursor; a side with no living target
// returns to the command menu (battle.gd _show_targets's empty branch).
func (b *BattleView) showTargets(e *battle.Engine, side string, pick battle.Command) {
	rows := TargetRows(e, side, pick)
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		b.Mode = modeCmd
		return
	}
	b.Mode = modeTarget
	b.rows = rows
	b.pages = nil
	b.cursor = 0
}

// confirmTarget confirms the cursor's fighter (battle.gd _on_target).
func (b *BattleView) confirmTarget(e *battle.Engine) {
	if b.cursor < 0 || b.cursor >= len(b.rows) || b.rows[b.cursor].Disabled {
		return
	}
	e.Chosen[b.current] = b.rows[b.cursor].Pick
	b.askNext(e)
}

// Back is Esc on the battle screen (battle.gd _unhandled_input): only
// the target cursor consumes it, returning to the command menu; the
// shell quits on Esc everywhere else (main.gd's branch).
func (b *BattleView) Back(e *battle.Engine) bool {
	if b.Phase != battleCmds || b.Mode != modeTarget {
		return false
	}
	b.Mode = modeCmd
	b.rows = CmdRows(e, b.current)
	b.pages = CmdPages(e, b.current, b.rows)
	b.cursor = b.firstEnabledOn(b.page)
	return true
}

// Vertical moves the cursor one enabled row up/down within the window
// (Godot's focus arrows ride enabled buttons only); -1 up, +1 down. The
// target cursor does not take the arrows (battle.gd's buttons jump
// focus, the cursor rides the command windows).
func (b *BattleView) Vertical(step int) {
	if b.Phase != battleCmds || b.Mode == modeTarget {
		return
	}
	all := b.windowRows()
	var enabled []int
	for _, ri := range all {
		if !b.rows[ri].Disabled {
			enabled = append(enabled, ri)
		}
	}
	if len(enabled) == 0 {
		return
	}
	pos := -1
	for i, ri := range enabled {
		if ri == b.cursor {
			pos = i
			break
		}
	}
	if pos < 0 {
		b.cursor = enabled[0] // the cursor sat off-page (a Back reset)
		return
	}
	b.cursor = enabled[(pos+step+len(enabled))%len(enabled)]
}

// windowRows is the open window's selectable row indexes: the command
// menu's current page, else every row (the party and target windows are
// single pages).
func (b *BattleView) windowRows() []int {
	if b.Mode == modeCmd && len(b.pages) > 0 && b.page < len(b.pages) {
		return b.pages[b.page]
	}
	out := make([]int, len(b.rows))
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = i
	}
	return out
}

// Cycle switches the category page (docs/battle-formulas.md §16.1:
// Left/Right cycle the categories); the cursor lands on the page's first
// enabled row.
func (b *BattleView) Cycle(step int) {
	if b.Phase != battleCmds || b.Mode != modeCmd || len(b.pages) < 2 {
		return
	}
	b.page = (b.page + step + len(b.pages)) % len(b.pages)
	b.cursor = b.firstEnabledOn(b.page)
}

func (b *BattleView) enabledOn(page int) []int {
	var out []int
	if page < 0 || page >= len(b.pages) {
		return out
	}
	for _, ri := range b.pages[page] {
		if ri >= 0 && ri < len(b.rows) && !b.rows[ri].Disabled {
			out = append(out, ri)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (b *BattleView) firstEnabledOn(page int) int {
	enabled := b.enabledOn(page)
	if len(enabled) == 0 {
		return -1
	}
	return enabled[0]
}

// Done reports the battle presentation finished (the shell then calls
// the flow's FinishBattle).
func (b *BattleView) Done() bool { return b.done }

// ---- the window builders (battle.gd's UI half) ---------------------------

// CmdRows is the ally's command list (battle.gd _show_commands's specs):
// 攻撃 (the equipped weapon's plain attack), the techs by name (a tech
// the catalog lacks drops, as the reference's has() check drops it), the
// equipped 道具 (docs/battle-formulas.md §16; an empty 腕4 hides the
// entry — the port's documented choice over the unusable page), 防御.
func CmdRows(e *battle.Engine, ally int) []CmdRow {
	a := e.Allies[ally]
	rows := []CmdRow{techRow(e, a, e.PlainTechFor(a), battle.CmdPlain, "攻撃")}
	for _, id := range a.Techs {
		if _, ok := e.D.Techniques[id]; !ok {
			continue
		}
		rows = append(rows, techRow(e, a, id, battle.CmdTech, e.D.Techniques[id].Name))
	}
	if it := e.BattleItemFor(a); it != nil {
		rows = append(rows, CmdRow{Label: it.Name,
			Pick: battle.Command{Kind: battle.CmdItem, ID: it.ID, Target: noTargetTarget}})
	}
	rows = append(rows, CmdRow{Label: "防御",
		Pick: battle.Command{Kind: battle.CmdDefend, Target: noTargetTarget}})
	return rows
}

// techRow is one tech command row: the cost suffix "(WP3)" / "(JP2)" and
// the affordance gate — the row is disabled while the pool can't pay
// (battle.gd _show_commands).
func techRow(e *battle.Engine, a *battle.Combatant, id string, kind battle.CommandKind, label string) CmdRow {
	row := CmdRow{Label: label, Pick: battle.Command{Kind: kind, ID: id, Target: noTargetTarget}}
	rec, ok := e.D.Techniques[id]
	if !ok || rec.Cost <= 0 {
		return row
	}
	which, pool := "WP", a.WP
	if rec.JPCost {
		which, pool = "JP", a.JP
	}
	row.Label = label + " (" + which + itoa(rec.Cost) + ")"
	row.Disabled = pool < rec.Cost
	return row
}

// CmdPages partitions the rows into the category pages (docs/
// battle-formulas.md §16.1: the window shows ONE category, Left/Right
// cycles, techs are category-scoped by their class byte). 攻撃 and 防御
// ride the plain attack's class page (パリイ sits on the 剣 page on the
// real machine); a class the plain attack does not share gets its own
// page; the 道具 page comes last. The rows stay one list — pages only
// filter it.
func CmdPages(e *battle.Engine, ally int, rows []CmdRow) [][]int {
	a := e.Allies[ally]
	keys := make([]int, len(rows))
	plainClass := plainPageKey
	if rec, ok := e.D.Techniques[e.PlainTechFor(a)]; ok {
		plainClass = rec.Class
	}
	hasItem := false
	var techKeys []int
	seen := map[int]bool{plainClass: true, itemPageKey: true}
	for i, row := range rows {
		switch {
		case row.Pick.Kind == battle.CmdItem:
			keys[i] = itemPageKey
			hasItem = true
		case i == 0 || row.Pick.Kind == battle.CmdDefend:
			keys[i] = plainClass
		default:
			k := plainPageKey
			if rec, ok := e.D.Techniques[row.Pick.ID]; ok {
				k = rec.Class
			}
			keys[i] = k
			if !seen[k] {
				seen[k] = true
				techKeys = append(techKeys, k)
			}
		}
	}
	sort.Ints(techKeys)
	order := append([]int{plainClass}, techKeys...)
	if hasItem {
		order = append(order, itemPageKey)
	}
	pages := make([][]int, 0, len(order))
	for _, k := range order {
		var pg []int
		for i := range keys {
			if keys[i] == k {
				pg = append(pg, i)
			}
		}
		if len(pg) > 0 {
			pages = append(pages, pg)
		}
	}
	return pages
}

// TargetRows is the target cursor's list (battle.gd _show_targets): the
// living side's fighters, enemies "名前 (HP)", allies "名前 (HP/MaxHP)";
// each row's pick carries the pending command aimed at that fighter.
func TargetRows(e *battle.Engine, side string, pending battle.Command) []CmdRow {
	var rows []CmdRow
	if side == "ally" {
		for i, t := range e.Allies {
			if !t.Alive {
				continue
			}
			pick := pending
			pick.Target = i
			rows = append(rows, CmdRow{
				Label: fmt.Sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", t.Name, t.HP, t.MaxHP), Pick: pick})
		}
		return rows
	}
	for j, t := range e.Enemies {
		if !t.Alive {
			continue
		}
		pick := pending
		pick.Target = j
		rows = append(rows, CmdRow{
			Label: fmt.Sprintf("%s (%d)", t.Name, t.HP), Pick: pick})
	}
	return rows
}

// PartyRows is the commander party window (battle 254 only, battle.gd
// _show_party_window): the decoded escape — the append gate C2:238B arms
// it once per round and the confirm gate C2:31EC needs $53 >= its cost
// byte 5 — plus the proceed entry. The engine window's remaining rows
// come from the undecoded formation-row commands.
func PartyRows(e *battle.Engine) []CmdRow {
	return []CmdRow{
		{Label: "逃げる", Disabled: e.Res53 < 5},
		{Label: "行動"},
	}
}

// WipeText is the defeat window's line (battle text 0x15; battle.gd
// _show_wipe_window, the live shot read ユリアンの...). The protagonist
// record's name stands in for the party.
func WipeText(e *battle.Engine) string {
	name := e.Allies[0].Name
	if pi := e.ProtagonistIndex(); pi >= 0 && pi < len(e.Allies) {
		name = e.Allies[pi].Name
	}
	return name + "のパーティーは全滅した・・・"
}

// StatusLines is the party status window (battle.gd _refresh_status):
// one line per fighter, marks in the engine's order. 守 is the port's
// 防御 marker (the engine's half flag the status window shows while the
// defender's guard holds).
func StatusLines(e *battle.Engine) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(e.Allies))
	for _, a := range e.Allies {
		marks := ""
		if a.Defending {
			marks += "守"
		}
		if a.Confusion {
			marks += "乱"
		}
		if a.Sleep > 0 {
			marks += "眠"
		}
		if a.Poison {
			marks += "毒"
		}
		if !a.Alive {
			out = append(out, a.Name+" 倒れた")
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d/%d WP%d JP%d %s", a.Name, a.HP, a.MaxHP, a.WP, a.JP, marks))
	}
	return out
}

// LogTail is the message window's last n lines (battle.gd's
// RichTextLabel scrolled to its bottom).
func LogTail(lines []string, n int) []string {
	if len(lines) > n {
		return lines[len(lines)-n:]
	}
	return lines
}
```

`internal/game/shell/bgm.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

// The BGM catalog (docs/music.md "catalog.json contract"): track id ->
// ogg file, ok-status entries only (map_view._play_bgm builds its map
// the same way). A track the catalog does not carry — a silent rip, an
// unknown id, or 0 the mute entry — falls back to the field theme 0x21;
// track -1 (no record) plays nothing.

// Track 0x01 is the battle theme (battle.gd _ready plays the same rip
// as data/bgm/battle.ogg) and 0x0A 全滅のテーマ rides the wipe window
// (docs/battle-defeat.md §6 item 2).
const (
	trackFieldTheme = 0x21
	trackBattle     = 0x01
	trackDefeat     = 0x0A
)

// Music is the loaded catalog: the ok tracks' ogg file names.
type Music struct {
	tracks map[int]string
}

// oggName is one catalog row's decode: id, ok-status, ogg file.
type oggName struct {
	ID     int    `json:"id"`
	OGG    string `json:"ogg"`
	Status string `json:"status"`
}

// loadMusic parses data/bgm/catalog.json. A missing or unparseable
// catalog is an error (loud failure): without it no track resolves.
func loadMusic(dataDir string) (*Music, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "bgm", "catalog.json"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load bgm catalog: %w", err)
	}
	var raw struct {
		Tracks []oggName `json:"tracks"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse bgm catalog: %w", err)
	}
	m := &Music{tracks: map[int]string{}}
	for _, t := range raw.Tracks {
		if t.Status == "ok" && t.OGG != "" {
			m.tracks[t.ID] = t.OGG
		}
	}
	return m, nil
}

// fileFor resolves a track to an ogg file name (map_view._play_bgm's
// lookup + fallback): "" = nothing plays (track -1), the field theme
// otherwise stands in for an unplayable id.
func (m *Music) fileFor(track int) string {
	if track < 0 {
		return ""
	}
	if f, ok := m.tracks[track]; ok {
		return f
	}
	return m.tracks[trackFieldTheme]
}

// oggPath is a track's file path under the data dir.
func (m *Music) oggPath(dataDir string, track int) string {
	f := m.fileFor(track)
	if f == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return filepath.Join(dataDir, "bgm", f)
}
```

```go
package shell

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func writeCatalog(t *testing.T, json string) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "bgm"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "bgm", "catalog.json"), []byte(json), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return dir
}

func TestLoadMusicMissing(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := loadMusic(t.TempDir()); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("missing catalog must error")
	}
}

func TestFileFor(t *testing.T) {
	dir := writeCatalog(t, `{"tracks": [
		{"id": 7, "ogg": "07_devil.ogg", "status": "ok"},
		{"id": 5, "ogg": "05_lance.ogg", "status": "ok"},
		{"id": 0, "ogg": "", "status": "silent"},
		{"id": 9, "ogg": "", "status": "failed"}
	]}`)
	m, err := loadMusic(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMusic: %v", err)
	}
	if got := m.fileFor(7); got != "07_devil.ogg" {
		t.Fatalf("track 7 = %q", got)
	}
	// 0 the mute entry and 9 the failed rip fall back to the field
	// theme; this catalog carries no 0x21, so the fallback misses and
	// nothing plays
	for _, track := range []int{0, 9, 99} {
		if got := m.fileFor(track); got != "" {
			t.Fatalf("track %d = %q, want none (no field theme in the catalog)", track, got)
		}
	}
	if got := m.fileFor(-1); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("track -1 = %q, want none", got)
	}
}

func TestFileForFieldThemeFallback(t *testing.T) {
	dir := writeCatalog(t, `{"tracks": [
		{"id": 5, "ogg": "05_lance.ogg", "status": "ok"},
		{"id": 33, "ogg": "21_field.ogg", "status": "ok"}
	]}`)
	m, err := loadMusic(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMusic: %v", err)
	}
	// catalog ids are decimal: the field theme 0x21 sits at id 33
	if got := m.fileFor(5); got != "05_lance.ogg" {
		t.Fatalf("track 5 = %q", got)
	}
	if got := m.fileFor(trackFieldTheme); got != "21_field.ogg" {
		t.Fatalf("field theme = %q", got)
	}
	if got := m.fileFor(99); got != "21_field.ogg" {
		t.Fatalf("fallback = %q, want the field theme", got)
	}
	if got := m.oggPath("/data", 99); got != filepath.Join("/data", "bgm", "21_field.ogg") {
		t.Fatalf("oggPath = %q", got)
	}
}

func TestFileForNoRecordTrack(t *testing.T) {
	dir := writeCatalog(t, `{"tracks": [
		{"id": 5, "ogg": "05_lance.ogg", "status": "ok"},
		{"id": 33, "ogg": "21_field.ogg", "status": "ok"}
	]}`)
	m, err := loadMusic(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMusic: %v", err)
	}
	// track -1 is no record: nothing plays, the field theme stands by
	// only for unplayable ids (fileFor's negative guard)
	if got := m.fileFor(-1); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("track -1 = %q, want none even with the field theme in the catalog", got)
	}
}

func TestBattleAndDefeatTrackIDs(t *testing.T) {
	// the audio wiring's constants: the battle theme is track 1
	// (battle.gd's battle.ogg rip) and the wipe swaps to 0x0A
	// (docs/battle-defeat.md §6 item 2)
	if trackBattle != 0x01 || trackDefeat != 0x0A || trackFieldTheme != 0x21 {
		t.Fatalf("track ids: battle %#x defeat %#x field %#x", trackBattle, trackDefeat, trackFieldTheme)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/camframe.go`:

```go
package shell

// The engine camera (map_view._update_camera, C0:8668-86E8): the screen
// window's left edge is the leader at x - (124 + cam_shift), top at
// y - 116, the leader held inside the follow window (map.json "camera")
// unless the map is open ($D0DD). Pure math; the renderer draws the
// window's pixels at the returned origin.

// viewW/viewH are the SNES screen size in map pixels (tile_layers draws
// at 8 px per tile; the 512x448 window is this at the zoom 2 scale).
const (
	viewW = 256
	viewH = 224
)

// camFollowX is the leader's x offset from the screen's left edge
// (C0:A33F: Controls bit 4 shifts it to 136 — map.json "cam_shift").
func camFollowX(camShift int) int { return 124 + camShift }

// camFrame resolves the window's top-left map pixel for a leader at
// (x, y). cam_shift applies to x only.
func camFrame(x, y, camShift int, bounds [4]int, open bool) (left, top int) {
	fx := camFollowX(camShift)
	left = x - fx
	top = y - 116
	if !open {
		left = clampInt(left, bounds[0]-fx, maxInt(bounds[0], bounds[2])-fx)
		top = clampInt(top, bounds[1]-116, maxInt(bounds[1], bounds[3])-116)
	}
	return left, top
}

// viewRect is the visible map-pixel rect for a camera at (left, top):
// the window's first row shows VOFS + 1 (the Camera2D sits at
// cam_top + 1, map_view._update_camera), clipped to the map's bounds —
// sprites just end past an edge (the wrap copies exist only for pans,
// which the shell does not model). Returns the source rect and the
// destination offset in window pixels (the draw scale is mapdata's
// tile_size / 8).
func viewRect(left, top, mapW, mapH int) (sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy int) {
	sx = maxInt(left, 0)
	ex := minInt(left+viewW, mapW)
	sy = maxInt(top+1, 0)
	ey := minInt(top+1+viewH, mapH)
	sw, sh = maxInt(ex-sx, 0), maxInt(ey-sy, 0)
	dx, dy = sx-left, sy-(top+1)
	return sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy
}

func minInt(a, b int) int {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

func clampInt(v, lo, hi int) int {
	if v < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if v > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return v
}

func maxInt(a, b int) int {
	if a > b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

```

```go
package shell

import "testing"

// The framing pins: the leader at (124, 116) from the screen's top-left
// (map_view._update_camera), the follow window clamps on closed maps,
// cam_shift moves x only, and the window's first row is VOFS + 1.
func TestCamFrameUnclamped(t *testing.T) {
	left, top := camFrame(400, 300, 0, [4]int{0, 0, 2000, 2000}, true)
	if left != 400-124 || top != 300-116 {
		t.Fatalf("camFrame = %d,%d", left, top)
	}
}

func TestCamFrameClamp(t *testing.T) {
	// bounds 136..624 x: the left edge holds the leader inside
	left, top := camFrame(100, 100, 0, [4]int{136, 128, 624, 400}, false)
	if left != 136-124 {
		t.Fatalf("left = %d, want 12", left)
	}
	if top != 128-116 {
		t.Fatalf("top = %d, want 12", top)
	}
	// past the right bound: max(b0, b2) - follow
	left, _ = camFrame(900, 300, 0, [4]int{136, 128, 624, 400}, false)
	if left != 624-124 {
		t.Fatalf("right clamp: left = %d, want 500", left)
	}
}

func TestCamFrameShift(t *testing.T) {
	// Controls bit 4: follow 136 on x, y untouched
	left, top := camFrame(500, 300, 12, [4]int{0, 0, 4000, 4000}, true)
	if left != 500-136 || top != 300-116 {
		t.Fatalf("camFrame shift = %d,%d", left, top)
	}
}

func TestViewRectInside(t *testing.T) {
	sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy := viewRect(100, 200, 800, 600)
	if sx != 100 || sy != 201 || sw != 256 || sh != 224 || dx != 0 || dy != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("viewRect = %d %d %d %d %d %d", sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy)
	}

	// an open map near (0, 0): the window shows past the top-left edge,
	// the draw shifts into the screen
	sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy := viewRect(-40, -20, 800, 600)
	if sx != 0 || sy != 0 || dx != 40 || dy != 19 {
		t.Fatalf("clip: %d %d %d %d %d %d", sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy)
	}
	if sw != 256-40 || sh != 224-19 {
		t.Fatalf("clip size: %d %d", sw, sh)
	}
}

	// the map ends inside the window (sprites just end, no wrap copies)
	_, _, sw, sh, _, _ := viewRect(700, 500, 768, 600)
	if sw != 768-700 || sh != 600-501 {
		t.Fatalf("edge: %d %d", sw, sh)
	}
```

```go
// Package shell is the Ebitengine shell: the window, input, audio and
// rendering around the ported game logic (docs/migration.md). It is the
// only package that imports ebiten; the logic packages (flow, field,
// battle, state, vm, gfx) never do.
//
// Split for the gate: the pure files (mapdata, camframe, bgm,
// battleview, fade, wrap, input's tables) carry the shell's decisions
// and run as plain go test with no display; the render files (font,
// figures, renderer, ui, audio, shell) hold the ebiten calls.
//
// Drawing data contract, from what flow exposes (its doc lists the
// screen state it carries): the leader draws tile-snapped from
// LeaderTile/LeaderFacing, NPCs from the map record list
// (Assets.Map(mapID).NPCs through field.PlacementPasses). The flow's
// live object table is unexported, so figures do not follow the live
// pixel positions and a defeated monster's record still draws — a
// reported interface gap (flow needs a read accessor for the field
// objects); the render follows what is committed, never re-simulates.
```

`internal/game/shell/fade.go`:

```go
package shell

// The arrival fade, simplified (map_view._start_arrival plays the full
// type-1 sequence, arrival_fade.gd — the arrivalcheck digests stay with
// the gfx domain): the shell draws a plain fade-in from black when a
// switch record carries bits, skipped by the record's no-fade bit
// (C0:0A22's skip). A record-less load (save CONTINUE, --map boot) plays
// nothing, like the reference's arrival < 0.

// arrivalDelayFrames is C0:065E's 16-tick hold at black before the
// sequence's colour steps (map_view ARRIVAL_DELAY); noFadeDelayFrames
// the record's bit-7 shape (ARRIVAL_DELAY_NO_FADE, but the shell skips
// the sequence entirely for no-fade records).
const (
	arrivalDelayFrames  = 16
	arrivalFadeFrames   = 28
	arrivalNoFadeFrames = 2
)

// ArrivalFade is the overlay's state across one map load.
type ArrivalFade struct {
	frames int // remaining; 0 = no fade
	total  int
}

// Start arms the fade for a switch record: bits 0x10/0x20 are the
// sequence-less records (C0:C3D9), no-fade records skip the hold, a
// zero-bits record carries no sequence at all.
func (f *ArrivalFade) Start(bits int, noFade bool) {
	f.frames = 0
	f.total = 0
	if bits == 0 || bits == 0x10 || bits == 0x20 || noFade {
		return
	}
	f.total = arrivalDelayFrames + arrivalFadeFrames
	f.frames = f.total
}

// Tick advances one frame.
func (f *ArrivalFade) Tick() {
	if f.frames > 0 {
		f.frames--
	}
}

// Level is the black overlay's opacity 0-255: black during the hold,
// then linearly fading out.
func (f *ArrivalFade) Level() uint8 {
	if f.frames <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	fading := f.total - arrivalDelayFrames
	done := f.total - f.frames
	if done < arrivalDelayFrames {
		return 255
	}
	shown := done - arrivalDelayFrames
	if shown >= fading {
		return 0
	}
	return uint8(255 * (fading - shown) / fading)
}

```

`internal/game/shell/fade_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import "testing"

func TestFadeSkips(t *testing.T) {
	var f ArrivalFade
	// the sequence-less records: no bits, the two type-1 bypasses, and
	// the no-fade bit
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		bits   int
		noFade bool
	}{{0, false}, {0x10, false}, {0x20, false}, {0x01, true}} {
		f.Start(tc.bits, tc.noFade)
		if f.frames != 0 || f.Level() != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("bits %#x noFade %v must skip: frames %d level %d",
				tc.bits, tc.noFade, f.frames, f.Level())
		}
	}
}

func TestFadeHoldAndRamp(t *testing.T) {
	var f ArrivalFade
	f.Start(0x40, false)
	if f.total != arrivalDelayFrames+arrivalFadeFrames {
		t.Fatalf("total = %d", f.total)
	}
	// the hold at black
	for i := 0; i < arrivalDelayFrames; i++ {
		f.Tick()
		if f.Level() != 255 {
			t.Fatalf("hold frame %d: level %d", i, f.Level())
		}
	}
	// the linear ramp down
	last := 255
	for i := 1; i <= arrivalFadeFrames; i++ {
		f.Tick()
		lv := int(f.Level())
		if lv >= last && i < arrivalFadeFrames {
			t.Fatalf("ramp not falling at %d: %d after %d", i, lv, last)
		}
		last = lv
	}
	if f.Level() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("end level %d", f.Level())
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/figures.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"
)

// The ROM field figures (docs/sprites.md; map_view's _rom_figure*):
// data/figures/<fig>/<stem>.png with offsets.json giving each frame's
// top-left offset from the object position, in map pixels. fig is a
// decimal graphic id ("226") or its h-prefixed variant ("h<gid>"); the
// stems are the facings up/down/left/right with walk-cycle frames
// <facing>_<n>. Missing figures draw the colored markers the GDScript
// port falls back to.

// facingStems are the facing names in the runner's dir order (0 up,
// 1 down, 2 left, 3 right).
var facingStems = [4]string{"up", "down", "left", "right"}

// leaderFig is map_view._leader_fig: the protagonist graphic's folder;
// graphic ids 0x70 and up sit in the h table.
func leaderFig(gid int) string {
	if gid >= 0x70 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("h%d", gid)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d", gid)
}

// npcFig is map_view._npc_fig: the event's high byte picks the h table
// (the 0Cxx/4Cxx variant-class records); a malformed event string reads
// as the plain table, the parse error's own shape in the reference.
func npcFig(gid int, event string) string {
	if hb, err := parseHexByte(event); err == nil && (hb == 0x0C || hb == 0x4C) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("h%d", gid)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d", gid)
}

// parseHexByte reads the leading hex byte of an event id string
// ("1862" -> 0x18).
func parseHexByte(ev string) (int, error) {
	if len(ev) < 2 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("event id %q: want four hex digits", ev)
	}
	v := 0
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		c := ev[i]
		switch {
		case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
			v = v*16 + int(c-'0')
		case c >= 'A' && c <= 'F':
			v = v*16 + int(c-'A') + 10
		default:
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("event id %q: bad hex digit", ev)
		}
	}
	return v, nil
}

// figureLib caches the figure folders' textures and offsets.
type figureLib struct {
	dir  string
	sets map[string]*figureSet
}

// figureSet is one folder's loaded frames.
type figureSet struct {
	imgs map[string]*ebiten.Image
	off  map[string][2]float64
}

func newFigureLib(dataDir string) *figureLib {
	return &figureLib{dir: filepath.Join(dataDir, "figures"), sets: map[string]*figureSet{}}
}

// get returns the folder's stem frame and its offset; ok=false when
// the folder or the frame is not exported (the marker fallback). A
// failed load caches an empty set — folders do not appear mid-run, so
// the miss never reloads.
func (l *figureLib) get(fig, stem string) (*ebiten.Image, [2]float64, bool) {
	set, ok := l.sets[fig]
	if !ok {
		set = l.load(fig)
		l.sets[fig] = set
	}
	if img, ok := set.imgs[stem]; ok {
		return img, set.off[stem], true
	}
	return nil, [2]float64{}, false
}

// frames is the facing's frame count (map_view._rom_fig_frames): 1 plus
// the offsets' <stem>_<n> run. A missing folder counts 1 (the marker
// fallback's single frame).
func (l *figureLib) frames(fig, stem string) int {
	set, ok := l.sets[fig]
	if !ok {
		set = l.load(fig)
		l.sets[fig] = set
	}
	n := 1
	for i := 1; ; i++ {
		if _, has := set.off[stem+"_"+itoa(i)]; !has {
			return n
		}
		n++
	}
}

// load reads one folder; an unreadable offsets.json or a folder with no
// decodable frame returns an empty set (the marker fallback's shape,
// like map_view's null texture).
func (l *figureLib) load(fig string) *figureSet {
	dir := filepath.Join(l.dir, fig)
	ob, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "offsets.json"))
	if err != nil {
		return &figureSet{imgs: map[string]*ebiten.Image{}}
	}
	var offs map[string][2]float64
	if err := json.Unmarshal(ob, &offs); err != nil {
		return &figureSet{imgs: map[string]*ebiten.Image{}}
	}
	set := &figureSet{imgs: map[string]*ebiten.Image{}, off: offs}
	for stem := range offs {
		p := filepath.Join(dir, stem+".png")
		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		img, err := png.Decode(bytes.NewReader(b))
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		set.imgs[stem] = ebiten.NewImageFromImage(img)
	}
	return set
}

// loadProtagonists reads figures/protagonists.json (the FE:961B pick ->
// field graphic table): ally id hex -> graphic id. A missing file is
// the export's own tolerance (map_view draws graphic 1, ユリアン); a
// file that fails to parse is an error.
func loadProtagonists(dataDir string) (map[string]int, error) {
	p := filepath.Join(dataDir, "figures", "protagonists.json")
	b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return map[string]int{}, nil
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load protagonists: %w", err)
	}
	var m map[string]int
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &m); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse protagonists: %w", err)
	}
	return m, nil
}

// walkLib loads the select screen's captures (data/walk_sprites/<sub>/
// [<id>/]<facing>.png — map_view's FIGURE_DIR captures, kept for the
// select screen the docs/sprites.md cutouts serve).
type walkLib struct {
	dir   string
	cache map[string]*ebiten.Image
}

func newWalkLib(dataDir string) *walkLib {
	return &walkLib{dir: filepath.Join(dataDir, "walk_sprites"), cache: map[string]*ebiten.Image{}}
}

// get returns the capture or nil when the export lacks it (the select
// screen falls back to the leader captures, then nothing).
func (l *walkLib) get(parts ...string) *ebiten.Image {
	key := joinPath(parts)
	if img, ok := l.cache[key]; ok {
		return img
	}
	var img *ebiten.Image
	if b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(append([]string{l.dir}, parts...)...)); err == nil {
		if dec, err := png.Decode(bytes.NewReader(b)); err == nil {
			img = ebiten.NewImageFromImage(dec)
		}
	}
	l.cache[key] = img // misses cached too; exports do not appear mid-run
	return img
}

func joinPath(parts []string) string {
	p := ""
	for i, s := range parts {
		if i > 0 {
			p += "/"
		}
		p += s
	}
	return p
}
```

`internal/game/shell/font.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"image/color"
	"os"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"
	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2/text/v2"
)

// uiKit holds the CJK face source (the same NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc the
// GDScript port loads at FONT_PATH) and the per-size face cache. A ttc
// is a collection: the shell reads its first face, the face Godot's
// FontFile default also lands on.
type uiKit struct {
	src   *text.GoTextFaceSource
	faces map[float64]text.Face
	white *ebiten.Image
}

func loadFont(path string) (*uiKit, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load font: %w", err)
	}
	r := bytes.NewReader(b)
	var src *text.GoTextFaceSource
	if bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("ttcf")) {
		faces, err := text.NewGoTextFaceSourcesFromCollection(r)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load font %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		if len(faces) == 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load font %s: empty collection", path)
		}
		src = faces[0]
	} else {
		if src, err = text.NewGoTextFaceSource(r); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load font %s: %w", path, err)
		}
	}
	w := ebiten.NewImage(1, 1)
	w.Fill(color.White)
	return &uiKit{src: src, faces: map[float64]text.Face{}, white: w}, nil
}

func (k *uiKit) face(size float64) text.Face {
	if f, ok := k.faces[size]; ok {
		return f
	}
	f := &text.GoTextFace{Source: k.src, Size: size}
	k.faces[size] = f
	return f
}

// metrics returns the natural line height of a size (ascent + descent).
func (k *uiKit) lineHeight(size float64) float64 {
	m := k.face(size).Metrics()
	return m.HAscent + m.HDescent
}

// drawText draws one string with its top-left at (x, y). Multi-line
// strings draw line by line through wrap (text.Draw handles \n itself
// but the shell wraps first, so pass one line).
func (k *uiKit) drawText(dst *ebiten.Image, s string, size float64, x, y float64, c color.Color) {
	op := &text.DrawOptions{}
	op.GeoM.Translate(x, y)
	op.ColorScale.ScaleWithColor(c)
	text.Draw(dst, s, k.face(size), op)
}

// drawCenter draws one line horizontally centered on cx.
func (k *uiKit) drawCenter(dst *ebiten.Image, s string, size float64, cx, y float64, c color.Color) {
	op := &text.DrawOptions{}
	op.LayoutOptions.PrimaryAlign = text.AlignCenter
	op.GeoM.Translate(cx, y)
	op.ColorScale.ScaleWithColor(c)
	text.Draw(dst, s, k.face(size), op)
}

// advanceRange measures a byte range's drawn width within its full
// string (the AdvanceAt prefix difference — prefix shaping keeps the
// whole line's context).
func (k *uiKit) advanceRange(full string, from, to int, size float64) float64 {
	f := k.face(size)
	return text.AdvanceAt(full, to, f) - text.AdvanceAt(full, from, f)
}

// drawRect fills a rect with a color (the 1x1 white stretched through
// the color scale; the StyleBoxFlat corner radius stays undrawn).
func (k *uiKit) drawRect(dst *ebiten.Image, x, y, w, h float64, c color.Color) {
	op := &ebiten.DrawImageOptions{}
	op.GeoM.Scale(w, h)
	op.GeoM.Translate(x, y)
	op.ColorScale.ScaleWithColor(c)
	dst.DrawImage(k.white, op)
}

// panel draws the flat stylebox shape the GDScript overlays share
// (dialogue, menus, the wipe window): bg fill + 3 px border. The
// colors come from the styles' rgba() values.
func (k *uiKit) panel(dst *ebiten.Image, x, y, w, h float64, bg, border color.Color) {
	k.drawRect(dst, x, y, w, h, bg)
	const bw = 3
	k.drawRect(dst, x, y, w, bw, border)
	k.drawRect(dst, x, y+h-bw, w, bw, border)
	k.drawRect(dst, x, y, bw, h, border)
	k.drawRect(dst, x+w-bw, y, bw, h, border)
}

// The overlay palette (main.gd / field_menus.gd / battle.gd styles):
var (
	textWhite    = color.NRGBA{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}
	panelBg      = color.NRGBA{0x05, 0x08, 0x1F, 0xEA} // (0.02, 0.03, 0.12, 0.92)
	panelBgSolid = color.NRGBA{0x05, 0x08, 0x1F, 0xF2} // the menus' 0.95 alpha
	panelBorder  = color.NRGBA{0xC0, 0xC7, 0xE6, 0xFF} // (0.75, 0.78, 0.9)
	textDim      = color.NRGBA{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x80} // the hints' 0.5 modulate
	cursorBlue   = color.NRGBA{0x66, 0xB3, 0xFF, 0xFF} // the naming cursor (0.4, 0.7, 1.0)
	wipeBg       = color.NRGBA{0x02, 0x03, 0x0C, 0xF0}
)
```

`internal/game/shell/input.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
)

// The keyboard map (main.gd's _unhandled_input + map_view._pad's
// shapes): arrows move, Enter/Space confirm, Esc backs (and quits where
// main.gd's Esc branch quit the app), M opens the field menus,
// Backspace deletes a kana, Tab toggles the naming grid. The GDScript
// port binds no WASD; neither does the shell. Shift is the joypad Y run
// bit in map_view._pad — the flow's padOf carries the arrows only
// (flow/keys.go: no consumer pins the run bit), so Shift maps to
// nothing yet.

// keyMap is the pressed-key table the shell feeds flow.Input.
var keyMap = map[ebiten.Key]flow.Key{
	ebiten.KeyRight:     flow.KeyRight,
	ebiten.KeyLeft:      flow.KeyLeft,
	ebiten.KeyDown:      flow.KeyDown,
	ebiten.KeyUp:        flow.KeyUp,
	ebiten.KeyEnter:     flow.KeyConfirm,
	ebiten.KeySpace:     flow.KeyConfirm,
	ebiten.KeyEscape:    flow.KeyBack,
	ebiten.KeyM:         flow.KeyMenu,
	ebiten.KeyBackspace: flow.KeyDelete,
	ebiten.KeyTab:       flow.KeyMode,
}

// keyName names an injected key for the --press spec (smoke tests).
var keyName = map[string]flow.Key{
	"right":   flow.KeyRight,
	"left":    flow.KeyLeft,
	"down":    flow.KeyDown,
	"up":      flow.KeyUp,
	"confirm": flow.KeyConfirm,
	"back":    flow.KeyBack,
	"menu":    flow.KeyMenu,
	"delete":  flow.KeyDelete,
	"mode":    flow.KeyMode,
}

// keyReader translates the live keyboard into flow key events, one per
// newly pressed or released key (the flow keeps the held state; the
// pressed events route to the owning screen).
type keyReader struct {
	held map[ebiten.Key]bool
}

func newKeyReader() *keyReader { return &keyReader{held: map[ebiten.Key]bool{}} }

func (r *keyReader) read() []flow.KeyEvent {
	var out []flow.KeyEvent
	for k, fk := range keyMap {
		if ebiten.IsKeyPressed(k) {
			if !r.held[k] {
				r.held[k] = true
				out = append(out, flow.KeyEvent{Key: fk, Pressed: true})
			}
			continue
		}
		if r.held[k] {
			r.held[k] = false
			out = append(out, flow.KeyEvent{Key: fk, Pressed: false})
		}
	}
	return out
}

// Press is one injected key (the smoke run's pad_override shape): the
// key held from frame Start through frame End inclusive.
type Press struct {
	Key        flow.Key
	Start, End int
}

func (p Press) covers(frame int) bool { return frame >= p.Start && frame <= p.End }

// ParsePress parses a --press spec: name:frame[:end].
func ParsePress(spec string) (Press, error) {
	name, rest, ok := cutAt(spec, ':')
	if !ok {
		return Press{}, fmt.Errorf("bad --press spec %q: want name:frame[:end]", spec)
	}
	k, ok := keyName[name]
	if !ok {
		names := make([]string, 0, len(keyName))
		for n := range keyName {
			names = append(names, n)
		}
		sort.Strings(names)
		return Press{}, fmt.Errorf("bad --press spec %q: unknown key %q (want %s)", spec, name, strings.Join(names, "|"))
	}
	f1s, f2s, has2 := cutAt(rest, ':')
	f1, err := parseFrame(f1s)
	if err != nil {
		return Press{}, fmt.Errorf("bad --press spec %q: %w", spec, err)
	}
	// frames are 1-based: a press starting at 0 never lands
	if f1 < 1 {
		return Press{}, fmt.Errorf("bad --press spec %q: want a start frame >= 1, got %d", spec, f1)
	}
	if !has2 {
		return Press{Key: k, Start: f1, End: f1}, nil
	}
	f2, err := parseFrame(f2s)
	if err != nil {
		return Press{}, fmt.Errorf("bad --press spec %q: %w", spec, err)
	}
	// held whole: an inverted range presses nothing and releases a key
	// that was never down
	if f2 < f1 {
		return Press{}, fmt.Errorf("bad --press spec %q: want 1 <= start <= end, got %d..%d", spec, f1, f2)
	}
	return Press{Key: k, Start: f1, End: f2}, nil
}

func cutAt(s string, sep byte) (string, string, bool) {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if s[i] == sep {
			return s[:i], s[i+1:], true
		}
	}
	return s, "", false
}

func parseFrame(s string) (int, error) {
	if s == "" {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("empty frame number")
	}
	v := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if s[i] < '0' || s[i] > '9' {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("frame %q: want digits", s)
		}
		v = v*10 + int(s[i]-'0')
	}
	return v, nil
}
```

```go
package shell

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
)

// The keyboard map pins (main.gd _unhandled_input + map_view._pad):
// arrows, Enter/Space confirm, Esc back, M menu, Backspace delete,
// Tab mode. No WASD — the GDScript port binds none.
func TestKeyMap(t *testing.T) {
	want := map[ebiten.Key]flow.Key{
		ebiten.KeyRight:     flow.KeyRight,
		ebiten.KeyLeft:      flow.KeyLeft,
		ebiten.KeyDown:      flow.KeyDown,
		ebiten.KeyUp:        flow.KeyUp,
		ebiten.KeyEnter:     flow.KeyConfirm,
		ebiten.KeySpace:     flow.KeyConfirm,
		ebiten.KeyEscape:    flow.KeyBack,
		ebiten.KeyM:         flow.KeyMenu,
		ebiten.KeyBackspace: flow.KeyDelete,
		ebiten.KeyTab:       flow.KeyMode,
	}
	if len(keyMap) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("keyMap holds %d keys, want %d", len(keyMap), len(want))
	}
	for k, fk := range want {
		if keyMap[k] != fk {
			t.Fatalf("key %v -> %v, want %v", k, keyMap[k], fk)
		}
	}
}

func TestParsePress(t *testing.T) {
	p, err := ParsePress("confirm:30")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParsePress: %v", err)
	}
	if p.Key != flow.KeyConfirm || p.Start != 30 || p.End != 30 {
		t.Fatalf("press = %+v", p)
	}
	p, err = ParsePress("right:10:19")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParsePress: %v", err)
	}
	if p.Key != flow.KeyRight || p.Start != 10 || p.End != 19 {
		t.Fatalf("press = %+v", p)
	}
	for _, bad := range []string{"", "confirm", "bogus:1", "confirm:", "confirm:a", "confirm:1:x",
		// frames are 1-based: 0 never lands; an inverted range presses
		// nothing and releases a key that was never down
		"confirm:0:5", "confirm:5:3",
		// frames are 1-based for the single-frame form too: 0 never lands
		"confirm:0", "confirm:0:1:1"} {
		if _, err := ParsePress(bad); err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("ParsePress(%q) must error", bad)
		}
	}
	// the unknown-key error names the valid set (sorted)
	_, err = ParsePress("x:1:2")
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), `unknown key "x" (want back|confirm|delete|down|left|menu|mode|right|up)`) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown-key error: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestPressCoversHoldsStartThroughEnd pins the injection window: the key
// is down on Start and End, up outside (Press.covers).
func TestPressCoversHoldsStartThroughEnd(t *testing.T) {
	p := Press{Key: flow.KeyConfirm, Start: 10, End: 19}
	if !p.covers(10) || !p.covers(19) || p.covers(9) || p.covers(20) {
		t.Fatalf("covers(10..19) = %v %v %v %v, want down on 10 and 19, up on 9 and 20",
			p.covers(10), p.covers(19), p.covers(9), p.covers(20))
	}
}

// TestKeyReaderReleasesHeldKeys pins the live keyboard's release half: a
// key the reader holds (the headless run's stand-in for a real press)
// emits one released event and clears, so the flow's held state drops.
func TestKeyReaderReleasesHeldKeys(t *testing.T) {
	r := newKeyReader()
	r.held[ebiten.KeyRight] = true
	r.held[ebiten.KeySpace] = true
	evs := r.read()
	if len(evs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("read() = %+v, want one released event per held key", evs)
	}
	for _, ev := range evs {
		if ev.Pressed {
			t.Fatalf("read() emitted %+v, want released only", ev)
		}
		if ev.Key != flow.KeyRight && ev.Key != flow.KeyConfirm {
			t.Fatalf("read() released %v, want the held keys only", ev.Key)
		}
	}
	for k, down := range r.held {
		if down {
			t.Fatalf("held[%v] still down after the release", k)
		}
	}
	if evs := r.read(); len(evs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("second read() = %+v, want nothing held", evs)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/livedraw.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"fmt"
	"image/color"
	"sort"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/field"
	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
)

// The live figures (map_view's draw half): every object in
// flow.FieldObjects draws at its live pixel position between the map's
// two layers, the lower one in front (FIGURE_Z + y). Walk figures cycle
// the per-facing frames (<facing>_<n>.png) once per step out of a
// tile-aligned position; op 27 shows the object's pose frame. A
// battle-dispatched slot (docs/field-monsters.md) keeps its figure,
// dimmed to the reference's 0.55 grey; a missing figure draws the
// markers the reference falls back to (leader red, NPC grey, encounter
// red).

// objAnim is one slot's walk-figure state: the frame the cycle shows and
// the position it last drew at.
type objAnim struct {
	frame        int
	lastX, lastY int
	seen         bool
}

// nextFrame is the walk cycle's advance rule (map_view _place_npc): a
// step out of a tile-aligned position advances the frame, wrapping at
// the facing's frame count; a step from a mid-tile position holds.
func nextFrame(a objAnim, x, y, frames int) int {
	if !a.seen || (x == a.lastX && y == a.lastY) || a.lastX&7 != 0 || a.lastY&7 != 0 {
		return a.frame
	}
	return (a.frame + 1) % frames
}

// drawObjects draws every live object between the map's layers, in the
// engine's y order.
func (r *fieldRenderer) drawObjects(dst *ebiten.Image, g *flow.Game, lm *loadedMap, left, top int) {
	objs := g.FieldObjects()
	sort.SliceStable(objs, func(i, j int) bool { return objs[i].Y < objs[j].Y })
	for _, ob := range objs {
		r.drawObject(dst, g, lm, ob, left, top)
	}
}

// drawObject draws one object's figure or marker at its live position.
func (r *fieldRenderer) drawObject(dst *ebiten.Image, g *flow.Game, lm *loadedMap, ob flow.ObjectSnap, left, top int) {
	fig, stem := objectFig(r.prot, g.ProtagAlly, ob)
	// the walk cycle (map_view _place_npc): the frame advances on a step
	// out of a tile-aligned position, whatever the direction
	anim, ok := r.anim[ob.Slot]
	if !ok {
		anim = &objAnim{}
		r.anim[ob.Slot] = anim
	}
	anim.frame = nextFrame(*anim, ob.X, ob.Y, r.lib.frames(fig, stem))
	anim.seen = true
	anim.lastX, anim.lastY = ob.X, ob.Y
	fr := anim.frame
	if ob.Op == 0x27 {
		fr = ob.Frame // the pose instruction's own frame ($D9A4)
	}
	stemFrame := stem
	if fr > 0 {
		stemFrame = stem + "_" + itoa(fr)
	}
	k := lm.k
	img, off, found := r.lib.get(fig, stemFrame)
	if !found && fr > 0 {
		img, off, found = r.lib.get(fig, stem)
	}
	// the screen position: the camera anchors at (left, top+1)
	// (viewRect's VOFS), the figure's offsets.json offset rides in map px
	px := (float64(ob.X-left) + off[0]) * k
	py := (float64(ob.Y-top-1) + off[1]) * k
	if found {
		op := &ebiten.DrawImageOptions{}
		op.GeoM.Scale(k, k)
		op.GeoM.Translate(px, py)
		if ob.Inert {
			// the dispatched slot's figure dims to 0.55 (map_view
			// defeat_monster's modulate) and stays where it parked
			op.ColorScale.Scale(0.55, 0.55, 0.55, 1)
		}
		dst.DrawImage(img, op)
		return
	}
	// the marker fallback: the leader's red square, NPCs grey or
	// encounter red (map_view _spawn_npcs), dimmed when inert
	ts := float64(lm.render.TileSize)
	mx := (float64(ob.X-left) + 4) * k
	my := (float64(ob.Y-top-1) + 4) * k
	c := npcMarkerPlain
	if ob.Leader {
		marker(dst, mx, my, ts*k, ts*k, leaderMarkerOuter, leaderMarkerInner)
		return
	}
	if _, enc := field.EncounterClass(ob.EventID); enc {
		c = npcMarkerEncounter
	}
	if ob.Inert {
		c = dimMarker(c)
	}
	marker(dst, mx, my, (ts-8)*k, (ts-8)*k, c, c)
}

// objectFig resolves the figure folder and facing stem (map_view
// _leader_fig/_npc_fig): the leader through the protagonist pick
// (graphic 1 ユリアン before a pick), NPCs by graphic with the event's
// h table; facings 4+ are their own stem groups (f4...), the leader
// falls back to facing down.
func objectFig(prot map[string]int, protagAlly int, ob flow.ObjectSnap) (fig, stem string) {
	if ob.Leader {
		gid := 1
		if protagAlly >= 0 {
			if v, ok := prot[fmt.Sprintf("%02X", protagAlly)]; ok {
				gid = v
			}
		}
		if ob.Dir < 4 {
			return leaderFig(gid), facingStems[ob.Dir]
		}
		return leaderFig(gid), facingStems[1]
	}
	if ob.Dir < 4 {
		return npcFig(ob.Graphic, fmt.Sprintf("%04X", ob.EventID)), facingStems[ob.Dir]
	}
	return npcFig(ob.Graphic, fmt.Sprintf("%04X", ob.EventID)), fmt.Sprintf("f%d", ob.Dir)
}

// dimMarker grays a marker color to the defeat modulate.
func dimMarker(c color.NRGBA) color.NRGBA {
	return color.NRGBA{uint8(float64(c.R) * 0.55), uint8(float64(c.G) * 0.55),
		uint8(float64(c.B) * 0.55), c.A}
}
```

```go
package shell

import (
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
)

// The live-figure draw rules (map_view's draw half), pinned on the pure
// helpers: the walk cycle's advance, the figure folder's h table, and
// the pose-group stems.
func TestNextFrame(t *testing.T) {
	// a step out of a tile-aligned position advances and wraps
	a := objAnim{frame: 0, lastX: 16, lastY: 8, seen: true}
	if got := nextFrame(a, 17, 8, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("frame after a step = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	a.frame = 3
	if got := nextFrame(a, 16, 9, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("frame wrap = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	// a step from a mid-tile position holds (the cycle advances once per
	// tile, not per pixel)
	a.frame = 1
	a.lastX, a.lastY = 17, 8
	if got := nextFrame(a, 18, 8, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("mid-tile step frame = %d, want held 1", got)
	}
	// no movement holds
	a.lastX, a.lastY = 16, 8
	if got := nextFrame(a, 16, 8, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("standing frame = %d, want held 1", got)
	}
	// the first draw of a fresh slot never advances (map_view seeds the
	// cycle at the spawn position)
	fresh := objAnim{}
	if got := nextFrame(fresh, 17, 9, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh slot frame = %d, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestObjectFig(t *testing.T) {
	prot := map[string]int{"04": 5}
	// the leader follows the protagonist pick, facings 4+ fall back down
	fig, stem := objectFig(prot, 4, flow.ObjectSnap{Leader: true, Dir: 2})
	if fig != "5" || stem != "left" {
		t.Fatalf("leader fig = %s/%s, want 5/left", fig, stem)
	}
	fig, stem = objectFig(prot, 4, flow.ObjectSnap{Leader: true, Dir: 6})
	if fig != "5" || stem != "down" {
		t.Fatalf("leader pose-group fig = %s/%s, want 5/down", fig, stem)
	}
	// before a pick the leader draws graphic 1 (ユリアン)
	if fig, _ := objectFig(nil, -1, flow.ObjectSnap{Leader: true, Dir: 1}); fig != "1" {
		t.Fatalf("default leader fig = %s, want 1", fig)
	}
	// NPCs: graphic with the plain table; the 0Cxx/4Cxx events pick the
	// h table (map_view _npc_fig)
	fig, stem = objectFig(nil, -1, flow.ObjectSnap{Graphic: 75, EventID: 0x1801, Dir: 0})
	if fig != "75" || stem != "up" {
		t.Fatalf("npc fig = %s/%s, want 75/up", fig, stem)
	}
	fig, _ = objectFig(nil, -1, flow.ObjectSnap{Graphic: 12, EventID: 0x4C20, Dir: 1})
	if fig != "h12" {
		t.Fatalf("h-table fig = %s, want h12", fig)
	}
	// facings 4+ are their own stem groups
	_, stem = objectFig(nil, -1, flow.ObjectSnap{Graphic: 75, EventID: 0x1801, Dir: 4})
	if stem != "f4" {
		t.Fatalf("pose-group stem = %s, want f4", stem)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/mapdata.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"saga3/internal/game/gfx"
)

// The render-side half of map.json (map_view.gd's render reads): the
// fields the flow's MapData does not carry — camera bounds, the screen
// registers, tile size, variant layer selection and the chest tile
// stamps. The flow owns the logic-side fields (walk grid, npcs,
// triggers); this file never decodes those twice.

// ScreenRegs is map.json's "screen" row (map_view._screen_regs): the
// $212C-$2132 values with their flag gate. Flag -1 = no gate.
type ScreenRegs struct {
	Flag, Lo, Hi int
	Main, Sub    int
	Sel, Math    int
	Fixed        int
}

// ChestStamp is one map.json chest row's render half (map_view
// _spawn_chests/_stamp_chest): the rect's layer, its closed/open word
// lists and the open flag. Rect is [x, y, w, h] in tiles.
type ChestStamp struct {
	Layer    int
	Rect     [4]int
	Closed   []int
	Open     []int
	OpenLoad []int
	OpenFlag int
}

// Variant is one flag-conditional layer variant (map_view switch_map's
// variant_<n> loop): variant_<i>_tiles.bin replaces tiles.bin while the
// flag value lies in [Lo, Hi).
type Variant struct {
	Index int
	Flag  int
	Lo    int
	Hi    int
}

// MapRender is one map's render-side fields.
type MapRender struct {
	TileSize   int
	CamBounds  [4]int
	Open       bool
	CamShift   int
	Screen     ScreenRegs
	BG3Top     bool
	ScrollMode int
	Chests     []ChestStamp
	Variants   []Variant
}

// loadMapRender reads map.json's render-side fields from the map's
// data dir. Every field defaults the way map_view.gd's get() calls do
// (tile_size 16, screen none, bg3_top true); a missing map.json is an
// error — the flow already reports the same load separately.
func loadMapRender(dataDir, id string) (*MapRender, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "maps", id, "map.json"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load map %s render: %w", id, err)
	}
	var raw struct {
		TileSize int `json:"tile_size"`
		Camera   [4]int
		Open     bool
		CamShift int `json:"cam_shift"`
		Screen   *struct {
			Flag   int `json:"flag"`
			Lo     int
			Hi     int
			Main   int
			Sub    int
			Select int `json:"select"`
			Math   int
			Fixed  int
		}
		BG3Top     *bool `json:"bg3_top"`
		ScrollMode int   `json:"scroll_mode"`
		Chests     []struct {
			Layer    int
			Rect     [4]int
			Closed   []int
			Open     []int
			OpenLoad []int `json:"open_load"`
			OpenFlag int   `json:"open_flag"`
		}
		Variants []struct {
			Flag int
			Lo   int
			Hi   int
		}
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse map %s render: %w", id, err)
	}
	m := &MapRender{
		TileSize:   16,
		CamBounds:  raw.Camera,
		Open:       raw.Open,
		CamShift:   raw.CamShift,
		ScrollMode: raw.ScrollMode,
		BG3Top:     true,
	}
	if raw.TileSize != 0 {
		m.TileSize = raw.TileSize
	}
	if raw.BG3Top != nil {
		m.BG3Top = *raw.BG3Top
	}
	if raw.Screen != nil {
		m.Screen = ScreenRegs{
			Flag: raw.Screen.Flag, Lo: raw.Screen.Lo, Hi: raw.Screen.Hi,
			Main: raw.Screen.Main, Sub: raw.Screen.Sub,
			Sel: raw.Screen.Select, Math: raw.Screen.Math, Fixed: raw.Screen.Fixed,
		}
	}
	for _, c := range raw.Chests {
		m.Chests = append(m.Chests, ChestStamp{
			Layer: c.Layer, Rect: c.Rect, Closed: c.Closed,
			Open: c.Open, OpenLoad: c.OpenLoad, OpenFlag: c.OpenFlag,
		})
	}
	// variant_<n> files are numbered from 0 with no gaps (the loop
	// breaks at the first missing file); a present json names the gate.
	for i := 0; ; i++ {
		p := filepath.Join(dataDir, "maps", id, fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d.json", i))
		vb, err := os.ReadFile(p)
		if err != nil {
			break
		}
		var v struct {
			Flag int
			Lo   int
			Hi   int
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(vb, &v); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse map %s variant %d: %w", id, i, err)
		}
		m.Variants = append(m.Variants, Variant{Index: i, Flag: v.Flag, Lo: v.Lo, Hi: v.Hi})
	}
	return m, nil
}

// tilesName picks the layer file the load draws (map_view switch_map's
// variant walk: the first variant whose gate holds wins).
func (m *MapRender) tilesName(vanilla func(int) int) string {
	for _, v := range m.Variants {
		if vanilla(v.Flag) >= v.Lo && vanilla(v.Flag) < v.Hi {
			return fmt.Sprintf("variant_%d_tiles.bin", v.Index)
		}
	}
	return "tiles.bin"
}

// regs resolves the screen registers for the current state (map_view
// _screen_regs): the map's row while its flag gate holds, else the
// default (both screens on, no math). Scroll mode 2 clears BG3 and OBJ
// from both masks ($D8F5 cleared, FF:687C uploads BG1/BG2 only).
func (m *MapRender) regs(vanilla func(int) int) gfx.Regs {
	r := gfx.Regs{Main: 0x17, Sub: 0x17}
	if m.Screen.Flag >= 0 {
		if v := vanilla(m.Screen.Flag); v >= m.Screen.Lo && v < m.Screen.Hi {
			r.Main = m.Screen.Main
			r.Sub = m.Screen.Sub
			r.Sel = m.Screen.Sel
			r.Math = m.Screen.Math
			r.Fixed = m.Screen.Fixed
		}
	}
	if m.ScrollMode == 2 {
		r.Main &^= 0x0C
		r.Sub &^= 0x0C
	}
	return r
}
```
