`internal/game/shell/mapdata_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/gfx"
)

func writeMap(t *testing.T, dir, id, json string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "maps", id), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "maps", id, "map.json"), []byte(json), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func TestLoadMapRenderDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	writeMap(t, dir, "0001", `{"width": 32, "height": 16, "bgm": 7}`)
	m, err := loadMapRender(dir, "0001")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMapRender: %v", err)
	}
	if m.TileSize != 16 || !m.BG3Top || m.ScrollMode != 0 || len(m.Chests) != 0 || len(m.Variants) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("defaults wrong: %+v", m)
	}
}

func TestLoadMapRenderMissing(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := loadMapRender(t.TempDir(), "9999"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("missing map.json must error")
	}
}

func TestMapRenderFields(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	writeMap(t, dir, "0002", `{
		"tile_size": 16, "camera": [136, 128, 624, 400], "cam_shift": 12,
		"open": true, "scroll_mode": 2, "bg3_top": false,
		"screen": {"flag": 66, "lo": 1, "hi": 3, "main": 23, "sub": 17,
			"select": 2, "math": 64, "fixed": 31},
		"chests": [{"layer": 1, "rect": [10, 8, 4, 2], "open_flag": 5,
			"closed": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], "open": [9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9],
			"open_load": [8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8]}]
	}`)
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "maps", "0002", "variant_0.json"),
		[]byte(`{"flag": 80, "lo": 2, "hi": 4}`), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m, err := loadMapRender(dir, "0002")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMapRender: %v", err)
	}
	if m.CamShift != 12 || !m.Open || m.ScrollMode != 2 || m.BG3Top {
		t.Fatalf("fields wrong: %+v", m)
	}
	if len(m.Chests) != 1 || m.Chests[0].Rect != [4]int{10, 8, 4, 2} || m.Chests[0].OpenFlag != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("chest wrong: %+v", m.Chests)
	}
	if len(m.Variants) != 1 || m.Variants[0].Flag != 80 {
		t.Fatalf("variants wrong: %+v", m.Variants)
	}
}

func TestTilesNameVariants(t *testing.T) {
	m := &MapRender{Variants: []Variant{
		{Index: 0, Flag: 80, Lo: 2, Hi: 4},
		{Index: 1, Flag: 81, Lo: 0, Hi: 2},
	}}
	vanilla := func(flag int) int {
		if flag == 80 {
			return 3
		}
		return 0
	}
	// variant 0's gate holds
	if got := m.tilesName(vanilla); got != "variant_0_tiles.bin" {
		t.Fatalf("tilesName = %q", got)
	}
	// no gate holds
	if got := m.tilesName(func(int) int { return 9 }); got != "tiles.bin" {
		t.Fatalf("tilesName default = %q", got)
	}
}

func TestRegsGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := &MapRender{Screen: ScreenRegs{Flag: 0x42, Lo: 1, Hi: 3,
		Main: 0x17, Sub: 0x11, Sel: 2, Math: 0x40, Fixed: 31}}
	open := m.regs(func(int) int { return 2 })
	if open.Main != 0x17 || open.Sub != 0x11 || open.Sel != 2 || open.Math != 0x40 || open.Fixed != 31 {
		t.Fatalf("gate open: %+v", open)
	}
	closed := m.regs(func(int) int { return 3 })
	if closed != (gfx.Regs{Main: 0x17, Sub: 0x17}) {
		t.Fatalf("gate closed: %+v", closed)
	}
}

func TestRegsScrollMode2ClearsBG3(t *testing.T) {
	m := &MapRender{ScrollMode: 2}
	r := m.regs(func(int) int { return 0 })
	if r.Main&0x0C != 0 || r.Sub&0x0C != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mode 2 must clear BG3/OBJ: %+v", r)
	}
	if r.Main&3 != 3 || r.Sub&3 != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("mode 2 keeps BG1/BG2: %+v", r)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/renderer.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"log"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
	"saga3/internal/game/gfx"
)

// fieldRenderer draws the field: the map's two screen classes through
// internal/game/gfx (the same compositor the tilecheck goldens pin),
// the live objects from flow.FieldObjects between them (livedraw.go),
// and the arrival fade overlay. Camera framing from
// map_view._update_camera.

// loadedMap is one map's prepared render state. Maps reload fresh on
// every switch (the engine respawns everything), so the chest stamps
// re-read the flags at each prepare.
type loadedMap struct {
	id      string
	render  *MapRender
	tm      *gfx.TileMap
	k       float64 // map pixel -> window pixel (tile_size / 8)
	lo, hi  *ebiten.Image
	chestOn []bool
}

// fieldRenderer owns the per-map render state.
type fieldRenderer struct {
	dataDir string
	lib     *figureLib
	prot    map[string]int
	cur     *loadedMap
	anim    map[int]*objAnim // the slots' walk-figure cycles, reset per map
	lastErr string
}

func newFieldRenderer(dataDir string) (*fieldRenderer, error) {
	prot, err := loadProtagonists(dataDir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &fieldRenderer{dataDir: dataDir, lib: newFigureLib(dataDir), prot: prot,
		anim: map[int]*objAnim{}}, nil
}

// prepare loads (or reloads) the map's render state. Errors are loud:
// the caller stops drawing the field and the message prints once.
func (r *fieldRenderer) prepare(id string, a *flow.Assets, g *flow.Game) error {
	mr, err := loadMapRender(r.dataDir, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tm, err := gfx.LoadMap(filepath.Join(r.dataDir, "maps", id), mr.tilesName(g.State.GetVanilla))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tm.Bg3Top = mr.BG3Top
	lm := &loadedMap{id: id, render: mr, tm: tm, k: float64(mr.TileSize) / 8}
	lm.chestOn = make([]bool, len(mr.Chests))
	for i, c := range mr.Chests {
		open := g.State.TreasureOpen(c.OpenFlag)
		lm.chestOn[i] = open
		lm.stamp(c, chestWords(c, open, true))
	}
	if err := r.redraw(lm, mr.regs(g.State.GetVanilla)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// a fresh map respawns every slot: the walk cycles start over
	r.anim = map[int]*objAnim{}
	r.cur = lm
	return nil
}

// redraw recomputes both screen classes through gfx (the SCREEN path,
// colour math included) and uploads them. Chest restamps land here too
// — the hitch is one frame, and the engine's own stamp is equally a
// full-window redraw.
func (r *fieldRenderer) redraw(lm *loadedMap, regs gfx.Regs) error {
	lo, err := lm.tm.Screen(false, regs)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("screen lo: %w", err)
	}
	hi, err := lm.tm.Screen(true, regs)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("screen hi: %w", err)
	}
	lm.lo = ebiten.NewImageFromImage(lo)
	lm.hi = ebiten.NewImageFromImage(hi)
	return nil
}

// stamp writes one chest's word list into the working tilemap (map_view
// _stamp_chest: rect row-major).
func (lm *loadedMap) stamp(c ChestStamp, words []int) {
	w := lm.tm.Width
	for i, word := range words {
		x := c.Rect[0] + i%c.Rect[2]
		y := c.Rect[1] + i/c.Rect[2]
		lm.tm.Words[c.Layer][y*w+x] = uint16(word)
	}
}

// chestWords picks a chest's stamp list: closed, opened-at-load, or the
// mid-session open (map_view's three states).
func chestWords(c ChestStamp, open, atLoad bool) []int {
	switch {
	case open && atLoad:
		return c.OpenLoad
	case open:
		return c.Open
	default:
		return c.Closed
	}
}

// poll re-stamps and redraws when a chest's open flag turned on since
// the last frame (flow.openChest sets the flag; the stamp is the
// shell's draw, map_view refresh_chest).
func (r *fieldRenderer) poll(g *flow.Game) {
	lm := r.cur
	if lm == nil {
		return
	}
	dirty := false
	for i, c := range lm.render.Chests {
		open := g.State.TreasureOpen(c.OpenFlag)
		if open && !lm.chestOn[i] {
			lm.chestOn[i] = true
			lm.stamp(c, chestWords(c, true, false))
			dirty = true
		}
	}
	if dirty {
		if err := r.redraw(lm, lm.render.regs(g.State.GetVanilla)); err != nil {
			r.report(err)
		}
	}
}

// report prints a render error once (the reference's push_error paths
// log and continue; the flow carries its own Diag lines).
func (r *fieldRenderer) report(err error) {
	msg := err.Error()
	if msg == r.lastErr {
		return
	}
	r.lastErr = msg
	log.Printf("shell: field render: %v", msg)
}

// draw composes one field frame.
func (r *fieldRenderer) draw(dst *ebiten.Image, g *flow.Game, fade *ArrivalFade) {
	if g.MapID == "" {
		return // blank map (map_view.blank): the black backdrop shows
	}
	lm := r.cur
	if lm == nil || lm.id != g.MapID {
		return // prepare has not landed yet; the next frame draws
	}
	tx, ty := g.LeaderTile()
	left, top := camFrame(tx*8, ty*8, lm.render.CamShift, lm.render.CamBounds, lm.render.Open)
	left, top = ScreenFXApply(r, g.State.GetVanilla, lm, left, top)
	sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy := viewRect(left, top, lm.tm.Width*8, lm.tm.Height*8)
	if sw <= 0 || sh <= 0 {
		return
	}
	k := lm.k
	op := &ebiten.DrawImageOptions{}
	op.GeoM.Scale(k, k)
	op.GeoM.Translate(float64(dx), float64(dy))
	dst.DrawImage(lm.lo.SubImage(image.Rect(sx, sy, sx+sw, sy+sh)).(*ebiten.Image), op)

	// the live figures between the layers (map_view's draw half)
	r.drawObjects(dst, g, lm, left, top)

	dst.DrawImage(lm.hi.SubImage(image.Rect(sx, sy, sx+sw, sy+sh)).(*ebiten.Image), op)

	if lv := fade.Level(); lv > 0 {
		drawColor(dst, 0, 0, 512, 448, color.NRGBA{0, 0, 0, lv})
	}
}

// marker fills the fallback square (the GDScript ColorRect shape).
func marker(dst *ebiten.Image, x, y, w, h float64, outer, inner color.Color) {
	drawColor(dst, x, y, w, h, outer)
	if inner != outer {
		drawColor(dst, x+w/4, y+h/4, w/2, h/2, inner)
	}
}

var (
	leaderMarkerOuter  = color.NRGBA{220, 60, 60, 255}
	leaderMarkerInner  = color.NRGBA{255, 220, 180, 255}
	npcMarkerPlain     = color.NRGBA{230, 230, 230, 255} // (0.9, 0.9, 0.9)
	npcMarkerEncounter = color.NRGBA{242, 77, 64, 255}   // (0.95, 0.3, 0.25)
)

// fillWhite is the 1x1 stretch base for drawColor.
var fillWhite = ebiten.NewImage(1, 1)

func init() { fillWhite.Fill(color.White) }

func drawColor(dst *ebiten.Image, x, y, w, h float64, c color.Color) {
	op := &ebiten.DrawImageOptions{}
	op.GeoM.Scale(w, h)
	op.GeoM.Translate(x, y)
	op.ColorScale.ScaleWithColor(c)
	dst.DrawImage(fillWhite, op)
}
```

`internal/game/shell/screenfx.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/gfx"
	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
)

// screenfx applies the SCREEN extras the plain redraw leaves out
// (map_view.gd's _tick_* half): the screen-effect waves, BG2's drift
// and walking parallax, the scroll modes' offsets, the 0A/0B bands,
// effect 09 and the graphics animations. The draw loop calls
// ScreenFXApply once per field frame; plain maps take the zero-cost
// path (the pre-rendered lo/hi images stay).
//
// Per-frame state lives here, keyed by map id (loadedMap is the
// renderer's), rebuilt whenever the map reloads. The animation engine
// runs on a private field RNG: the engine shares C0:0733 with NPC
// scripts, which the flow owns, so the chip/palette animations are
// visually right but a 9D43 entry's frame choice can differ from the
// engine's (the exact stream is pinned in gfx's digest tests).
//
// Unported here (reported, not modeled): figures' OBJ colour math on
// the draw calls (gfx.ObjMath is the primitive), the wrap copies past
// the map edge while a pan runs (viewRect clamps to the map), and the
// walking parallax's live speed row (flow-internal; the machine is
// gfx.ScreenFX's and pinned where fixtures allow).

// fxState is one map load's SCREEN extras.
type fxState struct {
	tm    *gfx.TileMap // reload detector (maps reload fresh)
	fx    *gfx.ScreenFX
	anims *gfx.GfxAnim
}

var fxRegistry = map[string]*fxState{}

// fxMapConfig is the SCREEN-side map.json fields the renderer's
// MapRender does not carry.
type fxMapConfig struct {
	Effect     int            `json:"effect"`
	Drift      [4]int         `json:"drift"`
	Parallax   bool           `json:"parallax"`
	ScrollMode int            `json:"scroll_mode"`
	LayerDims  [][2]int       `json:"layer_dims"`
	PalBank    int            `json:"pal_bank"`
	MapType    int            `json:"map_type"`
	GfxAnims   []gfx.AnimSpec `json:"gfx_anims"`
}

// ScreenFXApply ticks one field frame's extras and, when the map
// carries any, re-renders the lo/hi screen classes through
// gfx.ScreenOptsFull. It returns the camera with the pan's offset
// applied and wrapped at the map's pixel size (C0:8752); the draw loop
// uses them for the view rect. vanilla resolves the flag-gated screen
// registers (the flow's GetVanilla).
func ScreenFXApply(r *fieldRenderer, vanilla func(int) int, lm *loadedMap, left, top int) (int, int) {
	st := fxRegistry[lm.id]
	if st == nil || st.tm != lm.tm {
		st = loadFxState(r, lm)
		fxRegistry[lm.id] = st
	}
	if st.fx == nil && st.anims == nil {
		return left, top
	}
	if st.fx != nil {
		if pan := st.fx.Pan(); pan != [2]int{} {
			// C0:8752/87A2: $D6DD/$D6DF wrap while a pan's offset stands
			left = st.fx.WrapCam(left + pan[0])
			top = st.fx.WrapCam(top + pan[1])
		}
	}
	var opts *gfx.ScreenOpts
	if st.fx != nil {
		if st.anims != nil {
			st.fx.Frame = st.anims.Frame
		}
		opts = st.fx.Tick(left, top)
	}
	if st.anims != nil {
		if err := st.anims.Tick(); err != nil {
			r.report(err)
		}
	}
	if opts == nil && st.anims == nil {
		return left, top
	}
	if err := fxRedraw(vanilla, st, lm, opts); err != nil {
		r.report(err)
	}
	return left, top
}

// loadFxState reads the map's extras config and installs the
// animations. A map without extras keeps fx/anims nil (the plain path).
func loadFxState(r *fieldRenderer, lm *loadedMap) *fxState {
	st := &fxState{tm: lm.tm}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.dataDir, "maps", lm.id, "map.json"))
	if err != nil {
		r.report(err)
		return st
	}
	var cfg fxMapConfig
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &cfg); err != nil {
		r.report(err)
		return st
	}
	hasFx := cfg.Effect != 0 || cfg.Drift != [4]int{} || cfg.Parallax ||
		cfg.ScrollMode == 2 || cfg.ScrollMode == 3
	hasAnims := len(cfg.GfxAnims) > 0
	if !hasFx && !hasAnims {
		return st
	}
	if hasFx {
		fx := &gfx.ScreenFX{
			Effect:     cfg.Effect,
			Drift:      cfg.Drift,
			Parallax:   cfg.Parallax,
			ScrollMode: cfg.ScrollMode,
			CamShift:   lm.render.CamShift,
			MapW:       lm.tm.Width,
			MapH:       lm.tm.Height,
		}
		for i := 0; i < 3 && i < len(cfg.LayerDims); i++ {
			fx.Dims[i] = cfg.LayerDims[i]
		}
		if fx.Effect != 0 || cfg.Parallax {
			waves, err := gfx.LoadWaveSet(filepath.Join(r.dataDir, "effect_waves.json"))
			if err != nil {
				r.report(err)
			} else {
				fx.Waves = waves
			}
		}
		fx.Reset()
		st.fx = fx
	}
	if hasAnims {
		scripts, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.dataDir, "gfx_scripts.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			r.report(err)
			return st
		}
		palettes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.dataDir, "rom_palettes.bin"))
		if err != nil {
			r.report(err)
			return st
		}
		anim := gfx.NewGfxAnim(scripts, palettes, rng.NewField())
		anim.BG3On = lm.tm.Present[gfx.BG3]
		anim.Install(cfg.GfxAnims, lm.tm, cfg.PalBank)
		if cfg.MapType == 1 {
			anim.Darken(6)
		}
		if len(anim.Unsupported) > 0 {
			log.Printf("shell: map %s gfx anims: unsupported handlers % X", lm.id, anim.Unsupported)
		}
		st.anims = anim
	}
	return st
}

// fxRedraw re-renders both screen classes with the ticked extras (nil
// opts picks up the animation engine's chr/cgram writes) and swaps the
// drawn images.
func fxRedraw(vanilla func(int) int, st *fxState, lm *loadedMap, opts *gfx.ScreenOpts) error {
	regs := lm.render.regs(vanilla)
	lo, err := lm.tm.ScreenOptsFull(false, regs, opts)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	hi, err := lm.tm.ScreenOptsFull(true, regs, opts)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	lm.lo = ebiten.NewImageFromImage(lo)
	lm.hi = ebiten.NewImageFromImage(hi)
	return nil
}
```

`internal/game/shell/screenfx_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/gfx"
)

// The screenfx wiring's headless smoke: the plain path returns the
// camera untouched (no re-render, no ebiten work), and an extras map's
// state builds with its machines and animation engine installed. The
// extras path's re-render needs a GL context (ebiten images), so it
// runs only in the live shell / xvfb smoke; the renders it would make
// are pinned in internal/game/gfx's tests.

func TestScreenFXApplyPlain(t *testing.T) {
	dataDir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data")
	r, err := newFieldRenderer(dataDir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("newFieldRenderer: %v", err)
	}
	mr, err := loadMapRender(dataDir, "000E")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMapRender: %v", err)
	}
	lm := &loadedMap{id: "000E", render: mr}
	// a state with no machines: the cheap path
	fxRegistry[lm.id] = &fxState{}
	left, top := ScreenFXApply(r, func(int) int { return 0 }, lm, 100, 50)
	if left != 100 || top != 50 {
		t.Fatalf("plain apply moved the camera to (%d,%d), want (100,50)", left, top)
	}
	if lm.lo != nil || lm.hi != nil {
		t.Fatal("plain apply re-rendered the screens")
	}
	delete(fxRegistry, lm.id)
}

func TestScreenFXLoadState(t *testing.T) {
	dataDir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data")
	r, err := newFieldRenderer(dataDir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("newFieldRenderer: %v", err)
	}
	mr, err := loadMapRender(dataDir, "00FD")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMapRender: %v", err)
	}
	tm, err := gfx.LoadMap(filepath.Join(dataDir, "maps", "00FD"), "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadMap: %v", err)
	}
	lm := &loadedMap{id: "00FD", render: mr, tm: tm}
	st := loadFxState(r, lm)
	defer delete(fxRegistry, lm.id)
	// 00FD: effect 3 (the BG3 wave) plus gfx_anims — both machines build
	if st.fx == nil || st.fx.Effect != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("00FD fx state: %+v, want effect 3", st.fx)
	}
	if st.fx.Waves == nil {
		t.Fatal("00FD fx state carries no wave tables")
	}
	if st.anims == nil || st.anims.Installed() == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("00FD anims installed: %d entries, want some", st.anims.Installed())
	}
	if len(st.anims.Unsupported) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("00FD anims: unsupported handlers % X", st.anims.Unsupported)
	}
	// a bare map builds neither machine
	mr2, err := loadMapRender(dataDir, "000E")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("loadMapRender 000E: %v", err)
	}
	tm2, err := gfx.LoadMap(filepath.Join(dataDir, "maps", "000E"), "tiles.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadMap 000E: %v", err)
	}
	st2 := loadFxState(r, &loadedMap{id: "000E", render: mr2, tm: tm2})
	if st2.fx != nil || st2.anims != nil {
		t.Fatalf("000E built extras (fx %v anims %v), want none", st2.fx != nil, st2.anims != nil)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/shell.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/png"
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

// Shell is the ebiten.Game around a flow.Game: input, audio, and the
// per-screen drawing. Construct with New and hand it to ebiten.RunGame.

// Smoke carries the headless run's injection plan (--press, --frames,
// --screenshot): keys held across frames, one screenshot, and the final
// state line the smoke script greps.
type Smoke struct {
	Presses  []Press
	Frames   int    // 0 = run until the window closes
	ShotPath string // non-empty: the run's last rendered frame lands here
}

// Shell implements ebiten.Game.
type Shell struct {
	g      *flow.Game
	assets *flow.Assets
	kit    *uiKit
	snd    *audioSys
	fields *fieldRenderer
	walks  *walkLib
	battle BattleView
	fade   ArrivalFade
	keys   *keyReader
	smoke  Smoke

	lastMapID string // the loaded render's map, "" before the first
	lastTrack int    // the map player's track, -2 = unset
	choiceCur int    // the selection menu's shell-side cursor
	savePath  string

	endImg      *image.RGBA // the last drawn frame, the run-end shot's source
	endShotDone bool

	frame       int
	savedHeld   bool
	loadedHeld  bool
	arrowHeld   map[ebiten.Key]bool
	hadBattle   bool
	wipeBGMDone bool
}

// Config is the shell's wiring.
type Config struct {
	DataDir string
	Font    string
	Save    string
	Smoke   Smoke
}

// New wraps a flow.Game. The loads are loud: a missing font or catalog
// fails the boot, not the first frame.
func New(g *flow.Game, a *flow.Assets, cfg Config) (*Shell, error) {
	kit, err := loadFont(cfg.Font)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	music, err := loadMusic(cfg.DataDir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	fields, err := newFieldRenderer(cfg.DataDir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	snd := newAudioSys(cfg.DataDir, music)
	// the device probe gates the whole audio path (see probeAudioDevice):
	// without a device the context never exists and RunGame never sees
	// an audio error
	if !probeAudioDevice() {
		snd.disable(errNoAudioDevice)
	}
	return &Shell{
		g:         g,
		assets:    a,
		kit:       kit,
		snd:       snd,
		fields:    fields,
		walks:     newWalkLib(cfg.DataDir),
		keys:      newKeyReader(),
		smoke:     cfg.Smoke,
		lastTrack: -2,
		savePath:  cfg.Save,
		arrowHeld: map[ebiten.Key]bool{},
	}, nil
}

// walkSprite is the select screen's capture lookup.
func (s *Shell) walkSprite(sub, id, facing string) *ebiten.Image {
	parts := []string{sub}
	if id != "" {
		parts = append(parts, id)
	}
	parts = append(parts, facing+".png")
	return s.walks.get(parts...)
}

// Update runs one field frame (main.gd _physics_process's wiring): the
// keyboard, the flow tick, the battle drive, then the audio and render
// bookkeeping the outputs drive.
func (s *Shell) Update() error {
	// the run's bound first: the bound's own frame was the last one
	// ticked and drawn, this update only reports and stops — --frames n
	// ticks and renders exactly n frames (ebiten skips the Draw after a
	// Termination return, so the shot must land one update earlier)
	if s.smoke.Frames > 0 && s.frame >= s.smoke.Frames {
		s.reportState("final")
		return ebiten.Termination
	}
	s.frame++
	f := s.frame
	// the smoke injection first: the injected press lands like a real
	// one this frame; a Confirm press during a battle reaches the
	// battle screen (the flow drops keyboard events while one is up)
	for _, p := range s.smoke.Presses {
		if f == p.Start {
			if s.g.BattleUp && p.Key == flow.KeyConfirm {
				s.battle.Confirm(s.g.Battle())
				continue
			}
			s.g.Input(flow.KeyEvent{Key: p.Key, Pressed: true})
		}
		if f == p.End+1 {
			s.g.Input(flow.KeyEvent{Key: p.Key, Pressed: false})
		}
	}
	// the live keyboard
	for _, ev := range s.keys.read() {
		if ev.Key == flow.KeyBack && ev.Pressed {
			if s.g.BattleUp {
				// the battle consumes Esc only on the target cursor
				// (battle.gd _unhandled_input); everywhere else it quits
				// (main.gd's "Esc = quit still works")
				if !s.battle.Back(s.g.Battle()) {
					return ebiten.Termination
				}
				continue
			}
			if s.quitOnEsc() {
				return ebiten.Termination
			}
		}
		s.g.Input(ev)
	}
	// the shell-owned keys (main.gd's F5/F9 branches)
	if s.edge(&s.savedHeld, ebiten.KeyF5) {
		if err := s.g.Save(); err != nil {
			log.Printf("shell: save: %v", err)
		} else {
			log.Printf("shell: saved %s", s.savePath)
		}
	}
	if s.edge(&s.loadedHeld, ebiten.KeyF9) {
		loaded, err := state.LoadGame(s.savePath)
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("shell: load: %v", err)
		} else {
			s.g.State = loaded
			s.g.ProtagAlly = state.SelectRows[loaded.ProtagonistRow]
			log.Printf("shell: loaded %s", s.savePath)
		}
	}

	// the choice cursor rides the arrows while a selection menu waits
	// (main.gd's clickable options; the keyboard navigates and Confirm
	// resolves through flow.Choose)
	if len(s.g.Dialogue.Choices) > 0 {
		if s.choiceCur >= len(s.g.Dialogue.Choices) {
			s.choiceCur = 0
		}
		if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyUp) {
			s.choiceCur = (s.choiceCur + len(s.g.Dialogue.Choices) - 1) % len(s.g.Dialogue.Choices)
		}
		if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyDown) {
			s.choiceCur = (s.choiceCur + 1) % len(s.g.Dialogue.Choices)
		}
		if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyEnter) || s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeySpace) {
			s.g.Choose(s.choiceCur)
		}
	} else {
		s.choiceCur = 0
	}

	// the flow frame
	prevArrival := s.g.Arrival
	s.g.Tick()

	// the battle screen drives the headless rounds; while the command
	// windows are up the arrows ride them and Confirm presses the row
	// (the flow drops presses while a battle is up)
	if s.g.BattleUp {
		e := s.g.Battle()
		if e != nil {
			if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyUp) {
				s.battle.Vertical(-1)
			}
			if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyDown) {
				s.battle.Vertical(1)
			}
			if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyLeft) {
				s.battle.Cycle(-1)
			}
			if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyRight) {
				s.battle.Cycle(1)
			}
			if s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeyEnter) || s.arrowOnce(ebiten.KeySpace) {
				s.battle.Confirm(e)
			}
			s.battle.Step(e)
			if s.battle.Phase == battleWipe && !s.wipeBGMDone {
				s.wipeBGMDone = true
				if err := s.snd.playDefeat(); err != nil {
					log.Printf("shell: defeat bgm: %v", err)
				}
			}
			if s.battle.Done() {
				s.snd.stopAux()
				s.g.FinishBattle()
				s.battle = BattleView{}
				s.wipeBGMDone = false
			}
		}
	}

	// the map render follows the loaded map; the fade plays the switch
	// record's bits (the snapshot read before Tick is the record that
	// caused this load — flow clears Arrival inside switchMap)
	if s.g.MapID != s.lastMapID {
		s.lastMapID = s.g.MapID
		if s.g.MapID != "" {
			if err := s.fields.prepare(s.g.MapID, s.assets, s.g); err != nil {
				s.fields.report(err)
			} else {
				s.fade.Start(prevArrival.Bits, prevArrival.NoFade)
			}
		}
	}
	s.fields.poll(s.g)
	s.fade.Tick()

	// the map BGM follows the flow's track (map_view play_track)
	if s.g.Track != s.lastTrack {
		s.lastTrack = s.g.Track
		if err := s.snd.playMapTrack(s.g.Track); err != nil {
			log.Printf("shell: map bgm: %v", err)
		}
	}
	// the battle theme enters with the battle (battle.gd _ready)
	if s.g.BattleUp && !s.hadBattle {
		s.hadBattle = true
		if err := s.snd.playBattle(); err != nil {
			log.Printf("shell: battle bgm: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if !s.g.BattleUp {
		s.hadBattle = false
	}

	return nil
}

// quitOnEsc reports Esc's quit branch: the app quits wherever the
// GDScript quit — anywhere but the screens that consume Esc (the
// naming's finish, the menus' close, the select's ignore).
func (s *Shell) quitOnEsc() bool {
	if s.g.Screen == flow.ScreenNaming || s.g.Screen == flow.ScreenSelect {
		return false
	}
	if s.g.Menus.IsOpen() {
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// edge reports a key's press edge and tracks it for F5/F9 (the keyMap
// keys already route; these two stay shell-owned).
func (s *Shell) edge(held *bool, k ebiten.Key) bool {
	now := s.keys.held[k]
	was := *held
	*held = now
	return now && !was
}

func (s *Shell) arrowOnce(k ebiten.Key) bool {
	now := s.keys.held[k]
	was := s.arrowHeld[k]
	s.arrowHeld[k] = now
	return now && !was
}

// Draw composes the window: the screen, then its overlays (main.gd's z
// order: menus, dialogue; a battle replaces the field entirely — the
// map scene hides while one runs).
func (s *Shell) Draw(dst *ebiten.Image) {
	dst.Fill(color.Black)
	switch {
	case s.g.BattleUp:
		drawBattle(s, dst)
	case s.g.Screen == flow.ScreenTitle:
		drawTitle(s, dst)
	case s.g.Screen == flow.ScreenSelect:
		drawSelect(s, dst)
	case s.g.Screen == flow.ScreenNaming:
		drawNaming(s, dst)
	default:
		s.fields.draw(dst, s.g, &s.fade)
		if s.g.Menus.IsOpen() {
			drawMenus(s, dst)
		}
		if s.g.Dialogue.Open {
			drawDialogue(s, dst)
		}
	}
	s.dumpShot(dst)
}

// Layout is the 512x448 window (the 256x224 SNES screen at zoom 2).
func (s *Shell) Layout(outW, outH int) (int, int) { return winW, winH }

// dumpShot keeps the run's last drawn frame for FinalShot (ebiten's
// ReadPixels). The buffer is allocated once and re-read every Draw: the
// run's ends (the window close, the Esc quit, the smoke bound) all skip
// the Draw that would write the file, so only FinalShot can.
func (s *Shell) dumpShot(dst *ebiten.Image) {
	if s.smoke.ShotPath == "" {
		return
	}
	if s.endImg == nil {
		b := dst.Bounds()
		s.endImg = image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, b.Dx(), b.Dy()))
	}
	dst.ReadPixels(s.endImg.Pix)
}

// FinalShot writes the run-end screenshot (--screenshot, any run shape).
// main calls it after RunGame returns; the error fails the run.
func (s *Shell) FinalShot() error {
	if s.smoke.ShotPath == "" || s.endShotDone {
		return nil
	}
	if s.endImg == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("screenshot %s: no rendered frame", s.smoke.ShotPath)
	}
	if err := s.writeShot(s.endImg); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.endShotDone = true
	return nil
}

// writeShot encodes one frame, writes it to ShotPath and prints the
// smoke script's grep line.
func (s *Shell) writeShot(img *image.RGBA) error {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	if err := png.Encode(&buf, img); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("encode screenshot: %w", err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(s.smoke.ShotPath, buf.Bytes(), 0o644); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("write screenshot: %w", err)
	}
	px := img.Pix
	mean := 0
	for i := 0; i+2 < len(px); i += 4 {
		mean += int(px[i]) + int(px[i+1]) + int(px[i+2])
	}
	mean /= (len(px) / 4) * 3
	b := img.Bounds()
	fmt.Printf("SHELL-SHOT path=%s mean=%d size=%dx%d\n", s.smoke.ShotPath, mean, b.Dx(), b.Dy())
	return nil
}

// reportState prints the smoke script's grep line.
func (s *Shell) reportState(tag string) {
	tx, ty := s.g.LeaderTile()
	fmt.Printf("SHELL-STATE %s frame=%d screen=%d map=%s tile=%d,%d track=%d event=%s battle=%v\n",
		tag, s.frame, s.g.Screen, s.g.MapID, tx, ty, s.g.Track, s.g.EventID(), s.g.BattleUp)
}
```

`internal/game/shell/shot_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"image"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// The run-end screenshot's contract (--screenshot, any run shape): main
// calls FinalShot after RunGame returns; the run's end skips the Draw
// that would dump, so the last kept frame is the shot.
func TestFinalShotWithoutRenderedFrameErrors(t *testing.T) {
	empty := &Shell{smoke: Smoke{ShotPath: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "end.png")}}
	if err := empty.FinalShot(); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("FinalShot without a rendered frame must error")
	}
}

func TestFinalShotWritesOnce(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "end.png")
	s := &Shell{smoke: Smoke{ShotPath: path}, endImg: image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 4, 2))}
	if err := s.FinalShot(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FinalShot: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("no screenshot written: %v", err)
	}
	// the once-guard holds after the write (a retry writes nothing)
	s.endImg = nil
	if err := s.FinalShot(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("second FinalShot: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestFinalShotNoopWithoutShotPath(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Shell{smoke: Smoke{}}
	if err := s.FinalShot(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FinalShot without ShotPath: %v", err)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/smoke_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

// The smoke run's shell-level wiring over a real flow.Game: the F5/F9
// edge, the --press injection frames (press on Start, release on End+1)
// and the walk they drive. The exports skip like the flow suite's
// (testhelpers_test.go).

var (
	smokeAssetsOnce sync.Once
	smokeAssets     *flow.Assets
	smokeAssetsErr  error
)

func smokeDataDir() string { return filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "exports", "data") }

func smokeAssetsLoad(t *testing.T) *flow.Assets {
	t.Helper()
	smokeAssetsOnce.Do(func() {
		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(smokeDataDir(), "events.json")); err != nil {
			smokeAssetsErr = err
			return
		}
		smokeAssets, smokeAssetsErr = flow.LoadAssets(smokeDataDir())
	})
	if smokeAssetsErr != nil {
		t.Skipf("exports/data exports not available: %v", smokeAssetsErr)
	}
	return smokeAssets
}

// smokeFieldGame boots the field the battle suite enters (0049 at 24,51).
func smokeFieldGame(t *testing.T) *flow.Game {
	t.Helper()
	a := smokeAssetsLoad(t)
	gs := state.NewGameState()
	if err := gs.SetupNewGame(a.Allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g := flow.New(a, gs, t.TempDir()+"/save.json")
	if err := g.EnterField("0049", 24, 51); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("EnterField: %v", err)
	}
	return g
}

// newSmokeShell wires the shell for Update-level headless runs: the real
// field renderer, an empty music catalog (no track resolves, so the
// audio path never touches a device).
func newSmokeShell(t *testing.T, g *flow.Game, presses []Press) *Shell {
	t.Helper()
	dir := smokeDataDir()
	fields, err := newFieldRenderer(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("newFieldRenderer: %v", err)
	}
	return &Shell{
		g:         g,
		assets:    smokeAssetsLoad(t),
		fields:    fields,
		walks:     newWalkLib(dir),
		keys:      newKeyReader(),
		snd:       newAudioSys(dir, &Music{tracks: map[int]string{}}),
		lastTrack: -2,
		arrowHeld: map[ebiten.Key]bool{},
		smoke:     Smoke{Presses: presses},
	}
}

// TestSaveLoadEdgeFiresOncePerPress pins the shell-owned F5/F9 edge: one
// fire per press, held keys stay silent (main.gd's F5/F9 branches).
func TestSaveLoadEdgeFiresOncePerPress(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Shell{keys: newKeyReader()}
	s.keys.held[ebiten.KeyF5] = true
	if !s.edge(&s.savedHeld, ebiten.KeyF5) {
		t.Fatal("F5 press must fire the save edge")
	}
	if s.edge(&s.savedHeld, ebiten.KeyF5) {
		t.Fatal("a held F5 must not fire again")
	}
	s.keys.held[ebiten.KeyF5] = false
	if s.edge(&s.savedHeld, ebiten.KeyF5) {
		t.Fatal("a released F5 must not fire")
	}
	s.keys.held[ebiten.KeyF5] = true
	if !s.edge(&s.savedHeld, ebiten.KeyF5) {
		t.Fatal("a re-pressed F5 must fire again")
	}
}

// TestSmokePressInjectsOnItsStartFrame pins the injection frame: the
// press lands on its Start frame exactly (the smoke script's frame
// accounting), here the field menus open on the M press.
func TestSmokePressInjectsOnItsStartFrame(t *testing.T) {
	g := smokeFieldGame(t)
	s := newSmokeShell(t, g, []Press{{Key: flow.KeyMenu, Start: 3, End: 3}})
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		if err := s.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("update %d: %v", i+1, err)
		}
	}
	if !g.Menus.IsOpen() {
		t.Fatal("the field menus must be open at the press's Start frame")
	}
}

// TestSmokePressReleaseEndsTheWalk pins the release frame: the key
// releases on End+1, so the walk stops there (the smoke script's
// pad_override shape; a press that never releases walks on).
func TestSmokePressReleaseEndsTheWalk(t *testing.T) {
	g := smokeFieldGame(t)
	s := newSmokeShell(t, g, []Press{{Key: flow.KeyRight, Start: 2, End: 10}})
	if err := s.Update(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("update 1: %v", err)
	}
	x0, y0 := g.LeaderTile()
	for i := 1; i < 11; i++ {
		if err := s.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("update %d: %v", i+1, err)
		}
	}
	xHeld, yHeld := g.LeaderTile()
	if xHeld <= x0 || yHeld != y0 {
		t.Fatalf("held walk = (%d,%d) -> (%d,%d), want eastward", x0, y0, xHeld, yHeld)
	}
	// the release landed in update 11: the step in flight completes (the
	// field trail's own rule), then the walk stops for good
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if err := s.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("update %d: %v", 11+i+1, err)
		}
	}
	xEnd, yEnd := g.LeaderTile()
	for i := 0; i < 12; i++ {
		if err := s.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("update %d: %v", 19+i+1, err)
		}
	}
	if x, y := g.LeaderTile(); x != xEnd || y != yEnd {
		t.Fatalf("leader walked on after the release: (%d,%d) -> (%d,%d)", xEnd, yEnd, x, y)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/shell/ui.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"image/color"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"saga3/internal/game/flow"
	"saga3/internal/game/state"
)

// The screens the shell draws over the flow's state (main.gd's shapes
// kept where the GDScript pins them: panel geometry, font sizes, the
// title/select/naming layouts; the corner radii stay undrawn).

const (
	winW = 512
	winH = 448

	// the dialogue panel (main.gd _build_ui: viewport.x-40 x 150 at
	// (20, viewport.y-170), margin 12, font 16)
	dlgX, dlgY, dlgW, dlgH = 20.0, 278.0, 472.0, 150.0
	dlgMargin              = 15.0 // border 3 + margin 12
	dlgFont                = 16.0
	choiceFont             = 14.0

	// the menus panel (field_menus.gd open: viewport-Vector2(48, 40) at
	// (24, 20), font 14 for the tabs, 13 for the lists)
	menuX, menuY, menuW, menuH = 24.0, 20.0, 464.0, 408.0
	menuFont                   = 13.0
	tabFont                    = 14.0

	titleFont = 20.0
	rowFont   = 14.0
	bigFont   = 24.0 // the battle log
	statFont  = 20.0 // the battle status
)

// drawDialogue draws the dialogue box over an open event page (main.gd
// _build_ui + _show_page's segment reveal) and the pending selection
// menu with the shell's cursor.
func drawDialogue(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	k := s.kit
	k.panel(dst, dlgX, dlgY, dlgW, dlgH, panelBg, panelBorder)
	page := shownText(s.g.Dialogue.Segments, s.g.Dialogue.Shown)
	innerX := dlgX + dlgMargin
	innerW := dlgW - 2*dlgMargin
	lines := wrapLines(page, innerW-float64(8), func(full string, from, to int) float64 { return k.advanceRange(full, from, to, dlgFont) })
	y := dlgY + dlgMargin + 2
	for _, ln := range lines {
		k.drawText(dst, ln, dlgFont, innerX, y, textWhite)
		y += k.lineHeight(dlgFont)
	}
	if n := len(s.g.Dialogue.Choices); n > 0 {
		cx := dlgX + dlgW - 170
		cy := dlgY + dlgMargin
		for i, opt := range s.g.Dialogue.Choices {
			mark := "  "
			c := textWhite
			if i == s.choiceCur {
				mark = "> "
				c = cursorBlue
			}
			k.drawText(dst, mark+opt, choiceFont, cx, cy, c)
			cy += k.lineHeight(choiceFont) + 2
		}
	}
}

// drawMenus draws the field menus' two tabs (field_menus.gd open's
// layout: the 狀態 list + page, the 道具 list).
func drawMenus(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	k := s.kit
	k.panel(dst, menuX, menuY, menuW, menuH, panelBgSolid, panelBorder)
	m := &s.g.Menus
	tabY := menuY + 14
	for i, name := range flow.MenuTabs {
		c := textWhite
		if i != m.Tab() {
			c = textDim
		}
		k.drawText(dst, name, tabFont, menuX+16+float64(i)*80, tabY, c)
	}
	k.drawRect(dst, menuX+8, tabY+tabFont+6, menuW-16, 2, panelBorder)
	listX := menuX + 16
	listY := tabY + tabFont + 16
	lh := k.lineHeight(menuFont) + 4
	switch m.Tab() {
	case 0:
		for i, a := range m.Allies() {
			mark := "   "
			c := textWhite
			if i == m.AllyIndex() {
				mark = "> "
				c = cursorBlue
			}
			k.drawText(dst, mark+a.Name, menuFont, listX, listY+float64(i)*lh, c)
		}
		pageX := menuX + 150
		if i := m.AllyIndex(); i < len(m.Allies()) {
			a := m.Allies()[i]
			k.drawText(dst, a.Name, tabFont, pageX, listY, textWhite)
			k.drawText(dst, "HP", menuFont, pageX, listY+30, textDim)
			k.drawText(dst, itoa(a.HP), menuFont, pageX+30, listY+30, textWhite)
			k.drawText(dst, "LP", menuFont, pageX+90, listY+30, textDim)
			k.drawText(dst, itoa(a.LP), menuFont, pageX+120, listY+30, textWhite)
		}
	case 1:
		for i, it := range m.Items() {
			mark := "   "
			c := textWhite
			if i == m.ItemIndex() {
				mark = "> "
				c = cursorBlue
			}
			k.drawText(dst, mark+it.Name+"  ×"+itoa(it.Count), menuFont, listX, listY+float64(i)*lh, c)
		}
	}
}

// drawTitle draws the title screen (main.gd _show_title: black, the
// game name, then the two rows with the cursor).
func drawTitle(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	dst.Fill(color.Black)
	k := s.kit
	cy := 190.0
	k.drawCenter(dst, "Romancing SaGa 3", titleFont, winW/2, cy, textWhite)
	cy += k.lineHeight(titleFont) + 24
	for i, row := range flow.TitleRows {
		text := "  " + row
		if i == s.g.TitleRow {
			text = "> " + row
		}
		k.drawCenter(dst, text, rowFont, winW/2, cy, textWhite)
		cy += k.lineHeight(rowFont) + 4
	}
}

// drawSelect draws the character select (select_screen.gd _ready: the
// header, then one figure + name per candidate; the picked row bright,
// the rest dimmed to 0.6).
func drawSelect(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	dst.Fill(color.Black)
	k := s.kit
	k.drawCenter(dst, flow.SelectHeader, 16, winW/2, 20, textWhite)
	y := 54.0
	for row, ally := range state.SelectRows {
		name := s.assets.AllyName(ally)
		if name == "" {
			name = hex2(ally)
		}
		selected := row == s.g.SelectRow
		drawSelectFigure(s, dst, ally, selected, winW/2-120, y)
		label := "   " + name
		if selected {
			label = "> " + name
		}
		c := textWhite
		if !selected {
			c = color.NRGBA{0x99, 0x99, 0x99, 0xFF}
		}
		k.drawText(dst, label, rowFont, winW/2-80, y+16, c)
		y += 48
	}
}

// drawSelectFigure draws the candidate's capture
// (walk_sprites/protagonist/<ally hex>/down.png, the leader captures
// the fallback — select_screen.gd _figure_texture); no export, no
// figure.
func drawSelectFigure(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image, ally int, selected bool, x, y float64) {
	img := s.walkSprite("protagonist", hex2(ally), "down")
	if img == nil {
		img = s.walkSprite("leader", "", "down")
	}
	if img == nil {
		return
	}
	op := &ebiten.DrawImageOptions{}
	op.GeoM.Scale(32.0/16.0, 48.0/24.0)
	op.GeoM.Translate(x, y)
	if !selected {
		op.ColorScale.Scale(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 1)
	}
	dst.DrawImage(img, op)
}

// namingGrid returns the kana grid the window draws (naming_screen.gd
// HIRA_GRID/KATA_GRID, docs/naming.md "Grid"). The flow's input-model
// copy is unexported, so the shell keeps its own data copy of the same
// constant — a divergence here is a drawing bug only, the input path
// reads the flow's grid.
func namingGrid(katakana bool) [][]string {
	if katakana {
		return kataGridDraw
	}
	return hiraGridDraw
}

// drawNaming draws the name entry screen (naming_screen.gd _ready: the
// header, buffer, mode row, grid, 終了, hint).
func drawNaming(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	dst.Fill(color.Black)
	k := s.kit
	nrow, ncol, onEnd := s.g.NamingCursor()
	grid := namingGrid(s.g.NamingKatakana())
	cy := 34.0
	k.drawCenter(dst, flow.NamingHeader, 16, winW/2, cy, textWhite)
	cy += 30
	k.drawCenter(dst, s.g.NamingBuffer()+"_", 18, winW/2, cy, textWhite)
	cy += 34
	modeX := winW/2 - 60.0
	c := textWhite
	if s.g.NamingKatakana() {
		c = textDim
	}
	k.drawText(dst, "ひらがな", 13, modeX, cy, c)
	c = textDim
	if s.g.NamingKatakana() {
		c = textWhite
	}
	k.drawText(dst, "カタカナ", 13, modeX+80, cy, c)
	cy += 30
	for r, cells := range grid {
		for cI, cell := range cells {
			x := winW/2 - float64(len(cells))*14 + float64(cI)*28
			if cell == "" {
				k.drawText(dst, "　", 14, x, cy+float64(r)*24, textDim)
				continue
			}
			cc := textWhite
			if !onEnd && r == nrow && cI == ncol {
				cc = cursorBlue
			}
			k.drawText(dst, cell, 14, x, cy+float64(r)*24, cc)
		}
	}
	cy += float64(len(grid))*24 + 10
	cc := textWhite
	if onEnd {
		cc = cursorBlue
	}
	k.drawCenter(dst, "終了", 14, winW/2, cy, cc)
	k.drawCenter(dst, "Backspace: 1文字消す   Esc: 終了   Tab: ひらがな/カタカナ", 11, winW/2, cy+30, textDim)
}

// drawBattle draws the battle screen (battle.gd's UI half): the message
// log, the party status window, and the wipe window when defeat
// settles.
func drawBattle(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	k := s.kit
	e := s.g.Battle()
	if e == nil {
		return
	}
	lh := k.lineHeight(bigFont)
	y := 40.0
	for _, ln := range wrapLinesN(s, LogTail(e.Log, 9), bigFont, 432) {
		k.drawText(dst, ln, bigFont, 40, y, textWhite)
		y += lh + 4
	}
	y = 40.0
	for _, ln := range StatusLines(e) {
		k.drawText(dst, ln, statFont, 112, y, textWhite)
		y += k.lineHeight(statFont) + 6
	}
	if s.battle.Phase == battleWipe {
		k.panel(dst, 96, 170, 320, 120, wipeBg, panelBorder)
		text := wrapLines(WipeText(e), 280, func(full string, from, to int) float64 { return k.advanceRange(full, from, to, dlgFont) })
		ty := 182.0
		for _, ln := range text {
			k.drawCenter(dst, ln, dlgFont, 256, ty, textWhite)
			ty += k.lineHeight(dlgFont) + 2
		}
		k.drawRect(dst, 216, 250, 80, 28, panelBorder)
		k.drawCenter(dst, "進む", rowFont, 256, 258, textWhite)
	}
	if s.battle.Phase == battleCmds {
		drawBattleWindows(s, dst)
	}
}

// drawBattleWindows draws the active command window (battle.gd
// _build_ui's _commands geometry: (40, viewport.y-260) 500x240): the
// commander party window, the ally's command page, or the target
// cursor; the cursor rides the rows, disabled rows dim.
func drawBattleWindows(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image) {
	k := s.kit
	k.panel(dst, 40, 188, 500, 240, panelBgSolid, panelBorder)
	x, y := 60.0, 204.0
	lh := k.lineHeight(rowFont) + 6
	rows := s.battle.rows
	if s.battle.Mode == modeCmd && s.battle.page < len(s.battle.pages) {
		// one page at a time: draw its rows in the list's order
		for i, ri := range s.battle.pages[s.battle.page] {
			drawCmdRow(s, dst, rows[ri], ri == s.battle.cursor, x, y+float64(i)*lh)
		}
		return
	}
	for i, row := range rows {
		drawCmdRow(s, dst, row, i == s.battle.cursor, x, y+float64(i)*lh)
	}
}

// drawCmdRow draws one window row: the cursor mark on the selected row,
// disabled rows dim (Godot's disabled button).
func drawCmdRow(s *Shell, dst *ebiten.Image, row CmdRow, selected bool, x, y float64) {
	mark, c := "  ", textWhite
	if selected {
		mark, c = "> ", cursorBlue
	} else if row.Disabled {
		c = textDim
	}
	s.kit.drawText(dst, mark+row.Label, rowFont, x, y, c)
}

// wrapLinesN wraps each log line at the window width.
func wrapLinesN(s *Shell, lines []string, size float64, w float64) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, ln := range lines {
		out = append(out, wrapLines(ln, w, func(full string, from, to int) float64 { return s.kit.advanceRange(full, from, to, size) })...)
	}
	return out
}

// itoa is strconv for the few UI numbers, without the import per call
// site (fmt's allocations buy nothing here).
func itoa(v int) string {
	if v == 0 {
		return "0"
	}
	neg := v < 0
	if neg {
		v = -v
	}
	var b [20]byte
	i := len(b)
	for v > 0 {
		i--
		b[i] = byte('0' + v%10)
		v /= 10
	}
	if neg {
		i--
		b[i] = '-'
	}
	return string(b[i:])
}

// hex2 formats an ally id as its two hex digits ("%02X").
func hex2(v int) string {
	const digits = "0123456789ABCDEF"
	return string([]byte{digits[(v>>4)&0xF], digits[v&0xF]})
}
```

`internal/game/shell/wrap.go`:

```go
package shell

import "strings"

// Line wrap for the dialogue box: RichTextLabel wraps the page at the
// panel width automatically; text/v2 draws one line only, so the shell
// wraps by measuring. advance(full, from, to) returns the drawn width
// of full's bytes [from, to) — the caller passes the AdvanceAt prefix
// difference (Advance's own deprecation points at prefix shaping; the
// difference of two shaped prefixes keeps the full line's context).

// wrapLines breaks s at rune boundaries so every line's advance stays
// within maxWidth; an explicit \n always breaks. An overlong run of
// non-breaking text splits at the width (no break opportunities exist
// in CJK pages without spaces).
func wrapLines(s string, maxWidth float64, advance func(full string, from, to int) float64) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, para := range strings.Split(s, "\n") {
		if para == "" {
			out = append(out, "")
			continue
		}
		runes := []rune(para)
		start := 0
		for start < len(runes) {
			end := len(runes)
			from := runeByteIndex(runes, start)
			for end > start+1 && advance(para, from, runeByteIndex(runes, end)) > maxWidth {
				end--
			}
			out = append(out, string(runes[start:end]))
			start = end
		}
	}
	return out
}

// runeByteIndex is the byte offset of rune index i in the rune slice's
// source string (AdvanceAt measures byte prefixes).
func runeByteIndex(runes []rune, i int) int {
	n := 0
	for k := 0; k < i; k++ {
		n += len(string(runes[k]))
	}
	return n
}

// shownText is the dialogue page's visible text at a given segment
// count (main.gd's segment reveal; the flow splits the page on the op-2C
// marks and counts the shown segments).
func shownText(segments []string, shown int) string {
	if shown > len(segments) {
		shown = len(segments)
	}
	return strings.Join(segments[:shown], "")
}

```

`internal/game/shell/wrap_test.go`:

```go
package shell

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// advanceRuns measures a byte range as one pixel per rune (the fake
// advance for the shape tests; the real path is the AdvanceAt prefix
// difference).
func advanceRuns(full string, from, to int) float64 {
	return float64(len([]rune(full[from:to])))
}

func TestWrapLinesBreaks(t *testing.T) {
	got := wrapLines("あいうえおかきくけこ", 4, advanceRuns)
	want := []string{"あいうえ", "おかきく", "けこ"}
	if strings.Join(got, "|") != strings.Join(want, "|") {
		t.Fatalf("wrap = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestWrapLinesExplicitBreaks(t *testing.T) {
	got := wrapLines("あい\n\nう", 10, advanceRuns)
	want := []string{"あい", "", "う"}
	if strings.Join(got, "|") != strings.Join(want, "|") {
		t.Fatalf("wrap = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestWrapLinesNoBreakOpportunity(t *testing.T) {
	// a single rune wider than the box still draws (the loop keeps one)
	got := wrapLines("あ", 0, advanceRuns)
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0] != "あ" {
		t.Fatalf("wrap = %v", got)
	}
}

func TestWrapLinesMultiByte(t *testing.T) {
	// the measuring walks byte offsets over 3-byte runes
	got := wrapLines("ああああ", 3, advanceRuns)
	if len(got) != 2 || got[0] != "あああ" || got[1] != "あ" {
		t.Fatalf("wrap = %v", got)
	}
}

func TestShownText(t *testing.T) {
	segs := []string{"第一段落。", "第二段落。"}
	if got := shownText(segs, 1); got != "第一段落。" {
		t.Fatalf("shown 1 = %q", got)
	}
	if got := shownText(segs, 2); got != "第一段落。第二段落。" {
		t.Fatalf("shown 2 = %q", got)
	}
	// over the count clamps (the choices page shows whole)
	if got := shownText(segs, 9); got != "第一段落。第二段落。" {
		t.Fatalf("shown 9 = %q", got)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/state/doc.go`:

```go
// Package state is the game state for the event VM: the flag/variable
// spaces the gates read and the writers mutate, plus the runtime party,
// inventory, gold and equipment state events, menus and the save file
// touch. Translated from godot/game_state.gd (436 lines) and
// godot/save_manager.gd (131 lines); where reference and doc disagreed
// the docs' engine decodes won.
//
// The package implements the consumer-defined vm.State interface (plus
// vm.NameResolver through vm.FileNames in the callers): flags are
// zero-initialized and the runtime state seeds from the static exports
// (exports/data/allies.json) so a fresh game matches the ROM's opening
// state.
//
// Spaces (docs/vm-semantics.md §2.5, §6.1):
//
//   - vanilla nibble flags: one byte per two flags, even id = high
//     nibble (WRAM 7E:F46A); ops 33/34/35/36/37/38.
//   - packed4: byte-packed 4-bit fields, op 49.
//   - ext flags: same nibble semantics, separate space; op 0D 00-03.
//   - EF00 variables: ops 40/41/48 write, 45/3A/getItem/money ops read.
//   - inventory: 32 slots of (id, count) at WRAM $7EF32A in the engine;
//     a sparse id -> count map here (count saturates at 99, C0:2E54).
//   - gold: 16-bit at WRAM $7EF31A; receive caps at 30000 (C0:395E), pay
//     floors at 0 (C0:29A1); two bank deposits at $7EF31C/$7EF31E.
//   - party: ally ids, leader first. The engine keeps a 6-slot list at
//     $F323-$F328 with the count at $F319; membership is event-written
//     through op 4F_31 (C0:20EC) mapped to SetPartyList.
//
// Runtime-only and NOT persisted by SaveGame (the reference does not
// persist them either; the engine SRAM persistence of $F532/$F533 is
// undecoded): enemy_levels ($F532/$F533), ai_unlock_bits ($F4DA), the
// protagonist walk id ($F322) and the scratch spill ($7FF900). Nothing
// carries out of a wiped battle to begin with — the defeat path reboots
// the console (docs/battle-defeat.md §5) — so there is no wipe-state to
// model.
//
// Goldens: the main.gd --selftest e2e cases re-hosted as plain go tests
// — real events 00A6/000B/0029..002F/0B3C through the real vm package
// against this state (e2e_test.go), the opening-party + gold-0 seeding
// and the static-export joins against internal/charstats' ROM decode
// (seed_test.go), and the save v2 round-trip with the additive fields
// plus v1 old-format loads (save_test.go).
package state

```

`internal/game/state/e2e_test.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/vm"
)

// The main.gd --selftest e2e block re-hosted on the production state and
// the real Go VM (internal/game/vm) against the real export. Engine
// provenance lives in each pin's comment.

// newGameWithAllies is the selftest's fresh-game step: setup_new_game
// over the static export.
func newGameWithAllies(t *testing.T) *GameState {
	t.Helper()
	allies, err := LoadAllySeeds(alliesPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := NewGameState()
	if err := gs.SetupNewGame(allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return gs
}

// TestE2E00A6ItemAnd000BPause: real event 00A6 opens with set1B +
// getItem and gives item 0x1B (氷の剣); op 2C (C0:26C9) in 000B shows
// four lines, the button wait, then the next line in the same window —
// some page must carry the pause mark followed by more lines (main.gd
// selftest, run against the same mutated state).
func TestE2E00A6ItemAnd000BPause(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent(cat.RawOps(0x00A6), 0x00A6)
	v.AllPages()
	if gs.ItemCount(0x1B) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("00A6 inventory: item 1B count %d, want 1", gs.ItemCount(0x1B))
	}
	v2c := vm.New(cat)
	v2c.State = gs
	v2c.LoadEvent(cat.RawOps(0x000B), 0x000B)
	ok2c := false
	for _, p := range v2c.AllPages() {
		if at := strings.Index(p, "\f"); at > 0 && strings.HasPrefix(p[at+1:], "\n") {
			ok2c = true
		}
	}
	if !ok2c {
		t.Fatal("000B op 2C: no page holds a mark followed by more lines")
	}
}

// TestE2E0029GoldChain: 0029-002F are consecutive battle-end fragments
// (each one's entry is the previous one's end16; 002F [fa1244,fa1349)
// carries the +1500 grant at FA:12dc/FA:12e2, vm-semantics §6.2). The
// engine pops each frame at its end16 and the chain dispatches the next
// fragment, so the grant only fires when the fragment sequence runs;
// replay it in order. The 傭兵になる menu at FA:1298 registers two optB
// options and op 27 optC only opens the selection loop, so the replay
// answers 0 (傭兵になる) at every pause (main.gd selftest "runtime
// state ok": gold 1500).
func TestE2E0029GoldChain(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	for fid := 0x0029; fid <= 0x002F; fid++ {
		v.LoadEvent(cat.RawOps(fid), fid)
		guard := 0
		for {
			guard++
			if guard > 50 {
				t.Fatalf("0029..002F replay did not settle at %02X", fid)
			}
			v.ChoiceHandler = func([]string) {}
			v.AllPages()
			if len(v.PendingChoices) == 0 {
				break
			}
			v.PendingChoices = nil
			v.Choose(0)
		}
	}
	if gs.Gold() != 1500 {
		t.Fatalf("0029..002F gold: %d, want 1500", gs.Gold())
	}
}

// TestE2E0B3CMembership: event 0B3C is the range [FC:c7c3, c7d2):
// `40 00 18`, `4f 45 00 20`, `4f 31 00 01 02 ff ff ff`, then the frame
// end — a fixed path, so the party must be exactly [0, 1, 2] and
// survive save/load (main.gd selftest "membership ok"). The +2000
// rewards (`48 01 03 d0 07 00` / `4f 19` at FC:ca80/ca86 and FC:d318)
// lie in later fragments of the 0B31 block; the 0B3C run must stop at
// its own frame end and pay nothing (main.gd "0B3C gold drift" pin).
func TestE2E0B3CMembership(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent(cat.RawOps(0x0B3C), 0x0B3C)
	v.AllPages()
	if want := []int{0, 1, 2}; !equalInts(gs.Party(), want) {
		t.Fatalf("0B3C party %v, want %v", gs.Party(), want)
	}
	if gs.Gold() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("0B3C gold drift: %d, want 0 (frame end stops the +2000)", gs.Gold())
	}
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "save.json")
	if err := SaveGame(path, gs, "0B3C", "", -1, -1); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	loaded, err := LoadGame(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !equalInts(loaded.Party(), gs.Party()) {
		t.Fatalf("0B3C party save round-trip: %v -> %v", gs.Party(), loaded.Party())
	}
}

// equalInts is slices.Equal with nil == empty.
func equalInts(a, b []int) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// TestE2EOp4CGoldGateAndPay pins the gate-4C / 4F_10 pair on the dump
// instances of event 004E (神王教 donation shop, vm-semantics §6.2):
// `41 01 10 27` sets EF01 = 10000 and `4c` gates on gold >= word1
// (C0:2B4E, TRUE -> S+1, FALSE -> S+2); `41 00 10 27` + `4f 10` pays
// EF00 word0 with the floor 0 (C0:29A1).
func TestE2EOp4CGoldGateAndPay(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The dump carries no gate continuations for `4c`: the VM derives
	// TRUE -> S+1, FALSE -> S+2 from the op address (C0:2B4E).
	gateOps := []vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:1ed9", "41 01 10 27", "set2B"),
		cmdOp("FA:1edd", "4c", "op4C"),
		textOp("FA:1ede", "afford"),
		cmdOp("FA:1edf", "2a", "closeWin"),
		textOp("FA:1ee0", "too poor"),
		cmdOp("FA:1ee1", "2a", "closeWin"),
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs.GainGold(10000)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent(gateOps, 0)
	if pages := v.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "afford" {
		t.Fatalf("gold 10000 pages %v, want afford first", pages)
	}
	gs2 := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs2.GainGold(9999)
	v2 := vm.New(cat)
	v2.State = gs2
	v2.LoadEvent(gateOps, 0)
	if pages := v2.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "too poor" {
		t.Fatalf("gold 9999 pages %v, want too poor first", pages)
	}
	// The pay path: 4F_10 subtracts EF00 word0, flooring at 0.
	payOps := []vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:1ef7", "41 00 10 27", "set2B"),
		cmdOp("FA:1efb", "4f 10", "4F_10"),
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct{ gold, want int }{{10000, 0}, {5000, 0}} {
		gsp := newGameWithAllies(t)
		gsp.GainGold(tc.gold)
		vp := vm.New(cat)
		vp.State = gsp
		vp.LoadEvent(payOps, 0)
		vp.AllPages()
		if gsp.Gold() != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("pay from %d left %d, want %d", tc.gold, gsp.Gold(), tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestE2E4F19BankDeposit pins 4F_19's non-gold arm (C0:3947): with EF03
// != 0 the amount goes to the two bank deposits (EF01 word -> deposit 0,
// EF03 word -> deposit 1), gold untouched.
func TestE2E4F19BankDeposit(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0000", "40 03 01", "set1B"),    // EF03 = 1: deposit arm
		cmdOp("FA:0003", "41 01 d0 07", "set2B"), // EF01 word = 2000
		cmdOp("FA:0007", "4f 19", "4F_19"),
	}, 0)
	v.AllPages()
	if gs.Gold() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("gold %d after the deposit arm, want 0", gs.Gold())
	}
	if gs.Bank != [2]int{2000, 1} {
		t.Fatalf("bank %v, want [2000 1]", gs.Bank)
	}
}

// TestE2EFillGetItemScratch pins the §6 decodes on the production state
// (the same ops vm_test runs against its fake): fill with n == 0 means
// one byte (C0:21FD); getItem saturates at 99 (C0:2E1F); 4F_19 with
// EF03 == 0 grants gold capped at 30000 (C0:3947); the 0d 30/31 pair
// spills EF00[0] through the $7FF900 scratch (5A:C000/C020).
func TestE2EFillGetItemScratch(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0100", "48 10 00 07", "fill"),     // n == 0: EF10 = 07
		cmdOp("FA:0104", "42 10", "getItem"),        // give item EF10 = 07
		cmdOp("FA:0106", "41 01 d0 07", "set2B"),    // EF01 = 2000
		cmdOp("FA:010a", "4f 19", "4F_19"),          // gold += 2000
		cmdOp("FA:010c", "40 00 07", "set1B"),       // EF00 = 07
		cmdOp("FA:010f", "0d 30 50 00", "swapOut"),  // scratch[0] = EF00 (07)
		cmdOp("FA:0113", "40 00 99", "set1B"),       // EF00 = 99
		cmdOp("FA:0116", "0d 31 00 50", "swapBack"), // EF50 = 07
	}, 0)
	if pages := v.AllPages(); len(pages) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pages %v, want none", pages)
	}
	if got := gs.GetVar(0x10); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("EF10 = %d, want 7 (fill n==0 means one byte)", got)
	}
	if gs.ItemCount(7) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("item 7 count %d, want 1", gs.ItemCount(7))
	}
	if gs.Gold() != 2000 {
		t.Fatalf("gold %d, want 2000", gs.Gold())
	}
	if got := gs.GetVar(0x50); got != 7 || gs.GetScratch(0) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("swapBack: EF50 = %d scratch[0] = %d, want 7/0", got, gs.GetScratch(0))
	}
	// getItem saturation at 99.
	gs2 := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs2.Inventory[7] = ItemCountMax
	v2 := vm.New(cat)
	v2.State = gs2
	v2.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{cmdOp("FA:0100", "40 00 07", "set1B"), cmdOp("FA:0103", "42 00", "getItem")}, 0)
	v2.AllPages()
	if gs2.ItemCount(7) != ItemCountMax {
		t.Fatalf("item 7 count %d, want saturation at %d", gs2.ItemCount(7), ItemCountMax)
	}
}

// TestE2EPossessionGates pins the 0d 07/09 key-item gates
// (vm-semantics §6.2, PLAUSIBLE-class): 0d 07 vi checks the party
// carries the item whose id the VM reads from EF00[vi] — the reference
// reads one byte; 0d 09 id checks the direct id. Event 016A sets
// EF00 = 0x13D (レディホーク) before `0d 07 00`; event 076F sets 0x6D
// (白虎の鎧); event 06CB's `0d 09 f6` checks item $F6
// (タイニィフェザー). TRUE -> S+3, FALSE -> S+5.
func TestE2EPossessionGates(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := fullCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ops07 := []vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0100", "41 00 3d 01", "set2B"), // EF00 word = 0x13D
		cmdOp("FA:0104", "0d 07 00", "inparty?"), // TRUE S+3, FALSE S+5
		cmdOp("FA:0107", "4e 03", "skip"),        // TRUE arm skips to FA:010c
		textOp("FA:0109", "carried-false"),
		cmdOp("FA:010a", "2a", "closeWin"),
		textOp("FA:010c", "carried-true"),
		cmdOp("FA:010d", "2a", "closeWin"),
	}
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs.AddItem(0x3D)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent(ops07, 0)
	if pages := v.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "carried-true" {
		t.Fatalf("0d 07 with the item in the bag: pages %v", pages)
	}
	// The equipped slot counts too (party_has_item covers bag +
	// equipment): 白虎の鎧 0x6D worn by the leader.
	gs2 := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs2.Equipment[0] = []int{0x6D, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1}
	v2 := vm.New(cat)
	v2.State = gs2
	v2.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0100", "41 00 6d 00", "set2B"),
		cmdOp("FA:0104", "0d 07 00", "inparty?"),
		cmdOp("FA:0107", "4e 03", "skip"),
		textOp("FA:0109", "carried-false"),
		cmdOp("FA:010a", "2a", "closeWin"),
		textOp("FA:010c", "carried-true"),
		cmdOp("FA:010d", "2a", "closeWin"),
	}, 0)
	if pages := v2.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "carried-true" {
		t.Fatalf("0d 07 with the item equipped: pages %v", pages)
	}
	// Nothing carried: the FALSE arm.
	gs3 := newGameWithAllies(t)
	v3 := vm.New(cat)
	v3.State = gs3
	v3.LoadEvent(ops07, 0)
	if pages := v3.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "carried-false" {
		t.Fatalf("0d 07 with nothing carried: pages %v", pages)
	}
	// 0d 09 f6 (event 06CB's idiom): the direct id.
	ops09 := []vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0100", "0d 09 f6", "inparty_id?"),
		cmdOp("FA:0103", "4e 03", "skip"),
		textOp("FA:0105", "carried-false"),
		cmdOp("FA:0106", "2a", "closeWin"),
		textOp("FA:0108", "carried-true"),
		cmdOp("FA:0109", "2a", "closeWin"),
	}
	gs4 := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs4.AddItem(0xF6)
	v4 := vm.New(cat)
	v4.State = gs4
	v4.LoadEvent(ops09, 0)
	if pages := v4.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "carried-true" {
		t.Fatalf("0d 09 with the item: pages %v", pages)
	}
	gs5 := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs5.Equipment[0] = []int{-1, -1, -1, 0xF6, -1, -1, -1, -1}
	v5 := vm.New(cat)
	v5.State = gs5
	v5.LoadEvent(ops09, 0)
	if pages := v5.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "carried-true" {
		t.Fatalf("0d 09 with the item equipped: pages %v", pages)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/state/save.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"time"
)

// Save/load: snapshots the game state to a JSON file the project can
// round-trip (godot/save_manager.gd). Layout is versioned: version 2
// adds the runtime state (party, inventory, gold, bank, per-member
// equipment/techs/spells/HP/LP) and the additive protagonist fields;
// version 1 saves still load and get the fresh-game runtime defaults.
//
//	{"version": 2, "saved_at": "…", "event_id": "…", "position": {"map": "04", "x": 8, "y": 8},
//	 "state": {"vanilla": [ints], "packed4": [ints], "ext": [ints], "vars": [ints],
//	           "menu_selection": …, "menu_open": …, "menu_count": …,
//	           "party": [ids], "away": [ids], "inventory": [[id, count], …],
//	           "gold": …, "bank": [a, b], "equipment": {"id": [slots]},
//	           "techs": {"id": [ids]}, "spells": {"id": [ids]},
//	           "hp": {"id": …}, "lp": {"id": …}}}
const SaveVersion = 2

// ErrNoSave reports there is no save file (load_game()'s null).
var ErrNoSave = errors.New("no save file")

// Position is where the save was taken (save_manager.gd saved_position).
type Position struct {
	Map string
	X   int
	Y   int
}

// saveFile/saveState mirror save_manager.gd save_game's layout. The
// runtime-only cells ($F532/$F533 enemy levels, $F4DA AI unlock bits,
// $F322 walk id, $7FF900 scratch) have no fields: the reference does not
// persist them and their SRAM persistence is undecoded.
type saveFile struct {
	Version  int       `json:"version"`
	SavedAt  string    `json:"saved_at"`
	EventID  string    `json:"event_id"`
	Position Position  `json:"position"`
	State    saveState `json:"state"`
}

type saveState struct {
	Vanilla  []byte `json:"vanilla"`
	Packed4  []byte `json:"packed4"`
	Ext      []byte `json:"ext"`
	Vars     []byte `json:"vars"`
	Treasure []byte `json:"treasure"`
	Clock    []byte `json:"clock"`

	MenuSelection *int `json:"menu_selection,omitempty"`
	MenuOpen      *int `json:"menu_open,omitempty"`
	MenuCount     *int `json:"menu_count,omitempty"`

	Party []int `json:"party"`
	Away  []int `json:"away"`

	// Additive in v2: saves written before the select screen carry no row
	// and load with the engine default (row 0 = ユリアン). Saves from
	// before the naming screen carry no name and load with "" (the
	// engine default name is applied at display, not stored).
	ProtagonistRow  *int    `json:"protagonist_row,omitempty"`
	ProtagonistName *string `json:"protagonist_name,omitempty"`

	InventoryIDs    []int `json:"inventory"`
	InventoryCounts []int `json:"inventory_counts"`
	Gold            int   `json:"gold"`
	Bank            []int `json:"bank"`

	Equipment map[string][]int `json:"equipment"`
	Techs     map[string][]int `json:"techs"`
	Spells    map[string][]int `json:"spells"`
	HP        map[string]int   `json:"hp"`
	LP        map[string]int   `json:"lp"`
}

// SaveGame writes the state to path (save_manager.gd save_game).
func SaveGame(path string, gs *GameState, eventID, mapID string, x, y int) error {
	st := saveState{
		Vanilla:         slices.Clone(gs.Vanilla[:]),
		Packed4:         slices.Clone(gs.Packed4[:]),
		Ext:             slices.Clone(gs.Ext[:]),
		Vars:            slices.Clone(gs.Vars[:]),
		Treasure:        slices.Clone(gs.Treasure[:]),
		Clock:           slices.Clone(gs.Clock[:]),
		MenuSelection:   &gs.menuSelection,
		MenuOpen:        &gs.menuOpen,
		MenuCount:       &gs.menuCount,
		Party:           slices.Clone(gs.party),
		Away:            slices.Clone(gs.Away),
		ProtagonistRow:  &gs.ProtagonistRow,
		ProtagonistName: &gs.ProtagonistName,
		Gold:            gs.gold,
		Bank:            []int{gs.Bank[0], gs.Bank[1]},
		HP:              idMapInts(gs.HP),
		LP:              idMapInts(gs.LP),
	}
	for id := range gs.Inventory {
		st.InventoryIDs = append(st.InventoryIDs, id)
	}
	// Parallel arrays must stay paired; GDScript dict order is insertion
	// order, the map's is not, so sort by id.
	slices.Sort(st.InventoryIDs)
	st.InventoryCounts = make([]int, len(st.InventoryIDs))
	for i, id := range st.InventoryIDs {
		st.InventoryCounts[i] = gs.Inventory[id]
	}
	st.Equipment = sliceMap(gs.Equipment)
	st.Techs = sliceMap(gs.Techs)
	st.Spells = sliceMap(gs.Spells)
	data, err := json.Marshal(saveFile{
		// Informational timestamp (save_manager.gd: Time's datetime
		// string); nothing reads it back.
		SavedAt:  time.Now().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05"),
		EventID:  eventID,
		Position: Position{Map: mapID, X: x, Y: y},
		State:    st,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("save game: %w", err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("save game: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// LoadGame returns the state loaded from path (save_manager.gd
// load_game). ErrNoSave (or any other error) means the caller falls back
// to the new-game path, the reference's null; version 1 saves load with
// the runtime state zero-initialized. Runtime-only cells (enemy levels,
// AI unlock bits, walk id, scratch) come back zero: see saveState.
func LoadGame(path string) (*GameState, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %w", ErrNoSave)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %w", err)
	}
	var parsed saveFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &parsed); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: parse %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if parsed.Version > SaveVersion {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %s: version %d newer than supported %d", path, parsed.Version, SaveVersion)
	}
	s := parsed.State
	gs := NewGameState()
	fillBytes(gs.Vanilla[:], s.Vanilla)
	fillBytes(gs.Packed4[:], s.Packed4)
	fillBytes(gs.Ext[:], s.Ext)
	fillBytes(gs.Vars[:], s.Vars)
	fillBytes(gs.Treasure[:], s.Treasure)
	fillBytes(gs.Clock[:], s.Clock)
	if s.MenuSelection != nil {
		gs.menuSelection = *s.MenuSelection
	}
	if s.MenuOpen != nil {
		gs.menuOpen = *s.MenuOpen
	}
	if s.MenuCount != nil {
		gs.menuCount = *s.MenuCount
	}
	gs.party = s.Party
	gs.Away = s.Away
	if s.ProtagonistRow != nil {
		gs.ProtagonistRow = *s.ProtagonistRow
	}
	if s.ProtagonistName != nil {
		gs.ProtagonistName = *s.ProtagonistName
	}
	for i, id := range s.InventoryIDs {
		if i >= len(s.InventoryCounts) {
			break // mini(ids.size(), counts.size()), like the reference
		}
		gs.Inventory[id] = s.InventoryCounts[i]
	}
	gs.gold = s.Gold
	if len(s.Bank) >= 2 {
		gs.Bank = [2]int{s.Bank[0], s.Bank[1]}
	}
	for idStr, slots := range s.Equipment {
		id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %s: equipment key %q: %w", path, idStr, err)
		}
		gs.Equipment[id] = slots
	}
	for idStr, list := range s.Techs {
		id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %s: techs key %q: %w", path, idStr, err)
		}
		gs.Techs[id] = list
	}
	for idStr, list := range s.Spells {
		id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %s: spells key %q: %w", path, idStr, err)
		}
		gs.Spells[id] = list
	}
	for idStr, v := range s.HP {
		id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %s: hp key %q: %w", path, idStr, err)
		}
		gs.HP[id] = v
	}
	for idStr, v := range s.LP {
		id, err := strconv.Atoi(idStr)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load game: %s: lp key %q: %w", path, idStr, err)
		}
		gs.LP[id] = v
	}
	return gs, nil
}

// SavedPosition reads where the save was taken (save_manager.gd
// saved_position).
func SavedPosition(path string) (Position, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
		return Position{}, fmt.Errorf("saved position: %w", ErrNoSave)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return Position{}, fmt.Errorf("saved position: %w", err)
	}
	var parsed saveFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &parsed); err != nil {
		return Position{}, fmt.Errorf("saved position: parse %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return parsed.Position, nil
}

// fillBytes copies min(len(values), len(target)) values over a fixed
// array (save_manager.gd _fill: the rest keeps its fresh zero).
func fillBytes(target []byte, values []byte) {
	copy(target, values)
}

// idMapInts stringifies int-keyed maps: the ids travel as JSON object
// keys, so they are stored alongside the values (save_manager.gd
// _id_map's str(k)).
func idMapInts(m map[int]int) map[string]int {
	out := make(map[string]int, len(m))
	for id, v := range m {
		out[strconv.Itoa(id)] = v
	}
	return out
}

// sliceMap stringifies slice-valued int-keyed maps.
func sliceMap(m map[int][]int) map[string][]int {
	out := make(map[string][]int, len(m))
	for id, v := range m {
		out[strconv.Itoa(id)] = v
	}
	return out
}
```

`internal/game/state/save_test.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// persistedEqual compares every cell SaveGame writes (save_manager.gd's
// state dict). The runtime-only cells (enemy levels, AI unlock bits,
// walk id, scratch) are intentionally absent: they load zero.
func persistedEqual(t *testing.T, want, got *GameState) {
	t.Helper()
	if got.Vanilla != want.Vanilla || got.Packed4 != want.Packed4 ||
		got.Ext != want.Ext || got.Vars != want.Vars {
		t.Fatal("flag/variable spaces did not survive the round-trip")
	}
	if got.Treasure != want.Treasure || got.Clock != want.Clock {
		t.Fatal("treasure/clock did not survive the round-trip")
	}
	if got.MenuSelection() != want.MenuSelection() ||
		got.MenuOpen() != want.MenuOpen() || got.MenuCount() != want.MenuCount() {
		t.Fatal("menu state did not survive the round-trip")
	}
	if !equalInts(got.Party(), want.Party()) || !equalInts(got.Away, want.Away) {
		t.Fatalf("party/away %v/%v -> %v/%v", want.Party(), want.Away, got.Party(), got.Away)
	}
	if got.ProtagonistRow != want.ProtagonistRow {
		t.Fatalf("protagonist_row %d -> %d", want.ProtagonistRow, got.ProtagonistRow)
	}
	if got.ProtagonistName != want.ProtagonistName {
		t.Fatalf("protagonist_name %q -> %q", want.ProtagonistName, got.ProtagonistName)
	}
	if got.Gold() != want.Gold() || got.Bank != want.Bank {
		t.Fatalf("gold/bank %d/%v -> %d/%v", want.Gold(), want.Bank, got.Gold(), got.Bank)
	}
	if len(got.Inventory) != len(want.Inventory) {
		t.Fatalf("inventory %v -> %v", want.Inventory, got.Inventory)
	}
	for id, count := range want.Inventory {
		if got.Inventory[id] != count {
			t.Fatalf("inventory item %X: %d -> %d", id, count, got.Inventory[id])
		}
	}
	for _, m := range []struct {
		name      string
		want, got map[int][]int
	}{
		{"equipment", want.Equipment, got.Equipment},
		{"techs", want.Techs, got.Techs},
		{"spells", want.Spells, got.Spells},
	} {
		if len(m.got) != len(m.want) {
			t.Fatalf("%s %v -> %v", m.name, m.want, m.got)
		}
		for id, list := range m.want {
			if !equalInts(m.got[id], list) {
				t.Fatalf("%s ally %02X: %v -> %v", m.name, id, list, m.got[id])
			}
		}
	}
	if len(got.HP) != len(want.HP) || len(got.LP) != len(want.LP) {
		t.Fatalf("hp/lp %v/%v -> %v/%v", want.HP, want.LP, got.HP, got.LP)
	}
	for id, v := range want.HP {
		if got.HP[id] != v {
			t.Fatalf("hp ally %02X: %d -> %d", id, v, got.HP[id])
		}
	}
	for id, v := range want.LP {
		if got.LP[id] != v {
			t.Fatalf("lp ally %02X: %d -> %d", id, v, got.LP[id])
		}
	}
}

// TestSaveRoundTrip: the mutated state must survive save/load, including
// the additive protagonist fields (main.gd selftest "save round-trip"
// plus the select/naming pins: a non-default row and an entered name).
func TestSaveRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	gs.AddItem(0x1B)
	gs.GainGold(1500)
	gs.Bank = [2]int{100, 200}
	gs.Away = []int{6}
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC4, 2)
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC5, 6)
	gs.SetPacked4(0x10, 3)
	gs.SetExt(0x12, 4)
	gs.SetVarWord(1, 1500)
	gs.SetVar(3, 0)
	gs.SetScratch(5, 9) // not persisted: asserted zero after the load
	gs.ProtagonistWalkID = 6
	gs.SetTreasureOpen(14)
	gs.Clock = [4]byte{1, 2, 3, 4}
	gs.SetMenuSelection(1)
	gs.SetMenuOpen(1)
	gs.SetMenuCount(2)
	gs.ProtagonistRow = 3
	gs.ProtagonistName = "ゆうき"

	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "save.json")
	if err := SaveGame(path, gs, "00A6", "04", 8, 8); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	loaded, err := LoadGame(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	persistedEqual(t, gs, loaded)
	if loaded.ItemCount(0x1B) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("item 1B count %d after the round-trip, want 1", loaded.ItemCount(0x1B))
	}
	if loaded.Gold() != 1500 {
		t.Fatalf("gold %d after the round-trip, want 1500", loaded.Gold())
	}
	if len(loaded.Equipment[0]) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("equipment[0] lost in the round-trip")
	}
	// Runtime-only cells come back zero/-1: walk id and scratch are not
	// in the file (saveState).
	if loaded.ProtagonistWalkID != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("walk id %d after the round-trip, want -1 (not persisted)", loaded.ProtagonistWalkID)
	}
	if loaded.GetScratch(5) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("scratch[5] = %d after the round-trip, want 0 (not persisted)", loaded.GetScratch(5))
	}
	pos, err := SavedPosition(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if pos.Map != "04" || pos.X != 8 || pos.Y != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("saved position %+v, want 04/8/8", pos)
	}
}

// TestSaveInventoryRoundTrip: many items keep their counts through the
// parallel-array layout.
func TestSaveInventoryRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	gs := newGameWithAllies(t)
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		gs.AddItem(0x0A) // 傷薬 x5, the シノンの森 supply
	}
	gs.AddItem(0x1B)
	gs.RemoveItem(0x0A, 2)
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "save.json")
	if err := SaveGame(path, gs, "0B31", "", -1, -1); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	loaded, err := LoadGame(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if loaded.ItemCount(0x0A) != 3 || loaded.ItemCount(0x1B) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("inventory after round-trip: %v, want 0A x3, 1B x1", loaded.Inventory)
	}
}

// v1StateJSON is an old-format save (version 1: the flag/variable spaces
// only — "version 2 adds the runtime state", save_manager.gd header).
const v1StateJSON = `{"version": 1, "saved_at": "2026-11-01T10:00:00", "event_id": "0005",
 "position": {"map": "01", "x": 3, "y": 4},
 "state": {"vanilla": [18, 0], "packed4": [0], "ext": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 11], "vars": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 40]}}`

// TestLoadV1OldFormat: an old-format save loads with the engine defaults
// — flags preserved, runtime state zero-initialized, protagonist_row
// 0 (row 0 = ユリアン), name "" — the CONTINUE == new game convergence
// for the additive fields (main.gd _title_confirm: a null load falls
// through to setup_new_game).
func TestLoadV1OldFormat(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "save.json")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(v1StateJSON), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs, err := LoadGame(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if gs.GetVanilla(0) != 1 || gs.GetVanilla(1) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla flags %d/%d after load, want 1/2 (byte 0x12)", gs.GetVanilla(0), gs.GetVanilla(1))
	}
	if gs.GetExt(19) != 0x0B {
		t.Fatalf("ext flag 19 = %d, want B (ext byte 9 = 0x0B)", gs.GetExt(19))
	}
	if gs.GetVar(5) != 40 {
		t.Fatalf("var 5 = %d, want 40", gs.GetVar(5))
	}
	if gs.Gold() != 0 || len(gs.Party()) != 0 || len(gs.Inventory) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("runtime state not default after v1 load: gold %d party %v inv %v",
			gs.Gold(), gs.Party(), gs.Inventory)
	}
	if gs.ProtagonistRow != DefaultSelectRow {
		t.Fatalf("protagonist_row %d, want %d (the engine default)", gs.ProtagonistRow, DefaultSelectRow)
	}
	if gs.ProtagonistName != "" {
		t.Fatalf("protagonist_name %q, want empty", gs.ProtagonistName)
	}
	if gs.MenuSelection() != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("menu selection %d, want FF (the engine default)", gs.MenuSelection())
	}
	// Convergence: the additive fields equal a fresh new-game state's.
	fresh := newGameWithAllies(t)
	if gs.ProtagonistRow != fresh.ProtagonistRow ||
		gs.ProtagonistName != fresh.ProtagonistName ||
		gs.Gold() != fresh.Gold() {
		t.Fatal("v1 load does not converge with the new-game defaults")
	}
	pos, err := SavedPosition(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if pos.Map != "01" || pos.X != 3 || pos.Y != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("v1 position %+v, want 01/3/4", pos)
	}
}

// TestLoadV2WithoutAdditiveFields: a save written before the select /

// TestLoadNoSave: a missing file is ErrNoSave (load_game()'s null), the
// caller's cue to converge on the new-game path.
func TestLoadNoSave(t *testing.T) {
	missing := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "absent.json")
	if _, err := LoadGame(missing); !errors.Is(err, ErrNoSave) {
		t.Fatalf("missing-file error %v, want ErrNoSave", err)
	}
	if _, err := SavedPosition(missing); !errors.Is(err, ErrNoSave) {
		t.Fatalf("missing-position error %v, want ErrNoSave", err)
	}
	// A corrupt file errors too — the caller treats any load error the
	// same way the reference treats its null (new-game fallback).
	if err := os.WriteFile(missing, []byte("{not json"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := LoadGame(missing); err == nil || errors.Is(err, ErrNoSave) {
		t.Fatalf("corrupt-file error %v, want a parse error", err)
	}
}
```
