```go
	 "state": {"vanilla": [], "packed4": [], "ext": [], "vars": [], "inventory": [3, 5, 7], "inventory_counts": [2]}}`

		t.Fatalf("inventory %v, want item 3 x2 only (counts ran out)", gs.Inventory)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/state/seed.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
)

// AllySeed is one exports/data/allies.json row: the initial-state columns
// the ROM's 仲間 entry carries (docs/char-stats.md entry layout +31..+38
// equipment, +23..+30 initial techs/spells, +3/+4 HP, +5 LP). Item and
// tech ids are catalog ids; Equipment's -1 = empty slot.
type AllySeed struct {
	ID        int
	Name      string
	Equipment []int // EquipSlots entries, -1 = empty
	Techs     []int
	Spells    []int
	HP        int
	LP        int
}

// allyRowJSON mirrors the export's row shape: hex-string ids, null
// equipment slots.
type allyRowJSON struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	Name      string    `json:"name"`
	Equipment []*string `json:"equipment"`
	Techs     []string  `json:"techs"`
	Spells    []string  `json:"spells"`
	HP        int       `json:"hp"`
	LP        int       `json:"lp"`
}

// LoadAllySeeds reads the static export (exports/data/allies.json) into a
// map by ally id, the same rows game_state.gd setup_new_game walks.
func LoadAllySeeds(path string) (map[int]AllySeed, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load ally seeds: %w", err)
	}
	var rows []allyRowJSON
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rows); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	out := make(map[int]AllySeed, len(rows))
	for _, row := range rows {
		id, err := parseHexID(row.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		if _, dup := out[id]; dup {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: duplicate ally id %02X", path, id)
		}
		if len(row.Equipment) != EquipSlots {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: ally %02X equipment has %d slots, want %d", path, id, len(row.Equipment), EquipSlots)
		}
		seed := AllySeed{
			ID:        id,
			Name:      row.Name,
			Equipment: make([]int, EquipSlots),
			Techs:     make([]int, 0, len(row.Techs)),
			Spells:    make([]int, 0, len(row.Spells)),
			HP:        row.HP,
			LP:        row.LP,
		}
		for i, slot := range row.Equipment {
			if slot == nil {
				seed.Equipment[i] = -1
				continue
			}
			v, err := parseHexID(*slot)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: ally %02X equipment slot %d: %w", path, id, i, err)
			}
			seed.Equipment[i] = v
		}
		for _, v := range row.Techs {
			id, err := parseHexID(v)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: ally %02X tech %q: %w", path, seed.ID, v, err)
			}
			seed.Techs = append(seed.Techs, id)
		}
		for _, v := range row.Spells {
			id, err := parseHexID(v)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: ally %02X spell %q: %w", path, seed.ID, v, err)
			}
			seed.Spells = append(seed.Spells, id)
		}
		out[id] = seed
	}
	return out, nil
}

// parseHexID parses the export's two-digit hex ids ("08", "C0"); the
// GDScript reads them as ("0x" + str(slot)).hex_to_int().
func parseHexID(s string) (int, error) {
	v, err := strconv.ParseUint(s, 16, 8)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("malformed hex id %q", s)
	}
	return int(v), nil
}

// SetupNewGame seeds the runtime state from the static export so a fresh
// game matches the ROM's opening state (game_state.gd setup_new_game):
// party in the OpeningParty order (the opening events 0B31-0B3F build
// the same list with 4F_31), each member's initial equipment, techs and
// spells plus full HP/LP. Gold starts at 0: no event op or engine
// routine grants starting gold (the only $F31A writes are the 4F_19/4F_10
// event paths and the shop spend loop C5:AAE7), and the bokuno wiki
// オープニング page (https://www.wikihouse.com/bokuno/, EUC-JP) puts the
// first income at the opening-end reward (+2000/+4000 オーラム). Starting
// items likewise come from the opening supply events (getItem ops), not
// from engine init. Does not touch the flag spaces, the menu state, the
// treasure array or the clock, and leaves ProtagonistRow as it is (the
// select screen writes it after seeding).
func (s *GameState) SetupNewGame(allies map[int]AllySeed) error {
	s.party = nil
	s.Away = nil
	s.Inventory = map[int]int{}
	s.gold = 0
	s.EnemyLevels = [16]int{}
	s.GlobalLevel = 0
	s.AIUnlockBits = 0
	s.Bank = [2]int{}
	s.ProtagonistWalkID = -1
	s.ProtagonistName = ""
	s.scratch = [256]byte{}
	for _, id := range OpeningParty {
		seed, ok := allies[id]
		if !ok {
			// game_state.gd skipped a missing row silently; a party id
			// without a seed row is a broken export and surfaces here.
			return fmt.Errorf("setup new game: ally %02X has no seed row", id)
		}
		s.party = append(s.party, id)
		s.Equipment[id] = append([]int(nil), seed.Equipment...)
		s.Techs[id] = append([]int(nil), seed.Techs...)
		s.Spells[id] = append([]int(nil), seed.Spells...)
		s.HP[id] = seed.HP
		s.LP[id] = seed.LP
	}
	return nil
}
```

`internal/game/state/seed_test.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/charstats"
)

// TestLoadAllySeeds pins the export's opening rows; the ROM-side join
// that grounds them is TestStaticExportJoin below.
func TestLoadAllySeeds(t *testing.T) {
	allies, err := LoadAllySeeds(alliesPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	yurian := allies[0]
	if yurian.Name != "ユリアン" {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 name %q, want ユリアン", yurian.Name)
	}
	wantGear := []int{8, -1, -1, 0, 0x90, 0xC0, -1, -1}
	if !equalInts(yurian.Equipment, wantGear) {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 equipment %v, want %v (nulls = -1)", yurian.Equipment, wantGear)
	}
	if !equalInts(yurian.Techs, []int{0x0F}) {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 techs %v, want [0F]", yurian.Techs)
	}
	if len(yurian.Spells) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 spells %v, want none", yurian.Spells)
	}
	if yurian.HP != 80 || yurian.LP != 10 {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 hp/lp %d/%d, want 80/10", yurian.HP, yurian.LP)
	}
	if len(allies) < 8 {
		t.Fatalf("export holds %d allies, want at least the 8 protagonists", len(allies))
	}
}

// TestSetupNewGameSeeding: gold starts at 0 (no event op or engine
// routine grants starting gold, vm-semantics §6.5); the party seeds in
// the OpeningParty order with each member's initial equipment/techs/
// spells and full HP/LP (game_state.gd setup_new_game); the flag spaces
// and menu state stay untouched; the runtime counters reset.
func TestSetupNewGameSeeding(t *testing.T) {
	allies, err := LoadAllySeeds(alliesPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC4, 2)
	gs.EnemyLevels[1] = 5
	gs.GlobalLevel = 3
	gs.AIUnlockBits = 0xFF
	gs.AddItem(0x1B)
	if err := gs.SetupNewGame(allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !equalInts(gs.Party(), OpeningParty[:]) {
		t.Fatalf("party %v, want %v", gs.Party(), OpeningParty)
	}
	if gs.Gold() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("gold %d, want 0 at new game (§6.5)", gs.Gold())
	}
	if gs.EnemyLevels != [16]int{} || gs.GlobalLevel != 0 || gs.AIUnlockBits != 0 {
		t.Fatal("enemy-level / AI-unlock counters did not reset")
	}
	if gs.ItemCount(0x1B) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("inventory survived setup: item 1B x%d", gs.ItemCount(0x1B))
	}
	// Flags are untouched by the runtime seeding.
	if gs.GetVanilla(0xC4) != 2 {
		t.Fatal("setup_new_game must not touch the flag spaces")
	}
	if gs.MenuSelection() != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("menu selection %d after setup, want FF", gs.MenuSelection())
	}
	// Member seeds: ユリアン 80/10 with his gear; モニカ (record 5) seeded.
	if gs.HP[0] != 80 || gs.LP[0] != 10 {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 hp/lp %d/%d, want 80/10", gs.HP[0], gs.LP[0])
	}
	wantGear := []int{8, -1, -1, 0, 0x90, 0xC0, -1, -1}
	if !equalInts(gs.Equipment[0], wantGear) {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 equipment %v, want %v", gs.Equipment[0], wantGear)
	}
	if !equalInts(gs.Techs[0], []int{0x0F}) {
		t.Fatalf("ally 00 techs %v, want [0F]", gs.Techs[0])
	}
	if gs.HP[6] != allies[6].HP || gs.LP[6] != allies[6].LP {
		t.Fatalf("ally 06 hp/lp %d/%d, want the export's %d/%d", gs.HP[6], gs.LP[6], allies[6].HP, allies[6].LP)
	}
	if gs.ProtagonistWalkID != -1 || gs.ProtagonistName != "" {
		t.Fatalf("walk id / name %d/%q after setup, want -1/empty", gs.ProtagonistWalkID, gs.ProtagonistName)
	}
}

func TestSetupNewGameMissingRowErrors(t *testing.T) {

// seedRowJSON builds one allies.json row for the parser tests.
func seedRowJSON(id string) string {
	return `{"id": "` + id + `", "name": "t", "equipment": [null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null],
	 "techs": [], "spells": [], "hp": 80, "lp": 10}`
}

// TestLoadAllySeedsRejectsDuplicateIDs: two rows with one id are a
// broken export, not a silent overwrite.
func TestLoadAllySeedsRejectsDuplicateIDs(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "allies.json")
	body := "[" + seedRowJSON("00") + "," + seedRowJSON("00") + "]"
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := LoadAllySeeds(path); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("duplicate ally id must error")
	}
}

// TestLoadAllySeedsRejectsShortEquipment: the export's equipment is the

	 "techs": [], "spells": [], "hp": 80, "lp": 10}]`

// TestSetupNewGameCopiesSeedSlices: two games seeded from one allies map
// must not share the gear slices — editing one member's equipment
// cannot reach the other state or the seed row.
func TestSetupNewGameCopiesSeedSlices(t *testing.T) {
	allies, err := LoadAllySeeds(alliesPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g1 := NewGameState()
	if err := g1.SetupNewGame(allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g2 := NewGameState()
	if err := g2.SetupNewGame(allies); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g1.Equipment[0][0] = 0x99
	if g2.Equipment[0][0] != 8 || allies[0].Equipment[0] != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("seed slices aliased: g2[0] = %02X, allies[0] = %02X, want 08 both",
			g2.Equipment[0][0], allies[0].Equipment[0])
	}
}

// exportStatsRow reads the export's live-stat columns (腕 器 早 体 魔 意
// 魅) for the join test; equipment slots are hex strings or null.
type exportStatsRow struct {
	ID    string    `json:"id"`
	STR   int       `json:"str"`
	DEX   int       `json:"dex"`
	AGI   int       `json:"agi"`
	VIT   int       `json:"vit"`
	MAG   int       `json:"mag"`
	WIL   int       `json:"wil"`
	CHA   int       `json:"cha"`
	Equip []*string `json:"equipment"`
}

// TestStaticExportJoin: the allies.json opening rows agree with the
// ROM's 仲間 entries — the seven live stats (entry + 宿星 FE:9649 row +
// 得意武器 5B:7B20 row, C5:E92E; the opening live records $F000+ at
// frame 45076 matched, internal/charstats TestLiveStatsOpeningParty),
// the initial equipment/techs/spells (+31..+38, +23..+30, 0xFF = none)
// and HP/LP (docs/char-stats.md evidence).
func TestStaticExportJoin(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	allies, err := LoadAllySeeds(alliesPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var rows []exportStatsRow
	data, err := os.ReadFile(alliesPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := jsonUnmarshal(data, &rows); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	byID := map[string]exportStatsRow{}
	for _, r := range rows {
		byID[r.ID] = r
	}
	for _, id := range OpeningParty {
		a, err := charstats.AllyAt(rom, id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		live, err := charstats.LiveStats(rom, a, a.Destiny, a.ForteWeapon)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		row, ok := byID[hexID(id)]
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("export lacks ally %02X", id)
		}
		want := [7]int{row.STR, row.DEX, row.AGI, row.VIT, row.MAG, row.WIL, row.CHA}
		if live != want {
			t.Fatalf("ally %02X: live stats %v, export columns %v", id, live, want)
		}
		seed := allies[id]
		wantGear := make([]int, EquipSlots)
		for i, slot := range row.Equip {
			if slot == nil {
				wantGear[i] = -1
				continue
			}
			v, err := parseHexID(*slot)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("ally %02X equipment %q: %v", id, *slot, err)
			}
			wantGear[i] = v
		}
		if !equalInts(seed.Equipment, wantGear) {
			t.Fatalf("ally %02X: ROM equipment %v, export %v", id, wantGear, seed.Equipment)
		}
		if !equalInts(seed.Techs, filterNone(a.InitialTechs[:])) {
			t.Fatalf("ally %02X: ROM techs %v, export %v", id, filterNone(a.InitialTechs[:]), seed.Techs)
		}
		if !equalInts(seed.Spells, filterNone(a.InitialSpells[:])) {
			t.Fatalf("ally %02X: ROM spells %v, export %v", id, filterNone(a.InitialSpells[:]), seed.Spells)
		}
		if seed.HP != int(a.HP) || seed.LP != int(a.LP) {
			t.Fatalf("ally %02X: ROM hp/lp %d/%d, export %d/%d", id, a.HP, a.LP, seed.HP, seed.LP)
		}
	}
}

// filterNone drops the 0xFF = none entries (the export stores only the
// present ids).
func filterNone(ids []byte) []int {
	out := []int{}
	for _, v := range ids {
		if v != 0xFF {
			out = append(out, int(v))
		}
	}
	return out
}

```

`internal/game/state/state.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"saga3/internal/game/rng"
	"saga3/internal/game/vm"
)

// Engine constants (game_state.gd; docs/vm-semantics.md §6.1).
const (
	InventorySlots = 32 // engine WRAM $7EF32A slots; the port keeps a sparse map
	ItemCountMax   = 99 // getItem saturates here (C0:2E54 CMP #$63)
	EquipSlots     = 8  // 腕1-4, 体1-4 (char-stats entry +31..+38)
	GoldCap        = 30000
	BankCap        = 0xFFFF // the two 金取引所 deposits (C0:29B9/C0:39C5)
	PartyMax       = 6

	// WRAM windows of the arrays the mem model exposes (game_state.gd
	// VANILLA_WRAM/TREASURE_WRAM/CLOCK_WRAM).
	VanillaWRAM  = 0xF46A
	TreasureWRAM = 0xF4EA
	ClockWRAM    = 0xF30A

	DefaultSelectRow = 0
)

// RecordIDs is the opening member-record table: op 4F_31 lists RECORD
// slots k ($F000 + 0x80*k), not ally ids; record +0 (the ally id) is
// written by C5:F002 during the intro. The opening capture (hero
// ユリアン, frame 45076) held ids 00 01 02 03 04 06 in records 0-5, so
// the chains' `4f 31 00 01 02 03 04 05` (FC:c7f7) is ユリアン エレン
// サラ トーマス ハリード モニカ. Whether other heroes get other records
// is not captured; later joins rewrite records (not modelled).
// (vm-semantics §6.5 correction 2026-11-21; game_state.gd RECORD_IDS.)
var RecordIDs = [6]int{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6}

// OpeningParty is the party SetupNewGame seeds, the 4F_31-built opening
// list (vm-semantics §6.3; game_state.gd OPENING_PARTY).
var OpeningParty = [6]int{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6}

// SelectRows maps the character-select row to the ally id: the FE:961B
// table [0,3,5,4,2,1,6,7] (engine-verified 2026-11-17, vm-semantics
// §6.5; the old identity mapping was wrong: row 1 is ally 03 トーマス,
// not 01). ユリアン is the default selection.
var SelectRows = [8]int{0, 3, 5, 4, 2, 1, 6, 7}

// DefaultNames maps the select row to the default protagonist name. The
// engine's naming init (C5:8B39) copies the actor-name table entry
// FD:1480 + <actor id>*8 into the name buffer $7E:F300 (8 bytes,
// $50-terminated), actor id = SelectRows[row]; live capture run5
// (/tmp/naming, docs/naming.md): right after the select pick the buffer
// held A6 A9 82 AE 50... = ユリアン. Rows follow the decoded actor names
// (data/names/actors.txt) through SelectRows.
var DefaultNames = [8]string{"ユリアン", "トーマス", "ミカエル", "ハリード", "サラ", "エレン", "モニカ", "カタリナ"}

// ProtagonistWalkIDs maps the select row to the walk-figure graphic id
// (FE:961B+0 per row, byte-verified 2026-11-18): after the select
// confirm the leader member record holds $F000 = FE:961B+1 (ally id)
// and $F001 = FE:961B+0 (this byte) for all 8 rows. The intro montage
// walks every protagonist with the ensemble lead figure instead ($F322
// = 0A written by the shared 0846-chain 4F_45), so this byte is the
// pick's own figure for the field. (game_state.gd
// PROTAGONIST_WALK_IDS.)
var ProtagonistWalkIDs = [8]int{1, 3, 2, 6, 5, 4, 0, 0x6C}

// GameState is the flag/variable spaces plus the runtime state (see the
// package doc). Flags are zero-initialized. Construct with NewGameState:
// the zero value is not the engine state (menu selection $FF and the
// never-written walk id -1 are sentinels the constructor sets).
type GameState struct {
	Vanilla [256]byte
	Packed4 [256]byte
	Ext     [512]byte
	Vars    [256]byte

	// Selection menu state (WRAM $D3BF/$D3C0/$D3C1); the vm.State
	// accessors are the only read path, so these stay unexported.
	menuSelection int
	menuOpen      int
	menuCount     int

	// party: ally ids, leader first. Membership is event-written through
	// SetPartyList and menu-edited through Join/RemoveMember/SwapOut/
	// SwapBack; Party is the read path (vm.State).
	party []int
	Away  []int // members temporarily out (battle swap)

	Inventory map[int]int // item id -> count, sparse over the 32 engine slots

	gold              int
	Bank              [2]int // WRAM $7EF31C / $7EF31E
	ProtagonistRow    int    // character-select row
	ProtagonistWalkID int    // WRAM $F322 byte, -1 = never written
	ProtagonistName   string // WRAM $7E:F300 name buffer; "" = engine default

	scratch [256]byte // WRAM $7FF900 (0d 30/31 save slots)

	Equipment map[int][]int // ally id -> EquipSlots item ids (-1 = empty)
	Techs     map[int][]int // ally id -> technique ids
	Spells    map[int][]int // ally id -> spell ids
	HP        map[int]int   // ally id -> current HP
	LP        map[int]int   // ally id -> current LP

	// Enemy levels (engine WRAM $F532 global / $F533[race],
	// docs/field-monsters.md): per battle the global level and race 1's
	// level rise through the decoded threshold rolls; races 2-F stay 0.
	// Feeds the encounter composition at battle init. Not persisted
	// through SaveGame — engine SRAM persistence of $F532/$F533 is
	// undecoded (game_state.gd).
	GlobalLevel int
	EnemyLevels [16]int
	// AIUnlockBits is the AI-unlock bitmask $F4DA (C2:C18B marks a bit
	// when a battle first contains one of the entry's enemies; later
	// battles skip that entry's roll). Same SRAM-persistence status as
	// $F532: undecoded, not saved.
	AIUnlockBits int

	Treasure [32]byte // bit array at $F4EA, LSB first (FF:1D37)

	// The play clock $F30A-$F30D: hours (0-99), minutes, seconds, frames.
	// The hack's main loop ticks the frame byte once per logic frame
	// (C5:F327); the FF:00D1 NMI only carries seconds -> minutes -> hours
	// and stops at 99:59:59:59 ($D8D7). Measured rules (scratchpad
	// clock1/clock2 traces, new game to the first battle): the clock
	// RESETS to zero when the opening event 0800 starts (ClockReset — the
	// title/menu play never counts) and it holds during a map load's
	// black span and the battle handoff — not ported: the span's length
	// is the load's CPU cost, which the port does not model
	// (game_state.gd).
	Clock        [4]byte
	ClockStopped bool

	// Spawner and Installer are the field-side callbacks of the objOp
	// effects (nil = no field, like an unset Callable in the reference):
	// SpawnActor calls Spawner with EF00 graphic, EF01/EF02 tile, EF03
	// pose (C0:D72D); InstallAction calls Installer, whose false return
	// leaves the install recorded in Installs (C0:B1F7/B2D4).
	Spawner   func(gfx, tileHi, tileLo, pose int)
	Installer func(obj, id int, eventDriven bool) bool
	Installs  []Install

	// FieldRNG is the engine's field RNG cells ($0A/$0B, C0:0733,
	// docs/parity.md §4.4); FieldRand delegates to it. Consumers share
	// one stream: the random branch (C0:2EFA), the action-script
	// interpreter (C0:5D43-6FE1), the map loader (C0:4605) and bank FF
	// through C0:0726. Reseed (C0:019A-01B1, $0A = ~$213C, $0B untouched)
	// fires at boot, on queue dispatches (C0:B892-B9ED) and map jumps
	// (C0:C0D2); the value depends on cycle timing, so exact comparisons
	// inject the engine's seed at the same points.
	FieldRNG rng.Field
}

// Compile-time check: the production state implements the VM's surface.
var _ vm.State = (*GameState)(nil)

// NewGameState returns the engine's zero-initialized state (game_state.gd
// _init): menu selection $FF, walk id -1, empty maps.
func NewGameState() *GameState {
	return &GameState{
		ProtagonistRow:    DefaultSelectRow,
		ProtagonistWalkID: -1,
		menuSelection:     0xFF,
		Inventory:         map[int]int{},
		Equipment:         map[int][]int{},
		Techs:             map[int][]int{},
		Spells:            map[int][]int{},
		HP:                map[int]int{},
		LP:                map[int]int{},
	}
}
```

`internal/game/state/state_test.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"slices"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/game/vm"
)

// smallCatalog loads the committed parity subset (vm/testdata) once; it
// carries the actor-name table the name-insertion pins resolve through.
var smallCatalog = onceCatalog("../vm/testdata/events.json")

// TestNibbleFlagSpaces: the flag spaces pack two flags per byte — even
// id = high nibble, odd = low (vm-semantics §2.5) — and every write
// masks to 4 bits, so a value past 15 cannot leak into the neighbour
// flag's nibble.
func TestNibbleFlagSpaces(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVanilla(134, 6)
	if got := gs.GetVanilla(134); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla 134 = %d, want 6", got)
	}
	if got := gs.Vanilla[67]; got != 0x60 {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla byte 67 = %02X, want 60 (even id high nibble)", got)
	}
	gs.SetVanilla(135, 7)
	if got := gs.Vanilla[67]; got != 0x67 {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla byte 67 = %02X, want 67 (odd id low nibble)", got)
	}
	// A write past 4 bits keeps the low nibble only: flag 135 = 0x1C
	// stores C and leaves neighbour flag 134 alone.
	gs.SetVanilla(135, 0x1C)
	if got := gs.GetVanilla(135); got != 0xC {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla 135 = %X, want C (write masks to 4 bits)", got)
	}
	if got := gs.GetVanilla(134); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla 134 = %d after the 0x1C write, want 6", got)
	}
	gs.SetPacked4(2, 5)
	if got := gs.GetPacked4(2); got != 5 || gs.Packed4[1] != 0x50 {
		t.Fatalf("packed4 2 = %d byte %02X, want 5 / 50", gs.GetPacked4(2), gs.Packed4[1])
	}
	gs.SetExt(0x100, 3)
	if got := gs.GetExt(0x100); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("ext 100 = %d, want 3", got)
	}
}

// TestFlagSpaceIdRanges: ids wrap within each space — vanilla at 256,
// ext at 512 — and ext's upper half (id 0x100) is distinct storage from
// id 0.
func TestFlagSpaceIdRanges(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVanilla(256, 4)
	if got := gs.GetVanilla(0); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("vanilla 256 -> 0 = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	gs.SetExt(0x200, 9)
	if got := gs.GetExt(0); got != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("ext 200 -> 0 = %d, want 9", got)
	}
	gs.SetExt(0, 0)
	gs.SetExt(0x100, 3)
	if got := gs.GetExt(0); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ext 100 wrote id 0: got %d, want 0 (upper half is distinct storage)", got)
	}
}

func TestVarWords(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVarWord(0x20, 0x1234)
	if gs.GetVar(0x20) != 0x34 || gs.GetVar(0x21) != 0x12 {
		t.Fatalf("set2B bytes %02X %02X, want little-endian 34 12", gs.GetVar(0x20), gs.GetVar(0x21))
	}
	if got := gs.GetVarWord(0x20); got != 0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("word = %04X, want 1234", got)
	}
	// The +1 wraps within the EF00 page.
	gs.SetVar(0xFF, 0x56)
	gs.SetVar(0, 0x78)
	if got := gs.GetVarWord(0xFF); got != 0x7856 {
		t.Fatalf("wrapped word = %04X, want 7856 (vars[255] | vars[0]<<8)", got)
	}
	gs.SetVar(0, 0x99)
	if gs.GetVar(255) != 0x56 {
		t.Fatalf("vars[0] write clobbered the wrap: vars[255] = %02X", gs.GetVar(255))
	}
}

func TestMenuDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	if gs.MenuSelection() != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("fresh menu selection %d, want FF", gs.MenuSelection())
	}
	if gs.MenuOpen() != 0 || gs.MenuCount() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh menu open/count %d/%d, want 0/0", gs.MenuOpen(), gs.MenuCount())
	}
	gs.SetMenuSelection(1)
	gs.SetMenuOpen(1)
	gs.SetMenuCount(2)
	if gs.MenuSelection() != 1 || gs.MenuOpen() != 1 || gs.MenuCount() != 2 {
		t.Fatal("menu accessors did not round-trip")
	}
}

// TestMemReadByteFlagBytes: chkMem through $F4CC reads the flag byte
// holding ids C4 (high nibble) and C5 (low): event 0A7D compares it with
// values like 0x26 (main.gd selftest "flag bytes ok").
func TestMemReadByteFlagBytes(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC4, 2)
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC5, 6)
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF4CC); got != 0x26 {
		t.Fatalf("$F4CC = %02X, want 26 (flags C4=2, C5=6)", got)
	}
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF4CD); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("$F4CD = %02X, want 0", got)
	}
}

// TestMemGateChkMem45 runs the gate itself (45 a b, C0:2F22): the event
// points EF00 word at $F4CC and compares the byte — event 0A7D compares
// it with values like 0x26. TRUE -> S+3, FALSE -> S+5.
func TestMemGateChkMem45(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC4, 2)
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC5, 6)
	v := vm.New(nil)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0100", "41 20 cc f4", "set2B"), // EF20 word = $F4CC
		gateOp("FA:0104", "45 20 26", "chkMem"),
		textOp("FA:0107", "matched"),
		cmdOp("FA:0108", "2a", "closeWin"),
		textOp("FA:0109", "other"),
		cmdOp("FA:010a", "2a", "closeWin"),
	}, 0)
	if pages := v.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "matched" {
		t.Fatalf("chkMem through $F4CC: pages %v", pages)
	}
	gs.SetVanilla(0xC4, 0)
	v2 := vm.New(nil)
	v2.State = gs
	v2.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		cmdOp("FA:0100", "41 20 cc f4", "set2B"),
		gateOp("FA:0104", "45 20 26", "chkMem"),
		textOp("FA:0107", "matched"),
		cmdOp("FA:0108", "2a", "closeWin"),
		textOp("FA:0109", "other"),
		cmdOp("FA:010a", "2a", "closeWin"),
	}, 0)
	if pages := v2.AllPages(); len(pages) == 0 || pages[0] != "other" {
		t.Fatalf("chkMem miss: pages %v", pages)
	}
}

// TestMemReadByteModel walks the windows the mem model exposes
// (game_state.gd mem_read_byte): $F000 select pick, $F319 member count,
// $F322 walk id, the $F323-$F328 slot list with $FF empties, the EF00
// space, the treasure array and the play clock; $F30E stays unmodelled.
func TestMemReadByteModel(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetPartyList([]int{0, 1, 2, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF})
	for row, want := range SelectRows {
		gs.ProtagonistRow = row
		if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF000); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("row %d: $F000 = %02X, want %02X", row, got, want)
		}
	}
	gs.ProtagonistRow = DefaultSelectRow
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF319); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("$F319 = %d, want 3", got)
	}
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF322); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("$F322 never written = %02X, want FF (-1 & 0xFF)", got)
	}
	gs.ProtagonistWalkID = 6
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF322); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("$F322 = %02X, want 06", got)
	}
	for i, want := range []int{0, 1, 2, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF} {
		if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF323 + i); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("$F32%d = %02X, want %02X", 3+i, got, want)
		}
	}
	gs.SetVar(0x10, 0xAB)
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xEF10); got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("$EF10 = %02X, want AB", got)
	}
	gs.SetTreasureOpen(2)
	gs.Clock = [4]byte{1, 2, 3, 4}
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF4EA); got != 0x04 {
		t.Fatalf("$F4EA = %02X, want 04 (chest 2, LSB first)", got)
	}
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF30D); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("$F30D = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	// Unmodelled addresses read -1 for the VM to record as transparent.
	for _, addr := range []int{0xF30E, 0xF2D3, 0xF017, 0x0600} {
		if got := gs.MemReadByte(addr); got != -1 {
			t.Fatalf("unmodelled %#x = %d, want -1", addr, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestMemStoreByte(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	if !gs.MemStoreByte(0xF322, 0x0A) {
		t.Fatal("$F322 store refused")
	}
	if gs.ProtagonistWalkID != 0x0A {
		t.Fatalf("walk id = %d, want 0A (the 0846-chain 4F_45 write)", gs.ProtagonistWalkID)
	}
	if gs.MemStoreByte(0x1311, 1) {
		t.Fatal("unmodelled store accepted ($1311 must return false)")
	}
}

// TestTreasureBits: FF:1D37's bit array at $F4EA, LSB first (main.gd
// selftest: chest 14 -> $F4EB = 0x40).
func TestTreasureBits(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetTreasureOpen(14)
	if !gs.TreasureOpen(14) {
		t.Fatal("chest 14 not open")
	}
	if gs.TreasureOpen(15) {
		t.Fatal("chest 15 open (must stay closed)")
	}
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF4EB); got != 0x40 {
		t.Fatalf("$F4EB = %02X, want 40", got)
	}
	gs.SetTreasureOpen(0)
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF4EA); got != 0x01 {
		t.Fatalf("$F4EA = %02X, want 01 (chest 0, bit 0)", got)
	}
}

// TestPlayClock re-hosts the measured selftest pin: with the $EFFF
// contact-grace byte at 2, 3661*60+5 logic frames leave 1:01:01.05, the
// grace drained, and $F30D readable as 5 (main.gd "play clock ok"; the
// clock resets at the opening 0800 start, measured frame 10622).
func TestPlayClock(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.SetVar(0xFF, 2)
	for i := 0; i < 3661*60+5; i++ {
		gs.ClockTick()
	}
	if gs.Clock != [4]byte{1, 1, 1, 5} {
		t.Fatalf("play clock %v, want [1 1 1 5]", gs.Clock)
	}
	if gs.GetVar(0xFF) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("$EFFF = %d, want drained", gs.GetVar(0xFF))
	}
	if got := gs.MemReadByte(0xF30D); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("$F30D = %d, want 5", got)
	}
	gs.ClockReset()
	if gs.Clock != [4]byte{} {
		t.Fatalf("clock reset left %v", gs.Clock)
	}
	// The counter stops at 99:59:59:59 and the reset does not clear the
	// stop latch (game_state.gd clock_reset only zeroes the array).
	gs.Clock = [4]byte{99, 59, 59, 59}
	gs.ClockTick()
	if gs.Clock != [4]byte{99, 59, 59, 59} || !gs.ClockStopped {
		t.Fatalf("cap tick gave %v stopped=%v, want latch", gs.Clock, gs.ClockStopped)
	}
	gs.ClockReset()
	gs.ClockTick()
	if gs.Clock != [4]byte{} {
		t.Fatalf("tick after reset+cap gave %v, want held (latch stays)", gs.Clock)
	}
}

// TestSelectTables pins the engine tables (main.gd selftest "select ok",
// "walk ids ok", "naming ok"): FE:961B row -> ally id and -> walk figure,
// and the default names through the actor-name table order FD:1480
// rows 0-7 = ユリアン エレン サラ トーマス ハリード ミカエル モニカ
// カタリナ.
func TestSelectTables(t *testing.T) {
	if SelectRows != [8]int{0, 3, 5, 4, 2, 1, 6, 7} {
		t.Fatalf("SELECT_ROWS %v != FE:961B table", SelectRows)
	}
	if ProtagonistWalkIDs != [8]int{1, 3, 2, 6, 5, 4, 0, 0x6C} {
		t.Fatalf("PROTAGONIST_WALK_IDS %v != FE:961B+0 table", ProtagonistWalkIDs)
	}
	actorNames := [8]string{"ユリアン", "エレン", "サラ", "トーマス", "ハリード", "ミカエル", "モニカ", "カタリナ"}
	for row, ally := range SelectRows {
		if DefaultNames[row] != actorNames[ally] {
			t.Fatalf("default name row %d: %s != actor table %s", row, DefaultNames[row], actorNames[ally])
		}
		if got := NewGameStateWithRow(row); SelectRows[got.ProtagonistRow] != ally {
			t.Fatalf("row %d does not resolve to ally %02X", row, ally)
		}
	}
	// Row 3 = ハリード: the selftest's pick (ally 04, walk id 06).
	if SelectRows[3] != 4 || ProtagonistWalkIDs[3] != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("row 3: ally %02X walk %02X, want 04/06", SelectRows[3], ProtagonistWalkIDs[3])
	}
}

// NewGameStateWithRow is the test's select-confirm step: a fresh state
// with the row written (main.gd _on_select_picked sets protagonist_row).
func NewGameStateWithRow(row int) *GameState {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.ProtagonistRow = row
	return gs
}

// TestCustomNameResolution re-hosts the selftest "actor names ok" shape:
// with row 3 (ハリード) picked and ゆうき entered, `4a 04` and
// `4f 2f 00` print the entered name, `4a 01` keeps the table name; with
// the default kept, the leader falls back to the table name too.
func TestCustomNameResolution(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := smallCatalog()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.ProtagonistRow = 3
	gs.ProtagonistName = "ゆうき"
	gs.SetVar(0, 4)
	v := vm.New(cat)
	v.State = gs
	v.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		{Kind: "cmd", Addr: "FC:0000", Hex: "4a 04", Note: "spk4A"},
		{Kind: "cmd", Addr: "FC:0002", Hex: "4a 01", Note: "spk4A"},
		{Kind: "cmd", Addr: "FC:0004", Hex: "4f 2f 00", Note: "4F_2F"},
		{Kind: "cmd", Addr: "FC:0007", Hex: "43", Note: "end"},
	}, 0)
	if page := v.NextPage(); page != "ゆうきエレンゆうき" {
		t.Fatalf("actor-name ops with an entered leader name: %q", page)
	}
	// Default kept: "" resolves through the catalog table name.
	gs.ProtagonistName = ""
	v2 := vm.New(cat)
	v2.State = gs
	v2.LoadEvent([]vm.Op{
		{Kind: "cmd", Addr: "FC:0000", Hex: "4a 04", Note: "spk4A"},
		{Kind: "cmd", Addr: "FC:0002", Hex: "43", Note: "end"},
	}, 0)
	if page := v2.NextPage(); page != cat.ActorName(4) {
		t.Fatalf("default leader name %q, want the table name %q", page, cat.ActorName(4))
	}
}

// TestFieldRNGStream re-hosts the selftest's 40 live field RNG calls
// after the frame-10620 reseed ($0A = 83, $0B = 00) in the row-0 opening
// (main.gd rng_live; the formula reproduces 400 consecutive live calls).
func TestFieldRNGStream(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.FieldRNG.Reseed(0x83)
	live := [][3]int{
		{0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 2}, {0, 4, 3}, {0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 4}, {0, 4, 4},
		{0, 4, 3}, {0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 1}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 2}, {0, 4, 4}, {0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 0},
		{0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 2}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 3}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 0}, {0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 0},
		{0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 4}, {0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 3}, {0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 3}, {0, 4, 2},
		{0, 4, 0}, {0, 4, 1}, {0, 3, 3}, {0, 4, 2}, {0, 4, 4},
	}
	for i, c := range live {
		if got := gs.FieldRand(c[0], c[1]); got != c[2] {
			t.Fatalf("field rng call %d = %d, live %d", i, got, c[2])
		}
	}
}

// TestSwapBackRefusedWhenPartyFull: the six WRAM slots are the hard

// TestSpawnActorPassesVarBytes: objOp 17 2E (C0:D72D) calls the field's
// spawner with the EF00 graphic, EF01/EF02 tile and EF03 pose bytes;
// without a field (nil Spawner, like an unset Callable) nothing is
// created.
func TestSpawnActorPassesVarBytes(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	var spawned [4]int
	gs.Spawner = func(gfx, tileHi, tileLo, pose int) {
		spawned = [4]int{gfx, tileHi, tileLo, pose}
	}
	gs.SetVar(0, 0x40)
	gs.SetVar(1, 0)
	gs.SetVar(2, 1)
	gs.SetVar(3, 3)
	gs.SpawnActor()

		t.Fatalf("spawn args %v, want EF00..EF03", spawned)
	}
	gs.Spawner = nil
	gs.SpawnActor() // no field: nothing happens, no crash
}

// TestInstallActionRecordsRefusedInstall: objOp 17 1F/17 20 — the
// installer's false return (objects the field does not hold) leaves the
// install recorded for the caller, and a nil Installer records too
// (C0:B1F7/B2D4).
func TestInstallActionRecordsRefusedInstall(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGameState()
	gs.Installer = func(obj, id int, eventDriven bool) bool {
		return obj == 0x40
	}
	gs.InstallAction(0x40, 0x48, true)
	gs.InstallAction(0x80, 0x010A, false)
	if len(gs.Installs) != 1 || gs.Installs[0] != (Install{Obj: 0x80, ID: 0x010A, EventDriven: false}) {
		t.Fatalf("installs %v, want only the refused 0x80 install", gs.Installs)
	}
	gs2 := NewGameState()
	gs2.InstallAction(0x40, 0x48, true)
	if len(gs2.Installs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("installs %v without an installer, want the install recorded", gs2.Installs)
	}
}
```

`internal/game/state/testhelpers_test.go`:

```go
package state

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"sync"

	"saga3/internal/game/vm"
)

// hexID formats an ally id the way the export writes them.
func hexID(id int) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%02X", id) }

// jsonUnmarshal wraps json.Unmarshal for the export probes.
func jsonUnmarshal(data []byte, v any) error {
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, v); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("parse export json: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// Fixture paths — the fixtures are read in place, no copies
// (docs/migration.md working rules): the godot data exports and the
// committed parity subset under internal/game/vm/testdata.
const (
	godotData  = "../../../exports/data/"
	eventsPath = godotData + "events.json"
	alliesPath = godotData + "allies.json"
	romPath    = "../../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"
)

func onceCatalog(path string) func() (*vm.FileCatalog, error) {
	var once sync.Once
	var cat *vm.FileCatalog
	var err error
	return func() (*vm.FileCatalog, error) {
		once.Do(func() { cat, err = vm.LoadCatalog(path) })
		return cat, err
	}
}

// fullCatalog is the real export the selftest replays (199 MB, span-
// indexed; RawOps decodes one event's array on demand).
var fullCatalog = onceCatalog(eventsPath)

// cmdOp builds a cmd op.
func cmdOp(addr, hex, note string) vm.Op {
	return vm.Op{Kind: "cmd", Addr: addr, Hex: hex, Note: note}
}

// textOp builds a text op.
func textOp(addr, s string) vm.Op {
	return vm.Op{Kind: "text", Addr: addr, Hex: "81", Text: s}
}

// gateOp builds a 3-byte gate cmd op with both continuations (TRUE at
// S+3, FALSE at S+5, vm-semantics §2.1; the same contract 0d 07/09 and
// 45 carry).
func gateOp(addr, hex, note string) vm.Op {
	op := cmdOp(addr, hex, note)
	op.GateTrue = "addr " + bankAddr(addr, 3)
	op.GateFalse = "addr " + bankAddr(addr, 5)
	return op
}

// bankAddr formats addr + offset in the op's own bank.
func bankAddr(addr string, off int) string {
	v, err := strconv.ParseUint(addr[3:], 16, 16)
	if err != nil {
		panic("bad hex addr " + addr)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%04x", addr[:2], int(v)+off)
}
```

`internal/game/state/vmstate.go`:

```go
package state

// The vm.State implementation (internal/game/vm/state.go is the
// consumer-defined surface; godot/game_state.gd is the reference). Every
// method corresponds to one VM access; helpers outside the interface
// (clock, treasure, party edits) back the field/flow slices.

// ---- nibble flag spaces (vm-semantics §2.5: even id = high nibble) ----

// nibbleAt reads flag id's nibble of a packed array.
func nibbleAt(arr []byte, id int) int {
	b := arr[id>>1]
	if id%2 == 0 {
		return int(b >> 4)
	}
	return int(b & 0xF)
}

// setNibbleAt writes flag id's nibble, value masked to 4 bits.
func setNibbleAt(arr []byte, id, v int) {
	v &= 0xF
	i := id >> 1
	if id%2 == 0 {
		arr[i] = (arr[i] & 0x0F) | byte(v<<4)
	} else {
		arr[i] = (arr[i] & 0xF0) | byte(v)
	}
}

func (s *GameState) GetVanilla(id int) int { return nibbleAt(s.Vanilla[:], id&0xFF) }
func (s *GameState) SetVanilla(id, v int)  { setNibbleAt(s.Vanilla[:], id&0xFF, v) }
func (s *GameState) GetPacked4(id int) int { return nibbleAt(s.Packed4[:], id&0xFF) }
func (s *GameState) SetPacked4(id, v int)  { setNibbleAt(s.Packed4[:], id&0xFF, v) }
func (s *GameState) GetExt(id int) int     { return nibbleAt(s.Ext[:], id&0x1FF) }

// SetExt writes the ext flag space (op 0D 02/03; game_state.gd set_ext).
func (s *GameState) SetExt(id, v int) { setNibbleAt(s.Ext[:], id&0x1FF, v) }

// ---- EF00 variables (ops 40/41/48 write; 45/3A/getItem/money read) ----

func (s *GameState) GetVar(a int) int { return int(s.Vars[a&0xFF]) }
func (s *GameState) SetVar(a, v int)  { s.Vars[a&0xFF] = byte(v & 0xFF) }

// GetVarWord reads the EF00 word at index a, little-endian (the engine
// writes/stores 16-bit words); the +1 wraps within the page.
func (s *GameState) GetVarWord(a int) int { return s.GetVar(a) | s.GetVar(a+1)<<8 }
func (s *GameState) SetVarWord(a, v int)  { s.SetVar(a, v&0xFF); s.SetVar(a+1, (v>>8)&0xFF) }

// GetScratch/SetScratch back the WRAM $7FF900 spill array (0d 30/31,
// 5A:C000/C020). The index is an op byte, 0..255; out of range is a
// decoded-stream bug and crashes like the GDScript would.
func (s *GameState) GetScratch(i int) int { return int(s.scratch[i]) }
func (s *GameState) SetScratch(i, v int)  { s.scratch[i] = byte(v & 0xFF) }

// ---- selection menu state ($D3BF/$D3C0/$D3C1, vm-semantics §2.3) ----

func (s *GameState) MenuSelection() int     { return s.menuSelection }
func (s *GameState) SetMenuSelection(v int) { s.menuSelection = v }
func (s *GameState) SetMenuOpen(v int)      { s.menuOpen = v }
func (s *GameState) MenuCount() int         { return s.menuCount }
func (s *GameState) SetMenuCount(v int)     { s.menuCount = v }

// MenuOpen returns the $D3C0 window-open byte (optA clears it, optB/optC
// raise it); the VM only writes it today, the flow slice reads it.
func (s *GameState) MenuOpen() int { return s.menuOpen }

// ---- runtime state: gold, inventory, party ----

// Gold is the 16-bit WRAM $7EF31A value.
func (s *GameState) Gold() int { return s.gold }

// PayGold spends: the pay path floors at 0 (engine C0:29A1).
func (s *GameState) PayGold(amount int) { s.gold = max(s.gold-amount, 0) }

// GainGold receives: capped at GoldCap = 30000 (engine C0:395E, CMP
// #$7530).
func (s *GameState) GainGold(amount int) { s.gold = min(s.gold+amount, GoldCap) }

// AddBankGold adds to one of the two 金取引所 deposits ($7EF31C/$7EF31E),
// capped at 0xFFFF.
func (s *GameState) AddBankGold(slot, amount int) {
	s.Bank[slot] = min(s.Bank[slot]+amount, BankCap)
}

// AddItem gives one unit (getItem gives one per op, C0:2E1F): the count
// saturates at ItemCountMax = 99.
func (s *GameState) AddItem(id int) {
	s.Inventory[id] = min(s.Inventory[id]+1, ItemCountMax)
}

// RemoveItem drops count units (menus; game_state.gd remove_item): the
// entry disappears at zero.
func (s *GameState) RemoveItem(id, count int) {
	left := s.Inventory[id] - count
	if left <= 0 {
		delete(s.Inventory, id)
		return
	}
	s.Inventory[id] = left
}

// ItemCount returns the bag count.
func (s *GameState) ItemCount(id int) int { return s.Inventory[id] }

// PartyHasItem reports whether the party carries the item: in the bag or
// equipped by a member. Event evidence: the 0D 07 gates check key items
// (白虎の鎧, タイニィフェザー) that the game text treats as
// 「持っている」 without naming a slot (game_state.gd party_has_item).
func (s *GameState) PartyHasItem(id int) bool {
	if s.ItemCount(id) > 0 {
		return true
	}
	for _, memberID := range s.party {
		for _, slot := range s.Equipment[memberID] {
			if slot == id {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// Party returns a copy of the party slot list (ally ids, leader first).
func (s *GameState) Party() []int {
	return append([]int(nil), s.party...)
}

// SetPartyList is op 4F_31 (engine C0:20EC): it replaces the six party
// slots at $F323-$F328 with record slots; $FF = empty and is dropped;
// leader = first entry; duplicates collapse; the swap-out list clears.
// This is the only event op that writes membership (vm-semantics §6.3).
// A slot outside the record table is a decoded-stream bug and crashes
// like the GDScript's out-of-range read.
func (s *GameState) SetPartyList(slots []int) {
	s.party = nil
	s.Away = nil
	for _, k := range slots {
		if k == 0xFF {
			continue
		}
		id := RecordIDs[k]
		found := false
		for _, p := range s.party {
			if p == id {
				found = true
				break
			}
		}
		if !found {
			s.party = append(s.party, id)
		}
	}
}

// PartySize is the member count byte $F319 (the VM derives it from the
// list; vm-semantics §6.3).
func (s *GameState) PartySize() int { return len(s.party) }

// Join appends an ally (menus; game_state.gd join): no duplicates, capped
// at PartyMax.
func (s *GameState) Join(id int) {
	for _, p := range s.party {
		if p == id {
			return
		}
	}
	if len(s.party) >= PartyMax {
		return
	}
	s.party = append(s.party, id)
}

// RemoveMember drops an ally from the party and the swap-out list.
func (s *GameState) RemoveMember(id int) {
	party := s.party[:0]
	for _, p := range s.party {
		if p != id {
			party = append(party, p)
		}
	}
	s.party = party
	away := s.Away[:0]
	for _, a := range s.Away {
		if a != id {
			away = append(away, a)
		}
	}
	s.Away = away
}

// SwapOut moves an ally out (battle swap; game_state.gd swap_out).
func (s *GameState) SwapOut(id int) {
	for i, p := range s.party {
		if p == id {
			s.party = append(s.party[:i], s.party[i+1:]...)
			s.Away = append(s.Away, id)
			return
		}
	}
}

// SwapBack returns a swapped-out ally while a slot is free.
func (s *GameState) SwapBack(id int) {
	for i, a := range s.Away {
		if a == id {
			if len(s.party) >= PartyMax {
				return
			}
			s.Away = append(s.Away[:i], s.Away[i+1:]...)
			s.party = append(s.party, id)
			return
		}
	}
}

// ---- custom names (vm-semantics §2.7, docs/naming.md) ----

// CustomNameFor resolves the actor-name rule: the leader record's actor
// id ($F000, the select pick) maps to the entered name ($F300); "" for
// everyone else and when the default name was kept. Ops 4A (C0:3188) and
// 4F_2F (C0:31A6) both CMP $7EF000 and copy $F300 on a match.
func (s *GameState) CustomNameFor(actorID int) string {
	if actorID == SelectRows[s.ProtagonistRow] {
		return s.ProtagonistName
	}
	return ""
}

// ---- field RNG (C0:0733, docs/parity.md §4.4) ----

// FieldRand rolls lo..hi inclusive on the shared field RNG stream (8-bit
// width semantics; rng.Field.Roll).
func (s *GameState) FieldRand(lo, hi int) int {
	return s.FieldRNG.Roll(uint8(lo), uint8(hi))
}

// ---- field-side effects of objOps ----

// SpawnActor backs objOp 17 2E (C0:D72D): an event actor from EF00
// graphic, EF01/EF02 tile, EF03 pose. The field sets Spawner; without a
// field nothing is created (game_state.gd actor_spawner).
func (s *GameState) SpawnActor() {
	if s.Spawner == nil {
		return
	}
	s.Spawner(s.GetVar(0), s.GetVar(1), s.GetVar(2), s.GetVar(3))
}

// InstallAction backs objOp 17 1F/17 20 (C0:B1F7/B2D4): object obj runs
// action script id. The field sets Installer and runs the script on the
// object, whose op 09 words reach the queue when the object gets there;
// its false return (objects the field does not hold) leaves the install
// recorded for the caller (game_state.gd install_action's
// action_installer callable). The no-field fallback that walks the
// script bank for op 09 words (action_scripts.gd enqueued_words) lands
// with internal/game/actions — the event queue it feeds is drained by
// the field slice, so this package records the install until then.
func (s *GameState) InstallAction(obj, id int, eventDriven bool) {
	if s.Installer != nil && s.Installer(obj, id, eventDriven) {
		return
	}
	s.Installs = append(s.Installs, Install{Obj: obj, ID: id, EventDriven: eventDriven})
}

// Install is one recorded InstallAction call.
type Install struct {
	Obj         int
	ID          int
	EventDriven bool
}

// ---- the mem model (WRAM byte reads/writes through EF00 pointers) ----

// MemReadByte backs op 45 chkMem (C0:2F22): it reads the WRAM byte at
// the address held in the EF00 word, not the EF00 byte itself.
// Addresses the dump set points at and the port models: $F319 member
// count (156 gates), $F000 the leader record's actor id = the select
// pick (event 0800's protagonist route), $F322, the $F323-$F328 slot
// list, the vanilla flag bytes ($F4CC/$F4CD, $F4A5-7), the treasure
// array and the play clock, and the EF00 space itself. Others (F2D3,
// F017, F30E = the map header byte $D2F2, ...) return -1 for the VM to
// record as transparent. The engine's AND #$7F for member-record bytes
// +0x25..+0x2F (68:3730) only touches addresses this does not model.
func (s *GameState) MemReadByte(addr int) int {
	switch {
	case addr >= 0xEF00 && addr <= 0xEFFF:
		return s.GetVar(addr - 0xEF00)
	case addr >= VanillaWRAM && addr < VanillaWRAM+128:
		// whole bytes of the nibble-flag array (C0:370D reads
		// $7EF46A + id>>1): $F4CC/$F4CD gates compare two flags at once
		return int(s.Vanilla[addr-VanillaWRAM])
	case addr >= TreasureWRAM && addr < TreasureWRAM+32:
		return int(s.Treasure[addr-TreasureWRAM])
	case addr >= ClockWRAM && addr < ClockWRAM+4:
		return int(s.Clock[addr-ClockWRAM])
	case addr == 0xF000:
		return SelectRows[s.ProtagonistRow]
	case addr == 0xF319:
		return len(s.party)
	case addr == 0xF322:
		return s.ProtagonistWalkID & 0xFF
	case addr >= 0xF323 && addr <= 0xF328:
		if i := addr - 0xF323; i < len(s.party) {
			return s.party[i]
		}
		return 0xFF
	}
	return -1
}

// MemStoreByte backs op 4F_45 (C0:3688), a generic pointer store into
// WRAM $7E:EF00word(b). The only address the dump set writes is $F322;
// unknown addresses return false so the VM can record the op as
// unhandled (game_state.gd mem_store_byte).
func (s *GameState) MemStoreByte(addr, value int) bool {
	if addr == 0xF322 {
		s.ProtagonistWalkID = value & 0xFF
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// ---- treasure flags (FF:1D37: bit = byte[id>>3] >> (id&7), LSB first) ----

// TreasureOpen reports chest id open.
func (s *GameState) TreasureOpen(id int) bool {
	return (s.Treasure[id>>3]>>(id&7))&1 == 1
}

// SetTreasureOpen marks chest id open.
func (s *GameState) SetTreasureOpen(id int) {
	s.Treasure[id>>3] |= 1 << (id & 7)
}

// ---- the play clock ($F30A-$F30D) ----

// ClockReset zeroes the play clock. The engine resets it when the
// opening event 0800 starts (measured: 0002350E -> 00000000 at frame
// 10622; the title/menu play never counts). Only the counter zeroes —
// the stop latch stays (game_state.gd clock_reset).
func (s *GameState) ClockReset() {
	s.Clock = [4]byte{}
}

// ClockTick advances one logic frame (C5:F327): frames -> seconds ->
// minutes -> hours, stopping at 99:59:59:59 ($D8D7). Each second
// rollover also decrements the $EFFF contact-grace byte
// (docs/battle-defeat.md §6.7; game_state.gd clock_tick).
func (s *GameState) ClockTick() {
	if s.ClockStopped {
		return
	}
	s.Clock[3]++
	if s.Clock[3] < 60 {
		return
	}
	if s.Vars[0xFF] != 0 {
		s.Vars[0xFF]--
	}
	s.Clock[3] = 0
	s.Clock[2]++
	if s.Clock[2] < 60 {
		return
	}
	s.Clock[2] = 0
	s.Clock[1]++
	if s.Clock[1] < 60 {
		return
	}
	s.Clock[1] = 0
	s.Clock[0]++
	if s.Clock[0] < 100 {
		return
	}
	s.Clock = [4]byte{99, 59, 59, 59}
	s.ClockStopped = true
}
```

`internal/game/vm/catalog.go`:

```go
package vm

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Catalog is the event surface tail dispatch needs (consumer-defined).
// ActorName/PlaceName back the 4A/3B name-insertion ops.
type Catalog interface {
	HasEvent(nativeID int) bool
	RawOps(nativeID int) []Op
	End16(nativeID int) string
	ActorName(id int) string
	PlaceName(id int) string
}

// FileCatalog reads an events.json export in place, with the same lazy
// contract the GDScript port keeps: Load indexes event ids and frame ends
// without materializing op streams; RawOps decodes one event's raw array
// on demand. Side files, both optional (event_catalog.gd):
//
//	<dir>/events_index.json  frame end16 per event (cmd/dumpevents)
//	<dir>/events_names.json  actor and place name tables
type FileCatalog struct {
	eventsPath string
	spans      map[string]span // "%04X" id -> byte span of its raw array
	end16      map[string]string
	actors     map[string]string
	places     map[string]string
}

type span struct {
	off, len int64
}

// LoadCatalog indexes an events.json export. The full 133 MB catalog is
// only scanned, never materialized: each event keeps a byte span, decoded
// when RawOps asks for it.
func LoadCatalog(eventsPath string) (*FileCatalog, error) {
	cat := &FileCatalog{
		eventsPath: eventsPath,
		spans:      map[string]span{},
		end16:      map[string]string{},
		actors:     map[string]string{},
		places:     map[string]string{},
	}
	if err := cat.loadNames(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := cat.loadIndex(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := cat.scanEvents(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return cat, nil
}

// loadNames reads the actor/place name tables (events_names.json:
// {"actors": {"<id>": name, ...}, "places": {...}}).
func (c *FileCatalog) loadNames() error {
	path := strings.TrimSuffix(c.eventsPath, ".json") + "_names.json"
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return nil // optional file, like event_catalog.gd's FileAccess check
	}
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read names: %w", err)
	}
	var names struct {
		Actors map[string]string `json:"actors"`
		Places map[string]string `json:"places"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &names); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	for id, name := range names.Actors {
		c.actors[id] = name
	}
	for id, name := range names.Places {
		c.places[id] = name
	}
	return nil
}

// loadIndex reads the frame ends. The index writes end16 unpadded
// ("8ef" for 0800); op addrs are 4 digits, so pad here and compare
// directly in the VM's end16 check (event_catalog.gd).
func (c *FileCatalog) loadIndex() error {
	dir := c.eventsPath[:strings.LastIndex(c.eventsPath, "/")+1]
	path := dir + "events_index.json"
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read events index: %w", err)
	}
	var rows []struct {
		ID    string `json:"id"`
		Entry string `json:"entry"`
		End16 string `json:"end16"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rows); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	for _, row := range rows {
		if row.ID == "" || row.End16 == "" {
			continue
		}
		bank := "??"
		if len(row.Entry) >= 2 {
			bank = strings.ToUpper(row.Entry[:2])
		}
		c.end16[normalizeIDString(row.ID)] = bank + ":" + pad4(row.End16)
	}
	return nil
}

// scanEvents walks the events array once, recording each event's id and
// the byte span of its raw array.
func (c *FileCatalog) scanEvents() error {
	f, err := os.Open(c.eventsPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("open events: %w", err)
	}
	defer f.Close()
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bufio.NewReaderSize(f, 1<<20))
	tok, err := dec.Token()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
	}
	if d, ok := tok.(json.Delim); !ok || d != '[' {
		return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: want a top-level array", c.eventsPath)
	}
	for dec.More() {
		tok, err := dec.Token() // '{'
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
		}
		if d, ok := tok.(json.Delim); !ok || d != '{' {
			return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: want an object element", c.eventsPath)
		}
		id := ""
		var raw span
		for dec.More() {
			keyTok, err := dec.Token()
			if err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
			}
			key, _ := keyTok.(string)
			switch key {
			case "id":
				tok, err := dec.Token()
				if err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
				}
				s, _ := tok.(string)
				id = s
			case "raw":
				// Anchor the span at the '[' token: InputOffset taken at
				// the key still points before the ':' (the decoder consumes
				// it lazily, measured). The span's last byte is the array
				// closer; RawOps drops it and re-wraps the content in
				// brackets before decoding.
				start, err := skipArray(dec)
				if err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
				}
				raw = span{off: start, len: dec.InputOffset() - start}
			default:
				if err := skipValue(dec); err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
				}
			}
		}
		if _, err := dec.Token(); err != nil { // '}'
			return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
		}
		if id != "" && raw.len > 0 {
			c.spans[normalizeIDString(id)] = raw
		}
	}
	_, err = dec.Token() // top-level ']'
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", c.eventsPath, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// skipArray consumes one JSON array and returns the offset of its first
// content byte (just past the '[').
func skipArray(dec *json.Decoder) (int64, error) {
	tok, err := dec.Token()
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	if d, ok := tok.(json.Delim); !ok || d != '[' {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("want an array")
	}
	start := dec.InputOffset()
	depth := 1
	for depth > 0 {
		tok, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return 0, err
		}
		if d, ok := tok.(json.Delim); ok {
			switch d {
			case '[', '{':
				depth++
			case ']', '}':
				depth--
			}
		}
	}
	return start, nil
}

// skipValue consumes one JSON value of any shape.
func skipValue(dec *json.Decoder) error {
	tok, err := dec.Token()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	d, ok := tok.(json.Delim)
	if !ok {
		return nil // scalar
	}
	var openDelim, closeDelim json.Delim
	switch d {
	case '[':
		openDelim, closeDelim = '[', ']'
	case '{':
		openDelim, closeDelim = '{', '}'
	default:
		return nil // ']' or '}' never starts a value here
	}
	depth := 1
	for depth > 0 {
		tok, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if dd, ok := tok.(json.Delim); ok {
			if dd == openDelim {
				depth++
			} else if dd == closeDelim {
				depth--
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// pad4 left-pads an end16 to the 4-digit op-addr form ("8ef" -> "08ef"),
// the same lpad event_catalog.gd applies.
func pad4(s string) string {
	s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
	for len(s) < 4 {
		s = "0" + s
	}
	return s
}

// normalizeID maps a native event id to its catalog key. Native 4Cxx is
// cataloged under its 0Fxx alias (event_catalog.gd; engine 5A:AC70).
func normalizeID(nativeID int) string {
	if nativeID>>8 == 0x4C {
		nativeID = 0x0F00 + nativeID&0xFF
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%04X", nativeID)
}

// normalizeIDString normalizes an id string from the exports ("0800").
func normalizeIDString(id string) string {
	v, err := strconv.ParseUint(id, 16, 16)
	if err != nil {
		return strings.ToUpper(id)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%04X", v)
}

// HasEvent reports whether the catalog carries the event.
func (c *FileCatalog) HasEvent(nativeID int) bool {
	_, ok := c.spans[normalizeID(nativeID)]
	return ok
}

// AllIDs lists the cataloged event ids (event_catalog.gd all_ids).
func (c *FileCatalog) AllIDs() []string {
	ids := make([]string, 0, len(c.spans))
	for id := range c.spans {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	return ids
}

// RawOps decodes one event's raw op stream from the export, on demand.
func (c *FileCatalog) RawOps(nativeID int) []Op {
	span, ok := c.spans[normalizeID(nativeID)]
	if !ok {
		return nil
	}
	f, err := os.Open(c.eventsPath)
	if err != nil {
		panic("vm: reopen events: " + err.Error())
	}
	defer f.Close()
	buf := make([]byte, span.len)
	if _, err := f.ReadAt(buf, span.off); err != nil {
		panic("vm: read event raw: " + err.Error())
	}
	var ops []Op
	// The span ends one past the array closer: strip it and re-wrap.
	content := buf[:bytes.LastIndexByte(buf, ']')]
	full := make([]byte, 0, len(content)+2)
	full = append(full, '[')
	full = append(full, content...)
	full = append(full, ']')
	if err := json.Unmarshal(full, &ops); err != nil {
		panic("vm: decode event raw: " + err.Error())
	}
	return ops
}

// End16 returns the event's frame end address ("BANK:xxxx"), "" when the
// index lacks it (unbounded frame; event_catalog.gd).
func (c *FileCatalog) End16(nativeID int) string {
	return c.end16[normalizeID(nativeID)]
}

// ActorName returns actor id's table name ("" when absent).
func (c *FileCatalog) ActorName(id int) string {
	return c.actors[strconv.Itoa(id)]
}

// PlaceName returns place id's table name ("" when absent).
func (c *FileCatalog) PlaceName(id int) string {
	return c.places[strconv.Itoa(id)]
}
```

`internal/game/vm/names.go`:

```go
package vm

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
)

// NameResolver supplies the item and ally names the name-insertion ops
// place into pages: op 3A / 4F_50 item names, op 39 party member names.
// Actor and place names come from the Catalog. The GDScript reference
// loads exports/data items.json / allies.json lazily on first use.
type NameResolver interface {
	ItemName(id int) string
	AllyName(id int) string
}

// FileNames is the NameResolver backed by the data exports: rows with hex
// id strings and a "name" field.
type FileNames struct {
	itemsPath  string
	alliesPath string
	items      map[int]string
	allies     map[int]string
}

// NewFileNames reads items.json and allies.json on first use (the same
// lazy contract as event_vm.gd's _item_name/_ally_name).
func NewFileNames(itemsPath, alliesPath string) *FileNames {
	return &FileNames{itemsPath: itemsPath, alliesPath: alliesPath}
}

func (n *FileNames) ItemName(id int) string {
	if n.items == nil {
		n.items = loadNames(n.itemsPath)
	}
	return n.items[id]
}

func (n *FileNames) AllyName(id int) string {
	if n.allies == nil {
		n.allies = loadNames(n.alliesPath)
	}
	return n.allies[id]
}

// loadNames parses one data file's id -> name rows; a missing file yields
// an empty table (the GDScript checks FileAccess.file_exists first).
func loadNames(path string) map[int]string {
	out := map[int]string{}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return out
	}
	if err != nil {
		panic("vm: read names " + path + ": " + err.Error())
	}
	var rows []struct {
		ID   string `json:"id"`
		Name string `json:"name"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rows); err != nil {
		panic("vm: parse names " + path + ": " + err.Error())
	}
	for _, row := range rows {
		v, err := strconv.ParseUint(row.ID, 16, 16)
		if err != nil {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("vm: %s: malformed id %q", path, row.ID))
		}
		out[int(v)] = row.Name
	}
	return out
}
```

`internal/game/vm/op.go`:

```go
package vm

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Op is one decoded VM instruction or text run from an event dump
// (events.json "raw" arrays, produced by cmd/exportdialogue over
// internal/bokuno's walker).
type Op struct {
	Kind      string `json:"k"`                    // "cmd" | "text" | "jumpL" | "jump16" | "join"
	Addr      string `json:"addr"`                 // "BANK:xxxx" (upper bank, lower addr)
	Hex       string `json:"hex,omitempty"`        // opcode then operands, space-separated
	Note      string `json:"note,omitempty"`       // cmd note (internal/bokuno ops.go noteOf)
	Text      string `json:"text,omitempty"`       // text runs
	Target    string `json:"target,omitempty"`     // jumpL/jump16/join targets
	Operand   string `json:"operand,omitempty"`    // flag-op operand object (JSON)
	GateTrue  string `json:"gate_true,omitempty"`  // "addr XX:XXXX" | "event NNNN"
	GateFalse string `json:"gate_false,omitempty"` // same forms
}

// hexBytes parses an op's hex field ("4f 16 06") into bytes, opcode first.
func hexBytes(s string) []int {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, " ")
	out := make([]int, 0, len(parts))
	for _, p := range parts {
		v, err := strconv.ParseUint(p, 16, 8)
		if err != nil {
			panic("vm: malformed op hex " + s + ": " + err.Error())
		}
		out = append(out, int(v))
	}
	return out
}

// firstByteOf returns the op's first hex byte, or -1 when it has none
// (event_vm.gd _first_byte).
func firstByteOf(op Op) int {
	if len(op.Hex) < 2 {
		return -1
	}
	v, err := strconv.ParseUint(op.Hex[:2], 16, 8)
	if err != nil {
		panic("vm: malformed op hex " + op.Hex + ": " + err.Error())
	}
	return int(v)
}

// addrParts splits "FC:08ef" into bank and 16-bit address.
func addrParts(addr string) (int, int) {
	if len(addr) != 7 || addr[2] != ':' {
		panic("vm: malformed op addr " + strconv.Quote(addr))
	}
	bank, err := strconv.ParseUint(addr[:2], 16, 8)
	if err != nil {
		panic("vm: malformed op addr " + strconv.Quote(addr) + ": " + err.Error())
	}
	a, err := strconv.ParseUint(addr[3:], 16, 16)
	if err != nil {
		panic("vm: malformed op addr " + strconv.Quote(addr) + ": " + err.Error())
	}
	return int(bank), int(a)
}

// addrStr formats bank:addr the way the dumps write them ("FC:08ef": bank
// upper case, address lower case).
func addrStr(bank, a int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%02X:%04x", bank, a&0xFFFF)
}
```
