```go
// TestChoosePausesAndResumes: with a ChoiceHandler installed, selGoto
// pauses the VM with PendingChoices set; Choose applies the selection,
// clears the handler and runs the chosen record to the end (event_vm.gd
// pending_choices / choose).
func TestChoosePausesAndResumes(t *testing.T) {
	cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: selGotoMenu(true)}}
	st := newTestState()
	vm := New(cat)
	vm.State = st
	vm.ChoiceHandler = func([]string) {} // the UI hook; the VM only checks it is set
	vm.LoadEvent(cat.events[1], 1)

	menuPage := vm.NextPage()
	if menuPage == "" {
		t.Fatal("menu page empty before the choice pause")
	}
	if len(vm.PendingChoices) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PendingChoices %v set before selGoto ran", vm.PendingChoices)
	}

	pausePage := vm.NextPage()
	if pausePage != "" {
		t.Fatalf("pause returned page %q, want an empty page", pausePage)
	}
	if want := []string{"opt one", "opt two"}; !slicesEqualStr(vm.PendingChoices, want) {
		t.Fatalf("PendingChoices %v, want %v", vm.PendingChoices, want)
	}
	if vm.ChoiceHandler == nil {
		t.Fatal("handler cleared while the choice is still pending")
	}

	vm.Choose(1) // the reader picked the second option
	if !vm.IsFinished() {
		t.Fatal("Choose did not run the chosen record to the end")
	}
	if vm.ChoiceHandler != nil {
		t.Fatal("Choose left the handler installed")
	}
}

// ---- deferred map moves -------------------------------------------------------

// TestMapMoveDeferredUntilPageDismissed: ops 10/11 only enqueue their word
// in the engine (vm-semantics §2.8): a page already typed shows first, the
// move runs when the reader moves on (event_vm.gd _pending_moves).
func TestMapMoveDeferredUntilPageDismissed(t *testing.T) {
	cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		text("FC:0100", "page one"),
		cmd("FC:0104", "10 05", "op10"),
		text("FC:0106", "page two"),
	}}}
	st := newTestState()
	vm := New(cat)
	vm.State = st
	vm.TraceEnabled = true
	vm.MapMove = func(index int) { st.moved = append(st.moved, index) }
	vm.LoadEvent(cat.events[1], 1)
	first := vm.NextPage()
	if first != "page one" {
		t.Fatalf("first page %q, want page one", first)
	}
	if len(st.moved) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("move ran before the page was dismissed: %v", st.moved)
	}
	second := vm.NextPage()
	if second != "page two" {
		t.Fatalf("second page %q, want page two", second)
	}
	if len(st.moved) != 1 || st.moved[0] != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("moves %v, want [5] after the page", st.moved)
	}
	if m := traceLines(vm.Trace, "MAPMOVE"); len(m) != 1 || m[0] != "MAPMOVE addr=FC:0104 index=05" {
		t.Fatalf("mapmove lines %v", m)
	}
}

// ---- runtime state ops ---------------------------------------------------------

// TestFillAndGetItemMoney: the §6 decodes — fill with n == 0 means one
// byte (C0:21FD); getItem saturates the count at 99 (C0:2E1F); 4F_19
// grants capped at 30000 or deposits (C0:3947); the 0d 30/31 pair spills
// EF00[0] through scratch (5A:C000/C020).
func TestFillAndGetItemMoney(t *testing.T) {
	cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		cmd("FA:0100", "48 10 00 07", "fill"),     // n == 0: EF10 = 07
		cmd("FA:0104", "42 10", "getItem"),        // give item EF10 = 07
		cmd("FA:0106", "41 01 d0 07", "set2B"),    // EF01 = 2000
		cmd("FA:010a", "4f 19", "4F_19"),          // gold += 2000
		cmd("FA:010c", "40 00 07", "set1B"),       // EF00 = 07
		cmd("FA:010f", "0d 30 50 00", "swapOut"),  // scratch[0] = EF00 (07)
		cmd("FA:0113", "40 00 99", "set1B"),       // EF00 = 99
		cmd("FA:0116", "0d 31 00 50", "swapBack"), // EF50 = 07
		cmd("FA:011a", "43", "end"),
	}}}
	st := newTestState()
	pages, _ := runPages(t, cat, 1, cat.events[1], st)
	if len(pages) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pages %v, want none", pages)
	}
	if st.GetVar(0x10) != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("EF10 = %d, want 7 (fill n==0 means one byte)", st.GetVar(0x10))
	}
	if st.inventory[7] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("item 7 count %d, want 1", st.inventory[7])
	}
	if st.gold != 2000 {
		t.Fatalf("gold %d, want 2000", st.gold)
	}
	if st.GetVar(0x50) != 7 || st.GetScratch(0) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("swapBack: EF50 = %d scratch[0] = %d, want 7/0", st.GetVar(0x50), st.GetScratch(0))
	}
	// getItem saturation at 99 (C0:2E54 CMP #$63).
	st2 := newTestState()
	st2.inventory[7] = 99
	st2.vars[0] = 7
	vm := New(cat)
	vm.State = st2
	vm.LoadEvent([]Op{cmd("FA:0100", "42 00", "getItem")}, 0)
	vm.AllPages()
	if st2.inventory[7] != 99 {
		t.Fatalf("item 7 count %d, want saturation at 99", st2.inventory[7])
	}
}

// TestPartyWrite: 4f 31 stores six bytes into the party slot list ($FF =
// empty, dropped) — the only membership write (C0:20EC; vm-semantics
// §6.3: 0B31's `4f 31 00 01 02 03 04 05` builds the opening party).
func TestPartyWrite(t *testing.T) {
	cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		cmd("FC:c7f7", "4f 31 00 01 02 03 04 05", "4F_31"),
		cmd("FC:c7fb", "43", "end"),
	}}}
	st := newTestState()
	pages, _ := runPages(t, cat, 1, cat.events[1], st)
	want := []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6} // record slots through RECORD_IDS
	if !slicesEqual(st.party, want) {
		t.Fatalf("party %v, want %v", st.party, want)
	}
	if len(pages) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pages %v", pages)
	}
	// empties drop: `4f 31 00 ff ff ff ff ff` leaves a one-member party.
	st2 := newTestState()
	vm := New(cat)
	vm.State = st2
	vm.LoadEvent([]Op{cmd("FC:c73e", "4f 31 00 ff ff ff ff ff", "4F_31")}, 0)
	vm.AllPages()
	if !slicesEqual(st2.party, []int{0}) {
		t.Fatalf("party %v, want [0]", st2.party)
	}
}

// TestRuntimeVarOpsEdges: the EF00/WRAM edges — 4F_10 pays the EF00 word
// (C0:29A1), 4F_55 refuses to store a wrap past $FF (C0:2DD5), and 4F_45
// stores EF00[EF00[a]] through the WRAM byte model (C0:3688), recording a
// transparent op when the address is unmodeled.
func TestRuntimeVarOpsEdges(t *testing.T) {
	// 4F_10 pays the EF00 word at 0, not its low byte.
	cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		cmd("FA:0100", "41 00 34 12", "set2B"), // EF00 word = 0x1234
		cmd("FA:0104", "4f 10", "4F_10"),       // pay 0x1234
	}}}
	st := newTestState()
	st.gold = 5000
	runPages(t, cat, 1, cat.events[1], st)
	if st.gold != 5000-0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("gold %d after 4F_10, want %d (the EF00 word 0x1234 paid)", st.gold, 5000-0x1234)
	}

	// 4F_55 stops at the wrap: 0xFF + 1 must not store 0.
	cat2 := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		cmd("FA:0100", "4f 55 08", "4F_55"),
	}}}
	st2 := newTestState()
	st2.SetVar(8, 0xFF)
	runPages(t, cat2, 1, cat2.events[1], st2)
	if st2.GetVar(8) != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("EF08 = %#x after 4F_55 at $FF, want $FF (no wrap store)", st2.GetVar(8))
	}

	// 4F_45 stores EF00[EF00[a]] at the WRAM address EF00[b]: $F322 is
	// modeled, so WRAM[$F322] picks the value up as the walk id.
	cat3 := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		cmd("FA:0100", "40 01 05", "set1B"),    // EF01 = 5 (the indirection)
		cmd("FA:0103", "40 05 07", "set1B"),    // EF05 = 7 (the value)
		cmd("FA:0106", "41 02 22 f3", "set2B"), // EF02 word = 0xF322
		cmd("FA:010a", "4f 45 01 02", "4F_45"), // WRAM[$F322] = EF00[EF00[1]]
	}}}
	st3 := newTestState()
	runPages(t, cat3, 1, cat3.events[1], st3)
	if st3.walkID != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("walkID %d after 4F_45, want 7 (EF00[EF00[1]] stored)", st3.walkID)
	}

	// An unmodeled store address records the miss as a transparent op.
	cat4 := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: {
		cmd("FA:0100", "40 01 05", "set1B"),    // EF01 = 5
		cmd("FA:0103", "40 05 07", "set1B"),    // EF05 = 7
		cmd("FA:0106", "41 02 00 f3", "set2B"), // EF02 word = 0xF300 (unmodeled)
		cmd("FA:010a", "4f 45 01 02", "4F_45"),
	}}}
	vm := New(cat4)
	vm.State = newTestState()
	vm.LoadEvent(cat4.events[1], 1)
	vm.AllPages()
	missed := false
	for _, o := range vm.TransparentOps {
		if o == "4F_45->f300" {
			missed = true
		}
	}
	if !missed {
		t.Fatalf("transparent ops %v, want the 4F_45 miss record 4F_45->f300", vm.TransparentOps)
	}
}

func slicesEqual(a, b []int) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func slicesEqualStr(a, b []string) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// TestOp35OrAndMask: op 35 ors the flag's nibble with the mask when the
// operand says "or", ands it otherwise (vm-semantics §2.5).
func TestOp35OrAndMask(t *testing.T) {
	mk := func(operation string, mask int) []Op {
		op := cmd("FA:0100", "35 20 05", "op35")
		op.Operand = fmt.Sprintf(`{"space":"flag.vanilla","id":32,"mask":%d,"operation":%q}`, mask, operation)
		return []Op{op}
	}
	cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: mk("or", 0x5)}}
	st := newTestState()
	setNibbleAt(st.vanilla[:], 0x20, 0x2)
	runPages(t, cat, 1, cat.events[1], st)
	if got := st.GetVanilla(0x20); got != 0x7 {
		t.Fatalf("or: flag 0x20 = %#x, want 2|5 = 7", got)
	}
	cat2 := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: mk("and", 0xA)}}
	st2 := newTestState()
	setNibbleAt(st2.vanilla[:], 0x20, 0xF)
	runPages(t, cat2, 1, cat2.events[1], st2)
	if got := st2.GetVanilla(0x20); got != 0xA {
		t.Fatalf("and: flag 0x20 = %#x, want 15&10 = 10", got)
	}
}

// TestVanillaFlagWriters: op 36 stores the operand's value into the
// nibble, op 37 increments it, op 38 decrements it (vm-semantics §2.5).
func TestVanillaFlagWriters(t *testing.T) {
	run1 := func(ops []Op, start int) int {
		cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: ops}}

	dec.Operand = `{"id":48}`

	}
}

// TestOp49Packed4Writers: the op 49 family writes the packed4 nibble
// space — 02 or/and with the operand, 03 stores the value, 04/05
// inc/dec (vm-semantics §2.5).
func TestOp49Packed4Writers(t *testing.T) {
	run1 := func(note, operand string, start int) int {
		op := cmd("FA:0100", "49 20 05", note)
		op.Operand = operand
		cat := &fakeCatalog{events: map[int][]Op{1: []Op{op}}}

// TestCatalogMaps4CxxTo0Fxx: native 4Cxx ids are cataloged under their
// 0Fxx alias (engine 5A:AC70; event_catalog.gd) — HasEvent, RawOps and
// End16 all resolve through the alias.
func TestCatalogMaps4CxxTo0Fxx(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	events := `[{"id":"0F01","entry":"FC","raw":[{"k":"cmd","addr":"FC:0200","hex":"43","note":"end"}]}]`
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "events.json"), []byte(events), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "events_index.json"), []byte(idx), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)

	}
}
```

`internal/glyphs/table.go`:

```go
// Package glyphs parses the RS3 community code tables (RS3文字コード変換
// ver7.0 INIs, Shift-JIS) into the glyph assignment the runtime text model
// uses: character -> slot.
//
// Slot numbering follows rs3_runtime_text: single byte b (0x50..0xFC) is
// slot b-0x50; leads 0x20..0x23 are slot (lead-0x20)<<8 | next; lead 0x18
// is slot 0x400 | next (the ver7.0 added-kanji table).
package glyphs

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"strings"

	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/japanese"
)

var errNotObject = errors.New("assignment JSON: want {char: slot} object")

func jsonDecoder(raw []byte) *json.Decoder {
	return json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
}

const placeholder = "□" // addable-but-unassigned glyphs stay unmapped

// Assignment is insertion-ordered so the JSON we emit matches the retired
// Node builder byte for byte.
type Assignment struct {
	Order []string
	Slot  map[string]int
}

func (a *Assignment) add(ch string, slot int) {
	if ch == "" || ch == placeholder {
		return
	}
	if _, dup := a.Slot[ch]; dup {
		return
	}
	a.Slot[ch] = slot
	a.Order = append(a.Order, ch)
}

// Decode decodes a Shift-JIS table file to a string.
func Decode(raw []byte) string {
	b, err := japanese.ShiftJIS.NewDecoder().Bytes(raw)
	if err != nil {
		return string(raw)
	}
	return string(b)
}

// tableRow is one INI line: label ("00".."F0") plus its 16 cells.
type tableRow struct {
	label string
	cells []string
}

// parseTable returns rows in file order (duplicates keep the first row,
// per the INI spec). Rows starting "00" are kept — page row 00 holds real
// glyphs the ROM text uses (e.g. 怪 at page 0x21 +0A), and the single-byte
// table's non-glyph bytes are excluded by the byte range filter instead.
func parseTable(sjisText string) []tableRow {
	var rows []tableRow
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for raw := range strings.SplitSeq(sjisText, "\n") {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(raw, "\r"))
		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "//") {
			continue
		}
		label, rest, ok := strings.Cut(line, ",")
		if !ok || len(label) != 2 || !isHex2(label) {
			continue
		}
		if seen[label] {
			continue
		}
		cells := strings.Split(rest, ",")
		if len(cells) != 16 {
			continue
		}
		for i, c := range cells {
			cells[i] = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(c, " "), " ")
		}
		seen[label] = true
		rows = append(rows, tableRow{label, cells})
	}
	return rows
}

func isHex2(s string) bool {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		c := s[i]
		if !(c >= '0' && c <= '9' || c >= 'A' && c <= 'F' || c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func nibble(s string) int {
	v := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		c := s[i]
		switch {
		case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
			v = v<<4 | int(c-'0')
		case c >= 'A' && c <= 'F':
			v = v<<4 | int(c-'A'+10)
		default:
			v = v<<4 | int(c-'a'+10)
		}
	}
	return v
}

// Build takes the raw bytes of the table files (map keys: SB, 20, 21,
// 22, 23, MAIN) and returns the assignment. MAIN holds the 0x18 extension
// section; SB/20/21/22/23 are the per-table files.
func Build(files map[string][]byte) *Assignment {
	a := &Assignment{Slot: map[string]int{}}
	for _, row := range parseTable(Decode(files["SB"])) {
		base := nibble(row.label)
		for lo, ch := range row.cells {
			// Slot 0 is reserved: the runtime text model hardcodes it to
			// the halfwidth space, so a char mapped there is unreachable
			// (the Node builder lost it to its \s-eats-U+3000 regex).
			if b := base | lo; b >= 0x51 && b <= 0xfc {
				a.add(ch, b-0x50)
			}
		}
	}
	for p := 0x20; p <= 0x23; p++ {
		table := files[string([]byte{hexDigit(p >> 4), hexDigit(p & 0xf)})]
		for _, row := range parseTable(Decode(table)) {
			base := nibble(row.label)
			for lo, ch := range row.cells {
				a.add(ch, (p-0x20)<<8|base|lo)
			}
		}
	}
	for _, row := range parseTable(extract18(Decode(files["MAIN"]))) {
		base := nibble(row.label)
		for lo, ch := range row.cells {
			a.add(ch, 0x400|base|lo)
		}
	}
	return a
}

func hexDigit(v int) byte {
	if v < 10 {
		return byte('0' + v)
	}
	return byte('A' + v - 10)
}

// ParseAssignment reads the assignment JSON {"char": slot, ...} written by
// cmd/glyphtable, preserving insertion order.
func ParseAssignment(raw []byte) (Assignment, error) {
	var a Assignment
	a.Slot = map[string]int{}
	dec := jsonDecoder(raw)
	tok, err := dec.Token()
	if err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	if d, ok := tok.(json.Delim); !ok || d != '{' {
		return a, errNotObject
	}
	for dec.More() {
		keyTok, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return a, err
		}
		valTok, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return a, err
		}
		num, ok := valTok.(float64)
		if !ok {
			return a, errNotObject
		}
		ch := keyTok.(string)
		a.Order = append(a.Order, ch)
		a.Slot[ch] = int(num)
	}
	return a, nil
}

// extract18 returns the text of the "// 0x18" extension section of the
// main INI: everything from the line after the marker to the next comment
// line. The section's own column-header comment ("//  00, 01, ...") stays
// in — parseTable skips comment lines.
func extract18(main string) string {
	const marker = "// 0x18"
	i := strings.Index(main, marker)
	if i < 0 {
		return ""
	}
	nl := strings.Index(main[i:], "\n")
	if nl < 0 {
		return ""
	}
	rest := main[i+nl+1:]
	if end := strings.Index(rest, "\n//"); end >= 0 {
		rest = rest[:end]
	}
	return rest
}
```

`internal/growth/growth.go`:

```go
// Package growth implements the battle-end growth math (docs/
// battle-formulas.md §8.2, kaeru 成長関連まとめ) on top of the boundary
// row the engine reads from the ROM.
//
// VERIFIED in ROM (2026-11-16): the growth 境界値 row lives at FE:31AA
// (file 0x3E31AA, 21 B, descending by diff), read by the twin chance
// reader FE:E8E5 (`BF AA 31 FE` LDA $FE31AA,X with the same
// X = clamp(10 − diff, 0, 20) index math as the spark reader) — the same
// bytes kaeru's 差分→境界値 table lists. The verdict comparison is the
// spark shape (境界値 > 乱数+1), so P = (境界値−1)/256 and kaeru's
// worked percentages are (境界値−1)/256 (16 → 15/256 = 5.86%,
// 32 → 31/256 = 12.11% ≈ kaeru's 12.89% measured through the biased
// SFC RNG).
package growth

import (
	"fmt"

	"saga3/internal/battle"
)

// BoundaryTableOffset is the growth 境界値 row: FE:31AA, 21 bytes,
// descending by diff (row[0] = diff +10), byte-identical in vanilla and
// bokuno. The old chance-table reading called this row "open"; it is the
// growth table.
const BoundaryTableOffset = 0x3E31AA

// BoundaryTable decodes the 境界値 row into ascending-by-diff order
// (Index(diff) = diff+10 clamped), the same layout as battle.ChanceTable.
func BoundaryTable(rom []byte) (battle.ChanceTable, error) {
	var out battle.ChanceTable
	if BoundaryTableOffset+battle.ChanceTableSize > len(rom) {
		return out, fmt.Errorf("boundary row at %#x out of range", BoundaryTableOffset)
	}
	for i := 0; i < battle.ChanceTableSize; i++ {
		out[i] = rom[BoundaryTableOffset+battle.ChanceTableSize-1-i]
	}
	return out, nil
}

// boundaryAscending is the FE:31AA row ascending by diff; TestBoundaryTable
// pins the ROM decode against it.
var boundaryAscending = [21]int{
	0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 16, 32, 36, 40, 50, 60, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,
}

// Boundary is the ROM-free 境界値 lookup for diff = raise − lower,
// clamped to ±10.
func Boundary(diff int) int {
	i := diff + 10
	if i < 0 {
		i = 0
	}
	if i >= len(boundaryAscending) {
		i = len(boundaryAscending) - 1
	}
	return boundaryAscending[i]
}

// Grew is the verdict comparison shared with the spark roll: 境界値 > 乱数+1
// (乱数 0..255, kaeru 上昇判定; same shape as battle.SparkRolled). Boundary
// 0 and 1 never grow.
func Grew(boundary, rand0255 int) bool {
	return boundary > rand0255+1
}

// Roll runs one growth check: diff = raise − lower, boundary lookup, roll.
func Roll(boundaryTable battle.ChanceTable, raise, lower, rand0255 int) bool {
	return Grew(boundaryTable.Base(raise-lower), rand0255)
}

// HPRaise is the HP diff: raise = 敵上昇Lv + HP成長補正, lower =
// maxHP×5÷128 (kaeru 上昇率に影響する要因). 成長補正 255 (レオニード) keeps
// the diff huge and positive — callers must also honor the "255 = never"
// flag before rolling.
func HPRaise(riseLv, correction, maxHP int) int {
	return riseLv + correction - maxHP*5/128
}

// SkillRaise is the class/school 増幅 diff: raise = 敵上昇Lv +
// class成長補正 + 戦闘カウンタ×20÷256, lower = current level.
func SkillRaise(riseLv, correction, battleCounter, currentLv int) int {
	return riseLv + correction + battleCounter*20/256 - currentLv
}

// PoolRaise is the WP/JP diff: raise = 最も高い系統×2 + 全系統の合計, lower =
// the current maximum pool. 敵上昇Lv and the 成長補正 do not apply to pools
// (kaeru: WP・JP上昇には敵上昇Lvが無関係). The raise is the engine's pool
// fetch FE:CCA7, which clamps the formula at 250 (battle.EnginePool /
// battle.EnginePoolCap, VERIFIED 2026-11-17: FE:CCD7 CMP #$00FA, vanilla
// code kept in bokuno) — at all-50 classes the uncapped formula says 355 but
// the engine rolls against 250, so pools saturate at 250 (WP) and the roll
// math, not the cap, is what stops JP at 205 (kaeru 例2).
func PoolRaise(levels []int, currentMax int) int {
	return battle.EnginePool(levels) - currentMax
}

// PoolCap is the saturation ceiling: at current = raise + 5 the diff is
// −5 → 境界値 1 → P 0%, so pools stop at raise+5 (kaeru 例2: 朱鳥50/月50
// reaches JP 205 and stops there; the WP analogue is the same shape).
func PoolCap(raise int) int { return raise + 5 }

// ConsecutivePenalty is the 境界値 reduction after any earlier growth in
// the same victory, by the Σ skill levels (剣斧槍弓体 + schools + 増幅)
// table [VERIFIED: kaeru 連続成長時の確率低下]. Totals past 399 exceed
// kaeru's listed range; the +1-per-row pattern continues at 400
// (thresholds 4,16,36,64,100,144,196,256,324,400 — gaps 12,20,28,…,76).
func ConsecutivePenalty(skillTotal int) int {
	switch {
	case skillTotal <= 3:
		return 0
	case skillTotal <= 15:
		return 1
	case skillTotal <= 35:
		return 2
	case skillTotal <= 63:
		return 3
	case skillTotal <= 99:
		return 4
	case skillTotal <= 143:
		return 5
	case skillTotal <= 195:
		return 6
	case skillTotal <= 255:
		return 7
	case skillTotal <= 323:
		return 8
	case skillTotal <= 399:
		return 9
	default:
		return 10
	}
}

// HPGain is the per-success HP amount [VERIFIED: kaeru HPの上昇量]:
// HP上昇量 = (体力÷4 + 2) + (乱数 mod 体力÷4 + 1), the underlined term
// being 0 when 体力 ≤ 7 (体力÷4 ≤ 1). 体力 includes armor 体力補正 but
// not battle-only boosts.
func HPGain(vit, rand0255 int) int {
	gain := vit/4 + 2
	if q := vit / 4; q >= 2 {
		gain += rand0255%q + 1
	}
	return gain
}
```

```go
func rom(t *testing.T) []byte {

// TestBoundaryTableDecodesROMAscending pins the 境界値 row (FE:31AA,
// byte-identical vanilla and bokuno) against kaeru's 差分→境界値 list:
// −10以下 → 0, −9 → 0, −8..−5 → 1, −4 → 2, −3 → 3, −2 → 5, −1 → 8,

		}

		}

// TestBoundaryTableRejectsShortROM pins the range guard: a ROM that ends
// inside the FE:31AA row is an error naming the offset, and a ROM ending
// exactly at the row's last byte decodes.
func TestBoundaryTableRejectsShortROM(t *testing.T) {
	offset := BoundaryTableOffset
	end := offset + battle.ChanceTableSize
	if _, err := BoundaryTable(make([]byte, offset)); err == nil {
		t.Error("a ROM ending at the row start must be rejected, got nil error")
	}
	if _, err := BoundaryTable(make([]byte, end-1)); err == nil {
		t.Error("a ROM one byte short of the row must be rejected, got nil error")

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a ROM ending at the row's last byte must decode: %v", err)

		if got := bt.Base(diff); got != 0 {

		}

func TestGrewVerdictIsBoundaryOverRandPlusOne(t *testing.T) {

// TestRollLooksUpRaiseMinusLowerDiff pins Roll's wiring: the boundary is

	}
}
```

`internal/ips/ips.go`:

```go
// Package ips applies IPS patches.
//
// RLE records are count-then-value: offset(3) 00 00 count(2 BE) value(1).
// This is the convention Floating IPS (libips) writes and the one this
// project's patches use; the value-first reading silently corrupts bokuno's
// IPS (verified 2026-11-15 against Flips on ぼくのProto1.123.ips).
//
// Extension of the target beyond the source size is padded with 0x00,
// matching libips. An EOF marker stops parsing; up to 3 trailing bytes
// after EOF are honored as a big-endian truncation size (Lunar IPS
// convention).
package ips

import "errors"

var (
	ErrMagic     = errors.New("ips: not an IPS file (missing PATCH magic)")
	ErrTruncated = errors.New("ips: truncated record")
)

const eofOffset = 0x454F46

// Apply returns the patched ROM.
func Apply(rom, patch []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if len(patch) < 5 || string(patch[:5]) != "PATCH" {
		return nil, ErrMagic
	}
	out := make([]byte, len(rom))
	copy(out, rom)
	pos := 5
	truncateAt := -1
	for pos+3 <= len(patch) {
		offset := int(patch[pos])<<16 | int(patch[pos+1])<<8 | int(patch[pos+2])
		pos += 3
		if offset == eofOffset {
			if len(patch)-pos == 3 {
				truncateAt = int(patch[pos])<<16 | int(patch[pos+1])<<8 | int(patch[pos+2])
			}
			break
		}
		if pos+2 > len(patch) {
			return nil, ErrTruncated
		}
		length := int(patch[pos])<<8 | int(patch[pos+1])
		pos += 2
		var data []byte
		if length == 0 {
			if pos+3 > len(patch) {
				return nil, ErrTruncated
			}
			count := int(patch[pos])<<8 | int(patch[pos+1])
			data = make([]byte, count)
			for i := range data {
				data[i] = patch[pos+2]
			}
			pos += 3
		} else {
			if pos+length > len(patch) {
				return nil, ErrTruncated
			}
			data = patch[pos : pos+length]
			pos += length
		}
		end := offset + len(data)
		if end > len(out) {
			grown := make([]byte, end)
			copy(grown, out)
			out = grown
		}
		copy(out[offset:end], data)
	}
	if truncateAt >= 0 && truncateAt <= len(out) {
		out = out[:truncateAt]
	}
	return out, nil
}

```

`internal/ips/ips_test.go`:

```go
package ips

import (
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"testing"
)

func mustApply(t *testing.T, rom, patch []byte) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	out, err := Apply(rom, patch)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}
	return out
}

func patchBytes(records ...[]byte) []byte {
	p := []byte("PATCH")
	for _, r := range records {
		p = append(p, r...)
	}
	return p
}

func TestRLECountThenValue(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 16)
	// offset 0x000010, length 0x0000 (RLE), count 0x0004, value 0xEA:
	// count first, then the value — the Flips order.
	p := patchBytes(
		[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x04, 0xEA},
		[]byte("EOF"),
	)
	out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
	want := append(make([]byte, 16), 0xEA, 0xEA, 0xEA, 0xEA)
	if !bytes.Equal(out, want) {
		t.Fatalf("RLE record: got %x, want count 4 of value EA after the 16 base bytes", out)
	}
	// The same record read value-first (count 0x00EA of 0x04) parses fine
	// but must produce something different — the two orders are distinguishable.
	wrong := patchBytes(
		[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0xEA, 0x00, 0x04},
		[]byte("EOF"),
	)
	outWrong := mustApply(t, rom, wrong)
	if bytes.Equal(outWrong, want) {
		t.Fatal("value-first reading produced the same output as count-then-value")
	}
}

func TestRecordKeepsBaseBytesAndInputROM(t *testing.T) {
	rom := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xA7}, 16)
	p := patchBytes(
		[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x04, 0x00, 0x02, 'A', 'B'},
		[]byte("EOF"),
	)
	out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
	want := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xA7}, 16)
	copy(want[4:6], "AB")
	if !bytes.Equal(out, want) {
		t.Fatalf("record clobbered base bytes: got %x, want %x", out, want)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(rom, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xA7}, 16)) {
		t.Fatalf("Apply modified the input ROM: %x", rom)
	}
}

func TestGrowthKeepsPriorBytesAndPadsGapWithZeros(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 16)
	p := patchBytes(
		[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x04, 0x00, 0x02, 'A', 'B'}, // writes inside the ROM
		[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x20, 0x00, 0x01, 'Z'},      // grows to offset 0x21
		[]byte("EOF"),
	)
	out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
	if len(out) != 0x21 {
		t.Fatalf("output is %d bytes, want %d", len(out), 0x21)
	}
	if out[4] != 'A' || out[5] != 'B' {
		t.Fatalf("bytes written before the growth were lost: %x", out)
	}
	if gap := out[16:32]; !bytes.Equal(gap, make([]byte, 16)) {
		t.Fatalf("gap between ROM end and record start is %x, want 16 zero bytes", gap)
	}
	if out[32] != 'Z' {
		t.Fatalf("byte at offset 0x20 is %#U, want 'Z'", out[32])
	}
}

func TestOffsetHighByte(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x20000) // 128 KiB
	p := patchBytes(
		[]byte{0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 'X'},
		[]byte("EOF"),
	)
	out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
	if len(out) != 0x20000 {
		t.Fatalf("output is %d bytes, want %d", len(out), 0x20000)
	}
	if out[0x010000] != 'X' {
		t.Fatalf("byte at offset 0x010000 is %#U, want 'X'", out[0x010000])
	}
	if out[0x000100] != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("record landed at offset 0x000100 (%#U), the offset high byte was dropped", out[0x000100])
	}
}

func TestTruncationSize(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 16)
	record := []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 'A'}
	t.Run("three byte size truncates the output", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := patchBytes(
			[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0xAB, 0xCD},
			[]byte("EOF"),
			[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x08},
		)
		out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
		if len(out) != 8 || out[0] != 0xAB || out[1] != 0xCD {
			t.Fatalf("truncation to 8 bytes: got len %d, out %x", len(out), out)
		}
	})
	t.Run("size zero truncates to empty", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := patchBytes(record, []byte("EOF"), []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00})
		out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
		if len(out) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("truncation size 0 left %d bytes, want an empty ROM", len(out))
		}
	})
	t.Run("size larger than the output is ignored", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := patchBytes(record, []byte("EOF"), []byte{0x00, 0x10, 0x00}) // 4096
		out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
		if len(out) != 16 || out[0] != 'A' {
			t.Fatalf("oversized truncation size changed the output: len %d, out %x", len(out), out)
		}
	})
	t.Run("four trailing bytes are not a size", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := patchBytes(record, []byte("EOF"), []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x08, 0xFF})
		out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
		if len(out) != 16 {
			t.Fatalf("trailer 000008ff was read as a truncation size: output is %d bytes, want 16", len(out))
		}
	})
	t.Run("two trailing bytes are not a size", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := patchBytes(record, []byte("EOF"), []byte{0x00, 0x00})
		out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
		if len(out) != 16 {
			t.Fatalf("trailer 0000 was read as a truncation size: output is %d bytes, want 16", len(out))
		}
	})
}

func TestTruncatedRecordErrors(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		record []byte
	}{
		{"RLE record missing its value byte", []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x04}},
		{"data run shorter than its length", []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 'A'}},
		{"length field cut to one byte", []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			p := patchBytes(tc.record)
			out, err := Apply(make([]byte, 16), p)
			if !errors.Is(err, ErrTruncated) {
				t.Fatalf("record %x: got err %v, want ErrTruncated (out %x)", tc.record, err, out)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRecordMayEndAtPatchEnd(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 16)
	p := patchBytes([]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 'A', 'B'})
	out := mustApply(t, rom, p)
	if out[0] != 'A' || out[1] != 'B' || !bytes.Equal(out[2:], make([]byte, 14)) {
		t.Fatalf("record ending at patch end: got %x, want AB then 14 base bytes", out)
	}
}

func TestThreeByteTailWithoutEOFAborts(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 16)
	p := patchBytes(
		[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 'A'},
		[]byte{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}, // not EOF: a record offset with nothing after it
	)
	if _, err := Apply(rom, p); !errors.Is(err, ErrTruncated) {
		t.Fatalf("3-byte tail that is not EOF: got err %v, want ErrTruncated", err)
	}
}

func TestPatchMagic(t *testing.T) {
	rom := []byte{0x11, 0x22}
	t.Run("bare PATCH is a valid empty patch", func(t *testing.T) {
		out := mustApply(t, rom, []byte("PATCH"))
		if !bytes.Equal(out, rom) {
			t.Fatalf("bare PATCH: got %x, want the ROM unchanged", out)
		}
	})
	t.Run("wrong magic", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, err := Apply(rom, []byte("NOPE!")); !errors.Is(err, ErrMagic) {
			t.Fatalf("got err %v, want ErrMagic", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("patch shorter than the magic", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, err := Apply(rom, []byte("PATC")); !errors.Is(err, ErrMagic) {
			t.Fatalf("got err %v, want ErrMagic", err)
		}
	})
}

```

`internal/items/items.go`:

```go
// Package items decodes the item (道具) tables of the bokuno RS3 hack
// (patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, CRC32 7E165025). Offsets and layouts come from
// the community struct dump shipped in the patch archive
// (patches/ぼくの（略更新/テキスト/05_構造体.def.txt); see docs/items.md
// for the per-field evidence.
//
// Offsets are file offsets in the 8 MB ExHiROM image: banks 0xC0-0xFF map
// to file (bank-0xC0)*0x10000, banks 0x40-0x7D map to bank*0x10000.
package items

import "fmt"

// Table file offsets.
const (
	// Main (vanilla) tables, item IDs 0x000-0x0FF.
	dataMain   = 0x3E0000 // struct RS3_アイテムデータ, 1536 B
	usableMain = 0x3E9738 // 回復アイテム effect rows, 32 x 2 B
	priceMain  = 0x3E9958 // struct RS3_アイテム値段, 256 x 2 B (short LE)

	// bokuno extension tables (bank 5A expansion), item IDs 0x100-0x1FF.
	priceExt = 0x5B1D80 // struct RS3拡張_アイテム値段, 256 x 2 B
	dataExt  = 0x5B3480 // struct RS3拡張_アイテム性能, 1600 B

	// ID range bounds.
	MainIDBase = 0x000
	ExtIDBase  = 0x100
	IDCount    = 0x200
)

// Kind classifies an item; it fixes both the record stride and the field
// meanings.
type Kind int

const (
	Consumable Kind = iota // 道具, 4 B (battle-use attack items and HP medicines)
	Weapon                 // 武器, 4 B
	Shield                 // 盾, 4 B (0x15C-0x15F are 魔道書 tomes stored on the shield stride)
	Armor                  // 防具, 9 B
	Usable                 // 回復アイテム, 2 B (menu WP/JP/LP medicines)
)

func (k Kind) String() string {
	switch k {
	case Consumable:
		return "consumable"
	case Weapon:
		return "weapon"
	case Shield:
		return "shield"
	case Armor:
		return "armor"
	case Usable:
		return "usable"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("Kind(%d)", int(k))
}

// kindOf returns the record kind for an item ID. The kind boundaries are
// fixed per table: the main table is 8 道具 + 72 武器 + 16 盾 + 128 防具 +
// 32 回復, the extension table 80 武器 + 16 盾/書 + 128 防具 + 32 回復.
func kindOf(id int) Kind {
	n := id
	if id >= ExtIDBase {
		n -= ExtIDBase
		switch {
		case n < 80:
			return Weapon
		case n < 96:
			return Shield
		case n < 224:
			return Armor
		}
		return Usable
	}
	switch {
	case n < 8:
		return Consumable
	case n < 80:
		return Weapon
	case n < 96:
		return Shield
	case n < 224:
		return Armor
	}
	return Usable
}

// recordOffset returns the file offset of an item's performance record.
func recordOffset(id int) (int, Kind, error) {
	if id < 0 || id >= IDCount {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("item id %d out of range 0x000-0x1FF", id)
	}
	kind := kindOf(id)
	n := id
	base := dataMain
	if id >= ExtIDBase {
		n -= ExtIDBase
		base = dataExt
		// The extension table drops the 道具 block: weapons start at
		// offset 0 and the 16-shield block is 80 weapons + 4 tomes.
		switch kind {
		case Shield, Weapon:
			return base + n*4, kind, nil
		case Armor:
			return base + 0x180 + (n-96)*9, kind, nil
		case Usable:
			return base + 0x600 + (n-224)*2, kind, nil
		}
		return base + n*4, kind, nil
	}
	switch kind {
	case Consumable:
		return base + n*4, kind, nil
	case Weapon:
		return base + 0x20 + (n-8)*4, kind, nil
	case Shield:
		return base + 0x140 + (n-80)*4, kind, nil
	case Armor:
		return base + 0x180 + (n-96)*9, kind, nil
	default: // Usable
		return usableMain + (n-224)*2, kind, nil
	}
}

// WeaponCategoryNames maps a weapon/shield kind byte's group
// (byte & 0xF8) to its 攻撃 classify label, from struct アイテム通常攻撃指定
// in the struct dump (0x3E379F) plus the observed 銃 group.
var WeaponCategoryNames = map[byte]string{
	0x00: "剣",
	0x08: "剣（曲刀）",
	0x10: "小剣",
	0x18: "小剣（剣技可）",
	0x20: "斧",
	0x28: "棍棒",
	0x30: "棍棒（杖）",
	0x38: "剣（七星剣）",
	0x48: "精霊石",
	0x50: "火星の砂",
	0x58: "永久氷晶",
	0x60: "盾（スパイクシールド）",
	0x68: "傷薬",
	0x70: "盾",
	0x78: "ガーダー",
	0x80: "大剣",
	0x88: "大剣（刀）",
	0x90: "大剣（剣技可）",
	0x98: "槍",
	0xA0: "槍（矛槍）",
	0xA8: "槍（三椏）",
	0xB0: "弓",
	0xB8: "大剣（氷の剣）",
	0xC0: "詩人のフィドル",
	0xC8: "銃",
	0xF8: "聖杯",
}

// Resist is a defense byte of an armor piece: the low nibble is a
// multiplier mark (1 ×, 2 △, 3 ○, 4 ○+, 5 ◎, 7 ☆), the high nibble is the
// attribute bitmask it applies to. Physical attributes are 弓/射 0x10,
// 貫/突 0x20, 打/叩 0x40, 斬 0x80; magic attributes are 状 0x10, 雷 0x20,
// 冷 0x40, 熱 0x80.
type Resist byte

// Mark returns the multiplier mark nibble.
func (r Resist) Mark() byte { return byte(r) & 0x0F }

// AttrBits returns the attribute bitmask nibble.
func (r Resist) AttrBits() byte { return byte(r) & 0xF0 }

// Item is one decoded item record.
type Item struct {
	ID    int
	Kind  Kind
	Name  string // from the embedded name tables; "" when unknown
	Price int    // 値段 table, short little-endian

	// Weapon fields (Power; techs are 技データ IDs, -1 = none).
	Group        byte   // kind byte (group<<3 | weight)
	Category     string // WeaponCategoryNames label for Group&0xF8
	Weight       int    // kind byte & 7
	Power        int    // 威力 byte; bit 0x80 = 呪い (cursed)
	Cursed       bool
	Tech1, Tech2 int

	// Shield fields.
	Defense      int // 防御力 byte; bit 0x80 = cursed
	Evade        int // 回避率 (percent); bit 0x80 = 盾判定, clear = ガーダー判定
	ShieldBlock  bool
	ShieldResist byte // 0x01状 0x02雷 0x04冷 0x08熱 0x10射 0x20突 0x40叩 0x80斬

	// Armor fields.
	PhysDef      int
	PhysResist   Resist
	MagDef       int
	MagResist    Resist
	StatusBlock  byte // 0x01スタン 0x02毒 0x04精神 0x08暗闇 0x10眠り 0x20マヒ 0x40石化 0x80気絶
	TypeBits     byte // 0x01鎧 0x02服 0x04兜 0x08小手 0x10靴 0x20アクセサリ 0x80呪い (0x1D/0x1F 全身鎧)
	SchoolResist byte // 0x01蒼龍..0x08水 0x10投げ 0x20音波 0x40凝視 0x80浮遊
	StatBonus    byte // 0x01+2 0x02魅力 0x04意思 0x08魔力 0x10体力 0x20素早 0x40器用 0x80腕力
	Misc         byte // 0x0X重さ 0x40自動回復 0x80能力非表示

	// Consumable fields (battle-use items, 道具 records).
	RecoverPower      int  // 回復力 byte * 4 (the struct dump notes 実数値は4倍)
	CuresStatus       byte // 直す状態変化; 0x01 毒, 0x10 石化 observed
	ConsumableUnknown byte

	// Usable fields (menu medicines, 回復アイテム records).
	Effect byte // 0x01一人 0x02全体 0x08WP 0x10JP 0x20LP (0x40/0x80 unconfirmed flags)
	Amount int  // 回復量; 0x80 = full recovery
}

// Name returns the embedded decoded name for an item ID, or "" when the
// ID is out of range.
func Name(id int) string {
	switch {
	case id >= MainIDBase && id < ExtIDBase:
		return MainNames[id]
	case id >= ExtIDBase && id < IDCount:
		return ExtNames[id-ExtIDBase]
	}
	return ""
}

// nameBase returns the file offset and record stride of an item's name.
func nameBase(id int) (int, int, error) {
	if id < 0 || id >= IDCount {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("item id %d out of range 0x000-0x1FF", id)
	}
	if id >= ExtIDBase {
		return 0x5B2880 + (id-ExtIDBase)*12, 12, nil
	}
	return 0x3D0280 + id*8, 8, nil
}

// decodeNameRecord mirrors cmd/dumpnames: stop at the terminator 0x00 or
// 0x50; a lead byte below 0x50 always consumes one more byte.
func decodeNameRecord(rec []byte) []byte {
	var out []byte
	for i := 0; i < len(rec); i++ {
		b := rec[i]
		if b == 0x00 || b == 0x50 {
			break
		}
		out = append(out, b)
		if b < 0x50 {
			i++
			if i < len(rec) {
				out = append(out, rec[i])
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// RawNameRecord returns the raw glyph bytes of an item's name record.
func RawNameRecord(rom []byte, id int) ([]byte, error) {
	off, stride, err := nameBase(id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	end := off + stride
	if end > len(rom) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("rom too short for name at 0x%X: %d bytes", off, len(rom))
	}
	return decodeNameRecord(rom[off:end]), nil
}

// price returns the item's 値段 table entry.
func price(rom []byte, id int) (int, error) {
	base := priceMain
	if id >= ExtIDBase {
		base = priceExt
	}
	off := base + id*2
	if id >= ExtIDBase {
		off = base + (id-ExtIDBase)*2
	}
	if off+2 > len(rom) {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("rom too short for price at 0x%X: %d bytes", off, len(rom))
	}
	return int(rom[off]) | int(rom[off+1])<<8, nil
}

// ItemAt decodes one item record.
func ItemAt(rom []byte, id int) (Item, error) {
	off, kind, err := recordOffset(id)
	if err != nil {
		return Item{}, err
	}
	item := Item{ID: id, Kind: kind, Name: Name(id)}
	p, err := price(rom, id)
	if err != nil {
		return Item{}, err
	}
	item.Price = p

	rec := func(n int) ([]byte, error) {
		if off+n > len(rom) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("rom too short for item %#05x record at 0x%X: %d bytes", id, off, len(rom))
		}
		return rom[off : off+n], nil
	}
	b := func(n int) (byte, error) {
		r, err := rec(n)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, err
		}
		return r[n-1], nil
	}

	switch kind {
	case Weapon:
		k, err := b(1)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		power, err := b(2)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		r, err := rec(4)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		item.Group = k
		item.Category = WeaponCategoryNames[k&0xF8]
		item.Weight = int(k) & 7
		item.Power = int(power) & 0x7F
		item.Cursed = power >= 0x80
		item.Tech1, item.Tech2 = techRef(r[2]), techRef(r[3])
	case Shield:
		k, err := b(1)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		def, err := b(2)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		r, err := rec(4)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		item.Group = k
		item.Category = WeaponCategoryNames[k&0xF8]
		item.Weight = int(k) & 7
		item.Defense = int(def) & 0x7F
		item.Cursed = def >= 0x80
		item.Evade = int(r[2]) & 0x7F
		item.ShieldBlock = r[2] >= 0x80
		item.ShieldResist = r[3]
	case Armor:
		r, err := rec(9)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		item.PhysDef = int(r[0])
		item.PhysResist = Resist(r[1])
		item.MagDef = int(r[2])
		item.MagResist = Resist(r[3])
		item.StatusBlock = r[4]
		item.TypeBits = r[5]
		item.SchoolResist = r[6]
		item.StatBonus = r[7]
		item.Misc = r[8]
	case Consumable:
		k, err := b(1)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		r, err := rec(4)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		item.Group = k
		item.Category = WeaponCategoryNames[k&0xF8]
		item.Weight = int(k) & 7
		item.RecoverPower = int(r[1]) * 4
		item.CuresStatus = r[2]
		item.ConsumableUnknown = r[3]
	case Usable:
		r, err := rec(2)
		if err != nil {
			return Item{}, err
		}
		item.Effect = r[0]
		item.Amount = int(r[1])
	}
	return item, nil
}

// techRef converts a weapon 固有技 byte to a tech ID; 0xFF = none -> -1.
func techRef(b byte) int {
	if b == 0xFF {
		return -1
	}
	return int(b)
}

// AllItems decodes every item, main table first (0x000-0x0FF) then the
// extension table (0x100-0x1FF).
func AllItems(rom []byte) ([]Item, error) {
	out := make([]Item, 0, IDCount)
	for id := range IDCount {
		item, err := ItemAt(rom, id)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("item %#05x: %w", id, err)
		}
		out = append(out, item)
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

`internal/items/items_test.go`:

```go
package items

import (
	"bytes"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// fixtureROM builds a synthetic ROM covering both tables. Performance,
// price and name records are written at literal file offsets with the
// byte values the real ROM (patches/bokuno_jp.sfc, CRC32 7E165025) shows
// for the named items; the literals are the fixture's own claim about
// where each table lives, kept independent of the package's offset
// constants so a shifted constant cannot drag the fixture with it.
// Synthetic name records (IDs 0x09/0x0A/0x0B/0x0D) exercise
// terminator/lead edges the real rows do not.
func fixtureROM() []byte {
	// Size covers the extension performance table end (0x5B3480+0x640 =
	// the 倉庫アイテム並び順 table) and both price tables.
	rom := make([]byte, 0x5B3AC0)
	put := func(off int, b ...byte) { copy(rom[off:], b) }
	putShort := func(off int, v int) {
		rom[off] = byte(v)
		rom[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	}

	// Main 道具, 4 B per record at 0x3E0000.
	// 傷薬 0x00: kind 0x68 (傷薬 w0), 回復力 25 -> 100, cures 0x81 (毒).
	// 高級傷薬 0x01: 回復力 0x4B -> 300.
	put(0x3E0000+0*4, 0x68, 25, 0x81, 0x00)
	put(0x3E0000+1*4, 0x68, 0x4B, 0x81, 0x00)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0*2, 20)
	putShort(0x3E9958+1*2, 100)

	// Main 武器, 4 B per record at 0x3E0020.
	// 長剣 0x08: 剣 w3, power 8, no techs. 三日月刀 0x0B: 剣（曲刀） w2,
	// power 12, techs 0xDB/0xDC. 詩人のフィドル 0x28: power byte 0x80
	// (cursed, power 0).
	put(0x3E0020+0*4, 0x03, 0x08, 0xFF, 0xFF)
	put(0x3E0020+3*4, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0xDB, 0xDC)
	put(0x3E0020+(0x28-8)*4, 0xC2, 0x80, 0xFF, 0xFF)
	putShort(0x3E9958+8*2, 100)
	putShort(0x3E9958+11*2, 200)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0x28*2, 0)

	// Main 盾, 4 B per record at 0x3E0140.
	// 小盾 0x50: 盾 w2, def 10, 盾判定 evade 30, resist 0xF0 (斬打突射).
	// 大盾 0x51: def 15, evade 45.
	put(0x3E0140+0*4, 0x72, 0x0A, 0x80|30, 0xF0)
	put(0x3E0140+1*4, 0x74, 0x0F, 0x80|45, 0xF0)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0x50*2, 100)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0x51*2, 300)

	// Main 防具, 9 B per record at 0x3E0180.
	// 兵士の鎧 0x60: phys 15, mag 5, magres △雷 (0x22), type 鎧, w5.
	// 騎士の鎧 0x61: phys 20, mag 10, w6.
	put(0x3E0180+0*9, 15, 0x00, 5, 0x22, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 5)
	put(0x3E0180+1*9, 0x14, 0x00, 0x0A, 0x22, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 6)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0x60*2, 450)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0x61*2, 1000)

	// Main 回復, 2 B per record at 0x3E9738.
	// 技の香薬 0xE0: WP20 single target. 力の香薬 0xE1: WP50.
	put(0x3E9738+0*2, 0xC9, 20)
	put(0x3E9738+1*2, 0xC9, 0x32)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0xE0*2, 100)
	putShort(0x3E9958+0xE1*2, 300)

	// Extension 武器/盾, 4 B per record at 0x5B3480.
	// ブランダ一バス 0x100: 銃 w7, power 56. 魔王の盾 0x150.
	// 聖騎士の盾 0x157: def byte 0x99 (cursed, 25), evade byte 0xB2
	// (盾判定 50), resist 0xF0.
	put(0x5B3480+0*4, 0xC8|7, 56, 0xFF, 0xFF)
	put(0x5B3480+80*4, 0x75, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF)
	put(0x5B3480+(0x157-0x100)*4, 0x74, 0x99, 0xB2, 0xF0)
	putShort(0x5B1D80+0*2, 9999)
	putShort(0x5B1D80+0x57*2, 0)

	// Extension 防具, 9 B per record at 0x5B3480+0x180.
	// 魔王の鎧 0x160: phys 20, mag 40, 凝視/音波/投げ/水 (0x78),
	// 全ステータス+1 (0xFE), w7. 霊獣石の鎧 0x163: phys 23, physres
	// ○斬突 (0xA3), mag 21, 体+2 (0x11), w6.
	put(0x5B3480+0x180+0*9, 20, 0x00, 40, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x78, 0xFE, 7)
	put(0x5B3480+0x180+3*9, 0x17, 0xA3, 0x15, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x11, 6)
	putShort(0x5B1D80+0x63*2, 3000)

	// Extension 回復, 2 B per record at 0x5B3480+0x600. 0x1E0 is zeroed
	// in the real ROM.
	put(0x5B3480+0x600, 0x00, 0x00)
	putShort(0x5B1D80+0xE0*2, 0)

	// Name records: main 256 x 8 B at 0x3D0280, extension 256 x 12 B at
	// 0x5B2880. Real rows: 0x01 高級傷薬 (record fills all 8 bytes, and
	// the next row 0x02 最高傷薬 keeps reading past it non-terminating),
	// 0x08 長剣 (terminator at index 4), extension 0x100 ブランダ一バス
	// (7 decoded bytes), 0x129 ?子?林剣 (10 decoded bytes), 0x1BE
	// 火成岩の腕飾り (record fills all 12 bytes, next row 0x1BF 骨の腕輪
	// non-terminating) and 0x1BF. Synthetic rows: 0x09 stops at an 0x00
	// terminator, 0x0A hides terminators behind a lead byte, 0x0B uses
	// the 0x46 lead just below the 0x50 boundary, 0x0D ends on a
	// dangling lead byte.
	put(0x3D0280+0x01*8, 0x21, 0x47, 0x23, 0x91, 0x22, 0x5C, 0x21, 0xB7)
	put(0x3D0280+0x02*8, 0x20, 0xF9, 0x21, 0x47, 0x22, 0x5C, 0x21, 0xB7)
	put(0x3D0280+0x08*8, 0x21, 0x1F, 0x21, 0xA6, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50)
	put(0x3D0280+0x09*8, 0x21, 0x1F, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x21)
	put(0x3D0280+0x0A*8, 0x21, 0x50, 0x21, 0x00, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50)
	put(0x3D0280+0x0B*8, 0x46, 0x50, 0x46, 0x50, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	put(0x3D0280+0x0D*8, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x21)
	put(0x5B2880+0x00*12, 0xDC, 0xA8, 0xAE, 0xD5, 0xE5, 0xDA, 0x8E, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50)
	put(0x5B2880+0x29*12, 0x46, 0x1E, 0x20, 0xBF, 0x46, 0x1F, 0x23, 0x9E, 0x21, 0xA6, 0x50, 0x50)
	put(0x5B2880+0xBE*12, 0x22, 0x15, 0x21, 0x14, 0x22, 0xAE, 0x69, 0x21, 0xE4, 0x23, 0x4F, 0x77)
	put(0x5B2880+0xBF*12, 0x22, 0xAF, 0x69, 0x21, 0xE4, 0x22, 0x55, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50)
	return rom
}

// TestWeaponRecordDecodesCategoryWeightPowerAndTechs pins the 武器 record
// decode: kind byte splits into attack group (bits 7-3, labelled) and
// weight (bits 2-0), power from byte +1, the two 固有技 bytes +2/+3 map
// through techRef (0xFF = none -> -1). Anchors: 長剣 8/3 剣, 三日月刀
// 12/2 曲刀 with techs 0xDB/0xDC (docs/items.md wiki rows).
func TestWeaponRecordDecodesCategoryWeightPowerAndTechs(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	it, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x08)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if it.Kind != Weapon || it.Name != "長剣" || it.Price != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("長剣: kind %v name %q price %d", it.Kind, it.Name, it.Price)
	}
	if it.Category != "剣" || it.Weight != 3 || it.Power != 8 || it.Cursed || it.Tech1 != -1 || it.Tech2 != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("長剣 fields: %+v", it)
	}
	katana, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x0B)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if katana.Category != "剣（曲刀）" || katana.Weight != 2 || katana.Power != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("三日月刀 fields: %+v", katana)
	}
	if katana.Tech1 != 0xDB || katana.Tech2 != 0xDC {
		t.Fatalf("三日月刀 techs: %X/%X", katana.Tech1, katana.Tech2)
	}
	if katana.Price != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("三日月刀 price %d", katana.Price)
	}
}

// TestWeaponPowerHighBitMarksCursed pins bit 7 of the 威力 byte as the
// 呪い mark, masked out of Power. 詩人のフィドル (0x28) reads power byte
// 0x80 in the real ROM: cursed with power 0 — the exact-0x80 byte also
// separates >= from > on the flag.
func TestWeaponPowerHighBitMarksCursed(t *testing.T) {
	it, err := ItemAt(fixtureROM(), 0x28)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !it.Cursed {
		t.Fatalf("詩人のフィドル power byte 0x80: got cursed=false")
	}
	if it.Power != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("詩人のフィドル power %d, want 0 (bit 7 masked)", it.Power)
	}
}

// TestShieldRecordDecodesDefenseEvadeBlockAndResist pins the 盾 record
// decode: byte +1 防御力, byte +2 回避率 with bit 7 = 盾判定, byte +3
// 耐性 bitmask. Anchors: 小盾 10/30 斬打突射 (0xF0), 大盾 15/45
// (docs/items.md wiki rows) — the two records also pin the 4 B stride.
func TestShieldRecordDecodesDefenseEvadeBlockAndResist(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	it, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x50)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if it.Kind != Shield || it.Name != "小盾" || it.Price != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("小盾: kind %v name %q price %d", it.Kind, it.Name, it.Price)
	}
	if it.Category != "盾" || it.Weight != 2 || it.Defense != 10 || it.Evade != 30 || !it.ShieldBlock || it.ShieldResist != 0xF0 {
		t.Fatalf("小盾 fields: %+v", it)
	}
	grand, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x51)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if grand.Weight != 4 || grand.Defense != 15 || grand.Evade != 45 || grand.Price != 300 {
		t.Fatalf("大盾 fields: %+v", grand)
	}
}

// TestShieldDefenseHighBitMarksCursed pins bit 7 of the 防御力 byte as
// 呪い, masked out of Defense. 聖騎士の盾 (0x157) reads def byte 0x99 in
// the real ROM: cursed with defense 25 — which also separates the mask
// from a no-op; the record's offset (0x157 on the extension stride)
// pins the extension shield table.
func TestShieldDefenseHighBitMarksCursed(t *testing.T) {
	it, err := ItemAt(fixtureROM(), 0x157)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !it.Cursed {
		t.Fatalf("聖騎士の盾 def byte 0x99: got cursed=false")
	}
	if it.Defense != 25 {
		t.Fatalf("聖騎士の盾 defense %d, want 25 (bit 7 masked)", it.Defense)
	}
	if it.Evade != 50 || !it.ShieldBlock || it.ShieldResist != 0xF0 || it.Price != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("聖騎士の盾 fields: %+v", it)
	}
}

// TestArmorRecordDecodesNineFieldsInTableOrder pins each of the 9 防具
// record bytes to its field: the assertion values are chosen so any
// adjacent field swap changes at least one of them (兵士の鎧 15/5/△雷,
// 魔王の鎧 20/40/凝視音波投げ水/全+1 — docs/items.md wiki rows).
func TestArmorRecordDecodesNineFieldsInTableOrder(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	it, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x60)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if it.Kind != Armor || it.Name != "兵士の鎧" || it.Price != 450 {
		t.Fatalf("兵士の鎧: kind %v name %q price %d", it.Kind, it.Name, it.Price)
	}
	if it.PhysDef != 15 || byte(it.PhysResist) != 0x00 || it.MagDef != 5 || byte(it.MagResist) != 0x22 ||
		it.StatusBlock != 0x00 || it.TypeBits != 0x01 || it.SchoolResist != 0x00 || it.StatBonus != 0x00 || it.Misc != 0x05 {
		t.Fatalf("兵士の鎧 fields: %+v", it)
	}
	demon, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x160)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if demon.Name != "魔王の鎧" {
		t.Fatalf("魔王の鎧 name %q", demon.Name)
	}
	if demon.PhysDef != 20 || demon.MagDef != 40 || byte(demon.MagResist) != 0x00 ||
		demon.StatusBlock != 0x00 || demon.TypeBits != 0x01 || demon.SchoolResist != 0x78 || demon.StatBonus != 0xFE || demon.Misc != 0x07 {
		t.Fatalf("魔王の鎧 fields: %+v", demon)
	}
}

// TestArmorStrideIsNineBytesPerRecord pins the 防具 stride: record N
// starts at base + N*9, on both the main table (0x60 + 1) and the
// extension table (0x160 + 3). Anchors: 騎士の鎧 20/10 w6, 霊獣石の鎧
// 23 ○斬突 / 21 体+2 w6 (docs/items.md wiki rows).
func TestArmorStrideIsNineBytesPerRecord(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	knight, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x61)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if knight.PhysDef != 20 || knight.MagDef != 10 || knight.Misc != 0x06 || knight.Price != 1000 {
		t.Fatalf("騎士の鎧 fields: %+v", knight)
	}
	spirit, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x163)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if spirit.PhysDef != 23 || byte(spirit.PhysResist) != 0xA3 || spirit.MagDef != 21 || spirit.StatBonus != 0x11 || spirit.Misc != 0x06 || spirit.Price != 3000 {
		t.Fatalf("霊獣石の鎧 fields: %+v", spirit)
	}
}

// TestArmorResistByteSplitsIntoMarkAndAttributeNibbles pins the 耐性
// byte split: low nibble = multiplier mark, high nibble = attribute
// bitmask. △雷 (0x22) on 兵士の鎧 and ○斬突 (0xA3) on 霊獣石の鎧 cover
// both nibble masks with distinct halves.
func TestArmorResistByteSplitsIntoMarkAndAttributeNibbles(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	soldier, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x60)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if soldier.MagResist.Mark() != 0x02 || soldier.MagResist.AttrBits() != 0x20 {
		t.Fatalf("兵士の鎧 magres split: %X", soldier.MagResist)
	}
	spirit, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x163)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if spirit.PhysResist.Mark() != 0x03 || spirit.PhysResist.AttrBits() != 0xA0 {
		t.Fatalf("霊獣石の鎧 physres split: %X", spirit.PhysResist)
	}
}

// TestConsumableRecordDecodesRecoverPowerTimesFour pins the 道具 record
// decode: byte +1 回復力 is quadrupled (実数値は4倍, struct dump), byte
// +2 直す状態変化, byte +3 unknown. 傷薬 HP100 (25 x 4) 毒 (0x81) and
// 高級傷薬 HP300 (0x4B x 4) are the wiki-anchored rows; the second
// record also pins the 4 B stride.
func TestConsumableRecordDecodesRecoverPowerTimesFour(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	it, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x00)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if it.Kind != Consumable || it.Name != "傷薬" || it.Price != 20 {
		t.Fatalf("傷薬: kind %v name %q price %d", it.Kind, it.Name, it.Price)
	}
	if it.RecoverPower != 100 || it.CuresStatus != 0x81 || it.ConsumableUnknown != 0x00 || it.Category != "傷薬" {
		t.Fatalf("傷薬 fields: %+v", it)
	}
	superior, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x01)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if superior.RecoverPower != 300 || superior.CuresStatus != 0x81 || superior.Price != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("高級傷薬 fields: %+v", superior)
	}
}

// TestUsableRecordDecodesEffectAndAmount pins the 回復アイテム record
// decode: byte +0 使用効果 raw (0xC9 = 一人+WP with the ride-along
// bits), byte +1 回復量. 技の香薬 WP20 and 力の香薬 WP50 are the
// content-verified rows (docs/items.md); the second record pins the
// 2 B stride.
func TestUsableRecordDecodesEffectAndAmount(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	it, err := ItemAt(rom, 0xE0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if it.Kind != Usable || it.Name != "技の香薬" || it.Price != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("技の香薬: kind %v name %q price %d", it.Kind, it.Name, it.Price)
	}
	if it.Effect != 0xC9 || it.Amount != 20 {
		t.Fatalf("技の香薬 fields: %+v", it)
	}
	power, err := ItemAt(rom, 0xE1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if power.Effect != 0xC9 || power.Amount != 50 || power.Price != 300 {
		t.Fatalf("力の香薬 fields: %+v", power)
	}
}

// TestExtensionRecordsDecodeFromTheExtensionTables pins the extension
// table base offsets: 武器/盾 from 0x5B3480 (no 道具 block), prices from
// 0x5B1D80. ブランダ一バス 56/7 銃 9999, 魔王の盾 resist 0xFF are the
// wiki-anchored extension rows.
func TestExtensionRecordsDecodeFromTheExtensionTables(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	shotgun, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x100)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if shotgun.Kind != Weapon || shotgun.Name != "ブランダ一バス" || shotgun.Price != 9999 {
		t.Fatalf("ブランダ一バス: kind %v name %q price %d", shotgun.Kind, shotgun.Name, shotgun.Price)
	}
	if shotgun.Category != "銃" || shotgun.Weight != 7 || shotgun.Power != 56 {
		t.Fatalf("ブランダ一バス fields: %+v", shotgun)
	}
	demonShield, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x150)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if demonShield.Kind != Shield || demonShield.Name != "魔王の盾" || demonShield.ShieldResist != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("魔王の盾 fields: %+v", demonShield)
	}
	tail, err := ItemAt(rom, 0x1E0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if tail.Kind != Usable || tail.Effect != 0x00 || tail.Amount != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("ext usable 0x1E0 fields: %+v", tail)
	}
}

// TestKindBoundariesPinTheStrideRegions pins kindOf at every boundary:
// the stride regions 8/72/16/128/32 道具-武器-盾-防具-回復 (main) and
// 80/16/128/32 武器-盾/書-防具-回復 (extension, no 道具 block) are what
// fix each record layout.
func TestKindBoundariesPinTheStrideRegions(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	cases := []struct {
		id   int
		want Kind
	}{
		{0x07, Consumable}, {0x08, Weapon},
		{0x4F, Weapon}, {0x50, Shield},
		{0x5F, Shield}, {0x60, Armor},
		{0xDF, Armor}, {0xE0, Usable},
		{0x14F, Weapon}, {0x150, Shield},
		{0x15F, Shield}, {0x160, Armor},
		{0x1DF, Armor}, {0x1E0, Usable},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		it, err := ItemAt(rom, c.id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("id %#x: %v", c.id, err)
		}
		if it.Kind != c.want {
			t.Errorf("kind of %#x: got %v, want %v", c.id, it.Kind, c.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestKindStringReturnsKindLabels pins the classification labels the
// dump and error messages print.
func TestKindStringReturnsKindLabels(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[Kind]string{
		Consumable: "consumable",
		Weapon:     "weapon",
		Shield:     "shield",
		Armor:      "armor",
		Usable:     "usable",
		Kind(9):    "Kind(9)",
	}
	for k, want := range cases {
		if got := k.String(); got != want {
			t.Errorf("Kind(%d).String() = %q, want %q", int(k), got, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestAllItemsDecodesAllIDsInTableOrder pins AllItems over the whole
// ID space: 512 items, main table 0x000-0x0FF first, extension
// 0x100-0x1FF, each record carrying its own ID. The last extension
// usable rows read the zeroed tail (0x1E0-0x1FF are zeroed in the real
// ROM).
func TestAllItemsDecodesAllIDsInTableOrder(t *testing.T) {
	all, err := AllItems(fixtureROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(all) != IDCount {
		t.Fatalf("got %d items, want %d", len(all), IDCount)
	}
	for i, it := range all {
		if it.ID != i {
			t.Fatalf("position %d holds ID %#x", i, it.ID)
		}
	}
	last := all[IDCount-1]
	if last.Kind != Usable || last.Amount != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("last item: %+v", last)
	}
}

// TestAllItemsWrapsDecodeErrorsWithTheItemID pins the error context:
// a decode failure inside AllItems reports which item ID failed. The
// ROM cut at 0x3E9AD8 keeps every main record readable but ends inside
// the main price table, so item 0x0C0 is the first whose price row
// crosses the end.
func TestAllItemsWrapsDecodeErrorsWithTheItemID(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()[:0x3E9AD8]
	_, err := AllItems(rom)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("truncated rom: expected error")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "item 0x000c0") {
		t.Fatalf("error does not name the failing item: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestItemAtRejectsOutOfRangeIDs pins the ID range check on ItemAt:
// IDs outside 0x000-0x1FF fail with the range error, not a record or
// price read past the tables.
func TestItemAtRejectsOutOfRangeIDs(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	for _, id := range []int{-1, IDCount, 0x300} {
		_, err := ItemAt(rom, id)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("id %d: expected error", id)
			continue
		}
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "out of range 0x000-0x1FF") {
			t.Errorf("id %d: error %v, want the range message", id, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestItemAtTruncatedROMFails pins the ROM bounds checks: a ROM ending
// before the price table fails the price read; a ROM ending inside an
// extension record fails the record read instead of returning zero
// fields. A ROM ending exactly at a price row's last byte is long
// enough: the bounds check is off-by-one strict, not over-strict.
func TestItemAtTruncatedROMFails(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	if _, err := ItemAt(rom[:0x3E0010], 0x08); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "rom too short for price") {
		t.Fatalf("short rom, weapon 0x08: err %v, want the price bounds error", err)
	}
	if _, err := ItemAt(rom[:0x5B3A90], 0x1FF); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "rom too short for item") {
		t.Fatalf("short rom, ext usable 0x1FF: err %v, want the record bounds error", err)
	}
	// 傷薬's price row spans 0x3E9958-0x3E9959; a ROM ending at
	// 0x3E995A exactly still carries it.
	it, err := ItemAt(rom[:0x3E995A], 0x00)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rom ending at price row end: %v", err)
	}
	if it.Price != 20 {
		t.Fatalf("傷薬 price %d, want 20", it.Price)
	}
}

// TestNameReturnsEmbeddedTableNames pins Name against the real-ROM
// rows docs/items.md was verified with, and the empty result outside
// 0x000-0x1FF.
func TestNameReturnsEmbeddedTableNames(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		id   int
		want string
	}{
		{0x000, "傷薬"},
		{0x008, "長剣"},
		{0x050, "小盾"},
		{0x060, "兵士の鎧"},
		{0x0E0, "技の香薬"},
		{0x0FF, "カムシ一ン"},
		{0x100, "ブランダ一バス"},
		{0x103, "ロ一ドスタ一"},
		{0x160, "魔王の鎧"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := Name(c.id); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("name %#x: got %q want %q", c.id, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	for _, id := range []int{-1, IDCount, 0x300} {
		if got := Name(id); got != "" {
			t.Errorf("name %#x: got %q, want empty", id, got)
		}
	}
}

// TestRawNameRecordDecodesMainAndExtensionNameRecords pins the raw
// glyph-record read behind Name: main records are 8 B at 0x3D0280,
// extension records 12 B at 0x5B2880, decoded with the cmd/dumpnames
// semantics — stop at terminator 0x00 or 0x50, a lead byte below 0x50
// always consumes one more byte (hiding a terminator), a dangling lead
// at the record edge ends the record. Real rows: 長剣 (main 0x08),
// 高級傷薬 (main 0x01, record fills all 8 bytes), 最高傷薬 (main 0x02),
// ブランダ一バス (ext 0x100), ?子?林剣 (ext 0x129, 10 decoded bytes),
// 火成岩の腕飾り (ext 0x1BE, record fills all 12 bytes) and 骨の腕輪
// (ext 0x1BF).
func TestRawNameRecordDecodesMainAndExtensionNameRecords(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixtureROM()
	cases := []struct {
		id   int
		want []byte
	}{
		{0x08, []byte{0x21, 0x1F, 0x21, 0xA6}},
		{0x01, []byte{0x21, 0x47, 0x23, 0x91, 0x22, 0x5C, 0x21, 0xB7}},
		{0x02, []byte{0x20, 0xF9, 0x21, 0x47, 0x22, 0x5C, 0x21, 0xB7}},
		{0x09, []byte{0x21, 0x1F}},
		{0x0A, []byte{0x21, 0x50, 0x21, 0x00}},
		{0x0B, []byte{0x46, 0x50, 0x46, 0x50}},
		{0x0D, []byte{0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x21}},
		{0x100, []byte{0xDC, 0xA8, 0xAE, 0xD5, 0xE5, 0xDA, 0x8E}},
		{0x129, []byte{0x46, 0x1E, 0x20, 0xBF, 0x46, 0x1F, 0x23, 0x9E, 0x21, 0xA6}},
		{0x1BE, []byte{0x22, 0x15, 0x21, 0x14, 0x22, 0xAE, 0x69, 0x21, 0xE4, 0x23, 0x4F, 0x77}},
		{0x1BF, []byte{0x22, 0xAF, 0x69, 0x21, 0xE4, 0x22, 0x55}},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, err := RawNameRecord(rom, c.id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("id %#x: %v", c.id, err)
		}
		if !bytes.Equal(got, c.want) {
			t.Errorf("raw name %#x: got % X, want % X", c.id, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	// Out-of-range IDs and a truncated ROM fail loudly.
	for _, id := range []int{-1, IDCount} {
		if _, err := RawNameRecord(rom, id); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "out of range") {
			t.Errorf("raw name id %d: err %v, want the range error", id, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := RawNameRecord(rom[:0x3D0290], 0x09); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "rom too short for name") {
		t.Fatalf("short rom, name 0x09: err %v, want the name bounds error", err)
	}
}

```

`internal/items/names.go`:

```go
// Code generated from patches/bokuno_jp.sfc (CRC32 7E165025). Do not edit
// by hand; regenerate with the decode semantics of cmd/dumpnames
// (records NUL/fullwidth-space terminated, two-byte glyphs for lead bytes
// below 0x50, decoded through the glyphs_jp.json assignment).
//
// Sources: main name table file 0x3D0280 (FD:0280), 256 x 8 B, item IDs

// extension performance table 0x5B3480). Unmapped glyph slots render
// as "?".
```

`internal/mapfmt/anim.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
)

// AnimSpec is one flag2-bit-1 entry of the map record (FF:1C2F): the
// animated object's raw id and the animation kind ($D14A).
type AnimSpec struct {
	Object, Kind int
}

// AnimEntry is one registered tile animation (FF:1BF7) as FF:1695 runs
// it each field frame: the countdown starts at Start and reloads Timer;
// at zero the script (FF:1F04[kind]) steps: 0x81 n waits n frames, 0x80
// loops, any other byte v restamps object Object+v at (X, Y) on the
// layer (C0:0CC2, raw chip words: the load-time priority pass is not
// rerun). Frames holds that restamp rendered over Rect (tiles), split
// below/above the field sprites like the map images.
type AnimEntry struct {
	Kind, X, Y, Object int
	Timer, Start       int
	Script             []int
	Rect               image.Rectangle
	Frames             map[int][2]*image.RGBA
	// LayerKind is the layer the restamp hits; FrameWords its tile words
	// inside Rect for each frame (probes compare them with engine dumps).
	LayerKind  int
	FrameWords map[int]map[image.Point]Word
}

// animSlots is the size of the engine's entry table (FF:1695 walks 0x16
// entries of 16 bytes).
const animSlots = 0x16

// TileAnimations registers and renders the map's tile animations in the
// loader's stamp order (layer 2, 1, 3, then variant layers).
func TileAnimations(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantProps []int, specs []AnimSpec) ([]AnimEntry, error) {
	if len(specs) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	type stamp struct {
		kind, raw, x, y int
		flips           Word
		ovr             int
		spec            AnimSpec
	}
	var stamps []stamp
	curKind := 0
	AnimLog = func(raw, x, y int, flips Word, ovr int) {
		if !animBand(objs, raw) {
			return
		}
		for _, sp := range specs {
			if sp.Object == raw {
				stamps = append(stamps, stamp{curKind, raw, x, y, flips, ovr, sp})
				return
			}
		}
	}
	defer func() { AnimLog = nil }()
	byKind := map[int]*Layer{}
	for i, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1, h.Layer3} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		curKind = []int{0x20, 0x40, 0x10}[i]
		l, err := DecodeLayer(r, lp, objs)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		byKind[curKind] = l
	}
	for _, v := range variants {
		curKind = v.Kind
		if err := DecodeLayerOnto(r, v.Ptr, objs, byKind[v.Kind]); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	AnimLog = nil
	low, _, _, err := LowGridVariants(r, id, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	applyPriority(byKind, low, h.Flags1)
	cg, err := cgramPalettes(r, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pals := cg[:]
	sets, err := LoadChipsets(r, h.Chipset)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	g3, err := loadBG3(r, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(stamps) > animSlots {
		stamps = stamps[:animSlots]
	}
	var out []AnimEntry
	stagger := 0 // $D146
	for _, st := range stamps {
		k := st.spec.Kind & 0x7F
		tb := int(r[0x3F1EF5+k])
		e := AnimEntry{Kind: st.spec.Kind, X: st.x, Y: st.y, Object: st.raw, Timer: tb & 0x7F, Frames: map[int][2]*image.RGBA{},
			LayerKind: st.kind, FrameWords: map[int]map[image.Point]Word{}}
		e.Start = e.Timer
		if st.spec.Kind&0x80 != 0 { // FF:1C84
			if e.Timer > 0 {
				e.Start = stagger % e.Timer
				if e.Start == 0 {
					e.Start = e.Timer
				}
			}
			if tb&0x80 != 0 {
				e.Start += stagger * 32
			}
			stagger++
		}
		sp := 0x3F0000 + (int(r[0x3F1F04+k*2]) | int(r[0x3F1F04+k*2+1])<<8)
		for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
			b := int(r[sp+i])
			e.Script = append(e.Script, b)
			if b == 0x80 {
				break
			}
			if b == 0x81 {
				i++
				e.Script = append(e.Script, int(r[sp+i]))
			}
		}
		if e.Script[len(e.Script)-1] != 0x80 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("animation kind %#x: script has no loop", k)
		}
		base := byKind[st.kind]
		var frames []int
		rect := image.Rectangle{}
		for i := 0; i < len(e.Script); i++ {
			b := e.Script[i]
			if b == 0x81 {
				i++
				continue
			}
			if b == 0x80 {
				continue
			}
			frames = append(frames, b)
			if o := obj(objs, st.raw+b); o != nil {
				for _, c := range o.Chips {
					cx, cy := c.X, c.Y
					if st.flips&wordVFlip != 0 {
						cy ^= 0xF
					}
					if st.flips&wordHFlip != 0 {
						cx ^= 0xF
					}
					rect = rect.Union(image.Rect(st.x+cx, st.y+cy, st.x+cx+1, st.y+cy+1))
				}
			}
		}
		e.Rect = rect.Intersect(image.Rect(0, 0, base.W, base.H))
		for _, v := range frames {
			if _, done := e.Frames[v]; done {
				continue
			}
			o := obj(objs, st.raw+v)
			if o == nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("animation object %#x+%d not in the set", st.raw, v)
			}
			frame := &Layer{W: base.W, H: base.H, Tiles: append([]Tile(nil), base.Tiles...), Props: make([]byte, len(base.Props))}
			frame.stampObject(o, st.x, st.y, st.flips, st.ovr)
			words := map[image.Point]Word{}
			for y := e.Rect.Min.Y; y < e.Rect.Max.Y; y++ {
				for x := e.Rect.Min.X; x < e.Rect.Max.X; x++ {
					words[image.Pt(x, y)] = frame.Tiles[y*frame.W+x].Word
				}
			}
			e.FrameWords[v] = words
			layers := map[int]*Layer{}
			for kk, l := range byKind {
				layers[kk] = l
			}
			layers[st.kind] = frame
			under, over, err := renderRegion(layers, sets, pals, g3, e.Rect)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			e.Frames[v] = [2]*image.RGBA{under, over}
		}
		out = append(out, e)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// animBand is FF:1BF7's filter: animations need a second remap band
// ($D0BF); ids at or above it, and below $D0BD when that band is higher.
func animBand(set *ObjectSet, raw int) bool {
	t, u := set.RemapT, set.RemapU
	if u == 0 || raw < u {
		return false
	}
	return t == 0 || t < u || raw < t
}

// renderRegion draws rect (tiles) of the layers in the field order: the
// under image (BG2, BG1 without bit 13 over black) and the over image
// (BG2, BG1 with it, then all of BG3), both rect-sized.
func renderRegion(byKind map[int]*Layer, sets [][]byte, pals []Palette, bg3 bg3Gfx, rect image.Rectangle) (*image.RGBA, *image.RGBA, error) {
	b := image.Rect(0, 0, rect.Dx()*tileSize, rect.Dy()*tileSize)
	under := image.NewRGBA(b)
	for y := 0; y < b.Dy(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < b.Dx(); x++ {
			under.SetRGBA(x, y, color.RGBA{0, 0, 0, 255})
		}
	}
	over := image.NewRGBA(b)
	crop := func(l *Layer) *Layer {
		c := &Layer{W: rect.Dx(), H: rect.Dy()}
		for _, t := range l.Tiles {
			x, y := int(t.TX), int(t.TY)
			if image.Pt(x, y).In(rect) {
				t.TX, t.TY = x-rect.Min.X, y-rect.Min.Y
				c.Tiles = append(c.Tiles, t)
			}
		}
		return c
	}
	bg2, bg1 := byKind[0x20], byKind[0x40]
	for _, l := range []*Layer{bg2, bg1} {
		if l != nil {
			if err := drawLayer(under, crop(l), sets, pals, 0, 0, false); err != nil {
				return nil, nil, err
			}
		}
	}
	for _, l := range []*Layer{bg2, bg1} {
		if l != nil {
			if err := drawLayer(over, crop(l), sets, pals, 0, 0, true); err != nil {
				return nil, nil, err
			}
		}
	}
	if l3 := byKind[0x10]; l3 != nil {
		drawBG3(over, crop(l3), bg3.tiles, bg3.pal)
	}
	return under, over, nil
}

// bg3Gfx is layer 3's 2bpp tiles and palette (empty without layer 3).
type bg3Gfx struct {
	tiles []byte
	pal   Palette
}

func loadBG3(r ROM, h Header) (bg3Gfx, error) {
	if h.Layer3 < 0 {
		return bg3Gfx{}, nil
	}
	t, err := BG3Tiles(r, h.BG3Gfx)
	if err != nil {
		return bg3Gfx{}, err
	}
	p, err := BG3Palette(r, h.BG3Pal)
	if err != nil {
		return bg3Gfx{}, err
	}
	return bg3Gfx{t, p}, nil
}

// Footprints are C0:7C75's tile edits: an object leaving a tile whose
// class byte 3 has bit 1 (and byte 2 not bit 5) adds facing+1 (1-4) to
// that tile's word on the footprint layer (layer 2 when Controls bit 3,
// else layer 1) the first time (low-buffer bit 1). FootprintPatches
// renders those edits: Grid[y][x] indexes Combos (-1 = no footprints);
// each combo has under/over 8x8 images for deltas 1-4.
type FootprintSet struct {
	Grid   [][]int
	Combos [][4][2]*image.RGBA
}

func FootprintPatches(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantPtrs, variantProps []int, chests []ChestStamp) (*FootprintSet, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	attr, w, ht, err := AttrGridVariants(r, id, chests, variantPtrs, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	byKind, err := TileLayers(r, id, variants, variantProps, chests)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	kind := 0x40
	if h.Controls&0x08 != 0 {
		kind = 0x20
	}
	target := byKind[kind]
	if target == nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	cg, err := cgramPalettes(r, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pals := cg[:]
	sets, err := LoadChipsets(r, h.Chipset)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	g3, err := loadBG3(r, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	fs := &FootprintSet{Grid: make([][]int, ht)}
	seen := map[[3]Word]int{}
	any := false
	for y := 0; y < ht; y++ {
		fs.Grid[y] = make([]int, w)
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			fs.Grid[y][x] = -1
			row := 0x39A400 + int(attr[y][x])*4
			if r[row+3]&0x02 == 0 || r[row+2]&0x20 != 0 || x >= target.W || y >= target.H {
				continue
			}
			var key [3]Word
			for i, k := range []int{0x20, 0x40, 0x10} {
				if l := byKind[k]; l != nil && x < l.W && y < l.H {
					key[i] = l.Tiles[y*l.W+x].Word
				}
			}
			ci, ok := seen[key]
			if !ok {
				var combo [4][2]*image.RGBA
				for d := 1; d <= 4; d++ {
					one := map[int]*Layer{}
					for i, k := range []int{0x20, 0x40, 0x10} {
						if byKind[k] == nil {
							continue
						}
						wd := key[i]
						if k == kind {
							wd += Word(d)
						}
						one[k] = &Layer{W: 1, H: 1, Tiles: []Tile{{Word: wd}}}
					}
					u, o, err := renderRegion(one, sets, pals, g3, image.Rect(0, 0, 1, 1))
					if err != nil {
						return nil, err
					}
					combo[d-1] = [2]*image.RGBA{u, o}
				}
				ci = len(fs.Combos)
				fs.Combos = append(fs.Combos, combo)
				seen[key] = ci
			}
			fs.Grid[y][x] = ci
			any = true
		}
	}
	if !any {
		return nil, nil
	}
	return fs, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/chest.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
)

// ChestPatch is a treasure chest as tile words on its layer: the words
// of Rect (row-major) with the chest closed at load, opened at load (the
// loader stamps ChestObject+1 when the open flag is set), and opened at
// run time (FF:1D03 stamps ChestObject+1 over the closed words, after the
// priority pass).
type ChestPatch struct {
	Layer                  int // 0 BG1, 1 BG2, 2 BG3
	Rect                   image.Rectangle
	Closed, OpenLoad, Open []Word
}

// ChestWords computes c's patch with the same variants and priority pass
// as TileLayers.
func ChestWords(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantProps []int, c ChestStamp) (*ChestPatch, error) {
	kind, ok := map[int]int{1: 0x40, 2: 0x20, 3: 0x10}[c.Layer]
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: chest on layer %d", id, c.Layer)
	}
	closed, err := TileLayers(r, id, variants, variantProps, []ChestStamp{c})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	opened := c
	opened.Object++
	openLoad, err := TileLayers(r, id, variants, variantProps, []ChestStamp{opened})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	base := closed[kind]
	if base == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: chest layer %d absent", id, c.Layer)
	}
	x, y := (c.X-1)&0xFF, (c.Y-2)&0xFF
	rect := image.Rectangle{}
	for _, oid := range []int{c.Object, c.Object + 1} {
		o := obj(objs, oid)
		if o == nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: chest object %#x not in its set", id, oid)
		}
		for _, ch := range o.Chips {
			rect = rect.Union(image.Rect(x+ch.X, y+ch.Y, x+ch.X+1, y+ch.Y+1))
		}
	}
	rect = rect.Intersect(image.Rect(0, 0, base.W, base.H))
	frame := &Layer{W: base.W, H: base.H, Tiles: append([]Tile(nil), base.Tiles...), Props: make([]byte, len(base.Props))}
	frame.stampObject(obj(objs, c.Object+1), x, y, 0, noOverride)
	p := &ChestPatch{Layer: map[int]int{0x40: 0, 0x20: 1, 0x10: 2}[kind], Rect: rect}
	for yy := rect.Min.Y; yy < rect.Max.Y; yy++ {
		for xx := rect.Min.X; xx < rect.Max.X; xx++ {
			i := yy*base.W + xx
			p.Closed = append(p.Closed, base.Tiles[i].Word)
			p.OpenLoad = append(p.OpenLoad, openLoad[kind].Tiles[i].Word)
			p.Open = append(p.Open, frame.Tiles[i].Word)
		}
	}
	return p, nil
}
```
