`internal/mapfmt/chipattr.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// Engine walk-attribute bytes (docs/map-format.md "Chip default
// passability"). The engine keeps one byte per map tile in WRAM bank $7F
// at base DP $1C/$1B (map-size dependent, 0x1800 for 96x64; the move
// gate fetches it at C0:5BE1 LDA [$1C],Y and maps the byte through the
// ROM flag table at $F9:A400, file 39A400, 4 bytes per byte value). Byte
// layout measured from the engine's own writes (MesenCE write-watch,
// 2026-11-17):
//
//	bit 3        進入禁止 - the move gate aborts the step (C0:58CF BIT #$08)
//	bits 4-5     movement zone (0 connect, 1 land, 2 water, 3 deep water)
//	bits 0-2, 6-7 terrain effects (ripple, footprint, event), unverified
//
// Sources stamped into the buffer at map load, in the engine's order
// (write-watch tools/emulator/cs_grid5.lua on the 0x250 load, frames
// 28443-28516: FF/15AE+15CF x6143, FF/0DDE x3895, FF/1540 x232;
// tools/emulator/cs_grid6.lua re-watched the region through frame 43100
// with ZERO further writes, so nothing runs after load — the formerly
// open "runtime chip-default pass" does not exist, see
// docs/map-format.md):
//
//  1. the prop region's DEFAULT WALK BYTE replicated over the whole
//     grid (FF:14B3-14C3; map 0x250: 0x01 = plain walkable — this is
//     the fill-chip default the tile compositions leave untouched).
//  2. object chip property bytes (2-658's チッププロパティ): the engine
//     stores one byte per composed chip in its WRAM chip-entry table
//     ($7E:2400+, byte after each chip-low byte) and STA's it over the
//     tile the chip covers (FF:0D38 per object, FF:0DDA per tile; 0xFF
//     = no attribute). Map 0x250's composer wrote 3347 tiles (3226 x
//     0x1E tree walls, 121 x 0x24 pond water).
//  3. the prop region's overlay RLE (FF:14D7-1562, STA at FF:153E,
//     reported as writer PC FF/1540 by the watch) decoded INTO THIS
//     GRID — the value runs stamped after the composer (232 tiles on
//     map 0x250: 0x24 x134 pond water, 0x1E x87, 0x01 x7, 0x1F x4,
//     reproduced byte-exactly by applyAttrOverlay below). The blob was
//     formerly misread as 圧縮された足跡データ (footprint data) written
//     to the separate $7F:0000 buffer; both halves of that reading were
//     wrong.
//
// The party-side step gate (S_C0_57FF, decoded 2026-11-17 from
// decomp/src/rom_c0.asm + the cs_grid7 watch): the attr byte maps
// through the 39A400 table (S_C0_5BC6 -> $D8FC/$D8FE) and blocks on row
// byte 2 bit 3/bit 1, or byte 0 & 0xC0 == 0xC0 (the E0 進入禁止 rows),
// or byte 0 bit 4 for land-zoned actors, or the per-quadrant
// `byte0 & (8 >> quadrant)` test; INDEPENDENTLY the low-buffer byte
// (C0:58CC `LDA [$19],Y`, internal/mapfmt.LowGrid) blocks on bit 3.
// The gate's zone check (C0:58DA-58EA vs $D990) never blocks the
// on-foot party ($D991 = 0 measured) — it only clears a terrain flag.

// AttrGrid decodes id's engine walk-attribute byte grid (row-major,
// W*H bytes): the prop region's default byte underlies every tile, the
// object composer and the overlay RLE stamp over it (sources above).
// CAMERA-WINDOW CAVEAT RETRACTED 2026-11-17 (winorigin2.lua): the live
// grid is the FULL MAP at tile resolution and is never rewritten after
// load — zero $7F:1800-2FFF writes across frames 28900-42000 while the
// party walked 20 tiles north. The gate fetch `(py>>3)*D0D1 + (px>>3)`
// indexes TILES: $D9AA/$D9AC hold the leader's position in 8px units
// (px>>3 = tile), and D0C5>>1 grid bytes = W*H tiles. The fetch rows
// that motivated the window reading (59/25 cycling in pocket_probe2)
// were wandering-NPC fetches. The load-time bounds $D2EE-$D2F1 are map
// TILE margins set once by C0:4F6E (see docs/map-format.md). This
// decoder models the grid at map-tile resolution, which is now proven
// to be the engine's own resolution; engine captures match byte for
// byte (winorigin2 fetch (13,38) = model attr 01 at the party's stop
// cell).
func AttrGrid(r ROM, id int) ([][]byte, int, int, error) {
	return AttrGridVariants(r, id, nil, nil, nil)
}

// ChestStamp is one treasure chest as the loader draws it: the chest
// object (the map's closed-chest id, +1 once opened) stamped with its
// top-left at (X-1, Y-2) through the base composer (FF:1CEE-1D2B: no
// flips, no palette override).
type ChestStamp struct {
	X, Y   int
	Object int
	// Layer is Flags>>6: the tile buffer $D2D7+2*Layer the object also
	// stamps (1 layer 1, 2 layer 2, 3 layer 3; FF:1D0F).
	Layer int
}

// AttrGridVariants is AttrGrid plus the map's applicable variant layers
// (triggers.Variant kinds 0x10/0x20/0x40, file offsets in loader order),
// which the loader decodes with the same composer after the overlay RLE
// (C0:42C6-4403; 00C3's two unconditional layers wrote 1275 FF/0DDE
// stamps 20 frames after the base layers), then the applicable variant
// property regions (kind 0x80, C0:443D-4467): the loader sets $D8F3,
// which skips the fill (FF:15A6), and runs the region's overlay RLE
// over the grid (0174's region wrote 2036 FF/1540 stamps; 00C3's
// overlay ends at its first count byte and writes none).
//
// Chests stamp before the variant layers, after the overlay RLE (the
// loader's chest pass C0:3EF4 precedes the variant lists C0:42C6;
// 0166/0235/0229/0293 show the chest writes 8 frames after FF/1540).
func AttrGridVariants(r ROM, id int, chests []ChestStamp, variantLayers, variantProps []int) ([][]byte, int, int, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, err
	}
	// The grid takes the layers' size, not the header's: the engine's
	// stride D0D1 is the widest layer (sweep 2026-11-20: 01C7 header
	// 96x81, layers 64x96, engine stride 64; 014B header 65 wide, layers
	// 64, stride 64). The header size is used only without layers.
	w, ht := 0, 0
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x objects: %w", id, err)
	}
	// Load order: layer 2, layer 1, then layer 3 when flag1 bit5 is set
	// (C0:4930-49B5, the same composer, so its chip properties stamp
	// too: 00FD's layer 3 holds the 48-tile pond, attr 26).
	var layers []*Layer
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1, h.Layer3} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		l, err := DecodeLayer(r, lp, objs)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x layer: %w", id, err)
		}
		layers = append(layers, l)
		if l.W > w {
			w = l.W
		}
		if l.H > ht {
			ht = l.H
		}
	}
	if len(layers) == 0 {
		w, ht = int(h.SizeX)+1, int(h.SizeY)+1
	}
	grid := make([][]byte, ht)
	for y := range grid {
		grid[y] = make([]byte, w)
	}
	// The prop region's default walk byte underlies every tile: the
	// engine replicates it over the whole grid at map load
	// (FF:14B3-14C3, write-verified by tools/emulator/cs_grid5.lua —
	// map 0x250's grid = 0x01 x6144 before the composer runs). The
	// object property bytes below STA over it. The overlay stream runs
	// from the default byte on; applyAttrOverlay stops at its own
	// terminator or once W*H tiles are consumed, so an unbounded tail
	// slice is safe.
	var blob []byte
	fill := byte(0x00)
	if h.Prop >= 0 {
		_, f, blobStart, err := ParsePropRegion(r, h.Prop)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x prop: %w", id, err)
		}
		fill = f
		blob = r[blobStart:]
		for y := range grid {
			for x := range grid[y] {
				grid[y][x] = fill
			}
		}
	}
	// Layer order: layer 2 first, layer 1 over it (render order). The
	// engine decompresses both before the property pass; an object chip
	// on either layer stamps its property byte onto the tile. The
	// engine's composer skips only 0xFF (FF:0DDB CMP #$FF / BEQ), so a
	// 0x00 property stamps 0x00. Skipping 0x00 (keeping the fill byte)
	// was rejected by the batch map sweep (cmd/gridprint sweep, 2026-11-20):
	// it left 1431 tiles wrong on 004B, 1389 on 0322 and 13 on 024A, where
	// the engine holds 0x00; stamping it brings those to 76, 248 and 0
	// with 0x250 still byte-exact (TestAttrGridMap250).
	for _, l := range layers {
		for y := 0; y < l.H && y < ht; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < l.W && x < w; x++ {
				p := l.Props[y*l.W+x]
				if p != 0xFF {
					grid[y][x] = p
				}
			}
		}
	}
	// The overlay RLE is the grid's LAST load-time writer (frames
	// 28512-28516 on the 0x250 load, after the composer's 28477-28511;
	// cs_grid6.lua proves nothing writes the grid after load).
	if blob != nil {
		applyAttrOverlay(blob, w*ht, func(pos int, v byte) {
			grid[pos/w][pos%w] = v
		})
	}
	if len(chests) > 0 {
		scratch := &Layer{W: w, H: ht, Tiles: make([]Tile, w*ht), Props: make([]byte, w*ht)}
		for i := range scratch.Props {
			scratch.Props[i] = 0xFF
		}
		for _, c := range chests {
			if o := obj(objs, c.Object); o != nil {
				scratch.stampObject(o, (c.X-1)&0xFF, (c.Y-2)&0xFF, 0, noOverride)
			}
		}
		for i, p := range scratch.Props {
			if p != 0xFF {
				grid[i/w][i%w] = p
			}
		}
	}
	for _, vp := range variantLayers {
		// records only (FF:070B skips the base pass)
		size, err := r.u8(vp)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x variant layer: %w", id, err)
		}
		l := &Layer{W: int(size>>4) * 32, H: int(size&0xF) * 32}
		l.Tiles = make([]Tile, l.W*l.H)
		l.Props = make([]byte, l.W*l.H)
		for i := range l.Props {
			l.Props[i] = 0xFF
		}
		if err := DecodeLayerOnto(r, vp, objs, l); err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x variant layer: %w", id, err)
		}
		for y := 0; y < l.H && y < ht; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < l.W && x < w; x++ {
				if p := l.Props[y*l.W+x]; p != 0xFF {
					grid[y][x] = p
				}
			}
		}
	}
	for _, vp := range variantProps {
		_, _, vblob, err := ParsePropRegion(r, vp)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x variant prop: %w", id, err)
		}
		applyAttrOverlay(r[vblob:], w*ht, func(pos int, v byte) {
			grid[pos/w][pos%w] = v
		})
	}
	// The property rectangles are NOT part of this grid: engine
	// write-watch (cs_grid5.lua, 0x250 load) shows the attr region's
	// only load-time writers are the fill (FF/15AE+15CF), the composer
	// (FF/0DDE) and the overlay (FF/1540); FF/1563's rect stamps target
	// the separate $7F:0000 buffer (DP $19), whose byte feeds
	// C0:58CC's own check. See the Sources comment above.
	return grid, w, ht, nil
}

// applyAttrOverlay decodes the prop region's walk-attr overlay stream
// (FF:14D7-1562) over a W*H-tile grid, calling set for every tile the
// engine would write. Byte-exact against the engine's 232 observed
// writes on map 0x250 (TestAttrOverlay250).
//
// Grammar. Header: [v1][v2][v3?]; v1 is the transparent marker (the
// grid's fill byte — runs of it are skipped because the grid already
// holds it), v2 becomes the first write value, and when v2 == v1 a
// third byte replaces it (FF:14F6-150A). Then a run stream: a count
// byte (0xFF = 16-bit LE word follows) run of the current value; when
// the current value is v1 the tiles are skipped, when it is 0xFF the
// transparent value v1 is written instead (FF:1532-153E). After each
// run the current value toggles between v1 and the alternate (FF:154E-
// 155E). A 00 count is context-dependent: reached after a toggle
// (FF/150F) it is a VALUE CHANGE — the next byte replaces both the
// current and the alternate value (FF:1527-152E) — while reached after
// a value change (FF/150B) it ends the stream (FF/1562 RTS). The loop
// also stops once total tiles are consumed ($9C = $D0D5>>1).
func applyAttrOverlay(blob []byte, total int, set func(pos int, v byte)) {
	if len(blob) < 2 || total <= 0 {
		return
	}
	y := 0
	v1 := blob[y]
	y++
	cur := blob[y]
	y++
	alt := cur
	if cur == v1 {
		if y >= len(blob) {
			return
		}
		alt = blob[y]
		y++
	}
	atTerminator := true // next count read sits at FF/150B
	pos := 0
	for pos < total && y < len(blob) {
		cnt := int(blob[y])
		if cnt == 0 {
			if atTerminator {
				return // FF/150D: end of overlay
			}
			// FF/1511 -> FF/1527: value change
			y++
			if y >= len(blob) {
				return
			}
			cur = blob[y]
			alt = cur
			y++
			atTerminator = true
			continue
		}
		y++
		if cnt == 0xFF {
			if y+2 > len(blob) {
				return
			}
			cnt = int(blob[y]) | int(blob[y+1])<<8
			y += 2
		}
		for i := 0; i < cnt && pos < total; i++ {
			switch {
			case cur == 0xFF:
				set(pos, v1) // FF/1538-153E: FF writes the transparent value
			case cur != v1:
				set(pos, cur)
			}
			pos++
		}
		if cur == v1 {
			cur = alt
		} else {
			cur = v1
		}
		atTerminator = false // next count read sits at FF/150F
	}
}

// AttrWalkable reports whether the on-foot party may enter a tile with
// this attribute byte, by the move gate's ROM table row (S_C0_57FF
// order, zone-0 party, all four quadrant bits required clear):
//
//  1. row byte 2: (b2 & 0x88) == 0x08 blocks (rows 0x06/0x0A water,
//     0x31 tree-family), else b2 bit 7 clear + bit 1 set blocks
//     (0x0D/0x32/0x33/0x36);
//  2. row byte 0: (b0 & 0xC0) == 0xC0 blocks (the 0xE0 進入禁止 rows
//     0x0B/0x0E-0x27/0x37-0x3F...), else any quadrant bit set blocks
//     (byte0 & (8 >> quadrant), conservative all-quadrant mask).
//
// The former conservative zone-2 rule (attr & 0x30 == 0x20 blocked) is
// RETRACTED 2026-11-17: the gate's zone check never blocks a zone-0
// party, the table row for 0x24 (pond) is `00 08 00 00` = open, and the
// winorigin2.lua run BEHAVIORALLY confirmed it — the party stands on
// 0x24 tiles in the 0x250 arrival clearing (leader fetch (13,58) byte
// 0x24 at frame 28908) and wades the 0x24 band at rows 43-44 walking
// north (fetch (13,38)=01 stop cell, walls 1E above, all matching this
// model's AttrGrid byte for byte). The bit-3 event-point block lives in
// the LOW buffer (LowGrid bit 3), not this table.
func AttrWalkable(r ROM, attr byte) bool {
	row := 0x39A400 + int(attr)*4
	if row+3 >= len(r) {
		return false
	}
	b0, b2 := r[row], r[row+2]
	if b2&0x88 == 0x08 {
		return false
	}
	if b2&0x80 == 0 && b2&0x02 != 0 {
		return false
	}
	if b0&0xC0 == 0xC0 {
		return false
	}
	return b0&0x0F == 0
}
```

```go
func TestObjectPropsMatchEngineTables(t *testing.T) {
	r := requireROM(t)
	objs, err := LoadObjects(r, 0x02) // map 0x250's object config
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Engine WRAM (attrdump2 dump of $7E:2000-$3FFF): object 0's entries
	// are 03 01 04 00 02 04 10 11 04 01 12 04 11 (count + 4 chips) and its
	// property bytes FF FF FF FF.
	o := objs[0]
	if len(o.Chips) != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("obj0 chips = %d, want 4", len(o.Chips))
	}
	wantChips := []int{0x001, 0x002, 0x011, 0x012}
	for i, c := range o.Chips {
		if c.Word&0x3FF != wantChips[i] {
			t.Errorf("obj0 chip %d word = %#03x, want chip %#03x", i, c.Word&0x3FF, wantChips[i])
		}
	}
	if len(o.Props) != 4 || o.Props[0] != 0xFF || o.Props[3] != 0xFF { // 4 props = 4 chips

		t.Errorf("obj0 props = % x, want ff ff ff ff", o.Props)
	}
	// The 52-chip tree objects (0x34 count) carry 0x1E-heavy property runs
	// (blocked + zone 1); the engine's dump showed 1e runs with ff gaps.
	tree := objs[3]
	if len(tree.Chips) != 53 || len(tree.Props) != 53 {
		t.Fatalf("obj3 chips/props = %d/%d, want 53/53 (count byte 0x34)",
			len(tree.Chips), len(tree.Props))
	}
	ones := 0
	for _, p := range tree.Props {
		if p == 0x1E {
			ones++
		}
	}
	if ones == 0 {
		t.Errorf("obj3 props carry no 0x1E (blocked) bytes: % x", tree.Props)
	}
}

func TestAttrWalkable(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cases := []struct {
		attr byte
		walk bool
		note string
	}{
		{0x00, true, "no attribute"},
		{0x01, true, "the 0x250 default fill byte"},
		{0x1E, false, "tree trunk: row byte 0 = 0xE0"},
		{0x24, true, "pond: table row 00 08 00 00; party wades (winorigin2 behavioral evidence)"},
		{0x06, false, "水中00: row byte 2 (b2 & 0x88) == 8"},
		{0x0A, false, "水中01: row byte 2 (b2 & 0x88) == 8"},
		{0x08, true, "event point: the attr TABLE row is open; the block is the LOW buffer bit 3"},
		{0x10, false, "進入禁止1: row byte 0 = 0xE0"},
		{0x20, true, "layer mask: table row open; zone-2 conservative rule retracted 2026-11-17"},
		{0x32, false, "row byte 2 bit 1 with bit 7 clear"},
		{0x28, false, "row byte 0 = 0x08: a quadrant bit set blocks (ROM row 39A4A0)"},
		{0x2E, false, "row byte 0 = 0x44: a quadrant bit set blocks (ROM row 39A4B8)"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := AttrWalkable(ROM(rom), c.attr); got != c.walk {
			t.Errorf("AttrWalkable(%#02x) = %v, want %v (%s)", c.attr, got, c.walk, c.note)
		}
	}
}

func TestAttrGridMap250(t *testing.T) {
	r := requireROM(t)
	grid, w, h, err := AttrGrid(r, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if w != 96 || h != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("grid = %dx%d, want 96x64", w, h)
	}
	counts := map[byte]int{}
	for _, row := range grid {
		for _, v := range row {
			counts[v]++
		}
	}
	// Engine-verified build (write-watch tools/emulator/cs_grid5.lua,
	// 0x250 load): the default walk byte 0x01 fills the grid, the object
	// composer STA's per-chip property bytes (3347 tiles: 3226 x 0x1E
	// tree walls, 121 x 0x24 pond), and the prop region's overlay RLE
	// stamps 232 more tiles (134 x 0x24, 87 x 0x1E, 7 x 0x01, 4 x 0x1F;
	// TestAttrOverlay250 pins the writes). cs_grid6.lua proves nothing
	// writes the grid after load. This decoder recovers the composer and
	// overlay exactly except the composer placement gap: the engine's
	// settled capture (bank7f_A/B dumps, frames 43000) counts 0x1E x3260
	// / 0x01 x2629 / 0x24 x251 / 0x1F x4, and this grid differs from it
	// on exactly 1090 tiles, every one an engine-composed tile this
	// decoder's object stream decode fails to place (docs/map-format.md
	// "Property-phase gap"). No tile may fall back to 0x00 — the fill
	// byte underlies everything.
	if counts[0x00] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("fill byte missing: %d tiles decode as 0x00", counts[0x00])
	}
	// Composer gap CLOSED (2026-11-17, repeat-op grammar rewrite): the
	// counts now equal the engine's settled capture EXACTLY (0x1E x3260
	// / 0x01 x2629 / 0x24 x251 / 0x1F x4) — gridprint capture on the
	// cs_grid7 run log reports 0/6144 tiles differ, and the composer
	// write sequences are identical (3895/3895 writes, probe
	// TestProbeWriteSeq). The old 1090-tile gap is gone.
	want := map[byte]int{0x01: 2629, 0x1E: 3260, 0x24: 251, 0x1F: 4}
	for v, n := range want {
		if counts[v] != n {
			t.Errorf("attr %#02x count = %d, want %d", v, counts[v], n)
		}
	}
}

// applyAttrOverlay's RLE grammar (FF:14D7-1562) on synthetic streams: a
// leading count 0 ends the stream; runs of the transparent value v1 write
// nothing; runs of another value write it; current value 0xFF writes v1;
// a count byte 0xFF extends to a 16-bit LE word; a count 0 after a run is
// a value change and a count 0 after a value change ends the stream.
func TestApplyAttrOverlayGrammar(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		blob  []byte
		total int
		want  [][2]int // (pos, value) in write order
	}{
		{
			name:  "leading count 0 ends the stream",
			blob:  []byte{0x01, 0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x05, 0x03},
			total: 10,
			want:  nil,
		},
		{
			name:  "value runs alternate with transparent v1 runs",
			blob:  []byte{0x07, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x00},
			total: 16,
			want:  [][2]int{{0, 0x01}, {1, 0x01}},
		},
		{
			name:  "count FF reads a 16-bit LE word",
			blob:  []byte{0x07, 0x01, 0xFF, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00},
			total: 16,
			want:  [][2]int{{0, 0x01}, {1, 0x01}, {2, 0x01}, {3, 0x01}, {4, 0x01}},
		},
		{
			name:  "current value FF writes the transparent value",
			blob:  []byte{0x07, 0xFF, 0x02, 0x00},
			total: 8,
			want:  [][2]int{{0, 0x07}, {1, 0x07}},
		},
		{
			name:  "count 0 after a run changes the value",
			blob:  []byte{0x01, 0x02, 0x02, 0x00, 0x03, 0x02, 0x00},
			total: 8,
			want:  [][2]int{{0, 0x02}, {1, 0x02}, {2, 0x03}, {3, 0x03}},
		},
		{
			name:  "count 0 after a value change ends the stream",
			blob:  []byte{0x01, 0x02, 0x02, 0x00, 0x03, 0x00, 0x09},
			total: 8,
			want:  [][2]int{{0, 0x02}, {1, 0x02}},
		},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var writes [][2]int
			applyAttrOverlay(c.blob, c.total, func(pos int, v byte) {
				writes = append(writes, [2]int{pos, int(v)})
			})
			if len(writes) != len(c.want) {
				t.Fatalf("overlay wrote %d tiles (%v), want %d", len(writes), writes, len(c.want))
			}
			for i, w := range writes {
				if w != c.want[i] {
					t.Fatalf("write %d = tile %d val %#02x, want tile %d val %#02x",
						i, w[0], w[1], c.want[i][0], c.want[i][1])
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestWalkableMap250Maze(t *testing.T) {
	r := requireROM(t)
	g, err := Walkable(r, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	grid, _, _, err := AttrGrid(r, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Every 0x1E tile (tree trunks, the band the release-session wall
	// follower could not pass) must be blocked in the combined grid.
	blocked, open1E := 0, 0
	for y := 0; y < g.H && y < len(grid); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < g.W && x < len(grid[y]); x++ {
			if grid[y][x] == 0x1E {
				if g.At(x, y) {
					open1E++
				} else {
					blocked++
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if open1E > 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d of %d 0x1E tiles walkable, want all blocked", open1E, open1E+blocked)
	}
	if !g.At(60, 22) {
		t.Errorf("(60,22) blocked, want open arena floor")
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/chips.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
)

// ChipsetIDs returns the five chipset graphic IDs of chipset set set.
// A map word's chip index selects one ID via chip>>7.
func ChipsetIDs(r ROM, set byte) ([]byte, error) {
	off := chipsetListAddr + int(set)*chipsetsPerMap
	ids := make([]byte, chipsetsPerMap)
	for i := range ids {
		b, err := r.u8(off + i)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("chipset set %d: %w", set, err)
		}
		ids[i] = b
	}
	return ids, nil
}

// decodeBlock expands one run-coded block of a chipset graphic.
// Flag byte 01-7F: repeat the next byte flag+1 times. Flag 80-FE: copy
// (flag&0x7F)+1 literal bytes. Flag 00: end of block.
func decodeBlock(r ROM, pos int) ([]byte, int, error) {
	out := make([]byte, 0, 2048)
	for {
		flag, err := r.u8(pos)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("chip block at %06X: %w", pos, err)
		}
		pos++
		switch {
		case flag == 0x00:
			return out, pos, nil
		case flag < 0x80:
			b, err := r.u8(pos)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, 0, err
			}
			pos++
			for i := 0; i < int(flag)+1; i++ {
				out = append(out, b)
			}
		default:
			n := int(flag&0x7F) + 1
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				b, err := r.u8(pos + i)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, 0, err
				}
				out = append(out, b)
			}
			pos += n
		}
	}
}

// ChipTiles holds the decompressed 4bpp tile graphics of one chipset:
// 128 tiles of 64 bytes each in SNES bitplane order.
type ChipTiles = []byte

// DecodeChipset decompresses chipset graphic id into 128 SNES 4bpp tiles
// (32 bytes per tile, 8192 bytes total).
//
// The stream holds four same-size run-coded blocks, one per bitplane:
// block k supplies bitplane k. Each block holds 8 bytes per tile (one
// byte per row), interleaved into the standard SNES 4bpp tile layout of
// 16 bytes for bitplanes 0/1 followed by 16 bytes for bitplanes 2/3.
func DecodeChipset(r ROM, id byte) (ChipTiles, error) {
	ptr, err := r.u24snes(chipsetPtrAddr + int(id)*3)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("chipset graphic %d: %w", id, err)
	}
	blocks := make([][]byte, 4)
	pos := ptr
	for i := range blocks {
		blocks[i], pos, err = decodeBlock(r, pos)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	size := len(blocks[0])
	for _, b := range blocks[1:] {
		if len(b) != size {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("chipset graphic %d: block sizes differ (%v)", id, []int{len(blocks[0]), len(blocks[1]), len(blocks[2]), len(blocks[3])})
		}
	}
	tiles := size / 8
	out := make(ChipTiles, tiles*32)
	for t := 0; t < tiles && t < 128; t++ {
		for row := 0; row < 8; row++ {
			dst := t*32 + row*4
			for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
				out[dst+i] = blocks[i][t*8+row]
			}
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// LoadChipsets decodes all five chipset graphics of a chipset set into
// chip-index order: chip n lives in set[n>>7] at tile n&0x7F.
func LoadChipsets(r ROM, set byte) ([]ChipTiles, error) {
	ids, err := ChipsetIDs(r, set)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	sets := make([]ChipTiles, 0, len(ids))
	for _, id := range ids {
		t, err := DecodeChipset(r, id)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		sets = append(sets, t)
	}
	return sets, nil
}

// TilePixel returns the palette index of one pixel of a 4bpp tile.
// data is the 32-byte SNES tile; row and col are 0..7. Bit 7 of each
// plane byte is the leftmost pixel, per the SNES 4bpp format.
func TilePixel(data []byte, row, col int) (byte, error) {
	if len(data) < 32 || row < 0 || row > 7 || col < 0 || col > 7 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("tile pixel row %d col %d out of range", row, col)
	}
	bit := uint(7 - col&7)
	base := row * 4
	low := (data[base] >> bit) & 1
	if (data[base+1]>>bit)&1 != 0 {
		low |= 2
	}
	high := (data[base+2] >> bit) & 1
	if (data[base+3]>>bit)&1 != 0 {
		high |= 2
	}
	return low | high<<2, nil
}

// BG3Tiles decodes layer 3's 2bpp tiles (FF:1065): a 24-bit pointer at
// F9:AD00 + id*3 to a word stream for VRAM 0x3000: 0 ends, b < 0x80
// repeats the next word b+1 times, b >= 0x80 copies (b&0x7F)+1 words.
// The result holds 16 bytes per tile.
func BG3Tiles(r ROM, id byte) ([]byte, error) {
	p := 0x39AD00 + int(id)*3
	if p+3 > len(r) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("bg3 tiles %d: pointer outside ROM", id)
	}
	a := int(r[p]) | int(r[p+1])<<8 | int(r[p+2])<<16
	q := a & 0x3FFFFF
	if a>>16 < 0xC0 {
		q = a
	}
	var out []byte
	for {
		if q >= len(r) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("bg3 tiles %d: stream runs past the ROM", id)
		}
		b := int(r[q])
		q++
		if b == 0 {
			return out, nil
		}
		if b < 0x80 {
			for i := 0; i < b+1; i++ {
				out = append(out, r[q], r[q+1])
			}
			q += 2
		} else {
			n := (b & 0x7F) + 1
			out = append(out, r[q:q+2*n]...)
			q += 2 * n
		}
		if len(out) > 0x10000 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("bg3 tiles %d: stream too long", id)
		}
	}
}

// BG3Palette is the 16 colours FF:1179 loads into CGRAM 0-15 from
// EC:A000 + id*32: four 4-colour palettes for layer 3.
func BG3Palette(r ROM, id byte) (Palette, error) {
	var pal Palette
	off := 0x2CA000 + int(id)*32
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		w, err := r.u16le(off + i*2)
		if err != nil {
			return pal, fmt.Errorf("bg3 palette %d: %w", id, err)
		}
		pal.Colors[i] = RGB{byte((w & 31) << 3), byte((w >> 5 & 31) << 3), byte((w >> 10 & 31) << 3)}
	}
	return pal, nil
}

// drawBG3 paints layer 3 the way BG3 shows it: chip-0x280 indexes the
// 2bpp tiles, palette field p picks colours p*4..p*4+3, colour 0 is
// transparent, bits 14/15 flip.
func drawBG3(img *image.RGBA, l *Layer, tiles []byte, pal Palette) {
	for _, t := range l.Tiles {
		w := int(t.Word)
		chip := (w & 0x3FF) - 0x280
		if w&^0x2000 == 0 || chip < 0 || chip*16+16 > len(tiles) {
			continue
		}
		data := tiles[chip*16:]
		p := (w >> 10) & 7
		for row := 0; row < tileSize; row++ {
			for col := 0; col < tileSize; col++ {
				sr, sc := row, col
				if w&0x8000 != 0 {
					sr = 7 - row
				}
				if w&0x4000 != 0 {
					sc = 7 - col
				}
				bit := uint(7 - sc)
				v := (data[sr*2]>>bit)&1 | ((data[sr*2+1]>>bit)&1)<<1
				if v == 0 {
					continue
				}
				px, py := t.TX*tileSize+col, t.TY*tileSize+row
				if px >= img.Bounds().Dx() || py >= img.Bounds().Dy() {
					continue
				}
				c := pal.Colors[p*4+int(v)]
				img.SetRGBA(px, py, color.RGBA{c[0], c[1], c[2], 255})
			}
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/chipvals.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// ChipValues decodes the submap record's per-chip value table: the
// header flag3 bit-0x04 section, a count byte followed by count 16-bit
// little-endian words, each chip ID (bits 0-9) with a 6-bit value
// (bits 10-15, 0-63). A word at or above 0xFC00 instead carries an
// extended byte and sets no chip.
//
// 2-658's サブマップ解析 labels the section アニメーション設定 and reads
// the 6 bits as an animation pattern (未確定). Evidence gathered here:
// the value space of cleanly walking records spans 0-55 (a 6-bit field,
// not the 0x00-0x1D walk-attribute palette), and on maps 0x02/0x03 the
// canal chips carry value 8 while map 0x04's verified sea chips
// (0x180/0x187, inside the pixel-verified flag-04 rectangles) also carry
// 8 — consistent with water chips sharing one animation pattern. Across
// 58 maps only 34.8% of value-8 chip placements fall inside flag-04
// rectangles, so value 8 is NOT usable as a water signal on its own.
// The section has no verified effect on walkability.
//
// The record walk below mirrors internal/triggers' block grammar
// (docs/triggers.md); triggers does not expose this section, and
// importing it here would be an import cycle.
func ChipValues(r ROM, id int) (map[int]int, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	flag1, err := r.u8(off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: %w", id, err)
	}
	p := off + 1
	p += 3 // layer 1
	if flag1&0x40 != 0 {
		p += 3 // layer 2
	}
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		p += 3 // layer 3
	}
	p += 3 // property pointer
	p += 2 // chipset set, palette set
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		p += 2 // two undocumented bytes after the palette set
	}
	p += 1 // object config
	p += 2 // display position
	p += 2 // size
	p += 1 // name id
	p += 1 // 禁止操作
	flag2, err := r.u8(p)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: %w", id, err)
	}
	flag3, err := r.u8(p + 1)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: %w", id, err)
	}
	p += 2

	if flag2&0x01 != 0 {
		p += 2
	}
	if flag2&0x02 != 0 {
		n, err := r.u8(p)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: %w", id, err)
		}
		p += 1 + 4*int(n)
	}
	if flag3&0x80 != 0 {
		for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
			f, err := r.u8(p)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x characters: %w", id, err)
			}
			p++
			if f&0x80 != 0 {
				break
			}
			adv := 0
			if f&0x20 != 0 {
				adv += 2
			}
			if f&0x10 != 0 {
				adv += 3
			}
			if f&0x08 != 0 {
				adv++
			}
			if f&0x04 != 0 {
				adv += 2
			}
			if f&0x02 != 0 {
				adv += 2
			}
			p += adv
		}
	}
	if flag3&0x40 != 0 {
		n, err := r.u8(p)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x chests: %w", id, err)
		}
		p++
		for i := 0; i < int(n); i++ {
			cf, err := r.u8(p + 2)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x chests: %w", id, err)
			}
			if cf&0x18 == 0x08 {
				p += 8
			} else {
				p += 7
			}
		}
	}
	if flag3&0x20 != 0 {
		p += 5
	}
	if flag3&0x10 != 0 {
		b, err := r.u8(p)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x transparency: %w", id, err)
		}
		p++
		if b&0x20 != 0 {
			p += 2
		}
		p += 4
	}
	if flag3&0x08 != 0 {
		n, err := r.u8(p)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x counter: %w", id, err)
		}
		p += 1 + 2*int(n)
	}
	out := map[int]int{}
	if flag3&0x04 != 0 {
		n, err := r.u8(p)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x chip table: %w", id, err)
		}
		if n > 0x40 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x chip table: implausible count %d", id, n)
		}
		p++
		for i := 0; i < int(n); i++ {
			w, err := r.u16le(p)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x chip table: %w", id, err)
			}
			p += 2
			if w >= 0xFC00 {
				p++ // extended pattern byte
				continue
			}
			out[w&0x3FF] = w >> 10
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/chipvals_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "testing"

// ChipValues tests on the shared fixture: the record at fxSubData has
// 禁止操作/flag2/flag3 at +18/+19/+20, all zero until written here.

func setChipTable(f *fixture, flag3 byte, afterFlag3 []byte) {
	// flag1 bit6 set so the layer-2 pointer bytes exist as its own field,
	// the real-ROM layout the record walk follows.
	f.ROM[fxSubData] = 0x40
	// flag1 0x40 keeps the field offsets the record walk always used for
	// bit6-set maps: layer 2 present, so 禁止操作/flag2/flag3 land at
	// +18/+19/+20 exactly as before the ReadHeader fix.
	f.ROM[fxSubData+18] = 0x00 // 禁止操作
	f.ROM[fxSubData+19] = 0x00 // flag2
	f.ROM[fxSubData+20] = flag3
	copy(f.ROM[fxSubData+21:], afterFlag3)
}

func TestChipValues(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	// flag3 0x04: two chip words, 0x206A (chip 0x06A value 8) and
	// 0x0405 (chip 5 value 1).
	setChipTable(f, 0x04, []byte{0x02, 0x6A, 0x20, 0x05, 0x04})
	vals, err := ChipValues(f.ROM, 2)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(vals) != 2 || vals[0x06A] != 8 || vals[0x005] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("chip values = %v, want {0x06A:8, 0x005:1}", vals)
	}
}

func TestChipValuesAfterCharacters(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	// flag3 0x84: a character block (one NPC with X/Y/facing, graphic,
	// event id and quality; flag4 0x1F), the 0x80 terminator, then the
	// same two-word chip table.
	chars := []byte{
		0x1F,             // flag4: 0x10 X/Y/facing, 0x08 graphic, 0x04 event, 0x02 quality
		0x10, 0x20, 0x40, // X, Y, facing
		0x42,       // graphic
		0x74, 0x05, // event id, little-endian
		0x00, 0x06, // quality, little-endian
		0x80,                         // terminator
		0x02, 0x6A, 0x20, 0x05, 0x04, // chip table
	}
	setChipTable(f, 0x84, chars)
	vals, err := ChipValues(f.ROM, 2)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(vals) != 2 || vals[0x06A] != 8 || vals[0x005] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("chip values = %v, want {0x06A:8, 0x005:1}", vals)
	}
}

func TestChipValuesAbsent(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t) // flag3 stays 0
	vals, err := ChipValues(f.ROM, 2)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(vals) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("chip values = %v, want empty", vals)
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/indexed.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
)

// Indexed is a map as the PPU holds it after the load: the tile words of
// each layer, the chip graphics as palette indices, and CGRAM's BG
// palettes. The field draws it with a shader so that the graphics
// animations (FF:9CDB) can rewrite chips and colours at run time.
type Indexed struct {
	W, H int // tiles
	// Words holds BG1, BG2, BG3 (layers 1, 2, 3), W*H each, row-major;
	// nil when the map lacks that layer. BG3 words are the model's
	// (chip >= 0x280); the PPU sees chip - 0x280 with bit 13 set.
	Words [3][]uint16
	// CHR is 128 px wide: chip n at (n%16*8, n/16*8). Chips 0-0x27F are
	// the five 4bpp chip sets, 0x280 on BG3's 2bpp tiles.
	CHR   *image.Gray
	CGRAM [8]Palette
	// Dims holds each layer's own size in tiles (BG1, BG2, BG3); the
	// engine's tilemaps wrap at it (026B's BG3 is 32x32 on a 64x64 map).
	Dims [3][2]int
}

// chrChips is the atlas size: 0x280 4bpp chips and up to 0x80 BG3 tiles.
const chrChips = 0x300

// IndexedSubmap returns submap id in PPU form, with the same variants
// and priority pass as RenderSubmapVariants.
func IndexedSubmap(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantProps []int) (*Indexed, error) {
	pm, err := prepare(r, id, variants, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return indexedFrom(r, id, pm)
}

func indexedFrom(r ROM, id int, pm *prepared) (*Indexed, error) {
	ix := &Indexed{W: pm.w, H: pm.h2, CGRAM: pm.cgram}
	for i, kind := range []int{0x40, 0x20, 0x10} {
		l := pm.byKind[kind]
		if l == nil {
			continue
		}
		ix.Dims[i] = [2]int{l.W, l.H}
		grid := make([]uint16, ix.W*ix.H)
		for _, t := range l.Tiles {
			if t.TX < ix.W && t.TY < ix.H {
				grid[t.TY*ix.W+t.TX] = uint16(t.Word)
			}
		}
		ix.Words[i] = grid
	}
	ix.CHR = image.NewGray(image.Rect(0, 0, 128, chrChips/16*tileSize))
	for chip := 0; chip < 0x280; chip++ {
		set := chip >> 7
		if set >= len(pm.sets) {
			break
		}
		tile := pm.sets[set][(chip&0x7F)*32:]
		for row := 0; row < tileSize; row++ {
			for col := 0; col < tileSize; col++ {
				v, err := TilePixel(tile, row, col)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				ix.CHR.Pix[(chip/16*tileSize+row)*128+chip%16*tileSize+col] = v
			}
		}
	}
	if pm.h.Layer3 >= 0 {
		g, err := loadBG3(r, pm.h)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		n := len(g.tiles) / 16
		if n > chrChips-0x280 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: %d BG3 tiles", id, n)
		}
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			chip := 0x280 + k
			for row := 0; row < tileSize; row++ {
				for col := 0; col < tileSize; col++ {
					bit := uint(7 - col)
					v := (g.tiles[k*16+row*2]>>bit)&1 | ((g.tiles[k*16+row*2+1]>>bit)&1)<<1
					ix.CHR.Pix[(chip/16*tileSize+row)*128+chip%16*tileSize+col] = v
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return ix, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/layer.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// Word is a 16-bit layer chip entry: bits 0-9 chip index, bits 10-12
// palette field, bit 13 draw in front of characters, bit 14 horizontal
// flip, bit 15 vertical flip.
type Word int

const (
	wordChip     = 0x3FF
	wordPalShift = 10
	wordPalMask  = 7
	wordHFlip    = 1 << 14
	wordVFlip    = 1 << 15
)

// Chip returns the chip index of the word.
func (w Word) Chip() int { return int(w) & wordChip }

// PalField returns the 3-bit palette field of the word.
func (w Word) PalField() int { return (int(w) >> wordPalShift) & wordPalMask }

// HFlip reports the horizontal flip flag.
func (w Word) HFlip() bool { return int(w)&wordHFlip != 0 }

// VFlip reports the vertical flip flag.
func (w Word) VFlip() bool { return int(w)&wordVFlip != 0 }

// Tile is one placed tile of a decoded layer.
type Tile struct {
	Word   Word
	TX, TY int
}

// Layer is a decoded display layer: W x H tiles with every position
// filled (the base fill plus records; later records overwrite earlier).
// Props is parallel to Tiles: the walk-attribute byte each placement
// contributes (object chip property bytes; every other placement writes
// tile words only and leaves the tile's attributes unchanged, encoded as
// 0xFF = the engine's "skip the attribute STA" marker, FF:0DD8 CMP #$FF).
type Layer struct {
	W, H  int
	Tiles []Tile // row-major, W*H entries
	Props []byte
}

// AttrWriteLog, when non-nil, receives every object-composer attribute
// stamp in decode order (layer index, tile index within the layer grid,
// property byte). Test instrumentation for the engine write-watch
// comparisons (cs_grid7 logs, writer PC FF/0DDA).
var AttrWriteLog func(layer, tile int, prop byte)

// AttrWriteRec parallels AttrWriteLog with the record index.
var AttrWriteRec func(layer, rec int)

// AttrRecLog, when non-nil, logs every parsed record header (test probe).
var AttrRecLog func(layer, rec, x, y int, flag int)

// putTile writes one tile word, dropping cells outside the layer (the
// engine's coordinate wraps normalize almost everything back in-bounds;
// the remainder targets the $F0+ skip). prop 0xFF leaves a previous
// object's property byte in place, exactly like the engine's FF-skip.
func (l *Layer) putTile(tx, ty int, w Word, prop byte) {
	if tx < 0 || ty < 0 || tx >= l.W || ty >= l.H {
		return
	}
	l.Tiles[ty*l.W+tx] = Tile{Word: w, TX: tx, TY: ty}
	if TileTrace != nil {
		TileTrace(curRec, tx, ty, w)
	}
	if prop != 0xFF {
		l.Props[ty*l.W+tx] = prop
	}
}

// TileTrace, when non-nil, receives every tile word store with the
// record index (test probe).
var TileTrace func(rec, x, y int, w Word)

// tileWord writes the tile word only (rect fills, runs, copies: the
// engine's FF:0A2C writer stores the word and nothing else).
func (l *Layer) tileWord(tx, ty int, w Word) {
	l.putTile(tx, ty, w, 0xFF)
}

// DecodeLayer parses a display layer at file offset off, decoding the
// tile words AND the walk-attribute stamps exactly like the engine's
// layer walker at SNES $FF:0724 (byte-level disassembly 2026-11-17,
// docs/map-format.md "Display layer" and "The repeat-op grammar").
//
// Layout: size byte (high nibble*32 = width tiles, low*32 = height),
// 2-byte base chip word, 2-byte data size including this header, then
// placement records [X][Y][flag][args...].
//
// Base word: base&0x3FF >= 0x100 tiles the whole layer with the fill
// word base-0x100 (FF/0B9E..0BC6 MVN run); base&0x3FF < 0x100 names an
// OBJECT (low byte, remapped) that tiles the whole layer by its chip
// bounding box (FF/0BC8..0CC6 — including its property bytes, the sea
// of map 0x04). Records:
//
//	flag&3 == 0      object placement: 1 arg byte; flag bits 6-7 flip.
//	flag&3 == 1-2    one direct chip, word ((flag-1)<<8)|arg; no attrs.
//	flag&3 == 3      repeat op: dispatch on (flag>>1)&0x7E through the
//	                 13-entry table at $FF:0B7E (flags 03..33).
//
// The optional palette/flip override byte the handlers read when DP $A6
// bit 5 is set is NOT decoded: at map load $A6 bit 5 is clear (map 2's
// record stream consumes exactly dsize bytes with 4-byte object records
// and the shapes below — an extra byte would misalign every later
// record), and the record flag's bit 5 (values 23/2B/2F/33) is NOT the
// gate.
func DecodeLayer(r ROM, off int, set *ObjectSet) (*Layer, error) {
	size, err := r.u8(off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer at %06X: %w", off, err)
	}
	base, err := r.u16le(off + 1)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	dsize, err := r.u16le(off + 3)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if dsize < 5 || off+dsize > len(r) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer at %06X: bad data size %#04x", off, dsize)
	}
	l := &Layer{W: int(size>>4) * 32, H: int(size&0xF) * 32}
	decodeSeq++
	if l.W == 0 || l.H == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer at %06X: zero size byte %#02x", off, size)
	}
	// Real layers are 32-multiples bounded by the map's own size bytes,
	// 128 tiles to a side at most (0x253 is 64x128, the widest seen). A
	// bigger size byte is a garbage record the patch left in place (map
	// 0x3F2's 224x352): decoding it walks tens of millions of rect tiles
	// and never finishes, so reject it here instead.
	if l.W > 128 || l.H > 128 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer at %06X: implausible size byte %#02x (%dx%d tiles)", off, size, l.W, l.H)
	}
	l.Tiles = make([]Tile, l.W*l.H)
	l.Props = make([]byte, l.W*l.H)
	for i := range l.Props {
		l.Props[i] = 0xFF
	}

	// Base: the whole-layer fill or the whole-layer object tiling
	// (FF/0B98, called from FF/06EF before the record loop).
	if base&wordChip >= 0x100 {
		l.fill(Word(base-0x100), 0xFF)
	} else if id := set.Remap(int(base & 0xFF)); id < len(set.Objects) {
		l.stampBaseObject(&set.Objects[id], Word(base&0xC000)<<8)
	}

	if err := l.decodeRecords(r, off+5, off+dsize, set); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return l, nil
}

// DecodeLayerOnto runs a layer stream's records over an existing layer
// without its base fill: the variant-layer decode FF:070B parses the
// same header as FF:06EF but skips the base pass (JSR $0B98), so a
// variant only stamps its records (tiles and chip properties) onto the
// buffer the base load left.
func DecodeLayerOnto(r ROM, off int, set *ObjectSet, onto *Layer) error {
	dsize, err := r.u16le(off + 3)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if dsize < 5 || off+dsize > len(r) {
		return fmt.Errorf("layer at %06X: bad data size %#04x", off, dsize)
	}
	decodeSeq++
	return onto.decodeRecords(r, off+5, off+dsize, set)
}

// decodeRecords runs the record loop (FF:0724) from q to end.
func (l *Layer) decodeRecords(r ROM, q, end int, set *ObjectSet) error {
	for rec := 0; q < end; rec++ {
		curRec = rec
		x, y, flag := int(r[q]), int(r[q+1]), r[q+2]
		q += 3
		switch flag & 3 {
		case 0:
			oid, err := r.u8(q)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if AttrRecLog != nil {
				AttrRecLog(decodeSeq, rec, x, y, int(flag)|int(oid)<<8|q<<16)
			}
			q++
			ovr := noOverride
			if flag&0x20 != 0 {
				ovr = int(mustU8(r, q)) // the palette-override byte (FF/0774-0786)
				q++
			}
			// $A5 = flag<<8|oid; the render EORs $A5&C000 into every
			// chip word (FF/0E08) — the record's flip bits.
			if o := obj(set, int(oid)); o != nil {
				l.stampObject(o, x, y, Word(flag&0xC0)<<8, ovr)
			}
		case 1, 2:
			lo, err := r.u8(q)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if AttrRecLog != nil {
				AttrRecLog(decodeSeq, rec, x, y, int(flag)|int(lo)<<8|q<<16)
			}
			q++
			// word = (flag<<8|arg) - 0x100, keeps the flag's palette
			// and flip bits (FF/0749-075A, FF/0794-079A).
			w := Word(int(flag-1)<<8 | int(lo))
			l.tileWord(x, y, w)
		default:
			if AttrRecLog != nil {
				AttrRecLog(decodeSeq, rec, x, y, int(flag)|q<<16)
			}
			var err error
			q, err = l.repeatOp(r, q, set, x, y, flag)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// flipByte reads the optional palette-override byte the handlers read
// whenever DP $A6 bit 5 is set (FF/0774, FF/0905, FF/09A7): low nibble
// = the replacement palette field (+ priority bit 3), bits 2-4 = the
// palette field a chip must already carry for the override to apply.
// Returns 0xFF when the byte is absent. q is the offset of the first
// argument byte (the byte sits after all of them); the caller advances
// its own cursor past it.
// repeatOp decodes one tile-repeat record (flag&3 == 3). The dispatch
// index is (flag>>1)&0x7E (FF/073D-0746), selecting the 13-entry table
// at $FF:0B7E: 07AB 07C8 07CF 07D6 07E6 07F6 0806 0839 0860 088A 08A7
// 08C0 08D9. Returns the offset after the record's arguments.
func (l *Layer) repeatOp(r ROM, q int, set *ObjectSet, x, y int, flag byte) (int, error) {
	op := int(flag>>1) & 0x7E / 2
	u8 := func(i int) (byte, error) { return r.u8(q + i) }
	u16 := func(i int) (int, error) { v, err := r.u16le(q + i); return v, err }
	// step reads the two bytes of an argument word as (xstep<<8|ystep)
	// and adds one per nibble (the engine's ADC #$0101, FF/0806 et al).
	word := func(i int) (int, int, error) {
		v, err := u16(i)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, 0, err
		}
		return int(uint8(v)+1) & 0xFF, int(uint8(v>>8)+1) & 0xFF, nil
	}
	nib := func(b byte) (hi, lo int) { return int(b>>4) + 1, int(b&0xF) + 1 }

	var xEnd, yEnd, xStep, yStep, wrap, count int
	chip := 0
	rect := false // false = linear run (count), true = rect fill

	switch op {
	case 0, 3: // flag 03 / 0F: reader $0B04 — w1, w2, chip
		if err := reader0B04(r, q, &xEnd, &yEnd, &xStep, &yStep, &chip); err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		q += 6
		rect = true
		if op == 3 { // FF/07D6: brick offset
			wrap = xStep >> 1
			yStep >>= 1
		}
	case 1, 4: // flag 07 / 13: reader $0B4A — size, step, chip
		b, err := u8(0)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		s, err := u8(1)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		c, err := u8(3)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		xEnd, yEnd = nib(b)
		xStep, yStep = nib(s)
		chip = int(mustU8(r, q+2))<<8 | int(c)
		q += 4
		rect = true
		if op == 4 { // FF/07E6: brick offset
			wrap = xStep >> 1
			yStep >>= 1
		}
	case 2, 5: // flag 0B / 17: reader $0B20 — w1, size, chip
		w1, err := u16(0)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		s, err := u8(2)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		c, err := u8(4)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		xEnd = int(uint8(w1)+1) & 0xFF
		yEnd = int(uint8(w1>>8)+1) & 0xFF
		xStep, yStep = nib(s)
		chip = int(mustU8(r, q+3))<<8 | int(c)
		q += 5
		rect = true
		if op == 5 { // FF/07F6: brick offset
			wrap = xStep >> 1
			yStep >>= 1
		}
	case 6, 7, 8: // flag 1B / 1F / 23: count, steps, chip — linear runs
		b, err := u8(0)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		count = int(b) + 1
		if op == 6 { // FF/0806: step word
			xStep, yStep, err = word(1)
			if err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			if chip, err = chipWord(r, q+3); err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			q += 5
		} else { // FF/0839 / 0860: step nibble byte
			s, err := u8(1)
			if err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			xStep, yStep = nib(s)
			if chip, err = chipWord(r, q+2); err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			q += 4
			if op == 8 { // FF/0860: run walks left
				xStep = -xStep
			}
		}
	case 9: // flag 27: reader $088A — w1 end offsets, steps 1, chip
		w1, err := u16(0)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		if chip, err = chipWord(r, q+2); err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		xEnd = int(uint8(w1)+1) & 0xFF
		yEnd = int(uint8(w1>>8)+1) & 0xFF
		xStep, yStep = 1, 1
		q += 4
		rect = true
	case 10: // flag 2B: reader $08A7 — size byte end offsets, steps 1, chip
		b, err := u8(0)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		// FF/08A7 reads the size byte, then BRAs into 088A's tail: the
		// chip word follows the size byte directly.
		if chip, err = chipWord(r, q+1); err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		xEnd, yEnd = nib(b)
		xStep, yStep = 1, 1
		q += 3
		rect = true
	case 11, 12: // flag 2F / 33: end offsets + step word — stretch copy
		if op == 11 { // FF/08C0: size byte
			b, err := u8(0)
			if err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			xEnd, yEnd = nib(b)
			w1, err := u16(1)
			if err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			// FF/08E5: the word goes to $AE/$AF raw, the destination's
			// absolute top-left (FF/0A9C writes row $AF, column $AE)
			xStep = int(uint8(w1))
			yStep = int(uint8(w1 >> 8))
			q += 3
		} else { // FF/08D9: w1 word
			w1, err := u16(0)
			if err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			xEnd = int(uint8(w1)+1) & 0xFF
			yEnd = int(uint8(w1>>8)+1) & 0xFF
			w2, err := u16(2)
			if err != nil {
				return q, err
			}
			xStep = int(uint8(w2))
			yStep = int(uint8(w2 >> 8))
			q += 4
		}
		l.stretchCopy(x, y, xEnd, yEnd, xStep, yStep)
		return q, nil
	default:
		q += 4 // flags past 0x33 jump into garbage and never occur
		return q, nil
	}
	// DP $A6 bit 5 gates the optional palette-override byte. $A6 is the
	// high byte of the word in $A5: the record flag for direct
	// placements (case 0 above), the chip word here. The object rect and
	// run readers fetch the byte after the chip word when chip bit 13 is
	// set (FF/08FF-0917, FF/09A1-09B9); the chip rect/run never does,
	// and the record flag's bit 5 plays no part (0x250's 3094D2
	// records). Map 0056 rec 51 (chip 208B) desynced every later record
	// before this byte was consumed.
	ovr := noOverride
	if chip&wordChip < 0x100 && chip&0x2000 != 0 {
		b, err := r.u8(q)
		if err != nil {
			return q, err
		}
		ovr = int(b)
		q++
	}
	if rect {
		if chip&wordChip < 0x100 {
			l.objectRect(obj(set, chip&0xFF), x, y, xEnd, yEnd, xStep, yStep, wrap, Word(chip&0xC000), ovr)
		} else {
			l.chipRect(x, y, xEnd, yEnd, xStep, yStep, wrap, Word(chip-0x100))
		}
	} else {
		if chip&wordChip < 0x100 {
			l.objectRun(obj(set, chip&0xFF), x, y, count, xStep, yStep, Word(chip&0xC000), ovr)
		} else {
			l.chipRun(x, y, count, xStep, yStep, Word(chip-0x100))
		}
	}
	return q, nil
}

// chipWord reads a record's chip/object word the way every repeat-op
// reader does (LDA [$8D],Y / XBA, e.g. FF/081A, FF/0856, FF/089D,
// FF/0B76): the high byte comes first in the stream.
func chipWord(r ROM, off int) (int, error) {
	hi, err := r.u8(off)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	lo, err := r.u8(off + 1)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return int(hi)<<8 | int(lo), nil
}

// noOverride marks a record without a palette-override byte ($B4 = 0).
const noOverride = -1

func mustU8(r ROM, off int) byte {
	b, _ := r.u8(off)
	return b
}

// reader0B04 is the engine's 6-byte reader $FF/0B04: w1 (+1 each byte)
// into the rect end offsets $9C/$9D, w2 (+1 each byte) into the steps
// $AE/$AF, then the chip word stored high byte first (XBA, FF/0B1A).
func reader0B04(r ROM, q int, xEnd, yEnd, xStep, yStep *int, chip *int) error {
	w1, err := r.u16le(q)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	w2, err := r.u16le(q + 2)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c, err := r.u8(q + 4)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	cl, err := r.u8(q + 5)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	*xEnd = int(uint8(w1)+1) & 0xFF
	*yEnd = int(uint8(w1>>8)+1) & 0xFF
	*xStep = int(uint8(w2)+1) & 0xFF
	*yStep = int(uint8(w2>>8)+1) & 0xFF
	*chip = int(c)<<8 | int(cl)
	return nil
}

// chipRect tiles a chip word over a stepped rect (engine FF/09E1). All
// coordinates are 8-bit: the rect end is (base+offset)&0xFF and the
// loops compare the wrapped coordinate against it, stamping the row
// BEFORE advancing (FF/092C stamp, then the CMP $9E/$9D BCC loop), so a
// base near 255 wraps around the map edge.
func (l *Layer) chipRect(x, y, xEndOff, yEndOff, xStep, yStep, wrap int, w Word) {
	xEnd := (x + xEndOff) & 0xFF
	yEnd := (y + yEndOff) & 0xFF
	if xStep <= 0 || yStep <= 0 {
		return // degenerate steps would loop forever (engine hangs too)
	}
	for row := 0; ; row++ {
		xx := (x + wrap) & 0xFF
		if row&1 == 0 {
			xx = x & 0xFF
		}
		for {
			l.tileWord(xx, y&0xFF, w)
			xx = (xx + xStep) & 0xFF
			if xx >= xEnd {
				break
			}
		}
		y = (y + yStep) & 0xFF
		if y >= yEnd {
			break
		}
	}
}

// chipRun walks count cells diagonally, writing the chip word (FF/0AE8).
func (l *Layer) chipRun(x, y, count, xStep, yStep int, w Word) {
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		l.tileWord(x&0xFF, y&0xFF, w)
		x = (x + xStep) & 0xFF
		y = (y + yStep) & 0xFF
	}
}

// objectRect stamps an object over a stepped rect (engine FF/08F0): the
// same 8-bit wrapped loop as chipRect, x reset to the record's column
// at each row end with the brick wrap added on odd rows, both loops
// capped at $F0 (FF/0949/097D CMP #$F0).
func (l *Layer) objectRect(o *Object, x, y, xEndOff, yEndOff, xStep, yStep, wrap int, flips Word, ovr int) {
	if o == nil {
		return // a desynced parse must drop the stamp, not panic
	}
	obj := o
	xEnd := (x + xEndOff) & 0xFF
	yEnd := (y + yEndOff) & 0xFF
	if xStep <= 0 || yStep <= 0 {
		return
	}
	for row := 0; ; row++ {
		xx := (x + wrap) & 0xFF
		if row&1 == 0 {
			xx = x & 0xFF
		}
		for {
			l.stampObject(obj, xx, y&0xFF, flips, ovr)
			xx = (xx + xStep) & 0xFF
			if !rectContinues(xx, xEnd) {
				break
			}
		}
		y = (y + yStep) & 0xFF
		if !rectContinues(y, yEnd) {
			break
		}
	}
}

// rectContinues is objectRect's loop test on one 8-bit axis (x at
// FF/0943-0959, y at FF/0975-098B), after the coordinate advanced by
// its step: an end in the $F0+ wrap zone stops as soon as the
// coordinate wraps below $80 (BPL); otherwise a coordinate in the $F0+
// zone keeps going, and the loop runs while coordinate < end. A record
// at x=254 with end 255 and step 2 stamps once (0010 rec 29, 004B rec
// 31); the former `>= end || >= $F0` test kept stamping the whole row.
func rectContinues(c, end int) bool {
	if end >= 0xF0 {
		return c >= 0x80 && c < end
	}
	return c >= 0xF0 || c < end
}

// objectRun stamps an object count times, walking by the steps (FF/0992).
func (l *Layer) objectRun(o *Object, x, y, count, xStep, yStep int, flips Word, ovr int) {
	if o == nil {
		return // a desynced parse must drop the stamp, not panic
	}
	obj := o
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		l.stampObject(obj, x, y, flips, ovr)
		x = (x + xStep) & 0xFF
		y = (y + yStep) & 0xFF
	}
}

// obj resolves a remapped object id, nil when out of range (a desynced
// parse must drop the stamp, not panic).
// lastObjID is the raw (pre-remap) id of the latest obj() lookup, which
// the next stampObject reports through AnimLog.
var lastObjID int

// AnimLog, when non-nil, receives every object stamp: raw id, position,
// flips and palette override (TileAnimations).
var AnimLog func(rawID, x, y int, flips Word, ovr int)

func obj(set *ObjectSet, oid int) *Object {
	lastObjID = oid
	id := set.Remap(oid)
	if id < 0 || id >= len(set.Objects) {
		return nil
	}
	return &set.Objects[id]
}

// stampBaseObject tiles the whole layer with one object, positioned so
// the object's top-left chip lands at (-minX, -minY) (engine FF/0BC8:
// columns = ceil(W/w), rows = ceil(H/h), stepping by the bounding box;
// JSR $0CC2 per tile — so its property bytes stamp too).
func (l *Layer) stampBaseObject(o *Object, flips Word) {
	minX, minY, maxX, maxY := 0x0F, 0x0F, 0, 0
	for _, c := range o.Chips {
		if c.X < minX {
			minX = c.X
		}
		if c.X > maxX {
			maxX = c.X
		}
		if c.Y < minY {
			minY = c.Y
		}
		if c.Y > maxY {
			maxY = c.Y
		}
	}
	ow, oh := maxX-minX+1, maxY-minY+1
	if ow <= 0 || oh <= 0 {
		return
	}
	for yy := -minY; yy < l.H; yy += oh {
		for xx := -minX; xx < l.W; xx += ow {
			l.stampObject(o, xx, yy, flips, noOverride)
		}
	}
}

// stampObject composes one object at (x, y): per chip, the engine
// (FF/0D38-0E43) wraps y once into the layer height (skipping the chip
// at $F0+), normalizes x modulo the layer width, STA's the chip's
// property byte into the walk-attr grid unless it is 0xFF (FF/0DDA), and
// stores the tile word with the caller's flip bits EOR'd in (FF/0E08).
// OvrLog, when non-nil, receives the override of every object stamp
// (test probe).
var OvrLog func(ovr int)

func (l *Layer) stampObject(o *Object, x, y int, flips Word, ovr int) {
	if OvrLog != nil {
		OvrLog(ovr)
	}
	if AnimLog != nil {
		AnimLog(lastObjID, x, y, flips, ovr)
	}
	// flips (bit 14 horizontal, bit 15 vertical) flip the chip word AND
	// mirror the chip's position within the object's 16-chip grid: the
	// render EORs the pos byte with $0F (vertical, FF/0D6D) / $F0
	// (horizontal, FF/0D79) before extracting the nibbles. For direct
	// placements the bits come from the record flag, for repeat ops from
	// the stream chip word (the $A5&C000 / DP $A6 pair, both fed from
	// the same source bits).
	propIdx := 0
	for _, c := range o.Chips {
		cx, cy := c.X, c.Y
		if flips&wordVFlip != 0 {
			cy ^= 0xF
		}
		if flips&wordHFlip != 0 {
			cx ^= 0xF
		}
		yy := (y + cy) & 0xFF
		if yy >= l.H {
			if yy >= 0xF0 {
				continue // FF/0D93 JMP $0E3A: chip skipped
			}
			yy -= l.H
		}
		xx := (x + cx) & 0xFF
		for {
			if xx >= 0xF0 {
				if xx < l.W {
					break
				}
				xx = (xx + l.W) & 0xFF
				continue
			}
			if xx < l.W {
				break
			}
			xx -= l.W
		}
		// The property pointer walks the Props slice only across chips
		// that are actually rendered (a $F0-skipped chip bypasses the
		// LDA ($C0) / INC $C0 at FF/0DD4/0DE7), so prop[k] pairs with the
		// k-th rendered chip in stream order.
		var prop byte = 0xFF
		if propIdx < len(o.Props) {
			prop = o.Props[propIdx]
			propIdx++
		}
		if prop != 0xFF && AttrWriteLog != nil {
			AttrWriteLog(decodeSeq, yy*l.W+xx, prop)
			AttrWriteRec(decodeSeq, curRec)
		}
		w := Word(c.Word) ^ flips
		if match := ovr >> 2 & 0x1C; ovr != noOverride && match != 0 && c.Word>>8&0x1C == match {
			// FF/0DF7-0E23: $B4 = (byte>>2)&0x1C, zero disables the
			// override; a chip whose palette field equals byte bits 4-6
			// gets word & E3FF | (byte&0xF)<<10 — the low nibble ORs into
			// the cleared palette field and priority bit 13.
			w = w&0xE3FF | Word(ovr&0xF)<<10
		}
		l.putTile(xx, yy, w, prop)
	}
}

// ComposerA6 mirrors DP $A6 during map load (see stampObject).
// curRec is the record index stampObject is composing for (test logs).
var curRec int

// decodeSeq counts DecodeLayer calls so the write log can tell layers
// apart (AttrGrid decodes layer 2 then layer 1, the engine's load order).
var decodeSeq int

// stretchCopy copies each cell of a rect to (x+xStep, y+yStep), growing
// the x step by one per cell and the y step by one per row — the
// engine's diagonal stretch fill (FF/0A5A loop, FF/0A9C copier: reads
// the live grid, so copies chain). 8-bit wrapped coordinates, like the
// engine's INC $93/$94 counters.
// stretchCopy is FF/0A5A: the rect from (x, y) to (x+xEndOff, y+yEndOff)
// copies tile words, row by row, to the rect whose top-left is (dx, dy)
// in absolute tiles ($AE/$AF), each read from the buffer as it stands.
func (l *Layer) stretchCopy(x, y, xEndOff, yEndOff, dx, dy int) {
	xEnd := (x + xEndOff) & 0xFF
	yEnd := (y + yEndOff) & 0xFF
	for yy := y & 0xFF; ; {
		ddx := dx & 0xFF
		for xx := x & 0xFF; xx < xEnd; xx = (xx + 1) & 0xFF {
			if yy < l.H && xx < l.W {
				src := l.Tiles[yy*l.W+xx].Word
				l.tileWord(ddx, dy&0xFF, src)
			}
			ddx = (ddx + 1) & 0xFF
		}
		yy = (yy + 1) & 0xFF
		dy = (dy + 1) & 0xFF
		if yy >= yEnd {
			break
		}
	}
}

func (l *Layer) fill(w Word, prop byte) {
	for ty := 0; ty < l.H; ty++ {
		for tx := 0; tx < l.W; tx++ {
			l.putTile(tx, ty, w, prop)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"bytes"
	"image/color"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// Synthetic fixture: an in-memory ROM with one chipset graphic, one
// palette, one object config stream and one submap (id 2), laid out at
// the fixed data region addresses the decoders use.
type fixture struct{ ROM }

const (
	fxChipStream = 0x3C0000
	fxObjStream  = 0x3D0000
	fxSubData    = 0x381000 // submap table entry 2 -> +0x0100
	fxLayer      = 0x382000
	fxChipsetID  = 0x40 // chipset graphic id used by the fixture
	fxPaletteID  = 0x30 // palette id
)

func newFixture(t *testing.T) *fixture {
	t.Helper()
	f := &fixture{ROM: make(ROM, 0x800000)}
	setSnes := func(off, snes int) {
		f.ROM[off] = byte(snes)
		f.ROM[off+1] = byte(snes >> 8)
		f.ROM[off+2] = byte(snes >> 16)
	}

	// Chipset graphic: four blocks, each 1024 bytes (128 tiles x 8 rows),
	// one run-coded block per bitplane. Blocks carry 0x11, 0x22, 0x44,
	// 0x88 so pixel columns decode to distinct plane combinations.
	block := func(fill byte) []byte { return bytes.Repeat([]byte{fill}, 1024) }
	stream := runCode(block(0x11))
	stream = append(stream, runCode(block(0x22))...)
	stream = append(stream, runCode(block(0x44))...)
	stream = append(stream, runCode(block(0x88))...)
	copy(f.ROM[fxChipStream:], stream)
	setSnes(chipsetPtrAddr+fxChipsetID*3, fxChipStream+0xC00000)

	// Chipset set 0 lists five references to that graphic.
	for i := 0; i < chipsetsPerMap; i++ {
		f.ROM[chipsetListAddr+i] = fxChipsetID
	}

	// Palette set 0 references palette fxPaletteID seven times.
	for i := 0; i < palettesPerSet; i++ {
		f.ROM[paletteSetAddr+i] = fxPaletteID
	}
	// Palette color 1 = red (BGR555), color 2 = green, others black.
	f.set16(paletteDataAddr+fxPaletteID*32+2, 0x001F)
	// CGRAM palette 0 on a map without layer 3 is the text palette
	// (FD:E802 = colours 1-15): colour 1 = blue.
	f.set16(textPaletteOffset, 0x7C00)
	f.set16(paletteDataAddr+fxPaletteID*32+4, 0x03E0)

	// Object config 0 -> one stream with one 2-chip object.
	obj := []byte{
		0x00, 0x00, // config bytes 1 and 3 absent
		0x01, 0xFF, 0x02, // 2 chips, width 2
		0x0B, 0x00, // set common palette byte 0x00 (palette field 0)
		0x05, 0x06, // chips 5 and 6
		0xFF, 0x01, // two property bytes
		0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF, // terminator
	}
	copy(f.ROM[fxObjStream:], obj)
	setSnes(objectTableAddr, fxObjStream+0xC00000)
	setSnes(objectTableAddr+3, fxObjStream+len(obj)+0xC00000)

	// Submap table entry 2 -> header at fxSubData.
	setSnes(hackSubmapTableAddr+2*3, fxSubData+0xC00000)

	// Header: flag1 0 (palette bank 0), layer 1 only, chip set 0,
	// palette set 0, object config 0, size 32x32 tiles.
	hdr := []byte{
		0x00,
		0, 0, 0, // L1 (filled below)
		0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, // prop absent (overwritten by setPropFixture)
		0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // chipset, palette set, object config
		0x00, 0x00, // pos
		0x11, 0x11, // size byte: 1*32 = 32 tiles
		0x00, // name id
	}
	copy(f.ROM[fxSubData:], hdr)
	setSnes(fxSubData+1, fxLayer+0xC00000)

	// Layer: 32x32, base word 0x0200 -> chip 0x200 (set 4, tile 0) as
	// the whole-layer fill, then one object placement of object 0 at
	// tile (1,0).
	layer := []byte{
		0x11,
		0x00, 0x02, // base
		0x00, 0x00, // data size (filled below)
		0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // X=1 Y=0 flag=0 object 0
	}
	copy(f.ROM[fxLayer:], layer)
	f.set16(fxLayer+3, len(layer))
	return f
}

func (f *fixture) set16(off int, v int) {
	f.ROM[off] = byte(v)
	f.ROM[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
}

// runCode encodes src with the chipset run codec: 0x80|len-1 prefixes a
// literal run, 0x01 prefixes a repeated byte, 0x00 terminates the block.
func runCode(src []byte) []byte {
	var out []byte
	i := 0
	for i < len(src) {
		j := i + 1
		for j < len(src) && src[j] == src[i] && j-i < 0x7F {
			j++
		}
		if j-i > 1 {
			out = append(out, byte(j-i-1), src[i])
		} else {
			j = i + 1
			for j < len(src) && src[j] != src[j-1] && j-i < 0x7F {
				j++
			}
			out = append(out, byte(0x80|(j-i-1)))
			out = append(out, src[i:j]...)
		}
		i = j
	}
	return append(out, 0x00)
}

// The composer's palette override (FF/0DF7-0E23): with an override byte
// whose bits 4-6 match a chip's palette field, the chip word's palette
// field is replaced with the byte's low nibble (bits 10-12 cleared, low
// nibble ORed into bit 10); bit 13 priority survives. A chip whose field
// differs, or an override whose match field is zero, is left unchanged.
func TestStampObjectPaletteOverride(t *testing.T) {
	newLayer := func() *Layer {
		l := &Layer{W: 4, H: 4, Tiles: make([]Tile, 16), Props: make([]byte, 16)}
		for i := range l.Props {
			l.Props[i] = 0xFF
		}
		return l
	}
	// Override 0x12: match field 0x04 (bits 4-6), replacement palette 2
	// (low nibble). Chip 0x2401 carries priority bit 13 and field 0x04.
	l := newLayer()
	l.stampObject(&Object{Width: 1, Chips: []ChipRef{{Word: 0x2401, X: 0, Y: 0}}}, 0, 0, 0, 0x12)
	if got := l.Tiles[0].Word; got != 0x2801 {
		t.Fatalf("override 0x12 on chip word 0x2401 stamped %#04x, want 0x2801 (field replaced, priority kept)", got)
	}
	l = newLayer()
	l.stampObject(&Object{Width: 1, Chips: []ChipRef{{Word: 0x0401, X: 0, Y: 0}}}, 0, 0, 0, 0x12)
	if got := l.Tiles[0].Word; got != 0x0801 {
		t.Fatalf("override 0x12 on chip word 0x0401 stamped %#04x, want 0x0801", got)
	}
	// Field 0x08 does not match the override's 0x04: word unchanged.
	l = newLayer()
	l.stampObject(&Object{Width: 1, Chips: []ChipRef{{Word: 0x0801, X: 0, Y: 0}}}, 0, 0, 0, 0x12)
	if got := l.Tiles[0].Word; got != 0x0801 {
		t.Fatalf("override 0x12 on non-matching chip 0x0801 stamped %#04x, want 0x0801 unchanged", got)
	}
	// Match field zero (ovr bits 4-6 clear) disables the override.
	l = newLayer()
	l.stampObject(&Object{Width: 1, Chips: []ChipRef{{Word: 0x2401, X: 0, Y: 0}}}, 0, 0, 0, 0x03)
	if got := l.Tiles[0].Word; got != 0x2401 {
		t.Fatalf("override 0x03 (zero match field) on chip 0x2401 stamped %#04x, want 0x2401 unchanged", got)
	}
}

// Object headers without the 0xFF width marker take the default grid
// width 0x10 (chips wrap there), and the property phase's `FF n` escape
// writes n+1 literal 0xFF bytes.
func TestObjectWidthDefaultAndPropertyEscape(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	stream := []byte{
		0x00, 0x00, // no remap bands
		0x10, 0x00, // count 0x10 (17 chips); nb != FF, width defaults; the
		// nb byte is re-read as the chip phase's first byte
		// (plain chip: palette 0)
		0x01, // chip 1
	}
	for i := 2; i <= 17; i++ {
		stream = append(stream, 0x00, byte(i)) // plain chip: palette 0, chip i
	}
	stream = append(stream, 0xFF, 0x10) // property escape: 17 literal FF bytes
	stream = append(stream, 0xFF, 0xFF) // terminator
	copy(f.ROM[fxObjStream:], stream)
	p := fxObjStream + len(stream) + 0xC00000
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		f.ROM[objectTableAddr+3+i] = byte(p >> (8 * i))
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjects(f.ROM, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(objs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("objects = %d, want 1", len(objs))
	}
	o := objs[0]
	if o.Width != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("width = %d, want the default 16 (header nb != FF)", o.Width)
	}
	if len(o.Chips) != 17 {
		t.Fatalf("chips = %d, want 17 (count byte 0x10)", len(o.Chips))
	}
	if o.Chips[15] != (ChipRef{Word: 0x010, X: 15, Y: 0}) {
		t.Fatalf("chip 15 = %+v, want word 0x010 at the end of row 0", o.Chips[15])
	}
	if o.Chips[16] != (ChipRef{Word: 0x011, X: 0, Y: 1}) {
		t.Fatalf("chip 16 = %+v, want word 0x011 wrapped to row 1 at the default width 16", o.Chips[16])
	}
	if len(o.Props) != 17 {
		t.Fatalf("props = %d bytes, want 17 (FF 10 writes 16+1 literal FF)", len(o.Props))
	}
	for i, p := range o.Props {
		if p != 0xFF {
			t.Fatalf("prop %d = %#02x, want FF", i, p)
		}
	}
}

// Remap translates layer-side object ids through the stream header's two
// bands (FF/0CC2): the larger threshold wins at or above it.
func TestObjectSetRemap(t *testing.T) {
	// Bands T=0x20/O=0x30 and U=0x10/V=0x60: ids at or above 0x20 shift
	// by O-T, ids at or above 0x10 (below 0x20) shift by V-U.
	s := &ObjectSet{RemapT: 0x20, RemapO: 0x30, RemapU: 0x10, RemapV: 0x60}
	for _, c := range []struct{ id, want int }{
		{0x0F, 0x0F}, // below both thresholds
		{0x10, 0x60}, // band 2
		{0x1F, 0x6F},
		{0x20, 0x30}, // band 1 wins above the larger threshold
		{0x25, 0x35},
	} {
		if got := s.Remap(c.id); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("Remap(%#x) = %#x, want %#x", c.id, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	// The same bands declared in the other order remap identically.
	s = &ObjectSet{RemapT: 0x10, RemapO: 0x60, RemapU: 0x20, RemapV: 0x30}
	if got := s.Remap(0x20); got != 0x30 {
		t.Fatalf("Remap(0x20) with swapped band order = %#x, want 0x30", got)
	}
	// A single band and no band.
	s1 := &ObjectSet{RemapT: 5, RemapO: 9}
	if got := s1.Remap(5); got != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("single band Remap(5) = %#x, want 9", got)
	}
	if got := s1.Remap(4); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("single band Remap(4) = %#x, want 4 (below threshold)", got)
	}
	if got := (&ObjectSet{}).Remap(7); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("band-free Remap(7) = %#x, want 7", got)
	}
}

// animBand is FF:1BF7's filter: a raw object id animates only inside the
// second remap band (at or above $D0BF, below $D0BD when that band is
// higher); without a second band nothing animates.
func TestAnimBand(t *testing.T) {
	s := &ObjectSet{RemapT: 0x20, RemapU: 0x10}
	if animBand(s, 0x0F) {
		t.Fatal("id 0x0F below the band threshold animates, want excluded")
	}
	if !animBand(s, 0x10) {
		t.Fatal("id 0x10 at the band threshold excluded, want animated")
	}
	if !animBand(s, 0x1F) {
		t.Fatal("id 0x1F inside the band excluded, want animated")
	}
	if animBand(s, 0x20) {
		t.Fatal("id 0x20 at the first band's threshold animates, want excluded")
	}
	if animBand(&ObjectSet{RemapT: 0x20}, 0x30) {
		t.Fatal("id animates with no second band set, want excluded")
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/objects.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// ChipRef is one tile of a composed object: a chip word plus its position
// in the object's tile grid. Word bits 0-9 are the chip index, bits 10-12
// the palette field (1-7 selects a set palette; 0 renders with palette 0).
type ChipRef struct {
	Word int
	X, Y int
}

// Object is one composed map object: a grid of chips Width tiles wide.
// Props holds the object stream's chip-property bytes (2-658's
// チッププロパティ), one per Chips entry and positionally aligned with it:
// the engine writes these bytes into its per-tile walk-attribute buffer
// at map load (WRAM $7E:2400 chip entries, second byte; docs/map-format.md
// "Chip default passability"). A 0xFF property leaves the tile's
// attributes untouched.
type Object struct {
	Width int
	Chips []ChipRef
	Props []byte
}

// reader walks a compressed object stream.
type reader struct {
	r   ROM
	pos int
	end int
}

func (rd *reader) u8() (byte, error) {
	if rd.pos >= rd.end {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("object stream overrun at %06X", rd.pos)
	}
	b := rd.r[rd.pos]
	rd.pos++
	return b, nil
}

// streamRange returns the byte range of object config stream config.
// Streams are contiguous between consecutive table entries; a non-fitting
// successor entry (bank switch or absent marker) gets a bounded window.
func streamRange(r ROM, config byte) (int, int, error) {
	entries := (objectTableEnd - objectTableAddr) / 3
	if int(config) >= entries {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("object config %d out of range", config)
	}
	start, err := r.u24snes(objectTableAddr + int(config)*3)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, err
	}
	if start < 0 {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("object config %d absent", config)
	}
	end, err := r.u24snes(objectTableAddr + (int(config)+1)*3)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, err
	}
	if end < 0 || end <= start || end-start > 0x10000 {
		end = start + 0x8000
	}
	return start, end, nil
}

// LoadObjects decodes the object composition stream config into its
// object list. Layer placement records reference these by index.
//
// Grammar reverse-engineered from the engine's decompressor at
// SNES $FF/0E44 (verified against bokuno_jp.sfc):
//
//   - leading config bytes: b0; if b0 != 0 read b1; then b2; if b2 != 0
//     read b3 (0..4 bytes total)
//   - objects until a `00 FF FF` terminator (checked at each header):
//     read count byte + next byte; `00 FF w` is a zero-chip record that
//     still occupies an object slot; otherwise next byte 0xFF means the
//     third byte is the object width (else width defaults to 0x10)
//   - chip phase: exactly `count` chips emitted. Every byte is an op:
//     op = (b>>2)&3. 0 = skip (b>>4)+1 grid cells; 1 = emit (b>>4)+1
//     copies of chip lo (palette byte from common, else read one); 2 =
//     set common palette byte (bits 0-1 chip high, bits 2-4 palette
//     field); 3 = emit one transparent chip (chip 0xFF) if b&0xF0 != 0,
//     else clear common. An 0xFF byte is an escape prefix only when
//     common is set (next byte is re-dispatched); otherwise 0xFF is a
//     palette byte (pal field 7, chip high 3) for the next chip.
//   - property phase: `count` property bytes; 0xFF n writes n+1
//     literal 0xFF bytes. Consumed and discarded here.
//
// Overruns stop the object early (the game would read past the stream
// window; stream boundaries make that impossible here).
func LoadObjects(r ROM, config byte) ([]Object, error) {
	set, err := LoadObjectSet(r, config)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return set.Objects, nil
}

// ObjectSet is one decoded object config stream: the object list plus
// the stream header's id-remap band (leading bytes b0..b3 -> WRAM
// $D0BD/$D0BE/$D0BF/$D0C0, FF/0E68-0E8A). Every layer-side object id
// passes through Remap before lookup (FF/0CC2: the two-band translate
// the engine runs on every stamp).
type ObjectSet struct {
	Objects []Object
	RemapT  int // $D0BD threshold 1
	RemapO  int // $D0BE offset 1
	RemapU  int // $D0BF threshold 2
	RemapV  int // $D0C0 offset 2
}

// Remap translates an object id exactly like FF/0CC2: ids at or above a
// non-zero threshold shift by (offset - threshold), band 1 below band 2
// when both thresholds are set (larger threshold wins for id >= it).
func (s *ObjectSet) Remap(id int) int {
	T, O, U, V := s.RemapT, s.RemapO, s.RemapU, s.RemapV
	switch {
	case T != 0 && U != 0:
		hi, lo := T, U
		hOff, lOff := O, V
		if U > T {
			hi, lo = U, T
			hOff, lOff = V, O
		}
		switch {
		case id >= hi:
			return id + hOff - hi
		case id >= lo:
			return id + lOff - lo
		}
	case T != 0:
		if id >= T {
			return id + O - T
		}
	case U != 0:
		if id >= U {
			return id + V - U
		}
	}
	return id
}

func LoadObjectSet(r ROM, config byte) (*ObjectSet, error) {
	start, end, err := streamRange(r, config)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	rd := &reader{r: r, pos: start, end: end}
	set := &ObjectSet{}
	// leading config bytes: b0 -> $D0BD, b1 -> $D0BE (when b0 != 0),
	// b2 -> $D0BF, b3 -> $D0C0 (when b2 != 0) — FF/0E68-0E8A.
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		b, err := rd.u8()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if b != 0 {
			if i == 0 {
				set.RemapT = int(b)
			} else {
				set.RemapU = int(b)
			}
			v, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			if i == 0 {
				set.RemapO = int(v)
			} else {
				set.RemapV = int(v)
			}
		}
	}
	var objs []Object
	for {
		count, err := rd.u8()
		if err != nil {
			set.Objects = objs
			return set, nil
		}
		nb, err := rd.u8()
		if err != nil {
			set.Objects = objs
			return set, nil
		}
		width := 0x10
		switch {
		case nb == 0xFF:
			// words 00 FF FF terminate; other 00 FF w / count FF w
			// headers carry an explicit width byte
			w, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				set.Objects = objs
				return set, nil
			}
			if count == 0 && w == 0xFF {
				set.Objects = objs
				return set, nil // 00 FF FF terminator
			}
			width = int(w)
		default:
			rd.pos-- // nb is the first byte of the chip section
		}
		objs = append(objs, decodeObject(rd, int(count)+1, width))
	}
}

// decodeObject reads one object's chip records, emulating the engine's
// cursor mechanics exactly (SNES $FF/0ED3 handler loop):
//
//   - cursor (cx, cy); a placed chip advances cx with wrap at width
//     (cx == width -> cx = 0, cy++)
//   - op (b>>2)&3, where the low two bits of every stream byte select
//     plain-chip vs op dispatch; skips use the HIGH nibble
//   - skip (op 0): S = (b>>4)+1 cells; the engine computes A = cx+S
//     and loops INC cy / SBC width while no borrow, then ADC width and
//     DEC cy (FF/0F49-0F62): cx = A mod width, cy += A div width. cx is
//     always below width afterwards (the former reading "A mod width +
//     width" left cx past width, so every later chip stayed on one row:
//     016E object 5, 0085 object 38)
//   - repeat (op 1): emits (b>>4)+1 copies; palette byte comes from the
//     common when set (then only the chip byte follows), otherwise a
//     palette byte precedes the chip byte
//   - op 2 sets the common palette byte; op 3 emits one transparent
//     chip (0xFF) when b&0xF0 != 0, else clears the common
//   - a 0xFF byte with no common set is itself a palette byte (pal
//     field 7, chip high 3) for the following chip byte
//   - with the common set, every non-0xFF byte is a plain chip (pal =
//     common); without it, only bytes with b&3 != 3 are plain chips
//
// ChipRef X/Y record the rendered grid cell (cx&0xF, cy&0xF), matching
// the 8-bit pos byte (cx<<4 | cy) the engine stores per entry.
func decodeObject(rd *reader, count, width int) Object {
	if width <= 0 {
		width = 0x10
	}
	obj := Object{Width: width}
	common := -1 // common palette byte, -1 when unset
	cx, cy := 0, 0
	place := func(lo, pal int) {
		// The entry's palette byte maps 1:1 onto the high byte of the
		// layer chip word: bits 0-1 chip index high, 2-4 palette field,
		// 5 priority (draw in front), 6 horizontal flip, 7 vertical flip.
		obj.Chips = append(obj.Chips, ChipRef{
			Word: lo | pal<<8,
			X:    cx & 0xF,
			Y:    cy & 0xF,
		})
		cx++
		if cx == width {
			cx = 0
			cy++
		}
	}
	skip := func(s int) {
		cx += s + 1
		cy += cx / width
		cx %= width
	}
	op := func(b int) error {
		switch (b >> 2) & 3 {
		case 0:
			skip(b >> 4)
			return nil
		case 1:
			pal := common
			if pal < 0 {
				v, err := rd.u8()
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				pal = int(v)
			}
			lo, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			for i := 0; i < (b>>4)+1 && len(obj.Chips) < count; i++ {
				place(int(lo), pal)
			}
			return nil
		case 2:
			v, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			common = int(v)
			return nil
		default:
			if b&0xF0 != 0 {
				if len(obj.Chips) < count {
					pal := common
					if pal < 0 {
						pal = 0
					}
					place(0xFF, pal)
				}
			} else {
				common = -1
			}
			return nil
		}
	}
	for len(obj.Chips) < count {
		b, err := rd.u8()
		if err != nil {
			break
		}
		if b == 0xFF && common >= 0 {
			m, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				break
			}
			if err := op(int(m)); err != nil {
				break
			}
		} else if b == 0xFF {
			lo, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				break
			}
			if len(obj.Chips) < count {
				place(int(lo), 0xFF)
			}
		} else if common >= 0 {
			place(int(b), common)
		} else if b&3 != 3 {
			pal := int(b)
			lo, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				break
			}
			if len(obj.Chips) < count {
				place(int(lo), pal)
			}
		} else {
			if err := op(int(b)); err != nil {
				break
			}
		}
	}
	// Chip property records: one property byte per chip — count values,
	// aligned 1:1 with obj.Chips (the engine's WRAM layout stores exactly
	// len(Chips) property bytes after each object's chip entries:
	// attrdump2 dump, 2026-11-17); 0xFF n writes n+1 literal 0xFF values
	// from 2 bytes. Formerly consumed and discarded (docs/map-format.md).
	pc := 0
	for pc < count {
		b, err := rd.u8()
		if err != nil {
			break
		}
		if b == 0xFF {
			n, err := rd.u8()
			if err != nil {
				break
			}
			for i := 0; i < int(n)+1; i++ {
				obj.Props = append(obj.Props, 0xFF)
			}
			pc += int(n) + 1
		} else {
			obj.Props = append(obj.Props, b)
			pc++
		}
	}
	return obj
}
```
