`internal/mapfmt/palette.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// RGB is one 8-bit-per-channel color.
type RGB [3]byte

// PaletteSetIDs returns the seven palette IDs of a palette set. The map
// header's flag1 bits 0-1 supply the bank bits (id + bank<<8).
func PaletteSetIDs(r ROM, set byte) ([]byte, error) {
	off := paletteSetAddr + int(set)*palettesPerSet
	ids := make([]byte, palettesPerSet)
	for i := range ids {
		b, err := r.u8(off + i)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("palette set %d: %w", set, err)
		}
		ids[i] = b
	}
	return ids, nil
}

// LoadPalette reads the 16 BGR555 colors of palette id and converts them
// to RGB (5-bit channels scaled by <<3).
func LoadPalette(r ROM, id int) (Palette, error) {
	var pal Palette
	off := paletteDataAddr + id*32
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		w, err := r.u16le(off + i*2)
		if err != nil {
			return pal, fmt.Errorf("palette %d: %w", id, err)
		}
		r5 := w & 31
		g5 := (w >> 5) & 31
		b5 := (w >> 10) & 31
		pal.Colors[i] = RGB{byte(r5 << 3), byte(g5 << 3), byte(b5 << 3)}
	}
	return pal, nil
}

// Palette is one 16-color SNES palette. Index 0 is the transparent color.
type Palette struct {
	Colors [16]RGB
}

// LoadPalettes loads the seven palettes referenced by a palette set,
// banked by flag1 bits 0-1.
func LoadPalettes(r ROM, set byte, bank byte) ([]Palette, error) {
	ids, err := PaletteSetIDs(r, set)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pals := make([]Palette, 0, len(ids))
	for _, id := range ids {
		p, err := LoadPalette(r, int(bank)<<8|int(id))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		pals = append(pals, p)
	}
	return pals, nil
}
```

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"

	"testing"

// Probe: attr bytes around a given tile on 0x253 (the walk4 ping-pong
// band), for force-move / wall diagnosis. Env SAGA3_PROBE_X/Y center.
func TestProbe253Band(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE") == "" {
		t.Skip("probe only")
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	id := 0x253
	if v := os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_MAP"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%x", &id)
	}
	attr, w, h, err := AttrGrid(ROM(rom), id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	low, lw, lh, err := LowGrid(ROM(rom), id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cx, cy := 41, 37
	fmt.Sscanf(os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_X"), "%d", &cx)
	fmt.Sscanf(os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_Y"), "%d", &cy)
	for y := cy - 4; y <= cy+4 && y < h; y++ {
		row := ""
		for x := cx - 4; x <= cx+4 && x < w; x++ {
			lb := byte('.')
			if y < lh && x < lw && low[y][x]&0x08 != 0 {
				lb = 'E'
			}
			row += fmt.Sprintf(" %02X%c", attr[y][x], lb)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%3d %s\n", y, row)
	}
}
```

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"testing"

// Probe: list every submap whose header matches a (configByte, sizeW,
// sizeH) triple, for identifying the camp-journey chain's road maps by
// their (D2E3, D0D1, D0C5) runtime fingerprint. Probe only.
func TestProbeChainMaps(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE") == "" {
		t.Skip("probe only")
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// targets: (cfg, width, height)
	targets := [][3]int{{0x02, 64, 64}, {0x02, 96, 64}, {0x02, 64, 128},
		{0x13, 64, 96}, {0x2E, 64, 64}, {0x07, 32, 64}, {0x26, 64, 64}}
	for id := 0; id < 1024; id++ {
		off, err := SubmapDataOffset(ROM(rom), id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		h, err := ReadHeader(ROM(rom), off)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		w, ht := int(h.SizeX)+1, int(h.SizeY)+1
		for _, tg := range targets {
			if int(h.ObjectConfig) == tg[0] && w == tg[1] && ht == tg[2] {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "map %04X cfg=%02X %dx%d pos=(%d,%d)\n",
					id, h.ObjectConfig, w, ht, h.PosX, h.PosY)
			}
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_chipattr_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

// Exploration probe for the per-chip default passability table
// (docs/map-format.md open item). Run with
//
//	go test ./internal/mapfmt -run TestProbeChipDefault -v
//
// It classifies map 0x04's front-layer chips into "inside the
// pixel-verified flag-04 sea rectangles" (water) vs outside, then
// brute-force scans the ROM for a byte/word/bit table indexed by chip id
// that separates the classes. Print-only; no assertions yet.

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"testing"
)

func probeLoad(t *testing.T, id int) (ROM, *Header, []*Layer, []PropEntry) {
	t.Helper()
	romPath := os.Getenv("SAGA3_ROM")
	if romPath == "" {
		romPath = "../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no ROM: %v", err)
	}
	r := ROM(rom)
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var layers []*Layer
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
		if lp < 0 {
			layers = append(layers, nil)
			continue
		}
		l, err := DecodeLayer(r, lp, objs)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		layers = append(layers, l)
	}
	var props []PropEntry
	if h.Prop >= 0 {
		props, err = ParseProp(r, h.Prop)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return r, &h, layers, props
}

// surfaceChip picks the tile's visible collision-relevant chip: layer 1
// word when the layer carries one (non-transparent), else layer 2.
func surfaceChip(layers []*Layer, w, h, x, y int) int {
	if len(layers) > 1 && layers[1] != nil && y < layers[1].H && x < layers[1].W {
		c := int(layers[1].Tiles[y*layers[1].W+x].Word.Chip())
		if c != 0 && c != 0x100 { // 0x100 = the blank fill chip (docs/map-format.md)
			return c
		}
	}
	if layers[0] == nil || y >= layers[0].H || x >= layers[0].W {
		return -1
	}
	return int(layers[0].Tiles[y*layers[0].W+x].Word.Chip())
}

func TestProbeChipDefault(t *testing.T) {
	r, h, layers, props := probeLoad(t, 0x04)
	_ = r
	w, ht := 0, 0
	for _, l := range layers {
		if l != nil {
			if l.W > w {
				w = l.W
			}
			if l.H > ht {
				ht = l.H
			}
		}
	}
	// water tiles = flag 04/05 rects
	inSea := make([]bool, w*ht)
	for _, e := range props {
		if e.Flag>>1 != 2 {
			continue
		}
		for y := e.Y; y < e.Y+e.H; y++ {
			for x := e.X; x < e.X+e.W; x++ {
				if x < w && y < ht {
					inSea[y*w+x] = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	waterSet := map[int]int{}
	landCount := map[int]int{}
	wallOut := 0
	for y := 0; y < ht; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			c := surfaceChip(layers, w, ht, x, y)
			if c < 0 {
				continue
			}
			if inSea[y*w+x] {
				waterSet[c]++
			} else {
				landCount[c]++
			}
		}
	}
	_ = h
	_ = wallOut
	fmt.Printf("map 0x04 %dx%d, water chip classes %d\n", w, ht, len(waterSet))
	var ws []int
	for c := range waterSet {
		ws = append(ws, c)
	}
	sort.Ints(ws)
	for _, c := range ws {
		fmt.Printf("  water chip %#03x x%d  land x%d\n", c, waterSet[c], landCount[c])
	}
	// top land chips
	type lc struct {
		c int
		n int
	}
	var lcs []lc
	for c, n := range landCount {
		lcs = append(lcs, lc{c, n})
	}
	sort.Slice(lcs, func(i, j int) bool { return lcs[i].n > lcs[j].n })
	fmt.Printf("top land chips:")
	for i, e := range lcs {
		if i == 20 {
			break
		}
		fmt.Printf(" %#03x x%d,", e.c, e.n)
	}
	fmt.Println()
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_coarse_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// TestProbeCoarsePlan plans on the 16px movement grid (the engine walks
// 16px cells, sampling all four 8px sub-tiles) from the live party
// position and prints a waypoint plan for the walk harness.
func TestProbeCoarsePlan(t *testing.T) {
	// RESOLVED 2026-11-17 (winorigin2.lua): $D9AA/$D9AC are the leader's
	// position in 8px units and px>>3/py>>3 ARE the map tile — no window
	// origin exists (the walk grid is the full map, docs/map-format.md).
	// The BFS below therefore works; it is skipped only because the live
	// walker (tools/emulator/walk3loane.lua) supersedes it as the plan
	// instrument. Unskip with SAGA3_PROBE=1 to print a waypoint plan.
	t.Skip("superseded by the live walker's replan loop")
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no rom")
	}
	r := ROM(rom)
	grid, w, h, err := AttrGrid(r, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cw, ch := w/2, h/2
	walk := make([][]bool, ch)
	for y := 0; y < ch; y++ {
		walk[y] = make([]bool, cw)
		for x := 0; x < cw; x++ {
			ok := true
			for dy := 0; dy < 2; dy++ {
				for dx := 0; dx < 2; dx++ {
					if !AttrWalkable(r, grid[y*2+dy][x*2+dx]) {
						ok = false
					}
				}
			}
			walk[y][x] = ok
		}
	}
	// BFS from a start cell to any y=0 cell
	sx, sy := 8, 29 // party at px (136,464)
	start := [2]int{sx, sy}
	prev := map[[2]int][2]int{start: start}
	queue := [][2]int{start}
	var goal [2]int
	found := false
	for len(queue) > 0 && !found {
		cur := queue[0]
		queue = queue[1:]
		if cur[1] == 0 {
			goal = cur
			found = true
			break
		}
		for _, d := range [][2]int{{0, -1}, {0, 1}, {-1, 0}, {1, 0}} {
			n := [2]int{cur[0] + d[0], cur[1] + d[1]}
			if n[0] < 0 || n[1] < 0 || n[0] >= cw || n[1] >= ch {
				continue
			}
			if _, seen := prev[n]; seen || !walk[n[1]][n[0]] {
				continue
			}
			prev[n] = cur
			queue = append(queue, n)
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Fatal("no north route on the coarse grid")
	}
	// segment plan
	path := [][2]int{}
	for c := goal; c != start; c = prev[c] {
		path = append([][2]int{c}, path...)
	}
	fmt.Printf("start cell (%d,%d) -> goal (%d,%d), %d cells\n", sx, sy, goal[0], goal[1], len(path))
	segs := ""
	px, py := sx, sy
	dir := byte(0)
	count := 0
	for _, c := range path {
		var nd byte
		switch {
		case c[1] < py:
			nd = 'u'
		case c[1] > py:
			nd = 'd'
		case c[0] < px:
			nd = 'l'
		case c[0] > px:
			nd = 'r'
		}
		if nd != dir {
			if count > 0 {
				segs += fmt.Sprintf("%c%d ", dir, count)
			}
			dir = nd
			count = 0
		}
		count++
		px, py = c[0], c[1]
	}
	if count > 0 {
		segs += fmt.Sprintf("%c%d ", dir, count)
	}
	fmt.Println("plan:", segs)
	// waypoint list
	fmt.Printf("waypoints: %v %v", sx, sy)
	for _, c := range path {
		fmt.Printf(" %v", c)
	}
	fmt.Println()
	// ascii of the coarse grid around the route
	for y := 0; y < ch; y++ {
		row := ""
		for x := 0; x < cw; x++ {
			switch {
			case x == sx && y == sy:
				row += "S"
			case !walk[y][x]:
				row += "#"
			default:
				row += "."
			}
		}
		fmt.Printf("y=%02d %s\n", y, row)
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_composer_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// TestProbeComposerWrites compares the model's composer stamps (the
// decoded layer Props) against the engine's FF/0DDA write watch from a
// cs_grid7.lua run log, per map load. The log lines look like
//
//	GW frame=28477 off=7F0904 val=1F pc=FF/0DDE
//
// with off = 0x7E0000 + raw $7F offset. Load clusters are split on
// frame gaps; each cluster maps to the submap whose load precedes its
// first GEO line (passed in want).
func TestProbeComposerWrites(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no rom")
	}
	r := ROM(rom)
	logPath := os.Getenv("COMPOSER_LOG")
	if logPath == "" {
		t.Skip("COMPOSER_LOG not set")
	}
	type wr struct {
		frame int
		tile  int
		val   byte
	}
	var writes []wr
	f, err := os.Open(logPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1<<20), 1<<20)
	for sc.Scan() {
		line := sc.Text()
		if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "GW ") || !strings.Contains(line, "pc=FF/0DD") {
			continue
		}
		fe := strings.Fields(line)
		fr, _ := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(fe[1], "frame="))
		off, _ := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimPrefix(fe[2], "off="), 16, 32)
		v, _ := strconv.ParseUint(strings.TrimPrefix(fe[3], "val="), 16, 8)
		writes = append(writes, wr{fr, int(off) - 0x7E0000, byte(v)})
	}
	// cluster on frame gaps
	var clusters [][]wr
	for i, w := range writes {
		if i == 0 || w.frame-writes[i-1].frame > 100 {
			clusters = append(clusters, nil)
		}
		clusters[len(clusters)-1] = append(clusters[len(clusters)-1], w)
	}
	want := []int{0x24A, 0x250} // load order in the recorded walk
	for ci, cl := range clusters {
		if ci >= len(want) {
			break
		}
		id := want[ci]
		hdrOff, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		h, err := ReadHeader(r, hdrOff)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		set, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var layers []*Layer
		stride := 0
		for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
			if lp < 0 {
				continue
			}
			l, err := DecodeLayer(r, lp, set)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			layers = append(layers, l)
			if l.W > stride {
				stride = l.W
			}
		}
		// engine settled composer grid from the write cluster
		baseOff := 0
		switch id {
		case 0x249:
			baseOff = 0x1000
		case 0x24A:
			baseOff = 0x0800
		case 0x250:
			baseOff = 0x1800
		}
		eng := map[int]byte{}
		for _, w := range cl {
			eng[w.tile-baseOff] = w.val
		}
		// model composer grid
		mdl := map[int]byte{}
		for _, l := range layers {
			for y := 0; y < l.H; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < l.W; x++ {
					p := l.Props[y*l.W+x]
					if p != 0xFF {
						mdl[y*stride+x] = p
					}
				}
			}
		}
		miss, extra, diff := 0, 0, 0
		for ti, v := range eng {
			mv, ok := mdl[ti]
			if !ok {
				miss++
				if miss <= 10 {
					t.Logf("map %#04x tile (%d,%d): engine %02X, model none", id, ti%stride, ti/stride, v)
				}
				continue
			}
			if mv != v {
				diff++
				if diff <= 10 {
					t.Logf("map %#04x tile (%d,%d): engine %02X, model %02X", id, ti%stride, ti/stride, v, mv)
				}
			}
		}
		for ti := range mdl {
			if _, ok := eng[ti]; !ok {
				extra++
				if extra <= 10 {
					t.Logf("map %#04x tile (%d,%d): model %02X, engine none", id, ti%stride, ti/stride, mdl[ti])
				}
			}
		}
		fmt.Printf("map %#04x: composer writes engine=%d model=%d missing=%d extra=%d diffval=%d\n",
			id, len(eng), len(mdl), miss, extra, diff)
		fmt.Printf("map %#04x diff map (E=engine-only M=model-only d=diff):\n", id)
		for y := 0; y < 64; y++ {
			row := make([]byte, stride)
			for x := 0; x < stride; x++ {
				ti := y*stride + x
				ev, eok := eng[ti]
				mv, mok := mdl[ti]
				switch {
				case eok && !mok:
					row[x] = 'E'
				case !eok && mok:
					row[x] = 'M'
				case eok && mok && ev != mv:
					row[x] = 'd'
				default:
					row[x] = '.'
				}
			}
			fmt.Printf("%2d %s\n", y, string(row))
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_gate_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"testing"
)

// Probe: NPC gate results (GATE_LOG "CHK after57FF" lines) against the
// model's walk grid of GATE_MAP.
func TestProbeGate(t *testing.T) {
	r, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("GATE_LOG") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	id, _ := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("GATE_MAP"), 16, 32)
	walk, err := Walkable(ROM(r), int(id))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	attr, _, _, _ := AttrGrid(ROM(r), int(id))
	low, _, _, _ := LowGrid(ROM(r), int(id))
	f, _ := os.Open(os.Getenv("GATE_LOG"))
	re := regexp.MustCompile(`CHK after57FF pass=(\d+) y=(\w+) a=\w+ p=(\w+) x=(\w+) yy=(\w+) dir=\w+ ba=(\w+)`)
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1<<20), 4<<20)
	agree, disagree := 0, 0
	for sc.Scan() {
		m := re.FindStringSubmatch(sc.Text())
		if m == nil {
			continue
		}
		a, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[3], 16, 32)
		x, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[4], 16, 32)
		y, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[5], 16, 32)
		ba, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[6], 16, 32)
		off := 0x3F6700 + int(ba)*4
		dx := int(int16(uint16(r[off]) | uint16(r[off+1])<<8))
		dy := int(int16(uint16(r[off+2]) | uint16(r[off+3])<<8))
		tx := (int(x) + dx) / 8 % walk.W
		ty := (int(y) + dy) / 8 % walk.H
		engBlocked := a&0x02 == 0 // Z clear: BNE to the blocked branch
		modBlocked := !walk.Walk[ty][tx]
		if engBlocked == modBlocked {
			agree++
		} else {
			disagree++
			fmt.Printf("pass %s slot %s target (%d,%d) attr %02X low %02X engine blocked=%v model blocked=%v\n", m[1], m[2], tx, ty, attr[ty][tx], low[ty][tx], engBlocked, modBlocked)
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("gate: %d agree, %d disagree\n", agree, disagree)
}

// Probe: dump a map's walk grid as rows of 0/1 (WALK_MAP, WALK_OUT).

	out, _ := os.Create(os.Getenv("WALK_OUT"))

		for _, w := range row {
			if w {
				fmt.Fprint(out, "1")
			} else {
				fmt.Fprint(out, "0")
			}
		}
		fmt.Fprintln(out)
	}
}
```

```go
			}
		}
		OvrLog = nil

			fmt.Printf("map %04X active overrides %d\n", id, hits)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_recipes_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// TestProbeRecordDump decodes a submap's layers record by record with the
// repeat-op grammar and prints each record's decoded stamp shape, so a
// missing composer tile can be traced to its record.
func TestProbeRecordDump(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no rom")
	}
	r := ROM(rom)
	idStr := os.Getenv("REC_MAP")
	if idStr == "" {
		t.Skip("REC_MAP not set")
	}
	var id int
	fmt.Sscanf(idStr, "%x", &id)
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1, h.Layer3} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("layer at %06X\n", lp)
		size, _ := r.u8(lp)
		base, _ := r.u16le(lp + 1)
		dsize, _ := r.u16le(lp + 3)
		fmt.Printf("  size=%02X base=%04X dsize=%04X\n", size, base, dsize)
		q := lp + 5
		end := lp + int(dsize)
		n := 0
		for q < end {
			x, y, flag := int(r[q]), int(r[q+1]), r[q+2]
			q += 3
			switch flag & 3 {
			case 0:
				fmt.Printf("  rec %3d obj id=%02X at (%d,%d) flag=%02X\n", n, r[q], x, y, flag)
				q++
			case 1, 2:
				fmt.Printf("  rec %3d chip w=%04X at (%d,%d) flag=%02X\n", n, int(flag-1)<<8|int(r[q]), x, y, flag)
				q++
			default:
				op := int(flag>>1) & 0x7E / 2
				fmt.Printf("  rec %3d op=%02d flag=%02X at (%d,%d) args=% X\n", n, op, flag, x, y, r[q:min(q+8, end)])
				// decode like repeatOp for the summary line
				q = skipRepeat(r, q, flag)
			}
			n++
		}
		fmt.Printf("  %d records\n", n)
	}
}

func skipRepeat(r ROM, q int, flag byte) int {
	op := int(flag>>1) & 0x7E / 2
	switch op {
	case 0, 3:
		return q + 6
	case 1, 4:
		return q + 4
	case 2, 5:
		return q + 5
	case 6:
		return q + 5
	case 7, 8, 9, 12:
		return q + 4
	case 10, 11:
		return q + 3
	default:
		return q + 4
	}
}

func min(a, b int) int {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_seq_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

var layerEnd map[int]int

// TestProbeWriteSeq diffs the model's composer write sequence against the
// engine's FF/0DDA write watch (cs_grid7 log), per map load. The first
// diverging write pinpoints the record whose op shape still differs.
// COMPOSER_LOG = raw cs_grid7 log; COMPOSER_MAP = hex submap id.
func TestProbeWriteSeq(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no rom")
	}
	r := ROM(rom)
	logPath := os.Getenv("COMPOSER_LOG")
	idStr := os.Getenv("COMPOSER_MAP")
	if logPath == "" || idStr == "" {
		t.Skip("COMPOSER_LOG/COMPOSER_MAP not set")
	}
	var id int
	fmt.Sscanf(idStr, "%x", &id)

	type wr struct {
		frame int
		tile  int
		val   byte
	}
	var writes []wr
	f, _ := os.Open(logPath)
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1<<20), 1<<20)
	baseOff := map[int]int{0x249: 0x1000, 0x24A: 0x0800, 0x250: 0x1800}[id]
	for sc.Scan() {
		line := sc.Text()
		if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "GW ") || !strings.Contains(line, "pc=FF/0DD") {
			continue
		}
		fe := strings.Fields(line)
		fr, _ := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(fe[1], "frame="))
		off, _ := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimPrefix(fe[2], "off="), 16, 32)
		v, _ := strconv.ParseUint(strings.TrimPrefix(fe[3], "val="), 16, 8)
		if idStr == "24a" && fr >= 25000 || idStr == "250" && fr < 25000 {
			continue
		}
		writes = append(writes, wr{fr, int(off) - 0x7E0000 - baseOff, byte(v)})
	}

	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	set, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	layerEnd = map[int]int{}
	AttrRecLog = func(layer, rec, x, y int, flag int) {
		fmt.Printf("REC L%d r%d q=%06X end=%06X (%d,%d) f=%02X arg=%02X\n", layer, rec, flag>>16, layerEnd[layer], x, y, flag&0xFF, (flag>>8)&0xFF)
	}
	defer func() { AttrRecLog = nil }()
	// patch rEnd lookup after decoding is impossible; use the header
	// offsets directly

	var recs []int
	AttrWriteRec = func(layer, rec int) { recs = append(recs, rec) }
	defer func() { AttrWriteRec = nil }()
	var model []wr

	AttrWriteRec = func(layer, rec int) {
		if len(recs) < 3 || (layer == 2 && len(recs) >= 3400 && len(recs) < 3620) {
			fmt.Printf("RECL L%d w%d rec%d\n", layer, len(recs), rec)
		}
		recs = append(recs, rec)
	}
	AttrWriteLog = func(layer, tile int, prop byte) {
		model = append(model, wr{layer, tile, prop})
	}
	defer func() { AttrWriteLog = nil }()
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		ds, _ := r.u16le(lp + 3)
		layerEnd[len(layerEnd)] = lp + int(ds)
		l, err := DecodeLayer(r, lp, set)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		n := 0
		for _, p := range l.Props {
			if p != 0xFF {
				n++
			}
		}
		fmt.Printf("layer %06X prop stamps: %d (records %d)\n", lp, n, len(layerEnd))
	}
	fmt.Printf("engine writes %d, model writes %d, recs %d\n", len(writes), len(model), len(recs))
	if os.Getenv("RAW_DUMP") != "" {
		for i := 0; i < 45 && i < len(model); i++ {
			fmt.Printf("RAW %d (%d,%d) L%d r%d\n", i, model[i].tile%96, model[i].tile/96, model[i].frame, recs[i])
		}
	}
	if os.Getenv("REC_TRACE") != "" {
		want, _ := strconv.Atoi(os.Getenv("REC_TRACE"))
		for i := range model {
			if recs[i] == want && model[i].frame == 2 {
				x := model[i].tile % 96
				fmt.Printf("rec%d: (%d,%d) %02X\n", want, x, model[i].tile/96, model[i].val)
			}
		}
	}
	n := len(writes)
	if len(model) < n {
		n = len(model)
	}
	bad := -1
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if writes[i].tile != model[i].tile || writes[i].val != model[i].val {
			bad = i
			break
		}
	}
	if bad < 0 && len(writes) != len(model) {
		bad = n
	}
	if bad < 0 {
		fmt.Println("sequences IDENTICAL")
		return
	}
	lo := bad - 12
	if lo < 0 {
		lo = 0
	}
	fmt.Printf("first mismatch at write %d\n", bad)
	fmt.Println("       engine                      model")
	for i := lo; i < bad+16 && i < len(writes) || i < bad+16 && i < len(model); i++ {
		e, m := "--", "--"
		if i < len(writes) {
			e = fmt.Sprintf("(%3d,%3d) %02X f%d", writes[i].tile%96, writes[i].tile/96, writes[i].val, writes[i].frame)
		}
		if i < len(model) {
			m = fmt.Sprintf("(%3d,%3d) %02X L%d r%d", model[i].tile%96, model[i].tile/96, model[i].val, model[i].frame, recs[i])
		}
		mark := " "
		if i == bad {
			mark = ">>"
		}
		if os.Getenv("DUMP_MODEL") != "" && i >= bad-60 && i < bad+8 && i < len(model) {
			fmt.Printf("M %4d (%3d,%3d) %02X L%d r%d\n", i, model[i].tile%96, model[i].tile/96, model[i].val, model[i].frame, recs[i])
		}
		fmt.Printf("%s %4d  %-18s  %-18s\n", mark, i, e, m)
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_sweepseq_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"testing"
)

// Probe: model composer write sequence vs engine FF/0DDE writes (0257).
func TestProbeSweepSeq(t *testing.T) {
	r, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip(err)
	}
	logp := os.Getenv("SEQ_LOG")
	id64, _ := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("SEQ_MAP"), 16, 32)
	if logp == "" {
		t.Skip("SEQ_LOG unset")
	}
	f, err := os.Open(logp)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	base64v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("SEQ_BASE"), 16, 32)
	base := int(base64v)
	re := regexp.MustCompile(`off=(\w+) val=(\w+) pc=FF/0DDE`)
	type wv struct{ tile, v int }
	var eng []wv
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	for sc.Scan() {
		if m := re.FindStringSubmatch(sc.Text()); m != nil {
			o, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[1], 16, 32)
			v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[2], 16, 32)
			eng = append(eng, wv{int(o+0x10000-0x7F0000) - base, int(v)})
		}
	}
	id := int(id64)
	off, _ := SubmapDataOffset(ROM(r), id)
	h, _ := ReadHeader(ROM(r), off)
	objs, _ := LoadObjectSet(ROM(r), h.ObjectConfig)
	w := 0
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
		if lp >= 0 {
			l, _ := DecodeLayer(ROM(r), lp, objs)
			w = max(w, l.W)
		}
	}
	var mod []wv
	var recs []int
	cur := 0
	AttrWriteRec = func(layer, rec int) { cur = layer*10000 + rec }
	var widths []int
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
		if lp >= 0 {
			l, _ := DecodeLayer(ROM(r), lp, objs)
			widths = append(widths, l.W)
		}
	}
	seqW := map[int]int{}
	AttrWriteLog = func(layer, tile int, prop byte) {
		lw, ok := seqW[layer]
		if !ok {
			lw = widths[len(seqW)]
			seqW[layer] = lw
		}
		tile = tile/lw*w + tile%lw
		if prop != 0xFF {
			mod = append(mod, wv{tile, int(prop)})
			recs = append(recs, cur)
		}
	}
	AttrRecLog = func(layer, rec, x, y int, flag int) {
		if rec < 4 {
			fmt.Printf("  recLog layer=%d rec=%d x=%d y=%d flag=%02X\n", layer, rec, x, y, flag)
		}
	}
	defer func() { AttrWriteLog = nil; AttrWriteRec = nil; AttrRecLog = nil }()
	for li, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("layer%d start at model write %d\n", 2-li, len(mod))
		if _, err := DecodeLayer(ROM(r), lp, objs); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	byRec := map[int]int{}
	for _, rc := range recs {
		byRec[rc]++
	}
	for rc, c := range byRec {
		if c > 64 {
			fmt.Printf("  rec %d: %d writes\n", rc, c)
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("map %04X w=%d engine %d writes, model %d\n", id, w, len(eng), len(mod))
	n := len(eng)
	if len(mod) < n {
		n = len(mod)
	}
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if eng[i] != mod[i] {
			fmt.Printf("first divergence at %d: engine tile %d (%d,%d) v=%02X, model tile %d (%d,%d) v=%02X rec=%d\n", i,
				eng[i].tile, eng[i].tile%w, eng[i].tile/w, eng[i].v, mod[i].tile, mod[i].tile%w, mod[i].tile/w, mod[i].v, recs[i])
			for j := i - 3; j < i+8 && j < n; j++ {
				if j >= 0 {
					fmt.Printf("  %d eng (%d,%d)=%02X  mod (%d,%d)=%02X rec=%d\n", j, eng[j].tile%w, eng[j].tile/w, eng[j].v, mod[j].tile%w, mod[j].tile/w, mod[j].v, recs[j])
				}
			}
			return
		}
	}
	fmt.Println("sequences agree over the common prefix")
	for j := n; j < len(eng) && j < n+12; j++ {
		fmt.Printf("  engine extra %d (%d,%d)=%02X\n", j, eng[j].tile%w, eng[j].tile/w, eng[j].v)
	}
	for j := n - 4; j < n; j++ {
		fmt.Printf("  common %d (%d,%d)=%02X rec=%d\n", j, mod[j].tile%w, mod[j].tile/w, mod[j].v, recs[j])
	}
}

// Probe: model overlay writes vs engine FF/1540 writes (SEQ_LOG, SEQ_MAP,
// SEQ_BASE as above).
func TestProbeOverlaySeq(t *testing.T) {
	r, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("SEQ_LOG") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	base64v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("SEQ_BASE"), 16, 32)
	id64, _ := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("SEQ_MAP"), 16, 32)
	f, err := os.Open(os.Getenv("SEQ_LOG"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	re := regexp.MustCompile(`off=(\w+) val=(\w+) pc=FF/1540`)
	type wv struct{ tile, v int }
	var eng, mod []wv
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	for sc.Scan() {
		if m := re.FindStringSubmatch(sc.Text()); m != nil {
			o, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[1], 16, 32)
			v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[2], 16, 32)
			eng = append(eng, wv{int(o+0x10000-0x7F0000) - int(base64v), int(v)})
		}
	}
	off, _ := SubmapDataOffset(ROM(r), int(id64))
	h, _ := ReadHeader(ROM(r), off)
	_, fill, bs, err := ParsePropRegion(ROM(r), h.Prop)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, w, ht, _ := AttrGrid(ROM(r), int(id64))
	applyAttrOverlay(r[bs:], w*ht, func(pos int, v byte) { mod = append(mod, wv{pos, int(v)}) })
	fmt.Printf("fill %02X blob % x\n", fill, r[bs:bs+24])
	fmt.Printf("engine %d overlay writes, model %d\n", len(eng), len(mod))
	for i := 0; i < len(eng) && i < len(mod); i++ {
		if eng[i] != mod[i] {
			fmt.Printf("first divergence at %d: engine (%d,%d)=%02X model (%d,%d)=%02X\n", i, eng[i].tile%w, eng[i].tile/w, eng[i].v, mod[i].tile%w, mod[i].tile/w, mod[i].v)
			return
		}
	}
	if len(eng) > len(mod) {
		e := eng[len(mod)]
		fmt.Printf("engine continues at %d: (%d,%d)=%02X\n", len(mod), e.tile%w, e.tile/w, e.v)
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_tiles_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"bufio"
	"encoding/base64"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// Probe: model layer tile words vs the engine's layer buffers in a sweep
// dump (TILES_LOG, TILES_DUMP = dump name suffix like _i0D, TILES_MAP).
func TestProbeTiles(t *testing.T) {
	r, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("TILES_LOG") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	f, err := os.Open(os.Getenv("TILES_LOG"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1<<20), 4<<20)
	var data []byte
	in := false
	for sc.Scan() {
		l := sc.Text()
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(l, "DUMPBEGIN ") && strings.HasSuffix(l, os.Getenv("TILES_DUMP")):
			in, data = true, nil
		case in && strings.HasPrefix(l, "DUMPDATA "):
			b, _ := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(l[9:])
			data = append(data, b...)
		case in && strings.HasPrefix(l, "DUMPEND"):
			in = false
		}
	}
	var id int
	fmt.Sscanf(os.Getenv("TILES_MAP"), "%x", &id)
	off, _ := SubmapDataOffset(ROM(r), id)
	h, _ := ReadHeader(ROM(r), off)
	objs, _ := LoadObjectSet(ROM(r), h.ObjectConfig)
	for li, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		l, _ := DecodeLayer(ROM(r), lp, objs)
		bestBase, best := -1, 1<<30
		for base := 0; base+l.W*l.H*2 <= len(data); base += 0x200 {
			miss := 0
			for i, tl := range l.Tiles {
				if uint16(data[base+2*i])|uint16(data[base+2*i+1])<<8 != uint16(tl.Word) {
					miss++
					if miss >= best {
						break
					}
				}
			}
			if miss < best {
				best, bestBase = miss, base
			}
		}
		fmt.Printf("layer%d %dx%d best base %04X: %d/%d words differ\n", 2-li, l.W, l.H, bestBase, best, l.W*l.H)
		xor := map[uint16]int{}
		for i, tl := range l.Tiles {
			e := uint16(data[bestBase+2*i]) | uint16(data[bestBase+2*i+1])<<8
			if e != uint16(tl.Word) {
				xor[e^uint16(tl.Word)]++
			}
		}
		if len(xor) < 8 {
			fmt.Printf("  xor histogram %v\n", xor)
		}
		if os.Getenv("TILES_GRID") != "" {
			for y := 0; y < l.H; y++ {
				row := make([]byte, l.W)
				for x := 0; x < l.W; x++ {
					i := y*l.W + x
					e := uint16(data[bestBase+2*i]) | uint16(data[bestBase+2*i+1])<<8
					row[x] = '.'
					if e != uint16(l.Tiles[i].Word) {
						row[x] = 'X'
					}
				}
				if strings.Contains(string(row), "X") {
					fmt.Printf("  %3d %s\n", y, row)
				}
			}
		}
		shown := 0
		for i, tl := range l.Tiles {
			e := uint16(data[bestBase+2*i]) | uint16(data[bestBase+2*i+1])<<8
			if e != uint16(tl.Word) && shown < 8 {
				fmt.Printf("  (%d,%d) engine %04X model %04X\n", i%l.W, i/l.W, e, uint16(tl.Word))
				shown++
			}
		}
	}
}

// Probe: tile-word mismatches for every dump in TILES_LOGS (comma list);
// a layer counts only when its best buffer base matches > 50%.
func TestProbeTilesAll(t *testing.T) {
	r, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("TILES_LOGS") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	total, layers := 0, 0
	for _, path := range strings.Split(os.Getenv("TILES_LOGS"), ",") {
		f, err := os.Open(path)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
		sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1<<20), 4<<20)
		var data []byte
		name := ""
		for sc.Scan() {
			l := sc.Text()
			switch {
			case strings.HasPrefix(l, "DUMPBEGIN "):
				name, data = l[10:], nil
			case strings.HasPrefix(l, "DUMPDATA "):
				b, _ := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(l[9:])
				data = append(data, b...)
			case strings.HasPrefix(l, "DUMPEND"):
				var idx int
				fmt.Sscanf(name[strings.LastIndex(name, "_i")+2:], "%x", &idx)
				p := 0x3CFB00 + idx*5
				id := (int(r[p+1]) | int(r[p+2])<<8) & 0x3FF
				off, err := SubmapDataOffset(ROM(r), id)
				if err != nil {
					continue
				}
				h, err := ReadHeader(ROM(r), off)
				if err != nil {
					continue
				}
				objs, err := LoadObjectSet(ROM(r), h.ObjectConfig)
				if err != nil {
					continue
				}
				for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1} {
					if lp < 0 {
						continue
					}
					l, err := DecodeLayer(ROM(r), lp, objs)
					if err != nil {
						continue
					}
					best := 1 << 30
					for base := 0; base+l.W*l.H*2 <= len(data); base += 0x200 {
						miss := 0
						for i, tl := range l.Tiles {
							if uint16(data[base+2*i])|uint16(data[base+2*i+1])<<8 != uint16(tl.Word) {
								miss++
								if miss >= best {
									break
								}
							}
						}
						best = min(best, miss)
					}
					if best*2 < l.W*l.H {
						layers++
						total += best
						if best > 0 && os.Getenv("TILES_VERBOSE") != "" {
							fmt.Printf("map %04X layer %06X: %d differ\n", id, lp, best)
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		f.Close()
	}
	fmt.Printf("TOTAL %d layers compared, %d words differ\n", layers, total)
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/probe_winorigin_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"testing"
)

// Probe for the 0x250 window-origin verification (tools/emulator/
// winorigin2.lua): prints the attr bytes and low-buffer bit-3 stamps
// along the party's walked corridor (leader px 96..104 = cells 12..13,
// py 464->304 = rows 58..38 under the (py>>3)*D0D1+(px>>3) fetch), so
// the model-vs-engine mismatch at the stop cell can be attributed to
// the attr layer or the event-point layer. Not a regression test; run
// with -run TestProbeWinOriginCorridor -v when re-verifying.
func TestProbeWinOriginCorridor(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE") == "" {
		t.Skip("probe only")
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	attr, w, h, err := AttrGrid(rom, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	low, lw, lh, err := LowGrid(rom, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "attr %dx%d low %dx%d\n", w, h, lw, lh)
	for y := 33; y < h && y <= 63; y++ {
		row := ""
		for _, x := range []int{11, 12, 13, 14} {
			lb := byte('.')
			if y < lh && x < lw && low[y][x]&0x08 != 0 {
				lb = 'E'
			}
			row += fmt.Sprintf(" %02X%c", attr[y][x], lb)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%2d %s\n", y, row)
	}
}

// Probe: where the low-buffer bit-3 (event point) stamps and the north
// margin sit on 0x250, so the walker knows whether the N-edge event
// 084E fires from an event tile row or from the bounds edge. Probe only.
func TestProbeWinOriginEvents(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE") == "" {
		t.Skip("probe only")
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	low, lw, lh, err := LowGrid(ROM(rom), 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for y := 0; y < lh && y <= 8; y++ {
		row := ""
		for x := 0; x < lw; x++ {
			if low[y][x]&0x08 != 0 {
				row += "E"
			} else {
				row += "."
			}
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%2d %s\n", y, row)
	}
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(ROM(rom), 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(ROM(rom), off)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if h.Prop < 0 {
		t.Fatal("no prop region")
	}
	entries, err := ParseProp(ROM(rom), h.Prop)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "entry flag=%02X x=%d y=%d w=%d h=%d\n", e.Flag, e.X, e.Y, e.W, e.H)
	}
}

// Probe: diff a walk3loane.lua bank-$7F dump (decoded to a raw 32 KiB
// .bin) against the model's AttrGrid/LowGrid for map id in SAGA3_PROBE_ID
// (hex, default 4B). Args via env: SAGA3_PROBE_BANK=<path to .bin>.
// Settles the Loane water-rects question (open item (f)): which bytes
// the engine really holds at the overlay's high-valued runs and the
// coast, chip-derived vs rect-derived.
func TestProbeLoaneCapture(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE") == "" || os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_BANK") == "" {
		t.Skip("probe only")
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	bank, err := os.ReadFile(os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_BANK"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	id := 0x4B
	if v, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_ID"), 16, 32); err == nil {
		id = int(v)
	}
	attr, w, h, err := AttrGrid(ROM(rom), id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	low, lw, lh, err := LowGrid(ROM(rom), id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "map %04X attr %dx%d low %dx%d\n", id, w, h, lw, lh)
	base := int(w) * int(h) // engine: attr grid sits above the low buffer
	diffs := 0
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			eng := bank[base+y*w+x]
			if eng != attr[y][x] {
				diffs++
				if diffs <= 20 {
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "attr diff (%d,%d): engine %02X model %02X\n", x, y, eng, attr[y][x])
				}
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "attr diffs: %d/%d\n", diffs, w*h)
	ldiffs := 0
	for y := 0; y < lh; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < lw; x++ {
			eng := bank[y*lw+x]
			if eng&0x08 != (low[y][x] & 0x08) {
				ldiffs++
				if ldiffs <= 20 {
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "low bit3 diff (%d,%d): engine %02X model %02X\n", x, y, eng, low[y][x])
				}
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "low bit3 diffs: %d/%d\n", ldiffs, lw*lh)
}

// Probe: attr byte histogram for a map (SAGA3_PROBE_ID, default 4B) —
// the water-rects question's baseline: which bytes the model predicts
// for Loane before the capture diff.
func TestProbeAttrHistogram(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE") == "" {
		t.Skip("probe only")
	}
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	id := 0x4B
	if v := os.Getenv("SAGA3_PROBE_ID"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%x", &id)
	}
	attr, w, h, err := AttrGrid(ROM(rom), id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	counts := map[byte]int{}
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			counts[attr[y][x]]++
		}
	}
	for a := 0; a <= 255; a++ {
		if counts[byte(a)] > 0 {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "attr %02X x%d\n", a, counts[byte(a)])
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/render.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/draw"
)

// Rendered is a composed submap image.
type Rendered struct {
	Image   *image.RGBA // the whole screen order, Under then Over
	Under   *image.RGBA // drawn below field sprites (OBJ priority 2)
	Over    *image.RGBA // drawn above them; transparent where empty
	BG3     *image.RGBA // layer 3 alone (BG3), nil without layer 3; Image has it on top
	Indexed *Indexed    // the same map in PPU form (words, chip indices, CGRAM)
	Width   int         // tiles
	Height  int         // tiles
}

// RenderSubmap decodes and renders submap id in the PPU's order. Mode 1
// with the BG3 priority bit ($2105 = 09 on 0250 and 007A) and field
// sprites at OBJ priority 2 put, bottom to top: BG2 and BG1 tiles
// without word bit 13, the sprites, BG2 and BG1 tiles with it, then BG3.
// Layers 1/2/3 are BG1/BG2/BG3 (007A's VRAM tilemaps hold layer 1 and 2
// words verbatim); layer 3 words reach BG3 with bit 13 set. Not modeled:
// BG3 is 2bpp (the renderer draws it from the 4bpp chipsets) and some
// maps put BG3 on the sub screen with color math (007A: $212D = 04,
// $2131 = 13, additive).
func RenderSubmap(r ROM, id int) (*Rendered, error) {
	return RenderSubmapVariants(r, id, nil, nil)
}

// VariantLayer is one applicable variant layer: Kind is the selector bit
// (0x40 -> layer 1's buffer $D2D9, 0x20 -> layer 2's $D2DB, 0x10 ->
// layer 3's $D2DD; C0:42C6-4403) and Ptr the record stream, decoded
// records-only onto that layer (FF:070B).
type VariantLayer struct {
	Kind int
	Ptr  int
}

// RenderSubmapVariants renders submap id with the given variant layers
// stamped onto their layers and the variant property regions' low-buffer
// rects (which feed the priority pass) applied.
func RenderSubmapVariants(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantProps []int) (*Rendered, error) {
	pm, err := prepare(r, id, variants, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, sets, pals, byKind, w, ht := pm.h, pm.sets, pm.cgram[:], pm.byKind, pm.w, pm.h2
	ix, err := indexedFrom(r, id, pm)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	bounds := image.Rect(0, 0, int(w)*tileSize, int(ht)*tileSize)
	under := image.NewRGBA(bounds)
	black := color.RGBA{0, 0, 0, 255}
	for y := 0; y < bounds.Dy(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < bounds.Dx(); x++ {
			under.SetRGBA(x, y, black)
		}
	}
	over := image.NewRGBA(bounds)
	bg2, bg1, bg3 := byKind[0x20], byKind[0x40], byKind[0x10]
	for _, l := range []*Layer{bg2, bg1} {
		if l == nil {
			continue
		}
		if err := drawLayer(under, l, sets, pals, 0, 0, false); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	for _, l := range []*Layer{bg2, bg1} {
		if l == nil {
			continue
		}
		if err := drawLayer(over, l, sets, pals, 0, 0, true); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	// Layer 3 reaches the BG3 tilemap with bit 13 forced on and chip
	// - 0x280 (007A's 0AD0 is VRAM 2850, 00FD's buffer 205A for 02DA), so
	// all of it draws on top, from its own 2bpp tiles and palette.
	var bg3Img *image.RGBA
	if bg3 != nil {
		g, err := loadBG3(r, h)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		bg3Img = image.NewRGBA(bounds)
		drawBG3(bg3Img, bg3, g.tiles, g.pal)
	}
	img := image.NewRGBA(bounds)
	draw.Draw(img, bounds, under, image.Point{}, draw.Src)
	draw.Draw(img, bounds, over, image.Point{}, draw.Over)
	if bg3Img != nil {
		draw.Draw(img, bounds, bg3Img, image.Point{}, draw.Over)
	}
	return &Rendered{Image: img, Under: under, Over: over, BG3: bg3Img, Indexed: ix, Width: int(w), Height: int(ht)}, nil
}

// prepared is what both renderers start from: the header, chip sets,
// the BG palettes in CGRAM order, and the loader's tile layers.
type prepared struct {
	h      Header
	sets   []ChipTiles
	cgram  [8]Palette // CGRAM palettes 0-7: what a word's palette field selects
	byKind map[int]*Layer
	w, h2  int // tiles
}

// textPaletteOffset is FD:E802: CGRAM 0-15 on a map without layer 3
// (only FF:1179, the layer-3 palette load, writes CGRAM 0 at map load;
// 004E showed these 15 colours after colour 0, which stays black).
const textPaletteOffset = 0x3DE802

func prepare(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantProps []int) (*prepared, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if h.Layer1 < 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x has no layer 1", id)
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x objects: %w", id, err)
	}
	cg, err := cgramPalettes(r, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x palettes: %w", id, err)
	}
	sets, err := LoadChipsets(r, h.Chipset)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x chipsets: %w", id, err)
	}
	layers, byKind, err := loadLayers(r, id, h, objs, variants, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	low, _, _, err := LowGridVariants(r, id, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	applyPriority(byKind, low, h.Flags1)
	// The map takes the layers' size, like the walk grid (AttrGrid):
	// the engine's buffers are sized from the layer size byte (FF:06BC),
	// not from the header.
	pm := &prepared{h: h, sets: sets, cgram: cg, byKind: byKind}
	for _, l := range layers {
		pm.w = max(pm.w, l.W)
		pm.h2 = max(pm.h2, l.H)
	}
	return pm, nil
}

// cgramPalettes returns CGRAM palettes 0-7 after the map load: 0 is the
// layer-3 palette (or the text palette without layer 3), 1-7 the map's
// palette set.
func cgramPalettes(r ROM, h Header) ([8]Palette, error) {
	var cg [8]Palette
	pals, err := LoadPalettes(r, h.PaletteSet, h.Flags1&3)
	if err != nil {
		return cg, err
	}
	if len(pals) > 7 {
		return cg, fmt.Errorf("%d palettes in set %#02x", len(pals), h.PaletteSet)
	}
	copy(cg[1:], pals)
	if h.Layer3 >= 0 {
		g, err := loadBG3(r, h)
		if err != nil {
			return cg, err
		}
		cg[0] = g.pal
		return cg, nil
	}
	for i := 1; i < 16; i++ {
		w := int(r[textPaletteOffset+2*i-2]) | int(r[textPaletteOffset+2*i-1])<<8
		cg[0].Colors[i] = RGB{byte((w & 31) << 3), byte((w >> 5 & 31) << 3), byte((w >> 10 & 31) << 3)}
	}
	return cg, nil
}

// loadLayers decodes the map's layers in draw order (layer 2 back,
// layer 1 front: tree canopies etc., layer 3 overlay on top; verified
// against emulator screenshots of map 0x250) and applies the variant
// layers; byKind maps the variant selector bit (0x20 layer 2, 0x40
// layer 1, 0x10 layer 3) to its layer.
func loadLayers(r ROM, id int, h Header, objs *ObjectSet, variants []VariantLayer, chests []ChestStamp) ([]*Layer, map[int]*Layer, error) {
	layers := make([]*Layer, 0, 3)
	byKind := map[int]*Layer{}
	for i, lp := range []int{h.Layer2, h.Layer1, h.Layer3} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		l, err := DecodeLayer(r, lp, objs)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x layer: %w", id, err)
		}
		layers = append(layers, l)
		byKind[[]int{0x20, 0x40, 0x10}[i]] = l
	}
	// chests stamp their object into their layer before the variants
	// (loader pass 4, FF:1CEE)
	for _, c := range chests {
		if l := byKind[map[int]int{1: 0x40, 2: 0x20, 3: 0x10}[c.Layer]]; l != nil {
			if o := obj(objs, c.Object); o != nil {
				l.stampObject(o, (c.X-1)&0xFF, (c.Y-2)&0xFF, 0, noOverride)
			}
		}
	}
	for _, v := range variants {
		l := byKind[v.Kind]
		if l == nil {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: variant kind %#02x has no layer", id, v.Kind)
		}
		if err := DecodeLayerOnto(r, v.Ptr, objs, l); err != nil {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x variant: %w", id, err)
		}
	}
	return layers, byKind, nil
}

// TileLayers returns the map's tile layers as the loader leaves them,
// keyed by variant selector bit (0x40 layer 1, 0x20 layer 2, 0x10 layer
// 3), with the priority pass applied.
func TileLayers(r ROM, id int, variants []VariantLayer, variantProps []int, chests []ChestStamp) (map[int]*Layer, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x objects: %w", id, err)
	}
	_, byKind, err := loadLayers(r, id, h, objs, variants, chests)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	low, _, _, err := LowGridVariants(r, id, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	applyPriority(byKind, low, h.Flags1)
	return byKind, nil
}

// applyPriority is FF:19B7: word bit 13 (BG priority) is toggled
// (EOR #$20 on the high byte, FF:19D5) on layer-1 tiles whose low-buffer
// byte has bit 7 and, with flag1 bit 6, on layer-2 tiles whose low byte
// has bit 6. A toggle, not a set: map 0250's (5,16) chip word already
// carries the bit (composer writes 6D at FF:0E36) and the pass writes 4D
// (FF:19D9, write watch on $7F:480B).
func applyPriority(byKind map[int]*Layer, low [][]byte, flags1 byte) {
	toggle := func(l *Layer, bit byte) {
		for y := 0; y < l.H && y < len(low); y++ {
			for x := 0; x < l.W && x < len(low[y]); x++ {
				if low[y][x]&bit != 0 {
					l.Tiles[y*l.W+x].Word ^= 0x2000
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if l := byKind[0x40]; l != nil {
		toggle(l, 0x80)
	}
	if l := byKind[0x20]; l != nil && flags1&0x40 != 0 {
		toggle(l, 0x40)
	}
}

// drawLayer paints l's non-transparent tile pixels onto img, offset by
// (ox, oy) tiles: only the tiles whose word bit 13 equals priority.
func drawLayer(img *image.RGBA, l *Layer, sets [][]byte, pals []Palette, ox, oy int, priority bool) error {
	for _, t := range l.Tiles {
		if (t.Word&0x2000 != 0) != priority {
			continue
		}
		if t.Word&^0x2000 == 0 {
			continue // chip 0 with palette field 0: transparent fill
		}
		set := t.Word.Chip() >> 7
		if set >= len(sets) {
			continue
		}
		tile := sets[set][t.Word.Chip()&0x7F*32:]
		pal := pals[t.Word.PalField()]
		for row := 0; row < tileSize; row++ {
			for col := 0; col < tileSize; col++ {
				sr, sc := row, col
				if t.Word&0x8000 != 0 {
					sr = 7 - row
				}
				if t.Word&0x4000 != 0 {
					sc = 7 - col
				}
				v, err := TilePixel(tile, sr, sc)
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				if v == 0 {
					continue
				}
				px := (int(t.TX)+ox)*tileSize + col
				py := (int(t.TY)+oy)*tileSize + row
				if px < 0 || py < 0 || px >= img.Bounds().Dx() || py >= img.Bounds().Dy() {
					continue
				}
				c := pal.Colors[v]
				img.SetRGBA(px, py, color.RGBA{c[0], c[1], c[2], 255})
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// RenderObject draws object objID of submap id's object set alone, the
// way the composer places it with its top-left grid cell at the origin
// (no flips, no palette override), on a transparent 16x16-tile canvas.
// Chests stamp this way (FF:1CEE), so the field can draw a chest's
// closed (ChestObject) and opened (ChestObject+1) states.
func RenderObject(r ROM, id, objID int) (*image.RGBA, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	objs, err := LoadObjectSet(r, h.ObjectConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	o := obj(objs, objID)
	if o == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x: object %#02x not in its set", id, objID)
	}
	cg, err := cgramPalettes(r, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pals := cg[:]
	sets, err := LoadChipsets(r, h.Chipset)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	l := &Layer{W: 16, H: 16, Tiles: make([]Tile, 256), Props: make([]byte, 256)}
	l.stampObject(o, 0, 0, 0, noOverride)
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 16*tileSize, 16*tileSize))
	for _, prio := range []bool{false, true} {
		if err := drawLayer(img, l, sets, pals, 0, 0, prio); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	return img, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/rom.go`:

```go
// Package mapfmt decodes Romancing SaGa 3 submap data from the extended
// HiROM SFC image used by the bokuno hack.
//
// Addressing: SNES banks C0-FF map to file offset (bank-0xC0)*0x10000 and
// banks 40-7D map to file offset bank*0x10000. All data regions documented
// in docs/map-format.md live in the C0-FF range, so a pointer value such as
// 0xF70180 converts to file offset 0x370180.
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// ROM is a patched ExHiROM SFC image.
type ROM []byte

// ToFile converts a SNES address to a file offset in r.
func (r ROM) ToFile(snes int) (int, error) {
	bank := (snes >> 16) & 0xFF
	switch {
	case bank >= 0xC0:
		return snes - 0xC00000, nil
	case bank >= 0x40 && bank <= 0x7D:
		return snes, nil
	default:
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("snes address %06X is not cartridge ROM space", snes)
	}
}

// U8, U16LE and U24SNES are exported aliases of the raw readers, for
// tools outside the package that walk record streams directly.
func (r ROM) U8(off int) (byte, error) { return r.u8(off) }

func (r ROM) U16LE(off int) (int, error) { return r.u16le(off) }

func (r ROM) U24SNES(off int) (int, error) { return r.u24snes(off) }

func (r ROM) u8(off int) (byte, error) {
	if off < 0 || off >= len(r) {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("read at %06X outside ROM of %06X bytes", off, len(r))
	}
	return r[off], nil
}

func (r ROM) u16le(off int) (int, error) {
	lo, err := r.u8(off)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	hi, err := r.u8(off + 1)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return int(lo) | int(hi)<<8, nil
}

// u24le reads a 3-byte little-endian pointer as used by the layer and
// object tables.
func (r ROM) u24le(off int) (int, error) {
	lo, err := r.u16le(off)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	hi, err := r.u8(off + 2)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return lo | int(hi)<<16, nil
}

// u24snes reads a 3-byte little-endian SNES pointer and converts it to a
// file offset. 0xFFFFFF means "absent".
func (r ROM) u24snes(off int) (int, error) {
	v, err := r.u24le(off)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	if v == 0xFFFFFF {
		return -1, nil
	}
	f, err := r.ToFile(v)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("pointer at %06X: %w", off, err)
	}
	return f, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/submap.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// Fixed data region addresses, verified against patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and
// the community tool documentation (docs/map-format.md).
const (
	hackSubmapTableAddr = 0x5A6A50 // 3-byte SNES record pointers (5A:7650)
	submapCount         = 1024
	objectTableAddr     = 0x370000 // 3-byte SNES pointers, one per object config
	objectTableEnd      = 0x370180 // 128 entries, then the streams themselves
	chipsetListAddr     = 0x39A800 // 5 bytes per chipset set
	chipsetPtrAddr      = 0x39AD00 // 3-byte SNES pointers, per chipset graphic ID
	paletteSetAddr      = 0x3CF400 // 7 bytes per palette set
	paletteDataAddr     = 0x2CA400 // 32 bytes per palette (16 BGR555 words)
	chipsPerSet         = 128
	chipsetsPerMap      = 5
	palettesPerSet      = 7
	tileSize            = 8
	layerNoneSentinel   = -1
)

// Header is block 1 of a submap record, the display-related fields needed
// to render the map.
type Header struct {
	Flags1       byte // bit0-1 palette bank, bit6 layer 2 present, bit5 layer 3 present
	Layer1       int  // file offsets, layerNoneSentinel when absent
	Layer2       int
	Layer3       int
	Prop         int
	Chipset      byte // chipset set number (5 graphic IDs from chipsetListAddr)
	PaletteSet   byte // palette set number
	ObjectConfig byte // object configuration stream number
	PosX, PosY   byte
	SizeX, SizeY byte // tile dimensions minus one (sizeX byte 0x3F = 64 tiles)
	NameID       byte
	// Controls is the 禁止操作 byte after the name id ($D2F3, C0:3D4A):
	// bit 7 open map ($D0DD), bit 4 widens the horizontal bounds by 2
	// tiles each side (C0:3D59), bit 3 puts footprints on layer 2
	// ($D8D9, C0:3D66).
	Controls byte
	// BG3Gfx and BG3Pal are the two bytes after the palette set on maps
	// with layer 3 ($D2E1 -> FF:1065, $D2E2 -> FF:1179): layer 3's 2bpp
	// tiles and its 16 colours.
	BG3Gfx, BG3Pal byte
}

// SubmapDataOffset returns the file offset of submap id's data record.
// HasSubmap reports whether the submap table entry has a valid record.
func HasSubmap(r ROM, id int) bool {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	_, err = ReadHeader(r, off) // pointer target must decode
	return err == nil
}

// The hack replaced the record lookup: the loader passes the map id to
// 5A:7650, which reads a 24-bit pointer from 5A:6A50 + id*3 into [$B7]
// (C0:3C6F). 471 of the 1024 entries differ from the vanilla 2-byte
// table at 0x380500 (relocated records in banks 44-50, e.g. 00C3 at
// $44:6370 as the live [$B7] showed); decoding the vanilla table read
// stale records for those maps.
func SubmapDataOffset(r ROM, id int) (int, error) {
	if id < 0 || id >= submapCount {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("submap id %d out of range 0..%d", id, submapCount-1)
	}
	off, err := r.u24snes(hackSubmapTableAddr + id*3)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("submap table entry %d: %w", id, err)
	}
	return off, nil
}

// ReadHeader decodes the display block at file offset off.
func ReadHeader(r ROM, off int) (Header, error) {
	var h Header
	flag1, err := r.u8(off)
	if err != nil {
		return h, fmt.Errorf("submap header at %06X: %w", off, err)
	}
	h.Flags1 = flag1
	// Header walk as byte-verified in internal/triggers (docs/triggers.md):
	// layer 2 is present only when flag1 bit6 is set, and flag1 bit5 adds
	// two undocumented bytes after the palette-set byte. Reading layer 2
	// unconditionally desynced bit5-set maps (e.g. 0x249, object config
	// read as 225 instead of 0x26).
	p := off + 1
	if h.Layer1, err = r.u24snes(p); err != nil {
		return h, err
	}
	p += 3
	if flag1&0x40 != 0 {
		if h.Layer2, err = r.u24snes(p); err != nil {
			return h, err
		}
		p += 3
	} else {
		h.Layer2 = layerNoneSentinel
	}
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		if h.Layer3, err = r.u24snes(p); err != nil {
			return h, err
		}
		p += 3
	} else {
		h.Layer3 = layerNoneSentinel
	}
	if h.Prop, err = r.u24snes(p); err != nil {
		return h, err
	}
	p += 3
	fields := make([]byte, 10)
	for i := range fields {
		if fields[i], err = r.u8(p + i); err != nil {
			return h, err
		}
	}
	if flag1&0x20 == 0 {
		// no extra bytes: pull the trailing fields up
		copy(fields[4:], fields[2:8])
	}
	// fields[0..1] = chipset set, palette set; fields[2..3] = undocumented
	// extra bytes when flag1 bit5 is set; then object config, position,
	// size, name id.
	h.Chipset = fields[0]
	h.PaletteSet = fields[1]
	h.ObjectConfig = fields[4]
	h.PosX, h.PosY = fields[5], fields[6]
	h.SizeX, h.SizeY = fields[7], fields[8]
	h.NameID = fields[9]
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		h.BG3Gfx, h.BG3Pal = fields[2], fields[3]
	}
	ctl := p + 8
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		ctl = p + 10
	}
	if h.Controls, err = r.u8(ctl); err != nil {
		return h, err
	}
	return h, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/walkable.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import "fmt"

// The property layer (header Prop pointer) is a counted entry list
// followed by the walk-attr overlay stream. Layout, verified against the
// ROM, the community docs (docs/map-format.md) and the engine
// (FF:144A-14D6, write-watch tools/emulator/cs_grid5.lua):
//
//	[data size:2 LE][entries...] — entries consume exactly size bytes
//	[default walk byte] — replicated over the whole attr grid at load
//	[overlay RLE] — see chipattr.go applyAttrOverlay; starts AT the
//	default byte, whose value doubles as the stream's transparent marker
//
// Each entry is [flag][X][Y][size]: the flag's bit 0 selects the size
// encoding (even = two bytes W,H; odd = one byte, high nibble W, low
// nibble H). The engine counts entry bytes down from the size word
// (FF:1468-14AF DEC $90 per byte) and parses mechanically — it never
// validates flags and there is no terminator list, so neither does this
// decoder. (Maps such as 0x04 continue with further counted entry
// chunks after the overlay stream; they carry their own size words and
// the engine's chunk iterator consumes them separately — they never
// re-fill or re-overlay the attr grid, see docs/map-format.md.)
//
// Flag meanings: 08/09 event point, 20/21 layer mask, 40/41 layer-2
// front/back toggle and 80/81 layer-1 front/back toggle are verified
// (2-658's notes and every map parsed here). The remaining flags are
// tile walkability attributes from the map editor's property palette
// (進入許可00/01/02, 水中00/01, 進入禁止×3, ...).

// PropEntry is one property-layer rectangle: the attribute Flag written
// over the W x H tile region at (X, Y).
type PropEntry struct {
	Flag       byte
	X, Y, W, H int
}

// WalkGrid is a per-tile walkability grid; Walk[y][x] is true when a
// walking character may enter that tile.
type WalkGrid struct {
	W, H int
	Walk [][]bool
	// Attr and Low are the grids Walk is derived from: the attr byte per
	// tile and the low buffer ($7F:0000). The object gate C0:57FF reads
	// both with per-object rules Walk flattens away.
	Attr, Low [][]byte
}

// At returns the walkability of tile (x, y); out-of-range tiles are not
// walkable.
func (g *WalkGrid) At(x, y int) bool {
	if y < 0 || y >= g.H || x < 0 || x >= g.W {
		return false
	}
	return g.Walk[y][x]
}

// The former flagWalk layer (property rect entries applied directly as
// walkability) is REMOVED, engine-disproved 2026-11-17: the attr grid's
// only load-time writers are the fill, the composer and the overlay RLE
// (cs_grid5/6/7 write-watches), and the rect entries instead EOR-stamp
// flag&0xFE into the separate low buffer (LowGrid), where only bit 3 —
// the event points' stamps — reaches the party's step gate. The old
// flag-04 sea rectangles stamp 0x04, which blocks nobody; map 0x04's sea
// block therefore still rides whatever the 0x04 composer writes (open
// item, docs/map-format.md).

// readPropEntries reads property entries starting at q, mechanically
// (the engine validates nothing: FF:1468-14AF walks flag, X word and the
// size field by bit 0 alone), until the counted end offset. It returns
// the entries and the offset just past the counted region.
func readPropEntries(r ROM, q, end int) ([]PropEntry, int, error) {
	var entries []PropEntry
	for q < end {
		if q+4 > len(r) {
			return entries, q, nil
		}
		flag, err := r.u8(q)
		if err != nil {
			return entries, q, err
		}
		x, err := r.u8(q + 1)
		if err != nil {
			return entries, q, err
		}
		y, err := r.u8(q + 2)
		if err != nil {
			return entries, q, err
		}
		w, h, adv := 0, 0, 4
		if flag&1 == 0 {
			wb, err := r.u8(q + 3)
			if err != nil {
				return entries, q, err
			}
			hb, err := r.u8(q + 4)
			if err != nil {
				return entries, q, err
			}
			w, h, adv = int(wb), int(hb), 5
		} else {
			sb, err := r.u8(q + 3)
			if err != nil {
				return entries, q, err
			}
			w, h = int(sb)>>4, int(sb)&0xF
		}
		if q+adv > end {
			return entries, q, nil
		}
		entries = append(entries, PropEntry{Flag: flag, X: int(x), Y: int(y), W: w, H: h})
		q += adv
	}
	return entries, q, nil
}

// ParseProp decodes the property region at file offset off: the counted
// entry list plus (through ParsePropRegion) the walk-attr overlay.
func ParseProp(r ROM, off int) ([]PropEntry, error) {
	entries, _, _, err := ParsePropRegion(r, off)
	return entries, err
}

// ParsePropRegion decodes the property region and additionally returns
// the region's DEFAULT WALK BYTE and the offset of that byte — the walk
// attr overlay stream's start (the default byte doubles as the stream's
// transparent marker; see chipattr.go applyAttrOverlay).
//
// Engine flow (FF:144A-14D6, write-watch tools/emulator/cs_grid5.lua,
// 2026-11-17): the engine parses entries while the size word's byte
// count lasts, then reads ONE byte — the default walk byte — and
// replicates it over the whole walk-attribute grid ($7F:$1C+tile,
// FF:14B3-14C3 JSR $15A6, MVN fill; map 0x250's byte is 0x01). The
// object composer then STA's per-chip property bytes over it, so this
// byte is the fill-chip/default walk attribute the tile compositions
// leave untouched.
func ParsePropRegion(r ROM, off int) ([]PropEntry, byte, int, error) {
	size, err := r.u16le(off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("prop at %06X: %w", off, err)
	}
	if size > 0x2000 {
		return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("prop at %06X: implausible data size %d", off, size)
	}
	end := off + 2 + size
	if end > len(r) {
		return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("prop at %06X: data size %d overruns ROM", off, size)
	}
	entries, q, err := readPropEntries(r, off+2, end)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("prop at %06X: %w", off, err)
	}
	var fill byte
	if q < len(r) {
		fill = r[q] // the default walk byte = the overlay stream's v1 byte
	}
	return entries, fill, q, nil
}

// LowGrid decodes id's engine LOW-BUFFER byte grid ($7F:0000 + tile, the
// DP $19 buffer the move gate reads at C0:58CC `LDA [$19],Y`, stride =
// map width, base DP $1C = D0D5>>1 sits right above it). Engine evidence
// (write-watch tools/emulator/cs_grid7.lua, 2026-11-17, whole-$7F watch
// across the 0x249 -> 0x24A -> 0x250 loads):
//
//   - the load-time fill writes BOTH buffers: STA [$96] at $7F:0000 and
//     $7F:$1C (FF/15AE x2) followed by MVN runs (FF/15CF) — the low
//     buffer fills with 0x00 on all three maps (the attr grid fills with
//     the prop default byte above it).
//   - after the overlay pass, FF:1563's rect loop (STA at FF/158F) writes
//     the property entries into THIS buffer, one EOR per tile: value =
//     flag & 0xFE (bit 0 is the size encoding, dropped), rect =
//     (x, y, W+1, H+1). Byte-exact on all three maps: 0/4096, 0/2048 and
//     0/6144 tiles differ from the settled dumps (gridprint capture).
//     Value samples: event points (flags 08/09) stamp 0x08 — the gate's
//     bit-3 block, i.e. event tiles stop the step (bump-triggered); mask
//     rects (20/21) stamp 0x20 (zone 2), layer-2 toggles (40/41) 0x40,
//     layer-1 toggles (80/81) 0x80, EOR-accumulating (0x40 over 0x80 ->
//     0xC0, duplicate rect -> 0x00).
//
// Only bit 3 affects the on-foot party: the gate tests bit 3 and (when
// $D991 is set — not measured on foot) the bits-4-5 zone against $D990;
// bits 0-2 and 6-7 feed NPC gates and terrain effects elsewhere.
//
// The rect coordinates are MAP TILES, same as the whole walk grid
// (winorigin2.lua 2026-11-17: tile resolution, full map, no window):
// the stamps decode at face-value tile coordinates, matching the
// engine's writes byte-for-byte (cs_grid7 snapshots).
func LowGrid(r ROM, id int) ([][]byte, int, int, error) {
	return LowGridVariants(r, id, nil)
}

// LowGridVariants is LowGrid plus the rect entries of the applicable
// variant property regions (kind 0x80): the loader parses each region
// with the same FF:144A pass, whose rect loop FF:1563 EORs into this
// buffer (0174: 48 FF/158F writes during the variant pass, base region
// empty).
func LowGridVariants(r ROM, id int, variantProps []int) ([][]byte, int, int, error) {
	off, err := SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, err
	}
	h, err := ReadHeader(r, off)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, 0, err
	}
	// Same size rule as AttrGrid: the layers' size byte, not the header.
	w, ht := 0, 0
	for _, lp := range []int{h.Layer1, h.Layer2} {
		if lp < 0 {
			continue
		}
		size, err := r.u8(lp)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, err
		}
		w = max(w, int(size>>4)*32)
		ht = max(ht, int(size&0xF)*32)
	}
	if w == 0 {
		w, ht = int(h.SizeX)+1, int(h.SizeY)+1
	}
	grid := make([][]byte, ht)
	for y := range grid {
		grid[y] = make([]byte, w) // the load-time fill byte, 0x00 on every map watched
	}
	regions := variantProps
	if h.Prop >= 0 {
		regions = append([]int{h.Prop}, variantProps...)
	}
	for _, prop := range regions {
		entries, err := ParseProp(r, prop)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("submap %#04x prop: %w", id, err)
		}
		for _, e := range entries {
			v := e.Flag & 0xFE
			for y := e.Y; y < e.Y+e.H+1; y++ {
				for x := e.X; x < e.X+e.W+1; x++ {
					if y < 0 || y >= ht || x < 0 || x >= w {
						continue
					}
					grid[y][x] ^= v
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return grid, w, ht, nil
}

// Walkable decodes submap id's walkability: the engine's chip walk
// attributes (chipattr.go: fill byte, object chip property bytes, overlay
// RLE — bit 3 = 進入禁止, zone-2 water conservatively blocked on foot,
// see AttrWalkable) ANDed with the low buffer's bit-3 blocks (event
// points, LowGrid). The property RECT entries are NOT a walkability layer
// of the attr grid: the write-watch proves the attr grid's only load-time
// writers are the fill, the composer and the overlay, and the rect stamps
// target the low buffer where only bit 3 (event points) blocks.
func Walkable(r ROM, id int) (*WalkGrid, error) {
	return WalkableVariants(r, id, nil, nil, nil)
}

// WalkableVariants is Walkable over AttrGridVariants: the map as the
// loader leaves it with the given chests and applicable variants.
func WalkableVariants(r ROM, id int, chests []ChestStamp, variantLayers, variantProps []int) (*WalkGrid, error) {
	attr, w, ht, err := AttrGridVariants(r, id, chests, variantLayers, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	g := &WalkGrid{W: w, H: ht, Walk: make([][]bool, ht), Attr: attr}
	for y := range g.Walk {
		g.Walk[y] = make([]bool, w)
		for x := range g.Walk[y] {
			g.Walk[y][x] = AttrWalkable(r, attr[y][x])
		}
	}
	low, lw, lht, err := LowGridVariants(r, id, variantProps)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	g.Low = low
	for y := 0; y < ht && y < lht; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w && x < lw; x++ {
			if low[y][x]&0x08 != 0 {
				g.Walk[y][x] = false
			}
		}
	}
	return g, nil
}
```

`internal/mapfmt/walkable_test.go`:

```go
package mapfmt

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// Prop region for the fixture map: the counted region holds one event
// point (flag 09, odd flag -> nibble size), a water rectangle (flag 04),
// a walkable-zone rectangle (flag 00) and a nibble-sized blocked
// rectangle (flag 03); then the default walk byte and a null overlay
// stream ([v1][v1][v3?][00 terminator]).
const fxPropData = 0x384000

var fxPropBytes = []byte{
	0x12, 0x00, // counted size: 18 bytes
	0x09, 0x03, 0x04, 0x10, // event point at (3,4), nibble size 1x0
	0x04, 0x02, 0x02, 0x03, 0x02, // water: (2,2) 3x2
	0x00, 0x05, 0x05, 0x02, 0x01, // walkable zone 00: (5,5) 2x1
	0x05, 0x08, 0x08, 0x21, // blocked water zone: (8,8) nibble size 2x1
	0x01,                   // default walk byte, doubles as the overlay's transparent v1
	0x01, 0x01, 0x01, 0x00, // null overlay: v1=v2=01, alt=01, 00 ends
}

func setPropFixture(f *fixture) {
	copy(f.ROM[fxPropData:], fxPropBytes)
	p := fxPropData + 0xC00000
	off := fxSubData + 1 + 3 // header prop pointer field (no layer 2: flag1 bit6 clear)
	f.ROM[off] = byte(p)
	f.ROM[off+1] = byte(p >> 8)
	f.ROM[off+2] = byte(p >> 16)
}

func TestWalkableRects(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	setPropFixture(f)
	g, err := Walkable(f.ROM, 2)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if g.W != 32 || g.H != 32 {
		t.Fatalf("grid = %dx%d, want 32x32", g.W, g.H)
	}
	// Rect entries never write the attr grid (write-watch evidence,
	// LowGrid comment): the walk flags only reach the step gate through
	// the low buffer's bit 3, i.e. the event points. The nibble-size
	// event rect (w=1, h=0) stamps (x, y)-(x+w, y+h) = (3,4)-(4,4).
	cases := []struct {
		x, y int
		want bool
		note string
	}{
		{0, 0, true, "unmarked tile"},
		{2, 2, true, "water rectangle corner stamps 0x04, no gate bit"},
		{4, 3, true, "water rectangle far corner"},
		{3, 4, false, "event point stamps bit 3 into the low buffer"},
		{4, 4, false, "event point rect spans x+w too (w+1 tiles)"},
		{3, 5, true, "one row below the event point"},
		{8, 8, true, "nibble blocked rect stamps 0x04, no gate bit"},
		{9, 9, true, "below the nibble rectangle"},
		{10, 10, true, "beyond the counted region"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := g.At(c.x, c.y); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("At(%d,%d) = %v, want %v (%s)", c.x, c.y, got, c.want, c.note)
		}
	}
	for _, c := range [][2]int{{-1, 0}, {0, -1}, {32, 0}, {0, 32}} {
		if g.At(c[0], c[1]) {
			t.Fatalf("out-of-range tile (%d,%d) must not be walkable", c[0], c[1])
		}
	}
}

// The fixture's low buffer: EOR stamps of flag&0xFE over (w+1)x(h+1).
func TestLowGridFixture(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	setPropFixture(f)
	low, w, h, err := LowGrid(f.ROM, 2)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if w != 32 || h != 32 {
		t.Fatalf("grid = %dx%d, want 32x32", w, h)
	}
	cases := []struct {
		x, y int
		want byte
		note string
	}{
		{0, 0, 0x00, "unmarked tile"},
		{3, 4, 0x0C, "event point 0x08 EOR water rect 0x04 (overlap)"},
		{4, 4, 0x0C, "second tile of the nibble event rect"},
		{5, 4, 0x04, "water rect spans w+1 = 4 columns"},
		{2, 2, 0x04, "water rect stamps flag 04"},
		{4, 3, 0x04, "far corner of the even-size water rect"},
		{2, 5, 0x00, "one row below the water rect"},
		{8, 9, 0x04, "nibble rect (8,8) 2x1 -> rows 8-9"},
		{9, 9, 0x04, "nibble rect col w+1"},
		{11, 9, 0x00, "outside the nibble rect"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := low[c.y][c.x]; got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("LowGrid(%d,%d) = %02X, want %02X (%s)", c.x, c.y, got, c.want, c.note)
		}
	}
}

func TestWalkableAbsentProp(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t) // header prop pointer stays FFFFFF
	g, err := Walkable(f.ROM, 2)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for y := 0; y < g.H; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < g.W; x++ {
			if !g.Walk[y][x] {
				t.Fatalf("tile (%d,%d) blocked, want all walkable without a prop region", x, y)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestParsePropTerminator(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	setPropFixture(f)
	entries, err := ParseProp(f.ROM, fxPropData)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The counted region's four entries; parsing is bounded by the size
	// word alone (the engine validates nothing).
	if len(entries) != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("entries = %d (%+v), want 4", len(entries), entries)
	}
	want := []PropEntry{
		{Flag: 0x09, X: 3, Y: 4, W: 1, H: 0},
		{Flag: 0x04, X: 2, Y: 2, W: 3, H: 2},
		{Flag: 0x00, X: 5, Y: 5, W: 2, H: 1},
		{Flag: 0x05, X: 8, Y: 8, W: 2, H: 1},
	}
	for i, e := range entries {
		if e != want[i] {
			t.Fatalf("entry %d = %+v, want %+v", i, e, want[i])
		}
	}
}

// Golden facts from the engine capture (tools/emulator/cs_grid7.lua,
// 2026-11-17; gridprint capture reconstructs and diffs the settled $7F
// dumps). The EOR-stamp grammar reproduced the engine's low buffer
// exactly on all three maps (0/4096, 0/2048, 0/6144 tiles differ); these
// are spot values from those settled dumps.
func TestLowGridCaptured(t *testing.T) {
	romPath := "../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"
	romBytes, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no rom")
	}
	r := ROM(romBytes)

	// 0x249: no entries at all -> the whole low buffer stays 0x00
	// (engine dump b7f_f23088_cfg26: 00=4096).
	low, w, h, err := LowGrid(r, 0x249)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if w != 64 || h != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("0x249 grid = %dx%d, want 64x64", w, h)
	}
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			if low[y][x] != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("0x249 low buffer (%d,%d) = %02X, want 00 (empty prop region)", x, y, low[y][x])
			}
		}
	}

	// 0x250: seven flag-81 rects stamp 0x80 over 25 tiles, all else 00
	// (engine dump b7f_f30235_cfg02: 00=6119 80=25).
	low, w, h, err = LowGrid(r, 0x250)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	nonzero := 0
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			if low[y][x] != 0 {
				nonzero++
			}
		}
	}
	if nonzero != 25 {
		t.Fatalf("0x250 low buffer nonzero tiles = %d, want 25", nonzero)
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		x, y int
		want byte
	}{{5, 16, 0x80}, {7, 16, 0x80}, {8, 16, 0x00}, {37, 38, 0x80}, {19, 14, 0x80}, {14, 22, 0x80}, {51, 16, 0x80}} {
		if got := low[c.y][c.x]; got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("0x250 low buffer (%d,%d) = %02X, want %02X", c.x, c.y, got, c.want)
		}
	}

	// 0x24A: EOR accumulation (engine dump b7f_f26202_cfg02: 00=1573
	// 20=450 C0=15 60=3 40=3 28=2 08=1 A0=1; three bit-3 tiles).
	low, w, h, err = LowGrid(r, 0x24A)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	hist := map[byte]int{}
	bit3 := 0
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			hist[low[y][x]]++
			if low[y][x]&0x08 != 0 {
				bit3++
			}
		}
	}
	if bit3 != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("0x24A bit-3 tiles = %d, want 3 (the event points)", bit3)
	}
	wantHist := map[byte]int{0x00: 1573, 0x20: 450, 0xC0: 15, 0x60: 3, 0x40: 3, 0x28: 2, 0x08: 1, 0xA0: 1}
	for v, n := range wantHist {
		if hist[v] != n {
			t.Fatalf("0x24A low buffer value %02X count = %d, want %d", v, hist[v], n)
		}
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		x, y int
		want byte
		note string
	}{{26, 47, 0x08, "event point"}, {0, 6, 0x20, "mask rect corner"}, {31, 20, 0x20, "mask rect w+1 corner"},
		{26, 24, 0xC0, "0x80 EOR 0x40 overlap"}, {13, 14, 0xA0, "0x80 EOR 0x20 overlap"}, {26, 20, 0x60, "0x40 EOR 0x20 overlap"},
		{27, 27, 0x00, "duplicate 0x80 rect cancels"}, {8, 14, 0x28, "event over mask"}} {
		if got := low[c.y][c.x]; got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("0x24A low buffer (%d,%d) = %02X, want %02X (%s)", c.x, c.y, got, c.want, c.note)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/sprites/rom.go`:

```go
package sprites

import "fmt"

// ROM is a patched ExHiROM SFC image.
type ROM []byte

// ToFile converts a SNES address to a file offset in r: banks C0-FF map
// to (bank-0xC0)*0x10000, banks 40-7D map to bank*0x10000.
func (r ROM) ToFile(snes int) (int, error) {
	bank := (snes >> 16) & 0xFF
	switch {
	case bank >= 0xC0:
		return snes - 0xC00000, nil
	case bank >= 0x40 && bank <= 0x7D:
		return snes, nil
	default:
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("snes address %06X is not cartridge ROM space", snes)
	}
}

func (r ROM) u8(off int) (byte, error) {
	if off < 0 || off >= len(r) {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("read at %06X outside ROM of %06X bytes", off, len(r))
	}
	return r[off], nil
}

func (r ROM) u16le(off int) (int, error) {
	lo, err := r.u8(off)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	hi, err := r.u8(off + 1)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return int(lo) | int(hi)<<8, nil
}

func (r ROM) u24le(off int) (int, error) {
	lo, err := r.u16le(off)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	hi, err := r.u8(off + 2)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return lo | int(hi)<<16, nil
}

// tile reads one 32-byte SNES 4bpp tile at off and expands it to 64
// palette indices, row-major, leftmost pixel first. Rows interleave the
// two low bitplanes first, then the two high ones: bytes 0..15 hold
// (plane0, plane1) per row and bytes 16..31 hold (plane2, plane3).
func (r ROM) tile(off int) ([64]byte, error) {
	var tile [64]byte
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		b0, err := r.u8(off + y*2)
		if err != nil {
			return tile, err
		}
		b1, err := r.u8(off + y*2 + 1)
		if err != nil {
			return tile, err
		}
		b2, err := r.u8(off + 16 + y*2)
		if err != nil {
			return tile, err
		}
		b3, err := r.u8(off + 16 + y*2 + 1)
		if err != nil {
			return tile, err
		}
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			bit := 7 - x
			tile[y*8+x] = (b0>>bit)&1 | (b1>>bit&1)<<1 | (b2>>bit&1)<<2 | (b3>>bit&1)<<3
		}
	}
	return tile, nil
}
```
