`internal/sprites/sprites.go`:

```go
// Package sprites decodes the submap walking-character graphics
// ("マップキャラグラフィック") of the Romancing SaGa 3 ExHiROM image used
// by the bokuno hack.
//
// Character graphic ID -> graphics offset comes from the 4-byte table at
// file offset 0x5A8370 ({kind, 3-byte SNES address}), and the matching
// 16-color BGR555 palette from the pool that directly precedes it, one
// 32-byte palette per table entry. Graphics are raw SNES 4bpp tiles.
//
// Frame layout (docs/sprites.md): the blob is a 24-px-wide vertical
// filmstrip. Tiles 0..62 form seven 24x24 blocks of three 24x8 bands
// (three tiles each, stride nine tiles); tiles 63..67 hold the trailing
// 16x16 object graphic (金塊グラフィック). The game composites the
// visible sprite from these blocks with per-band X offsets stored
// outside the blob (not yet located), so blocks as decoded here show
// the figure in diagonal slices; bands of one figure line up at the
// documented offsets only in-game. See docs/sprites.md.
package sprites

import "fmt"

// Fixed data region addresses, verified against patches/bokuno_jp.sfc and
// the community tool configs (docs/sprites.md).
const (
	// GraphicTableAddr holds {kind, offset[3]} per character graphic ID.
	GraphicTableAddr = 0x5A8370
	// GraphicTableEntries is the table length the community BNE2 config
	// declares (1020 entries).
	GraphicTableEntries = 1020
	// PalettePoolAddr is the palette pool that ends where the graphic
	// table starts: one 32-byte BGR555 palette per table entry, palette
	// for graphic ID i at PalettePoolAddr + i*32.
	PalettePoolAddr = GraphicTableAddr - GraphicTableEntries*32

	// Frame layout of a townsfolk blob: 68 tiles = seven 24x24 blocks
	// (stride 9) + one 16x16 object graphic.
	frameW     = 24 // pixels per block band
	frameH     = 24 // pixels per block
	bandTiles  = 3  // tiles per 24x8 band
	bandsFrame = 3  // bands per 24x24 block
	tilesFrame = bandTiles * bandsFrame
	framesWalk = 7 // blocks in tiles 0..62
	tileSize   = 8
)

// Kind is the first byte of a graphic table entry.
type Kind byte

// Graphic kinds as named by the community config オフセット種類.idn.
const (
	KindParty     Kind = 0x00 // 仲間: party-member sprite set
	KindTownsfolk Kind = 0x01 // 一般住人: townsfolk walking sprite
	KindUnique    Kind = 0x1C // ユニークキャラ
	KindOneTile   Kind = 0x2D // 一枚絵(3x4)
)

// Entry is one character graphic table row.
type Entry struct {
	Kind   Kind
	Offset int // file offset of the graphic data, -1 when the entry is absent
}

// TableEntry returns graphic table entry id.
func TableEntry(r ROM, id int) (Entry, error) {
	if id < 0 || id >= GraphicTableEntries {
		return Entry{}, fmt.Errorf("graphic id %d out of range 0..%d", id, GraphicTableEntries-1)
	}
	kind, err := r.u8(GraphicTableAddr + id*4)
	if err != nil {
		return Entry{}, fmt.Errorf("graphic table entry %d: %w", id, err)
	}
	snes, err := r.u24le(GraphicTableAddr + id*4 + 1)
	if err != nil {
		return Entry{}, fmt.Errorf("graphic table entry %d: %w", id, err)
	}
	e := Entry{Kind: Kind(kind), Offset: -1}
	if snes != 0 {
		off, err := r.ToFile(snes)
		if err != nil {
			return Entry{}, fmt.Errorf("graphic table entry %d: %w", id, err)
		}
		e.Offset = off
	}
	return e, nil
}

// Frame is one decoded 24x24 block: palette indices, row-major.
type Frame struct {
	Pixels []byte // frameW*frameH entries
}

// Frames decodes the character graphic at file offset off into its
// 24x24 blocks.
//
// Tile layout: the blob is a 24-px-wide filmstrip. Block k keeps band b
// (b = 0..2, top to bottom) in tiles 9k+3b..9k+3b+2, left to right.
// Tile 63 begins the trailing 16x16 object graphic, not a frame.
func Frames(r ROM, off int) ([]Frame, error) {
	if off%32 != 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("walk frames at %06X: graphic base is not 32-byte aligned", off)
	}
	base := off / 32 // first tile of the blob
	frames := make([]Frame, framesWalk)
	for k := range frames {
		dst := &frames[k]
		dst.Pixels = make([]byte, frameW*frameH)
		for b := 0; b < bandsFrame; b++ {
			for c := 0; c < bandTiles; c++ {
				ti := base + k*9 + b*bandTiles + c
				t, err := r.tile(ti * 32)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("walk frames at %06X: %w", off, err)
				}
				for y := 0; y < tileSize; y++ {
					for x := 0; x < tileSize; x++ {
						dst.Pixels[(b*tileSize+y)*frameW+c*tileSize+x] = t[y*tileSize+x]
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return frames, nil
}

// ObjectTile returns the 16x16 object graphic that trails a townsfolk
// blob (金塊グラフィック layout): palette indices, row-major.
func ObjectTile(r ROM, off int) ([]byte, error) {
	if off%32 != 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("object graphic at %06X: graphic base is not 32-byte aligned", off)
	}
	base := off/32 + framesWalk*9 // tile 63 of the blob
	px := make([]byte, 16*16)
	for c := 0; c < 2; c++ {
		for rr := 0; rr < 2; rr++ {
			t, err := r.tile((base + rr*2 + c) * 32)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("object graphic at %06X: %w", off, err)
			}
			for y := 0; y < tileSize; y++ {
				for x := 0; x < tileSize; x++ {
					px[(rr*tileSize+y)*16+c*tileSize+x] = t[y*tileSize+x]
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return px, nil
}

// RGB is one 8-bit-per-channel color.
type RGB [3]byte

// Palette is one 16-color SNES palette. Index 0 is the transparent color.
type Palette struct {
	Colors [16]RGB
}

// LoadPalette reads graphic id's 16-color BGR555 palette from the pool and
// scales the 5-bit channels to 8 bits.
func LoadPalette(r ROM, id int) (Palette, error) {
	return LoadPaletteAt(r, PalettePoolAddr+id*32)
}

// LoadPaletteAt decodes the 16-color BGR555 palette at file offset off.
func LoadPaletteAt(r ROM, off int) (Palette, error) {
	var pal Palette
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		w, err := r.u16le(off + i*2)
		if err != nil {
			return pal, fmt.Errorf("palette at %06X: %w", off, err)
		}
		pal.Colors[i] = RGB{
			byte((w & 31) << 3),
			byte(w >> 5 & 31 << 3),
			byte(w >> 10 & 31 << 3),
		}
	}
	return pal, nil
}
```

`internal/sprites/sprites_test.go`:

```go
package sprites

import "testing"

// encodeTile builds 32 SNES 4bpp tile bytes from 64 palette indices:
// rows interleave plane0/plane1 first, then plane2/plane3.
func encodeTile(px [64]byte) [32]byte {
	var t [32]byte
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			v := px[y*8+x]
			bit := 7 - x
			if v&1 != 0 {
				t[y*2] |= 1 << bit
			}
			if v&2 != 0 {
				t[y*2+1] |= 1 << bit
			}
			if v&4 != 0 {
				t[16+y*2] |= 1 << bit
			}
			if v&8 != 0 {
				t[16+y*2+1] |= 1 << bit
			}
		}
	}
	return t
}

// blobROM returns a ROM of n zero 4bpp tiles (32 bytes each) at file
// offset 0, so graphic offset 0 doubles as the start of a townsfolk blob.
func blobROM(tiles int) ROM {
	return make(ROM, tiles*32)
}

// TestFrames builds a synthetic blob of seven 24x24 blocks with three
// 24x8 bands each (stride nine tiles): every pixel of block k band b
// column c carries one value per (block, band, column), so the decoder
// must reproduce the exact interleave to pass.
func TestFrames(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+GraphicTableEntries*32)
	graphic := 0x100000 // 32-byte aligned
	for k := 0; k < framesWalk; k++ {
		for b := 0; b < bandsFrame; b++ {
			for c := 0; c < bandTiles; c++ {
				val := byte(1 + (k+b+c)%(16-1))
				var px [64]byte
				for i := range px {
					px[i] = val
				}
				t32 := encodeTile(px)
				ti := graphic/32 + k*9 + b*bandTiles + c
				copy(rom[ti*32:(ti+1)*32], t32[:])
			}
		}
	}
	frames, err := Frames(rom, graphic)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Frames: %v", err)
	}
	if len(frames) != framesWalk {
		t.Fatalf("got %d frames, want %d", len(frames), framesWalk)
	}
	for k := 0; k < framesWalk; k++ {
		for b := 0; b < bandsFrame; b++ {
			for c := 0; c < bandTiles; c++ {
				val := byte(1 + (k+b+c)%(16-1))
				for y := 0; y < tileSize; y++ {
					for x := 0; x < tileSize; x++ {
						got := frames[k].Pixels[(b*tileSize+y)*frameW+c*tileSize+x]
						if got != val {
							t.Fatalf("block %d band %d column %d pixel (%d,%d): got %d want %d",
								k, b, c, x, y, got, val)
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestFramesAtRomStart decodes a full 63-tile blob at file offset 0:
// the alignment guard passes offset 0 and the first read is ROM byte 0.
func TestFramesAtRomStart(t *testing.T) {
	frames, err := Frames(blobROM(framesWalk*tilesFrame), 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Frames at offset 0: %v", err)
	}
	if len(frames) != framesWalk {
		t.Fatalf("got %d frames, want %d", len(frames), framesWalk)
	}
}

// TestFramesTruncatedBlob rejects a blob missing its last tile: the
// final read lands on the byte at len(ROM) and must error, not panic.
func TestFramesTruncatedBlob(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := Frames(blobROM(framesWalk*tilesFrame-1), 0); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Frames over a 62-tile blob: got nil error, want a read-beyond-ROM error")
	}
}

// TestFramesNegativeBase rejects a negative graphic base instead of
// aliasing palette bytes in front of the blob.
func TestFramesNegativeBase(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := Frames(blobROM(framesWalk*tilesFrame), -32); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Frames at -32: got nil error, want a negative-offset error")
	}
}

// TestFramesUnaligned rejects a graphic base that is not tile-aligned: a
// silent shift would decode garbage.
func TestFramesUnaligned(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+GraphicTableEntries*32)
	if _, err := Frames(rom, 0x100002); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("unaligned base: expected error")
	}
}

// TestObjectTile checks the trailing 16x16 object graphic: tiles 63..66
// of the blob fill the four 8x8 quadrants in row-major order.
func TestObjectTile(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+GraphicTableEntries*32)
	graphic := 0x100000
	obj := graphic/32 + 63 // tile 63 of the blob
	for ti := 0; ti < 4; ti++ {
		var px [64]byte
		for i := range px {
			px[i] = byte(1 + ti)
		}
		t32 := encodeTile(px)
		copy(rom[(obj+ti)*32:(obj+ti+1)*32], t32[:])
	}
	got, err := ObjectTile(rom, graphic)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ObjectTile: %v", err)
	}
	for ti := 0; ti < 4; ti++ {
		ry, rx := ti/2, ti%2
		if v := got[(ry*8+4)*16+rx*8+4]; v != byte(1+ti) {
			t.Fatalf("object quadrant %d pixel: got %d want %d", ti, v, 1+ti)
		}
	}
}

// TestObjectTileUnaligned rejects an object graphic base that is not
// tile-aligned, like Frames does for the blob itself.
func TestObjectTileUnaligned(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+GraphicTableEntries*32)
	if _, err := ObjectTile(rom, 0x100001); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ObjectTile at unaligned base: got nil error, want an alignment error")
	}
}

// TestTilePixelOrder pins the pixel order inside one 4bpp tile: bit 7
// of each row byte is the leftmost pixel. Every pixel carries a
// different value (uniform tiles cannot tell bit 7 from bit 0), so any
// horizontal mirror of the byte decode fails.
func TestTilePixelOrder(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, 32)
	var px [64]byte
	for y := 0; y < tileSize; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < tileSize; x++ {
			px[y*tileSize+x] = byte((x*3 + y*5) % 16)
		}
	}
	t32 := encodeTile(px)
	copy(rom[:], t32[:])
	got, err := rom.tile(0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("tile: %v", err)
	}
	for i, want := range px {
		if got[i] != want {
			t.Fatalf("tile pixel (%d,%d): got %d want %d", i%tileSize, i/tileSize, got[i], want)
		}
	}
}

// entryROM returns a ROM through graphic table entry 6, with entry id
// preloaded: kind in byte 0, SNES address in bytes 1..3 (little-endian).
func entryROM(id int, kind Kind, snes int) ROM {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+(id+1)*4)
	rom[GraphicTableAddr+id*4] = byte(kind)
	rom[GraphicTableAddr+id*4+1] = byte(snes)
	rom[GraphicTableAddr+id*4+2] = byte(snes >> 8)
	rom[GraphicTableAddr+id*4+3] = byte(snes >> 16)
	return rom
}

// TestEntry parses a present graphic table row: entry 5 points at SNES
// address DE:8800 (bank DE maps to file 0x1E8800) with kind 0x01.
func TestEntry(t *testing.T) {
	e, err := TableEntry(entryROM(5, KindTownsfolk, 0xDE8800), 5)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(5): %v", err)
	}
	if e.Kind != KindTownsfolk {
		t.Fatalf("entry 5 kind: got %#x want %#x", e.Kind, KindTownsfolk)
	}
	if e.Offset != 0x1E8800 {
		t.Fatalf("entry 5 offset: got %06X want %06X", e.Offset, 0x1E8800)
	}
}

// TestEntryAbsent keeps Offset -1 for a zeroed row: SNES address 0
// marks the entry absent, not file offset 0.
func TestEntryAbsent(t *testing.T) {
	e, err := TableEntry(entryROM(6, 0, 0), 6)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(6): %v", err)
	}
	if e.Offset != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("zeroed entry 6: got offset %06X want -1", e.Offset)
	}
}

// TestEntryIDOutOfRange rejects ids past the 1020-row table.
func TestEntryIDOutOfRange(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+GraphicTableEntries*4+16)
	if _, err := TableEntry(rom, GraphicTableEntries); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(%d): got nil error, want an out-of-range error", GraphicTableEntries)
	}
}

// TestEntryNegativeID rejects negative ids instead of aliasing bytes in
// front of the table.
func TestEntryNegativeID(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, GraphicTableAddr+GraphicTableEntries*4+16)
	if _, err := TableEntry(rom, -1); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(-1): got nil error, want an out-of-range error")
	}
}

// TestEntryLowBank maps a 40-7D bank address to the same file offset:
// FastROM banks carry no header displacement.
func TestEntryLowBank(t *testing.T) {
	e, err := TableEntry(entryROM(5, KindTownsfolk, 0x408800), 5)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(5): %v", err)
	}
	if e.Offset != 0x408800 {
		t.Fatalf("entry 5 offset for bank 40: got %06X want %06X", e.Offset, 0x408800)
	}
}

// TestEntryBankOutsideROM rejects a SNES address outside cartridge ROM
// space (bank 7F is neither 40-7D nor C0-FF).
func TestEntryBankOutsideROM(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := TableEntry(entryROM(5, KindTownsfolk, 0x7F8000), 5); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(5) at bank 7F: got nil error, want a not-cartridge-ROM error")
	}
}

// TestPalette checks BGR555 -> RGB conversion against palette id 7:
// R takes bits 0-4, G bits 5-9, B bits 10-14, each scaled <<3. Color 15
// pins the sixteenth entry and full-scale white.
func TestPalette(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make(ROM, PalettePoolAddr+GraphicTableEntries*32+16)
	off := PalettePoolAddr + 7*32
	rom[off+2] = 0x1F // color 1: R=31 -> 248 with <<3
	rom[off+3] = 0x00
	rom[off+4] = 0xE0 // color 2: G=31 -> 248
	rom[off+5] = 0x03
	rom[off+6] = 0x00 // color 3: B=31 -> 248
	rom[off+7] = 0x7C
	rom[off+30] = 0xFF // color 15: all channels 31 -> 248
	rom[off+31] = 0x7F
	pal, err := LoadPalette(rom, 7)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Palette(7): %v", err)
	}
	if pal.Colors[1] != (RGB{248, 0, 0}) {
		t.Fatalf("color 1: got %v want {248 0 0}", pal.Colors[1])
	}
	if pal.Colors[2] != (RGB{0, 248, 0}) {
		t.Fatalf("color 2: got %v want {0 248 0}", pal.Colors[2])
	}
	if pal.Colors[3] != (RGB{0, 0, 248}) {
		t.Fatalf("color 3: got %v want {0 0 248}", pal.Colors[3])
	}
	if pal.Colors[15] != (RGB{248, 248, 248}) {
		t.Fatalf("color 15: got %v want {248 248 248}", pal.Colors[15])
	}
}
```

`internal/techs/techs.go`:

```go
// Package techs decodes the technique (技) and spell (術) tables of the
// bokuno ROM. Both tables hold 14-byte 技の性能 records — the spells use
// the same layout, per the community struct dump reproduced in the bokuno
// patch archive (テキスト/05_構造体.def.txt, structs RS3_技データ and
// RS3拡張_術データ).
//
// Layout (file offsets; CPU banks in parentheses, see docs/techniques.md
// for the wiki cross-verification behind each address):
//
//	tech table    0x3E0F00 (FE:0F00)  256 entries x 14 B, ids 0x00-0xFF
//	tech names    0x3D27C0            256 entries x 10 B
//	spell table   0x5BAA00 (5B:AA00)  256 entries x 14 B, ids 0x00-0xFF
//	spell names   0x5BA000 (5B:A000)  256 entries x 10 B
//
// The enemy tech table (0x3E1D00, 敵技データ, same record size) follows
// the tech table directly; it is a different ID space and not decoded
// here.
package techs

import "fmt"

// File offsets, strides, and extents of the technique and spell tables.
const (
	TechTableOffset      = 0x3E0F00 // FE:0F00
	EnemyTechTableOffset = 0x3E1D00 // FE:1D00 敵技データ
	TechNameOffset       = 0x3D27C0
	SpellTableOffset     = 0x5BAA00 // 5B:AA00
	SpellNameOffset      = 0x5BA000 // 5B:A000
	EntrySize            = 14
	// 敵技性能 records are 技の性能 (14 B) + 見切り対応技 + 未使用 = 16 B
	// (struct dump: struct 敵技性能 //【技の性能】のコピー). Verified
	// against the ROM: stride 14/15 reads garbage while 16 yields
	// ブレード hit 120 / power 0x0A (= wiki 威力 40 with the ×4 scale),
	// and マヒ爪 (id 0x1F, FE:1EF0) carries effect byte 0x05 マヒ.
	EnemyTechEntrySize = 16
	// Hack extension enemy tech table (struct RS3拡張_敵技性能,
	// space[5982912] = 0x5B4AC0), ids 0x100-0x1FF, same stride.
	ExtEnemyTechTableOffset = 0x5B4AC0
	ExtEnemyTechIDBase      = 0x100
	NameStride              = 10
	Count                   = 256

	// 追加効果設定テーブル (struct 拡張用RS3_技の追加効果 in the def
	// file: BYTE space[4190720] = file 0x3FF200, then one 6-byte
	// 技の追加効果 per effect id). The 技の性能 byte +3 indexes it; ids
	// 0x00-0x2F match the vanilla table (kaeru 追加効果一覧), the hack
	// extends the ids. FF/FE in byte +3 = no added effect.
	AddedEffectTableOffset = 0x3FF200
	AddedEffectEntrySize   = 6
	AddedEffectCount       = 128
)

// Class codes in byte +12 (種類); e.g. Class(0x21) == ClassAxe.
const (
	ClassSword      = 0x00 // 剣
	ClassGreatsword = 0x10 // 大剣
	ClassAxe        = 0x21 // 斧
	ClassMace       = 0x31 // 棍棒
	ClassShortsword = 0x42 // 小剣
	ClassSpear      = 0x52 // 槍
	ClassBow        = 0x63 // 弓
	ClassMartial    = 0x74 // 体術
	ClassAojiRyu    = 0x85 // 蒼竜術
	ClassSuzaku     = 0x96 // 朱鳥術
	ClassByakko     = 0xA7 // 白虎術
	ClassGenbu      = 0xB8 // 玄武術
	ClassTaiyo      = 0xC9 // 太陽術
	ClassTsuki      = 0xDA // 月術
	ClassFormation  = 0x0E // 陣形技
	ClassItem       = 0x0F // アイテム
)

// Spell-school codes in byte +11 (術タイプ).
const (
	SchoolPhysical = 0x00
	SchoolTaiyo    = 0x01 // 太陽
	SchoolTsuki    = 0x02 // 月
	SchoolAbyss    = 0x03 // アビス
	SchoolAojiRyu  = 0x08 // 蒼竜
	SchoolSuzaku   = 0x10 // 朱鳥
	SchoolByakko   = 0x18 // 白虎
	SchoolGenbu    = 0x20 // 玄武
)

// Cost flag bits in byte +13 (消費); the low five bits are the amount.
const (
	CostWP     = 0x00 // default resource is WP
	CostJP     = 0x20
	CostAll    = 0x40 // 全消費
	CostBreaks = 0x80 // 武器破壊
)

// Technique is one decoded 14-byte 技の性能 record.
type Technique struct {
	ID uint16

	// Byte +0: hit or activation rate in percent (命中・発動率).
	// 255 means no roll is made (guaranteed).
	HitRate byte

	// Byte +1: base power (基本ダメージ). The battle formulas scale this
	// by 4 — see docs/battle-formulas.md §2 (威力×4×回数).
	BasePower byte

	// Byte +2: high nibble hit count (回数), low nibble growth term (成長).
	HitCount byte
	Growth   byte

	StatusEffect byte // +3, 追加効果

	// Byte +4: damage attributes (0x01 状態, 0x02 雷, 0x04 冷, 0x08 熱,
	// 0x10 射, 0x20 貫, 0x40 叩, 0x80 斬).
	Attributes byte

	// Byte +5: target range (0x02 味方, 0x04 敵, 0x08 横一列, 0x10 縦一列,
	// 0x20 全体, 0x40 遠単, 0x80 両手).
	Range byte

	// Byte +6: special effects (0x02 盾有効, 0x08 見切り可, 0x10
	// カウンター有効, 0x80 閃き派生有効).
	SpecialEffects byte

	// Byte +7: secondary attributes (0x01 水, 0x08 投げ, 0x10 音波,
	// 0x20 凝視, 0x40 飛行特攻, 0x80 地面).
	Attributes2 byte

	// Byte +8: special settings (0x02 カウンター技, 0x04 行動最後,
	// 0x08 行動最初, 0x20 固有技扱い, 0x80 追加効果有効).
	SpecialSettings byte

	// Byte +9: special target pick (C2:575D), tried from bit 7 down to 3:
	// 0x80/0x40 sex (record +3 & E0), 0x20 weighted, 0x10 uniform,
	// 0x08 lowest HP.
	TargetPick byte

	TechType byte // +10, 技タイプ: selects the damage formula family

	// Byte +11: spell school (術タイプ), a School constant.
	SpellType byte

	// Byte +12: weapon/school class (種類), a Class constant.
	Class byte

	// Byte +13: cost (消費). Low five bits are the WP/JP amount; the flag
	// bits CostJP, CostAll, CostBreaks select the resource and side
	// effects.
	Cost byte
}

// CostAmount returns the WP/JP amount in the cost byte.
func (t Technique) CostAmount() byte { return t.Cost & 0x1F }

// DecodePerformance decodes one 14-byte 技の性能 record. Exported so the
// enemy-tech table (敵技性能: 技の性能 + 見切り対応技 + 未使用, 15 B) can
// reuse the same field decode.
func DecodePerformance(id uint16, rec []byte) Technique {
	return decodePerformance(id, rec)
}

// decodePerformance decodes one 14-byte 技の性能 record.
func decodePerformance(id uint16, rec []byte) Technique {
	return Technique{
		ID:              id,
		HitRate:         rec[0],
		BasePower:       rec[1],
		HitCount:        rec[2] >> 4,
		Growth:          rec[2] & 0x0F,
		StatusEffect:    rec[3],
		Attributes:      rec[4],
		Range:           rec[5],
		SpecialEffects:  rec[6],
		Attributes2:     rec[7],
		SpecialSettings: rec[8],
		TargetPick:      rec[9],
		TechType:        rec[10],
		SpellType:       rec[11],
		Class:           rec[12],
		Cost:            rec[13],
	}
}

func entryAt(rom []byte, table int, id uint16) ([]byte, error) {
	off := table + int(id)*EntrySize
	if id >= Count {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("id %#x outside table (0x00-0xFF)", id)
	}
	if off+EntrySize > len(rom) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("id %#x: entry at file %#x out of range", id, off)
	}
	return rom[off : off+EntrySize], nil
}

// EnemyTechAt decodes the 敵技データ record for enemy pattern tech ids
// 0x00-0x1FF: 0x00-0x0FF in the main table (0x3E1D00) and 0x100-0x1FF in
// the hack extension table (0x5B4AC0, struct RS3拡張_敵技性能), both with
// the 16 B stride.
func EnemyTechAt(rom []byte, id uint16) (Technique, error) {
	base := EnemyTechTableOffset
	if id >= ExtEnemyTechIDBase {
		if id >= ExtEnemyTechIDBase+Count {
			return Technique{}, fmt.Errorf("id %#x outside enemy tech tables (0x00-0x1FF)", id)
		}
		base = ExtEnemyTechTableOffset
	}
	off := base + int(id%Count)*EnemyTechEntrySize
	if off+EnemyTechEntrySize > len(rom) {
		return Technique{}, fmt.Errorf("id %#x: entry at file %#x out of range", id, off)
	}
	return decodePerformance(id, rom[off:off+EntrySize]), nil
}

// AddedEffect is one 6-byte 技の追加効果 record (0x3FF200), indexed by the
// 技の性能 byte +3 when the 特殊設定 byte carries bit 0x80 (追加効果有効).
type AddedEffect struct {
	Species byte // +0 特効/クリティカル: 0x00 none, 0x01 獣人 0x02 獣 0x03 蛇
	// 0x04 ドラゴン 0x05 カエル 0x06 鳥 0x07 昆虫 0x08 植物 0x09 スライム
	// 0x0A 魚 0x0B 水棲 0x0C 玄竜 0x0D 悪魔 0x0E 骸骨 0x0F 巨人
	// 0x10-0x1F 地精系/拡張, +0x20 アンデッド, +0x40 女, +0x80 男.

	Status1 byte // +1 状態異常1: 0x01 スタン 0x02 毒 0x04 混乱 0x08 暗闇
	// 0x10 眠り 0x20 マヒ 0x40 石化 0x80 即死.

	Status2 byte // +2 状態異常2: 0x01 自分透明化 0x02 かすみ2段
	// 0x04 自分強制スタン 0x80 術スタン; hack-era bits (docs/techniques.md
	// "Open questions"): 0x08 weapon-power damage scaling (黄龍剣/共震剣),
	// 0x10 damaged-before-use scaling (無明剣), 0x20 own-LP-scaled power
	// (不動剣), 0x40 HP drain (enemy サクション 0xAE) [bit wiring VERIFIED:
	// ROM rows + dispatcher C2:C637; damage semantics PLAUSIBLE: bokuno
	// wiki effect text].

	StatDown byte // +3 能力低下: 0x01 物理熱防 0x02 魅 0x04 意 0x08 魔
	// 0x10 体 0x20 早 0x40 器 0x80 腕.

	DownAmount byte // +4 能力値低下量

	StatUp byte // +5 能力上昇: low 3 bits = 増加量 (×2 on use),
	// 0x08 魔防 0x10 早 0x20 体 0x40 魔 0x80 腕.
}

// Status1Names maps Status1 bits to the Japanese status names used
// throughout the docs.
var Status1Names = map[byte]string{
	0x01: "スタン", 0x02: "毒", 0x04: "混乱", 0x08: "暗闇",
	0x10: "眠り", 0x20: "マヒ", 0x40: "石化", 0x80: "即死",
}

// Status2Names maps the Status2 bits: the four vanilla ones plus the
// hack-era damage-modifier bits (see the Status2 field comment for the
// evidence split VERIFIED/PLAUSIBLE).
var Status2Names = map[byte]string{
	0x01: "自分透明化", 0x02: "かすみ2段", 0x04: "自分強制スタン", 0x80: "術スタン",
	0x08: "武器攻撃力依存ボーナス", 0x10: "被弾ボーナス",
	0x20: "残LP依存ボーナス", 0x40: "HP吸収",
}

// SpeciesNames maps the low-nibble species codes of Species.
var SpeciesNames = map[byte]string{
	0x01: "獣人", 0x02: "獣", 0x03: "蛇", 0x04: "ドラゴン", 0x05: "カエル",
	0x06: "鳥", 0x07: "昆虫", 0x08: "植物", 0x09: "スライム", 0x0A: "魚",
	0x0B: "水棲", 0x0C: "玄竜", 0x0D: "悪魔", 0x0E: "骸骨", 0x0F: "巨人",
}

// SpeciesFlags maps the high-bit species flags of Species.
var SpeciesFlags = map[byte]string{
	0x20: "アンデッド", 0x40: "女", 0x80: "男",
}

// StatDownNames maps StatDown bits (the defense row is 物理・熱防御力).
var StatDownNames = map[byte]string{
	0x01: "物熱防", 0x02: "魅", 0x04: "意", 0x08: "魔",
	0x10: "体", 0x20: "早", 0x40: "器", 0x80: "腕",
}

// StatUpNames maps StatUp bits.
var StatUpNames = map[byte]string{
	0x08: "魔防", 0x10: "早", 0x20: "体", 0x40: "魔", 0x80: "腕",
}

// AddedEffectAt decodes the effect-setting record for the given id. Ids
// beyond AddedEffectCount error.
func AddedEffectAt(rom []byte, id byte) (AddedEffect, error) {
	if int(id) >= AddedEffectCount {
		return AddedEffect{}, fmt.Errorf("effect id %#x outside table (0x00-%#x)", id, AddedEffectCount-1)
	}
	off := AddedEffectTableOffset + int(id)*AddedEffectEntrySize
	if off+AddedEffectEntrySize > len(rom) {
		return AddedEffect{}, fmt.Errorf("effect id %#x: entry at file %#x out of range", id, off)
	}
	rec := rom[off : off+AddedEffectEntrySize]
	return AddedEffect{
		Species:    rec[0],
		Status1:    rec[1],
		Status2:    rec[2],
		StatDown:   rec[3],
		DownAmount: rec[4],
		StatUp:     rec[5],
	}, nil
}

// TechAt decodes the technique record for the given tech ID (0x00-0xFF)
// from the ROM file image.
func TechAt(rom []byte, id uint16) (Technique, error) {
	rec, err := entryAt(rom, TechTableOffset, id)
	if err != nil {
		return Technique{}, err
	}
	return decodePerformance(id, rec), nil
}

// AllTechniques decodes the full technique table, IDs 0x00-0xFF.
func AllTechniques(rom []byte) ([]Technique, error) {
	return all(rom, TechTableOffset)
}

// SpellAt decodes the spell record for the given spell ID (0x00-0xFF).
func SpellAt(rom []byte, id uint16) (Technique, error) {
	rec, err := entryAt(rom, SpellTableOffset, id)
	if err != nil {
		return Technique{}, err
	}
	return decodePerformance(id, rec), nil
}

// AllSpells decodes the full spell table, IDs 0x00-0xFF.
func AllSpells(rom []byte) ([]Technique, error) {
	return all(rom, SpellTableOffset)
}

func all(rom []byte, table int) ([]Technique, error) {
	out := make([]Technique, 0, Count)
	for id := uint16(0); id < Count; id++ {
		t, err := entryAt(rom, table, id)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out = append(out, decodePerformance(id, t))
	}
	return out, nil
}

// NameRecord returns the raw bytes of the name record for the given ID
// from the name table at base, trimmed at the first terminator (0x00 NUL
// or 0x50 fullwidth space). Decode the bytes with the glyph assignment
// (internal/glyphs + internal/bokuno), as cmd/dumpnames does.
func NameRecord(rom []byte, base int, id uint16) ([]byte, error) {
	if id >= Count {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("id %#x outside name table (0x00-0xFF)", id)
	}
	start := base + int(id)*NameStride
	if start+NameStride > len(rom) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("id %#x: name record at file %#x out of range", id, start)
	}
	rec := rom[start : start+NameStride]
	for i, b := range rec {
		if b == 0x00 || b == 0x50 {
			return rec[:i], nil
		}
	}
	return rec, nil
}

// TechNameRecord returns the raw name record for tech ID id.
func TechNameRecord(rom []byte, id uint16) ([]byte, error) {
	return NameRecord(rom, TechNameOffset, id)
}

// SpellNameRecord returns the raw name record for spell ID id.
func SpellNameRecord(rom []byte, id uint16) ([]byte, error) {
	return NameRecord(rom, SpellNameOffset, id)
}

```

`internal/techs/techs_test.go`:

```go
package techs

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"
)

// fixture builds a ROM image large enough for both tables and their name
// tables. It holds two kinds of rows: real ROM records (each cited to its
// address) and synthetic rows whose bytes are all distinct, so a swapped
// field offset or a wrong stride cannot decode to the expected values by
// coincidence.
func fixture() []byte {
	need := SpellTableOffset + Count*EntrySize
	rom := make([]byte, need)
	put := func(off int, b []byte) { copy(rom[off:], b) }

	// Tech 0x13 十文字斬り: hit 120, power byte 20 (in-game 80), 2 hits,
	// growth 4, WP 4.
	put(TechTableOffset+0x13*EntrySize, []byte{
		120, 20, 0x24, 0x0B, 0x80, 0x04, 0xF2, 0x00, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x04,
	})
	// Tech 0x0F パリイ: hit 45, growth-only record with JP cost flag.
	put(TechTableOffset+0x0F*EntrySize, []byte{
		45, 2, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x21,
	})
	// Synthetic tech 0x77: bytes 0x01-0x0D all distinct and cost 0x1E
	// (bit 0x10 set), so every field offset and the cost mask are
	// individually observable.
	put(TechTableOffset+0x77*EntrySize, []byte{
		0x01, 0x02, 0x34, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x1E,
	})

	// Spell 0x14 ウィークネス: activation 60, JP 4, school 月.
	put(SpellTableOffset+0x14*EntrySize, []byte{
		60, 254, 0x00, 0x05, 0x01, 0xC4, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0x96, 0x24,
	})

	// Enemy tech 0x1F マヒ爪 (ROM FE:1EF0): hit 120, power 0, 1 hit,
	// growth 2, effect 0x05 マヒ, settings 0x80, martial class. The two
	// trailing bytes (見切り対応技 0xFF, 未使用 0xA1) sit outside the
	// 14-byte 技の性能 view.
	put(EnemyTechTableOffset+0x1F*EnemyTechEntrySize, []byte{
		120, 0, 0x12, 0x05, 0x80, 0x04, 0x72, 0x00, 0x80, 0x02, 0x03, 0x00, 0x74, 0x01, 0xFF, 0xA1,
	})
	// Synthetic enemy main 0x80: pins the table split's main side — ids
	// below 0x100 read the main table even in its upper half.
	put(EnemyTechTableOffset+0x80*EnemyTechEntrySize, []byte{
		0x61, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x51, 0x00, 0x52, 0x21, 0x00, 0x00,
	})
	// Extension enemy tech 0x10B (ROM 5B:4B70): the same 16-byte stride in
	// the hack table at 0x5B4AC0.
	put(ExtEnemyTechTableOffset+(0x10B-ExtEnemyTechIDBase)*EnemyTechEntrySize, []byte{
		0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0xA6, 0x40, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x32, 0x00, 0xDA, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00,
	})
	// Synthetic ext slot 0 (id 0x100): pins the split's extension side —
	// the first extension id reads the hack table's first record.
	put(ExtEnemyTechTableOffset, []byte{
		0x64, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x55, 0x00, 0x66, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
	})

	// Effect table: id 0x01 毒 (vanilla row), id 0x5D カース composite
	// (ROM FE:42E: スタン + 魔/体/早/器/腕 down 5), synthetic 0x20 with all
	// six bytes distinct.
	put(AddedEffectTableOffset+0x01*AddedEffectEntrySize, []byte{0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00})
	put(AddedEffectTableOffset+0x5D*AddedEffectEntrySize, []byte{0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0xF8, 0x05, 0x00})
	put(AddedEffectTableOffset+0x20*AddedEffectEntrySize, []byte{0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44, 0x55, 0x66})

	// Names: 十文字斬り (NUL-terminated), ウィークネス (full stride, no
	// terminator), synthetic tech name 0x0F whose fullwidth-space (0x50)
	// terminator comes before the NUL.
	name := func(slot ...byte) []byte { return slot }
	put(TechNameOffset+0x13*NameStride, append(name(0xA2, 0xAE, 0xCD, 0x20, 0xC6), 0x00, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50))
	full := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x51}, NameStride) // no terminator inside
	put(SpellNameOffset+0x14*NameStride, full)
	put(TechNameOffset+0x0F*NameStride, append(name(0x71, 0x72), 0x50, 0x73, 0x00, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50, 0x50))
	return rom
}

// TechAt maps every byte of the 14-byte 技の性能 record to its documented
// Technique field; the synthetic row makes a swapped offset visible.
func TestTechAtDecodesEveryFieldOffset(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	got, err := TechAt(rom, 0x77)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := Technique{
		ID: 0x77, HitRate: 0x01, BasePower: 0x02, HitCount: 0x03, Growth: 0x04,
		StatusEffect: 0x04, Attributes: 0x05, Range: 0x06, SpecialEffects: 0x07,
		Attributes2: 0x08, SpecialSettings: 0x09, TargetPick: 0x0A, TechType: 0x0B,
		SpellType: 0x0C, Class: 0x0D, Cost: 0x1E,
	}
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("TechAt(0x77) = %+v, want every record byte in its documented field", got)
	}
	if got.CostAmount() != 0x1E {
		t.Errorf("CostAmount() = %d, want 30 (the 0x1F mask keeps cost bit 0x10)", got.CostAmount())
	}
}

// Real ROM rows pin the decode against hand-transcribed records.
func TestTechAt(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	got, err := TechAt(rom, 0x13)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := Technique{
		ID: 0x13, HitRate: 120, BasePower: 20, HitCount: 2, Growth: 4,
		StatusEffect: 0x0B, Attributes: 0x80, Range: 0x04, SpecialEffects: 0xF2,
		SpecialSettings: 0x80, Cost: 0x04,
	}
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("TechAt(0x13) = %+v, want 十文字斬り's record", got)
	}

	got, err = TechAt(rom, 0x0F)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.HitRate != 45 || got.Cost&CostJP == 0 || got.CostAmount() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("TechAt(0x0F) = %+v, want パリイ: hit 45, JP cost 1", got)
	}
}

func TestSpellAt(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	got, err := SpellAt(rom, 0x14)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.HitRate != 60 || got.SpellType != SchoolTsuki || got.Class != ClassSuzaku {
		t.Errorf("SpellAt(0x14) = %+v, want activation 60, school 月, class 朱鳥", got)
	}
	if got.Cost&CostJP == 0 || got.CostAmount() != 4 {
		t.Errorf("SpellAt(0x14) cost = %02X, want JP flag with amount 4", got.Cost)
	}
}

// AllTechniques and AllSpells walk their whole table in id order, decoding
// each slot the same way TechAt/SpellAt do.
func TestAllTablesDecodeAllIDs(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	list, err := AllTechniques(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(list) != Count {
		t.Fatalf("AllTechniques len = %d, want %d", len(list), Count)
	}
	if list[0].ID != 0 || list[Count-1].ID != Count-1 {
		t.Errorf("AllTechniques ids = %d..%d, want 0..%d", list[0].ID, list[Count-1].ID, Count-1)
	}
	techAt, err := TechAt(rom, 0x77)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if list[0x77] != techAt {
		t.Errorf("AllTechniques()[0x77] = %+v, want the tech-table record TechAt decodes", list[0x77])
	}
	spells, err := AllSpells(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(spells) != Count {
		t.Fatalf("AllSpells len = %d, want %d", len(spells), Count)
	}
	if spells[0x14].SpellType != SchoolTsuki {
		t.Errorf("AllSpells()[0x14].SpellType = %02X, want 月 (the spell table, not the tech table)", spells[0x14].SpellType)
	}
}

// Ids outside a table error: techs and spells hold 0x00-0xFF, enemy techs
// 0x000-0x1FF, added effects 0x00-0x7F, names 0x00-0xFF.
func TestIDOutsideTableErrors(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	if _, err := TechAt(rom, Count); err == nil {
		t.Error("TechAt(id 0x100): want outside-table error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := SpellAt(rom, Count); err == nil {
		t.Error("SpellAt(id 0x100): want outside-table error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := EnemyTechAt(rom, 2*Count); err == nil {
		t.Error("EnemyTechAt(id 0x200): want outside-table error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := AddedEffectAt(rom, AddedEffectCount); err == nil {
		t.Error("AddedEffectAt(id 0x80): want outside-table error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := TechNameRecord(rom, Count); err == nil {
		t.Error("TechNameRecord(id 0x100): want outside-table error, got nil")
	}
}

// A ROM cut one byte short of an entry errors instead of decoding or
// panicking — the bound is off+size, not off.
func TestTruncatedROMErrors(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	if _, err := TechAt(rom[:TechTableOffset+EntrySize-1], 0x00); err == nil {
		t.Error("TechAt on ROM ending 1 byte before entry end: want error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := TechAt(rom[:TechTableOffset], 0x00); err == nil {
		t.Error("TechAt on ROM ending at table start: want error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := EnemyTechAt(rom[:EnemyTechTableOffset+EnemyTechEntrySize-1], 0x00); err == nil {
		t.Error("EnemyTechAt on ROM ending 1 byte before entry end: want error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := AddedEffectAt(rom[:AddedEffectTableOffset+AddedEffectEntrySize-1], 0x00); err == nil {
		t.Error("AddedEffectAt on ROM ending 1 byte before entry end: want error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := TechNameRecord(rom[:TechNameOffset+NameStride-1], 0x00); err == nil {
		t.Error("TechNameRecord on ROM ending 1 byte before record end: want error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := AllTechniques(rom[:TechTableOffset]); err == nil {
		t.Error("AllTechniques on truncated ROM: want error, got nil")
	}
}

// Enemy techs use the 16-byte 敵技性能 stride; ids 0x00-0xFF read the main
// table (0x3E1D00), 0x100-0x1FF the hack extension (0x5B4AC0). The two
// trailing bytes (見切り対応技, 未使用) must not shift the 技の性能 fields.
func TestEnemyTechAt(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	got, err := EnemyTechAt(rom, 0x1F)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.HitRate != 120 || got.BasePower != 0 || got.HitCount != 1 || got.Growth != 2 {
		t.Errorf("EnemyTechAt(0x1F) = %+v, want マヒ爪: hit 120 power 0 n1 g2", got)
	}
	if got.StatusEffect != 0x05 {
		t.Errorf("EnemyTechAt(0x1F) effect = %02X, want 05 (マヒ)", got.StatusEffect)
	}
	if got.SpecialSettings&0x80 == 0 {
		t.Errorf("EnemyTechAt(0x1F) settings = %02X, want bit 0x80 set", got.SpecialSettings)
	}
	main, err := EnemyTechAt(rom, 0x80)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if main.HitRate != 0x61 || main.Class != 0x52 {
		t.Errorf("EnemyTechAt(0x80) = %+v, want main-table record (hit 0x61, class 0x52)", main)
	}
	ext, err := EnemyTechAt(rom, ExtEnemyTechIDBase)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if ext.HitRate != 0x64 || ext.Class != 0x66 {
		t.Errorf("EnemyTechAt(0x100) = %+v, want first extension record (hit 0x64, class 0x66)", ext)
	}
	ext, err = EnemyTechAt(rom, ExtEnemyTechIDBase+0x0B)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if ext.Class != ClassTsuki || ext.TechType != 0x32 {
		t.Errorf("EnemyTechAt(0x10B) = %+v, want class 月術, tech type 0x32", ext)
	}
}

// AddedEffectAt maps the six bytes of a 技の追加効果 record (0x3FF200, stride
// 6) to the AddedEffect fields.
func TestAddedEffectAt(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	eff, err := AddedEffectAt(rom, 0x01)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if eff.Status1 != 0x02 || Status1Names[eff.Status1] != "毒" {
		t.Errorf("AddedEffectAt(0x01) = %+v, want Status1 毒", eff)
	}
	eff, err = AddedEffectAt(rom, 0x5D)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if eff.Status1 != 0x01 || eff.StatDown != 0xF8 || eff.DownAmount != 5 {
		t.Errorf("AddedEffectAt(0x5D) = %+v, want スタン + 魔/体/早/器/腕 down 5", eff)
	}
	eff, err = AddedEffectAt(rom, 0x20)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := AddedEffect{Species: 0x11, Status1: 0x22, Status2: 0x33, StatDown: 0x44, DownAmount: 0x55, StatUp: 0x66}
	if eff != want {
		t.Errorf("AddedEffectAt(0x20) = %+v, want every record byte in its documented field", eff)
	}
}

// NameRecord returns the 10-byte name record trimmed at its first
// terminator: 0x00 NUL or 0x50 fullwidth space.
func TestNameRecords(t *testing.T) {
	rom := fixture()
	rec, err := TechNameRecord(rom, 0x13)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// 十文字斬り's first glyphs before the NUL terminator.
	if !bytes.Equal(rec, []byte{0xA2, 0xAE, 0xCD, 0x20, 0xC6}) {
		t.Errorf("TechNameRecord(0x13) = % X, want A2 AE CD 20 C6", rec)
	}
	rec, err = TechNameRecord(rom, 0x0F)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(rec, []byte{0x71, 0x72}) {
		t.Errorf("TechNameRecord(0x0F) = % X, want 71 72 (trimmed at the 0x50 space)", rec)
	}
	rec, err = SpellNameRecord(rom, 0x14)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(rec) != NameStride {
		t.Errorf("SpellNameRecord(0x14) len = %d, want %d (no terminator)", len(rec), NameStride)
	}
}
```

`internal/toolargs/toolargs.go`:

```go
// Package toolargs holds the cmd tools' shared argument convention: the
// canonical ROM and glyph-assignment paths are repo constants, and a
// tool may omit leading positionals — the leftmost omitted slot is the
// ROM, the next the glyph assignment. Arity alone decides, never
// content.
package toolargs

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

const (
	// DefaultROM is the canonical patched ROM every decode tool reads.
	DefaultROM = "patches/bokuno_jp.sfc"
	// DefaultGlyphs is the glyph assignment glyphtable builds and the
	// text decoders read.
	DefaultGlyphs = "data/glyphs_jp.json"
)

// WithROM prepends DefaultROM when args holds exactly one value less
// than min (the short form). Arity outside [min, max] — max 0 means
// unbounded — prints usage to stderr and exits 2.
func WithROM(args []string, min, max int, usage string) []string {
	if len(args) == min-1 {
		return append([]string{DefaultROM}, args...)
	}
	if len(args) < min-1 || (max > 0 && len(args) > max) {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, usage)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	return args
}

// WithROMGlyphs resolves the fixed-arity [<rom> [<glyphs>]] <out>
// tools: one arg prepends both defaults, two prepend DefaultROM, three
// map as given, anything else prints usage and exits 2.
func WithROMGlyphs(args []string, usage string) []string {
	switch len(args) {
	case 1:
		return []string{DefaultROM, DefaultGlyphs, args[0]}
	case 2:
		return []string{DefaultROM, args[0], args[1]}
	case 3:
		return args
	}
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, usage)
	os.Exit(2)
	return nil
}
```

`internal/triggers/jump.go`:

```go
package triggers

import (
	"fmt"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// JumpTable decodes the global movement-destination table at 0x3CFB00 that
// event-code 11xx (VM op 0x11 mapJump, 2 bytes: opcode + index) jumps to.
// The table holds exactly 256 five-byte records and ends at 0x3D0000,
// which is also where the FD bank's pointer page starts — the one-byte
// operand indexes it from zero with no gaps.
//
// Record layout (identical to a map's block-4 destination record):
//
//	0  flag: bit4-7 transition effect, bit3 hide character,
//	   bit2 music change valid, bit0-1 facing after the jump
//	1-2  little-endian word: bits 10-15 music id, bits 0-9 map id
//	3  target X
//	4  target Y
func JumpTable(r mapfmt.ROM) ([]Destination, error) {
	ds := make([]Destination, 0, jumpTableEntries)
	for i := 0; i < jumpTableEntries; i++ {
		p := jumpTableAddr + i*destRecordSize
		if p+destRecordSize > len(r) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jump table entry %d outside ROM", i)
		}
		ds = append(ds, decodeDestination(r, p))
	}
	return ds, nil
}
```

`internal/triggers/probe_exits_test.go`:

```go
package triggers

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// Probe: which maps' exits or destination records lead to EXIT_TO maps.
func TestProbeExitsTo(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("EXIT_TO") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	want := map[int]bool{}
	for _, s := range strings.Split(os.Getenv("EXIT_TO"), ",") {
		v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(s, 16, 32)
		want[int(v)] = true
	}
	r := mapfmt.ROM(rom)
	for id := 0; id < 0x400; id++ {
		m, err := Decode(r, id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		for _, e := range m.Exits {
			if want[e.TargetMap] {
				fmt.Printf("exit  %04X (%d,%d) -> %04X\n", id, e.X, e.Y, e.TargetMap)
			}
		}
		for k, ev := range m.EdgeEvents {
			if ev>>8 == 0x10 && ev&0xFF < len(m.Destinations) && want[m.Destinations[ev&0xFF].TargetMap] {
				fmt.Printf("edge  %04X side %d (%04X) -> %04X\n", id, k, ev, m.Destinations[ev&0xFF].TargetMap)
			}
		}
		for _, tr := range m.Triggers {
			if tr.EventID>>8 == 0x10 && tr.EventID&0xFF < len(m.Destinations) && want[m.Destinations[tr.EventID&0xFF].TargetMap] {
				fmt.Printf("point %04X (%d,%d) %04X -> %04X\n", id, tr.X, tr.Y, tr.EventID, m.Destinations[tr.EventID&0xFF].TargetMap)
			}
		}
	}
	jt, _ := JumpTable(r)
	for i, d := range jt {
		if want[d.TargetMap] {
			fmt.Printf("jump  idx %02X -> %04X\n", i, d.TargetMap)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/triggers/probe_mapreach_test.go`:

```go
package triggers

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/bokuno"
	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// Static map-move reachability (docs/roadmap.md "RECHECK NEEDED
// 2026-11-20"): can the party reach Loane 004B — or the maps that walk
// into it, 0248 and 03D6 — from the fresh-game start, through any edge the
// ROM bytes define?
//
// The graph's nodes are maps. Edges, all read from data:
//
//   - exits: map event points whose id is 10xx (block-4 destination record)
//   - map-edge / X-button / event-chest 10xx ids
//   - op `10 xx` inside an event script: moves via the executing map's
//     block-4 destination xx (vm-semantics.md §2.8 op 10)
//   - op `11 xx` inside an event script: moves via the global jump-table
//     record xx at 3CFB00 (vm-semantics.md §2.8 op 11)
//
// An event executes with map M as context when M is reachable and the
// event is placed on M (point events, NPCs, edges, X button, chests) or
// dispatched by another event running on M. Dispatch forms followed, all
// from vm-semantics.md: gates' <0x0C tail pairs (the walker's
// GateTrue/GateFalse), syscall `0b xx` -> 0Bxx, op `32 b0 b1` -> $b0b1
// with b0 < 0x0C, `4f 16 nn` -> E+1..E+nn, selGoto/op49 tail pairs. Gate
// conditions and placement checks are taken as open, so the full graph is
// an over-approximation: an "unreachable" verdict cannot be a false
// negative, but a "reachable" one must be checked by hand — data blobs
// that misdecode as scripts (0380, 0Axx) generate bogus edges.
//
// The verified tier keeps only edges the decode machinery anchors: the
// structural triggers/exits (docs/triggers.md) and the script ops of the
// four engine-dispatched story-hook events 0B31/0800/0BF1/0846, whose
// walks the repo anchors behaviorally (parity.md §10 boot timeline: 0800
// at frame 10625, 0846 at 10694; naming.md "opening 0B31").
//
// Set MAPREACH=1 to print every edge adjacent to the reachable set, and
// MAPREACH_FROM=<hex maps> to override the seed maps.
func TestMapReach(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip()
	}
	r := mapfmt.ROM(rom)
	ops := bokuno.NewOps(rom)

	moves := scanEventMoves(t, rom, ops)
	jumpTable, err := JumpTable(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	maps := map[int]*MapTriggers{}
	for id := 0; id < 0x400; id++ {
		if m, err := Decode(r, id); err == nil {
			maps[id] = m
		}
	}

	seedMaps := []int{0x249, 0x05}
	if v := os.Getenv("MAPREACH_FROM"); v != "" {
		seedMaps = nil
		for _, s := range strings.Split(v, ",") {
			x, _ := strconv.ParseInt(s, 16, 32)
			seedMaps = append(seedMaps, int(x))
		}
	}
	// Fresh game: the engine runs the opening event 0B31 (naming.md) and
	// dispatches 0800/0BF1/0846 at fixed story points (parity.md §10).
	storyEvents := []int{0x0B31, 0x0800, 0x0BF1, 0x0846}
	story := map[int]bool{}
	for _, id := range storyEvents {
		story[id] = true
	}

	type edge struct {
		from, to int
		verified bool
		desc     string
	}
	var edges []edge
	addScriptEdges := func(mid string, m *MapTriggers, id int, verified bool) {
		mv := moves[id]
		if mv == nil {
			return
		}
		for _, xx := range mv.op10 {
			if xx >= len(m.Destinations) {
				continue
			}
			to := m.Destinations[xx].TargetMap
			edges = append(edges, edge{from: 0, to: to, verified: verified,
				desc: fmt.Sprintf("map %s event %04X op 10 %02X -> %04X", mid, id, xx, to)})
		}
		for _, xx := range mv.op11 {
			to := jumpTable[xx].TargetMap
			edges = append(edges, edge{from: 0, to: to, verified: verified,
				desc: fmt.Sprintf("event %04X op 11 %02X -> %04X", id, xx, to)})
		}
	}
	for _, mid := range sortedInts(mapKeys(maps)) {
		m := maps[mid]
		name := fmt.Sprintf("%04X", mid)
		for _, id := range storyEvents {
			addScriptEdges(name, m, id, true) // story hooks run on any current map
		}
		for _, id := range dispatchClosure(moves, placementEvents(m), storyEvents) {
			if !story[id] {
				addScriptEdges(name, m, id, false)
			}
		}
		for _, e := range m.Exits {
			edges = append(edges, edge{from: mid, to: e.TargetMap, verified: true,
				desc: fmt.Sprintf("map %04X exit (%d,%d) %04X -> %04X", mid, e.X, e.Y, e.EventID, e.TargetMap)})
		}
		for side, ev := range m.EdgeEvents {
			if ev>>8 == 0x10 && ev&0xFF < len(m.Destinations) {
				edges = append(edges, edge{from: mid, to: m.Destinations[ev&0xFF].TargetMap, verified: true,
					desc: fmt.Sprintf("map %04X edge side %d %04X -> %04X", mid, side, ev, m.Destinations[ev&0xFF].TargetMap)})
			}
		}
		if m.XButtonEvent>>8 == 0x10 && m.XButtonEvent&0xFF < len(m.Destinations) {
			edges = append(edges, edge{from: mid, to: m.Destinations[m.XButtonEvent&0xFF].TargetMap, verified: true,
				desc: fmt.Sprintf("map %04X X button %04X -> %04X", mid, m.XButtonEvent, m.Destinations[m.XButtonEvent&0xFF].TargetMap)})
		}
		for _, tr := range m.Triggers {
			if tr.EventID>>8 == 0x10 && tr.EventID&0xFF < len(m.Destinations) {
				edges = append(edges, edge{from: mid, to: m.Destinations[tr.EventID&0xFF].TargetMap, verified: true,
					desc: fmt.Sprintf("map %04X point (%d,%d) %04X -> %04X", mid, tr.X, tr.Y, tr.EventID, m.Destinations[tr.EventID&0xFF].TargetMap)})
			}
		}
		for _, c := range m.Chests {
			if c.EventID>>8 == 0x10 && c.EventID&0xFF < len(m.Destinations) {
				edges = append(edges, edge{from: mid, to: m.Destinations[c.EventID&0xFF].TargetMap, verified: true,
					desc: fmt.Sprintf("map %04X chest (%d,%d) %04X -> %04X", mid, c.X, c.Y, c.EventID, m.Destinations[c.EventID&0xFF].TargetMap)})
			}
		}
	}
	// story-hook op10 edges carry the placeholder map they were decoded
	// against; op11 edges are context-free. Fix from-maps here.
	for i := range edges {
		if edges[i].from == 0 {
			edges[i].from = -1 // "any reachable map"
		}
	}

	bfs := func(verifiedOnly bool) (map[int]bool, map[int]edge) {
		seen := map[int]bool{}
		for _, s := range seedMaps {
			seen[s] = true
		}
		parent := map[int]edge{}
		queue := append([]int{}, seedMaps...)
		for len(queue) > 0 {
			cur := queue[0]
			queue = queue[1:]
			for _, e := range edges {
				if verifiedOnly && !e.verified {
					continue
				}
				fromOK := e.from == cur || (e.from == -1 && seen[cur])
				if !fromOK || seen[e.to] {
					continue
				}
				seen[e.to] = true
				parent[e.to] = e
				queue = append(queue, e.to)
			}
		}
		return seen, parent
	}

	chain := func(want int, parent map[int]edge) string {
		var parts []string
		for m := want; !contains(seedMaps, m); m = parent[m].from {
			e := parent[m]
			if e.to == 0 && e.desc == "" {
				break
			}
			parts = append([]string{e.desc}, parts...)
		}
		return strings.Join(parts, "\n    then ")
	}

	cleanSeen, cleanParent := bfs(true)
	fullSeen, _ := bfs(false)

	if os.Getenv("MAPREACH") != "" {
		for _, e := range edges {
			if cleanSeen[e.from] || e.from == -1 && (cleanSeen[0x249] || cleanSeen[0x05]) {
				fmt.Printf("edge   v=%v %s\n", e.verified, e.desc)
			}
		}
	}

	t.Logf("verified-tier reachable map count: %d (full tier: %d)", len(cleanSeen), len(fullSeen))
	for _, want := range []struct {
		id      int
		inClean bool
		inFull  bool
		what    string
	}{
		{0x248, true, true, "world map west of Loane"},
		{0x3D6, true, true, "pass into Loane"},
		{0x4B, true, true, "Loane"},
	} {
		if cleanSeen[want.id] != want.inClean || fullSeen[want.id] != want.inFull {
			t.Errorf("map %04X (%s): reachability changed — clean=%v (want %v), full=%v (want %v)\nchain:\n  %s",
				want.id, want.what, cleanSeen[want.id], want.inClean, fullSeen[want.id], want.inFull,
				chain(want.id, cleanParent))
		}
		if cleanSeen[want.id] {
			t.Logf("map %04X (%s) reachable; chain:\n  %s", want.id, want.what, chain(want.id, cleanParent))
		}
	}
}

func contains(set []int, v int) bool {
	for _, x := range set {
		if x == v {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func mapKeys(m map[int]*MapTriggers) []int {
	var ks []int
	for k := range m {
		ks = append(ks, k)
	}
	return ks
}

func sortedInts(xs []int) []int {
	out := append([]int{}, xs...)
	sort.Ints(out)
	return out
}

// placementEvents lists the event ids map m can trigger: point events,
// placed NPCs, the four map edges, the X button and event chests.
func placementEvents(m *MapTriggers) []int {
	var ids []int
	for _, tr := range m.Triggers {
		ids = append(ids, tr.EventID)
	}
	for _, n := range m.NPCs {
		ids = append(ids, n.EventID)
	}
	ids = append(ids, m.EdgeEvents[:]...)
	ids = append(ids, m.XButtonEvent)
	for _, c := range m.Chests {
		if c.EventID != 0 {
			ids = append(ids, c.EventID)
		}
	}
	return ids
}

// evMoves is one event's static map-move and dispatch edges, collected with
// the same walk machinery as cmd/dumpevents (WalkReachable: unconditional
// jumps, skips, gate continuations and callL targets followed; gate
// conditions open).
type evMoves struct {
	op10     []int // operands xx of `10 xx`: the executing map's block-4 index
	op11     []int // operands xx of `11 xx`: the global jump-table index
	dispatch []int // event ids a tail-dispatch or call from this event can reach
}

func scanEventMoves(t *testing.T, rom []byte, ops *bokuno.Ops) map[int]*evMoves {
	res := map[int]*evMoves{}
	var work []int
	enqueue := func(id int) {
		if id <= 0 {
			return
		}
		if _, done := res[id]; done {
			return
		}
		res[id] = &evMoves{}
		if _, ok := ops.NativeRange(id); ok {
			work = append(work, id)
		}
	}
	for id := 1; id <= 0xeff; id++ {
		enqueue(id)
	}
	for id := 0x4c00; id <= 0x4cff; id++ {
		enqueue(id)
	}

	byteAt := func(addr string, plus int) (b int, ok bool) {
		var bank, a int
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(addr, "%02X:%04x", &bank, &a); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("record addr %q: %v", addr, err)
		}
		off, ok2 := bokuno.CPUToFile(bank, (a+plus)&0xffff)
		if !ok2 || off+1 >= len(rom) {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(rom[off]), true
	}

	for len(work) > 0 {
		id := work[0]
		work = work[1:]
		m := res[id]
		_, recs, _, _ := ops.WalkReachable(id)
		for _, rec := range recs {
			if rec.Kind != "cmd" {
				continue
			}
			h := strings.Fields(rec.Hex)
			hexAt := func(i int) int {
				v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(h[i], 16, 32)
				return int(v)
			}
			switch {
			case rec.Note == "op10" && len(h) == 2:
				m.op10 = append(m.op10, hexAt(1))
			case rec.Note == "mapJump" && len(h) == 2:
				m.op11 = append(m.op11, hexAt(1))
			case rec.Note == "syscall" && len(h) == 2:
				// `0b xx` enqueues word $0Bxx: event 0Bxx (vm-semantics.md §2.8).
				m.dispatch = append(m.dispatch, 0x0b00|hexAt(1))
			case rec.Note == "op32" && len(h) == 3:
				// `32 b0 b1` tail-dispatches the big-endian pair when b0 < 0x0C.
				if hexAt(1) < 0x0C {
					m.dispatch = append(m.dispatch, hexAt(1)<<8|hexAt(2))
				}
			case rec.Note == "4F_16" && len(h) == 3:
				// `4f 16 nn` tail-dispatches one of E+1..E+nn
				// (vm-semantics.md §2.5).
				for k := 1; k <= hexAt(2); k++ {
					m.dispatch = append(m.dispatch, id+k)
				}
			case rec.Note == "selGoto":
				// pairs after the opcode; a record with first byte < 0x0C
				// dispatches (b<<8)|next. The record count is not stored;
				// scan the next 16 pair slots as an over-approximation.
				for k := 0; k < 16; k++ {
					b, ok := byteAt(rec.Addr, 1+2*k)
					if !ok {
						break
					}
					if b < 0x0C {
						b2, _ := byteAt(rec.Addr, 2+2*k)
						m.dispatch = append(m.dispatch, int(b)<<8|int(b2))
					}
				}
			case strings.HasPrefix(rec.Note, "op49_") &&
				rec.Note != "op49_00_check" && rec.Note != "op49_01_bitcheck":
				// the 49-family tail is the same <0x0C pair gate; write
				// sub-ops pass through it too (vm-semantics.md §2.1).
				for _, plus := range []int{len(h), len(h) + 2} {
					if b, ok := byteAt(rec.Addr, plus); ok && b < 0x0C {
						b2, _ := byteAt(rec.Addr, plus+1)
						m.dispatch = append(m.dispatch, int(b)<<8|int(b2))
					}
				}
			}
			for _, g := range []string{rec.GateTrue, rec.GateFalse} {
				if strings.HasPrefix(g, "event ") {
					v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(g[6:], 16, 32)
					m.dispatch = append(m.dispatch, int(v))
				}
			}
		}
		for _, d := range m.dispatch {
			enqueue(d)
		}
	}
	return res
}

// dispatchClosure returns ids reachable through dispatch chains from the
// union of a map's placements and the engine story hooks.
func dispatchClosure(moves map[int]*evMoves, placed, story []int) []int {
	seen := map[int]bool{}
	var out []int
	var visit func(id int)
	visit = func(id int) {
		if seen[id] {
			return
		}
		seen[id] = true
		out = append(out, id)
		var disp []int
		if moves[id] != nil {
			disp = moves[id].dispatch
		}
		for _, d := range disp {
			visit(d)
		}
	}
	for _, id := range placed {
		visit(id)
	}
	for _, id := range story {
		visit(id)
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
package triggers

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"

	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"

// Probe: flag-conditional overlay entries per map (VAR_MAPS=hex,...).
func TestProbeVariants(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("VAR_MAPS") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	r := mapfmt.ROM(rom)
	n, maps := 0, 0
	for _, s := range strings.Split(os.Getenv("VAR_MAPS"), ",") {
		var ids []int
		if s == "all" {
			for i := 0; i < 0x400; i++ {
				ids = append(ids, i)
			}
		} else {
			v, _ := strconv.ParseInt(s, 16, 32)
			ids = []int{int(v)}
		}
		for _, id := range ids {
			m, err := Decode(r, id)
			if err != nil || len(m.Variants) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			maps++
			n += len(m.Variants)
			if s != "all" {
				for _, v := range m.Variants {
					fmt.Printf("map %04X kind %02X always=%v flag %02X [%d,%d) ptr %06X\n", id, v.Kind, v.Always, v.Flag, v.Lo, v.Hi, v.Ptr)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("%d maps with variants, %d entries\n", maps, n)
}

func TestProbeConditionalVariants(t *testing.T) {
	rom, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil || os.Getenv("CONDVAR") == "" {
		t.Skip()
	}
	maps, n := 0, 0
	for id := 0; id < 0x400; id++ {
		m, err := Decode(mapfmt.ROM(rom), id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		c := 0
		for _, v := range m.Variants {
			if !v.Always {
				c++
			}
		}
		if c > 0 {
			maps++
			n += c
			if c <= 6 {
				fmt.Printf("map %04X:", id)
				for _, v := range m.Variants {
					if !v.Always {
						fmt.Printf(" k%02X f%02X[%d,%d)", v.Kind, v.Flag, v.Lo, v.Hi)
					}
				}
				fmt.Println()
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("%d maps, %d conditional variants\n", maps, n)
}
```
