`internal/triggers/triggers.go`:

```go
// Package triggers decodes per-map movement exits and event triggers
// (doors, placed NPCs, treasure chests) from the Romancing SaGa 3 submap
// records in the extended HiROM SFC image used by the bokuno hack.
//
// Structure source: the community analysis 新バイナリ神ロダ補完/
// ツール・テキスト.zip → 解析結果（2-658氏）/サブマップ解析.txt, plus the
// AL982 supplement, byte-verified against patches/bokuno_jp.sfc for maps
// 0x02 and 0x04 (see docs/triggers.md for the evidence and the deviations
// from the community doc that the byte checks forced).
//
// Block layout of a submap record:
//
//	block 1  display header (flags2/flags3 gate optional fields)
//	block 2  placed characters (flag3 bit7), each with an event id
//	block 3  chests, screen effects, animation, X-button, map-edge
//	         events, then the event point list (terminated by 0xFF)
//	block 4  movement destinations, one 5-byte record per 10xx id
//
// The event point positions live in the map's property layer (the block-1
// prop pointer): records with flag 0x08/0x09, paired with the block-3
// event list in left-top-first order.
package triggers

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// Exit is one event point whose id is a movement event (10xx): stepping on
// the rectangle moves the party to another map.
type Exit struct {
	X, Y        int // tile of the rectangle's top-left corner
	W, H        int // rectangle size in tiles (raw size field + 1)
	EventID     int // big-endian list id, always 0x10xx
	TargetMap   int
	TargetX     int // landing tile on the target map
	TargetY     int
	Facing      int // 0-3, low bits of the destination flag byte
	DestFlags   byte
	Music       int // valid when MusicChange
	MusicChange bool
	Hide        bool // character hidden during the transition
}

// Trigger is one event point whose id is a native event (NPC spots, doors
// with scripts, map-specific encounters).
type Trigger struct {
	X, Y    int
	W, H    int
	EventID int // big-endian list id; native event id space
}

// NPC is one placed character with an event id (block 2). Event ids are
// little-endian in this block; 0x2000 recurs on battle-placed characters.
type NPC struct {
	X, Y    int
	Facing  int
	Graphic int
	EventID int
	Quality int // 性質 16-bit field
	// Judged mirrors flag4 bit6 (設置判定): when true, the engine runs the
	// placement gate before spawning (C0:4A7D-4A9A via $8E); when false,
	// the NPC spawns unconditionally. PlaceID/PlaceLo are flag bit5's
	// placement-check bytes: at map load the NPC is spawned only while the
	// 2-bit value of WRAM flag PlaceID lies in [PlaceLo>>4,
	// (PlaceLo&0x0F)+1) (fetched from $7EF46A+id/2 via C0:370D, or the
	// 0Cxx/4Cxx variants $5AB044/$5AE004). Decode does not apply the gate
	// - it depends on runtime flag state - but the bytes are exported so
	// consumers can. PlaceID/PlaceLo inherit like the other fields; the
	// zero value means no placement check appeared in the block before
	// this entry. Judged is per-entry, never inherited.
	Judged  bool
	PlaceID int
	PlaceLo int
}

// Chest is one treasure chest (block 3, flag3 bit4).
type Chest struct {
	X, Y int
	// Flags bits 6-7 pick the layer buffer the chest object stamps
	// into ($D2D7 + 2*(Flags>>6), FF:1D0F); bits 2-3 == 0x08 mark an
	// event chest.
	Flags      int
	EventID    int // event chests
	ContentID  int // item chests
	OpenFlagID int // bit index into the flag array at $F4EA (FF:1D37)
}

// Destination is one raw block-4 movement record, and one row of the
// global op-0x11 table.
type Destination struct {
	TargetMap   int
	TargetX     int
	TargetY     int
	Facing      int
	DestFlags   byte
	Music       int
	MusicChange bool
	Hide        bool
}

// gfxScriptTable is FF:A6CF, the graphics script pointers (bank FF).
const gfxScriptTable = 0x3FA6CF

// screenEffectByOp maps a graphics script's first byte to the screen
// effect it selects (FF:9B2B-9B8F); later list entries override earlier.
var screenEffectByOp = map[byte]int{0xFF: 1, 0xFE: 2, 0xFD: 3, 0xFC: 7, 0xFB: 8, 0xFA: 0x0A, 0xF9: 0x0B, 0xF8: 0x0D, 0xF7: 0x0F, 0xF6: 0x10}

// screenEffect returns the screen effect the graphics list selects.
func screenEffect(r mapfmt.ROM, anims []GfxAnim) int {
	effect := 0
	for _, g := range anims {
		pi := gfxScriptTable + (g.Script-1)*2
		ptr := int(r[pi]) | int(r[pi+1])<<8
		if e, ok := screenEffectByOp[r[0x3F0000+ptr]]; ok {
			effect = e
		}
	}
	return effect
}

// GfxAnim is one flag3-bit-2 entry (see MapTriggers.GfxAnims).
type GfxAnim struct {
	Chip   int `json:"chip"`
	Script int `json:"script"`
}

// Screen is a map's PPU screen setup (see MapTriggers.Screen).
type Screen struct {
	Main   int `json:"main"`
	Sub    int `json:"sub"`
	Select int `json:"select"`
	Math   int `json:"math"`
	Fixed  int `json:"fixed"`
	Flag   int `json:"flag"`
	Lo     int `json:"lo"`
	Hi     int `json:"hi"`
}

// TileAnimation is one flag2-bit-1 entry: the animated object id, the
// animation kind ($D14A: low 7 bits index FF:1EF5/FF:1F04, bit 7
// staggers the timers), and the script step at which sound Sound plays
// ($D14B/$D14C, FF:16C1).
type TileAnimation struct {
	Object, Kind, SoundStep, Sound int
}

// MapTriggers is the decoded trigger data for one map.
type MapTriggers struct {
	ID         int
	Offset     int // file offset of the submap record
	NameID     byte
	Width      int // tiles
	Height     int
	Exits      []Exit
	Triggers   []Trigger
	NPCs       []NPC
	Chests     []Chest
	EdgeEvents [4]int // north, south, west, east; native ids
	// Scroll is the flag2-bit-7 pair $D976/$D977 (C0:40E4): $D977 bits
	// 0-1 a scroll mode (1, 3 skip the drift setup, C0:40ED), bit 6 BG2
	// drift with x rate FF:2A98[$D977 & 0C] when $D976 & 0C (bit 3
	// negates) and y rate FF:2A98[($D976 & 3)*4] when $D976 & 30 (bit 5
	// negates); $D976 bit 6 a slower BG2 parallax while walking (C0:8478).
	Scroll    [2]int
	HasScroll bool
	// Type is the map type $D2D7: bits 1-4 of the flag2-bit-0 word's
	// first byte ($D2F6, C0:3D9A), 0 without it. C0:A3C7 runs a special
	// setup for types 1 (FF:6806), 2, 3 and 8.
	Type int
	// GfxAnims is the flag3-bit-2 list: each entry runs graphics
	// script Script (1-based index into the FF:A6CF pointer table) on
	// the tile graphics of chip Chip. A script whose first byte is
	// FB-FF instead selects a screen effect ($D77B, FF:9B57-9B8F).
	GfxAnims []GfxAnim
	// GfxAnimsOnce: count bit 7. The scripts' first step is installed at
	// load and the per-frame count ($E45A) is cleared (C0:407D).
	GfxAnimsOnce bool
	// Effect is the screen effect ($D77B, run each field frame from
	// C0:DEEC) the list selects, 0 for none; 3 is the BG3 horizontal
	// wave (C0:E162).
	Effect int
	// Screen is the flag3-bit-4 block ($D009-$D00D -> $212C/$212D/
	// $2130/$2131/$2132, C0:3F55 and C0:3FCB): main and sub screen
	// layers, colour-math select and enable, fixed colour. With Flag >= 0
	// it applies only while that vanilla flag nibble is in [Lo, Hi);
	// otherwise, and on maps without the block, the screen is 17/17 with
	// no colour math. nil when absent.
	Screen *Screen
	// Animations is the flag2-bit-1 list ($D148/$D149, FF:1C2F): objects
	// the composer stamps with one of these ids get a tile-animation
	// entry (FF:1695 restamps object id + the script byte each step).
	Animations []TileAnimation
	// Slope is the $D2F7 bit-6 byte ($D2FB, C0:44C0): bit 6 slants
	// north/south steps, bit 5 west/east steps, bit 7 picks the other
	// diagonal, bit 0 the slope kind (C0:8090-829B); -1 when absent.
	Slope        int
	XButtonEvent int
	// ChestObject is the closed-chest object id ($D0ED); an opened chest
	// stamps ChestObject+1 (FF:1D03-1D0B).
	ChestObject int
	// EncounterPartyBase is the flag2-0x20 section's third byte: the map
	// loader stores it in $D2FE (C0:42B3, 0 when the byte is absent,
	// C0:428B) and the bump copies it to $1308, whose high nibble the
	// encounter party term adds (C2:16B0, docs/field-monsters.md
	// "Encounter composition").
	EncounterPartyBase int
	// Variants are the flag-conditional overlay lists (flag2 bit4), in
	// the order the loader applies them after the base map.
	Variants []Variant
	// Destinations is block 4 verbatim; Exits reference it by index.
	Destinations []Destination
	// Warnings record structural oddities met while decoding; an empty
	// list means the record walked cleanly end to end.
	Warnings []string
}

const (
	maxListEntries   = 256
	maxPropSize      = 0x400 // sanity bound for one property chunk
	propTailBytes    = 4     // skipped after each property chunk (unverified)
	destRecordSize   = 5
	jumpTableAddr    = 0x3CFB00 // global op-0x11 destination table
	jumpTableEntries = 256
)

// ErrZeroed reports a submap record the patch zeroed out.
var ErrZeroed = fmt.Errorf("submap record is zeroed")

func isZeroed(r mapfmt.ROM, off int) bool {
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if off+i >= len(r) {
			break
		}
		if r[off+i] != 0 {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// Decode decodes map id's triggers, exits and placed characters.
func Decode(r mapfmt.ROM, id int) (*MapTriggers, error) {
	off, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if isZeroed(r, off) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w at %06X", ErrZeroed, off)
	}
	m := &MapTriggers{ID: id, Offset: off}
	p := off

	flag1 := int(r[off])
	p++
	p += 3 // layer 1
	if flag1&0x40 != 0 {
		p += 3 // layer 2
	}
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		p += 3 // layer 3
	}
	prop := snesToFile(r, p)
	p += 3
	p += 2 // chipset set, palette set
	if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
		p += 2 // two undocumented bytes after the palette set
	}
	p++    // object config
	p += 2 // display position
	m.Width = int(r[p]) + 1
	m.Height = int(r[p+1]) + 1
	p += 2
	m.NameID = r[p]
	p++
	p++ // 禁止操作
	flag2, flag3 := int(r[p]), int(r[p+1])
	p += 2

	ext := 0 // $D2F7: the flag2-bit0 block's second byte (C0:3D88-3D93)
	if flag2&0x01 != 0 {
		m.Type = int(r[p]) >> 1 & 0x0F // $D2D7 (C0:3D9A)
		ext = int(r[p+1])
		p += 2
	}
	if flag2&0x02 != 0 {
		n := int(r[p])
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			e := p + 1 + 4*i
			m.Animations = append(m.Animations, TileAnimation{Object: int(r[e]), Kind: int(r[e+1]), SoundStep: int(r[e+2]), Sound: int(r[e+3])})
		}
		p += 1 + 4*n
	}

	if flag3&0x80 != 0 {
		p = m.decodeCharacters(r, p)
	}

	var pointIDs []int
	p, pointIDs = m.decodeBlock3(r, p, flag2, flag3, ext)

	// The edge and X-button ids also reference block 4 when they are 10xx.
	var allIDs []int
	allIDs = append(allIDs, pointIDs...)
	allIDs = append(allIDs, m.EdgeEvents[:]...)
	if m.XButtonEvent>>8 == 0x10 {
		allIDs = append(allIDs, m.XButtonEvent)
	}
	m.Destinations = decodeDestinations(r, p, block4End(r, off, p, allIDs))
	if err := m.decodeProperty(r, prop, pointIDs); err != nil {
		m.warn("%v", err)
	}
	return m, nil
}

// block4End bounds block 4. The record has no length field: the tightest
// bound is the next record start in the submap table, but unrelated table
// entries can alias into the middle of a record (e.g. maps 0x3CF/0x3E2
// point into map 0x04's block 4), so the destinations the event list
// references always widen the bound.
func block4End(r mapfmt.ROM, off, block4 int, ids []int) int {
	end := off + recordSize(r, off)
	needed := block4
	for _, id := range ids {
		if id>>8 == 0x10 && id&0xFF >= (needed-block4)/destRecordSize {
			needed = block4 + (id&0xFF+1)*destRecordSize
		}
	}
	if needed > end {
		return needed
	}
	return end
}

func (m *MapTriggers) warn(format string, args ...any) {
	m.Warnings = append(m.Warnings, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
}

// recordSize returns the byte length of the submap record that starts at
// off: the distance to the next non-empty record in the submap table, or
// the ROM end. The records are variable length with no size field, so this
// is only a bound for block 4, not an exact size.
func recordSize(r mapfmt.ROM, off int) int {
	next := len(r)
	for id := 0; id < 1024; id++ {
		o, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
		if err != nil || o <= off {
			continue
		}
		if isZeroed(r, o) {
			continue
		}
		if o < next {
			next = o
		}
	}
	return next - off
}

func snesToFile(r mapfmt.ROM, off int) int {
	v := int(r[off]) | int(r[off+1])<<8 | int(r[off+2])<<16
	if v == 0xFFFFFF {
		return -1
	}
	f, err := r.ToFile(v)
	if err != nil {
		return -1
	}
	return f
}

// decodeCharacters walks block 2 with the engine's field semantics
// (disassembled 2026-11-16, C0:3E07-3E82): every entry starts from the
// save set - the values the last entry whose flag had bit0 set stored
// aside (JSR $4A3D restores them at the loop top, JSR $4A02 stores them
// on bit0) - not from the previous entry. Fields the entry carries
// overwrite the restored values; a field carried by neither reads as
// zero. flag bit0 is therefore a save marker, not an inherit marker: a
// field an entry carries does NOT reach later entries unless that entry
// also has bit0. The list ends with a flag byte that has bit7 set.
//
// The zero-initialized save set approximates the engine's, which begins
// each block from WRAM leftovers ($B904-$B90D) of earlier loads - a
// runtime value no static decode can recover. Every entry with flag bit6
// set (Judged) also passes the placement gate before spawning (see
// NPC.PlaceID); the gate's outcome is runtime flag state, so the decoded
// list is the record's placement list, and entries can legitimately share
// coordinates (map 0x249 stacks 12).
func (m *MapTriggers) decodeCharacters(r mapfmt.ROM, p int) int {
	var saved NPC
	for p < len(r) {
		flag4 := int(r[p])
		p++
		if flag4&0x80 != 0 {
			return p
		}
		c := saved
		c.Judged = flag4&0x40 != 0
		if flag4&0x20 != 0 {
			c.PlaceID, c.PlaceLo = int(r[p]), int(r[p+1])
			p += 2
		}
		if flag4&0x10 != 0 {
			c.X, c.Y, c.Facing = int(r[p]), int(r[p+1]), int(r[p+2])
			p += 3
		}
		if flag4&0x08 != 0 {
			c.Graphic = int(r[p])
			p++
		}
		if flag4&0x04 != 0 {
			c.EventID = int(r[p]) | int(r[p+1])<<8 // little-endian
			p += 2
		}
		if flag4&0x02 != 0 {
			c.Quality = int(r[p]) | int(r[p+1])<<8 // little-endian
			p += 2
		}
		if flag4&0x01 != 0 {
			saved = c
		}
		m.NPCs = append(m.NPCs, c)
	}
	m.warn("character block ran past the end of the record")
	return p
}

// Variant is one entry of a map's flag-conditional overlay lists
// (flag2 bit4, parsed by the loader at C0:42C6-4476 after the base
// layers and the overlay RLE). A selector byte names the lists present;
// each list is a count byte (bit7 = every entry unconditional, low 7
// bits = entries) and per entry an optional [flag index, range] pair
// plus a 24-bit pointer. A conditional entry applies when the vanilla
// flag nibble ($F46A, C0:370D) satisfies Lo <= value < Hi.
type Variant struct {
	// Kind is the selector bit: 0x10/0x20/0x40 decode an extra layer
	// into the layer buffers $D2DD/$D2DB/$D2D9 (JSL FF:0670, the base
	// composer, so its chip properties stamp the attr grid); 0x80 runs
	// a property region and its overlay RLE (JSL FF:0674/0678).
	Kind   int
	Always bool
	Flag   int
	Lo, Hi int
	Ptr    int // file offset, -1 when not cartridge ROM
}

// Applies reports whether the loader decodes v under the given vanilla
// flag nibble reader.
func (v Variant) Applies(flag func(idx int) int) bool {
	if v.Always {
		return true
	}
	f := flag(v.Flag)
	return f >= v.Lo && f < v.Hi
}

// FreshLoad lists what the loader adds after the base map in a fresh
// game, as mapfmt.AttrGridVariants takes it: every chest closed and the
// unconditional variants (layers in loader order, then property
// regions). Conditional counts the variants left out because they
// depend on runtime flags.
func (m *MapTriggers) FreshLoad() (chests []mapfmt.ChestStamp, layers, props []int, conditional int) {
	for _, c := range m.Chests {
		chests = append(chests, mapfmt.ChestStamp{X: c.X, Y: c.Y, Object: m.ChestObject, Layer: c.Flags >> 6})
	}
	for _, v := range m.Variants {
		switch {
		case !v.Always:
			conditional++
		case v.Kind == 0x80:
			props = append(props, v.Ptr)
		default:
			layers = append(layers, v.Ptr)
		}
	}
	return chests, layers, props, conditional
}

// decodeVariants parses the flag2-bit4 block and returns the offset
// after it. The engine loops DEC count / AND #$7F / BNE, so a count of
// n entries runs n times.
func (m *MapTriggers) decodeVariants(r mapfmt.ROM, p int) int {
	sel := int(r[p])
	p++
	for _, kind := range []int{0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80} {
		if sel&kind == 0 {
			continue
		}
		cnt := int(r[p])
		p++
		for {
			v := Variant{Kind: kind, Always: cnt&0x80 != 0}
			if !v.Always {
				v.Flag = int(r[p])
				v.Lo, v.Hi = int(r[p+1])>>4, int(r[p+1])&0x0F+1
				p += 2
			}
			v.Ptr = snesToFile(r, p)
			p += 3
			m.Variants = append(m.Variants, v)
			cnt = (cnt - 1) & 0xFF
			if cnt&0x7F == 0 {
				break
			}
		}
	}
	return p
}

// decodeBlock3 walks the event block and returns the file offset after it
// plus the event point list ids (big-endian, high byte 0x10 marks movement
// events whose xx indexes block 4). The field order is the loader's
// (C0:3DFD-4626): flag3 bits 6-1, then flag2 bits 7-3, then the $D2F7
// blocks (ext) with flag2 bit2's two bytes between ext bits 7 and 5.
func (m *MapTriggers) decodeBlock3(r mapfmt.ROM, p, flag2, flag3, ext int) (int, []int) {
	if flag3&0x40 != 0 {
		p = m.decodeChests(r, p)
	}
	if flag3&0x20 != 0 {
		p += 5 // display-range masks
	}
	if flag3&0x10 != 0 { // screen block (C0:3F55-3F7E)
		sc := &Screen{Main: int(r[p]) & 0x1F, Flag: -1}
		b := int(r[p])
		p++
		if b&0x20 != 0 {
			sc.Flag, sc.Lo, sc.Hi = int(r[p]), int(r[p+1])>>4, int(r[p+1])&0x0F+1
			p += 2
		}
		sc.Sub, sc.Select, sc.Math, sc.Fixed = int(r[p]), int(r[p+1]), int(r[p+2]), int(r[p+3])
		p += 4
		m.Screen = sc
	}
	if flag3&0x08 != 0 {
		p += 1 + 2*int(r[p])
	}
	if flag3&0x04 != 0 { // graphics animations (C0:4054, FF:9935)
		n := int(r[p]) & 0x7F
		m.GfxAnimsOnce = r[p]&0x80 != 0
		p++
		for i := 0; i < n && p+1 < len(r); i++ {
			w := int(r[p]) | int(r[p+1])<<8
			p += 2
			g := GfxAnim{Chip: w & 0x3FF, Script: w>>10 + 1}
			if g.Script == 0x40 {
				g.Script = int(r[p]) + 1
				p++
			}
			m.GfxAnims = append(m.GfxAnims, g)
		}
		m.Effect = screenEffect(r, m.GfxAnims)
	}
	if flag3&0x02 != 0 {
		m.XButtonEvent = int(r[p])<<8 | int(r[p+1])
		p += 2
	}
	if flag2&0x80 != 0 { // scroll setup $D976/$D977 (C0:40DB)
		m.Scroll = [2]int{int(r[p]), int(r[p+1])}
		m.HasScroll = true
		p += 2
	}
	if flag2&0x40 != 0 {
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			m.EdgeEvents[i] = int(r[p])<<8 | int(r[p+1])
			p += 2
		}
	}
	if flag2&0x20 != 0 {
		p++ // default battle background ($D2FC)
		if flag3&0x01 == 0 {
			m.EncounterPartyBase = int(r[p+1]) // $D2FD at p, $D2FE at p+1
			p += 2
		}
	}
	if flag2&0x10 != 0 {
		p = m.decodeVariants(r, p)
	}
	if flag2&0x08 != 0 {
		p += 3 // transition effect and sounds
	}
	p = m.skipExtBlocks(r, p, flag2, ext)

	ids := make([]int, 0, 8)
	for p+1 < len(r) && r[p] != 0xFF {
		ids = append(ids, int(r[p])<<8|int(r[p+1]))
		p += 2
		if len(ids) >= maxListEntries {
			m.warn("event point list did not terminate within %d entries", maxListEntries)
			return p, ids
		}
	}
	p++ // 0xFF terminator
	return p, ids
}

// skipExtBlocks steps over the blocks the loader reads after flag2
// bit3 (C0:44B9-4626). flag2 bit2's two bytes ($0033, C0:4543) sit
// between ext bits 7 and 5; the walk formerly read them right after the
// X-button event, two bytes early on every map with flag2 bit2 (024E,
// 00F0: engine variant selector at +52/+4A, walk at +54/+4C).
func (m *MapTriggers) skipExtBlocks(r mapfmt.ROM, p, flag2, ext int) int {
	m.Slope = -1
	if ext&0x40 != 0 {
		m.Slope = int(r[p]) // $D2FB
		p++
	}
	if ext&0x80 != 0 {
		p += 2 // $D00C/$D00D, then 2-byte entries until a 00 byte
		for r[p] != 0 {
			p += 2
		}
		p++
	}
	if flag2&0x04 != 0 {
		p += 2
	}
	if ext&0x20 != 0 {
		n := int(r[p]) // DEC $92 / BNE: n entries
		p++
		for {
			p += 2
			b := r[p]
			p++
			if b&0x80 != 0 {
				p += 2
			}
			n = (n - 1) & 0xFF
			if n == 0 {
				break
			}
		}
	}
	if ext&0x10 != 0 {
		p += 3
	}
	if ext&0x08 != 0 {
		p++ // $E2D8, then groups of 4-byte entries: FF ends a group, FE the list
		for {
			b := r[p]
			p++
			if b < 0xFE {
				p += 3
				continue
			}
			if b == 0xFE {
				break
			}
		}
	}
	return p
}

// decodeChests walks the treasure block. Chests with content flag bit2-3
// == 0x08 carry a 2-byte event id (little-endian) instead of a content id.
func (m *MapTriggers) decodeChests(r mapfmt.ROM, p int) int {
	// Engine layout (C0:3E88-3EEE): count, the closed-chest object id
	// ($D0ED; the opened chest is id+1, FF:1D03), one more byte ($D0EE),
	// then per chest: flag, content (absent when flag&0x0C == 0x08), open
	// flag, x, y, and an event word (XBA, high byte first) when
	// flag&0x0C == 0x08. The former 7/8-byte stride re-read the two
	// header bytes per chest, so every multi-chest map desynced the rest
	// of the record walk.
	n := int(r[p])
	m.ChestObject = int(r[p+1])
	p += 3
	for i := 0; i < n && p < len(r); i++ {
		c := Chest{Flags: int(r[p])}
		p++
		event := c.Flags&0x0C == 0x08
		if !event {
			c.ContentID = int(r[p])
			p++
		}
		c.OpenFlagID = int(r[p])
		c.X, c.Y = int(r[p+1]), int(r[p+2])
		p += 3
		if event {
			c.EventID = int(r[p])<<8 | int(r[p+1])
			p += 2
		}
		m.Chests = append(m.Chests, c)
	}
	return p
}

// decodeDestinations reads block 4: 5-byte movement records filling the
// rest of the record.
func decodeDestinations(r mapfmt.ROM, p, end int) []Destination {
	var ds []Destination
	for p+destRecordSize <= end {
		ds = append(ds, decodeDestination(r, p))
		p += destRecordSize
	}
	return ds
}

func decodeDestination(r mapfmt.ROM, p int) Destination {
	b := Destination{DestFlags: r[p]}
	f := int(r[p])
	b.Facing = f & 0x03
	b.MusicChange = f&0x04 != 0
	b.Hide = f&0x08 != 0
	w := int(r[p+1]) | int(r[p+2])<<8 // little-endian
	b.Music = w >> 10
	b.TargetMap = w & 0x3FF
	b.TargetX, b.TargetY = int(r[p+3]), int(r[p+4])
	return b
}

// decodeProperty walks the property layer chunks and pairs the 0x08/0x09
// event point rectangles with the pending list ids in left-top-first
// order, as the community doc describes for the engine.
func (m *MapTriggers) decodeProperty(r mapfmt.ROM, prop int, ids []int) error {
	if prop < 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("map has no property pointer")
	}
	rects, err := propEventPoints(r, prop, len(ids))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var inBounds []propRect
	for _, rc := range rects {
		if rc.X < m.Width && rc.Y < m.Height {
			inBounds = append(inBounds, rc)
		}
	}
	if len(inBounds) < len(ids) {
		m.warn("property layer has %d in-bounds event points for %d list entries", len(inBounds), len(ids))
	}
	sort.Slice(inBounds, func(i, j int) bool {
		if inBounds[i].Y != inBounds[j].Y {
			return inBounds[i].Y < inBounds[j].Y
		}
		return inBounds[i].X < inBounds[j].X
	})
	for i, id := range ids {
		if i >= len(inBounds) {
			break
		}
		rc := inBounds[i]
		if id>>8 == 0x10 {
			xx := id & 0xFF
			if xx >= len(m.Destinations) {
				continue
			}
			d := m.Destinations[xx]
			m.Exits = append(m.Exits, Exit{
				X: rc.X, Y: rc.Y, W: rc.W, H: rc.H,
				EventID:     id,
				TargetMap:   d.TargetMap,
				TargetX:     d.TargetX,
				TargetY:     d.TargetY,
				Facing:      d.Facing,
				DestFlags:   d.DestFlags,
				Music:       d.Music,
				MusicChange: d.MusicChange,
				Hide:        d.Hide,
			})
		} else {
			m.Triggers = append(m.Triggers, Trigger{
				X: rc.X, Y: rc.Y, W: rc.W, H: rc.H, EventID: id,
			})
		}
	}
	return nil
}

type propRect struct {
	X, Y, W, H int
}

// propEventPoints collects the 0x08/0x09 event point rectangles from the
// property layer: a sequence of chunks, each [u16 size][records][4-byte
// tail]. A record is [flag][X][Y][size], 1 size byte when the flag is odd
// (hi nibble X span, lo nibble Y span), 2 bytes (X, Y) when even.
//
// The layer's end is not stored anywhere. Neighboring maps' property
// pointers alias into each other's layers (map 0x6B's layer starts at map
// 0x04's third chunk), so the tightest bound can truncate the walk. When
// the first walk collects fewer in-bounds rectangles than the event list
// needs, the walk retries with the next larger property pointer as bound.
func propEventPoints(r mapfmt.ROM, prop int, want int) ([]propRect, error) {
	bound := nextProp(r, prop)
	for attempt := 0; attempt < 8; attempt++ {
		rects, err := propWalk(r, prop, bound)
		if err != nil {
			return rects, err
		}
		if len(rects) >= want {
			return rects, nil
		}
		next := nextProp(r, bound)
		if next == bound {
			return rects, nil
		}
		bound = next
	}
	return propWalk(r, prop, bound)
}

func propWalk(r mapfmt.ROM, prop, bound int) ([]propRect, error) {
	var rects []propRect
	p := prop
	for p+2 <= bound {
		size := int(r[p]) | int(r[p+1])<<8
		if size == 0 || size > maxPropSize || p+2+size+propTailBytes > bound {
			break
		}
		recEnd := p + 2 + size
		q := p + 2
		for q < recEnd {
			flag := int(r[q])
			if q+3 > recEnd {
				return rects, fmt.Errorf("property chunk at %06X ends mid-record", p)
			}
			x, y := int(r[q+1]), int(r[q+2])
			var w, h int
			if flag&1 != 0 {
				if q+4 > recEnd {
					return rects, fmt.Errorf("property chunk at %06X ends mid-record", p)
				}
				w, h = int(r[q+3]>>4)+1, int(r[q+3]&0x0F)+1
				q += 4
			} else {
				if q+5 > recEnd {
					return rects, fmt.Errorf("property chunk at %06X ends mid-record", p)
				}
				w, h = int(r[q+3])+1, int(r[q+4])+1
				q += 5
			}
			if flag == 0x08 || flag == 0x09 {
				rects = append(rects, propRect{X: x, Y: y, W: w, H: h})
			}
		}
		p = recEnd + propTailBytes
	}
	return rects, nil
}

// nextProp returns the smallest property pointer larger than after, or
// after itself when none exists.
func nextProp(r mapfmt.ROM, after int) int {
	best := after
	for id := 0; id < 1024; id++ {
		off, err := mapfmt.SubmapDataOffset(r, id)
		if err != nil || isZeroed(r, off) {
			continue
		}
		flag1 := int(r[off])
		q := off + 1 + 3
		if flag1&0x40 != 0 {
			q += 3
		}
		if flag1&0x20 != 0 {
			q += 3
		}
		other := snesToFile(r, q)
		if other > after && (best == after || other < best) {
			best = other
		}
	}
	return best
}

// ProbeZeroed reports whether the record at off begins with 32 zero bytes.
// Debug helper for the dump tooling; not part of the decoded data model.

```

`internal/triggers/triggers_test.go`:

```go
package triggers

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"saga3/internal/mapfmt"
)

// Synthetic fixture: an in-memory ROM with one submap record (table id 5)
// exercising every block the decoder walks, and the global jump table.
// Table id 6 holds the next record so recordSize has a real bound — its
// start lands 111 bytes in, INSIDE the block-4 span, which is the aliasing
// case block4End exists for (cf. maps 0x3CF/0x3E2 aliasing map 0x04): the
// event list references destination 2, whose bytes are record 2's first 5
// header bytes, so the widened bound must reach past the next record.
const (
	fxRecord  = 0x382000
	fxRecord2 = 0x38206F // fxRecord + 111: next record starts inside block 4's span
	fxProp    = 0x383000
)

func newFixtureROM() mapfmt.ROM {
	rom := make(mapfmt.ROM, 0x800000)
	setEntry := func(id, file int) { // the hack's table at 5A:6A50
		v := file + 0xC00000
		rom[0x5A6A50+id*3] = byte(v)
		rom[0x5A6A50+id*3+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		rom[0x5A6A50+id*3+2] = byte(v >> 16)
	}
	setEntry(5, fxRecord)
	setEntry(6, fxRecord2)

	// Map record (map 5), 64x32 tiles. flag2 0x53: type/ext block,
	// animations, variants, edge events. flag3 0xD6: characters, chests,
	// screen block, graphics animations, X-button.
	rec := []byte{
		0xC2,             // flag1: layer 2 present, no layer 3
		0x00, 0x80, 0xF3, // layer 1 pointer (unused)
		0x00, 0x81, 0xF3, // layer 2 pointer (unused)
		0x00, 0x30, 0xF8, // property pointer -> fxProp
		0x22, 0x11, 0x33, // chipset, palette set, object config
		0x00, 0x00, // display position
		0x3F, 0x1F, // size: 64 x 32 tiles
		0x42, // map name id
		0x20, // 禁止操作
		0x53, // flag2
		0xD6, // flag3
		// flag2 bit0 type/ext block: type byte + ext selector
		0x2A, // $D2F6: map type = 0x2A>>1 & 0x0F = 5
		0x40, // ext bit6: one slope byte follows the flag2 walk
		// flag2 bit1 animation list: one 4-byte object entry
		0x01, 0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF,
		// block 2: one character, then the 0xFF end flag
		0x1C,             // flag4: position, graphic, event
		0x10, 0x20, 0x40, // X, Y, facing
		0x2A,       // graphic
		0x01, 0x05, // event id 0x0501, little-endian
		0xFF,
		// block 3 chests: one item chest, one event chest
		0x02,       // chest count
		0xBB, 0x00, // closed-chest object id ($D0ED), $D0EE byte
		0x00,       // chest 1 flags: item chest
		0xCC,       // content id
		0xDD,       // open flag id
		0x30, 0x40, // X, Y
		0x48,       // chest 2 flags: event chest (bits 2-3 == 0x08), layer bits 6-7 = 1
		0xEE,       // open flag id
		0x50, 0x60, // X, Y
		0x07, 0x02, // event id 0x0702, big-endian
		// flag3 bit4 screen block
		0x37,       // main screen layers 0x17, gate bit5 set: flag pair follows
		0x15, 0x34, // flag 0x15, window byte 0x34: applies in [3, 5)
		0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, // sub, colour-math select, enable, fixed colour
		// flag3 bit2 graphics animations: 2 entries, count bit7 (once)
		0x82,
		0x55, 0x01, // word 0x0155: chip 0x155, script 1
		0x01, 0xFC, // word 0xFC01: chip 1, script field 0x40 -> escape byte
		0x2F, // script = 0x2F + 1 = 0x30
		// flag3 bit1 X-button event 0x0560, big-endian
		0x05, 0x60,
		// flag2 bit6 map-edge events N/S/W/E, big-endian
		0x10, 0x00,
		0x20, 0x00,
		0x20, 0x00,
		0x10, 0x01,
		// flag2 bit4 variant lists: kinds 0x10 (2 conditional), 0x20 (1
		// always), 0x80 (1 always)
		0xB0,
		0x02,                         // kind 0x10: 2 conditional entries
		0x05, 0x34, 0x00, 0x60, 0xF8, // flag 5, [3,5), snes F8:6000
		0x06, 0x8F, 0x10, 0x60, 0xF8, // flag 6, [8,16), snes F8:6010
		0x81,             // kind 0x20: 1 always entry
		0x20, 0x60, 0xF8, // snes F8:6020
		0x81,             // kind 0x80: 1 always entry
		0x30, 0x60, 0xF8, // snes F8:6030
		0x55, // ext bit6 slope byte ($D2FB)
		// event point list: movement 1001, movement 1002, native 054E,
		// terminator. The ascending 10xx pair 1001 then 1002 makes the
		// block-4 bound depend on both ids (the second widens a bound the
		// first already widened).
		0x10, 0x01,
		0x10, 0x02,
		0x05, 0x4E,
		0xFF,
		// block 4: destination 0 -> map 2 at (17,18) with music change;
		// destination 1 -> map 7 at (33,34). Destination 2 lies past the
		// next record's start and decodes from record 2's header bytes.
		0x04, 0x02, 0x00, 0x11, 0x12,
		0x00, 0x07, 0x00, 0x21, 0x22,
	}
	copy(rom[fxRecord:], rec) // 111 bytes: the record proper

	// Next record header. Its first 5 bytes are destination 2 (flags 0xC2,
	// little-endian word 0x00,0x80 = 0x8000 -> map 0, music 32, X F3, Y 00);
	// bytes 7-9 are its property pointer (00 32 F8 -> file 0x383200), which
	// bounds the property walk.
	next := []byte{0xC2, 0x00, 0x80, 0xF3, 0x00, 0x81, 0xF3, 0x00, 0x32, 0xF8}
	copy(rom[fxRecord2:], next)

	// Property layer: one chunk, walk order ≠ sorted order, plus one
	// out-of-bounds point the in-bounds filter must drop. Sorted
	// (Y then X): (12,3), (4,9) 2x3, (20,25) — pairing ids 1001, 1002,
	// 054E in that order.
	prop := []byte{
		0x10, 0x00, // chunk size: 16 bytes of records
		0x09, 0x64, 0x02, 0x00, // (100, 2) 1x1 — X >= width 64: filtered
		0x09, 0x04, 0x09, 0x12, // (4, 9), size byte 0x12: 2x3
		0x09, 0x0C, 0x03, 0x00, // (12, 3) 1x1
		0x09, 0x14, 0x19, 0x00, // (20, 25) 1x1
		0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // chunk tail
		0xFF, 0xFF, // implausible next chunk size: stop
	}
	copy(rom[fxProp:], prop)

	// Graphics script table (FF:A6CF): script 1 -> ptr 0x0100, script 0x30
	// -> ptr 0x0200. Script 1's first byte 0xFB selects screen effect 8;
	// script 0x30's 0x42 selects none, so the later entry must not clear
	// the earlier one's effect.
	rom[0x3FA6CF], rom[0x3FA6D0] = 0x00, 0x01
	rom[0x3FA6CF+0x5E], rom[0x3FA6CF+0x5F] = 0x00, 0x02
	rom[0x3F0100] = 0xFB
	rom[0x3F0200] = 0x42

	// Global jump table: entry 3 -> map 0x123 at (42,43), flags 0x86
	// (facing 2, music change); entry 5 -> map 0x064 at (64,65), flags
	// 0x88 (hide, no music change), word 0xC464 (music 49).
	j := 0x3CFB00 + 3*5
	rom[j] = 0x86
	rom[j+1], rom[j+2] = 0x23, 0x01 // word 0x0123
	rom[j+3], rom[j+4] = 0x2A, 0x2B
	k := 0x3CFB00 + 5*5
	rom[k] = 0x88
	rom[k+1], rom[k+2] = 0x64, 0xC4 // word 0xC464
	rom[k+3], rom[k+4] = 0x40, 0x41

	// Table id 7 points at 32 zero bytes: Decode must report ErrZeroed.
	setEntry(7, 0x384000)
	return rom
}

func decodeFixture(t *testing.T) *MapTriggers {
	t.Helper()
	m, err := Decode(newFixtureROM(), 5)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Decode map 5: %v", err)
	}
	return m
}

// BuildFixture exposes the synthetic ROM for debugging harnesses.
func BuildFixture() mapfmt.ROM { return newFixtureROM() }

// TestDecodeRecordHeader pins the block-1 walk: sizes are stored -1, and
// a clean walk emits no warnings.
func TestDecodeRecordHeader(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	if len(m.Warnings) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("record should walk cleanly end to end, got warnings %v", m.Warnings)
	}
	if m.Width != 64 || m.Height != 32 || m.NameID != 0x42 {
		t.Errorf("header: got %dx%d name %#x, want 64x32 name 0x42", m.Width, m.Height, m.NameID)
	}
	if m.Type != 5 {
		t.Errorf("map type: got %d, want 5 (byte 0x2A >> 1 & 0x0F)", m.Type)
	}
	if m.Slope != 0x55 {
		t.Errorf("slope byte: got %#x, want 0x55 (the ext-bit6 byte after the flag2 walk)", m.Slope)
	}
	if len(m.Animations) != 1 || m.Animations[0] != (TileAnimation{Object: 0xDE, Kind: 0xAD, SoundStep: 0xBE, Sound: 0xEF}) {
		t.Errorf("animations: got %+v, want one entry {DE AD BE EF}", m.Animations)
	}
}

// TestDecodeExitsPairSortedRectsToDestinations pins the event-point
// pairing: movement ids pair with the property layer's in-bounds
// rectangles in left-top-first order (Y then X) and resolve through block
// 4 — 0x1001 -> record 1 (map 7), 0x1002 -> the aliased record-2 header
// (map 0x80). The out-of-bounds point (100,2) must be filtered before the
// pairing.
func TestDecodeExitsPairSortedRectsToDestinations(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	if len(m.Exits) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("exits: got %d, want 2", len(m.Exits))
	}
	e0 := m.Exits[0]
	if e0.EventID != 0x1001 || e0.X != 12 || e0.Y != 3 || e0.W != 1 || e0.H != 1 {
		t.Errorf("exit 0x1001 rect: got id %#x (%d,%d %dx%d), want (12,3) 1x1 — the Y-then-X first rectangle", e0.EventID, e0.X, e0.Y, e0.W, e0.H)
	}
	if e0.TargetMap != 7 || e0.TargetX != 0x21 || e0.TargetY != 0x22 {
		t.Errorf("exit 0x1001 target: got map %d at (%#x,%#x), want 7 at (21,22) via destination 1", e0.TargetMap, e0.TargetX, e0.TargetY)
	}
	if e0.DestFlags != 0 || e0.Facing != 0 || e0.MusicChange || e0.Music != 0 || e0.Hide {
		t.Errorf("exit 0x1001 flags: got flags %#x facing %d music %d change %v hide %v, want all clear", e0.DestFlags, e0.Facing, e0.Music, e0.MusicChange, e0.Hide)
	}
	e1 := m.Exits[1]
	if e1.EventID != 0x1002 || e1.X != 4 || e1.Y != 9 || e1.W != 2 || e1.H != 3 {
		t.Errorf("exit 0x1002 rect: got id %#x (%d,%d %dx%d), want (4,9) 2x3 — size byte 0x12 = hi+1/lo+1", e1.EventID, e1.X, e1.Y, e1.W, e1.H)
	}
	if e1.TargetMap != 0 || e1.TargetX != 0xF3 || e1.TargetY != 0 || e1.Music != 32 {
		t.Errorf("exit 0x1002 target: got map %#x at (%#x,%#x) music %d, want map 0 at (f3,00) music 32 from the aliased record-2 header word 0x8000", e1.TargetMap, e1.TargetX, e1.TargetY, e1.Music)
	}
	if e1.DestFlags != 0xC2 || e1.Facing != 2 || e1.MusicChange || e1.Hide {
		t.Errorf("exit 0x1002 flags: got flags %#x facing %d change %v hide %v, want 0xC2 facing 2, change and hide clear", e1.DestFlags, e1.Facing, e1.MusicChange, e1.Hide)
	}
}

	}

// TestDecodeChestsItemAndEventForms pins the two chest record forms: an
// item chest carries a content byte, an event chest (flag bits 2-3 ==
// 0x08) carries a big-endian event word instead; the block header's second
// byte is the closed-chest object id.
func TestDecodeChestsItemAndEventForms(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	if len(m.Chests) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("chests: got %d, want 2", len(m.Chests))
	}
	item := m.Chests[0]
	if item.Flags != 0 || item.X != 0x30 || item.Y != 0x40 || item.ContentID != 0xCC || item.OpenFlagID != 0xDD || item.EventID != 0 {
		t.Errorf("item chest: got flags %#x (%d,%d) content %#x open %#x event %#x, want flags 0 (30,40) content 0xCC open 0xDD no event",
			item.Flags, item.X, item.Y, item.ContentID, item.OpenFlagID, item.EventID)
	}
	event := m.Chests[1]
	if event.Flags != 0x48 || event.X != 0x50 || event.Y != 0x60 || event.ContentID != 0 || event.OpenFlagID != 0xEE || event.EventID != 0x0702 {
		t.Errorf("event chest: got flags %#x (%d,%d) content %#x open %#x event %#x, want flags 0x48 (50,60) no content, open 0xEE, event 0x0702 big-endian",
			event.Flags, event.X, event.Y, event.ContentID, event.OpenFlagID, event.EventID)
	}
	if m.ChestObject != 0xBB {
		t.Errorf("chest object id: got %#x, want 0xBB (header byte after the count)", m.ChestObject)
	}
}

// TestDecodeScreenBlock pins the flag3-bit4 block: the gate byte's bit5
// selects the flag-window pair, the low 5 bits are the main screen layers,
// and sub/select/math/fixed follow.
func TestDecodeScreenBlock(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	if m.Screen == nil {
		t.Fatalf("screen block: got nil, want a decoded Screen")
	}
	want := Screen{Main: 0x17, Sub: 0x11, Select: 0x12, Math: 0x13, Fixed: 0x14, Flag: 0x15, Lo: 3, Hi: 5}
	if *m.Screen != want {
		t.Errorf("screen: got %+v, want %+v (main 0x17 from gate byte 0x37, window byte 0x34 = [3,5))", *m.Screen, want)
	}
}

// TestDecodeGfxAnimationsAndScreenEffect pins the flag3-bit2 list: the
// count byte's low 7 bits are entries and bit7 is the once flag; each
// word is chip (low 10 bits) / script-1 (high 6), with the 0x40 script
// field escaping to a follow-up byte; the screen effect is the last
// script whose first byte maps to one.
func TestDecodeGfxAnimationsAndScreenEffect(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	if !m.GfxAnimsOnce {
		t.Errorf("gfx anims once: got false, want true (count byte bit7)")
	}
	want := []GfxAnim{{Chip: 0x155, Script: 1}, {Chip: 1, Script: 0x30}}
	if len(m.GfxAnims) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("gfx anims: got %d entries, want 2", len(m.GfxAnims))
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if m.GfxAnims[i] != w {
			t.Errorf("gfx anim %d: got %+v, want %+v (chip from low 10 bits, 0x40 script field escapes to the follow-up byte)", i, m.GfxAnims[i], w)
		}
	}
	if m.Effect != 8 {
		t.Errorf("screen effect: got %d, want 8 (script 1's first byte 0xFB); a later script mapping to no effect must not clear it", m.Effect)
	}
}

// TestDecodeXButtonAndEdgeEvents pins the two always-big-endian event

func TestDecodeXButtonAndEdgeEvents(t *testing.T) {

	}
}

// TestDecodeDestinationRecordsAndAliasedBound pins block 4: one 5-byte
// record per referenced 10xx id, with the bound widened past the aliased
// next record (its header bytes are destination 2) because the event list
// and edge events reference index 2.
func TestDecodeDestinationRecordsAndAliasedBound(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	if len(m.Destinations) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("destinations: got %d, want 3 (bound must widen past the aliased next record for 10xx index 2)", len(m.Destinations))
	}
	d0 := m.Destinations[0]
	if d0.TargetMap != 2 || d0.TargetX != 0x11 || d0.TargetY != 0x12 || d0.DestFlags != 0x04 || !d0.MusicChange {
		t.Errorf("destination 0: got map %d at (%#x,%#x) flags %#x change %v, want map 2 at (11,12) flags 0x04 with music change",
			d0.TargetMap, d0.TargetX, d0.TargetY, d0.DestFlags, d0.MusicChange)
	}
	d1 := m.Destinations[1]
	if d1.TargetMap != 7 || d1.TargetX != 0x21 || d1.TargetY != 0x22 {
		t.Errorf("destination 1: got map %d at (%#x,%#x), want map 7 at (21,22)", d1.TargetMap, d1.TargetX, d1.TargetY)
	}
	d2 := m.Destinations[2]
	if d2.TargetMap != 0 || d2.TargetX != 0xF3 || d2.TargetY != 0 || d2.DestFlags != 0xC2 || d2.Facing != 2 || d2.Music != 32 {
		t.Errorf("destination 2: got map %#x at (%#x,%#x) flags %#x facing %d music %d, want the aliased record-2 header: map 0 at (f3,00) flags 0xC2 facing 2, word 0x8000 = music 32",
			d2.TargetMap, d2.TargetX, d2.TargetY, d2.DestFlags, d2.Facing, d2.Music)
	}
}

// TestDecodeVariantsLists pins the flag2-bit4 lists: the selector byte
// names the kind lists, decoded in 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 order; the count
// byte's bit7 marks every entry of its list unconditional; conditional
// entries carry a flag index plus a [Lo,Hi) window from the nibble pair;
// pointers land as file offsets.
func TestDecodeVariantsLists(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	want := []Variant{
		{Kind: 0x10, Always: false, Flag: 5, Lo: 3, Hi: 5, Ptr: 0x386000},
		{Kind: 0x10, Always: false, Flag: 6, Lo: 8, Hi: 16, Ptr: 0x386010},
		{Kind: 0x20, Always: true, Ptr: 0x386020},
		{Kind: 0x80, Always: true, Ptr: 0x386030},
	}
	if len(m.Variants) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("variants: got %d, want %d", len(m.Variants), len(want))
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if m.Variants[i] != w {
			t.Errorf("variant %d: got %+v, want %+v (Lo/Hi from the window byte's hi/lo nibble, Lo exclusive-bounded by Hi)", i, m.Variants[i], w)
		}
	}
}

// TestFreshLoadChestStampsAndUnconditionalVariants pins the loader-view
// helper: every chest closed on its flag-bits-6-7 layer, always-entries
// split into layers (kind 0x20) and property regions (kind 0x80) in list
// order, conditional entries counted.
func TestFreshLoadChestStampsAndUnconditionalVariants(t *testing.T) {
	m := decodeFixture(t)
	chests, layers, props, conditional := m.FreshLoad()
	wantChests := []mapfmt.ChestStamp{
		{X: 0x30, Y: 0x40, Object: 0xBB, Layer: 0},
		{X: 0x50, Y: 0x60, Object: 0xBB, Layer: 1},
	}
	if len(chests) != len(wantChests) {
		t.Fatalf("fresh chests: got %d, want %d", len(chests), len(wantChests))
	}
	for i, w := range wantChests {
		if chests[i] != w {
			t.Errorf("fresh chest %d: got %+v, want %+v (object = chest header id, layer = flag bits 6-7)", i, chests[i], w)
		}
	}
	if len(layers) != 1 || layers[0] != 0x386020 {
		t.Errorf("fresh layers: got %v, want [386020] (the kind-0x20 always entry)", layers)
	}
	if len(props) != 1 || props[0] != 0x386030 {
		t.Errorf("fresh property regions: got %v, want [386030] (the kind-0x80 always entry)", props)
	}
	if conditional != 2 {
		t.Errorf("conditional count: got %d, want 2 (the kind-0x10 entries left out on flag state)", conditional)
	}
}

// TestVariantAppliesWindowBounds pins the placement window semantics:
// unconditional entries apply regardless of flag state; conditional
// entries apply while the flag value lies in [Lo, Hi) — Lo inclusive, Hi
// exclusive — querying exactly the entry's flag index.
func TestVariantAppliesWindowBounds(t *testing.T) {
	v := Variant{Flag: 5, Lo: 3, Hi: 5}
	cases := []struct {
		value int
		want  bool
	}{{2, false}, {3, true}, {4, true}, {5, false}}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := v.Applies(func(int) int { return c.value }); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("flag value %d: Applies = %v, want %v (window [3,5))", c.value, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	asked := -1
	v.Applies(func(idx int) int { asked = idx; return 3 })
	if asked != 5 {
		t.Errorf("flag index queried: got %d, want 5 (the entry's own flag index)", asked)
	}
	always := Variant{Always: true, Lo: 1, Hi: 2}
	if !always.Applies(func(int) int { return 0 }) {
		t.Errorf("unconditional variant should apply regardless of the flag value")
	}
}

func TestJumpTableEntries(t *testing.T) {
	ds, err := JumpTable(newFixtureROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("JumpTable: %v", err)
	}
	if len(ds) != jumpTableEntries {
		t.Fatalf("entries: got %d, want %d", len(ds), jumpTableEntries)
	}
	d := ds[3]
	if d.TargetMap != 0x123 || d.TargetX != 0x2A || d.TargetY != 0x2B {
		t.Errorf("entry 3: got map %#x at (%#x,%#x), want 0x123 at (2a,2b)", d.TargetMap, d.TargetX, d.TargetY)
	}
	if d.DestFlags != 0x86 || d.Facing != 2 || !d.MusicChange || d.Hide || d.Music != 0 {
		t.Errorf("entry 3 flags: got flags %#x facing %d music %d change %v hide %v, want 0x86: facing 2, music change, no hide",
			d.DestFlags, d.Facing, d.Music, d.MusicChange, d.Hide)
	}
	d5 := ds[5]
	if d5.TargetMap != 0x64 || d5.TargetX != 0x40 || d5.TargetY != 0x41 {
		t.Errorf("entry 5: got map %#x at (%#x,%#x), want 0x064 at (40,41)", d5.TargetMap, d5.TargetX, d5.TargetY)
	}
	if d5.Music != 49 {
		t.Errorf("entry 5 music: got %d, want 49 (word 0xC464 >> 10)", d5.Music)
	}
	if d5.DestFlags != 0x88 || !d5.Hide || d5.MusicChange {
		t.Errorf("entry 5 flags: got flags %#x hide %v change %v, want 0x88: hide set, no music change", d5.DestFlags, d5.Hide, d5.MusicChange)
	}
}

func TestDecodeZeroed(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := Decode(newFixtureROM(), 7)

		t.Fatalf("Decode zeroed record: got %v, want ErrZeroed", err)
	}
}

// NPC fixture: a minimal record (no layer 2/3, no property pointer, no
// event points) whose block 2 exercises the engine's save-set semantics
// (C0:3E07-3E82): entry 0 carries every field plus the save bit, entry 1
// re-positions without saving, entries 2-3 carry only a graphic and must
// fall back to the SAVE set's position, not to the previous entry's.
// Entries 4-5 separate the flag bits: bit6 alone (judged, no placement
// bytes) and bit5 alone (placement bytes, not judged).
const (
	fxNPCRecord  = 0x385000
	fxNPCRecord2 = 0x385100
)

func newNPCFixtureROM() mapfmt.ROM {
	rom := make(mapfmt.ROM, 0x800000)
	setEntry := func(id, file int) { // the hack's table at 5A:6A50
		v := file + 0xC00000
		rom[0x5A6A50+id*3] = byte(v)
		rom[0x5A6A50+id*3+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		rom[0x5A6A50+id*3+2] = byte(v >> 16)
	}
	setEntry(8, fxNPCRecord)
	setEntry(9, fxNPCRecord2)

	rec := []byte{
		0x00,             // flag1: no layer 2/3, no extra header bytes
		0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, // layer 1 pointer (unused)
		0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, // property pointer: none
		0x00, 0x00, // chipset, palette set
		0x00,       // object config
		0x00, 0x00, // display position
		0x3F, 0x1F, // size: 64 x 32 tiles
		0x00, // map name id
		0x00, // 禁止操作
		0x00, // flag2
		0x80, // flag3: bit7 characters only
		// block 2.
		0x7F,       // entry 0: judged, place, position, g, ev, q, save
		0x07, 0x12, // placement check: flag id 7, window byte 0x12
		0x10, 0x14, 0x00, // X=16, Y=20, facing 0
		0x11,       // graphic
		0x01, 0x05, // event id 0x0501, little-endian
		0x02, 0x00, // quality 0x0002, little-endian
		0x10,             // entry 1: position only, no save bit
		0x1E, 0x28, 0x01, // X=30, Y=40, facing 1
		0x08, 0x22, // entry 2: graphic only
		0x08, 0x33, // entry 3: graphic only
		0x40,       // entry 4: judged bit only (no placement bytes)
		0x20, 0x09, // entry 5: placement bit only, bytes flag id 9
		0x34, // window byte
		0xFF, // block 2 end
		0xFF, // block 3: empty event point list
	}
	copy(rom[fxNPCRecord:], rec)

	next := []byte{0x80, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00}
	copy(rom[fxNPCRecord2:], next)
	return rom
}

// TestDecodeNPCSaveSet pins the engine's block-2 field inheritance: absent
// fields come from the save set (the last entry with flag bit0 set), not
// from the previous entry (disassembly C0:3E0E JSR $4A3D restore at loop
// top, C0:3E7A JSR $4A02 save on bit0), and the flag bits are per-entry:
// bit6 = judged (設置判定), bit5 = placement-check bytes present.
func TestDecodeNPCSaveSet(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := Decode(newNPCFixtureROM(), 8)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Decode: %v", err)
	}
	if len(m.NPCs) != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("npcs: got %d, want 6", len(m.NPCs))
	}
	want := [6]NPC{
		{X: 16, Y: 20, Facing: 0, Graphic: 0x11, EventID: 0x0501, Quality: 0x0002,
			Judged: true, PlaceID: 0x07, PlaceLo: 0x12},
		{X: 30, Y: 40, Facing: 1, Graphic: 0x11, EventID: 0x0501, Quality: 0x0002,
			Judged: false, PlaceID: 0x07, PlaceLo: 0x12},
		{X: 16, Y: 20, Facing: 0, Graphic: 0x22, EventID: 0x0501, Quality: 0x0002,
			Judged: false, PlaceID: 0x07, PlaceLo: 0x12},
		{X: 16, Y: 20, Facing: 0, Graphic: 0x33, EventID: 0x0501, Quality: 0x0002,
			Judged: false, PlaceID: 0x07, PlaceLo: 0x12},
		// bit6 alone: judged, no placement bytes read, rest from the save
		// set (graphic 0x11 — entries 2-3 carry no save bit)
		{X: 16, Y: 20, Facing: 0, Graphic: 0x11, EventID: 0x0501, Quality: 0x0002,
			Judged: true, PlaceID: 0x07, PlaceLo: 0x12},
		// bit5 alone: placement bytes read (7 -> 9, 0x12 -> 0x34), not judged
		{X: 16, Y: 20, Facing: 0, Graphic: 0x11, EventID: 0x0501, Quality: 0x0002,
			Judged: false, PlaceID: 0x09, PlaceLo: 0x34},
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if m.NPCs[i] != w {
			t.Errorf("npc %d: got %+v, want %+v", i, m.NPCs[i], w)
		}
	}
}

// TestDecodeMap0249NPCs pins map 0x249's true block-2 list against the
// running ROM: 14 entries - one battle monster at (36,52), a kind-05 馬 at
// (36,52) and TWELVE entries stacked at (16,63). The duplicates are
// engine-true: the block's entries 2..13 are flag-0x00 continuations and
// every one spawns unless the placement gate (PlaceID/PlaceLo, all
// inherited from before the block on this map) fails at runtime.
func TestDecodeMap0249NPCs(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("ROM not available: %v", err)
	}
	rom := mapfmt.ROM(data)
	m, err := Decode(rom, 0x249)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Decode 0x249: %v", err)
	}
	if len(m.NPCs) != 14 {
		t.Fatalf("npcs: got %d, want 14", len(m.NPCs))
	}
	first := m.NPCs[0]
	if first.X != 36 || first.Y != 52 || first.Graphic != 0 || first.EventID != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("npc 0: got (%d,%d) g=%d e=%#x", first.X, first.Y, first.Graphic, first.EventID)
	}
	second := m.NPCs[1]
	if second.X != 36 || second.Y != 52 || second.Graphic != 0x61 {
		t.Errorf("npc 1: got (%d,%d) g=%d", second.X, second.Y, second.Graphic)
	}
	stacked := m.NPCs[2:]
	for i, n := range stacked {
		if n.X != 16 || n.Y != 63 || n.Facing != 0x40 || n.Graphic != 0x63 || n.EventID != 0x2000 {
			t.Errorf("npc %d: got (%d,%d) f=%#x g=%d e=%#x, want (16,63) f=0x40 g=0x63 e=0x2000",
				i+2, n.X, n.Y, n.Facing, n.Graphic, n.EventID)
		}
	}
}

// EncounterPartyBase = the flag2-0x20 section's third byte ($D2FE).
// Live (tools/emulator/encounter_comp.lua, /tmp/encounter run2): the
// 0x250 load streamed $D2FC = 0D (C0:42A0), $D2FD = 0D (C0:42AD), $D2FE
// = 00 (C0:42B3), and both traced battles on it read $1308 = 00; reading
// one byte early yields 0D, the live $D2FD. Map 0x019 carries 01. Map
// 0x014 (flag2 0x24) carries 00: the loader reads flag2 bit2's two bytes
// after this section (C0:4543 vs C0:4296); the former walk read them
// first and took 7F from two bytes later.
func TestDecodeEncounterPartyBase(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("../../patches/bokuno_jp.sfc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("ROM not available: %v", err)
	}
	rom := mapfmt.ROM(data)
	for _, c := range []struct{ id, want int }{{0x250, 0x00}, {0x014, 0x00}, {0x019, 0x01}} {
		m, err := Decode(rom, c.id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Decode %#x: %v", c.id, err)
		}
		if m.EncounterPartyBase != c.want {
			t.Errorf("map %#x EncounterPartyBase = %#x, want %#x", c.id, m.EncounterPartyBase, c.want)
		}
	}
}
```

`scripts/gate.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# saga3 gate: everything that must pass before a commit.
# All steps are Go since the godot/ GDScript tree retired (2026-11-23);
# each step names the check it replaced — the full mapping is
# docs/migration.md's audit table. exports/ (formerly godot/) keeps only the engine-neutral
# data (data/, translations/, fonts/) and the tests/ fixture goldens the
# Go packages read in place.
# Scopes cover every Go tree of the module: internal, cmd and tools.
# ref/, repo/ and decomp/ hold foreign or non-Go material and stay
# outside (checked 2026-11-24). The shell smoke step is new coverage —
# the Ebiten shell has no GDScript predecessor.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# go test prints one "ok" line per package, which buries the step headers;
# capture it and print only on failure, so a green gate is silent per step.
run_test() {
    log=$(mktemp)
    if ! go test "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; then
        cat "$log"
        rm -f "$log"
        exit 1
    fi
    rm -f "$log"
}

echo "== gofmt =="
test -z "$(gofmt -l internal cmd tools)" || { gofmt -l internal cmd tools; exit 1; }

echo "== go vet =="
go vet ./internal/... ./cmd/... ./tools/...

echo "== staticcheck =="
go tool staticcheck ./internal/... ./cmd/... ./tools/...

echo "== go test =="
run_test ./internal/... ./cmd/... ./tools/...

echo "== translations (checktranslations over exports/data + exports/translations) =="
go run ./cmd/checktranslations exports/data/events.json exports/translations

echo "== flow e2e, routes, screens, objects (was: godot --selftest) =="
run_test ./internal/game/flow/ -count=1

echo "== battle engine pins (was: godot --battle --battleselftest) =="
run_test ./internal/game/battle/ -count=1

echo "== tile renders vs baked map images (was: tests/tilecheck.gd) =="
run_test ./internal/game/gfx/ -run TestGoldenTilecheck -count=1

echo "== animation engine vs emulator digests (was: tests/gfxcheck.gd over gfx_digests.json) =="
run_test ./internal/game/gfx/ -run 'TestGoldenGfxDigests|TestDigestSelfTest|TestGoldenDigestDetectsMutation' -count=1

echo "== type-1 arrival sequence vs emulator digests (was: tests/arrivalcheck.gd over the 12 arrival_*.json) =="
run_test ./internal/game/gfx/ -run 'TestGoldenArrivals|TestArrivalDigestSelfTest|TestGoldenArrivalDetectsMutation' -count=1

echo "== opening cutscene vs emulator capture (was: tests/cutscenecheck.gd over cutscene_opening.json) =="
run_test ./internal/game/flow/ -run TestCutsceneOpening -count=1

echo "== shell smoke: the game boots, renders, walks, fights (xvfb) =="
bash scripts/shell-smoke.sh

echo "== event VM gate parity (skips without MesenCE/ROM, docs/parity.md §6 M3) =="
bash scripts/parity_gate.sh

echo "GATE OK"

```

`scripts/parity_gate.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# M3 gate/branch parity: replay the headless-reachable events on the real
# ROM (MesenCE) and verify the fresh capture against the golden the Go
# VM's lockstep test pins (internal/game/vm parity_test, docs/parity.md
# §6 M3, §12). The GDScript replay side retired with godot/ 2026-11-23;
# the compared side is internal/game/vm's lockstep (PARITY PASS 9/9/0).
#
# Runs three stages in a private numbered output dir under /tmp:
#   1. MesenCE -testRunner tools/emulator/parity_gate.lua  -> rom.log
#   2. paritygate prepare                                  -> jobs.json + rom_meta.json
#   3. the fresh capture must reproduce the committed capture golden
#      (internal/game/vm/testdata, run-236) byte for byte, then the
#      lockstep test re-runs for the verdict line
#
# Skips with a loud SKIP (exit 0) when the emulator or ROM is absent, so the
# gate stays green on machines without the capture environment.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

ROM=patches/bokuno_jp.sfc
EMU_SRC=/tmp/mesence
RUN_BASE=/tmp/saga3-parity-runs
GOLDEN=internal/game/vm/testdata

if [ ! -f "$ROM" ]; then
    echo "PARITY SKIP: no ROM at $ROM (MesenCE headless capture needs it)"
    exit 0
fi
if [ ! -x "$EMU_SRC/Mesen" ]; then
    echo "PARITY SKIP: no MesenCE binary at $EMU_SRC/Mesen (MesenCE headless capture needs it)"
    exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$RUN_BASE"
prev=$(ls -d "$RUN_BASE"/run-* 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)
n=1
if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
    n=$(( ${prev##*run-} + 1 ))
fi
run_dir="$RUN_BASE/run-$n"
mkdir -p "$run_dir"

# private emulator copy: another agent may be using /tmp/mesence right now
emu_dir="$run_dir/mesence"
cp -r "$EMU_SRC" "$emu_dir"

echo "== parity: ROM-side capture (MesenCE headless) =="
# the capture runs to its own PARITY-DONE (~24k frames); -timeout is the
# watchdog, generous because parallel agents load the machine
timeout 1500 "$emu_dir/Mesen" -testRunner tools/emulator/parity_gate.lua "$PWD/$ROM" \
    -enableStdout -timeout=1400 > "$run_dir/rom.log" 2> "$run_dir/rom.err" || true
if ! grep -q "^PARITY-DONE" "$run_dir/rom.log"; then
    echo "PARITY FAIL: ROM capture did not reach PARITY-DONE (see $run_dir/rom.log)"
    exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q "^PARITY-LOADED" "$run_dir/rom.log"; then
    echo "PARITY FAIL: Lua script never loaded (silent TestRunner catch, see $run_dir/rom.err)"
    exit 1
fi

echo "== parity: prepare jobs =="
go run ./cmd/paritygate -mode prepare -rom-log "$run_dir/rom.log" \
    -jobs "$run_dir/jobs.json" -meta "$run_dir/rom_meta.json"

echo "== parity: fresh capture vs the committed golden =="
for f in jobs.json rom_meta.json; do
    if ! cmp -s "$run_dir/$f" "$GOLDEN/$f"; then
        echo "PARITY FAIL: fresh $f differs from $GOLDEN/$f (capture drifted; refresh internal/game/vm/testdata deliberately, then re-pin the lockstep golden)"
        exit 1
    fi
done

echo "== parity: Go VM lockstep (internal/game/vm parity_test) =="
if ! go test ./internal/game/vm/ -run 'TestParityGateLockstep|TestParityComparatorMutation' -count=1 -v \
        > "$run_dir/lockstep.log" 2>&1; then
    echo "PARITY FAIL: the lockstep test failed (see $run_dir/lockstep.log)"
    exit 1
fi
grep "coverage: compared=9 matched=9 conflicts=0" "$run_dir/lockstep.log" || {
    echo "PARITY FAIL: lockstep coverage line not 9/9/0 (see $run_dir/lockstep.log)"
    exit 1
}

echo "PARITY PASS: fresh capture equals $GOLDEN (run-236); the Go VM lockstep agrees 9/9/0"

```

`scripts/shell-smoke.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The Ebiten shell's xvfb smoke run (the shell cannot be fully headless,
# docs/migration.md): boots cmd/saga3 on the opening landing tile of 0250,
# injects a held walk key, saves one screenshot, and fails unless the
# binary booted, rendered a non-black frame, and the leader moved; a
# second run walks the leader into 0049's monster and fails unless the
# field battle takes the frame with a non-black screenshot of its own.
set -e
set -o pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if ! command -v xvfb-run >/dev/null; then
    echo "SHELL-SMOKE SKIP: no xvfb-run in PATH (install xvfb; the Ebiten shell needs an X server)"
    exit 0
fi

OUT=/tmp/shell-smoke-$$
mkdir -p "$OUT"
trap 'rm -rf "$OUT"' EXIT

echo "== build =="
go build -o "$OUT/saga3" ./cmd/saga3

echo "== xvfb run =="
xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 800x600x24" "$OUT/saga3" \
    --map 0250 12 58 --frames 120 --press right:30:60 \
    --screenshot "$OUT/field.png" 2>"$OUT/err" | tee "$OUT/log"

echo "== boot and render =="
grep -q '^SHELL-SHOT' "$OUT/log" || { echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL no screenshot"; exit 1; }
mean=$(sed -n 's/^SHELL-SHOT .* mean=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$OUT/log")
[ "$mean" -gt 0 ] || { echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL black frame (mean=$mean)"; exit 1; }
[ -s "$OUT/field.png" ] || { echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL empty screenshot"; exit 1; }

echo "== injected walk =="
grep '^SHELL-STATE final' "$OUT/log"
if grep '^SHELL-STATE final' "$OUT/log" | grep -q 'tile=12,58'; then
    echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL leader did not move"
    exit 1
fi

echo "== battle bump =="
# 0049's record 0 monster stands at (24,50); the leader boots one tile
# below and a held Up walks into it — the field battle takes the frame
# (map_view's bump dispatch, C0:5635's shape).
xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 800x600x24" "$OUT/saga3" \
    --map 0049 24 51 --frames 220 --press up:10:60 \
    --screenshot "$OUT/battle.png" 2>"$OUT/battle-err" | tee "$OUT/battle-log"

echo "== battle took the frame =="
grep -q '^SHELL-SHOT' "$OUT/battle-log" || { echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL no battle screenshot"; exit 1; }
bmean=$(sed -n 's/^SHELL-SHOT .* mean=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$OUT/battle-log")
[ "$bmean" -gt 0 ] || { echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL black battle frame (mean=$bmean)"; exit 1; }
[ -s "$OUT/battle.png" ] || { echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL empty battle screenshot"; exit 1; }
grep '^SHELL-STATE final' "$OUT/battle-log" | grep -q 'battle=true' || {
    echo "SHELL-SMOKE-FAIL battle did not start"
    grep '^SHELL-STATE final' "$OUT/battle-log"
    exit 1
}

echo "SHELL-SMOKE-OK mean=$mean battle-mean=$bmean $(grep -o 'tile=[0-9,]*' <(grep '^SHELL-STATE final' "$OUT/log") | tail -1)"

```

`scripts/xlab.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# xlab.sh - the lab-side GUI debug loop for the Godot port.
#
# A persistent Xvfb display (:99) runs the Godot map view; xdotool sends
# keys (XTEST); import captures frames. This is how agents "play" the
# port visually on lab — no Mac mini round-trip, no TCC permissions.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/xlab.sh start [mapid] [x] [y]  # ensure Xvfb + Godot; no map id
#                                          # boots the title flow
#   scripts/xlab.sh shot [out.png]  # capture the display
#   scripts/xlab.sh key <KEY>...    # send keys (Down Up Left Return space ...)
#   scripts/xlab.sh stop
set -euo pipefail
DISP=${XLAB_DISPLAY:-:99}
export DISPLAY=$DISP

case "${1:-}" in
start)
    mapid=${2:-}
    spawn=${3:-}
    spawn_y=${4:-}
    if ! pgrep -x Xvfb >/dev/null || ! xdpyinfo -display "$DISP" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        pkill -x Xvfb 2>/dev/null || true
        setsid nohup Xvfb "$DISP" -screen 0 1152x648x24 > /tmp/xlab_xvfb.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
        sleep 3
    fi
    pkill -f "godot --path" 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 1
    # No map id boots the title flow (NEW GAME/CONTINUE); a map id keeps
    # the --map debug skip.
    godot_args=(--audio-driver Dummy --)
    if [ -n "$mapid" ]; then
        godot_args+=(--map "$mapid")
        [ -n "$spawn" ] && godot_args+=("$spawn")
        [ -n "$spawn_y" ] && godot_args+=("$spawn_y")
    fi
    # XLAB_GODOT_ARGS: extra user args after -- (e.g. "--battlehp 3000")
    if [ -n "${XLAB_GODOT_ARGS:-}" ]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        godot_args+=($XLAB_GODOT_ARGS)
    fi
    setsid nohup godot --path /home/newlix/projects/saga3/godot \
        "${godot_args[@]}" \
        > /tmp/xlab_godot.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    sleep 15
    import -window root /tmp/xlab_last.png
    echo "started; frame at /tmp/xlab_last.png"
    ;;
shot)
    out=${2:-/tmp/xlab_last.png}
    # Capture the Godot window when it is mapped; fall back to the screen.
    win=$(xdotool search --name "saga3" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    if [ -n "$win" ]; then
        import -window "$win" "$out"
    else
        import -window root "$out"
    fi
    echo "$out"
    ;;
key)
    shift
    # Xvfb runs no window manager: focus is PointerRoot, so route keys by
    # putting the pointer over the Godot window.
    win=$(xdotool search --name "saga3" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    if [ -n "$win" ]; then
        eval $(xdotool getwindowgeometry --shell "$win")
        xdotool mousemove $((X + WIDTH / 2)) $((Y + HEIGHT / 2))
    fi
    sleep 0.2
    for k in "$@"; do
        xdotool key "$k"
        sleep 0.15
    done
    ;;
stop)
    pkill -f "godot --path" 2>/dev/null || true
    pkill -x Xvfb 2>/dev/null || true
    echo stopped
    ;;
*)
    echo "usage: xlab.sh start [mapid] [x] [y] | shot [png] | key <KEY>... | stop"
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

```

`tools/emulator/actscript.lua`:

```lua
-- actscript.lua - object action scripts during the row-0 opening.
--
-- Same boot/press schedule as protag_route.lua (cold boot; delete
-- /tmp/mesence/Saves/bokuno_jp.srm first). Logs every action-script
-- opcode fetch: C0:53BA `STA $D9B9,Y` runs with A = the opcode read from
-- [$8D] = F8:(D9B3+D9B5) for object Y. Also logs objOp 17 20 installs
-- (C0:B2D4 entry: EF00/EF01 word) and queue writes from C0:67E1.

local END_FRAME = 15000
local PRESSES = {}
for f = 300, 6800, 60 do PRESSES[f] = { start = 1 } end
PRESSES[7000] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[7780] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[8600] = { start = 1 }
PRESSES[9000] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[9800] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[10600] = { a = 1 }

local frames = 0
local hits = 0
local function wr(o) return emu.read(o, emu.memType.snesWorkRam) end
local function rd(a) return emu.read(a, emu.memType.snesMemory) end

emu.addMemoryCallback(function()
	if frames < 10600 or hits > 20000 then return end
	hits = hits + 1
	local st = emu.getCpuState(emu.cpuType.snes)
	local y = st.y
	local base = wr(0xD9B3 + y) | (wr(0xD9B4 + y) << 8)
	local pos = wr(0xD9B5 + y) | (wr(0xD9B6 + y) << 8)
	local a = 0xF80000 + ((base + pos) & 0xFFFF)
	local b = {}
	for i = 0, 5 do b[#b + 1] = string.format("%02X", rd(a + i)) end
	print(string.format("ACT frame=%d obj=%04X script=%04X pos=%04X op=%02X bytes=%s", frames, y, base, pos,
		st.a & 0xFF, table.concat(b, " ")))
end, emu.callbackType.exec, 0xC053BA, 0xC053BA, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesMemory)

emu.addMemoryCallback(function()
	if frames < 10600 then return end
	print(string.format("OBJ20 frame=%d ef00=%02X ef01=%04X", frames, wr(0xEF00), wr(0xEF01) | (wr(0xEF02) << 8)))
end, emu.callbackType.exec, 0xC0B2D4, 0xC0B2D4, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesMemory)

local last_id = -1
emu.addMemoryCallback(function(_, val)
	local id = wr(0xD51B) | (val << 8)
	if id ~= last_id then
		last_id = id
		print(string.format("ID frame=%d id=%04X", frames, id))
	end
end, emu.callbackType.write, 0xD51C, 0xD51C, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)

emu.addEventCallback(function()
	frames = frames + 1
	local p = PRESSES[frames]
	if p == nil and frames > 11000 and frames % 30 == 0 and wr(0x76) ~= 0 then p = { a = 1 } end
	emu.setInput(p or { start = 0, a = 0 }, 0, 0)
	if frames >= END_FRAME then
		print(string.format("ACT-END frame=%d hits=%d", frames, hits))
		emu.stop(0)
	end
end, emu.eventType.inputPolled)
print("ACT-LOADED")

```

`tools/emulator/acttrail.lua`:

```lua
-- acttrail.lua - per-frame object trail during the row-0 opening (the
-- reference for porting action-script frame timing).
--
-- actscript.lua's fetch log (ACT) plus, once per LOGIC pass of the
-- object loop from frame 11800 to 13500 (a pass starts when the driver
-- call C0:51F7 sees Y not above the previous call's; sampling per input
-- poll instead shows 31 lag frames as false freezes), one TR line per
-- slot y = 0x40*n (n < 16) whose $D99A bit 7 (running) is set: script
-- base $D9B3, position $D9B5, counters $D9B7/$D9B8, opcode $D9B9,
-- pixel position $D9AA/$D9AC and facing $D9A9; f= is the pass number.
-- The godot selftest's action-runner md5 was computed from this trail.
--
-- Same boot/press schedule as protag_route.lua (cold boot; delete
-- /tmp/mesence/Saves/bokuno_jp.srm first). Logs every action-script
-- opcode fetch: C0:53BA `STA $D9B9,Y` runs with A = the opcode read from
-- [$8D] = F8:(D9B3+D9B5) for object Y. Also logs objOp 17 20 installs
-- (C0:B2D4 entry: EF00/EF01 word) and queue writes from C0:67E1.

local END_FRAME = 13500
local PRESSES = {}
for f = 300, 6800, 60 do PRESSES[f] = { start = 1 } end
PRESSES[7000] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[7780] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[8600] = { start = 1 }
PRESSES[9000] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[9800] = { a = 1 }
PRESSES[10600] = { a = 1 }

local frames = 0
local hits = 0
local function wr(o) return emu.read(o, emu.memType.snesWorkRam) end
local function rd(a) return emu.read(a, emu.memType.snesMemory) end

emu.addMemoryCallback(function()
	if frames < 10600 or hits > 20000 then return end
	hits = hits + 1
	local st = emu.getCpuState(emu.cpuType.snes)
	local y = st.y
	local base = wr(0xD9B3 + y) | (wr(0xD9B4 + y) << 8)
	local pos = wr(0xD9B5 + y) | (wr(0xD9B6 + y) << 8)
	local a = 0xF80000 + ((base + pos) & 0xFFFF)
	local b = {}
	for i = 0, 5 do b[#b + 1] = string.format("%02X", rd(a + i)) end
	print(string.format("ACT frame=%d obj=%04X script=%04X pos=%04X op=%02X bytes=%s", frames, y, base, pos,
		st.a & 0xFF, table.concat(b, " ")))
end, emu.callbackType.exec, 0xC053BA, 0xC053BA, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesMemory)

emu.addMemoryCallback(function()
	if frames < 10600 then return end
	print(string.format("OBJ20 frame=%d ef00=%02X ef01=%04X", frames, wr(0xEF00), wr(0xEF01) | (wr(0xEF02) << 8)))
end, emu.callbackType.exec, 0xC0B2D4, 0xC0B2D4, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesMemory)

local last_id = -1
emu.addMemoryCallback(function(_, val)
	local id = wr(0xD51B) | (val << 8)
	if id ~= last_id then
		last_id = id
		print(string.format("ID frame=%d id=%04X", frames, id))
	end
end, emu.callbackType.write, 0xD51C, 0xD51C, emu.cpuType.snes, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)

emu.addEventCallback(function()
	frames = frames + 1
	local p = PRESSES[frames]
	if p == nil and frames > 11000 and frames % 30 == 0 and wr(0x76) ~= 0 then p = { a = 1 } end
	emu.setInput(p or { start = 0, a = 0 }, 0, 0)
	if frames >= END_FRAME then
		print(string.format("ACT-END frame=%d hits=%d", frames, hits))
		emu.stop(0)
	end
end, emu.eventType.inputPolled)
print("ACT-LOADED")

					wr(0xD9AA + y) | (wr(0xD9AB + y) << 8), wr(0xD9AC + y) | (wr(0xD9AD + y) << 8), wr(0xD9A9 + y)))
			end
		end
		print(string.format("PASS %d frame=%d", pass, frames))
	end
	lastY = st.y
```

```lua
local alphabet = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
local function b64encode(bytes)
	local out = {}
	for i = 1, #bytes, 3 do
		local a, b, c = bytes:byte(i, i + 2)
		b = b or 0
		c = c or 0
		local n = a * 65536 + b * 256 + c
		local q = { math.floor(n / 262144) % 64, math.floor(n / 4096) % 64, math.floor(n / 64) % 64, n % 64 }
		out[#out + 1] = alphabet:sub(q[1] + 1, q[1] + 1) .. alphabet:sub(q[2] + 1, q[2] + 1)
			.. alphabet:sub(q[3] + 1, q[3] + 1) .. alphabet:sub(q[4] + 1, q[4] + 1)
	end
	local rem = #bytes % 3
	if rem == 1 then
		out[#out] = out[#out]:sub(1, 2) .. "=="
	elseif rem == 2 then
		out[#out] = out[#out]:sub(1, 3) .. "="
	end
	return table.concat(out)
end

	print("DUMPEND " .. name)

emu.addEventCallback(function()
	frames = frames + 1
	local cok, cerr = pcall(function()
		local st = emu.getState()
		local br = st["ppu.screenBrightness"]
		if st["ppu.forcedBlank"] then br = 0 end
		print(string.format("C f=%d c=%02X%02X%02X%02X map=%04X br=%d ev=%04X", frames,
			wr(0xF30A), wr(0xF30B), wr(0xF30C), wr(0xF30D), wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF, br, wr16(0xD51B)))
	end)
	if not cok then print("LUAERR " .. tostring(cerr)); emu.stop() end
	local p = PRESSES[frames]
	if p == nil and frames > 11000 and frames < START and frames % 30 == 0 and wr(0x76) ~= 0 then p = { a = 1 } end
	emu.setInput(p or { start = 0, a = 0 }, 0, 0)
	if injected_at ~= nil and qoff == nil then qlog = true end
	if qoff ~= nil and frames > qoff then qlog = false end
	if frames < START then return end
	if injected_at == nil then
		step = step + 1
		if step > #JUMPS then
			print(string.format("SWEEP-END frame=%d", frames))
			emu.stop(0)
			return
		end
		if wr(0xD6BD) ~= 0xFF or wr(0x76) ~= 0 then
			-- an arrival event left a window open or the queue busy:
			-- press A every 30 frames as during boot, then retry
			if frames % 30 == 0 then emu.setInput({ a = 1 }, 0, 0) end
			step = step - 1
			return
		end
		if RETARGET ~= nil then
			local off = 0x3CFB00 + 5 * JUMPS[step] + 1
			emu.write(off, RETARGET, emu.memType.snesPrgRom)
			local r = {}
			for i = -1, 3 do r[#r + 1] = string.format('%02X', emu.read(off + i, emu.memType.snesPrgRom)) end
			print('RETARGET rec=' .. table.concat(r, ' '))
		end
		cfg_before = wr(0xD2E3)
		emu.write(0xD6BE, JUMPS[step], emu.memType.snesWorkRam)
		emu.write(0xD6BD, 0x11, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)
		injected_at = frames
		changed_at = nil
		print(string.format("INJECT frame=%d index=%02X cfg=%02X", frames, JUMPS[step], cfg_before))
		return
	end
	if map_before == nil then map_before = wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF end
	if changed_at == nil and (wr(0xD2E3) ~= cfg_before or (wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF) ~= map_before) then changed_at = frames end
	local since = (move_i == 0) and changed_at or move_changed
	if move_i < #MOVES and since ~= nil and frames >= since + 60 and last_gi >= since and frames >= last_gi + 120 then
		if wr(0xD6BD) ~= 0xFF or wr(0x76) ~= 0 then
			if frames % 30 == 0 then emu.setInput({ a = 1 }, 0, 0) end
			return
		end
		move_from = wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF
		move_i = move_i + 1
		move_changed = nil
		emu.write(0xD6BE, MOVES[move_i], emu.memType.snesWorkRam)
		emu.write(0xD6BD, 0x10, emu.memType.snesWorkRam)
		moved_at = frames
		print(string.format("MOVEINJECT frame=%d dest=%02X from=%04X", frames, MOVES[move_i], move_from))
		return
	end
	if move_i > 0 and moved_at ~= nil and move_changed == nil and (wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF) ~= move_from then move_changed = frames end
	local settled = (#MOVES == 0 and changed_at ~= nil and frames >= changed_at + 60) or (move_i == #MOVES and move_changed ~= nil and frames >= move_changed + 60)
	if settled and trail_from == nil then trail_from = frames; passes = 0
		print(string.format("TRAILMAP index=%02X map=%04X frame=%d", JUMPS[step], wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF, frames)) end
	local ready = (trail_from ~= nil and passes >= 2600) or frames >= injected_at + TIMEOUT + 5000
	if ready then
		local cfg = wr(0xD2E3)
		print(string.format("SWEEP index=%02X cfg=%02X changed=%s", JUMPS[step], cfg, tostring(changed_at ~= nil)))
		-- $D0A7 = current map word (music<<10 | map id): the jump handler
		-- saves it to $FE01 as the return point (C0:C115).
		print(string.format("GEO frame=%d cfg=%02X D0C5=%04X D0D1=%02X D0D5=%04X zone=%02X leader=(%d,%d) map=%04X",
			frames, cfg, wr16(0xD0C5), wr(0xD0D1), wr16(0xD0D5), wr(0xD990), wr16(0xD9AA) // 8, wr16(0xD9AC) // 8,
			wr16(0xD0A7) & 0x3FF))
		trail_from = nil
		injected_at = nil
	end
end, emu.eventType.inputPolled)
```

`tools/emulator/arrival_retarget.lua`:

```lua
-- arrival_retarget.lua - record one type-1 arrival capture for
-- tests/arrival_*.json: cold boot (delete Saves/bokuno_jp.srm) plays the
-- row-0 opening to map 0x250, then the queue word `11 D5` enters the
-- arrival chain. The eight maps without a reachable entering record are
-- captured by retargeting jump D5's record map byte in emulator ROM
-- (emu.write snesPrgRom at 0x3CFB00 + 5*0xD5 + 1; RETARGET below, patch
-- with sed before a run, one run per map). The exec watches log GINSTALL
-- (FF:9935), OBJOP51 (C0:CFE3) and per-tick TK lines (FF:9CDB: frame,
-- $14, RNG, CGRAM) - the inputs of
--   godot -s tests/arrivalcheck.gd -- <log> 19563 19581 vm_first 21478 \
--       <map> 847 --record
-- (GINSTALL 19556, objOp 51 19581, next GINSTALL 21478 on this
-- schedule). These runs produced tests/arrival_027B.json and the other
-- seven 2026-11-23; docs/map-format.md, type-1 arrival.

local TIMEOUT = 1500

	for i = 1, #bytes, 3 do
		local a, b, c = bytes:byte(i, i + 2)
		b = b or 0
		c = c or 0
		local n = a * 65536 + b * 256 + c
		local q = { math.floor(n / 262144) % 64, math.floor(n / 4096) % 64, math.floor(n / 64) % 64, n % 64 }
		out[#out + 1] = alphabet:sub(q[1] + 1, q[1] + 1) .. alphabet:sub(q[2] + 1, q[2] + 1)
			.. alphabet:sub(q[3] + 1, q[3] + 1) .. alphabet:sub(q[4] + 1, q[4] + 1)
	end
	local rem = #bytes % 3
	if rem == 1 then
		out[#out] = out[#out]:sub(1, 2) .. "=="
	elseif rem == 2 then
		out[#out] = out[#out]:sub(1, 3) .. "="
	end
	return table.concat(out)
end

local function dump_bank7f(name)
	local bytes = {}
	for i = 0, 0x7FFF do bytes[#bytes + 1] = string.char(wr(0x10000 + i)) end
	local s = table.concat(bytes)
	print("DUMPBEGIN " .. name)
	for i = 1, #s, 3000 do print("DUMPDATA " .. b64encode(s:sub(i, math.min(i + 2999, #s)))) end
	print("DUMPEND " .. name)
end

function dump_ppu()
	local t = {}
	for _, reg in ipairs({0x2105, 0x2107, 0x2108, 0x2109, 0x210B, 0x210C, 0x212C, 0x212D, 0x2130, 0x2131}) do
		t[#t + 1] = string.format("%04X=%02X", reg, regs[reg] or 0xFFFF)
	end
	print("PPU " .. table.concat(t, " "))
	local u = {}
	for _, reg in ipairs({0x210D, 0x210E, 0x210F, 0x2110, 0x2111, 0x2112}) do
		local v = scroll[reg] or {0, 0}
		u[#u + 1] = string.format("%04X=%d", reg, v[1] * 256 + v[2])
	end
	print("SCROLL " .. table.concat(u, " "))
	local st = emu.getState()
	local keys = {}
	for k, v in pairs(st) do
		local lk = string.lower(k)
		if string.find(lk, "scroll") or string.find(lk, "ofs") or string.find(lk, "offset") then
			keys[#keys + 1] = k .. "=" .. tostring(v)
		end
	end
	table.sort(keys)
	print("STATE " .. table.concat(keys, " "))
	local cg = {}
	for i = 0, 511 do cg[#cg + 1] = string.format("%02X", emu.read(i, emu.memType.snesCgRam)) end
	print("CGRAM " .. table.concat(cg))
	local b3 = {}
	for i = 0x6000, 0x6000 + 0x1000 - 1 do b3[#b3 + 1] = string.format("%02X", emu.read(i, emu.memType.snesVideoRam)) end
	print("BG3CHR " .. table.concat(b3))
	for _, chip in ipairs({}) do
		local t = {}
		for i = 0, 31 do t[#t + 1] = string.format("%02X", emu.read(chip * 32 + i, emu.memType.snesVideoRam)) end
		print(string.format("CHR %03X %s", chip, table.concat(t)))
	end
	for _, base in ipairs({0x5000, 0x5800, 0x2800}) do
		for row = 0, 31 do
			local w = {}
			for col = 0, 63 do
				local wa = base + (col >= 32 and 0x400 or 0) + row * 32 + (col % 32)
				local lo = emu.read(wa * 2, emu.memType.snesVideoRam)
				local hi = emu.read(wa * 2 + 1, emu.memType.snesVideoRam)
				w[#w + 1] = string.format("%02X%02X", hi, lo)
			end
			print(string.format("VRAM base=%04X row=%d %s", base, row, table.concat(w, " ")))
		end
	end
	print(string.format("CAM leader=%d,%d", emu.read(0xD9AA, emu.memType.snesWorkRam) | (emu.read(0xD9AB, emu.memType.snesWorkRam) << 8), emu.read(0xD9AC, emu.memType.snesWorkRam) | (emu.read(0xD9AD, emu.memType.snesWorkRam) << 8)))
end
```
